sig_004c838b95cf7ec892b3.description: Issuing Agency: Project Management Office (PMO) Uncrewed Aircraft Systems Capability Program Executive, Aviation SFAE-AVN-U Agencies Capable of Issuing Contracts/Agreements: Army Contracting Command - Redstone Period of Availability: This Department of War (DoW) Drone Commercial Solutions Opening, open solicitation, will remain open in perpetuity until canceled. Call for Solutions will specify individual response times and requirements. Description of Program: In accordance with Executive Order 14307, the DoW Drone Marketplace is the strategy to scale the industrial base and accelerate production deliveries while empowering Soldiers with freedom of choice to meet mission needs. As part of this approach, the DoW will better incentivize industry innovation. DoW Drone Marketplace marks a significant pivot from traditional DoW acquisition business models to a free-market approach founded on the concept of continuous competition that drives innovation, where Soldiers’ demands are directly linked to industry provided capabilities. This CSO will enable the DoW to rapidly acquire and deliver innovative solutions to the Warfighter using commercial technology. SECTION A – INTRODUCTION AND AUTHORITY The DoW has identified the following needs: (1) to accelerate the adoption of advanced commercial technology; (2) to transform DoW Drone Marketplace capabilities; and (3) to grow the industrial base to appropriately support the DoW. This solicitation aims to provide the DoW with access to innovative solutions enabling the DoW to evolve quickly and maintain a competitive edge over adversaries. Industry is at the forefront of innovation, developing cutting-edge capabilities that will enhance the DoW capabilities and protect the Warfighter. The DoW will select vendors whose solutions demonstrate the greatest potential to achieve the DoW's missions. The DoW is maximizing existing authorities by publishing this CSO, open solicitation, combining any single authority or a combination of the authorities below: Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) 6.102(d)(2) – Other Competitive Procedures 10 U.S.C. §3458 – Authority to acquire innovative commercial products and commercial services using general solicitation competitive procedures / DFARS 212.70 – Defense Commercial Solutions Opening SECTION B - GENERAL INFORMATION The DoW anticipates that the CSO will be updated frequently to improve processes and to keep pace with evolving threats, needs and innovations. The CSO will be open in perpetuity until canceled bythe DoW. Companies are informed that ONLY a warranted Government Contracting/Agreements Officer (KO/AO) (not a Contracting Officer Representative or other personnel) may contractually bind the Government. The Government shall not be liable to pay for work performed by a company unless a warranted KO/AO has signed an agreement in writing stating that the Government shall pay. The Government shall not fund preparation of solution briefs/proposals, or support work efforts or tasks that are inferred from discussions with technical project officers. SECTION C – AREAS OF INTEREST (AOI) This CSO, open solicitation, covers any of the following example areas. These example areas shall be viewed as suggestive, rather than limiting, and are not reflective of the ONLY AOIs or in any priority of order. Intelligence, Electronic, Warfare, and Sensors Tactical Communications Soldier Equipment Ancillary Items Payloads Simulation and Stimulation Training and Instrumentation Unmanned Aircraft Systems (UAS): Full Systems Air Vehicles Maritime Systems: Surface and Undersea Systems Maritime Reconnaissance and Domain Awareness Littoral and Amphibious Support Ground Systems: Reconnaissance and Surveillance Systems Logistics and Equipment Transport Combat and Tactical Support Platforms Counter- UAS: Mutli-Domain Sensing and Detection Command, Control and Data Fusion Defeat Mechanisms (Kinetic and Non-Kinetic) Platform & Operation Integration Supply Chain and Logistics Installation Support and Innovation Additive Manufacturing Autonomous Vehicles Software Autonomous Behaviors Command & Control Launched Effects Drone Production (build at scale) SECTION D – COMMERCIAL SOLUTIONS OPENING (CSO) PROCEDURES There are two methods for responding under this CSO: (1) Innovative Warfighter Solutions submissions and (2) Call for Solution submissions. Method 1 - Innovative Warfighter Solutions (IWS) Provides a flexible and open-ended opportunity for industry partners to submit solution briefs to any AOI in Section C. This aspect of the CSO is designed to identify and bridge gaps in mission-critical capabilities by inviting innovative solutions from the private sector. The purpose is to encourage a wide range of responses that can enhance and support the example AOIs, foster collaboration and leverage cutting-edge technologies and methodologies to meet evolving operational needs. Companies shall follow the procedures outlined in the attachment when providing a submission to an IWS. The submission mailbox for AOI is identified in Section J. Method 2 - Call for Solutions (C4S) Provides an opportunity for industry partners to submit innovative solutions in response to Government issued C4S under any AOI in Section C. C4S aim to pinpoint and address critical gaps in essential capabilities by welcoming creative proposals from private sector entities. Companies shall follow the procedures outlined below and within the specific C4Ss posted. The individual C4S will identify how responses are to be submitted. Method 1 - IWS Overview Companies submitting an IWS in response to the AOIs shall follow the procedures outlined in the attachment. If the Government does not select a company’s submission for, as applicable, for phase 2 and/or 3, the submission may be retained in the Solution Basket. This allows the Government to reconsider the submission for future needs and funding opportunities, maximizing its value to both the vendor and the DoW. The IWS award procedures will utilize up to three (3) phases, as appliable: Solution Brief Live Demonstration and/or Pitch (optional) Commercial Solution Proposal (CSP) Method 2 - C4S Overview CS4 (referred to as “Calls”) will be released and posted via SAM.gov as an amendment under this CSO. The Call will include all relevant submission requirements and evaluation procedures and shall govern the process for evaluations and award. Submission requirements may vary in phases and may take the form of solution briefs, white papers, demonstrations, live pitches, etc. C4S are independent from the IWS procedures discussed above in Section D.1 IWS procedures do not apply to individual Calls. Calls may be written in a broad manner to maximize efficiency, innovation and application when approaching a problem and to allow for maximum participation from vendors who may not be familiar with submitting proposals to Government solicitations. The Government may post Calls at any time. Interested companies are encouraged to frequently check SAM.gov for updates to this solicitation and posted C4S. SECTION E - AWARDS The Government may choose to issue an award(s) in accordance with IWSs or C4S procedures and subject to the availability of funds. The KO/AO reserves the right to negotiate directly with the company on terms and conditions prior to execution of the resulting award instrument, including payment terms, and will execute the instrument on behalf of the Government. All payment obligations of the Government shall be subject to receipt of appropriations from Congress for the purpose, time, and amount of the obligation. Be advised, only a KO/AO has the authority to enter into, or modify, a binding instrument on behalf of the United States Government. Awards issued under this CSO may include, but are not limited to the following award instruments: FAR contracts under FAR Part 12 Commercial Procedures; any fixed price, or fixed price incentive contract type specified under FAR Part 16; and non-FAR agreements such as transaction agreements under 10 U.S.C. 4022 and 10 U.S.C. 4023; for the DoW and/or its customers that are directly relevant to enhancing the effectiveness of the AOI identified in Section J. In order to receive an award, the following must be met: Companies shall have a Unique Entity Identification (UEI) number and must register in the System for Award Management (SAM) prior to receiving an instrument. If a company does not possess a valid and active SAM registration, companies are advised to commence SAM registration before responding to a Call or IWS. Companies are required to maintain registration in SAM throughout the period of performance of the instrument and during any subsequent follow-on award. Companies shall also register in the prescribed Government invoicing system (Wide Area Work Flow: https://wawf.eb.mil/xhtml/unauth/registration/notice.xhtml.) Companies shall represent their small business size and status as required in this solicitation. Companies shall be determined to be responsible by the KO/AO and must not be suspended or debarred from award by the Federal Government nor be prohibited by Presidential Executive Order and/or law from receiving an award. Any actual or potential OCIs shall be identified to KO/AO prior to award. SECTION F – ITERATIVE PROTOTYPING Iterative prototyping is a development methodology where a prototype is created, tested, and refined through multiple cycles, incorporating user feedback and improvements in each iteration, to ensure the final product meets user requirements and expectations effectively. An Other Transaction (OT) for a prototype awarded or an award using 10 U.S.C. 4023 against this open solicitation shall allow for an iterative prototyping process and will be delineated in the award document. An iterative prototyping process will allow the Government to modify, by mutual agreement, the scope of a prototype contract or OT to allow for the adaptation and modification of the technology being prototyped to meet additional unique and discrete purposes/mission sets. The sequential prototype iterations may result in separate phased prototype awards rather than a modification of the original prototype award. These additional unique and discrete purposes/mission sets can be generated by the Government. SECTION I – NON-GOVERNMENT ADVISORS Non-Government advisors may be used in the evaluation of Solution Briefs, Pitches and during the Commercial Solution Proposal phase and negotiations under the IWS procedures or in C4S. Non-Government advisors will have signed non-disclosure agreements (NDAs) with the Government. The company understands that the Government may share proprietary company information with non-Government personnel for evaluation and administrative purposes only. The Government understands that information provided in response to this open solicitation is presented in confidence and may contain trade secret or commercial or financial information, and it agrees to protect such information from unauthorized disclosure to the maximum extent permitted or required by Law, to include: 18 U.S.C. 1905 (Trade Secrets Act); 18 U.S.C. 1831 et seq. (Economic Espionage Act); 5 U.S.C. 552(b)(4) (Freedom of Information Act); Executive Order 12600 (Pre-disclosure Notification Procedures for Confidential Commercial Information); and, Any other statute, regulation, or requirement applicable to Government employees. Companies shall label any information they want protected as confidential. Submissions will not be returned. The original copy of each submission received will be retained by the DoW and all other non-required copies destroyed. SECTION J - CONTACT INFORMATION IWS Solution Brief submissions as detailed in Section D, shall be submitted to the email address listed below and shall include the associated AOI in the subject line of the e-mail. If the respondent does not include the AOI in the subject line of the e-mail, the submission will NOT be reviewed. Area of Interest in Subject Line usarmy.redstone.cpe-avn.mbx.uasmarketplaceiws@army.mil C4S Brief submissions (Section D) shall be submitted in accordance with the instructions and points of contact provided in the Call. General questions surrounding this open solicitation shall be submitted to: Email address: USARMY Redstone Arsenal PEO AVN Mailbox DoW Drone Marketplace SECTION K - DEFINITIONS "Call for Solution" (C4S) an announcement posted on SAM.gov, which may result in a contract or OT and includes submission instructions, evaluation criteria, timelines, how the DoW will treat late submissions, points of contact, and other specific information. The Call is a request for response from prospective industry partners. “Commercial Solutions Opening” (CSO) is a competitive procedure KO/AO may use to acquire innovative commercial items, technologies, or services. “Innovative” means any item that is (1) Any technology, process, or method, including research and development, that is new as of the date of submission of a proposal; or (2) Any application that is new as of the date of submission of a proposal of a technology, process, or method existing as of such date. “Innovative Warfighter Solutions” (IWS) is a competitive procedure for submitting an Innovative Warfighter Solution in response to a posted Area of Interest (AOI) under this Commercial Solutions Opening (CSO). These procedures create a pathway we call the Solution Basket. The IWS gives industry the opportunity to approach the Government with their innovative solutions. “Nontraditional Defense Contractor” is defined by DFARS 202.101 as an “entity that is not currently performing and has not performed any contract or subcontract for DoW that is subject to full coverage under the cost accounting standards prescribed pursuant to 41 U.S.C. 1502 and the regulations implementing such section, for at least the 1-year period preceding the solicitation of sources by DoW for the procurement (10 U.S.C. 3014).” “Nonprofit Institution” is defined in 15 U.S.C. § 3703 an organization owned and operated exclusively for scientific or educational purposes, no part of the net earnings of which insures to the benefit of any private shareholder or individual. "Other Transaction" refers to the statutory authority to enter into transactions other than procurement contracts, grants, or cooperative agreements. The DoW has the authority to enter into OTs for Research Projects (10 USC 4021), OT for Prototype Projects (10 USC 4022), and DoW relevant OT that support research (10 U.S.C. 4021). “Commercial Solution Proposal” (CSP): is a proposal that is submitted in response to a Call that is governed by a CSO or a response to an unsolicited proposal that is invited to Phase III. CSPs may be requested as a result of Solution Briefs and/or presentations/pitches. “Small Business” is defined under Section 3 of the Small Business Act (15 U.S.C. 632).

sig_008fcbd451c57a3642ec.description: In compliance with the principles of necessity, suitability and efficiency established in Article 28 of the LCSP, the nature and extent of the needs intended to be covered by the conclusion of this contract fall within the scope of the functions and powers attributed to this Management Centre, determining with precision the suitability of the object and content of the contract in the Specifications of Technical Requirements. The contract aims to respond to the need to comply with the provisions of Article 3.2.a of Royal Decree 1046/2022, of 27 December, which regulates the governance of the Strategic Plan of the Common Agricultural Policy in Spain and of the European agricultural funds EAGF and EAFRD (hereinafter, Royal Decree 1046/2022), which stipulates that the regional Management Authorities, responsible for the management and execution of the CSP in their territorial scope, shall participate in relation to the evaluation plan and ex-post evaluation, in the establishment of the CSP evaluation plan and in the monitoring and evaluation tasks corresponding to their sphere of competence, reporting on their development and outcome to the Strategic Plan Management Authority. Such an evaluation must necessarily be carried out by functionally independent experts, as required by Article 140 of Regulation (EU) 2021/2115 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 2 December 2021 laying down rules on support for strategic plans to be drawn up by Member States under the common agricultural policy (CAP strategic plans) and financed by the European Agricultural Guarantee Fund (EAGF) and by the European Agricultural Fund for Rural Development (EAFRD) and repealing Regulations (EU) No. 1305/2013 and (EU) No. 1307/2013. Therefore, the corresponding tender must be carried out by this Department so that a team of independent expert evaluators in the field—since the Department of Agriculture, Livestock and Rural Development currently lacks this type of human resource among its staff capable of carrying out the necessary functions to perform this type of work and with the necessary knowledge to be able to carry out thematic evaluations within the framework of the CSP Strategic Plan in the territorial scope of Castile and Leon—can carry it out. In compliance with the provisions of Article 3.2 of DECREE 23/2025, of 30 December, regulating the conditions for the extension of the General Budgets of the Community of Castile and Leon for 2024 in the 2026 financial year, it is noted that the contract proposed to be initiated is considered a continuation of the CAP Strategic Plan approved on 31 August 2022 by the European Commission.
sig_008fcbd451c57a3642ec.title: The purpose of the contract is the provision of the service to the Regional Management Authority of Castile and Leon for thematic evaluations during the years 2026 and 2027.

sig_009721ae1d261a05ddf5.description: This document is not a contract notice or a call for tenders but an invitation to a market dialogue. The City of Helsinki's Urban Environment Division (hereinafter the contracting authority) is preparing the procurement of a traffic signal central control system. The City of Helsinki's Urban Environment Division is procuring a new traffic signal control and monitoring system as a service procurement. The new system to be procured is intended to replace the traffic signal control and monitoring system, which is at the end of its life cycle and covers approximately 200 control units. Helsinki currently has a total of approximately 500 traffic signal control units and uses several control and monitoring systems. In principle, only control units using the RSMP interface will be connected to the system to be procured. The contracting authority's inventory of units comprises devices of different models from different eras, and some of the current units do not support the RSMP interface. For a diverse inventory of units, the control and monitoring system is required to support not only the latest versions of the RSMP interface but also several older versions supported by the current control units. The city will renew older control units in the coming years as separate projects, and the renewed control units will be connected to the system to be procured in connection with the unit replacements. Further information on the subject of the procurement is described in the document Introduction to the Procurement, as well as in the appendix Technical Environment and Responsibility Limits. The purpose of this market dialogue is to explore the market for these services and to obtain information regarding the procurement so that the procurement can be carried out appropriately. The material obtained through the request for information may influence how the procurement criteria are set and which procurement procedure will be used. The contracting authority is not bound by the information provided in this notice or its appendices; as the preparation progresses, the subject and requirements of the procurement may change. We request that you notify us if, in your view, the response contains trade secrets or other confidential information. We request that you identify and mark this information clearly. The responses provided in the request for information are not binding on the supplier, and responding is not a prerequisite for participating in the actual call for tenders later. Responding or failing to respond to the request for information does not affect a potential supplier's position in the actual call for tenders. No compensation will be paid for responding to the request for information. We request that you answer the questions presented in the request for information Forms survey as comprehensively as possible. We request that the answers be written in the fields provided in connection with the questions. Registration for the market dialogue sessions takes place using the same aforementioned Forms survey, where the participant indicates the most suitable time for the market dialogue session. The language used in the market dialogue sessions is Finnish or English. Link: https://forms.office.com/e/sWs6DmPME6
sig_009721ae1d261a05ddf5.title: CALL FOR MARKET DIALOGUE: Procurement of a central traffic light control system

sig_00cb4035c1e3f4f6e4ff.description: Background Innovate UK Business Connect brings together businesses, researchers, investors and partners to accelerate innovation across the UK. As part of UK Research and Innovation (UKRI), and a strategic delivery partner to Innovate UK, we connect organisations to funding opportunities, partnerships and expertise to help ideas move from concept to scale. One of the key tools for making these connections is events. We deliver a diverse portfolio of in-person, virtual and hybrid events, ranging from webinars and workshops to large-scale conferences and exhibitions. To support the effective planning, delivery and evaluation of these events, we are seeking proposals from suppliers who can provide a modern event management system that streamlines event operations, enhances the participant experience and supports data-driven decision-making. Description of work Innovate UK Business Connect is seeking tenders from providers who can supply a single event management system that supports the end-to-end event lifecycle, including event creation, registration management, attendee communications, speaker and exhibitor management, networking, reporting and post-event evaluation. The system should integrate with existing business systems where required and provide a single source of truth for event delivery teams. This aligns with the organisation's wider objective of ensuring events are outcome-led, measurable and supported by efficient registration, communication and reporting processes. The event management system should: • Deliver an intuitive and user-friendly delegate journey from registration through to post-event follow-up • Improve the event experience for speakers and exhibitors • Reduce manual administration and improve operational efficiency • Provide real-time visibility of registrations, attendance, engagement and event performance • Support both virtual and in-person event delivery models • Enable consistent data capture and reporting to demonstrate event impact and ROI • Support accessibility, compliance and data protection requirements The platform must support multiple user roles and permission levels to reflect different operational needs across the organisation. As a minimum, the system should accommodate the following user groups: • Event Managers o Full end-to-end event management capabilities o Creation, configuration and administration of events o Management of registrations, attendee communications, speakers and exhibitors o Access to event-level reporting, analytics and post-event evaluation data • Marketing Managers o Access to update and manage event webpages and associated content o Access to registration, engagement and performance reporting • Integrated Systems o Administration of integrations between the event management platform and our CRM system (Workbooks) o Management of data flows, field mapping, data quality and synchronisation processes o Access to reporting, data exports and system configuration relating to integrations • System Administrators o A small number of designated super users (typically two to three individuals) o Full platform administration rights, including user management, permissions, integrations, security settings and system configuration We deliver a large and diverse portfolio of business-to-business events. Historically, this has included more than 300 events per year and generating approximately 60,000 delegate registrations annually. The event management platform must be capable of supporting a range of event formats, scales and audience sizes, including: • In person events: We deliver approximately 100 in-person events each year, typically attracting between 30 and 2,000 delegates to each. Most events are free to attend and may span one or more days. We do not require onsite event delivery support from the appointment supplier; however the platform must provide the functionality and tools to enable our team to manage attendee registration and onsite event operations, and provide a seamless and efficient onsite experience for attendees • Online Events: We deliver close to 200 fully online events annually. The majority are webinars, including webinar series and interactive workshops. We also run a small number of larger-scale virtual conferences and exhibitions, some of which take place over multiple days. The platform should provide a seamless user experience for both organisers and attendees and support the delivery of events of varying size and complexity. • Hybrid: A smaller proportion of our events are hybrid, combining in-person and virtual attendance. The platform should support hybrid event delivery and provide a consistent registration, communication and reporting experience across both audience groups. The proposed solution must be capable of supporting this volume of activity while providing robust registration management, attendee communications, data integration, reporting and analytics across all event formats. sig_011055b01c4d88cc16cc.description: A national programme is being established to encourage increased levels of physical activity and sustained participation in movement across England. The programme comprises a number of complementary workstreams, including marketing and communications, partnerships and engagement, rewards and recognition, educational content, and a digital component intended to support participation, engagement and long-term habit formation. The contracting authority is considering the future procurement of a supplier to design, build, operate and support the digital elements of the programme. A digital discovery exercise is currently underway and will provide an evidence-based recommendation for the future digital service, including user needs, service design, delivery approach and implementation roadmap. Whilst the final solution has not yet been determined, the discovery is expected to narrow the scope significantly and provide sufficient detail to support rapid delivery. The digital service may comprise a digital product, web-based service, social and community capability, AI-enabled engagement service, integration with existing consumer platforms, or a combination of these approaches. The successful supplier will be expected to take the outputs of the discovery phase through detailed design, build, deployment and live operation. The appointed supplier will work alongside other specialist partners responsible for marketing, communications, partnerships, rewards and wider programme delivery. The role of the digital supplier will be to translate programme objectives into effective digital services and experiences rather than duplicate functions delivered elsewhere within the programme. The programme is operating to ambitious timescales, with an initial digital capability expected to be launched before the end of 2026 and subsequently enhanced through live operation. The authority is therefore interested in engaging with suppliers who can demonstrate experience of delivering, operating and evolving user-centred digital services at pace. Additional information: HI NENC would like to invite potential providers of Digital services to apply to our Dynamic Purchasing System (DPS) DN670401 as a supplier. If your company is not registered with the Proactis (ProContract) Due North Portal, click on this link Supplier registration (due-north.com) and complete your organisation name and email address and continue your registration. If you are already registered on the portal, log in as normal. In the "search" box in upper right-hand corner, type in DN670401 (this is the HI NENC DPS reference number). This opportunity will be developed as a further competition under Lot 5 of our DPS. You should therefore ensure you apply to Lot 5 to be able to bid to provide this service. You are also welcome to apply for any other Lots on our DPS that you feel are relevant to your organisation. Should we decide to proceed to procurement, we are expecting to publish the Invitation to Quote to our Lot 5 suppliers towards the end of July 2026. This timeline is subject to change. Interested suppliers are advised to apply to the DPS promptly to ensure they have been accepted to the framework and receive the competition notification. This notice is for information and engaging with the supply market only. It is not a binding statement of intent or call for competition. HI NENC reserves the right not to enter a formal procurement process and not award a contract. The information contained in this notice, including information relating to the nature and scope of the requirements, the service classification of this requirement from the list of CPV codes, is only indicative of the HI NENC's current thinking and is neither exhaustive nor binding. The procurement is preliminarily aimed at the following software and related services: 1. HR system The HR system must support at least the following areas: - HR master data (organisation data management, personal data management, employment relationship and salary basis management) - Competence management (competence management, competence profile, learning and renewal) - Training management (training and other events) - Continuous coaching discussion / development discussions - Salary discussion - Onboarding - Offboarding - Time management: holidays and absences - HR analytics and reporting 2. Payroll system - E-payslip distribution service 3. Working time management system The working time management solution must include at least: - Working time clocking - Working time reporting (allocation of working time to activities and projects) - Possible shift planning for period-based work (preliminary need) The delivery of the solution preliminarily involves the following requirements: - The solution must meet the functional and non-functional requirements set by Kela - A delivery and deployment project led by the supplier - Necessary integration implementations into other systems - Necessary conversion and migration implementations - Necessary training and documentation - Expert services that may be ordered separately (e.g. system development and consulting) Number of users: There are estimated to be approximately 8 500 users of the system at Kela. The objective of the market dialogue is, among other things: - to form an objective and comprehensive picture of solutions and implementation models on the market - to receive feedback on the content of the procurement subject and service package - to gather views on contract terms - to obtain information on prices and pricing bases Registration for the market dialogue: Kela requests interested suppliers to register and submit a short preliminary presentation of their solution (1-3). The market dialogue can also be conducted as Teams discussions. Registrations are requested to be sent by email: - Address: it.tarjouskilpailut@kela.fi - Message subject: HR-järjestelmä, ilmoittautuminen (1-3) - Content: company's official name and contact person's email address - Deadline: 21.4.2026. We particularly welcome views on the following themes: - Description of how the proposed system package meets Kela's needs - Access rights management, information security and data protection - Customer-specific test environment and related pricing - Integrations into other systems (principles, technologies, interfaces) - Usability-supporting solutions The material to be delivered is expected to include at least: - basic information on the system and architecture - description of support and maintenance - development roadmap - information security and data protection practices (e.g. role assignment, logging, auditing, data location)

sig_016a9e65957eaf90c03b.description: Sahlgrenska Life Building 1 is part of a combined Life Science cluster together with Building 2 and Building 3. Sahlgrenska Life Building 1 is located at Sahlgrenska Hospital, Building 3 on Medicinareberget and Building 2 is a link building over Per Dubbsgatan that connects Building 1 and Building 3. Sahlgrenska Life is an investment for the future of healthcare and research and one of the largest Life Science initiatives in the Nordic region. With Sahlgrenska Life, conditions are created where research and education operate in a close and mutual exchange between healthcare and industry. Västra Götalandsregionen through Västfastigheter Construction and Management is the developer for Sahlgrenska Life Building 1, which is a building with eleven floors above ground and one culvert level. On the building's roof there is a helicopter airport with a runway and parking area for helicopters. The building's gross area is approximately 61 000 m2. In Building 1, both clinical and research premises are planned for Regional Laboratory Medicine and Biobank Väst. Plans are also in place for three healthcare operations - a new emergency department with an associated ambulance hall, an intensive care unit and an operating department. A new helicopter airport for Sahlgrenska Hospital will be located on the roof. Stage 1, which concerns groundworks and a prefabricated frame, has been procured and is ongoing as a general contract. Stage 2 concerns the building envelope, frame completions and installations. This procurement concerns the production management organisation for planning, procurement, implementation, handover and follow-up during the warranty period of the production regarding Stage 2. The stage will be procured and carried out through separate contracts.

sig_01ec67e5684cc534c0b2.description: Arkham Special Mission Processor (SMP): The Government is conducting market research to identify potential sources that possess the expertise, capabilities, facilities, and experience to manufacture, assemble, test, and deliver a total of 94 Arkham SMP Production Kits and 55 Spares. The Arkham SMP is a mission processor utilizing Sensor Open System Architecture (SOSA) in support of AC/MC-130J system integration. The Arkham SMP is separated into two (2) major processing areas: Video Processing/General Processing and Safety Critical Processing. The Video Processing/General Processing is done on five (5) Intel based General Purpose Processor Modules. The Safety Critical Processing is done on two (2) ARM based Safety Critical Processor (SCP) modules. The network includes a red and an internal NextGen SMP gold (same classified level with different subnets), and two unclassified black for multiple levels of security. Safety Critical Processing is separated into Red/Gold and Black zones. The Arkham SMP must utilize LYNXOS and Red Hat Enterprise Linux as the operating system. The acquisition strategy is for the contractor to provide kit production with a period of performance of seven (7) Years. The kit will include the following: Two (2) Arkham Units, two (2) External Data Storage (EDS) Devices, two (2) one (1) TB Delkin Solid State Drives (SSD), and other hardware required for aircraft installation. This will provide the AC/MC-130J mission with enhanced abilities for search and rescue in increased threat environments. Potential Sources must be capable of developing prototype hardware, software, and all associated technical data necessary to be able to produce and deliver the Arkham Production Kit and Spares. The Potential Source must be able to fully test and evaluate the function and performance of the Arkham Production Kit and Spares. The Potential Source must be capable of developing and providing the source data necessary to update AFTO’s and TDPs.
sig_01ec67e5684cc534c0b2.title: AC/MC-130J Arkham SMP Production

sig_01efe81c3a9dc347733b.description: The tender comprises the procurement, establishment and subsequent service—i.e. application operation, support and maintenance—of a joint SRO/SCADA system for the Contracting Authority’s 20 supply plants, as well as physical replacements of electrical equipment at 12 plants. The delivery is carried out as a turnkey contract consisting of the system, application operation and physical replacement. The procurement also includes time-based consultancy services throughout the term of the contract. The purpose is to establish a single uniform and operationally stable platform for monitoring, control and regulation within electricity, water, district heating and facility management, as well as to ensure access to reliable operational data. The overall solution must cover the following supply areas: •The water area comprising three waterworks, two wellfields with 13 extraction boreholes and 11 sectional wells or houses. •The electricity area comprising five transformer stations. •The heat area comprising seven heat generation plants, three pump or booster stations and ten grid metering points. •The facility area comprising the building management at GEV’s head office. The environment also includes 30 Siemens PLCs, 15 Schneider Electric PLCs and other automation equipment. The system delivery comprises the establishment and commissioning of the joint SRO/SCADA system with the necessary programs, licences and components. The system is established on GEV’s IT infrastructure and connected to the relevant plants and systems. The existing PLC and automation plants must be integrated with the new joint SRO/SCADA platform. For designated plants, the existing physical TAG labelling is retained even if it deviates from GEV’s TAG standard. In such cases, the solution must support unambiguous mapping between the physical TAG labelling and the corresponding TAG IDs in the solution. The service delivery comprises application operation of the SRO/SCADA application, monitoring, support, maintenance, bug fixes, updates and further development. The delivery also comprises necessary training and documentation. At 12 plants, the delivery comprises the dismantling and disposal of existing components as well as the replacement or establishment of switchboards, PLCs, connections, UPS systems and frequency converters, among other things. Affected documentation, including signal lists and technical diagrams, must be updated. The delivery is carried out step-by-step per plant and comprises clarification, establishment, training, documentation, installation, testing and commissioning. The supplier must ensure that the system, service and physical works together constitute a functional solution. GEV Holding A/S is conducting the tender on behalf of the following group-affiliated companies: Grindsted Elnet A/S, GEV Varme A/S and GEV Vand A/S. sig_0214ef7a73c691b97c0e.description: The HSE is issuing this Request to Participate (“RTP”) in a Dynamic Purchasing System (hereafter ‘the DPS’) for the provision of Remote Health Monitoring Technologies to support the implementation of Virtual Ward care models via a fully end to end vendor managed solution. The HSE is the Contracting Authority for this public procurement competition on its own behalf and on behalf of all organisations funded by the HSE. A Virtual Ward is a time-limited, safe, and efficient alternative to bedded care enabled by technology that aims to support people who have an acute condition, or exacerbation of a chronic condition requiring hospital-level care, to receive this high acuity care in the place they call home. This approach can provide both an alternative to hospital admission at the Emergency Department, and/or facilitate an earlier discharge from a hospital ward for medical and surgical patients. This DPS will support the implementation of Virtual Wards and associated service capabilities within adult, older persons, and paediatric services across, but not limited to, respiratory, cardiology, and endocrinology pathways. The HSE is seeking to procure an effective and successful market proven, end-to-end vendor managed solution ready for immediate deployment. A central component of the Virtual Ward Solution supported by Remote Health Monitoring Technologies service will be a comprehensive fully vendor managed (end-to-end) solution, including the provision and support of a suite of web-based application(s) and clinical measurement equipment, to facilitate acute clinical care delivered remotely by a multidisciplinary team (MDT) if clinically appropriate and with clear lines of clinical responsibility and governance. This solution will facilitate the avoidance of hospital admission and/or early hospital discharge by providing safe technology that allows suitable patients to be clinically monitored from where they call home.
sig_0214ef7a73c691b97c0e.title: DPS Qualification__Provision of Remote Health Monitoring Technologies to Support the Implementation of Virtual Ward Care Model Solutions (HSE ref. 23112)

sig_021d3e32b4f73b363049.description: Avfall Sør would like to invite the market to a dialogue on the future solution for weighing residual waste at the recycling stations. The aim is to find a system with a high degree of automation/self-service, user friendliness and effective customer flow. It must take care of HSE considerations and be adapted to both the current and future needs for effective resource utilisation and sustainable operation. Avfall Sør has three recycling stations with high availability and access control. The residue waste is collected in large containers with compression; either closed compressor containers or open containers with rolling compressors. This can be changed, but a compressor system is wanted and protection from weather and wind. Key figures are given in the annex. We would like to charge for residual waste based on the weighted amount per customer, in order to comply with the polluter-payer principle and to ensure that sorting pays off. Avfall Sør has examined known systems in the market, but not found satisfactory systems. We would therefore like to have a dialogue with a tenderer who believes that they can offer this. The system must handle weighing and payment of residue waste in an efficient and user friendly way, without a requirement for dedicated manpower. Integration to established systems is not required, but we would like to present the possibilities. Tenderers are invited to submit a solution proposal with a description of relevant systems and price estimates, as well as a reference system. Deadline: 10.12.25, 16.00.Solution proposal can be sent in communication module in Mercell. Deadline for this: 03.12.25, 16:00.
sig_021d3e32b4f73b363049.title: Market dialogue - solution for weighing residual waste at recycling stations for Avfall Sør AS

sig_023870867493cccf1f1e.description: The scope of this contract is to acquire the full range of technical, management and support services necessary to obtain and maintain access to US food and cosmetic products. The contract is divided into the following task areas: Project Management Data Access Data Collection Training Support 6.1 Technical Requirements 6.1.1 Datasets The processed food and cosmetic products and their package data (as well as menu data) shall be from a currently existing, commercially available database(s) that shall provide immediate automated access. The data shall include products from all regions of the US (Appendix B indicates the US Census regions) and be accurate, quality-assured, and easily-validated; well organized; stored as relationally searchable information for trend and other analyses; and fully exportable. The database(s) shall be regularly updated and maintained in a current state throughout the base and option periods. Information will be required for the following product types: Processed, and retail food products (e.g. foods, infant formula, etc.; minimum 400,000 products that are selling on the market in the contract year) and thus, over 2 million historical products; (Optional) Restaurant food products/menu items (minimum 50,000 products from top chains) Dietary supplements (minimum 100,000 products); shall be categorized according to the definition in Appendix A Cosmetics (minimum 300,000 products) The following attributes (as shown on the package) shall be required: Package images (legible images of all surfaces (e.g. sides, top, bottom) of product packaging, including internal and external packaging Count of available images per product Information contained on and in product packaging – shall include the following at minimum (each data entry line in the database must be quality assured and -controlled (QA/QC’d) for accuracy as the database is populated) GTIN/UPC/Barcode Nutrition Facts label, including single and dual columns and including multi-packs (shall be displayed in format according to 21 CFR 101.9) and Supplement Facts label (shall be displayed in format according to 21 CFR 101.36(e)(10) (i), (ii), (iii), and (iv)) Additional nutrients presenting on package labels Indication of added sugars Ingredients list (e.g. food additives, active ingredients for dietary supplements) Allergen labeling information (Contains/may contain) and advisory statements Pack size and weight Number of servings per package Brand Manufacturer Location of manufacturer, packer, or distributor Written and/or pictorial statements signaling the presence of one or more allergens (according to the Food Allergen Labeling and Consumer Protection Act (FALCPA) of 2004; e.g. “Contains”) and/or caution statements about the product (e.g. “warning statements”) Insignificant amounts for certain nutrients Claims on package (e.g., regulated, health, nutrition, efficacy, marketing, and all other types) including indication of “healthy” on package Statements/icons/signages and similar information that features the nutrition, health, organoleptic, processing, suggested usages (e.g., recipes), and other properties of the product (e.g., written and/or pictorial statements that feature nutrient content claim languages, front-of-pack language/icons) Certifications on package GE/Bioengineered/GMO language on package Verbatim language of all text (e.g. product description, instructions, etc.) and icons from product packaging Product source where collected Product category Dates of when product information is a) released to the market and on shelf, b) collected, c) published, d) updated, and e) discontinued Indication of “previous” or “new” nutrition facts label FNDDS 8-digit and 7-digit food codes; SR 5-digit sub codes (8-digit food code shall be linked to food products and ingredients;7-digit food codes are mapped to 8-digit at the product level; 5-digit SR sub codes are mapped to 8-digit food codes at the ingredient level) through 2019 GSFA (General Standard for Food Additives) categories through 2019 Food packaging types (primary and secondary) and codes Food content type Moreover, the data shall provide additional valid and verifiable information on the product ingredients; at a minimum, the data shall provide all available synonym name(s), allergen status, and technical or functional effect descriptors in a usable format. Additionally, FDA shall have access to other Mintel products, such as Mintel Leap, Mintel Food & Drink, Mintel Reports, Mintel Trends, Comperemedia Direct, Market Dynamics, and Global Consumer Research. 6.1.2 Product Requirements Overarching product requirements: Unlimited access for up to 200 FDA personnel; Located external to FDA network (access via weblink); Universal access from any FDA computer hardware (desktops, laptops with docking stations and/or scientific workstations) using internet browsers compatible with FDA current standards; Product access shall not be restricted according to product price; Capability to perform relational searching and analyses of the food and cosmetic product labeling and packaging datasets and menu datasets in functional environments using appropriate methodologies, which shall be valid, reliable, and robust; Ability to support disclosure of scientific and technical articles, study results, presentations, public health advisories, and similar works involving aggregated data to entities outside the Agency including the general public; High resolution, readable images for all sides of the package labels (and optionally, menu images) for validation and other research purposes. Images shall be displayed with product data from all sides of the package so that information may be easily verifiable by the user. Accurate data reflective of verbatim language and icons of product labels (and menus). Verification that products are still being sold in the US marketplace. Users shall be able to analyze and summarize their searches into summary reports and all available data and search results and outputs shall be downloadable and exportable within an accepted timeframe into Microsoft Excel Spreadsheets and Access Data Base Software, SAS Business Analytics Software, and other common formats. Regular, updated, extracted bulk/batch raw data of the full dataset shall be available by API and in MS Excel compatible format (e.g. single pipe delimited txt, csv) and shall be accessible in a secure FTP or cloud service acceptable by FDA. In addition to the product label (and menu) database(s), all sales data, other accompanying databases, and market research reports, when available, shall be provided. This information shall apply to food, dietary supplement, restaurant, and cosmetic products when available Data and UI status updates shall be posted on the system website main page and identified users shall be notified via email System usage statistics (including statistics regarding individual login usage and length of time logged in) shall be available in monthly reports and upon request All data and files shall undergo quality control checks prior to accessibility/delivery to FDA. Documentation on quality control procedures shall be provided (at the onset and with any changes over time) for all data and image collection and data processes (e.g. ingestion of data, quality assurance of data in different formats, etc.) as noted below. Web Interface A user-friendly and data comprehensive interface that is transparent and flexible and allows both predefined (i.e., canned) and custom reports shall be provided. The user should be able to conduct a multi-variable search (i.e. searching a combination of factors concurrently). The user should be able to search and filter according to product category, year, product name, UPC, brand, company, claims, ingredients, allergens, other product attributes, and user-entered keywords in any and all fields. Raw Data Files Raw files (e.g. MS Excel compatible, single pipe-delimited txt, csv) for all data (food, supplements, cosmetics, etc.) shall be delivered a minimum of quarterly as defined by FDA or downable without file size restriction. The file sizes should be appropriate so that they can be opened and readily used. Files shall be accessible in a secure FTP or cloud service acceptable by FDA and organized based on FDA specifications. All files shall also be available by API with fields as specified by FDA. The database(s) shall be scientific based on FDA’s definition: able to verify the data entry line(s) via product images, and the product’s contents may be analyzed, if the user chooses to have the item purchased and analyzed, to verify the accuracy/truthfulness of the product label, the offeror(s) shall provide this as a purchasable service. System maintenance during the base and all option periods, if exercised, shall be provided. Maintenance shall include upgrades and updates to the software and data, continued use of and access to the database system and data, and updates to technical and analytical documentation. 6.1.3 Documentation The Contractor shall compile and submit full documentation to the Contracting Officer Representative (COR) and Project Officer (PO) within 14 days of the beginning of the contract as well as any updated documentation through the contract years. After approval by the COR, all documentation shall be available to access online in the database(s) system with downloadable format into MS Word. The Contractor shall provide documentation on the following: All data collection and acquisition processes so that the source data is clearly understood Documentation on the status of all products found in the databases relative to what is selling on the market each year of the contract (e.g., is the product verified as being available in retail for purchase and/or is it discontinued). The methodologies used for any data cleaning and ingestion processes and those used to develop the data as well as information on pertinent software used as part of the process Data dictionary and a code book defining all data elements/fields that are included in the data package, which includes information on how calculations are performed relative to certain data fields Documentation on the process of standardizing and cleaning data from different sources as well as information on UPCs that are duplicated (e.g. historical vs, duplicated) Any related technical specifications on the technologies or software that is used Information on how to access and use the data in all formats Written methodology regarding quality control procedures for all data and images collected, ingested into a database, exported, and categorized, including information on the oversight of quality control to ensure above 98% accuracy Interface documentation and user guides Any updates to general processes, methodologies, data sources, QC processes, Documentation on limitations of database, errors in the database, and plans for mitigation and/or resolution of issues Full-disclosure 6.1.4 Support / Training A. Support: Ongoing technical and analytical support by phone or by e-mail shall be provided to all certified users of the data during business hours (9:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m. Eastern Time) throughout the period of performance (POP) in accordance with the service levels established in the contract. The Contractor shall notify the COR regarding any issues as they relate to Acceptable Quality Level (AQL) standards. All technical related issues would need to be addressed and resolved in 5 business days or within a reasonable timeframe agreement upon with COR and TCOR. B. Training: The Contractor shall provide up to two (2) one-day training sessions per year (on-site or via web-based methods). This training can be divided into shorter time periods. Additional options for additional “on-demand” sessions either in person or via web-based methods shall be made available under the IDIQ portion of the award. 6.1.5 Data Disclosure Clearance As part of its regulatory activities, FDA shall, at times, require disclosure of scientific and technical articles, study results, presentations, public health advisories, and similar works involving aggregated data to entities outside the Agency including the general public. For activities that require disclosure of aggregated data the Contractor shall accept and adhere to the FDA Data Disclosure Clearance Procedures and form found in Appendices D. The FDA shall continue to require the ability to release aggregated data through the FDA Data Disclosure Clearance process for data obtained during the contract period for the period of all Option Periods. The FDA will require the services of processing clearance requests. As part of its regulatory activities, FDA shall, at times engage in collaborative research projects with third parties outside of FDA for specific research projects of public health importance that are initiated by and for the benefit of FDA. These collaborations shall require FDA to have the ability to share project specific aggregated or raw data with third parties for collaborative research projects. For these collaborations that require sharing of aggregated or raw data, the Contractor shall accept and adhere to the Data Disclosure Clearance Procedures and form to be found in Appendices D. These Procedures include terms and conditions for third party collaborations. 6.2 Project Management The Contractor shall be responsible for creating, managing and updating project plans, schedules and managing resources for the project. 6.2.1 Quality Control The Contractor shall ensure that quality control procedures are conducted prior to providing FDA access to data. The Contractor shall provide written methodology on quality control procedures for all data and images collected, ingested into a database, exported, and categorized, including information on the oversight of quality control to ensure above 98% accuracy. The Contractor shall notify the COR should any issues with the data be noticed and shall flag it in the interface. Should FDA notice issues with the data, the Contractor shall address and fix the issues immediately within an agreed upon timeframe with the COR. 6.2.2 Reporting The Contractor shall provide a brief work plan outlining the strategy for supporting each of the areas outlined in Section 4 of the SOW to the COR within 10 days of award. Each month the Contractor shall provide a status report giving brief descriptions of activities performed. The monthly status report shall, at minimum, contain the following: usage statistics for databases and other resources; usage statistics of technical support feature by FDA staff; technical issues reported by FDA staff; other technical issues (ex. log of times when database(s)/resources were inaccessible), data ingestion success and failure rates with mitigation plans should issues be present. The Contractor shall conduct yearly face-to-face presentation meetings with the COR and other FDA staff as well as deliver final written progress reports about contract performance for the preceding period of performance. The Contractor shall submit to the COR a final report which documents and summarizes the results of the contract work 10 days prior to the end of each period of performance. The final report shall include tables, graphs, diagrams, curves, sketches, photographs and drawings as necessary and in sufficient detail to comprehensively explain the results achieved under this contract. 6.3 Contract Services Requirements The Contractor shall perform the following types of tasks as needed: Contractor shall collect information for selected products. The list of products and data fields to be collected shall be defined by the COR. Contractor shall conduct search(es) for products using search criteria defined by the COR. The option shall be available to purchase identified products. Contractor shall conduct exports for products using search criteria defined by the COR as needed. sig_0273419f3619102cfe5e.description: Link Group, the Contracting Authority, is seeking to modernise its telephony and contact management environment as part of a wider customer experience transformation. The requirement is not limited to a like-for-like telephony replacement. Link is seeking to understand how the market can support a move from fragmented channels and siloed systems towards a single, integrated and insight-led contact management platform. The primary objective is to implement a modern, scalable, cloud-based Contact Centre as a Service (CCaaS) solution capable of supporting seamless multi-channel customer engagement across voice, live chat, messaging, social media and future digital channels. Link is particularly interested in solutions that can provide a single view of the customer, intelligent routing based on customer intent and need, real-time operational visibility, workforce engagement capability and data-driven insight across the end-to-end customer journey. This Prior Information Notice (PIN) is issued solely to initiate a Preliminary Market Consultation exercise. The purpose is to test market capability, understand available delivery models, inform Link’s emerging specification and procurement strategy, and explore how suppliers can support both technology replacement and service transformation outcomes, including automation, virtual assistants, AI-assisted colleague support, workforce management and customer journey-led redesign. Link’s emerging priorities include reducing repeat contact, redials, avoidable transfers and misdirected queries; improving colleague access to customer history and knowledge prompts; enabling real-time demand management and reporting; increasing digital adoption through automation and self-service; and ensuring that future technology is aligned to priority customer journeys rather than being designed around existing channel structures. Lot 1: . Link Group is a group of social enterprise companies and one of Scotland’s largest social landlords. Link Group provides affordable housing, property management, regeneration, advice, financial inclusion, employability, care and support services to a large and diverse customer base across Scotland. Link Group serves more than 20,000 customers and provides housing management services to circa 16,000 tenants in social rented accommodation, including general needs and sheltered housing. The Link Group structure includes a number of related organisations and service areas that collectively deliver housing, property, care, support and community-based services. These include Link Group Ltd, which provides core group functions; Link Group Housing Services, which delivers housing management services for social rented tenants; C~urb, which brings together development, property management, letting, factoring and property maintenance activities; Horizon Housing Association, which provides affordable housing and services that support people with impairments to live independently; Larkfield Housing Association, a community-based Registered Social Landlord in Greenock; LinkLiving, which provides person-centred care, housing support and wellbeing services, and West Highland Housing Association, which provides affordable housing, property management, and maintenance services across the Lorn area and the Inner Hebridean islands of Scotland. The proposed replacement of telephony and contact centre systems is intended to support the wider Link Group operating environment rather than a single isolated service area. The future solution may therefore need to support multiple customer-facing and colleague-facing functions across housing, repairs, property management, factoring, care and support, advice, employability, development and corporate services. The Customer Service Centre (CSC) acts as a primary customer contact function, managing enquiries across housing, repairs, income, complaints and related services. Link also operates specialist customer-facing teams, including services supporting housing applications, registrations, lettings, responsive repairs, planned maintenance, compliance activities and property-related enquiries. These teams collectively support high-volume contact across a broad range of customer journeys. For market-sizing purposes, Link currently anticipates a future licence requirement in the region of 250–500 user licences across the Group, subject to confirmation through future operating model development, service design and multi-skilling activity. Given the scale and breadth of these services, effective contact management is central to Link’s ability to provide responsive, accessible and joined-up services to tenants, owners, applicants, private rented sector customers, supported people, partners and other stakeholders. This group-wide context is important because suppliers may be required to demonstrate how their proposed solution can support different operating models, service hours, customer journeys, user groups, reporting requirements, call flows, contact channels and integration needs across Link Group. Link is therefore seeking market insight into solutions that can provide scalable, resilient and configurable contact management capability across the full breadth of the group, while enabling consistent customer experience, improved colleague access to information and better operational insight.. sig_02f3081ecfb6290db6c4.description: For over 25 years, the Authority has relied on its existing Information Technology Service Management (ITSM) platform to manage IT services. It has been the backbone of logging, tracking and resolving requests—everything from fixing technical issues to setting up new starters. The technology landscape has moved on: cloud platforms, automation and integrated digital services are now standard, and the Authority now wishes to explore this technology. The Authority is now moving to Enterprise Service Management (ESM). In simple terms, ESM means creating one front door for services—a single, easy‐to‐use platform where staff and customers can make requests, check progress and get help quickly, regardless of which team provides the service. Behind the scenes, it uses proven good‐practice processes (ITIL) to ensure work is handled consistently and efficiently. It will also integrate with tools we already use, enabling automation, clearer customer journeys and, over time, the use of AI to enhance the experience. The Authority’s current version of its ESM platform is hosted on‐premise, and the contract ends in March 2026. The Authority’s version of this ESM tool provides a single platform for multiple service areas, not just IT. The Authority’s ambition for this Procurement is to implement, migrate to and continue to support a cloud hosted ESM platform that provides a modern, flexible and integrated approach to organisation wide service delivery. The Authority plans to retire its I.T. Asset Management (ITAM) tool as part of this tender. This will allow the Authority to leverage greater capabilities within a single platform, providing better data for decision‐making through modern dashboards and reporting. The Contract is expected to commence on Thursday 19th February 2026 and will run for a core period of five (5) years, unless terminated or extended in accordance with the terms set out in the Contract. The estimated total value of the requirement over the Contract’s five-year core period is £935,000, which also represents the maximum budget available for Supplier Tenders and the resulting ESM Contract. Any Tender submissions exceeding this value will be rejected in accordance with the assessment criteria outlined in Stage 1: Procurement Specific Questionnaire (PSQ) and Stage 2: Tender Evaluation Criteria. The Contract will have a core period of five (5) years, subject to the termination provisions set out within the Contract. In addition, the Authority reserves the right to extend the Contract by up to five (5) additional years, through two separate extension options: • One extension of three (3) years • One extension of two (2) years If both extension options are exercised, the maximum potential duration of the Contract would be ten (10) years. The estimated contract value of £1,910,000.00, as stated in this Contract Notice, is based on the Authority awarding the contract at its maximum budget of £935,000 for the initial 5-year core term, and subsequently exercising all five optional extension years. For the extension period (years 6 to 10), an estimated annual inflation rate of 4% has been applied to reflect projected cost increases over time. The estimated value is provided in good faith to assist Suppliers in preparing their Tenders. It does not constitute a commitment by the Authority to spend the full amount. No stated value shall create a binding financial obligation unless explicitly confirmed within the Contract. Lot 1: .

sig_03a8ffb79be762f7adf3.description: UKSBS currently operates an on-premise infrastructure and network monitoring capability that provides visibility across critical infrastructure, networks, applications and databases. sig_04513333c2a298124a08.description: Network Rail is seeking to engage the market regarding the future procurement of a Certificate Lifecycle Management (CLM) solution. This project is driven by significant industry changes, including the CA/Browser Forum’s decision to reduce the maximum lifespan of public SSL/TLS certificates over the coming years. By 2029, certificates will require renewal as frequently as every 47 days, and domain validation reuse will be limited to just 10 days. These changes are intended to enhance security but will introduce substantial operational overhead, making manual certificate management impractical and automation essential. Network Rail operates across a complex landscape of on-premises, cloud, and supplier-managed environments. A key challenge is the fragmented ownership and lack of central visibility over certificates, particularly those issued and managed by third-party suppliers. This fragmentation increases the risk of outages due to expired or misconfigured certificates and limits Network Rail’s ability to monitor, renew, or enforce compliance directly. The CLM project aims to address these challenges by implementing a solution that enables the centralised, automated management of certificates throughout their lifecycle, regardless of where they are issued or managed. The solution must provide comprehensive visibility across all environments, support robust automation for renewal and validation, and enable clear supplier accountability through contractual mechanisms. This includes the ability to track certificates managed by third parties, enforce renewal responsibilities, and ensure that incidents caused by supplier failures can be managed contractually. Network Rail is inviting suppliers to demonstrate how their solutions can meet these requirements, including the ability to: Centrally track and manage certificates across all environments and suppliers. Automate certificate renewal, validation, and compliance processes. Provide visibility and control over third-party issued certificates. Support supplier accountability and contractual enforcement. Align with upcoming industry standards and security requirements. Deliver proven solutions at scale, with references from similar large infrastructure organisations. This market engagement will inform Network Rail’s approach to the procurement of a CLM solution that ensures security, operational resilience, and compliance in a rapidly evolving digital landscape. sig_04bd4dfefcc7481716c7.description: Provision of a marketplace platform The advertised online portal is to be connected to SAP SRM as a catalogue via an interface based on the Open Catalog Interface (OCI) standard. In the intended process, the catalogue is called up by the user via a link from SAP SRM; it opens in a new browser window and is displayed there in a frame. In this catalogue, the user compiles a shopping basket from the required items. In the supplier's catalogue application, the user then completes the shopping basket after a verification step and initiates the transfer of the catalogue shopping basket to SAP SRM via the OCI interface. All items, quantities, and prices are transferred to the SRM shopping cart via the interface. The order is then completed by the user within the university according to a specified approval process and transmitted to the supplier. Direct order triggering from the supplier's online portal must not take place. The catalogue solution offered must therefore meet the conditions for connection from Appendix 5 "OCI Catalogue Performance Requirements" and for order transmission from Appendix 4 "IDOC Interface". SAP SRM is expected to be replaced by a successor product in the year 2026. Any necessary system adjustments to the marketplace connection will be supported by the contractor.
sig_04bd4dfefcc7481716c7.title: Marketplace

sig_04c9fc335f9ffdb6cd6f.description: The contract consists of principal project management services for the construction phase of the Rochepinard junction. This project for a new Tours Rochepinard interchange on the A10 motorway is located between the existing junctions no. 21 (Tours centre) and no. 22 (Saint Avertin), around the PS 155 (PR 208+950), and includes the construction of the 4 slip roads and all the junctions and roads necessary to ensure the connection with the local network. This junction is located in an urban area and will be toll-free. It also includes the construction of a Multimodal Exchange Hub (PEM). It also includes the redevelopment and upgrading to current standards of the 2 slip roads of the 1⁄2 existing junction no. 22 of Saint Avertin. The services covered by the contract concern the principal project management services in the study phases starting from the appropriation of the AVP and the Impact Study, the PRO, the G2 PRO/DCE (excluding surveys) then the preparation of the DCE, and the DCE, ACT, G2 ACT, VISA, DET, OPC, AOR, and ITS phases. The services covered by the contract concern the principal project management services in the construction phase. The principal project management mission includes the project management missions for the PRO, G2 PRO/DCE (excluding surveys), DCE, ACT, G2 ACT, VISA, DET, OPC, AOR phases, within the meaning of the MOP law and its implementing texts. The principal project management mission also includes a phase for the appropriation of the AVP and the Impact Study File, and a phase for assistance to the project owner for the ITS (Technical and safety inspection of FCA before commissioning). The description of the works is as follows: -the creation of a complete junction (4 slip roads) but without tolls at the level of the PS155 (PR 208+950) including the construction of the 4 slip roads and all the junctions and roads necessary to ensure the connection with the local network. -the complete redevelopment of the 2 slip roads of the existing Saint Avertin half-junction -the construction of a multimodal exchange hub including 8 bus stop bays and a bus turning area. The operation also includes the following developments (the exhaustive list will be determined in the study phase and optimised or modified if necessary according to technical possibilities): -Construction of the 4 new entry and exit slip roads; -Creation of connection junctions with the secondary network of the roundabout, urban or traffic light type; with facilities for high-level service bus traffic on a dedicated site -Removal/modification of existing junctions on the secondary network; -Integration and construction of lanes reserved for certain soft modes (pedestrians, cycles); -Restoration of roads intercepted by the project (Boulevard Georges Pompidou for example); -Resumption of safety and operational equipment intercepted by the project, on existing structures, main section and existing slip roads of the A10 motorway -Resumption and additions to drainage and construction of new basins, including in the central reservation -Installation and resumption of existing and additional signage announcing the new junction; -The construction of visual and acoustic screens; -the construction of retaining walls -the re-cutting and construction of a lower structure for the restoration of a stream -the construction of an underpass for pedestrians under secondary roads -the relocation of 2 shelters with emergency call stations on the A10 motorway -soil decontamination -utility diversions in an urban environment. The contract holder will have the role of principal project manager and will, in this capacity, ensure the coordination of all additional service providers. A risk and cost management system must be put in place. The candidate must necessarily include specialists in all aspects of the operation as cited.
