sig_0582aba2ee02a37a2288.description:
Supply of a forest fire location system divided into two parts. Part No. 1 - Supply, installation and commissioning of a forest fire monitoring system based on long-range fire-fighting cameras together with software for automatic smoke detection. Part No. 2 - Supply, installation and commissioning of a complete unmanned aerial vehicle system with an automatic docking station for fire monitoring of forest areas. A detailed description can be found in the relevant parts of the contract. The subject of the contract consists of sets of equipment together with installation and commissioning, the task of which will be to enable automatic detection and location of forest fires, including long-range fire-fighting cameras mounted on observation towers together with necessary accessories and the equipment of the Inspectorate's Alarm and Dispatch Point (ADP). The purpose of the system will be to carry out continuous fire monitoring of forest areas. Fire-fighting cameras mounted on observation towers are to work with the supplied software for automatic fire detection, which is intended to increase the effectiveness of monitoring in the given area. The image from the cameras must be sent to the ADP via a radio link in the unlicensed band, supplied and installed under this contract. The transmission system must be designed in a way that enables the future change of the transmission medium from radio to fibre-optic without the need to replace cameras, software and active network devices, with the exception of terminal devices used for connecting the fibre optic.. The Baczków and Hysne towers should be retrofitted with an Off-Grid power supply installation, and the ADP with a UPS emergency power supply system. The power supply must meet the requirements of PN-EN 62040-5-3:2017-05 (UPS systems) or equivalent. The installation must meet the requirements of PN-EN 62446-1:2016-08 (Photovoltaic installations) or equivalent, PN-EN 62446-1:2016-08/A1:2019-01 (Testing of PV installations) or equivalent, PN-EN 62109-2:2011 (Inverter safety) or equivalent and PN-EN IEC 62619:2023-02 (Lithium battery safety) or equivalent. The contract includes: - dismantling of the existing fire monitoring system, - supply and installation of 3 cameras for observing forest areas on the Baczków, Hysne and Dąbrowa fire-fighting towers, - supply and installation of sprinklers together with a fluid tank for the mounted cameras, - supply and installation of an off-grid power supply on the Baczków and Hysne towers. The installation must meet the requirements of PN-EN 62548 (Photovoltaic installations) or equivalent, PN-EN 62446 (Testing of PV installations) or equivalent, PN-EN 62109 (Inverter safety) or equivalent and PN-EN IEC 62619 (Lithium battery safety) or equivalent. - supply and installation of an alarm system and anti-burglary cameras on the fire-fighting towers, - supply and installation of radio links establishing connections: ● Baczków tower – Hysne tower in the 5 GHz band, ● Hysne tower – Dąbrowa tower in the 5 GHz band, ● Dąbrowa tower – Church in the 60 GHZ band with a backup 5 GHz, ● Church – Inspectorate building in the 60 GHZ band with a backup 5 GHz, ● Baczków tower – Dąbrowa tower in the 5 GHz band (redundant connection), - supply and installation of devices to provide backup communication 5G/LTE, - supply and installation of ADP equipment: ● supply and installation of 3 televisions for observing images from fire-fighting cameras, ● supply and installation of a computer with two monitors, ● supply and installation of a control console, ● supply and installation of a UPS emergency power supply. The power supply must meet the requirements of PN-EN 62040 (UPS systems) or equivalent. - supply, installation and commissioning of an automatic smoke detection system, - training on system operation. The Contractor is obliged to execute a complete work from the point of view of the purpose it is to serve. The Contracting Authority permits the installation of additional devices not included in the specification if they are necessary to achieve the required functionalities. Other information can be found in the procurement documents - Appendix No. 2 to the ToR; Supply, installation and commissioning of a complete unmanned aerial vehicle system with an automatic docking station for fire monitoring of forest areas - equipment under the FEnIKS project entitled: Comprehensive project for the adaptation of forests and forestry to climate change - prevention, counteracting and limiting the effects of threats related to forest fires (FIRE 2). 1. Subject of the contract 1.1. The subject of the contract is the supply of one complete, factory-new and unused UAS system comprising an unmanned aerial vehicle, an automatic docking station, a multi-sensor observation head, a control device, software, accessories, installation, configuration, commissioning, training and warranty service. 1.2. The system will be intended primarily for: automatic and ad-hoc patrols of forest areas during the fire hazard period; remote verification of smoke or fire alarms, including alarms transmitted by the alarm and dispatch point, camera system or rescue services; locating heat sources and determining their coordinates; live transmission in the visible and thermal imaging band; monitoring fire development, access roads, endangered objects and control after extinguishing a fire. 1.3. The subject of the contract has been described through functional requirements and minimum performance parameters. The Contracting Authority does not require a product of a specific brand or a single manufacturer's solution. However, all elements must form one compatible system, for the correct operation of which the Contractor is responsible. 2. Basis and rules for describing the subject of the contract. The description was drawn up taking into account in particular Article 16, Article 99, Article 101 and Article 105–107 of the Act of 11 September 2019 on Public Procurement Law (unified text: Journal of Laws of 2026, item 793 as amended). References to standards are to be understood as references to the indicated standard or an equivalent standard.

• Each indicated parameter is a minimum parameter, unless expressly stated otherwise. • Structurally different technical solutions are permitted if they ensure at least the same functionality, level of security and performance parameters. • If meeting a requirement requires an additional module, licence, modem, antenna, service or accessory, this element must be included in the tender and price. • All costs necessary to use the full functionality of the system for the period indicated in the OPZ must be itemised in the price form. Other information can be found in the procurement documents - Appendix No. 2 to the ToR

sig_0611fab13b4f11434e43.description: Performance recording software for Technical Operations (municipal works yard) as Software as a Service (SaaS) The Technical Operations department of the City of Bochum (4, 44793 Bochum) currently maintains and services municipal infrastructure in the areas of urban greenery, road and drainage facilities, and municipal cemeteries with approx. 600 employees. It also operates a crematorium. The department has four divisions: Central Tasks, Greenery Division, Roads and Drainage Division, and Cemeteries and Crematorium Division. Within the divisions, a total of 27 operational units are active in providing these services. In addition, there is the technical administrative department, which awards services externally to third parties. Technical Operations is subject to continuous task review and optimisation, meaning that the organisational structure and workflows must be adapted regularly. New tasks and business processes may be added. This therefore also applies to the regularly required reports and evaluations. The employees work within the scope of the collective agreement for the public service (TVöD-VKA and TVöD-NRW) and provide numerous services. Management and administrative roles are partly filled by civil servants who are subject to the regulations of the North Rhine-Westphalia State Civil Service Act (Landesbeamtenrecht NRW). In order to record the services provided and the associated costs efficiently and purposefully, Technical Operations is looking for recording software for municipal works yards / depots. All services provided ("products") must be recorded, evaluated, and analysed. These services arise from the budget structure of Technical Operations. The services are provided in the area of predefined facilities or georeferenced points. In addition, services provided in connection with vehicles are to be evaluated. In particular, the software solution must be used not only to record performance but also to record hardship allowances in accordance with TVöD. For this purpose, the current regulations from the relevant collective agreements must be observed (in particular TVöD in the area of the Association of Municipal Employers' Associations (TVöD-VKA) and the regional collective agreement for the TVöD in the area of KAV NW (TVöD-NRW)). In this context, Technical Operations is planning the introduction of a cloud solution in which the bidder provides and maintains a software solution and the associated cloud (Software as a Service (SaaS)). The bidder provides a Software as a Service (SaaS), supports the setup, provides the IT infrastructure required for this, and carries out maintenance. The provider takes care of maintenance, upgrades, support, security, and all other aspects of software administration, including the cloud required for operation. A Software as a Service (SaaS) provider undertakes several important tasks to enable customers to use the software smoothly and efficiently: - Provision and maintenance of the infrastructure: The provider provides the necessary hardware and network infrastructure and ensures its maintenance and updating. - Software updates and maintenance: Regular updates and maintenance work are carried out to keep the software up to date and close security gaps. - Security and data protection: The provider implements security measures to protect users' data and ensures that data protection regulations are complied with. - Customer support: Effective customer support is provided to help with technical problems or questions regarding the use of the software. - Scalability: The provider ensures that the software is scalable and meets the growing demands of users. - Accessibility and availability: The software is made available around the clock so that users can access it at any time. This list is not exhaustive. Rather, it is intended to ensure a common understanding of what is generally meant by SaaS. In particular, the client's requirements are specified by this specification of services, the bill of quantities, and the EVB-IT cloud contract. However, the provision of the software solution must imperatively take place as a SaaS / cloud solution. The SaaS or cloud solution must be entirely browser-based and must not require any additional local components on the part of the client for its operation. The software already exists in its basic functions and does not first need to be developed. It must be adapted to the client's requirements (customisation). A service contract will be concluded with a base term of 24 months from the award of contract. Thereafter, the contract is automatically extended by a further 12 months each time, unless the contract is terminated by either party. The offer price is to be calculated for a term of 48 months.

This Sources Sought is a market research tool being used to determine potential and eligible business firms that are capable of providing the services described herein prior to determining the method of acquisition and issuance of a Request for Proposal. The existing contract was previously competed, with two offers received. Nevertheless, the Government would like to ensure that there is adequate competition for this procurement. All interested large and small businesses are encouraged to respond with a capability statement, but only those businesses or teaming arrangements that are considered small under NAICS 541330-1 will be considered for small business set-aside decisions. INTRODUCTION The Naval Air Warfare Center Aircraft Division (NAWCAD) Webster Outlying Field (WOLF) at Patuxent River, MD announces its intention to procure, on a competitive basis services to provide Command, Control, Communications, Computers, Cyber, Combat Systems, Intelligence, Surveillance, and Reconnaissance (C6ISR) integration and installation; systems engineering support; In-Service Engineering Agent (ISEA); and logistics support to Mission Systems programs, systems, and technological areas within the SAIW project portfolio. Further details are provided in the Draft Performance Work Statement (PWS)/Statement of Work (SOW) attached to this synopsis (Attachment 1). The services are currently being performed by The MIL Corporation of Bowie, MD under N00421-24-D-0002. The current contract is Cost-Plus Fixed Fee (CPFF) containing both performance-based Completion CLINs and Level-of-Effort (LOE) CLINs. This contract is due to expire 14-FEB-2029. Although the current Period of Performance (PoP) of this requirement is scheduled to end Q2 FY2029, the estimated exhaustion date is now within Q1 FY2028. PROGRAM BACKGROUND As the organic Lead Systems Integrator® (oLSI®) for the Naval Air Warfare Center Aircraft Division (NAWCAD), Webster Outlying Field (WOLF) operates under a product-based business model whereby NAWCAD WOLF civilians lead and manage the execution of the requirements with combined Government-Industry teams. Using this oLSI® approach, the Government maintains control of intellectual property and data rights, enabling WOLF to rapidly adapt solutions to the dynamic needs of the warfighter. The NAWCAD WOLF Ship & Air Integrated Warfare (SAIW) Division is the oLSI® providing design, procurement, integration, testing, and training of Command, Control, Communications, Computers, and Intelligence (C4I) electronic systems that meet the requirements of the United States Navy operating forces. The SAIW Division, operating under the oLSI® model, has requirements for services to provide Command, Control, Communications, Computers, Cyber, Combat Systems, Intelligence, Surveillance, and Reconnaissance integration and installation (C6ISR); systems engineering support; In-Service Engineering Agent; and logistics support to Mission Systems programs, systems, and technological areas within the SAIW project portfolio. REQUIREMENTS Please review Attachment 1, Draft PWS/SOW and Attachment 2, Draft Hours. If your company has any questions about the PWS/SOW, Draft Hours, or any areas that may need further explanation, please also identify those in the response. The labor categories anticipated to execute the contemplated effort are included in Attachment 2, Draft Hours. Since the resultant contract will be a cost-type effort, the successful awardee will also be required to have a Government approved accounting system upon award. All Contractors that propose must either have or be able to obtain a TOP SECRET facility clearance. A DD Form 254 Contract Security Classification Specification shall apply to this requirement and the prime contractor shall have a “Top Secret” Facility Clearance and a “Secret” Safeguarding Clearance. ELIGIBILITY The applicable North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) Code for this requirement is 541330-1 Engineering Services with a Small Business Size standard of $47 Million. Businesses of all sizes are encouraged to respond; however, each respondent must clearly identify their business size in their capabilities statement. The Product Service Code (PSC) for this effort will be K058: Modification of Equipment - Communication, Detection, and Coherent Radiation Equipment PLACE OF PERFORMANCE % On-Site Government % Off-Site Contractor WOLF St. Ingioes, MD 100% 22% 78% ANTICIPATED CONTRACT TYPE The requirement is anticipated to be a Single Award, Indefinite Delivery Indefinite Quantity (SA IDIQ) contract with Cost-Plus-Award-Fee (CPAF) Level of Effort (LOE)/Term Contract Line Item Numbers (CLINs) for a portion of labor, Firm Fixed Price (FFP) CLINs for the remaining labor, and cost reimbursable CLINs for Other Direct Costs (ODCs). The proposed contract is anticipated to include tasking and labor categories that are subject to the Service Contract Act. ANTICIPATED PERIOD OF PERFORMANCE It is anticipated that the resultant contract is estimated to begin in Q1 FY2028 and will have a five-year ordering period It is anticipated performance will commence approximately in December 2027. The estimated manhours hours by CLIN type are as follows: For the FFP CLINs: 272,910 manhours (for estimating purposes only, based on projections from historical data.) For the CPAF CLINs: 892,097 manhours SUBMITTAL INFORMATION It is requested that interested businesses submit to the contracting office a brief capabilities statement package (no more than 15 pages in length, single spaced, 12 point font minimum) demonstrating the ability to perform the effort listed in the attached Draft PWS/SOW, Attachment 1. This documentation must address, at a minimum, the following: Title of the PWS/SOW to which you are responding; Company profile to include number of employees, annual revenue history, office location(s), CAGE code, DUNS number, and a statement regarding current small/large business status; Respondents to this notice must also indicate whether they qualify as a Small, Small Disadvantaged, Service Disabled Veteran Owned Small Business, Women-Owned, 8(a), Historically Underutilized Business (HUB) Zone, or Veteran Owned Small Business concern; If a small business, provide an explanation of your company's ability or your company’s ability combined with a similarly situated entity’s ability to perform at least 50% of the tasking described in this PWS/SOW; Resources available such as corporate management and currently employed personnel to be assigned to tasks under this effort to include professional qualifications, specific experience of such personnel, and the ability to have personnel located at the city specified; Management approach to staffing this effort with qualified personnel; Statement regarding capability to obtain the required industrial security clearances for personnel; Company's ability to meet the requirements in the Facility and Safeguarding requirements; Company's ability to begin performance upon contract award; Company's ability to manage a team of subcontractors, including a list of contracts and teaming arrangements; Prior/current corporate experience performing efforts of similar size and scope within the last three years, including contract number, organization supported, indication of whether as a prime or subcontractor, contract values (dollars and hours), Government point of contact with current telephone number, and a brief description of how the referenced contract relates to the services described herein. What specific technical skills does your company possess which ensures capability to perform the tasks? It is requested that, in the response to the Sources Sought, the company explain its capability to accomplish the work specified under the paragraphs 3.3.1 and 3.3.2 of the draft PWS/SOW Technical Requirements. If the company finds itself not capable to perform all parts of the PWS/SOW, please specify which portions of the PWS/SOW it is not capable of accomplishing. If the company will be teaming or utilizing subcontracts, please include information regarding which work the subcontractor will be responsible for and how the prime will determine the subcontractor is capable of accomplishing the work. The capability statement package shall be sent by email to nicholas.a.suhosky.civ@us.navy.mil and carolyn.a.emmart.civ@us.navy.mil. sig_06e3026067216c0f322c.description: NEW mobil und aktiv Mönchengladbach GmbH and NEW mobil und aktiv Viersen GmbH are public undertakings responsible for transport and swimming pool operations in the cities of Mönchengladbach and Viersen. Furthermore, the companies hold line concessions in the Rhein-Kreis Neuss, the Kreis Viersen and the Kreis Heinsberg. In the following, NEW mobil und aktiv Mönchengladbach GmbH is named for both companies. The two transport companies of the NEW Group, NEW mobil und aktiv Mönchengladbach GmbH and NEW mobil und aktiv Viersen GmbH, intend to introduce an ID-based ticketing system (IDBT) for the digitalisation and modernisation of sales in local public passenger transport. The aim is to implement cash-free and paperless ticketing based on EMV-compatible bank cards (open loop) as well as supplementary closed-loop EMV credit cards for user groups without a bank account. The project comprises the creation of an overall system. The scope of supply and services is structured as follows: 1. contactless sales devices (validators), 2. software and interfaces (purchase licences via a one-off fee) as well as 3. supplementary services such as installation and commissioning in the vehicle, project management, documentation and training. Following overall system acceptance, the overall IDBT system is to be operated with the following services: 1. operation of hardware, software and interfaces, 2. operation of a cloud, 3. processing of the transit payment service as well as 4. provision of supplementary services such as system service, software maintenance and conclusion of mobile communications contracts. The aim is customer-friendly, rapid and cash-free sales within the vehicle, in which, after a tap with an open-loop EMV or closed-loop EMV card at the validator, the encrypted token identity serves as a digital ticket. Initially, predefined tariff products (KFT) will be offered at the validator, and check-in-check-out (MTT) will also be used from a prospective perspective. For the project tendered here, "Introduction of an ID-based ticketing system (IDBT) for the digitalisation and modernisation of sales in local public passenger transport", funding is being sought via the Verkehrsverbund Rhein-Ruhr (VRR) in order to finance the introduction and operation. NEW mobil und aktiv Mönchengladbach GmbH and NEW mobil und aktiv Viersen GmbH are each carrying out the project "Introduction of an ID-based ticketing system" as an independent funding measure in accordance with the scheduling notifications of the VRR (OM 2025 02116 or 2025 04166). The present project can only be implemented if funding is granted to the extent previously discussed with the funding body. There is currently no reason to fear that the envisaged funding notifications would not be issued. Nevertheless, it must be clearly stated that at the time of the commencement of this procurement procedure, no funding notification is available. Therefore, the explicit notice must be given here that, should it – for whatever reasons – not have happened by immediately prior to the award of contract of this procurement procedure that NEW mobil und aktiv Mönchengladbach GmbH or NEW mobil und aktiv Viersen GmbH have received funding notifications from the aforementioned funding programme in the extents previously discussed with the funding body, the contract cannot be awarded. Either the binding period must then be extended in agreement with the bidders or the procurement procedure must be terminated by cancellation, especially in the event that there is ultimately no prospect whatsoever of obtaining funding. Then the procurement procedure cannot be concluded by contract award. As the general contractor, the contractor assumes overall responsibility for the planning, delivery, integration, commissioning and stable operation of the ID-based overall ticketing solution ("NEW IDBT") including all hardware and software components as well as all interfaces and dependencies. It shall ensure that the overall solution is fully functional in accordance with the specification over the entire contract term and that the relevant requirements of the card schemes (inter alia transit/retail-like and PAYG/MTT transactions) are complied with. The EVB-IT contract underlying the tender shall begin with the award of contract and end upon the expiry of 120 months after overall system acceptance. The contract shall be extended after the expiry of 120 months three times by 24 months each under the same conditions, if it is not terminated by the contracting authority with a notice period of six months to its end. However, it shall end at the latest after 72 months of extension without the need for termination.
sig_06e3026067216c0f322c.title: IDBT – ID-based ticketing system Procurement of hardware and software and procurement of the services required for the introduction and operation of the IDBT.

sig_06ff8a92cd27e8fa2ab4.description: The procurement concerns a framework agreement relating to services within the IT and information security field for the call-off of consultants within the tender areas specified in this document. A further success factor is to act with high flexibility regarding staffing in the short term and with short notice in order to meet new assignments, projects and changes in existing assignments. The consultants shall support the Ordering Party's ongoing operations as needs arise. Assignments will preferably be carried out on-site at the Ordering Party. The following two tender areas are included: - Identity management and access control (IAM) - Penetration testing and security review Tenders may be submitted for one or both tender areas. sig_070576f1552b42207971.description: Groupe E currently uses the ServiceNow platform as a central tool for several internal and customer-oriented processes. The instance, named "Nestor", has been progressively configured to meet the operational and organisational needs of the Group. ServiceNow is used in particular for business request management, offering a centralised portal and automated workflows to facilitate the processing and tracking of internal requests. The platform also constitutes an essential pillar of ITSM, covering incident, change, task and problem management. Beyond internal processes, ServiceNow is used for customer request management, allowing for better traceability, improved service quality and optimal management of commitments (SLAs). The solution also integrates a module dedicated to vehicle fleet management, ensuring the operational and administrative monitoring of the Group's mobility resources. The ServiceNow instance is currently maintained and evolved by an external partner, who provides application support, specific developments and technical integration, in collaboration with internal governance teams. As the ServiceNow licence contract and service contract with the integrator are expiring, Groupe E is launching this call for tenders to ensure the continuity of these services, optimise costs and guarantee consistent development of the platform for the coming years. This lot concerns the acquisition of licences necessary for the use of the ServiceNow solution; The purpose of this lot is the provision of support services related to our ServiceNow instances

sig_0760e24a0b69917d78f5.description: The contract covers services relating to the study for the development of a single bathing profile on the Île de Monsieur in Sèvres. The opening of permanent bathing in the Seine at the departmental nautical park of the Île de Monsieur in Sèvres, as a legacy of the Paris Olympic and Paralympic Games 2024, requires the prior preparation of a complete bathing profile. The main purpose of this contract is therefore to carry out this comprehensive study in accordance with the methodology provided by the national guide for the development of a bathing profile, including in particular the following phases: - Phase I: Status report, - Phase II: Diagnosis, - Phase III: Management measures. The contract also provides for covering the needs for additional missions identified during the contract to ensure the successful completion of this study

sig_07640451e48c0e61345e.description: RFI Pursuant to Revolutionary Federal Acquisition Regulation Overhaul RFO FAR 15.101(c) DISCLAIMER This is a Request for Information (RFI) issued in accordance with RFO FAR 15.101(c). The Government does not intend to award a contract on the basis of this RFI or otherwise pay for the information requested. Responses to this RFI will be treated as information only and shall not be construed as a proposal. This is not a Request for Proposal (RFP), nor does it constitute a solicitation and shall not be construed as a commitment by the Government. Responses in any form are not offers and the Government is under no obligation to award a contract from this announcement. No funds will be made available to pay for the preparation of responses to this announcement. Any information submitted to this notice is strictly voluntary and will not be returned. Not responding to this notice does not preclude participation in future solicitations. INTENT Background: HQDA G-2. CASTLE KEEP is a customer-facing portal that provides automated workflow services and Sensitive Compartmented Army SCI program reporting, metrics, analysis, and information sharing within the Army SCI community in accordance with DoDM 5105.21 requirements. This is non-personal services contract to provide Software Development and Software Sustainment Support of the Department of Army (DA) SSO’s CASTLE KEEP. The Army Contracting Command Aberdeen Proving Ground (ACC-APG) is issuing this RFI to conduct market research. The intent of the RFI is to identify parties having an interest in bidding on and the resources to support solicitations for G2’s CASTLE KEEP’s sustainable solution for the SSO/SSR community to develop and sustain CASTLE KEEP in Army Commercial Cloud Solutions Provider (AC2SP). The Government retains ownership to software and application tools; upon completion this contract all information will be turned over to the U.S. Government and is U.S. Government property. The identified questions are to encourage competition and exchanges of information. Any voluntary response received will be reviewed to assist the Government in arriving at the most suitable approach. The Government is seeking responses to this RFI that describes vendors’ existing capabilities. Small Business Participation: This RFI is issued on an unrestricted basis (Full and Open) to maximize industry responses. The Government highly encourages submissions from all business sizes and socioeconomic categories (e.g., Small Business, SDVOSB, 8(a), WOSB, HUBZone). Infrastructure Assessment: Vendor shall simulate the realistic threat exploitation techniques within the legacy, existing, and emerging software system's cybersecurity in the mission context of the representative operating environment. Vendor shall apply the cybersecurity testing process with blue teams of Government and Vendor equivalent organizations and red teams of the certified Government and Vendor equivalent organizations during Developmental/Operational Test & Evaluation (D/O T&E).The Blue team assesses the operational network vulnerability with findings for the independent technical review of the network security posture and implements the mitigation techniques for integration into the community security solution to increase the cybersecurity readiness posture. The Blue teams evaluate the security threats/risks in the operating environment and study the network environment and its current state of security readiness. The Red teams simulate the potential adversary's exploitation capabilities against an enterprise's security posture to enhance the enterprise IA/Cybersecurity via demonstration of the impacts of the successful attacks and the needed countermeasure by the blue teams in the operational environment. Cyber Integration: Vendor shall coordinate with Government Agencies and industry partners to support interoperability and integration of other capabilities, maintain adequate certified personnel to meet requirements, and provide qualified staff for CASTLE KEEP software development and sustainment. Vendor shall lease workspace with NIPRNet and JWICS access to support three to four personnel. Multi-level Security: Vendor personnel performing work under this action must have an active Top Secret (TS) security clearance with eligibility for obtaining Sensitive Compartmented Information (SCI) (SI, TK, G, and HCS security clearance IAW DoD 5200.1-R at the time of award and must maintain the level of security required for the life of a contract. This action will require TSI/SCI, but future work related to this action may require a TS/SCI with Counterintelligence Polygraph (TS/SCI w/CI Poly) clearance. The security requirements are IAW the attached DD Form 254, Security Classification Specification. Personnel must perform within the security limitations of AR 381-10, USSID 18, and other security regulations. Any vendor personnel that will need access to SIPRNet terminals will require a TS/SCI clearance because all SIPRNet terminals are in Sensitive Compartmented Information Facility (SCIFs) Security Boundary Clarification: The vendor shall understand and apply all applicable security classification guidance. Users should notify the originator if information indicates a need to update the guidance. Classification determinations remain the responsibility of the Government Contracting Agency (GCA). The Contract Security Classification Specification (DD254) is required for performance on a classified contract. Infrastructure for Cyber Operations: The vendor shall leverage infrastructure as code such as terraform or related for deployments and cloud management. Cyber-Network Architecture: develop, maintain, and update documentation which includes Standard Operating Procedures, System Architecture Guides, Entity Relationship Diagram (ERD), Install Guides, and Department of Defense Architectural Framework (DoDAF) diagrams for all related system and hardware configurations adhering to organizational templated and policies quarterly. The vendor shall leverage cross-domain solutions for implementation for tempest hardening and significant equipment installations. The vendor shall not implement solutions that have licenses or incur additional costs without written approval from the Government stakeholders, COR, and ACOR. Post-RFI Events: Following the evaluation of RFI responses, the Government anticipates hosting an Industry Day to facilitate open exchanges of information and provide further program details. A separate announcement containing registration, scheduling, and security clearance instructions for the Industry Day will be published on SAM.gov. The feasibility of conducting associated physical site visits is currently under evaluation and will be announced at a later date, if applicable. SUBMISSION INSTRUCTIONS Vendors may only submit one (1) submission per CAGE code. Interested sources are requested to submit a response of no more than five (5) pages, written in Times New Roman font of 12-point size or larger. Times New Roman of 10-point size is acceptable for graphics, tables, or exhibits. Responses must be in either Microsoft Word or character recognized and searchable Adobe Portable Document Format (PDF). If your company has different business sectors which hold different CAGE codes, each sector may submit a response. In addition, each CAGE code must provide separate facility clearance documentation which will not count against the 5 page limit. If teaming, use the Prime Vendor's CAGE code in the response. Submission of proprietary and other sensitive information must be marked and identified with disposition instructions. The Government shall not be liable or suffer any consequential damage for any improperly identified proprietary information. Proprietary information will be safeguarded in accordance with the applicable Government regulations and requirements. The information provided and received in response to this announcement is subject to the conditions set forth in RFO FAR 15.101(c). RFI responses and any questions shall be submitted via email to the following: Questions and responses may be sent using either of the following methods: Emailed to: ricardo.a.rivera50.civ@army.mil and cesar.m.mencia.civ@army.mil Sent via DOD Secure Access File Exchange (SAFE) (https://safe.apps.mil) to: ricardo.a.rivera50.civ@army.mil and cesar.m.mencia.civ@army.mil DO NOT SEND CLASSIFIED INFORMATION. All submissions and attachments to this RFI must be UNCLASSIFIED or Controlled Unclassified Information (CUI). The subject line of all emails sent in response to this RFI shall be " W56KGY26CKRFI0001". All emails shall identify respondents’ organization, point(s) of contact, and classification/caveats. Responses to this request shall be submitted via email and must be received no later than 12:00 pm, ET, 22 September 2026. The Government is not committed nor obligated to pay for the information provided, and no basis for claims against the Government shall arise from a response to this RFI. Respondents to this RFI may be requested to provide additional information via secure methods which may include travel or access to secure locations. REQUESTED INFORMATION Interested parties shall provide a response of no more than five (5) pages that address each of the following items: Administrative Information: Company name Mailing Address and Website The Unique Entity ID (generated by SAM.gov) Commercial and Government Entity (CAGE) Code Indicate business size and socioeconomic status (e.g., Large Business, Small Business, Service-Disabled Veteran-Owned Small Business (SDVOSB), 8(a), etc.) under NAICS 541611." Location of facility(s) Point(s) of Contacts name and contact information Facility Security Officer (FSO) name and contact information Confirmation of ability to safeguard Controlled Unclassified Information (CUI) at your facility. SIPRNet/JWICS email address (if available) Assessment Approach: Ensuring the following is conducted: code quality, unit testing, functional testing, integration testing, performance testing, Static, Dynamic, and Passive Security testing (DAST, SAST, and RASP). Describe your methodology for code quality, unit testing, functional testing, integration testing, performance testing, Static, Dynamic, and Passive Security testing (DAST, SAST, and RASP). Modification Capabilities: Ensuring CASTLE KEEP capability software baseline configurations are documented, maintained, updated and operationally available to all users. Details of vendor’s functional, and technical knowledge and experience of products and process being supported Security: a. Detail your experience in working within Department of Defense (DoD) military and Intelligence Community (IC) facilities. b. What percentage of your current workforce already holds active TS/SCI clearances versus those requiring upgrades? c. Confirm your company’s capability to provide fully cleared personnel on Day 1 of contract award. Maintenance: Outline your plan for in-service engineering, preventative maintenance, troubleshooting, life-cycle support, and your ability to provide staff cleared up to the TS/SCI level. Data Rights: Discuss your approach to Intellectual Property (IP). Identify any anticipated proprietary components, software, or technical data that would restrict the Government's ability to achieve organic sustainment or 'right to repair'. Please provide additional information that you believe we should know about your company. sig_076d9e425446174684f7.description: External receipt and processing of documents for invoice verification processes in accordance with Section 302 of the Fifth Book of the Social Code (SGB V) and the Eleventh Book of the Social Code (SGB XI). Lot LOT-0001: Comprehensive scanning service with end-to-end overall responsibility. In order to achieve further efficiency gains in the processes, invoice processing is to be digitalised. This specifically affects billing processes pursuant to Section 302 SGB V and Section 105 SGB XI. The scope of incoming mail digitalisation covers the invoice processes for aids, remedial therapies, travel expenses, rehabilitative sport and functional training, midwifery/obstetric care, care benefits in kind, day and respite care, and advisory visits pursuant to Section 302 SGB V as well as Section 105 SGB XI. The contractor receives the unopened letter and parcel post of the contracting authority (e.g. invoices or invoice components) in paper form. The contractor must independently perform all preparatory work necessary for scanning the documents. This includes, for example, opening envelopes and dispatch material, documenting the date of receipt and, if necessary, removing staples or other materials such as adhesive tape. The incoming documents must be scanned by the contractor and provided as a PDF document of PDF version 1.7 in the PDF/A 1 format. The contracting parties shall jointly agree on deviating versions. Scanning must be carried out in colour and with a resolution of at least 200 DPI. Both the front and back of the documents must be scanned. Scanning also includes the digitalisation of accompanying attachments. The contractor must ensure that documents deemed irrelevant by the contracting authority can be subsequently deleted or redacted by the contracting authority. These may include, for example, medical records that should not normally have been made available to the health insurance fund for data protection reasons. Following digitalisation and provision of the documents to the contracting authority, they must be stored for 30 calendar days and subsequently destroyed by the contractor. The contracting authority is entitled to request the original documents (e.g. for auditing purposes) within 30 calendar days. The contractor shall ensure that the documents are transmitted to the contracting authority within 14 calendar days. The documents must be provided with a qualified electronic signature/seal by the contractor immediately after scanning.

sig_07beccca6e5ca63f195b.description: This is a relaunch following the declaration of the previous consultation as unsuccessful. Competent in this matter, the City of Aix-en-Provence manages the hierarchy of travel by all modes on its territory. To this end, the City relies, on the one hand, on the collection of flow data for pedestrians, cyclists (and other personal mobility devices) and motorised vehicles (public transport, private vehicles, heavy goods vehicles, motorised two-wheelers) to establish an inventory of the situation (diagnosis) or to evaluate the impact of a development, for example; and on the other hand, on studies of traffic plans, junction design, etc., making it possible to respond to the various challenges of sharing public space in terms of mobility. Thus, the purpose of this contract is to carry out travel surveys in an urban environment, and specific studies, at all scales, from the junction to the city. This contract includes 2 lots, - The 1st lot relating to surveys/counting, has the purpose of carrying out flow data collection, inventories, diagnoses and evaluations of the developments carried out, - And the 2nd lot relating to studies, has the purpose of reflecting on the design of developments with a view to securing modes of travel. The framework agreement will be executed by the issuance of order forms. Each lot will be the subject of a separate award. The services are paid for by unit prices. The contract provides for an insertion clause: - Lot 1 - Collection/counting of flow data for all modes: 100 hours/year - Lot 2 - Traffic and junction design studies of all types; implementation of traffic light junction programming: 50 hours/year or 3 weeks of internship per year Collection of travel flow data for all modes; Traffic and junction design studies of all types; implementation of traffic light junction programming

sig_0880688c47c473ebd0e9.description: Provision of support services and implementation of international actions Provision of support services and implementation of international actions The purpose of this framework agreement is the provision of support services, studies and the implementation of international-dimension actions, in support of the regional strategy for internationalisation, economic attractiveness and the development of excellence sectors of the Région des Pays de la Loire. As part of its international strategy, the Region has set as a priority, in particular, the reinforcement of the international position of the territory's strategic sectors. The aim is to improve their international visibility and to encourage the conquest of new markets. To this end, it will deploy an "international task force" for each strategic sector, whose purpose is to draw up and implement action programmes concerted with businesses and partners in these sectors, tailored to their challenges and their export maturity. Consequently, these "international task forces" will be able to address a diversity of actions, ranging from market scanning, the organisation of commercial missions, discovery missions on innovation or sector marketing actions. Furthermore, the regional international strategy integrates an international economic attractiveness dimension. It aims to reinforce the positioning of Pays de la Loire among economic actors and foreign investors. In this context, the Region conducts prospecting, promotion and networking actions in order to attract international businesses, particularly in strategic sectors with high added value. It also supports the development and reinvestment of foreign businesses established in the regional territory. They aim to support the international development of businesses, facilitate their access to new markets, reinforce their visibility and attractiveness, and encourage their networking with economic, institutional and financial partners. This framework agreement covers in particular: - The carrying out of market studies, sector analyses and strategic framing work on targeted geographical areas or sectors of activity; - The preparation, organisation and implementation of international actions, individual or collective (missions, appointment programmes, professional visits, business meetings); - The organisation of or support for participation in trade fairs, professional events and promotion operations internationally or in the regional territory; - Economic networking, prospecting and partnership development actions, including with institutional or financial partners. These services are entrusted to economic operators, responsible for ensuring their design, preparation, coordination and implementation, in conjunction with the institutional partners and economic ecosystems concerned, both in France and abroad and under the supervision of the Region. The actions may be deployed in France and internationally, depending on the geographical and sectoral priorities defined by the Region. This framework agreement aims to endow the Region with an operational framework enabling the coordinated, clear and effective implementation of its international actions in the service of regional businesses and sectors. The framework agreement takes effect from the date of its notification to the holder. It is concluded for a duration of 12 months, renewable 3 times by tacit renewal for a new period of 12 months, without its duration being able to exceed 48 months. Where applicable, the buyer shall take the decision in writing not to renew the framework agreement at least 3 months before the anniversary date of notification of the framework agreement to the holder. In the event of non-renewal, the holder may not claim any compensation. This framework agreement may be executed by means of order forms on the basis of the prices indicated in the unit price schedule. The framework agreement may also be executed by means of subsequent contracts which may be: - either lump-sum and fixed-price; - or unit-price; - or mixed-price. This framework agreement is single-supplier. The cumulative minimum and maximum amounts of orders and subsequent contracts that can be carried out under this framework agreement are defined as follows: - minimum amount: 50 000 € excluding VAT for 12 months - maximum amount: 500 000 € excluding VAT for 12 months

sig_08fcc417ba7e7ee3891e.description: The Region of Southern Denmark is facing the procurement of a new regional IT solution for the imaging diagnostics areas (hereinafter the "Solution"). The Solution must encompass RIS, PACS, VNA, Clinical Viewer as well as support for breast cancer screening and constitutes the central clinical tool for radiological and nuclear medicine departments at the Region of Southern Denmark. The Solution must be put into operation at 4 hospital units distributed across 12 radiological departments, 3 nuclear medicine departments as well as the regional breast cancer screening. The Region of Southern Denmark has several hundred imaging modalities and performs over 1 million examinations annually. The Solution must support an efficient clinical workflow in a patient-safe and user-friendly manner, as well as ensure the coherent patient pathway across hospital units, departments and specialties. The Solution must be a robust, stable and well-functioning tool in the clinicians' daily work while simultaneously possessing the flexibility necessary to accommodate future improvement initiatives and changed needs. The tendered procurement is described in further detail in Appendix-03 with sub-appendices. The procurement itself encompasses functionality to support workflows within radiology, nuclear medicine and mammography screening, as well as the storage of imaging diagnostics examinations. The procurement furthermore encompasses the implementation and maintenance of the new solution. BDSYD principles: The procurement is made on the basis of four overarching principles, which the Parties must correspondingly use as fundamental principles for the Solution and the collaboration: • Efficient support of the patients' journey: The Solution is patient-safe, labour-saving, intuitive and user-friendly. • Stable operation: The large volume of imaging diagnostics examinations can take place securely, unperturbed by downtime and operational stoppages to the benefit of patients, employees and efficiency. • Performance: Short system response times in the solution and good performance, which is important for patients, employees and efficiency. • Standard solution: The Solution is well-functioning and well-tested in a comparable setup and has open and well-defined interfaces. There is an option for the Central Denmark Region and the North Denmark Region for the procurement of a corresponding solution, cf. Appendix-19 with sub-appendices. The Region of Southern Denmark is conducting the procurement on behalf of all the regions, and separate contracts will subsequently be concluded between the chosen Supplier and the individual region. It is noted that the Region of Southern Denmark has geoblocking in relation to a number of countries as listed in Appendix-02.A. The list can be requested by contacting via the communication tab on the Ethics tender site and can be received by interested suppliers upon a confidentiality declaration from the requesting party. This has been accounted for in the determined tender deadline.
sig_08fcc417ba7e7ee3891e.title: Procurement, implementation and maintenance of an imaging diagnostics solution

sig_091918c49ae03344e714.description: The NHS Counter Fraud Authority (NHSCFA) is a health authority charged with identifying, investigating and preventing fraud and other economic crime within the NHS and the wider health group. As a health authority focused entirely on counter fraud work, the NHSCFA is independent from other NHS bodies and directly accountable to the Department of Health and Social Care (DHSC). THE NHSCFA currently operate two separate systems for the provision of an intelligence database and a case management system. The intention is to identify if there is a single solution that can replace the existing systems. If that is not possible then the aim would be to have two separate products that connect and align with each other to avoid duplication and operational inefficiencies. This market engagement exercise seeks the views and opinions of those organisations that may be interested in delivering the requirements. The scope of this market engagement covers is provided within the draft service specification. This exercise and any subsequent responses are in no way legally binding on any party. Participation in the engagement exercise is not a mandatory requirement for participating in any potential future procurement; however, responses received will assist to inform the Contracting Authority as to the level of interest from the market and will be used to evidence a decision as to whether or not to undertake a competitive procurement. The Market Engagement Questionnaire and current Service Specifications can be downloaded from SAP Ariba Portal at the below link: https://discovery.ariba.com/rfx/23496944 Please return your completed MEQ through the Portal no later than 5pm on 30 October 2025.

sig_091adee7794510240399.description: The Contractor shall provide Think Trends Software as an Agentic AI and Document Intelligence solution capable of processing structured, semi-structured, and unstructured adverse event documents, including scanned PDFs, handwritten or machine-generated forms, narratives, attachments, medical records, product complaints, lab reports, follow-up submissions, and case correspondence. The solution shall support end-to-end adverse event document processing through the following capabilities: A. Agentic Document Intake and Classification Think Trends Software AI agents shall automatically receive, classify, and route adverse event documents by submission type, FDA Center, product category, source, urgency, and case-processing requirements. The intake agent shall identify whether a document relates to drugs, biologics, devices, veterinary products, tobacco products, combination products, or other FDA-regulated products. Key capabilities include: • Automated ingestion of scanned PDFs, forms, emails, images, attachments, and electronic documents. • Classification of documents by Center-specific workflow, product type, and reporting pathway. • Detection of new cases, follow-up cases, duplicate submissions, incomplete submissions, and supporting attachments. • Intelligent routing to appropriate review queues, case-processing teams, or downstream systems. B. Agentic OCR and Intelligent Data Extraction Think Trends Software Agentic OCR shall combine optical character recognition, computer vision, natural language processing, large language models, and rule-based validation agents to extract key adverse event data elements from complex documents. The platform shall extract and structure critical case information, including: • Reporter, patient, animal, subject, or consumer information. • Product information, including drug, biologic, device, tobacco, or veterinary product details. • Adverse event terms, symptoms, outcomes, seriousness, and event narratives. • Dates, timelines, exposure details, dose, route, duration, lot numbers, manufacturer information, and product identifiers. • Medical history, concomitant products, lab results, device problem codes, clinical narratives, and follow-up information. • Center-specific data elements required for CVM-Drugs and CVM-Food, CDRH, CTP, CDER, CBER and HFP. C. Center-Specific Adverse Event Processing Agents The Contractor shall configure specialized AI agents within Think Trends Software to support unique regulatory and operational needs across FDA Centers. Each agent shall apply Center-specific data models, validation logic, terminology, business rules, and review workflows. Examples include: • CVM Agent: Processes veterinary adverse event reports, animal species, breed, weight, product exposure, dosage, outcome, and veterinarian/reporter information. • CDRH Agent: Processes device-related adverse events, device identifiers, manufacturer information, malfunction details, patient impact, and device problem descriptions. • CTP Agent: Processes tobacco product adverse experiences, product use patterns, health effects, consumer narratives, and product category information. • HFP Agent: Processes HFP-specific adverse event reporting requirements and associated workflows. • CDER Agent: Process drug product adverse experiences, product use patterns, health effects, consumer narratives, and product category information. • CBER Agent: Processes biologics product adverse experiences, product use patterns, health effects, consumer narratives, and product category information. D. Case Validation, Quality Control, and Human-in-the-Loop Review Think Trends Software shall incorporate validation agents to compare extracted data against business rules, required fields, confidence thresholds, terminology standards, and case-processing logic. Records that meet defined thresholds may proceed automatically, while exceptions shall be routed for human review. Key quality-control features include: • Confidence scoring at field, document, and case levels. • Source traceability to page, section, table, and line references. • Automated flagging of missing, inconsistent, conflicting, or low-confidence data. • Human-in-the-loop review screens for case processors and safety reviewers. • Reviewer acceptance, correction, override, and approval workflows. • Full audit trail of AI extraction, human edits, and final approved values. E. Data Standardization and Regulatory Output Generation Think Trends Software shall transform extracted adverse event information into structured formats required for case management, analytics, and downstream regulatory processing. The platform shall support configurable mappings to FDA data standards, Center-specific systems, XML structures, APIs, and reporting formats. Capabilities include: • Normalization of adverse event terms, product names, dates, identifiers, and narrative fields. • Mapping to Center-specific safety data models and controlled terminology. • Generation of structured case records for downstream review and processing. • API-based integration with FDA systems, case-processing platforms, data lakes, document repositories, and workflow tools. • Export to XML, JSON, CSV, database tables, or other required formats. F. Agentic Workflow Automation and Triage Think Trends Software shall automate repetitive case-processing steps while maintaining reviewer control for regulatory decisions. The system shall support configurable AI agents capable of executing multi-step workflows, requesting missing information, summarizing case narratives, identifying seriousness indicators, detecting duplicates, and prioritizing work queues. Workflow automation shall include: • Case prioritization based on seriousness, product risk, event severity, due dates, and Center-defined rules. • Automated summarization of long adverse event narratives and supporting attachments. • Duplicate and follow-up detection across submissions. • Exception handling and escalation workflows. • Generation of reviewer-ready case summaries. • Dashboard visibility into case volumes, processing status, aging, backlog, error rates, and productivity metrics. G. AI-Enabled Redaction for FOIA Compliance ThinkTrends will provide AI-powered redaction capabilities to support FDA's obligations under the Freedom of Information Act (FOIA). The platform will automatically identify and redact personally identifiable information (PII), protected health information (PHI), commercially confidential data, law-enforcement-sensitive content, and other exemption-covered materials from adverse event documents prior to public release or response to FOIA requests. Key capabilities include: • Automated detection and redaction of PII and PHI, including patient names, addresses, dates of birth, medical record numbers, Social Security numbers, and other personal identifiers. • Identification and suppression of trade secrets, proprietary formulations, manufacturing processes, and commercially confidential submitter information protected under FOIA Exemption. • Detection of law-enforcement-sensitive and inter-agency deliberative content subject to FOIA Exemptions. • Configurable exemption profiles aligned to FDA FOIA policy, Center-specific guidance, and applicable federal regulations. • Confidence-scored redaction recommendations with source traceability, enabling FOIA reviewers to accept, modify, or override AI-proposed redactions. • Human-in-the-loop review workflow allowing FOIA analysts to validate, annotate, and finalize redacted documents before release. • Generation of redacted PDF and document versions with visible redaction markers, exemption codes, and reviewer audit annotations. • Full audit trail recording every AI-proposed redaction, reviewer decision, exemption code applied, and final release determination. • Support for bulk redaction processing across large FOIA request batches, including multi-document packages and rolling requests. • Integration with FDA FOIA tracking systems, document repositories, and case management workflows. 1.3 SALIENT FEATURES OF THINK TRENDS SOFTWARE Think Trends Software provides the following differentiating capabilities relevant to FDA adverse event reporting modernization: 1. Agentic OCR Beyond Traditional OCR: Think Trends Software does not merely convert images to text. It applies AI agents that read, interpret, validate, cross-check, and structure regulatory information from complex adverse event documents. 2. Center-Agnostic Core with Center-Specific Configuration: The platform provides a common document intelligence foundation while allowing FDA Centers such as CVM, CDRH, CTP, and HFP to configure unique workflows, data models, rules, and outputs. 3. End-to-End Adverse Event Case Automation: Think Trends Software supports intake, classification, extraction, validation, triage, routing, human review, data transformation, and downstream submission/output generation. 4. Human-in-the-Loop Regulatory Control: The system keeps FDA reviewers in control by allowing them to review, correct, approve, or override AI-generated outputs before final case acceptance. 5. Explainability and Source Traceability: Each extracted field can be traced back to the original source document, page, section, and text reference, supporting transparency, auditability, and reviewer confidence. 6. Confidence-Based Processing: Think Trends Software assigns confidence scores to extracted data and automatically routes low-confidence or inconsistent records for human review. 7. Multi-Document and Multi-Format Processing: Think Trends Software shall process scanned PDFs, structured forms, unstructured narratives, tables, handwritten content where feasible, images, attachments, correspondence, and supporting records. 8. Duplicate and Follow-Up Detection: AI agents shall compare incoming submissions against existing records to identify potential duplicates, follow-ups, related cases, and case-history updates. 9. Reviewer-Ready Case Summaries: Think Trends Software shall generate concise adverse event summaries, chronology, product-event relationships, missing-field lists, and review-ready case packages. 10. Secure FDA-Aligned Deployment: Think Trends Software shall be deployable in secure government cloud, FDA-managed, or approved hosting environments with role-based access, audit logs, encryption, and integration with enterprise identity management. 1.4 TECHNICAL REQUIREMENTS Implementation of Think Trends Software for adverse event document processing is expected to deliver the following outcomes: • Reduction in manual data entry and repetitive case-processing tasks. • Faster adverse event intake, triage, and reviewer preparation. • Improved data quality through AI-assisted validation and standardization. • Greater consistency across FDA Centers while preserving Center-specific workflows. • Enhanced traceability, auditability, and regulatory transparency. • Improved ability to manage high-volume document backlogs and surge workloads. • Increased reviewer productivity through AI-generated summaries and exception-based review. • Scalable platform foundation for future FDA adverse event modernization initiatives. Please view the attached Request for Quote (RFQ) RFQ FDA-SOL-75F40126Q00384 document for additional information.

sig_099b0112a30dff83d078.description: The forest management services will be awarded in the year 2026 (field phase 2027) by concluding a public procurement contract for the Medias Forestry Office. The total area of the Medias Forestry Office is 6357,88 ha. The services involve the development of the forest management plan, a product of the management activity with technical-organisational content, ecologically grounded, through which, for a period of time, the works necessary to be executed in a production unit are established, for the purpose of bringing and, subsequently, maintaining the structural characteristics of the stands and the forest as a whole to the values corresponding to the optimal structural model defined in accordance with the ecological, social and economic objectives pursued through sustainable management. According to the provisions of Art. 63 para. (11) of Law no. 331/2024 regarding the Forestry Code, with subsequent amendments and additions, it is necessary that the development of forest management plans be carried out through public procurement procedures. The management of the state-owned public forest fund constitutes a priority obligation of the forest fund administrators. The method of managing the state-owned public forest fund is regulated by forest management plans. Forest management plans and their amendments are approved by order of the head of the Authority. In the case of state-owned public lands, the management plans provide data and information necessary for their registration/updating in the centralised inventory of assets in the state's public domain and for registration in the integrated cadastre and land register system. Requests for clarification formulated by tenderers during the advertising period of the participation notice can be made with a deadline of at most 15 days before the deadline for submission of tenders. The contracting authority will respond to all requests for clarification formulated in compliance with the above deadline, once, in a consolidated manner, 10 days before the deadline for submission of tenders. Services for the development of the forest management plan for the state-owned public forest fund managed by the Sibiu Forestry Directorate – Medias Forestry Office, field phase 2027, for the area of 6357,88 ha. The services include preparatory work, field data collection, data processing and drafting of the forest management plan, development of the GIS database and management maps, preparation of the necessary environmental documentation, obtaining the regulatory act issued by the competent authority for environmental protection, supporting the documentation within the Technical Commission for Forestry Approval (CTAS) and obtaining the order for approval of the forest management plan.
sig_099b0112a30dff83d078.title: Forest management services-Medias Forestry Office 2026 Sibiu Forestry Directorate

sig_09cf39cca538396dd30e.description: The NSF FINDERS FOUNDRY program supports collaboration among K-12 educators, technologists, and researchers to develop innovative solutions to persistent challenges in learning and workforce development. These challenges are identified by K-12 students, families, and educators. The program aims to create and scale evidence-based practices, tools, and technologies that improve learning outcomes and prepare students for a digital, Artificial Intelligence (AI)-driven future. A key focus is early exposure to AI to build curiosity, understanding, and readiness for future careers. The program encourages partnerships across sectors - schools, universities, industry, government, and nonprofits - to co-design responsive, technology-based solutions. NSF FINDERS FOUNDRY program includes two phases: Planning and Development. Planning proposals help teams explore one of several focus areas. Only teams awarded Planning grants may submit Development proposals, which support the growth and implementation of promising ideas. The program aligns with national priorities, including the Executive Order 14277, “Advancing Artificial Intelligence Education for American Youth ” (April 23, 2025), and the CHIPS and Science Act of 2022, Public Law 117-167 , Sections 10381-10383 and 10395.
sig_09cf39cca538396dd30e.title: National Science Foundation Fostering Interdisciplinary Networks to Develop Emergent and Responsive Solutions Foundry

sig_09e895f98228c208ef6a.description: LOT 26.02.275: Support for rbb online services The Rundfunk Berlin-Brandenburg (rbb) - hereinafter referred to as the contracting authority (“CA”) - intends to retender the support services for the operational IT running of the online services from 01.01.2027. To this end, the CA will conclude a contract with a contractor (“CO”). rbb operates the following web presences: - www.rbb-online.de - www.rbb24.de - www.radioeins.de - www.fritz.de - www.rbb888.de - www.antennebrandenburg.de - www.inforadio.de - www.radiodrei.de - www.ohrenbaer.de - www.radioberlin.de - www.sandmann.de - www.preussenchronik.de - www.deutsche-und-polen.de - www.chronik-der-wende.de Information published on the rbb internet pages is subject to a high degree of updating and change, which stems in particular from the topicality of the programmes. News events in particular change their significance over time; consequently, the form, scope and location of presentation also change. Within a short time, a short report can become a top story on the home page with an attached background dossier. The online CMS AEM 6.5 used has been functionally expanded according to rbb's requirements and makes it possible to map these changes “on the fly” without significant effort. At the same time, large amounts of data, such as programme data and playlists, flow automatically into the CMS. They are offered automatically on the internet presence, but some are also modified manually by the editorial team. For the editorial teams, the possibility of time control, i.e. the timing of contributions, also plays a major role. It makes it possible to offer attractive content with a high degree of variety even on days when the editorial teams are shorthanded or not staffed at all. The CMS largely enables the editorial teams to respond flexibly to these situations. For example, as part of broadcast accompaniment, the editorial teams can create contributions and image galleries in the CMS and integrate them into overview pages. The editorial team can also create new navigation structures. A set of interactive elements such as votings and quizzes is available. Furthermore, charts and playlists can be managed and newsletters sent, among other things. Streaming servers distribute content live and on-demand to the internet. In addition, rbb supplies the ARD Mediathek and ARD Sounds as well as various social media platforms with content and the associated metadata. Linux-based virtual server systems are used to operate this infrastructure. The complex interaction of these servers enables the provision of services with high availability.
sig_09e895f98228c208ef6a.title: Support for rbb online services

sig_0a036bc1542d0c97b215.description: The overarching goal of this notice of funding opportunity (NOFO) and its companion opportunities is to establish the Precision Medicine with AI: Integrating Imaging with Multimodal Data (PRIMED-AI) Program to support development of innovative, reliable, cost-effective, and sustainable multimodal AI-based clinical decision support (CDS) tools. PRIMED-AI CDS tools are based on the integration of clinical imaging with other types of multimodal health data to enhance care for patients with a wide range of health conditions. The PRIMED-AI Program seeks to catalyze the adoption of AI-based CDS tools into clinical workflows to enable novel personalized medicine strategies that address significant health challenges. The purpose of this NOFO is to solicit applications for the design, development, and preliminary validation of robust frameworks for the application of multimodal-artificial intelligence (AI) models for clinical use. Frameworks developed through these awards would populate a "playbook", defined as a collection of actionable guidelines, standardized protocols, and/or standard operating procedures (SOPs) for reliable and effective development and deployment of multimodal AI tools. It is expected that the frameworks delineated in this playbook will directly address PRIMED-AI objectives and needs, while also remaining flexible enough to enable sufficient extensibility and interoperability for use across a broad spectrum of multimodal biomedical AI applications, both internal and external to the PRIMED-AI Program.
sig_0a036bc1542d0c97b215.title: Development and Testing of a Multi-use Frameworks Playbook for Precision Medicine with AI: Integrating Imaging with Multimodal Data (PRIMED-AI) (U01 Clinical Trial Not Allowed)

sig_0a04296a220e598f302b.description: The subject of this public procurement includes the selection of a contractor to provide technical and logistical support for the organisation and conduct of specialised and public events, the development of professional communities, the conduct of information and advertising campaigns, the management of social media profiles, media planning, the provision of advertising materials and consumables for events, the creation of an online community and other related activities with the aim of promoting project No 101250707 BRAIN++, implemented under the Horizon Europe Programme. Within the scope of the procurement, it is envisaged to organise and conduct two types of events, provisionally called Type A events and Type B events: – Large Type A events (conferences, forums, hackathons) – approximately 11 in number, with a minimum of 100 participants per event, whereby by 30.11.2026 the goal is to conduct events for 600 participants, and for the entire period until 30.11.2028 – for no fewer than 5 000 participants. Type A events are organised and conducted entirely by the Contractor, following prior coordination with the Contracting Authority, including communication, media coverage, advertising materials, catering, provision of speakers and moderators, preparation of a list of suitable guests, filming, provision of technical equipment, logistics and installation of equipment, provision of a stage, sound reinforcement and other similar activities. – Small Type B events (conferences, forums, competitions, webinars, networking, seminars, discussions, etc.) – a minimum of 42 in number, with between 20 and 100 participants per event and a minimum of 3 000 participants in total for the duration of the procurement. For Type B events, the Contractor is a provider of specific services required by the Contracting Authority for the organisation and conduct of the respective event, including communication, media coverage, advertising materials, catering, provision of speakers and moderators, preparation of a list of suitable guests, filming, provision of technical equipment, logistics and installation of equipment, provision of a stage, sound reinforcement and other similar activities. For the Contracting Authority, the number of participants is a priority over the number of events conducted, and the contract shall be considered fulfilled upon achieving a minimum of 8 000 participants in total across both types of events. The execution of the procurement specifically includes: planning, organisation and coordination of events, including communication with participants, speakers, moderators, partners and other stakeholders; registration and management of participants, including through an electronic registration platform; technical provision and logistics for events, including the provision of the necessary audio-visual, presentation, lighting and other technical equipment according to the specific event; provision of speakers and moderators, filming and other organisational and technical services necessary for the conduct of the events; media planning and coverage of events, including the preparation and dissemination of information and advertising content; management and maintenance of social media profiles and the conduct of advertising campaigns; production and provision of advertising and information materials and consumables for events; creation and maintenance of an online community in connection with the project activities; provision of catering, where applicable for the specific event; provision of other organisational, technical and logistical support according to the specific requests of the Contracting Authority and the requirements of the Technical Specification. The events will be held on the territory of the Republic of Bulgaria, with over 80% of them expected to be held in the city of Sofia. The service of renting premises/halls is not included in the subject of the public procurement. The provision of premises/halls is paid for by the Contracting Authority according to the final choice of venue for the respective event and the number of participants, and the Contractor may assist with proposals for suitable halls/premises.
sig_0a04296a220e598f302b.title: Provision of technical and logistical support for the organisation and conduct of specialised events and the development of professional communities, and for the organisation of public events, information campaigns, management of social media profiles, media planning, advertising campaigns, provision of advertising materials and consumables for events, creation of an online community and provision of logistical support.
