This initiative is intended to improve accessibility, user experience and efficiency in delivering financial support services. 3. Scope (Indicative Only) The Council is seeking information on solutions capable of delivering some or all of the following: Eligibility checking and signposting to relevant financial support End-to-end application functionality, including submission to one or more schemes Access for both self-service users and council staff/caseworkers Workflow and case management functionality, including tracking application progress and outcomes Reporting and analytics to support service planning and performance monitoring Integration with existing council systems (e.g. CRM, revenues and benefits, case management systems) Compliance with data protection legislation, including GDPR, and appropriate security standards Accessible, user-friendly design supporting inclusive access (including assisted digital support where required) Suppliers are invited to highlight any additional relevant functionality or innovative approaches. 4. Purpose of Notice This Prior Information Notice is issued to: Provide early visibility of a potential future procurement Understand the range of solutions available in the market Inform the development of the Council’s requirements and specification Gather information on delivery models, implementation approaches and indicative costs This notice is for information only and does not constitute a call for competition. 5. Market Engagement The Council invites suppliers to provide the following information: Overview of solution and key functionality Relevant experience, particularly within local government or the public sector Indicative pricing and commercial models Implementation approach, including indicative timescales and resource requirements Integration approach and technical requirements Any key risks, dependencies or considerations The Council may undertake further engagement, including supplier briefings, demonstrations or questionnaires.. Responses are requested not later than 2nd July 2026

sig_0a5c83b7d683c744e649.description: The procurement is being carried out as a procurement consortium involving the City of Helsinki and DigiHelsinki Oy (hereinafter the "Client"). The subject of the procurement is delivery and operational services for Microsoft Dynamics 365 and Power Platform systems and related technologies (hereinafter also "Applications"), as well as further development and other expert services included in this package. Services refer to both expert services during implementation projects and development projects, as well as continuous services after implementation, such as support and maintenance services, further development, processing of change requests, technical expert support, architecture and integration expertise, service management tasks, and training. The services may include the definition, design, implementation, testing, and deployment of the Applications, as well as operation, maintenance, support, and development services, architecture services, any data migrations and integrations included in the implementations, support for process harmonisation during deliveries, and assessment of licence needs, as well as training services and documentation. The Applications to be implemented on the basis of this procurement subject will be produced on the Microsoft Dynamics 365 or Power Platform. A framework arrangement will be formed from the procurement, from which three suppliers will be selected in order of priority. The tendering process will be carried out using an open procedure. Each participant in the procurement consortium will make its own procurement decision and contract with the tenderers selected for the framework arrangement. The maximum value of the procurement is nine (9) million euros (VAT 0 %). Based on the framework arrangement, the Client and the Client's sectors, agencies, public utility services, and DigiHelsinki Oy may procure the Services or Continuous services referred to in the framework arrangement through separate delivery contracts. Delivery contracts may also relate to Applications implemented by the Client itself or in cooperation with other contractual partners. If several suppliers participate in the implementation, maintenance, or further development of the same Application, the division of responsibilities and the suppliers' cooperation obligations will be defined in the delivery contract. Deliveries may also include components implemented with other technologies in connection with Microsoft Dynamics 365 and Power Platform implementations, such as integration into an external database, interface, or software component, etc. The subject and scope of the procurement are set out in more detail in the call for tenders and its appendices.

Before you run your mini competition, find out which suppliers could meet your requirements using the DPS marketplace. This DPS is organised into 4 categories: services location clearance scalability The steps below outline how to search for suppliers, create a shortlist and carry out a mini competition. Register as a buyer on the DPS marketplace. Although pages are headed ‘Supplier registration’ this is also where you can register as a buyer. Navigate to the Quality Assurance and Testing for IT Systems 2 DPS under Technology and choose the ‘Access as a buyer’ option and confirm your acceptance of the customer access agreement. On your ‘Manage your DPS Category Exports’ page you now have 2 options: view appointed suppliers click on the link to create a new category export This is how you filter the suppliers that can meet your requirements. when creating a new category use the filtering tool (select all that apply) to specify your requirements and create your supplier shortlist Save your filtered list of capable suppliers by clicking the ‘Save Category’ option and give the shortlist a unique name specific to your competition. The tool is free to use for public sector buyers, or you can use your organisation’s own procurement tool. Your tender process should be proportionate to the value and complexity of your requirement. Suppliers will need a reasonable period of time to review and prepare a response. sig_0a89bbe21c6f6d346762.description: AMENDMENT 0001: The purpose of this amendment is to formally publish industry Q&A, update technical layout page exemptions, re-baseline the Attachment 2a pricing template, and delete the GSA MAS prerequisite. Notice Type: Combined Synopsis / Solicitation (Amendment 0001) Solicitation Number: 75R60226R00026 Title: HRSA/MCHB Newborn Screening Systematic Evidence Review IDIQ (with Concurrent Award of Task Order 1) Classification Code: R499 – Support—Professional: Other NAICS Code: 541690 – Other Scientific and Technical Consulting Services Response Deadline: Tuesday, September 22, 2026, at 5:00 PM EDT The Health Resources and Services Administration, Maternal and Child Health Bureau (HRSA/MCHB) has officially released Amendment 0001 for Solicitation #75R60226R00026. This amendment addresses industry pre-proposal inquiries, issues the official Government Q&A log, updates Technical Volume layout exemptions, and distributes an updated pricing template vehicle. Offerors are strictly cautioned that initial proposals must adhere to the revised Core Task framework and utilize the re-baselined spreadsheet template to be eligible for the Best Value Trade-off evaluation pool. Proposals utilizing the original version 1 spreadsheet template will be rendered non-responsive and excluded from evaluation. 1. Core Revisions and Material Document Changes Eradication of Standalone Task 8: The master procurement vehicle contains seven (7) evaluated Core Tasks. The post-award "Artificial Intelligence Compliance and Risk Management Plan" requirement—previously designated as an isolated Task 8—has been completely removed as an independent task area. The AI Compliance requirements are officially absorbed as an administrative sub-component under Task 2 (Program Management) across all attachments. Standalone "Task 8" terminology has been entirely removed from the modified statements of work and deliverable schedules. Expanded Volume I Technical Page Count Exemptions: To ensure the Government receives the level of resource granularity necessary to execute a rigorous price realism evaluation under Subfactor (c), the administrative Compliance Matrix and the comprehensive Staff Loading Chart are now classified as page-exempt Appendices. These components may be appended to Volume I and will not count against the strict 25-page narrative ceiling. Electronic Document Layout Flexibility: Offerors are explicitly authorized and encouraged to configure digital page sizes for the Staff Loading Chart or complex timeline graphics to an 11 x 17-inch landscape "Tabloid" format within their PDF submissions to maximize legibility. Primary Principal Investigator (PI) Mandate: Bidders may name multiple co-PIs or workstream leads across the varied newborn screening scientific tasks to ensure adequate specialized coverage. However, the proposal must clearly designate one single Primary Principal Investigator whose resume will serve as the baseline for compliance scoring under Subfactor (b). GSA MAS Prerequisite Deletion: Section 6.1 of the solicitation package has been amended to delete the text indicating that an active GSA Multiple Award Schedule (MAS) contract is an ordering prerequisite. This is a standalone, full and open competitive procurement vehicle. 2. Volume III Price Template Re-Baseline (Attachment 2a) Offerors are strictly required to download and utilize the updated Attachment 2a spreadsheet template uploaded with this notice. Key corrections implemented include: Travel NTE Plug Correction: Hardcoded formulas on the Summary Tab have been adjusted to lock Option Periods 2 through 4 to "NA," lowering the evaluated travel footprint from $175,000.00 down to $70,000.00 to match the exact 2-year active duration of Task Order 1. LCAT Rate Cell Activation: Structural data-entry fields have been enabled for the Senior Medical Officer / Clinician LCAT role, and Tab 4 mapping cells have been unlinked from the Epidemiologist tracking structures. Task 6 Unit Uniformity: The Unit Type designation for the Simultaneous Systematic Review capacity line item has been re-baselined from "Each" to "LOT" to reinforce that this deliverable operates on a firm-fixed capacity lot model. 3. Critical Administrative Milestones Past Performance Questionnaires (PPQs): Offerors must instruct their client references that completed PPQs must be sent directly to the Government via email no later than Friday, September 18, 2026, by 5:00 PM EDT. Final Electronic Submission: The electronic proposal closing date remains unchanged and is strictly due no later than Tuesday, September 22, 2026, by 5:00 PM EDT. All submissions must be split across sequential emails if they exceed the 25 MB HRSA server constraints. 4. Acknowledgment Requirements Offerors must acknowledge receipt of Amendment 0001 by signing and returning the completed SF-30 form within Volume III (Price and Administrative Proposal) of their final electronic submission packet. All other terms, clauses, and conditions of the initial Request for Proposal announcement remain entirely unchanged and in full legal force. Primary Points of Contact: Elizabeth Van Absher, Contracting Officer: EVanAbsher@hrsa.gov Ms. Shawn Horton, Contract Specialist: SHorton@hrsa.gov List of Uploaded Attachments: SF-30 Amendment 0001 (Signed PDF) Attachment 1c - TO 1 SOW-A1 (PDF) Attachment 1d - TO Deliverables-A1 (PDF) Attachment 1e – TO 1 QASP-A1 (PDF) Attachment 2 - Instructions to Offerors-A1 (PDF) Attachment 2a - Pricing_Template-A1 (Excel) Attachment 2b - PPQ-A1 (PDF) HRSA-75R60226R00026 - Consolidated Questions (PDF) The Health Resources and Services Administration, Maternal and Child Health Bureau (HRSA/MCHB) is releasing this full and open competitive solicitation to establish a Multiple-Award pool of approximately three (3) to five (5) Indefinite-Delivery, Indefinite-Quantity (IDIQ) contracts. The primary objective is to secure highly specialized scientific methodologies, systematic clinical evidence reviews, and core programmatic support for the Newborn Screening Recommended Uniform Screening Panel (RUSP). The master IDIQ ordering period is five (5) years (a 12-month Base Period plus four sequential 12-month Option Periods) with an aggregate collective ceiling value of $15,111,361.00. 2. Acquisition Framework & RFO Protocols This commercial services procurement is being conducted under the dual frameworks of FAR Part 12 (Commercial Products and Services) and the streamlined negotiated procedures of FAR Part 15 under the Revolutionary FAR Overhaul (RFO) framework. 3. Concurrent Track 1 Award Stream Concurrently with the establishment of the Master IDIQ pool, the Government will award Task Order 1 (“Support for Evidence Reviews and Newborn Screening Processes and Reports”) as a strict Firm-Fixed-Price (FFP) order. Award Without Negotiations: In accordance with RFO protocols, the Government intends to evaluate proposals and award the Master IDIQ contracts and the concurrent Task Order 1 based strictly on initial proposals received, without formal negotiations. Offerors are strongly cautioned to submit their most competitive technical approaches and binding ceiling pricing in their initial volumes. Future Agility: The restriction against negotiations applies solely to the initial master pool setup and Task Order 1. For all subsequent task order competitions, the Contracting Officer fully reserves discretionary authority to conduct streamlined negotiations, request spot-discounts, or issue clarifications. 4. Proposal Structure and Submission Instructions All qualified commercial, academic, non-profit, or public entities may submit a proposal. Submissions must consist of three separate volumes: Volume I – Technical Proposal: Strictly limited to 25 pages (resumes and letters of commitment may be appended dynamically and are excluded from the limit). Volume II – Past Performance: Submission of three (3) prime or major subcontractor references. Volume III – Price Proposal: Utilizing the mandatory Government-provided Excel template to establish binding ceiling rates. 5. Important Milestones Pre-Proposal Questions: All technical, administrative, or pricing questions must be submitted via email no later than Wednesday, September 9, 2026, at 3:00 PM EDT. Inquiries must utilize Attachment 4 – Q&A Submission Template (Excel format). Final Proposal Submission: Proposals must be submitted electronically via email no later than Tuesday, September 22, 2026, at 5:00 PM EDT. LIST OF ATTACHMENTS. The following documents form a part of this RFP and any resulting Indefinite Delivery Indefinite Quantity vehicle: 1449 (PDF) Attachment 1: IDIQ Statement of Work (SOW) – HRSA-RUSP Priorities (PDF Format, 8 pages) Attachment 1a: IDIQ Schedule of Deliverables for SOW (Word Format, 3 pages) Attachment 1b: IDIQ QASP (PDF Format, 2 pages) Attachment 1c: Task Order 1 Statement of Work (SOW) Attachment 1d: Task Order 1 Schedule of Deliverables Attachment 1e: Task Order 1 QASP Attachment 2: Instructions to Offerors and Evaluation Factors for Award (PDF Format, 11 pages) Attachment 2a: Pricing Spreadsheet (Volume III, Excel Format) Attachment 2b: Past Performance Questionnaire (Word Format, 12 Pages) Attachment 3: Section K Contractor Representations and Certifications (PDF Format, 2 pages) Attachment 4: QA Submission Template (Excel)

sig_0af15c6dca7c7933c989.description: The services requested under this procurement procedure are the continuation of Software Assurance as well as the acquisition of licences incl. Software Assurance for software products from Microsoft and / or the acquisition of online products from Microsoft that Microsoft offers via the corporate programme, in accordance with the terms of the framework agreement (corporate agreement) of the Federal Ministry of the Interior (BMI) and Microsoft via a corresponding commercial partner. The services requested in the context of this procurement procedure are described in the specification of services (Section 6 of the procurement documents) including the appendices listed therein. The technical, legal and organisational framework conditions are contained in Section 5. Westdeutscher Rundfunk Köln (WDR) is advertising a framework agreement on behalf of the following broadcasting corporations and institutions of the broadcasting corporations: ARD-Hauptstadtstudio (ARD-HSB, represented by rbb), ARD ZDF Deutschlandradio Beitragsservice (ZBS), Bayerischer Rundfunk (BR), Deutschlandradio (DLR), Deutsche Welle (DW), Hessischer Rundfunk (HR), Informationsverarbeitungszentrum (IVZ, represented by rbb), Mitteldeutscher Rundfunk (MDR), Norddeutscher Rundfunk (NDR), Radio Bremen (RB), Rundfunk Berlin-Brandenburg (rbb), Saarländischer Rundfunk (SR), Südwestrundfunk (SWR), Westdeutscher Rundfunk (WDR) and Zweites Deutsches Fernsehen (ZDF). Also eligible are all other companies affiliated with the aforementioned broadcasting corporations and institutions, provided that these are "Authorised Institutions" within the meaning of the opening clause of the BMI contract. Affiliated and authorised companies associated with the aforementioned broadcasting corporations and institutions that do not meet the minimum order quantity of 250 qualified devices or users intend, if required, to join together with the affiliated broadcasting corporations and institutions in accordance with the BMI contract, Appendix 1 Section 3, a., (iii) to form a joint accession in order to reach the minimum order quantity. The framework agreement shall enter into force upon the award of contract and shall end upon expiry of the BMI corporate agreement, which entered into force on 01.06.2025, on 31.05.2028 or, taking into account its extension option, on 31.05.2029. During the term of the framework agreement, eligible entities may make accessions to the BMI corporate agreement. In doing so, each eligible entity may, if required and where applicable, also make accessions on the basis of various enrolments (e.g. EA Enterprise, EA SCE, EA Subscription enrolment). The effective date of each accession shall mark the commencement of a separate framework agreement (see template agreement in the appendix) between the respective eligible entity as the client and the commercial partner as the contractor. These individual framework agreements have independent terms, which are presented below, and shall therefore also apply to the respective contracting parties beyond the aforementioned end of the term of the framework agreement where applicable. Each eligible entity that makes an accession / concludes a framework agreement acts under its own responsibility, places orders and pays at its own expense. Joint and several liability between the various eligible entities is excluded. Insofar as individual clients guarantee minimum purchase quantities, these result from the appendix Minimum Purchase Quantities.xlsx of these procurement documents. Purchase quantities going beyond this are not guaranteed. The respective framework agreement shall end after 36 months without the need for termination. The framework agreement partner grants the clients the right to extend the respective framework agreement once by one year under the same conditions. The respective client must declare the exercise of the option in writing to the framework agreement partner before the expiry of the contract. The subsequent further extension option shall serve in particular the purpose of ensuring the possibility of an interruption-free commissioning of Software Assurance as well as operation for the respective client if a procurement procedure for such commissioning cannot be carried out / completed in good time. The framework agreement partner therefore grants the clients the right in each case to extend the respective framework agreement once again by up to 6 further months. The conditions may change for this extension period. An adjustment of the dealer's mark-up or markdown on its purchase prices may be made by mutual agreement in this case. The dealer must explain the circumstances altering the calculation. Insofar as further adjustments to the framework agreement have to be made due to Microsoft licence programme changes, these shall likewise be coordinated by mutual agreement. If and to the extent that valid successor agreements already exist between the Federal Ministry of the Interior and Microsoft at the time the extension option for the further 6 months is exercised - where applicable also on the basis of a different Microsoft licence programme -, these may be selected as the basis. The framework agreement partner further agrees that during this extension term, any client may terminate the framework agreement at any time and without observing a notice period and carry out a change of commercial partner. The currently existing EA accessions expire for all eligible entities on 31.05.2026. It is intended to make accessions to the new BMI corporate agreement on the following dates: 01.06.2026 The clients will announce the products and quantities for their respective initial orders in good time. The contractor will then promptly provide the respective client with the prices valid for the initial order, taking into account the Microsoft price and the discount for the EA commercial partners in accordance with the BMI corporate agreement as well as the mark-up or markdown to be offered.

sig_0b0d93c7d1fd46b33203.description: NIS-2-compliant transformation of OT systems cooling supply area Lot LOT-0001: Modernisation of automation and network technology water treatment works.. The subject of the tender is the renewal and modernisation of the automation, visualisation and network technology in two water treatment works and one elevated reservoir. The aim of the measure is to upgrade the systems to the state of the art, taking into account the requirements for cybersecurity, network segmentation, availability and operational reliability in the environment of NIS-2 requirements. The scope of services includes the planning, supply, installation, parametrisation, programming, migration, commissioning and documentation of the automation technology, including the replacement of existing PLC systems, decentralised automation components and the required communication and telecontrol interfaces. The replacement of the automation technology will take place on the basis of the Siemens system platform using current SIMATIC S7-1500 controllers, including engineering in the TIA Portal. The central process visualisation is to be supplied, configured and put into operation ready for use on the basis of Siemens WinCC Unified. The visualisation is to be integrated with the automation systems to be newly constructed and the existing technical equipment. Furthermore, the service includes the renewal and expansion of the industrial network infrastructure, including active network components, network segmentation, secure communication connections, remote access solutions and the components required to implement a modern IT/OT security concept. The service also includes the migration of existing functions and process data, the execution of factory, function and data point tests, commissioning during ongoing plant operation, training of operating personnel and the handover of complete as-built and inventory documentation. The specification of the Siemens system platform is intended to ensure a uniform system architecture within the client's facilities, guarantee compatibility with existing standards, secure the ability of operating personnel to perform their own maintenance, and avoid additional training, licensing and interface expenses. The targeted system continuity serves in particular to ensure long-term operational and investment security as well as the implementation of a consistent cybersecurity concept. Special requirements arise from the maintenance of the water supply during the conversion measures. The contractor must plan and execute the work in such a way that necessary operational interruptions are limited to the technically necessary minimum. Comparable references from water treatment works, wastewater facilities or other critical infrastructure facilities are required.
sig_0b0d93c7d1fd46b33203.title: NIS-2-compliant transformation of OT systems cooling supply area

sig_0b3b2603ff6a58a15a82.description: The ESG data management system serves as a centrally controlled, specialised Software-as-a-Service platform (SaaS platform) for the integrative procurement, processing, quality assurance and provision of external ESG data for the KfW Group. The external ESG data delivery route (hereinafter also referred to as "XEDALI") replaces the previous decentralised and heterogeneous procurement and connection of external ESG data sources through a standardised ETL process (Extract – Transform – Load). The application will regularly query ESG data at the software interfaces to various external data providers, transfer it into a uniform data model and provide it for use in subsequent processes. It thus provides users with a consistent data source for external ESG data. XEDALI thus makes a significant contribution to the technical support and fulfilment of new regulatory requirements (in particular the EBA Guidelines on ESG risks (EBA/GL/2025/01), MaRisk as well as the VSME standard and the requirements from BCBS239), further details see "Specification of Services". sig_0ba0f15daf63d69f0175.description: Die Landesmesse Stuttgart GmbH & Co. KG (LMS) is advertising services of an external Information Security Officer (ISO). The LMS intends to commission services of an external Information Security Officer (ISO) in order to improve the level of security comprehensively and sustainably. The implementation of an internationally recognised standard for information security management systems is envisaged. The security level of the LMS is intended to be aligned with ISO 27001. Certification is not currently planned, but could become relevant from a perspective standpoint (e.g. due to customer requirements). The external Information Security Officer shall be assigned the following tasks in particular: - Development and implementation of security strategies: Creation of security concepts, policies and guidelines tailored to the specific needs of the LMS. This includes the further development of the Information Security Management System (ISMS). - Risk management: Implementation and continuous updating of risk analyses and business impact analyses (BIA) to identify and assess potential threats. - Reporting: Establishment of reporting processes as well as regular evaluation and presentation of security-related information to the specialist departments and management. - Continuous monitoring: Monitoring the effectiveness of the implemented security measures and, as required, adjustment of the implemented measures. - Compliance with statutory requirements: Ensuring that the LMS complies with all relevant laws, regulations and industry standards in the field of information security. - Security incidents: Investigation, processing and risk assessment of security incidents incl. taking measures for damage limitation - Collaboration: Close cooperation with the internal "Information Security Manager" as well as the other specialist departments (especially IT) as well as the Security Operations Center (SOC), the Data Protection Officer and management - Internal and external audits: Support in preparation for internal and external audits on information security - Technical security measures: Involvement in the conception, evaluation and decision on the introduction or modernisation of technologies (e.g. new EDR solution, network segmentation), which is why corresponding IT and IT security architecture know-how should be available with the contractor. The contractor does not have to be responsible for the decisions, but must be able to advise accordingly in the sense of an advisory function in accordance with their role. The subject matter of the procedure is now the Europe-wide procurement of services of an external Information Security Officer (ISO) by means of a negotiated procedure with a preceding call for competition. Further information on the content of the tender will be made available to the bidders who are invited to submit tenders. The services are to be awarded for a period of 24 months (2 years), provisionally commencing on 1 April 2026.
sig_0ba0f15daf63d69f0175.title: Landesmesse Stuttgart GmbH & Co. KG - Europe-wide procurement of services of an external Information Security Officer (ISO)

The ECM programme is responsible for the integration, introduction and further development of the newly developed information system OPUS, which is gradually replacing the previously used solution. As an integrated information and work platform, OPUS forms the basis for digital and workflow-based case processing for the affiliated 16 social insurance companies. The introduction will take place in stages as part of a multi-year transformation programme until the end of 2030. The subject of this tender is the provision of services in the areas of programme management, project management and Project Management Office (PMO). The services include, in particular, the management, conception, planning, control, coordination, monitoring and completion of programme and project initiatives as well as support for the further development, migration, introduction, transformation and transfer of the solution into operational use. The services are provided in a complex technical and organisational environment. This is characterised by the parallel management of system integration, product development, rollout and organisational transformation, as well as by the cooperation of numerous stakeholders from the participating implementation bodies, external suppliers and the IGS. Depending on requirements, the services may additionally include tasks in the areas of business analysis, test management and quality assurance. The tender is looking for a provider that can provide the required services independently or, where permitted, with the involvement of subcontractors. A framework agreement with a term of four years will be concluded with the successful bidder. There is no purchase obligation on the part of the contracting authority; services are called off as required in accordance with the framework agreement.

sig_0c33f8ce5717cafc61b0.description: THIS IS NOT A CONTRACT NOTICE OR A CALL FOR TENDERS BUT AN INFORMATION REQUEST FOR MARKET RESEARCH AND TECHNICAL DIALOGUE. This information request is used to survey the market and obtain information regarding the procurement. The contracting authority is not initiating a procurement procedure with the publication of the information request; rather, a potential contract notice and call for tenders will be published later. The information request does not oblige the contracting authority to carry out the actual procurement. Answering the information request is not a prerequisite for participating in any later procurement procedure that may be organised. Suppliers will not be paid compensation for answering the information request or participating in the market dialogue. The responses provided to this information request will be used in planning the procurement of a medical device processing RFID system and related supplies for the needs of HUS-yhtymä. The system and supplies to be procured must be suitable for use in hospital sterile services environments. The purpose of the information request is to survey suppliers on the market as well as their product and service ranges. The purpose is to ascertain technical solutions, pricing principles and the cost level for budgeting purposes. HUS-yhtymä requests your written comments in particular on the following questions: 1. Durability and lifecycle of tags in a hospital environment 1.1. How do the RFID tags you offer withstand medical device processing sterilisation and washing processes? State the maximum temperature resistance of the tags (e.g. autoclave +134 °C), pressure resistance, and chemical tolerance (such as alkaline detergents). 1.2. What is the estimated lifecycle of the tags you offer (measured as operational reliability in washing and sterilisation cycles)? Do you offer a warranty for the durability of the tags in a sterile services environment? 2. Compatibility with existing automation and standards 2.1. Another unit of ours already uses RFID-controlled automation. What frequency bands and standards (e.g. UHF / RAIN RFID, HF, ISO 18000-63) does your system support to ensure seamless compatibility with existing equipment? 2.2. Does your system and readers support general global identification and data standards (such as GS1/EPC)? 2.3. Is your system "vendor-independent" (open standard) with regard to tags? Can we in future freely purchase tags that meet the requirements from third parties, or does the system require your own identifiers? 3. Reliability in a metal environment (On-Metal) 3.1. Medical device processing handles almost exclusively metal (baskets, containers, instruments). How are your system's reader devices and so-called on-metal tags optimised to operate in this environment without dead zones or signal reflection interference? 3.2. How reliably does your system perform bulk reading (e.g. a situation where an entire trolley of overlapping steel baskets is pushed through the reading area at once)? What is the tested margin of error in this scenario? 4. Software integrations and interfaces 4.1. What ready-made integrations or interface solutions (API) does your system have? HUS Sterile Services uses the Gemini production control system supplied by CGI. 4.2. How is data transferred from RFID reading to the main system: does the data transfer take place in real time and does it require the maintenance of a separate middleware? 5. Cost structure and implementation 5.1. What is the preliminary cost structure of your solution (one-off equipment and installation costs vs. recurring licence, maintenance and tag costs)? 5.2. According to the plan, the system is being procured for two sterile services centres (Jorvi and Meilahti). What is your preliminary estimate of the duration of the implementation project in units of this type? On what kind of schedule after signing the agreement would you be capable of starting/executing the implementation project? 6. Other 6.1 Would you like to raise any other aspects related to the subject of the procurement or the solution you offer? HUS-yhtymä requests suppliers interested in the procurement described above to notify the contracting authority of their interest and answer the questions presented above, and to attach to the response a general description/brochure of the solutions you offer for the need described above. Please note that all material is intended solely for conducting this market dialogue. The contracting authority will treat your responses confidentially. Based on the responses to the information request, clarifying questions may be posed to the supplier and/or an opportunity may be offered to present their solutions in a manner to be announced later. Suppliers that have responded to the information request may potentially receive preliminary call for tender documents for comment. We kindly ask you to submit your responses to the information request and notify your interest no later than 23.9.2026 at 12:00 to the address kilpailutus.ict@hus.fi. The subject line of the message must mention "HUS 578-2025 - Medical Device Processing RFID System".
sig_0c33f8ce5717cafc61b0.title: Information request: Medical Device Processing RFID System

sig_0c93152b017493f28e8a.description: THIS IS NOT A CONTRACT NOTICE OR A CALL FOR COMPETITION BUT A REQUEST FOR INFORMATION FOR MARKET RESEARCH AND DIALOGUE. The City of Pori has a need for a tool that covers the entire lifecycle of construction and premises projects and supports early-stage design of projects, simulation of alternatives and the reporting required to support decision-making. The aim is to improve the design quality, cost control and comparability of alternatives of projects and to support the preparation of investment decisions qualitatively and economically. The purpose of the request for information is to survey cost simulation software services available on the market that support the design and decision-making of construction and premises projects. The market research clarifies suppliers' solutions, pricing models, service content, integration possibilities and technical requirements before the preparation of the actual procurement. No tenders are submitted in response to the request for information; instead, by registering for the market consultation, the supplier declares its willingness to participate in the preparation of the procurement. SUBJECT: Kela is preparing the procurement of an organisation-wide AI governance tool (AI Governance Tool), which provides a centralised solution for the registration, risk classification, lifecycle management, documentation of AI systems, and verification of compliance in accordance with the EU Artificial Intelligence Act (AI Act). The subject of the procurement is an off-the-shelf software delivered as a cloud service, which brings together processes, workflows, monitoring and reporting, enabling transparent, auditable and efficient AI governance across Kela's operations. The solution supports the initial setup of the 20–50 system and will scale according to growing needs, providing comprehensive maintenance, information security and support services as well as role-based access control. MARKET CONSULTATION: Participants are requested to, inter alia: - present solutions available on the market - answer questions concerning the procurement - comment on minimum requirements, for example for the removal of conflicts of interest - provide ideas for improving the solution and the tendering process The consultation will be carried out in multiple formats: Presentation sessions may be held remotely via Microsoft Teams, and requirement definitions, for example, will be handled by email. As part of the market survey, the signing of a non-disclosure agreement may be required for the sharing of confidential material. The material and procurement documentation provided by Kela are in Finnish, and the contracting authority will not translate the material. PARTICIPATION: Interested participants are requested to declare their willingness to participate in the market survey by email to it.tarjouskilpailut@kela.fi 27.3.2026 by 12. Example of message content: Message subject: Company xx's participation in the market consultation for the procurement of the AI governance tool Message content: The message should ideally indicate the supplier's name, business ID and contact person through whom the consultation will be conducted. We also hope that a short presentation material on the offered solution would be attached to the participation message. The presentation material is expected to describe concisely the key features of the solution, the technical architecture, the implementation of AI Act requirements, and any experience of similar implementations. OTHER: The request for information does not oblige the contracting authority to carry out the actual procurement or to execute the procurement in the manner described in the request for information. sig_0dede13dbac2a395a289.description: The overall goal of this program is to accelerate scientific discovery, improve research efficiency, and enhance the translation of research findings into improved health outcomes. Centers funded under this program will also foster multidisciplinary collaboration, support workforce development across career stages, and promote training in emerging areas such as data science, artificial intelligence, and implementation research. The National Institute of Arthritis and Musculoskeletal and Skin Diseases (NIAMS) requests applications for the NIAMS P30 Centers Program to support integrated research Centers within its mission areas of skin biology and diseases; bone, muscle, and orthopaedic research; and rheumatic diseases. The NIAMS P30 Centers Program supports Centers that provide coordinated research infrastructure, shared resources, and methodological expertise to advance basic, translational, and clinical research. These Centers are expected to integrate state-of-the-art research resources with capabilities that support clinical and translational research, including the development, testing, and dissemination of novel analytical methods, study designs, outcome measures, and data-driven approaches. The overall goal of this program is to accelerate scientific discovery, improve research efficiency, and enhance the translation of research findings into improved health outcomes. Centers funded under this program will also foster multidisciplinary collaboration, support workforce development across career stages, and promote training in emerging areas such as data science, artificial intelligence, and implementation research.

sig_0df6b64ec2f9021fef92.description: This Special Notice provides interested parties with information regarding the availability of the draft Request for Proposal (dRFP), review requirements, the tentative acquisition schedule, and the upcoming Industry Day and Site Visit. This notice is for planning purposes only and does not constitute an invitation for bids, request for proposals, or quotes, nor does it indicate that the Government will contract for the items described herein. The Government will not reimburse respondents for any costs associated with submitting feedback or attending the events outlined in this notice. The 30th Contracting Squadron (30 CONS/PKD) at Vandenberg Space Force Base (VSFB), CA, is requesting industry feedback on the dRFP for the Facility Readiness and Maintenance Execution (FRAME) contract. FRAME is the follow-on acquisition to the current Launch Operations Support Contract (LOSC) (Contract #FA4610-23-D-0001, currently performed by Call Henry, Inc.). FRAME follow-on acquisition is 100% Small Business Set-Aside. The North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) code for this effort is 561210 Facilities Support Services (small business size standard is $47M). Description of Services, Background, and Objective: FRAME is a non-personal services contract that provides maintenance, repair, modification, and modernization for?over 130?facilities, property, and equipment (P&E)?supporting?the nation’s space mission, defense, and test activities at VSFB and its associated geographically-separated locations. The scope of work involves facility infrastructure and systems (including water and gas mains, roads, generators, power distribution, HVAC, waste systems, and roofing) alongside the execution of distinct sustainment projects and?standby support for urgent repairs during select?launch operations to ensure maximum operational readiness. Additionally, the contract encompasses the inspection,?testing,?and certification of all Space Launch Delta 30 cranes and elevators. A key change under this follow-on acquisition is that the South Vandenberg Power Plant (SVPP) is no longer a requirement and will not be carried over from the legacy LOSC to the new FRAME contract. The primary objective of the FRAME contract is to ensure Real Property Installed Equipment (RPIE) and facilities are maintained and operationally ready for a variety of ballistic missile, space, guided weapon, and aircraft test and evaluation missions in support of Space Launch Delta 30 (SLD 30), 30th Civil Engineer Squadron (30 CES), 4th Launch Squadron (4 LS), 2nd Range Operations Squadron (2 ROPS), Missile Defense Agency (MDA), U. S. Space Forces - Space (S4S), 18th Space Defense Squadron (18 SDS), Sentinel, 30th Operations Support Squadron (30 OSS), 2nd Space Launch Squadron (2 SLS), the National Reconnaissance Office (NRO), and various other Range Users. Mission Essential Services: The FRAME contract contains some mission-essential requirements which require continued support during peacetime, national emergency, and/or wartime scenarios. Tentative Acquisition Schedule: dRFP Release: 8 Sep 26 Final RFP Issuance: 12 Nov 26 Proposals Due: 16 Jan 27 Anticipated Award: 18 Dec 27 Performance Start:?1 Apr 28 4. Industry Day and Site Visit Event Details Interested businesses are invited to register for the upcoming two-day event. Representatives will have the opportunity to attend a briefing detailing the contract structure, tour key range facilities, and participate in one-on-one sessions with the Government program team. Dates: September 22, 2026 (General Briefing & Tour) – September 23, 2026 (One-on-One Sessions) Location: Vandenberg Space Force Base (VSFB), CA Maximum Attendees: Limited to two (2) representatives per prospective company due to base logistical constraints. Registration and RSVP Deadlines: Attendee RSVP & Security Vetting Submission: No later than Friday, September 11, 2026, at 16:30 Pacific Time. Provide your full name and company. Late requests may not be processed. One-on-One Meeting Request: Companies interested in booking a one-on-one session with the program office must explicitly request it via email by Tuesday, September 15, 2026, at 16:30 Pacific Time. Slots are limited and will be scheduled on a first-come, first-served basis. Maps and a tentative agenda are attached to this announcement to assist registered attendees with navigation and scheduling. Base Access & Entry Requirements: All site visit attendees must report to the Vandenberg Visitor Control Center (VCC), located at 6 California Blvd (Santa Maria Gate) prior to entry (VCC hours: 0600-1800). Arrive Early: Attendees are strongly encouraged to arrive early to the Visitor Control Center to allow sufficient time for base entry processing and to avoid delays getting to the briefing. Identification for Non-CAC Holders: Attendees who do not possess a Common Access Card (CAC) must present a REAL ID-compliant credential or a valid U.S. Passport. If an attendee does not have a REAL ID or a Passport, they must bring and present a standard state-issued Driver's License or ID card, a Birth Certificate, and a physical Social Security Card to obtain a base visitor pass. Foreign Nationals will not be able to participate due to the time necessary to vet access. 5. Important Site Visit Disclaimers & Rules of Conduct: Change of Solicitation Terms: Please understand that nothing said during the Industry Day briefings, site tours, or one-on-one sessions by any Government representative changes the terms, conditions, specifications, or requirements of the solicitation. If a change to the solicitation is determined to be necessary based on what is discussed or observed, it will be formally issued as a written amendment via email. Photography and Video Restrictions: No photography or video recording is permitted on this installation at any time, unless specific, designated areas are explicitly pointed out and authorized by the hosting Facility Manager. 6. Submission of Questions & Comments (CRM) The Government is actively seeking industry feedback on the Draft PWS and planned acquisition strategy to ensure clear, high-performing requirements. To submit questions or comments concerning the acquisition and dRFP, prospective offerors must use the official Comment Resolution Matrix (CRM) Excel spreadsheet (which will be posted with the Draft RFP documents). Completed CRM spreadsheets must be returned to the Points of Contact listed below. The deadline for submitting dRFP and Industry Day comments is September 29, 2026, by 16:30 Pacific Time. 7. Primary Points of Contact For all RSVP submissions, one-on-one requests, CRM question submittals or administrative questions, please send correspondence via email to BOTH of the following representatives: Primary POC (Contracting Officer): Katherine Williams, 30 CONS/PKD Email: katherine.williams.9@spaceforce.mil Secondary POC (Contract Specialist): Sabrina Swain, 30 CONS/PKD Email: sabrina.swain.1@spaceforce.mil 9/8/2026: This office is updating this draft RFP to update and add additional attachments.

sig_0dfccdff75d47ebcc6f8.description: SOURCES SOUGHT Title: Atrium Replacement at Chickamauga Visitor Center, Chickamauga and Chattanooga National Military Park Project: CHCH 315696 Notice ID: 140P5126R0014 Posted Date: September 9, 2026 Response Date: October 9, 2026 Set Aside: TBD – Market Research Only NAICS Code: 236220 – Commercial and Institutional Building Construction Size Standard: $45,000,000.00 1. DISCLAIMER This Sources Sought Notice is issued for market research and acquisition-planning purposes only and does not constitute a solicitation, Request for Proposal (RFP), Request for Quote (RFQ), Invitation for Bid (IFB), or commitment by the Government. The Government is not obligated to issue a solicitation or award a contract as a result of this notice. Responses to this notice are not considered offers and cannot be accepted by the Government to form a binding contract. Respondents are solely responsible for all expenses associated with responding to this notice. Information received may be used by the Government to determine the appropriate acquisition strategy, including whether the anticipated requirement should be set aside for one or more small business programs. 2. AGENCY INFORMATION Department of the Interior National Park Service Contracting Operations (ConOps) East Point of Contact: Edward Dingle, Jr. Edward_dingle@ios.doi.gov 3. DESCRIPTION OF REQUIREMENT The Department of the Interior, National Park Service (NPS), is conducting market research to determine the availability and capability of qualified construction contractors to perform the Atrium Replacement at the Chickamauga Visitor Center, Chickamauga and Chattanooga National Military Park, Fort Oglethorpe, Georgia, Project CHCH 315696. The contemplated project generally consists of replacement of the existing Visitor Center atrium, limited parking-lot modifications, reconfiguration of the north and south plazas, and associated fire-protection, plumbing, mechanical, electrical, communications, fire-alarm, architectural, structural, civil/site, and landscape improvements. The work is anticipated to be performed under a single prime construction contract and includes multiple interdependent construction disciplines requiring significant coordination by the prime contractor. Major elements of work include, but are not necessarily limited to: • Selective demolition and demolition of the existing Visitor Center atrium. • Construction of the replacement atrium, including structural, architectural, roofing, building-envelope, curtain-wall/glazing, entrance, and interior-finish work. • Civil, landscape, parking, pedestrian pathway, paving, grading, earthwork, stormwater, and related site improvements. • Fire-protection modifications, including dry-pipe sprinkler-system work. • Plumbing and facility drainage improvements. • HVAC/mechanical modifications, including associated piping, ductwork, equipment, controls, supports, vibration/seismic requirements, and testing and balancing. • Electrical modifications, including demolition, conductors, raceways, grounding, panelboards, wiring devices, lighting, and associated electrical distribution work. • Fire-alarm, communications, and related life-safety systems. • Temporary facilities and controls, environmental protection, construction waste management, testing, commissioning, project documentation, and closeout. The specifications separately identify contract line items covering site demolition, demolition of the existing Visitor Center atrium, civil and landscape improvements, construction of the new atrium, fire-sprinkler upgrades, plumbing/drainage upgrades, mechanical improvements, and electrical improvements. Occupied Facility and Public Access The work will occur at an active National Park Service visitor facility. Areas outside the construction limits are expected to remain occupied by NPS personnel and accessible to park visitors. Construction activities must therefore be planned and coordinated to protect employees and the public, maintain access and required exits, and minimize disruption to park and Visitor Center operations. Temporary construction controls include fencing, barriers, and separation of construction activities from occupied/public areas. The project also contains requirements concerning historic-preservation treatment, protection of existing resources, ground-disturbing activities, construction scheduling, quality control, environmental protection, fire/life-safety continuity, and multidisciplinary construction coordination. Accordingly, the Government is particularly interested in determining whether firms—especially qualified small businesses—possess the experience, personnel, subcontractor resources, bonding capacity, and management systems necessary to serve as the prime contractor and integrator for the complete multidisciplinary requirement. 4. SMALL BUSINESS PROGRAMS OF INTEREST The Government is seeking capability statements from firms under the applicable NAICS code 236220, including: • Small Business • Small Disadvantaged Business • 8(a) Business Development Program Participant • HUBZone Small Business • Service-Disabled Veteran-Owned Small Business (SDVOSB) • Women-Owned Small Business (WOSB) • Economically Disadvantaged Women-Owned Small Business (EDWOSB) • Indian Small Business Economic Enterprise (ISBEE) • Other eligible socioeconomic categories • Large Business Responses will assist the Government in evaluating the availability of capable firms and determining an appropriate acquisition strategy. 5. REQUESTED INFORMATION Interested firms should submit a capability statement addressing the following information. i. Business Information Name of Firm: ______________________________________ Address: ___________________________________________ Phone Number: ______________________________________ Email Address: ______________________________________ UEI Number: ________________________________________ Cage Code: __________________________________________ Business Size Under NAICS 236220: _____________________ SAM Registration Status: ? Yes/Active?? Yes/Inactive?? No ii. Size Status/SBA Certification Mark all that apply: ? Small Business ? Small Disadvantaged Business ? 8(a) ? HUBZone ? Service-Disabled Veteran-Owned Small Business (SDVOSB) ? Women-Owned Small Business (WOSB) ? Economically Disadvantaged Women-Owned Small Business (EDWOSB) ? Indian Small Business Economic Enterprise (ISBEE) ? Other: __________________________ ? Large Business iii. Relevant Prime-Contractor Experience Provide information for up to three comparable projects completed or substantially completed within the past five years. For each project, provide: a. Project name and location. b. Contract number, if applicable. c. Customer/owner and current point of contact. d. Original and final contract value. e. Period of performance. f. Whether your firm performed as the prime contractor, joint-venture member, or subcontractor. g. Approximate percentage of work self-performed. h. Number and types of major subcontractors/trades managed. i. Description of the work performed and explanation of why the project is comparable to this requirement. The Government is particularly interested in projects involving visitor centers, museums, historic buildings, public/institutional facilities, or other occupied facilities involving multiple architectural, structural, civil/site, building-envelope, MEP, fire-protection, electrical, and life-safety disciplines under a single prime contract. iv. Bonding and Financial Capacity Provide: a. Single-project bonding capacity. b. Aggregate bonding capacity. c. Largest construction project for which the firm has obtained performance and payment bonds. d. Name of surety or bonding agent, if available. v. Technical and Management Capability Describe your firm's capability to serve as the prime/general contractor responsible for managing, coordinating, and integrating multiple construction disciplines on a project of similar size, scope, and complexity. Address the following areas: a. Multi-Trade Construction Integration and Coordination Describe experience managing projects involving architectural, structural, civil/site, fire-protection, plumbing, HVAC/mechanical, electrical, fire-alarm, and communications work. The project specifications require coordination drawings addressing architectural, structural, mechanical, plumbing, fire-protection, fire-alarm, and electrical elements, including ceiling/plenum coordination, mechanical rooms, structural penetrations, embedded items, electrical equipment, and fire-protection piping. The detailed coordination of these systems is the Construction Contractor's responsibility. For comparable projects, describe: 1. Number and types of major subcontractors/trades managed; 2. Methods used to coordinate architectural, structural, MEP, and life-safety systems; 3. Experience identifying and resolving conflicts between trades; and 4. How coordination activities were incorporated into the construction schedule. b. Construction in Occupied and Publicly Accessible Facilities Describe experience performing major construction or renovation while the facility remained occupied or open to employees, visitors, customers, or the public. Address experience with: 1. Maintaining public and employee access; 2. Construction barriers and separation; 3. Maintenance of required exits and life-safety systems; 4. Utility and system shutdown coordination; 5. Dust, noise, debris, and vibration control; 6. Construction traffic and deliveries; and 7. Coordination with facility operations. c. Historic-Preservation Construction Describe experience performing construction, rehabilitation, alteration, or demolition involving historic buildings, historic materials, National Park Service facilities, National Register properties, or similarly sensitive resources. The specifications require preservation planning addressing staging and sequencing, disassembly and reassembly techniques, equipment and tools, skilled trades and crafts, anticipated testing and analysis of historic fabric, protective measures, seasonal limitations, and alternative treatment methods. Existing historic materials must also be protected during construction, and temporary protections may not deface or remove existing materials. Identify whether your firm or proposed subcontractors have personnel with specialized historic-preservation experience. d. Archeological and Ground-Disturbing Work Describe experience managing excavation, grading, foundations, utilities, or other ground-disturbing construction at historic, archeologically sensitive, park, or environmentally sensitive sites. Address procedures used to: 1. Control and document ground-disturbing work; 2. Protect cultural or archeological resources; 3. Respond to unexpected discoveries; 4. Coordinate with owner/cultural-resource personnel; and 5. Protect existing survey monuments, benchmarks, and site features. The specifications require existing benchmarks, control points, land corners, and triangulation points to be preserved, with written permission required before removal of interfering monuments. e. Fire-Protection and Life-Safety Coordination Describe experience managing sprinkler, fire-alarm, and other life-safety system modifications as part of an occupied-building renovation. The specifications require sprinkler-system engineering, fabrication, installation, calculations, and testing by qualified personnel and identify compliance with NFPA 13 and NFPA 24. Existing sprinkler service serving occupied facilities cannot be interrupted without advance notification and written authorization, and temporary sprinkler service may be required. Describe experience coordinating shutdowns, temporary protection, inspections, testing, commissioning, and restoration of service. f. CPM Scheduling and Construction Sequencing Describe your firm's ability to develop and maintain a Critical Path Method (CPM) construction schedule for a multi-trade construction project. The specifications require a baseline schedule associated with the Schedule of Values and CPM reports containing activity descriptions, cost/resource loading, durations, early/late dates, and total float. Schedule revisions may require Time Impact Analyses and Fragmentary Networks (Fragnets). The contractor's designated scheduler is required to have prepared and maintained at least five previous schedules of similar size and complexity and demonstrate proficiency in scheduling software. Indicate whether qualified scheduling personnel are currently available within your organization or would be obtained through a subcontractor or consultant. g. Quality Control, Testing, and Special Inspections Describe experience implementing formal construction quality-control procedures on federal or similarly complex institutional construction. Address experience coordinating: 1. Submittals and shop drawings; 2. Delegated designs; 3. Manufacturer requirements; 4. Preparatory and follow-up inspections; 5. Independent testing; 6. Special inspections; 7. Deficiency tracking and corrective actions; and 8. Testing and closeout documentation. The specifications identify structural special inspections involving high-load shear walls, anchoring within the seismic-force-resisting system, and wood-frame construction at the high-roof area. h. Environmental Protection and Construction Controls Describe experience implementing environmental protection measures at federal, park, historic, or environmentally sensitive sites. Address experience with erosion and sediment controls, storm-drain protection, construction waste, pollution prevention, dust control, protection of existing vegetation/landscaping, and management of construction-generated materials. The specifications include measures to protect landscaping, and storm drains and to prevent construction solids and pollutants from entering drainage systems. i. Prime Contractor Organizational Capability Describe the project-management organization your firm would anticipate using for a project of this nature. Identify whether the following functions would be performed by company personnel or subcontracted/consultant personnel: Project Manager; Superintendent; Quality Control; Site Safety; CPM Scheduling; Historic Preservation; Environmental Compliance; MEP Coordination; and Fire-Protection Coordination. Describe the firm's experience managing submittals, RFIs, coordination drawings, schedules, testing and inspection documentation, project records, commissioning/closeout activities, and communications with a federal Contracting Officer. vi. Small-Business Prime Contractor Capability Small business respondents should specifically address their capability to perform this requirement as the prime contractor. If your firm is a small business under the applicable NAICS code, provide: a. A statement as to whether your firm believes it can successfully perform the complete contemplated requirement as the prime contractor. b. Construction disciplines your firm anticipates self-performing. c. Major portions of work anticipated to be subcontracted. d. Whether your firm currently has established relationships with qualified subcontractors capable of performing the anticipated structural, glazing/curtain-wall, roofing, fire-protection, plumbing, mechanical, electrical, fire-alarm, civil/site, landscape, and specialty historic-preservation work. e. Whether your firm anticipates competing independently or through a joint venture, mentor-protégé joint venture, or other teaming arrangement. f. The largest comparable project your firm has successfully managed as the prime contractor, including contract value, approximate self-performance percentage, and number of major subcontractors/trades managed. g. Your firm's ability to obtain the bonding necessary for a project of comparable size. h. Your firm's anticipated ability to comply with applicable limitations on subcontracting if the acquisition is set aside for small business. i. Any aspect of the contemplated requirement that could materially limit your firm's ability to compete or perform as the prime contractor. j. Any acquisition, packaging, scheduling, phasing, or solicitation approach the Government should consider to facilitate meaningful competition among capable small-business prime contractors. vii. Self-Performance and Subcontractor Availability All respondents should identify: a. Work anticipated to be self-performed. b. Major work anticipated to be subcontracted. c. Availability of qualified subcontractors in the project region for major specialty disciplines. d. Any specialty trade or material for which limited market availability could affect competition, price, or schedule. e. Any anticipated long-lead materials or equipment. viii. Project Schedule and Constraints Based on your firm's experience with projects of comparable scope and complexity, provide: a. Recommended overall construction period. b. Significant sequencing or phasing considerations. c. Major long-lead materials/equipment. d. Potential constraints associated with maintaining Visitor Center and park operations. e. Any seasonal, environmental, historic preservation, or specialty-trade constraints that could materially affect the construction schedule. ix. Interest in Future Solicitation State whether your firm intends to compete for this requirement if a solicitation is issued. Identify the anticipated role: ? Prime Contractor ? Joint Venture ? Mentor-Protégé Joint Venture ? Subcontractor ? Other: ______________________ If your firm does not intend to compete as a prime contractor, briefly identify the principal reason(s). 6. SUBMISSION INSTRUCTIONS Responses shall be no longer than five (5) pages, excluding the completed business information and certification portion if provided as a separate form, and shall be submitted electronically in PDF format. The Government is primarily interested in concise, project-specific information demonstrating actual capability. General marketing literature is discouraged. Submit responses to: edward_dingle@ios.doi.gov The subject line shall read: “Sources Sought Response – Chickamauga Visitor Center Atrium Replacement, CHCH 315696” Responses are due no later than: October 09, 2026. The Government anticipates that any future solicitation will be posted electronically to SAM.gov. Interested parties are responsible for monitoring SAM.gov for subsequent notices regarding this requirement. 7. QUESTIONS Questions regarding this Sources Sought Notice may be submitted by email to the contracting point of contact identified above. The Government may elect to provide responses to questions to all interested parties when the information is considered relevant to the market research. 8. NOTICE This Sources Sought Notice is for informational, market-research, and acquisition-planning purposes only and does not constitute an RFP, RFQ, IFB, or commitment to issue a solicitation. Submission of a capability statement is voluntary. The Government will not reimburse respondents for costs associated with preparing or submitting a response. Information obtained through this notice may be used to develop the Government's acquisition strategy, including assessment of the availability of responsible small-business concerns capable of performing the contemplated requirement as prime contractors.

sig_0eae879ae512de7f35df.description: Tenderers are hereby invited to a market dialogue for the procurement of 2026/68199 for the procurement of an ID card for access and login to the health companies in Helse Vest. The market dialogue is a part of the preliminary work for the procurement and is being carried out as the Contracting Authority would like input for the procurement from possible suppliers and other interested parties. It will be central to identify, among other things, how the supplier market can cover the need and relevant environmental considerations. At the same time, the contracting authority would like to make the market aware that Helse Vest is looking into future possibilities for acquiring a regional access administration system that shall collect identity and access management in a common platform. This is seen to have close connections with cards that shall be procured and it will be important to clarify the dependencies and important requirements against this so that it works together. We would like, in this market dialogue, to respond in writing to concrete questions in order to map the supplier market, environmental impact and relevant areas for the requirement specifications. It is also of interest to gain insight into important links and possibilities toward a future regional access management system. In order to limit the use of resources in the further dialogue after written responses, the Contracting Authority reserves the right to limit the number of participants who will be invited to one-to-one meetings.

sig_0ecf3f0ae5930329bd86.description: UCLH wishes to procure a transformation partner to improve efficiency and productivity of the radiotherapy department, challenging current ways of working and offering new insights. Lot 1: . University College London Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust, "UCLH", is one of the largest NHS trusts in the United Kingdom and provides first-class acute and specialist services. UCLH comprises of the following hospitals: University College Hospital, Elizabeth Garrett Anderson Wing, MacMillan Cancer Centre, University College Hospital Grafton Way Building, University College Hospital at Westmoreland Street, Royal National ENT and Eastman Dental Hospitals, National Hospital for Neurology and Neurosurgery, Hospital for Tropical Diseases, Royal London Hospital for Integrated Medicine, and the Institute of Sport, Exercise and Health. UCLH delivers world class cancer care to patients from across the country. Cancer at UCLH spans across multiple sites and departments within the Trust and has included the opening of the Grafton Way Building one of two national Proton Beam Therapy services in December 2021. UCLH is a lead provider within the North Central London Cancer Alliance, as well as providing tertiary services for wider patient populations in specialist services, such as sarcoma for patients from across South East England. In early 2020, UCLH was selected by NHS England as the preferred tertiary cancer provider to take over management of the Mount Vernon Cancer Centre. This transition is subject to a due diligence process during which UCLH are providing transitional support to the Mount Vernon Cancer Centre team, building upon a number of years of collaborative working between the two services. Our Radiotherapy department offers cutting edge and specialised therapy to adult and paediatric patients treating over 2400 new patients a year. UCLH Radiotherapy is a national leader in complex/highly technical radiotherapy in: • Brain and was recently designated a Tessa Jowell Brain Cancer Centre of Excellence • Paediatrics, with the largest paediatric radiotherapy unit in the UK • Sarcomas - one of Europe’s largest service • Head and Neck – (ENT) third largest in the UK • Stereotactic Ablative Radiotherapy (SABR) • Haematological including total body radiation • Brachytherapy • Molecular Radiotherapy - National Referral centre (Paediatric, TYA and adult). The department works closely with a number of specialist hospitals to support cancer pathways which span multiple centres including Great Ormond Street, St. Mary's, Oxford, Southampton and the Royal National Orthopaedic Hospital. The UCH radiotherapy department contains six bunkers with four Varian TrueBeams and one Varian Halcyon. There is a large difference between the national and UCLH complexity profile, 92% of the UCH workload is classed as complex and approximately 8% of the workload is paediatric. The radiotherapy service is delivered by a team of staff including clinical oncologists, radiotherapy physics and engineers, therapeutic radiographers, healthcare play specialists, admin and clerical staff and dedicated nurses. UCLH is also one of two national Proton Beam Therapy centres, providing services to patients from the south of the UK. The departments run an integrated workforce model, with physicists, dosimetrists and radiographers rotating across Radiotherapy and PBT. In total there are around 300 WT across both services. UCLH wishes to procure a transformation partner to improve efficiency and productivity of the radiotherapy department, challenging current ways of working and offering new insights. This could include but is not limited to: • Delivering Cancer Waiting Time Access standards. • Scheduling of patients. • Machine downtime. • Patient pathway and organisation of workflow. • Radiotherapy physics pathways. • Process for commissioning of new linacs. • Use of automation and AI. Expression of Interest The purpose of this preliminary market engagement is to engage with potential partners to gather information and insights from the market to aid the development of the requirements and scope of opportunities for efficiencies to inform the procurement of a transformation partner. Suppliers are requested to provide expressions of interest, including responses to the below questions by e-mail to steviejay.cavanagh@nhs.net by 15:00 on 26th September 2025. 1. What innovative or new ways of working are you currently seeing in the market that may benefit the NHS, and more specifically UCLH, including those that have been included in procurements over the past 12 months? 2. Please describe how you think this contract should be best structured to deliver an efficient Radiotherapy service? 3. Is there anything you think that the Trust should consider before going out to market for these services? 4. What would be your expectations from a partnership with an NHS organisation? This notice does not constitute a formal call for competition.
