sig_0ee3c5cbeb5360d3ded0.description: The project "Supporting a Just Transition in Mexico" aims to strengthen the capacities of key public, private and civil society actors to design and implement socially just decarbonization processes in strategic sectors of the Mexican economy, with a particular focus in key industrial (incl. industrial parks) and the energy sector. The project is commissioned by the German Federal Ministry for Economic Cooperation and Development (BMZ) and implemented by GIZ, with the Mexican Ministry of Economy (SE) as technical partner. It contributes to the BMZ core theme "Climate and energy", to Mexico's implementation of the Paris Agreement and Agenda 2030 SDGs 13, 9, 7, 5, 16 and 17. Mexico's export-oriented industrial model, the rapid expansion of industrial parks and rising energy demand create pressure and opportunities for low-carbon transformation. Building on the updated climate targets set out in Mexico's Nationally Determined Contribution (NDC), the country faces the challenge of turning these commitments into coherent implementation. Regulatory gaps, insufficient technical and financial capacities, and social and gender inequalities still limit progress towards a decarbonised economy. The project responds to these challenges by promoting an integrated approach that combines climate protection, industrial competitiveness and social justice. The overall objective is to strengthen the capacities of key actors to implement just transition processes in strategic sectors of the Mexican economy. To achieve this, the project supports the development of participatory governance frameworks for a just transition. Multistakeholder dialogue formats will foster coordination between federal and subnational authorities, the private sector, financial institutions, workers' representatives and civil society organisations. At the meso and micro levels, the project aims to improve the enabling conditions for the adoption of green technologies by companies and industrial parks in selected sectors. This includes technical and economic feasibility studies, advisory services on energy-efficient and renewable energy solutions, and targeted capacity development for park operators, firms and service providers, with special attention to SMEs and the qualification of women and groups in vulnerable situations for future-oriented jobs. In addition, the project works with public development banks and other financial institutions to align their product portfolios with the needs of companies and park operators investing in green technologies and sustainable infrastructure. Together with these actors, it promotes demand-oriented "just transition finance" instruments that are consistent with Mexico's emerging sustainable finance taxonomy and that can be deployed in and around industrial parks, among other industry sectors. The project also supports the design and implementation of social and gender justice strategies in at least one subnational context. Together with public institutions, private sector actors and social partners, it will pilot mechanisms to identify and mitigate negative social impacts of industrial transformation, and to ensure that women and other groups in vulnerable situations benefit from new economic opportunities. Lessons learned will be documented and shared with key institutions across the country to enable replication in additional industrial parks and regions. By 2028, the project expects that several just transition-oriented policy and regulatory instruments have been adopted; that industrial parks and companies in prioritised sectors have taken investment decisions leading to measurable GHG emission reductions; that financial institutions provide suitable financing instruments for such investments; and that institutions in other regions make use of the experience gained with social and gender justice approaches in the Mexican just transition. The project is implemented from October 2024 to September 2028. Lot LOT-0001: 10040388-Consulting Services for Fostering a Just Transition in the Mexican Industrial Sector. Under the framework of the bilateral technical cooperation project "Supporting a Just Transition in Mexico", GIZ intends to award a contract for consulting services to foster a just transition in the Mexican industrial sector. The assignment will provide technical advisory services to support the design and implementation of socially just decarbonisation processes in key industrial sectors, with a particular focus on industrial parks and their interaction with the energy sector. The contract is tendered through an international competitive procedure in line with GIZ rules and applicable EU public procurement regulations. In close coordination with GIZ, the contractor will support Mexican partner institutions and other stakeholders in translating just transition principles into concrete action in emissions-intensive industries. This includes promoting industrial decarbonisation, enabling the deployment of clean energy and circular economy solutions, and integrating social and gender considerations in industrial transformation processes. The assignment contributes directly to the achievement of the project's outcome and to four key result areas: strengthening governance frameworks for a just transition; improving enabling conditions for green technologies in industry and energy; advancing "just transition finance"; and piloting social and gender justice strategies at subnational level. A first core area of work is the provision of on-demand technical advice and specialised analysis on just transition in the industrial sector, including industrial parks. The contractor will support partners in assessing and designing regulatory and policy approaches to improve the business environment for low-carbon investments, and identifying opportunities where industrial decarbonisation can be aligned with energy transition planning, industrial policy, circular economy models and the use of green materials. All support is expected to systematically address social and gender dimensions, in line with the project's just transition approach. A second core area involves in-depth analytical work on mitigation potential and decarbonisation pathways for selected industrial parks and industrial clusters. This may include the development of emissions baselines and marginal abatement cost curves, scenario modelling for different technology and investment options, and the analysis of economic, social and environmental co-benefits under a just transition perspective. The contractor will work closely with GIZ and national partners to define the scope of these analyses and to translate findings into practical recommendations for policymakers, industrial park operators, companies and financial institutions. A third area of work is strategic communication and knowledge management. The contractor will support the development of narratives around just transition in the Mexican industrial sector and will produce communication and knowledge products such as policy briefs, reports, infographics, editorial and audiovisual materials. The services may also include conceptual and organisational support to events, dialogue formats and peer-learning activities, to disseminate lessons learned and good practices from pilot interventions in industrial parks and other industrial contexts. A fourth area focuses on capacity development. The contractor will design and implement training formats, workshops and other learning tools for key actors at national and subnational levels, including public institutions, industrial park operators, companies, financial institutions, academia and civil society. These activities aim to strengthen technical competencies and practical know-how on just transition, industrial decarbonisation, green and climate finance, circular economy and energy transition, with particular attention to the inclusion of women and groups in vulnerable situations. The contract is expected to run from February 2027 to August 2028. Primary target groups include key actors from the energy, industrial sectors and industrial park operators, as well as state-level economic and environmental authorities and relevant federal institutions. Secondary target groups comprise affected communities, labour representatives, civil society organisations and academic institutions. The assignment builds on and complements cooperation with national and international partners, including UNIDO, Mexican state-level associations such as AMSDE and ANAAE, and the Mexican Association of Private Industrial Parks (AMPIP). To deliver these services, the contractor is expected to provide a multidisciplinary expert team. This includes a team leader with strong experience in industrial decarbonisation and just transition, as well as experts in energy, industrial technologies and eco-industrial park developments, green and climate finance, social and gender impact analysis, strategic communication and capacity development. A pool of additional short-term specialists with national and international experience should be available to cover specific thematic and methodological needs. Bidders are expected to demonstrate substantial experience in climate change mitigation, industrial and energy transitions, and collaboration with public and private stakeholders, and previous work with international cooperation, preferably in Mexico or Latin America. The services will be delivered through a combination of on-demand support and the implementation of result-oriented activities and milestones agreed with GIZ. The assignment includes robust project and knowledge management, results-based monitoring and regular reporting, and must comply with GIZ requirements on data protection, information security, gender equality and environmental and climate safeguards.

sig_0f15f690a6a1f19f021a.description: NHS Wales Shared Services Partnership (NWSSP), hosted by Velindre University NHS Trust, are issuing this Market Engagement Notice to engage with the suppliers to gather feedback on market capabilities and capacity for the provision of managed services to support the operation of a finance, procurement and warehouse management system. The Central Team eBusiness Services (CTeS), within NWSSP, manage and supervise several core national enterprise systems which are used by Health Boards, Trusts, Special Heath Authorities, and Hosted Organisations, in Wales. These systems are collectively known as the FMS Enterprise System and include: - An e-Business Application System, including auxiliary services, which is facilitated through the Oracle eBusiness suite. - A Business Intelligence (BI) reporting system, facilitated through Qlik Sense. - An OCR Intelligent Scanning Management System - A Warehouse Management System - Other BI Reporting Systems The purpose of this market engagement exercise is to gather greater insight into the market’s capacity and capabilities in relation to provision of managed services and NWSSP are specifically seeking engagement from suppliers who are e-Business Suite experts with supply chain capabilities specifically covering warehouse management and who can also support to roll out and further development of discrete manufacturing processes within a regulated environment. The analysis of feedback obtained from this exercise will allow NWSSP to further develop its strategy and refine its service delivery requirements ahead of any potential procurement. The main objectives of this exercise are to: - Assess the level of interest in the marketplace from suppliers who can support the Oracle eBusiness Suite (EBS), - Test market capability and capacity, - Validate the proposed scope and service model, - Understand delivery approaches, innovations and commercial models and indicative rates, and - Explore development and innovation in relation to AI and the benefits that may be realised with its deployment through the Oracle eBusiness Suite. The provision of the Oracle EBS is facilitated through existing perpetual licences, and the scope of this engagement exercise does not include migrating the e-Business Application System to a Software as a Service (SaaS) model. This exercise is not a formal procurement process, does not constitute a call for competition and does not commit NHS Wales to any future procurement. However, information gathered through this engagement will help inform the development, scope and future direction of the project. Suppliers can express their interest in this process and request a copy of the Market Engagement Briefing Document, which contains further details on the requirement and engagement process, by contacting Chris Squires (christopher.squires@wales.nhs.uk). When submitting an expression of interest, suppliers are requested to confirm that they acknowledge and understand that: - the proposed managed service requirement relates specifically to Oracle E-Business Suite (Oracle EBS) and does not include support for Software-as-a-Service (SaaS) solutions; - they have the necessary supply chain capabilities to support the requirements of the service; and - they possess the capability and expertise to support the development of warehouse management systems within discrete manufacturing environments. Suppliers will have the opportunity to participate in a structured engagement session which are scheduled for the 5th, 8th and 14th October. There are 10 sessions available and these will be allocated on a first come first served basis. However, NWSSP reserves the right, at its sole discretion, to make additional sessions available should there be sufficient interest from the market. No guarantee is given that additional sessions will be offered. Lot 1: . None

sig_0f4c5d5d65aa6b4c1926.description: This competition replaces the previously announced competition 2026/2237, which was cancelled 14.08.2026. The system shall contribute to strengthening situational comprehension in Norwegian sea areas by using image forming sensors (optical and SAR – Synthetic Aperture Radar). This shall enable: verification of AIS data detection of vessels that do not send AIS (so-called "dark vessels") improved situation understanding and decision support in the operative contexts The coastal system has tested the use of non-cooperative sensor data from satellites in the summer and autumn 2025 through the company Vake AS's presentation and analysis system (vake.ai.). The testing of data in Vake is based on optical and SAR sensor data from Sentinel-1 and 2 satellites in the EU's Copernicus programme and on AIS data from the Norwegian Coastal Administration. Developments in this procurement cannot be included. Tenderers shall document that the offered system was established and operative at the tender deadline. The documentation shall, at a minimum, consist of: A technical description of the offered system, including main functionality, used data sources and central analysing functions. Screen images showing central functions in the system, including visualisation of satellite data, object detection and analysis functionality. Information on the date of production of the system to the customer. Description of the system's operative use for at least one customer or final user. Documentation that substantiates actual operative operations before the tender deadline expiry, e.g. customer confirmation, operational reports, uptime reports, user statistics or equivalent. The contract will be valid for one (1) year, with an option for an extension.

sig_0f53a03dbad4c54b0407.description: The purpose of this contract is the SERVICES FOR THE ANALYSIS, DESIGN, DEVELOPMENT AND IMPLEMENTATION OF A VIRTUAL AGENT COORDINATION SYSTEM (CoVA) APPLIED TO INTERGENERATIONAL ASSISTANCE FOR THE ADMINISTRATION OF THE PRINCIPALITY OF ASTURIAS which enables a proactive and efficient administration, covering both processes and people and the technology necessary for its proper use, security and management. This contract is part of Public Procurement of Innovative Technology (CPTI), its purpose has an innovative content and employs functional specifications, rather than technical requirements: It is aimed at the acquisition of a service that does not exist in the Principality of Asturias, but can be developed in a reasonable time, given that the technology is at a degree of development that allows it to do so. The main tasks included in this contract are the following: a. Implementation of a virtual agent coordination system based on artificial intelligence applied to intergenerational assistance for the Administration of the Principality of Asturias that allows the exploitation of the data generated and managed. b. All services necessary for the commissioning of the contracted elements, necessary subscriptions/licences, as well as their management and maintenance during the pilot demonstration phase. c. The exploitation of the potential of the data of the Administration of the Principality of Asturias (hereinafter, APA) to implement new forms of public management based on interoperability and data analytics. d. Establish the technological and procedural bases for the implementation of a proactive administration that allows the optimisation of public expenditure while maximising its performance. e. The development of techniques/rules for the automated management and classification of data, documents and files using advanced Artificial Intelligence techniques. f. The incorporation of deep learning techniques since these digitalisation processes can produce immense amounts of data for training and thus be able to provide processing that increases efficiency, effectiveness and intelligence in the processing of data in the processes of Public Administrations. g. The creation of a corporate data space that includes origin data, those that may have been inferred during the scope of use of the system, as well as facilitating interoperability and administrative processing circuits. h. Creation of a proactive care and assistance environment with citizens. i. Creation of a specialised sandbox that serves as an ideation and experimentation environment. j. Integration with the APA's electronic file processing system (SITE), and other applications and systems indicated in these specifications. k. Ensuring the artificial intelligence (AI) supply chain, for which measures will be implemented to guarantee the integrity and security of the artificial intelligence models at all stages, components and data used, with strict legal compliance with EU Regulation 2024/1689, and compliance with the decree 98/2025 regulating the use of artificial intelligence in the Administration of the Principality of Asturias.

sig_0f56c5668e9676b95423.description: THIS IS NOT A CONTRACT NOTICE OR A REQUEST FOR TENDERS BUT AN INFORMATION REQUEST FOR MARKET CONSULTATION AND TECHNICAL DIALOGUE. The procurement entity HUS-yhtymä (hereinafter also referred to as the contracting authority) is using this information request to survey the market to support the planning of a potential readiness communication and alert system procurement carried out as a joint procurement (possibly on a Uusimaa regional co-operation area scale). The purpose of the information request is to survey suppliers on the market and their product and service ranges. The aim is to obtain information on, among other things, various solutions, functionalities, pricing models, and the boundary conditions for a potential joint procurement. The details of the joint procurement will be specified later as the procurement preparation progresses. Preliminary objectives of the procurement: The entity under review may consist of one or more parts. Potential use cases include, among others: - critical 2-way alerting and communication as well as video conferencing - regional communication crossing organisational boundaries - workstation messaging and operational communication - situational picture collection and reporting (collection also from actors outside the organisation) - call-outs for work and resource alerts - lone worker safety - browser-based notifications. The solution must take into account multiple communication channels (mobile, SMS, workstations), the information security and operational reliability requirements of the authorities' environment, and integration with other systems. Key themes of the market consultation: - operational reliability and usability in disruption situations - scalability of user numbers - suitability of the joint procurement model - pricing models and potential add-ons - integrations and interfaces - information security, data protection, and the location of the server infrastructure - key benefits and risks (e.g. vendor lock-in). RESPONDING TO THE INFORMATION REQUEST AND MARKET DIALOGUE We kindly ask suppliers interested in the procurement to describe the solutions you offer, taking into account the procurement objectives and themes mentioned above. If you wish, you can also attach brochures or other information about your offered products and services to your response. Please submit responses to the information request by 25.3.2026 to the address kilpailutus.ict@hus.fi. The subject line of the message should state "HUS 105-2026 - Readiness communication and alert system". The contracting authority may, at its discretion, propose clarifying market dialogue discussions with those who have responded to this information request. The responses provided may be utilised in the further preparation of the procurement, potential market dialogue, and requirement definition. Please note that all material is intended solely for conducting this market dialogue. The contracting authority will treat your response confidentially. INFORMATION ON THE PROCEDURE The contracting authority is not initiating a tendering procedure by publishing the information request; instead, a potential contract notice and request for tenders will be published later. The information request does not oblige the contracting authority to carry out the actual procurement. Responding to the information request is not a prerequisite for participating in a potential subsequent tendering procedure. Suppliers will not be paid compensation for responding to the information request or participating in the market dialogue. The contracting authority tentatively plans to publish the request for tenders during the year 2026.

sig_0f683c0f3f7996dd9f88.description: The Eunice Kennedy Shriver National Institute of Child Health and Human Development (NICHD) intends to publish a Notice of Funding Opportunity (NOFO) to solicit applications for research on the impact of technology and digital media on children and adolescents. Technology and digital media (TDM) encompasses social media, applications, websites, television, motion pictures, artificial intelligence, mobile devices, computers, video games, virtual and augmented reality, and other content, networks, or platforms disseminated through the internet, broadcasted, or other media technologies, as applicable. Collectively, they have become an integral part of our children’s and families’ daily lives. Most children and adolescents now engage with TDM starting from an early age, often with high levels of exposure across multiple devices and contexts and involving a wide range of content. There is therefore an urgent need to understand how TDM use and exposure impacts children’s health and development, as well as how it alters the very nature of interactions between children and their family members, peers, and society at large. As TDM has evolved with breathtaking speed, our understanding of its impacts – whether positive, neutral, or negative – on children’s health and development has not kept pace. This initiative intends to address this expanding gap by inviting research proposals on the impact of TDM on children and adolescents, including potential broader effects on their families and communities. Please note that applications are not being solicited at this time . This notice is being provided to allow potential applicants sufficient time to develop meaningful collaborations and responsive projects. This NOFO will utilize a phased R61/R33 mechanism. Investigators with interests at the intersection of TDM and child/adolescent development are encouraged to apply. In addition, collaborative teams that combine expertise across domains such as behavioral sciences, cognition and learning, computational and statistical modeling, computer science, geographic information science, library and information sciences, neurodevelopment, pediatrics, social and affective development and social sciences will be encouraged, and these investigators should also consider applying for this opportunity.
sig_0f683c0f3f7996dd9f88.title: Notice of Intent to Publish a Funding Opportunity Announcement for Impact of Technology and Digital Media Exposure Usage on Child and Adolescent Development

sig_0f68a6f5d8c0a8a88d05.description: Asker municipality would like to invite suppliers of the geographical information system (GIS) to a dialogue. Asker municipality currently has Askerkart for executive officers and residents. Askerkart is a web-based map system, but in connection with the current system supplier having notified transition to cloud, the municipality wants to update itself on the market situation and the different possibilities that exist. The dialogue meetings will be held in Asker municipality ́s premises in the period 3.11-7. 11.2025. The GIS tool shall be able to support the municipality ́s work with knowledge based decisions. It shall be a map solution for case handling in accordance with the Planning and Building Act and other legislation, at the same time that the system should be able to give inhabitants access to relevant information from the same knowledge basis. We would like the map system to be easy to administer and it has a user friendly interface. We would like tenderers to give a general system demonstration so that we can get an understanding of whether this will fit into Asker municipality ́s ICT architecture/portfolio. We want the demo to say something about: • User administration of the system • Inhabitant services • 3D display in the system. • Analysing and reporting possibilities • data flow and possible system integrations • How the system itself is administered - what can we do ourselves Each tenderer can have up to three persons with good competence in the system. Asker municipality will provide an ICT consultant, as well as three representatives from the department Analyse og Geodata. Business sensitive information that is shared in the individual meetings will be handled confidentially. Tenderers wishing to participate can register their interest by email to elfrid.nygaard.stabellini@asker.kommune.no and at the same time state the preferred date for holding the meeting (03.11, 04.11, 05.11, 06.11 or 07.11). Any questions to the market dialogue can also be directed here and will be answered continuously. The registration deadline is 31.10.2025 Agenda for the dialogue meeting: 1. Presentation of meeting participants and cards on the municipality ́s need for a GIS tool. 2. General demo of the supplier ́s system. Documentation that shall be submitted after the dialogue meeting (deadline: 14.11.2025) 1. Presentation from the dialogue meeting. 2. Three reference customers with an equivalent system (with contact information). 3. Upper and lower price estimates for licences/subscriptions, rolling out and training per annum, including support. The estimates are not binding.

sig_0fb50bed29e9ea0eee15.description: The Trust is seeking a single strategic partner to deliver an integrated suite of corporate and professional services that enable school leaders to focus on educational outcomes while ensuring the Trust operates efficiently, safely, compliantly and sustainably. Managed ICT Services- Secure, resilient network, servers, connectivity, filtering, cyber security, helpdesk, backup and device management across both schools and the nursery. Estates Management Services - Strategic and operational facilities and estates management, statutory compliance, estates/asset/carbon strategy and H&S support. Communications, Marketing & PR - Brand and reputation management, media and PR, website and social media, prospectus and admissions materials, internal communications. Governance Support Services - Company secretarial and governance support, clerking and minutes (Convene), statutory filings and governance advice. Managed Procurement Services - Procurement advice, tendering and quotations, contracts register, supplier management and Procurement Act 2023 compliance. The full Specification, including service-level agreements, key performance indicators and technical standards for each area, is available to download via the Delta eSourcing website. All compliant tenders received by the deadline will be assessed against the Conditions of Participation, the exclusion grounds and the award criteria in this ITT, and the Contract will be awarded to the Most Advantageous Tender under section 19 of the Act. sig_10a5fd60bbf1d7997fd5.description: Die Bäder, Sport und Freizeit Salzgitter GmbH (BSF) originated from Thermalsolbad Salzgitter GmbH and Sport und Freizeit Salzgitter GmbH. BSF is a subsidiary of the City of Salzgitter and performs numerous tasks, particularly in the field of public services of general economic interest. It operates the thermal brine baths in Salzgitter-Bad with their extensive offerings, the municipal pool in Salzgitter-Lebenstedt with attractive family offerings, and the ice sports centre at Salzgittersee with various leisure offerings. In addition, BSF is the point of contact for organised sport in Salzgitter provided by the district sports association (Kreissportbund) and its numerous sports clubs, as well as the primary contact address for all queries relating to Lake Salzgitter. The contracting authority is planning the introduction of a uniform, cloud-based point of sale and administration system for its three facilities - the Thermalsolbad Salzgitter-Bad, the Stadtbad Salzgitter-Lebenstedt, and the Eissporthalle am Salzgittersee. The aim is to optimise internal working processes and create a seamless, consistent customer experience across all premises. Currently existing, disparate software systems lead to significant organisational and technical challenges. Customers cannot use products (e.g. value cards or vouchers) across different premises, and support provided by various service providers complicates administration. A uniform system with central support by a single supplier is intended to solve these challenges, standardise technical operations, and improve customer service. A solution involving multiple different systems and subsequent connection to a common back-end system is not considered expedient from a technical and economic perspective. The subject matter of the contract comprises the following partial services: a. Upgrading the access hardware and providing the point of sale hardware for the Eissporthalle Salzgittersee b. Optional: Upgrading the access hardware and providing the point of sale hardware for the Stadtbad - Salzgitter-Lebenstedt c. Optional: Delivery of new access hardware and point of sale hardware for the Thermalsolbad Salzgitter-Bad d. Provision and operation of the SaaS-based back-end solution. The introduction is to take place in phases: - Eissporthalle Salzgittersee: after the season 2025/2026 from the 2. quarter 2026. Completion by no later than 15.09.2026 (season opening of the ice sports centre is on the last weekend of September). - Stadtbad Salzgitter-Lebenstedt: expected in the 4. quarter 2026 - Thermalsolbad Salzgitter-Bad: expected from the 1. quarter 2027.
sig_10a5fd60bbf1d7997fd5.title: Cloud-based point-of-sale and management system for the Salzgittersee ice rink, the Salzgitter-Lebenstedt municipal pool, and the Salzgitter-Bad thermal brine bath

sig_114957fe11a47c6380ea.description: Nordhessischer VerkehrsVerbund (NVV) has been 1995 the pace-setter for mobility in the North Hesse region. As a management level, we combine planning, financing and quality management for buses, trams and trains in the districts of Kassel, Hersfeld-Rotenburg, Werra-Meißner, Schwalm-Eder and Waldeck-Frankenberg as well as the city of Kassel. The subject of this tender is the commissioning of an agency or a service provider for the comprehensive support and strategic further development of our social media channels. The service contract is awarded for a fixed term of 3 years with options for the client to extend twice by one further year each time. The contractor must provide the following services: 1. The core task of the service provider consists in the long-term support of the existing social media channels of NVV. This includes the continuous adaptation of content and strategies to the changing dynamics of the respective platforms in order to ensure optimal reach and interaction with the target groups. The service provider creates a monthly editorial plan that prepares relevant topics of NVV, regional events (e.g. events with combo tickets such as ski jumping in Willingen or the Kassel Kulturzelt) and product presentations in a channel-specific manner. The plans are drawn up in close coordination with NVV and can be adapted at short notice if necessary. Furthermore, the service provider is responsible for planning and carrying out cross-platform campaigns (such as competitions etc.) taking data protection into account. Another important aspect is the maintenance of cooperations with regional providers and content creators. An advent calendar for one of the platforms is to be conceived and implemented annually, including the required photo production. In the field of photography and videography, the service provider is responsible for the needs-based creation and editing of image material. This includes at least one video shoot per month on site (A-content), the creation of at least two video contents with existing material (B-content) as well as at least two moving-image contents with animations (C-content). 2. The tasks of the contractor also include the strategic further development of the social media presence of NVV. 3. Furthermore, the contractor has to fulfil the task of community management including dialogue management. For this purpose, the necessary tools for processing social media activities must be provided and compliance with the community guidelines of NVV must be ensured. A prompt response to comments, fan posts, messages and reviews within eight hours during working hours (working days 8-17 o'clock) must be ensured. 4. The success of the social media activities is measured by quarterly reports from the contractor, which contain the most important key performance indicators (KPIs) of the platforms. The service provider interprets the statistics and derives recommendations for action. In addition, an annual report is produced. 5. For the fixed contract term of 3 years, a total budget of 400.000 euros net is available. This includes an annual advertising budget of 18.000 euros for all channels.
sig_114957fe11a47c6380ea.title: Social Media

sig_12967e5c18c4f730c06a.description: SKI hereby invites tenders for a dynamic purchasing system (hereinafter the System) regarding the procurement of management consultancy services. The System includes the procurement of management consultancy services within the 6 service areas below. The content of the service areas is defined in more detail in Annex C. Subject of the System: Service area 1: Strategy and organisational development. Under this service area, services falling within one or more of the following five sub-areas may be purchased: 1. Sub-area 1: Strategy analysis 2. Sub-area 2: Strategy development 3. Sub-area 3: Strategy implementation 4. Sub-area 4: Organisational analysis and design as well as 5. Sub-area 5: Structural implementation. Service area 2: Business processes and efficiency. Under this service area, services falling within one or more of the following three sub-areas may be purchased: 1. Sub-area 1: Process analysis and process optimisation 2. Sub-area 2: Outsourcing 3. Sub-area 3: Public-private partnership (PPP). Service area 3: Analyses and evaluations. Under this service area, services falling within the following sub-area may be purchased: 1. Sub-area 1: Analyses and evaluations. Service area 4: Systems and management. Under this service area, services falling within one or more of the following three sub-areas may be purchased: 1. Sub-area 1: Finance and economic management 2. Sub-area 2: Quality and risk management 3. Sub-area 3: Control and optimisation of administrative processes. Service area 5: Human resources. Under this service area, services falling within one or more of the following three sub-areas may be purchased: 1. Sub-area 1: Leadership and employee development 2. Sub-area 2: Culture and behavioural development 3. Sub-area 3: Personnel policy. Service area 6: Green services. Under this service area, services falling within the following sub-area may be purchased: 1. Sub-area 1: Green services. The system is divided into 2 categories: • Category 1 Competence purchase • Category 2 Task purchase. Both categories concern the procurement of services, where those in category 1 are procured as hours, while those in category 2 are procured as a finished result (report, analysis, etc.). The procurement of services in both categories assumes that these are commonly used and generally available on the market at the time of procurement. The system can therefore not be used to procure services that are not generally available on the market. It is voluntary for all SKI customers, as listed in Annex B, Customer List, to make use of the system when they need to procure management consultancy services. Procurement of Competence purchase. In category 1, customers can procure management consultancy services within the 6 service areas described in Annex C, to meet the customer's competence needs. The consultancy services can be procured in the following way: Purchase of consultancy hours (number of hours x hourly rate).; Procurement of management consultancy services for task resolution. In category 2, customers can procure management consultancy services within the 6 service areas described in Annex C, to fulfil a specific task. The consultancy services can be procured in the following way: Purchase of task resolution at a fixed price.

sig_12a083211a68763a96cf.description: This market exploration serves the purpose of gathering insights for the contracting authority with the aim of preparing a planned procurement project. After completion of the market exploration, the results will be evaluated by the contracting authority and are expected to be incorporated neutrally into the tender documents of the intended award procedure. The market exploration is to be implemented as follows. Feedback from interested companies is requested by 20.04.2026 at the contact address: echtzeit@nasa.de. Step 1: To do this, please first send an email to the address: echtzeit@nasa.de, with which you declare your interest in the market exploration. With this query, please submit at least one reference intended to serve as proof that you have already implemented a similar project as a supplier in a company. The reference should contain: name of the contracting authority, specification of the implementation period, cost scope, brief description of the content. Step 2: If the required reference is available, you will then receive the URL for downloading the documents as well as the password required for this. Step 3: If there is still an interest in the market exploration, the interested parties are expected to present the offered system after viewing these documents available online. The contract documents are available in German. The procedural language is German. The feedback should include, alongside the details of NASA GmbH (technical requirements), the presentation of the product (presentation, promotional film or similar), completed questionnaire, expected cost framework (investment and ongoing), possible special features of the product, possible implementation periods to establish this product in the company, and an explanation of what steps would be necessary for this. The feedback from interested parties should be sent to echtzeit@nasa.de by 18.05.2026. In the next step, up to 5 interested parties will be invited by NASA GmbH to a virtual interview, on-site interview at NASA GmbH or an on-site interview at their company at the beginning of June. Participation is voluntary and has no connection with subsequent participation in any later award procedure. Participation is also not a prerequisite for a later commission. In a later procedure, NASA GmbH will ensure that participants in the market exploration do not have an information advantage. Any expenses incurred by the companies participating in this market exploration will generally not be reimbursed.

Technical requirements: Guarantee the integration of the AI system for radiological diagnosis support of bone and thoracic lesions with the existing corporate systems at the Ministry of Health. The Ministry currently has an artificial intelligence system orchestrator integrated into the corporate GIMD solution (Blackford), as well as an image integration engine (IDONIA). Guarantee the clinical performance measured by the sensitivity, specificity and response time of the AI system for radiological diagnosis support of bone and thoracic lesions. Ensure regulatory compliance regarding data protection, information security (National Security Framework), medical devices and Artificial Intelligence. Provide initial training and updated documentation for the clinical and technical profiles involved. Offer support for system incidents

sig_12c02ab808cda33bc30f.description: HTE is a field of chemistry that expanded exponentially in the past five years, and most pharmaceutical companies are currently using it in their workflows. This methodology allows multi-parameter optimisation of chemical reactions but also synthesis of multiple compounds (96 to 384) on a small-scale using plate chemistry. Combined with the implementation of Direct-to-Biology (D2B) approaches, which involves the direct testing of non-purified mixtures, biological data is obtained faster. The combination of these methods greatly improves the Design, Make, Test, and Analyse (DMTA) cycle. Lot 1: . The option is a cloud-based design platform, accessible via a secure web interface, offering enhanced scalability and reduced infrastructure overhead. The solution will integrate with a University of Dundee-hosted virtual machine to enable secure data exchange and computational workflows. Installation of server-side components will be managed by the DDU Data Management and Computational Chemistry teams, with network provisioning supported by DTS. Ongoing maintenance and updates will be provided by the vendor.
sig_12c02ab808cda33bc30f.title: High-Throughput Experimentation (HTE) Software for Drug Discovery

sig_13a32b2b94765d0369f0.description: I. INTRODUCTION This Special Notice announces the Department of Navy Rapid Capabilities Office (DONRCO) Disruptor Days. The purpose of this event is to provide industry access to unique Government assets (test ranges, Labs, equipment, data) to support the development of mission-critical solutions. This initiative explicitly highlights a strategic partnership between Portfolio Acquisition Executive Mission Systems (PAE MS) and Office of Naval Intelligence (ONI). PAE MS will serve as the primary evaluators, and the ONI will be actively involved throughout the planning, evaluation, and review process to ensure solutions meet rigorous operational demands. Disclaimer: This announcement does not constitute a solicitation and shall not be construed as a commitment by the Government. Responses in any form are not offers, and the Government is under no obligation to award a contract as a result of this announcement. Any submission of information is strictly voluntary. II. TOPIC DESCRIPTION Globally significant maritime chokepoints present dense, asymmetrical, and highly dynamic threat environments. To address these operational challenges, the DONRCO seeks to identify and evaluate commercial data and technologies capable of performing rapid data fusion and multi-sensor correlation to support real-time Maritime Domain Awareness (MDA). Technical Focus The Department of the Navy (DON) needs to detect, locate, identify, and track all maritime vessels. The DON needs data solutions that can follow all types of vessels, from cooperative ships that report their location (self-reporting vessels) to non-cooperative "dark targets" that try to hide their positions. Dark targets may be involved in illegal, unreported and unregulated fishing, illicit drug trafficking, illegal arms trafficking, terrorism activities, or piracy. The DON is interested in novel data sources and analytics tools that can plug into and enhance the DON’s unclassified MDA tool, called SeaVision (https://info.seavision.volpe.dot.gov/). This event will experiment with novel combinations of data and analytics tools to demonstrate improvements in analytical MDA results by showing: the direct output of vessel positions, types, and predicted tracks. For this Disruptor Day event, data provided by participants should be in GeoJSON format. Data provided to participants for analysis will also be in GeoJSON format. Innovative Industry Solutions Submissions and demonstrations will focus on the following key operational and analytical capability areas. Participants can demonstrate in one or both capability areas. 1. Novel Data Sources After registration, the DON will specify a preferred location and window of time for data collection so that different data sources can be most easily overlaid with baseline SeaVision data. Advanced Data Solutions: Participants could demonstrate novel, previously untapped information pipelines to feed MDA analytical tools. High-Granularity Insights: Participants could demonstrate precise entity resolution and deep tracking capability. Latency and Timing: Participants should provide information regarding latency of data collected as well as how often data can be collected. 2. Novel Analytics Tools Correlation Engines: Participants could demonstrate automated calculators or AI tools to rapidly identify and report hidden relationships across disparate datasets. Source Identification: Participants should include identification of all data sources used to generate analytical results (e.g., a specific Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) image, Automatic Identification (AIS) data feed, or Radio Frequency (RF) signal). Methodology Description: Participants should provide a high-level description of the analytic process or algorithms used. This information must be sufficient for the DON to understand the methodology, verify its legitimacy, and assess effectiveness during operational use. In-Scope Data Sources for Both Capability Areas New data sources and platforms must be capable of supporting the possibility of ingestion, correlation, and analysis using a standardized GeoJSON format. In addition to the following data types, vendors are encouraged to propose data sources beyond this list and/or ways to enhance these data types with additional attributes or analytics provided in GeoJSON format: Electro-Optical (EO) imagery and intelligence data, Infrared (IR) data and thermal imaging feeds and RF data, including signal emissions, intercept feeds, and spectrum analysis tools. SAR imagery and processing tools. Commodities Data (e.g., cargo manifests, shipping declarations, port-of-origin records, global trade statistics). Other Data (social media, acoustics, etc.) III. EVENT DETAILS The Disruptor Days event will occur starting the Week of November 30, 2026 (with a planned 2-week testing window) at NIWC Pacific in San Diego, CA. The event will take place in a specialized laboratory environment that allows vendors to brief their products in a traditional industry day format and execute live analytical evaluations. The DON anticipates using Limited Purpose Cooperative Research and Development Agreements (LP-CRADAs) to support this effort. More detailed information to follow. Following the event, selected vendors will receive structured feedback and scoring performance summaries from the Government evaluation panel. IV. REGISTRATION To Register for the Maritime Domain Awareness Disruptor Days, interested vendors should submit their information here: https://forms.osi.apps.mil/r/PaVKy9YV3S Additionally, DONRCO will host a virtual Q&A session prior to the event to answer vendor questions. Attending the virtual Q&A Session is optional and not required for Disruptor Day registration. Registration via the above form also serves to sign up for the Virtual Q&A session. Virtual Q&A session will be held: 1300 EDT, Wednesday, September 30, 2026 Sign-up Deadline for the Virtual Q&A session: 1200 EDT, on September 29, 2026 Pre-registration is REQUIRED for both the virtual Q&A and the Disruptor Days event. No walk-ins will be permitted. A downs selection will occur depending on interest due to limitations of space and time constraints. Additional information will be required prior to final event registration. V. SIGNIFICANT DATES AND TIMES Event / Milestone Date & Time Special Notice Announcement Released 18 September 2026 Virtual Pre-Event Q&A Sign-Up Deadline 1200 EDT on 30 September 2026 Virtual Pre-Event Q&A Session 1300 EDT on 1 October 2026 Final Survey Submission Closes 1600 EDT on 9 October 2026 Attendance & Invitation Approvals Sent 16 October 2026 Technical Q&A Session (Data Sharing & Setup) 21 October 2026 Disruptor Week Event Begins (NIWC Pacific, San Diego, CA) Week of 30 November 2026 (2-Week Duration) Disruptor Day Distinguished Visitor Day (NIWC Pacific, San Diego, CA) 10 December 2026 VIII. POINTS OF CONTACT Any questions regarding this announcement, data integration requirements, or event logistics should be submitted via email to: DisruptorDay@us.navy.mil

sig_13f9daed6ed6129e1bbd.description: ESPO is a public sector-owned professional buying organisation offering a comprehensive range of procurement services, including access to over 100 free-to-access framework solutions for the wider public sector. We are establishing a framework to cover the provision document management solutions including digitisation, off-site storage, and confidential shredding of documents. The Framework is divided into 7 lots. Please refer to the tender documents for any further details (including further details on each of the lots) - the closing date for submission of Tenders is 12:00 (12 noon / 12pm) on 12 October 2026. To tender (please proceed to step (e) if an expression of interest has already been completed): (a) Go to https://www.eastmidstenders.org/ (b) Register (if not already registered on ProContract e.g., via https://procontract.due-north.com/Register); (c) Search for tender opportunity 390_27 (via "View Opportunities" from the EastMidsTenders Portal, or alternatively via searching on https://procontract.due-north.com/Opportunities/Index); (d) Express an interest; (e) Download the tender documents (from the ProContract Activity summary screen). Any questions or clarifications relating to this tender opportunity should be submitted to ESPO as a message on the eProcurement Portal, once an Expression of interest has been completed. Lot 1: Electronic Document Scanning and Software. This Lot requires Suppliers to provide a full end-to-end scanning solution including preparation, scanning, indexing, encryption, electronic storage, transportation and secure disposal of documents. To include the supply, implementation and maintenance of EDRM (Electronic Document & Records Management Software), associated Project management and training. Lot 2: Document Storage and Retrieval Services. This Lot requires Suppliers to provide preparation, collection, storage, retrieval and the secure disposal of documents plus any associated services. Lot 3: Total Document Management Solution. This Lot requires Suppliers to provide a full end-to end solution for all scanning, storage and consultancy requirements. This includes scanning, indexing, encryption, electronic storage, transportation and secure disposal of documents, storage, retrieval and associated training. Suppliers will also be required to provide a consultancy Service designed to scope and shape a full document management solution to help customers manage all their documents. Lot 4: Enhanced Handling and Security Requirements. This Lot requires Suppliers to provide enhanced safe and secure document management solutions for all scanning, storage and consultancy requirements. This includes secure handling of documents, scanning, indexing, encryption, electronic storage, transportation and secure disposal of documents, storage, retrieval and associated and training. Lot 5: Confidential On-Site Shredding. This Lot requires suppliers to provide on-site confidential shredding services. Lot 6: Confidential Off-Site Shredding. This Lot requires suppliers to provide off-site confidential shredding services. Lot 7: On-Site and Off-Site High Security Shredding to NPSA Standards. This Lot requires suppliers to provide high security shredding services to NPSA standards.

The section of county road DJ 792C km 77+626 – 81+228 is classified as a road with a cobbled road surfacing and is in a poor technical condition. The road section exhibits degradations specific to cobbled roads in an advanced stage of wear, namely: disintegration and loss of stone material from the running layer; appearance of ruts and longitudinal and transverse unevenness; surfaces with local settlements and deformations; potholes and areas with water accumulations; degradation of verges; silting up or absence of rainwater drainage systems; pronounced dust generation during dry periods and mud formation during periods of precipitation; depletion of bearing capacity and of the uniformity of the running surface. The existing technical condition significantly affects traffic conditions and road safety, leading to:  reduction in travel speed;  increase in journey times;  discomfort for road users;  increase in motor vehicle operating costs;  difficulties in traffic flow under adverse weather conditions;  impairment of road connectivity to the Romanian-Hungarian border area. Considering the above, it is necessary to modernise the county road DJ 792C km 77+626 – 81+228 Dorobanți – RO/HU Border, following the drawing up of technical documentation: update of DALI+PT+DE+CS, DTAC, documentation for obtaining approvals and verification of the project. General objective: as a result of the implementation of the county road modernisation investment, which will be carried out in accordance with DALI+PT+DE+CS, the following will be facilitated:  development of regional and cross-border connectivity;  stimulation of the economic and social development of the area;  facilitation of access to the border crossing point with Hungary by ensuring optimal traffic conditions and increasing the operational lifespan of the road infrastructure;  rapid transport of residents. The specific objective is the provision of design services and technical assistance from the designer for the DALI+PT+DE+CS, DTAC phase, documentation for obtaining the Urbanism Certificate, approvals, verification of the project for the investment ''Modernisation of DJ 792C km 77+626 – 81+228 Dorobanți – RO/HU Border”. The existing technical condition significantly affects traffic conditions and road safety, leading to:  reduction in travel speed;  increase in journey times;  discomfort for road users;  increase in motor vehicle operating costs;  difficulties in traffic flow under adverse weather conditions;  impairment of road connectivity to the Romanian-Hungarian border area. Considering the above, it is necessary to modernise the county road DJ 792C km 77+626 – 81+228 Dorobanți – RO/HU Border, following the drawing up of technical documentation: update of DALI+PT+DE+CS, DTAC, documentation for obtaining approvals and verification of the project. General objective: as a result of the implementation of the county road modernisation investment, which will be carried out in accordance with DALI+PT+DE+CS, the following will be facilitated:  development of regional and cross-border connectivity;  stimulation of the economic and social development of the area;  facilitation of access to the border crossing point with Hungary by ensuring optimal traffic conditions and increasing the operational lifespan of the road infrastructure;  rapid transport of residents. The specific objective is the provision of design services and technical assistance from the designer for the DALI+PT+DE+CS, DTAC phase, documentation for obtaining the Urbanism Certificate, approvals, verification of the project for the investment ''Modernisation of DJ 792C km 77+626 – 81+228 Dorobanți – RO/HU Border” and involves the following stages: 1. Stage 1 - production of the technical-economic documentation for the DALI phase, including the drawing up and submission of the documentation for obtaining the Urbanism Certificate, the approvals requested through the UC, the drawing up of studies regarding land occupation, namely expropriation, for the Modernisation of DJ 792C km 77+626 – 81+228 Dorobanți – RO/HU Border objective; 2.

Stage 2 - production of the technical-economic documentation for the PT+DE+CS+DTAC phase, the documentation for obtaining the ISC agreement and the verification of the technical project, namely the drawing up of technical projects for utility relocation/protection, if applicable, for the Modernisation of DJ 792C km 77+626 – 81+228 Dorobanți – RO/HU Border objective; 3. Stage 3 - provision of technical assistance during the execution period of the works, participation in the reception upon completion of works and in the drawing up of the Technical Book of the Construction for the Modernisation of DJ 792C km 77+626 – 81+228 Dorobanți – RO/HU Border objective. “In accordance with the provisions of art. 160 para. The Contracting Authority reserves the right to make contract modifications, in accordance with the provisions of art. 221 of Law no. 98/2016, with subsequent amendments and completions.”

sig_14fcd19448edc9fd42e2.description: This Challenge notice is issued under the Innovation for Defence Excellence and Security (IDEaS) Program Call for Proposals (CFP) Call 006 (W7714-248676/A). Solicitation Documents reference: See bidding details section. *For additional general information on the IDEaS Program, visit: https://www.canada.ca/en/department-national-defence/programs/defence-ideas.html _____________ This challenge is open to receive proposals for Component 1a, Component 1b and Component 2. Proposed solutions that fall within technology readiness levels (TRL) 1-9 can be submitted to this challenge. Steps to apply: Step 1: read this challenge Step 2: read the Call for Proposals : See bidding details section Step 3: propose your solution here : https://defence-innovation-portal.my.site.com/ _____________ Maximum Funding and Performance Period Multiple contracts could result from this Challenge. The individual maximum contract funding available under Component 1a (TRL 1-3) is up to $250,000 CAD (excluding applicable taxes) for a maximum performance period of up to 6 months. The maximum individual contract funding available under Component 1b (TRL 4-5) is up to $1,500,000 CAD (excluding applicable taxes) for a maximum performance period of 12 months. The maximum individual contract funding available under Component 2 (TRL 6-9) is up to $5,000,000 CAD (excluding applicable taxes). The period of performance will be determined at the time of contract negotiation. The maximum individual contractual funding and the maximum performance period offered under Component 3 will be determined by Canada at the time of contract negotiation. This disclosure is made in good faith and does not commit Canada to contract for the total approximate funding. _____________ Challenge Details Challenge Title: W7714-248676/017 - RF Data Fusion for Command and Control The Department of National Defence (DND) and the Canadian Armed Forces (CAF) are seeking innovative software-based solutions to seamlessly convert, analyze, and fuse real-time, domain-specific, content-rich data transmitted over radio frequency (RF) bearers into a secure, standardized pan-domain Command and Control (C2) format to enhance interoperability and enable timely, data-driven decision-making across all domains and levels of command. Background and context Radio frequency (RF) communications in military operations are inherently bandwidth-constrained and vulnerable to jamming, interference, and environmental effects, making them unreliable in contested environments. To maintain timely and effective support across all warfighting domains, data transmitted over RF bearers should be transformed into compact, structured messages, such as eXtensible Markup Language (XML)-based Message Text Formats (MTF) or other machine-readable schemas. Such messages should be optimized for transmission over tactical networks including Low Frequency (LF), Very Low Frequency (VLF), High Frequency (HF), Ultra High Frequency (UHF), and Satellite Communications (SATCOM). This approach enables resilient, standards-based communication across domains (land, air, maritime, cyber, and space) and functional services (e.g., Joint Intelligence Surveillance and Reconnaissance (JISR), medical, logistics), in line with doctrinal requirements for pan-domain operations. CAF tactical messaging remains largely dependent on legacy systems. These systems are inflexible, poorly suited to machine-to-machine exchange, and increasingly misaligned with NATO’s shift toward XML-based, data-centric frameworks. CAF operators currently lack integrated, machine-readable messaging systems. As a result, they must manually convert voice, chat, and text inputs into formal military products including orders, situation reports, and Requests for Information (RFIs) to comply with command structures and coalition standards. Modern, pan-domain operations require that doctrinal and technical Information Exchange Requirements (IERs) be met at the speed of operational relevance, with messaging that is interoperable, standardized, and capable of supporting real-time, data-driven decision-making in joint and coalition environments. As NATO, the U.S. Department of Defense, and other Five Eyes partners adopt XML-based, machine-readable messaging frameworks, the CAF is prioritizing alignment with these emerging data models to improve interoperability, operational agility, and mission effectiveness. The DND/CAF are seeking innovative, interoperable, and scalable solutions that will contribute to the development of a next-generation digital military RF messaging and data exchange. Innovators are invited to propose technologies, platforms, or integrated systems. Essential Outcomes The proposed solution must: • Be a software-based capability (e.g., standalone application, plug-in, middleware, or service). • Support DND/CAF operations across all domains (land, air, maritime, space, cyber) and functional services (e.g., C2, intelligence, logistics). • Implement structured, standards-compliant messaging (e.g., MTF-XML) and data exchange protocols (e.g., National Information Exchange Model (NIEM), NATO Core Data Framework (NCDF)), with documented interfaces for importing, exporting, and exchanging data using those standards. • Be configurable and modular, supporting Character-Oriented Information Exchange (COIE) processing and designed for future extensibility (e.g., to accommodate emerging or disruptive standards). • Provide documented interfaces and standards-based data exchange mechanisms to support system integration, including use within experimentation, simulation, and wargaming environments. Desired Outcomes The proposed solution should include capabilities such as, but not limited to, the following: • Operability in Denied, Degraded, Intermittent, and Low Bandwidth (DDIL) environments, with scalability to support evolving mission requirements and force structures. • Enhanced user experience features such as intuitive interfaces, multilingual support, automation of routine workflows, and built-in decision aids. • Standardized, documented integration interfaces (e.g., application programming interfaces (APIs)) to enable integration with at least one Service Management or Service Monitoring tools or platforms (e.g., ServiceNow, Splunk, Dynatrace, Microsoft System Center, Azure Monitor, etc.). • Readiness for future integration of Artificial Intelligence (AI)/Machine Learning (ML) capabilities to support data fusion, intelligent message prioritization, and real-time decision support.

The contracting authority intends to introduce enterprise-wide uniform, legally compliant and digital records management (e-file). The aim of this market consultation is to gain an overview of available solutions as well as established professional, technical and organisational implementation approaches. In particular, insights are to be gained into: - suitable solution architectures and implementation approaches - integration options into the existing system landscape - requirements for operation, support and governance - automation and AI functionalities - licence, operating and cost models - scalability and future-proofing of the solutions - procedural models for introduction, migration and rollout - experiences from comparable organisations, particularly in the public environment and among KRITIS operators 1. Initial situation The contracting authority currently has a heterogeneous system and information landscape with different storage locations, applications and forms of documentation. Information and documents are stored, among other things, in Microsoft 365 applications (e.g. Outlook, Teams and SharePoint), various document management systems, SAP applications and local storage structures. As an operator of Critical Infrastructures (KRITIS), the contracting authority is subject to special requirements regarding information security, compliance, traceability and the long-term availability of information. The aim is to introduce central and standardised digital records management. 2. Target vision (functional requirements) We are looking for a solution that supports the following requirements in particular: - Central management and provision of files, documents and information - Role- and permission-based access control - Mapping of filing plans, metadata and retention rules - Audit-proof documentation and traceability - Integration of relevant enterprise applications and specialist procedures - Support for automated filing, search and research functions - Scalability for enterprise-wide deployment The contracting authority is expressly interested in different solution approaches and technological implementation options. 3. Operation and support requirements In addition to the provision of the solution, support services for the operation and further development of digital records management are expected. The future solution is to be operated as a cloud-based service (SaaS). In particular, the contracting authority shall assume the professional management, governance and user and role management. The technical operation of the solution shall be provided by the vendor. Support is expected in the following areas in particular: - Maintenance and further development of the solution - Technical support and error analysis - Implementation of updates and release changes - Support for configurations and system adjustments - Support for operations, performance and interface management - Training and qualification offers for administrators and users Solutions with an established cloud operating model, transparent support services and clearly defined service level agreements (SLAs) are sought. 4. Questions for the market The contracting authority asks interested companies for feedback on the following points: Solution & architecture - What solution approaches do you offer for the introduction of digital records management? - How are file structures, metadata, retention periods and archiving mapped in your solution? - What integration options exist with Microsoft 365, SAP and other enterprise applications? - What automation and AI functions are available? Operation & organisation - How is user, role and permission management carried out? - How are traceability, audit-proofness and audibility ensured? - What governance and compliance functions does your solution offer? - What operating and support models do you offer (e.g. SaaS, on-premises or hybrid)? - What experience do you have regarding the operational effort before and after the introduction of your solution? Scaling & costs - How does your solution scale in terms of user numbers, file volumes and organisational units? - What licence and pricing models are used? - Is the solution multi-tenant capable? - What essential cost and effort factors must be taken into account? Introduction & implementation - How is the introduction of your solution typically carried out (e.g. project procedure and phased model)? - What timeframe can be expected from experience for the introduction of digital records management? - What success factors and typical challenges should be taken into account on the customer side? - What experience do you have in introducing comparable solutions in public sector companies or operators of critical infrastructures? The contracting authority is initially interested in the submission of company documents, presentations or comparable documents with which the above-mentioned questions are answered. On the basis of the incoming feedback, the contracting authority reserves the right to hold in-depth discussions as well as presentation or demonstration appointments with selected companies. sig_16216e6067c6b0f1fedb.description: The Canada Deposit Insurance Corporation (“CDIC”) has a requirement to establish a contract for application maintenance and development services. CDIC maintains a suite of tools and applications that collectively support operations during an Intervention or in the unlikely event of a Member Institution ("MI") failure. Due to the nature of CDIC’s business, much of CDIC’s mandate application functionality is only leveraged during elevated preparedness activities on higher risk MIs, an Intervention or a Simulation. However, it is within CDIC’s mandate to ensure they are ready to support an Intervention or Simulation at any point in time. During elevated preparedness activities, an Intervention or Simulation, the primary application that is used is ROADMAP, which integrates with other applications. CDIC is looking to establish a multi-year Agreement with a single, qualified supplier to provide application maintenance and development services to support CDIC’s mandate application as further described in this RFP. The term of any resulting agreement will be for an initial term of three (3) years with up to five (5) consecutive option periods of one (1) year, which if exercised, may be exercised individually or multiple at a time, at CDIC’s sole discretion. This procurement is subject to the Policy on Prioritizing Canadian Suppliers and Canadian Content in Strategic Federal Procurement and includes clauses that prioritizes Canadian Suppliers and Canadian Value-Added Content. This includes eligibility provisions, evaluation methodology and related compliance obligations. This means that only Canadian Suppliers, or Suppliers of an applicable trading partner, as defined in the Statement of Work, are eligible to submit proposals as part of this procurement. Any proposals submitted by non-Canadian Suppliers or a supplier of a non-trading partner will be rejected, as non-Canadian Suppliers and suppliers of a non-trading partner are not eligible to compete or be awarded a contract, pursuant to Section 5.2.1 of the Policy on Prioritizing Canadian Suppliers and Canadian Content in Strategic Federal Procurement. Addendum No.1, Addendum No.2, and Addendum No.3.
sig_16216e6067c6b0f1fedb.title: Application Maintenance and Development Services

sig_16964a072bf6f2732818.description: INVITATION TO MARKERT DIALOGUE With this RFI Yle invites interested suppliers to participate in the market dialogue held prior publishing the call for tenders (RFQ or RFP). In this RFI, Yle is looking to identify the solutions available in the market that could meet Yle’s needs. In the RFI process, Yle may schedule meetings with a few chosen suppliers. Yle is preparing a public procurement concerning a solution for media management, archiving, preservation and security. SHORT DESCRIPTION OF THE PROCUREMENT The planned procurement concerns a comprehensive solution for: * Long-term Preservation: Archiving and preserving media assets for the long term. * Asset Management and Security: Securely managing, storing, and enabling the retrieval of media assets. * Lifecycle and Metadata Management: Managing the content lifecycle and associated metadata. * System Integration: Seamlessly integrating with existing production and content management systems. * Data Integrity: Guaranteeing data availability, security, and compliance. You can also propose a solution that partly fits our procurement. The procurement is described in detail in the appendices of this RFI. HOW TO PARTICIPATE? Interested suppliers are invited to take part in the market dialogue by sending the response by email to tarjoukset.yle(at)yle.fi at latest by 5th of June 2026. In case you have any questions, please don’t hesitate to contact us. We look forward to your replies. We will review them as soon as they are received. Please include a description or additional appendices covering the following topics in your response: 1) Description of the solution you provide, including a description of which key features are included in your solution a. Description of the proposed solution b. Deployment models (cloud, on-premise, hybrid) c. Scalability and performance capabilities d. Metadata management and search capabilities 2) A short company presentation, including the size of the company in terms of revenue and number of employees. 3) Reference architecture view a. Integration Capabilities, APIs and integration methods 4) Experience with media production ecosystems 5) Description of your cyber security policies and continuity planning a. Data security measures (encryption, access control, auditing) b. Compliance with relevant regulations (e.g., GDPR) c. Certifications and standards 6) Delivery and Readiness a. Typical implementation timelines b. Migration approach and tooling c. Resource requirements from the customer Also we kindly ask you to answer questions in Appendix 3 Questions: Media Preservation and Processing Solution We invite an open discussion and would appreciate your vision for building a solution. Please include different alternatives, any other possibilities, or any potential risks that might interfere with our vision. Yle may invite selected suppliers to bilateral meetings during weeks 21–25/2026. We’ll thrive to send the invitations by early June 2026 at the latest. Appendices RFI, Media storage solution for archiving, preservation, and security Appendix 1 Architecture: Media Preservation and Processing Solution Appendix 2 Use cases: Media Preservation and Processing Solution Appendix 3 Questions: Media Preservation and Processing Solution
