sig_16a29305aca3aa2c1ef0.description: The DOE Office of Science (SC), Office of Critical Minerals and Energy Innovation (CMEI), Office of Environmental Management (EM), Office of Nuclear Energy (NE), Office of Electricity (OE), and Hydrocarbons and Geothermal Office (HGEO) hereby announce interest in receiving applications from interdisciplinary teams addressing the Genesis Mission National Science and Technology Challenges to accelerate scientific discovery and research and development (R&D) workflows using novel artificial intelligence (AI) models and frameworks. By achieving AI advantage, these teams will advance the DOE's mission and ensure America’s security and prosperity by addressing energy, environmental, and nuclear challenges through science and technology. Teams are encouraged to leverage the extensive scientific and data resources of the DOE/National Nuclear Security Administration (NNSA), the National Laboratories, U.S. industry, and academia. The resulting AI models and workflows, if successful, may be integrated into the American Science Cloud. DOE is soliciting new FY26 Phase I small team and Phase II large team applications in the following topic areas: advanced manufacturing, biotechnology, critical materials, nuclear fission, nuclear fusion, quantum information science, semiconductors and microelectronics, discovery science, and energy (see specific focus areas in Section III Program Descriptions). In addition, this RFA will remain available to allow the recipients of FY26 Phase I awards to apply for larger team Phase II awards. In a few weeks, DOE plans to amend the RFA to clarify the LOI and application guidelines for FY26 Phase II awards. In FY27, DOE plans to amend the RFA or to issue an alternative funding opportunity to update the topic and focus areas to allow a second competition of Phase I small team applications and Phase II large team applications.
sig_16a29305aca3aa2c1ef0.title: The Genesis Mission: Transforming Science and Energy with AI

sig_16a777e75b86af434518.description: The Ministry of Defence (MOD), through the Defence AI Accelerator Task Force (TF RAID), intends to procure a secure, scalable capability to support operational planning across Defence. TF RAID exists to accelerate the responsible adoption of artificial intelligence (AI) and data-enabled capabilities in support of Defence outcomes, working with users, technical specialists and industry to identify, test and transition operationally relevant solutions. This requirement is expected to support operational planners by improving access to authorised planning information, enabling reusable machine-readable planning knowledge, orchestrating analytical services, and supporting the modelling, testing and comparison of alternative Courses of Action (COAs). The procurement will be structured as a single competition with 2 Lots: - Lot 1 will focus on planning data, knowledge and analytical orchestration services; and - Lot 2 will focus on COA testing, evaluation and adaptation services. Suppliers are invited to bid for 1 or both lots. Together, the Lots are intended to improve the speed, quality, traceability and robustness of operational planning while maintaining appropriate human oversight, governance, transparency, security and interoperability within Authority-approved environments, including those handling information up to SECRET UK EYES ONLY where required. MOD will be seeking to compete this requirement through the Government Commercial Agency Artificial Intelligence Dynamic Purchasing System (AI DPS/RM6200). Participation in any subsequent competition will therefore be limited to suppliers appointed to the relevant Lots of the AIDPS Framework who pass the shortlist filter exercise. Lot 1: Planning Data, Knowledge and Analytical Orchestration Services (PDKAOS). The requirement is expected to support operational planning activities through the integration of planning data, machine-readable planning knowledge and advanced analytical services. The Authority seeks a capability that improves the speed, quality and scale of operational planning whilst maintaining appropriate human oversight, governance, transparency and security. Requirement Summary: The Authority requires an initial capability to support operational planners by enabling them to: • Discover, access and exploit authorised planning information from multiple sources. • Create and maintain reusable representations of planning knowledge, expertise, assumptions, dependencies and relationships. • Assemble, configure and reuse analytical services in support of operational planning tasks. • Improve traceability between planning inputs, analytical activities and planning outputs. • Reduce dependency on fragmented information sources, manual processes and specialist knowledge bottlenecks. The capability is expected to support planning activity across multiple domains, operational functions and echelons of command rather than providing a single-purpose planning application. Lot 2: COA Testing, Evaluation and Adaptation Services for Operational Planning. The requirement is expected to support operational planning activities through the representation of operational environments, modelling of Courses of Action (COAs), evaluation of alternative scenarios and adversary responses, and generation of evidence-based insights to support planning and decision-making. The Authority seeks a capability that improves the speed, quality and robustness of operational planning whilst maintaining appropriate human oversight, governance, transparency and security. The Authority requires an initial capability to support operational planners by enabling them to: • Represent operational environments, actors, assumptions, constraints and dependencies in reusable and machine-readable forms. • Model, test and compare alternative Courses of Action. • Explore multiple operational scenarios, environmental conditions, assumptions and adversary responses. • Generate evidence-based insights to support adaptation and refinement of operational plans. • Improve traceability between planning inputs, analytical activities and planning outputs. • Reduce reliance on manual wargaming, fragmented information sources and time-intensive analytical processes. The capability is expected to support planning activity across multiple domains, operational functions and echelons of command rather than providing a single-purpose planning application.
sig_16a777e75b86af434518.title: DDAITF/013 Planning Data, Knowledge and Analytical Orchestration Services & COA Testing, Evaluation and Adaptation Services for Operational Planning

sig_176a5d3078f78a0949cf.description: The Scottish Government’s Directorate for Digital is seeking an innovative service management solution to support a growing portfolio of digital services, including ScotAccount, ScotPayments, mygov.scot, Cloud Platform Services, and more. As demand, complexity and user expectations increase, we require scalable, technology-enabled approaches that can grow as our services grow, while delivering value for money. A successful solution will help ensure resilient, secure and efficient service operations, reducing risks to service quality, productivity, revenue and public trust, while supporting the future development of Scotland’s digital public services. Lot 1: . CivTech’s mission is to drive daring and innovation in the public sector by collaboratively solving Challenges that make people’s lives better – and in doing so create generations of sustainable, high growth businesses. CivTech brings together public sector expertise and private sector innovation to solve real problems, develop new products, and deliver better, faster and easier services for everyone. Central to the approach is co-production with the citizen. Part of the Scottish Government’s Directorate for Digital, CivTech’s approach is helping transform public sector engagement with tech and innovation, delivering significant benefits to public services, producing genuine uplifts for the Scottish economy - and along the way, making lives better. Across the country there are problems public sector organisations would like to solve and in the current environment the need for smart, efficient and effective products has never been greater. The Scottish Government is aware innovation is a good way to create them and is committed to ensuring a large part of its tech spend goes to innovative businesses - whatever stage they’re at, or size they are. This is where CivTech comes in. The CivTech Innovation Flow is designed to create products as quickly and effectively as possible, and uses a true Accelerator model at the heart of its Innovation Flow model. For you – whether you’re an individual, team or company – it’s an opportunity to take on a Challenge, solve it, and win contracts with a blue-chip public sector organisation. You’ll build a product, and a business to take it as far as possible. Because here’s the kicker: the Challenges we issue aren’t ‘single organisation’ problems – most of the problems we are solving exist worldwide. In short: Open Challenges are set. Any organisation, team or individual can respond. Applications are assessed, and shortlisted proposals go into an Exploration Stage where they’re developed further together with the Challenge Sponsor and the CivTech [for which participating applicants are paid]. The best go through to the Accelerator – a period of intensive work to create the solution, and through CivTech’s unique business growth workshop system, a business capable of taking the product to the world. Please visit our website for information on CivTech and how to get involved https://www.civtech.scot/how-to-apply-civtech-12 https://www.civtech.scot/civtech-12-challenge-2-scaling-dynamically-service-management-capabilities
sig_176a5d3078f78a0949cf.title: Civtech 12 - Challenge 12.2 - How can technology enable fast-growing digital public service providers to dynamically scale their service management capabilities as demand, complexity and customer expectations increase?

sig_1800193b1f4f616c40fd.description: The object of this procurement is the acquisition of specialised retro-digitisation services for documents belonging to the physical archive held by the General Directorate of Local Taxes and Fees Sector 3, for an estimated volume of 10.000 linear metres of archive. The requested services aim to convert documents from physical to digital format, as well as ensuring their archival and technical compliance, with a view to implementing an efficient electronic document management system that ensures rapid, secure and legal access to the stored information. The services that are the subject of the procurement include, but are not limited to, the following activities: - collection, handling and organisation of the physical documents existing in the institution's archive; - scanning of documents at technical parameters that ensure the legibility, integrity and fidelity of the digital reproduction; - indexing and association of metadata related to each document or file, in order to facilitate the rapid identification and retrieval of information; - structured organisation of digital documents, so that they can be integrated into existing electronic document management information systems; - quality verification of images and indexing accuracy, to ensure a high level of precision and compliance; - handover of physical documents, together with the resulting digital archive. The final result of the contract will consist of: - digitised and indexed documents, organised in a logical and coherent structure; - an organised and easily accessible archival fund, which allows for the rapid retrieval of documents and their integration into the institution's electronic workflows. By carrying out this procurement, the aim is to create a structural and digitised archive, which ensures transparency, information security, operational efficiency and compliance with the applicable legal regulations in the field of archives and document management. Through the procurement of specialised consultancy services for project management, the necessary framework will be ensured for the efficient implementation of the project "Consolidation and rehabilitation of the Dumbrăveni Chronic Psychiatric Hospital, Vrancea County", in compliance with the obligations assumed through the financing contract, the requirements of the financier and the applicable legislation. The consultancy services will aim to support the beneficiary in the general coordination of the project, monitoring physical and financial progress, tracking compliance with assumed deadlines, managing documents related to implementation, supporting the procurement process, monitoring contracts, verifying that expenses fall within the approved budget, as well as drafting the documentation and reports requested by the financier. Proper implementation of the project requires permanent monitoring of the degree of completion of activities, assumed indicators and proposed results, as well as the identification and management of any risks that may arise during the project. In this context, the experience and skills of an economic operator specialised in the management of projects with non-reimbursable financing represent an important element for ensuring efficient and compliant implementation. Thus, to achieve this objective, the bidder declared the winner of the award procedure will ensure at least the following categories of services: - Assistance and support for monitoring the financing contract and the attached documents, for compliance with the assumed terms and conditions; - Assistance in monitoring public procurement contracts concluded within the project; - Management of the MySMIS2021 platform dedicated to project implementation; - Assistance in the creation and monitoring of cash flow throughout the project implementation period; - Drafting and documentation of pre-financing/payment/reimbursement requests; - Assistance in the relationship between the contracting authority and the REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT AGENCY FOR THE SOUTH-EAST DEVELOPMENT REGION (ADR SE), in its capacity as Management Authority for the South-East Regional Programme 2021-2027, during project implementation; - assistance in monitoring compliance with the rules regarding the visibility of the European Union, in accordance with the visual identity manual applicable to the South-East Regional Programme 2021-2027; - drafting of activity reports, as well as those established by the application and the financing contract. Further details can be found in the Specifications. The number of days by which clarifications can be requested before the deadline for the submission of tenders is 20 days. The Contracting Authority will respond only once to requests for clarification on the 11 day before the deadline for the submission of tenders. The object of the contract to be awarded through this public procurement procedure consists of the purchase of consultancy services for the implementation of the project "Consolidation and rehabilitation of the Dumbrăveni Chronic Psychiatric Hospital, Vrancea County". The consultancy services will aim to support the beneficiary in the general coordination of the project, monitoring physical and financial progress, tracking compliance with assumed deadlines, managing documents related to implementation, supporting the procurement process, monitoring contracts, verifying that expenses fall within the approved budget, as well as drafting the documentation and reports requested by the financier. Proper implementation of the project requires permanent monitoring of the degree of completion of activities, assumed indicators and proposed results, as well as the identification and management of any risks that may arise during the project. In this context, the experience and skills of an economic operator specialised in the management of projects with non-reimbursable financing represent an important element for ensuring efficient and compliant implementation. Thus, to achieve this objective, the bidder declared the winner of the award procedure will ensure at least the following categories of services: - Assistance and support for monitoring the financing contract and the attached documents, for compliance with the assumed terms and conditions; - Assistance in monitoring public procurement contracts concluded within the project; - Management of the MySMIS2021 platform dedicated to project implementation; - Assistance in the creation and monitoring of cash flow throughout the project implementation period; - Drafting and documentation of pre-financing/payment/reimbursement requests; - Assistance in the relationship between the contracting authority and the REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT AGENCY FOR THE SOUTH-EAST DEVELOPMENT REGION (ADR SE), in its capacity as Management Authority for the South-East Regional Programme 2021-2027, during project implementation; - assistance in monitoring compliance with the rules regarding the visibility of the European Union, in accordance with the visual identity manual applicable to the South-East Regional Programme 2021-2027; - drafting of activity reports, as well as those established by the application and the financing contract. The main benefits resulting from meeting the need are: • ensuring efficient coordination of all project activities and integrated implementation of technical, financial and administrative components; • increasing the contracting authority's capacity to manage the investment by supporting the implementation team with specialised expertise; • permanent monitoring of project progress and early identification of potential risks, delays or non-conformities; • ensuring that activities fall within the implementation schedule and the approved budget;

• supporting the beneficiary in carrying out the procedures, documentation and reporting requested by the financier; • reducing the risk of financial corrections or ineligible expenses as a result of non-compliance with the rules for implementing projects financed from European funds; • ensuring good management of contractual relationships with contractors, suppliers and other participants involved in the investment; • contribution to achieving the specific objectives of the project, namely the consolidation and rehabilitation of hospital buildings, increasing user safety, improving energy efficiency and reducing the impact on the environment. By achieving these objectives, the existing deficiencies of the hospital infrastructure will be remedied, the technical condition of the buildings will be improved and adequate conditions will be created for carrying out medical activities in conditions of safety, comfort and efficiency. Meeting the identified need thus contributes to the successful completion of the investment, the efficient use of allocated funds and the achievement of the results assumed through the Financing Application.
sig_184c9288d6aa54ffb935.title: Management consultancy services for the project “Consolidation and rehabilitation of Dumbrăveni Chronic Psychiatry Hospital, Vrancea County”

sig_18505bd007cfba2ea6ae.description: Following an analysis of existing systems that revealed functional gaps related to reporting, early warning and funding tracking, the contracting authority has determined that the complexity of the Merheim campus project and the requirements of the funding providers necessitate an effective and transparent controlling and communication system. For this purpose, the contracting authority wishes to commission the implementation of an IT-supported system for construction and project controlling for the compliant and auditable management of all projects and sub-projects of the new health campus at the Merheim site, whereby transparency, traceability and early warning in particular must be ensured on all levels via system support. It must be ensured that the integration of existing systems and the connection of relevant interfaces take place smoothly. This includes the transfer and exchange of cost and financial data, the transmission of procurement information and contract award statuses, as well as the provision of structured, role-based access to relevant project data, plans and approvals for external service providers and suppliers. Furthermore, internal audit must be enabled through read-based access rights to ensure the traceability and documentation of internal audits.

Südwestrundfunk (SWR), as a public service broadcaster of the ARD, is strictly dependent on a functioning IT infrastructure to fulfil its tasks. In the age of digital communication, central elements are necessary for efficient process control in order to be able to plan, execute, and implement processes digitally, both internally and across the entire ARD. Different software solutions for network management are currently in use at Südwestrundfunk and the eligible state broadcasting corporations. The network management tool CheckMK is already in use across the board at a large number of the eligible entities and is deeply integrated into the system landscape. As part of the ARD structural reform, a holistic solution is to be established across the entire ARD. For this purpose, services for the Checkmk product are to be procured for Südwestrundfunk and other eligible state broadcasting corporations. Furthermore, the eligible entities require further services such as consulting and support in the area of network management and for the CheckMK product. Südwestrundfunk (SWR) as the contracting authority and the eligible broadcasting corporations therefore intended to procure in two lots: • Lot 1: Services for the Checkmk product incl. support • Lot 2: Development and consulting in the area of Checkmk The contracting authority (SWR) / eligible entities place the following essential requirements on the services to be provided by the contractor: Lot 1: - Contract Framework agreement for the basic term of 24 months - Delivery services Services of the Checkmk product incl. support for a limited period. - Optional additional services Extension of the framework agreement by 12 to then 36 months Extension of the framework agreement by a further 12 to a total of 48 months Advance payment guarantee Services in accordance with the requirements of the technical specifications (see contract documents and Annex 17 – Service and Price Sheet for Lot 1) The acceptance quantities for Lot 1 are shown in the procedural and contract documents, Chapter 5.6 Acceptance Quantities: Acceptance quantities Number of services in units for Checkmk incl. support: Minimum acceptance quantity: 1.000.000 units, Planned acceptance quantity: 1.400.000 units, Optional maximum acceptance quantity: 1.800.000 units Acceptance quantities Checkmk Synthetic Monitoring: Minimum acceptance quantity: 10 units, Planned acceptance quantity: 200 units, Optional maximum acceptance quantity: 500 units Acceptance quantities virtual appliances: Minimum acceptance quantity: 0 units, Planned acceptance quantity: 0 units, Optional maximum acceptance quantity: 1 units per licence scale up to 600.000 services Lot 2: - Contract Framework agreement for the basic term of 24 months - Services Consulting and support services for the Checkmk product from Lot 1 Development, migration, and integration services - Optional additional services Extension of the framework agreement by 12 to then 36 months Extension of the framework agreement by a further 12 to a total of 48 months Services in accordance with the requirements of the technical specifications (see contract documents and Annex 21 – Service and Price Sheet for Lot 2) The acceptance quantities for Lot 2 are shown in the procedural and contract documents, Chapter 6.8 Acceptance Quantities: Acceptance quantities Service in hours: Minimum acceptance quantity: 200 hours, Planned acceptance quantity: 400 hours, Optional maximum acceptance quantity: 600 hours Acceptance quantities Flat rate for incidental costs (incl. travel times) per on-site deployment: Minimum acceptance quantity: 0 hours, Planned acceptance quantity: 0 hours, Optional maximum acceptance quantity: 10 hours The start of the framework agreement for each lot is planned for 01.03.2027. In addition to the SWR as the contracting authority, the following public service broadcasting corporations as well as their subsidiaries and affiliated companies, provided that the participation of the public service broadcasting corporations is at least 50%, are involved in this framework agreement as eligible entities: • Deutschlandradio (DR) • Hessischer Rundfunk (HR) • ARD-Sternpunkt (represented by HR) • Mitteldeutscher Rundfunk (MDR) • Norddeutscher Rundfunk (NDR) • Rundfunk Berlin Brandenburg (RBB) • ARD-POC + Text (represented by RBB) • IVZ (represented by RBB) • Saarländischer Rundfunk (SR) • Südwestrundfunk (SWR) • Westdeutscher Rundfunk (WDR) Joint facilities (GSEA) for which the respective eligible entity has the lead are also eligible. The aim of the procurement procedure is to conclude one framework agreement per lot. The framework agreements will be concluded with an initial basic term of 24 months and two extension options of a further 12 months each. sig_18f8d0df9b89e8cfffab.description: SOURCES SOUGHT SYNOPSIS SIMPLIFIED ACQUISITION OF BASE ENGINEERING REQUIREMENTS (SABER) Grissom Air Reserve Base, Indiana Reference Number: FA465426RFI0003 NAICS Code: 236220 – Commercial and Institutional Building Construction Size Standard: $45.0 Million Socioeconomic Target: Competitive 8(a) / Small Business Set-Aside Determination 1.0 INTRODUCTION & PURPOSE The 434th Contracting Flight (434 CONF/PK) at Grissom Air Reserve Base (ARB), Indiana, is conducting market research to identify capable, qualified, and experienced Small Business sources—specifically SBA Certified 8(a), HUBZone, Service-Disabled Veteran-Owned (SDVOSB), and Women-Owned Small Businesses (WOSB)—capable of performing a Simplified Acquisition of Base Engineering Requirements (SABER) Indefinite-Delivery/Indefinite-Quantity (IDIQ) contract. This is a Sources Sought Synopsis for planning and market research purposes only. This is not a Request for Proposal (RFP), and no contract will be awarded directly from this posting. 2.0 PROJECT DESCRIPTION & ACQUISITION STRATEGY 2.1 Scope of Work The Grissom ARB SABER contract will provide a rapid, highly flexible vehicle to execute a broad range of multi-trade maintenance, repair, minor construction, and renovation projects on military real property. Core capabilities required include, but are not limited to: carpentry, roofing, excavation, interior/exterior electrical, plumbing, HVAC, masonry, demolition, concrete, and localized hazardous material abatement. The anticipated contract structure is a single-award IDIQ with a 5-year ordering period and a maximum ceiling of $9,000,000. The minimum order threshold will be $2,000, which will also serve as the minimum contract guarantee to be obligated at basic contract award. 2.2 Pricing Mechanism & Database Specifications To drastically accelerate procurement lead times and eliminate the heavy administrative burden on the Civil Engineering Squadron, Grissom ARB intends to utilize a streamlined, coefficient-only price evaluation model (Weighted Coefficient Formula) for source selection. The Government will not utilize a traditional "mock project" during the evaluation phase. To execute this "no mock project" model legally and defensibly under FAR Part 16 and Part 36, the Government intends to utilize the proprietary Gordian Construction Task Catalog (CTC) / eGordian estimating database, or a technically equal pre-priced unit price database. Technical Justification for Database Specification (The "Why"): Minimization of Non-Prepriced Items (NPIs): Standard commercial cost databases (such as standard flat RSMeans, e4Clicks, or adjacent cost books) typically contain only 60,000 to 85,000 generalized, national-average tasks. This limited scope leads to severe NPI "creep" (frequently exceeding 30–40% of task order values), which forces the Government into extensive, post-award, line-item negotiations and manual competitions, defeating the primary speed purpose of a SABER contract. Technical Equivalence Threshold (275,000+ Localized Tasks): To support a "no mock project" model, the database must be comprehensive enough to pre-price virtually all anticipated work. The Gordian CTC provides over 275,000+ highly detailed, client-specific line items where labor, material, and equipment costs are researched, verified, and localized specifically for the Grissom ARB, Indiana market. Prevention of Unbalanced Bidding: Standard databases require separate, manual calculations for demolition, quantity discounts, and modifiers. The Gordian CTC pre-incorporates quantity discounts and demolition costs directly into its line-item structures. This high level of granularity prevents contractors from exploitatively lowballing standard-hour coefficients and recovering margins through unpriced NPIs, after-hours markups, or modifications. Contractor-Provided Software & Overhead Absorption: To facilitate joint-scoping, the awarded contractor will be required to obtain, maintain, and fund all licensing and training fees for the JOC estimating software platform (eGordian or an approved technically equal platform) for both the contractor and a minimum of two (2) Government Civil Engineering users. All software overhead must be absorbed entirely within the contractor's bidded coefficients. 3.0 CAPABILITY STATEMENT SUBMISSION REQUIREMENTS Interested firms possessing the capabilities to perform this requirement are invited to submit a Capability Statement (not to exceed 5 pages) in PDF format. Submissions must address the following areas: 3.1 Company Profile Company Name, Address, Point of Contact (Name, Phone, Email). UEI Number, CAGE Code. Socioeconomic Status under NAICS 236220 (e.g., SBA Certified 8(a) with program graduation date, HUBZone, SDVOSB, WOSB, or Small Business). Active State of Indiana General Contractor licensing status. 3.2 Bonding Capacity Proof of bonding capability from a Treasury-listed surety (Circular 570). Minimum single-project bonding limit of $1.0 Million. Minimum aggregate bonding limit of $5.0 Million. 3.3 Technical Experience with JOC and CTC Databases CTC Database Experience: Describe your firm's experience executing federal, state, or commercial construction contracts utilizing a pre-priced unit price database (such as Gordian CTC, RSMeans Unit Price Book, or eGordian). Software Proficiency: Confirm your firm's capability to utilize, license, and maintain the eGordian software platform (or a technically equal JOC estimating system) for joint scoping and task order estimation. Relevant Past Performance: Provide up to three (3) examples of multi-trade projects performed as a prime contractor within the past three (3) years valued between $100,000 and $1,000,000. For JOC/SABER contracts, list the contract type, customer agency, ordering period, and overall bidded coefficients. 3.4 Industry Feedback on the Pricing Model If your firm utilizes a different proprietary database that you believe is technically equal to the 275,000+ line-item Gordian CTC, please provide technical documentation demonstrating that it meets or exceeds the local localization, NPI mitigation, and pre-factored quantity discount capabilities outlined in Section 2.2 of this synopsis. Confirm your willingness to bid under a competitive, coefficient-only solicitation where standard, secure, and after-hours coefficients are fixed for the life of the contract, and standard inflation adjustments are handled annually via the catalog's City Cost Index (CCI) update. 4.0 SUBMISSION INSTRUCTIONS Please submit responses electronically in PDF format via email to: Contracting Officer: Cedric Roberts, cedric.roberts@us.af.mil Disclaimer: This Sources Sought Notice is for informational purposes only. The Government is under no obligation to issue a solicitation based on this notice. All information received in response to this notice that is marked Proprietary will be handled accordingly.

The purpose of the contract is the provision of services relating to physico-chemical analyses in various environmental matrices such as: soils, sediments, water and fertilising materials. Description of the services to be performed: Analyses of pollutants and physico-chemical parameters on samples of soils, sediments, water and fertilising materials and transmission of a report detailing the analysis results. These services fall under the CPV code: 79311300-0. This is a framework agreement for services in a sector sensitive to fraud: NO. Lot(s): The contract is divided into lots. - Lot 1 : Determination of pollutants and physico-chemical parameters on soils and sediments. In accordance with Article 15 of the Law of 17 June 2016 on public procurement, this lot is reserved for social economy insertion enterprises: NO - Lot 2 : Determination of pollutants and physico-chemical parameters on groundwater, surface water or wastewater. In accordance with Article 15 of the Law of 17 June 2016 on public procurement, this lot is reserved for social economy insertion enterprises: NO - Lot 3 : Determination of pollutants and physico-chemical parameters on fertilising materials. In accordance with Article 15 of the Law of 17 June 2016 on public procurement, this lot is reserved for social economy insertion enterprises: NO You may submit an offer for several lots. You may propose discounts or improvements in the event of being awarded several lots: NO. The contracting authority reserves the right not to award one or more lots. It also reserves the right to relaunch a procurement procedure for any lot not awarded. Furthermore, the award of a lot does not entail any obligation to order on the part of the contracting authority, which reserves the right not to follow up, in whole or in part, on the needs covered by this contract. Variant(s): This contract does not include any authorised, required or free variants. You may not introduce a variant. Free variants are prohibited. Any variants that may be proposed will not be taken into account. Option(s): This contract does not include any authorised or free options. Free options are prohibited. This contract contains one or more required option(s): 'supplement linked to emergency analyses', detailed more precisely in the award criteria. You must introduce an option. If you do not introduce an option, this will result in the irregularity of your base offer. Ensure that you respect the following minimum and specific requirements: within the framework of the various analyses, the tenderer must offer the possibility of performing emergency analyses. Tranche(s): The contract is not divided into tranches. The analyses may, in particular, be carried out for soils and sediments on: 1) the PFAS listed in the technical protocol CMA/3/D in compliance with this technical protocol; 2) the leaching of PFAS in compliance with the technical protocol CMA/2/II/A.26 ; 3) the analysis on eluate of the PFAS listed in the technical protocol WAC/IV/A/025 in compliance with this technical protocol; 4) the analysis on eluate of Trifluoroacetic acid (TFA), CAS no. 76‐05‐1 in compliance with the technical protocol WAC/IV/A/026 ; 5) the pH-KCl acidity; 6) the organic matter content (by loss on ignition); 7) the particle size: 5 fractions (<2,<16,<45,<63 and<2000 μm); 8) the parameters included in Annex 1 of the Soil Decree of 01/03/2018 (with analysis of the phenol index rather than phenol). The referenced technical protocols are available via the following links: https://emis.vito.be/nl/erkende-laboratoria/bodem-en-afvalstoffen-ovam/compendium-cma https://emis.vito.be/nl/erkende-laboratoria/water/compendium-wac As these protocols may evolve during the contract, the successful tenderer must always ensure that they comply with the latest available version (list of parameters subject to change). At the time of submitting the offer, the tenderer specifies the limits of quantification for each parameter. As leaching is a pre-treatment operation, no limit of quantification is expected for this item. The results are transmitted to the ISSeP according to the formats and mode of communication set out in point 2 : Documentation. The samples are kept at the laboratory until receipt and validation of the results by the ISSeP. They are then disposed of by the laboratory. Random checks by the ISSeP of the transmitted results may be carried out on an ad hoc basis. As a required option, the tenderer must propose the performance of emergency analyses (within a period of 24 h, 48 h or 72 h) and specify, as a percentage of the price of the analysis, the amount of the corresponding applicable surcharge.; The analyses may, in particular, be carried out for groundwater, surface water or industrial wastewater on: 1) the PFAS listed in the technical protocol WAC/IV/A/025 in compliance with this technical protocol; 2) the PFAS 'FTOH and C6O4' as follows: o 2-(Perfluorohexyl)ethyl alcohol (6:2 FTOH), CAS no. 647-42-7 o 2-(Perfluorooctyl)ethanol (8:2 FTOH), CAS no. 678-39-7 o 2,2-difluoro-2-((2,2,4,5-tetrafluoro-5-(trifluoromethoxy) -1,3-dioxolan-4-yl) oxy) acetic acid (C6O4), CAS no. 1190931-41-9 3) Trifluoroacetic acid (TFA), CAS no. 76‐05‐1 in compliance with the technical protocol WAC/IV/A/026 ; 4) the parameters included in Annex 1 of the Soil Decree of 01/03/2018 (with analysis of the phenol index rather than phenol). The referenced technical protocols are available via the following link: https://emis.vito.be/nl/erkende-laboratoria/water/compendium-wac As these protocols may evolve during the contract, the successful tenderer must always ensure that they comply with the latest available version (list of parameters subject to change). At the time of submitting the offer, the tenderer specifies the limits of quantification for each parameter.

The results are transmitted to the ISSeP according to the formats and communication method set out in point 2 : Documentation. The samples are kept at the laboratory until receipt and validation of the results by the ISSeP. They are then disposed of by the laboratory. Random checks of the transmitted results by the ISSeP may be carried out on an ad hoc basis. As a required option, the tenderer must propose the performance of urgent analyses (within a period of 24 h, 48 h or 72 h) and specify, as a percentage of the analysis price, the amount of the corresponding applicable surcharge.; The analyses may, in particular, be carried out for fertilising materials on: 1) the PFAS listed in the technical protocol CMA/3/O in compliance with this technical protocol; 2) the leaching of PFAS in compliance with the technical protocol CMA/2/II/A.26; 3) the analysis on eluate of the PFAS listed in the technical protocol WAC/IV/A/025 in compliance with this technical protocol; 4) the analysis on eluate of Trifluoroacetic acid (TFA), CAS No. 76‐05‐1 in compliance with the technical protocol WAC/IV/A/026; 5) the Total Oxidizable Precursors (TOP Assay) according to the Houtz and Sedlak method; 6) the Extractable Organic Fluorine (EOF); 7) the pH-H2O acidity; 8) the organic matter content (by loss on ignition); 9) the impurity content by gravimetry (S-IV-1); 10) the parameters included in Annex 1 of the Soil Decree of 01/03/2018 (with analysis of the phenol index rather than phenol). The referenced technical protocols are available via the following links: https://emis.vito.be/nl/erkende-laboratoria/bodem-en-afvalstoffen-ovam/compendium-cma https://emis.vito.be/nl/erkende-laboratoria/water/compendium-wac https://cwea.issep.be/cwea/ As these protocols may evolve during the contract, the successful tenderer must always ensure compliance with the latest available version (list of parameters subject to change). At the time of submission of the tender, the tenderer shall specify the limits of quantification for each parameter. Note that as leaching is a pre-treatment, no limit of quantification is expected for this item. The results are transmitted to the ISSeP according to the formats and communication method set out in point 2 : Documentation. The samples are kept at the laboratory until receipt and validation of the results by the ISSeP. They are then disposed of by the laboratory. Random checks of the transmitted results by the ISSeP may be carried out on an ad hoc basis. As a required option, the tenderer must propose the performance of urgent analyses (within a period of 24 h, 48 h or 72 h) and specify, as a percentage of the analysis price, the amount of the corresponding applicable surcharge.

sig_1951d05192e6de448c03.description: CLARIFICATION: This is ONLY a market exploration procedure to determine whether and, if so, which companies can offer the service intended for procurement. This preliminary information does not serve the purposes of Section 38 of the Public Procurement Ordinance (VgV). ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- The Munich Fire Department is planning, in a lead management capacity for a nationwide joint procurement on a framework agreement basis with purchasing authorization for all operators of control centres for fire and rescue services in Germany, to tender and introduce an interface management system (≠ interface modelling system, see below) named "RESQON". RESQON is intended to make it possible to network all Integrated Control Centres (ILS) nationwide with one another and exchange data amongst each other. In addition, the system is to be used to connect external services with partly proprietary protocols to the various computer-aided dispatch systems of the respective control centre. RESQON consists of local instances at the control centres, which are to be combined into a network. This network is referred to as RESQON Mesh. Participating control centres can exchange incident data via RESQON Mesh. Within the RESQON Mesh there is a central instance, the so-called RESQON Core. RESQON Core provides external connections to standardised services such as, for example, AML and the nora emergency call app. Furthermore, connections to statutory health insurance control centres, to TPS service providers for eCall and police control centres are to be possible in the future. An elementary component of RESQON is an interface modelling system which allows various protocols and data to be transformed and, if necessary, process logic to be mapped using it. The interface modelling system is a component of every local RESQON instance. -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- PLEASE NOTE: The purpose of this market exploration is to evaluate the availability of such interface modelling systems. This is also in particular in preparation for a possible direct award - in a lead management capacity for a nationwide joint procurement on a framework agreement basis with purchasing authorization for all operators of control centres for fire and rescue services in Germany - in accordance with Section 14 Paragraph 4 No. 2 letter b) of the Public Procurement Ordinance (VgV), since the objective absence of competition for technical reasons must be demonstrated and, if necessary, proven by the contracting authority. This market exploration is therefore an essential part of the required comprehensive market analysis at European level. --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- See additionally the document "2025-11-25_Markterkundung_Schnittstellenmodellierungssystem.pdf". This can be requested from the contact point via the e-tendering system. ======================================================== PROCEDURE FOR INTERESTED COMPANIES: Interested companies that consider themselves in a position to offer a corresponding product are requested to contact the contact point by email at: info@mayburg.de (providing contact details, at least email and telephone) by no later than Thu., 08.01.2025. The LH Munich - Fire Department - will then be informed accordingly and will seek further contact for the continuation of the market exploration or the market exploration procedure.

sig_1a09837a3d46dc7fd567.description: The Norwegian Defence Materiel Agency (FMA) is the contracting authority and responsible for implementing the procurement. FMA shall ensure that the Norwegian Armed Forces and other entities in the defence sector have access to cost efficient and secure material and services in line with approved long-term plans. Internal processes are based on flexible frameworks (Scrum, SAFE), the Security Act and different industry standards for safety and ITIL for operation. DRIV consists of approx. 150 persons, most of whom are located in Oslo. Both employees and consultants staff the organisation. The consultant shall assist with test coordination for product teams, as well as follow-up of teams within logistics, for the purpose of removing obstacles and ensuring speed and flow. The consultant will work closely with the manager of Value Management Office, the solution architects and the various product teams. The role can involve cooperation with other departments and/or projects in the Norwegian Armed Forces.

sig_1a35f66b83334eac618f.description: Background Trøndelag county needs a modern and comprehensive system for electronic substance register, which can support the entity's work on health, safety and the environment. The procurement is being carried out in order to ensure easy access to updated chemical information, contribute to compliance with the current regulations and facilitate safe handling of chemical products throughout the entire organisation. The county has a compound entity with different user groups and work areas, including sixth form colleges, laboratories, operation and cleaning functions, workshops, dental health services, road operation, administration and teaching environments. This sets requirements for a system that is user friendly, accessible and suitable for both employees and pupils, while at the same time being managed in an efficient way across units and professional environments. The aim of the procurement is to establish a joint system that provides a better overview of chemicals, supports local needs and at the same time enables central management and follow-up. Tenderers must therefore understand that the system shall function in a large and varied organisation, with a need for both broad availability and appropriate administration. Description of the assignment Trøndelag county shall procure an electronic substance register that is delivered as a site license for approx. 5,000 employees and 20,000 students. The system shall cover the county ́s need for registration, disclosure and management of information on chemical products across the entity. The delivery includes a digital system with functionality for i.a. search and access to safety data sheets, an overview of chemicals, as well as support for the accompanying HSE work such as risk assessment, substitute and exposure register. The system shall be suitable for different types of users and it can be used in both teaching related and operational contexts. Furthermore, the system shall support secure and efficient access management, including log-on and user administration adapted to the county ́s established identity management. A system is requested that combines user friendliness for local units with the possibility for general administration and control across the organisation. The design of the tender Tenderers shall fill in and respond to all points in the ESPD form, requirement specifications and price form. Any documentation beyond replies directly to the requirement specification shall be uploaded as pdf files, unless otherwise specified. The following shall be completed and submitted with the tender: · Complete Annex 1 - Tender Form · Digital requirement specifications and price form with reference to any annexes. · Completed data processing agreement with annexes. · Censured version of the offer
sig_1a35f66b83334eac618f.title: Electronic substance register

sig_1a5940830d6984d0e477.description: Oulun kaupunki community and environmental services invite tenderers to a market dialogue. The market dialogue concerns the preparation of the procurement of passenger counting devices to be installed on buses in Oulu Region Transport (OSL). The aim of the request for information is to ascertain the technical solutions, cost level and feasibility available on the market. The aim of the market dialogue is to obtain information on: • the suitability of passenger counting devices for public transport use • available counting technologies • power supply and connection to vehicles' ITxPT network • data transfer solutions (vehicle network vs. own network) • remote management and administration • installation solutions and setup methods • vibration damping and other durability-related solutions • lifecycle costs Additional information This is not a procurement notice or a call for tenders, but a notice of the initiation of a market dialogue for potential industry operators and potential tenderers interested in the procurement. This invitation to a market dialogue does not request or submit tenders, but informs the market about the upcoming procurement procedure. Industry operators interested in the procurement are requested to provide comments relating to the design, implementation and practical arrangements of the passenger counting devices to be procured, so that the tender process can be carried out in the most appropriate manner possible. One joint information meeting will be held in the market dialogue between the contracting authority and the service providers. The information collected in the market dialogue will remain strictly confidential and will be used solely for the development and planning of the procurement. The market dialogue does not oblige the contracting authority to carry out the procurement in the manner described in this document, and therefore the final procurement notice and call for tenders may differ from the information presented in this invitation or in the market dialogue. Participation in the market dialogue does not bind a company to participate in the tender process, nor is it a prerequisite for participation in the actual tender process later on. Participation in the market dialogue also does not affect the tenderer's position in the actual tender process. Those who have replied and participated in the market dialogue will not be paid any compensation for their participation. The aim is to obtain views from industry operators on passenger counting devices, their requirements, installations and aspects related to the length of the contract period. MARKET DIALOGUE MEETINGS A joint market dialogue meeting will be held on 29.5.2026 at 10:00-11:00 The meeting will be held as a Teams meeting. Registration for the market dialogue meeting must be made in advance by email to tomi.paananen@ouka.fi at the latest by 20.5.2026. Preliminary programme of the market dialogue meeting: 1. Opening of the meeting: Public transport planner Tomi Paananen, Oulun kaupunki 2. Preliminary timetable and content of the procurement 3. Discussion Bilateral, confidential market dialogue meetings (1 h / meeting) will be held if necessary. Registration for bilateral meetings must also be made in advance at the same time as the joint market dialogue meeting. The exact times for each participant will be confirmed after the registration period has ended. Those participating in the market dialogue may also submit comments regarding the planned procurement package in writing after the market dialogue meeting; any comments are requested by 12.6.2026 at 14.00 so that their consideration can be considered in the preparation of the procurement procedure. The actual procurement notice and call for tenders will be published according to the preliminary plan in August 2026.
sig_1a5940830d6984d0e477.title: Invitation to market dialogue: procurement of passenger counting devices for Oulu Region Transport

sig_1a7ed3e9d28a3e919c24.description: This is not a procurement notice nor a call for tenders, but a request for information through which Etelä-Karjalan hyvinvointialue is surveying system suppliers to register for a potential tendering procedure. The wellbeing services county is responsible for social welfare, healthcare and rescue services. It is the largest employer in the region, employing approximately 6 000 professionals from various fields. Our vision is to be a pioneering community where services are accessible, the wellbeing of our population is among the best in Finland, and the occupational wellbeing of our employees is high. Our mission is to increase the health, functional capacity and security of our residents throughout their lives. Our values are “Mie turvaan”, “Mie uskallan”, “Mie vastaan” and “Mie välitän”. Strategic priorities include investing in personnel, smooth processes and the gradation of services. The realisation of these requires efficient, safe and user-friendly digital solutions. The roster planning system plays a central role in supporting the smooth flow of everyday operations, the occupational wellbeing of the staff and cost-efficiency. The purpose of the market dialogue is to obtain a comprehensive overview of the roster planning systems and related services available on the market. The information obtained can be used to assess what kinds of solutions exist on the market, what benefits they generate and how they suit the needs of the wellbeing services county. Through the market dialogue, the wellbeing services county aims to: 1. Obtain information on the market offering and various suppliers' solutions 2. Understand the functionalities and key use cases of the systems 3. Explore integration possibilities with existing systems and platforms 4. Assess the implementation of information security and data protection 5. Gain an overview of pricing models and cost structures (no individual tenders) 6. Survey delivery and service models 7. Obtain concrete examples and demos from suppliers to illustrate the suitability of the solutions for the needs of the wellbeing services county. The market dialogue is open to all suppliers that can offer systems or services falling within the scope of this solution package. The focus of the dialogue is on solutions that are already in production or available on the market. Suppliers are requested to present systems and services that are available and where the key functionalities have already been implemented. The presentation of solutions under development or merely at the concept stage is not desired on this occasion. In connection with registration, suppliers are requested to briefly describe: • what ready-made solutions and services they offer • in what kinds of environments the solutions have been deployed (example descriptions, no mandatory references) • the key features of the solution that they wish to present in the market dialogue All participants are offered equal opportunities to obtain information regarding the market dialogue. The dialogue does not bind Etelä-Karjalan hyvinvointialue to initiate a procurement, nor are procurement decisions made on the basis of it. If there is a large number of registered suppliers, the wellbeing services county may hold both a joint information session and a limited number of individual meetings. The market dialogue focuses in particular on how solutions can support the key operations of the wellbeing services county. These are not procurement requirements, but thematic areas intended as a basis for discussion and illustration: • User management and information security • Working hours and shift management • Consideration of collective agreements and local agreements • Competence, qualifications and occupational health management • Usability and multi-user support • Reporting and information-driven management • Integrations with other systems • Mobile usage and employee services • Main administration, maintenance and support services • Intelligence and automation Pricing models and lifecycle services Participating suppliers have the opportunity to illustrate their solutions also through a demo or practical example scenarios. The wellbeing services county will provide a set of questions in advance to guide the discussion and ensure that the presentations of different suppliers can be compared on an equal basis. The market dialogue will be conducted as supplier-specific meetings via remote connection (Teams). The duration of an individual meeting is approximately 60 to 90 minutes. The supplier will have the opportunity to present their solution and its key features. The wellbeing services county will also ask pre-defined questions that support the equality and comparability of the discussion. Meetings will be held on the following days: 21.10., 22.10., 27.10., 28.10. and 29.10.2025. The exact time will be agreed with the registered suppliers based on the order of registration and schedule coordination. The language of potential presentations/meetings is Finnish. Registrations are requested to be sent by 3.10.2025 at 12:00. This request for information / market survey does not request tenders to be submitted nor are tenders given in response to this request for information; it requests ONLY procurement-related information. Participating or refraining from participating in the market survey / request for information does not affect the tenderer's position in any potential tendering procedure. The market dialogue invitation does not bind the respondent (supplier) to participate in the tendering procedure, nor is responding to this notice a precondition for participating in the actual tendering procedure later. Those participating in the market survey have no right to compensation for participation. The contracting authority does not undertake to carry out the procurement in question. Decisions on launching a potential procurement process will be made after the market survey. The submitted material will be handled as confidential in accordance with section 24, subsection 1, point 20 of the Act on the Openness of Government Activities.

sig_1ab06211e4c143eb8191.description: Hereon requires external support for the migration of its SAP ERP system to S/4. The brownfield approach is to be used. This is a technical migration; potential improvements or optimisations will be carried out subsequently, decoupled from the migration. The subject matter of Lot 1 is the provision of comprehensive consultancy services for the planning, execution and documentation of the migration of the existing SAP ERP system to SAP S/4HANA. The services shall be performed in close coordination with the client's specialist departments. The contractor shall assume the following tasks: 3.1. Project planning and design - Preparation of a project schedule and content plan in close coordination with Hereon - Development of a migration concept including test design, definition of responsibilities and accompanying documentation 3.2. System analysis and process evaluation - Review of the existing SAP ERP systems with regard to the S/4HANA migration - Identification and evaluation of correction requirements in the implemented business processes - Communication of correction requirements to the specialist departments and verification of implementation 3.3. Archiving and system preparation - Archiving of FI and MM documents from completed financial years 2014-2019 - Setup of a sandbox system - Execution of necessary system copies from production to test systems 3.4. Migration and customising - Execution of the necessary customising - Execution and testing of the S/4HANA migration on sandbox, test and production systems - Review and adjustment of structural authorisations in connection with the Cross-Application Time Sheet (CATS) - Analysis of existing roles and authorisations in the SAP ERP system as well as evaluation and application of new authorisation objects in the context of S/4HANA - Execution of the H4S4 conversion - Review and migration of the personnel cost commitment processor, ensuring functionality and data integrity in personnel cost planning - Connection of the SAP Enterprise Portal and support for the connection of the above-mentioned non-SAP products 3.5. Documentation and quality assurance - Preparation of audit-compliant final documentation of the migration - Support in the review of non-SAP software - Support during an internal security check (SAP Basis) 3.6. Training and hypercare - Preparation of (delta) training materials - Conducting training sessions for participating employees and key users - Provision of live support (hypercare) after the migration 3.7. Cooperation with the client - All services shall be provided in close coordination with the responsible specialist departments - Tasks that can sensibly be carried out by Hereon itself (e.g. non-SAP software, authorisation roles) shall be processed internally accordingly 3.8. Period and scope - The consultancy service is to be provided over a period from early 2026 to mid-2027.; As part of an ongoing SAP migration project, an external service provider is commissioned with Lot 2 to technically accompany and evaluate the project phases of concept review, test preparation and test execution as well as the final documentation. The objective is quality assurance and risk minimisation in the migration process, as well as ensuring audit-compliant documentation. The contract specifically comprises the following services: 4.1. Review of the migration concept - Analysis of the migration concept for completeness, consistency and feasibility - with a particular focus on ensuring that the planned documentation meets the requirements of an audit - Identification of potential risks and vulnerabilities, particularly with regard to the traceability and audibility of the migration steps - Preparation of an evaluation with recommended actions to ensure audit-compliant documentation 4.2. Support for test preparation and test execution - Advice on the planning and organisation of test activities (e.g. system, integration and acceptance tests) - Support in the definition of test cases and test data so that traceability and audibility for an audit are guaranteed at all times - Quality assurance during test execution with a particular focus on complete and audit-compliant logging - Evaluation of test results and derivation of measures 4.3. Review of the final documentation - Evaluation of project documentation regarding traceability, completeness and conformity with project objectives - Support in the preparation of handover documents so that all necessary evidence for a subsequent audit is available 4.4. Conditions of participation - Demonstrable experience in supporting SAP migration projects - Specialist knowledge of SAP ERP and SAP S/4HANA - Experience in test management and quality assurance - Knowledge of standard project management and IT service management standards (e.g. PRINCE2, ITIL) 4.5. Period and scope The consultancy service is to be provided alongside the project over a period from early 2026 to mid-2027. The exact scope will be agreed upon when the contract is awarded.

sig_1b0f9e55c5675486433d.description: Universitatea din Oradea has signed the financing contract for the project 'Modernisation of educational spaces at Universitatea din Oradea – Building C', call code PRNV/2023/623/1, Contract no. 459/24.12.2025, SMIS code 305032. Thus, a public procurement is required for Consultancy and supervision services and technical assistance services from the designer for the objective 'Modernisation of educational spaces at Universitatea din Oradea – Building C'. The infrastructure that is the subject of the project, Building C – block C7 – Campus A (heritage building), does not meet all the building performance requirements imposed by the legislation in force – Law 10 – Quality in Construction: safety in operation – including accessibility for persons with disabilities, hygiene and environmental protection, thermal insulation and energy economy (however, as they are heritage buildings, they are treated as such), durability and sustainability, nor the European quality standards for teaching and research-innovation activity. Currently, the targeted building (Building C – block C 7 – Campus A) is vulnerable to water action, with infiltrations in the roof area and their basement, the roofs being partially degraded and, at the same time, there are no watertight pavements, waterproofing elements at their lower part and an efficient rainwater collection network. From the point of view of seismic vulnerability, the building that is the subject of the project does not correspond in terms of design to the CR6/2013 code and the P 100/2006/2013/2019 code, being made of unreinforced load-bearing masonry, not seismically compliant, dating from 1913, so they cannot be classified in Seismic Risk Class Rs IV, which includes constructions where the expected seismic response is similar to that obtained for constructions designed based on the regulations in force. According to the Technical Project, the building is classified in Seismic Risk Class Rs III, which includes constructions that, under the effect of the design earthquake, may present structural degradation that does not significantly affect structural safety, but where non-structural degradation may be significant. For the targeted building, the following are required: rehabilitation and modification of the roof, sealing the construction against water infiltrations in the roof area and in the basement area; thermal insulation of the top floor slab; modernisation of the electrical installation as well as the emergency lighting circuit; modernisation of the heating installation; restoration of the building's exterior finishes, and in some places the interior ones, these being degraded/morally and physically worn out; replacement of existing joinery with new ones, made of wood, suitable for heritage buildings, respecting its initial design, with additional thermal insulation; making the building accessible for persons with disabilities by equipping it with a lifting platform and arranging a sanitary group for persons with locomotor disabilities. This documentation establishes the contracting conditions for: - Lot 1 – Technical assistance services from the designer according to the separate terms of reference during the execution period of the works according to the provisions of Law no. l0/1995 on quality in construction, republished, with subsequent amendments and additions - Lot 2 – Consultancy and Supervision services related to the proper monitoring of the Contractor's compliance with the provisions of Government Decision no. 1/2018 for the approval of general and specific conditions for certain categories of procurement contracts, related to investment objectives financed from public funds. The Contractor shall ensure the technical and financial management of the project and the execution of the works. According to the award documentation: LOT 1 - Terms of reference Technical assistance from the designer; According to the award documentation: LOT 2 - Terms of reference Consultancy and Supervision
sig_1b0f9e55c5675486433d.title: Consultancy services, supervision and technical assistance services from the designer for the objective 'Modernisation of educational spaces at Universitatea din Oradea – Building C' 2 lots

December 2027. A chargeable extension of the maintenance period is only possible until the end of 2030. Furthermore, reporting is to be set up with SAP applications available in the Canton. The reports can be evaluated for analysis purposes with the SAP Analytics Cloud add-in for Microsoft Excel, and on the other hand, they are to be integrated into SAP Disclosure Management for the preparation of financial reporting. In addition, the solution includes the optional data migration of historical closing data from the current systems (SAP SEM-BCS, SAP BW). The subject of the submission is the commissioning of a provider who has the necessary professional and technical skills to introduce the new consolidation solution consisting of the components consolidation with SAP Group Reporting, reporting and integration into SAP Disclosure Management (hereinafter referred to as "new consolidation solution") in the Finanzverwaltung. Public digital infrastructure is built on intricate systems and interconnected environments that are constantly exposed to cyber risks. A vulnerability management service enables organisations to identify and assess these environments, detect security weaknesses, optimise remediation efforts, and optimise vulnerability management workflows. Conducting regular efforts to detect vulnerabilities reduces the likelihood of data breaches, service disruptions, and other expensive incidents, while supporting a more proactive and structured approach to information security.

The object of the contract to be awarded consists of the supply and provision of development and implementation services for an "INTEGRATED OPERATIONAL MONITORING IT SYSTEM" which will be able to ensure the company's general long-term sustainability in terms of staff availability and mobility, from the perspective of ensuring logistical support and implicitly in terms of costs, during the agreed period and in accordance with the obligations assumed under the contract, with the following main components: 1. GIS component, which will allow the management and analysis of spatial data concerning the entire water production infrastructure and water networks (catchments, adductions, transport networks, etc.) 2. SCADA component - modernisation and improvement of the system 3. IoT integrated IT system component and digitalisation of the smart metering component, consisting of a number of new flow meters equipped with an IoT-type communication module, which will create a unified system for monitoring water networks b Digital platform component for collecting data from flow meters and managing information from flow meters (MDC – Meter Data Collection) C Digital platform component for storing and analysing data from flow meters, as well as for the general management of the flow meter fleet (MDM – Meter Data Management) The general objective of the project is to optimise infrastructure operation and monitoring, and to detect losses or topology or network execution defects by: installing an efficient metering and monitoring system; implementing an integrated IT system for infrastructure and water loss management, which offers specific solutions for water supply and distribution management; a system that integrates existing systems and provides the foundation for further developments, creating the foundation of the smart water network. Achieving this objective will ensure the efficiency and sustainability of investments in the water sector and will allow for the acceleration of decisions to improve service quality, maintaining the main parameters (pressure, flow, quality) at a high level, as well as customer satisfaction regarding operability. The IT system proposed for procurement will be a completely new platform, common to the target user groups and activities, with a database core and operating systems compatible with the existing SCADA system, for integration and interoperability. It will be a unified construction, but with user rights structured on distinct personalised modules. These modules are distinct software applications, personalised by user groups, which allow both the editing of field data, as well as the addition of files such as images, PDFs or videos to the common database/storage system, and user access to all technical, telemetry, SCADA and geospatial (GIS) information. The software modules will be web-based with GPRS-GSM data transmission, but will allow editing and access to all GIS project data or without map components and in the absence of a GSM signal, in deficient areas with subsequent automatic or semi-automatic synchronisation. The applications will be secured for each device by password and username and will be able to function on the project implemented locally and offline on the installed module, as well as via WEB/online. sig_1bc16e8744033d7305a3.description: THIS IS NOT A CONTRACT NOTICE OR A CALL FOR COMPETITION BUT A REQUEST FOR INFORMATION FOR MARKET SOUNDING AND TECHNICAL DIALOGUE. HUS-yhtymä (hereinafter also the contracting authority) is using this request for information to survey the market to support the planning of the procurement of a virtual learning and procedure training platform. The purpose of the request for information is to find out what kind of solutions are available on the market to support specialist surgical training, what content and service models suppliers offer, and how the solutions suit the training needs of HUS. The subject of the procurement is a virtual training and learning platform intended for surgical teaching, which supports e.g. step-by-step learning of procedures, understanding of anatomy, studying of surgical techniques and monitoring of training. The potential procurement may include: - ready-made procedure and anatomy content - the ability to produce and manage the organisation's own teaching content - multimodal learning materials (text, image, video, 3D models) - analytics and user-specific learning monitoring - support, maintenance and expert services. We ask suppliers interested in the procurement to reply in writing to the following questions. Description of the platform and content: - What kind of virtual learning, procedure teaching or training environment solution does your solution offer? - What ready-made content (anatomy, procedures, surgical steps, complications, training videos, etc.) does the platform contain? - How is the content updated and how is its up-to-date status ensured? - Is it possible to produce and manage the subscriber organisation's own content (e.g. videos, images, texts, 3D models) in the solution? Suitability for Finnish training and care practices: - How does the solution support surgical care practices and training requirements used in Finland? - Does the platform have ready-made Finnish-language content or is it possible to produce them? - How does the platform support nationally defined competence objectives for specialist fields? - Is it possible to adapt the content according to local training requirements? Licensing, access rights and user management: - What kind of licensing model (e.g. user-specific, organisation-specific, fixed-term) does the platform have? - How can user licence transfers and user changes be implemented? - How is licence pricing determined in a situation where the user does not actively use the service? - What access rights are granted to content produced by the organisation? Technical implementation and information security: - With what technologies has the platform been implemented and what kind of device, browser or connection requirements does it have? - How does your service take into account information security, data protection, processing of patient and personal data, GDPR requirements and the requirements of the client data act (703/2023) and LVV? - Have external information security assessments been carried out on the platform? Commissioning, support and expert services: - What training, maintenance and support services do you offer (e.g. commissioning, technical support, trainer training)? - How quickly are support services available and in which channels? Delivery and service model: - Through what delivery or commissioning model is the solution you offer available (e.g. SaaS, cloud service, hybrid environment, local installation)? - If the solution is cloud-based, where is the data located and are there options for different geographical locations? - If the solution can be delivered as a locally installed version, what infrastructure requirements are associated with it? - Is it possible to choose between different service models? - What kind of reporting or analytics tools do you offer? - How are updates delivered and are they included in the price of the service? References: - What kind of references do you have from medical training, surgical teaching or similar learning platforms? - Is the solution in use in Finland or other Nordic countries? You may also attach brochures or other information about your products and services to your reply if you wish. Please submit replies to the request for information by 15.5.2026 to the address kilpailutus.ict@hus.fi. Subject of the message: "HUS 652-2024: Training and learning platform for surgical procedures". The replies given to this request for information may be used in procurement planning. The contracting authority may, at its discretion, suggest clarifying market dialogue discussions with those who have replied to this request for information. Please note that all material is intended solely for conducting this market dialogue. The contracting authority will treat your reply confidentially. The contracting authority does not initiate a tendering procedure by publishing the request for information, but a potential contract notice and call for competition will be published later. The request for information does not oblige the contracting authority to carry out the actual procurement. Answering the request for information is not a precondition for participating in a potentially organised subsequent tendering procedure. Suppliers will not be paid compensation for answering the request for information or participating in the market dialogue.

Furthermore, all judge and participant seating positions are to be equipped with connections for displaying digital evidence, which can be shown via a media control system in the chamber on large monitors that can be lowered into sideboards. The chamber is also to be equipped with PTZ cameras as well as technology and software for video and streaming control, for video conferences and for video connections of participants. In addition to the purchase of the described components, the tender covers the planning of the acoustic and discussion system, the on-site technical implementation as well as a multi-year maintenance contract for the operation of the technology.
sig_1bc977fcaa964a3bf71b.title: Technical modernisation of the historical Grand Chamber of the Federal Administrative Court in Leipzig
