sig_1bfc9551359fa9ac27e6.description: SKI hereby invites tenders for a dynamic purchasing system (hereinafter the System) regarding the procurement of management consultancy services. The System includes the procurement of management consultancy services within the 6 service areas below. The content of the service areas is defined in more detail in Annex C. Subject of the System: Service area 1: Strategy and organisational development. Under this service area, services falling within one or more of the following five sub-areas may be purchased: 1. Sub-area 1: Strategy analysis 2. Sub-area 2: Strategy development 3. Sub-area 3: Strategy implementation 4. Sub-area 4: Organisational analysis and design as well as 5. Sub-area 5: Structural implementation. Service area 2: Business processes and efficiency. Under this service area, services falling within one or more of the following three sub-areas may be purchased: 1. Sub-area 1: Process analysis and process optimisation 2. Sub-area 2: Outsourcing 3. Sub-area 3: Public-private partnership (PPP). Service area 3: Analyses and evaluations. Under this service area, services falling within the following sub-area may be purchased: 1. Sub-area 1: Analyses and evaluations. Service area 4: Systems and management. Under this service area, services falling within one or more of the following three sub-areas may be purchased: 1. Sub-area 1: Finance and economic management 2. Sub-area 2: Quality and risk management 3. Sub-area 3: Control and optimisation of administrative processes. Service area 5: Human resources. Under this service area, services falling within one or more of the following three sub-areas may be purchased: 1. Sub-area 1: Leadership and employee development 2. Sub-area 2: Culture and behavioural development 3. Sub-area 3: Personnel policy. Service area 6: Green services. Under this service area, services falling within the following sub-area may be purchased: 1. Sub-area 1: Green services. The system is divided into 2 categories: • Category 1 Competence purchase • Category 2 Task purchase. Both categories concern the procurement of services, where those in category 1 are procured as hours, while those in category 2 are procured as a finished result (report, analysis, etc.). The procurement of services in both categories assumes that these are commonly used and generally available on the market at the time of procurement. The system can therefore not be used to procure services that are not generally available on the market. It is voluntary for all SKI customers, as listed in Annex B, Customer List, to make use of the system when they need to procure management consultancy services. Procurement of Competence purchase. In category 1, customers can procure management consultancy services within the 6 service areas described in Annex C, to meet the customer's competence needs. The consultancy services can be procured in the following way: Purchase of consultancy hours (number of hours x hourly rate).; Procurement of management consultancy services for task resolution. In category 2, customers can procure management consultancy services within the 6 service areas described in Annex C, to fulfil a specific task. The consultancy services can be procured in the following way: Purchase of task resolution at a fixed price.

sig_1c0d2bf1cf4e03d6b7b2.description: Background and Objectives of the Pathfinder Project: The Public Sector AI (PSAI) Directorate within the Department of Science, Innovation and Technology (DSIT) exists to help the government make brilliant public services that empower people in the UK. We work at the very centre of government to drive digital transformation focused on user needs and to reimagine how government uses AI to deliver public services and initiatives. The newly established Government Efficiency Accelerator (GEA) programme is a flagship initiative aimed at driving operational efficiencies across some of the government's key enabling functions (Finance, Policy, HR) through the safe and responsible adoption of AI. The GEA is working in collaboration with the GCF Commercial Innovation Hub (CIH) to better understand the availability of AI based solutions that can be used by teams across government departments to drive efficiency and increase productivity. The goal of this Pathfinder Project is to engage with the market to understand current capabilities, initially focusing on three core business areas: Finance, HR and policy (more details on a specific problem area below). Applicants should note that this engagement is not intended to lead to the procurement of a particular solution for DSIT or any other UK Government Department. Rather, we are looking to build a catalogue of tested and "kitemarked" products that will be made available to public sector organisations to consider procuring them in the knowledge that they have been tested and will meet requirements such as security, usability, transparency etc. We are interested in hearing from all types of suppliers and would particularly encourage SMEs and VCSEs to submit proposals. Challenge Summary: As noted above, the GEA and CIH are engaging with the market to build a deeper understanding of how AI based solutions and products can help make government departments more efficient and productive. We appreciate there are a multitude of potential use cases so for this initial engagement we have chosen to focus on problems relating to budgeting and workforce forecasting. We are inviting suppliers to submit proposals outlining how their products could be used by finance teams across UK government departments in a safe, transparent and unbiased way. We are keen to explore solutions which can reduce the level of repetitive tasks required specifically when budgeting and conducting workforce forecasting. Submissions should demonstrate how the solution can streamline tasks, improve accuracy, and shorten time spent on repetitive work in order to free colleagues up to complete higher-value work. There is no fixed scope, as we aim for platform-agnostic, AI driven and innovative tools that adapt to various organisational needs. Solution should be accessible to organisations of all sizes and is not dependent on any specific ERP platform.
sig_1c0d2bf1cf4e03d6b7b2.title: GEA Pathfinder

sig_1ce7e51c86c3539cc86c.description: This is not a procurement notice or a call for tenders, but an information request with which Etelä-Karjalan hyvinvointialue is surveying comprehensive digital solutions for the administration and implementation of surrogate payment for the personal assistance employer model, as well as the management of informal care, foster care and other fee-based contracts, and the payment of fees, other expenses, etc., and statutory official contributions. The aim of the survey is to find out what kind of comprehensive solutions containing the functionalities described below are available on the Finnish market. Through the market dialogue, the wellbeing services county aims to: 1. Obtain information on market supply and different suppliers' solutions 2. Potential implementation of integrations into various platforms or systems 3. Assess the implementation of information security and data protection 4. Obtain an overview of pricing models and cost structures (no individual tenders) 5. Survey delivery and service models The market dialogue is open to all suppliers that can offer comprehensive solutions falling within the scope of this solution package. The dialogue will focus on solutions that are already in production. Suppliers are requested to present services that are available and in which the key functionalities have already been implemented. The presentation of solutions under development or merely at the conceptual stage is not desired on this occasion. When registering, suppliers are requested to briefly describe: Intended use and environment The system must be suitable for use by the wellbeing services county to manage the following service forms: - Informal care support and contract management - Foster care assignment contracts - Surrogate payment for the personal assistance employer model - Management of contracts for support families and support persons - Other similar contractual relationships User groups are: - Wellbeing services county employees (contract management) - Informal and foster carers (data entry) - Personal assistants and their employers - Other persons in a contractual relationship Key functionalities Contract management: - Electronic drafting and maintenance of assignment contracts - Contract lifecycle management - Recording of care days and working hours - Management of statutory leave Fee and salary processing: - Calculation of fees in accordance with care intensity categories - Payroll processing for personal assistants - Statutory payments and deductions - Processing of substitute carers' fees - Automatic inclusion of index adjustments Payment transmission: - Payment transmission operations approved by the Financial Supervisory Authority - Automatic payment processing - Generation of payment data files Integrations: - Direct data transmission connection to the Tax Administration - Possibility of integration into the wellbeing services county's other systems, particularly an interface to the accounting system - Data export and reporting (Data lake) - User account management via Entra ID Technical requirements - Cloud-based SaaS solution - Information security-audited system - Finnish-language user interface - Implementation in accordance with the Accessibility Directive - Continuous maintenance and updates - User support in Finnish We kindly ask you to answer the following questions: General description of the solution - Do you offer a system solution containing the functionalities described above? - What is the name of your solution and a short description? - What are the key strengths of your solution? Functionalities - How does your solution meet the described contract management needs? - What kind of fee and salary calculation features does the system include? - Does your solution have a licence from the Financial Supervisory Authority for payment transmission? - How is the Tax Administration integration implemented? Technical features - What is the technical architecture of the solution? - How is information security ensured? - What language options does the system support? Experience and references - In which wellbeing services counties / municipalities is your solution in use? - How many users does the system have? - Can you provide reference information on similar deliveries? Additional information - What other essential features does your solution include? - How is the system implementation typically carried out? - What kind of support and training do you offer? Responses to the questions are requested to be sent by 1.12.2025 at 15:00. Responses should be brief and informative. Responses are requested to be sent to the address hankinnat@ekhva.fi. Subject of the message: "Markkinakartoitus - omais- ja perhehoidon sekä henkilökohtaisen avun hallintajärjestelmästä ja ym. palkkioperusteisten sopimusten hallinta ja maksatus" This information request / market survey does not request tenders to be submitted, nor are tenders submitted in response to it; it requests ONLY procurement-related information. Participation or non-participation in the market survey does not affect a tenderer's position in a potential tendering procedure. The market dialogue invitation does not bind the respondent (Supplier) to participate in a tendering procedure, and answering this notice is not a prerequisite for participating in the actual tendering procedure at a later stage. Participants in the market survey shall not be entitled to compensation for participation. The contracting authority does not commit to carrying out the procurement in question. Decisions on launching a potential procurement process will be made after the market survey. The supplied material will be treated as confidential in accordance with section 24, subsection 1, point 20 of the Act on the Openness of Government Activities. Etelä-Karjalan hyvinvointialue thanks you in advance for your responses. They are valuable in defining our system needs and preparing for a potential procurement.
sig_1ce7e51c86c3539cc86c.title: Information request / Market survey: Survey of a complete solution for a management and payment system for family care, foster care and personal assistance, as well as similar fee-based contracts

sig_1cf19cc31175e55206aa.description: This is a SMALL BUSINESS SOURCES SOUGHT NOTICE. This is NOT a solicitation for proposals, proposal of abstracts or quotations. The purpose of this notice is to obtain information regarding: (1) the availability and capability of qualified small business sources; (2) whether they are small businesses (e.g., 8(a), Veteran-owned small businesses, service-disabled Veteran-owned small businesses, HUBZone small businesses, small disadvantaged businesses, and women-owned small businesses); (3) their size classification relative to the North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) code for the proposed acquisition; and (4) whether commercials sources and services are available in the marketplace. Your response to the information requested will assist the Government in determining the appropriate acquisition method, including whether a set-aside is possible. An organization that is not considered a small business under the applicable NAICS code 541715 should not submit a response to this notice. This notice is issued to help determine the appropriate acquisition method including small business socioeconomic set aside possibilities and to determine the availability of commercial or non-commercial companies technically capable of meeting the Government's potential requirement. It is not construed as a commitment by the Government to issue a solicitation or ultimately award a contract. Responses will not be considered as proposals or quotes. No award will be made as a result of this notice. The Government will NOT be responsible for any costs incurred by the respondents to this notice. This notice is strictly for research and information purposes only. Furthermore, it should be noted that any future solicitations that may be issued as a result of this notice, or in response to this requirement, may be issued using a different solicitation number from the one identified above. Background The National Institute on Drug Abuse (NIDA) was established in 1974, and in 1992 it became part of the National Institutes of Health, Department of Health and Human Services. NIDA’s mission is to advance science on drug use and addiction and to apply that knowledge to improve individual and public health through: 1) strategically supporting and conducting basic, clinical, and epidemiological research on drug use, its consequences, and the underlying neurobiological, behavioral, and social mechanisms involved; and 2) advancing the translation, effective implementation, and dissemination of scientific research findings to improve the prevention and treatment of SUDs, reduce adverse health consequences associated with drug use, and enhance public awareness of addiction as a chronic but treatable medical illness. NIDA’s Clinical Trials Network (CTN) was established in 1999 to bridge the gap between research and practice to improve treatment of substance use disorders (SUD) nationwide. The CTN seeks to address critical research questions with direct relevance to clinical practice and the needs of patients. Over the last two decades, the CTN’s research infrastructure and agenda have evolved to reflect the changing landscape of the SUD treatment community, transformation of health care systems, and emerging scientific advancements. The CTN has been engaging providers in general medical settings and healthcare systems, and in 2015 the Network built upon and expanded its research portfolio encouraging adoption of innovative bioinformatics approaches, new technology, and "learning healthcare system" principles to enhance the efficiency of SUD clinical research and clinical care. The CTN conducts clinical trials in sites located across the nation and in other countries. These are usually studies of behavioral, pharmacological, and integrated behavioral and pharmacological treatment interventions in rigorous, clinical trials to determine efficacy, effectiveness, practicality, and feasibility across a broad range of treatment settings and diversified patient populations, and to transfer research results to physicians, clinicians, providers, and patients. These studies are typically Phase III clinical trials, but can also include Phase I, Phase II, Phase IV, and/or registry trials or surveys. More information on the CTN and the CTN’s research portfolio is available at https://nida.nih.gov/organization/center-clinical-trials-network-cctn/clinical-trials-network-ctn. Requirement NIDA is seeking capability statements from small businesses having the capability to act as a data, statistics, and clinical trial service center; providing data and clinical research services and resources in managing and carrying out approximately 20 independent trials in drug use and addiction research at any given time. NIDA requires vendors capable of providing systems for data management, statistical analysis, document management and clinical trial services. The data systems will be used to manage and implement clinical data capture, data analysis, information exchange, scientific discovery efforts and clinical evaluation of promising new substance use disorder treatment medications and interventions in order to further NIDA’s mission. NIDA conducts single and multi-site clinical trials through grants, contracts and cooperative agreements in sites located across the nation and in other countries. These are usually studies of behavioral, pharmacological, and integrated behavioral and pharmacological treatment interventions in rigorous, clinical trials to determine efficacy, effectiveness, practicality, and feasibility across a broad range of treatment settings and diversified patient populations and to transfer research results to physicians, clinicians, providers, and patients. These studies could be Phase I, Phase II, Phase III, and/or Phase IV type trials. They may also include registry type trials or surveys. Although no actual clinical trials will be conducted under this requirement, the project activities will be integrated and central to NIDA trials in the following areas: Establish and administer state-of-the-art, secured web-based systems for the collection, storage, management, quality assurance, and reporting of study data as well as systems to facilitate the collection and management of participant and site level electronic health records data. Assist in the design and analysis of clinical trials, including the development of the statistical sections of protocols, study design, randomization and stratification methods, power and sample size calculations, interim monitoring and analysis plans, and data analytic plans. Review and monitor the quality of study data including the development and management of a computerized data monitoring system that executes quality assurance and quality control procedures to evaluate accuracy, timeliness and completeness of data submitted by the clinical sites, including verification of the clinical and laboratory data used to determine that study participants have reached protocol-defined endpoints. Monitor trial performance and progress and maintain a secure web-based clinical trial performance monitoring system to track key trial performance metrics (e.g. key dates, recruitment, availability of primary outcomes, missing data, etc.). Coordinate meetings of study Data and Safety Monitoring Boards (DSMB) to include the preparation and presentation of reports on safety, data integrity, and site performance as well as coordination of meeting sites, materials, travel support, etc. Participate in relevant committee and subcommittee meetings including representation by the contract Principal Investigator on the CTN Steering Committee and representation by other senior data and statistical experts on other relevant CTN committees, subcommittees and workgroups. Provide consultation, data analytical services, and expertise in certain fields relating to study design and analysis, compiling and editing of clinical data, and other services related to clinical trials operations that might be required. Instructions: The established NAICS code is 541715 Research and Development in the Physical, Engineering, and Life Sciences (except Nanotechnology and Biotechnology). The U.S. Small Business Administration establishes a size standard for 541715 of 1,000 employees or fewer. Interested small business organizations shall demonstrate and document in the submitted capability statement extensive experience in the technical areas listed above. Furthermore, information sent should be relevant and specific in the technical area under consideration, on each of the following qualifications: Work Experience: Capable Vendors must demonstrate the capability and experience to act as a data, statistics, and clinical trial service center; providing data and clinical research services and resources in managing and carrying out approximately 20 independent trials in drug use and addiction research at any given time. NIDA requires vendors capable of providing systems for data management, statistical analysis, document management and clinical trial services. The data systems will be used to manage and implement clinical data capture, data analysis, information exchange, scientific discovery efforts and clinical evaluation of promising new substance use disorder treatment medications and interventions in order to further NIDA’s mission. Organizational Experience: Capable Vendors should describe previous similar projects in the area(s) specified above and where the work was of a similar size and scope. In the response be sure to indicate if you were the prime contractor or a subcontractor. If a subcontractor, be sure to identify your roles and responsibilities as the subcontractor; what percentage of work your subcontract was responsible for; and identify the prime contractor. Personnel: Capable Vendors should identify personnel with the appropriate education, credentials, training, qualifications, experience, and competence to carry out the projects and the tasks identified above. Knowledge and experience in this field of work is critical, and the overall work efforts should be led by professionals who have earned a doctorate degree in a related field of study. Individual efforts and tasks should be led by professionals who have earned a master’s degrees in a related field of study. Basic credentials for proposed personnel will require experience in clinical trials management, biostatistics, drug use and addiction research, data management, statistics. Capable Offerors shall demonstrate how they have staffed similar key personnel on other contracts. Facilities: Capable Vendors should describe the physical space (e.g. offices, meeting rooms, server room, etc.) necessary to accommodate the required staff and equipment as well as the necessary mechanical systems (e.g. HVAC, fire suppression, redundant power, etc.); IT systems and hardware necessary to support the work including sufficient internet access, electronic data collection systems for study data, in-house or cloud based servers for storage of study data, and business software such as the MS Office suite; and security measures including physical and IT access controls, system monitoring, data backup processes, and firewalls. Interested Offerors should describe their facilities or demonstrate its ability to obtain the facilities necessary to support the requirements discussed above. The Government will assess the appropriateness of the responses based on the described work experience, organizational experience, personnel, and facilities described in the capability statement. If the Vendor proposes to team with another organization, please be sure to include the capabilities of any potential proposed partners. The Government will consider any other specific and relevant information about this procurement that would improve our consideration and assessment of the information presented. Documentation may include, but not be limited to, contracts both Government and commercial the organization performed, references, i.e., names, titles, telephone numbers and any other information serving to document the organizations capability, e.g., awards, commendations, etc. THIS IS NOT A REQUEST FOR PROPOSALS: This notice is for information and planning purposes only and does not commit the Government to any contractual agreement. The Government does not intend to award a contract based on responses under this announcement nor otherwise pay for preparing any information sent for the Government's use. Any proprietary information should be so marked. The Government reserves the right to use information provided by respondents for any purpose deemed necessary and legally appropriate. Any organization responding to this notice should ensure that its response is complete and sufficiently detailed to allow the Government to determine the organization’s qualifications to perform the work. Respondents are advised that the Government is under no obligation to acknowledge receipt of the information received to provide feedback to respondents with respect to any information submitted. All capability statements must provide the following: 1) company name, address; and DUNS number; 2) point of contact; 3) phone/fax/email; 4) NAICS Code(s); 5) business size and status; 6) the capability information in response to the requirement and qualification identified in this notice; and; 7) type of small business your organization classifies itself as (i.e.: women-owned, HUBZONE, etc.). Based on preliminary market research, the Government has determined that the requirements described herein do not meet the definition of a commercial product or commercial service as defined in RFO 2.101, and therefore, RFO Part 12 procedures are not applicable to this requirement. However, if a capable vendor believes that these services or products qualify as commercial under FAR 2.101, the vendor may submit a written justification for the Contracting Officer's consideration. Such submissions must be provided to the Contracting Officer no later than September 30, 2026 at 1:00 PM EST. Capability statements must be SUBMITTED ELECTRONICALLY NO LATER THAN 1:00 P.M. (EST) WEDNESDAY, SEPTEMBER 30, 2026 to the primary point of contact. The Subject line for the submission should include the Title and this Small Business Sources Sought Number (75N98026R00157SB).

sig_1d3ac604a526b988e9fa.description: By the present procurement procedure, the EIT KIC Urban Mobility S.L. hereby being referred to as “EIT UM” or the “Company” is aiming to identify a provider (hereinafter, referred to as “Provider”) to support the Digital Platform for EIT Urban Mobility community, presently known as “Mobility Innovators”. This document, along with its annexes, constitute a Request for Proposal (RFP) issued by EIT Urban Mobility for a potential procurement of services in the field of online communities. EIT Urban Mobility community is made of over 270 partners and larger ecosystem of more than 1,200 stakeholders as we work together to make the transition to more sustainable urban mobility and liveable urban spaces. This community includes industry, including large enterprises, SMEs, and startups, universities and education institutions; students and alumni; research and technology organisations; governments at local, regional, national and EU-level; and non-governmental organisations (NGOs). Two years ago, EIT Urban Mobility launched its private digital community platform, Mobility Innovators, which brings together our vibrant community of innovators described above. The platform already has more than 1,500 active users and serves as the central platform for collaboration and engagement within our community. Mobility Innovators enables partners and stakeholders to access information, documents and opportunities shared by EIT Urban Mobility, register for events, and engage in discussions with peers across sectors. It connects organisations from industry, research, academia, and the public sector, fostering collaboration to advance the transition towards more sustainable and liveable urban mobility. Our goal in this next phase is to further grow and activate the community, expand platform functionalities, and enhance user experience to ensure Mobility Innovators continues to support EIT Urban Mobility’s role as Europe’s leading innovation community for urban mobility.
sig_1d3ac604a526b988e9fa.title: Rfp Digital & Private Platform for EIT Urban Mobility Community - “Mobility Innovators”, 26-28

sig_1e36e4da8b700c63d492.description: South of Scotland Enterprise (SOSE) are notifying the market of a potential market opportunity for a supplier to deliver a fully managed, end-to-end IT service for the Mountainbike Innovation Centre (MTBIC) facility. This is to include the design, supply, installation, configuration, and ongoing support and operation of all IT equipment, network infrastructure, and associated services. Lot 1: . South of Scotland Enterprise (SOSE) are notifying the market of a potential market opportunity for a supplier to deliver a fully managed, end-to-end IT service for the Mountainbike Innovation Centre (MTBIC) facility. This is to include the design, supply, installation, configuration, and ongoing support and operation of all IT equipment, network infrastructure, and associated services. The MTBIC is a new build, being built in partnership with Hub South East. Morrisons are the main contractor. The appointed supplier will need to source, provide and install all required equipment per an IT matrix that has been produced and will be issued as part of the tender documentation. They will also need to provide a managed service provision to the tenants and SOSE within the building. Key requirements will likely include but will not be limited to: - Full Wi-Fi network, both internal and external - EDUROM Network - Ability for segregation of network to tenants - Ability to link into fire alarm and CCTV systems where appropriate - Managed service provision - Ability to live stream from the building - Potential for 100 concurrent users at select times - IT security compliant with relevant statutory requirements - Managed and maintained equipment - Service desk provision SOSE will require a comprehensive service, from inception to completion. The MTBIC is a brand new building, and the contractor will provide the cable routes and CAT install but SOSE is required to undertake all other aspects. Any infrastructure required e.g. WAPs, cabinets will need to be costed and provided for as part of this tender. SOSE will not be seeking discrete components or partial delivery — the requirement is for a single, fully managed service covering all IT and network requirements for the building. The purpose of the MTBIC is to provide workshop space to companies interested in developing new and exciting technology, hot desk space and office space, events space both internal and external. This is to be a hub out of which businesses will operate.
sig_1e36e4da8b700c63d492.title: Fully managed IT service for the Mountainbike Innovation Centre (MTBIC), Innerleithen

sig_1e423071dce60e34e86c.description: The subject of the public contract is the delivery, installation, configuration, testing, commissioning and maintenance of a Security Orchestration, Automation and Response (SOAR) System for the National Visa Information System (NVIS) at the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, in connection with project No BG65BVPR001-2.002-0002 „Development and upgrading of the software and hardware provision of NVIS“, financed under an administrative grant contract with reg. No 812108-81/20.11.2024 from the Border Management and Visa Policy Instrument 2021–2027, co-financed by the European Union. The scope of the public contract includes the following activities: - Activity 1 - Delivery of a Security Orchestration, Automation and Response (SOAR) System for the needs of the National Visa Information System (NVIS). - Activity 2 - Installation, configuration, testing and commissioning services for the delivered Security Orchestration, Automation and Response (SOAR) System at the Primary and Backup Visa Centre of NVIS. - Activity 3 - Expert support services for the Security Orchestration, Automation and Response (SOAR) System. - Software support of the Security Orchestration, Automation and Response (SOAR) System, in accordance with the Contracting Authority's Technical Specification – Annex 1. The envisaged activities cover the delivery, installation, configuration, implementation, software and expert support of a Security Orchestration, Automation and Response (SOAR) System and software licences ensuring the functionality and right of use of the system, including support intended for the needs of the National Visa Information System (NVIS). The Security Orchestration, Automation and Response (SOAR) System will ensure significant development of the NVIS infrastructure. This solution will increase the level of security and resilience of the system by providing the necessary monitoring and prevention against potential risks and threats related to the operation and access to information of NVIS. The requirements for the execution of the public contract are described in detail in the Contracting Authority's Technical Specification – Annex No 1. All documents submitted by participants that are issued in a foreign language must be accompanied by a translation into Bulgarian. sig_1e637cd62aa7b58e2ba3.description: The Authority intends to procure a modern Corporate Technology Platform (Ecosystem) to replace fragmented and ageing legacy corporate systems and provide an integrated digital platform supporting key enabling services across Police Scotland. The requirement is for an integrated Enterprise Resource Planning (ERP) and Human Capital Management (HCM) Ecosystem, together with the associated hosting, integration, implementation, data migration, training, transition, support and professional services required to deliver and sustain the solution. The Contract is expected to be for a period of seven (7) years with options, exercisable solely at the Authority's discretion, to extend by up to three (3) further periods of twelve (12) months each, giving a maximum potential duration of ten (10) years. Lot 1: . The Authority intends to award a contract to a single service provider for the provision of a Corporate Technology Platform (EcoSystem). The requirement is for an integrated Enterprise Resource Planning (ERP) and Human Capital Management (HCM) Ecosystem, together with the associated hosting, integration, implementation, data migration, training, transition, support, and professional services required to deliver and sustain the solution. The scope of the Ecosystem contract will cover the following elements: MVP / Minimum Commitment (This is the minimum the Authority will commit to purchase as part of this contract): - HR - Payroll - Duty Management - Common platform services Optional Requirements (May be procured as either: a) additional modules within the proposed Ecosystem that will replace the system/solution currently in place, or b) integrations between the Ecosystem and the existing system or service, enabling data exchange, reporting, workflow triggers, or other interoperability without necessarily replacing the existing system): - Estates - Fleet - Finance - Procurement Contract Duration & Value: The Contract is expected to be for an initial period of seven (7) years with options, exercisable solely at the Authority's discretion, to extend by up to three (3) further periods of twelve (12) months each, giving a maximum potential duration of ten (10) years (120 months). The estimated total value of the Contract is approximately 51,000,000 GBP over the maximum potential contract duration. This includes initial and ongoing software licensing, software support and maintenance, cloud hosting, implementation services, and system integration services. Procedure & Negotiation Parameters: This procurement is being conducted using the Competitive Procedure with Negotiation (CPN). The Authority intends to invite a minimum of 5 qualified candidates to participate in Stage 2 (Invitation to Tender), subject to a sufficient number of compliant Stage 1 SPD submissions being received. In order to identify the Most Economically Advantageous Tender (MEAT), the Authority reserves the right to either: 1. Evaluate all initial tenders and award the contract without entering into negotiations; or 2. Commence negotiations with Bidders who submit compliant initial tenders in order to improve tender content. Bidders should note that initial tenders should be fully compliant and capable of assessment on their own merits without relying on negotiation or clarification. The Authority also reserves the right to apply successive stages during negotiations to reduce the number of tenders to be negotiated. Note: The Authority's minimum requirements and final award criteria are non-negotiable. Candidates must refer to the Corporate Technology Platform (EcoSystem) Information and Instructions for Candidates document available on PCS-Tender for full procurement details and instructions.. Candidates must refer to the Corporate Technology Platform (EcoSystem) Information & Instructions for Candidates on PCS-Tender. Non-compliance may result in submission rejection. Economic operators may be excluded from this competition under Regulation 58 of the Public Contracts (Scotland) Regulations 2015.

sig_1ebfb88fba73a943890a.description: THIS IS A RETENDER TO OCID ocds-h6vhtk-058a17 Carmarthenshire County Council Healthy Communities & Public Protection Service are looking to procure an EPOS system that is multifunctional and can operate across several facilities. The system should be able to manage both catering and retail operations as well as having the capability to offer additional functionality detailed in the specification below, to help facilities manage their daily financial transactions with a key driver being to reduce costs, drive sales and deliver better customer service. The EPOS system will be installed in cafés and restaurants within leisure-based facilities such as leisure centres, country parks, small hotel, museums, art venues and theatres. The system will be expected to help facilitate the daily operation of such venues to varying degrees, the capability to tailor the system set up based on a venues requirement will be an important factor (i.e. some facilities will only require an EPOS to run F&B and retail sales, where another may need to be able to facilitate F&B, Retail, Ticketing and Membership capability etc.). The ability to manage facility admissions, retail sales, daily stock management and provide comprehensive real time back-office management data are just some of the key functionalities expected of the system. Lot 1: . None

sig_1ee047eb41c952cf8874.description: In the field of road safety, the Safe System approach, recognised internationally and included in the “European Union Road Safety Policy 2021-2030” and the European Commission’s “Strategic Action Plan on Road Safety”, suggests acquiring greater knowledge about the different variables that influence road accidents —beyond the usual indicators, such as the number of accidents, deaths and serious injuries—, recommending the acquisition of other indicators, called Key Performance Indicators (KPIs), directly related to the prevention of deaths and injuries in traffic accidents. Among these indicators are the use of seat belts and child restraint systems, the use of helmets, vehicles travelling within the speed limit, drivers travelling within the legal blood alcohol limit, driver distractions and vehicle safety. These indicators constitute the object of this tender. The object of this lot is the design of a sampling plan for lots 2 and 3 and for the alcohol indicator and EDAP Study, obtaining the KPIs (except for KPI 6, whose calculation work remains within the scope of lot 4), and preparation of the dashboard.; The objective of lot 2 consists of carrying out measurements of speed and other characteristics of vehicle flow in a sample of 150 sections of the Spanish road network, in order to serve as a basis for the preparation and acquisition of the KPI 1 indicator; Carrying out fieldwork for the collection of data on the use of seat belts, child restraint systems (CRS), helmets and driving using mobile devices, by conducting non-participatory surveys in a sample of urban and interurban road sections, which allow the successful bidder of lot 1 to obtain these indicators (KPI 2, 3 and 5).; The object of this lot is the acquisition of the vehicle safety indicator (KPI 6).; The object of this lot is the management and supervision of the work of lots 1,2,3 and 4.
sig_1ee047eb41c952cf8874.title: Service for the preparation of reports on key performance indicators in road safety. 5 lots.

Contract Duration: The contract period will be from the date of contract to 2030-03-31 Solicitation Method: Competitive Number of Contracts: One (1) Comprehensive Land Claim Agreement Applies: No Applicable Trade Agreements: The requirement is subject to the provisions of the World Trade Organization Agreement on Government Procurement (WTO-AGP), the Canada-Chile Free Trade Agreement (CCFTA), the Canada-Peru Free Trade Agreement (CPFTA), the Canada-Colombia Free Trade Agreement (CColFTA), the Canada-Panama Free Trade Agreement (CPanFTA), the Canada-European Union Comprehensive Economic and Trade Agreement (CETA), Canada Korea Free Trade Agreement (CKFTA), Comprehensive and Progressive Agreement for Trans-Pacific Partnership (CPTPP), Canada-Honduras Free Trade Agreement, Canada-Ukraine Free Trade Agreement, Canada-United Kingdom Trade Continuity Agreement (Canada-UK TCA) and the Canadian Free Trade Agreement (CFTA). Requirement Details Tendering Procedure: Selective Tendering This requirement is open only to those TBIPS Supply Arrangement Holders who qualified under Tier 1 for services in the National Capital Region for the following categories: • Category A.1. Application/Software Architect Level 3 • Category I.2. Database Administrator Level 3 • Category I.6. Network Analyst Level 3 • Category I.11. Technology Architect Level 3 The following SA Holders have been invited to submit a proposal: • Accenture Inc. • ADRM Technology Consulting Group Corp. • BoonBridge Corporation • CDW Canada Corp. • CGI Information Systems and Management Consultants Inc. • Cofomo Inc. • Deloitte Inc. • Donna Cona Inc., IBM Canada Limited Joint Venture • Flex Tech Services Inc • Primex Project Management Limited • Prologic Systems Ltd., and Maplesoft Consulting Inc. in JV • Skyfly Solutions Inc., iFathom Corp., EPI-Use Now Inc. in Joint Venture • Spaghetti Logic Inc. • TRM Technologies Inc. • Xelerance Corporation Description of Work: The objective of this requirement is to augment knowledge within the Department of Justice Canada’s (JUS) Cloud team to gather expertise and meet project requirements and specific AI initiatives. The required professional services will support the delivery of key infrastructure components, networking fixes and improvements as well as high visibility projects such as Otto , Artificial Intelligence and the Lakehouse. The Cloud Engineer will implement, configure, automate, and support cloud infrastructure, platform services, and cloud-native solutions in accordance with Government of Canada Cloud Guardrails, departmental standards, enterprise architecture principles, and security controls. The Cloud Engineer will support the deployment, integration, modernization, and operational management of Microsoft Azure services, enterprise applications, AI-enabled solutions, and hybrid cloud environments. The Cloud Engineer will collaborate with the Cloud Centre of Expertise (CCoE), Shared Services Canada (SSC), Security Operations, infrastructure teams, application teams, and project stakeholders to deploy, configure, monitor, troubleshoot, automate, and document cloud services, platform components, application hosting environments, identity services, storage, networking, and operational processes while supporting continuous improvement, operational excellence, and knowledge transfer. The Cloud Architect will design, document, and provide technical leadership for the Department's cloud architecture, ensuring compliance with Government of Canada Cloud Guardrails, departmental standards, security controls, and enterprise architecture principles. The Cloud Architect will support cloud infrastructure, cloud-native applications, application modernization initiatives, Azure platform services, AI-enabled solutions, and hybrid architectures. Responsibilities include the design of governance models, subscription hierarchies, landing zones, security architecture, integration patterns, DevSecOps practices, application hosting models, and reference architectures to support enterprise cloud adoption and integration with on-premises and cloud-based services. The Network Specialist will design, implement, document, and support cloud and hybrid networking solutions that provide secure, resilient, and high-performing connectivity between cloud, on-premises, partner, and externally hosted environments. The specialist will support enterprise cloud platforms, cloud-native applications, application modernization initiatives, AI-enabled solutions, and hybrid architectures by designing and implementing networking services, secure integration patterns, and connectivity solutions. The Network Specialist will collaborate with Shared Services Canada (SSC), internal Security Operations, infrastructure teams, application teams, and project stakeholders to design, implement, validate, and document network connectivity, firewall configurations, DNS services, certificate management, identity integration, private connectivity, and network security controls in accordance with Government of Canada standards and departmental policies. The Database Administrator will design, implement, maintain, and optimize database platforms across on-premises and Azure environments, ensuring the availability, performance, security, and recoverability of business-critical systems. The Database Administrator will implement and support backup, restore, high availability, disaster recovery, monitoring, and security controls, while providing technical advice and documentation related to database migrations, cloud integration, and operational best practices in coordination with application teams, Shared Services Canada (SSC), and internal security stakeholders. Bidders must submit a bid for all resource categories. Security Requirement: All Contractor personnel must hold at a minimum, a Personnel security screening level of Reliability. Privileged users require a Personnel Security screening level of Secret. Unscreened personnel are prohibited from performing services under the Contract. Minimum Corporate Security Required: Reliability Minimum Resource Security Required: Secret Contract Authority Name: Ryan Greig Phone Number: 437-295-5631 Email Address: Ryan.Greig@justice.gc.ca Inquiries Inquiries regarding this RFP requirement must be submitted to the Contracting Authority named above. Request for Proposal (RFP) documents will be e-mailed directly from the Contracting Authority to the Qualified Supply Arrangement Holders who are being invited to bid on this requirement. BIDDERS ARE ADVISED THAT “BUYANDSELL.GC.CA” IS NOT RESPONSIBLE FOR THE DISTRIBUTION OF SOLICITATION DOCUMENTS. The Crown retains the right to negotiate with any supplier on any procurement. Documents may be submitted in either official language. NOTE: Task-Based Informatics Professional Services (TBIPS) Method of Supply is refreshed three (3) times per year. If you wish to find out how you can be a “Qualified SA Holder”, please contact RCNMDAI.-NCRIMOS@pwgsc.gc.ca

sig_1f3a2b4a4dcc01e9576c.description: The Norwegian Correctional Service shall procure parallel framework agreements for consultancy services. Consultants with experience within strategic consultancy, but not limited to: a) Strategy: scenario methodology and foresight, outside world analyses and strategy development b) Change management: Structured approach to leading individuals, teams and organisations from a current condition to a desired future condition. c) Performance management – some key words (not limited to, but relevant topics: process improvement, management tool/management system, target and result management, risk analyses and internal control. d) Reviews, analyses and evaluations: evaluation methodology and effect analyses. The Norwegian Correctional Service shall be more data driven and it needs more advanced analyses, predictive models, risk profile, prognoses etc., therefore there is a need for competence in data modelling and advanced analyses. e) Socio-economic analysis: methods for assessing and comparing the total costs and benefits of a measure for society as a whole. f) Cost estimation and uncertainty analysis: The process of calculating what a measure or project will cost, as well as assessing how secure or uncertain these estimates are and what factors can affect them. g) Profit planning/follow-up: Identifying, planning and ensuring that the expected gains from a measure or project are actually realised and measured over time. h) Innovation, design and service development: Need for competence in system design/management design in addition to service design i) KI: this means competence in KI and how the organisation can use this in an appropriate way. This also includes competence and experience on prerequisites and other consequences connected to implementation, from the technical to the more organisational sides. Competence/certification within recognised methods will be relevant. The sub-area covers the business perspective, and in some cases may overlap sub-area 2A.; Consultants with experience within operative management and consultancy services. The consultants shall contribute to the execution of deliveries in the form of, but not limited to: a) Project management: planning, organising, implementing and following-up a project in order to achieve defined goals within given frameworks for time, cost and quality. b) Management of development projects - competence in flexible methodology c) Alteration projects: manage and coordinate activities that shall carry out a planned change, with a focus on both technical deliveries and human factors such as involvement, communication and anchoring. d) Implementation project: ensure new systems, systems or processes in an organisation and ensure that they are implemented, anchored and used as planned. e) Digitalisation projects - The Norwegian Correctional Service shall digitalise several internal work processes and externally between actors in the criminal case chain as well as management cooperation partners. f) Preliminary projects and concept reviews: reviews the needs, assesses alternative solutions and recommends the most appropriate concept before the main project starts. g) Test management: Planning, managing and following-up test activities to ensure that a system or product fulfils the requirements and functions as expected. sig_1f546ffb36a174b5d647.description: To ensure efficient, secure and appropriate use of social media, Myndigheten för civilt försvar (the Authority) needs appropriate tools that support planning, publication, coordination, monitoring and analysis of communication efforts. The requested tool must comply with the Authority's social media strategy, i.e., it must prioritise presence in the social media channels that are largest in Sweden. The presence in social media must function as an extended arm of the Authority's social media, in addition to the channels in which the Authority otherwise operates (websites, apps, tools/services, etc.). Through this, the tool must ensure that the Authority can: - Promote dialogue and participation with the target group and thereby reduce the distance between the Authority and its target groups. - Take part in discussions, views and comments as part of the Authority's horizon scanning. - Reach out to target groups that the Authority otherwise finds difficult to reach in other channels. - Be present where the target groups expect the Authority to be. - Manage and answer comments in the social media channels where they are made. - Increase awareness of the Authority's operations. - Maintain and increase trust in the Authority as a government agency. - Drive traffic to the Authority's own channels.
sig_1f546ffb36a174b5d647.title: RFI - Tool for social media management

sig_1f78a83939231b7ec8b5.description: Award of services for the implementation of the Frankfurt Founders' Fund. We are looking for a contractor to take over the central management of the Frankfurt Founders' Fund and the numerous associated tasks. Background: The Founders' Fund, operated by Wirtschaftsförderung Frankfurt on behalf of the City of Frankfurt, has been a cornerstone of Frankfurt's start-up support since its introduction in 2010. The Frankfurt Founders' Fund has since established itself and is now an integral part of the start-up activities of the City of Frankfurt am Main, Wirtschaftsförderung Frankfurt and the Frankfurt-Rhine-Main ecosystem. In 2009, the foundation stone for the Frankfurt Founders' Fund was laid. The microfinance study commissioned at that time revealed that young companies were facing a financing gap for credit requirements. On this basis, the Frankfurt Founders' Fund was launched. The Frankfurt Founders' Fund project is currently being operated by an external contractor (hereinafter referred to as the Contractor) and is the responsibility of Wirtschaftsförderung Frankfurt GmbH as the contracting authority (hereinafter referred to as the Contracting Authority). In addition, professional administration is necessary to ensure transparency, efficiency and sustainability. The Contractor, who is commissioned with the administration and implementation of the fund, must therefore have sound experience in the field of start-up financing, project and portfolio management and, ideally, in working with public institutions. Furthermore, knowledge of risk management, supporting founders and developing suitable monitoring and evaluation instruments is required. The Contractor will work closely with the Bürgschaftsbank Hessen and partner banks and offer founders a proven financing and coaching model. An essential part of the success model is not just the financial support for start-ups, for which Wirtschaftsförderung Frankfurt assumes 80 % of the guarantee, but also extensive support included in the Founders' Fund programme in the form of coaching by the Contractor throughout the entire loan term. In summary, the Contracting Authority expects the following services from the new Contractor: - Organisational services - Information and enquiry management - Review and processing of financing enquiries - Support/accompaniment of financing projects - Measures for loan defaults, early warning system - Debt collection and processing - Reporting and monitoring - Marketing/communication - Cooperation and community network maintenance
sig_1f78a83939231b7ec8b5.title: Frankfurt Founders' Fund

sig_1fc48376af54810c10dd.description: The assignment includes a guidance process for a period of 3 years. The assignment potentially includes: 1. Analysis and independent quality assurance The contractor analyses and understands the project documentation of the digital transformation programme. The contractor acquires high-level knowledge of the offered and/or selected solutions and the suppliers' implementation approach. The contractor proactively identifies risks, dependencies, gaps and points of attention that may have an impact on the realisation of the project objectives and formulates concrete recommendations regarding these. 2. Support for project management and programme control The contractor acts as an independent sounding board for the project management and those responsible for change management. The contractor supports the preparation, assessment and validation of project deliverables, including implementation plans, communication and adoption plans, process documentation, functional analyses and other project-related documentation. In addition, the contractor supports the monitoring of the alignment between project objectives, programme objectives and the decisions of the steering committee. 3. Independent implementation guidance (optional) The contractor supports the client during the implementation phase of the selected solutions and monitors the quality, feasibility and coherence of the implementation approach. The contractor critically assesses the implementation plans, proposed configurations, migration strategies, test approaches, training plans and commissioning processes of the suppliers. sig_200ce3d85d4db0a3975c.description: Description of the Project: Local Governance Reform Programme (LGRP) III The "Multi-Donor Action (EU-BMZ) - Strengthening Capacities and Institutional Readiness of Reform Actors in Palestine" co-financed by the European Union (EU) and the Federal Ministry for Economic Cooperation and Development (BMZ) and implemented by Deutsche Gesellschaft für Internationale Zusammenarbeit (GIZ) GmbH, aims to enhance the institutional capacity, operational effectiveness, and coordination functions of MoFP and PMO ERO as leading entities in national planning and reform management. The Action will support MoFP in its role as the central coordinating body for national planning by enhancing its capacity to embed data-driven policymaking, ensure coherent approaches across line ministries, and improve coordination across all levels of governance. The Palestinian Authority (PA) faces significant institutional and technical challenges in managing, measuring, and demonstrating public sector performance. Monitoring and evaluation (M&E) functions across line ministries and agencies (LMAs) are narrowly defined, fragmented, and largely disconnected from planning and budgeting decisions. Indicators are poorly formulated, feeder data is weak and uncoordinated, and M&E reporting serves administrative compliance rather than evidence-based management. The Strategic Results Framework (SRF), which is the principal instrument for measuring national results delivery, lacks a usable structure, theory of change, and coherent indicator set. No overarching national M&E strategy exists, and data management responsibilities across government institutions remain undefined and unanchored. Lot LOT-0001: 10037895-Development of a National M&E System in Palestine. Description of Work and Services to be Provided: structured around eight work packages (WPs) covering the full cycle from system design through operationalization, capacity development, and digital enablement. WP1: Inception, Alignment, and Mobilization. It establishes the analytical and operational foundation for the assignment. The contractor reviews and consolidates the OECD/Sigma diagnostic findings, conducts targeted design assessments to collect operational information required for subsequent WPs, including data feasibility mapping, institutional baseline mapping, planning-budgeting process validation, pilot site readiness assessment, and a digital systems inventory. The contractor establishes the governance and coordination arrangements, detailed workplan, stakeholder engagement plan, and risk register. The primary deliverable is a comprehensive Inception Report. WP2: National M&E System Framework and Governance. It produces the foundational design of the national M&E system, developed jointly with MoFP and key government stakeholders rather than as an externally designed product. It defines the system"s purpose, scope, institutional roles, governance mechanisms, core M&E processes, data governance principles, integration logic with planning and budgeting, evaluation framework, and system stewardship mandate. The deliverable is a government-endorsed National M&E Framework. WP3: Results and Measurement Architecture. It redesigns the Strategic Results Framework using a methodology-first, pilot-based approach that accounts for the current limitations of the national development plan. The contractor develops a comprehensive SRF methodology and standards framework designed for the next national planning cycle, conducts a participatory results clarification exercise with a pilot of sectors, and produces a transitional indicator set for the remaining current planning cycle to enable piloting. Deliverables include the revised SRF Methodology Document and the Updated SRF and Indicator Framework. WP4: Institutional and Functional Design. It defines the organizational arrangements required to anchor M&E and data management as permanent government functions. Through a participatory process with MoFP and LMAs, the contractor develops functional design models, organizational options with feasibility assessments against General Personnel Council (GCP) civil service frameworks, RACI matrices, workflow systems, and HR alignment proposals. The deliverable is an Institutional and Functional Design Report. WP5: Integration with Planning, Budgeting, and Oversight. It defines how M&E information can flow into and influences core government decision-making processes, including annual planning, budget preparation, and performance oversight at CoM level. The contractor maps actual planning and budgeting processes, assesses linkage feasibility, designs standard decision-informing M&E products, and proposes integration mechanisms. Deliverables include M&E Integration Framework and Updated Planning and Budgeting Guidance Notes. WP6: Operationalization and Piloting. It translates the system design into operational reality through co-developed SOPs, data collection instruments, reporting templates, and interim digital tools, tested with 3-5 pilot LMAs selected on the basis of a readiness assessment conducted in WP1. The pilot tests real workflows and data flows, generating feedback that is incorporated into system refinements. The deliverable is a Pilot Implementation Report. WP7: Capacity Development, Change Management, and Sustainability. It builds the professional and institutional capacities required for sustained system operation. The contractor develops competency frameworks, training programs, and materials; delivers training in two waves; designs and initiates change management and communication strategies; proposes institutionalization and incentive mechanisms in coordination with GPC; and, importantly, builds system stewardship capacity enabling MoFP and LMAs to maintain, update, and evolve the system independently after assignment conclusion. Deliverables include the Capacity Development and Change Management Strategy, Competency Frameworks and Training Roadmap, Training Modules and Materials, System Stewardship Package, and System Handover and Transition Protocol. WP8: Digital Enablement Design and Procurement-Ready Specifications. It produces the complete technical basis for procuring a digital M&E platform. The contractor defines functional requirements, designs the data architecture and interoperability framework, conducts a technology options assessment including AI and emerging technology analysis, designs a public results portal concept, and produces a vendor-neutral technical and procurement specifications package.

sig_214e7ee6c2bc7fe072c3.description: The City of Helsinki Urban Environment Division is establishing a dynamic purchasing system, within which equipment and goods procurements for snow management solutions will be tendered. The dynamic purchasing system will remain valid until the end of 2033, unless the contracting authority shortens or extends the duration of the dynamic purchasing system. During the duration of the dynamic purchasing system, all interested candidates may submit a request for participation. The operation and scope of the dynamic purchasing system are described in more detail in the invitation to participate and its attachments. According to the preliminary estimate, dozens of procurements will be carried out within the dynamic purchasing system over the coming years. The total value of the procurements is estimated to be a total of 19 500 000 euros during the entire duration of the DPS for comprehensive service procurements. The dynamic purchasing system is used to prepare for future procurement needs, which will be implemented in sufficient numbers to achieve the objectives. This is an estimate, and the contracting authority is not committed to any procurement quantities. The number of procurements may be significantly lower than estimated if the objectives of the snow management entity are met by other means. sig_216416e022596aba1c25.description: The purpose of this award procedure is to expand the capacity of the existing data/system backup and recovery solution, and its related subsystems, so that they cover the volume and diversity of systems and data generated by the implementation and operationalisation of the Gamma system and related technological systems/experimental areas, in accordance with the requirements of the Specifications. Pursuant to the provisions of Art. 160 of Law no. 98/2016, as subsequently amended and supplemented, interested economic operators shall request clarifications or additional information regarding the award documentation up to 20 days before the deadline for the submission of tenders. The contracting authority shall respond clearly and completely to all requests for clarification/additional information addressed by economic operators, on the 12rd day before the deadline for the submission of tenders, in accordance with Art. 161 of Law no. 98/2016, as subsequently amended and supplemented, read in conjunction with Art. 27 paragraph (3) of Government Decision no. 395/2016 as subsequently amended and supplemented. The purpose of this award procedure is to expand the capacity of the existing data/system backup and recovery solution, and its related subsystems, so that they cover the volume and diversity of systems and data generated by the implementation and operationalisation of the Gamma system and related technological systems/experimental areas by: - Expanding the licensed capacity and hardware resources allocated to the existing system backup and recovery solution, incl. those dedicated to its secure and unified administration, and to the immutable storage of the resulting backup copies, separate from the resources protected through it; - Implementing a replication capacity for unstructured experimental and operational data, in order to ensure the operational resilience of the existing primary storage subsystem for this data, through dedicated hardware resources; - Expanding the existing shared and deduplicated storage capacity for structured data; - Ensuring a centralised capacity for monitoring the status of the components of the expanded backup and recovery solution, and for the unified display of relevant information; - Expanding the existing network infrastructure to be able to manage the technical traffic generated by the newly introduced components.

sig_2193a5a43f82bc13e8db.description: The Finnish Defence Forces use a DDI system used for IP address management, which is based on the Infoblox product. A need has arisen for the FDF to expand the DDI system to several instances and administrative units. The subject of the present procurement is additional licences for the Infoblox product or a corresponding compatible product in accordance with this invitation to tender. The IP address management system is a single entity combining different instances and information security classes, the different instances of which must interoperate and communicate with each other. The systems (licences) of the different instances and different information security classes must be able to exchange information with each other and know what and how many IP addresses are in use or unused and to which devices and systems they have been allocated. The procurement includes licence maintenance. If the tenderer offers licences of another brand, the tenderer shall be responsible for all additional, modification and maintenance costs of matching them, as well as for ensuring that the licences in question fulfil the requirements set for them. In the invitation to tender and its appendices, the subject of the procurement is also referred to as Services or licences.

sig_21ba0d133a5814d63252.description: The Energie Vorpommern GmbH (hereinafter: EVP) intends to re-award the commercial management for the sales division. The EVP is an energy supply company and supplies customers with electricity and natural gas in, among other places, the towns of Grimmen, Gützkow, Wolgast and the surrounding villages, as well as the island of Usedom. In the natural gas sector, the EVP is the basic supplier in the aforementioned region. The subject of this tender is the award of commercial services for energy operations. The contractor's activities include commercial management for the sales division. Details regarding the scope of services and the remuneration system can be found in the attached draft service contract (Annex A). The following points highlight essential key aspects. The individual service requirements arise in particular from the contract annexes (1a to 1h). The contractor's activities include the services described in more detail in contract annex 1: Description of Services, from the following areas: - Sales in general (cf. contract annex 1a: Sales) - Finance and accounting (cf. contract annex 1b: Finance and accounting) - Legal services (cf. contract annex 1c: Legal services) - Shared services sales (cf. contract annex 1d: Shared services) - Payroll accounting (cf. contract annex 1e: Payroll accounting) - Controlling and other services (cf. contract annex 1f: Controlling and other services) - Energy data management (cf. contract annex 1g: Energy data management) - IT infrastructure (cf. contract annex 1h: IT infrastructure) Furthermore, the contractor shall ensure the prior transfer of the EVP's digital data from the system of the previous service provider, SERVICE PLUS GMBH, to the new system. The EVP will inform the successful bidder upon award whether the data migration is to be carried out. The data migration must be completed by no later than 31.12.2027 in accordance with the concept to be created by the contractor (contract annex 5: Concept for data migration), so that the assumption of commercial management is possible for the contractor from this point in time. The EVP intends to award the services initially from 01.01.2027 to 31.12.2032, combined with the option of contract extension. The contract shall automatically extend by a further three years each time if the contract is not terminated by one of the contracting parties 18 months before the end of the term.

sig_2256a758078072d2765c.description: OsloMet plans to enter into a contract for security monitoring services (SOC). The objective of the RFI is to: • Avoid erroneous or inappropriate requirements. • Uncover and correct uncertainties. • Use competence in the supplier market. • Reduce the risk for both the contracting authority and suppliers. • Better goal achievement in the procurements and learning in their organisation. Background: OsloMet would like to strengthen monitoring and immediate response to events in our systems and network, by acquiring a 24/7/365 SOC service. Scope: As a starting point, we would like to reuse licenses in our Azure/M365 portfolio to the greatest possible degree, as well as the security products associated with them (Defender + Sentinel products). In addition it is a prerequisite that the data processing occurs in such a way that OsloMet retains historical data over time, also when the supplier is changed. OsloMet would like input on the following: - Will the questions and requirements answer the overall description? - Can you provide such a service with the set or easily adapted requirements? What notes do you have regarding the requirements? Has OsloMet set the right requirements to get a system that covers the need? - Are there requirements that are unnecessary growing? - What competence should be emphasised in the team that shall support OsloMet and what ought to be a minimum requirement? - Since OsloMet has never used a SOC service. Are there requirements that have not been set that should have been made? sig_22950ad748b46de96910.description: Forsvarsministeriets Materiel- og Indkøbsstyrelse (”FMI) wishes to enter into a contract regarding the delivery, operation, maintenance, support and further development of an internet-based booking system for the Danish Defence's pool vehicles. The existing system is intended to be replaced by a more modern, reliable and user-friendly solution that supports efficient booking, lending and return of pool vehicles as well as providing FMI with access to relevant operational and administrative data. The purpose of the contract is to ensure the Danish Defence a comprehensive solution that, with a minimum of resource consumption from FMI, enables secure, flexible and efficient management of pool vehicles across the organisation. The solution must support both open and closed vehicle pools, be able to handle a large number of users and vehicles, and contribute to high availability and continuity in the Danish Defence's transport solutions. The contract comprises the supplier's delivery, operation, maintenance, support and further development of the overall system, including both the application and the infrastructure necessary therefor, for use by the Danish Defence's pool vehicles, as well as the delivery, installation and operation of electronic car-sharing equipment in the vehicles. The contract includes a start-up period consisting of a development period and an implementation period, during which the system is adapted, developed and commissioned in accordance with FMI's requirements. The supplier is responsible for the delivery of the application and for the infrastructure necessary therefor, including hosting the system on servers located in Denmark. The system is delivered as an internet-based solution (SaaS), and the supplier is responsible for all operation of the underlying infrastructure. The supplier is responsible for the integration of existing data regarding users, pools, pool vehicles and bookings, as well as for any reuse of already installed electronic car-sharing equipment. The system must support self-service access for users, comprehensive administration and reporting functions for FMI, as well as technical support and a round-the-clock manned helpdesk. The contract runs for 72 months from signature. The contract may be extended on the same terms by up to 2 times 24 months. It is a requirement that the development period must have a maximum duration of 6 months and that the implementation period must have a maximum duration of 6 months. The current system handles approx. 25.000 users and 2.800 pool vehicles. During the contract period, the solution is as a starting point expected to be able to handle up to approx. 5.000 pool vehicles. In view of the uncertain international security policy situation, however, the Danish Defence has a need for an option to be able to scale the solution so that the application and the associated infrastructure can, upon the customer's request, be expanded to handle up to 10.000 pool vehicles without impairment of functionality, response times, availability or the other requirements and service levels set out in the contract. In addition, the contract includes an option regarding the choice of access technology for the pool vehicles, whereby the customer, instead of using the Danish Defence's existing access carriers (RFID etc.), can choose an access and locking system supplied by the supplier on the terms set out in the requirements specification and the contract.
sig_22950ad748b46de96910.title: Tender for a contract regarding the supply, operation, maintenance, support, and further development of an internet-based booking system for the Danish Defence's pool vehicles
