sig_22ef79c3fb93659935ec.description: In order to protect Statens IT (Ordering Party) against current and future cyber threats, the Ordering Party uses a number of security technologies, including an Extended Detection and Response (XDR) platform. The XDR platform supports the collection, correlation and analysis of security-related incidents across the Ordering Party's IT environment in order to protect systems, services and data, as well as to ensure the confidentiality, integrity and availability of the data. In view of this, the Ordering Party is tendering a contract whose purpose is to support and strengthen the Ordering Party's own operational IT security through the provision of a Managed Detection and Response (MDR) service from a Security Operations Center (SOC). The MDR service must use and supplement the Ordering Party's XDR platform with round-the-clock monitoring, analysis, detection, validation, escalation and handling of security incidents. The service must be delivered 24 hours a day, 365 days a year, and contribute to the rapid identification, assessment and handling of cyber threats and security incidents. The services constitute an essential element in the Ordering Party's ongoing maturation and development process in the field of cybersecurity with a focus on technology, processes, competencies and collaboration across internal and external stakeholders. Through the procurement, the Ordering Party wishes to gain access to a professional MDR service that can meet the Ordering Party's high demands for quality, robustness and efficiency, as well as a supplier that can continuously engage in dialogue with the Ordering Party on developments within cybersecurity, including the threat picture, technological opportunities, automation, competence development and ongoing improvements to the security level. The supplier must carry out a technical, organisational and procedural Transition In, which ensures that the ongoing MDR services can be delivered from the transition to the operational phase. The Ordering Party draws attention to the fact that the Ordering Party has concluded a contract with two (2) suppliers to handle the Ordering Party's existing XDR platform, with whom the supplier must cooperate in connection with Transition In. As part of this, the supplier must establish and configure the necessary integrations between the Ordering Party's XDR platform and other relevant security sources, as well as the supplier's tools and platforms used for the fulfilment of the contract. The supplier must deliver Ongoing MDR Services; including continuous monitoring, analysis, correlation, validation and detection of alarms and security incidents. The supplier must carry out triage and qualification of alarms in order to identify actual security incidents and ensure timely escalation and notification in accordance with agreed processes and service levels. These ongoing MDR services include: • Continuous SOC monitoring of security-related incidents and alarms. • Analysis, correlation and qualification of incidents across relevant data sources. • Identification, detection and validation of security incidents. • Preparation, implementation and ongoing optimisation of detection rules, use cases and analysis models. • Application of relevant Threat Intelligence to support the detection and analysis work. • Ongoing assessment of the threat picture and its relevance to the Ordering Party's environment. • Proactive identification of potential security incidents and security risks, including through Threat Hunting activities. • Escalation, notification and reporting of security incidents in accordance with agreed processes and service levels. • Maintenance of existing integrations and establishment of new integrations as needed. • Optimisation and further development of the Ordering Party's XDR platform and other security solutions. • Advice regarding the development and maturation of the Ordering Party's security organisation, security processes and governance. • Execution of targeted Threat Hunting courses and analyses of suspicious activities. • Incident Response assistance in the event of security incidents upon requisition from the Ordering Party, including analysis, delimitation, handling, remediation and recovery. • Assistance during major security incidents, cyber crises and coordination with relevant stakeholders. • Security-related advice and strategic sparring on developments within cybersecurity. The contract also includes cross-cutting services, including documentation, reporting, governance, quality assurance and information security, which are delivered throughout the contract period. Furthermore, the contract includes obligations upon contract termination (Transition Out), which must ensure a controlled, secure and documented transfer of knowledge, data, processes, integrations and other contract-related deliverables to the Ordering Party or a subsequent supplier.
sig_22ef79c3fb93659935ec.title: Managed Detection and Response (MDR)

sig_23103fc3ebc0597973b3.description: The project includes the supply and installation of equipment for the creation of a national electronic citizen authentication system compliant with the highest security standards and compatible with the European Regulation (eIDAS 2.0) and the European Digital Identity Regulation, which will offer an advanced set of authentication services. Additionally, it includes the creation of a central Citizen Identity Hub and the infrastructure for providing qualified electronic signature certificates to Greek citizens. Overall, the offered system must be able to successfully serve the entire production-issuance cycle (collection of supporting documents and biometric data, management of applications and data, personalisation of security documents, quality control of personalised documents) of security documents. The Contracting Authority considers the reasonable delivery deadline for the Integrated Security Documents Information System, its related implementation services, as well as the digital identity and authentication services (hereinafter “Main Project”), to be the period of 18 months. Within the framework of the Main Project, the Contractor must implement and deliver the following: Implementation Study, Delivery of Project Equipment and ready-to-use Software, Implementation services for development - operational environment and development, Integration Services, Trial migration and Acceptance Testing period, Training, Trial Operation Period. After the final delivery and acceptance of the Main Project, the operation and maintenance period of ten (10) years begins, during which the contractor will provide the following services: - Operation and maintenance of the system - On site support - Telecommunications services - Supply of other consumable materials (envelopes, barcode labels, cardboard boxes). - Supply and Personalisation of security documents. Specifically: Period A (3 years): During the first three (3) years from the final acceptance of the Main Project, the contracting authority will procure 6.420.000 security documents of type ID1 and 1.050.000 security documents of type ID3. Period B (7 years): During the remaining seven (7) years of the contract duration, the contracting authority will procure up to 32.580.000 security documents of type ID1 and up to 7.150.000 of type ID3, according to its needs. At the same time, it will be able to personalise other security documents (format ID-1, ID-3) in case it is required in the future. At any time during the operation and maintenance period, following a decision by the Contracting Authority, an option may be exercised with the object of: a) extending the provision of the operation and maintenance period services for an additional period of up to 5 years in total, from its original expiry date, and/or b) extending the duration of the supply and personalisation services for security documents until the quantities of the contract are exhausted and, in any case, not beyond five (5) years from the original expiry date of the operation and maintenance period. The option may be exercised by a unilateral declaration of the contracting authority to the contractor once or more times for a minimum period of one (1) year and a maximum of five (5) years.
sig_23103fc3ebc0597973b3.title: Supply of a new Integrated Security Documents Information System (O.P.S.E.A.), for the printing – personalisation of security documents, including the new Hellenic Police Identity Card - Citizen Card, with the related E-Government services

sig_232475129d1df2071ec3.description: The EU tender concerns a contract for the provision of a payment gateway/payment window as well as the acquiring and processing of payments from citizens and businesses. The payment gateway/payment window is understood as the payment page that the payer will encounter in the payment situation. It is also here that the integrations from the specialist systems that are to use the payment solution will go. The payment gateway/payment window is responsible for the integration to the offered payment products. The tender includes payments with international payment cards and open banking, etc. International payment cards are basically understood as payment cards of the Visa or Mastercard type. The tender also includes payment via so-called wallets, including MobilePay. Finally, payments based on "open banking" will also be part of the tender. Payments with Dankort will also have to use the payment gateway/payment window. Acquiring of Dankort is, however, not covered by the tender. In principle, the tender only covers single payments and not so-called recurring payments, i.e. payments that take place in accordance with a payment agreement at a fixed interval and typically with approximately the same amount each time. It is, however, included as a possibility that the payment gateway/payment window in the future will be used for recurring payments based on payment cards.
sig_232475129d1df2071ec3.title: Tender for payment gateway/payment window as well as payments with international payment cards and open banking, etc.

sig_235a502906ce9de990f9.description: This notice is a prior information notice regarding a forthcoming procurement of service design expert services by the City of Tampere. The purpose of the notice is to inform the market of the upcoming procurement and to invite operators to participate in market consultation. This notice does not constitute a call for tenders. The City of Tampere has had framework arrangements for service design expert services in place during 2014–2017, 2018–2022 and 2023–2026. The city plans to establish a new framework arrangement for the years 2027–2030 upon the expiry of the current contract period on 12/2026. The City of Tampere has a need for service design expert services across many different development targets. The contract will be widely used by almost all city units. In the years 2023-2025 the combined annual value of orders has been approximately 400 000 €. We invite operators interested in the procurement to participate in market consultation, the purpose of which is to discuss the procurement object, its definition and preliminary plans. The views of potential tenderers are very important to us in preparing the procurement, and we are happy to hear new ideas regarding both the content of the procurement and its implementation method. We welcome views on, among other things: • preliminary lot division • service description • minimum requirements • quality evaluation criteria Companies registered for the market consultation will be invited to an event held via Teams on Wednesday 11.3.2026 at 13:30-14:50, where plans related to the procurement will be presented. Questions and comments concerning the procurement may also be raised at the event. Operators interested in the procurement are requested to register by Mon 9.3 at 16:00. sig_2366bcd26f0a92db294b.description: HUS (hereinafter also referred to as the Contracting Authority or Client) requests to participate in the procurement of imaging solution and related services. The procurement will be carried out through a competitive dialogue procedure (see Annex 1 Description of the Procedure). The object of the procurement is imaging solution and related services. This procurement concerns the Picture Archiving and Communication System (PACS), which is intended to be replaced with a new solution. The solution entity may also include functionalities of a Radiology Information System (RIS), an artificial intelligence (AI) platform designed to support the achievement of the objectives, and functionalities related to appointment booking/scheduling, as well as a speech recognition solution. The objective is to ensure that the service path between appointment booking system, the radiological information system (RIS), and the picture archiving and communication system (PACS) operates optimally. The aim is to develop customer experience based on a unified service model. The objective is to provide patients with more efficient diagnostics and good care also in the future. In addition, the objective is to reduce the manual and overlapping work. The imaging solution must enable smooth workflows for all user groups and support the development of processes to improve productivity. The deployment project may include the migration of images, image metadata, and RIS data from the Client’s current PACS system. The service includes support and maintenance activities and may also include 1 level support provided by the Supplier. The objective is also to explore solutions for scalability regarding a joint archiving solution for digital pathology and imaging. A more detailed description of the current state, the solution to be procured, and the services included in the procurement can be found in Annex 2 Current and target state description of imaging systems. Please also take into account the other annexes to the request to participate (Annexes 2.1–2.6, and 4), which provide additional information on the current and target state. These annexes are not binding on the Contracting Authority in the later stages of the procurement procedure and may be subject to change during the negotiations. If the documents have been drawn up in both Finnish and English, in the event of conflict of interpretation, the Finnish text shall prevail. The request for participation, along with all related documentation and any clarifying questions, must be submitted in Finnish or English in accordance with the instructions provided in the request to participate. sig_23789b5d84af3c7a2046.description: SKI hereby offers a dynamic purchasing system (hereinafter the System) regarding the procurement of servers and storage. It is voluntary for all of SKI's customers, as listed in Annex B Customer List, to make use of the System when they need to procure servers and storage. The System comprises two procurement categories: • Category 1 Supplementary purchases • Category 2 Solution purchases The content of the categories is described in more detail in Annex C The System's subject matter. The System's subject matter, as defined via the product and service areas, cf. Annex C, is identical in both categories, which means that the same products and services can be procured in both category 1 and category 2. The categories differ by the nature of the need that a specific procurement must meet, and thus not necessarily by the subject of the procurement as such. Category 1 must be used when a Customer has a specific need to supplement or expand their existing solution. Category 2 must be used when a Customer has a need to procure a new overall solution that is not based on an existing installation. Category 1 must be used when a Customer has a specific need to supplement or expand their existing solution. If there is already an established solution, and the procurement must be adapted to this both functionally and technically, the need falls under category 1. It includes components or units that must function together with the existing solution, without changes occurring in the solution's overall architecture. This may, for example, be the purchase of more CPUs or more storage capacity of a technology that the Customer already has. Similarly for network equipment, where there may, for example, be the establishment of rack capacity, cooling, emergency power, licences, etc.; Category 2 must be used when a Customer has a need to procure a new overall solution that is not based on an existing installation. This applies to both simple and complex solutions, including the establishment of a data centre solution, regardless of whether the solution subsequently must function together with or be integrated into one or more existing solutions, and where the tenderer must design, describe and deliver the full solution. This may, for example, be an overall expansion of a data centre's capacity or an overall purchase to support a new specific task in the data centre, e.g. a particularly heavy calculation task (weather models) or a task that requires a special technology (e.g. AI, which requires large GPU capacity).

sig_23e920630a744f4942a8.description:
SKI hereby establishes a dynamic purchasing system for standard software and related services (02.06 Standard Software). The system comprises two purchasing categories: Category 1 – Simple Solution and Category 2 – Complex Solution. The system may be used to procure the following service areas: 1) Standard Software 2) Support and maintenance agreements 3) Installation/implementation and/or configuration 4) Training 5) Consultancy Standard software is defined as software that is prefabricated and commercially available. Standard software is also referred to as COTS (Commercial Off The Shelf). A more detailed definition of the nature of the software is set out in Appendix C, which also includes a more detailed description of the 5 service areas. All 5 service areas may be procured in both categories. The difference between the two categories lies in a differentiation in the customer's need for tenders for the solution. Category 1 is used when the customer has a precisely specified purchasing need / standard purchase, where the customer has defined the solution prior to the purchase and solely wishes to receive tenders for this solution from suppliers. The customer evaluates solely on price, cf. point 14.1 of the tendering conditions. Category 2 is used for specialised and complex solution purchases, where the customer has a need for the supplier to define the solution based on the customer's described needs, and where a need thereby arises to evaluate the quality of the suppliers' various offered solutions. In Category 2, evaluation is based on both price and the suppliers' offered solutions (quality), cf. point 14.2 of the tendering conditions. In both categories of the system, standard software and related services, as delimited by the 5 service areas above, may be procured within the following functional areas: 1. Applications - 1 Customer Experience and Relationship Management (CRM) - 2 Enterprise Resource Planning (ERP) - 3 Supply Chain Management (SCM) - 4 Project and Portfolio Management - 5 E-mail and Authoring - 6 Content Services - 7 Other Application Software 2. Application Platforms - 1 Application Infrastructure and Middleware - 2 Data Management - 3 Analytics and Business Intelligence 3. Infrastructure Software - 1 Operating Systems - 2 Storage Management - 3 Virtualization Infrastructure - 4 Other Infrastructure Software 4. Development and Operations Tools - 1 Application Development - 2 IT Operations 5. IT Security Software - 1 Security Appendix D, Overview of functional standard software areas, describes in more detail which functional areas of software and services linked to these functional standard software areas are included in the service areas 1-5. It is voluntary for all SKI customers, as shown in the published customer list, to make use of the System when they are to procure standard software or related services. The customer list in Appendix B.1 specifies the customers and their organisations that are customers of SKI at the time of tender and can thus use the system. However, the dynamic purchasing system may, throughout the term of the system, be used by all contracting authorities that are customers of SKI at the time of publication of a specific purchase in the system. All parts of the Danish state, regions and municipalities – including public companies and publicly owned companies subject to the obligation to tender as a result of their public ownership – can become customers of SKI by taking out a subscription covering their organisation. When new contracting authorities become customers of SKI, SKI will update the customer list on SKI.dk and announce on SKI.dk that a change has been made to SKI's customer list, as well as which contracting authorities are new customers of SKI and from what date these can publish purchases in the system. The customer list in Appendix B.1 is not updated after the time of tender. Instead, SKI's customer list valid at any given time will be publicly available on SKI.dk. Special attention is drawn to the fact that KL and the Ministry of Finance in the "Agreement on municipal finances for 2026" have agreed that 4-5 inter-municipal IT service organisations are to be established, which are to handle various tasks and establish solutions in the IT field for the participating municipalities. It appears from the agreement: "There is [...] agreement that the municipalities will, no later than d. 1. January 2027, establish themselves in new inter-municipal partnerships in the form of 4-5 municipal IT service organisations with a geographical starting point in the four regions. The new IT service organisations will be established as municipal units and will before the end of 2027 take over the municipalities' operation of server and network infrastructure. The parties have a shared ambition that the units will subsequently also gradually take over the operation of user management and monitoring, PCs and other end-user equipment as well as service desk and support leading up to 2030 and will continuously discuss the progress of the work." These inter-municipal IT service organisations are to be considered customers of SKI from the time they are established as an independent legal entity and will thereafter be able to use the system for specific purchases published in the system after their establishment. At the time of tender, the inter-municipal IT service organisations appear in Appendix B.1 Customer List with the designations [It-Service Nord], [It-Service Midt], [It-Service Syd], [It-Service Øst] and [It-Service Hovedstaden]. These designations will be updated according to the process stated in the foregoing when the units have been established. Whether 4 or 5 IT service organisations are established does not affect the fact that the total group of participants across the IT service organisations, i.e. the municipalities, is the same. Like all the other customers in the system, the inter-municipal IT service organisations have a right – but not an obligation – to use the system. Category 1 - Simple Solution Is used when the customer has a precisely specified purchasing need / standard purchase, where the customer has defined the solution prior to the purchase and solely wishes to receive tenders for this solution from suppliers.;

Category 2 – Complex Solution Is used for specialised and complex solution purchases, where the customer has a need for the supplier to define the solution based on the customer's described needs, and where a need thereby arises to evaluate the quality of the suppliers' various offered solutions.

sig_2453dc705bb5a4bd32f4.buyer_name: City of Helsinki, Urban Environment Division
sig_2453dc705bb5a4bd32f4.description: The Urban Environment Division of the City of Helsinki (hereinafter "Contracting Authority") is requesting requests to participate in a dynamic purchasing system (DPS) to be established for the procurement of digital twin platforms. The Contracting Authority uses digital twin services to make official operations and citizens' participation more efficient. Digital twin platforms are used in use-case-specific pilot projects of agile development in the Urban Environment as well as in production solutions. The platforms are intended to be able to combine and visualise data from various sources, such as e.g. city information model data, building and infrastructure information models, point cloud data and basic data of the built environment. The objective is to utilise the industry's best platforms and resources in creating services. Digital twin services are being developed for internal use in the urban environment for stakeholders, for official use, and for citizens. Some of the services will probably contain confidential official information and will only be accessible by authorities, which must be taken into account in their implementation. This contract notice establishes a dynamic purchasing system. The dynamic purchasing system is in two stages. In the first stage, service providers apply to join the purchasing system by submitting a request to participate. All candidates fulfilling the suitability requirements will be admitted to the dynamic purchasing system. In the second stage, the contracting authority makes procurements as procurements internal to the established dynamic purchasing system and selects, on the basis of the internal competition, the platform solution best suited to each use case. Admission to the dynamic purchasing system is not binding on the candidate. The candidate may choose which competitions organised within the system it participates in. Requests to participate may be submitted to the dynamic purchasing system throughout its duration. The dynamic purchasing system is valid for eight (8) years. The content of the dynamic purchasing system and the implementation of procurements are described in more detail in the appendix documents. The estimated value of the dynamic purchasing system is a total of approximately 2,3 million euros.
sig_2453dc705bb5a4bd32f4.title: Dynamic purchasing system (DPS) for digital twin platforms

sig_25691773fadd0d99dd05.description: Gloucestershire ICB and Bristol, North Somerset and South Gloucestershire (BNSSG) ICB are merging to form a single integrated body in April 2027. Both organisations currently rely on external providers for the delivery of their IT services. A new, unified service model is required; one that supports the merged organisation from day one, is commercially sustainable, and is capable of evolving as the ICS matures. Six principles shape the design of the future service: 1. Cloud-first and 'secure by design'. All new and renewed services will be cloud-based wherever possible. On-premises infrastructure will be exited as part of transition. This is both a strategic choice and a compliance requirement under the Government Cloud First Policy and Technology Code of Practice. 2. Outcome-focused. The service is defined by what it must deliver, not how it must be delivered. The supplier is expected to bring expertise, innovation and accountability for outcomes, not simply execute a prescriptive technical specification. 3. Single point of accountability. The preferred model is a single managed service provider with end-to-end accountability for operational delivery. This avoids the fragmentation and unclear ownership that characterises the current multi-supplier landscape and reduces the management overhead on the ICB digital team. 4. Lean governance. The ICB digital team will provide strategic oversight, roadmap ownership and supplier governance. It will not carry operational delivery responsibilities. This reflects the lean, strategically focused character of the merged organisation and the direction set by the Model ICB Blueprint. 5. Interoperable by design. The service must integrate cleanly with nationally contracted NHS platforms, in particular NHS.net Connect, the Health and Social Care Network (HSCN) and NHS Secure Boundary Service, as well as local platforms, such as the Gloucestershire ICS WAN and into UHBW and Crown Datacentres in Corsham. Service interfaces with these platforms should be clearly defined before the procurement specification is finalised. 6. Sustainable. The ICB's carbon neutral commitments should be reflected in technology choices, including energy-efficient end-user devices, PoE-powered monitors and cloud-based infrastructure in preference to on-premises data centre equipment. The following service stacks are in scope for the new managed service, reflecting services currently provided across both incumbents, consolidated and extended to support the merged organisation: - Service desk. The primary user-facing support channel, available 08:00-18:00 Monday to Friday. - Desktop support. Onsite presence at both sites as and when required, including end-user support, moves, adds and changes to desktop arrangements, MFD, Audio Visual equipment, and Teams Room management. The onsite support model must include provision for routine physical tasks including WFH equipment management, peripheral replacement, cable and hardware swap-outs, and stock management. - End-user compute. Device lifecycle management including provisioning, refresh (five-year target cycle), configuration, and secure disposal. - Telephony and unified communications. Microsoft Teams Phone as the unified platform for the merged ICB. - Print. Cloud-managed secure print at both sites. - Meeting rooms. Physical teams Room management and audio-visual support at 2 locations with 15 meeting rooms at one and at Shire Hall, Gloucester and 9 at the second location. - Asset management. Asset tagging, recording, and lifecycle tracking for all ICB-owned IT equipment. - Supplier and procurement management. The supplier will assume management of all ongoing third-party technology relationships and will procure all IT equipment and recurring support contracts on behalf of the ICB. Licence management across the estate is required. - DSPT support. The supplier is expected to provide the ICB with the technical evidence and assurance data required to support annual DSPT submission, including patch management records, asset inventory, access control logs and incident reports. - Project, change and architecture. The supplier will own project and change management, problem management, and architecture design. - Digital signatures. Digital signature capability is required as part of the new service. Full details are provided in the service specification. The total maximum contract value for the initial 3-year Contract is £1,920,000 inclusive of VAT (where applicable). At the end of the initial contract term the Commissioner will have two, separate, consecutive one-year extension option periods that can be exercised at the discretion of the Commissioner, giving a maximum possible contract value of £2,700,000 inclusive of VAT (where applicable) over 5 years if the full contract term is fulfilled. The Commissioner is of the view that TUPE does not apply to this service. The Contracting Authority reserves the right to use the Direct Award procedure under the Procurement Act 2023 for any subsequent extensions or new contracts for similar requirements. The new contract will commence on 1st April 2027, although implementation of the services will start during January 2027. Lot 1: .

sig_25c6ee616eddbb076711.description: As part of its steering duty, the RIVM is responsible for the monitoring and evaluation of prenatal screening. This concerns the Non-Invasive Prenatal Test (NIPT) and the Structural Ultrasound Examination (SEO), including prior counselling. In this context, two national monitors (plus an English translation) are drawn up annually to monitor the quality and accessibility of this screening, identify bottlenecks (in the care chain), enable adjustments to be made, and also to account for performance to the commissioning party, the VWS, and the chain partners. Activities with the current supplier expire on 31 December 2026. A new agreement for the monitoring of PNS must be tendered by the contracting authority. Scope of the contract The contract concerns the performance of the annual national monitoring of NIPT-SEO based on established indicators. This consists of: 1. a monitor aggregated at the national level in Dutch and English; 2. a more detailed professionals monitor aggregated at the regional level in Dutch. Products from previous years can be found at Monitor | Prenatal and neonatal screenings (www.pns.nl). This also shows that the VWS monitor displays the general trend in recent years. The professionals monitor also addresses regional differences. Trends at the national level are also presented here. Duration of the agreement The aim of this European procurement procedure is to conclude a service agreement with a single contractor for the monitoring of PNS. The intended commencement date of the agreement to be concluded is 1 January 2027. The contracting authority wishes to conclude an agreement with the contractor for an initial period of four (4) years, with an additional three (3) times an option to extend by one (1) year. This results in a maximum term of the agreement of seven (7) years.
sig_25c6ee616eddbb076711.title: Prenatal Screening Monitor - Non-Invasive Prenatal Test (NIPT) and the structural ultrasound examination (SEO)

sig_260a7549f454066c9180.description: This public contract (VZ) will be implemented as part of the SLIM (Sustainable Landscape through Integrated Management) Project, which is being implemented by the Czech Development Agency from October 2023 to September 2027 and co-financed by the European Union and Sweden. Its aim is to introduce an integrated landscape management (ILM) approach and contribute to increasing the resilience of ecosystems and preserving biodiversity in Zambia using freely accessible satellite data in areas such as forestry, agriculture, water management, and environmental protection, including predicting and mitigating the destructive effects of natural disasters. This contract will specifically contribute to the implementation of the SLIM project activity entitled "Provision of adequate technological capacities, tools, data access, and geospatial data storage infrastructure for the crucial data domains." The subject of this contract is the supply, installation, and commissioning of server infrastructure required to support the SLIM project in Zambia. The contract will deliver two server environments, including related installation, configuration, baseline security settings, system testing, technical training, and final commissioning. The first part of the delivery covers a centralized GIS server environment installed at the National Remote Sensing Centre (NRSC). This environment consists of two physical servers, where one performance server is used for computationally intensive satellite data operations and one GIS server hosts virtual machines for ArcGIS Enterprise components and a PostgreSQL/PostGIS enterprise database. The solution also includes a disk array for backups and file storage, and a firewall, serving as a shared spatial data repository providing access, web services, and applications to multiple SLIM project stakeholders. The second part of the delivery covers an operational open-source GIS server environment for the Forestry Department (FD). This environment consists of one physical server hosting two virtual machines for database and web application services, a disk array, a UPS, a firewall, and a new rack cabinet. It will support internal forestry data management, web mapping applications, and future integration with field data collection systems. The subject matter of this contract is described in more detail in Annex No. 1 – "Supply Specification".
sig_260a7549f454066c9180.title: Supply and Deployment of Server Infrastructure for the SLIM Project

sig_267c5f44064b1be068ef.description: The purpose of this PIN is to inform market operators of a potential future exercise to procure services supporting the marketing and communications for a new nationwide programme to increase physical activity and reduce inactivity. Health Innovation North East and North Cumbria (HI NENC) is commissioning an agency partner to design and deliver the marketing, PR, and communications strategy for a national behaviour change programme designed to increase physical activity and reduce inactivity across England. The Programme responds directly to the Government's 10 Year Health Plan commitment to motivate millions to walk - and where possible run - regularly. Sir Brendan Foster has convened expert partners to support this. The Programme aims to reframe movement as personal, cumulative and achievable through the core proposition: The Programme is not a traditional sports campaign. It is a long-term national behaviour change movement designed to: - • Increase movement among inactive adults • Address health inequalities • Build a recognisable, inclusive national movement brand • Enable sustainable habit formation through digital tools and rewards • Advertising - including advertising investment to launch and sustain the campaign within the first year. The associated marketing campaign must inspire participation at scale, whilst remaining grounded in behavioural science and public health evidence. The appointed agency will be responsible for developing and delivering a full set of campaign materials, frameworks, strategies, activation plans, toolkits, digital assets, evaluation reports, and all content needed to deliver the programme end to end. This must be aligned to the overall narrative framework. This will include planning major PR and press moments, building momentum towards launch dates and engaging with key stakeholders to strengthen partnerships. Additional information: HI NENC would like to invite potential providers of Marketing and Communications services to apply to our Dynamic Purchasing System (DPS) DN670401 as a supplier. You can do this by following this link: https://procontract.due-north.com/SupplierPostLoginHome/ActivityDashboard?projectId=c1881153-e6f3-ed11-8122-005056b64545&callingPage=Home This opportunity will be developed as a further competition under Lot 5 of our DPS. You should therefore ensure you apply to Lot 5 to be able to bid to provide this service. You are also welcome to apply for any other Lots on our DPS that you feel are relevant to your organisation. We are expecting to put out the Invitation to Quote (ITQ) to our Lot 5 suppliers by the end of March 2026. This timeline is subject to change. Interested suppliers are advised to apply to the DPS promptly to ensure they have been accepted to the framework and receive the competition notification. Failure to be accepted to the framework ahead of the ITQ publication will mean that you will be unable to bid to supply. This notice is for information and engaging with the supply market only. It is not a binding statement of intent or call for competition. HI NENC reserves the right not to enter a formal process and not award a contract. sig_26a98529eaa32684637e.description: The subject matter of this procurement comprises the procurement of a SaaS solution, which encompasses various functions and services. The focus is on the provision of an extensive digital communication solution based on OX 8. The MBJS is looking for an experienced contractor capable of providing a corresponding solution based on OX 8 while meeting the specific requirements and needs of a state-level solution for the State of Brandenburg regarding high security standards (BSI IT-Grundschutz), data protection compliance (GDPR), integrity, flexibility and scalability. Lot LOT-0001: Communication solution for 25.000 persons in the education sector (teacher mail). In the year 2019, on behalf of the Ministry for Education, Youth and Sport (hereinafter referred to as MBJS), a complex IT infrastructure was built based on the products Univention UCS and Univention UCS@School, consisting of a central identity management system, hereinafter referred to as IDM, and the groupware and email solution Open Xchange from the manufacturer of the same name, hereinafter referred to as OX. An extensive communication solution was created for 20.000 teaching staff at publicly maintained schools in the State of Brandenburg. The schools mapped in UCS and UCS@School in the form of separate school OUs form the basis for the contexts set up in OX. Each school is thus assigned to a separate context in OX. The creation, modification and deletion of accounts in the IDM are carried out via the specialist procedures developed by the MBJS. After several years of operation, due to the lifecycle of OX, it is necessary to transition to the current version 8. The transition to OX 8 requires extensive changes to the UCS OX connector and the IT infrastructure. The version OX 8 requires Docker runtime environments that are not provided by the existing IT infrastructure. It is not possible to simply update the software in the existing system. The MBJS therefore intends to have the groupware and email solution for teaching staff based on OX operated in future as a SaaS solution by a provider. In this context, the user accounts in the existing IDM shall continue to form the basis for the email mailboxes and the existing provisioning processes shall be retained. Only the mail stack of the existing IT infrastructure is to be replaced by a SaaS solution.
sig_26a98529eaa32684637e.title: Communication solution for 25.000 persons in the education sector (teacher mail)

sig_26e1b91d8504330c38df.description: This is not a contract notice or a call for tenders, but a request for information with which the contracting authority is conducting a market survey of potential tenderers and solutions available on the market for its procurement need. The information obtained through the market survey will be used in the preparation of the future procurement. Länsi-Uudenmaan hyvinvointialue (LUVN) has a need to procure technology to be taken home for the use of the wellbeing services county's residents, as well as an alarm system that receives the alarms produced by the aforementioned technology. Länsi-Uudenmaan hyvinvointialue is assembling and launching as its own operation a so-called Safety Assistance Service, the goal of which is to enable and support customers' independent coping in their own homes around the clock. A central element in the Safety Assistance Service is the technology utilised in it that is taken to homes or home-like services, and the receiving system for the alarms produced by them. With this request for information, LUVN wants to survey the technology solutions available on the market that are suitable for social and health care, that ensure the customer's safety at home, and solutions suitable for receiving alarms related to these. Länsi-Uudenmaan hyvinvointialue estimates that the procurement entity according to its needs will consist of the following parts, but changes may occur in the entity: - Technology installed at home for the customer's safety (e.g. sensors, detectors, wristbands) as well as their maintenance and backup device services - Safety alarm centre system and mobile software possibly related to it - Service implementation project - Continuous services, support, maintenance and service of the technology and alarm centre system - Expert services related to the aforementioned technology and its utilisation and use during the contract period according to the subscriber's need. To support the specification of its procurement needs, the planning of the procurement and the preparation of the tendering documents, Länsi-Uudenmaan hyvinvointialue wants to engage in a market dialogue with suppliers offering solutions corresponding to the procurement need. Through the market dialogue, the wellbeing services county hopes to receive information generally about solutions on the market corresponding to the object of the procurement. We are interested in your solutions and services related to safety technology supporting living at home and how the solutions direct alarms to the safety alarm receiving system and what features the receiving system includes. We also want to know what kind of information your system produces to support the planning of services offered to the customer for the professional, in addition to alarm information. Suppliers are requested to register for the market dialogue by email to the address: hankinta@luvn.fi Registration is requested to be sent by 3.10.2025 at 12. The registration should be titled as follows: “Kodin turvapalvelulaitteet ja hälytysten vastaanottojärjestelmä” (Home safety service devices and alarm receiving system). The content of the email message is sufficient to be the supplier's name and the contact details of the supplier's contact person. LUVN will be in contact with the contact persons of the suppliers who have registered to agree on the implementation of the market dialogue. According to the wellbeing services county's plans, the market dialogue should include both discussion sessions and the exchange of written material, but the exact schedule of the dialogue will be specified later. The subscriber reserves the possibility to organise one-to-one market dialogue discussions in addition to commenting on written material. The subscriber reserves the right to select a suitable number of Suppliers for one-to-one discussions based on the written responses. The times for the one-to-one discussions will be agreed separately with the Suppliers. The market survey notice does not oblige the contracting authority to carry out the actual procurement procedure. The description of the procurement and the estimated schedule of the procurement procedure as well as other information presented in the market survey notice are preliminary and indicative advance information. Responding or not responding by companies does not prevent participation in a possible procurement procedure. No compensation is paid for participation. The contracting authority will treat the information provided by the registered companies confidentially, and the names of the companies or other information will not be published.

sig_26fc285d05c35f03de8a.description: NHS Scotland intends to establish a national Framework Agreement for the provision of a Digital Diabetes Prevention and Primary Hypertension Programme. The programme will support individuals identified as being at risk of developing Type 2 Diabetes and/or those diagnosed with primary hypertension, through the delivery of evidence-based, digitally enabled lifestyle and behaviour change interventions. The Authority intends to appoint a single supplier to a national Framework Agreement. The procurement will be conducted using a Restricted Procedure, comprising a Selection Stage and an Invitation to Tender (ITT) stage. Suppliers will be shortlisted following evaluation of their suitability, technical and professional capability, capacity and relevant experience, with a maximum of five suppliers invited to submit a tender. Lot 1: . NHS Scotland intends to establish a national Framework Agreement for the provision of a Digital Diabetes Prevention and Primary Hypertension Programme. The Framework will support NHS Scotland's strategic objectives to improve population health outcomes, reduce health inequalities and support the prevention and management of long-term conditions through evidence-based, digitally enabled interventions. The requirement comprises a single integrated service with two pathways: - Digital Diabetes Prevention Programme (DDPP) for individuals identified as being at increased risk of developing Type 2 Diabetes; and - Primary Hypertension Programme (PHP) for individuals diagnosed with primary hypertension, supported through lifestyle and behaviour change interventions designed to improve health outcomes and reduce cardiovascular risk. The appointed Framework Participant will be required to deliver evidence-based, digitally enabled lifestyle and behaviour change interventions designed to support participants in achieving sustainable improvements in health behaviours and clinical outcomes. The service will utilise a digital platform/application supported by appropriately trained personnel, including health coaching and clinical governance arrangements, to facilitate participant engagement, self-management, education, monitoring and behaviour change. The service is expected to support a range of participant needs and will include, as appropriate, digital onboarding, risk assessment, lifestyle intervention, coaching support, educational resources, progress monitoring, outcome reporting and onward referral or escalation processes where clinically indicated. The Authority seeks a solution that is accessible, inclusive and capable of supporting diverse populations across Scotland, including individuals who may experience barriers to participation arising from geography, deprivation, language, disability or digital exclusion. The Framework Participant will be expected to work collaboratively with NHS Scotland, NHS Boards, Primary Care and other relevant stakeholders to support the promotion of the programme, participant recruitment and self-registration, service mobilisation, programme delivery, performance monitoring and continuous improvement. Current funding has been identified to support approximately 15,000 participants through the Diabetes Prevention pathway during the initial three-year term of the Framework Agreement. The Hypertension pathway is anticipated to support approximately 500 participants per annum. These figures are provided for information only and do not constitute a guarantee of volumes. The Authority reserves the right, subject to future funding availability and service requirements, to increase participant volumes and/or expand the scope of the Framework to include additional prevention cohorts, pathways, clinical indicators or service requirements that are closely aligned to the subject matter of the Framework Agreement. The Authority intends to appoint a single supplier to a national Framework Agreement. The procurement will be conducted using a Restricted Procedure. Suppliers will first be assessed at Selection Stage through completion of the Single Procurement Document (SPD) and Pre-Qualification Questionnaire (PQQ), which will assess suitability, technical and professional capability, capacity and relevant experience. A maximum of five suppliers will be shortlisted and invited to participate in the Invitation to Tender stage.
sig_26fc285d05c35f03de8a.title: Digital Diabetes Prevention and Primary Hypertension Programme

sig_2792874424dbe87cff07.description: The aim of the commission is the identification and assessment of dependencies of Germany/German companies in global supply chains. To this end, supply chain indices for various analytical purposes are to be developed in a first step (Module A). In a second step, national dependencies on trading partners are to be derived (Module B). The analytical framework is then to be expanded to include indirect dependencies (Module C) and supplemented by the assessment of actual vulnerabilities at the national level using suitable criteria (Module D). Based on the findings, an interactive (partially) visual IT-based representation suitable for analytical purposes is to be developed, which provides users with analytical functions across different levels of analysis and visualises them (Module E). Finally, dependencies and vulnerabilities at a disaggregated level are to be linked with supply, value-added and technology chains in order to be able to identify affected supply chains in scenarios and to consider impacts in a model-supported manner (Module F).
sig_2792874424dbe87cff07.title: National vulnerability analysis of international supply chains

sig_27944c4b719203d14292.description: The objective of the procurement is to enter into an agreement for the procurement of digital teaching aids and teaching resources for the Oslo School. The purchasing system has previously been announced on Doffin/TED and is being re-announced to continue the scheme in Oslo municipality ́s new KGV. See the attached qualification documentation for further information. The Oslo School has participated in a R&D project together with KS since 2017. the R&D project ends in its current form in summer 2024. In order to achieve autonomy and freedom of methodology in the choice of teaching aids, a use-based payment model is required where schools have access to all products and pay in arrears in arrears in accordance with actual use. Digital teaching aids and teaching resources consist of a market that is constantly developing. To a small degree, traditional approaches cover the schools ́need for flexible access to a wide range of teaching aids. The aim is also that an overall ecosystem shall make the procurement process of digital teaching aids and learning resources easier for school owners and more in line with the needs of the schools and pupils. The dynamic procurement scheme is for continuous delivery of digital teaching aids (freestanding or as part of teaching aids/learning universe), teaching resources, resource banks (news, pictures, movies, audio, music, etc.), teacher guides, teacher resources, assignment/trial collections and mapping tool with accompanying teacher overview, glosses, etc. that are delivered over the internet ("Software-as-a-service") for teaching purposes. The agreement also includes digital books and installed apps with Feide sign-in for teaching purposes. The diagnostic tool, which requires special competence to use, is not included. Digital services, which only have a functionality for delivering teaching aids that shall be physically implemented, are also not included. The agreement does not include the purchase of services that do not have Feide sign-in, including apps for iPads that are purchased via the App Store/Apple School Manager.
sig_27944c4b719203d14292.title: 1-UDE-2024 Dynamic procurement scheme for digital teaching aids in the Schools of Oslo (USE)

sig_281c9720188caf79b3db.description: Border to Coast wishes to procure sustainability and climate data services to support implementation of its Responsible Investment and Engagement Strategies, including portfolio risk management, investment decision-making, stewardship activities, external reporting and Partner Fund support. The required information and analytics will support the identification, assessment and management of sustainability-related risks and opportunities relevant to long-term investment performance. The scope of information required is expected to include sustainability metrics and assessments; controversy and conduct-related indicators; human rights and international norms data (including UN Global Compact-related information); information supporting the monitoring of exclusions; climate and net zero analytics; and data to support portfolio monitoring, stewardship activities, risk management and reporting requirements. The tender is currently expected to be structured across three Lots.Border to Coast recognises that no single provider may be able to meet all requirements and therefore reserves the right to appoint multiple providers, both across Lots and within individual Lots, where this delivers the most effective solution. Border to Coast may choose not to procure data in certain areas where relevant information is already available through existing provider relationships outside the scope of this contract. The solution should be provided under an enterprise-wide license, enabling access across multiple teams, including Responsible Investment, Research, Investment and Portfolio Risk. The required coverage spans a broad range of asset classes, including listed equities, corporate credit, sovereign credit, private markets and real estate. The contract is expected to support reporting and disclosure requirements across Border to Coast and its Partner Funds, including climate-related, stewardship and wider sustainability-related reporting. Certain headline sustainability and climate metrics will also need to be made available to Partner Funds through reporting processes. Partner Funds must be permitted to use relevant outputs and data for their own reporting, disclosure, stewardship and regulatory requirements. Appropriate redistribution rights within the Border to Coast partnership will therefore be required. The provider's operating model must be capable of integrating with Border to Coast's Investment Research and Data Platform, including BlackRock Aladdin, to support efficient data management, investment analysis, risk oversight and reporting activities. Providers should demonstrate an ability to support changing sustainability-related reporting requirements, market standards and regulatory frameworks over the life of the contract. Lot 1: Sustainability Data. Sustainability data (including): - Sustainability metrics and assessments; - Corporate accountability and governance data; - Human rights and international norms data; - Nature and biodiversity data; - Controversy and conduct-related data; and - Responsible Investment policy monitoring (including controversial weapons). Lot 2: Climate and transition data and analytics. Climate and transition data and analytics: - Emissions metrics; - Transition and net zero analytics; - Climate risk and scenario analysis; and - Climate resilience-related data. Lot 3: Sustainable bond and impact data. Sustainable bond and impact data: - Use of proceeds data; - Sustainable bond analytics; - Labelled bond data; - Impact measurement and reporting data; and - Data aligned to recognised impact frameworks
sig_281c9720188caf79b3db.title: Sustainability and Climate Data Services

sig_28949b4799d8edb1223e.description: Chiltern Railways is seeking to procure supplier-hosted software solutions and associated services to replace its existing Train Planning and Rostering systems. The procurement is divided into two Lots: Lot 1 - Train Planning System; and Lot 2 - Rostering System. Lot 1 is for the provision, implementation, hosting, support and maintenance of a Train Planning System. The solution is required to support train planning and diagramming activities, including the creation, import, editing, validation, management and publication of timetables, schedules, rolling stock diagrams and traincrew diagrams. The solution must support planning data management, timetable change management, scenario modelling, auditability, version control, reporting, user permissions and secure data exchange with relevant operational and business systems. Lot 2 is for the provision, implementation, hosting, support and maintenance of a Rostering System. The solution is required to support base, weekly and daily rostering for relevant staff groups, including traincrew, station staff and fleet/engineering staff. The solution must support roster creation, validation, publication and management, allocation of staff to duties, management of leave, overtime, shift swaps, fatigue and risk assessment, identification of uncovered turns and roster coverage gaps, employee self-service, reporting, auditability, user permissions and secure data exchange with relevant operational and business systems. For each Lot, the successful supplier will be required to provide a fully managed, vendor-hosted solution. This includes the software, hosting, configuration, implementation, data migration, integration, testing, training, change management, documentation, support, maintenance, updates, service management, information security, business continuity, disaster recovery, contract management and exit assistance required to deliver and operate the relevant solution. Bidders may participate in respect of Lot 1, Lot 2, or both Lots. Chiltern Railways may award Lot 1 and Lot 2 to different suppliers or may award both Lots to the same supplier in accordance with the procurement documents and award methodology. The estimated value of Lot 1 is £140,000 to £430,000 per annum and £1,000,000 to £3,000,000 over the full contract term, including any optional extension period. The estimated value of Lot 2 is £210,000 to £500,000 per annum and £1,500,000 to £3,500,000 over the full contract term, including any optional extension period. The estimated combined value of Lot 1 and Lot 2 is £2,500,000 to £6,500,000 excluding VAT over the full contract term, including any optional extension period. The estimated contract start date is 26 July 2027. The indicative operational go-live date is 1 March 2028, being the date from which the system is expected to start being rolled out and used by Chiltern Railways staff. The indicative implementation complete date is 30 June 2028, being the date by which the system is expected to be fully implemented, tested, accepted where applicable, ready for and/or used in live operational production, and to have completed dual running with the incumbent tools. The initial contract term is expected to be 60 months, with an option for Chiltern Railways to extend for a further period or periods of up to 24 months in total. Lot 1: Train Planning System. sig_293d60a574586a8b78e6.description: AI infrastructure components are being procured to expand the contracting authority's existing structure due to increased requirements resulting from project participation. Lot LOT-0001: AI Existing Infrastructure Extension - Project Racoon. 2.1 NVIDIA Deep Learning System DGX B300 Cluster - Lot 1 Required procurement of four NVIDIA DGX B300 systems for the efficient processing of computationally intensive AI issues (e.g. medical imaging, digital pathology, omics, and NLP). The system serves as central infrastructure and enables the flexible provision of GPU workstation environments for university partners in the RACOON joint project via advanced virtualization with DGX OS / NVIDIA Enterprise AI. The new systems integrate seamlessly into the existing management infrastructure, which is based on the NVIDIA Base Command Manager and NVIDIA Mission Control. This ensures highly efficient, consistent administration without additional familiarisation or migration effort for the operations team. Since all algorithms and AI models are based on the proprietary NVIDIA CUDA architecture, the system has no technical alternative; a transition to other architectures or APIs would be associated with a disproportionately high and economically unjustifiable effort. In addition, the existing GPU cluster management is built natively on this software stack. The selected Blackwell generation (B300) offers the only adequate performance class with 8x NVIDIA B300 GPUs, 2304 GB total memory, and a 800 Gbit/s InfiniBand connection. Furthermore, the enormous power density (10 U in the rack at max. 15,1 kW per system) guarantees resource-saving integration into the capacity-limited data centre. Lot LOT-0002: AI Existing Infrastructure Extension - Projects Athene. 2.2 NVIDIA GPU servers, network, and Spark cluster - Lot 2 The procurement serves to expand and optimize the existing infrastructure of the Research Compute Cluster (RCC) to meet the growing demand for high-performance resources for AI and data-intensive research applications. The NVIDIA DGX Spark systems enable the development, testing, and inference of AI models in the same NVIDIA software environment as the central GPU servers of the RCC. As a result, developed applications can be transferred to the higher-performance RCC resources without fundamental adaptations. The additional GPU server expands the central computing capacity of the RCC and is used in particular for medical AI, image analysis, genomics/metagenomics, as well as the training and inference of large AI models. Integration takes place into the existing Slurm-based infrastructure. To connect the additional components, the existing management and BMC network infrastructure is also expanded by a technically identical SuperMicro SSE-G3748R-SONIC. This ensures a uniform and operationally consistent infrastructure without establishing a separate network solution.
sig_293d60a574586a8b78e6.title: AI Existing Infrastructure Extension - Projects Racoon & Athene

sig_295c2cc6d2cf6fcac330.description: Development of 3D Models for Nuclear Facilities. The International Atomic Energy Agency (IAEA) maintains its ability to verify the nuclear programmes of non-nuclear weapon State (NNWS), including the capability to rapidly respond to any significant changes required for the implementation of safeguards-related activities in the field. As one part of its longer-term preparedness activities to date, the Department of Safeguards has already been able to acquire and demonstrate a limited technical capability in using Virtual Reality (VR) navigation inside real-world 3D scans, including the ability to attach relevant geobased data sources to 2D optical imagery. Lessons learned from previous VR projects have already been applied in the development of the current capability. However, to be more effective in its ability to rapidly respond to potentially significant changes in the short term, there is a need for the Department of Safeguards to develop 3D models of a number of very specific critical facilities. As part of its long term preparedness activities, the Department of Safeguards needs to develop the ability to develop and use 3D and Virtual Reality (VR) models for training, analysis and knowledge management. This task will support the creation of models for a number of different nuclear facilities and sites, in close consultation with IAEA experts and inspectors. The 3D models will provide tangible benefits in terms of knowledge management and implementation of safeguards. This will include the training/familiarization of inspectors who may have limited experience of the specific processes at the selected critical nuclear facilities and implementation of safeguards therein. The activity within this task is highly specialised, requiring significant technical knowledge and capabilities with advanced state-of-the-art 3D modelling technology. The proposed contractor must have experience of developing 3D models and resources similar to the facilities of interest. In addition, models must have the capability of being integrated with relevant IAEA Safeguards IT architecture, standards, policies and procedures. The proposed contractor must demonstrable experience of working with the nuclear sector. The specific target for the research is considered sensitive and, therefore suppliers must meet the minimum security requirements to handle, OFFICIAL SENSITIVE information. Lot 1: .
sig_295c2cc6d2cf6fcac330.title: Modelling of Critical Nuclear Facilities

sig_29714e9c55d9c6aac73c.description: The subject matter of this contract is: "Implementation of integration of the Information System for Management and Maintenance of the Public Register under the Environmental Liability Prevention and Remedying Act (ISMMPR under ELPRA), including migration of existing data, with the identified information systems of bodies under Article 16, paragraph 1 of ELPRA" The main objective of the project is the integration of the ISMMPR under ELPRA with other information systems (IS), both within the Ministry of Environment and Water (MoEW) and with external systems maintained by other state bodies. Main aspects of the subject matter of the contract: Analysis of existing information systems: • The project includes validating the analysis of the designated information systems of executive power bodies under Article 16, paragraph 1 of ELPRA for their integration into the ISMMPR under ELPRA and their functionalities that can be integrated with the ISMMPR under ELPRA. This validation of the analysis aims to determine the electronic nomenclatures in these systems, as well as the possibilities for copy-pasting existing data. Integration requirements: • The contract covers the definition of architectural and functional requirements for the integration of the systems, including automated data exchange between the ISMMPR under ELPRA and other registers of administrative bodies, as well as the maintenance of compatibility with information systems outside the MoEW. • Integration of the ISMMPR under ELPRA with information systems of executive power bodies under Article 16 of ELPRA, in accordance with the Ordinance on the Public Register of Operators Performing Activities under Annex No 1 to Article 3, item 1 of the Environmental Liability Prevention and Remedying Act and Guidelines on the provision of information for entry in the public register of operators performing the activities under Annex No 1 to Article 3, item 1 of ELPRA, including: • Validating the identified information systems of the executive power bodies under Article 16, paragraph 1 of ELPRA and their integration into the ISMMPR under ELPRA for data, as well as providing new functionalities for connecting the systems. Improvement of the public register under ELPRA: • The project provides for the modernisation and upgrading of the ISMMPR under ELPRA with the aim of ensuring centralised access to data and greater interoperability with other systems, while maintaining high information security and eliminating duplicate data. Maintenance services: • Information on the maintenance services of the integrated systems will be provided, including updating and monitoring of their operation. Compliance with regulatory requirements: • The requirements of the contract are aligned with the regulatory framework of the Electronic Governance Act (EGA) and subordinate legislation, as well as with the business analysis that establishes additional requirements for the implementation of the project. The subject matter of the contract covers the development and deployment of effective integration of information systems, ensuring interoperability between registers and systems maintained by various state administration bodies, and guaranteeing the proper functioning of the ISMMPR under ELPRA, in accordance with the requirements of ELPRA. Scope: The described objectives are achieved through the implementation of the following main stages: 1. Data and requirements analysis; 2. Preparation of a system design; 3. Development of the software solution; 4. Testing; 5. Deployment; 6. Training; 7. Warranty support. Project activities: Activity 1: Design; Activity 2: Integration/Construction.

sig_297cba6376cc721dae63.description: The National Institutes of Health (NIH) intends to award a Firm-Fixed-Price Purchase Order to Thomas Jefferson University to Obtain Clinical Cohort of Patients with Associated Clinical Outcomes, Radiologic Images, and Associated De-Identified Radiology Reports. In accordance with FAR 6.302-1, Only One Responsible Source and No Other Services Will Satisfy Agency Requirements, The requested clinical cohorts, radiographic imaging datasets, clinical outcomes data, and de-identified radiology reports are required to support artificial intelligence-based research focused on evaluating liver cancer risk in patients with cirrhosis and indeterminate liver lesions. The research requires datasets that combine specific patient populations with associated imaging studies and clinical outcomes information to enable the development, validation, and evaluation of predictive models. Alternative datasets that do not include the required patient populations, imaging data, clinical outcomes information, and associated radiology reports would not provide the information necessary to support the approved research objectives. The absence of any of these data elements would limit the ability to correlate imaging findings with clinical outcomes and would reduce the scientific validity and reliability of the resulting analyses. Therefore, only datasets containing the required clinical cohorts and associated imaging and outcomes data will satisfy the Government's minimum needs and support the approved research objectives. The objectives of the maintenance agreement are as follows: The objective of this requirement is to acquire clinical patient cohorts, associated imaging data, clinical outcomes data, and de-identified radiology reports to support the development and evaluation of A.I. models for liver disease and liver cancer research conducted by the Liver Diseases Branch. A determination by the Government to compete this proposed acquisition based upon responses received to this notice is solely within the discretion of the Government. The proposed contractor maintains an existing cohort of patients with cirrhosis and associated radiographic images collected at six-month intervals, as well as an existing cohort of patients with cirrhosis and indeterminate liver lesions, including associated clinical outcomes data and radiographic images. These clinical cohorts and associated datasets represent a unique research resource available through the proposed contractor. The combination of longitudinal imaging data, clinical outcomes data, and radiographic images associated with these patient populations is available only through the proposed contractor. As a result, only the proposed contractor can provide the requested deliverables necessary to support the research project. It is anticipated that an award will be issued approximately five (5) calendar days after the closing date of this notice, unless the Government determines that another vendor has the capability to meet this requirement. Please submit responses electronically to davisroshonna@mail.nih.gov no later than 9:00 a.m. EDT on September 25, 2026. Please reference Notice No. 75N98026Q01240 in the subject line of the response.
sig_297cba6376cc721dae63.title: Obtain Clinical Cohort of Patients with Associated Clinical Outcomes, Radiologic Images, and Associated De-Identified Radiology Reports

sig_29f1d86e081e4bd7b62b.description: Revolutionizing Engineering Departments (hereinafter referred to as RED) is designed to build upon previous efforts in engineering education research. Specifically, previous and ongoing evaluations of the NSF Engineering Education and Centers Division program and its predecessors, as well as those related programs in the Directorate for STEM Education, have shown that prior investments have significantly improved the first year of engineering students’ experiences, incorporating engineering material, active learning approaches, design instruction, and a broad introduction to professional skills and a sense of professional practice – giving students an idea of what it means to become an engineer. Similarly, the senior year has seen notable change through capstone design experiences, which ask students to synthesize the technical knowledge, skills, and abilities they have gained with professional capacities, using reflective judgment to make decisions and communicate these effectively. However, this ideal of the senior year has not yet been fully realized, because many of the competencies required in capstone design, or required of professional engineers, are only partially introduced in the first year and not carried forward with significant emphasis through the sophomore and junior years. The Directorates for Engineering (ENG) and STEM Education (EDU) are funding projects as part of the RED program, in alignment with the Improving Undergraduate STEM Education (IUSE) framework and Professional Formation of Engineers (PFE) initiative. These projects are designing revolutionary new approaches to engineering education, ranging from changing the canon of engineering to fundamentally altering the way courses are structured to creating new departmental structures and educational collaborations with industry. A common thread across these projects is a focus on organizational and cultural change within the departments, involving students, faculty, staff, and industry in rethinking what it means to provide an engineering program. In order to continue to catalyze revolutionary approaches, while expanding the reach of those that have proved efficacious in particular contexts, the RED program supports four tracks: RED Planning (Track 1), RED Adaptation and Implementation (Track 2), RED Innovation (Track 3), and RED Innovation Partnerships (Track 4). Two- and four-year institutions are encouraged to submit to any track as appropriate for their goals and context. RED Planning (Track 1) projects will support capacity-building activities at institutions of special interest to NSF’s mission, including two-year engineering-centered programs building transfer partnerships, two-year or four-year institutions in EPSCoR jurisdictions, Primarily Undergraduate Institutions (PUIs), and Institutions of Higher Education (IHEs) in order to create more opportunities in engineering for students in every part of the country. Planning projects should provide the support for such institutions to explore the development of a RED Projects in Tracks 2, 3, & 4. RED Adaptation and Implementation (Track 2) projects will adapt and implement evidence-based organizational change strategies and actions to the local context, which helps propagate this transformation of undergraduate engineering education. RED Innovation (Track 3) projects will develop new, revolutionary approaches and change strategies that enable the transformation of undergraduate engineering education. RED Innovation Partnerships (Track 4) projects will achieve the same goals as Track 3 projects across multiple institutions. Of particular interest to this track are projects partnering two-year institutions with other eligible institutions. Projects in tracks 2, 3, & 4 will include consideration of the cultural, organizational, structural, and pedagogical changes needed to transform one or more departments to ones in which students are engaged, develop their technical and professional skills, and establish identities as professional engineers or technologists. The focus of projects in these tracks should be on the department’s disciplinary courses and program. RED project initiatives are expected to be institutionalized at the end of the funding period. Proposals are especially encouraged that address areas of increased national interest including but not limited to advanced manufacturing, advanced wireless, artificial intelligence, biotechnology, microelectronics and semiconductors, net zero technologies, sustainability, systems engineering, and quantum engineering.
sig_29f1d86e081e4bd7b62b.title: IUSE / Professional Formation of Engineers: Revolutionizing Engineering Departments (IUSE/PFE: RED)
