sig_2a19c6e7c46b70946e86.description: Framework agreement iBS II Lot LOT-0001: Integrated Control System (iBS). The integrated control system (iBS) is a subsystem of the integrated control and operating system (iLBS) and includes, amongst other things, the central services of the iBS (iBS-Z), integrated operator terminals (iBP) in accordance with the redundancy regulation 2, the reference image function (RBF), iBS communication (iBS-Kom) as well as the iBS-Z console. The iBS subsystem is connected to other iLBS subsystems via standardised interfaces, thereby enabling the operation of integrated sub-centres (iUZ) with electronic interlocking / digital interlocking (ESTW/DSTW). Lot LOT-0002: Transfer network router. The transfer network is a component of the iLBS system and implements communication between all transfer network participants (e.g. iBS-Z, iLBS-ZE and central directory service) in the overall iLBS system up to the network layer (OSI layer 3). This does not include: VPN LST gateway modules, all components of the transport network, the time standard receiver (e.g. DCF-77) or the middleware broker. (including all system components for redundancies). The components are thus used both at the interlocking location (TSO or existing interlocking) and at the locations of the individual iBS, the BSO. Lot LOT-0003: Broker and directory service. A component of the iLBS is a network of broker servers via which the components and subsystems communicate with each other (via Advanced Message Queuing Protocol (AMQP)). (including all system components for redundancies). The brokers are thus used at the iBS and LMC locations. A broker pair (redundant design) is always required at each location. The brokers use the AMQP protocol or Red Hat JBoss Enterprise Application Platform (JBoss EAP) as a platform. For the hardware, 2 HU per physical broker instance in the computer cabinet are provided in the 19 inch rack. The installation depth of 700 mm must not be exceeded. Cooling of the brokers must take place from the front. (see also system specifications requirements specification DiB-0454). The local directory service is a local replica of the central directory service, which is functionally restricted to read access; it serves as a central source of higher-level information such as network addresses, operating relations, user data and roles. (including all system components for redundancies). The local directory service is located at the iBS locations (BSO) and is connected via the transfer network to the central directory service in the LMC. The task of the ZVD is the management and regulation of access rights within the iLBS. Lot LOT-0004: Local routing plan management (LLPV). The local directory service is a local replica of the central directory service, which is functionally restricted to read access; it serves as a central source of higher-level information such as network addresses, operating relations, user data and roles. (including all system components for redundancies). The local directory service is located at the iBS locations (BSO) and is connected via the transfer network to the central directory service in the LMC. The task of the ZVD is the management and regulation of access rights within the iLBS. Lot LOT-0005: Operational management of the central directory service (ZVD) of the LMC and the transfer network of the iLBS . The operational management for the central directory service and the transfer network (transmission system consisting of transfer network router, broker, etc.) comprises organisational, technical and documenting activities required to keep the test systems usable for planned tests. These systems already exist in the ITU. Procurement of the components is not intended. Operational management of productive systems is excluded. Lot LOT-0006: Operational management of the central routing plan management (LPV) for the LMC . The operational management for the central routing plan management comprises organisational, technical and documenting activities required to keep the test systems usable for planned tests. This system already exists in the ITU. Procurement of the component is not intended. Operational management of productive systems is excluded.

sig_2a1f8f660027b868c5b8.description: This procurement covers the Population Health Management framework. The framework will cover population health management software solutions that enable analysis and management of health data from a variety of sources to improve healthcare delivery and decision-making. This will empower Approved Organisations and stakeholders to deliver proactive, personalised care while improving efficiency and supporting preventative health interventions. Also can support addressing health inequalities and the wider social determinants and support the decision-making process across the health and social care sector. The framework is divided into three lots: Lot 1: Population Health Management Digital Solutions Delivery of population health management systems that will support the NHS's and other public sector organisations desire to deliver population level health and care across whole, or large-scale areas of the population - for example, an integrated care system, a city or town, a health community, a large acute Trust or a local authority - or multiples of these. Lot 1 is suitable for solutions with the below characteristics: • Solutions that can address large scale populations, however defined. • Multiple features and functionality, covering a wide range of Population Health Management. • Typically draws data from a range of sources of other organisations. • Horizontal integration to provide large populations to manage. • May or may not include the features and functionality of more specialist solutions. Lot 2: Consultancy &Support Services The nature of services will be to address a variety of needs through providing information, advice, direction and potential solutions to customers. Suppliers will be expected to be able to assist customers to make more informed decisions surrounding their population health programme. • Support of the delivery of population health management to the NHS and broader public sector. • Consultancy services are about helping the NHS or other public sector organisations that may use this framework to implement and deliver population support for some or all of the people who live in the areas they either commission or provide health and care services to. • Consultancy could extend across the NHS, wider health, public health, local government, broader policy areas impacting on health (such as transportation policy, housing policy, employment, environmental - other areas of policy relating to population health management and social determinants of health. • Consultancy might also be more targeted, dealing with a more limited area of healthcare, such as risk stratification, social prescribing, medicines usage, etc. Lot 3: Combined Solutions This Lot covers the provision of Population Health Management solutions that deliver bundle services or comprehensive workflows. Population Health Management provided under this Lot should ensure a seamless, integrated approach, delivering all the necessary components required for Approved Organisations. Across all lots, suppliers must provide: • Software licences or subscriptions • Implementation, configuration, and integration services • Training, onboarding, and change management support • Ongoing maintenance, updates, and technical support • Clear service level agreements and performance reporting Lot 1: .

In addition, Istekki Oy reserves the right to temporarily close the submission of requests to participate in the dynamic purchasing system during its period of validity (e.g. holiday periods). No competitions shall be organised within the dynamic purchasing system during this time.

sig_2a671b9bb2dbe8b36c87.description: The subject of the public contract is the provision of the role of cyber security manager for the contracting authority – Mendel University in Brno in accordance with the requirements of Act No. 264/2025 Coll., on cyber security, as amended (hereinafter also "ZKB"). The contracting authority is a mandatory person under the ZKB. The contracting authority is seeking the service of a Cyber Security Manager (MKB) in the form of outsourcing from a qualified external provider — a legal or natural person. The provider will ensure the performance of the MKB role in the form of outsourcing and will fulfil all obligations arising from: 1. the Act on Cyber Security, 2. implementing regulations, 3. regulator requirements, 4. the contracting authority's internal security regulations, including methodological management of the Information Security Management System (ISMS), coordination of the implementation of security measures, support for cyber risk and incident management, and communication with the regulator. The MKB service will be provided with professional care and in quality corresponding to the position of the contracting authority as a provider of a regulated service in a regime of higher obligations. The minimum requirements for the subject of the public contract are defined by the technical and commercial conditions set out in this tender documentation, in particular in Annexes No. 1 – specification of the subject of the contract and No. 2 – draft contract for the provision of cyber security manager services.

sig_2aa163ce49268f17239a.description: THIS IS NOT A PRIOR INFORMATION NOTICE, CONTRACT NOTICE OR CALL FOR COMPETITION, BUT A NOTICE OF THE LAUNCH OF MARKET DIALOGUE AS PART OF PROCUREMENT PLANNING. Länsi-Uudenmaan hyvinvointialue is surveying suppliers' interest in a tender concerning a recruitment system. Suppliers interested in the procurement are requested to express their interest in the procurement by email. Expressing interest in the request for information does not bind the service provider/supplier to participate in the tendering procedure, nor is it a prerequisite for participating in the actual tendering procedure later. The subject of the request for information is a recruitment system package that supports all stages of Länsi-Uudenmaan hyvinvointialue's recruitment process and enables the smooth execution of the process. The system must be flexible, user-friendly and easily developable according to future needs. With its help, routine tasks and the documentation of the recruitment process required by the Local Government Act can be largely automated, and it is possible to transfer data electronically between other systems from the system through integrations. The aim is to offer applicants a good applicant experience, and the system must adapt to various recruitment needs and clearly depict the progress of recruitments. Flexible functions are required for substitute recruitment, such as the automatic contacting of those registered in the substitute pool at the time of publishing the substitute need, as well as the possibility of automated applicant selection and information. 1. General description of the system, also in the role of a jobseeker. 2. Functional features: - Building the organisation in the system, user rights at different levels, creating user rights ("mass" creation in the implementation phase) - Stages of the recruitment process (permit processing, notices, applications, communication and message templates (applicants, line managers, main users), video interviews, comparisons, reporting/statistics, monitoring the progress of recruitments, "desktop" views of recruitments for line managers and main users, document templates (possibility to create various document templates)) - Stages and functionalities of substitute recruitment (is it possible to transfer data electronically for drawing up the employment contract) - Publishing interfaces (e.g. Job Market Finland, other channels) - Customisability of application forms - Booking interviews via the interview calendar, anonymous recruitment, video interview, artificial intelligence utilisation possibilities, social media - Co-operation tool / module, if the supplier's solution includes the functionality, functionality means the organisation and automation of obligations related to job offering, re-placement, re-engagement obligation and lay-offs - Artificial intelligence utilisation possibilities in different stages of the recruitment process 3. Technical requirements: - Browser and terminal device support (PC, tablet, mobile; Chrome, Firefox, Edge) - Multilingualism (Finnish, Swedish, English) - Ensuring usability and performance, fault tolerance 4. Delivery project and training: - Implementation schedule and project management model - Training package - Support and orientation for main users 5. Support and advisory services: - Support channels for users and jobseekers (telephone, email, chat) - Support for user management and permit processes - Service level reporting and incident management 6. Flexibility and extensibility: - Support for the further development of the system and integrations e.g. to the HR system, electronic archive and document management system. 7. References and user experiences: - Comparable implementations in the public sector - Success of implementations and customer satisfaction Länsi-Uudenmaan hyvinvointialue requests that responses to the request for information be submitted no later than 23.12 at 12 to the email address marja.ahola@luvn.fi. You may, if you wish, submit a brochure/presentation of your solution as an email attachment. Länsi-Uudenmaan hyvinvointialue will select 4 suppliers for further discussions. We will organise separate discussions with the selected suppliers in January 2026 during weeks 4-6 (the exact time will be specified later) via Teams.
sig_2aa163ce49268f17239a.title: Procurement of a recruitment system

sig_2ad20d2b02e40250ad87.description: The Department for Science, Innovation and Technology (DSIT) intends to create a pathway to link problems identified by large organisations with solutions provided by innovative cyber small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) known as the Cyber Accelerator Programme. If you are interested in this potential opportunity, DSIT would like to engage with you. The Bidder presentation is due to take place Wednesday 23rd September 11:00 ( details at the bottom of the notice, on how to register) The Authority is seeking to engage the market to gather information, insights and feedback, while also providing an opportunity for Suppliers to better understand and discuss our requirements. This activity is not a procurement or a commitment to purchase goods or services. Its purpose is to facilitate open dialogue, improve our understanding of available solutions and supplier capabilities, and help shape the requirement and future approach, ensuring any subsequent procurement activity is informed, proportionate and delivers the best possible outcome. The principal objective of the programme is to create a credible pathway from agreed challenges facing the public sector to the commercial adoption of cyber innovation by public-sector buyers. It is intended to link problems identified by public-sector organisations with solutions provided by innovative cyber small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs). The programme will use structured, pro bono design partnerships between public-sector organisations with identified cyber challenges and innovative cyber SMEs capable of developing and testing solutions. Participation will not provide funding, an assurance of future work or preferential treatment in any subsequent procurement. The appointed supplier will be expected to: - identify and recruit suitable public-sector Challenge Council members; - build a broad pipeline of potential Programme Innovators and select suitable innovators against defined challenges; - support challenge development and match innovators to challenges; - establish, facilitate and oversee at least five design partnerships; - provide programme governance and a light-touch commercial, procurement, data protection and security compliance wrapper; - support routes to adoption or other lawful commercial progression; - organise one Showcase Day and other programme activity; - report on progress and produce a final report; and - create and disseminate a pattern library of repeatable approaches to support public-sector adoption of cyber innovation. Lot 1: . None
sig_2ad20d2b02e40250ad87.title: Webinar Invitation: Cyber Accelerator Programme - Design Partnerships

sig_2ad57a51f6fa26648b0f.description: Through this Research Announcement (RA), the Office of Pipeline Safety, at the Pipeline and Hazardous Materials Safety Administration (PHMSA), an operating administration of the U.S. Department of Transportation, solicits applications for research projects awarded and funded as Other Transaction Agreements (OTAs). A comprehensive administrative and technical review will be conducted to determine the merits of the proposals and their relevance to the topic areas of focus. All proposals will be evaluated using only the materials provided in each proposal. PHMSA will reject proposals that duplicate work already planned, completed, or validated under recent initiatives. PHMSA reserves the right to fund all, some, or none of the proposals submitted in response to this RA. PHMSA will not reimburse any proposal development costs. All proposals will be treated as sensitive, competitive information and their contents will be used for evaluation and award purposes only. Any questions are to be directed at the PHMSA Acquisition Services Division as listed in this solicitation. Any questions on solicitation content, issues, or procedures must be submitted via email to Stephen Jones at stephen.jones@dot.gov with a cc to Tremayne Terry at Tremayne.Terry@dot.gov no later than 5:00 p.m. EST, Friday, October 9, 2026. The research announcement number (693JK326RA001) must be included in the subject line. Responses to questions submitted on time will be posted publicly on SAM.gov within 2-3 business days after questions deadline. A full proposal package is defined as the proposal that includes Appendices A and B, and the proposal attachments. No award will be made if any of the above documents are missing from the full proposal package. Please submit the proposal and the proposal attachments in PDF format, except for Attachment #3 “Technical and Deliverable Milestone Schedule,” which should be submitted as an editable Excel document. The procedure for submitting a proposal is as follows: Prior to submitting a proposal package: All offerors must be registered in the Federal Government’s System for Award Management (SAM) (www.sam.gov). Each organization must complete an online registration form to access PHMSA’s Pipeline Safety R&D Management Information System (MIS). More information can be found at: https://primis.phmsa.dot.gov/matrix/RfpHome.rdm?rfp=109. Credentials from past registration will still be valid. To avoid account duplications and for questions or concerns with the registration or application, please submit an e-mail to rd-support@dot.gov prior to starting your submittal to ensure you don’t already have an existing account. Submit Proposal Package: Only electronic submissions, through MIS, will be accepted. Additional instructions regarding the preparation and electronic submission of proposals along with individual questions and answers are available on the website above. Proposals must be uploaded by 5:00 p.m. EST, Monday, November 2, 2026. Late or incomplete submittals will not be considered.

sig_2af5c184c2748a3998bb.description: The Maynooth University School of Business was established in 2007 and currently employs over 100 academic, administrative, and support staff as well as a student body of over 4,000 full time undergraduate and postgraduate students. The School of Business offers a range of undergraduate, postgraduate, and PhD programmes across a wide range of business disciplines as well as offering a suite of modules within the Arts programme. The teaching and learning experience of our students involves a series of face-to-face lectures within our state-of-the-art facilities within Maynooth’s campus delivered primarily by academic faculty but can also include guest lectures from industry. The School’s collective pedagogical strategy is further enhanced by Moodle, an online learning environment whereby learning materials, supplementary readings, case studies, or other media resources facilitating additional student engagement with individual modules. As evidence from students remains a critical element of our ongoing curriculum review procedures, we require a comprehensive student feedback solution to curate, distribute, and manage live student surveys as well as to analyse and disseminate the collected data.

sig_2af5c97b910435612743.description: The University of Sussex (Sussex) is preparing to seek a partner for the provision of Online Programme Management (OPM) Services, with the current contract set to expire on 5 October 2027 and the new contract commencing on 6 October 2027. Under the existing arrangement, Sussex has collaborated with a partner to deliver a portfolio of Masters-level degree courses accessible to students both nationally and internationally via online distance learning. The current contract encompasses a range of services across three core areas. • Marketing and Recruitment: Market Research and Strategy, Lead Generation, Inquiry Management, Admissions Support, Application Processing, Reporting and Analysis. • Course Development and Delivery Model: Course Design and Development, Content Creation, Platform Integration, Technical Support, Continuous Improvement, Compliance and Reporting. • Student Support: Induction and Orientation, Ongoing Support, Monitoring and Communication, Reporting. As the end of the current collaboration approaches, Sussex is actively reviewing its strategy for online learning. The University's strategic aims are to establish a sustainable, high-quality online provision aligned with the University's strategic priorities, enhancing our institutional reputation globally. The provision will be future-ready in terms of modularity, flexibility, and compliance with regulatory frameworks such as the Lifelong Learning Entitlement. Further details regarding this engagement are available in the Instruction Document, which can be accessed via the e-sourcing portal, Proactis: https://supplierlive.proactisp2p.com/account/login While participation in this engagement is not mandatory for involvement in any future procurement process, responses received will help inform the Contracting Authority about the level of market interest. Additionally, feedback from this engagement may help shape the final service requirements and inform the design of the forthcoming procurement strategy, ensuring it reflects both institutional priorities and sector best practice. sig_2b020043dab52be83960.description: The Immigration and Refugee Board of Canada (IRB) requires professional services support to the Chief Innovation and Technology Office (CITO) to advance the modernization of the IRB’s current case management application ecosystem through the Digital Case Modernization (DCM) initiative. This support will enable the IRB to define, design, validate, and implement modern digital solutions that improve the sustainability, interoperability, security, and scalability of its case management capabilities. The DCM initiative is intended to address current limitations in the IRB case management environment. Through this requirement, the IRB seeks specialized expertise to support analysis, architecture, technical design, software development, integration, testing, documentation, and knowledge transfer activities required to modernize the platform in a controlled and phased manner. More specifically, the objective is to support the transition of the IRB case management ecosystem toward a modernized, cloud-aligned microservices architecture and operating model that can better support future service improvements, business agility, data sharing, reporting, and the introduction of emerging capabilities such as advanced automation and Artificial Intelligence.
sig_2b020043dab52be83960.title: IRB Digital Case Management TBIPS

sig_2b3d1b37455cdeebf582.description: The Danish Agency for Digital Government (Digitaliseringsstyrelsen) operates on behalf of the Danish State a national qualified trust service for the management of qualified electronic signature creation devices under Regulation (EU) No 910/2014 as amended by Regulation (EU) 2024/1183 (eIDAS2). As part of securing and modernising the signing service to meet the requirements of eIDAS2, the Agency is procuring Data Diode solutions to be installed and operated within the Agency's data centres (currently two). The Contract includes an Option to extend the deployment to a third data centre and an Option to extend the Contract and replace the Data Diode Hardware. The Contract covers the Initial Delivery of certified Data Diode appliances, comprising dedicated Hardware and associated Software, certified in accordance with Common Criteria or EUCC at EAL4 or higher. The Initial Delivery includes all Licences, Documentation, and support necessary for the Agency to install and operate the Data Diode solutions as part of its trust service infrastructure. The Data Diode solutions must provide one way traffic from the Agency's isolated Root CA environment to other network zones, while preventing any data transfer in the reverse direction. The solutions must support integration with the Agency's existing infrastructure and the required protocols for transfer of files, time information, monitoring and logging data. The Supplier's principal obligations comprise: (a) the Initial Delivery of four Data Diode appliances for deployment across the Agency's production and staging environments in two data centers, together with the required Standard Software and deployment in the Agency's test and development environments; (b) Ongoing Services, including support and maintenance of the Standard Software and Hardware, security patching, product lifecycle management and hardware replacement; and (c)Ordered Services, comprising Time-Based Services (services for installation, configuration, key ceremonies, and similar tasks) and Options; and (d) Cross-cutting Services, comprising Documentation and security, provided as an integral part of the Ongoing Services and Ordered Services throughout the term of the Contract.
sig_2b3d1b37455cdeebf582.title: Data Diode

sig_2b5692f3148d86ac1b9e.description: Type 1 diabetes (T1D) is a complex disease involving interactions among many different cell types, tissues, organs and biological processes. Genetics, the environment, and lifestyle all play a role in disease development and progression. Over the past two decades, the National Institute of Diabetes and Digestive and Kidney Diseases (NIDDK) has supported major T1D research consortia covering basic, translational, and clinical research. Each consortium has focused on different aspects of T1D, such as specific organs, stages of disease or clinical outcomes. Together, these consortia have collected large longitudinal and multimodal datasets using standardized protocols and coordinated studies. While individual consortia have improved our understanding of specific areas, combining their work offers a rare opportunity to see how different biological processes interact to drive T1D development and progression. This integrated view can answer fundamental questions about T1D biology that cannot be answered using individual datasets or studies alone. Recent advances in artificial intelligence (AI) now make it possible to integrate these complementary datasets and study T1D across various tissues, disease stages, and biological levels. Building on these resources, NIDDK will support a coordinated, milestone-driven research project to answer fundamental questions about T1D biology and accelerate the development of personalized medicine. The project will combine multimodal human pancreas and clinical datasets to better understand how biological processes interact as T1D develops and progresses. The research will generate new insights into T1D biology, help us understand the different forms and stages of T1D, identify biomarkers, and inform new approaches for disease prevention, intervention, and treatment. To support the research, the project will develop and test advanced multimodal AI models. It will also develop AI-enabled research workflows, new methods to integrate data, and privacy-preserving synthetic datasets.
sig_2b5692f3148d86ac1b9e.title: Multimodal AI to Accelerate Precision Medicine for Type 1 Diabetes (U01- Clinical Trials Not Allowed)

sig_2b6c2b108529c3c12843.description: The scope of this contract is to acquire the full range of technical, management and support services necessary to obtain and maintain access to US food and cosmetic products. The contract is divided into the following task areas: Project Management Data Access Data Collection Training Support 6.1 Technical Requirements 6.1.1 Datasets The processed food and cosmetic products and their package data (as well as menu data) shall be from a currently existing, commercially available database(s) that shall provide immediate automated access. The data shall include products from all regions of the US (Appendix B indicates the US Census regions) and be accurate, quality-assured, and easily-validated; well organized; stored as relationally searchable information for trend and other analyses; and fully exportable. The database(s) shall be regularly updated and maintained in a current state throughout the base and option periods. Information will be required for the following product types: Processed, and retail food products (e.g. foods, infant formula, etc.; minimum 400,000 products that are selling on the market in the contract year) and thus, over 2 million historical products; (Optional) Restaurant food products/menu items (minimum 50,000 products from top chains) Dietary supplements (minimum 100,000 products); shall be categorized according to the definition in Appendix A Cosmetics (minimum 300,000 products) The following attributes (as shown on the package) shall be required: Package images (legible images of all surfaces (e.g. sides, top, bottom) of product packaging, including internal and external packaging Count of available images per product Information contained on and in product packaging – shall include the following at minimum (each data entry line in the database must be quality assured and -controlled (QA/QC’d) for accuracy as the database is populated) GTIN/UPC/Barcode Nutrition Facts label, including single and dual columns and including multi-packs (shall be displayed in format according to 21 CFR 101.9) and Supplement Facts label (shall be displayed in format according to 21 CFR 101.36(e)(10) (i), (ii), (iii), and (iv)) Additional nutrients presenting on package labels Indication of added sugars Ingredients list (e.g. food additives, active ingredients for dietary supplements) Allergen labeling information (Contains/may contain) and advisory statements Pack size and weight Number of servings per package Brand Manufacturer Location of manufacturer, packer, or distributor Written and/or pictorial statements signaling the presence of one or more allergens (according to the Food Allergen Labeling and Consumer Protection Act (FALCPA) of 2004; e.g. “Contains”) and/or caution statements about the product (e.g. “warning statements”) Insignificant amounts for certain nutrients Claims on package (e.g., regulated, health, nutrition, efficacy, marketing, and all other types) including indication of “healthy” on package Statements/icons/signages and similar information that features the nutrition, health, organoleptic, processing, suggested usages (e.g., recipes), and other properties of the product (e.g., written and/or pictorial statements that feature nutrient content claim languages, front-of-pack language/icons) Certifications on package GE/Bioengineered/GMO language on package Verbatim language of all text (e.g. product description, instructions, etc.) and icons from product packaging Product source where collected Product category Dates of when product information is a) released to the market and on shelf, b) collected, c) published, d) updated, and e) discontinued Indication of “previous” or “new” nutrition facts label FNDDS 8-digit and 7-digit food codes; SR 5-digit sub codes (8-digit food code shall be linked to food products and ingredients;7-digit food codes are mapped to 8-digit at the product level; 5-digit SR sub codes are mapped to 8-digit food codes at the ingredient level) through 2019 GSFA (General Standard for Food Additives) categories through 2019 Food packaging types (primary and secondary) and codes Food content type Moreover, the data shall provide additional valid and verifiable information on the product ingredients; at a minimum, the data shall provide all available synonym name(s), allergen status, and technical or functional effect descriptors in a usable format. Additionally, FDA shall have access to other Mintel products, such as Mintel Leap, Mintel Food & Drink, Mintel Reports, Mintel Trends, Comperemedia Direct, Market Dynamics, and Global Consumer Research. 6.1.2 Product Requirements Overarching product requirements: Unlimited access for up to 200 FDA personnel; Located external to FDA network (access via weblink); Universal access from any FDA computer hardware (desktops, laptops with docking stations and/or scientific workstations) using internet browsers compatible with FDA current standards; Product access shall not be restricted according to product price; Capability to perform relational searching and analyses of the food and cosmetic product labeling and packaging datasets and menu datasets in functional environments using appropriate methodologies, which shall be valid, reliable, and robust; Ability to support disclosure of scientific and technical articles, study results, presentations, public health advisories, and similar works involving aggregated data to entities outside the Agency including the general public; High resolution, readable images for all sides of the package labels (and optionally, menu images) for validation and other research purposes. Images shall be displayed with product data from all sides of the package so that information may be easily verifiable by the user. Accurate data reflective of verbatim language and icons of product labels (and menus). Verification that products are still being sold in the US marketplace. Users shall be able to analyze and summarize their searches into summary reports and all available data and search results and outputs shall be downloadable and exportable within an accepted timeframe into Microsoft Excel Spreadsheets and Access Data Base Software, SAS Business Analytics Software, and other common formats. Regular, updated, extracted bulk/batch raw data of the full dataset shall be available by API and in MS Excel compatible format (e.g. single pipe delimited txt, csv) and shall be accessible in a secure FTP or cloud service acceptable by FDA. In addition to the product label (and menu) database(s), all sales data, other accompanying databases, and market research reports, when available, shall be provided. This information shall apply to food, dietary supplement, restaurant, and cosmetic products when available Data and UI status updates shall be posted on the system website main page and identified users shall be notified via email System usage statistics (including statistics regarding individual login usage and length of time logged in) shall be available in monthly reports and upon request All data and files shall undergo quality control checks prior to accessibility/delivery to FDA. Documentation on quality control procedures shall be provided (at the onset and with any changes over time) for all data and image collection and data processes (e.g. ingestion of data, quality assurance of data in different formats, etc.) as noted below. Web Interface A user-friendly and data comprehensive interface that is transparent and flexible and allows both predefined (i.e., canned) and custom reports shall be provided. The user should be able to conduct a multi-variable search (i.e. searching a combination of factors concurrently). The user should be able to search and filter according to product category, year, product name, UPC, brand, company, claims, ingredients, allergens, other product attributes, and user-entered keywords in any and all fields. Raw Data Files Raw files (e.g. MS Excel compatible, single pipe-delimited txt, csv) for all data (food, supplements, cosmetics, etc.) shall be delivered a minimum of quarterly as defined by FDA or downable without file size restriction. The file sizes should be appropriate so that they can be opened and readily used. Files shall be accessible in a secure FTP or cloud service acceptable by FDA and organized based on FDA specifications. All files shall also be available by API with fields as specified by FDA. The database(s) shall be scientific based on FDA’s definition: able to verify the data entry line(s) via product images, and the product’s contents may be analyzed, if the user chooses to have the item purchased and analyzed, to verify the accuracy/truthfulness of the product label, the offeror(s) shall provide this as a purchasable service. System maintenance during the base and all option periods, if exercised, shall be provided. Maintenance shall include upgrades and updates to the software and data, continued use of and access to the database system and data, and updates to technical and analytical documentation. 6.1.3 Documentation The Contractor shall compile and submit full documentation to the Contracting Officer Representative (COR) and Project Officer (PO) within 14 days of the beginning of the contract as well as any updated documentation through the contract years. After approval by the COR, all documentation shall be available to access online in the database(s) system with downloadable format into MS Word. The Contractor shall provide documentation on the following: All data collection and acquisition processes so that the source data is clearly understood Documentation on the status of all products found in the databases relative to what is selling on the market each year of the contract (e.g., is the product verified as being available in retail for purchase and/or is it discontinued). The methodologies used for any data cleaning and ingestion processes and those used to develop the data as well as information on pertinent software used as part of the process Data dictionary and a code book defining all data elements/fields that are included in the data package, which includes information on how calculations are performed relative to certain data fields Documentation on the process of standardizing and cleaning data from different sources as well as information on UPCs that are duplicated (e.g. historical vs, duplicated) Any related technical specifications on the technologies or software that is used Information on how to access and use the data in all formats Written methodology regarding quality control procedures for all data and images collected, ingested into a database, exported, and categorized, including information on the oversight of quality control to ensure above 98% accuracy Interface documentation and user guides Any updates to general processes, methodologies, data sources, QC processes, Documentation on limitations of database, errors in the database, and plans for mitigation and/or resolution of issues Full-disclosure 6.1.4 Support / Training A. Support: Ongoing technical and analytical support by phone or by e-mail shall be provided to all certified users of the data during business hours (9:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m. Eastern Time) throughout the period of performance (POP) in accordance with the service levels established in the contract. The Contractor shall notify the COR regarding any issues as they relate to Acceptable Quality Level (AQL) standards. All technical related issues would need to be addressed and resolved in 5 business days or within a reasonable timeframe agreement upon with COR and TCOR. B. Training: The Contractor shall provide up to two (2) one-day training sessions per year (on-site or via web-based methods). This training can be divided into shorter time periods. Additional options for additional “on-demand” sessions either in person or via web-based methods shall be made available under the IDIQ portion of the award. 6.1.5 Data Disclosure Clearance As part of its regulatory activities, FDA shall, at times, require disclosure of scientific and technical articles, study results, presentations, public health advisories, and similar works involving aggregated data to entities outside the Agency including the general public. For activities that require disclosure of aggregated data the Contractor shall accept and adhere to the FDA Data Disclosure Clearance Procedures and form found in Appendices D. The FDA shall continue to require the ability to release aggregated data through the FDA Data Disclosure Clearance process for data obtained during the contract period for the period of all Option Periods. The FDA will require the services of processing clearance requests. As part of its regulatory activities, FDA shall, at times engage in collaborative research projects with third parties outside of FDA for specific research projects of public health importance that are initiated by and for the benefit of FDA. These collaborations shall require FDA to have the ability to share project specific aggregated or raw data with third parties for collaborative research projects. For these collaborations that require sharing of aggregated or raw data, the Contractor shall accept and adhere to the Data Disclosure Clearance Procedures and form to be found in Appendices D. These Procedures include terms and conditions for third party collaborations. 6.2 Project Management The Contractor shall be responsible for creating, managing and updating project plans, schedules and managing resources for the project. 6.2.1 Quality Control The Contractor shall ensure that quality control procedures are conducted prior to providing FDA access to data. The Contractor shall provide written methodology on quality control procedures for all data and images collected, ingested into a database, exported, and categorized, including information on the oversight of quality control to ensure above 98% accuracy. The Contractor shall notify the COR should any issues with the data be noticed and shall flag it in the interface. Should FDA notice issues with the data, the Contractor shall address and fix the issues immediately within an agreed upon timeframe with the COR. 6.2.2 Reporting The Contractor shall provide a brief work plan outlining the strategy for supporting each of the areas outlined in Section 4 of the SOW to the COR within 10 days of award. Each month the Contractor shall provide a status report giving brief descriptions of activities performed. The monthly status report shall, at minimum, contain the following: usage statistics for databases and other resources; usage statistics of technical support feature by FDA staff; technical issues reported by FDA staff; other technical issues (ex. log of times when database(s)/resources were inaccessible), data ingestion success and failure rates with mitigation plans should issues be present. The Contractor shall conduct yearly face-to-face presentation meetings with the COR and other FDA staff as well as deliver final written progress reports about contract performance for the preceding period of performance. The Contractor shall submit to the COR a final report which documents and summarizes the results of the contract work 10 days prior to the end of each period of performance. The final report shall include tables, graphs, diagrams, curves, sketches, photographs and drawings as necessary and in sufficient detail to comprehensively explain the results achieved under this contract. 6.3 Contract Services Requirements The Contractor shall perform the following types of tasks as needed: Contractor shall collect information for selected products. The list of products and data fields to be collected shall be defined by the COR. Contractor shall conduct search(es) for products using search criteria defined by the COR. The option shall be available to purchase identified products. Contractor shall conduct exports for products using search criteria defined by the COR as needed. The County Municipality wants a market dialogue with suppliers who can offer case processing of applications and/or planning of assisted school transport. The County Municipality is responsible for school transport pursuant to the Education Act and is subject to the Public Procurement Act and Regulations (LOA and FOA). Purpose of the market dialogue The County Municipality is planning to procure new agreements for a system for case processing of applications for school transport. It is also planned to procure a system for the planning and execution of assisted school transport by taxi and minibus. These systems can be supplied separately or in a single delivery. The purpose of the market dialogue is to gain an overview of existing solutions and how they can meet the County Municipality's needs, expectations and requirements for the case processing of applications for school transport, and the planning and execution of school transport. Participation in the market dialogue will not commit either the supplier or the County Municipality with regard to subsequent procurements. The market dialogue is not to be considered part of upcoming procurement processes. Final decisions and choices for the procurement processes have not been made upon publication of the invitation. Practical information about the market dialogue Suppliers are invited to present their services in one-to-one meetings at Vestfold fylkeskommune's premises. The exact time for these meetings will be scheduled after the registration deadline. Execution of the market dialogue The dialogue meetings are planned to be held on 28 May and 29 May. The meetings will be held at Svend Foyns gate 9, 3126 Tønsberg or, at the request of the supplier, as an online meeting using Teams. 1,5 hour of meeting time will be allocated to each supplier meeting. Registration Deadline for registration: 13 May at 12:00. Upon registration, a meeting summons with an agenda for the market dialogue will be sent to the supplier. All suppliers will receive the same agenda. Please provide the company name, name and email address of participants in the market dialogue upon registration, as well as any request for an online meeting. Suppliers will subsequently receive a meeting invitation by email. Registration must be sent by email to: oyvind.hanssen@vestfoldfylke.no Costs The parties are responsible for their own costs associated with the market dialogue. Use of information and confidentiality Information that has emerged in the market dialogue can/will be used in the further work on drafting the requirement specifications. The County Municipality has a duty to prevent others from gaining access to or knowledge of information about technical devices, procedures or operating and business secrets that it would be of competitive importance to keep secret, cf. sig_2c56641cf3974755ac6f.description: This program will advance scientific community datasets to enable scientific discovery and innovation using artificial intelligence (AI) and other methods. Its goal is to increase the value that can be derived from existing scientific datasets by leveraging novel methods and artificial intelligence (AI). This will unlock new AI-driven insights. It can enable interdisciplinary research. It also enables investigations outside of the original motivation for data collection and analysis. The program seeks to 1) apply AI-based capabilities to feature extraction and metadata generation, and the integration of multiple datasets. 2) Develop robust data pipelines necessary for automated analysis of existing datasets and similar use-cases by AI tools and systems. 3) Augment and/or harmonize existing datasets to better enable use by AI data pipelines and automated analysis. Proposals should address dataset security and integrity. Governance and the process for scientific communities to contribute to the datasets should also be addressed. Proposals are encouraged to leverage existing resources. These may include NSF data platforms , the NSF Integrated Data Systems and Services program , the NSF-led National AI Research Resource , the Genesis Mission platform , or other national infrastructure. NSF is open to exploring partnerships with philanthropy, private industry, or the non-profit sector to support additional proposals or collaborative opportunities that will advance AI-driven scientific discovery through unlocking the value of high-impact scientific datasets. Expanding Participation in STEM, NSF Priorities, and Gold Standard Science: NSF prioritizes cutting-edge discovery science and engineering research, advancing technology and innovation, and creating opportunities for all Americans. NSF has established priorities set forth by Congress, the administration and the NSF director to promote NSF's mission . Proposers should review the list of NSF priorities and are encouraged to align their proposals with them, where appropriate. NSF also expects the highest standards of scientific rigor, integrity and adherence tenets of Gold Standard Science in proposals, as appropriate for the field of science and research modality.
sig_2c56641cf3974755ac6f.title: Unlocking Dataset Value for AI-Enabled Scientific Discovery (AI Datasets)

sig_2d2fe4d469eae77b6d37.description: The University is undertaking discovery work under the External Digital Experience (EDE) Programme. This RFI is intended to test the market before any formal procurement decision is made. It is not a tender and it does not commit the University to procure a solution or to follow a particular route. The purpose of this RFI is to gather supplier perspectives on a future Content Management System (CMS) and the implementation, migration, governance and operating model considerations that would support a more coherent external digital experience. The RFI is CMS-only. The University is not seeking CRM supplier proposals through this exercise. CRM should only be referenced where it relates to CMS integration, enquiry/form hand-off, campaign source tracking, consent capture, student journey data, or future interoperability. This RFI is intended to help the University: • understand credible CMS options available in the market, including traditional, headless, hybrid, composable or DXP-aligned approaches • test assumptions from CMS discovery, the EDE Strategy and the CMS Discovery Checklist • understand how suppliers would support content governance, structured content, publishing workflows, accessibility, IA, SEO, internal search, migration and editor experience • understand how a CMS could integrate with CRM and other systems without making CRM part of this RFI • obtain indicative views on delivery approach, sequencing, risks, University-side resourcing and cost drivers; • inform any subsequent CMS business case, procurement strategy, RFP/tender documentation and evaluation criteria. The University of Manchester no longer meets the criteria of a 'body governed by public law' and is therefore not considered a contracting authority for the purposes of the Public Contracts Regulations 2015 and/or any replacement legislation. As a result, the University of Manchester will no longer be subject to the regime contained in The Public Contracts Regulations 2015 and/or any replacement legislation with effect from 1 August 2023. However, as an institution founded for the public good, an exempt charity and an organization in receipt of public funds, the University has a duty to manage expenditure in an appropriate manner and aims to deliver value for money across its non-pay spend by adhering to good procurement practice. Information, formalities and necessary requirements to be met will be set out in the RFI document, all of which are freely available via the University's procurement portal In-Tend - https://in-tendhost.co.uk/manchesteruniversity

sig_2d3c0ee9ffdbb46ff944.description: This request for information is intended to examine questions and price estimates related to the procurement of a dictation transcription service and speech recognition solution for use in pathology by Fimlab Laboratoriot Oy (hereinafter referred to as "Fimlab" or the "contracting authority"). This is not a contract notice or a call for competition, but rather a request for information for a market survey, the objective of which is to obtain comprehensive additional information regarding the planned procurement so that any future tendering procedure can be carried out as appropriately as possible, taking into account the latest technologies and market trends. Fimlab invites interested suppliers to participate in the market survey and requests your views regarding the planned procurement. Fimlab does not bind itself to carry out the procurement that is the subject of the request for information. Decisions on launching a potential procurement process will be made after the market survey. The procurement would potentially consist of the following parts: 1) Dictation transcription service 2) Speech recognition solution The contracting authority will evaluate the division of the procurement into parts based on suppliers' responses. Dictations for the dictation transcription service and the speech recognition solution are divided into three categories by length: Short: under 499 characters Medium: 500–1500 characters Long: over 1501 characters. DICTATION TRANSCRIPTION SERVICE In the dictation transcription service, a digital dictation recorded by a healthcare professional in audio file format in text format is transcribed into text format and saved in Fimlab's IT management systems using an encrypted remote connection. The dictation transcription service must include a cloud-based (SaaS) dictation management system and associated workstation and mobile applications used for recording dictation. The dictation transcription service will be integrated into Fimlab's LIS (Whitelake Software Point's LabVantage Medical Suite). The dictation transcription service must be provided in Finnish and Swedish. The dictation transcription service must recognise the medical terminology and vocabulary used in specialised medical care as well as foreign words related to the context. The dictation transcription service must be provided on weekdays (Mon-Fri) between 08:00-18:00 according to Fimlab's needs. The dictation system must be available 24/7. Users of the dictation transcription service are employees of the pathology unit, with pathology physicians as the primary users. Not all physicians may necessarily start using the service immediately at the deployment stage, but they must have the opportunity to join as users of the service later. The service must include maintenance, technical support, user support and a sufficient number of user licences related to the use of the dictation system and the provision of the transcription service. Approximately 50 000 - 60 000 reports are routed to the transcription service annually. SPEECH RECOGNITION SOLUTION The speech recognition solution is procured as a cloud service (SaaS service), and the procurement also includes deployment, user and support services. The speech recognition solution must include real-time direct speech recognition in Finnish and Swedish. The speech recognition application must produce text content that is easily transferable to the target system. The speech recognition application must have medical vocabulary capabilities. The application will not be integrated or connected to existing Fimlab IT systems. The speech recognition solution must operate as an application installed on users' desktops. RESPONDING TO THE REQUEST FOR INFORMATION Companies interested in the procurement are requested to answer the questions attached to the request for information ("Questions for the Request for Information") and submit the completed attachment via the Tender Service Portal. You may submit your response in Finnish or English in a free-form manner (in writing). Your responses will be utilised in the preparation of the procurement and in finalising the contract notice and its attachments. All responses will be treated confidentially. Information will not be shared with other suppliers without written consent to disclose the information. Please follow the numbering of the questions. Also clearly indicate trade secrets or confidential information. The procurement parts described above are Fimlab's preliminary views. We would gladly hear if you have alternative solutions to offer. Responding to the request for information does not affect a potential tenderer's position in the actual tendering procedure. No compensation is paid to those who responded to the request for information for their participation. If the contracting authority deems it necessary, it is possible that the contracting authority will continue supplier-specific discussions with a maximum of 5 suppliers.
sig_2d3c0ee9ffdbb46ff944.title: Market consultation - Information request: Dictation transcription service and speech recognition solution

sig_2d9632169b86508efd34.description: Ambient Voice Technology (AVT) for Berkshire Healthcare NHS Foundation Trust Lot 1: . Berkshire Healthcare NHS Foundation Trust is seeking to procure an Ambient Voice Technology (AVT) solution to support clinical documentation across a range of services and care settings. The solution should enable clinicians to capture consultations and generate structured clinical outputs including but not limited to documentation, clinical record notes, summaries, and correspondence, while integrating seamlessly into existing clinical workflows and digital systems. The aim is to reduce administrative burden and support more meaningful patient interactions, improving the overall patient experience through more engaged consultations, higher quality documentation, reduced errors, improved continuity of care, and shorter turnaround times for clinic letters and updates. It should also enable clinicians to spend more time focusing on the patient, while maintaining high standards of clinical safety, transparency, and documentation quality. The solution must support use across a range of real-world clinical environments, including inpatient wards, outpatient clinics, and community settings, where factors such as background noise, shared spaces, and variable connectivity may impact performance. The solution must also support consultations involving third parties (e.g. carers, family members, or interpreters), ensuring accurate capture, speaker differentiation, and appropriate inclusion within the output. The contract will be for 2 years with optional extensions for two more years. The procurement will be undertaken using the Artificial Intelligence Dynamic Purchasing System (DPS) RM6200. If you wish to register on this DPS you can find out how to do so here: https://supplierregistration.cabinetoffice.gov.uk/dps/RM6200?nav=0 Please note that all bidders for this requirement must be certified under NHS England's Ambient Voice Technology Self-Certified Supplier Registry. Details can be found here: https://digital.nhs.uk/services/ambient-scribing/ambient-voice-technology-self-certified-supplier-registry. Additional information: Berkshire Healthcare NHS Foundation Trust intends to create a DPS supplier shortlist on 13th October 2026 with the intention of issuing a capability assessment on 14th October 2026, to be returned by 21st October 2026. The intention is for the tender documents to be issued on 10th November 2026 to those bidders who have met the capability assessment requirements. Berkshire Healthcare reserves the right to amend these dates.

sig_3090213e0d67fc3a8a4c.description: Legal and management support on the implementation of components of the European Space Programme Expected outcome: selecting a set of companies able to provide ad hoc support on various programmatic, managerial and legal aspects on IRIS2, Space Traffic Management and Space Economy for the next 4 years. In the scope of the Regulation (EU) 2023/588 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 15 March 2023 establishing the Union Secure Connectivity Programme for the period 2023- 2027, the European Commission has signed a 12-year Concession Contract on 126 December 2024 for the development, the deployment and the operation of the Infrastructure for Resilience, Interconnectivity and Security by Satellite (IRIS2) programme. IRIS2 consists in 264 LEO satellites, 18 MEO satellites and a ground infrastructure to be deployed by 2030 which aim at providing a secure, low-latency connectivity to EU Members States, Governmental users and Commercials users with a worldwide coverage. The programme will be split in 4 phases: 1. Phase 1: Supply chain consolidation This maximum 1-year phase will enable the IRIS2 Concessionaire to finalise suppliers’ selection. This should also allow the creation of a Special Purpose Vehicle to handle the Concession Contract until its end in 12 years. 2. Phase 2: Development phase This 2-year phase will be mainly dedicated to the design and the development of the infrastructure. 3. Phase 3: Deployment phase This phase is expected to last 3 years and will be dedicated to the industrialisation, production and launch of the infrastructure. 4. Phase 4: Operation phase The rest of period of 12 years will consist in operating the IRIS2 infrastructure and providing services. During these 4 phases, the European Commission will supervise the Concessionaire’s activities and collaborate with it to ensure the proper execution of the Concession Contract respecting the contractual performances, cost and schedule of IRIS2. The envisaged Framework Contract is expected to cover these Phases 1, 2 and 3.; EU Space Surveillance and Tracking (EU SST) is a key capability that helps to protect space infrastructure and services from in-orbit collisions between space objects and other disruptions. It thereby safeguards European economies, societies and citizens who increasingly rely on space-based services such as navigation or Earth observation, and so contributes to the resilience of European space assets and to a higher level of EU strategic autonomy. Integrated in 2021 as a full-fledged subcomponent of the EU Space Programme, EU SST is fully operational, with its own network of sensors from EU Member States, a database connecting national Operations Centres, and services provided to users through the EU SST Front Desk at EUSPA. It is also security relevant: its internal data policy protects sensitive information and the security interests of EU SST partners, and gives guidelines on handling SST data. In the framework of the current ECF proposal, new services are proposed and a new governance might emerge. The Commission adopted on 25 June 2025 the EU Space Act – a legislative proposal for a Regulation on the safety, resilience and environmental sustainability of space activities. The EU Space Act is a groundbreaking proposal, responding directly to the need to strengthen the Union’s resilience and competitiveness. It is the first European regulatory answer to the market fragmentation that hinders our space industry’s competitiveness and to the emerging risks of safety and security to space infrastructure and satellites orbits. This Act is linked directly to EUSST activities. It foresees the involvement of EUSST in future activities and services aiming to protect safety and sustainability in space.; To secure Europe’s competitiveness on the global level, on 25 June 2025 the European Commission adopted its Communication “A Vision for the European Space Economy” . It is the first Commission’s initiative to define and address the entire space economy, including the emerging in-space economy. The Vision takes a holistic approach, looking beyond the EU Space Programme components to strengthen Europe’s space economy from the upstream (manufacturing, assembly, and launch infrastructures) to the downstream sector (space-based data, products, and services), including in-orbit and (cis)lunar space. It aims to help EU companies deliver space-derived products and services to a wide range of economic sectors on Earth, while also supporting Mmember Sstates in achieving their national space programme objectives. The Communication proposes forty-six actions points that willto place Europe as a leader in global space economy by 2050. Space-based technologies and services are vital to the maintenance and improvement of the European Union's strategic non-dependence, security, resilience and global competitiveness. The EU already boasts world-class space-based services, from Global Navigation Satellite Systems (Galileo) and Earth Observation (Copernicus) to secure satellite communications (IRIS2 and GOVSATCOM). Yet, the global space economy continues to evolve rapidly, driven by international competition, technological innovation, and geopolitical tensions. By some estimates, its economic value is projected to reach USD 1.8 trillion by 2035 and the launch of approximately 100.000 satellites are expected to be launched in just this decade.

sig_3151f322b1e4d24de2ed.description: Market consultation: The contracting authority intends to ascertain current market solutions for Special Protection Schemes (SpPS). To this end, it wishes to use this market consultation to test the feasibility of its own company requirements and the integrability of the market solutions. The contracting authority understands a Special Protection Scheme (SpPS) to be a special protection system used in power transmission grids to restore grid security in extraordinary or fault situations. The SpPS module monitors the transmission grid for limit violations and detects events that endanger the normal state of the transmission grid. It implements measures to mitigate the effects of limit violations and events and to return the transmission grid to a secure state. These may include measures such as disconnecting assets or changing the feed-in of generators. The SpPS module is designed to increase the reliability and security of the power grid through fast and coordinated responses. The purpose of the SpPS module is not to perform calculations, but rather to draw upon calculations and results from other systems.
sig_3151f322b1e4d24de2ed.title: Market exploration: Special Protection Schemes (SpPS) in the 50Hertz Control Center

sig_318bd616166ca5bb4253.description: The European Centre for Medium Range Weather Forecasts (ECMWF) invites Tenders for the future acquisition of an Advanced Hierarchical Data Storage Management System. The ITT seeks proposals from Tenderers for licensing and support services for an advanced hierarchical data storage management system and related consultancy services. The aim is to enter into a long-term contract for the procurement of these services, include commissioning, training of ECMWF staff and supporting the solution over the lifetime of the contract. Full information is available on ECMWF’s eProcurement Portal which will is accessible via https://procurement.ecmwf.int/. Further details of the scope and overview of the procurement are provided below: ECMWF’s data archive is based on HPSS (High Performance Storage System) software and underpinned by large capacity disk and automated tape library infrastructure. Overall HPSS holds 1.5 Exabytes of data and the expectation is that by the end of 2032 they will have grown to hold well over 4 Exabytes and by the end of 2035, well over 8 Exabytes. HPSS is primarily used by two applications, both developed at ECMWF; MARS and ECFS: MARS, the Meteorological Archival and Retrieval System, provides access to a powerful abstraction engine that allows the thousands of registered users to access the meteorological data that has been collected or generated at ECMWF for more than 40 years. ECFS, the ECMWF Common File System, provides users with a logical view of a seemingly very large file system and is used for data in formats that are not suitable for storing in MARS. The archives are very busy, most of their activity is responding to read workloads from the HPC systems. However, around 620TB of new data is being added every day, and it is expected that daily growth will be close to 1.5PB following the introduction of the new HPC in 2027. Further details on activity and existing equipment will be provided in the ITT. The intention is to determine whether to remain with HPSS or to migrate to a new storage solution, whichever provides the most compelling case based on long-term growth potential, stability and pricing. ECMWF is seeking to enter a long-term relationship with a vendor to supply a license and provide 24/7 support for the software. The initial installation will be at the Centre's Bologna data centre in Italy. If there are optimisation benefits, it will be possible to supply hardware in this tender, however the main intention is for this to be predominantly a software solution, with commodity hardware being purchased elsewhere. The ITT has an estimated value exceeding 3 million EUR. Further details are available in the ITT volumes accessible via the ECMWF procurement portal. The closing date for the Tender, as indicated in Volume IA is Thursday, 05 March 2026, 15:00 (UK Local time).
sig_318bd616166ca5bb4253.title: Acquisition of an Advanced Hierarchical Data Storage Management System

sig_31b430e006143bd2c907.description: We kindly request you to submit your response to this information request regarding the procurement OMNI360 AI solutions embedded in healthcare. We greatly appreciate all responses received, and each of them will be taken into account in the preparation of a potential tendering process. The purpose of the information request is to ensure that the preparers of the tendering process have as comprehensive and up-to-date a picture of the market and available solutions as possible. With this information request, we wish to survey suppliers' capability and interest in acting as a development partner for AI solutions embedded in the OMNI360 system. In addition, we are exploring ready-made or near-ready-made OMNI360 embedded AI solutions available on the market. We also aim to familiarise ourselves with the market situation of services and solutions, related products, contract terms and commercial conditions such as pricing. The procurement will be put out to tender within the dynamic purchasing system for Artificial intelligence and automation solutions and related services 2026-2033. Based on the responses to the information request, market dialogue sessions and/or technical market dialogues may be organised. In the market dialogue sessions, suppliers can present their own services, products and alternatives for the implementation of the procurement object. If market dialogue sessions are organised, they will be conducted in the Finnish language. Istekki will notify the companies participating in the sessions of the more detailed schedules and the Teams meeting link later. sig_325870b72bba15601c84.description: THIS IS NOT A PRIOR INFORMATION NOTICE, CONTRACT NOTICE OR CALL FOR TENDERS BUT A NOTICE OF THE COMMENCEMENT OF A MARKET DIALOGUE AS PART OF PROCUREMENT PLANNING. Länsi-Uudenmaan hyvinvointialue is planning a tender process where the subject of the procurement is an HR system package for payroll, employment relationship management, personnel development, and travel and expense claim management, including an outsourced payroll service and a travel and expense claim service. The package also potentially includes a statutory archiving solution. The subject of the procurement also includes system implementation and commissioning, support and maintenance services, operational services, and further development services. Länsi-Uudenmaan hyvinvointialue’s payroll and travel and expense claim services are currently outsourced to Sarastia Oy. The services are managed in systems administered by the service provider, S365 HR and M2. S365 HR acts as the master data for personal information. Supervisors, employees and HR have access to the current HR system, which is currently used for employment lifecycle functions - HRD functions are not in use. The new system and service to be procured will support Länsi-Uusimaa’s desire to facilitate and lighten the administrative work of supervisors and to develop the HR system towards a more modern solution that includes HRD functions such as development discussions and the management of permits and qualifications. The goal is not only to select systems but also to build a functional and sustainable partnership with the supplier. The procurement tentatively includes, among other things, the following functionalities and features: - Outsourced payroll service, which will be implemented for all Länsi-Uudenmaan hyvinvointialue personnel, excluding social benefits. The service includes customer service for supervisors and employees. - Payroll system as part of the outsourced payroll service solution. - HR system, which acts as the client’s HR master and covers employment lifecycle management as well as HRD functions such as development discussions, management of permits and qualifications, and support for on-boarding and off-boarding processes. The system must have an electronic signature capability. - Travel and expense claim system, which will be implemented for all Länsi-Uudenmaan hyvinvointialue personnel. - Outsourced travel and expense claim service, which includes, among other things, customer service, weekly payments, and the handling of official reports. - Integrations with the subscriber’s other systems via interfaces. - Advanced automation technologies, which can be used to automate, for example, tasks related to supervisory work and the delivery of data to payroll. The procurement will be carried out using a competitive dialogue procedure. The preliminary procurement schedule is: - Publication of the contract notice by the end of September. - Participation applications by the end of October. - Selection of tenderers by the end of October. - Preliminary call for tenders and sending of invitations to negotiate in November. - Two rounds of negotiations, which will take place in weeks 48 and 50. - Final call for tenders in week 2-3/2026. - Procurement decision in March 2026. - Estimated start time for implementation April 2026. - Services and systems into production use 1.4.2027. Companies interested in the procurement are requested to register by 19.9.2025 at 12.00 to the address: hankinta@luvn.fi. The registration must be titled as follows: “HR kokonaisratkaisun hankinta” (Procurement of HR overall solution). The registration must also contain the following information: - Name of the participating company - Name, telephone number and email address of the contact person - Name of the solution offered by the company. The market survey notice does not oblige the contracting authority to carry out the actual procurement procedure. The description of the procurement and the estimated schedule of the procurement procedure as well as other information presented in the market survey notice are preliminary and indicative advance information. Responding or not responding to the market survey does not prevent participation in a possible procurement procedure. No compensation will be paid for participation. The contracting authority will treat the information provided by the registered companies confidentially, and the names of the companies or other information will not be published.
