sig_32723177a2d39dba9299.description: The object of the contract is the supply of a set of software and hardware elements within the project “CAPITALISING ON THE ADVANTAGES OF DIGITALISATION FOR THE BENEFIT OF THE CITIZENS OF SECTOR 2”. Within the contract, the economic operator will ensure the following activities: 1. Design services The provider will ensure design services which will include the drafting of the technical project and execution details, the performance of site surveys and the definition of technical solutions, the sizing of equipment and related infrastructure, as well as the preparation of documentation necessary for the implementation of the project in accordance with the Specifications. 2. Supply and installation of equipment The provider/supplier will ensure the supply of equipment necessary for the implementation of the system, including CCTV equipment, storage equipment and network equipment, as well as their installation and configuration in the locations determined by the contracting authority, the creation of the communications infrastructure and the integration of hardware components into a unitary system in accordance with the Specifications. 3. Software platform development and implementation services (PMDI) The provider will ensure the installation, configuration and implementation of the integrated management and dispatching platform (PMDI), including the development and customisation of necessary functionalities, integration with existing or future systems of the contracting authority, as well as the provision of monitoring, analysis, alerting and reporting functionalities in accordance with the Specifications. 4. Cybersecurity and data protection services The provider will ensure the implementation of cybersecurity measures necessary for the protection of the infrastructure and managed data, including the configuration of access control mechanisms, auditing, communications protection and compliance with legal requirements regarding information security and data protection in accordance with the Specifications. 5. Testing, commissioning and reception services The provider/supplier will ensure the functional testing of the implemented system, the performance of operational trials, the remediation of any identified non-conformities, as well as the commissioning of the system and the support necessary in the reception process in accordance with the Specifications. 6. Staff training services The provider will ensure the training of staff designated by the contracting authority for the purpose of using and operating the system, including the drafting of training materials and the provision of necessary support for the efficient use of the implemented solution in accordance with the Specifications. 7. Maintenance and technical support services The provider will ensure maintenance and technical support services during the contractual period, including interventions for fault remediation, software component updates, as well as measures necessary to ensure the continuity of system operation in accordance with the Specifications. The estimated duration of the contract is 13 months from the date of issuance of the start order, structured as follows: • maximum 4 months for carrying out the analysis, design and drafting activities for the technical documentation related to the project; • maximum 9 months for the supply, implementation, installation, configuration, integration, testing and commissioning of the hardware and software solutions provided in the specifications. The duration of the contract was determined taking into account the technical complexity of the project, the need for phased integration of the PMDI components and the video surveillance system, as well as the testing, reception and operationalisation activities necessary to ensure the proper functioning of the entire implemented digital ecosystem. Annex No 1 to the Specifications sets out the quantities corresponding to the requested services. The detailed final bill of quantities, with the highlighting of the quantities resulting from the Technical Project, will be drawn up and presented after its drafting and approval.

sig_327fc5adf712e23ce6fc.description: 1. INTRODUCTION & SYNOPSIS This announcement is a formal Request for Prototype Proposal (RPP) issued by the Mission & Installation Contracting Command (MICC) – Fort Campbell on behalf of the Directorate of Public Works (DPW) at Fort Campbell, Kentucky. The Government is seeking competitive prototype proposals to design, integrate, and execute a modernized facility management solution across 58 unaccompanied housing (barracks) facilities. The prototype will integrate an advanced, secure Enterprise Asset Management (EAM) software platform with cross-trained physical maintenance execution to streamline work order triage, optimize Between Occupancy Maintenance (BOM), and execute proactive Preventative Maintenance Orders (PMO). Authority: 10 U.S.C. § 4022, Other Transaction Authority (OTA) for Prototype Projects. Agreement Type: The Government intends to award a single Other Transaction (OT) agreement. Follow-on Production / Sustainment: Offerors are advised that in accordance with 10 U.S.C. § 4022(f), successful completion of this prototype project may result in the award of a non-competitive, follow-on production/sustainment agreement or contract without further competition. 2. BACKGROUND Fort Campbell DPW is responsible for maintaining unaccompanied housing infrastructure that directly impacts Soldier readiness and Quality of Life (QoL). The current operating model relies heavily on manual administrative workflows, disparate tracking mechanisms, and reactive maintenance practices, leading to extended vacancy timelines during unit rotations, misdiagnosed service dispatches, and increased facility wear. This prototype project seeks to validate a modernized operational model that combines commercial best practices with enterprise Army platforms (including integration with ArMA, GFEBS, and the forthcoming enterprise IBM Maximo migration). Key modernization elements include QR-code-enabled request intake, automated work order routing, decentralized parts staging solutions (e.g., smart lockers), and dual-track maintenance (physical inspections for legacy systems and sensor-based monitoring for modern equipment). 3. ELIGIBILITY This RPP is open to all responsible business entities. In accordance with 10 U.S.C. § 4022(d)(1), an award may only be made if at least one of the following conditions is met: At least one nontraditional defense contractor or small business participates to a significant extent in the prototype project; OR All significant participants in the transaction other than the Federal Government are small businesses or nontraditional defense contractors; OR At least one-third (1/3) of the total cost of the prototype project is to be paid out of funds provided by sources other than the Federal Government (cost share); OR The Senior Procurement Executive provides written approval for exceptional circumstances. 4. PROPOSAL SUBMISSION & KEY DATES Proposal Instructions: Interested Offerors shall submit a comprehensive proposal package consisting of: Technical Approach (addressing EAM integration, physical maintenance, and predictive monitoring) Integrated Logistics & Sustainability Plan (addressing supply chain, SOPs, and knowledge transfer) Management, Programmatic, & Lifecycle Approach (Integrated Master Schedule, risk management, and scaling) Cost / Price Proposal Performance Work Statement (PWS) (directly derived from Attachment 001, Statement of Objectives) Key Dates: Questions Due Date: Sep 16, 2026, at 11:00 AM Central Time (CT) Site Visit Date: Sep 17, 2026, at 10:00 AM CT Proposal Due Date: Sep 25, 2026, at 11:00 AM Central Time (CT) Submission Instructions: Method: All questions and proposals must be submitted electronically via email. Email Address: evan.m.rea.civ@army.mil 5. GOVERNMENT POINTS OF CONTACT (POCs) Agreements Officer (AO): Eric C. Boston (eric.c.boston.civ@army.mil) Agreements Specialist / Contract Specialist: Evan M. Rea (evan.m.rea.civ@army.mil)

sig_33000f3352f4e6bdda41.description: According to SURF and its members, the future of ICT and associated services for education and research lies to a significant extent in the cloud. The members (institutions) therefore wish to be able to make flexible use of the cloud and combine it with their own ICT infrastructures (hybrid infrastructure). In practice, transitioning to the cloud is not a simple step, and for many institutions, little experience has been gained with it. As a result, unexpected challenges can arise during the execution of cloud projects as well as in the subsequent management phase. The initially intended benefits are then not achieved, which can lead to a risk of failure or capital destruction. To support institutions with these challenges, it is therefore desirable to make SURFcumulus Professional Services available to them via a SURF tender. SURF has chosen to conduct this via a DPS. The delivery of SURFcumulus Professional Services is explicitly linked to the SURFcumulus service. Specifically, this concerns executive, common services intended for cloud implementation, migration, and management. Delivery takes place on the basis of a fixed price and a fixed delivery date. A further description of the service components is as follows: Setting up a cloud landing zone, integrated into an institution's existing (hybrid) architecture, at least including: Account setup: based on the administrative organisation, compliance guidelines, existing environments, and structures of the institution. Network configuration: according to guidelines, within cloud environments and between on-premise and these cloud environments. Security baseline: identity and access management based on SURFconext, availability of standardised, hardened machine images, security policies, network monitoring, and log analytics. Automation: standardised setup of security, governance, and cost optimisation. Executing/supporting cloud migrations, by means of: Lift-and-shift migration scenario: moving (part of) an ICT infrastructure from a data centre to the cloud without major changes. Re-design migration scenario: making (part of) an existing ICT infrastructure cloud-ready and/or implementing replacement, newly built solutions so that the potential of the cloud can be optimally utilised. Delivering cloud managed services in the (hybrid) cloud infrastructure, including, for example: Operations (account management, software update management, licence management, network management, backup & restore, monitoring, platform management) Application management (technical application management, functional application management, data management, application configuration management) Service support (incident, problem & change management, multi-vendor coordination, second and third-line support, escalation handling) Service delivery (service level management, capacity, cost, and continuity management) Information security and privacy protection (detection, prevention, reporting, adjustment). See further the added document "Toelatingsleidraad DAS SURFcumulus Professional Services".
sig_33000f3352f4e6bdda41.title: DAS SURF Cumulus Professional Services 2023

sig_3302b5a39cb60ed79550.description: Cold homes, damp, mould and fuel poverty are driving poor health outcomes, increasing pressure on healthcare services and deepening inequalities. While Registered Social Landlords are investing in warmer, more energy-efficient housing and responding to new regulatory requirements, fuel poverty means many vulnerable residents remain at risk, even in high-quality homes. Current approaches are often reactive and lack mechanisms to target support for those that might be the very most vulnerable, addressing issues only after harm has occurred. This Challenge seeks innovative solutions that can help registered social landlords identify where housing conditions, fuel poverty and individual vulnerability combine to create the greatest risk of harm, then translate that insight into practical, targeted action that combats these impacts, improves tenants’ health and wellbeing outcomes, protects homes and makes better use of limited housing and support resources. Solutions must be affordable at RSL scale, protect tenant privacy, and connect insight to action so that Cloch can complete investigation and repair work within statutory timescales.

sig_332ac9ded4e88023b8e6.buyer_name: Medical University of Lusatia - Carl Thiem
sig_332ac9ded4e88023b8e6.description: This ex-ante notice is published in addition to a planned negotiated procedure. For the proper operation of the model medical degree programme at the Lausitz Medical University - Carl Thiem, the use of a specialised software solution for integrated timetable, room, group and lecturer planning as well as course registration is strictly necessary. The degree programme is characterised by very high planning complexity. This arises in particular from rotation- and model-based curricula, small-scale medical teaching formats, changing small and extra-small groups, the integration of clinical teaching locations, and the necessity of medical-specific course registration with mandatory attendance. Several tens of individual appointments per semester must be planned taking into account rooms, travel times, groups, teaching capacities and didactic dependencies. Manual or semi-manual planning is organisationally unachievable, non-scalable and highly prone to error. Without a suitable software solution, there is a considerable risk of overlaps, capacity errors, delays in study operations and failure to comply with organisational and legal requirements. The procurement is therefore a mandatory prerequisite for ensuring stable, transparent and rule-compliant teaching operations, for the medical-specific integration of timetabling and course registration, and for the further development of the study provision of the Lausitz Medical University - Carl Thiem.
sig_332ac9ded4e88023b8e6.title: Procurement of a software solution for integrated timetable, room, group and lecturer planning as well as course registration for the model medical degree programme

Due to the restriction of 6000 characters, please refer to the Specifications. This tender documentation contains the requirements, criteria, rules and information necessary to provide potential tenderers with complete, accurate and explicit information regarding the application procedure for awarding the contract concerning Services for the systematic registration of real estate in the Integrated Cadastre and Land Book System within the administrative-territorial unit of Sudiți, Ialomița County, and the implementation of a GIS IT platform – a multi-year service contract (maximum duration 46 months), with the issuance of firm orders during its performance. The services concern the real estate located in the cadastral sectors within UAT Sudiți. The total area related to the contract is divided into 4 zones, each consisting of a minimum number of 500 and a maximum of 4000 properties. For each zone, a firm order will be issued specifying the cadastral sector(s), the number of related properties and the set of software modules. The first order will be issued within a maximum of 30 days from the entry into force of the contract, and the other orders will be scheduled over a duration of a minimum of 6 months to a maximum of 40 months from the entry into force of the contract, depending on budgetary availabilities. Two deliveries are planned for each zone: Delivery 1 - Technical cadastral documents for publication and Delivery 2 - Final technical cadastral documents. In this regard, the provision of the services forming the subject of this procurement contributes to achieving the general objective of the contracting authority, namely the systematic registration of real estate in the aforementioned cadastral sectors and the implementation of the IT platform, by establishing a unified spatial database that will lead to the improvement of the quality and efficiency of services provided by the local public administration and to the reduction of the processing time for requests from citizens and institutions. Through the preparation of the technical cadastral documents, the ex officio registration of real estate in the land book, the establishment of the street nomenclature register, and the implementation and updating of the GIS platform, the contracting authority will benefit from the necessary tools for the efficient administration of assets, the support of urban planning processes, the execution of public investments and the prevention of legal risks associated with the lack of compliant technical and cadastral records. The works are carried out within the National Cadastre and Land Book Programme, in compliance with the Cadastre and Real Estate Publicity Law no. 7/1996, republished, with subsequent amendments and completions, the Order of the Director General of ANCPI no. 1/2020 and the Regulation on the payment procedure intended for the co-financing of systematic registration works initiated by administrative-territorial units, approved by the Order of the Director General of ANCPI no. 1065/2018, with subsequent amendments and completions. The procured services shall be provided in accordance with the detailed requirements in the Specifications and its annexes, in compliance with the applicable legislation and the contractual conditions established by the contracting authority. Deadline for receiving requests for clarifications: interested economic operators shall transmit requests for clarifications at least 18 days before the deadline established for the submission of tenders, in accordance with art. 160 and 161 of Law no. 98/2016 on public procurement, as amended and supplemented. Deadline for responding to requests for clarifications: the contracting authority will fully respond to all requests for clarifications, only once, 11 days before the deadline established for the submission of tenders. The contracting authority will only respond to requests for clarifications transmitted via SEAP up to the established deadline. The public procurement has as its object the provision of services for the systematic registration of real estate in the Integrated Cadastre and Land Book System within UAT Sudiți, Ialomița County, and the implementation of a GIS IT platform, within a multi-year service contract, with a maximum duration of 46 months, executed through the issuance of firm orders, depending on the needs of the contracting authority and the budgetary credits approved annually. The services concern the real estate located in cadastral sectors 0, 1, 3, 5, 14, 15, 16 and 17 of UAT Sudiți and include, by way of orientation: carrying out the public information campaign, preliminary activities and specialized works (identification of property and building boundaries, identification of holders and collection of documents, registration of de facto possession), preparation of technical cadastral documents, publication thereof, receipt and resolution of rectification requests, updating of technical documents and ex officio registration of properties in the land book, as well as the implementation of the GIS IT platform, establishment of the street nomenclature register, provision of hardware infrastructure, user training, and provision of warranty and technical support. The total area related to the contract is divided into 4 zones, each consisting of a minimum number of 500 and a maximum of 4000 properties. For each zone, a firm order will be issued specifying the cadastral sector(s), the number of related properties and the set of software modules. The first order will be issued within a maximum of 30 days from the entry into force of the contract, and the other orders will be scheduled over a duration of a minimum of 6 months to a maximum of 40 months, depending on budgetary availabilities. Two deliveries are planned for each zone: Delivery 1 – Technical cadastral documents for publication and Delivery 2 – Final technical cadastral documents.

The nature, content and quantities of the services are detailed in the Specifications and its annexes, which form an integral part of the tender documentation. sig_3469edc6b80bcab2496a.description: The Centers for Disease Control and Prevention's (CDC) National Center for Injury Prevention and Control (NCIPC) is soliciting investigator-initiated gold standard research proposals to rigorously evaluate programs and policies for their impact on primary prevention of child sexual abuse (CSA) or problematic sexual behavior (PSB) among youth. For the purposes of this NOFO: CSA is defined as sexual victimization during childhood (younger than 18 years of age) perpetrated by an adult. PSB is defined as sexual behaviors among children (younger than 18 years of age) that are not developmentally appropriate and have the potential to cause harm to the child or children involved (including behaviors that are unintentionally harmful or inappropriate as well as behaviors intended to cause harm). Research funded under this announcement will strengthen the evidence base for primary prevention of CSA and PSB. Applicants must propose to rigorously evaluate a program or policy for primary prevention of CSA or PSB that addresses one of the following three research priorities: Programs or policies focused on primary prevention of CSA or PSB in digital spaces (e.g., downloading or possession of illegal images of children, nonconsensual image sharing, use of artificial intelligence to create fake explicit images of children); Programs or policies addressing the use of digital spaces for commercial sexual exploitation of children (CSEC) or sex trafficking (e.g., online recruitment of minors for sexual content creation, online advertisements soliciting minors for commercial sex acts, using technology to facilitate in-person meetings with minors for the purpose of sex); Organizational policy approaches focused on primary prevention of CSA or PSB in youth-serving organizations (e.g., community centers, youth development organizations, juvenile residential care facilities, faith-based organizations, group foster care).
sig_3469edc6b80bcab2496a.title: Rigorously Evaluating Approaches to Prevent Child Sexual Abuse and Problematic Sexual Behavior among Youth

INTRODUCTION & SYNOPSIS This announcement is a formal Request for Prototype Proposal (RPP) issued by the Mission & Installation Contracting Command (MICC) – Fort Campbell on behalf of the Directorate of Public Works (DPW) at Fort Campbell, Kentucky. The Government is seeking competitive prototype proposals to design, integrate, and execute a modernized facility management solution across 58 unaccompanied housing (barracks) facilities. The prototype will integrate an advanced, secure Enterprise Asset Management (EAM) software platform with cross-trained physical maintenance execution to streamline work order triage, optimize Between Occupancy Maintenance (BOM), and execute proactive Preventative Maintenance Orders (PMO). Authority: 10 U.S.C. § 4022, Other Transaction Authority (OTA) for Prototype Projects. Agreement Type: The Government intends to award a single Other Transaction (OT) agreement. Follow-on Production / Sustainment: Offerors are advised that in accordance with 10 U.S.C. § 4022(f), successful completion of this prototype project may result in the award of a non-competitive, follow-on production/sustainment agreement or contract without further competition. 2. BACKGROUND Fort Campbell DPW is responsible for maintaining unaccompanied housing infrastructure that directly impacts Soldier readiness and Quality of Life (QoL). The current operating model relies heavily on manual administrative workflows, disparate tracking mechanisms, and reactive maintenance practices, leading to extended vacancy timelines during unit rotations, misdiagnosed service dispatches, and increased facility wear. This prototype project seeks to validate a modernized operational model that combines commercial best practices with enterprise Army platforms (including integration with ArMA, GFEBS, and the forthcoming enterprise IBM Maximo migration). Key modernization elements include QR-code-enabled request intake, automated work order routing, decentralized parts staging solutions (e.g., smart lockers), and dual-track maintenance (physical inspections for legacy systems and sensor-based monitoring for modern equipment). 3. ELIGIBILITY This RPP is open to all responsible business entities. In accordance with 10 U.S.C. § 4022(d)(1), an award may only be made if at least one of the following conditions is met: At least one nontraditional defense contractor or small business participates to a significant extent in the prototype project; OR All significant participants in the transaction other than the Federal Government are small businesses or nontraditional defense contractors; OR At least one-third (1/3) of the total cost of the prototype project is to be paid out of funds provided by sources other than the Federal Government (cost share); OR The Senior Procurement Executive provides written approval for exceptional circumstances. 4. PROPOSAL SUBMISSION & KEY DATES Proposal Instructions: Interested Offerors shall submit a comprehensive proposal package consisting of: Technical Approach (addressing EAM integration, physical maintenance, and predictive monitoring) Integrated Logistics & Sustainability Plan (addressing supply chain, SOPs, and knowledge transfer) Management, Programmatic, & Lifecycle Approach (Integrated Master Schedule, risk management, and scaling) Cost / Price Proposal Performance Work Statement (PWS) (directly derived from Attachment 001, Statement of Objectives) Key Dates: Questions Due Date: Sep 16, 2026, at 11:00 AM Central Time (CT) Site Visit Date: Sep 17, 2026, at 10:00 AM CT Proposal Due Date: Sep 25, 2026, at 11:00 AM Central Time (CT) Submission Instructions: Method: All questions and proposals must be submitted electronically via email. Email Address: evan.m.rea.civ@army.mil 5. GOVERNMENT POINTS OF CONTACT (POCs) Agreements Officer (AO): Eric C. Boston (eric.c.boston.civ@army.mil) Agreements Specialist / Contract Specialist: Evan M. sig_34cfb216a1e442309086.description: The Republic of Moldova is undergoing an accelerated and complex European Union accession process following the opening of accession negotiations with the EU in 2024. The accession process requires comprehensive alignment of Moldova's legal, institutional and policy framework with the EU acquis, as well as strengthened governance structures, institutional coordination mechanisms and implementation capacities at national and local level. In September 2025, Moldova successfully completed the screening process for all chapters of the EU acquis, enabling the transition to structured technical negotiations and implementation of opening benchmarks and subsequent requirements identified during the screening process. These developments generate increasing demand for specialised expertise, institutional capacity development and practical support for the implementation of EU-related reforms. Particular importance is attached to reforms related to rule of law, democratic governance, public administration, justice and internal security, especially under Cluster I "Fundamentals", including Chapter 23 (Judiciary and Fundamental Rights) and Chapter 24 (Justice, Freedom and Security). At the same time, Moldova's EU accession process also requires stronger local governance capacities, improved multi-level coordination and increased participation of civil society, diaspora organisations and other stakeholders in EU-related reform processes. In this context, Deutsche Gesellschaft für Internationale Zusammenarbeit (GIZ) GmbH implements the projects "EU Integration Support Project" (EUISP), financed by the German Federal Foreign Office (FFO), and "Facilitating the EU Accession process through Coordination and Engagement in Moldova" (FACE), financed by the German Federal Ministry for Economic Cooperation and Development (BMZ). To support the implementation of these projects, GIZ foresees the establishment of a comprehensive Short-Term Expert Pool (STEP), enabling flexible and demand-driven mobilisation of national and international expertise. The STEP will support activities related to legislative and policy approximation to the EU acquis, negotiation preparation and benchmark fulfilment, institutional and organisational capacity development, strategic planning and coordination, strengthening local governance capacities, facilitation of international cooperation and peer-to-peer exchange, as well as structured stakeholder engagement and support for local initiatives. The contractor implementing the STEP will provide technical advisory services, analytical support, capacity development measures, international exchange formats and implementation support in close cooperation with GIZ and Moldovan partner institutions. The overall objective is to strengthen the capacities of national and local actors to effectively coordinate, implement and support Moldova's EU accession and alignment process. The procurement concerns the establishment and operation of a comprehensive Short-Term Expert Pool (STEP) supporting the implementation of activities under the GIZ projects "EU Integration Support Project" (EUISP) and "Facilitating the EU Accession process through Coordination and Engagement in Moldova" (FACE), both contributing to the Republic of Moldova's EU accession and alignment process. The contractor will provide flexible, demand-driven and results-oriented consultancy and implementation support services aimed at strengthening the capacities of national and local actors involved in Moldova's EU accession process. The services will combine technical advisory support, institutional and organisational capacity development, international experience exchange, stakeholder engagement and support for local initiatives. The contractor will be responsible for identifying, mobilising, coordinating and managing national and international experts and support measures in close cooperation with GIZ and Moldovan partner institutions. The assignment may include the following services and activities: - technical, legal and methodological advisory services related to EU acquis alignment, policy development and implementation of EU-related reforms; - preparation and revision of draft laws, regulations, strategies, methodologies, guidelines and analytical documents; - institutional, legislative and implementation gap analyses, including assessment of institutional capacities and implementation readiness; - support for negotiation process, fulfilment of opening and closing benchmarks and related monitoring and reporting processes; - development and strengthening of strategic planning, coordination, monitoring and reporting mechanisms related to EU accession and EU-aligned reforms; - provision of thematic expertise related to rule of law, democratic governance, justice, internal security, public administration reform and local governance; - design and delivery of trainings, workshops, mentoring, coaching and institutional learning activities for representatives of public institutions and other stakeholders; - organisation and facilitation of international peer-to-peer exchange, study visits, policy dialogues, expert discussions and cooperation formats involving EU Member States, accession countries and international experts; - support for strengthening coordination, cooperation and communication mechanisms between national institutions, local public authorities and other stakeholders involved in the accession process; - support for participatory and stakeholder engagement processes involving civil society organisations, diaspora representatives, women"s organisations and organisations representing vulnerable groups; - support for strengthening local governance capacities and practical application of EU-related planning, implementation and monitoring approaches at local level; - support for the conceptualisation, management and implementation of small-scale support initiatives and local contributions linked to EU accession-related objectives; - facilitation of innovative cooperation, consultation and policy development formats, including policy labs, simulation exercises and practical learning approaches; - monitoring, reporting, documentation and knowledge management activities related to the implementation of the assignment. The contractor will ensure process-oriented and implementation-oriented delivery of services, including quality assurance, operational coordination, backstopping and effective mobilisation of expertise throughout the contract period. Particular emphasis will be placed on ensuring the practical applicability of delivered support, strengthening institutional ownership and supporting sustainable implementation of EU-related reforms at both national and local level. Services will be implemented in close coordination with GIZ and relevant Moldovan partner institutions, including the Bureau for European Integration within the State Chancellery, line ministries, local public authorities, civil society organisations and other relevant stakeholders. Given the dynamic nature of the EU accession process, the assignment requires a high degree of flexibility and responsiveness in order to address evolving priorities, reform needs and operational requirements related to Moldova's EU accession and alignment process.

sig_34d88c631a5b77984883.description:
In times of crisis, information, both correct and incorrect, spreads to an unprecedented extent. Social media in particular contribute to the spread of intentional disinformation and unintentional misinformation due to their high speed of dissemination and perceived anonymity. Furthermore, artificial intelligence opens up unprecedented possibilities in the generation and dissemination of disinformation. In radiological emergencies, this can lead to uncertainty and to citizens not adhering to protective measures. Furthermore, disinformation (e.g. about a necessary evacuation) can lead the population to potentially harmful behaviour and trigger chaotic conditions. While the spread of disinformation is problematic in many respects, the problem in a radiological emergency is that institutions and decision-makers have to identify and react to it under high time pressure. The BMUKN and BfS would also be confronted with the citizens' need for information and a flood of misinformation and disinformation, which makes the rapid and targeted dissemination of correct information very difficult. However, rapid and effective crisis communication is essential in a radiological emergency. The research project is intended to compile the current state of knowledge on disinformation and misinformation and to systematically analyse and prepare it for the purposes of crisis communication and radiological emergency protection for the BMUKN and BfS. The focus is on the following questions: - What disinformation and misinformation exist in the context of radiological emergencies or could arise? - What types of actors and motivations can be identified/categorised? - What strategic deductions for crisis communication already exist or can be drawn? - Which strategies against disinformation and misinformation are classified as promising in the context of radiological emergencies, and which are less so? The aim of the research project is to (1) identify tools and methods for the detection of disinformation that the BfS can use in a radiological emergency and (2) to develop concrete recommendations for the strategic handling of disinformation in crisis communication in a radiological emergency. It should become clear which findings on existing disinformation and misinformation in radiological emergencies and other crises relevant to the issue are available and which strategies can be used for communication in a radiological emergency as well as for the development of communication exercises to prepare for an actual situation. The project is not intended to comprise a general treatise on disinformation and misinformation in general, but rather to be specifically tailored to the needs of the BfS and BMUKN. At the end of the project, there will be an overview of concrete tools for detection and guidance on the strategic handling of disinformation in a radiological emergency. The present research project thus offers the BMUKN and BfS an important basis for informing the population both about a radiological situation and about precautionary or protective recommendations and thus serves the implementation of the Radiation Protection Act, in particular §105 and §112. The basis for the performance of tasks by the BMUKN/BfS is the current state of science and technology in accordance with atomic and radiation protection law. The investigations, studies and expert reports commissioned by the BMUKN/BfS must therefore be based on the current state of science and technology in the respective field of work. In this context, new findings and scientific-technical progress must be identified and evaluated with a view to the objectives of the project. The bidder must be in a position to carry out the required investigations on a scientifically sound basis in accordance with the requirements for scientific practice in the described areas of responsibility. The provision of services must be carried out in a data protection-friendly manner. All currently applicable legal requirements, such as the GDPR and BDSG, must be implemented. If personal data (Art. 4 No. 1 GDPR) or even certain categories of personal data, e.g. health data, political opinions, etc. (Art. 9 Para. 1 GDPR) are processed, a data processing agreement (DPA) or an agreement on joint processing may have to be concluded. The contractor must submit a data protection concept and comply with all obligations of the GDPR. The data must not leave the scope of the GDPR. sig_353a5497188f16ab5553.description: Stirling Council, as part of the Stirling and Clackmannanshire City Region Deal’s Digital Quarter, is soon to undertake a procurement exercise for the operation of new digital and coworking space being developed in Callander. This will be located in a newly extended and refurbished library building in Callander (on Church Street, a short distance from the Main Street in Callander). The proposal is for a flexible space where some rooms will be bookable in their entirety for meetings or other use, alongside desk space for individual rentals and access to other services. A feasibility previously commissioned highlighted the need for informal space for networking as well as the more formal space for desks and meetings. In addition there will be shared access to equipment such as a printer, and also a newly installed kitchen. Early consultation with the market as part of the feasibility stage has indicated that 24/7 access to the hub is essential, as is a welcoming and person-centric feel to the facility. A membership model could be considered. To support early market engagement and inform the development of the service specification, we are pleased to invite potential operators of the facility to attend an information session about the forthcoming business opportunity. The purpose of this session is to: - Share initial proposals regarding the scope of the procurement - Gather insights and feedback from potential service providers particularly in terms of possible design layouts before the design is finalised. - Understand market capabilities and any operational constraints - Explore innovative approaches to operating a coworking space. Session Details: Date: Wednesday 10 December 2025 Time: 3pm-4pm Location: Callander Library, South Church Street, Callander, FK17 8BN We welcome your participation and would be grateful for your input. Please confirm your attendance by 5pm on Tuesday 9 December by emailing investinstirling@stirling.gov.uk. We look forward to engaging with you at the session. Lot 1: . sig_35dff215c51ce3c4f509.description: Dumfries and Galloway Council has a requirement to progress the proposed 500km North Solway Coastal Path project to RIBA Stage 4 technical design. The project is part of the Solway Coast and Marine Project – landscape connections project, part funded through the National Lottery Heritage Fund (NLHF) Landscape Connections programme. Lot 1: . Dumfries and Galloway Council has a requirement to progress the proposed 500km North Solway Coastal Path project to RIBA Stage 4 technical design. The project is part of the Solway Coast and Marine Project – landscape connections project, part funded through the National Lottery Heritage Fund (NLHF) Landscape Connections programme. The project has been awarded a stage 1 development and the timescale for this element of the project is expected to include tender requests being issued in December 2025/ January 2026 with a delivery phase for this stage of 11-12 months ending in December 2026. It is anticipated that the construction phase will commence in late 2027, dependent on a successful stage 2 application to the NLHF Landscape Connections programme, with an 8-year implementation period. Many sections of the route are already designated core paths however there are gaps in the coast network, and the existing access infrastructure is variable in quality. The deliverables from the design phase will be based on an agreed physical sub-division of the route provided which is based on an initial business case proposal and will include: · Creation of a GIS digital mapping information layer to an agreed format · Detailed information on land ownerships derived from SCOTLIS, investigations, existing records and local knowledge. · Survey of agreed routes and existing route infrastructure including an audit of existing Core Path sections for current condition, useability and signage · Recommendations for upgrading of existing path sections to an agreed standard for a promoted route · Identification of potential candidate fully accessible route sections suitable for all abilities to viewpoints/ places of interest from access points and linking to coastal gateway sites and car parks. · Directional signage strategy and detailed recommendations for implementation · Detailed design access infrastructure proposals for existing Core Path sections · Options appraisal for new path section and initial discussions with landowners · Detailed design proposals for new path route sections including access infrastructure and surfacing types · Detailed costings and designs for proposed works for each route section and sub divided into each individual landholding · A full project delivery plan based on sections and schedule in both electronic and hard copy format · Proposals and recommendations for a phased delivery.
sig_35dff215c51ce3c4f509.title: DGC North Solway Coast Path for RIBA 2-4 design

INTRODUCTION The Personal Property Activity (PPA) is conducting market research to understand how integrating vendor systems with a government central platform via an Application Programming Interface (API) will affect household goods (HHG) moving, shipping, transportation, and storage service providers. Accordingly, the PPA invites industry partners and service providers to submit detailed information regarding integration costs, associated software development timelines, standard industry practices, and recommendations for testing and risk mitigation when connecting their internal software systems to a central Government platform. This RFI enables industry stakeholders to provide direct feedback on how this type of integration will impact their current systems and operations, helping to shape future technical requirements and acquisition decisions. This RFI is issued solely for informational and planning purposes and does not constitute a solicitation for proposals. Responses to this notice are not offers and cannot form a binding contract. The PPA is not under any obligation to pursue any acquisition alternative based on this RFI, and the Government will not compensate respondents for any information received. All submissions will be kept confidential, will become the property of the U.S. Government, and will not be returned. sig_36c73f863cc6fd0a94ab.description: Lofoten IKT is an intermunicipal ICT company that provides ICT services to the municipal sector in Lofoten. We currently serve approx. 4,000 employees in all municipal sectors. From 1 January 2027 the company will be organised in two separate ICT companies, with each company serving approx. 2,000 employees. The operation will be carried out with very small professional environments (approx. 5-6 persons per company). Vestvågøy and Moskenes will be run by one company, while Vågan and Flakstad are operated by another company. Værøy may expire from 2027 and Flakstad may be operated from Vestvågøy/Moskenes from 2028. Actual requirement holders are i.a.: * Development Department * The Agency for Buildings and Property * The Agency for Housing Management * Water and sewage department * Agency for Urban Environment * The Agency for Sports Affairs * The Agency for Planning and Building RELATION TO EXISTING AGREEMENTS The dynamic purchasing system will supplement the existing framework agreements. sig_36e28a04fdccdd85b452.description: The Institute of Public Administration (IPA) proposes to engage in a competitive process for the establishment of a Panel of training and digital learning subject matter experts to design, develop and deliver a comprehensive suite of digital learning solutions to the Public Service. The training portfolio will utilise both synchronous and asynchronous delivery methods including virtual instructor-led, self-paced eLearning and other modes of digital learning. The IPA will use this Panel to develop a new portfolio of digital learning solutions for the Public Service. The existing OneLearning course portfolio will be merged with other offerings in the IPA to remove duplication and will be developed into thematic Learning Pathways. Components of the pathways will be developed and delivered using a range of digital learning tools and technologies, including live instructor-led, self-paced learning and enhanced collaborative learning. In addition, the IPA will also introduce a new digital learning platform in 2026 that will build on existing digital learning capabilities and will be accessible to the public service from 2027. Full list of requirements are outlined in the procurement documents.
sig_36e28a04fdccdd85b452.title: The establishment of a Panel for the design, development and delivery of digital learning solutions for the Institute of Public Administration

sig_36e2e3179fda25959c97.description: Review of the IT security of the contracting authority's systems and applications through targeted penetration tests and supplementary security analyses. The objective is the identification of vulnerabilities as well as the derivation of measures for risk minimisation. 1.2. Overarching procurement objectives of the CA The CA pursues at least the following strategic objectives with the award of the contract: • Raising the level of information security • Preventive risk minimisation • Compliance with internal and regulatory requirements for information security 1.3. Subject-matter of the contract The CA intends, within the framework of an EU-wide tender procedure, to award the provision of services for the execution of penetration tests, security analyses as well as evaluations and reportings. The scope of services comprises in particular: - the review of the IT security of the systems and applications of the contracting authority through targeted penetration tests and supplementary security analyses - the identification of vulnerabilities as well as the derivation of measures for risk minimisation. The contractor (C) may furthermore propose additional tests, provided these represent a comprehensible added value for the CA. A specific result, in particular the complete identification of all vulnerabilities, is not owed. 2. Service call-off and contract structure: The services are provided on the basis of an EVB-IT service contract, whereby there is initially an initial conception phase and subsequently the individual tests are provided on the basis of individual call-offs. The services are provided on the basis of an EVB-IT service contract. At the beginning of the contract term, a preparation and conception phase takes place for the coordination of the procedure, prioritisation of the test items as well as creation of a call-off and prioritisation plan. The C draws this up together with the CA. The plan serves for the definition and prioritisation of the penetration tests to be carried out in the respective service period as well as the planning and coordination of the individual service call-offs. The call-off and prioritisation plan is to be updated jointly by the CA and C as required during the contract term and adapted to changed functional, technical or security-relevant requirements. The execution of the penetration tests takes place on a demand-driven basis on the basis of individual call-offs by the CA. The CA is entitled to commission and have carried out several individual call-offs in parallel, insofar as this is necessary from a functional, organisational or security-technical perspective. For the contract term, an annual maximum call-off volume of approx. 120 person-days (PD) is assumed as a non-binding calculation and planning basis. The stated quantity is based on the currently expected demand and serves exclusively as orientation for contract implementation. It does not constitute a minimum purchase quantity and neither establishes a claim by the contractor to the call-off of specific services nor an obligation by the contracting authority for the full utilisation of the estimated service volume. The actual demand for penetration test services can vary during the contract term and is commissioned by the contracting authority in line with demand in accordance with operational, technical and security-relevant requirements. 2.1. Remuneration and billing Remuneration is made exclusively on the basis of the services actually commissioned and provided at the person-day rates specified in the offer and other contractually agreed conditions. Billing takes place monthly in arrears. A verifiable statement of services must be attached to the invoice, showing the respective individual call-off, the service period, the activities provided, the roles deployed and the person-days rendered per role. Billing takes place at the person-day rates agreed in the price sheet for Senior Consultant, Consultant and Junior Consultant. Each individual call-off contains at least: - the description of the test item, - the intended test scope and test depth, - the test type to be applied (e.g. black box, grey box or white box), - the prioritisation of the call-off, - the planned service period as well as - where applicable, special functional or technical requirements. Planned project phases per year: The subsequent project phases form the annually recurring framework for the planning, execution and evaluation of all individual call-offs. The overall planning worked out in the preparation and conception phase as well as the call-off and prioritisation plan form the basis for the subsequent individual call-offs. Several individual call-offs can be carried out in parallel or staggered in time within the testing phase. Preparation phase: 2-4 weeks. Testing phase: 4-6 weeks. Evaluation phase: 4 weeks. The actual duration of the individual project phases may deviate depending on the scope, complexity, criticality and availability of the respective test items.

sig_3702bd1c5c5b310e8b6b.description: The objective of the Finnish Institute for Health and Welfare (also THL) is to initiate a procurement process targeting two (2) new digital pathology glass scanners for the histology laboratories of THL's forensic medicine unit located in Helsinki and Turku (one device in both). The subject of the planned procurement would include the software and systems/system integrations required by the scanners, as well as the services required for the maintenance of the devices and software. The assumption is that the procurement would not need to separately account for specific device-bound supplies or spare parts. With the procurement of the scanners, the forensic medicine unit would be introducing digital pathology investigation methods, where the histological deceased samples from the unit's five (5) locations would be scanned into digital format so that they could be examined regardless of location. On an annual basis, the deceased samples to be scanned would be approximately 80 000 items and would be divided equally between the two (2) scanners. A total of approximately 50 users should have the ability to view the images. The baskets entering the scanners must be compatible with the baskets of the Sakura Prisma automated staining machine used by the contracting authority. The preliminary idea is to tender the procurement as a single entity, because the devices and their associated services must be uniform. The devices can be procured as a service solution, on a leasing model, or as owned; the procurement model will be specified later. During the market dialogue, alternatives will be explored and the impacts of regulation will also be taken into account (most recently the amendment to the Energy Efficiency Act, ETL 1382/2025). ADDITIONAL INFORMATION This notice is a market consultation notice. This notice does not request tenders. Associated with the market consultation notice is an invitation to register for the market dialogue. 1. Market Dialogue The market dialogue may consist of, for example, answering questions posed by the contracting authority, providing written comments on preliminary tender request materials, and possibly Teams meetings before the publication of the tender request. No compensation is paid for participating in the market dialogue. Participation in the market dialogue does not bind a potential tenderer interested in the procurement to participate in a tender competition that may be implemented later. Nor does the market dialogue obligate the contracting authority to implement the actual procurement procedure. All information presented in this market consultation notice and during the market dialogue is preliminary and indicative advance information, and is not binding on any kind of solution. 2. Registration We kindly ask interested companies to register for the market dialogue and answer preliminary questions via the Forms form no later than Mon 20.4.2026 at 12:00 (Finnish time): https://forms.cloud.microsoft/e/rn9RbaN4xJ Please note that registrations should not be made via Tarjouspalvelu. Hansel Oy will act in a consulting role in the possible procurement.
sig_3702bd1c5c5b310e8b6b.title: Digipatologian skannerit

sig_3795cc158346f9b397b4.description: The Hochschule für Angewandte Wissenschaften Campus Wien (HCW) (abbreviated as 'HCW') is issuing a call for tenders for the introduction and operation of an integrated controlling, planning and reporting system as a software-as-a-service solution for the HCW and its affiliated companies. The solution is intended to replace the existing controlling system and consolidate financial, personnel and project controlling, multi-year budgeting, forecasting and simulation, as well as management reporting, on a uniform, comprehensible data basis. Essential elements include the automated connection of existing legacy systems (in particular BMD, REXX, DOXIS, LEAP and HCW-Portal), the distribution and planning of personnel costs at the level of individual employees, a collaborative planning process with around 200 decentralised planners, and a self-service reporting landscape based on Power BI. Power BI licensing will be provided by the HCW. Implementation is scheduled for 2027, with go-live from 2028. In addition to implementation, the scope of services also includes operation, support, maintenance and further development of the solution over a contract period that, from today's perspective, is expected to last several years. The objective of this procurement procedure is therefore the conclusion of a 'contract for a controlling, planning and reporting system' (abbreviated as 'service contract') between the HCW on the one hand and the bidder ranked best in this procurement procedure on the other. Please refer to the procurement documents for further information.
sig_3795cc158346f9b397b4.title: University of Applied Sciences Campus Vienna – Controlling, Planning and Reporting System

sig_38315dbd07a92a335666.description: Procurement of an operating environment for the Geoportal-Hessen Lot LOT-0000: Procurement of an operating environment for the Geoportal-Hessen. The Hessian State Office for Land Management and Geoinformation is an administrative unit of the Federal State of Hesse and houses, among other things, the central competence centre for geoinformation. In accordance with Section 3 Para. 2 No. 2 of the Ordinance for the Execution of the Hessian Surveying and Geoinformation Act (HVGGAusfVO), this centre is responsible for the operation, administration and further development of the Geoportal Hessen (Section 36 Para. 2 HVGG). The Geoportal Hessen (www.geoportal.hessen.de) is the central access node to the spatial data infrastructure Hesse (GDI-Hessen). It serves as a central platform for spatial data, spatial data services and the associated metadata provided by the state administration and municipal local authorities. For continued operation, the central competence centre for geoinformation is seeking an IT service provider to provide and operate the necessary infrastructure for the technical operation of the Geoportal Hessen. The frontend of the geoportal must be accessible via the internet. Secure remote access via the NdB (Network of the Federal Administration) is required for the maintenance and care of the software components used. The aim is to conclude an EVB-IT contract. All services must be provided by the contractor in close consultation with the client. The provision of the operating environment including all communication requirements in accordance with the migration roadmap stage 1 for the Geoportal Hessen must take place by 31.12.2026. The contractor's data centre must be designed for the highly secure and highly available operation of specialist applications, and the contractor must have sound experience in operating complex IT specialist procedures. The software to be used is fixed, does not form part of the tendered service and is based exclusively on open source components. These include in particular: • Linux operating system (currently Debian), • Mapbender 2.8 (<3), • PostgreSQL with PostGIS, • MapServer, • Django framework, • MediaWiki. The software can be viewed at: • https://github.com/GDI-HE/Mapbender2.8 and • https://github.com/GDI-HE/GeoPortal.rlp The software is based on the aforementioned open source components. The GitHub links serve to specify the software versions to be used and do not represent a product specification, but rather specify the functional requirements for the operating environment. Further details can be found in the specification of services.
sig_38315dbd07a92a335666.title: Procurement of an operating environment for the Geoportal-Hessen
