sig_3b620a3ab5318fcf7c14.description: Digital Payments & Associated Data Services Summary This framework will give the public sector access to various innovative digital payment and data services. These services include merchant acquiring and gateway services. They also include Bacs, Direct Debit, open banking payments, and account information services. RM6411 is let under the Procurement Act 2023. Description RM6411 Digital Payments & Associated Data Services will replace RM6325 Payment Acceptance 2 . It will provide the public sector with a compliant and cost-effective way to access: transactional payment services advanced financial data services This enables the movement of funds in and out of government. Let under the Procurement Act 2023, this agreement aims to: drive payments and financial data innovation simplify and speed up access to financial solutions and data provide a compliant route to market that offers good value for money open up financial data to provide actionable intelligence. The framework will cover a range of digital payments and associated data services. It focuses on these key areas: digital payment management: handling both incoming and outgoing digital payments high-volume transaction capabilities: facilitating the execution of large-scale, bulk payments enhanced security and data insights: using financial data to: provide operational transparency minimise processing errors reduce fraud Benefits: range of payment methods: buyers can choose familiar options like credit/debit cards and direct debits lower transaction costs : open banking infrastructure allows buyers to bypass some card network fees accelerated fund settlement: improving cash flow through near-real-time fund availability paperless financial data verification: instantly verify a citizen’s income or expenditure advanced identity fraud prevention: using secure, real-time bank account ownership verification frictionless user experience: users can authorise payments using their own banking apps Product types: The agreement plans to deliver a wide range of financial capabilities, including: card processing: enabling the acceptance of credit and debit card payments through: online portals phone systems physical terminals bacs & direct debit payments: access to established “bulk” payment rails, including: direct debit for recurring collections faster payments for near-instant transfers CHAPS (clearing house automated payment system) for high-value, same-day transactions open banking payments: allows citizens to pay using their own banking app open banking data services: provide authorised access to a user’s real-time financial data Customer engagement Engagement sessions started in April 2026. They will continue to run until November 2026. If you would like to speak to us about the proposed agreement, please email: digitalpayments@gcagov.uk . sig_3ba4914c5d3ffaf3e707.description: This public notice is a combined synopsis/solicitation for commercial items prepared in accordance with FAR Part 12 and utilizing FAR Part 15 procedures. The solicitation is being released as an Indefinite Delivery, Indefinite Quantity (IDIQ) contract competition. This contract shall include two performance areas to encompass all aspects of procuring new Digital Talking Book Machines and maintaining the new and existing stock at the Library. Performance Area 1 (PA1): DTBM DA2 Production, Parts, and Support This PA includes DA2 units, warranties, spare parts, software development, and other requirements described in Section C. NLS requires Digital Talking Book Machine (DTBM) version DA2 units in quantities sufficient to continue distribution to all audio readers enrolled in the program and maintain a reasonable stock to allow timely replacement of devices in the field to facilitate service, repair, or maintenance of removed devices. NLS requires support for those units including spare parts, software development, and warranty repairs. Performance Area 2 (PA2): Existing Device Support, Incumbent This PA includes proprietary spare parts and software development as described in Section C. NLS also requires repair and support services for the existing incumbent-manufactured NLS DTBM DA2 units (approximately 63,000). This includes spare parts and platform sprints to ensure the units remain safe, functional, and accessible so that the Library’s patrons have the fullest access to materials in the NLS collection. Please see all attachments for the full details of this requirement and instructions for submitting a proposal. Questions are due by 5:00pm eastern time, September 14, 2026. Proposals are due by 5:00pm eastern time, October 5, 2026. Solicitation Amendment -0001 answers Offeror questions. Please see 030ADV27R0001 -0001, Attachment J-6, and revised Attachment J-1.

sig_3bf92bd83107d3529882.description: With this request for information, Fingrid Oyj (hereinafter referred to as Fingrid) initiates a market survey in preparation for a future procurement. Participation in the market dialogue is voluntary, does not create obligations, and does not preclude participation in any subsequent procurement. INSTRUCTIONS FOR RESPONDING TO THE REQUEST FOR INFORMATION We kindly ask you to review attachment: "Appendix 1, Request to participate in the PMC process .pdf" included with this request for information and provide your responses to the questions presented therein. In particular, please answer the six questions listed in Section 5 (“Instructions for responding”) of the document. The response can be submitted using the Tarjouspalvelu.fi (Supplier Portal) functionality or by sending email to jukka.keski-valkama@fingrid.fi before January 28, 2026 at 12:00 (GMT+2).

sig_3c0929d8cf24a9326d56.description: Open, electronic tender, above the thresholds for the conclusion of a contract for the supply of: 1. Supply of SIEM/SOAR system software licence (Security Information and Event Management – SIEM, Security Orchestration, Automation, and Response - SOAR), 2. Renewal of the Software Assurance (SA) Programme for the Ministry's Microsoft software licences 3. Renewal and extension of support licences (Firmware Updates, Enhanced Support and Phone Support) for the FortiAuthenticator system of the Secure Transmission System (STS) infrastructure, with a total estimated value of 140.300,00€ excluding (without) VAT 24% or 173.972,00€ including VAT 24%. Lot 1 : Supply of SIEM/SOAR system software licence (Security Information and Event Management – SIEM, Security Orchestration, Automation, and Response - SOAR). The requested supply concerns the need to adopt modern security solutions for the Ministry of Education, Religious Affairs and Sports. In this context, it is necessary to procure a SIEM/SOAR system software licence (Security Information and Event Management – SIEM, Security Orchestration, Automation, and Response - SOAR), which will detect threats and automate the response to them, supplementing the technical measures already maintained by the Agency. In detail, a SIEM/SOAR system allows for the centralised collection and analysis of logs from multiple sources, facilitating the timely detection of and immediate response to security incidents. At the same time, it strengthens compliance with regulatory frameworks and supports effective risk management. The installation of such a system in our organisation will provide better oversight of all critical systems, more effective management of security incidents and greater compliance with legal requirements.; Lot 2 : Renewal of the Software Assurance (SA) Programme for the Ministry's Microsoft software licences. The requested service provision concerns the renewal of the Software Assurance (SA) programme for the Microsoft software licences held by the Service. It is noted that, following a tender procedure for the conclusion of a contract by the competent financial services, its procurement was carried out, valid until October 2026 (31-10-2026). However, as the programme in question is considered essential for the smooth operation, security and continuous support of the Ministry's information systems, its renewal for three (3) years is deemed necessary.; Lot 3 : Renewal and extension of support licences (Firmware Updates, Enhanced Support and Phone Support) for the FortiAuthenticator system of the Secure Transmission System (STS) infrastructure. The requested service provision concerns the support of firmware upgrade licences (firmware and general updates), enhanced technical support, as well as phone support for the FortiAuthenticator system of the Secure Transmission System (STS) infrastructure, which is expected to expire on 23-10-2026. Taking into account the criticality of the system in question for the smooth operation of the STS, the renewal and extension of the above support licences up to and including 23-02-2030 is deemed necessary.

Renewal and Extension of Support Licences (Firmware Updates, Enhanced Support and Phone Support) for the FortiAuthenticator System of the Secure Transmission System (STS) Infrastructure

sig_3c0f126a91ca2b9fbc53.description: The subject of the framework agreement is the provision, introduction, integration, support and further development of a software solution for permanently operable vulnerability management, including licences, services, interfaces as well as analysis, reporting and control functions. The subject of the tender is the conclusion of a framework agreement for the provision, introduction, integration, support and further development of vulnerability management for the contracting authority's IT landscape. The goal of the procurement is the transition of an already existing basic technical structure into a stable, permanently operable and future-proof regular operation. For this purpose, a suitable software solution including the necessary licences or subscriptions as well as the services required for operation and further development must be provided. The solution should enable the structured identification, analysis, assessment, prioritisation and tracking of vulnerabilities within the contracting authority's IT landscape. The scope of services includes in particular the provision, setup, configuration, integration, optimisation and ongoing support of the solution. This includes integration into the contracting authority's existing system and process landscape, support in establishing and ensuring operational readiness, improvement of scan coverage, optimisation of data quality, and the provision of suitable reporting, analysis and control functions. Furthermore, existing IT service management processes are to be supported and suitable interfaces for the acquisition, processing and transfer of relevant information are to be provided. The framework agreement does not establish any minimum purchase obligation for the contracting authority. The quantities, hourly rates, reference quantities, demand values and maximum quantities specified in the tender documents serve exclusively to determine the contract value, the comparability of the tenders and the award evaluation. There is no entitlement to the actual call-off of these quantities or services.
sig_3c0f126a91ca2b9fbc53.title: Procurement of software for vulnerability management including licences, implementation, operational and support services

sig_3c13bd877635fb3771d3.description: Open 1.The subject of the Contract is the modernisation, development and maintenance of the 35mm.online platform together with the implementation of the AI Film Chatbot functionality (hereinafter referred to as the "Platform" or "System"). 2.The platform must constitute a coherent IT environment supporting the presentation, searching, sharing, playback and management of the Contracting Authority's audiovisual and audio resources, including VOD/OTT content, audio materials within the Phonotheque, materials intended for professional user support within the PRO Catalogue and future distribution channels, in particular FAST channels, to the extent specified in the Description of the Subject of the Contract (hereinafter "OPZ"). 3.As part of the execution of the Contract, the Contractor is obliged at least to: 1)conduct a pre-implementation analysis, covering business processes, data, current Platform components, integration, migration, security, digital accessibility, the AI Film Chatbot, maintenance, hosting and user requirements; 2)develop a functional and technical design, logical architecture, UX/UI design and system design for the web service, mobile applications, SZT, AI Film Chatbot, Phonotheque, PRO Catalogue and integration interfaces for existing and future access channels; 3)implement the modernisation of the 35mm.online web service, including public and logged-in views, content library at "/vod" and category paths, detail pages, creator pages, collections, series modules, search engines (simple and advanced search engine using AI mechanisms), user account, registration, login and contact forms with field validation and anti-spam mechanisms, including reCAPTCHA or an equivalent solution, "Watchlist", newsletter process support, web-side payments, help centre and player; 4)provide native Android and iOS mobile applications, integrated with the Platform, user accounts and settings, playback, search engine, Push notifications and offline download mechanism; 5)implement one logical Content Management and Platform Support System (SZT), ensuring coherent management of content, metadata, publication, users, permissions, payments, products, reports, VOD materials, Phonotheque, PRO Catalogue and configuration of selected Platform elements; 6)implement an AI Film Chatbot supporting VOD section users in searching, discovering, recommending and explaining Platform resources, in a multilingual model covering at least Polish and English, using an approved knowledge base and maintaining security requirements; 7)modernise the Phonotheque (https://fonoteka.35mm.online) as a functionally separate part of the Platform intended for the presentation, searching, playback and management of audio materials; 8)modernise the PRO Catalogue (https://katalog.35mm.online) as a part of the Platform intended for professional users, including the presentation of the catalogue of materials in the possession of the Contracting Authority, access to screeners and the possibility of downloading the content list of the Pro Catalogue in PDF file format, creating an enquiry or a licence order basket directed to the Contracting Authority's licensing department; 9)provide streaming mechanisms, including live event transmission, transcoding, DRM, geoblocking, CDN/origin, encoding profiles, playback, subtitle support, audio tracks, audio description and 4K/UHD quality for materials and channels for which the Contracting Authority provides such a variant; 10)perform integration with the Contracting Authority's existing systems and services and external services indicated in the OPZ or agreed upon in the pre-implementation analysis; 11)perform migration of data, content, metadata, user accounts, SSO, consents, payment history, subscription history and other data indicated in the OPZ; 12)conduct tests, production launch, post-implementation stabilisation, handover of documentation, conduct training and provide warranty, start-up support, hosting, maintenance and service services to the extent and for the period specified in the Contract; 13)prepare the architecture, data and interfaces of the Platform for supporting FAST channels or equivalent linear internet distribution channels, to the extent specified in the OPZ and approved in the pre-implementation analysis. 14) A detailed description of the Contract is contained in the Description of the Subject of the Contract, which constitutes Annex no 1 to the SWZ. The contract is being executed in connection with the Contracting Authority's participation in the project FERC.02.03-IP.01-0012/25 entitled: "Digital reconstruction and digitisation of film materials, digital film education using AI algorithms and modernisation and development of digital systems for e-sharing of WFDiF film resources", implemented under the European Funds for Digital Development Programme 2021-2027 (FERC 2021+), Priority FERC.02 Advanced digital services; Measure FERC 02.03 Digital accessibility and re-use of information.

sig_3c6906217ed34d1b7a09.description:
Väylävirasto is preparing a procurement, the subject of which is the operating services for the road information systems of Väylävirasto, which suppliers will produce with the help of expert teams. The expert service to be procured includes operator services for six different information systems of Väylävirasto. The procurement is divided into the following four sub-areas. - Sub-area 1 Operation of Tievelho; - Sub-area 2 Operation of the Structural Register; - Sub-area 3 Operation of maintenance and - Sub-area 4 Location reference operation. The goal of the procurement is to ensure the smooth use of information system data from the perspective of data utilisation and updating, and to support the development of information systems. The expert teams will consist of road data experts, structural experts, operators, and technical experts. The roles include both senior and junior-level professionals. The length of the contract has been tentatively set at three years, plus an option of up to two years. Companies interested in the procurement are requested to register for the market survey in accordance with the registration instructions presented below. In the call for tenders, the tenderer may submit a tender for one or more sub-areas. A tender may be submitted independently, together with subcontractors, or as a consortium. Companies interested in the market survey are requested to notify as soon as possible, but no later than 30.9.2026 at 23.00 by filling out the electronic registration form: https://forms.cloud.microsoft/e/ErRyRq6yXZ The market survey consists of the opportunity to comment on the draft material of the tender before the publication of the call for tenders. Please note that this is a market survey notice and this notice does not yet request tenders. Failure to respond to the market survey notice does not prevent participation in a potential call for tenders. The information presented in this market survey notice and the estimated publication date of the call for tenders are preliminary and indicative advance information, which does not bind Väylävirasto to any kind of decision. The preliminary goal of Väylävirasto is to publish the contract notice in January 2027. The market survey notice does not oblige Väylävirasto to carry out the actual procurement procedure. The procurement will form an expert team to support system development, maintenance, and specification, which will be responsible for user support, training, supporting data production processes, data processing and updating, quality management, information services, and documentation and communication related to operation. The experts will identify development needs that arise during operation and convey them to the client and to the separately procured development task specification service. The experts will act at the interface between Väylävirasto, system users, data producers, and maintenance, specification, and further development suppliers. The planned expert team will consist of road data experts, operating service experts, technical data management experts, and project data management experts. The expert team will have both junior and senior-level professionals. A short description of the information system that the supplier's expert team will operate: Basic data repository for road information (Tievelho): Basic data repository for road network infrastructure, condition and measurement data, restrictions, decisions, and classification data.; The procurement will form an expert team, whose tasks include, among others, quality assurance of the Structural Register data, checking and updating data, checking data to correspond to prevailing guidelines, checking data content and quality assurance, checking and updating process diagrams, and specifying data content. The planned expert team will consist of structural experts who have experience in using the Structural Register. A security clearance will be conducted on the experts. A short description of the information system that the supplier's expert team will operate: Structural Register: The Structural Register is a basic data repository for structures and an asset management system. In addition to administrative and structural data, it contains, for example, damage and condition data on structures such as bridges, tunnels, and fixed sea marks. In addition to objects owned by Väylävirasto, the register also contains data on structures owned by municipalities and cities. The Structural Register serves, for example, the experts and service providers of Väylävirasto, Centres for Economic Development, Transport and the Environment, as well as municipalities and cities. The system is being developed and the data content is being expanded continuously.; The procurement will form an expert team, whose tasks include ensuring the smooth use of maintenance information system data from the perspective of data utilisation and updating. A key goal is to ensure that maintenance information systems contain and are provided with up-to-date, high-quality, and structurally uniform data. The background is an identified need to: • Develop and implement quality control of data in maintenance information systems. • Maintain data in maintenance systems. • Produce data and materials for the needs of experts. • Develop and implement a uniform way of data management • Support data production processes in the production and utilisation of road data and maintenance data. • Develop, support, and supervise the data management related to road maintenance of Väylävirasto and Centres for Economic Development, Transport and the Environment • Develop and maintain instructions and documentation related to the utilisation and updating of maintenance data • Support Väylävirasto in development projects related to maintenance and road data management. The planned expert team will consist of operating service experts. The expert team will have both junior and senior-level professionals. Short descriptions of the information systems that the supplier's expert team will operate: YHA: Repair management system YHA (formerly

maintenance management system) is used for programming repair sites (selection, prioritisation and timing of sites and measures), calculating the impact of the planned programme, reporting and monitoring condition data, and exporting contracts to the Harja system. The system is used to manage repair measures for existing paved roads, walking and cycling routes, and gravel roads. Harja: The Harja system is used to monitor, supervise and report on the financial, qualitative, temporal and quantitative execution of highway maintenance contracts, surfacing and road marking contracts, lighting contracts and waterway canalisation contracts. The content of different contract types varies. Harja is one of väylävirasto's largest information systems.; The procurement establishes an expert team whose tasks include supporting the operation, testing and definition of systems related to the Väylävirasto location referencing framework. Tasks include, among others, road addressing of roads related to the creation of the road address network in conjunction with the Centres for Economic Development, Transport and the Environment, work related to the maintenance of Suravage geometry, support for the testing and definition of Viite (Road Address System) and the Framework Converter, and tasks related to the maintenance of the road address network. The expert team will consist of road data experts. Brief descriptions of the information systems that the supplier's expert team will operate: Viite: Road address system maintenance application. There is a need to make changes to road addresses due to the completion of road projects or administrative decisions. There are three tasks in the maintenance of the road address system: Maintenance of road addresses (including carriageway data (but not lane data)), maintenance of road names, and maintenance of nodes and junctions. In Viite, road addresses are linked to the frozen road link geometry of the Centre Line Geometry Repository, and road address maintenance takes place in a map user interface based on road link geometry. When maintaining road addresses, road address history is also preserved in Viite. Road addresses are used to record the locations of data related to highways. The most significant system utilising road addresses is Tievelho. Framework Converter (Viitekehysmuunnin): A REST-type interface application used to convert road locations from one location referencing framework to another, for example to obtain coordinates for a road address. The data to be converted is sent to the Framework Converter using a GET/POST request, the application processes the data and returns the converted data to the calling application as a response. The interface service is publicly available on the internet. In addition, there are separate authorised interface addresses for the service.
sig_3c6906217ed34d1b7a09.title: Procurement of operating services for road information systems

sig_3c84a101b6a6579c69c9.description: The National Institute of Neurological Disorders and Stroke (NINDS), with other NIH Institutes and Centers (ICs), intends to publish a Notice of Funding Opportunity (NOFO) to investigate the mechanisms of action of therapeutic medical devices with the overall goal of improving clinical outcomes with device-based approaches. Medical devices are essential in managing health conditions, complementing drugs and behavioral interventions, and often offer unique benefits. Despite the commercial availability of numerous medical devices and ongoing development of new technologies, many have shown inconsistent results in preclinical studies, failed translation to humans, and exhibit varied patient outcomes. To overcome these challenges, it is crucial to understand the mechanisms by which medical devices produce a therapeutic effect, to identify physiological markers of neurological conditions, and to assess how device-based therapies influence these markers. Advancing this knowledge will improve device-based interventions, inspire new device designs, and optimize current clinical approaches. Applications will be invited from interdisciplinary teams pursuing innovative research on how medical devices produce a therapeutic effect. Applicant teams will likely exhibit expertise in areas such as engineering, biology, pathophysiology, surgery, clinical care, healthcare delivery, biostatistics, software development, computational modeling, artificial intelligence, regulatory science, and clinical trials. This program will accept projects on investigational devices and those already FDA-approved and in clinical use. Applications are expected to include strategies for developing or optimizing therapies that could significantly improve patient care. Supported research may include mechanistic clinical trials, animal studies, and computational modeling or simulation. Applications are not being solicited at this time. Notice is being provided to allow potential applicants sufficient time to develop meaningful collaborations and responsive projects.
sig_3c84a101b6a6579c69c9.title: HEAL Initiative: Optimization of Therapeutic Medical Devices through Team Science Mechanistic Research (RM1)

sig_3e158d950d7f50ced64b.description: Digital Care Hub is seeking an independent evaluation partner to assess the delivery, impact, sustainability and value for money of the Better Security, Better Care (BSBC) programme. Funded by the Department of Health and Social Care, BSBC supports approximately 28,000 CQC-registered adult social care locations in England to improve cyber security, data protection and information governance, including compliance with the Data Security and Protection Toolkit (DSPT). Delivery is led nationally by Digital Care Hub through more than 30 Local Support Organisations, combining central leadership, guidance, training, communications, data analysis and performance management with trusted local support. The supplier will design and deliver a proportionate mixed-method evaluation covering programme governance and delivery, stakeholder engagement, partner effectiveness, reach, changes in awareness and behaviour, adoption of good practice, DSPT outcomes, organisational resilience, wider benefits, cost effectiveness, return on investment and social and economic value. The work should identify lessons, good practice and evidence-based recommendations while providing ongoing insight to support continuous improvement. Key deliverables are an evaluation framework and inception report within three months; ongoing data collection, analysis and stakeholder engagement; monthly progress meetings; an interim report by September 2027; and a final evaluation report, shorter executive report, presentation and dissemination-ready outputs by October 2028. Close-down and dissemination support will continue to March 2029. The proposed contract runs from October 2026 to March 2029, with a maximum budget of £125,000 inclusive of VAT. Bidders must demonstrate strong experience in programme and economic evaluation, publicly funded programmes, mixed-method research, stakeholder engagement and report writing. Knowledge of adult social care, health and care systems, cyber security, digital transformation or information governance is required. Tender responses must include organisation and personnel details, methodology, data collection and analysis plans, delivery timetable, resourcing, quality assurance, risk management, up to three relevant examples, a full pricing schedule, assumptions and proposed social value. Evaluation weightings are: understanding 15%, methodology 35%, experience 20%, project management 10%, social value 10% and price 10%. The supplier must comply with UK GDPR, the Data Protection Act 2018, confidentiality, insurance, procurement, equality and safeguarding requirements. Clarification questions are due by 14 October 2026 and tenders by 18 October 2026. Please see attachment for full specifications.
sig_3e158d950d7f50ced64b.title: Independent Evaluation of the Better Security, Better Care Programme (October 2025 to October 2028)

sig_3e73758e8dae6ea8c0b8.description: The Directorate of DigitalIsation (Digdir) invites tenderers to give input on collaboration models for issuing a digital wallet in Norway. This request for information is related to the ongoing work with a CONCEPT CHOICE assessment (KVU) for issuing a digital wallet in accordance with the eIDAS2.0 regulation. This has been efficient and given us rapid and high spreading of eID in the population, and thus contributed to the fact that public and private actors have been able to digitalise a great many services. The national eID strategy has, however, pointed to some challenges with the current model, i.a. connected to not everyone having access to eID "High" within the current market-based systems. The eIDAS2.0 Regulation requires Norway to offer inhabitants and residents a free digital wallet at a security level "High". The regulation also requires most social sectors, both public and private, to accept the wallet for log-in, identification and different areas of use. This also applies across EU/EEA countries, which means that Norway be required to accept the digital wallets of others in norway. In addition to this, we see the introduction of digital wallets in the work with the KVU in connection with the challenges and needs described in the national eID strategy. Reply This is an open invitation to market participants, and there are no special form requirements for the feedback. Each market participant is free to emphasise what they find most relevant in their responses. However, we have prepared an overview of questions that can function as a guide, which gives an indication of which areas we would like feedback on. Response to this RFI (both questions and input) is sent via the communication module in Mercell.Deadline for written responses: 18 December 2025Se attached documents for further information.
sig_3e73758e8dae6ea8c0b8.title: RFI - Collaboration models for issuing of digital wallets

This goal is to be achieved primarily by drafting and publishing reference documentation ("blueprints") for common documents required as part of a conformity assessment or certification procedure. The BMG plans to support AI developers, in particular small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs), in drawing up such "blueprints" together with relevant experts. A prerequisite for funding is that the resulting "blueprints" are published in full in order to achieve added value for non-funded AI developers as well. The "blueprints" drawn up within the scope of the project are intended in their entirety to address various challenges that are highly relevant to the market and which currently make it difficult to place innovative AI systems on the market for healthcare provision.
sig_3ea638f44527d5fd54fb.title: Market exploration for the establishment of AI regulatory living labs by the Bundesministerium für Gesundheit (BMG)

sig_3ee832445041b66999b9.description: The Kölner Verkehrs-Betriebe AG (KVB) intends to publish one or, where applicable, several procurement procedures for the procurement of validators including a background system and relevant software interfaces, likely from the year 2026. In order to improve KVB's level of knowledge regarding the technical and commercial aspects of such a procedure, KVB is conducting a market consultation pursuant to Section 26 of the Sectoral Procurement Ordinance (SektVO) ("industry dialogue"). As part of the industry dialogue, KVB will inform itself about, inter alia, 1. Functionalities of validators (hardware, software) and background systems 2. implementation options for KVB 3. commercial aspects (pricing models, price range, cost factors). Subject of the industry dialogue: KVB intends to replace the mobile ticket vending machines in the trains and buses with validators. These are intended to function without paper and cash based on contactless EMV transactions and to be embedded in an ABT/IDBT-capable system. Travel entitlements are to be stored as encrypted tokens in a cloud-based background system, whereby both providers and cloud storage must at least have the necessary ISO 27001 certification. The operation of the background system in a cloud environment must be subject to the European General Data Protection Regulation. The validators must make it possible to purchase a specific, independently configurable range of tickets (pre-selection) and additionally support an interoperable check-in/check-out procedure with integrated best-price calculation for the customer. All physical and virtual payment instruments that comply with the EMV standard (EC card, credit card, Google Pay, Apple Pay, etc.) must be accepted; in addition, payment via a prepaid card (closed-loop) must be possible. KVB reserves the right to commission a financial/payment service provider with the processing of payments. Corresponding software interfaces/APIs must therefore be supported/addressed. The payment options are to be expandable in the future. The customer must be able to view and manage their travel entitlements (ABT) independently via an online portal (web portal). The web/online portal is to be provided in KVB's corporate design. In addition, further software interfaces to a central customer account, which is set up internally by KVB, are to be provided. It must be possible to use a token that is linked to another person's payment medium. The control of the issued travel entitlements must be ensured across transport associations (at least throughout NRW) and made possible by corresponding software interfaces from the provider. A control option must also be possible when the validator is offline. The regular processing of blacklists is supported. Current and future developments of VDV-KA and (((eTiCore must be taken into account. The background system must contain at least the following software interfaces: - Ticketing back office with payment gateway and connection to payment service provider - Device management - Key management - Customer management - Enterprise asset management system - Fault notification software interface The background system should promote interoperability and must be able to be integrated into an overarching system landscape. The accounting data from the validators must be able to be integrated from there into the sales accounting system PATRIS (LHIND). Participation in the industry dialogue / qualification criteria: If potential bidders are interested in participating in the industry dialogue, KVB requests notification by email by no later than 23.9.2025, 10:00 hours, to the contact point daniela.lehnert@kvb.koeln. The references must be submitted in full by this time. When expressing interest in participating in the industry dialogue, the following qualification criteria / capabilities of the bidders must be proven and submitted. KVB reserves the right to exclude bidders whose qualification is not proven or is not sufficient based on proven references / documents from the industry dialogue and not allow them to participate in the industry dialogue. Submission of 2 references regarding previously executed contracts / services that are comparable to the advertised service in terms of subject matter and scope. The comparability of a reference requires that the subject matter of the reference contract includes at least the successful implementation / introduction of an ABT/IDBT system including mobile validators and a background system in public transport. In one of the reference contracts, the system must have been implemented on the basis of contactless EMV transactions. The reference contracts must not date back more than 5 years. The reference projects must have been implemented in Europe. The relevant factor in this regard is the date of acceptance or complete performance of the service. The following details must be provided in the reference: a) Name and address of the respective reference client b) Brief description of the reference project c) Contractual role of one's own company in the reference project d) Meaningful description of the nature and scope of the service provided (by oneself) e) Details of any (own) subcontractors f) Description of the comparability of the project (essential overlaps / parallels to the present industry dialogue) g) Duration of the project h) Contact person (naming a contact person who can confirm the reference and is authorized to provide information to KVB regarding the quality of service provision)
sig_3ee832445041b66999b9.title: Ticketing with validators, incl. back-end system

sig_3f443255f38bcabd6daa.buyer_original: Bundesamt für Sicherheit in der Informationstechnik
sig_3f443255f38bcabd6daa.description: Artificial Intelligence (AI) methods demonstrate astonishing performance in many application areas and are increasingly used in areas that affect daily life. The field of cybersecurity has not remained untouched by AI either. New AI tools are published almost daily in this context, and large AI language models (LLMs) in particular are already being used today for various application purposes. At the same time, the threat landscape is changing significantly as benignly intended models are misused for attack purposes (dual use). As a consequence, it must sometimes be assumed that vulnerabilities will be discovered and exploited ever faster in future with the increasing capabilities of AI. Against this background, the defensive side must also take action, which is why this project is intended to investigate how AI can be used profitably in the SSDLC and what effects ongoing developments have on the security of software. For this purpose, the project is divided into three parts, with related but distinct services: In work package 1-4 [HM1.1], a study on the current state of the art and science in the field of AI in the Secure Software Development Life Cycle is to be drawn up. In addition, best practices for the use of identified AI tools are to be developed. The results are to be published. In work package 5-6 [HM2.1], based on the study and in cooperation with the BSI, the contractor shall review the evaluation criteria for AVA scoring in Common Criteria certification and update them in view of new circumstances. In addition, an implementation plan for the use of AI tools for conformity assessment bodies is to be created. In work package 7, a reference architecture is created for the Open CoDE platform, which illustrates how AI tools can be integrated into the Secure Software Development Life Cycle and the software environment of Open CoDE. Suitable tools are to be proposed in this regard. Lot LOT-0000: KI im Secure Software Development Life Cycle (KISDL). sig_3f48acbeeee6adfeb946.description: The aim of the procurement is to establish a framework agreement for the delivery of equipment, consumables and production services for the production of standardised brands for locations and equipment in Helse Sør-Øst. The procurement shall support the implementation and use of uniform physical and digital identification of locations and equipment based on international GS1 standards. Locations shall be able to be identified by use of GS1 GLN and the equipment shall be able to be identified by use of GS1 GIAI, in the form of GS1 Digital Link and other standardised GS1 syntaxes. Through the use of international standards, marks shall be able to be used by digital systems in Helse Sør-Øst, e.g. systems for Facility Management (FM)/property management, clinical logistics, medical engineering, ERP, etc. The procurement shall result in: - Standardised types of brands for locations and equipment. - Support for multiple information carriers on brands - Support for local production of brands - Support for production of large volumes of brands as external services. - Standardised production basis. - Secure management of business critical information. The procurement includes systems for both local production of brands in the health companies, and production of large volumes of brands. The system for local production can include production equipment, necessary software and/or integration components, consumables, equipment for encoding/programming NFC and UHF RFID, training, support, maintenance and documentation. The contracting authority will, together with the chosen supplier, establish a set of standardised brand types that will be used for the production of labels for locations and equipment. A tag type is a documented specification that specifies how a brand should be designed and produced.

sig_3f802b583452cebe66b9.description: The ITEBO GmbH intends to tender and award a web-based software solution for security awareness and phishing simulation. Due to increasingly intelligent cyberattacks, there is a growing need for practical and continuous training for employees in public administrations. For this reason, the ITEBO GmbH is tendering the provision of such a solution as a SaaS model for the shareholders of the ITEBO GmbH. In addition to the provision of the software, German-speaking support is requested for the entire duration of 48 months. Lot LOT-0001: EU-wide tender for a software solution for security awareness and phishing simulation. The ITEBO GmbH plans to award a framework agreement for the web-based software solution for security awareness and phishing simulation. Due to increasingly intelligent cyberattacks, there is a growing need for practical and continuous training for employees in public administrations. For this reason, the ITEBO GmbH is tendering the provision of such a solution as a SaaS model for the shareholders of the ITEBO GmbH. The framework agreement can be used by the ITEBO GmbH itself as well as for all shareholders of the ITEBO GmbH, whereby the ITEBO GmbH calls off the necessary services from the framework agreement as required, coordinates them and handles billing with the respective shareholders. The ITEBO GmbH is therefore both the contracting authority and the tendering body for the service to be procured.

sig_3ffeb196ed0e1227775e.description: The subject of the contract is the implementation of a production planning tool for capacity-oriented planning and control. The use of the software, including maintenance and support, is to run for a total of four years. Lot LOT-0001: Implementation of planning software. The subject of the tender is the commissioning of a qualified provider to implement an advanced planning and scheduling (APS) system that enables very detailed scheduling of all required resources using finite resource planning. The primary objective of implementing the planning tool is to generate the most realistic and actionable planning possible by optimally scheduling all resources, linked with feedback from the operational units in SAP S/4HANA in almost real time. By mapping all weapon systems and equipment in the planning tool and providing a simulation capability, equipment availability is to be simulated and visualised for future scenarios alongside planned measures. The focus is on conceptual design, implementation, customising, provision of licences, support, and training and qualification of users and administrators. System provision and server operation are carried out by the contracting authority's existing system operations IT service provider.

sig_401c9b3a1aeaaeac68f3.description: This is a Prior Information Notice (PIN) with the purpose of assisting the Driver and Vehicle Licensing Agency (DVLA) in engaging the market by gathering information. This PIN has the purpose of a fact-finding exercise and only. Background Driver and Vehicle Licensing Agency (DVLA) are exploring options to digitalise payments out of the Agency in a bid to reduce payable orders. A specific user case includes invoice-based payments. Invoices are returned with information to support a customer's application. These applications, information and invoices are currently paper based which are scanned and digitalised in-house. On receipt of the information and sufficient checks, a payment is made by payable order to those named on the invoice. The payable order process is also managed in-house and posted from DVLA. Volumes In this example, for the financial year 2025-26, 221,406 individual payable orders were issued, with a net value of approximately £14.8M. Considerations - The payments are made to anyone qualified to complete the supporting evidence, so there is no static list of payees. There could be around 60,000 individual payees which fluctuates. Some are repeat payees and some are one off payees. - The payees include individuals and company accounts from across the UK. - The invoices (currently paper based) include the payee bank information (account number, sort code). - The invoices are then scanned and a digital copy held. - As a Government Agency we are required to follow all HM Treasury guidance outlined in the 'Managing Public Money' published documentation. - This includes not being able to use intermediary bank accounts outside of the Exchequer pyramid. - DVLA do not have an existing BACs business as usual process for payments out. - DVLA has explored Open Banking for this user case and feel that due to the considerations above it doesn't fully meet our requirements. Project aims - Digitalise movement of funds - Reduce/remove payable orders - Improve invoice management processes - Improve customer experience Information required - Potential solutions to support the project aims aligned to the considerations - Any costs associated with developing and implementing the solution including any licences or additional external costs. - Any ongoing costs associated with ongoing running of the solution. - Time taken to develop and implement the solution. - Any wider considerations, fees or any other supporting information. - Do you provide this type of service for any other large organisations? - How can DVLA procure from your organisation? e.g. Are they on a framework? If so which one? Do we need to go through any third parties to obtain their services? Please provide a response via email to the above question to Michelle Palmer - Michelle.Palmer@dvla.gov.uk by 5pm on May 13th 2026
sig_401c9b3a1aeaaeac68f3.title: DVLA Payments Out

sig_403c58c4744a84b8e20d.description: Liikenne- ja viestintävirasto Traficom is a central government agency operating within the administrative branch of the Ministry of Transport and Communications. Traficom is a service-oriented permit, register and supervisory authority in the transport and communications sector. The agency promotes the functionality and safety of the transport system and accelerates the development of the digital society. It supports sustainable development and ensures that high-quality, safe and affordable communications connections and services are available in Finland. Liikenne- ja viestintävirastoon and its operations can be explored in more detail at www.traficom.fi. Traficom is planning the procurement of EUDI access authenticator services. The planned procurement is described in more detail in the request for information attachment 1 (Description of the subject of the procurement). With this request for information, Traficom is exploring companies capable of carrying out the study for the planned procurement. The aim is to obtain comprehensive information concerning the implementation of the procurement so that a potential tendering procedure can be carried out in an appropriate manner. All information presented in the request for information regarding the planned procurement is preliminary and may change for the actual procurement. The request for information is not a procurement notice initiating a procurement. Traficom does not commit to carrying out the procurement; instead, the decision on launching a potential procurement process will be made after the market consultation. The information provided in connection with the request for information does not bind companies to participate in a potentially later procurement. Companies do not have the right to claim compensation for responding to the request for information. RESPONDING TO THE REQUEST FOR INFORMATION The request for information includes the following preliminary documents: 1) Draft description of the subject of the procurement 2) Draft procurement contract Traficom invites companies interested in the procurement to share their views on key issues related to the procurement by answering the questions set out in the request for information attachment 1. The response to the request for information must be in Finnish. Please send your response to the questions set out in attachment 1 by the deadline for the request for information to: hankinnat.ktk@traficom.fi From the aforementioned email address (hankinnat.ktk@traficom.fi), you may also request further information regarding the request for information if necessary. Please attach the necessary contact details to your request for information response (contact person's name, email address and telephone number) so that we can contact you if necessary. Please mark the subject field of the response email with "Tietopyyntövastaukset, EUDI-pääsyvarmentajan palveluiden hankinta". Traficom may present follow-up questions to companies that have responded to the request for information and may also hold market consultation meetings if necessary. Traficom may process request for information responses already during the deadline of the request for information. Responses to the request for information are requested to be submitted by the deadline set out below. CONFIDENTIALITY OF REQUEST FOR INFORMATION RESPONSES Companies responding to the request for information are requested to clearly mark any trade secret information in the responses in accordance with Section 24.1, Paragraph 20 of the Act on the Openness of Government Activities. Trade secret information will be processed in accordance with the Act on the Openness of Government Activities.

sig_40c2ff71c3f189a8ba37.description: The Metropolitan Police intend to establish a Dynamic Market in line with section 35 of the PA23. The market will not include Lots. The Dynamic Market is being established to accelerate how the Metropolitan Police deliver technology and data products to frontline officers. It will establish and bring together a new delivery model, procurement framework, ways of working and rapid prototyping, to work on a series of prioritised initiatives. This to support the Metropolitan Police commitment for A New Met for London, to building More Trust, Less Crime, and Higher Standards. The Dynamic Market is being established to meet current and future operational needs and the Commissioner's transformative change programme, "Precise Policing", and the Digital Data and Technology strategy. This strategy is structured around 6 strategic themes: Foundation, Data, Transformation, Efficiency & Resiliency, Capabilities, and Ways of Working. These act as guides allowing us to: plan, select, deploy and run digital technology that works for the Metropolitan Police. The scope of requirements for the dynamic market also includes technology capabilities within the following categories: • Technology professional services - A wide range of digital and data services such as software development, testing and data engineering; • Transformation and automation - AI and data enabled products and services including agentic AI, video processing, workflow and business process modelling; • Digital workplace modernisation -Products and capabilities to modernise legacy systems, support the rapid building of applications (such as situational awareness apps); • Data Management - Covering the building of search, integration, data analytics, data engineering and reporting; • Video processing and analysis - Video management, video ingestion, video analysis and searching using technology such as AI to identify and detect objects; • Cyber security - Products and services to manage and mitigate risks across our cyber estate; The specific user cases for the next 18 months are outlined below and are subject to change: • Video Redaction; • Situational awareness; • Video Searching; • Data intelligence / Intel scanning. Graph based data analytics alongside the MPS Enterprise Data Platform; • Public order planning; • Digital Asset Management System (DAMS) and improvements to end-to-end digital processes. Preliminary Market Engagement: The Metropolitan Police have carried out a preliminary market engagement Webinar via Tech UK. This has introduced the Precise Policing Phase 2 and the creation of a Dynamic Market to Tech Uk members and the wider marketplace. The webinar took place on the 7th of August 2025 at 11am. The slide deck presented at the webinar is available upon request from the Metropolitan Police Commercial team. To register your interest in this Dynamic Market, please ensure you are registered with Coupa and provide company contact details to the email specified on this notice. Lot 1: .
sig_40c2ff71c3f189a8ba37.title: Precise Policing Phase 2

sig_4109de053106f368a495.description: Further to the UK1 Pipeline Notice published on 19th November 2025 by BlueLight Commercial Limited (ref: 2025/S 000-077692) in relation to a Victim & Citizen Engagement Technology Solution which will be used by UK law enforcement agencies, this UK2 Preliminary Market Engagement Notice is issued to inform the market of a potential future opportunity. This Pre-Market Engagement Notice is issued solely for the purposes of information gathering and engagement with the market. It does not constitute a call for competition and create any obligation on the Authority to proceed with a procurement exercise, or enter into any commercial arrangement. Please note the procurement route and anticipated publication date for this opportunity are yet to be determined. These elements will be confirmed following completion of the market engagement process and development of the Authority’s commercial strategy. Any future procurement will be subject to separate formal notice and the publication of full procurement documentation via the Find a Tender Service (FTS). BlueLight Commercial Limited (BLC) are conducting Preliminary Market Engagement to gain a better understanding of the market, supplier appetite, capacity, and capability, as well as perceived risks and opportunities. Any learnings will be used to formulate the associated procurement strategy. BLC work in collaboration with blue light organisations to maximise commercial benefit to UK emergency services. The focus of this solution will be improving Victim & Citizen Engagement, building trust and confidence, reducing demand within control rooms, and reducing the costs of serving the public by using innovative software to keep both victims and citizens more engaged. The aim is to ensure all forces have access to the most effective, reliable, and innovative solutions available in the market. This Solution needs to facilitate the force contact engagement from first contact with a police force to final closure of the contact, and via integration with police systems, e.g. Command and Control, Records Management Systems providing contact and updates throughout the journey without the need to call the force contact centre. It seeks to further drive standardisation and consistency, whilst helping forces to develop capability and invest in technology which will not only improve the service at first point of contact but will improve the overall contact experience. This Solution must facilitate Victim & Citizen engagement to reduce failure demand whilst proactively engaging to ensure high levels of customer (internal and external) trust and confidence. The delivery of the desired solution may be considered to follow the same customer service path as an online application or ordering process. For example, acknowledgement of the initial contact, time appropriate follow up contacts at defined points within the communication journey, and a closure contact at the end of the process. All communication will be auditable and align with the Victims code as appropriate. We are looking for solutions that can meet individual force needs and achieve the following: *Improve experience of members of the public accessing the policing service *Provide the public with consistent updates in a timely manner, *Improve public trust, confidence, and satisfaction, *Reduce Contact Management demand, *Improve force's overall Contact Management performance. Lot 1: .

sig_418d8d9a6769dfce9ec2.description: As part of the FSA’s commitment to ensure food is safe and is what it says it is, the FSA undertakes food safety risk assessments which underpin these decisions in line with the internationally recognised ‘Codex Working Principles for Risk Analysis for Food Safety’. A key component of food safety risk assessment is exposure assessment, which estimates the amount of a hazard consumed through the diet. Exposure assessment combines food consumption data with information on the concentrations of substances such as contaminants, food additives or pesticide residues in food to estimate the levels consumers may be exposed to. To conduct UK dietary exposure assessments, the FSA uses consumption data in combination with occurrence data for hazards and other substances in food. UK consumption data is primarily obtained from the UK National Diet and Nutrition Survey (NDNS). The National Diet and Nutrition Survey (NDNS) is a co-funded programme between the Department of Health and Social Care (DHSC) Office for Health Improvement and Disparities (OHID) and FSA. NDNS is a rolling programme which assesses the diet, nutrient intake and nutritional status of the general population of the UK. Tenders are invited to carry out the recoding of NDNS consumption data to FoodEx2, a standardised system for classifying and describing food. Lot 1: . None
sig_418d8d9a6769dfce9ec2.title: Coding NDNS Consumption data into EFSA’s food classification+description -FoodEx

sig_41c87f8b745600783b86.description: Grounds Maintenance System RFI Lot 1: . Fife Council is seeking to understand the market for modern Grounds Maintenance Solutions capable of supporting operational delivery, financial management, and performance monitoring. The existing system used within the Grounds Maintenance Service presents a number of challenges, including limited mobile functionality, reliance on manual processes, and constraints in reporting and system integration. The Grounds Maintenance Service has been using its current back-office system for a number of years to support key activities such as scheduling, asset management, and billing. The Council is therefore seeking input from suppliers to help inform its future requirements and shape a potential procurement approach. The Council is now seeking to explore alternative solutions available within the market that may better meet its current and future Grounds Maintenance requirements. sig_4241ee1527fd0e26e35d.description: NHS Scotland intends to procure a National Digital Diabetes Prevention Programme to support individuals identified as being at risk of developing Type 2 Diabetes. The programme will deliver a structured, evidence-based lifestyle intervention through a digital platform, including access to health coaching, peer support, and tools to support behaviour change and self-management. The procurement is expected to be undertaken via a Restricted Procedure, with a single supplier appointed to a national framework. Lot 1: . This Prior Information Notice (PIN) relates to NHS Scotland’s intention to tender for a National Digital Diabetes Prevention Programme. The programme will identify individuals at risk of Type 2 Diabetes based on clinical indicators (including HbA1c and fasting plasma glucose levels) or a previous diagnosis of gestational diabetes. It will provide a tailored, nine-month, evidence-based lifestyle intervention aimed at reducing the risk of progression to Type 2 Diabetes. The digital service will support Service Users via an application-based platform, providing access to trained health coaches, online peer support communities, and functionality to set, track, and monitor personalised health goals. The successful bidder will be required to deliver the programme in a way that is inclusive and accessible to Service Users from diverse linguistic and cultural backgrounds. This will include ensuring the service is culturally sensitive to local populations and flexible enough to meet the needs of users with diverse requirements, including appropriate language support. Participants will be able to access the programme through multiple referral routes, including Primary Care (e.g. GP referral) and self-referral pathways. Current funding has been allocated to support up to 15,000 users over a three-year period. The proposed framework will operate as a single-supplier arrangement and will also include provision for the delivery of a Hypertension Pathway for approximately 500 users per annum. Eligibility for the hypertension pathway will be based on a confirmed diagnosis of primary hypertension alongside a BMI ≥25 (or BMI ≥23 for minority ethnic groups). Please Note: During the term of the Framework Agreement, NHS Scotland reserves the right, should funding become available, to increase the volume of service users (current estimate of 15000 over the initial 3-years of the Framework Agreement term) who may access the Programme. For example, additional purchases may be made which exceed the level of funding currently secured as a result of clinical and service outcomes and benefits which support wider adoption of the Programme. The Authority also reserves the right to expand the scope of the service to include additional cohorts, pathways, or clinical indicators (for example, the inclusion of further at-risk populations identified through screening), which may increase overall demand under the Framework. The procurement is expected to be conducted using a Restricted Procedure, comprising two stages: Stage 1 Selection Stage (SPD Assessment): Suppliers will be required to complete and submit a Single Procurement Document (SPD). This stage will assess bidders’ suitability to proceed and will include a combination of pass/fail criteria (e.g. mandatory and discretionary exclusion grounds, economic and financial standing) and scored evaluation. As part of the SPD, the Authority will assess technical and professional ability, including responses to scored questions and requests for relevant examples of previous experience. These responses will be weighted and scored to enable the Authority to evaluate capability and rank suppliers. A shortlist of the highest-ranking bidders will be invited to progress to Stage 2. Stage 2 – Invitation to Tender (ITT): Only suppliers shortlisted at Stage 1 will be invited to submit a full tender. Bidders will be required to respond to a Statement of Requirements (SoR), setting out how they will deliver the contract, including proposed methodology, service delivery model, and pricing. Tenders will be evaluated in accordance with the published award criteria, based on quality and price, to determine the Most Economically Advantageous Tender (MEAT). Stage 1 is expected to commence mid to late August 2026, with Stage 2 anticipated to commence in early October 2026.. This project is derived from the Accelerated National Innovation Adoption (ANIA) Pathway. This is an initiative focused on using technology to fast-track proven innovations into the healthcare frontline on a Once for Scotland basis. See link:https://www.nhscfsd.co.uk/our-work/innovation/accelerated-national-innovation-adoption-ania-pathway/

A dynamic purchasing system in accordance with Section 120 paragraph 1 of the German Act against Restraints of Competition (GWB) is a time-limited, exclusively electronic procedure for the procurement of standard market services where the characteristics generally available on the market meet the requirements of the contracting authority. An unlimited number of contractors are publicly invited to submit non-binding declarations for the provision of services, and all suitable contractors that have submitted admissible declarations for the provision of services are admitted to participate in the system for the entire duration of the system. An application to participate is possible at any time. Companies will be informed of their admission to the dynamic purchasing system via the communication area on the procurement marketplace. Following the publication of the dynamic purchasing system, an initial time limit of 30 days must be observed before opening applications to participate. Thereafter, no further time limits apply and new applications can be opened immediately. These applications will be evaluated within ten working days of receipt. If an individual award is pending, all admitted companies will be invited to submit a tender.

Requirements for vehicle operating systems from a cybersecurity perspective are to be derived from the valid regulations and standards. This includes requirements for tests within the framework of type approval and market surveillance. In addition to a source search for the market overview, practical analyses are also to be carried out on various operating systems. These are to be carried out within the framework of work package 5 (AP 5). The test catalogue to be created should be practically verifiable here. The result of the project is a study that includes the above-mentioned contents.

sig_43d2a12892c49a99bb9c.description: Høje-Taastrup Kommune is considering procuring the purchase and support of AV equipment as well as devices (PCs and tablets) for the schools sector as operational leasing. This means a solution where the supplier undertakes the delivery, assembly, operation, maintenance and support of equipment as a solution where the supplier owns the equipment and the municipality obtains the right of use via payment of an annual fee. Therefore, the municipality wishes to enter into a dialogue with 2 - 3 suppliers of such types of IT equipment to discuss what the municipality should pay attention to in connection with procurement. Some documents are enclosed that describe some of the intended content in a procurement (requirements, wishes, etc.). The dialogue will be based on these documents. Initially, the municipality wishes an indication of whether you will enter into a dialogue with the municipality regarding such a procurement, as well as a response with some initial thoughts that you as a supplier have regarding a procurement of this type of operational leasing. As inspiration for this, here are some initial questions: Is the best way to procure the goods and services via 2 procurement or can both types of services (AV and PC/tablets) advantageously be combined in one procurement? Is there anything we should be aware of that a contract must contain and/or absolutely not contain: e.g. breach of contract, penalty - how do we handle defects in the equipment? Will the fact that the supplier owns, assembles and services e.g. AV equipment provide an advantage e.g. via the supplier's strict control of drivers/software as well as versioning of these components in relation to a more stable, well-functioning and cohesive AV solution across the municipality? Are there other things we should be aware of? Here, consideration is given to advantages the municipality can achieve and the disadvantages that may lie in such a solution. The intention is that equipment is to be replaced in an ongoing process. This means the supplier will take over support on e.g. existing AV equipment. The dialogue is intended as an informal discussion of advantages and disadvantages/risks of establishing such solutions. It is not immediately intended that actual transfer of employees should take place; the intention is to establish another and more efficient way to operate and support the mentioned solution areas.
sig_43d2a12892c49a99bb9c.title: Consultation regarding the procurement of leasing for AV equipment and devices for the schools sector in Høje-Taastrup Kommune

sig_43e7d2d7b65e40a467aa.description: Provision, implementation and operation of a cloud-based, SaaS-based data-centric security platform (DSP) for the analysis, monitoring and protection of data and access permissions in a hybrid IT environment (on-premises and cloud) of the Stadtwerke Düsseldorf AG including affiliated companies. The aim of the procurement is to create transparency regarding data stocks, access authorizations and security-relevant activities, as well as to support measures to increase information security and comply with regulatory requirements in the KRITIS environment. In addition to the provision of the platform, the service also includes supportive services for the analysis, evaluation and prioritisation of security-relevant events as well as for the derivation of suitable measures. The processing of all data shall take place exclusively within the scope of the EU GDPR. An uninterrupted transition from existing near-production operations must be ensured. The aim is to conclude a contract for the provision, implementation and operation of a scalable, cloud-based data-centric security platform (DSP) for the analysis, monitoring and protection of data and access permissions in a hybrid IT environment (on-premises and cloud). The solution must cover the following functions and services in particular: - Analysis and evaluation of data stocks, data access and permission structures, including the identification of potential security and data protection risks, - The solution should have integrated functions for detecting anomalies in user and system behaviour (User and Entity Behavior Analytics) - Creation of transparency regarding effective accesses and permissions, - Detection and evaluation of conspicuous, risk-prone or security-relevant activities, - Provision of monitoring, reporting and verification functions to support audit, compliance and security requirements, particularly in the regulated KRITIS environment, - Support in deriving and implementing suitable measures for risk reduction (e.g. adjustment of permissions or restriction of access rights), - Integration into the client's existing hybrid system landscape (in particular identity services, file and cloud storage as well as collaboration platforms) via standardised interfaces, - Provision and operation of the solution including maintenance, ongoing development, updates and technical documentation in a SaaS model. In addition, services are to be provided that support continuous evaluation, assessment and prioritisation (managed detection and response) of security-relevant events and provide recommendations for action. If configured accordingly, these services may also include operational support services. Continued operation requirements: - Ensuring an uninterrupted transition from existing near-production operations, including a suitable migration and transition concept, - Taking over existing configurations, evaluations and settings as far as technically possible, - Guaranteeing compatibility with existing system landscapes, role and permission models, - Minimising migration, integration and training efforts while taking cost-effectiveness over the entire life cycle into account, - Ensuring continuous operational capability during the transition phase. sig_440b8f725103f2f00d82.description: It is proposed to contract the maintenance service for the IT solution named SIRA, the research information and management system that enables researchers and managers to handle their activity (CV, scientific production, projects) in a centralised, streamlined and user-friendly manner. This IT solution is necessary to maintain research activity at the UIB, both by researchers and the management thereof by support staff in the offices and departments of the UIB. The SIRA application is the basis of the UIB's Research Management System. To ensure proper operation, as well as the incorporation of updates and regulatory adaptations, it is necessary to contract the right to use the IT solution as well as corrective and evolutionary maintenance.

sig_44131f6f7ae9b0452a62.description: The subject of the contract is the functional expansion of the Road Traffic Area Control System (SOSRD), consisting in the implementation of mechanisms for acquiring, processing and transmitting real-time road traffic volume data, together with their classification, to the internet portal of the Municipal Road Authority in Rzeszów. Size/Scope: The expansion of the system aims to increase the transparency of information concerning road traffic in the city of Rzeszów, so that users of the service can easily and intuitively gain access to current and historical traffic data. The expansion of the presentation layer and the automation of information processing and sharing processes will allow a fuller understanding of the situation on the roads, including traffic volume, communication trends and changes over time.
sig_44131f6f7ae9b0452a62.title: Expansion of SOSRD to include real-time traffic flow data sharing along with its classification

sig_44160aacf2c87da6ae79.description: United Utilities is seeking to establish a framework for the supply, storage, stock management, fulfilment and delivery of water efficiency devices and flow regulators. The framework will support United Utilities’ AMP8 and AMP9 water demand reduction commitments, including reductions in domestic Per Capita Consumption and non-household business demand. The requirement is divided into two lots: Lot 1 covers water efficiency devices, associated fulfilment services and a UU-branded customer water usage survey and ordering platform; Lot 2 covers flow regulators in agreed sizes, flow rates and specifications. Appointed supplier(s) must be able to provide compliant, reliable and scalable products and services that support planned programmes, customer campaigns, bulk orders and changes in operational demand. Suppliers must demonstrate product quality, regulatory compliance, supply chain resilience, accurate reporting, effective stock management and appropriate customer support. This includes relevant approvals and assurance evidence, secure handling of customer data where applicable, and the ability to respond flexibly as programme volumes and priorities evolve. The overall objective is to secure a robust, value-for-money supply arrangement that enables United Utilities to deliver water efficiency activity at scale, maintain continuity of supply, protect customer experience and contribute to measurable reductions in water consumption across the North West. Lot LOT-0001: PRO005128-Goods-Framework-Water Saving Devices - Lot 1. Supply, storage, stock management, picking, packing, fulfilment and delivery of water efficiency devices such as flow regulators, water butts, shower regulators, tap inserts, showerheads, cistern devices, toilet leak detection strips and other approved or innovative water saving products. Lot LOT-0002: PRO005128-Goods-Framework-Water Saving Devices - Lot 2. Supply, storage, stock management, fulfilment and delivery of flow regulators in a range of sizes, flow rates and specifications suitable for UU programmes. Devices must meet all applicable regulatory, quality and testing requirements, including WRAS and Regulation 31 approval where required.
sig_44160aacf2c87da6ae79.title: PRO005128-Goods-Framework-Water Saving Devices

sig_444b9b641566e8afae3c.description: Local Enterprise Office Longford invites applications from suitably qualified and experienced training providers to join a panel of trainers for the delivery of future training programmes, workshops, seminars, mentoring and business development supports to clients of Local Enterprise Office Longford. The panel will operate for a two-year period from 1 January 2027 to 31 December 2028. Training requirements may cover a broad range of business topics, including start-up support, business growth, management development, digitalisation, sustainability, sales and marketing, financial management, innovation and other areas relevant to the needs of small businesses and entrepreneurs. The current Framework Agreement will expire on 31 December 2026 and will be replaced by this new Training Services Panel. Appointment to the panel does not guarantee any minimum level of work, and training assignments will be awarded in accordance with the requirements of Local Enterprise Office Longford during the panel term. Applications are invited from individuals and organisations with the appropriate qualifications, expertise and proven experience in the provision of business training and facilitation services. Applications will be evaluated using the Most Economically Advantageous Tender (MEAT) methodology, with assessment based on quality and price criteria as set out in the tender documentation.
