sig_445f611665444a7ce2b6.description: The Bavarian State Forests AöR (BaySF) intends to procure and introduce an integrated production planning and control system (PPS) for the digital planning, control, execution and evaluation of forestry measures. The aim of the project is the end-to-end digitisation and optimisation of the strategic, operational and dispositive processes of forest management, as well as the replacement of existing isolated solutions and media discontinuities with a central, integrated system. The PPS is intended in particular to support measure planning, resource and capacity control, mobile and offline-capable work processes in the forest, cooperation with external service providers, the integration of GIS and SAP systems, and comprehensive reporting. The introduction will take place in a modular and step-by-step manner within the framework of a competitive dialogue. In addition to the software, the subject of the procurement also includes the necessary implementation, integration, project management, training, operation and software maintenance services.
sig_445f611665444a7ce2b6.title: Integrated production planning and control BaySF

sig_447c2e139382109633ed.description: Traficom's web services are a central channel for transactions, advice and information for citizens, companies and other stakeholders. Up-to-date information, instructions, decisions and services are published on the web services. The objective of the procurement is to support the continuous development, monitoring and quality assurance of Traficom's web services. With the procured services, Traficom can monitor the use of web services, user feedback, accessibility and quality, and develop web services based on information. The subject of the procurement is a web service quality and feedback tool for the Client's use as a software service. The software service consists of three modules: module 1 accessibility, module 2 visitor feedback and module 3 analytics. The modules can be taken into use and removed from use flexibly according to needs during the contract period. The contract is valid for a fixed term of five (5) years from the signing of the contract. The Client has the right to extend the contract with two (2) one (1) year options. The Client shall notify the Supplier of the use of the option no later than three (3) months before the end of the actual contract period or the first option period. The use of the option is at the Client's sole discretion. A more detailed description of the subject of the procurement, service requirements and contract terms are presented in the documents attached to this call for tenders.

sig_44927bea86389180d737.description: The tender aims to achieve and promote the stable and future-proof operation of the "Schleupen.CS" ERP system on a highly available and secure infrastructure for use by the client's employees and external service providers, including migration, SaaS operation, interfaces, administration, and support. The SWH is tendering for the provision of a highly available cloud infrastructure in the contractor's data centre. The service consists not only of providing data centre capacity but, due to the intended role as a solution provider, encompasses holistic responsibility for the stable and future-proof operation of Schleupen.CS. The services to be provided include, in particular: - the provision of the necessary hardware and data centre infrastructure, - the provision of software necessary for the operation of the systems (including current versions of Microsoft Windows Server, Microsoft SQL Server, Remote Desktop Services, and Citrix if applicable for the publication of remote apps, as approved by Schleupen SE), - the takeover or migration of the existing system (including the sub-systems necessary for operation) into the data centre environment, - the takeover of existing interfaces to third-party service providers (mandatory requirements: SMGWA, ticket system, customer portal), - the operation of the Schleupen.CS system (including sub-systems) in the data centre: production and test systems with the existing tenants, - the sufficiently performant - at least with symmetrical 200 Mbit/s - internet connection of the client to the contractor's data centre. Connection must be established via an encrypted VPN tunnel or by providing the service provider's own hardware, which is integrated into the contractor's internal network, - the takeover of support services within the scope of data centre operations, - the takeover of support services for the Schleupen.CS system, in particular holistic, independent communication with Schleupen SE in the event of application and problem cases, - the provision and maintenance of current hardware and software (operating system software, database software, application software), which are operated with active maintenance contracts / software assurance, - the monitoring of systems and applications, - immediate error detection, communication to the client in the event of an error, and error rectification, - the maintenance of highly available system operation (24 h/ 7 days a week) throughout the entire contract term. It is mandatory that strict, logical isolation from the contractor's other customers is maintained. The precise details regarding the subject matter of the contract can be found in the specifications (Annex B of the procedural letter).

sig_44988596b4418aad1d58.description: A total of three lots in the area of support - technical system administration are sought. Lot 1: SAP Basis Support, Lot 2: Software Development Support and Lot 3: Software Development Support Risk/Cont Lot LOT-0001: SAP Basis. SAP Basis administration is responsible, taking into account that LfA has outsourced the SAP operations of its ERP and BW systems to the SAP Cloud, for the smooth operation of our SAP systems in close cooperation with SAP. The core tasks in the SAP Basis environment include daily monitoring of the SAP landscape to ensure high-performance and error-free operation. Standard Basis transactions are regularly checked for error messages - both directly in the relevant SAP transactions and on the basis of incoming system messages via email, or via active evaluation of reports in SAP for Me. Another essential component is the importation of hotfixes as well as SAP and LfA specialist releases in order to keep the systems constantly up-to-date and secure. This also includes the analysis, assessment and processing of vulnerabilities in the Baramundi system to ensure IT security on a sustained basis. Tasks in SAP Basis also include operation and maintenance of SAP Solution Manager (e.g. importing security patches, creating new change cycles, analysing transport problems). New incoming tickets (incident, problem and change management) are processed continuously. Quarterly system and client copies are carried out jointly with SAP, with the focus of activities at LfA being, on the one hand, on the coordination of individual work packages, including the involvement of SAP peripheral systems, and, on the other hand, on follow-up work in the SAP systems. Lot LOT-0002: Software Development Support. - Analyses of requirements - Support of productive operations / support (error analysis and remediation) - Preparation of IT concepts and test concepts - Implementation / execution of customer-developed solutions o Open Text Team Developer development o ABAP development o Pl/Sql developments o C# developments o Interfaces - Maintenance of the data model - Test Lot LOT-0003: Risk Software Development Support. - Software development for the RISK/CONT system - Interface programming for data supply to RISK/CONT from operational systems and data delivery from RISK/CONT to other disposition systems - Preparation of functional, computer science and test concepts - Clarification and coordination of functional requirements with the specialist department - Effort estimation for implementations from functional requirements - Test - Support of productive operations / support (error analysis and remediation) in the RISK/CONT system. - Preparation and maintenance of documentation of technical systems and processes for the RISK/CONT system.

F... further distribution only as directed by Commander, Naval Sea Systems Command, code 09T. 6.3 Information regarding abbreviations, symbols and codes appearing on DD Form 1423 - The following information is provided to assist in understanding the intent of the requirement to provide a deliverable item to the government. The explanation of abbreviation, symbols and codes found in a block follows the block number as they appear on the DD Form 1423. Block A: Is the actual contract line item no. Block B: Is the actual collective physical list of the deliverable item(s) which are part of the total requirement of the contract/purchase order. Block C: Is the category of data required, TDP is defined in MIL-T-31000. TM is defined in Part 1X, Section B of DODI 5000.2. NAVSUP-WSS has reasoned that most DD Form 1423's included in our solicitations meet the requirement of TDP as NAVSUP-WSS does not regularly purchase only Technical Manuals without purchasing hardware and related TDP software. Therefore, most NAVSUP-WSS DD Form 1423 category code will be TDP. Block D: Is the name of the parent system, next higher assembly, or the item being purchased. Block E: Is the purchase request number, request for proposal number, invitation for bid number or another number for tracking and monitoring purposes. Block F: Is the successful offerors name and or cage code. Block G: Is the name of the individual and or the code/activity of the individual who prepared the DD Form 1423 and included the requirement in the Technical Data Package (TDP). Block H: Self explanatory. Block I: Is the name and signature of the individual who approved the content and the need for inclusion of the DD Form 1423 in the TDP. Block J: Self explanatory. Block 1: Is the Exhibit Line Item Number (ELIN). Block 2: Is the title of the data item cited in Block 4. Block 3: Is the subtitle of the data item cited in Block 4 and is used if the title requires clarification. Block 4: Is the actual Data Item Description (DID) number or the actual Technical Manual Contract Requirements Number. In the event the DD Form 1423 is requiring a technical manual the numbered TMCR will be an attachment to the contract/purchase order. Block 5: Is the section and paragraph area, where the requirement statement for the DD Form 1423 will be found. Block 6: Is the activity that will inform the contractor of approval, conditional approval or disapproval of the deliverable item. Block 7: Is a code which designates authority for inspection and acceptance of the deliverable item. The definition of the codes is as follows: DD Form 250 Code Inspection Acceptance SS (1) (2) DD (3) (4) SD (1) (4) DS (3) (5) LT (6) (7) NO (8) (8) XX (9) (9) (1) Inspection at source. (2) Acceptance at source. (3) No inspection performed at source. Final inspection performance at destination. (4) Acceptance at destination. (5) Acceptance at source. Acceptance based on written approval from the Contract Officer. (6) Letter of transmittal only. LT should not be used when inspection is required. The data is sent by the contractor directly to the personnel listed in Block 14 of the DD Form 1423. LT is used when the contracting agency does not desire to have a DD Form 250 for each and every piece of data developed by the contractor. The only other authorized use of LT is the special case where the contracting agency does not desire to have separate DD Forms 250 but desires to have a Government quality assurance representative perform inspection. The Government quality assurance representative shall be listed on the distribution in Block 14 and requested to provide comments via the quality assurance letter of inspection. Use of the symbol LT is not authorized for data comprising final delivery of Technical Data Package of for Technical Manuals. (LT may, however, be used for delivery of preliminary TDP's or TM's). (7) As specified in Block 8 of the DD Form 1423. (8) No inspection or acceptance required. No DD Form 250 or letter of transmittal required. Use of the symbol NO is not authorized for data comprising Technical Data Packages or for Technical Manuals. (9) Inspection and acceptance requirements specified elsewhere in the contract. Block 8: Is the approval code - Items of critical data requiring specific advanced written approval prior to distribution of the final data item will be identified by placing an "A" in this field. This data item requires submission of a preliminary draft prior to publication of a final document. When a preliminary draft is required, Block 16 of the DD Form 1423 will show length of time required for Government approval/disapproval and subsequent turn-around time for the contractor to resubmit the data after Government approval/disapproval has been issued. Block 16 will also indicate the extent of the approval requirements, e.g., approval of technical content and/or format. Block 9: Is the distribution statement code which explains how the Government can circulate the deliverable item. The definition of codes A, B, C, D, E, or F is as follows: A. Distribution of the item is unrestricted. B. Distribution of the item is limited to agencies only. C. Distribution of the item is limited to contractors with a cage code and have a DD Form 2345 on file with the DLA Logistics Information Services (DLIS) Battle Creek, Mich. or Government activities. D. Distribution of the item is limited to DOD activities and DOD contractors only. E. Distribution of the item is limited to DOD components only. F. Distribution of the item is restricted from Foreign Nations and Foreign Nationals. Block 10: Is the frequency which the deliverable item is expected to be delivered to the Government. The abbreviations and their meaning. ANNLY Annually ASGEN As generated ASREQ As required BI-MO Every two months BI-WE Every two weeks DAILY Daily DFDEL Deferred Delivery MTHLY Monthly ONE/R One time with revisions QRTLY Quarterly SEMIA Every six months WEKLY Weekly XTIME Number of times to be submitted (1time, 2times...9times) Use of these codes requires further explanation in Block 16 to provide the contractor with guidance necessary to accurately price the deliverable data item. Other abbreviations not appearing on the above list may on occasion be used in Block 10 of the DD Form 1423. When other abbreviations are used they will be fully explained in Block 16 of the DD Form 1423. Block 11: Is the last calendar date, expressed in year/month/day format, the deliverable item is to be received by the requiring office cited in Block 6 of the DD Form 1423 for an item with a Block 10 entry indication a single delivery. If the item is to be submitted multiple times, the number stated is the number of calendar days after the frequency cited in Block 10 the item is to be received by the requiring office cited in Block 6 of the DD Form 1423. On occasion the deliverable item will be required to be submitted prior to the end of the frequency cited in Block 6. In that event the requirement will be fully explained in Block 16 of the DD Form 1423. Block 12: Is the date of first submission of the deliverable item to the requiring office (Block 4) expressed in year/month/day format. The abbreviations and their meaning are as follows: ASGEN As generated ASREQ As required DAC Days after contract date DFDEL Deferred Delivery EOC End of contract EOM End of month EOQ End of quarter Specific instructions for these requirements will be provided in Block 16. If the deliverable item is constrained by a specific event or milestone the constraint will be fully explained in Block 16 of the DD Form 1423. "As generated", "As required", and "Deferred Delivery" will always be fully explained in Block 16. Block 13: Is the date of subsequent submission of the deliverable item, after the initial submission. Subsequent submission is only used to indicate the specific time period. The data is required when Block 10 of the DD Form 1423 indicates multiple delivery is required. This does not apply to resubmission of a deliverable item that has been reviewed by the requiring office and determined to be only conditionally acceptable or unacceptable. Block 14a: Will contain the activity name(s) where the deliverable item is to be sent. If the activity is other than DCMA or NAVSUP-WSS the full name, address (including code) will be specified. That specific information will be located in Block 16 of the DD Form 1423. Block 14b: Is the number of copies of draft and or final copies to be submitted. When final "Repro" copies are to be submitted Block 16 will clarify the type of Repro copies required. (e.g., vellum, negative, etc.) Block 15: Is the total of each type of copies to be submitted as required by Block 14. Block 16: Is the block used to provide additional or clarifying information Blocks 1 through 15. This block is also the only area used to tailor the document listed in Block 4. Only deletions to the minimum requirements stated in the document in Block 4 are allowed. Block 16 may also be used to specify the medium for delivery of the data. Block 17: Is the block where the bidder or offeror is to enter the appropriate price group. The price groups are defined as follows: A. Group I - Data which the contractor prepares to satisfy the Government's requirements. The contractor does not need this type of data to perform the rest of the contract. Price would be based on identifiable direct costs, overhead, General and Administrative (G&A) and profit. B. Group II - Data essential to contract performance which must be reworked or amended to conform to Government requirements. The price for data in this group would be based on the direct cost to convert the original data to meet Government needs and to deliver it, plus allocable overhead, G&A and profit. C. Group III - Data which the contractor must develop for his own use and which requires no substantial change to conform to Government requirements regarding depth of content, format, frequency of submittal, preparation, and quality of data. Only the costs of reproducing, handling and delivery, plus overhead, G&A and profit, are considered in pricing data in this group. D. Group IV - Data which the contractor has developed as part of his commercial business. Not much of this data is required and the cost is insignificant. The item should normally be coded "no charge." An example is a brochure or brief manual developed for commercial application which will be acquired in small quantities, and the added cost is too small to justify the expense of computing the charge that otherwise would go with the acquisition. Block 18: Enter the total estimated price equal to that portion of the total price which is estimated to be attributable to the production or development for the government of that ITEM OF DATA. THE ENTRY "N/C" FOR "NO CHARGE" is acceptable. ZZ= MIL-V-3 DATE OF FIRST SUBMISSION=EOC Submit at the time of material delivery a Certificate of Compliance per DI-MISC-81356 to NAVSUP-WSS code N9433. A separate Certificate of Compliance shall be prepared and submitted for each unique combination of Contract/Purchase Order Number, National Stock Number and Item Nomenclature specified in the schedule of Supply/Services. sig_44a5edc90074deb6f12b.description: The Council of Europe’s Group of States against Corruption (GRECO) regularly produces statistical, analytical and visual information related to its monitoring activities, including the implementation of GRECO recommendations by its member States, trends identified through evaluation and compliance procedures and other activities falling within its mandate. In that context, the Organisation is seeking up to 8 (eight) providers for the provision of consultancy services in statistical analysis, data processing, data verification, data visualisation and institutional reporting relating to GRECO’s monitoring activities, to be requested on an as-needed basis, in compliance with the ordering procedure defined in the Framework Contract. Similar services may also be required for analysing data pertaining to cooperation activities in the area of fight against economic crime. The deadline for submission of tenders is 30 September 2026 at 23:59 (Strasbourg/CET time). Link to tender : https://www.coe.int/en/web/greco/-/call-for-tender-intellectual-services-for-the-preparation-processing-analysis-reporting-and-visualisation-of-greco-monitoring-data .

sig_44b2d3d848ec11c2e831.description: The purpose of this Contract Notice is to establish a Panel of Trainers for the provision of Training Services for the Local Enterprise Office in Leitrim County Council. LEO Leitrim is compiling a panel of trainers, from which future training programmes, workshops and seminars for a 3-year period will be selected. Applications are invited from those with appropriate skills and experience that wish to be included in the LEO Leitrim Training panel. Applications will be accepted throughout the lifecycle of the Panel at any stage, however in order to be considered for the first tranche of contracts, applicants should apply by 1st June 2026. The existing Framework Agreement will expire on the 31st July 2026, and will be replaced by this Panel which will operate from 1st August 2026 for a period of 3 years. The contracting authority intends to conclude the framework agreement for the provision of design services consisting of: Technical expertise for the resistance and stability requirement, technical expertise for the fire safety requirement, technical expertise for installations, geotechnical survey / land analysis and stability studies, including uncovering, hydrological and hydrogeological survey, topographical survey including OCPI approval, study on the possibility of using high-efficiency alternative systems to increase energy performance, study on NZEB building compliance, RADON study, detailed urban planning scheme, zonal urban planning scheme, energy audit and initial energy performance certificate, pre-feasibility study, intervention works feasibility documentation DALI, opportunity study, feasibility study, fire safety study, preliminary archaeological diagnostic report for expropriation purposes, study on the value of the cultural resource / historical study, circulation study / traffic study, landscape study, dendrological study, environmental study - Biodiversity Monitoring MB, population health impact study, documentation for obtaining approvals required in the urbanism certificate, technical documentation for authorising construction works (PAC), technical documentation for authorising demolition works (PAD), technical documentation for works execution organisation (POE), technical project and execution details (PTDE), support during the award procedure of the works execution contract, technical assistance (AT), energy performance certificate upon completion of works, drawing up the technical book (as-built), drawing up the designer's viewpoint upon completion of works, drawing up the funding application for accessing non-reimbursable European or governmental funds, DNSH study. Any interested economic operator has the right to request clarifications or additional information regarding the tender documentation. To the extent that clarification requests are requested within the deadline provided in Chap. I.1) NAME, ADDRESS AND CONTACT POINT((s)), section - Number of days by which clarifications may be requested before the deadline for submission of tenders/applications, respectively 20 days (before the deadline for submission of tenders/applications), the contracting authority shall respond to clarification requests 10 days before the deadline set for the submission of tenders. Maximum estimated value of the framework agreement excluding VAT 32.928.643,33 Currency: RON Minimum estimated value of the framework agreement excluding VAT: 16.879.100,00 Currency: RON Estimated value of the largest subsequent contract excluding VAT: 18.436.350,00 Currency: RON Estimated value of the smallest subsequent contract excluding VAT: 1.762.185,67 Currency: RON The Contracting Authority intends to adopt measures that will lead to the improvement of the living standard, which measures will require extensive intervention, rehabilitation, modernisation and building development works. The construction works for which the procurement of design services is intended are classified into the following main investment directions: • Increasing housing quality • Improving the quality of safety and functional conditions of spaces • Eco-efficient "smart" solutions for the benefit of the community • Superior performance support for individuals and the community in Sector 5 • Environmental protection and ecological management of the territory The design services will refer to the following stages: 1. Technical expertise for resistance and stability requirement 2. Technical expertise for fire safety requirement 3. Technical expertise for installations 4. Geotechnical survey / land analysis and stability studies, including uncovering 5. Hydrological and hydrogeological survey 6. Topographical survey including OCPI approval 7. Study on the possibility of using high-efficiency alternative systems to increase energy performance 8. Study on NZEB building compliance 9. RADON study 10. Detailed urban planning scheme 11. Zonal urban planning scheme 12. Energy audit and initial energy performance certificate 13. Pre-feasibility study 14. Intervention works feasibility documentation DALI 15. Opportunity study 16. Feasibility study 17. Fire safety study 18. Preliminary archaeological diagnostic report for expropriation purposes 19. Study on the value of the cultural resource / historical study 20. Circulation study / traffic study 21. Landscape study 22. Dendrological study 23. Environmental study - Biodiversity Monitoring MB 24. Population health impact study 25. Documentation for obtaining approvals required in the urbanism certificate 26. Technical documentation for authorising construction works (PAC) 27. Technical documentation for authorising demolition works (PAD) 28. Technical documentation for works execution organisation (POE) 29. Technical project and execution details (PTDE) 30. Support during the award procedure of the works execution contract 31. Technical assistance (AT) 32. Energy performance certificate upon completion of works 33. Drawing up the technical book (as-built) 34. Drawing up the designer's viewpoint upon completion of works 35. Drawing up funding application for accessing non-reimbursable European or governmental funds 36. DNSH study The technical-economic documentations related to the types of buildings and design stages presented shall be drawn up in accordance with the legislative requirements in force. At the same time, the type of documentations and services that the contracting authority wishes to contract for each category of works separately are detailed in the annex to this specification.

The designer has the obligation, in the event that changes occur to the conditions established by the Specific Guide drawn up for P.N.R.R., P.O.R, local budget, without being limited to these, to revise the technical documentation accordingly, without claiming additional costs, within a reasonable term requested by the beneficiary or imposed by A.D.R.B.I./M.D.R.A.P/any other institution, etc., so as to eliminate the risks of losing funding. The drafting of technical documentations shall begin only after receiving a notification from the contracting authority; this shall be transmitted to the economic operator, as a rule, within a maximum of 10 days from the date of signing the subsequent contract. Delivery deadlines shall be established depending on the complexity of each individual subsequent contract, but shall not exceed 20 calendar days for drafting SF/DALI, 30 calendar days for drafting DTAC and DTOE and 40 calendar days for drafting PTE, technical assistance during the award process of the execution works and during the execution of construction works until the completion of the project. Note: depending on complexity, the deadlines presented above may be adjusted by mutual agreement. sig_44d830b444d6a9ed8fb8.description: The subject of the public contract is the supply, installation and commissioning of a complex interactive projection system for shooting training intended for the training of security forces and other authorised users. The system must form one functional unit enabling the implementation of shooting training using both live weapons and weapons with laser shooting simulation. The system includes, in particular, projection technology, hit detection equipment, control and evaluation software, audiovisual and communication equipment, as well as all related technical and safety elements necessary for operation in a shooting range environment. The system must allow for the projection of static and dynamic shooting scenarios, real-time hit evaluation, archiving and subsequent analysis of shooting progress, and support for the creation and editing of custom training scenarios by the user. The supply also includes complete integration into the shooting range space, including installation, calibration and commissioning of all components, the supply of necessary hardware and software equipment, the provision of safety measures and protection of technologies against the effects of shooting, as well as the supply of related accessories for the implementation of training. The supply also includes training and maintenance of the system for a period of three (5) years. sig_45182218dce81071619d.description: The objective of the request is to establish a dynamic purchasing system (DPS), the preliminary subject of which is the security technologies and related services required for the implementation of technical information security and compliance. The DPS to be established would enable, among other things, the procurement of the following solutions, technologies and services as needed: - Security event management, analytics and response automation. Examples include SIEM, SOAR and other similar solutions, security alert enrichment, correlation, prioritisation, workflow automation, hyperautomation and AI agent-based automation. - Analytics and artificial intelligence solutions to support security monitoring and response. Examples include AI/ML-based solutions to support SOC operations, improving analyst efficiency, automation of threat hunting, and supporting anomaly detection and investigation. - Threat intelligence management and utilisation in security monitoring and response. Examples include the management, combination, automation, analysis and utilisation of threat intelligence collected from public, open, commercial and other sources in anomaly forecasting, enrichment and decision-making, including Threat Intelligence Platform (TIP) solutions. - Asset management for security monitoring needs. Examples include solutions that create and maintain up-to-date and unified visibility into environments containing IT, OT, IoT and medical devices, including devices, software, software versions, dependencies, integrations with existing asset management solutions, and the utilisation of SBOM data. - Third-party and supply chain risk management. Examples include automated solutions supporting supplier information security risk assessment, continuous monitoring and software supply chain risk management. - Network traffic security event detection and response. Examples include Network Detection and Response (NDR) and other similar solutions for analysing network traffic, identifying anomalies and supporting automated or guided response. - Safe utilisation of artificial intelligence and usage monitoring. Examples include solutions for managing, monitoring and protecting the use of artificial intelligence, generative artificial intelligence and AI agents in the organisation, as well as the risks associated with their use. - A system/solution intended for the handling of security incidents (case management), into which all data related to incident handling, such as memory dumps, log data, actions taken, evidence, etc., can be collected securely as part of the DFIR process. - SandBox tools for malware investigation and operational analysis. In addition, probable general requirements/boundary conditions concerning all potential procurement packages are: - Solutions should in principle support a multi-tenant model or otherwise be suitable for a multi-tenant environment. - Solutions should in principle be integrable with security event management and response automation solutions (e.g. SOAR) as well as log management solutions, and support the large-scale utilisation of artificial intelligence. - Procurements to be implemented may include, inter alia, the following: consulting, maintenance, development, deployment, integration and expert services. - Istekki may procure technologies for its own use, exclusively for customers' use, or for the use of both Istekki and customers. The objective is for the establishment phase of the dynamic purchasing system to commence in May-June 2026. Please note that this is a prior information notice (hereinafter referred to as the notice), and this notice does not yet constitute a request to participate. The information provided in this notice is preliminary and may change as preparation progresses. REGISTRATION. Companies interested in this dynamic purchasing system (DPS) are requested to register for the market dialogue by email at: hankinnat@istekki.fi no later than 17.4.2026 (with the subject "Tietoturvapalveluiden DPS"). The personal data of registered persons will be used solely for contacts related to the preparation of this dynamic purchasing system. MARKET DIALOGUE. Draft material related to the dynamic purchasing system under preparation will be sent to registered companies for comments, in a so-called market dialogue, during an estimated period of 05/2026. Registered companies will be given the opportunity to comment on the draft material in writing. The market dialogue and materials will be in Finnish. Participation or non-participation in the market dialogue does not preclude participation in a potential procurement procedure.

The contract is divided into lots as follows: • Lot 1 "Audit Consultancy"; • Lot 2 "Finance Consultancy"; • Lot 3 "Internal Control Consultancy". The exact nature and characteristics of each lot are defined in Part III of these special tender conditions, "Technical Requirements". Each tenderer has the opportunity to submit a tender for one, several or all lots. No limit is set regarding the number of lots that can be awarded to a single tenderer. Organisation of sessions Sessions shall be organised on demand. Only sessions actually ordered shall be invoiced. Consultancy team For all lots, consultancy sessions taking place in accordance with receptive bilingualism (participants expressing themselves in their language role), the tenderer must, on pain of nullity of the tender, propose consultants who understand the interventions of the participants in both official languages of the Brussels-Capital Region (French or Dutch); or must propose at least 1 primary French-speaking consultant and at least 1 primary Dutch-speaking consultant. In addition, the tenderer may propose substitute consultants in each of the two language roles. Place of performance The various lots of the support system may be organised in an in-person or remote format, depending on the circumstances and the needs of the administrations. In-person services shall be provided in Brussels on the premises of ERAP or within the Brussels administrations benefiting from the services carried out under the contract. Estimated quantity The duration of this contract is set at 36 months and commences on the date indicated upon notification of the contract award decision. During this period, the contracting authority may place subsequent contracts (orders) in accordance with the arrangements defined in these special tender conditions, without however exceeding the maximum volume of orders specified below. The contracting authority does not undertake to order up to the maximum quantity, which therefore does not constitute a quantity to which the contractor is entitled upon conclusion of the framework agreement. Conversely, if the maximum quantity of orders is reached, the framework agreement has exhausted its effects and no further orders may be placed, even if the framework agreement has not reached its term in terms of duration. Estimated quantity: 780 half-days of 3h00 of consultancy for lot 1 "Audit Consultancy" for the duration of the public contract. 252 half-days of 3h00 of consultancy for lot 2 "Finance Consultancy" for the duration of the public contract. 189 half-days of 3h00 of consultancy for lot 3 "Internal Control Consultancy" for the duration of the public contract. These estimates are not binding on the contracting authority. Lot 1 "Audit Consultancy" The mission of ERAP is to support Brussels public administrations in strengthening their organisational control through a dynamic and continuous management cycle. This cycle, based on the Deming approach (Plan-Do-Check-Act), includes the planning, execution, verification and adjustment of processes, thereby enabling continuous improvement. Internal audit, an independent function within public administrations, intervenes ad hoc in this cycle to evaluate the effectiveness of management systems and measure their performance. It makes it possible to identify process weaknesses, analyse risks, and propose recommendations. Furthermore, within the more specific context of whistleblowers, audit ensures the independence and objectivity of the handling of reports, while ensuring process compliance and the implementation of corrective actions when necessary. The services consist of carrying out audits to evaluate management systems and internal processes, while providing expertise to improve internal audit systems. This support is primarily intended for Managers and Internal Auditors of the administrations.; Lot 2 "Finance Consultancy" In a context of increasingly limited resources and growing demands, local authorities face complex challenges to ensure the continuity and efficiency of their missions. Maintaining a short- and medium-term budgetary balance while reconciling financial imperatives with a citizen-centred approach constitutes a major challenge. In this context, exploring new sources of funding, optimising expenditure and strategic management of investments are becoming essential priorities. Finance consultancy services consist of supporting the efficient management of financial resources by proposing tailored solutions adapted to the specific features of the public sector. They aim to optimise the organisational structure of financial services, support the improvement of financial processes and accompany the transition towards new practices, while fostering team buy-in for the necessary changes.; Lot 3 "Internal Control Consultancy" The Brussels-Capital Region has driven the implementation of internal control within local authorities through several legislative articles, including articles 263-11, 12 and 13 of the ordinance of 5 March 2009 "amending the New Communal Law", as well as those of the Ordinance of 14 March 2019 amending the law of 8 July 1976 and the organic law of CPAS. These provisions make communes and CPAS responsible for the implementation and monitoring of internal control of their activities. This internal control, defined as a set of measures and procedures, aims to guarantee security, compliance and performance in several key areas: 1.

The achievement of objectives 2. Compliance with laws and procedures 3. The reliability of financial and management information 4. The efficient use of resources 5. The protection of assets 6. The prevention of fraud In this context, the services consist of supporting a global and integrated approach to internal control, with an emphasis on risk management, process optimisation and the strengthening of an organisational culture geared towards continuous improvement. They intervene by identifying, evaluating and managing risks, while establishing and optimising action plans aimed at controlling these risks. In parallel, they thereby strengthen the culture of internal control within the administrations. Finally, they introduce practices making it possible to continuously evaluate and improve the internal control system, thereby guaranteeing its long-term effectiveness.

sig_458037be25f5ba8cc32b.description: 1. Objective As part of this market survey, suitable software solutions for the digital management and tracking of human milk processes (mother's own milk and donated human milk) in a clinical environment are being sought. The goal is a system for the complete, audit-proof mapping of all processes, taking into account the requirements of the SoHo Regulation, with a focus on patient safety, traceability and process automation. 2. General requirements The software must ensure end-to-end digital documentation and traceability; provide interfaces to SAP and Copra 5/6; automate workflows and notifications; integrate label printing and scanning processes; and enable role-based access. 3. Mother's Own Milk The software should enable the registration of mothers on the ward with an SAP connection, assign a unique mother ID, record CMV status including information and consent, document the amount of milk expressed, allow labels to be created by staff or the mother, track the storage location and inventory, and provide automatic alerts for CMV inactivation (day 7 and 32+0 weeks of gestation). Data on the children such as name, date of birth, week of gestation and weight should be automatically transferred from SAP or Copra. 4. Processing Mother's Own Milk CMV-inactivated milk should be pooled by day, assigned in batches by bottle, labelled, inactivation documented, and cooling processes and storage locations noted. Centrifuged milk should be processed analogously, including documentation of duration and revolutions, labelling as skimmed, assignment of analyses and storage. 5. Administration The software should enable the assignment of milk batches to children, offer interfaces to Copra 5/6, record partial quantities via scan and document retrievals. 6. Batch management The software must automatically generate batches based on mother ID, week of gestation, calendar week of birth, calendar week of milk collection and processing type (raw or pasteurised). Colour coding by week of gestation should be adjusted automatically, as should the documentation of the processing day. 7. Human Milk Bank Potential donors should be identified automatically (e.g. >600 ml/day), be able to fill out digital information and anamnesis forms with a signature, and receive a donor ID. Interfaces to SAP, Copra and the laboratory (e.g. ix.serv) should automatically adopt laboratory findings. The software should enable approvals by specialist staff, evaluation of findings and labelling of pasteurisation requirements. 8. Donated milk The software should record milk quantity, date, time, calendar week, temperature, microbiological samples and storage locations. 9. Processing of donated milk Raw milk should be pooled by day, assigned in batches and stored until release. Pasteurised milk should be processed with documentation of pasteurisation, cooling and storage. CMV-inactivated milk should document pooling, inactivation, cooling and release. Centrifuged milk is processed analogously to mother's own milk, if necessary with additional pasteurisation. 10. Non-released milk The software should document measures such as discarding, re-pasteurisation, training of the donor and repeat samples. 11. Dispensing The software should enable the assignment of batches to wards and individual children and record partial quantities via scan. 12. Summary We are looking for an integrated software solution for the secure, automated management of human milk processes with complete traceability, high system integration and user-friendliness. 13. Participation in the market survey Interested companies are requested to submit their participation and information on the solution by email to vergabestelle@klinikum-stuttgart.de no later than 15.05.2026. The market survey serves exclusively to prepare for a possible procurement procedure. There is no entitlement to the implementation of such a procedure.

sig_4586e1f913821c03159c.description: Forest management services will be awarded in the year 2026 (field phase 2027) by concluding a contract for each lot. The cumulative area of the lots is 5.370,57 ha. The area of each lot is specified in the description of the lots. The services involve the development of the forest management plan, a product of the management activity with technical-organisational content, ecologically grounded, through which, for a period of time, the works necessary to be executed in a production unit are established, for the purpose of bringing and, subsequently, maintaining the structural characteristics of the stands and the forest as a whole to the values corresponding to the optimal structural model defined in accordance with the ecological, social and economic objectives pursued through sustainable management. According to the provisions of Art. 63 paragraph (11) of Law no. 331/2024 regarding the Forestry Code, with subsequent amendments and additions, it is necessary that the development of forest management plans be done through public procurement procedures. The management of the state-owned public forest fund constitutes a priority obligation of the forest fund administrators. The method of managing the state-owned public forest fund is regulated by forest management plans. Forest management plans and their amendments are approved by order of the head of the Authority. In the case of state-owned public lands, the management plans provide data and information necessary for their registration/updating in the centralised inventory of goods in the state's public domain and for registration in the integrated cadastre and land register system. Number of days by which clarifications can be requested before the deadline for the submission of tenders/applications 18 days. The contracting authority will clearly respond to requests for clarifications on the 11-th day before the deadline set for the submission of tenders. NOTE: The contracting authority is not obliged to respond to requests for clarifications/additional information that have not been addressed within the established deadline. Forest management services for the Săcueni Forestry District - Bihor Forestry Directorate, with an area of 3131,36 ha. sig_45aa5d107594438d760c.description: The London Violence Reduction Unit (VRU) is undertaking a virtual market engagement exercise Wednesday 5th August 2026 @ 10am , via MS Teams, to inform the commissioning of the Online Harms Digital Youth Work Pilot Programme. The London Violence Reduction Unit (VRU) is committed to understanding the factors that place children and young people at risk of violence, exploitation and harm, and to working collaboratively with partners to deliver long-term, sustainable solutions. We work across communities and sectors, including youth services, local government, education, health, policing and the voluntary and community sector, championing a public health approach that combines prevention, early intervention and effective support for those experiencing the greatest levels of risk and vulnerability. At the heart of our approach is the belief that violence is preventable, not inevitable. We recognise, however, that many children and young people are already navigating the impacts of trauma, exploitation, abuse and complex community dynamics. As such, our work seeks not only to prevent harm before it occurs, but also to strengthen the systems, services and trusted adults responsible for safeguarding, supporting and intervening with those most affected. Central to this approach is a commitment to partnership working, evidence-informed practice and ensuring that the voices, experiences and expertise of young people and communities shape the solutions designed to support them. The Mayor's Violence Reduction Unit (VRU) is seeking to engage with the market in advance of a forthcoming procurement opportunity relating to the delivery of its flagship Digital Youth Work Pilot Programme. The programme forms part of the VRU's wider public health approach to violence reduction and sits within a London-wide model developed following extensive consultation with young people, practitioners, safeguarding professionals, academics and sector experts. Digital life brings clear benefits for many children. Ofcom found that 99% of 13–17-year-olds see at least one benefit to being online, including help with schoolwork, learning new skills and maintaining social connections. 93% of children in the UK play video games, and children report that gaming helps them socialise with friends, learn new skills and have fun, with most online interactions taking place with friends they already know offline. At the same time, the VRU is concerned that these same digital environments expose children and young people to a wide range of harms and risks. Digital safety is increasingly a public safety and public health concern. Children and young people are navigating identity, relationships, influence, exploitation and conflict across interconnected online and offline environments. However, systems, services and safeguarding responses have often struggled to keep pace with the rapidly evolving nature of digital spaces. This matters for the VRU because online harms do not sit separately from wider concerns about violence, vulnerability, exploitation and safeguarding. The VRU is seeking delivery partners to pilot innovative Digital Youth Work (DYW) approaches across London that drive new models of engagement with young people and promote safeguarding in digital spaces. The VRU is seeking approaches that: Design, deliver and test new or existing digital youth work models Extend trusted, relationship-based youth work into digital environments Strengthen early intervention, prevention and safeguarding online Generate learning, insight and practical outputs to strengthen future activity The programme aims not only to deliver effective pilot activity, but also to contribute to sector-wide innovation and the development of scalable models of digital youth work across London. Scope of delivery The programme will be structured into three complementary lots: Lot 1: Supporting High-Need and Digitally Dependent Young People Testing approaches that improve accessibility and engagement for young people who face barriers to traditional provision, including SEND. Lot 2: Early Intervention and Prevention of Online Harms Testing models that enable early identification, prevention and response to online risks, with a focus on safeguarding and preventative practice of deterring online to offline violence. Lot 3: Universal Digital Youth Work and Positive Opportunities Exploring how digital youth work can foster connection, creativity, play, participation and digital citizenship for all young people. Bidders may apply for one, two or all three lots. Applications may be submitted by individual organisations or as partnerships/consortia. Target Audience The programme will focus on delivering digital youth work to children and young people aged 11–25 across London, including but not limited to: Young people at higher risk of being impacted by online harms Those facing barriers to traditional youth provision, including SEND and young people who may be more digitally dependent and/or digitally excluded Young people experiencing vulnerability linked to violence, exploitation or disadvantage Young people with caring responsibilities Young people in the care system Young people affected by Violence Against Women and Girls (VAWG) The wider youth population through universal provision Potential delivery settings and workforces may include, but are not limited to: Community-based youth organisations and youth services Detached, outreach and neighbourhood-based provision Faith and community organisations SEND and disability-focused youth provision Organisations supporting young people experiencing vulnerability, exclusion or barriers to traditional youth provision Specialist services working with young people affected by violence, exploitation or online harms Informal education, mentoring and participation-based youth provision Indicative Outcomes The programme is expected to contribute to: Increased engagement of young people in safe, supportive digital environments Improved accessibility of youth work for young people who do not traditionally engage with youth work and are digitally dependent and/or digitally excluded) Strengthened early identification and prevention of online harms in the digital space Increased use of technology to foster positive opportunities Strengthen young people’s digital citizenship Increased workforce confidence and capability in incorporating digital youth work into traditional practice and safeguarding policy Development of scalable models, guidance and practical tools A stronger London-wide evidence base on digital youth work and online safety Timeframe and Budget The maximum estimated budget for this programme is up to £650,000 excl. VAT over a full contract period from November 2026 – March 2029, subject to confirmation of funding, internal governance and relevant approvals. This comprises: £390,000 core funding across the 2026/27 and 2027/28 financial years from November 2026 to March 2028 An extension option of up to £260,000 for a further 12 months from April 2028 The VRU welcomes bids from individual organisations as well as collaborative partnerships and consortia. We recognise that expertise may be distributed across different organisations, and we encourage applications that bring together complementary skills, knowledge and experience. Providers do not need to demonstrate strength across every area independently, provided that the partnership as a whole can evidence the required expertise and capacity to deliver the programme. This may include, for example, combining specialist knowledge in DYW, supporting SEND or neurodiverse children, digital safety, contextual safeguarding, fostering positive digital opportunities, and preventative violence reduction approaches. Market Engagement / Response The VRU welcomes engagement from organisations with expertise in: Youth work and youth engagement Digital youth work Gaming, AI, technology Safeguarding and contextual safeguarding Online harms, exploitation and violence prevention Working with vulnerable and hard-to-reach young people Youth participation and co-production Learning, evaluation and evidence generation If you are interested in the opportunity and meet the core capabilities as set out above, then please join us for our early market warming event on Wednesday 5th August 2026 at 10:00AM. Attending the early market warming session does not constitute a commitment to participate in any future procurement process. The Eventbrite link for market warming session can be found here - https://www.eventbrite.co.uk/e/london-vru-online-harms-digital-youth-work-pilot-market-warming-session-tickets-1994744836503?aff=oddtdtcreator Please note that this exercise is in no way a call for competition and will not result in the award of a contract to any respondents to this notice. If have any further questions about this opportunity, please contact: vruprocurement@london.gov.uk For more information about this opportunity, please visit the eSourcing portal at: https://www.delta-esourcing.com/tenders/UK-UK-London:-Digital-mapping-services./5SJUMP2G3Z To respond to this opportunity, please click here: https://www.delta-esourcing.com/respond/5SJUMP2G3Z Lot 1: Supporting high-need and digitally dependent young people. Test and develop Digital Youth Work approaches that improve accessibility, inclusion and engagement for young people who face barriers to traditional provision, particularly those with SEND, neurodiverse needs or higher levels of digital dependency. Lot 2: Early intervention and prevention of online harms. Test Digital Youth Work approaches that strengthen early identification, prevention and safeguarding responses to online harms, vulnerabilities and online-to-offline risks. Lot 3: Universal digital youth work and positive opportunities. Explore how Digital Youth Work can foster connection, belonging, creativity, participation and positive opportunities for children and young people through universal and strengths-based approaches.

sig_45c985c19003ef2cd69f.description: 1. Contracting Authority The EWE Group, headquartered in Oldenburg, is one of the large regional energy supply companies in Germany. EWE is active in various business areas, including energy (gas/electricity), telecommunications, information technology, mobility and hydrogen. With over 10.000 employees and a turnover of around 8,7 billion euros in the 2024 financial year, EWE is one of the significant players in the German energy industry. EWE pursues a clear strategy towards a sustainable, innovative and future-oriented energy supply - including through projects in the field of wind energy and the hydrogen economy. The EWE Group is predominantly in municipal hands and supplies around one million households in the electricity segment alone. 2. Subject of the tender The EWE Group as the contracting authority (CA) intends to procure a software solution for Business Process Management (BPM) that meets the company's specific professional and technical requirements. The subject of the tender is the acquisition, implementation and operation of BPM software, including initial user training and the migration of existing data and process models from the legacy system to the new system. The software should enable intuitive modelling of processes - with a focus on Business Process Model and Notation (BPMN). For this purpose, user-friendly drag-and-drop editors are required for the simple creation, adaptation and maintenance of process models. In addition, the following functionalities are required: - Independently configurable workflows, e.g. for the approval of process models - Extensive commenting and collaboration options for all user groups - Versioning of process models and the possibility to manage several variants of a process - Comprehensive reporting and analysis functions Also desired are: - A flexibly configurable authorisation and role concept - Interfaces to other IT systems to support import and export processes, in particular: * Import of data from IT systems (e.g. organisational units) * Export of data to third-party systems, such as analysis platforms like SAP Datasphere, Snowflake or Azure OneLake
sig_45c985c19003ef2cd69f.title: Process modelling tool

sig_45f32c762884493871f0.description: The Digital and Population Data Services Agency (Digi- ja väestötietovirasto, DVV) is preparing a public procurement for Finland’s European Digital Identity Wallet. The procurement concerns a digital identity wallet solution provided as a software development kit (SDK), related backend services and certificate/attestation issuance. The wallet solution will be comprised of the wallet unit clients for both iOS and Android mobile operating systems as well as the related wallet back-end functionalities and will be available for certification using the NOBCCS (Nordic and Baltic Common Certification Scheme) by the end of Q3/2026. Also, other wallet-related functionalities, such as for example, but not limited to PID provisioning, identity matching service, or QEAA provisioning, may be part of the procurement. Suppliers interested in this planned procurement can contact DVV by email hankinnat@dvv.fi. DVV reserves the right to invite suppliers for further discussions regarding the planned procurement. This can be done to obtain information on market and suppliers providing relevant services, and to clarify any possible issues related to the object of the procurement. DVV may use the information it receives during these discussions for planning and preparation of the actual invitation to tender. NOTE For the sake of clarity, this is not a request for information or an invitation to market dialogue. The information provided by DVV is preliminary at this point and it is subject to change. Taking or not taking contact with DVV at this point does not change the standing or status of a supplier in the eventual procurement process.

sig_460aa04dd287c2d25cb0.description: HUS-yhtymä is establishing a dynamic purchasing system (hereinafter DPS) for the procurement of Quality register systems. The registers to be procured will be defined in more detail in each call for competition within the dynamic purchasing system. We invite applications for participation in the HUS 605-2023 dynamic purchasing system (hereinafter also DPS) concerning Quality register systems and related expert work. The subject of the procurement is: - Disease-specific, disease-group-specific or patient-group-specific quality register systems procured as software services - Integration products related to quality registers - Expert work Quality registers serve as a daily tool for clinicians, and they can be used to monitor different stages of care and assess the quality of care. The registers also provide information on procedures performed and problems related to care. Quality registers can be used to improve the quality of care and develop new care practices. The metrics and results of HUS quality registers are also nationally comparable, and data is collected into THL registers for national comparison. HUS's objective is to procure system solutions for monitoring the effectiveness of patient care using a flexible and simple procedure. HUS has dozens of different disease-group-specific quality registers in use, which are integrated into the Apotti patient system and other care-related systems. Some of the quality registers are integrated into national applications. The contracts for these currently used quality registers will also be renewed or replaced through this dynamic purchasing system. The HUS 605-2023 DPS dynamic purchasing system is valid until 31.12.2035, unless it is shortened or extended by a separate notice. At the time of publication of the call for participation, HUS estimates that 30 - 60 calls for competition will be published within the dynamic purchasing system during the years 2025-2035. The number is a preliminary estimate, which may change significantly as the need for competition and the grouping of products becomes clearer. At the time of publication of the call for participation, HUS estimates the total value of the entire duration of the dynamic purchasing system to be a maximum of 20 000 000 euros, taking into account all procurements potentially made in the system. The estimate is preliminary and is based on the procurement need known at this time. HUS does not commit to any procurement volumes or mandatory purchase obligations with this notice. Applications for participation can be submitted to the dynamic purchasing system throughout its duration. It is valid until the date stated in the contract notice, unless it is suspended or amended while the dynamic purchasing system is in force. The actual procurements are made through calls for competition within the dynamic purchasing system, in which the subject of the procurement is described and specified. A separate contract is concluded for each internal call for competition. The contract period is defined separately in each internal call for competition on a case-by-case basis. You can apply to be a tenderer for the dynamic purchasing system if you meet the suitability requirements stated in the ESPD form and in the section on criteria for the subject of the procurement. All candidates who meet the suitability requirements will be accepted into it.

sig_46d1eb55ab861ad2d53b.description:
Background and problem: The DEHSt has been operating end-to-end digitised specialist procedures for approx. 20 years. Central components of the IT landscape used by the DEHSt are in a phase of renewal. The number of software artefacts to be developed by the DEHSt is growing continuously – schedules are therefore becoming increasingly tight and parallelisation and complexity are increasing. Several legacy systems must also be completely replaced. To remedy this, the DEHSt has developed a Software Development Kit (SDK), which consists of software and extensive documentation, for example for commissioning a test and integration environment. The aim of the SDK is, on the one hand, to carry out a technological renewal and, on the other, to significantly increase development speed while maintaining standards. The SDK provides documentation, software libraries, several independent services for the centralised control (workflow control) of the specialist applications, as well as a base and an example application that integrates into the existing software and process landscape of the DEHSt (i.e. addresses existing central services, the so-called 'DEHSt platform'). The SDK and the DEHSt platform are based on a separation of frontend (AngularJS, NgRx, Material), backend (Spring-Boot), distributed web services and a build pipeline in GitLab as well as scalable operation on a container basis (Docker images on RedHat OKD). . Aim and subject of the project: This procurement measure is for a framework agreement with a term of 4 years. The framework agreement can be extended twice by one year each. The project is to include the development and maintenance of the entire Software Development Kit (SDK) as well as the development of specialist applications based on it. We distinguish between three related but parallel task areas: 1) Lot 1: SDK maintenance and management 2) Lot 2: New development of specialist applications 3) Lot 3: Migration and replacement of legacy systems For the SDK team, the goal is to increase the benefit for the administrative staff but also to positively influence the development time of the developer teams. For the developer teams, it must be a goal to develop a high-quality application in the shortest possible time based on an elaborated specification. Lot 1: SDK maintenance and management . According to the current planning status, the contracting authority intends to commission tasks with up to 2.560 person-days (PD) in the first four years. Subject to possible changes in the legal situation regarding European and national emissions trading, the contracting authority expects that at least 50% of the upper limit for person-days mentioned here will be commissioned. Should the contract be extended by one year each, the contracting authority expects tasks amounting to 640 PD per extension (up to 25% of the original scope). For the purpose of approximate capacity planning, we see a demand of approximately 960 PD in the first year and an average of 500 PD per subsequent year. It is assumed that the workload can be distributed relatively evenly over the months so that a constant utilisation of a development team can be achieved.; Lot 2: New development of specialist applications . According to the current planning status, the contracting authority intends to commission tasks with up to 3.056 person-days (PD) in the first four years. Subject to possible changes in the legal situation regarding European and national emissions trading, the contracting authority expects that at least 50% of the upper limit for person-days mentioned here will be commissioned. Should the contract be extended by one year each, the contracting authority expects tasks amounting to 764 PD per extension (up to 25% of the original scope). For the purpose of approximate capacity planning, we generally see a demand of 500 PD per year, but in 2028 and 2029 an increased demand of about 1.000 PD. The utilisation over the course of the year can vary greatly. In most cases, the provision of the specialist applications must take place by fixed legal deadlines. This means that several development projects must be processed in parallel. This is accompanied by an increased personnel requirement that must be covered by the contractor (e.g. two to four development resources work on one specialist application, at the same time up to four specialist application projects must be processed). The legal deadline can unfortunately generally not be influenced by the contracting authority.; Lot 3: Migration and replacement of legacy systems . According to the current planning status, the contracting authority intends to commission tasks with up to 4.472 (person-days) PD in the first four years. Subject to possible changes in the legal situation regarding European and national emissions trading, the contracting authority expects that at least 50% of the upper limit for person-days mentioned here will be commissioned. Should the contract be extended by one year each, the contracting authority expects tasks amounting to 1.118 PD per extension (up to 25% of the original scope). For the purpose of approximate capacity planning, we generally see a demand of 650 PD per year, but in particular from mid 2028 until the change of the trading period in 2030 an increased demand of about 1.450 PD annually. The utilisation over the course of the year can vary greatly. The provision of the specialist applications must in most cases take place by fixed legal deadlines. This means that several development projects must be processed in parallel. This is accompanied by an increased personnel requirement that must be covered by the contractor (e.g.

two to four development resources work on one specialist application, at the same time up to four specialist application projects must be processed). The legal deadline can unfortunately generally not be influenced by the contracting authority.

sig_46fb2e372f65af999757.description: The subject of the procurement procedure is the design, development, testing and piloting of an Artificial Intelligence Virtual Assistant application for Citizens and Administration (AVIACA) in Sebeș and Vințu de Jos to facilitate access by citizens and companies to the public services of the 2 communities. Details regarding the procurement can be found in the Specifications. NOTE: Deadlines for submitting/responding to requests for clarifications/additional information: A. In accordance with the provisions of Article 160 paragraph (1) of Law No. 98/2016 with subsequent amendments and completions, the deadline by which any interested economic operator has the right to request clarifications or additional information regarding the tender documents is 18 days before the deadline for submitting tenders; B. In accordance with the provisions of Article 160 paragraph (2) of Law No. 98/2016, with subsequent amendments and completions, the contracting authority shall clearly and completely respond to all requests for clarifications in a single day, specifically the 11-th day before the deadline for submitting tenders, through a consolidated response, provided that the requests for clarifications are submitted within the specified period. The subject of the procurement procedure is the design, development, testing and piloting of an Artificial Intelligence Virtual Assistant application for Citizens and Administration (AVIACA) in Sebeș and Vințu de Jos to facilitate access by citizens and companies to the public services of the 2 communities, introducing a tool based on Artificial Intelligence (AI) to facilitate interaction between users (citizens of the two partner localities) and the services offered to them by the two partner mayoralties. Thus, the introduction of the Virtual Assistant aims to create intuitive interfaces, easy to use by users regardless of their level of digitalisation, based on natural language conversational trees that allow users to ask direct questions while the Virtual Assistant, through its specific functions, indexes information and presents users with relevant answers, relevant links or even presents forms to be completed in the event that online requests are made. All these functionalities are intended to increase interest and adoption of electronic services by the citizens of the Municipality of Sebeș and the Commune of Vințu de Jos, thereby contributing directly to the project/call indicator for the number of users of new and optimised digital public services, products and processes.

sig_4702e05e930780e5c8a5.description: The subject of this public contract is a security solution – software and hardware (hereinafter: equipment) for the contracting authority's cyber resilience needs, divided into three lots, namely: • LOT 1: NOZOMI GUARDIAN • LOT 2: SANITISATION OF USB DATA MEDIA • LOT 3: INCREASE OF LICENCE CAPACITY FOR SPLUNK Each tenderer may submit a tender for an individual lot or all lots together. It must be clearly evident from the submitted tender for which lot or lots the tender is being submitted. The exact specifications and requirements of the contracting authority for each individual lot are described in the document Technical Specifications and Requirements of the Contracting Authority, no. 285-60/4-2026 dated 20. 8. 2026, which is an integral part of the documentation related to the award of the public contract or the tender documentation. The subject of lot 1 is the expansion of the existing Nozomi ADS solution for monitoring and detecting cyber threats in the operational and IoT environment - Guardian. The purpose of the lot is to provide sufficient capacities for processing the increased volume of data and thereby maintain an appropriate level of protection and resilience of operational systems. More detailed requirements of the contracting authority are in the document Technical Specifications in point 2.1.; The subject of lot 2 is the supply of a solution for the secure use of removable USB data media in the information and operational environment. The purpose of the lot is to reduce the risk of system compromise via portable media and to ensure a controlled and secure way of transferring data between different environments.
