sig_47117cc1f7e8df31d55e.description: This is not a procurement notice or a call for tenders, but a request for information (RFI) whereby the wellbeing services counties of South Karelia and Päijät-Häme invite system suppliers to register their interest for a potential procurement procedure. This is an RFI/market dialogue through which the wellbeing services counties of South Karelia and Päijät-Häme are exploring potential system suppliers for an income and wealth assessment service to determine client fees in social welfare home care and housing services (community-based and round-the-clock living), as well as for compiling maintenance calculations in family law services and potentially for utilisation in other social welfare calculations. With this RFI, the wellbeing services counties of South Karelia and Päijät-Häme are exploring digital solutions for compiling income and wealth assessments for client fee decisions using robotics. The client fee decision is made in connection with the client's service decision, and this has an impact on the management of the client process as well as on invoicing interruptions and terminations. The aim of the market survey is to find out what kind of product solutions containing the functionalities described below are available on the Finnish market. Through the market dialogue, the wellbeing services counties aim to: 1 Obtain information on market supply and different suppliers' solutions 2 Potential implementation of integrations into various platforms or systems 3 Evaluate the implementation of information security and data protection 4 Obtain an overview of pricing models and cost structures (no individual tenders) 5 Explore delivery and service models The market dialogue is open to all suppliers that can offer product solutions falling within the scope of this solution package. The focus of the dialogue is on solutions based on the automated compilation of income and wealth assessments to support client fee decisions. Suppliers are requested to present services that are under development or ready-made solutions. Suppliers participating in the dialogue are expected to present functionality to be put into production and information on how cooperation with the necessary actors to implement integrations has been taken into account in the preparation of the income and wealth assessment service. There is no need for a system solution based on process control, as this would result in additional recording requirements due to system changes. The core data contents consist of, inter alia, the Incomes Register and tax decisions of the Finnish Tax Administration, and benefit data from Kela. In connection with registration, suppliers are requested to briefly describe: Purpose of use and environment The system must be suitable for the wellbeing services county's use for managing the following service forms: - income and wealth assessment for home care - income and wealth assessment for community-based housing, - income and wealth assessment for round-the-clock living - maintenance calculation for family law services, which forms part of a maintenance agreement concluded by parents. The maintenance calculation requires the data of both parents. - In all fees, the income data of spouses must be taken into account where necessary User groups include - children's supervisors - makers of client fee decisions in wellbeing services counties Key functionalities - produce, as part of the determination of client fees, income and wealth data on the basis of which a proposal for the amount of the client fee or solvency is formed - the calculation must not be saved in the income and wealth assessment service, meaning it does not create an archiving obligation. However, it must be possible to generate a PDF/PDF-A document from the document, which the wellbeing services county can attach as part of the decision and archive in a manner it deems fit. Integrations - Data transfer connection to the Finnish Tax Administration via the LIPA service bus (Incomes Register and tax data) - Data transfer connection to Kela's benefit data service via the LIPA service bus Technical requirements - The system must meet DPIA information security requirements - Data flow diagram and architecture description - User authentication and access control - Generation and management of log data Additional information - What other essential features does your solution include? - How is the implementation of the system typically carried out? - What kind of support and training do you offer? - Estimate from decision to implementation - The wellbeing services county's resource requirement Responses to the questions are requested to be sent by 14.9.2026 at 15:00. Responses are requested to be brief and informative. Responses are requested to be sent to hankinnat@ekhva.fi and hankinnat@paijatha.fi Message subject: "Market survey - Income and wealth assessment service system" This RFI/market survey does not request tenders nor are tenders submitted in response to this RFI; it requests ONLY information related to the procurement. Participation or non-participation in the market survey/RFI does not affect the tenderer's position in a potential tendering procedure. The market dialogue invitation does not bind the respondent (Supplier) to participate in a tendering procedure, nor is responding to this notice a prerequisite for participating in the actual tendering procedure later. Those participating in the market survey are not entitled to receive compensation for their participation. The contracting authority does not undertake to carry out the procurement in question. Decisions on launching a potential procurement process will be made after the market survey. The submitted material will be treated as confidential in accordance with section 24 subsection 1 paragraph 20 of the Act on the Openness of Government Activities. The wellbeing services counties of South Karelia and Päijät-Häme thank you in advance for your responses. They are valuable in defining our system needs and preparing for a potential procurement.
sig_47117cc1f7e8df31d55e.title: Information request / Market survey: Income and wealth assessment service system

sig_475872817e19da0f367f.description:
Delivery/provision of a cloud-based software system for time recording (time management - ZWS) & personnel deployment planning (PEP) for medical services, nursing services & other service types. The subject of the procurement procedure is the provision of a cloud-based software solution (Software as a Service) for time recording (time management – ZWS) and personnel deployment planning (PEP) for the medical service (approx. 720 employees), the nursing service (approx. 2.180 employees) and other service types (approx. 1.372 employees – medical-technical service, functional service, administrative service, personnel of the training centres). In addition, approx. 500 internal and approx. 300 external students must also be managed in the system. A market-available standard solution is expressly being tendered, which can be adapted to the client's requirements through parameterisation. Individual solutions or in-house developments are excluded. This applies in particular to the bidirectional interface to the existing SAP ERP R/3 HCM infrastructure as well as to the new SAP S/4HANA environment. Further requirements for implementation, parameterisation, training and process standardisation are part of the tender documents or the specifications. The software must cover the following task areas in particular and must be provided as an integrated overall solution: -Personnel deployment planning incl. holiday and absence management (PEP) -Time management (ZWS) -Preparatory payroll accounting through the creation of collective agreement-relevant wage types in hourly or € values -Employee Self Service (ESS) -Manager Self Service (MSS) -Reporting and statistics. The interaction of these task areas is indispensable for efficient and modern personnel deployment planning, control and accounting. For this reason, these tasks must be closely linked and should appear as a single unit from a technological and user perspective. The solution must be able to be integrated without problems into the IT infrastructure available at the KC (SAP ERP R/3 HCM & SAP S/4HANA HCM & SAP IS-H/i.s.h.med) and must necessarily communicate with the software solutions already in use via standardised interfaces (state of the art). Both master data as well as attendance, absence and wage data must flow uni- and bidirectionally (depending on the data type) via the interfaces. The interface must necessarily work with change data records (data records to be changed in SAP are deleted and newly created or overwritten with new data records) in order to ensure the highest degree of automation and to minimise the need for manual intervention as far as possible. To map smooth processes, the PEP solution must ensure a consistent, secure and media-break-free data exchange. This is essential, especially for employee payroll accounting, and if it were to fail, it would have a lasting negative impact on the operation of the KC. The most automated transfer possible of required data from the legacy systems must be ensured. The new PEP solution must be able to import data from the IS-H/i.s.h.med, convert it into personnel requirements and integrate it into the deployment planning. With the help of the PEP solution, the wage types currently required at the Klinikum Chemnitz for the correct payroll accounting of all service types must be generated in accordance with the collective agreement regulations and transferred to the SAP HCM payroll and salary system in a time-controlled manner. In the medical collective agreement, 39 different wage types must currently be mapped, and in the non-medical collective agreement, 32 wage types. In some cases, wage types are created on an individual employee basis and depend on different conditions such as department, employee qualification, individual agreement. Especially with on-call duties, it happens that within a department, on-call duties are remunerated according to a fixed flat rate or according to the collective agreement regulations. The software solution must be able to map these constellations even within a month (see also the specifications). The connection of employees to the new PEP software solution is to take place in pre-defined waves. Accordingly, it must be ensured that some of the employees continue to be managed on the SAP PEP and other employees on the new PEP solution. The contractor must ensure that both systems function productively in parallel for the duration of the implementation and rollout and do not influence each other. The S/4HANA migration of the SAP ERP R/3 HCM planned in 2026 (Unicode conversion, database migration and S/4 application) must be taken into account. This concerns both project management and the function (bidirectional integration with the legacy systems HCM and ERP and the migration target, no PEP function maintenance after S/4HANA migration in the HCM). In addition, integration with the parallel project S/4HANA migration is required. The PEP solution is to be introduced on the current SAP HCM version ECC 8. Starting 2026, the transition of the SAP ERP R/3 HCM to SAP S/4HANA HCM is to take place, and with it the migration of the PEP software to the new system. Accordingly, it is assumed that the contractor has already successfully migrated the interfaces of their software solution from SAP ECC to S/4HANA and that all required functions are also fully available in the integration with an S/4HANA system (HCM and ERP). A project-specific EVB-IT cloud contract & service contract will be concluded for the procurement. The draft contract is part of this publication as well as the tender documents for the initial offer and can be further specified by the client within the framework of the procurement negotiations. The procurement is for a minimum contract term of 36 months after operational readiness has been established.

Thereafter, the contract shall be extended by one year at a time, unless it is terminated by one of the parties six months before the end of the contract. Details on this can also be found in the tender documents of the subsequent offer phase or offer phases.

sig_481d915845bee0d7d205.description: Tampereen Vesi Oy (3381716-4) is a wholly owned subsidiary of the City of Tampere. The company was established in 2023 and, at the beginning of 2024, operations were transferred from the City of Tampere's municipal enterprise to a corporate form. Tampereen Vesi Oy provides water utility services in its operating area. The operating area mainly covers the zoned area of the City of Tampere. Tampereen Vesi Oy is inviting tenders for total payroll services, a time and attendance system and an HR system. The procurement is divided into parts as follows: PROCUREMENT PART A: Total payroll services (incl. payroll accounting, salary payment and expert services, as well as the payroll system used by payroll clerks) and a time and attendance system (incl. time and attendance tracking and shift planning). OPTION IN PROCUREMENT PART A: Travel management services (incl. travel ledger and travel and expense claim system). PROCUREMENT PART B: HR system (incl. personal data system and HRD system). Both procurement parts also include the commissioning of services and systems, related advisory and expert services, and system support services. sig_482c9301eb09a942aa13.description: Kirkon keskusrahasto is launching a market consultation with this notice regarding the procurement of a core financial management system. Operating alongside the Church Office is the bookkeeping and payroll service centre of the Evangelical Lutheran Church of Finland, which manages the bookkeeping, purchase invoices, accounts payable, sales invoices, accounts receivable, fixed asset accounting, payroll, travel and expense claims, and associated payment transactions for parishes, parish unions, dioceses, kirkon keskusrahasto and the church pension fund. At the Church Service Centre, core financial management processes are currently supported by a SAP-based solution. The end-of-version support schedule announced by the manufacturer of the current SAP environment requires the contracting entity to evaluate system alternatives for the coming years on a broad scale. The market consultation will examine the suitability of alternative core financial management systems alongside SAP. The aim of the market consultation is to build a comprehensive picture of the technical, functional and economic benefits of the various alternatives and to help evaluate them objectively before launching the actual procurement. Based on the results of the market consultation, the contracting entity may opt for a technology-neutral tender or, for a reasoned reason, restrict the procurement to the current SAP technology. If the technology restriction is justified, the tender will focus on the upgrade of the SAP solution and the selection of an implementation partner. Otherwise, the tender will be implemented as open to all suppliers, including solutions utilising SAP technology. Any future tender will most likely be implemented as a competitive dialogue procedure in compliance with the principles of the Public Procurement Act. If a supplier has references from projects where a client has transitioned from a SAP-based financial management solution to another system, these references are of particular interest from the contracting entity's perspective. The purpose of these references is to help the contracting entity understand the implementation model, workload, risk areas and overall scope of such a transition - not to anticipate the system selection of any potential future procurement. Suppliers can express their interest in participating in the market consultation by submitting an expression of interest and a brief presentation of the core financial management system they offer, along with reference projects, by email to anette.tolvanen@evl.fi NO LATER THAN FRIDAY 17.4.2026. The presentation is requested to be submitted in either PDF or Office file format. As a starting point, 6 suppliers will be invited to the dialogue, selected by comparing the submitted system presentations and named reference projects against the subject of the procurement described below. The comparison will be made as an overall assessment taking into account, inter alia, the scope of the services currently being procured and the comparability of the submitted reference clients/projects to the operations of Kirkon keskusrahasto. Preliminary subject of the procurement The Church Service Centre is planning to tender a core financial management system. The aim of the future procurement is to overhaul and harmonise key financial management processes and ensure a modern, integrated system entity that supports automation. The content of the procurement may consist of, for example, the following core financial management functions: • bookkeeping, financial statements and fixed assets • processing of purchase invoices and accounts payable • sales invoicing, accounts receivable and debt collection • payment transactions • financial reporting and monitoring • financial planning, budgeting and forecasting • archiving • as well as options for extensions and functionalities to be procured later The purpose of this request for information is to map out supplier and solution alternatives related to the procurement. This notice is not a procurement notice or a call for tenders, but an invitation to participate in a market consultation implemented via a prior information notice as part of the preparation of a possible procurement. This request for information does not oblige the contracting entity to carry out the procurement. Current financial management processes are partially automated, but still involve a lot of manual work steps, resolution of exceptions, and fragmented practices between different service areas. The development of the system entity aims, for example, at: • harmonising processes and increasing automation • improving data transfer and integrations • reducing exceptions and errors • improving turnaround times and cost efficiency • better transparency and reporting to support management The aim of the market consultation is to map out solutions available on the market and obtain suppliers' views in particular on: • automation opportunities and best practices • streamlining the current processes of the Church Service Centre using the supplier's offered solution • integrations in a challenging multi-vendor environment • development model and service level requirements • price level and scalability of total costs in light of various scenarios • implementation and migration of the system, including schedule and costs • information security and data protection • architecture

sig_48594db611947be29a74.description: THIS IS NOT A PROCUREMENT NOTICE OR A CALL FOR TENDERS BUT A REQUEST FOR INFORMATION FOR MARKET RESEARCH AND TECHNICAL DIALOGUE: The dialogue of this request for information / notice surveys the market and obtains information regarding the procurement. The contracting authority does not initiate a competitive tendering procedure by publishing the request for information, but a possible procurement notice and call for tenders will be published later. The request for information does not oblige the contracting authority to carry out the actual procurement. Responding to the request for information is not a prerequisite for participation in a subsequent procurement that may be organized. Suppliers are not paid compensation for responding to the request for information or participating in the market dialogue. The responses given to this request for information will be used in planning the procurement of a radar-based remote sensing system and related services. The scope of the procurement may include, for example: 1. Radars to be installed in the care facilities of HUS and the City of Helsinki and an artificial intelligence solution utilizing these for detecting patient falls and monitoring condition. 2. Development work to develop new necessary features. 3. An application installed on a smartphone, to which information about the patient's condition is transmitted. 4. Possible integrations into already existing systems (e.g. nurse call system, AD.). The purpose of the request for information is to survey suppliers on the market and their product and service portfolios. The purpose is to ascertain technical solutions, pricing principles and cost levels for budgeting. We primarily request that a written report on the requested matters be submitted. Based on the responses to the request for information, suppliers may be offered the opportunity to present their solutions in a manner to be announced later. Suppliers that have responded to the request for information may possibly receive preliminary tender documents for comment. HUS-yhtymä and the City of Helsinki request the following information regarding the radar-based remote sensing system: • List of current capabilities and features of the system • Description from the user's perspective: possible functions, limitations, user interfaces for managing the system • Description from the service owner's perspective, management, maintenance, reports, analytics • Radar models suitable for the use of the system, and possible limitations • Average accuracy percentage of the system in detecting falls and other changes in the patient's condition or location, and average delay between the event and detection • Features and hardware requirements of the smartphone application • Implemented and planned integration possibilities • New features planned and under development • Delivery times for new orders • Warranty and maintenance, and resources available to the supplier • GDPR compliance • Previous references from the care sector • Cooperation and operating model that the supplier sees as appropriate. HUS-yhtymä and the City of Helsinki request the following price information for budgeting: • What the system's invoicing of the customer is based on and an example of pricing • Description of the pricing structure of the required software licences (licence policy) We kindly ask you to send your response to the request for information by 6.3.2026 at 12.00 by email to the address kilpailutus.ict@hus.fi. Mention "HUS Tutkapohjainen etäseuranta" as the subject of the message.

sig_48ec3dda190e795f6681.description: The "Strengthening environmental and social governance in the extractive sector" component, co-financed by FONAREDD from CAFI (Central Africa Forest Initiative) resources and BMZ, will be implemented by GIZ for the Ministry of the Environment and Sustainable Development (MEDD) of the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC). The project is being carried out by the Integrated Economic Development of the Mining Sector Project (DISM II), in partnership with the Congolese Environment Agency (ACE), which is responsible for environmental and social assessments and for monitoring and controlling the implementation of ESMPs at national level. Following a 1st Strategic Environmental and Social Study of the mining sector in the DRC in 2010, and in view of the changing international context, it is planned, in agreement with the donor and partners, to launch Strategic Environmental and Social Studies (SESES) for the key sector of mining and hydrocarbons, in order to analyse the expected positive and negative impacts of their development at national level. This work will make it possible to identify good and bad practices in the provinces affected; and in partnership with the various partners and civil society, to propose recommendations integrating REDD+ standards into the extractive sectors. Finally, best practice guides will also be drawn up, based on the experience gained with dialogue platforms in the extractive sector. Adaptations of the various texts relating to the legal and regulatory provisions linked to the environmental and social governance of the extractive sectors will also be proposed in order to be consistent with REDD+ standards and the principles of the Extractive Industries Transparency Initiative (EITI). Lot LOT-0001: 10007377-Strategic Environmental and Social Assessment (SESA) of the oil and gas sector to be carried out in the DRC. An open international call for a tender is published for services to be provided for 12 months, requiring a total of 5 experts, including 2 experts with international experience, respectively head of mission and deputy head of mission, with skills in the environment, strategic studies, and knowledge of the hydrocarbon sector. The team will be backed up on site by 3 experts with national experience with skills in social responsibility and oil and gas sector law and public policy. The services to be provided under this contract include measures for human capacity development and organisational and strategy advice in the following thematic areas: 1. Identifying and increasing attention to potential environmental and social risks, direct and indirect impacts and concerns around the development of the oil and gas sector; 2. Identifying and strengthening environmental and social management approaches and practical tools for the Government to manage sectoral environmental and social governance 3. Identifying and strengthening instruments and approaches that can improve environmental and social accountability, including by increasing the transparency of processes in the oil and gas sector and establishing simple, safe and accessible feedback and/or complaint mechanisms. 4. Support strengthening actors" capacity relevant for the sector to manage environmental and social risks related to the development of the oil and gas sector according to the mitigation hierarchy (avoid, minimise, mitigate and offset). The Contractor is responsible for the performance of the services and the production of the following outputs: 1) Strategic environmental and social assessment (SESA) of the oil and gas sector in the DRC. 2) SWOT analysis and recommendations for the oil and gas sector. 3) Socio-environmental management standards for the DRC. 4) Guide to good environmental and social practices for the DRC 5) Draft implementing legislation for the DRC.
sig_48ec3dda190e795f6681.title: 10007377-Strategic Environmental and Social Assessment (SESA) of the oil and gas sector to be carried out in the DRC

sig_48f22d7bbaabae436448.description: Scotland has the highest drug and alcohol related death rates in the UK and Europe. People with substance use issues (PWSUI) often need help outside normal 'office' hours or from a distance from offices, and support is not uniformly available throughout Scotland. The support landscape in Scotland is fragmented, hard to navigate, and varies by locality. When support isn’t readily available (or isn’t trusted), people and their families and friends often default to emergency services or remain unsupported. As a result, those who use substances often experience avoidable crisis escalation, or remain in extremely difficult situations, and support services miss opportunities for early, harm-reducing interventions. The Preventing Harm, Promoting Recovery: Scotland’s Alcohol & Drugs Strategic Plan 2026 – 2035 specifically addresses the crucial need to tackle early intervention and widen an individual’s ‘circle of support’. This ‘circle of support’ is at the heart of this Challenge, and a successful solution would enable people to access the right support sooner, regardless of locality. It should harness the power of existing trusted services, family and community to reduce avoidable demand on emergency and NHS services – and if possible, create a ‘feedback loop’ of learning, intelligence and insight so that the overall issue can be tackled in a continually improving manner.
sig_48f22d7bbaabae436448.title: CivTech 12.1 - How can digital technologies assist people living with substance use issues (and their families/friends) to easily connect with trusted help and substance use support when services are unavailable?

sig_48f32dddb54d3d920708.description: ERP system in healthcare, the subject of the procurement is the acquisition, introduction, migration, integration, and commissioning of a new, integrated ERP solution to completely replace the client's existing commercial and logistics-related system landscape. The scope of services includes, alongside the provision of the software, the design, implementation, data migration, integration, commissioning, and support for testing and going live with the new solution. The existing system landscape is to be replaced taking into consideration operations that are as uninterrupted as possible. A further component of the contract is the provision and implementation of the required interfaces to the legacy systems that remain in use. This includes in particular the connection to the SAP IS-H patient billing system as well as integration with i.s.h.med to support material, medication, and implant documentation. All interfaces must be provided in such a way as to ensure seamless, secure, and consistent data exchange between the systems. There are no individual licences at the user or terminal workstation level. A quantity-independent licence (so-called campus licence) is required. The scope of services further includes the delivery and assignment of the required software licences or usage rights, setup and parameterisation, data migration from legacy systems, connection of legacy systems, training and documentation, as well as subsequent software maintenance and support. The contractual basis for the supplies and services to be provided will be an EVB-IT framework agreement, which consists in particular of elements of the EVB-IT System, the EVB-IT Assignment Agreement Type A, the EVB-IT Cloud Contract, and the EVB-IT Maintenance S Contract, each with the corresponding EVB-IT general terms and conditions

sig_492da5f8ba39144d025c.description: THIS IS NOT A PROCUREMENT NOTICE OR A CALL FOR TENDERS, BUT A REQUEST FOR INFORMATION FOR MARKET RESEARCH AND TECHNICAL DIALOGUE. This request for information is used to survey the market and obtain information regarding the procurement. The contracting authority is not initiating a tendering procedure with the publication of the request for information; instead, any potential procurement notice and call for tenders will be published later. The request for information does not oblige the contracting authority to carry out the actual procurement. Responding to the request for information is not a precondition for participation in any subsequent tendering procedure that may be organised. Suppliers will not be paid compensation for responding to the request for information or for participating in the market dialogue. The responses provided to this request for information will be used in planning the procurement of a personnel planning system. The subject of the procurement is a personnel planning system which: - supports strategic personnel planning and takes into account the qualitative (incl. staff competency structure) and quantitative planning of personnel required for organising service operations - enables the planning of personnel resources at the supervisory level - operates in accordance with processes defined by labour legislation (takes into account the starts, changes, terminations, etc., of employment relationships) - takes into account that the volume of personnel resources is guided by the level of service operations (increases / decreases / remains the same), care intensity and the budget, rather than a static, administrative vacancy system - can be integrated into HUS's other systems - scales to HUS's current personnel and organisational structure and its potential future changes - is a ready-made overall solution / service package. Personnel planning has a close connection to financial planning / the planning system (personnel costs). BACKGROUND TO THE PROCUREMENT Personnel planning is based on HUS's strategy and objectives. Personnel planning is carried out in both the short and long term. Strategic personnel planning is the organisation's long-term personnel planning. It can be used to anticipate changes in the operating environment and evaluate cost impacts. Personnel planning supports the organisation in achieving its objectives by ensuring access to the right capabilities, in the right place and at the right time. The objectives of planning are: - To identify the required number and structure of personnel as well as competence - To define the measures needed to ensure the personnel in accordance with the objective. These may include: • structural solutions related to the organisation of work and divisions of labour • development of personnel competence • renewal of processes • utilisation of digitalisation / new technologies The purpose of the request for information is to survey suppliers on the market and their product and service ranges. The purpose is to ascertain technical solutions, pricing principles and the cost level for the budget. HUS-yhtymä requests your written comments in particular on the following questions: - What kind of system / service package are you offering (description of implementation) and with what functionalities does the solution meet the needs of the contracting authority described in this request for information? - What are the integration possibilities of the solution you are offering? - What is the pricing model of the solution you are offering (e.g. licences, maintenance and support)? - Is the system / service package you are offering in use in other similar organisations (wellbeing services counties, health and social services operators)? Please note that all material is intended solely for conducting this market dialogue. The contracting authority will process your responses confidentially. Based on the responses to the request for information, suppliers may be offered an opportunity to present their solutions in a manner to be announced later. Suppliers that have responded to the request for information may be given preliminary call for tenders documents for comment. We kindly ask you to submit your responses to the request for information and notify us of your interest no later than 11.12.2025 by 12:00 to the address kilpailutus.ict@hus.fi. The subject line of the message must state "HUS 495-2025 - Request for information: Personnel planning system".
sig_492da5f8ba39144d025c.title: Request for Information: Human Resources Planning System

sig_49677a748a77a2a2c212.description: Maintenance, support and management of CEFTA cloud infrastructure, hosting, managed services, security and business continuity. The contract will cover the end-to-end operation, administration, monitoring, maintenance, security, backup, disaster recovery, business continuity, and optimisation of CEFTA’s cloud-hosted infrastructure and related ICT services. This includes Microsoft Azure, Oracle Cloud Infrastructure (OCI), Oracle databases, WebLogic middleware components, cloud and software licences, security platforms and tools, hosting environments, and associated support arrangements. The services will ensure the stable, secure, resilient, and continuous operation of CEFTA digital systems and applications, including Customs SEED+, CEFTA TRACES NT, and other related platforms and services. The contractor shall ensure the availability, confidentiality, integrity, and resilience of CEFTA’s infrastructure, systems, applications, and data, in line with industry best practices and applicable security, compliance, and governance requirements. The scope includes infrastructure and platform administration, performance monitoring and tuning, capacity planning, availability management, patch and configuration management, incident, problem, change and release management, and service request fulfilment. The contractor shall provide a combination of proactive and reactive operational support. Proactive services will include continuous monitoring, preventive maintenance, performance and capacity management, security assessments, vulnerability management, patching, security hardening, resilience improvements, cost optimisation, compliance support, and recommendations for continuous service enhancement. Reactive services will include incident response, troubleshooting, service restoration, problem resolution, emergency remediation activities, security incident handling, and support for unplanned events affecting the availability, performance, integrity, or security of CEFTA systems and services. The contract will also include security monitoring, threat detection, cybersecurity risk assessments, vulnerability remediation, backup management, disaster recovery planning and testing, business continuity planning and validation, data protection measures, recovery readiness activities, cloud cost management, infrastructure lifecycle management, operational reporting, service-level performance tracking, documentation maintenance, knowledge transfer, and technical and architectural advisory services, ensuring alignment with CEFTA’s operational, security, and strategic business objectives while maintaining the confidentiality, integrity, availability, and recoverability of CEFTA information assets and digital services. Maintenance, support and management of CEFTA cloud infrastructure, hosting, managed services, security and business continuity. The contract will cover the operation, monitoring, security, backup, continuity and optimisation of CEFTA’s cloud-hosted infrastructure and related ICT services, including Microsoft Azure, Oracle Cloud Infrastructure, Oracle databases, WebLogic components, licences, security tools and related hosting and support arrangements. The services will support the stable, secure and continuous operation of CEFTA digital systems and applications, including Customs SEED+, CEFTA TRACES NT and related platforms, as well as incident and change management, security monitoring, vulnerability management, cybersecurity assessment and remediation, disaster recovery, business continuity, cost optimisation, technical advisory support and reporting.
sig_49677a748a77a2a2c212.title: CEFTA Cloud Infrastructure, Hosting, Managed Services, Security and Business Continuity

sig_49699bf79cfa029bec3b.description: West Northamptonshire Council (WNC) is a relatively new Local Authority that has inherited a wide range of electronic document systems and storage methods from predecessor councils. These legacy solutions vary in functionality, levels of automation, and overall maturity, which often results in manual processes to meet compliance, retention, and operational needs. Key services such as Housing, Revenues & Benefits, Regulatory Services, the post room and Pensions and Payroll rely heavily on electronic document and records management to process and store critical information from residents, businesses, and other stakeholders. The Council uses several inherited systems for records management, each supporting different service areas. Additionally, WNC have an archive and heritage service that require archiving for long-term retention of digital materials. The project will consider opportunities to bring these capabilities together into a more consistent and modern corporate approach; in some cases, for archive data only.
sig_49699bf79cfa029bec3b.title: Electronic Document Record Management System

sig_4a270e1f30b203ded6d0.description: Framework Agreement for the Call-Off Provision of Associate Trainers: Digital Skills, Management Skills, Marketing including digital marketing and social media, Communication and Soft Skills, Health and Safety, Construction and Trade, Training and Assessment, Care, Mindfulness and Wellbeing, HR Training, Procurement, Tendering and bid writing, Accountancy systems, Visual Merchandising, Customer Service and Retail Optimisation Lot 1: Digital Skills. Digital skills, Artificial intelligence (AI) and automation skills, data literacy and data management, digital transformation and innovation capability, cybersecurity skills, digital marketing and e-commerce. With the acceleration of digital, the following are also subject areas that are in high demand: Digital skills focus on strong digital communication and collaboration abilities alongside cloud and productivity fundamentals. Artificial intelligence (AI) and automation skills centre on understanding foundational and responsible AI principles as well as applying process automation tools. Data literacy and data management priorities include the ability to interpret and visualise data effectively and uphold good data governance and ethics. Digital transformation and innovation capability requires skills in digital strategy and change leadership, paired with service design and user centred design approaches. Cybersecurity skills focus on building strong cyber hygiene and user awareness, supported by basic risk management and incident response knowledge. Digital marketing and e commerce emphasise SEO and analytics, combined with content creation and digital advertising to drive engagement and growth. Accredited and non-accredited opportunities ranging from SCQF5 and above requested. Training in widely used, industry standard digital tools- such as Microsoft Teams, OneNote for collaborative working, and digital bookkeeping platforms - is also in high demand. Lot 2: Management Skills. Strategic leadership & future planning, workforce development & talent management, change management and digital adoption, people, leadership & wellbeing management, operational & performance management. Businesses require managers who can demonstrate strong strategic leadership and future planning, workforce development and talent management, change management and digital adoption, people focused leadership and wellbeing management, and effective operational and performance management. Building these capabilities ensures leaders can respond to rapid technological change, manage skills gaps, and support resilient, high performing teams. Training should develop practical management capabilities including project management, change management, managing through crisis situations, supervising hybrid or home based teams, leading and motivating others, and building strong supervisory skills. Programmes should also strengthen interpersonal and developmental capabilities such as assertiveness, change and recovery management, coaching skills, developing individuals, and Insights Discovery profiling to support self awareness and team effectiveness. These subject areas are designed for new supervisors, emerging managers, and those seeking to upskill for career progression. Both accredited and non accredited options should be available. Non accredited workshops can be delivered as half day or full day sessions and should be contextualised to the specific needs of the business, particularly for bespoke contracts or sector specific requirements. Lot 3: Marketing. Businesses require marketing training across a wide range of evolving subject areas, including AI enhanced marketing skills, agile and adaptive marketing capability, data driven marketing and analytics, search engine optimisation SEO, content strategy and digital advertising, customer engagement and trust building, omnichannel and customer experience design, and advanced digital platforms and mobile first technologies. Alongside these, there is growing demand for brand creation and management, communications and PR, marketing strategy development, crisis communications, and video production, as well as understanding the difference between amplification and publication as businesses seek growth, explore new markets, or reposition for new audiences. Practical creative skills such as graphic design — particularly 2D/3D animation and Photoshop/Illustrator upskilling to enhance in house capability and deliver more impactful digital content. Digital marketing and social media skills are increasingly essential, enabling businesses to build visibility, engage target audiences, and compete effectively across fast moving online platforms. Lot 4: Communication and Soft Skills. Communication & interpersonal skills, teamwork and collaboration, adaptability & resilience, emotional intelligence & people skills, leadership & soft aligned skills, customer focused skills. Strong communication and soft skill capabilities to help teams adapt to rapid technological, economic and workforce change, clear and confident workplace communication, active listening, teamwork, collaboration, resilience, adaptability and emotional intelligence, as well as core interpersonal skills such as delivering effective presentations, problem solving, assertiveness and customer service communication. Training to mitigate the widening internal skills gaps and meet the growing importance of adaptability, creativity and strong communication. Seeking non accredited, introductory to intermediate level training, typically delivered in half day or full day formats, allowing staff to quickly upskill in essential, business ready soft skills that support productivity and workforce effectiveness. Lot 5: Health and Safety. Practical, compliance focused health and safety training that ensures staff are competent, up to date and able to manage modern workplace risks. Address gaps in documentation, risk assessments and ongoing training. COSHH Awareness, Human Factors in Health and Safety, IOSH Managing Safely, IOSH Working Safely, IOSH SHECW, NEBOSH qualifications, and broader Occupational Health and Safety training, support with legal duties around safe working environments. Fire risk awareness, mental health and wellbeing, and maintaining workforce competency through regular refresher learning. Alongside accredited options, non accredited, short format courses to provide flexible, cost effective, introductory or refresher training tailored to SME’s operational needs. Lot 6: Construction and Trades. Essential electrical safety and compliance training, including the City & Guilds 18th Edition Electrical Wiring Regulations (full qualification and industry update) and PAT Testing and Inspection & Testing Upskilling for renewable energy systems, EV charging installation, battery storage safety, Lock Out–Tag Out (LOTO) procedures and electrical diagnostics. Ensuring staff remain competent, compliant and able to work safely with modern technologies. These may be delivered through accredited qualifications or short, non accredited practical courses to support flexible, cost effective workforce development. Lot 7: Training and Assessing. Workforce development training that strengthens internal capability, particularly through Assessor and Verifier qualifications, Coaching and Mentoring, and Train the Trainer programmes, enabling businesses to build in house expertise, support staff progression and maintain quality assurance across learning and development activities. Delivered as accredited or non accredited options, offering flexible, cost effective pathways that allow organisations to choose between formal qualification routes or shorter, practical sessions tailored to operational needs. Lot 8: Care, Mindfulness and Wellbeing. Safeguarding, Child Protection and Adult Protection training to ensure staff can recognise, respond to and escalate concerns in line with current legislation and best practice. Autism training, including delivery aligned to D&A certificated programmes and SQA certificated courses, supporting organisations to work confidently and inclusively with neurodiverse individuals. Trauma Informed Practice, Mental Health First Aid, Equality, Diversity & Inclusion (EDI) awareness, De escalation and Behaviour Support, and Professional Boundaries & Safer Working Practices, reflecting an increased emphasis on safe, ethical and inclusive service delivery. All programmes can be offered as accredited or non accredited options, providing flexible, practical learning tailored to organisational and sector requirements. Lot 9: HR Training, Procurement, Tendering and Bid Writing. HR training to strengthens effective people management, support compliance and improve workplace capability. HR focused training in areas such as employment practice, performance management and fair work aligned people processes. Procurement training to help understand and navigate Scotland’s public procurement system, the Scottish Government’s SME and Third Sector Procurement Action Plan (2024–2026), improve supplier readiness and expand SME participation in public contracts. Training for procurement rules, compliance expectations, sustainable procurement requirements and effective use of Public Contracts Scotland. Tendering and bid writing: practical support to build confidence and competence in preparing competitive bids. Training to facilitate understanding of evaluation criteria and improved tender preparation directly and to win contracts. Training in tender structure, evidence development and persuasive, compliant bid writing. Lot 10: Accountancy Systems. Cloud accounting training, including tools to report major internal and external cost savings while simplifying invoicing, reconciliation and reporting. Software including but not limited to: Xero, QuickBooks Online, Sage Business Cloud. Training for real time reporting & dashboard use, automated reconciliation & digital invoicing, integration of cloud accounting with payroll, inventory & CRM. Automation & Digital Bookkeeping Skills, including AI assisted bookkeeping & categorisation, Automated VAT and payroll workflows Cybersecurity in Financial Systems, including secure logins & multi factor authentication, data backup & GDPR compliant data handling, fraud prevention & financial system risk awareness Digital Taxation & Compliance, including making Tax Digital (MTD) for VAT & self assessment, digital record keeping, submission of returns via cloud platforms. Data Driven Finance & Business Partnering Skills, including training for financial dashboards & data visualisation, forecasting & scenario modelling, KPI development & management reporting, business partnering & commercial analysis. Lot 11: Visual Merchandising, Customer Service and Retail Optimisation. Creative and strategic visual merchandising, high quality customer service and communication and operational retail skills for efficient and profitable store management Visual Merchandising Skills including window display design & in store presentation - creating eye catching, brand aligned displays, store layout planning & product placement - designing customer flow, optimising lighting, and using fixtures effectively to guide purchasing decisions. Understanding customer behaviour & retail psychology. Customer Service Skills for retail, including high quality customer interaction skills- effective communication, problem solving, and managing queries or complaints. Service excellence & personalisation- delivering tailored shopping experiences, a key differentiator in modern retail. Retail Optimisation Skills to improve store performance and operational efficiency, including retail operations management- record keeping, staffing, stock control and security procedures. Maximising retail profitability, including evaluating sales data, identifying improvement opportunities, and applying merchandising strategies. Marketing products effectively - basic retail marketing skills to support promotions, product visibility and brand positioning.

The assignments tendered through this DPS may include, for example: • expert advice and support to EDUFI and to developing country ministries and organizations in development of education, • conducting analytical studies, reviews and evaluations • drafting and updating policy guidelines and other documentation, • designing and supporting the developing of action/project plans, • organizing and delivering training and capacity building sessions. Below is a list of the major work that included in the DPS, but not limited to: • externally funded projects of the Finnish National Agency for Education, such as Team Europe Initiatives - The Regional Teachers Initiative for Africa (RTIA) which supports teacher education and teacher professional development in Sub-Saharan Africa, including providing Technical Assistance to ministries of education. - Opportunity-Driven Skills and Vocational Education and Training in Africa (TEI OP-VET) which provides targeted support to (re)orient existing or planned sector-specific skills and VET interventions in partner countries across Sub-Saharan Africa, including Technical Assistance. • and other similar work of the Finnish National Agency for Education The scope and subject-matter of the DPS is described in more detail particularly in annex 1 "Subject-matter of the DPS". sig_4a319478693abcf3c4d0.description: The subject of the procurement is the management of the public energy advisory office of the RKBM from 01.01.2028 to 31.12.2031. The Bern-Mittelland public energy advisory service runs the independent energy advisory office (EBS) on behalf of the Canton of Bern. The aim of the energy advisory service is to promote an efficient, economical, cost-effective and environmentally friendly energy supply and use. The energy advisory service covers all topics relating to the construction and operation of properties, such as energy-efficient construction and renovation, selection of the correct heating system, reduction of energy demand (lighting, hot water, etc.), conversion to alternative energy sources, etc. Depending on the request, advice is provided by telephone or email, at the RKBM location in Bern as well as in one or two decentralised municipalities within the perimeter of the RKBM or directly at the customer's premises.

sig_4a6474b58e4b8521487b.description: RTE, the public electricity transmission system operator, is launching a multi-supplier framework agreement for intellectual services providing operational support for infrastructure construction and modification projects (overhead and underground lines, substations): project management support and technical support for projects, and operational management of national programmes. Main characteristics: – Multi-supplier framework agreement implemented through subsequent contracts with systematic competitive tendering among the holders of the relevant lot. – Maximum duration of six years, namely a firm period of three years (36 months) followed by three optional periods of twelve months. Planned commencement of services envisaged for 1 September 2027. – Estimated forecast volume: 254 million euros excluding VAT over the total duration (Lot 1 : 126 million euros; Lot 2 : 128 million euros). – Profiles deployed: engineers (junior, experienced, expert) and experienced technicians specialised in complex infrastructure construction projects. This support for RTE’s Project teams applies to all or part of the rollout phases of infrastructure projects: So-called "decision-making" phase: Design and phasing technical studies, scheduling, risk analysis, cost estimation, Detailed Preliminary Design Purchasing phases: Technical and Administrative Clause Document (CCTP), consultations, tender analysis, order preparation and monitoring Works phases: Support for works monitoring Project monitoring: Support for preparation of reviews (technical, budget and schedule monitoring) Asset checks: checking and updating of RTE databases (data, plans, etc.) We invite you to participate in the presentation webinar - Project Owner Assistance contracts for Project Operational Support (AOP) and Authorisation Consultation Support (AAC) on Monday 7 September 2026 09:00-10:30 https://teams.microsoft.com/meet/341814531863472?p=6bCsYkiiCs1nbv6qud Intellectual services providing operational support to RTE project teams for the construction and modification of the public electricity transmission network infrastructure (overhead lines, underground connections, substations): project management support (preparation and monitoring of schedules, dashboards, budgetary and contractual monitoring, preparation of bodies, interface coordination) and technical support (production and verification of technical deliverables during study and works phases, analyses, consultations and monitoring of works contracts, site monitoring). The lot is broken down into 7 regional sub-lots, each attached to a RTE regional centre: sub-lot 1 Nancy, sub-lot 2 Lille, sub-lot 3 Paris, sub-lot 4 Nantes, sub-lot 5 Lyon, sub-lot 6 Marseille, sub-lot 7 Toulouse. A carte of the geographical perimeters is appended to this notice. Candidates may apply for one, several or all of the sub-lots. It is planned to select 4 awardees per sub-lot, subject to the admissibility of tenders. The framework agreement is implemented through subsequent contracts. The services utilise engineer profiles (junior, experienced, expert) with a mission located at RTE sites within the regional perimeter at a rate of two days per week minimum and/or in accordance with the CCTP of the mission. Estimated volume over 6 years Sub-lot 1 - Nancy - 14 million euros excluding VAT Sub-lot 2 - Lille - 12 million euros excluding VAT Sub-lot 3 - Paris - 30 million euros excluding VAT Sub-lot 4 - Nantes - 22 million euros excluding VAT Sub-lot 5 - Lyon - 10 million euros excluding VAT Sub-lot 6 - Marseille - 16 million euros excluding VAT Sub-lot 7 - Toulouse - 22 million euros excluding VAT Total - 126 million euros excluding VAT; Intellectual services for the operational management of RTE national programmes: management and coordination of projects carried out in series across the entire territory (for example, renewal programmes or installation of equipment deployed in several regions), supervision of works and production of management deliverables and associated technical deliverables. The mission includes in particular the structuring and monitoring of the progress of operations, the coordination of internal and external stakeholders, the supervision of execution during study and works phases, and consolidated reporting. Single national lot: It is planned to select 5 awardees, subject to the admissibility of tenders. The framework agreement is implemented through subsequent contracts. The services mainly utilise engineer profiles experienced in managing complex infrastructure projects and require a national organisation with regional relays allowing for flexibility in connection with programmes concerning several RTE sites or a gradual rollout across all or some RTE sites.

sig_4a884ec3ae603cdea1bd.description: Sources Sought / Request for Information (RFI) Control Head Unit (CHU) The Army Contracting Command – Aberdeen Proving Ground (ACC-APG), on behalf of the Capability Program Executive – Aviation (CPE AVN) and the Project Manager, Aviation Mission Systems and Architecture (PM AMSA), is conducting market research to identify qualified sources capable of delivering a high Technology Readiness Level (TRL) and Manufacturing Readiness Level (MRL) Control Head Unit (CHU). This critical hardware effort supports the immediate fielding of the Air to Ground Communications (A2GC) system—the Army’s next-generation, federated replacement for the legacy SINCGARS system. To bypass traditional, multi-year aircraft integration timelines and meet emerging Next Generation Command and Control (NGC2) requirements, PM AMSA is seeking an intelligent, airworthy, modular open-systems-compliant controller capable of hosting multiple software applications, enabling rapid, iterative evolutionary capability updates directly to the warfighter. Classification Original Set Aside: N/A Product Service Code: 6610 – Flight Instruments NAICS Codes: 334511 - Search, Detection, Navigation, Guidance, Aeronautical, and Nautical System and Instrument Manufacturing; 541330 – Engineering Services Place of Performance: Army Contracting Command – Aberdeen Proving Ground 6590 Reconnaissance Street, Building 6010 APG, MD 21005 Description Notice This Sources Sought is issued for informational purposes and market research only, it does not constitute a solicitation. The Government will not reimburse any company or individual for expenses associated with preparing/submitting information in response to this posting. The information provided may be used by the Government in developing its acquisition strategy, statement of work/statement of objectives, and performance specifications. Interested parties are responsible for adequately marking proprietary or competition sensitive information contained within their response. 1.2.Scope The United States Government (USG) Capability Program Executive – Aviation (CPE AVN), Project Manager, Aviation Mission Systems and Architecture (PM AMSA) is conducting market research to identify possible sources capable of providing Control Head Unit (CHU) to control the Air to Ground Communications(A2GC) system. The USG is interested in information regarding control head system hardware, real-time operating systems, and software at a high Technology Readiness Level (TRL) and Manufacturing Readiness Level (MRL), with environmental qualification that support Air-Worthiness Release (AWR) as specified in Section 3.3(C). 2.1. Background The A2GC system is the Army’s replacement for the legacy SINCGARS system. Unlike its predecessor, this system will be federated from aircraft systems, thus it will need a CHU of its own. To field critical communications capabilities immediately, we must bypass traditional, slower system integration timelines in favor of rapid, iterative evolutionary updates. Emerging waveforms requirements and nascent Next Generation Command and Control (NGC2) Army requirements are driving inclusion of additional onboard computational capabilities and available interfaces. Multiple software defined radios require use of an intelligent control head capable of hosting multiple software applications to support Design Assurance Level (DAL) and non-DAL applications. 2.2 Instructions to Potential Respondents Respondents to this RFI must submit evidence which demonstrates their current ability to manufacture and sustain a control head unit if it has been demonstrated. Respondents are asked to submit documents in easily readable pdf formats not to exceed 5 pages. 3. Requested Information 3.1 Company Information Company Name Address Point of Contact (include phone number and email address) CAGE Code UEI Web Page URL State the country of ownership for the company State whether the company is a non-traditional defense contractor Please identify your company's size standard per the primary NAICS code of 334511- Search, Detection, Navigation, Guidance, Aeronautical and Nautical System and Instrument Manufacturing. The Small Business Size Standard for this NAICS code is 1,350 employees. For more information on small business, refer to: https://www.sba.gov/document/support--table-size-standards If your company is a small business, indicate whether any of the small business categories below apply: 8(a): Small Disadvantaged Business (DB): Woman-Owned Small Business: Historically Underutilized Business Zone (HUBZone): Veteran-Owned Small Business: Service-Disable Veteran-Owned Small Business: If you identify your company as a SB or any of the SB subcategories as stipulated in section j, is your company intending to submit a proposal as a prime contractor? Is your company capable of performing at least 51% of the work? If so, please explain how your company will perform the work within the parameters of the Ostensible Subcontractor Affiliation rule. Does your company possess the capabilities to provide the entire range of products and services discussed in this RFI? If NO, please provide specific capabilities that you intend to provide? 3.2 Capabilities The USG is particularly interested in the physical characteristics and performance capabilities including: Describe the configuration of your proposed solution. Include: Operational startup time Number and type of connectors (e.g., data/audio I/O, control, discrete, antenna, key fill, Ethernet, MIL-STD-1553, serial, RF). For consideration, respondents must include RS-485/422/232 serial control, full duplex 1553, and Ethernet Chipset and computational resources (RAM, ROM, GPU, etc.) Total weight and dimensions of proposed solution Display – 4.3 inches (minimum diagonal) Desired Dimensions Width - 5.75 inches Height - 3.35 inches Depth - Not to exceed 3.9 inches (DZUS rail to connector opening) Any mounting hardware required (e.g., shock isolators, cooling plates, DZUS rails) For consideration, solution must be compatible with DZUS rail mounting Maximum and nominal input power requirements of your proposed solution. Include voltage and current. For consideration, nominal power should not exceed - 14W (0.5 A @ 28VDC) Cooling method(s) used on proposed solution Supply chain considerations (e.g., countries of origin, obsolescence) Operating System options (e.g. Linux, VxWorks, Deos, etc.) Describe any non-standard (non-conformant) material used in the proposed solution Provide the Mean Time Between Failure (MTBF) of your proposed solution and describe how the MTBF was determined. Note that the Army considers MIL-HDBK-217F an unacceptable source for reliability estimates. Describe how the system architecture of the proposed solution would operate functionally and physically in DoD Modular Open System Approach (MOSA). Describe any experience with the Hardware Open Systems Technologies (HOST) Technical Standard and how the standard can be applied to the controller solution Describe how the solution can be deployed Describe any past experience with similar Department of Defense (DoD) implementations and lessons learned from past experiences Describe knowledge and experience in product line engineering (PLE) Describe how the developed solution would achieve Cyber Security Compliance IAW AR 25-2. Describe the data rights, licensing structures, or intellectual property (IP) assertions associated with the proposed solution’s external hardware and software interfaces, external drawings, and technical manuals. Consistent with commercial-first preferences (FAR Part 12), please identify if these items are commercial products/services with standard commercial licenses, or if they are offered with Government Purpose Rights (GPR) or Custom/Limited Rights. Compliance with Mandates State the DO-178 design assurance level of the controller operating system and board support package and how it was obtained; if not already DAL C, provide a path to DAL C certification. State the DO-254 compliance and how it was obtained Human Factors IAW MIL-STD-1472H. Include: Sound levels of components such as cooling fan(s) included with your proposed solution. Human factors characteristics of any displays included with your proposed solution. Daylight readability Describe compliance with MIL-STD-3009 for Type 1, Class A, Night Vision Goggles How your proposed solution is designed for maintainability. Prominence of knobs, buttons, and other hardware UI features that enable gloved operations in all required conditions 3.3 Environmental and Electrical Describe the controller’s compliance with the following environmental, electrical, and electromagnetic specifications. Describe the specific method(s) and procedure(s) utilized for test. Describe any specific test criteria (e.g. limits, duration, number of cycles). If not compliant, discuss future plans to gain compliance. Requirements for the Control of Electromagnetic Interference (EMI) Characteristics of subsystems, equipment, all ancillaries for EMI / Radio Frequency Interference (RFI) requirements defined in MIL-STD-461H and MIL-STD-464D, as modified by ADS-37A-PRF, electrostatic discharge, and electrical bonding. Requirements for the Interface Standard for Aircraft Electric Power Characteristics as defined in MIL-STD-704A-F and the performance specification utilized to determine compliance. sig_4a9603b4a5842b828a5b.description: The project concerns the provision of services for the design, implementation and operation of a digital environment and the operational support of the process for transferring assets of interconnected Users of the Hellenic Electricity Transmission System (ESMHE) to the Independent Power Transmission Operator (IPTO), for a period of twenty-four (24) months. In the context of the project's implementation, the Contractor undertakes the integrated design, implementation and operational support of a unified digital environment for managing the cases of transferring fixed assets of interconnected ESMHE Users to IPTO, as well as the parallel operational management, maturation and clearance of the relevant outstanding issues. Specifically, the project includes two distinct but complementary workflows: • firstly, the design, development and commissioning of an integrated digital environment for managing asset transfer cases, which will support the entire lifecycle of asset transfer cases, ensuring structured registration, monitoring of the progress of procedures, traceability and administrative oversight, • secondly, the active operational management and clearance of up to one hundred and fifty (150) outstanding cases of old (already electrified) User connections, through coordinated actions of collection, verification, completion of data, communication with involved parties and provision of specialised opinions. The total estimated value of the contract amounts to the sum of two million, one hundred thousand euros (€2.100.000,00), plus VAT and is broken down as follows: • €1.400.000,00 budget for the subject of the contract, for a period of twenty-four (24) months, for the provision of services for the design, implementation and operation of a digital environment and the operational support of the process for transferring assets of interconnected ESMHE Users to IPTO. The amount of the subject's budget constitutes the maximum offer limit. • Option Rights, with a total estimated value of up to €700.000,00, plus VAT (50% of the budget): A) Extension right: IPTO unilaterally reserves the right to extend the duration of the contract, for up to twelve (12) months, under the same terms and unit prices, with an estimated value of up to 50% of the initial contract value and any increases to the subject that have been applied, i.e. up to a maximum of €700.000,00 euros, plus VAT: - the total duration of the contract with or without a corresponding increase in the physical and financial scope, and/or - the duration of the maintenance and support period for production operation (Phase A.2.5), and/or - the duration of the Workflow B services, beyond the provided twelve (12) months, under the same terms and unit prices, and/or B) Right to increase the contract subject, with a total estimated value of up to 50% of the initial contract value: IPTO reserves, throughout the duration of the contract's execution, the right to increase the physical scope under the same terms and unit prices, for the increase of the services of W.P.1.1 and W.P.1.2, by assigning additional cases beyond the provided one hundred and fifty (150). In the event of exercising the option right for additional cases, the total duration of the contract's execution may be extended accordingly, for a time period to be mutually agreed upon between the parties, in order to ensure the completion of the increase within the new agreed period, which shall not exceed the maximum time limit of the extension right, provided for in the above para. A.

sig_4b3f74a5947c2ee26d6e.description: Statistics Finland invites you to participate in a market dialogue concerning a potential procurement of a data collection tool for survey purposes. The minimum requirements for the solution are presented in Annex 2: List of Requirements. The questions for the dialogue are presented in Annex 3: Response Form. We encourage suppliers interested in the procurement to actively participate and to provide comprehensive and high-quality responses. The objective is to assess whether there are solutions on the market that enable collecting data from individuals and organisations via questionnaires and interviews according to the minimum requirements listed in Annex 2. The questions for the market dialogue are presented in Annex 3: Response Form. Please provide your answers in the designated response fields in the form. Suppliers are requested to address the questions of the market dialogue only by responding to the questions listed in Annex 3: Response Form. Please ensure that you use the response fields provided in the form, as the response column will be transferred as such into the contracting authority’s internal summary table. The completed response form must be submitted to Supplier Portal no later than 6 January 2026.

sig_4c05dfb055e110b6aa7c.description: The purpose of this contract is a specialised technical assistance service intended to support the design, promotion and evaluation of the strategic and operational planning instruments of the Mental Health Commissioner. In particular, the purpose of the contract shall comprise the external evaluation of the current Mental Health Strategy of the National Health System 2022-2026, as well as the technical support necessary for the design and promotion of the new mental health strategy, with a horizon from 2027 onwards, involving all key stakeholders in the institutional sphere, especially the autonomous communities, and in the social sphere. Likewise, the purpose of the contract shall include the evaluation of the Mental Health Action Plan 2025-2027 and of the Action Plan for Suicide Prevention 2025-2027, contemplating both an interim evaluation and a final evaluation, in order to analyse their degree of implementation, results achieved and to guide the improvement of public policies in this area. Said actions shall be developed in accordance with the principles of the community mental health model, incorporating in a cross-cutting manner the human rights approach, the gender perspective, the consideration of the social determinants of health and the integration of mental health into all public policies, and shall take into account the principles and requirements established in Act 27/2022, of 20 December, on the institutionalisation of public policy evaluation in the General State Administration.
sig_4c05dfb055e110b6aa7c.title: Specialised technical assistance service to support the design, promotion and evaluation of the strategic and operational planning instruments of the Mental Health Commissioner

sig_4c47cea478f16d9de663.description: In order to meet its legal obligations (Section 146a of the German Fiscal Code (AO) and the Cash Register Security Ordinance (KassenSichV)), the BSI must update the protection profiles BSI-CC-PP-0104 Cryptographic Service Provider (CSP) and BSI-CC-PP-0111 CSPLight (CSPL). To this end, the aforementioned protection profiles are also to be adapted within the project for broader use in the eID / EUDI wallet, 5G and FIDO / passkeys areas. This also requires the drafting of a standardised interface description for CSPLight products in central data centre operations in order to increase interoperability and minimise dependencies on proprietary architectures. The project is divided into three separate lots (professional lots within the meaning of Section 97 Paragraph 4 of the Act against Restraints of Competition (GWB)): - Lot 1: Adaptation and updating of the CSP protection profile and CSPL protection profile (Update-CSPL) - Lot 2: Evaluation of CSP-PP/CSPL-PP (Eval-CSPL) - Lot 3: Standardised interface description (API-CSPL) Lot 1 comprises the updating and modularisation of the protection profiles PP-CSP and PP-CSPL. Following on from this, in Lot 2, an evaluation of the CSP and CSPL protection profiles is carried out in accordance with EUCC. Finally, in Lot 3, a uniform, standardised interface description for the CSP Light is drawn up on the basis of the protection profile created in Lot 1. Details can be found in the specifications (see attachments). Lot LOT-0001: Lot 1: "Adaptation and updating of the CSP protection profile and CSPL protection profile (Update-CSPL)". The objective in Lot 1 is the adaptation and updating of the protection profiles PP-CSP and PP-CSPL. In this context, the two protection profiles are to be merged while pursuing the multi-assurance approach. The new protection profile is to be designed modularly so that it is possible to serve various application purposes and enable broad application. The core of the PP is to be restricted to the minimum necessary functionality of the CSP(L). All functionalities that are only required for specific purposes are to be outsourced to modules. Dedicated PP configurations are to be drawn up for the individual application scenarios mentioned above, which can in each case contain suitable combinations of functional modules. In this lot, a draft concept is first drawn up together with the contracting authority, then the detailed architecture is to be described, and in a further work package the focus lies on the actual creation of the PP. The objective of the lot is an updated and modularised protection profile as well as at least one corresponding PP configuration for the cash registers and eID use case. Lot LOT-0002: Lot 2: "Evaluation of CSP-PP/CSPL-PP (Eval-CSPL)". The subject of the contract in Lot 2 is the evaluation of the protection profile created in Lot 1. The result of Lot 2 consists of complete individual inspection reports, so that the available reports can be submitted for certification of the protection profile and its configuration and all formal requirements are met. Lot LOT-0003: Lot 3: "Standardised interface description (API-CSPL)". The objective in Lot 3 is the creation of a uniform, standardised interface description for the CSP, so as to enable manufacturer-independent use of a CSP on a secure server architecture for external applications. The basis for the interface description shall be the updated and modularised protection profiles, or the merged protection profile from Lot 1, as well as the current BSI TR-CSP2.
sig_4c47cea478f16d9de663.title: Project 1025 "CSP Update, Evaluation, Recertification and API (CUERA)"
