sig_4cfea7ef85d8ad403f01.description: Sanctuary Group is undertaking Preliminary Market Engagement (PME) with prospective suppliers and other interested organisations operating within the technology services market. This is a broad, multi-service opportunity across an enterprise technology estate currently estimated at approximately 265-300 applications, spanning SAP, Salesforce, Microsoft platforms and other enterprise technologies and supporting both operational and transformational technology services. Sanctuary Group's Technology Directorate has undergone significant change across its operating model and technology estate. Sanctuary Group is therefore assessing sourcing arrangements for technology services that support the delivery, development, transformation and ongoing operation of the estate in 2027. This engagement gives participating organisations an opportunity to contribute market insight and inform potential service groupings, sourcing approaches and procurement considerations before final decisions are made. The purpose of this engagement is to: • Provide an overview of Sanctuary Group, its technology landscape and strategic objectives. • Obtain market feedback on potential service groupings and sourcing approaches. • Understand supplier capability, capacity and appetite. • Explore potential procurement structures, routes to market and commercial models. • Understand mobilisation, transition and service-delivery considerations. • Inform the development of Sanctuary Group's technology procurement strategy. Organisations interested in participating should register with Group Procurement from publication. The supplier questionnaire is intended to be issued with, or shortly after, the notice. A supplier webinar is proposed for early-mid October 2026, with questionnaire responses proposed to close in October 2026. The indicative timetable is set out below. Procurement Objectives Sanctuary Group is considering requirements across a range of technology service areas, including: • Application Managed Services (AMS) • Application Development, Product Management, Project Delivery and Programme Delivery Services • Technology Consultancy & Advisory Services • Data Services (Data Engineering, Data Governance, Data Quality Management, Master Data Management, Data Architecture, Data Modelling, Reporting & Analytics, Data Platforms and Storage Management) • Data Integration & Ingestion Services • Cloud Services & Platform Support • Licensing & Software Asset Management • AI, Innovation & Emerging Technologies These services may apply across a range of technology platforms and business capabilities, including SAP, Salesforce, Microsoft platforms and other enterprise applications. The service areas above are indicative and are intended to support market engagement and feedback. The final service structure, grouping, boundaries, scope, sourcing model and procurement approach have not been determined and will be informed by market feedback, commercial assessment, legal advice and governance decisions. Sanctuary Group is interested in approaches that: • Encourage innovation, continuous improvement and thought leadership. • Support effective competition and system integrations. • Enable participation by SMEs, specialist providers and larger organisations where appropriate. • Provide flexibility and scalability to meet changing requirements. • Support efficient procurement and call-off arrangements. • Deliver demonstrable value for money. • Support both business-as-usual and strategic transformational requirements. • Enable access to specialist skills and capabilities when required. Areas where Market Feedback is Sought Sanctuary Group welcomes feedback on: • Service groupings and lotting structures. • Supplier appetite for individual service areas and combinations of services. • Supplier capability and partnerships across individual and multiple service groupings. • The benefits and risks of platform-specific versus platform-agnostic service models. • Suitable procurement routes, commercial frameworks and contractual arrangements. • Commercial and pricing approaches. • Information required to support supplier participation and commercial engagement. • The most appropriate treatment of Data Services and Integration Services, including whether they are best delivered separately, together, embedded within wider services or through alternative arrangements. • Transition and mobilisation considerations. • Supplier participation barriers and opportunities. • Any aspects of the proposed scope or approach that suppliers believe could be improved. • Approaches that maximise innovation, market participation and long-term value. Engagement Activities Sanctuary Group currently intends to undertake the following engagement activities: Supplier Webinar Interested organisations may be invited to attend a market engagement webinar covering: • Introduction to Sanctuary Group. • Overview of Sanctuary Group's technology environment. • Strategic objectives and priorities. • Potential service areas, sourcing considerations and procurement approaches. • Indicative timelines. • Questions and answers. Supplier Questionnaire Interested organisations may be invited to complete a structured questionnaire seeking feedback on: • Service areas and capabilities. • Supplier appetite. • Service grouping and sourcing approaches. • Procurement and commercial considerations. • Procurement vehicle and route-to-market considerations. • Transition and mobilisation considerations. • Participation barriers. • Innovation opportunities. • Comparable market experience. Supplier Discussions Sanctuary Group may invite organisations to participate in follow-up discussions to further explore market feedback or clarify responses where appropriate. Expressions of Interest Organisations wishing to participate in this engagement should register their interest by contacting Group Procurement at: group.procurement@sanctuary.co.uk Using the subject line: Technology Services PME 2026 When registering interest, organisations should provide: • Organisation name. • Primary contact name. It is the responsibility of the primary contact to forward the invitation to other attendees within their organisation. • Contact email address. • Summary of relevant services and capabilities. • Areas of interest. • Proposed attendees (where applicable). Following registration, Group Procurement will provide further information regarding engagement activities, webinar arrangements, questionnaires and any subsequent supplier discussions. Indicative Timetable PME Notice Publication: 21st September 2026 Supplier Registration From Publication to 9th October 2026 Supplier Questionnaire Issue: Minimum 1 week prior to the Supplier Webinar: Early- mid October 2026 Supplier Discussions: October 2026 Questionnaire Submission Deadline: Late October 2026 Review of Market Feedback: Late October 2026 Procurement Strategy Confirmation: Following review of market feedback and internal advice These dates are indicative only and may be amended. Important Information Sanctuary Group has not reached a final decision regarding: • Procurement structure. • Service groupings. • Lotting arrangements. • Procurement vehicle. • Route to market. • Commercial model. • Contractual arrangements. • Supplier model. • Contract duration. • Estimated value. • Implementation approach. The purpose of this engagement is to obtain market feedback and challenge assumptions before any final decisions are made. Feedback may inform: • Procurement strategy. • Sourcing approach. • Procurement vehicle and route-to-market decisions. • Service structures and groupings. • Qualification and participation considerations. • Procurement and call-off mechanisms. • Commercial arrangements. • Contractual arrangements. • Transition considerations. Participation in this engagement is entirely voluntary and will not form part of any subsequent procurement process. Participation, non-participation, discussions or responses provided during this engagement will not provide any advantage or disadvantage in any subsequent procurement process. Sanctuary Group reserves the right to amend, refine, combine, separate, postpone or discontinue any aspect of the proposed approach following completion of this engagement. Sanctuary Group is not obliged to proceed with any procurement activity and makes no commitment to award any contract as a result of this engagement. To support transparency, consistency of information and equal treatment, organisations should communicate through Group Procurement regarding this engagement. Lot 1: .

sig_4d5284f9043563e34175.description: Ørsted is tendering for a new Vessel Monitoring System (VMS) based service to document the performance of its fleet of Crew Transfer Vessels (CTV’s) operating in wind farms in Europe, Asia and US. 2.2.5 The solution should provide Ørsted with: a) A log of the daily activities of the CTV fleet using onboard logger boxes. Daily activities could be Transit, Dockings with transfers and crane lifts, etc. b) Give the captain access to make comments throughout the shift. c) Video record the transfer area on the vessel while docking and provide access to these re-cordings. d) Analyse the vessel speed, comfort, and dockings. e) Analyse both the transfer quality and the impact on the WTG when the CTVs are docking. f) Collect and analyse engine data. g) Deliver the collected and analysed data to Ørsted daily. h) Provide excellent and fast service and support when needed. i) The Scope of Services will be compromised of Services as well as Goods/Hardware. j) Fast and flexible supply, installation and commissioning to avoid interruption with offshore operations
sig_4d5284f9043563e34175.title: Tender for ​Supply, Delivery, Installation and Operation of a Vessel Monitoring System

sig_4e0f3a5f7e829612a581.description: The Piedmont Region, within the scope of the Electronic Health Record (EHR), manages radiological images through local and regional PACS systems, but the current architecture is fragmented and poorly standardised across the various Healthcare Authorities. This situation generates inefficiencies, difficulties with updates and suboptimal access to images, especially in clinical contexts where timeliness is crucial. Furthermore, viewing functionalities are limited and not fully integrated with regional digital services and telemedicine. To respond to the new requirements of interoperability, continuity of care and telemedicine, it is necessary to evolve towards a federated, scalable and user-centred platform capable of guaranteeing immediate, secure and integrated access to radiological images. With this market sounding, CSI-Piemonte therefore intends to verify the presence on the market of solutions that meet the aforementioned technical-functional and organisational requirements.

sig_4e2be62957b3ffaefa98.description: Puolustusvoimien logistiikkalaitos (hereinafter the contracting authority) invites you to submit a request to participate in the Haapajärvi charging plant production line development project for the Finnish Defence Forces in accordance with this call for requests to participate and its annexes. Subject of the procurement: Planning and development site located in the production area of the Haapajärvi unit of the explosives centre. The main tasks are: The contracting authority wishes to develop the production line using automation and robotics. The aim is simultaneously to minimise the number of personnel. The candidate must state the number of personnel required for the modernised line at the stated capacities. The contracting authority has selected the following objects for automation: Renewal of the existing lower conveyor, including automation of the existing laboratory work (includes thread cleaning and inspection, attaching / installing the intermediate piece, and loading the upper conveyor), automation of the attachment of the existing cavity base and automation of the existing weighing operation. The procurement includes all necessary design work, dismantling of obsolete technology, and delivery and installation of new technology in the explosive premises (IP54 T4) as a turnkey delivery in accordance with the procurement documents. The selected supplier must design all possible operations of the procurement object to be automated and to operate automatically. Likewise, the machines and equipment to be modernised must be designed to function as independent parts of the rest of the existing production equipment. The modernised line must meet the ergonomics requirements and capacity needs with 81 VRTKR, 120 VRTKR and 155 TKR products. There are various versions of these products, and these versions are specified in separately delivered drawings. The main tasks included in the delivery are listed as follows: 1) Production capacity in accordance with requirements and minimisation of the number of personnel 2) Renewal of the existing lower conveyor 3) Automation of the operations of the existing laboratory work (including thread cleaning and inspection, installation of the detonator, attaching / installing the intermediate piece, and loading the upper conveyor) 4) Automation of the operations of the existing cavity base attachment 5) Automation of the existing weighing operation. Items 2 to 5 include design, dismantling of the existing redundant part, and necessary equipment deliveries and installations. The objective is to carry out the procurement (including the design phase) during the years 2026 to 2027, such that the timing of the installation of the new technology would be as follows: Working hours at the site are possible 19.07.2027 to 15.10.2027 (weeks 29 to 41). The delivery must be ready by 15.10.2027. Working on site is permitted during installations around the clock every day of the week, if necessary. Before starting the installations, the selected supplier must carry out all necessary design. The selected supplier must present (in written and oral form) the entire implementation proposal for the procurement (including necessary plans and capacity calculations) to the Customer in good time, i.e. when the necessary plans are, in the supplier's opinion, ready for presentation. The final implementation documentation is included in the delivery scope of the procurement. The contracting parties shall agree on the more precise installation schedule within the aforementioned delivery schedule in accordance with the terms of the procurement contract to be signed after the selection of the supplier. The final acceptance is preceded by trial runs (cold run / hot run), capacity runs, training, delivery of final documentation and official inspections. The new equipment must be fully ready for use and production by 15.10.2027. The contracting authority will send the invitation to tender and its annexes (incl. technical specification) on the basis of this call for requests to participate to the tenderers approved by the contracting authority.
sig_4e2be62957b3ffaefa98.title: Request for participation: HAAPAJÄRVI CHARGING STATION DEVELOPMENT PROCUREMENT_ROUND NO. II

sig_4e71d728d133d6d9af83.description: Aarhus Vand is a utility group that manages water and wastewater activities. In this context, Aarhus Vand owns, operates, and maintains many kilometres of water and wastewater pipes distributed across the supply area. To ensure efficient operation of the pipes, Aarhus Vand requires accurate, updated, and accessible registration of the pipe network. For this purpose, Aarhus Vand needs a pipe registration system. Aarhus Vand wishes for a collective agreement comprising both the licences for the pipe registration system itself and consultancy services for ongoing development and maintenance of the system. Aarhus Vand hereby invites to a market dialogue regarding the above. The purpose of the market dialogue includes determining which systems are on the market that can fulfil Aarhus Vand's factual and objective needs. Aarhus Vand has identified the following requirements as being important in relation to a future pipe registration system. It is important to Aarhus Vand that these requirements can already be fulfilled now. The list is not considered exhaustive: 1. Full support for DANVA's latest models, currently: Dandas 3.1.2, TV inspection and manhole report 3.1.2, Danvand 2.1.2, cables, third-party pipes, and areas 1.1, burst registration 1.1.1. For all models, this applies to all concepts, attributes, codes, relations, and interfaces as well as DANVA's guidelines and data manuals. The system is configurable so that it can be easily and quickly adapted to changes in both the models and the user interface 2. All registrations are saved / data resides in one and the same database 3. The system must support data exchange in XML format. There must be an option for direct updating via e.g. SQL. There must be direct access to data, as well as the possibility of making direct integrations with other systems. 4. Quality assurance. XSD validation, predefined validations, etc., which support pipe registration and work with data, and thus ensure and maintain good data quality. 5. Possibility to work in "jobs" in connection with the digitalisation of an area / project / subject, which can subsequently be upgraded to be the master. That is, so that one does not work in the master until changes have been upgraded to the master. 6. The language in the system must be Danish. To a minor extent, it can be in English. 7. User interface. An intuitive and user-friendly user interface. Workflows must be supported by configurable templates/flows. Must contain a tool for replacing, splitting, and merging objects, e.g. pipes. Must have various construction tools. Must have 3D support. 8. User management via AD integration. Users must be able to have different roles/rights. 9. The solution must have stable and high performance 10. There must be an auto-save feature, or recovery of unsaved work or similar. All market operators who believe they can meet the above requirements are encouraged to register for the market dialogue. FRAMEWORK AND PARTICIPATION OF THE DIALOGUE As a general rule, the market dialogue will take place physically at Aarhus Vand, Hasselager Allé 29, 8260 Viby J. The dialogue is held individually per market operator. Interest in the market dialogue must be reported to Christoffer Larsen at christoffer.larsen@aarhusvand.dk or indkob@aarhusvand.dk no later than 20.10.2025. The dialogue meetings are held in the period from 21.10.2025 to 31.10.2025.
sig_4e71d728d133d6d9af83.title: Invitation to market dialogue regarding IT system for utility registration in connection with water, wastewater, etc.

sig_4f709663903d0fe20a2b.description: Single Project RFP Set-Aside for Small Businesses NAICS Code: 236220 – Commercial and Institutional Building Construction The Hawaii National Guard intends to issue a Request for Proposals (RFP) to award a single firm fixed-price contract for services, non-personal, to provide all plant, labor, transportation, materials, tools, equipment, appliances and supervision necessary for the Construction of “KNMD209085 Munitions Maintenance and Inspection (M&I) Facility” and “KNMD209086 Conventional Munitions Cube Storage Addition” located on the Hawaii Air National Guard campus, at Joint Base Pearl Harbor-Hickam (JBPHH), Hawaii. - KNMD209085 Munitions Maintenance and Inspection (M&I) Facility - Construct a new Munitions Maintenance & Inspections facility by utilizing conventional design and construction methods to accommodate the facility mission. This project has a statutory cost limitation $14M for Unspecified Minor Military Construction (UMMC) Project – Adjustment of Dollar Limitations for Location pursuant to 10 USC §2805. Project square footage is estimated at 2,400 SF. Work covered in this project includes but is not limited to: Micro-pile Foundations: Specialized foundation engineering featuring micro-piles to mitigate challenging soil conditions and ensure seismic structural integrity. Cast-in-Place Concrete: Constructing robust concrete slab-on-grade, concrete walls, capping beams, and associated structural masonry elements. Structural Framing & Enclosure: Utilizing cold-formed metal framing, insulated metal wall panels, and structural steel support systems. Roofing: Installation of high-performance standing seam metal roofing, complete with prefinished gutters, downspouts, and weather barrier wraps. Specialized Systems: Installation of mechanical HVAC systems (including specialized 20-ton air conditioning systems), interior plumbing, lightning/grounding protection, and communication infrastructure. Fire Protection: A complete fire alarm-mass notification system and wet-pipe sprinkler suppression system. In addition to the base work described above, the solicitation will include the following option line items: 1. MAC Pad - Construct 1,167 SY concrete pad for the Material Assembly Center (MAC), required for constructing munitions, along with new asphalt pavement for access and egress to the facility's maintenance bays. - KNMD209086 Conventional Munitions Cube Storage Addition - Construct an addition to the Munitions Cube Storage Facility (B3552) utilizing conventional design and construction methods to support the F-22 mission. This project has a statutory cost limitation $14M for Unspecified Minor Military Construction (UMMC) Project – Adjustment of Dollar Limitations for Location pursuant to 10 USC §2805. Project square footage is estimated at 1,320 SF. Work covered in this project includes but is not limited to: Substructure & Enclosure: Micro-pile foundations, concrete wall structures, cast-in-place concrete slabs, and 12" thick concrete walls designed for high-hazard storage specifications. Framing & Roofing: Structural steel framing, roof joists, and standing seam metal roofing matching existing facility standards. Exterior Elements: Erection of new asphalt pavement adjacent to the existing facility access to provide adequate logistics and material handling access around the new facility addition. Specialized Protection: Maintenance facility lightning and grounding protection systems, along with integrated fire detection and alarm reporting systems connected back to the base reporting system. APPLICABLE TO BOTH PROJECTS RAB Lighting exterior wall packs and area lights are sole source/brand name specific for compatibility with existing installation systems (noted justifications will be included with solicitation). Project Phasing & Security Gates: The contractor will be required to erect a temporary security fence around the construction zone in accordance with the project staging and phasing drawings. Escort Requirements: Escort personnel shall be required when erecting the temporary security fence, performing work occurring outside the temporary security fence, and connecting utilities to the existing system. Secured Zone Access: Once the temporary security fencing is approved and accepted by the Contracting Officer’s Representative (COR), no escort shall be required within the active secured work zone during construction, allowing the contractor to work within the secured boundary unimpeded. sig_500928eb240e422aaf60.description: This Market Engagement seeks to identify options to enable procurement of a dedicated backup collection tool for Operational Technology (OT) environments. The solution will ensure that the complete data state of critical OT assets is consistently captured and securely stored across multiple sites, serving as the organisation's data of last resort. The tool must collect the full backup state of OT assets including configurations, control logic, firmware, hardware metadata, and associated files. It must support both automated, policy-driven backup collection and authorised manual backup initiation, operating through secure and non-intrusive protocols that do not interact with OT control or programming interfaces and have no impact on live operations or safety-critical systems. The solution must be vendor-agnostic, deployable fully on-premise or within a private cloud, and capable of operating in air-gapped environments, with full audit trails and compliance reporting. IMPORTANT: Please read this section before deciding whether you wish to register for this event. This section provides you with information regarding the scope of this procurement and details some of the key requirements that a successful applicant MUST be able to deliver.

sig_505d98c363533a938268.description: As part of this market sounding, DAK-Gesundheit would like to gain an overview of the existing market situation in the field of software-supported occupational integration management. To support occupational integration management (BEM), DAK-Gesundheit is examining the procurement of a cloud-based standard software solution (Software as a Service - SaaS). sig_50a618e0b85da91cb217.description: "Evaluation services regarding the implementation of the South-West Oltenia Regional Programme interventions 2021-2027" will be purchased in order to obtain an independent, objective and evidence-based evaluation regarding the implementation and results of the South-West Oltenia Regional Programme 2021–2027, which will support the programme management and the preparation of the future programming period. The services will be provided in accordance with the minimum requirements in the specifications. The contracting authority will respond clearly and completely to all requests for clarifications on the 11-th day before the deadline for the submission of tenders. An evaluation study regarding the implementation of the South-West Oltenia Regional Programme interventions 2021-2027" will be purchased, which consists of providing consulting services for the implementation of the Evaluation of the implementation of the South-West Oltenia Regional Programme interventions 2021-2027, respectively the evaluation in an integrated approach of the investment priorities related to the South-West Oltenia Regional Programme 2021-2027, for the Managing Authority of the PR SV Oltenia. The general objective of the evaluation of the use of PR SV Oltenia resources 2021-2027 is to determine the effectiveness, efficiency, relevance, coherence (internal and external), added value for the Union, of the interventions financed through PR SV Oltenia 2021-2027, including through the technical assistance priority. In accordance with the Evaluation Plan of the PR SV Oltenia 2021-2027, the evaluations also follow the assessment of visibility, regional social cohesion, inclusiveness, the green character and the non-discriminatory one. The programme evaluation must highlight, in particular, the progress and performance recorded in the management and implementation of the PR SV Oltenia interventions through the prism of the criteria mentioned above and the evaluation questions. The evaluation aims to analyse the implementation method of the South-West Oltenia Regional Programme 2021–2027, in an integrated approach, at the level of all priorities (P1–P10). Specific objectives of the evaluation • determining the coherence of the interventions within the PR SV Oltenia 2021-2027 for the period for which the evaluation is carried out; • determining the EU visibility through the interventions financed within the PR SV Oltenia 2021-2027; • constituting a source of new information regarding the achievement of the objectives formulated within the PR SV Oltenia 2021-2027 of the interventions financed within the PR SV Oltenia 2021-2027 which will contribute to making decisions based on real information; • analysing the evolution of the priorities targeted by the evaluation; • analysing the fulfilment of the enabling conditions for the adequate implementation of the interventions; • analysing the complementarity and synergy of the interventions with other interventions financed from Union funds and from other national and European instruments as well as their added value for the EU; • analysing the necessity and ease of accessing funding opportunities by potential beneficiaries; • analysing the capacity to carry out investments, including adopting new technologies by applicants and beneficiaries; • analysing the way in which the target groups of people, firms and institutions, targeted by the priorities, are engaged in the supported activities; • analysing the way of integrating horizontal principles (equality between women and men, non-discrimination, accessibility, inclusiveness, sustainable development, including the principle of doing no significant harm) in the selected projects and their implementation; • measuring the effects of the interventions from the perspective of the specific objectives of the programme, to support its effective and efficient implementation.
sig_50a618e0b85da91cb217.title: Evaluation services regarding the implementation of the South-West Oltenia Regional Programme interventions 2021-2027

sig_5105c2b1d87c2c0fa1e4.description: suHCO (Systemic Sustainability Transition Solution for Health Care Organisations) is a European project funded under the Horizon Europe programme (Grant Agreement No. 101226802) and implemented through a Pre-Commercial Procurement (PCP) scheme. The project aims to support health and care organisations in their transition towards more sustainable and environmentally responsible models by fostering the development of innovative digital solutions. Through the PCP process, suHCO will procure research and development services for the creation of an AI-enabled digital platform capable of helping healthcare organisations assess their sustainability performance, identify improvement opportunities, plan and implement actions, monitor progress, and support evidence-based decision-making. The future solution is expected to integrate sustainability knowledge, regulatory requirements, standards, best practices and relevant data sources, providing users with practical guidance tailored to their organisational context. It should also support sustainable procurement processes, impact assessment, reporting activities and organisational change management. The project is driven by a Buyers Group composed of healthcare organisations from Spain, Italy and Wales. The solutions developed during the PCP will be progressively designed, prototyped and validated in real healthcare environments to ensure their relevance, usability and scalability. By bringing together healthcare providers, technology developers and sustainability experts, suHCO seeks to stimulate innovation and contribute to the sustainability objectives of European health systems. Procurement will take the form of pre-commercial procurement (PCP), where R&D service contracts will be awarded in parallel to different R&D providers in a phased approach. This will allow alternative, competing solutions to be compared. Each selected operator will receive a framework contract covering three R&D phases. The three phases are: Solution design, prototype development, original development and validation and testing of a limited volume of the first products or services. After each phase, interim evaluations are conducted to select the best of the competing solutions. The contractors with the best value for money will be offered a specific contract for the next phase. The selected operators will retain ownership of the intellectual property rights (IPRs) they generate during the PCP and will be able to use them to exploit the full market potential of the solutions developed. Testing is expected to take place in Catalonia (Spain), West Wales (UK), Treviso (Italy). This testing may also serve as a first customer test reference for the contractors. The selected suppliers will retain ownership of the intellectual property rights (IPRs) they generate during the PCP and will be able to use them to exploit the full market potential of the solutions developed, i.e. beyond the procurement. This procurement is funded by the European Union's Horizon Europe Research and Innovation Programme under Grant Agreement No. 101226802- suHCO (https://suhco.eu/). The EU has awarded a grant for this procurement but is not participating as a contracting authority in the procurement.
sig_5105c2b1d87c2c0fa1e4.title: Pre-commercial Procurement of an innovative Systemic Sustainability Transition Solution for Health Care Organisations (suHCO)

sig_51dd928abedab57fcef9.description: The U.S. Military Academy at West Point's mission is "to educate, train, and inspire the Corps of Cadets so that each graduate is a commissioned leader of character committed to the values of Duty, Honor, Country and prepared for a career of professional excellence and service to the Nation as an officer in the United States Army." The United States Military Academy is located at West Point, New York. USMA executes research to enhance the education of cadets, develop the faculty professionally, and address important issues facing the Army and the Nation. In addition, the Academy conducts research and analysis in emerging fields that may realize novel or vastly improved Army capabilities. At West Point, research is organized and administered through centers and institutes, most of which reside within academic departments. These centers and institutes, affiliated with each other through the Academy Research Council (ARC), coordinated and supported by the Academic Research Division (ARD), provide the infrastructure necessary to tackle the nation’s and the world’s most challenging problems. Our research centers and institutes bring context to the classroom, are central to our vibrant and pioneering faculty, and are one way West Point connects to the Army and to the Nation. Our students are driven, our faculty is world-class, and through our centers, scholars and scientists thrive and produce their best work. Cadets regularly win Best Paper Awards at national and international graduate-level conferences, our faculty hold fellowships and chairmanships in their discipline's national organizations and our products are deployed to the soldier. In addition to applied research, there are centers and institutes at West Point that focus on other aspects of the USMA mission. The USMA BAA identifies topics of interest to the USMA departments, directorates, and research centers and institutes. These groups focus on executing in-house research programs, with a significant emphasis on collaborative research with other organizations. The groups fund a modest amount of extramural research in certain specific areas, and those areas are described in this BAA. The USMA BAA seeks proposals from institutions of higher education, nonprofit organizations, state and local governments, foreign organizations, foreign public entities, and for-profit organizations (i.e., large and small businesses) for research based on the following campaigns: Socio-Cultural; Information Technology; Ballistics, Weapons, and Protections; Energy and Sustainability; Materials, Measurements, and Facilities; Unmanned Systems and Space; Human Support Systems; and Artificial Intelligence, Machine Learning, and Quantum Technologies. Proposals are sought for cutting-edge innovative research that could produce discoveries with a significant impact to enable new and improved Army technologies and related operational capabilities and related technologies. The specific research areas and topics of interest described in this document should be viewed as suggestive, rather than limiting.

This is a total Small Business Set Aside. The solicitation number is W911S7-26-Q-A006, and the solicitation is issued as a Request for Quote (RFQ) (see attachments). Written quotes must be emailed to Mr. Zakhireh, contact details provided below, no later than 22 September 2026, at 4:00PM CST. The Mission and Installation Contracting Command (MICC), Ft. Leonard Wood, MO, hereby announces a solicitation for a small business set-aside, Firm Fixed-Price, purchase order contract for Marquee signage procurement and replacement in supporting the United States Army Fort Leonard Wood, Missouri. The duration of the contract – to include installation of the two-marquee signage will not exceed 180 days. The North American Industry Classification Code (NAICS) for this requirement is 339950 (Sign Manufacturing). The size standard for this NAICS Code is 500 employees. There will not be a site visit for this requirement. There will be no Q/A period for this requirement. The contractor will remove and lawfully dispose of the existing non-functional/obsolete sign cabinets and hardware, provide all required cellular data service and CMS licensing for five years at no recurring cost to the Government, and ensure compatibility with major carriers and modern web browsers. The Government will provide electrical service within three feet of each sign, while the contractor will connect, power up, and test the new signs to verify proper operation. The contractor will deliver a project schedule, coordinate site access and compliance with all OPSEC, antiterrorism, and local security training and policies, and provide user manuals (PDF and hard copy) plus up to a one-hour training session for up to six Government personnel on remote content management and sign operation, with all work completed within 120 days of contract award during normal duty hours. It is the Offerors responsibility to check for any posted changes to the solicitation, including any subsequent solicitation amendments or responses to Requests for Information (RFls) during the solicitation open period. Offerors must have and/or maintain an active registration with the System Award Management (SAM) website. To register in SAM, go to https://sam.gov. sig_520df3d5418ed50bc328.description: 1. Introduction and Purpose The United States Air Force is seeking information on industry capabilities for the Advanced Radar Threat System (ARTS) Variant 3 (V3) Variable Aperture Digital Radar (VADR) [ST1] Third-Party Software initiative. This RFI seeks input from industry to: Understand existing commercial and near-term planned capabilities relevant to the development of software for advanced threat emulation for systems like ARTS-V3. Attract both traditional and non-traditional defense contractors. Gauge industry interest in the proposed C5 structure. Refine the acquisition strategy for this software approach 2. Program Background: The ARTS-V3 program develops highly channelized digital Active Electronically Scanned Array (AESA) radar systems to emulate and replicate advanced adversary threat systems. As a ruggedized, closed-loop threat emulator, ARTS-V3 functions as a representative adversary fire control or multi-functional ground-based radar. It is designed with a high degree of hardware and software flexibility, allowing it to incorporate various adversary radar models to simulate how adversaries counter and adapt to contested environments. 3. Proposed OTA Consortium Structure The Government is executing this modernization effort utilizing the Consortium for Command, Control, and Communications in Cyberspace (C5) Other Transaction Authority (OTA) agreement, pursuant to 10 U.S.C. § 4022. Managed by the Consortium Management Group (CMG), this OTA framework significantly compresses acquisition timelines compared to traditional FAR-based contracts. The ARTS-V3 program will issue Requests for White Papers (RWPs) directly to the C5 member base, leveraging an established ecosystem of technology innovators. Eligibility: Interested parties must be members of the C5 consortium to receive awards. Registration: Information on joining can be found at the CMG C5 Overview Portal https://cmgnetworks.org/become-c5-member/ 4. Key Principles for Participation Prospective partners must adhere to the following principles: System Integration: Partner with the Lead System Integrator (LSI) to manage configurations, integrate legacy baselines, test code compliance, and perform post-deployment troubleshooting. Establish formal communication channels with the LSI. MBSE Compliance: Deliver and maintain technical baselines as dynamic, digital model elements using Cameo/SysML. The Government will provide necessary Government Furnished Information (GFI). DevSecOps & Cyber: Utilize the Government's cloud-based software factory and automated CI/CD pipelines. All developments must align with Zero-Trust Architecture (ZTA) and Department of War (DoW) cybersecurity requirements. Development Isolation: Do not reuse, copy, or integrate proprietary code from adjacent vendors. Maintain strict separation between ARTS-V3 ("Red") systems and friendly ("Blue") systems; no cross-system technology reuse is permitted. Cost-Sharing: Provide a one-third (33.3%) cost-share of the total project cost if operating as a traditional DoW vendor acting as the prime performer. 5. Scope of Work, Technical Requirements, & Desired Capabilities Successful partners must demonstrate deep expertise in developing, updating, and integrating advanced threat implementations into the ARTS-V3 system using rigorous, modern software engineering practices. 5.1 Scope of Work & Required Technical Capabilities Radar Integration & DSP: Integrate existing radar or transmit-only reactive models into the ARTS-V3 system. Partner must demonstrate an understanding of radar physics, Electronic Warfare (EW) principles, and the optimization of Digital Signal Processing (DSP) algorithms. Notional Example: Development of software to emulate an emerging X-band threat for an initial capability release. Software Updates & RTOS: Update and maintain existing radar software (e.g., streamlining calibration, improving tracking algorithms, and developing multi-target kinematic tracking filters). Development requires experience with Real-Time Operating Systems (RTOS) including VxWorks, real-time Linux, modern C++ (C++14/17/20), and hardware-accelerated computing (CUDA, OpenCL). C2 User Interface & Protocols: Update the Command and Control (C2) user interface software, specifically the VADR App (VAPP), with enhanced user interfaces or expanded range capabilities. Design open, non-proprietary APIs (REST, gRPC) aligned with Lead System Integrator (LSI) Interface Control Documents (ICDs) and ensure all messaging functions remain fully compatible with existing system protocols. AESA Resource Management: Develop and implement advanced beam-scheduling and power-management algorithms optimized for Active Electronically Scanned Arrays (AESA). Zero Trust Communications: Implement micro-segmentation and secure communications, enforcing mutual TLS (mTLS 1.3) using FIPS 140-3 validated cryptographic modules to exceed baseline DoW cybersecurity mandates. Modern Programming Practices: Utilize memory-safe programming languages (e.g., Rust, Go, Python, Java) where applicable. Deep working knowledge of C++ remains necessary to successfully utilize the Government Furnished Information (GFI) Software Development Kit (SDK). AI-Assisted Development & Safety: The use of AI coding tools is permitted, provided vendors prevent CUI/DoW data exfiltration. All AI-assisted logic must be clearly identified in an automatically generated Software Bill of Materials (SBOM), undergo strict Human-in-the-Loop (HITL) review, and pass Static (SAST) and Dynamic (DAST) Application Security Testing. AI-Optimized Algorithms: Ensure the development process for advanced tactical edge algorithms aligns directly with Cognitive Electronic Warfare (CogEW) methodologies. 5.2 Desired Capabilities The Government is highly interested in partners who can deliver next-generation enhancements, specifically: Advanced Digital Twin & Closed-Loop Emulation: Novel, closed-loop threat simulations for Software-in-the-Loop (SIL) and Hardware-in-the-Loop (HIL) testing. AI/ML for Sensor Fusion & Cognitive EW: Embedded tactical-edge capabilities to enhance sensor fusion and threat reaction times. Predictive Maintenance: Advanced algorithms utilizing real-time system telemetry and diagnostic data to predict component failures. Development & Analysis Ecosystems: Specialized radar development environments, code-writing assistance tools, novel radar applications, and robust system analysis tools. GOVERNMENT FURNISHED INFORMATION (GFI) The Government will provide: Applicable threat data from intelligence community members. A Modular Threat Design and Development Template and documentation. Access to the following equipment for testing: Subscale Threat System Anechoic Chamber Cloud-based radar testing Environment Cloud-based Software code verification and Integration Environment Access to the following tools for collaboration: ARTS-V3 VADR and VAPP Software Development Kits (SDK) Containerization tools (e.g., Pod Manager, Docker, Kubernetes) Cameo Models Git repository and container registry (e.g., GitLab) 7. SECURITY Facility: Respondents should describe their classified handling and storage capabilities. An active security clearance is required to access the subscale threat system. Networks: Once under contract, personnel may need access to unclassified and classified networks up to SIPRNet (primarily for Cloud Access). Future Requirements: Respondents do not necessarily have to have a Top Secret clearances nor SAP and SCI access, but the government would like to understand each respondent’s current and future security posture up to TS/SAR and/or TS/SCI including willingness to obtain clearances and estimated timeline. 8. INDUSTRY RESPONSE AND SUBMISSION INSTRUCTIONS: The Air Combat Command (ACC) and other DoW organizations are supported by this project. The ARTS-V3 Program Office anticipates releasing a request for white papers through the C5 consortium as early as November 2026, with an estimated project award around June 2027. Please submit responses electronically to Kristina Lenderman (kristina.lenderman@us.af.mil) and Tyler Newey (tyler.newey@us.af.mil) no later than 3 Aug 2026. 9. Submission Format: Submissions should be Unclassified. If including restricted data, mark the cover page and each relevant page clearly. Responses are limited to one (1) cover page and five (5) content pages. Use size 12 Times New Roman font with one-inch margins. Please provide the following information: Company Name and Commercial and Government Entity (CAGE) code. Point of contact details (Name, phone, email). Interest as a prime performer or as a partner. Agreement with NAICS 541511 (if not, suggest an alternative) Number of personnel with security clearances on your envisioned software team. Willingness to operate within the proposed OTA structure. For traditional DoW vendors: your thoughts on a cost-sharing model. Suggestions for the acquisition strategy. Details of any Anechoic Chamber capabilities you possess. Your security posture as referenced in Section 7. 10. SOFTWARE DEVELOPMENT CAPABILITIES QUESTIONS: Respondents are required to submit a comprehensive capability statement. Submissions must directly address each of the four domains outlined below, structured exactly as defined. 10.1 Technical Capabilities & Experience Respondents must detail their technical proficiency and past performance in the following areas: Radar Innovation & Intelligence-Based Models: Detail your organization's experience with intelligence-based threat radar models. Describe any existing radar products or novel software-defined capabilities/telemetry tools that could directly support the ARTS-V3 mission. Enterprise C++ & RTOS: Describe your company's depth of experience migrating legacy codebases, using C++ (necessary for utilizing the VADR SDK and understanding the base system), and optimizing software for High-Performance Computing (HPC) and RTOS environments. Also, list all the various software languages your company has experienced with. Please rate your proficiency with each language (i.e. C++ = 50%). Memory-Safe Languages & Zero Trust: Describe your company's experience with memory-safe programming languages (e.g., Rust, Go, Python, Java, Swift, etc). Outline your secure coding practices and experience securing sensor-to-C2 interfaces via mutual TLS (mTLS). C2 Software Development: Describe your experience developing remotely operated C2 software and web applications (necessary to understand or utilize the VAPP SDK). Model-Based Systems Engineering (MBSE): Describe your practical experience using Cameo or other SysML tools to drive agile system development and maintain technical baselines. AI Validation, Supply Chain & DevSecOps: AI Tools & CUI Protection: If utilizing AI-assisted coding tools, specify which tools are used and detail your protocols to prevent CUI/DoW data exfiltration. Validation Pipeline: Describe your DevSecOps pipeline for testing, validating, and scanning AI-generated code (SAST/DAST). SBOM Generation: Detail your capability to produce an automated Software Bill of Materials (SBOM) that explicitly distinguishes between human-authored and AI-generated code. Environment Operations: Detail your experience operating software and CI/CD pipelines within heavily restricted cloud environments (IL5+) and utilizing Kubernetes orchestration. 10.2 Security & Infrastructure Posture Personnel Clearances: Provide the total number of personnel holding active Secret and Top Secret security clearances. Facility Safeguarding: Detail your facility safeguarding capabilities (including SCIF/SAPF) and network access to SIPRNet. Special Access Roadmap: Provide a detailed roadmap demonstrating your capability to operate within Special Access Program (SAP) environments and handle Sensitive Compartmented Information (SCI) data. 10.3. Strategic Alignment & Cost-Sharing Structure Cost-Sharing (Traditional Contractors Only): Proposed models, co-investment strategies, or financial structures to meet the statutory one-third (1/3) cost-sharing requirement under the OTA. Acquisition Strategy Feedback: Provide actionable feedback, identify key risks, or offer suggestions regarding the proposed OTA strategy, software lifecycle timeline, and Intellectual Property (IP) approach.[JH9] 11. POINTS OF CONTACT: Kristina Lenderman Agreements Officer 801-775-4427 kristina.lenderman@us.af.mil Tyler Newey Agreements Specialist 801-586-5097 tyler.newey@us.af.mil Rajathi Noel Program Manager 801-777-0598 rajathi.noel@us.af.mil Eric Fink Technical POC 777-0829 eric.fink.2.ctr@us.af.mil 12. DISCLAIMERS AND NOTICES This is a Request for Information (RFI) for market research and planning purposes only. It is not a solicitation for proposals, and responses cannot be accepted by the Government to form a binding contract. Participation is voluntary, and the Government will not reimburse respondents for any costs associated with this RFI. All information submitted will be used for market analysis and will not be returned. Not responding to this notice does not preclude participation in any future solicitation. All responses are limited to one cover page and five (5) pages, size 12 Times New Roman font, one-inch margins on all sides. Responses longer than one cover page and five content pages will only be read through the first five content pages. 13. GLOSSARY: C2: Command and Control Threat: Desire to emulate behaviors and functionality of a particular adversary Surface-to-Air system. Radar Function Software: RFS is the collection of programs, algorithms, and computational tools that control a radar system's hardware, process the raw data it collects, and translate that data into understandable information for analysis and decision-making.

sig_5228e894e80d04057f74.description: The purpose of the contract is to guarantee the continuity of the corporate data analytics services currently implemented in an on-premise model, as well as their modernisation and technological evolution through their transition to a managed cloud model. The supply in cloud mode that is the subject of this contract includes, within the price of the right to use the licences, the provision of the infrastructure necessary for the operation of the platform in separate production and development environments, the comprehensive management service, corrective and evolutionary maintenance, periodic software updates, the third-party software necessary for its operation, specialised technical support, continuous monitoring of the service and the application of appropriate security measures, as well as the definition and compliance of service levels (SLAs). Likewise, the contract comprises the planning and execution of the migration from the current on-premise environment to the cloud model, including configuration, parametrisation, testing and commissioning tasks, as well as the provision of specialised technical and functional support consulting services during the transition process. The contract is structured through unit prices per licence typology, establishing a minimum number of licences to be supplied during the term of the contract, and the number of licences may be increased, depending on needs, up to the maximum contract amount envisaged.

sig_526a6b73b5712fbec3ec.description: DCMS is seeking to commission a two-phase research project to investigate UK media consumption habits and public trust in media. Phase 1 would consist of a behavioural cohort study (or another appropriate methodology) to map the specific "user pathways" audiences take to find, consume, and value information across different media sources, such as traditional news broadcasts and social media, across different demographics. Building on these findings, Phase 2 would explore how individuals perceive trust in different media sources due to their own perception of mis/disinformation, assess the broader effects of these consumption pathways on factors such as viewer retention and wider social cohesion, as well as overall integrity of the UK's information ecosystem. This project will be commissioned either through a Competitive Flexible Procedure under the Procurement Act 2023, or through the RM6126 Research and Insights framework. This is part of the DCMS Science and Analysis R&D Programme, which supports R&D capability within the department. This project will run concurrently alongside three other large projects across 2027-2030; these include 'what works' research into AI adoption in DCMS sectors; a continuation of previous research to develop data-intensive approaches for capturing engagement at unticketed cultural, heritage, and sporting events/activities/locations, e.g. using mobile app data to model how people participate in our events; and a continuation of previous research to design and improve methods for holistically tracking the long-term impact of major events, tested on a major event. Lot 1: .
sig_526a6b73b5712fbec3ec.title: 105016 - Media Consumption Pathways and Trust

sig_5277a0e2729f55acd4d9.description: Ingeus is seeking Expressions of Interest (EOI) from suitably qualified suppliers to participate in an upcoming procurement for a next-generation Employment Services platform. The solution will support the end-to-end management of participant journeys, from referral and onboarding through assessment, personalised support, intervention delivery, employment outcomes, sustainment and programme performance management. The opportunity encompasses a broad range of functional, technical and integration requirements, including participant engagement, advisor enablement, workflow orchestration, reporting and analytics, accessibility, AI-assisted administration, and integration with external platforms and services. The requirements have been developed through extensive business analysis, stakeholder engagement and user-centred design activities and are documented within a comprehensive Requirements Traceability Matrix (RTM) and supporting User Experience (UX) and User Interface (UI) requirements catalogue. Suppliers interested in participating are invited to submit an Expression of Interest outlining their organisation, relevant experience, solution capability and suitability for the opportunity. Following an initial evaluation of EOI responses, a shortlist of suppliers will be selected to progress to the next stage of the procurement process. The objective of the EOI stage is to identify suppliers with demonstrable capability in delivering modern, configurable platforms that support complex participant management, workflow-driven service delivery, digital self-service, operational reporting, accessibility standards and future AI enablement requirements. Suppliers selected to proceed beyond the EOI stage will be required to enter into a Non-Disclosure Agreement (NDA) before receiving the full tender pack. Contract start date Award: late 2026 Project: Q1 / Q2 2027 MVP: Q3 2027 Contract end date On Going (TBC) How to respond Suppliers wishing to be considered should submit a short written response setting out a short introduction to their company to Alistair Armit. Additional information: Ingeus reserves the right to: - award contracts to one or more suppliers - separate or combine work packages - withdraw or amend this opportunity Feedback will not be provided to unsuccessful respondents.

Following notification in due form and time, the respective company will promptly receive a questionnaire sent by e-mail to the specified contact point from the contracting authority's IT purchasing department, which the company must complete fully and truthfully and return to the contracting authority's IT purchasing department within 14 days. Responses submitted late may be disregarded. The contracting authority will examine the company's responses received in due time and, if necessary, invite them to market consultation discussions, which can take place online as a video conference or in person as an on-site appointment at the contracting authority's registered office. The contracting authority reserves the right, at its dutiful discretion and in compliance with the principles of transparency and equal treatment, to ask follow-up questions and to request clarifications and subsequent submissions. Upon completion of the market consultation, the results will be definitively evaluated by the contracting authority and taken into account within the scope of the intended award procedure. If it turns out after completion of the market consultation that the contracting authority's requirements can indeed only be fulfilled by a single company, a negotiated procedure without a call for competition pursuant to § 14 para. 4 no. 2 of the Public Procurement Ordinance (VgV) will be conducted with the affected company, otherwise a competitive award procedure.

sig_52e3c59ec11b9c31cf76.description: The Ogden Air Logistics Complex (OO-ALC) at Hill Air Force Base, Utah, intends to issue a solicitation to provide comprehensive management and supply of aircraft coatings and sealants. This effort aims to ensure uninterrupted aircraft maintenance operations through robust inventory management, timely delivery, and technical support. This effort will include frequent ordering and quick delivery on specified items. The selected contractor will be responsible for continuous deliveries and support of Coatings and Sealants, including: 1. Order Fulfillment and Material Handling: Sourcing, storing, and delivering all required coatings and sealants (see attached list). This includes meeting a strict four (4) hour delivery timeline for urgent requirements and handling specialized materials, such as Premixed Frozen Material (PFM) requiring transit at -80F. The contractor must maintain a minimum of 85% shelf life for all products upon delivery. The contractor will also be responsible for managing shelf-life and ensuring proper storage and handling of the products prior to delivery. 2. FMS-3600 Coating Management: For this specialized product, implementing a lock and key ITAR-compliant storage system and maintaining rigorous chain of custody for the material. 3. Technical Assistance: Providing technical assistance that includes rapid response (within one business day) to material failures, on-site technical support during monthly visits, product change support, and quality audit reporting. 4. Online Ordering System: Furnishing a secure, web-based ordering and tracking system with real-time visibility of lead times and minimum stock levels (MSLS). 5. Ramp-Up Plan: Executing a ramp-up plan to achieve full performance readiness within eight (8) months of contract award. The anticipated contract will be a Firm Fixed Priced (FFP) IDIQ to include an 8-month ramp up period, a 5-year ordering period, and a 6-month allowance for remaining deliveries on the back end. Total period of performance is anticipated to be 6 years and 2 months. This is a total small business set-aside. The Government anticipates awarding a single contract. All interested small businesses are encouraged to respond. The official solicitation will be posted on SAM .gov. The Government intends to award a single contract resulting from the upcoming solicitation to the responsible offeror whose proposal represents the best value to the Government. This effort requires Contractors to be CMMC level 2 self-certified, therefore if you are not currently level 2 certified and are interested in this requirement you will need to begin the process to become level 2 certified immediately. The solicitation draft documents are attached. Dates on the solicitation are subject to change based on the actual award date. Please review and submit any questions or suggestions to the point of contacts on this 15-day synopsis. The anticipated solicitation number is FA8224-26-R-0010 (subject to change). The anticipated solicitation release date is October 2, 2026 (subject to change).

sig_536b19268a0dacc0c406.description: The subject of the contract is the implementation of pilot and standardisation studies for the evaluation of a battery of tests designed to measure mathematical, linguistic and scientific research aptitudes under the project "Supporting the accessibility of education for children and young people" (project number: FERS.01.06-IP.05-0002/23). The implementation of the study by the Contractor means conducting research using innovative diagnostic tools to measure mathematical, scientific-research and linguistic aptitudes for children aged 7-17 years. The aim of the subject of the contract is a pilot study (verification of the correctness of the created tools) and a standardisation study (development of norms). The study will be conducted in a mixed format: electronic and traditional (paper-and-pencil). The participants in the study will be pupils aged 7 - 17 years. It is planned that a total of 5 650 pupils will be examined in both stages (pilot and standardisation). The study will be conducted in schools - at the pilot stage, sample selection (in accordance with the Contracting Authority's guidelines) remains the responsibility of the Contractor, while at the standardisation study stage, the drawn sample (main and reserve) will be provided by the Contracting Authority. Questionnaires will also be completed by parents and teachers. The description of the subject of the contract and the description of the method of executing the contract are contained in the Specification of Contract Terms and Annexes. sig_53859266daf39dfe09a0.description: 2M-IT Oy (hereinafter also the "Contracting Authority" or "Client") is establishing a dynamic purchasing system (DPS) for data-driven management and artificial intelligence services. Organisations providing services under the dynamic purchasing system (DPS) may submit requests to participate in the dynamic purchasing system throughout its duration. All candidates who have submitted a request to participate and who meet the suitability requirements set for candidates will be admitted to the dynamic purchasing system. The internal competitions of the dynamic purchasing system to be established will cover data-driven management and AI platforms, solutions and services, licences, and expert services, as well as various combinations thereof. The aforementioned are to be procured for services produced for social and healthcare organisations, which will be specified in more detail in the call for tenders for the DPS internal competition. Solutions may be procured for use in specialised medical care, primary healthcare, and social services, as well as in support activities related to these tasks. They may be implemented in the service production of 2M-IT Oy as part of the services for one or more clients. In addition, 2M-IT Oy may also procure solutions for the needs of its own business operations. The actual procurements will be made on the basis of separate calls for tenders as internal competitions within the DPS, in which the contracting authority will specify and describe its detailed procurement need. The subject of the procurement of platforms and licences may be, for example, a solution based on commercial off-the-shelf software for data-driven management or AI, software usage rights, licences, and/or an open-source software solution. The subject may also include, among other things, tools for data-driven management, data warehouse automation, integration, analytics and reporting, and visualisation. The solutions and services to be procured may consist of the supplier's own services and products or services and products licensed by a subcontractor provided through the supplier. In service production, either the Client's existing own operating service and other capacity can be utilised, or this can be included in the subject of the procurement. The subject of expert services can be specified in areas such as: • Data-driven management and AI consulting • Planning and management of data management and governance projects • Concept, data, and interface modelling and architecture definition • Development, testing, training, and planning of maintenance, management, and monitoring of data pipelines (ETL) and integrations • Knowledge of open interfaces and standards and integrating AI as part of applications • Planning, development, testing, training, and planning of maintenance, management, and monitoring of data warehouses, data cubes, and data lakes • Development of analytics, advanced analytics, machine learning, and robotics • Development of AI algorithms into finished products in various technologies • Implementation expertise in various technologies (e.g. Google AI, AWS Cloud computing, Microsoft AI) • User interface and application development (Chatbot etc.) • Definition and development of cost accounting • Definition of services, processes, and governance models • Selection, consulting, and training of tools used in development • Machine training, converting original material into a processable format, and teaching artificial intelligence
sig_53859266daf39dfe09a0.title: Knowledge management and artificial intelligence (AI) services

sig_53930fa9072f523f79cf.description: The Rheumazentrum Mittelhessen has decided to tender for a complete hospital information system for the site, which fulfils the KHZG funding requirements 3- 6 and which, furthermore, maps all administrative and clinical processes of an acute, AHB and (DRV) rehabilitation clinic. At the site in Bad Endbach, an acute clinic with 80 beds and an Anschlussheilbehandlung (AHB) and rehabilitation clinic with 36 beds are available for the holistic therapy of acute and chronic rheumatic diseases. The clinic complex also includes two practices with medical rheumatology consultations and an outpatient therapy facility for physiotherapy, physical therapy and occupational therapy. Over the years, the clinic area has been constantly modernised and the infrastructure expanded. The Rheumazentrum Mittelhessen has decided to tender for a complete hospital information system for the site, which fulfils the KHZG funding requirements 3- 6 and which, furthermore, maps all administrative and clinical processes of an acute, AHB and (DRV) rehabilitation clinic. The future HIS is to be set up in such a way that it is the patient-leading system in interaction with other subsystems/modules. The HIS is to be introduced on the basis of a "best practice" approach within the framework of joint project work. The contractor is accordingly expected to provide a consultative and optimising process approach within the framework of the software implementation. The software to be supplied must have the capabilities and instruments that, for example, enable users to manage the patient's treatment progress as efficiently as possible, as well as to document and bill services quickly, in a revenue-secure manner and in compliance with the KHZG (FTB 3-6). The providers are therefore requested to submit a tender for a complete KHZG-compliant HIS including all necessary services for implementation and maintenance/service, which fulfils the mandatory criteria of the KHZG funding requirements 2 - 6 (the mandatory criteria for the admission and treatment management of the FTB 2 are fulfilled via the portal solution of the company Samedi, the discharge and transfer management via the solution of the company Verbund Pflegehilfe (see "Interfaces" tab of Annex 1), the contractor only owes the connection in this area in accordance with the technical requirements and interoperability standards of the KHZG). The new HIS is intended to significantly support the digitalisation and efficiency of hospital processes and thus optimise patient care.
sig_53930fa9072f523f79cf.title: Hospital information system

sig_53a626abe4f48fbd998b.description: Dumfries and Galloway Council – WEF Wanlock Water, Wanlockhead and WEF Nith Nature Reserve, Dumfries. The work is split across two Lots: Lot 1 Wanlock Water (RIBA1); Lot 2 Nith Nature Reserve, Dumfries(RIBA 1&2). Because of the multidisciplinary nature of the work, we would welcome either a single consultancy/ company that has all the skills in house or a consortium that can bring all of the skills required together. However, we appreciate it may be unlikely that a single consultancy has capacity and multiple disciplines. A detailed Description of Services for Lot 1 and 2 is currently being prepared. Lot 1: Wanlock Water Restoration Project- Indicative scope and outputs. The Contracting Authority intends to procure a feasibility study focusing on improving water quality and flows along with enhanced biodiversity, industrial heritage awareness and climate resilience for the Wanlock catchement and its communities. The commission is tasked to develop the project brief and test the feasibility of potential interventions, gathering information on constraints, risks, costs and potential delivery routes. The study is expected to be undertaken within the policy and funding context of the Scottish Environment Protection Agency’s (SEPA) Water Environment Fund (WEF), which supports the identification and delivery of measures to improve the ecological status of water bodies. As such, the feasibility work should consider the objectives of the Water Framework Directive (WFD) and identify opportunities for restoration and enhancement that may be eligible for future WEF support. The commission for the Wanlock Water is anticipated to require a minewater pollution reduction and treatment feasibility assessment, based on existing knowledge and characterisation of the problem, along with a scoping and feasibility study of wider opportunities and constraints to define future locations of works. Opportunities may exist to undertake treatment trials and to deliver multiple benefits within the riparian zone and floodplain and on the hill and moor landscape. The commission shall allow the project to complete Stage 1 of the framework of the Royal Institute of British Architects (RIBA) Plan of Work.. Scope TBC Review existing data and info - gap analysis. Targeted field surveys/assessments Delivery of opportunities & constraints mapping to assess feasibility. Baseline hydrological assessment of catchment. Outputs: project brief; feasibility report and high level summary; opportunity and constraints mapping; risk register; recommended next steps Lot 2: Lot 2 Nith Nature Reserve - Indicative scope and concept design outputs. The commission for the Nith Nature Reserve Project is to complete RIBA stages 1 and 2. This project aims to deliver a riverside nature reserve for people and wildlife by creating an enhanced natural setting for the Nith River. We will deliver significant ecological improvements, enhance the biodiversity and natural habitat and create a multiuse recreational area that is accessible to everyone in the community and provides multi-sensory experiences and educational opportunities. There are opportunities for improvements that would reduce morphological pressure capacity through habitat creation and could benefit flood risk and reduce sediment deposition further downstream. Dumfries and Galloway Council aim to deliver the drivers for biodiversity, climate resilience and better access to blue green infrastructure, access and amenity for local communities. The commission shall allow the project to complete Stage 1 and Stage 2 of the framework of the Royal Institute of British Architects (RIBA) Plan of Work.. TBC: Review existing data & gaps Field surveys/assessments Opportunities and constraints mapping to assess feasibility. RIBA Stage 1: project brief, geomorphological assessment, feasibility, constraints/risk register, next steps RIBA stage 2: preferred option report, concept designs informed by geomorphologist and landscape architect, visualisations and arcGIS style storyboard to present
sig_53a626abe4f48fbd998b.title: Dumfries and Galloway Council – WEF Wanlock Water, Wanlockhead and WEF Nith Nature Reserve, Dumfries.

sig_5439fdf38566ca016a1f.description: The new State Parliament of the Federal State of Brandenburg is located at the site of the 1959 demolished City Palace on the Alter Markt in the city centre of Potsdam and commenced operation in the year 2014. Alongside offices for members of parliament, parliamentary group staff and the parliamentary administration, it features a large number of meeting and conference rooms. The heart of the State Parliament is the centrally located plenary chamber. The plenary chamber as well as the larger meeting and conference rooms are equipped with complex conference and multimedia systems that were implemented during the construction phase and upgraded during ongoing operations. Given their long service life, the equipment is now largely technologically obsolete and, due to wear and tear, also exhibits declining reliability and functionality, as well as reduced compatibility with current media formats. It is therefore to be renewed, adapted, supplemented and updated in several steps over time through the measure described here. In some cases, components have already been replaced by devices corresponding to the current state of the art. These are to continue to be used and integrated into the new systems. Overview of Equipment The scope of the envisaged measure covers the media-technology equipment of the following rooms: - Plenary chamber with control room, including speaker and interpreter booths - State press conference / visitor room (3-fold partitionable) - 3 meeting rooms on the ground floor - 3 meeting rooms on the first floor (1), partially partitionable - 2 meeting rooms on the second floor (2), partially partitionable - 2 meeting rooms on the third floor (3) - 1 meeting room (secure against eavesdropping) in the basement - Central control room in the lower ground floor - Mobile sound reinforcement including projection The multimedia systems in the plenary chamber and the other large meeting and conference rooms currently consist essentially of the following subsystems: - Video projections or displays - Cameras with controls (including video follows audio) - Conference systems with delegate units - Loudspeaker / PA systems for playback - Video conferencing systems - Vision mixers / scalers - Media control systems For recording and signal playback as well as for AV transmission, all these rooms are networked via a central control room in the lower ground floor using dedicated infrastructure (fibre optics, etc.) via a digital matrix. In addition, a digital signage system with a large number of screens in a server/player architecture is operated within the house network. The focus of the systems is on high reliability as well as ease of use for users and operators. In particular, virtually all components should be centrally operable and capable of being monitored. The aforementioned systems are to retain their fundamental function and structure, but are to be renewed, adapted, supplemented and updated in several steps within the scope of the measure described here. In this context, it must be noted that all affected rooms are fully utilised almost all year round and that, during the planned renewals or adaptations, only minimal operational interruptions are possible outside of times when no meetings are taking place. Scope of Services, Overview The following services are to be tendered: - Preparation of planning documentation: working and assembly planning in consultation with the client - Procurement, installation, configuration and commissioning of all media-technology components - Dismantling and disposal of old technology in consultation with the client The following additional services are to be tendered: - Cabling (local connection cables in the individual rooms, mainly CAT7) - Commissioning and user-appropriate parameterisation - Briefing / training - Documentation - SLA (service level agreement) where applicable with remote maintenance / remote monitoring / remote control - Suitable spare parts package.
sig_5439fdf38566ca016a1f.title: Renewal of media technology
