sig_5477f5bfdf0227efa4b8.description: This is a negotiated procedure with a call for competition in accordance with Section 11 ( 1 ) sentence 1 alternative 2 of the VSVgV. The subject of the contract to be awarded is the procurement for the supply and setup of software as a complete system a) for the analysis, IT-supported comparison and research of mass data in a repository of several partially federated source databases as well as ad-hoc imported data, in particular from the backups of digital evidence by the Polizei SH, b) for the technical integration of existing data sources into a central data integration platform (data integration component). The initial licence requirement comprises 30 concurrent users; the required number of licences for this must be procured. Optionally, there should be the possibility to expand the number to up to 75 concurrent users. This option must be included in the tender; however, the actual take-up is optional. The contracting authority envisages a staggered approach for the further licences to be acquired optionally. The additional licences are offered in stages: Option 1 allows for the procurement of 20 further licences (a total of 50 users), Option 2 for a further 25 licences each, so that a maximum number of 75 users can be reached. The term of the licence is three years from the award of the contract. The contracting authority has the right to extend the term up to three times by twelve months each. Licences acquired within the scope of options 1 and 2 have a term of three years from their provision, which can also be extended three times by twelve months each, but the licences procured through the exercise of options shall end no later than the term of the initially procured base licences. The contracting authority uses an EVB-IT transfer contract Type B, an EVB-IT maintenance contract and an EVB-IT service contract as the basis for the contractual agreement. These will be made available together with the other documents during the tendering phase. The procurement essentially comprises the following services: The rental of a complete system consisting of • analysis software for the comprehensive analysis, IT-supported comparison and research of mass data in the repository of several partially federated source databases as well as ad-hoc imported data, in particular from the backups of digital evidence by the Polizei SH and • a central data integration platform (data integration component) for the integration of existing data sources, which can be installed in the Dataport data centre - on premise. This includes a production, development and test system, which is to be integrated into the existing IT infrastructure of the Polizei SH. Regarding the distinction between data integration and IT-supported comparison and automated data analysis, reference is made to the attached document "Definition of terms for analysis and data integration". Further details can be found in the document "Part A - General Part Call for Competition". The procedure concerns a classified contract in accordance with Section 104 ( 3 ) no. 2 of the GWB or Art. 2 letter b and d of Directive 2009/81/EC and is carried out in accordance with the VSVgV. According to the decision of the public contracting authority, only economic operators resident in an EU Member State or Iceland or Norway are entitled to participate (by application and tender) ("eligible participants"). Applicants and tenderers may not provide for subcontractors in their application and tenders who are resident in a state other than those mentioned in the previous sentence ("third country"). This also applies to any other reliance on the capacities of such companies. For the determination of residence, the definition of origin in Art. 3 ( 1 ) of Regulation (EU) 2022/1031 applies accordingly; for economic operators as groups, Art. 3 ( 2 ) of the aforementioned regulation applies.
sig_5477f5bfdf0227efa4b8.title: Mass data analysis platform - VSVgV

sig_54936bac90e770b5de98.description: Denbighshire County Council (The Authority) are looking to engage with the market in relation to a comprehensive digital solution/s to support and enhance its waste management operations. The Authority is looking for solutions to include Customer Interaction, Operations Management, Route Optimisation and In-Cab Technologies. Aims of Engagement The purpose is to: - Understand supplier capabilities and solutions available in the market - Identify opportunities for innovation and best practice - Understand the customer interaction options available to the Authority, allowing for robust and comprehensive bilingual (Welsh and English) self-service Understand the market’s ability to integrate with existing systems, particularly CRM. - Test assumptions on costs, timescales, and implementation approaches. - Explore data migration options High Level Requirements for Route Optimisation Software. The Authority requires Route Optimisation Software which allows the Authority to: - Minimise travel time and fuel consumption across collection routes - Maximise vehicle utilisation and crew productivity - Adapt to real-time changes such as traffic, missed bins, or service requests - Ensure compliance with service schedules and environmental targets - Provide actionable insights for planning and continuous improvement - Easily update routes to allow for new addresses. The route optimisation software will provide for optimisation of Waste collection routes, Winter Maintenance (gritting) routes, Street Cleansing. The authority is interested in exploring route optimisation solutions that can be expanded into other teams, for example, Passenger Transport. The route optimisation software should also have: - The ability to export routes for loading into the Authority’s Waste Management solution - Import/export capabilities with GIS and the Authority’s Local Land and Property Gazetteer High Level Requirements for In-Cab Technologies. The Authority requires In-Cab technologies to allow the authority to equip waste collection vehicles with integrated in-cab technologies that support real-time communication, route execution, service verification, and health & safety compliance. The solution should have: - A Touchscreen Display Unit which should be Rugged, weather-resistant and interface suitable for vehicle environments, have Real-time route guidance and job list display and interactive map with GPS tracking and bin location overlays - An end-to-end digital customer enquiry process with tasks being received, verified and pushed out to crews to be resolved in real time. - the ability to allocate work and monitor performance against allocations. - An improved customer experience and Performance Indicators (PI) utilised to monitor and continually improve the service. - Increased business intelligence – using data to drive efficiencies and service improvements on a continual basis and provide real data for reporting. The Authority is interested in exploring solutions that support a deployment model whereby all in-cab devices are supplied, owned, and managed directly by the Authority. High Level Requirements for Operations Management. - Comprehensive reporting suite, including dashboards and the ability for the Council to report on any data in the solution - Automated Back-Office Operations - Secure and robust infrastructure supporting GDPR requirements - Subscription management e.g. AHP service and garden waste Lot 1: .

Participation in bilateral discussion, registration for the market consultation, commenting on procurement documents or other participation in the market consultation does not oblige tenderers to participate in the tendering competition and is not a prerequisite for participation in the actual tendering competition later, nor does it affect the tenderer's position in the tendering competition itself. This is not a procurement notice or an invitation to tender, but a notice of the initiation of a market consultation as part of the preparation of the procurement. The actual procurement procedure will be initiated by the publication of a procurement notice. All information in this notice consists of preliminary estimates that are not binding on the contracting authority. The final terms and information relating to the subject matter of the procurement and the procurement process will be published in the actual procurement notice. It should be noted that this notice or the market consultation itself does not oblige Istekki Oy to carry out the procurement in the manner presented in this document or its appendices. sig_559688f76cf5b25e25a5.description: INVITATION TO MARKET DIALOGUE With this RFI Yle invites interested suppliers to participate in the market dialogue held prior publishing the call for tenders (RFP). With this RFI Yle gathers insights and proposals for solutions that will help us achieve a system (or systems), which meets all Yle's requirements as well as both the current and future production needs. The system and all of its components should create an environment, which workflows are easy for users, and which communicates flawlessly with other systems that Yle has. Yle is looking for either a) a single vendor system with all the features or; b) a modular solution from different vendors. The description and object of the RFI, as well as the schedule of the procurement process, are preliminary and Yle will specify the needs and objectives of the procurement in the final RFP. It may also be that no invitation to tender is published in case Yle decides not to proceed with the renewal. At this point Yle is looking to identify the solutions available in the market that could meet Yle’s needs. It is possible that there will be round 2 of RFI before publishing the final request for proposals (RFP). In case, at this point, Yle feels it is needed, we will schedule meetings with the few chosen suppliers. Please see the appendix of this RFI for further information. INTERESTED? Interested suppliers are invited to take part in the market dialogue by sending a request to participate by email to tarjoukset.yle(at)yle.fi at latest by 15th of November 2025. In case you have any questions, please don’t hesitate to contact us. Please include a description or additional appendices covering the following topics in your email: - Description of the solution you provide, including a description of which key features are included in your solution - A short company presentation, including the size of the company in terms of revenue and number of employees. - Your previous experience and few appropriate reference cases. - Reference architecture view - Description of your licence and pricing model - Description of your cyber security policies and continuity planning - Description of your GDPR policies - Your general agreement terms and conditions and description of SLA terms if possible We will review the answers as soon as they are received.

sig_55ff42074617d6c781f4.description: SKI hereby invites tenders for a dynamic purchasing system regarding the procurement of IT consultancy services within 14 service areas with associated sub-areas, sub-categories and services. Below are the 14 service areas with associated sub-areas indicated. The actual services that can be procured in the 14 service areas are described in detail in Appendix C. Subject of the system: Service area 1: IT-related strategies Sub-area: Preparation of IT-related strategies Sub-area: Implementation of IT-related strategies Sub-area: Evaluation and updating as well as impact assessment of strategies Service area 2: Business needs, business case and benefit realisation Sub-area: Identification of business needs and preparation of business cases Sub-area: Realisation of business cases Sub-area: Follow-up on business cases Service area 3: IT tendering Sub-area: Preparation of tenders Sub-area: Execution of tenders Service area 4: IT security, business continuity and IT compliance Sub-area: Establishment of IT security Sub-area: Crisis management, business continuity and disaster recovery Sub-area: IT compliance Service area 5: IT architecture Sub-area: Establishment of an IT architecture Sub-area: Review and adjustment of existing IT architecture Service area 6: IT governance Sub-area: Establishment of IT governance Sub-area: Organisation of system management Sub-area: Establishment of IT supplier management Service area 7: Project and programme management Sub-area: Project management – the traditional waterfall model Sub-area: Management of agile projects Sub-area: Programme management Service area 8: Data processing Sub-area: Data analysis and reporting Sub-area: Use of external data Sub-area: Conversion, cleaning and archiving of data Service area 9: Advice on software licences Sub-area: Open source software vs. closed source software Sub-area: Determination of the size of specific licences, as well as the conditions associated with the use Service area 10: Infrastructure and hardware Sub-area: Setup, configuration and operation of networks Sub-area: Setup, configuration and operation of servers Sub-area: Setup, configuration and operation of clients Service area 11: Test Sub-area: IT testing of development according to the traditional waterfall model Sub-area: Agile IT testing Service area 12: Development of new functionality Sub-area: IT development according to the traditional waterfall model Sub-area: Agile IT development Service area 13: Adaptation of existing IT systems Sub-area: IT development with a view to adapting existing IT systems Service area 14: IT system operation Sub-area: Operation of IT systems The system is divided into 2 categories: • Category 1 Competence purchase • Category 2 Task purchase The same services can be procured in both categories, but the categories differ in that the customer in category 1 must procure one or more specific competence(s), while the customer in category 2 must have a specific task solved. The customer's objective purchasing need thus dictates which category is to be used. • In category 1 the customer specifies their need for competencies within IT consultancy services and need for number of hours, after which the Tenderer offers competencies and prices. • In category 2 the customer defines the task, after which the tenderer offers a task solution in accordance with the customer's statement of requirements. It is voluntary for all SKI's customers, as stated in Appendix B, Customer List, to make use of the system when they need to procure IT consultancy services. Procurement of Competence purchase In category 1 customers can procure IT consultancy services within the 14 service areas described in Appendix C, to fulfil the customer's competence needs. The consultancy services can be procured in 2 ways. 1. Remuneration form 1: Purchase of consultancy hours (number of hours x hourly rate). 2. Remuneration form 2: Purchase of ongoing services (monthly remuneration x number of months + estimated number of hours (time spent) x hourly rate).; Procurement of IT consultancy services for task solution In category 2 the customers can procure IT consultancy services within the 14 service areas described in Appendix C, to fulfil a specific task. The consultancy services can be procured in 3 ways. 1. Remuneration form 1: Purchase of IT consultancy services for the solution of the described task (number x hourly rate). 2. Remuneration form 2: Purchase of ongoing services (monthly remuneration x number of months + estimated number of hours (time spent) x hourly rate). 3. Remuneration form 3: Purchase of task solution at a fixed price.

The procurement comprises the following work packages: Work package 1: Detailed design as preparatory work for the implementation of work package 2 This work package comprises the detailed designs necessary for the provision and, above all, the customising of the data management system. In particular, the following points are to be addressed in the detailed design: - Overall architecture (hardware and software, instance and tenant model) - Data modelling, tagging and representation - Role and rights system, user groups - User interfaces / UI (data input) - Quality standards and duplicate checking or consolidation - Data synchronisation between instances and connectors for importing from external data management systems via API - Implementation of compliance requirements (accessibility, data protection, laws / regulations (EU AI Act, EmpCo etc.)) - Representation of data upon export in data output management - Dashboards for system management and monitoring (KPIs) - Initial data migration for import from existing data inventories Work package 2: Customising (input and output management), incl. data migration, training and documentation At its core, this work package comprises the provision and, above all, the customising of the data management system building upon work package 1. This includes the implementation of standard settings (data model, roles / rights, interfaces, API management, etc.) and the setup of 12 instances incl. data synchronisation. To introduce the system, data migration from legacy systems as well as two legacy APIs (XML) for maintaining data flows for interface consumers to previous data systems must also be implemented. The work package comprises training for the TMB (administrators and operators of regional instances), training materials and documentation. Work package 3: Operation of API management As part of the project, the API infrastructure is to be transitioned from the historically grown logic of XML exports to modern API management. The contractor shall take over ongoing technical operation of the data management system's API management and ensure the reliable, secure and high-performance provision of APIs for the users to be connected. Work package 4: System operation, hosting, support The contractor shall take over ongoing technical operation, hosting and technical support of the data management system, including the system components required for this, and ensure their reliable, secure and high-performance availability during the term of the contract. This includes, in particular, monitoring the system environment, maintenance and updating of the components used, as well as the processing and rectification of technical faults. For the ongoing system operation and hosting of all components, the following services are required, which are to be provided either directly by the contractor or by third parties commissioned by the contractor. In both cases, the contractor is the central point of contact for the contracting authority and must ensure the following requirements (where applicable, together with its subcontractors or the third parties to be designated). Work package 5: Conception and setup / integration of a Graph-RAG-capable infrastructure into the data management system Graph-RAG-capable services are necessary where fact-based, context-sensitive answers from curated content are to be generated using AI systems, for example in the tourism network (as a state-wide information system e.g. for tourist information offices), in service assistants, chatbots or in internal knowledge systems. To become future-proof in this area, this work package is being tendered. Work package 6: Operation of a Graph-RAG-capable infrastructure The contractor shall take over the technical operation of the Graph-RAG-capable infrastructure provided for the TMB and ensure its reliable, secure and high-performance use during the term of the contract. Operation comprises in particular the availability of the required components for semantic search and the provision of knowledge for connected applications. Work package 7: Further development of the data management system and connected components This work package serves for the calculation of further development orders that are triggered and implemented via individual commissioning. Work package 8: Consulting for API management The contractor shall support the TMB in advising and supporting the approximately 200 existing and newly added users of the data management system's APIs. The aim is to provide API users with professional and technical support in the individual use, configuration and further development of their data connections and to ensure the most frictionless possible use of the data streams provided. The volume of the contract is estimated at 332.500,00 Euro for a period of four years. Lot LOT-0001: Provision, customising, operation and further development of a state-wide tourist data management system. The procurement is associated with the following needs and requirements (objectives): Against the background of new strategic and legal bases (Brandenburg tourism strategy (2023), TMB corporate concept (2025), EU Artificial Intelligence Act or the Artificial Intelligence Regulation, among others) on the one hand, and general developments in the field of digitalisation (in particular AI) on the other, the TMB wishes to procure a new uniform data management system as the basis for work in the Brandenburg content network. At its core, a data management system for all kinds and

types of data and content (B2C and B2B) with the following components are to be provided: - Input management / maintenance layer - AI and service layer - Output management / distribution layer The targeted target architecture is based on technologies established on the market, maintainable and manageable by personnel, as well as open standards. To safeguard digital sovereignty, proprietary special developments are deliberately avoided in favour of modular, future-proof software structures. A consistent API-first approach is also intended to ensure that individual functional modules can be replaced and expanded at any time independently of the manufacturer and seamlessly connected to any third-party systems. The current separation of POIs and tours (DAMAS), events (TDH) and media (media archive) is to be consolidated into a single data management system. This also applies to the content of the B2B portal as well as the portals of the B2C website frameworks. This is intended to promote the implementation of a "headless CMS approach", which aims for a complete separation of content and design. In its current form, data management is - for historical reasons - centrally structured. Control and coordination of the system lies with the TMB. For example, all tenants are created by the TMB (incl. user management, rights control, contractual matters, etc.). In the future system, a less hierarchical and flexible system is to be applied. In this context, the eleven travel regions of the state are taking on a more central role than previously. They are to receive their own instances of the state system, for example to manage regional editors independently. The regional instances are technically completely independent systems. Therefore, this is not a classic central tenant system with merely logically separated views of a state-wide data inventory. Rather, each instance has its own data storage or database with its own tenant structure. Data exchange is to take place via defined synchronisation mechanisms between the independent instances. Database architecture - Central data input for the TMB and the Brandenburg content network is distributed, as shown above, across the POI database DAMAS, the events database (TDH) and the media archive. Thus, apart from the geographic information system QGIS, there is no centralised and generic data storage. The main objective is to operate only a single system for data and content management. This also applies to the currently standalone B2B portal and the portals of the B2C website frameworks. - The architecture is to be decentralised at the same time by implementing an instance model in order to utilise the advantages of state-wide cooperation while also enabling the individuality of partners, in particular the travel regions. This enables a lean standard roles and rights system that can be differentiated within the instances. - The data model is being further developed - building upon the integration of data from the databases described above and the previously separate B2B data. A data model for all data types is designed as a state standard. - A state-wide quality standard is being introduced. - The merging of all data and content into a uniform data model and technical infrastructure provides the basis for implementing a "headless CMS approach". Input management - There is to be only a single interface for entering data and content. - Content is to be importable from external systems into the state system via API. - The use of responsive, as accessible as possible input interfaces is aimed for. AI and service layer - Data entry is to be largely automated with the support of AI applications. - Provision of AI-driven dashboards for management and monitoring of the database as well as an associated task manager. - Development and management of a Graph-RAG-capable infrastructure as the basis for internal knowledge systems and guest services Output management - Provision of an easy-to-use management interface for output management - Provision of configurable standard APIs (REST / GraphQL) - Provision of connectors to common inventory systems - Provision of configurable accessible widgets - Provision of a configurable MCP server and a WebMCP service - Provision of a reading WebDAV interface for media, with which data can be displayed directly, e.g. as directories in Windows Explorer - Provision of a media portal on which media is made available for download by various interested parties with the stored licences.

sig_57834ae89fbcdf435cb5.description: RVK is a modern transport company that has been under municipal ownership since 1996. The company was formed in 1976 through a merger of railway and postal omnibus services. Its transport area extends across the Rheinisch-Bergischer Kreis, the left-bank Rhein-Sieg-Kreis, the Euskirchen district, and the cities of Cologne, Bonn, Leverkusen, Hürth, Brúhl, and Wesseling. RVK thus connects urban population centres with sparsely populated, rural areas. With capacity, competence, and years of experience, RVK ensures that people in the region travel reliably and safely – in an environmentally friendly, sustainable, and innovative manner. The RVK bus fleet comprises over 600 vehicles, some of which are operated independently and some on behalf of RVK. The transport network encompasses 132 routes with a total length of 2.595 km. In addition, 58 routes are operated by RVK for other transport companies. In total, RVK provides a transport performance of approx. 22,6 million km with approx. 23 million passengers annually. In order to successfully drive forward the vision of sustainable, clean mobility in the service area in the future and thus sustainably reduce local pollutant emissions, Regionalverkehr Köln GmbH (RVK) is implementing extensive measures for digitalisation and networking, and thereby more attractive public transport to reduce NOx and other pollutant emissions, as part of its internal "Null Emission" project (https://www.rvk.de/projekt-null-emission). Based on successful projects in the field of sales backend systems with electronic tickets, subscription online (Abo-Online), and digital timetable information, a stable basis for central customer management has already been established. The planned measure of developing a mobility app within the framework of the "Mobility App and Platform" project builds upon these existing structures and must be seamlessly integrated into the existing sales landscape. As part of this new measure, which is particularly tailored to rural areas, a multitude of previously analogue or isolated mobility offerings are to be bundled into an integrated, intermodal mobility app. Both regional and interregional transport services will be integrated to give users seamless access to various forms of mobility. The project is funded by the Federal Ministry of Transport (BMV). The approval period is fixed until 31.12.2026 and cannot be extended. Encompasses the programming of frontend, backend, and interfaces as well as the integration of the application into the existing system landscape.; Development of a user-centred design concept including UX design, design system, wireframes, prototyping, and accessible design. The results serve as the basis for technical implementation in Lot 1. Both lots are closely related from a technical perspective and will be implemented in parallel or sequentially. sig_57ee5d561469897c12b5.description: The purpose of this Notice is to invite market operators to a Market Engagement Event for the potential future exercise to procure services supporting the development of an innovative obesity pathway in North East and North Cumbria on Thursday 8th January at 10:45 via Teams Integrated Care Board (NENC ICB) is developing a new, community-first obesity pathway as part of the Obesity Pathway Innovation Programme (OPIP). The pathway will support adults with obesity who are waiting lists or at risk of economic activity due to obesity and related long-term conditions. To enable this at scale, NENC ICB is exploring options to procure a digital partner to provide an integrated platform that will act as the digital "spine" for the pathway. The intended service is expected to support the following: 1. Identification and invitation of eligible patients (for example via population-health tools and waiting-list data) 2. Digital referral, consent and triage 3. Patient-facing tools for self-assessment, remote monitoring and behavioural support (including AI meal planning) 4. Role based portals for community pharmacies, specialist teams and programme staff. The platform will need to integrate with existing NHS systems (for example NHS App, GP clinical systems and provider electronic patient records), support high standards of clinical safety, information governance and cybersecurity, and generate data and dashboards required for independent evaluation of outcomes, equity and value for money. This Market Engagement Event is intended to help NENC ICB understand the capabilities, innovations and constraints within the digital health market, and to test our emerging requirements and delivery approach. sig_581f3be67b191e7d1eff.description: The aim of the project is the implementation of the new Diavgeia taking into account modern institutional, operational and technological developments, the more correct implementation of the institutional framework with emphasis on the General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR) and the optimal utilisation of Diavgeia information with a data-based architecture and secondarily document-based. The project seeks to increase the efficiency and productivity of public services by enriching the applications of the Diavgeia Programme, supplementing functionality for the collaborative drafting and management of documents to be published based on standardised documents and data structures, and also to add value to the Programme by utilising and enriching the information gathered within it through the use of other information sources with the aim of creating a system of complex reports and other complementary application subsystems and solutions. The new system will allow the monitoring of the operation and organisational structure of public administration in combination with information related to the competences of bodies in the context of multi-level governance and also of personnel as recorded in the Human Resources Register of the Hellenic Republic. The aim is to provide objective evidence for the implementation of the National Administrative Procedures Policy and the prioritisation of the actions of the National Programme for Administrative Simplification. To this end, care has been taken to significantly enhance its interoperability with third-party public sector systems for the dissemination of information without necessarily requiring intervention from the end user. Additionally, through the expansion of information kept in a structured manner (metadata set), it will be possible to capture data groups with special characteristics that enhance transparency at the level of monitoring/evaluation by the general public of indicators related to, for example, the operation and structure of public administration and/or financial figures (public spending). For this purpose, data from other sources and publicly available data will also be utilised to support the monitoring of the operation and action of bodies and to support decision-making. The solution will include the creation of a system for the correct (and as complete as possible per sector) structured collection and processing of data from various public data sources and subsequently making them available to the general public. Illustrative examples of sources are data from systems under development for GOV ERP, HRMS, the Civil Society Organisations Register, ESIDIS, KHMDIS. A distinct subsystem will be developed for further utilisation and extraction of specialised reports with the aim of monitoring the structure, operation and action of public administration as well as monitoring expenditure and procurement and supporting the decision-making process. The system will be scalable for the addition of new sources arising from other actions. Also, within the framework of the action, improvements will be made in relation to identified problems associated with the management of the very large volume of documents collected by Diavgeia at a sharply increasing rate, which also led to the necessary migration of the infrastructure to public cloud services. In this context, advanced services provided by public clouds will be better utilised in order to ensure the uninterrupted provision of services and the monitoring of their provision at the lowest possible cost. The action, taking into account the life cycle of the administrative documents that are published, will address challenges such as the cleaning of multiple copies of the same documents, the extraction of all information in data format and the optimisation of the quality of Diavgeia metadata as well as the automatic publication of important data sets in the central open public data repository www.data.gov.gr. The project also aims to adopt a new architecture that will allow a drastic reduction, by at least 65%, of the required storage space and computational resources while ensuring the proper functioning of the system. To achieve the above goal, both emerging artificial intelligence and language model technologies and techniques for the correct entry of metadata into relevant information will be utilised to facilitate their search, categorisation and utilisation. This contract concerns a single subject matter and is not subdivided into lots due to the project's architecture, the strong interdependencies and complementarity of the individual services that compose it, as well as the high interoperability requirements that must be ensured on the one hand between the functional units (subsystems) to be developed within the framework of this project and on the other hand with third-party systems of Hellenic Republic bodies. The non-subdivision of the contract enhances the quality and security of the project, since unified management reduces the chances of security gaps or incompatibilities appearing between the different systems and facilitates the coordination of its implementation. The duration of the contract is set at thirty-two (32) months including the procedure for checking and acceptance of deliverables. The contract will be awarded on the basis of the most economically advantageous tender, based on the best price-quality ratio. [para. 1.3. & ANNEX I of the Call for Tenders]
sig_581f3be67b191e7d1eff.title: «Restructuring of the DIAYGEIA Programme - DIAYGEIA III»

sig_585545d84402cc436169.description: Iarnród Éireann (IÉ) currently operates and maintains a national GSM-R mobile network which provides driver to CTC communications via on-board GSM-R cab-mobile equipment provided by Siemens Mobility. Currently, GSM-R is in operation on the DART network, with national rollout expected to occur in 2026 on the rest of IE’s fleets. As part of the overall maintenance of the GSM-R mobile network, IÉ carry out monitoring and drive- testing which at present requires IÉ Telecoms personnel to perform this task. The task requires staff to travel onboard IÉ Trainsets with monitoring equipment, which can be both onerous and time consuming. IÉ require the provision of an automated drive-testing and RF monitoring solution that will negate the requirement for staff to travel. To achieve this requirement, it is therefore required to provide a GSM-R Modem and hardware (option)/software/firmware capable of interfacing with the modem and providing the end-user (IE) with a HTTP REST API. This can be integrated with the existing IÉ hosted servers which run a combination of NodeJS applications, InfluxDB and Grafana for recording and visualization of the obtained data or hosted on a supplier provided cloud-based solution that is accessible by IÉ. sig_5969e08dd968e183af0a.description: Helse Sør-Øst c/o Sykehuspartner would like to gain better insight into existing and new technological systems in electronic maternity journals. The aim is to gather information on available systems, understand the market ́s capacity and gain insight into current and future systems connected to this area. The electronic maternity journal is used in the health service to document and follow-up information related to pregnancy, birth and childcare. The electronic maternity journal is currently in use at 8 health authorities in Helse Sør-Øst RHF. The system is closely integrated with the central electronic patient journal system (EPJ) and supports the entire patient pathway connected to pregnancy, birth and childcare. The system also meets the requirements for obligatory reports to national authorities, including the Medical Birth Register and The Norwegian Tax Administration.The current system serves approx. 3,500 users divided in 2,700 PCs and covers 8 health trusts and 18 maternity wards. Sykehusinnkjøp HF is carrying out the market survey on behalf of Sykehuspartner HF. Attention is also agreed that the market survey is non binding and does not involve an obligation to hold a competition or enter into a contract. Deadline for replying: 30 September 2025 (10:00). Answers are to be sent in the communication module.

sig_59fd16c23a30647b6211.description: This is not a procurement notice or a call for tenders, but a Request for Information directed at potential Suppliers. Therefore, no tenders are requested or to be submitted in response to this request for information. No comments or questions received via the request for information will be answered. One of the tasks of the Finnish National Agency for Education is the publishing of learning materials and publications. Customers include both private individuals and organisations, in particular schools and educational institutions. Products are delivered to the customer either physically (e.g. textbooks) or digitally (e.g. electronic learning materials). We request up-to-date information on a comprehensive service encompassing product logistics, licensing, and online shop services. The service to be procured includes • a SaaS online shop solution where customers can purchase non-fiction books, textbooks, publications, and licences for digital learning materials published by the Finnish National Agency for Education, as well as downloadable files, using commonly used payment methods • a logistics and distribution service for textbooks and publications, including distribution to key resellers such as Library Service, bookshops, and learning material intermediaries • a digital product licence management service, and • a sales settlement service, including inventory value reporting. Service requirements • The online shop must serve our customers in Finnish, Swedish, and English. • The service must meet the accessibility requirements of the Act on the Provision of Digital Services. • It shall be possible to integrate the service with the Finnish National Agency for Education's digital learning platform (licence management) and product register. • The online shop solution must provide the capability for the Finnish National Agency for Education to edit the layout, texts, and settings of the online shop. In addition, it must be possible to add sample pages, reading samples, and promotional videos to the online shop. We request the following information 1. Does the Supplier have a comprehensive service meeting the above description to offer? 2. What pricing model does the Supplier use? 3. Based on the above description, does the Supplier have any comments on the potential requirement specification for the procurement? 4. Optional additional question: The Finnish National Agency for Education is exploring alternatives to replace its self-developed product information system and royalty register. Is it possible to tailor a product and royalty register into the Supplier's service that includes the necessary databases and user interface? The request for information does not oblige the contracting authority to carry out the actual procurement or to implement it in the manner described in the request for information. The contracting authority is not obliged to take account of responses received to the request for information when drawing up the call for tenders. Responding to the request for information does not bind the tenderer or affect the tenderer's position in any potential procurement procedure. No compensation will be paid for responding to the request for information or for any product demonstration.
sig_59fd16c23a30647b6211.title: Request for information: The Finnish National Agency for Education's logistics and user licence service for fee-charging products as well as an online shop

This procurement forms part of the project "Transformation of public services through digitalisation in Comuna Chetani, Mureș County", financed through the Central Regional Programme 2021–2027, within project call PRC/444/PRC_P2/OP1, and aligns with the objective of supporting the digital development of the Commune of Chetani Town Hall. It targets the development, testing and piloting of two innovative digital solutions: a front-office type solution and a back-office type solution, intended to improve the interaction between the authority and the citizen/taxpayer and to facilitate access. The project supports the transition to an intelligent and innovative economy. In the context of a decentralised software infrastructure within the town hall, where each department uses specific software, the need is highlighted for two integrated solutions that unify e-government services and document management, ensuring the traceability of the town hall's internal and external activities. Thus, the project pursues the development, testing and piloting of two complex digital solutions: 1. The front-office digital solution – an online solution that facilitates the digitalisation of public administration by offering online services by the ATU to citizens, supporting the interaction between the Town Hall and the citizen/taxpayer. The front-office solution is designed to optimise the flow of information between the Town Hall and citizens, addressing both individuals and legal entities. The platform will allow users intuitive and efficient access to relevant and personalised information. The front-office solution will include the following: Info-kiosk application (IoT); Digital solution for offering online services Tax online services, Digital solution for offering online services regarding the agricultural register, Digital solution for urban planning online services, Information publication and management portal, Local Official Gazette digital solution, Participatory budgeting mechanism, Online communication solution for data and documents with judicial executor offices, Digital solution for offering online services to citizens, Mobile device application with shared services addressed to citizens 2. The back-office digital solution – an integrated computer system intended for the automation, streamlining and securing of the institution's internal workflows and supporting collaboration between departments. Designed to centralise and manage data and administrative processes, this system includes functionalities adapted to the operational specifics of local public administration, ensuring optimised management of internal activities. The front office solution will include the following: Digital Document Management solution, Registry Module, Mobile solution for the inventory of fixed assets and inventory items, Digital solution for ROeID, Electronic archive solution, Cyber security solution of IDS type, Citizen and address data aggregator (web and mobile), prescriptive debits management module, treasury import solution, F2201/F2202 / Garnishments, Court of Accounts Module, Communication of documents and data in structured electronic format with the DRPCIV, Video surveillance solution, Information application regarding energy efficiency. sig_5a32dbec0ca34f9d4152.description: The subject of the contract is the implementation of Sub-Project 2 "Strengthening of the RAA and Development of Social Innovation" of the Action "Support Mechanism of the Regional Coordination Authority of Thessaly for the development of social innovation as a means to address the crisis", with MIS code 6039177. The purpose of the contract is the operational strengthening of the RAA and the creation of a functional cooperation and social innovation mechanism, with the aim of supporting employment, social inclusion, social entrepreneurship and the resilience of the affected areas of Thessaly. Sub-Project 2 "Strengthening of the RAA and Development of Social Innovation" concerns the creation of a permanent COOPERATION NETWORK FOR SOCIAL INNOVATION, the strengthening of human resources and the skills development of the Regional Coordination Authority and the members of the NETWORK, the development of a culture of social entrepreneurship, the interconnection of the RAA with European social innovation networks, as well as the creation of the necessary digital applications that will contribute to the sustainability of the RAA and of the COOPERATION NETWORK FOR SOCIAL INNOVATION. It also concerns the provision of consultancy and support to affected persons for their activation in social innovation actions, the implementation of pilot social entrepreneurship actions and civil protection volunteer groups
sig_5a32dbec0ca34f9d4152.title: SUB-PROJECT 2 Strengthening of the RAA and Development of Social Innovation

sig_5a8a8674fd6defb8d9a6.description: The subject of the contract is the implementation and maintenance of an Information Security Management System (ISMS) and a SOC, along with training, at the Prof. W. Orłowski Independent Public Clinical Hospital of the Centre of Postgraduate Medical Education in Warsaw, which has been divided into two packages. Package no. 1 - Implementation and maintenance of an Information Security Management System (ISMS) The subject of the contract is the implementation and maintenance for the Contracting Authority of an Information Security Management System (ISMS) compliant with the PN-EN ISO/IEC 27001:2023-08 standard, covering: a) the drawing up of comprehensive ISMS documentation and procedures, including an Information Security Policy, operational procedures and incident response procedures, b) the implementation of the ISMS within the Contracting Authority's structures, together with appropriate technical and organisational configuration guidelines, c) the planning of processes for monitoring the effectiveness of the implemented ISMS and its continuous improvement, d) the provision of training to the Contracting Authority's personnel: e-learning training on the implemented ISMS documentation and raising awareness in the field of cybersecurity (cyber hygiene) — for current and future employees — as well as on-site training for the Contracting Authority's manager. e) the maintenance and improvement of the ISMS for a period from the implementation and formal handover of the ISMS up to 36 months from the date of signing the contract, covering periodic ISMS reviews, the updating of documentation and the risk register, compliance reviews, support during inspections and audits, and recommendations for corrective and improvement actions. A detailed description of the subject of the contract concerning package no. 1 can be found in attachment no. 2 to the SWZ. Package no. 2 - Provision of a Security Operations Centre service (SOC Service) The subject of the contract is the provision of a Security Operations Centre service (hereinafter: SOC Service), covering: a) The SOC Service shall be provided for a period of 36 months from the date of conclusion of the contract (including pre-implementation analysis and commissioning). b) The SOC Service must be performed by an entity providing cybersecurity services that meets the organisational and technical conditions resulting from the Act of 5 July 2018 on the national cybersecurity system, in the wording in force from 3 April 2026 (amended by the Act of 23 January 2026, Journal of Laws of 2026, item 252), and the implementing acts to this Act. c) The SOC Service shall be provided in real time, on a continuous basis, 24 hours a day, 7 days a week, for 365 days a year (24/7/365). d) For the purposes of providing the SOC Service, the Contractor shall provide a SIEM system and an Incident Management System in a service model, on the Contractor's platform or within the Contracting Authority's infrastructure, together with documentation and technical support for the entire duration of the provision of the SOC Service. e) The operational procedures of the SOC Service (incident classification, response scenarios, playbooks) must be consistent with the ISMS documentation being prepared under this procedure, in particular with the major incident management procedure and the logging and monitoring policy. A detailed description of the subject of the contract concerning package no. 2 can be found in attachment no. 3 to the SWZ. The Contracting Authority does not require the submission of evidentiary means regarding the subject matter together with the tender. Information on evidentiary means regarding the parties can be found in Chapter 8 of the Specification of Contract Conditions. A detailed description of the subject of the contract constitutes attachment no. 2 to the SWZ.; A detailed description of the subject of the contract constitutes attachment no. 3 to the SWZ.

sig_5a9387b58d272c68c288.description: The International Charter: Space and Major Disasters (“the Charter”) is a global agreement which aims to provide a unified system of space data acquisition and delivery to those affected by natural or man-made disasters. It provides and enables transmission of earth observation satellite data and pre-authorised resilience/emergency response bodies in response to “activations”. Further details on the Charter can be found at https://disasterscharter.org/ Unlike many space faring nations in the Charter, the UK Government does not own or operate its own national EO satellite system assets. The UK Government therefore fulfils its Charter commitments through partnership with the UK EO commercial sector. This procurement seeks to maintain and strengthen that model by securing operational support from an organisation with UK licensed and operated EO satellite data assets that can be contributed to Charter activations. The continued participation of UK EO commercial satellite operators in the Charter delivers both public benefit and strategic value by showcasing sovereign EO capabilities, supporting international disaster response and demonstrating operational utility of UK-developed EO missions. The Contracting Authority is intending to launch this requirement by the 9th of October - prospective bidders should note it may launch earlier at the Contracting Authority's discretion: all dates provided are estimates at this stage. Lot 1: . None

sig_5b301cb276368d0fd0c5.description: Forest management services will be awarded in the year 2026 (field phase 2027) by concluding a public procurement contract for the Sascut Forestry Office. The total area of the Sascut Forestry Office is 6725,70 ha. The services involve the development of the forest management plan, a product of the management activity with technical-organisational content, ecologically grounded, through which, for a period of time, the works necessary to be executed in a production unit are established, for the purpose of bringing and, subsequently, maintaining the structural characteristics of the stands and the forest as a whole to the values corresponding to the optimal structural model defined in accordance with the ecological, social and economic objectives pursued through sustainable management. According to the provisions of Art. 63 para. (11) of Law no. 331/2024 regarding the Forestry Code, with subsequent amendments and additions, it is necessary that the development of forest management plans be carried out through public procurement procedures. The management of the state-owned public forest fund constitutes a priority obligation of the forest fund administrators. The method of managing the state-owned public forest fund is regulated by forest management plans. Forest management plans and their amendments are approved by order of the head of the Authority. In the case of state-owned public lands, the management plans provide data and information necessary for their registration/updating in the centralised inventory of state public domain assets and for registration in the integrated cadastre and land registry system. Requests for clarification formulated by tenderers during the advertising period of the participation notice can be made with a deadline of at most 15 days before the deadline for the submission of tenders. The contracting authority will respond to all requests for clarification formulated in compliance with the above deadline, once, in a consolidated manner, 10 days before the deadline for the submission of tenders. Services for the development of the forest management plan for the state-owned public forest fund managed by the Bacau Forestry Directorate – Sascut Forestry Office, field phase 2027, for the area of 6725,70 ha. The services include preparatory works, field data collection, data processing and drafting of the forest management plan, development of the GIS database and management maps, preparation of the necessary environmental documentation, obtaining the regulatory act issued by the competent authority for environmental protection, supporting the documentation within the Technical Commission for Forestry Approval (CTAS) and obtaining the order for the approval of the forest management plan.
sig_5b301cb276368d0fd0c5.title: Forest management services-Sascut Forestry Office 2026 DSBC

sig_5b6f66aa5bfd3cada2e4.description: Verkehrsgesellschaft Landkreis Gifhorn mbH (VLG) intends to gradually convert its bus fleet to electromobility within the framework of the requirements of the Clean Vehicles Procurement Act. For this purpose, electric buses and the charging infrastructure required for their operation are to be procured and integrated into operational processes. VLG plans to initially provide charging infrastructure for initially 11 vehicles by the year 2027. A charging and load management system is to be introduced for the centralised control and monitoring of charging processes, for limiting grid load as well as for supporting operational vehicle dispatching and vehicle stabling. With the introduction of electromobility, additional requirements arise for the planning and control of vehicle deployment, charging processes and available electrical power. Vehicle availability, battery charge state, energy demand, planned departure times, charging point occupancy and available grid capacity must in future be brought together and taken into account in a system-supported manner. The initial expansion stage comprises the charging infrastructure for 11 vehicles. The exact number and design of the charging points, their technical properties as well as the operational systems and data sources to be integrated are described in a binding manner in the quantity framework, in the interface descriptions and in the appendices to this specification. The increasing requirements in the course of the progressive electrification of the bus fleet as well as the expansion of the charging infrastructure require a high-performance charging, load and energy management system. With the introduction of an LMS, charging processes are to be controlled taking into account the boundary conditions from charging infrastructure, vehicle data, battery charge states and range requirements. The LMS must control the charging processes in such a way that the charge states required for the planned vehicle deployment are reached in good time. The charging infrastructure is to be integrated into the LMS so that the status of the charging units can be centrally monitored and controlled.
sig_5b6f66aa5bfd3cada2e4.title: Procurement and introduction of a charging management system for VLG

sig_5bd60a64138ad98ac5e2.description: The Scottish Government is pursuing a comprehensive programme to reform and modernise Scotland’s compulsory purchase system. Lot 1: . The overall aim of this research is to provide information about the compensation received by those whose land is acquired under compulsory purchase powers. The evidence generated through the research is intended to inform decisions on potential future legislation by the Scottish Government and scrutiny of any such legislation by the Scottish Parliament. The objectives of the project are to address the following questions: a. How frequently and to what extent are compensation payments affected by the prospect of future planning permission (“hope value”)? b. In cases where hope value is a factor, to what extent are payments affected by the timing, costs and risks of implementing any such prospective planning permission? c. To what extent does the current condition of property affect the market value calculated for the purpose of compensation?
sig_5bd60a64138ad98ac5e2.title: Compulsory Purchase Compensation Research

sig_5c570f68fc4d8b9d2297.description: Our Workplace Innovation Leadership Academy supports the ongoing development of business leaders at all levels and stages of experience. The Leadership Academy delivers programmes under a framework agreement with multiple suppliers across the Scottish Enterprise area, the programme plays a key role in cultivating leadership capability and innovation within businesses. The current framework expires early April 2026 and we anticipate commencing a new procurement process in December 2025. To inform this process, we are seeking to engage with the market to better understand current capabilities and approaches to delivering high-impact leadership development. We welcome expressions of interest from suppliers who possess specialist knowledge, proven experience, and the capacity to deliver innovative and effective leadership programmes tailored to diverse business needs. The Workplace Innovation Leadership Development Framework will consist of a series of one-day workshops, one-to-one coaching sessions, and topic specific diagnostic tools, delivered over a period of 2 - 6 months, depending on the Lot. Delivery will follow a hybrid model, combining online and face-to-face formats to maximise accessibility and impact. The Framework will deliver programmes across the Scottish Enterprise area, responding to demand. Where appropriate, programmes may also be delivered in collaboration with other enterprise agencies across Scotland. Lot 1: Transformational Leadership Programme. A cohesive leadership programme designed for both emerging and established leaders, with consistent core themes and tailored content to reflect each group's unique needs and experiences. Lot 2: Innovating Leadership: AI, Data & Emerging Tech. To empower leaders to embed AI, data, and emerging tech into strategy, foster ethical leadership, and drive internal innovation in a tech-enabled world. Lot 3: Growth Through Risk & Ambition. To support leaders in evaluating growth strategies, embracing risk as a catalyst for innovation, and exploring strategic options like investment, mergers, and ESG-aligned finance. Encourages a culture of learning through experimentation. Lot 4: Leadership in Times of Geopolitical & Economic Volatility. Helps leaders build resilience, agility, change capability and foresight to lead through uncertainty, global disruption, and change—while staying focused on long-term sustainability and stakeholder trust.
sig_5c570f68fc4d8b9d2297.title: Workplace Innovation Leadership Development Programme (P26-0006)

sig_5c727857a741fda27c52.description: The Norwegian Defence Materiel Agency (FMA) is the contracting authority and responsible for implementing the procurement. FMA is a part of the defence sector, directly under the Ministry of Defence (FD). FMA shall ensure that the Norwegian Armed Forces and other entities in the defence sector have access to cost efficient and secure material and services in line with approved long-term plans. FMA ́s main assignments are planning, procurement, management and disposal of material for the Norwegian Armed Forces and other departments under FD. Organisational reasons can be required during the contract period to transfer the resource to Cyber Defence ́s IT Department (CIT) DRIV. DRIV is responsible for the technical operation and further development (DEVSECOPS) of the Joint Integrated Management System (FIF). FIF is a SAP ERP system integrated with a number of other different applications. Internal processes are based on flexible frameworks (Scrum, SAFE), the Security Act and different industry standards for safety and ITIL for operation. DRIV consists of approx. 150 persons, most of whom are located in Oslo. Both employees and consultants staff the organisation. The aim of this notice is to fill the role of Process Consultant for Signavio modelling and integrations between SolutionManager 7.2 and Signavio in project P1160 "Critical Upgrade of ERP". The role shall contribute with competence in modelling in Signavio, assistance with the integration between Signavio and SolutionManager 7.2 and assist teams in process modelling. The role will work closely with the manager of Value Management Office, the solution architects and the different product teams. The role can involve cooperation with other departments and/or projects in the Norwegian Armed Forces.
sig_5c727857a741fda27c52.title: Procurement of a Signavio Process Modeling Consultant

sig_5cb6de6c4d3736be684f.description: Description: The State of Saxony-Anhalt has its own state data network, which is currently operated technically by an IT service provider. The state data network was set up by this IT service provider. The intention now is to retender the operation of the state data network as a high-performance and integrated state data network (LAN/WAN) as well as all measures and services necessary for this. The operation of the operations centre with, among other things, network-related services, the operation of components and systems within a data centre and necessary operational and technical tools are also to be awarded. To prepare for this retender, the MID as the responsible authority for the State of Saxony-Anhalt is conducting a market exploration in accordance with § 28 of the VgV. The aim is in particular to explore what organisational, technical and economic solutions are available on the market to ensure operation on a permanent, secure, reliable and scalable basis, as well as the conditions that may be necessary for this and the general time schedule. This is expressly not a call for competition or any other bidding procedure, but rather a non-binding market analysis for orientation and as a basis for decision-making for the preparation of any subsequent procurement procedure. Companies that wish to participate in the market exploration will be provided with further documents in the market exploration procedure. In order to gain access to these documents, an expression of interest and the submission of a non-disclosure agreement are required to protect sensitive data regarding critical infrastructure. Interested parties are therefore requested to express their interest in participating in the present market exploration procedure by 28.11.2025 at the latest by sending an email with the subject 'Market exploration procedure state data network' to the following email address: lnstender@sachsen-anhalt.de and stating the necessary contact details (name of the company, registered office of the company, address of the company and email address). You will then receive a draft non-disclosure agreement, which must then be completed and returned signed. Upon receipt of the non-disclosure agreement, the further documents for the market exploration will be sent to the interested parties concerned. These contain further information and documents. It is planned to conduct online market exploration discussions with the interested parties. These are expected to be scheduled in the four calendar weeks following the above-mentioned deadline. To prepare for the discussions, participants are asked to complete and submit a prepared questionnaire. Further information on this can be found in the market exploration documents, which will be made available after the submission of the non-disclosure agreement.
sig_5cb6de6c4d3736be684f.title: Market consultation on the operation of the state data network

sig_5cc4c0f83b92a53b2a33.description: The contractor shall provide Ground Ambulance Services at Fort Polk, LA in accordance with the Performance Work Statement included in the SF1449. All offerors shall provide the following items: Please complete the SF1449: Blocks 17 (to include the CAGE code and the Unique Entity ID Number) and 30 A - C. Please provide a statement that the offeror will hold its price firm for at least 90 days from the due date for receipt of proposals, subject to any changes that may occur as a result of discussions (if applicable). Please complete the provisions, as listed in the solicitation. Alternately, complete all provisionsin System for Award Management (SAM) and provide confirmation of completion and accuracywith offer. Potential contractors must be registered in SAM to be eligible for award. The SAM website is http://www.sam.gov. Proposals are due by no later than (NLT) 8:00 AM/CDT on 21 October 2026. Proposals shall be submitted via email to marc.a.flores3.civ@health.mil and salameya.paulouskaya2.civ@health.mil. Proposals received after the deadline will be considered untimely and will not be eligible for award. Questions are due by NLT 8:00 AM/CDT on 24 September 2026. All questions must be submitted in writing to marc.a.flores3.civ@health.mil and salameya.paulouskaya2.civ@health.mil. Electronic submissions with files larger than 20MB will need to be submitted in separate emails. All emails, regardless of the size, need to be received by the Government server, by the stated date and time. It is the offeror's responsibility to ensure the Government receives the entire proposal Factor 1. Technical: The technical proposal shall be addressed in sufficient written detail for the Government to determine if the Offeror understands the technical aspects of the Government's requirement. Offerors shall demonstrate how they will comply with the following subfactors: Subfactor 1: Technical Capabilities: - Offeror shall submit a detailed technical approach demonstrating its ability to perform all requirements of the Performance Work Statement (PWS), including the full range of ground ambulance services required under the contract. - Offeror shall provide management and operational plans, including safety procedures, staffing, training, quality control, and transition/start-up timelines from contract award through full operational capability. - Offeror shall provide a contingency plan addressing staffing shortages, vehicle breakdowns, severe weather, communications failures, emergency evacuations, and continuity of operations. - Offeror shall demonstrate its capability to respond to multiple simultaneous emergency dispatches, peak workload periods, and installation training events while maintaining required response times. - Offeror shall demonstrate its ability to provide and sustain the required staffing, vehicles, equipment, and operational resources necessary to support continuous 24-hour, 7-day, 365-day emergency medical services. - Offeror shall demonstrate its understanding of and ability to comply with all applicable Federal, State of Louisiana, Department of Defense, DHA, Army EMS, OSHA, HIPAA, and other regulatory requirements governing contract performance. Subfactor 2: Personnel Qualifications and Staffing - Offeror shall provide a staffing plan identifying labor categories, staffing levels, work schedules, and surge staffing capability necessary to meet all Performance Work Statement (PWS) requirements. - Offeror shall provide an organizational chart identifying key personnel, including the Program Manager, EMS Medical Director, Paramedics, and EMTs. - Offeror shall provide resumes for all key personnel demonstrating the education, certifications, licensure, qualifications, and experience required to perform the services outlined in the PWS. - Offeror shall demonstrate its ability to recruit, retain, and sustain qualified personnel while maintaining required staffing levels and minimizing vacancies to ensure uninterrupted mission support. Subfactor 3: Vehicle and Equipment Maintenance - Offeror shall provide a comprehensive vehicle and equipment maintenance plan demonstrating how ambulances and medical equipment will be inspected, cleaned, tested, and maintained in accordance with manufacturer recommendations and applicable regulatory requirements. - Offeror shall demonstrate its capability to maintain continuous operational readiness through preventive maintenance, equipment inspections, inventory control, and timely replacement or repair of vehicles and medical equipment. - Offeror shall provide procedures for documenting vehicle inspections, equipment maintenance, corrective actions, and quality assurance activities to ensure uninterrupted mission support. - Offeror shall demonstrate its ability to maintain operational capability during vehicle or equipment failures through contingency planning and resource management in accordance with the Performance Work Statement. Subfactor 4: Quality Management and Performance Assurance - Offeror shall provide a Quality Control Plan (QCP) demonstrating how contract performance will be monitored to ensure compliance with all Performance Work Statement (PWS) requirements. - Offeror shall describe its quality management processes for identifying, documenting, correcting, and preventing recurring performance deficiencies throughout contract performance. - Offeror shall provide procedures for monitoring personnel qualifications, certifications, credentialing, mandatory training, and regulatory compliance to ensure continuous mission readiness. - Offeror shall provide a continuous quality improvement approach demonstrating how performance data, customer feedback, and operational trends will be used to improve service delivery and reduce performance risk. Factor 2. Past Performance: The Offeror shall submit with its proposal evidence of recent and relevant past performance under which YOUR company (the Offeror) provided the same or similar services in the public and/or private sector. Performance must have been by the Offeror (not by a subsidiary or sister company) either as the prime contractor or subcontractor. Offerors shall complete and provide the Project Summary Sheet (Attachment 1) on three (3) task orders or stand-alone contracts/purchase orders the Offeror will complete or has completed within the past three (3) years from the closing date of this solicitation that the Offeror considers most relevant in demonstrating YOUR company's (the Offeror's) ability to perform the proposed effort. Past Performance must be with the Department of the Army, other US Government departments or agencies, state and local governments and/or commercial/private sector clients. If the Offeror performed as a subcontractor on the reference project, the Project Summary Sheet shall explain what percentage and type of work that was performed by the Offeror as subcontractor. In the instance that an offeror submits more than three (3) Project Summary Sheets, only the first three (3) will be evaluated. Offerors shall use the attachment provided. Past Performance Questionnaires (PPQs) (Attachment 2) may be submitted (however not required) for each past performance reference identified on the project summary sheet (Attachment 1). Contractor Performance Assessment Reports (CPARs) will also be accepted. For projects that have CPARs, Offerors can submit CPARs with Project Summary Sheets in lieu of PPQs. Offerors shall ensure CPARs are finalized and reference the exact same projects detailed in the Project Summary Sheet. If a PPQ or CPARs was not received for any of the past performance references identified on the project summary sheet, the Government may conduct interviews to validate performance/quality information. A past performance reference will not be evaluated if it does not contain valid/current POC contact information, or if the POC provided cannot validate work identified on the project summary sheet. The Government reserves the right to use both the information provided in the Offeror's Past Performance submittals and information obtained from other sources available to the Government, to include, but not limited to, the CPARs, Federal Awardee Performance and Integrity Information System (FAPIIS), Electronic Subcontract Reporting System (eSRS), or other databases; interviews with Program Managers, Contracting Officers, and commercial sources and/or non-Government sources, such as any commercial business or customers referenced by the Offeror in any of the past performance information disclosed. Factor 3. Price: Offeror shall complete the pricing for each of the contract line items (CLINs) on the Pricing Worksheet (Attachment 3).
