sig_5d9a534841588521dec8.description: The task is to prepare the licensing and detailed design plans for the Eger bypass road in accordance with the technical content specified in the design task description issued as part of the procurement documentation. The Eger bypass road starts from the roundabout junction of the M25 motorway, runs on the eastern side of the town of Eger, provides a connection between main road Nos 25 and 24, and connects to main road No. 25 by bypassing the Felnémet district. Tasks: Preparation of complete licensing plans together with the decision-preliminary documentation providing the basis for its details and individual technical parameters, obtaining permits, preparation of a feasibility study, as well as the preparation, licensing, and approval of complete detailed design plans, in accordance with the technical content specified in the design task description issued as part of the procurement documentation. The main estimated quantities for information purposes: Approximately 17 km of national public road, which is planned to have a 2x2 lane layout over a length of ~1,4 km (by rebuilding the existing 2x1 lane road), and a continuous national public road with 2x1 traffic lanes (designed on a new alignment) over a continuous length of ~15,6 km. The project includes the design of approximately 9 km of local public roads (~6 km of new alignment, ~3 km of pavement strengthening), 13 roundabout junctions (of which 3 are turbo roundabouts), the reconstruction of 7 at-grade junctions, the creation of 12 simple junctions or junctions with vehicle sorting lanes, the construction of 6 new structures, as well as the reconstruction of 3 existing structures, and the establishment of 1 at-grade railway crossings. Among the structures, a new national public road bridge over a railway with 2x2 lanes and a maximum superstructure length of 81,8 m is planned. The design of climbing lanes, retaining walls, and cuttings on certain sections of the bypass road, as well as the design of cycle path sections (new alignment, length of ~1 km), the creation of footpaths and pavements (over a length of 2,7 km), and the expected creation of 2 pedestrian crossings are also part of the project. The successful tenderer is obliged to cooperate in the public procurement procedures conducted for the implementation of the construction investment based on the plans prepared by them or parts thereof, as detailed in the draft contract. In the case of complete licensing and complete detailed design plans, building information modelling (BIM) based design shall take place, in accordance with Decree 31/2024 of the Ministry of Construction and Transport (VIII. 22.). The BIM requirements are contained in the design task description. The Contracting Authority draws attention to the fact that - the basic task to be performed within the framework of the contract to be concluded as a result of this procedure is the preparation of the decision-preliminary documentation, the feasibility study, and the complete licensing plans, and obtaining the permits; - with regard to the preparation of the complete detailed design and tender plans, as well as volumes III, IV, and V of the (public) procurement documentation suitable for construction, the Contractual Agreement issued as part of the procurement documentation contains a separate entry-into-force condition in view of Article 41 paragraph (1) of the Public Procurement Act; - the designer's site supervision arising during the implementation phase of the state construction investment, specified in Article 19 paragraph (1) of the Public Procurement Act, will be called upon as an option (for more details see: point "II.2.11) Information relating to options", field BT-53). Within the framework of the designer's site supervision, the tasks of the successful tenderer are: - to monitor the execution of the project, - to verify the implementation of the detailed design documentation prepared by them, - to draw attention to factors hindering or promoting implementation according to the plans, - to make proposals for the professional resolution of technical uncertainties and problems arising during construction, - to facilitate the resolution of professional questions arising during construction in connection with the detailed design documentation. A detailed description of the task is contained in the design task description.
sig_5d9a534841588521dec8.title: Preparation of permission and detailed design plans for the Eger bypass road

sig_5da6ceb78d04d0340f8b.description: This bid solicitation is being issued to satisfy the requirement of one (1) G.5 Geographic Information System Data Architect, Level 3 for Housing, Infrastructure and Communities Canada for Task-Based Informatics Professional Services (TBIPS) under the TBIPS Supply Arrangement (SA) method of supply. The primary objective is to establish a centralized geospatial data environment within the organization’s Azure-based Unified Data Platform (UDP). This environment will enable the efficient ingestion, validation, storage, integration, sharing, and spatial analysis of geospatial data across the organization, while supporting real-time relationships between spatial data and enterprise business datasets, automation, and more consistent, data-driven decision-making. In addition, the organization is looking for a cost-benefit analysis and recommendation of options to procure a modern geospatial platform, including how these options compare and integrate with HICC’s existing spatial capabilities and data ecosystems. The analysis will assess the potential value, costs, and implementation considerations associated with these platforms, and identify opportunities for location-based analysis, research, reporting, evaluation, automation, and application geoprocessing capabilities across the department.

sig_5ddac62cdd050fb6ea26.description: LapIT Oy is an IT company owned by the municipalities, joint municipal authorities, and municipal limited companies of Lapland and Koillismaa, which provides comprehensive information management and IT services. Our company's head office is located in Rovaniemi. LapIT is considering putting the financial management system out to tender and offering it to its owner-customers. Currently, there are 10 municipal customers interested in the procurement. According to preliminary plans, the procurement would cover the following processes: - from financial planning to forecasting - from procurement to payment - from sales to debt collection - from bookkeeping to financial statements - authority reporting (municipal reporting) Based on preliminary information, the procurement would cover the financial management solution as a comprehensive service, including implementation and user training, migrations from old systems, and integrations. LapIT requests willing potential tenderers to participate in a dialogue. In principle, we will accept into the market dialogue those tenderers who meet at least the following criteria: - The supplier must have at least 2 references for the solution for municipal customers. The systems reported as references must have been in production use for at least 2 years. - The solution must comply with high data security and the data must be located in the EU/EEA area. - The tenderer must offer implementation support and continuous service support in the Finnish language. The tenderer must attach to their registration: - A description of their service in Finnish. - Presentations of at least two reference deliveries as stated above. - The description should show the lifecycle status and development roadmap of the system. Willing participants can register for the dialogue by notifying us by email at jasmine.suopanki@lapit.fi by 5.11.2025. The intention is to start the market dialogues as soon as possible. LapIT will select the suppliers it chooses for the market dialogue based on the descriptions. LapIT reserves the right to limit the number of those who have participated in the market dialogue. The implementation method of the market dialogue will be decided later (written/meetings). Participation in the market dialogue does not in any way affect the tenderer's position in a possible future tendering process. The market dialogue will be carried out in the Finnish language. Everything presented in the market dialogue and the discussions held during it are preliminary and do not bind LapIT Oy or the tenderer. No compensation will be paid to those who have participated in the market dialogue for their participation. This is not a procurement notice or a call for tenders but a request for information/invitation to a market dialogue. This preliminary information notice does not bind the client to the procurement; the actual procurement notice will possibly be published later. The decision on launching a possible procurement process will be made later.

The subject of the procurement is described at a preliminary level in the appendices to this request for information. The preliminary description of the subject of the procurement and the contracting authority's current view of the needs are presented in the appendices to the request for information 1-5. Questions about the materials are presented in the appendix to the request for information 6. The contracting authority will later provide the registered suppliers with a draft contract for comment. This request for information is implemented as a technical dialogue. 3 OTHER MATTERS TO BE NOTED The request for information is not a contract notice, a call for tenders or an invitation to tender. Responding to the request for information does not bind the respondent or the contracting authority to a subsequent procurement procedure. The contracting authority will utilise the received responses in the planning of a possible future procurement and in the preparation of the call for tenders. It is good to note that this request for information does not oblige Istekki Oy to carry out the procurement in the manner presented in this document or its appendices. A possible call for tenders may also be left unorganised. No separate compensation will be paid for responding to the request for information or participating in presentation events. This is a request for information, not an advance notice, a contract notice or a call for tenders. The purpose of the request for information is to get to know the market situation and to collect information related to the subject of the procurement to support the planning of the future competitive tendering. Responding to the request for information is voluntary, and it is not a prerequisite for participating in a possible call for tenders and does not bind Istekki to publish a call for tenders. Please note that the information, descriptions and estimates of the schedule for the competitive tendering presented in this request for information are preliminary and indicative. The final schedules will be refined as the preparation progresses. We greatly appreciate the information provided by the suppliers, as it helps us to build the future competitive tendering as functional and clear a whole as possible.

sig_5ee014d4aebe9663afd1.description: Project reason TenneT requires a portfolio management system (PMS) to support electricity trading in the short-term market (day-ahead and intraday) in Germany. Objective of the tender The objective is the procurement of a high-performance PMS to support electricity trading. In accordance with TenneT's architectural guidelines, the solution is to be cloud-based, preferably operated in the tenderer's cloud. In coordination with TenneT, deployment in a third-party provider's cloud (e.g. Azure) or at TenneT is also possible. The system must enable the management of multiple portfolios and support the processes for participating in day-ahead and intraday auctions as well as continuous intraday trading. The system will be used in the electricity trading sector and must cover the following main functions: - Portfolio management - Connection to power exchanges - Trading overviews & GUI - Algo-trader / trading support in continuous intraday trading - Data management - Reporting & analysis - Settlement - Schedule management Scope of services - Provision of a COTS software solution (licences) - Support & maintenance of this solution (maintenance) - Hosting of the solution - Application management services - Consulting and training services Procedural notice A detailed specification of services as well as other procedural-relevant documents will be provided after signing a non-disclosure agreement. Please send this to us completed and signed via the Mercell messaging function. The tender is being conducted in accordance with the SektVO (Sectoral Procurement Ordinance) via a negotiated procedure with a call for competition. Accordingly, TenneT is already bound to confidentiality pursuant to Section 15 SektVO. As things stand, the value of the tender cannot be reliably estimated.

sig_5ee2299248e7774e26b5.description: Issuing Agency: Project Management Office (PMO) Uncrewed Aircraft Systems Capability Program Executive, Aviation SFAE-AVN-U Agencies Capable of Issuing Contracts/Agreements: Army Contracting Command - Redstone Period of Availability: This Department of War (DoW) Drone Commercial Solutions Opening, open solicitation, will remain open in perpetuity until canceled. Call for Solutions will specify individual response times and requirements. Description of Program: In accordance with Executive Order 14307, the DoW Drone Marketplace is the strategy to scale the industrial base and accelerate production deliveries while empowering Soldiers with freedom of choice to meet mission needs. As part of this approach, the DoW will better incentivize industry innovation. DoW Drone Marketplace marks a significant pivot from traditional DoW acquisition business models to a free-market approach founded on the concept of continuous competition that drives innovation, where Soldiers’ demands are directly linked to industry provided capabilities. This CSO will enable the DoW to rapidly acquire and deliver innovative solutions to the Warfighter using commercial technology. SECTION A – INTRODUCTION AND AUTHORITY The DoW has identified the following needs: (1) to accelerate the adoption of advanced commercial technology; (2) to transform DoW Drone Marketplace capabilities; and (3) to grow the industrial base to appropriately support the DoW. This solicitation aims to provide the DoW with access to innovative solutions enabling the DoW to evolve quickly and maintain a competitive edge over adversaries. Industry is at the forefront of innovation, developing cutting-edge capabilities that will enhance the DoW capabilities and protect the Warfighter. The DoW will select vendors whose solutions demonstrate the greatest potential to achieve the DoW's missions. The DoW is maximizing existing authorities by publishing this CSO, open solicitation, combining any single authority or a combination of the authorities below: Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) 6.102(d)(2) – Other Competitive Procedures 10 U.S.C. §3458 – Authority to acquire innovative commercial products and commercial services using general solicitation competitive procedures / DFARS 212.70 – Defense Commercial Solutions Opening SECTION B - GENERAL INFORMATION The DoW anticipates that the CSO will be updated frequently to improve processes and to keep pace with evolving threats, needs and innovations. The CSO will be open in perpetuity until canceled bythe DoW. Companies are informed that ONLY a warranted Government Contracting/Agreements Officer (KO/AO) (not a Contracting Officer Representative or other personnel) may contractually bind the Government. The Government shall not be liable to pay for work performed by a company unless a warranted KO/AO has signed an agreement in writing stating that the Government shall pay. The Government shall not fund preparation of solution briefs/proposals, or support work efforts or tasks that are inferred from discussions with technical project officers. SECTION C – AREAS OF INTEREST (AOI) This CSO, open solicitation, covers any of the following example areas. These example areas shall be viewed as suggestive, rather than limiting, and are not reflective of the ONLY AOIs or in any priority of order. Intelligence, Electronic, Warfare, and Sensors Tactical Communications Soldier Equipment Ancillary Items Payloads Simulation and Stimulation Training and Instrumentation Unmanned Aircraft Systems (UAS): Full Systems Air Vehicles Maritime Systems: Surface and Undersea Systems Maritime Reconnaissance and Domain Awareness Littoral and Amphibious Support Ground Systems: Reconnaissance and Surveillance Systems Logistics and Equipment Transport Combat and Tactical Support Platforms Counter- UAS: Mutli-Domain Sensing and Detection Command, Control and Data Fusion Defeat Mechanisms (Kinetic and Non-Kinetic) Platform & Operation Integration Supply Chain and Logistics Installation Support and Innovation Additive Manufacturing Autonomous Vehicles Software Autonomous Behaviors Command & Control Launched Effects Drone Production (build at scale) SECTION D – COMMERCIAL SOLUTIONS OPENING (CSO) PROCEDURES There are two methods for responding under this CSO: (1) Innovative Warfighter Solutions submissions and (2) Call for Solution submissions. Method 1 - Innovative Warfighter Solutions (IWS) Provides a flexible and open-ended opportunity for industry partners to submit solution briefs to any AOI in Section C. This aspect of the CSO is designed to identify and bridge gaps in mission-critical capabilities by inviting innovative solutions from the private sector. The purpose is to encourage a wide range of responses that can enhance and support the example AOIs, foster collaboration and leverage cutting-edge technologies and methodologies to meet evolving operational needs. Companies shall follow the procedures outlined in the attachment when providing a submission to an IWS. The submission mailbox for AOI is identified in Section J. Method 2 - Call for Solutions (C4S) Provides an opportunity for industry partners to submit innovative solutions in response to Government issued C4S under any AOI in Section C. C4S aim to pinpoint and address critical gaps in essential capabilities by welcoming creative proposals from private sector entities. Companies shall follow the procedures outlined below and within the specific C4Ss posted. The individual C4S will identify how responses are to be submitted. Method 1 - IWS Overview Companies submitting an IWS in response to the AOIs shall follow the procedures outlined in the attachment. If the Government does not select a company’s submission for, as applicable, for phase 2 and/or 3, the submission may be retained in the Solution Basket. This allows the Government to reconsider the submission for future needs and funding opportunities, maximizing its value to both the vendor and the DoW. The IWS award procedures will utilize up to three (3) phases, as appliable: Solution Brief Live Demonstration and/or Pitch (optional) Commercial Solution Proposal (CSP) Method 2 - C4S Overview CS4 (referred to as “Calls”) will be released and posted via SAM.gov as an amendment under this CSO. The Call will include all relevant submission requirements and evaluation procedures and shall govern the process for evaluations and award. Submission requirements may vary in phases and may take the form of solution briefs, white papers, demonstrations, live pitches, etc. C4S are independent from the IWS procedures discussed above in Section D.1 IWS procedures do not apply to individual Calls. Calls may be written in a broad manner to maximize efficiency, innovation and application when approaching a problem and to allow for maximum participation from vendors who may not be familiar with submitting proposals to Government solicitations. The Government may post Calls at any time. Interested companies are encouraged to frequently check SAM.gov for updates to this solicitation and posted C4S. SECTION E - AWARDS The Government may choose to issue an award(s) in accordance with IWSs or C4S procedures and subject to the availability of funds. The KO/AO reserves the right to negotiate directly with the company on terms and conditions prior to execution of the resulting award instrument, including payment terms, and will execute the instrument on behalf of the Government. All payment obligations of the Government shall be subject to receipt of appropriations from Congress for the purpose, time, and amount of the obligation. Be advised, only a KO/AO has the authority to enter into, or modify, a binding instrument on behalf of the United States Government. Awards issued under this CSO may include, but are not limited to the following award instruments: FAR contracts under FAR Part 12 Commercial Procedures; any fixed price, or fixed price incentive contract type specified under FAR Part 16; and non-FAR agreements such as transaction agreements under 10 U.S.C. 4022 and 10 U.S.C. 4023; for the DoW and/or its customers that are directly relevant to enhancing the effectiveness of the AOI identified in Section J. In order to receive an award, the following must be met: Companies shall have a Unique Entity Identification (UEI) number and must register in the System for Award Management (SAM) prior to receiving an instrument. If a company does not possess a valid and active SAM registration, companies are advised to commence SAM registration before responding to a Call or IWS. Companies are required to maintain registration in SAM throughout the period of performance of the instrument and during any subsequent follow-on award. Companies shall also register in the prescribed Government invoicing system (Wide Area Work Flow: https://wawf.eb.mil/xhtml/unauth/registration/notice.xhtml.) Companies shall represent their small business size and status as required in this solicitation. Companies shall be determined to be responsible by the KO/AO and must not be suspended or debarred from award by the Federal Government nor be prohibited by Presidential Executive Order and/or law from receiving an award. Any actual or potential OCIs shall be identified to KO/AO prior to award. SECTION F – ITERATIVE PROTOTYPING Iterative prototyping is a development methodology where a prototype is created, tested, and refined through multiple cycles, incorporating user feedback and improvements in each iteration, to ensure the final product meets user requirements and expectations effectively. An Other Transaction (OT) for a prototype awarded or an award using 10 U.S.C. 4023 against this open solicitation shall allow for an iterative prototyping process and will be delineated in the award document. An iterative prototyping process will allow the Government to modify, by mutual agreement, the scope of a prototype contract or OT to allow for the adaptation and modification of the technology being prototyped to meet additional unique and discrete purposes/mission sets. The sequential prototype iterations may result in separate phased prototype awards rather than a modification of the original prototype award. These additional unique and discrete purposes/mission sets can be generated by the Government. SECTION I – NON-GOVERNMENT ADVISORS Non-Government advisors may be used in the evaluation of Solution Briefs, Pitches and during the Commercial Solution Proposal phase and negotiations under the IWS procedures or in C4S. Non-Government advisors will have signed non-disclosure agreements (NDAs) with the Government. The company understands that the Government may share proprietary company information with non-Government personnel for evaluation and administrative purposes only. The Government understands that information provided in response to this open solicitation is presented in confidence and may contain trade secret or commercial or financial information, and it agrees to protect such information from unauthorized disclosure to the maximum extent permitted or required by Law, to include: 18 U.S.C. 1905 (Trade Secrets Act); 18 U.S.C. 1831 et seq. (Economic Espionage Act); 5 U.S.C. 552(b)(4) (Freedom of Information Act); Executive Order 12600 (Pre-disclosure Notification Procedures for Confidential Commercial Information); and, Any other statute, regulation, or requirement applicable to Government employees. Companies shall label any information they want protected as confidential. Submissions will not be returned. The original copy of each submission received will be retained by the DoW and all other non-required copies destroyed. SECTION J - CONTACT INFORMATION IWS Solution Brief submissions as detailed in Section D, shall be submitted to the email address listed below and shall include the associated AOI in the subject line of the e-mail. If the respondent does not include the AOI in the subject line of the e-mail, the submission will NOT be reviewed. Area of Interest in Subject Line usarmy.redstone.cpe-avn.mbx.uasmarketplaceiws@army.mil C4S Brief submissions (Section D) shall be submitted in accordance with the instructions and points of contact provided in the Call. General questions surrounding this open solicitation shall be submitted to: Email address: USARMY Redstone Arsenal PEO AVN Mailbox DoW Drone Marketplace SECTION K - DEFINITIONS "Call for Solution" (C4S) an announcement posted on SAM.gov, which may result in a contract or OT and includes submission instructions, evaluation criteria, timelines, how the DoW will treat late submissions, points of contact, and other specific information. The Call is a request for response from prospective industry partners. “Commercial Solutions Opening” (CSO) is a competitive procedure KO/AO may use to acquire innovative commercial items, technologies, or services. “Innovative” means any item that is (1) Any technology, process, or method, including research and development, that is new as of the date of submission of a proposal; or (2) Any application that is new as of the date of submission of a proposal of a technology, process, or method existing as of such date. “Innovative Warfighter Solutions” (IWS) is a competitive procedure for submitting an Innovative Warfighter Solution in response to a posted Area of Interest (AOI) under this Commercial Solutions Opening (CSO). These procedures create a pathway we call the Solution Basket. The IWS gives industry the opportunity to approach the Government with their innovative solutions. “Nontraditional Defense Contractor” is defined by DFARS 202.101 as an “entity that is not currently performing and has not performed any contract or subcontract for DoW that is subject to full coverage under the cost accounting standards prescribed pursuant to 41 U.S.C. 1502 and the regulations implementing such section, for at least the 1-year period preceding the solicitation of sources by DoW for the procurement (10 U.S.C. 3014).” “Nonprofit Institution” is defined in 15 U.S.C. § 3703 an organization owned and operated exclusively for scientific or educational purposes, no part of the net earnings of which insures to the benefit of any private shareholder or individual. "Other Transaction" refers to the statutory authority to enter into transactions other than procurement contracts, grants, or cooperative agreements. The DoW has the authority to enter into OTs for Research Projects (10 USC 4021), OT for Prototype Projects (10 USC 4022), and DoW relevant OT that support research (10 U.S.C. 4021). “Commercial Solution Proposal” (CSP): is a proposal that is submitted in response to a Call that is governed by a CSO or a response to an unsolicited proposal that is invited to Phase III. CSPs may be requested as a result of Solution Briefs and/or presentations/pitches. “Small Business” is defined under Section 3 of the Small Business Act (15 U.S.C. 632).

sig_5f2082f484acfba2ed95.description: 1.0 INTRODUCTION & PURPOSE This Request for Information (RFI) is issued solely for market research, planning, and information-gathering purposes in accordance with FAR Part 10 and FAR 15.201. This is not a Sources Sought synopsis or a Request for Proposal (RFP). No contract will be awarded directly from this posting, and the Government is under no obligation to issue a solicitation based on this notice. The 434th Contracting Flight (434 CONF/PK), in coordination with the 434th Civil Engineer Squadron (434 CES) at Grissom Air Reserve Base, is seeking technical feedback from the commercial construction and unit-price estimating software industry. The primary goal of this RFI is to gather industry input on a streamlined, performance-based acquisition structure for a future SABER contract. The Government is particularly interested in receiving feedback on how to structure its pricing database requirements to maximize open competition, eliminate the administrative burden of traditional "mock projects," and prevent post-award "Non-Prepriced Item (NPI) creep." 2.0 PROGRAM DESCRIPTION & ANTICIPATED STRATEGY The Government is planning a Single-Award or Multiple-Award Indefinite-Delivery/Indefinite-Quantity (IDIQ) SABER contract with the following anticipated structure: Estimated Ordering Ceiling: $9,000,000.00 over a five (5) year ordering period. Minimum Contract Guarantee: $2,000.00 (to be obligated at time of basic contract award). Scope of Work: Multi-trade maintenance, repair, minor construction, and renovation projects across real property facilities at Grissom ARB. Core trades include carpentry, roofing, excavation, electrical, plumbing, HVAC, masonry, demolition, concrete, and localized hazardous material abatement. Streamlined Price Evaluation (No Mock Project): To drastically accelerate procurement lead times and eliminate unpaid proposal preparation costs for industry, the Government intends to evaluate price strictly based on competitively bidded coefficients (adjustment factors) applied to pre-disclosed, weighted government workload estimates. The traditional "mock project" estimating phase will be bypassed during source selection. Performance-Based Unit Price Database: To support a "no mock project" model legally and defensibly under FAR Part 16 and Part 36, the contract must rely on a highly comprehensive, pre-priced Unit Price Book (UPB) or Contractor Pricing Guide (CPG) that is locally researched, standardized, granular, and capable of keeping post-award NPIs under 10% of total task order values. 3.0 SPECIFIC AREAS OF INQUIRY & QUESTIONNAIRE Firms choosing to respond are requested to provide detailed, objective feedback on the following five administrative and technical categories: Section 3.1: Performance-Based Technical Equivalency vs. Database Size The Government wants to ensure the pricing database is comprehensive enough to prevent post-award "NPI creep" without establishing arbitrary restrictions that limit competition. Rather than relying on a raw line-item record count as a proxy for database quality, does your firm support defining technical equivalency based on performance outcomes? Specifically, how should the Government measure a database's ability to minimize NPIs to less than 10% of total task order values? To prove database capability without running a labor-intensive "mock project," would your firm support an automated "Coverage Mapping Report" during source selection? Under this method, the Government would provide a standard, historical list of approximately 100 typical Air Force repair and maintenance tasks. Offerors would run this list against their database to prove they can pre-price 90% or more of the workload value. Detail any software or database limitations to executing this type of coverage report. To ensure transparent bidding, does your estimating database allow prospective contractors to view bare labor, material, equipment (L/E/M) costs and crew compositions prior to award, or are these components hidden behind a flat unit price? Describe how this impacts a contractor's ability to bid sharp, accurate coefficients. Describe how your estimating platform and database ensure that unit prices are derived from direct local market research (localized labor, material, equipment, and productivity rates for the Grissom ARB/Indiana area) rather than relying on national averages adjusted by a flat regional index. Section 3.2: Coefficient Absorption & Overhead Definitions To ensure a fair "apples-to-apples" price evaluation, the bidded coefficients must cover all operational overhead. Please confirm your firm's capability to absorb the following overhead costs directly within your proposed bidded coefficients, with no separate or direct billing to the Government: All cost-estimating software licensing, support, and maintenance fees (including providing a minimum of two concurrent user licenses to 434 CES and 434 CONF personnel). Unrestricted on-base office operations, project manager training, and material storage yard maintenance. Maintenance of a localized physical/digital material submittal library. Basic design, drafting, site verification, and as-built drawing preparation. From a software perspective, what is your platform's licensing fee structure? Is it offered via a flat, predictable subscription model (monthly/annual per user) or as a percentage of construction volume (fee-on-volume) applied against awarded task orders? Detail the cost impact of these competing licensing models on a contractor's overhead bidded coefficients. What standard RFP definitions are required in Section L to ensure all offerors are absorbing these exact overhead elements on a common basis? Section 3.3: Safeguards Against Unbalanced Bidding Without a mock project, a primary risk is that a contractor may submit an artificially low standard-hours coefficient to win the award, intending to recover margins through unconstrained Non-Prepriced Items (NPIs) or non-standard hours. Does your firm support a solicitation restriction that locks the NPI coefficient (the markup applied to raw subcontractor quotes) to a factor equal to, or less than, the competitively bidded standard-hours coefficient? What are the industry best practices to prevent unbalanced bidding across auxiliary coefficients (such as secure areas or after-hours work)? Does your firm support capping auxiliary coefficients at a fixed percentage above the standard-hours baseline? What measures does your JOC software platform employ to prevent a contractor from altering unit prices or manipulating quantities after the basic contract is awarded? Section 3.4: Database Update Frequency & Pricing Baselines SABER contracts are subject to severe market and economic price fluctuations over a five-year period. Many commercial cost databases are updated quarterly (90-day cycles). Please detail the administrative impact quarterly updates create on your estimating team regarding pending task order proposals, active Independent Government Estimates (IGEs), and ongoing negotiations. Can your software lock the cost database to a fixed annual baseline for Grissom ARB, adjusting base unit prices once a year via a localized City Cost Index (CCI) or localized economic update, while keeping bidded coefficients fixed? Does your firm recommend utilizing a separate Economic Price Adjustment (EPA) clause, or do annual localized database updates sufficiently protect both parties from inflation? Section 3.5: Software Cloud Security & Network Access Grissom's local communications squadron maintains strict software security protocols. Is your JOC/SABER estimating software platform a web-based, cloud-accessed system? Does your software platform comply with Cybersecurity Maturity Model Certification (CMMC) 2.0 or hold FedRAMP authorization? Provide details of any active Authorities to Operate (ATOs) currently held by your estimating software platform on any active DoD, Air Force, or other federal networks. 4.0 RESPONSE SUBMISSION INSTRUCTIONS Interested firms are requested to submit their RFI Response packages matching the following instructions: Cover Page: Include Company Name, Address, Point of Contact (Name, Phone, Email), UEI, CAGE Code, active State of Indiana General Contractor licensing status, and active SBA Socioeconomic Status (e.g., active 8(a) program graduation date). Technical Response: Provide detailed, objective feedback to all items listed in Section 3.0 (Inquiries 3.1 through 3.5). Past Performance: Provide a list of up to three (3) active or completed federal contracts of similar scope and complexity executed within the past five (5) years. For each contract, specify: Contract Number, Agency, and Point of Contact. Pricing mechanism used (e.g., JOC with bidded coefficients, SABER, or traditional lump sum). Total contract value and NPI performance history (demonstrated percentage of work priced out of the pre-priced catalog vs. NPIs). Format & Page Limit: Responses must be in PDF format and are limited to a total of fifteen (15) pages (excluding cover page and licensing/surety attachments). Submission: Submit electronically via email directly to the Contracting Officer: cedric.roberts@us.af.mil. END OF REQUEST FOR INFORMATION

sig_5fb1260d8f4da49f764c.description: Excerpt from article 3 of the tender documentation as amended by Clarification of Tender Documentation No 4: 3.1 Public contracts awarded under a DPS shall be supply public contracts pursuant to Section 14 subsection 1 of the Act. Supplies under this DPS shall mean the acquisition of items, which apart from purchase shall also mean rental, usufructuary lease, leasing or operational leasing. 3.2 The subject matter of public contracts awarded under the DPS shall be the supply of office printers, photocopying machines and multi-function printing equipment (hereinafter also collectively referred to as "Printing Equipment"). 3.3 Part of the subject matter or a separate subject matter of public contracts awarded under the DPS may be service and material performance. 3.4 Service and material performance shall mean: a) regular inspection and comprehensive maintenance of the Printing Equipment according to the number of printed pages or the service plan of the Printing Equipment manufacturer; b) complete service and repairs of the Printing Equipment including fault clearance, adjustment and commissioning of the Printing Equipment, complete supply and replacement of all spare parts; c) supply of consumables (e.g. office paper, toners, waste containers, belt units, fixing units, heads, rollers, manufacturer-prescribed maintenance kits, developer units, imaging units, etc.) including take-back of used consumables; d) system update of the Printing Equipment; e) software tools for the management of the service and material performance of the Printing Equipment; and f) other performance required as part of the inspection, service or maintenance of the Printing Equipment. 3.5 The subject matter of the public contract may also be the supply and implementation of software for the printing solution. This shall mean software that can centrally in particular: a) determine individual persons authorised to use the Printing Equipment, including determining the scope of authority of a specific person (e.g. setting the requirement for black-and-white or duplex printing, setting quotas); b) make the use of the Printing Equipment conditional upon logging in of the authorised person via a card reader or other device of similar function; c) manage document workflows; d) ensure reporting and cost allocation of executed printing or other tasks of the Printing Equipment; e) enable printing from mobile devices; and f) protect against document theft or data loss. 3.6 Part of the supply and implementation of software for the printing solution may also be the procurement of card readers or other similar devices and, where applicable, the procurement of such cards or other similar devices. 3.7 The subject matter of public contracts awarded under this DPS may also be service and material performance or software for the printing solution whose subject matter will be only some of the items listed in subsections 3.5 and 3.6 of the TD. 3.8 Part of the service and material performance or software for the printing solution may also be other customary components thereof, even if they are not explicitly stated in this TD. 3.9 The Central Purchasing Body anticipates awarding public contracts under the DPS at pre-determined irregular intervals depending on its operational needs and the operational needs of the commissioning contracting authorities. The volumes of individual public contracts awarded under the DPS are likewise dependent on the operational needs of the Central Purchasing Body and individual Commissioning Contracting Authorities, and their number may range from units up to hundreds of units in a specific public contract. 3.10 The subject matter of public contracts awarded under the DPS and its technical conditions will always be detailed in individual calls for tenders pursuant to Section 141 of the Act. 3.11 The Central Purchasing Body is entitled, within the scope of public contracts awarded under the DPS, to require the submission of a tender in the form of an electronic catalogue pursuant to Section 215 of the Act. sig_5fce472d03558e520413.description: The Tribal Colleges and Universities Program (TCUP) provides awards to federally recognized 1 Tribal Colleges and Universities, Alaska Native-serving institutions, and Native Hawaiian-serving institutions to promote high quality science (including sociology, psychology, anthropology, linguistics, economics and bioeconomics, statistics, and other social and behavioral sciences; natural sciences; computer science, including, but not limited to, artificial intelligence, quantum information science, and cybersecurity), technology, engineering and mathematics (STEM), STEM education, research, and outreach. Support is available to TCUP-eligible institutions (see the Additional Eligibility subsection of Section IV of this solicitation) for transformative capacity-building or community engagement projects through Instructional Capacity Excellence in TCUP Institutions (ICE-TI) , Targeted STEM Infusion Projects (TSIP) , TCUP for Secondary and Elementary Teachers in STEM (TSETS) , TCU Enterprise Advancement Centers (TEA Centers) , Cyberinfrastructure Health, Assistance, and Improvements (CHAI) , and Preparing for TCUP Implementation (Pre-TI) . Collaborations led by TCUP institutions that involve non-TCUP institutions of higher education are supported through TCUP Partnerships , with the participation of other NSF programs to support the work of non-TCUP institutions. Finally, research studies that further the scholarly activity of individual faculty members are supported through Small Grants for Research (SGR) . Through the opportunities highlighted above, as well as collaborations with other National Science Foundation (NSF) divisions and directorates, and other organizations, TCUP aims to increase Native individuals' participation in STEM careers, improve the quality of STEM programs at TCUP-eligible institutions, and facilitate the development of a strong STEM enterprise in TCUP institutions' service areas. TCUP supports transformative capacity-building, community engagement, or research projects at TCUP-eligible institutions through the following funding tracks: Instructional Capacity Excellence in TCUP Institutions (ICE-TI) projects provide support to design, implement, and assess comprehensive institutional improvements in STEM education and research capacity at TCUP-eligible institutions of higher education. By strengthening STEM education and STEM education research, successful projects will increase the number of STEM students and improve the quality of their preparation. ICE-TI projects create and/or adapt and assess innovative models and materials for teaching and learning in STEM, embody knowledge about how students learn most effectively in STEM teaching and learning activities, and bring STEM disciplinary advances into the undergraduate or graduate experience. The objective of this strand is to expand STEM degrees offered by TCUP-eligible institutions or significantly enhance instructional approaches. Targeted STEM Infusion Projects (TSIP) support the attainment of a short-term, well-defined goal to improve the quality of STEM education at an eligible institution. Targeted STEM Infusion Projects could, for example, enhance academic infrastructure by systematically adding traditional knowledge to the scope or content of a STEM course, updating curricula, modernizing laboratory research equipment, developing and delivering professional development for K-12 STEM educators, or improving the computational infrastructure. The objective of this strand is to expand STEM degrees or significantly enhance instructional approaches. TCUP for Secondary & Elementary Teachers in STEM (TSETS) supports in-service professional development in STEM disciplinary or STEM education content and/or research for K-12 STEM teachers in the relevant service area. Examples of project activities include, but are not limited to, professional development involving seminar series and engagement in STEM instruction and content during the academic year, structured series of summer intensive workshops and trainings, and summer research opportunities. The objective of this strand is to broaden the instructional capacity for STEM in the K-12 workforce and thereby to the entire community, and to build the capacity for STEM disciplinary or education research among participating educational professionals. TCU Enterprise Advancement Centers (TEA Centers) coalesce the STEM and/or STEM education expertise into a team, designed to support and promote the STEM goals, needs, aspirations, or interests of the chartering reservation or tribe(s). TEA Centers may address a critical tribal or community need or focus on a realm of research or design that is beyond the scope of individual research grants or that is of interest to multiple tribes. The objective of this strand is to build on the capacity developed through prior TCUP support and apply expertise to collaborations with communities in the institution’s service area, or nationally. The Cyberinfrastructure Health, Assistance, and Improvements (CHAI) strand supports projects at TCUP-eligible institutions of higher education to upgrade the cyberinfrastructure necessary to conduct, expand, manage and administer STEM programs of study, including research. The objective of this strand is to equip TCUP institutions to meet the demands of virtual instruction, advanced computing, and data science opportunities. Preparing for TCUP Implementation (Pre-TI) provides support for activities that prepare an institution for Implementation-level projects. Consequently, they are available only to TCUP-eligible institutions of higher education that have never received TCUP support, have not received TCUP support within the previous five years, or are embarking on a significantly novel STEM strategic plan. Examples of supported activities include completing an institutional assessment of its current STEM instructional capacity, or engaging in conversations necessary to formulate a shared vision of what that capacity should be and how to achieve it. Pre-TI awards can support staff and faculty release time, travel, stakeholder gatherings, and associated administrative costs. The objective of this strand is to conduct self-studies and formulate strategic plans for the development of STEM instructional programs of study. The TCUP Partnerships strand provides support for collaborations that will improve TCUP institutions' instructional and research capacity in STEM fields supported by NSF; attract, retain, and support TCUP students in internships and research endeavors deemed to be necessary for a complete curriculum offering; and engage partner universities to provide an academic grounding and a successful transition for students who wish to study or attain degrees in STEM fields supported by NSF. TCUP Partnerships broaden the number of scientific disciplines available to students at TCUP institution through collaborations with non-TCUP institutions. Active Pre-Engineering Education Collaboratives or Partnerships in Geoscience Education awards are not affected by this revision. The objective of this strand is the development, through instructional and research capacity-building, of academic and career pathways for TCUP students through supporting collaborative projects between and among TCUP and non-TCUP institutions. Interested teams of collaborators for which a TCUP institution serves as lead should contact the TCUP program directors. Support for non-TCUP partners must be obtained from other NSF programs, which follows the procedures of the prior Partnership strands. Small Grants for Research (SGR) strand support STEM or STEM Education faculty members at TCUP-eligible institutions to initiate or pursue research projects or programs that may include undergraduate or graduate student engagement. Awards are intended to help further the faculty member's research capability and effectiveness; improve research and teaching at his or her home institution and create and study new models and innovations in STEM teaching and learning. International research or collaborations are strongly encouraged. TCUP students may seek support for international research opportunities under the guidance of a TCUP STEM or STEM education faculty member and an international research collaborator. These awards are particularly appropriate as a means of recruiting and retaining highly qualified scientists, engineers, and educators at TCUP-eligible institutions. The objective of this strand is to support faculty research and professional development that build research capacity at TCUP institutions. [1] Executive Order 13021 defines Tribal Colleges and Universities ("tribal colleges") as those institutions cited in section 532 of the Equity in Educational Land-Grant Status Act of 1994 (7 U.S.C. 301 note), and other institutions that qualify for funding under the Tribally Controlled Community College Assistance Act of 1978, (25 U.S.C. 1801 et seq.), as well as Navajo Community College as authorized in the Navajo Community College Assistance Act of 1978, Public Law 95-471, Title II (25 U.S.C. 640a note). The term "Alaska Native-serving institution" means an institution of higher education that is an eligible institution under section 1058(b) of the Higher Education Act; and that, at the time of submission, has an undergraduate enrollment that is at least 20 percent Alaska Native students. The term "Native Hawaiian-serving institution" means an institution of higher education that is an eligible institution under section 1058(b) of the Higher Education Act; and that, at the time of submission, has an undergraduate enrollment that is at least 10 percent Native Hawaiian students. Most TCUP-eligible institutions of higher education are two-year or community colleges. See the Who May Submit Proposals section in this solicitation for further details.

sig_60106b1aa7da1b8b3fdd.description: We ask you to submit your answers to this information request concerning the procurement of a certificate automation system. We greatly appreciate all the answers we receive, and each of them will be taken into account in the preparation of a possible tendering procedure. The purpose of the information request is to ensure that those preparing the tendering procedure have as comprehensive and up-to-date a picture of the market and the solutions on offer as possible. With this information request, we want to survey suppliers' offerings of systems that support the automatic renewal of public SSL certificates and the managed installation of certificates for systems using them. At the same time, we aim to familiarise ourselves with the market situation of services related to the systems, products possibly related to the use of the system, contract terms and conditions, and commercial terms such as pricing. Based on the responses to the information request, market dialogue sessions may be organised, where suppliers can present their own services, products and alternatives for the implementation of the procurement subject. If market dialogue sessions are organised, they will be conducted in the Finnish language. Istekki will announce more detailed schedules and a Teams meeting link to the companies participating in the sessions later. Please note that the information, descriptions and estimates of the publication date of the tendering procedure presented in this information request are still preliminary and indicative. Final schedules will become more precise as the preparation progresses. We ask you to submit your answers by email to hankinnat@istekki.fi no later than 15.4.2026 at 12.00. We hope that the answers are submitted in a separate enclosure in Finnish, so that their processing is as smooth as possible. If you wish, you can also include Finnish-language brochures or other material that supports the content of your answer. Based on the answers received, Istekki will, at its discretion, select 1-5 tenderers to present their solution in a market dialogue meeting. By default, the presentation will be implemented as an approximately one (1) hour Teams meeting between Istekki and the supplier in question at one of the following preliminary times: • Time 1: 24.04.2026, at 09-10 • Time 2: 24.04.2026, at 10-11 • Time 3: 29.04.2026, at 9-10 • Time 4: 29.04.2026, at 10-11 • Time 5: 29.04.2026, at 13-14 All answers received to the information request will be taken into account in the preparation of the invitation to tender, and they are an important part of understanding the entity as a whole. It is good to note that this information request does not oblige Istekki Oy to carry out the procurement in the manner presented in this document or its enclosures. A possible tendering procedure may also not be organised. No separate compensation will be paid for responding to the information request or participating in possible presentation sessions. We would like to mention once again that this is an information request, not a prior information notice, a procurement notice or an invitation to tender. The purpose of the information request is to familiarise ourselves with the market situation and to gather information related to the subject of the procurement to support the planning of the upcoming tendering procedure. Responding to the information request is voluntary and is not a prerequisite for participation in a possible tendering procedure, nor does it bind Istekki to publish a tendering procedure. At the same time, however, we greatly appreciate the information provided by suppliers, as it helps us build the future tendering procedure into as functional and clear a whole as possible.

sig_601883fad91c3c7ec905.description: The Legal AI Workspace software to be procured must, as a specialised working environment, support legal specialist work within the KfW Group with the aid of generative artificial intelligence. The software will be used in particular for legal research, analysis and processing of legal content, as well as for the (semi-)automated creation, revision and structuring of documents and other legal work results. Users are individuals from the Legal department as well as other specialist departments and subsidiaries within the KfW Group. A Legal AI Workspace connects large language models with specialised processing layers optimised for working with legal content. It differs from general AI assistants in that it brings together specialist legal processes in a uniform working environment and deploys mechanisms that are indispensable for professional legal application. These include in particular: the traceable anchoring of generated statements in verifiable sources, the structured processing of complex documents, and the rule-based checking of contract contents. The software must provide the following core functions. Legal research: The software must be capable of answering complex legal questions on the basis of relevant legal sources. Every generated statement must be traced back to specific, verifiable sources (in particular legislation, case law, commentaries) and made transparent to users. KfW regards integrated access to curated legal databases as a quality-enhancing feature. Furthermore, the software must be able to work with documents and internal knowledge databases provided by KfW. Document analysis and contract evaluation: The software must be able to process and evaluate the content of documents, including complexly structured contracts, tabular content and scanned documents, without losing essential structural information. This includes the ability to systematically and completely reconcile contract content against specified verification standards. Text creation and drafting support: The software must support the creation and revision of legal texts, in particular draft contracts, memoranda and opinions. Proposed changes must be traceable directly within the document; merely providing generated text for manual adoption by users does not meet the requirements. The software complements general AI software already in use at KfW. The new software will be operated as a standalone tool and uses model infrastructure provided by the contractor. It is expected that the software will achieve significant efficiency and quality gains in daily legal advice, document creation and review, and recurring standard legal tasks. Without prejudice to the provision of the Software as a Service (SaaS) described in this document and the rights of use granted in connection therewith, the software must be provided in such a way that it at least meets the intended purpose. KfW is entitled to at least those rights of use required to fulfil the intended purpose for this. The contractor is therefore indebted to the following services: (a) provision of software with the functional scope, (b) execution of a project for the introduction of the software, (c) operation as SaaS, (d) provision of additional services as required, (e) termination support. Further details can be found in the "Specification of Services" and in particular the must-criteria according to the annex to the Specification of Services "Must and Can Criteria".
sig_601883fad91c3c7ec905.title: Legal AI Workspace

sig_606b5336ce6482179de4.description: Scientific services: Annual preparation of an impact report for Green Federal Securities based on the impact data provided by the client: determination, aggregation and documentation of standardised environmental impact indicators according to the ICMA standard, report preparation in English. The subject is the provision of scientific services for the annual preparation of impact reports for Green Federal Securities. The contractor shall check the impact data provided by the client for selected budget headings for suitability and consistency and shall determine from this - by drawing on scientific evaluations, studies and - if necessary - specially developed methods - standardised impact indicators compatible with the ICMA Core Indicators. These are to be aggregated into an overall impact across all expenditure headings; assumptions, estimates and methods used must be documented in a comprehensible manner, and forecasts must be marked. The impact report is to be prepared in English, supplemented by a tabular overview of the determined impact indicators per budget heading in Excel format. The contractor shall undertake the associated project management, including coordination with the client.

sig_60d35749096b28e61262.description: SUBJECT OF THE PROCUREMENT Yle is planning a tendering procedure for AWS public cloud services. Our goal is to tender a supplier of cloud capacity services produced by Amazon Web Services (hereinafter "AWS") for Yle's use, which can be either AWS itself or an authorised reseller of AWS. Yle has no need to procure expert services related to the service. See further details in the attachment "Information request AWS public cloud services, YLE20250031". HOW TO PARTICIPATE? If you are interested in the upcoming tendering procedure, we kindly ask you to contact us by 6.11.2025 by email at tarjoukset.yle@yle.fi. Please attach to the message your answers to the questions listed in the attachment "Information request AWS public cloud services, YLE20250031" as well as a short introduction of your company and services. We reserve the right to meet potential tenderers if we deem it necessary at this stage of the procurement process. GENERAL INFORMATION ABOUT THE INFORMATION REQUEST This document is not a contract notice or an invitation to tender, but an information request published as part of a market consultation. Yle will treat the responses to the information request as confidential and will use them solely in the preparation of the invitation to tender and the procurement procedure. Answering the questions does not oblige your company to participate in the actual tendering procedure. On the other hand, even if you do not answer these questions, you may participate in the tendering procedure later. Answering does not affect your company's position in the actual tendering procedure. The market consultation does not oblige Yle to carry out the procurement in the manner described in the information request. Nor is Yle obliged to take into account the responses received to the information request when drawing up the invitation to tender. We may carry out the tendering procedure differently, postpone its schedule or decide not to carry it out at all. We will only make decisions on initiating a possible procurement process after the market consultation. No compensation will be paid to those who responded to the information request for answering it, nor will any costs arising from it be reimbursed.

sig_60d872e0eccc0a60472a.description: The Gemeente Zaanstad wishes to renew the existing DRIS. Flagpole displays must be replaced with the possibility of reusing the existing poles. The Municipality wishes to replace shelter displays with E-ink displays in a bus stop sign that can be attached to a pole or to a (stop) post. At Zaandam station and the “De Vlinder” interchange, the DRIS is being renewed. The Municipality receives a subsidy from Vervoerregio Amsterdam for the renewal of displays, but must pay for maintenance itself. The subsidy requires completion to be finalized before 30 September 2027. For the full description of the assignment, including all requirements set for it, we refer you to the appendices belonging to this Invitation to Tender. Approximately 45 flagpole displays must be replaced, reusing existing poles and foundations. Approximately 90 shelter displays supplemented by 15 E-ink displays for Zaandam station and the De Vlinder interchange (total 105) must be replaced by E-ink displays in a bus stop sign that are attached to a pole (to be supplied). At Zaandam station and De Vlinder, the DRIS is being renewed as part of improving wayfinding (6 overview displays for Zaandam station and 1 overview display for De Vlinder). These estimates are intended solely to give an impression of the scope of the Assignment: you cannot derive any rights from them. See tendering documents.
sig_60d872e0eccc0a60472a.title: Dynamic Passenger Information System (DRIS)

sig_611e8af3117c69f7b205.description: The contracting authority will purchase a complete Enterprise GIS solution (software, hardware, dedicated application development, integration) within the ANRMPSG to ensure: - a unified and scalable enterprise database; - multi-user versioning and secure collaboration mechanisms; - a 2D/3D analysis capability; - integration of mobile applications with GNSS/RTK positioning; - interoperability with government platforms and European registers. The contracting authority will purchase a complete Enterprise GIS solution (software, hardware, dedicated application development, integration) within the ANRMPSG. Benefits sought: - centralisation and unified management of geospatial data in an enterprise database with full traceability and audit; - rapid publication of datasets and reports through automated ETL workflows; - increased decision-making accuracy through complex spatial and temporal analyses, including 3D visualisations and predictive scenarios; - operational efficiency through mobile applications with offline work, synchronisation and GNSS/RTK support; - full interoperability with national and European platforms (OGC, INSPIRE, DCAT-AP RO); - security of classified data, through exclusive operation of the platform on-premise, with separation of workflows; - grounding of public policies and technical documentation on the basis of precise, updated and standard-compliant data. - Secure web access for: - Interactive visualisation of perimeters; - Search and filter by thematic criteria; - Data import and export (CSV, GeoJSON, SHP, GPKG); - Topological and spatial analyses for: - validation of overlaps between perimeters; - intersection with protected areas, zones of strategic interest, other licences; - Field data collection through compatible mobile applications; - Access based on user account and roles. Products/services to be purchased: 1 Rackable servers - 1 pcs 2 Hybrid storage - 1 pcs 3 Backup & Recovery appliance - 1 pcs 4 Backup & Recovery software - 1 pcs 5 Ethernet network switches - 2 pcs 6 Firewalls - 2 pcs 7 Installation, configuration, training services - 1 pcs 8 Migration/development/application migration services - 1 pcs 9 Enterprise GIS server licence - 1 pcs 10 GIS server licence for publishing and processing raster data and images - 1 pcs 11 Advanced desktop GIS application licence - 3 pcs 12 Standard desktop GIS application licence - 11 pcs 13 Desktop GIS application extension licence for geostatistical analysis - 1 pcs 14 Desktop GIS application extension licence for spatial analysis - 3 pcs 16 Desktop GIS application extension licence for data interoperability - 3 pcs 16 Desktop GIS application extension licence for 3D analysis - 3 pcs 17 Installation and configuration services, dedicated application development and technical support - 1 pcs

sig_6143c592915d750b899f.description: Hereon requires external support for the migration of its SAP ERP system to S/4. The brownfield approach is to be used. This is a technical migration; potential improvements or optimisations will be carried out subsequently, decoupled from the migration. The subject matter of Lot 1 is the provision of comprehensive consultancy services for the planning, execution and documentation of the migration of the existing SAP ERP system to SAP S/4HANA. The services shall be performed in close coordination with the client's specialist departments. The contractor shall assume the following tasks: 3.1. Project planning and design - Preparation of a project schedule and content plan in close coordination with Hereon - Development of a migration concept including test design, definition of responsibilities and accompanying documentation 3.2. System analysis and process evaluation - Review of the existing SAP ERP systems with regard to the S/4HANA migration - Identification and evaluation of correction requirements in the implemented business processes - Communication of correction requirements to the specialist departments and verification of implementation 3.3. Archiving and system preparation - Archiving of FI and MM documents from completed financial years 2014-2019 - Setup of a sandbox system - Execution of necessary system copies from production to test systems 3.4. Migration and customising - Execution of the necessary customising - Execution and testing of the S/4HANA migration on sandbox, test and production systems - Review and adjustment of structural authorisations in connection with the Cross-Application Time Sheet (CATS) - Analysis of existing roles and authorisations in the SAP ERP system as well as evaluation and application of new authorisation objects in the context of S/4HANA - Execution of the H4S4 conversion - Review and migration of the personnel cost commitment processor, ensuring functionality and data integrity in personnel cost planning - Connection of the SAP Enterprise Portal and support for the connection of the above-mentioned non-SAP products 3.5. Documentation and quality assurance - Preparation of audit-compliant final documentation of the migration - Support in the review of non-SAP software - Support during an internal security check (SAP Basis) 3.6. Training and hypercare - Preparation of (delta) training materials - Conducting training sessions for participating employees and key users - Provision of live support (hypercare) after the migration 3.7. Cooperation with the client - All services shall be provided in close coordination with the responsible specialist departments - Tasks that can sensibly be carried out by Hereon itself (e.g. non-SAP software, authorisation roles) shall be processed internally accordingly 3.8. Period and scope - The consultancy service is to be provided over a period from early 2026 to mid-2027.; As part of an ongoing SAP migration project, an external service provider is commissioned with Lot 2 to technically accompany and evaluate the project phases of concept review, test preparation and test execution as well as the final documentation. The objective is quality assurance and risk minimisation in the migration process, as well as ensuring audit-compliant documentation. The contract specifically comprises the following services: 4.1. Review of the migration concept - Analysis of the migration concept for completeness, consistency and feasibility - with a particular focus on ensuring that the planned documentation meets the requirements of an audit - Identification of potential risks and vulnerabilities, particularly with regard to the traceability and audibility of the migration steps - Preparation of an evaluation with recommended actions to ensure audit-compliant documentation 4.2. Support for test preparation and test execution - Advice on the planning and organisation of test activities (e.g. system, integration and acceptance tests) - Support in the definition of test cases and test data so that traceability and audibility for an audit are guaranteed at all times - Quality assurance during test execution with a particular focus on complete and audit-compliant logging - Evaluation of test results and derivation of measures 4.3. Review of the final documentation - Evaluation of project documentation regarding traceability, completeness and conformity with project objectives - Support in the preparation of handover documents so that all necessary evidence for a subsequent audit is available 4.4. Conditions of participation - Demonstrable experience in supporting SAP migration projects - Specialist knowledge of SAP ERP and SAP S/4HANA - Experience in test management and quality assurance - Knowledge of standard project management and IT service management standards (e.g. PRINCE2, ITIL) 4.5. Period and scope The consultancy service is to be provided alongside the project over a period from early 2026 to mid-2027. The exact scope will be agreed upon when the contract is awarded.

sig_6147e73e78c8ff9c06ad.description: Consultants from COWI are currently conducting a feasibility study for Sporveien in Oslo. The purpose of this study is to define technology-independent and supplier-independent functional requirements for the future signalling system of the Oslo tram network, which consists of more than 130km of tracks with almost 100 stopping points. The tram infrastructure in Oslo has a history stretching back over 150 years, and has recently seen significant investment in modern rolling stock. This provides a unique opportunity to assess future solutions for a modern signalling system, and Sporveien has expressed a desire to invest in a future signalling system for the trams. As part of this project, we wish to gather information from suppliers of signalling and light rail systems. We therefore invite relevant suppliers to share information about your solutions, technologies, and experiences. We are particularly interested in systems that support safe, modern operation and that are adaptable to both the current and future needs of the Oslo tram network. Additionally, Sporveien AS and COWI AS are planning a dialogue conference with suppliers in Oslo on November 13th. This conference will provide an opportunity to discuss future collaborations and explore new opportunities for growth and development. We hope to see you at this conference. Once we have established contact with your organization and received your company’s contact information we will send you a letter of invitation with the complete aganda. Please see https://www.sporveien.no/for-leverandorer/trikkens-fremtidige-signalsystem/dialogue-conference/ for more information.

sig_615a7ad8699f790a495c.description: The North East Mayoral Strategic Authority (North East MSA) seeks to commission an external consultant to undertake an independent programme level evaluation of the Child Poverty Action Plan 2025-2030. The evaluation will assess the design, implementation, and impact of a complex, multi-strand programme delivered between August 2025 and March 2030. This will include directly funded activities, wider activities mobilised through the programme and selected aligned activities where appropriate and supported by the available evidence. The commissioned evaluation is intended as a cross-cutting programme-level evaluation of the Child Poverty Action Plan as a whole. It is recognised that individual projects, interventions and delivery activity within the wider programme will be subject to separate monitoring, evaluation and research activity commissioned by the North East MSA or undertaken by delivery partners. The evaluation will synthesise evidence generated through proportionate project level evaluations (including light touch monitoring and in depth project deep dives) to provide a coherent, programme wide assessment and will not be responsible for conducting primary project-level evaluations, except where explicitly agreed. This will support strategic assurance, learning and decision making, and inform future iterations of the Action Plan and wider North East MSA and regional policy and investment decisions. The programme-level evaluation will therefore consider both the evidence relating to individual interventions and the combined contribution of the wider programme towards the intended outcomes of the Child Poverty Action Plan. The programme‐level evaluation will also seek to determine the degree to which reducing child poverty has been embedded as a cross-cutting theme across North East MSA activity, and that of partners. This will include examining how the Child Poverty Reduction Unit and the regional Child Poverty Action Plan have influenced strategic priorities, programme and project design, funding and delivery decisions, and whether they have contributed to changes in policies, practices and activities beyond those directly funded through the programme. Advisory services for the format "Digi-Expert-kommunal" for the Hessian Ministry for Digitalisation and Innovation in two lots Lot LOT-0001: Foundations of digital transformation. Hessian municipalities are currently in very different phases of digital transformation. Municipalities have very different advisory needs in the course of digital transformation and in the planning and implementation of digitalisation projects. Projects with a high degree of innovation in particular bring with them a wide range of issues that must be answered promptly and individually for successful implementation. This can also be clearly observed in the digitalisation projects funded via the promotion of smart municipalities and regions under the "Starke Heimat Hessen" programme. The Smart Region office anchored in the Hessian Ministry for Digitalisation and Innovation (HMD) will therefore expand its advisory services for municipalities. The new advisory format "Digi-Expert-kommunal" is intended to offer Hessian municipalities individual, provider- and product-neutral ad hoc advice on various topics: from digital strategy, change management, project management to specialist topics such as data platforms, open source, artificial intelligence (AI), digital twin, digitalisation of services of general interest (smart city/smart region). The HMD will make available a pool of experts via the Smart Region office, from which municipalities can choose as needed. They can book them for various occasions/settings via the Smart Region office. This is intended to provide an impetus for the digital transformation of the municipalities and to dismantle hurdles in digitalisation. From October to December 2025, the format "Digi-Expert-kommunal" was piloted with selected topics and a limited quota. In the three-month pilot phase, a total of 52 advisory discussions were brokered. These were accounted for by 40 municipalities. 26 municipalities were each brokered one advisory discussion, 14 municipalities were brokered two or three advisory discussions. The advisory effort (= duration of discussion + preparation and follow-up) per municipality was limited to ten hours. Each of the advised municipalities took up an average of 5,7 hours of advisory effort from the following topics in the short pilot phase: AI in administration/AI in services of general interest, procurement advice (not the subject of this call for competition), digital strategy, digital services of general interest/smart region in general, change management/digital mindset, digital twin, project management/project control, open source/proprietary solutions. The format was very well received within a very short time and with minimal communication effort. The feedback from the municipalities was consistently positive and once again confirmed the need for tailor-made and short-term advice. The advisory need could not be nearly covered within the pilot phase. During the evaluation, the municipalities wished for a continuation and expansion of the offer. Lot 1 comprises general advisory topics relating to digital transformation and thus creates the basis for municipalities to deal with technical implementation later (Lot 2). In particular advice on: • Digital strategy, • Project management, • Change management, • Digital services of general interest, • Citizen participation. For this lot, based on the figures from the pilot phase and an assumed number of 270 interested municipalities, a demand of 810 hours per year is estimated. This estimated quantity serves calculation purposes only. There is no entitlement to call off this quantity. Further details can be found in the specification of services.
