sig_6174fa7d86935402e7f5.description: Support for the school data centre in the IT services and project environment. The specific tasks and project priorities are defined, specified and fleshed out in the course of the individual awards. The main areas of support focus on the new and further development of software solutions (including in the area of official school administration). This support relates both to the implementation of new functional requirements and to technical software updates. The requirements can lead to either existing applications having to be revised or new independent applications having to be developed. Should a new application be necessary, it must be embedded in the existing system landscape. In particular, the new development of software modules requires the drafting and analysis of software architecture designs. For the school administration area, the following must be observed: For legal and organisational reasons, this is a distributed software system. Both central services are operated in the IT-DLZ, but, depending on the software component, components are also operated on-premise by different operators on up to 1.600 servers. The central components include, among others, an identity management system and a central school server, as well as other applications. Software components, such as lesson management, are operated decentrally. The central components are used by all schools and must be designed for a corresponding load. It should be noted that Windows, Linux and MacOS must be supported for the operation of the decentralised components. Web components are expected to function for different browsers on different operating systems (e.g. Chrome, Firefox, Safari). As a rule, the implementation of new requirements means that both the central components and the decentralised components must be taken into account. The new and further development of the applications takes place on the basis of individual development packages. The basis is formed by the functional compilation of requirements for the system. Technical requirements are compiled by the IT-DLZ and bundled with the desired functional requirements. These technical requirements are subsumed under the term 'maintenance and care'. The IT-DLZ is responsible for the existing software modules to ensure that the functionality of the software is maintained. This means in particular that the software components are adapted to new versions of, for example, operating systems, application servers, databases or third-party libraries used. The functional requirements are drawn up, for example, by the StMUK and coordinated with the IT-DLZ. The IT-DLZ as the contracting authority then coordinates the requirements with the contractor. One part of the tasks will be the preparation of a rough technical implementation proposal with an assessment of the effort. On the basis of the analyses, the functional requirements are prioritised and bundled into development packages. Following the complete compilation of a further development package, the final estimate of effort for the implementation of this further development package takes place. Based on this estimate of effort, the StMUK, for example, commissions the contracting authority (IT-DLZ) with the implementation of the further development package. The implementation of released further development packages follows an agile software development process.

sig_61db8c2d935dbc508fe1.description:
Nordværk I/S is inviting tenders for the procurement, implementation, and subsequent operation and maintenance of a new specialised system for the administration and support of waste collection, hereinafter referred to as the Solution. The procurement is carried out with the aim of replacing the current system support for Nordværk's waste management area and establishing a comprehensive, modern and future-proof Solution that can support the business processes associated with the administration, planning, case processing, execution, registration, follow-up and documentation of waste collection. The procurement includes the delivery and implementation of the Solution as well as the services necessary to establish and commission the Solution. This includes, among other things, clarification and configuration, migration and establishment of relevant data, establishment and adaptation of integrations, testing, training, documentation, commissioning, as well as subsequent operation, support, maintenance and further development in accordance with the Contract and the Contract's appendices. The Solution must support Nordværk's entire value chain in the waste management area from a citizen's or customer's scheme, enquiry or order to the planning and execution of the specific waste management task, as well as subsequent registration, case processing, follow-up, controlling, documentation and the basis for billing. The procurement is part of Nordværk's work to ensure efficient, cohesive and data-driven administration and operation of waste collection. The Solution must support standardised and verifiable workflows, high data quality, a reduced need for manual processes and better opportunities for management, follow-up and ongoing development of the waste management area. At the same time, the Solution must be able to integrate appropriately into Nordværk's other system landscape and support organisational, operational and technological changes over the term of the Contract. The overall purpose of the Solution is in particular: i) to support cohesive and efficient workflows within customer administration, case processing, operational planning, task execution, registration, controlling and follow-up, ii) to support operational waste collection for both Nordværk's own and external waste collectors, including planning, routes, navigation, registration of completed tasks, handling of deviations and operational follow-up, and iii) to establish a flexible and future-proof system foundation with high data quality and good opportunities for integration, configuration, automation, reporting and ongoing further development. The business processes and functionality applicable to the Solution are described in more detail in Appendix 3 of the tender documents – Delivery Description. The Solution is expected to support several different internal and external user groups. This includes, among others, approx. 186-200 internal waste management employees, 55-65 administrative employees, 10-20 administrators/superusers, 40-50 administrative users at external waste collectors and 100-110 waste management employees at external waste collectors. The user groups will have different roles and access needs in the Solution. The Solution must be established on a technical platform that supports the requirements for availability, security, integration, scalability, operation and further development set out in the Contract and the Contract's appendices. The more detailed technical requirements for the Solution and its establishment appear in the relevant appendices of the tender documents. The Solution must have an open, transparent and well-documented architecture and must be able to be integrated into Nordværk's overall system landscape. The Supplier must deliver and maintain the documentation necessary for, inter alia, operation, administration, integrations, configuration, troubleshooting and further development of the Solution, in accordance with the requirements of the Contract and the Contract's appendices. The Solution supports business-critical processes in connection with the daily administration and execution of waste collection. Requirements are therefore set for, among other things, the Solution's availability, stability, security, traceability and data integrity, so that data and registrations can be used reliably in operational management, customer service, case processing, controlling, documentation and as a basis for billing. The Solution must be integrated with a number of Nordværk's other systems and technical solutions. This includes, among other things, relevant interfaces to the billing system, GIS and data basis, self-service solutions, registration equipment, weighing systems and other third-party solutions where data exchange is necessary to support cohesive workflows. The specific requirements for integrations and interfaces appear in the relevant appendices of the tender documents. The tender also contains a number of options for additional functionality and deliveries that Nordværk may choose to use in accordance with the Contract. The specific options and the terms thereof appear in the Contract and the Contract's appendices, including Appendix 3 – Delivery Description. Commissioning of the Solution must take place after the completion of the agreed activities regarding, among other things, clarification, configuration, data migration, integrations, testing, training and approval. The detailed procedure and schedule for implementation and commissioning are determined in accordance with the Contract and the relevant appendices. The Contract thus contains an implementation period of up to 12 months as well as, after commissioning, an operating period of 6 years with the possibility of extension by 2 times 12 months. sig_623fb288af1e8254cc09.description: The subject of the procurement procedure is the establishment of a dynamic purchasing system in accordance with Section 138 et seq. of Act No. 134/2016 Coll., on Public Procurement, as amended (hereinafter referred to as the "Act"). The subject of performance of public contracts awarded under the DPS will be the supply of active or passive network elements or hardware or software technologies for ensuring cybersecurity or perimeter protection. The subject of performance of individual public contracts awarded under the DPS may also be the acquisition or renewal of software licences, the provision of extended warranties or service support in an SLA regime, or the provision of related service, implementation or consulting services relating to these elements or technologies. Individual public contracts will be awarded under the DPS on the basis of individual calls for tenders in accordance with Section 141 of the Act. The procurement conditions for specific public contracts awarded under the DPS will be set out in each individual call for tenders. The awarding of public contracts under the DPS will take place at pre-determined and irregular intervals depending on the operational needs of the contracting authority.

sig_62522eb6d83997d63de7.description: THIS IS NOT A PROCUREMENT NOTICE OR INVITATION TO TENDER BUT A REQUEST FOR INFORMATION FOR MARKET RESEARCH AND TECHNICAL DIALOGUE. This request for information is used to survey the market and obtain information concerning the procurement. The contracting authority does not initiate a tendering procedure by publishing the request for information; instead, a potential procurement notice and invitation to tender will be published later. The request for information does not oblige the contracting authority to carry out the actual procurement. Answering the request for information is not a precondition for participating in a potentially organised subsequent tendering procedure. Suppliers are not paid compensation for answering the request for information or participating in the market dialogue. HUS-yhtymä is preparing the procurement of an Information Security Monitoring and Management Service (CSOC) to maintain the cybersecurity of ICT systems and services owned and managed by HUS-yhtymä and procured from third parties. The procurement may potentially be implemented as a procurement ring with one or more wellbeing services counties of Southern Finland. The answers given to this request for information will be used in planning this procurement. The service to be procured will be delivered by the selected supplier with a 24/7/365 service period under the requirements and service level agreements defined later in the invitation to tender. The offered service must be able to detect, analyse, respond to, report on, and, if necessary, escalate cyber security-related threats, observations and disruptions within the response times given to the customer, and report the aforementioned events and the information security situation in accordance with reporting requirements. The objective of this request for information is to inform about the upcoming procurement and to survey suppliers that have the capability and interest to offer HUS-yhtymä an information security monitoring and management service. The service must include, among other things, CSOC services, vulnerability management, threat hunting, situational awareness service and digital forensics service. The supplier must implement the service using a hybrid model utilising HUS-yhtymä's devices and systems. These systems include, inter alia, SIEM, XDR, NDR, IPS, DLP, SOAR, as well as other modern information security solutions, such as automation utilising artificial intelligence. The supplier must also be able to offer assistance in developing automation. HUS-yhtymä's CSOC experts must retain the necessary rights to all systems. In addition, the purpose is to ascertain suppliers' views on the subject of the procurement and the implementation of the planned tendering. We also want to hear suppliers' views on a contemporary and modern information security monitoring and management solution for a supply-critical organisation of HUS-yhtymä's size. We request suppliers interested in the procurement to submit a service description of their available services in accordance with the request for information in PDF format. sig_626e0fe9980779c88162.description: Digitalisation of invoice processing in relation to billing processes in accordance with § 302 SGB V and § 105 SGB XI. The AOK Baden-Württemberg (hereinafter: AOK BW or contracting authority) is a body governed by public law with joint self-administration by insured persons and employer representatives. It is divided into 14 district directorates and the head office in Stuttgart and insures over 4,6 million people in the state of Baden-Württemberg. To further increase efficiency in the processes, invoice processing is to be digitalised. Specifically, this concerns the billing processes in accordance with § 302 SGB V and § 105 SGB XI. The currently practised workflows differ according to the type of documents transmitted. In around 80-85 % of cases, a data record with a collective invoice is transmitted. In this case, invoice verification by the staff of the AOK Baden-Württemberg is difficult, as the invoice receipts cannot be directly assigned to a file. Around 10 % of cases are purely paper-based. The remaining cases are transmitted with a structured data set and an image. The postal recipients are filled in automatically. The task of the future service provider will be to scan the paper documents and generate a single invoice together with the associated documents. The requirements of the BSI TR-03138 RESISCAN requirements catalogue must be strictly adhered to. Participation in the initiated competition requires that the requirements of the BSI TR-03138 RESISCAN requirements catalogue are met and that the future contractor either proves certification in accordance with the BSI TR-03138 RESISCAN requirements catalogue with the tender or undertakes to submit the application in relation to the services covered by the contract within two months of the award of the contract. If the certificate is not submitted within twelve months of the award of the contract, the contracting authority is entitled to immediate extraordinary termination. Details are set out in the service description.

sig_62902b9bc476a5f53fa6.description: This PIN provides early information about the expected starting date and purchase volume for a pre-commercial procurement (PCP) carried out by the THERESA PCP project and about the open market consultation (OMC) that is organised in preparation of this pre-commercial procurement (PCP). The THERESA Buyers Group of healthcare providers have identified a shared need for innovative and sustainable solutions to treat hospital wastewater (HWW) at the source, before it reaches the municipal network, to reduce environmental and health risks linked to pharmaceutical residues, antimicrobial-resistant microorganisms and genes, and other hazardous contaminants. The THERESA PCP aims to stimulate the development of environmentally sustainable, cost-effective, and scalable on-site HWW treatment systems capable of efficiently removing cytostatic drugs, X-ray contrast agents, antibiotics, antimicrobial-resistant bacteria (ARB) and genes (ARG), while minimising energy consumption, chemical use, and carbon footprint. The contract notice is expected to be published in May-2026 and phase 1 to be started in January 2027, following the PCP timeline. The procurement will take the form of a Pre-Commercial Procurement (PCP) awarding R&D service contracts to several providers in parallel, through a phased and competitive process comprising three stages: Solution design, prototyping, and original development and validation/testing of the first products in real hospital environments. After each phase, intermediate evaluations will down-select the best-performing and most innovative solutions. The contractors with the best-value-for-money solutions will be offered a specific contract for the next phase. The PCP is a joint cross-border initiative coordinated by Fundación Miguel Servet (Spain) as Lead Procurer, on behalf of a Buyers Group of hospitals and public health institutions from Spain, Estonia, Poland, Belgium and the Netherlands, supported by technical and innovation partners. Testing is expected to take place in Spain, Estonia, Poland and the Netherlands to ensure adaptability. Price is not the only award criterion, and all criteria are stated only in the procurement documents. The selected contractors will retain ownership of the Intellectual Property Rights (IPRs) generated during the PCP and will be able to commercially exploit the developed solutions beyond the scope of the procurement. The R&D services will be carried out primarily within the European Union and/or countries associated with the Horizon Europe Programme. At least 50% of the total value of R&D activities will take place within the EU or associated countries. In addition, contractors must ensure that none of the contracted services are performed in countries nor by entities that are subject to EU restrictive measures under Article 29 of the Treaty on the European Union (TEU) and Article 215 of the Treaty on the Functioning of the EU (TFEU)23 (sanctions). They must ensure that none of the goods procured or used for the procurement were developed, produced or supplied in countries or by entities that are subject to such restrictive measures. Duration of the contract in months: 30 months (January 27 to June 29). The duration covers all three PCP phases: Solution design, prototyping, and original development and validation/testing of the first products. The PCP is expected to start after the publication of the Contract Notice and to end upon completion of the validation phase. This contract is not subject to renewal.
sig_62902b9bc476a5f53fa6.title: Pre-Commercial Procurement (PCP) of innovative and sustainable solutions to treat Hospital and Healthcare System Wastewater – THERESA PCP

sig_62c985fe42f03983f924.description: This concerns the procurement of an intelligent (web-based) SaaS application for the automated execution of self-scans, acting as a gateway for all ground-breaking work. Users (engineers, work preparers and contractors) must be able to import route alignments or enter them manually. Subsequently, on the basis of map layers, the system generates a real-time status (Green/Orange/Red) for soil, unexploded ordnance, archaeology, and flora and fauna respectively. Based on the information currently known to us, we estimate the volume of this tender at a range of 28.000 to 45.000 self-scans per year. One self-scan here comprises the automated assessment on all four research themes (soil quality, archaeology, flora & fauna and unexploded ordnance). Calculated over the duration of the framework agreement, this amounts to: • Estimated quantity over the initial term (4 years): approximately 112.000 to 180.000 self-scans; • Estimated quantity over the total maximum term (8 years, including both extension options): approximately 224.000 to 320.000 self-scans.

sig_648565ddafa50b14b32a.description: 1.0 INTRODUCTION & PURPOSE This Request for Information (RFI) is issued solely for market research, planning, and information-gathering purposes in accordance with FAR Part 10 and FAR 15.201. This is not a Sources Sought synopsis or a Request for Proposal (RFP). No contract will be awarded directly from this posting, and the Government is under no obligation to issue a solicitation based on this notice. The 434th Contracting Flight (434 CONF/PK), in coordination with the 434th Civil Engineer Squadron (434 CES) at Grissom Air Reserve Base, is seeking technical feedback from the commercial construction and unit-price estimating software industry. The primary goal of this RFI is to gather industry input on a streamlined, performance-based acquisition structure for a future SABER contract. The Government is particularly interested in receiving feedback on how to structure its pricing database requirements to maximize open competition, eliminate the administrative burden of traditional "mock projects," and prevent post-award "Non-Prepriced Item (NPI) creep." 2.0 PROGRAM DESCRIPTION & ANTICIPATED STRATEGY The Government is planning a Single-Award Indefinite-Delivery/Indefinite-Quantity (IDIQ) SABER contract with the following anticipated structure: Estimated Ordering Ceiling: $9,000,000.00 over a five (5) year ordering period. Minimum Contract Guarantee: $2,000.00 (to be obligated at time of basic contract award). Scope of Work: Multi-trade maintenance, repair, minor construction, and renovation projects across real property facilities at Grissom ARB. Core trades include carpentry, roofing, excavation, electrical, plumbing, HVAC, masonry, demolition, concrete, and localized hazardous material abatement. Streamlined Price Evaluation (No Mock Project): To drastically accelerate procurement lead times and eliminate unpaid proposal preparation costs for industry, the Government intends to evaluate price strictly based on competitively bidded coefficients (adjustment factors) applied to pre-disclosed, weighted government workload estimates. The traditional "mock project" estimating phase will be bypassed during source selection. Performance-Based Unit Price Database: To support a "no mock project" model legally and defensibly under FAR Part 16 and Part 36, the contract must rely on a highly comprehensive, pre-priced Unit Price Book (UPB) / Construction Task Catalog (CTC) that is locally researched, standardized, granular, and capable of keeping post-award NPIs under 10% of total task order values. 3.0 SPECIFIC AREAS OF INQUIRY & QUESTIONNAIRE Firms choosing to respond are requested to provide detailed, objective feedback on the following five administrative and technical categories: Section 3.1: Performance-Based Technical Equivalency vs. Database Size The Government wants to ensure the pricing database is comprehensive enough to prevent post-award "NPI creep" without establishing arbitrary restrictions that limit competition. Rather than relying on a raw line-item record count as a proxy for database quality, does your firm support defining technical equivalency based on performance outcomes? Specifically, how should the Government measure a database's ability to minimize NPIs to less than 10% of total task order values? To prove database capability without running a labor-intensive "mock project," would your firm support an automated "Coverage Mapping Report" during source selection? Under this method, the Government would provide a standard, historical list of approximately 100 typical Air Force repair and maintenance tasks. Offerors would run this list against their database to prove they can pre-price 90% or more of the workload value. Detail any software or database limitations to executing this type of coverage report. Describe how your estimating platform and database ensure that unit prices are derived from direct local market research (localized labor, material, equipment, and productivity rates for the Grissom ARB/Indiana area) rather than relying on national averages adjusted by a flat regional index. Section 3.2: Coefficient Absorption & Overhead Definitions To ensure a fair "apples-to-apples" price evaluation, the bidded coefficients must cover all operational overhead. Please confirm your firm's capability to absorb the following overhead costs directly within your proposed bidded coefficients, with no separate or direct billing to the Government: All cost-estimating software licensing, support, and maintenance fees (including providing a minimum of two concurrent user licenses to 434 CES and 434 CONF personnel). Unrestricted on-base office operations, project manager training, and material storage yard maintenance. Maintenance of a localized physical/digital material submittal library. Basic design, drafting, site verification, and as-built drawing preparation. What standard RFP definitions are required in Section L to ensure all offerors are absorbing these exact overhead elements on a common basis? Section 3.3: Safeguards Against Unbalanced Bidding Without a mock project, a primary risk is that a contractor may submit an artificially low standard-hours coefficient to win the award, intending to recover margins through unconstrained Non-Prepriced Items (NPIs) or non-standard hours. Does your firm support a solicitation restriction that locks the NPI coefficient (the markup applied to raw subcontractor quotes) to a factor equal to, or less than, the competitively bidded standard-hours coefficient? What are the industry best practices to prevent unbalanced bidding across auxiliary coefficients (such as secure areas or after-hours work)? Does your firm support capping auxiliary coefficients at a fixed percentage above the standard-hours baseline? Section 3.4: Database Update Frequency & Pricing Baselines SABER contracts are subject to severe market and economic price fluctuations over a five-year period. Can your software lock the cost database to a fixed annual baseline for Grissom ARB, adjusting base unit prices once a year via a localized City Cost Index (CCI) update, while keeping bidded coefficients fixed? Does your firm recommend utilizing a separate Economic Price Adjustment (EPA) clause, or do annual localized database updates sufficiently protect both parties from inflation? Section 3.5: Software Cloud Security & Network Access Grissom's local communications squadron maintains strict software security protocols. Is your JOC/SABER estimating software platform a web-based, cloud-accessed system? Does your software platform comply with Cybersecurity Maturity Model Certification (CMMC) 2.0 or hold FedRAMP authorization? Provide details of any active Authorities to Operate (ATOs) currently held by your estimating software platform on any active DoD, Air Force, or other federal networks. 4.0 RESPONSE SUBMISSION INSTRUCTIONS Interested firms are requested to submit their RFI Response packages matching the following instructions: Cover Page: Include Company Name, Address, Point of Contact (Name, Phone, Email), UEI, CAGE Code, active State of Indiana General Contractor licensing status, and active SBA Socioeconomic Status (e.g., active 8(a) program graduation date). For each contract, specify: Contract Number, Agency, and Point of Contact. Pricing mechanism used (e.g., JOC with bidded coefficients, SABER, or traditional lump sum). Total contract value and NPI performance history (demonstrated percentage of work priced out of the pre-priced catalog vs. NPIs). Format & Page Limit: Responses must be in PDF format and are limited to a total of fifteen (15) pages (excluding cover page and licensing/surety attachments). sig_64c0b8872f81ca6650b8.description: REQUEST FOR INFORMATION (RFI) Personnel Security Alert Management (PSAM) Platform Defense Counterintelligence and Security Agency (DCSA) RFI Reference: DCSA-PSAM-RFI-2026-001 Response Instructions: Due Date: September 22, 2026 @ 1:00pm ET Vendors shall fill out the attached questionnaire and submit it via email to Lindsay Weindruch: lindsay.a.weindruch.civ@mail.mil Disclaimer: This RFI is for informational and planning purposes only. It is not a Request for Proposal, does not commit the Government to any award, and responses are not offers the Government can accept to form a contract. The Government will not pay for information submitted. Do not include classified information in responses; proprietary information will be protected to the extent permitted by law. 1. Purpose DCSA seeks information from Security Information Event Management (SIEM) and Security Operations Center (SOC) platform vendors on commercial capabilities that can support personnel-security operations through cybersecurity event correlation, alert triage, risk-based prioritization, and workflow automation. DCSA is particularly interested in solutions that can identify, correlate, prioritize, and route cybersecurity alerts and incidents associated with members of the trusted workforce for appropriate personnel-security review. 2. Problem Statement DCSA's Continuous Vetting (CV) program faces high daily detection volumes from many sources, much of it low-value noise. Alerts which are drawn from dozens of criminal, financial, terrorism-screening, foreign-contact, foreign-travel, and public-record data sources are still worked largely first-in-first-out rather than by risk, so high-consequence alerts can wait behind routine, low-risk items and case queues have grown faster than staffing. While CV has made progress in detecting potential risk indicators far faster than legacy periodic-reinvestigation models, it is still triaging risk with case-management approaches built for a lower-volume era. 3. Desired Capability DCSA seeks a solution that will incorporate the following capabilities: Ingests and normalizes 40+ structured and unstructured data sources—including APIs, databases, PDFs, and open-source information—into a unified alert stream. Correlates alerts to individual subjects using privacy-preserving tokenization, enabling cross-source analysis without unnecessary exposure of personal data. Applies explainable AI/ML risk scoring aligned with federal adjudicative guidelines—such as financial considerations, criminal conduct, and foreign influence—rather than generic threat categories. Analyst-facing outputs must provide clear rationale (for example, LIME, SHAP, or an equivalent method). Automates low-value alert handling through configurable business rules that suppress duplicates, auto-clear qualifying low-risk alerts, and reduce false positives. Routes alerts through tiered, human-in-the-loop workflows for validation, investigation, and adjudication. The system must prioritize alerts by assessed risk—not age—and immediately escalate critical or high-risk alerts. Supports continuous improvement by feeding adjudicator outcomes back into the rules engine and AI/ML models, subject to appropriate oversight and validation. Integrates with—not replaces—authoritative case-management systems of record through documented, open-standard APIs, including OpenAPI 3.1 and REST. The capability must generate upstream triage signals rather than create a parallel case-management silo. Provides leadership and operational dashboards showing key performance measures, including time to detect, time to respond, false-positive rate, and backlog by priority, with near-real-time visibility into detection, response, and workload status. Avoids vendor lock-in. Proprietary data formats or closed APIs are disqualifying. Can operate in controlled IL5 and classified IL6 environments appropriate for intelligence-derived derogatory information and consistent with Department of War cross-domain security requirements.

The Contractor will be tasked with carrying out information activities about the consultations, holding consultation meetings and conferences concerning the plan update throughout the country. The Contractor will be responsible for collecting comments, including coordinating the process of collecting and addressing them, along with preparing a public consultation report containing a table of how the comments were addressed. • Detailed description of the contract: The Contractor's duties will include: 1. Launching and running, for the duration of the project, a website dedicated to public consultations, including developing and posting information on the aforesaid website. 3. Preparing an electronic version of the poster and banner regarding the public consultations. 4. Preparing and printing leaflets concerning the consultations. 5. Preparing and printing a roll-up concerning public consultations of planning document drafts in water management (width 100 cm, height 200 cm) – 2 pieces. 6. Publishing information about the consultations in the regional press – 32 pieces. 7. Coordinating work on drawing up the table for addressing comments and motions, including: designing the table, supplementing it with the content of submitted comments, cooperating with other entities (e.g. distributing and collecting completed tables regarding responses). 8. sig_64f2881c21c0394e8649.description: 1.0 Overview The U.S. Army Contracting Command (ACC), on behalf of Portfolio Acquisition Executive (PAE) Maneuver Ground, Project Manager Maneuver Medical Systems (PM M2S), is issuing this Request for Prototype Proposals (RPP) to solicit prototype project proposals for a modernized Anesthesia Workstation System (AWS). This RPP is issued pursuant to the Other Transaction Authority (OTA) under 10 U.S.C. § 4022. This is a DIRECT OTA and is NOT a solicitation for a procurement contract under the Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR). Consortium membership is not required to respond to this RPP. 2.0 Mission Need & Scope The U.S. Army requires a Commercial-Off-The-Shelf (COTS) or Non-Developmental Item (NDI) anesthesia workstation system capable of supporting life-saving medical operations in austere environments at Role of Care (ROC) 3 with little to no modification. The system must overcome the capability gaps of legacy systems, specifically regarding interoperability with Army Oxygen Generation Systems, heavy logistical footprint (weight), and proprietary maintenance constraints. The Government intends to award one (1) OT Agreement for the delivery of two (2) prototype units. These units will undergo rigorous operational testing by the Medical Test and Evaluation Activity (MTEAC) and environmental testing conducted in accordance with MIL-STD-810H. Proposed solutions must be FDA-cleared for human use and Trade Agreements Act (TAA) compliant. A high priority for this effort is organic supportability. The Government strongly prefers systems designed to be maintainable by military Biomedical Equipment Technicians (BMETs) at the Field and Depot levels without reliance on proprietary vendor service contracts. 3.0 Follow-On Production Authority In accordance with 10 U.S.C. § 4022(f), this OT Agreement is issued with a provision for follow-on production. Upon successful prototype completion and validation, the Government may award a follow-on production contract or OT Agreement for approximately one hundred and eighty (180) AWS units without further competitive procedures. 4.0 Proposal Submission Instructions All proposal instructions, technical specifications (CODS and APAs), and evaluation criteria are detailed in the attached Request for Prototype Proposals (RPP) document. Questions: All questions must be submitted in writing via email to the Agreements Officer and Agreements Specialist no later than 15:00 ET on 17 September 2026. Proposals: Proposals must be submitted via DoD SAFE file transfer or secure email no later than 16:00 ET on 01 October 2026. Communications: Unauthorized contact with program office personnel or technical end-users regarding this RPP may result in disqualification. All communications must be directed to the points of contact listed below. Attachments The Final RPP Document (which includes Appendix E) The Standalone ADRL Document Attachment A (The blank TAA Certificate) Attachment C / OTA Articles Points of Contact Primary Point of Contact: Timothy Compton Agreements Officer Email: timothy.j.compton7.civ@army.mil Secondary Point of Contact: Roxanne A. Dalrymple Agreements Specialist Email: roxanne.a.dalrymple.civ@army.mil

sig_6512f77e4da294323564.description: This notice is not an official launch of our procurement(s), it is to alert the market to future opportunities and allow us to begin conversations that will shape plans for multiple future requirements. The Cabinet Office (Government Skills Group) is transforming the way learning and development (L&D) is designed, procured, and delivered across the Civil Service. Following the announcement by the Chief Secretary to the Prime Minister, the government is establishing the new National School of Government and Public Services (hereon The National School). The National School is tasked with delivering high-quality, targeted training to approximately 558,000 civil servants, developing executive leadership in the wider public sector, and to partner with public sector training bodies. The strategic goal of the National School is to shift away from the historically outsourced prime-supplier managed-service model. In its place, the Cabinet Office is building an insourced, hybrid capability. Under this new Future Operating Model (FOM), the Cabinet Office will directly manage core operations, standard curricula, and stakeholder engagement. However, expert external provision will remain a critical element of the programme. The National School transformation programme relies on three core, interdependent pillars to transition Civil Service training away from fully outsourced prime-supplier models toward an in-house, hybrid operating model by April 2028. Together, these pillars work to build direct relationships with suppliers, provide a modern digital learning infrastructure, and establish robust in-house operational workflows. Pillar 1: Future Supplier Partnerships (FSP) The FSP project serves as the commercial enabler of the new operating model, building the in-house capability required to buy learning services and manage supply chains directly. We aim to establish direct, value-driven contractual relationships with UK-based SMEs, universities, business schools, and niche providers. The project team have identified an indicative Three-Stage Roadmap to enable this delivery: Stage 1 (Immediate - April 2027): Procuring urgent digital and specialist training needs that cannot be fulfilled through existing frameworks. Stage 2 (April 2027-March 2028): Phased procurement for core, National School-sponsored curriculum, coaching, and talent programmes. Stage 3 (March 2028 onwards): On-going phased procurements falling out of Stages 1 and 2, depending on the length of contracts identified. The scope of the requirements will cover several key procurement categories, including, but not limited to, specialised coaching pools (including for neuro-diverse leaders), blended training delivery, learning design (retaining Crown Intellectual Property), access to subject matter experts including within academia, independent research and evaluation, helpdesk/admin surge, and off-the-shelf qualifications. Pillar 2: Future Technologies (FT) The Future Technologies project focuses on designing and implementing the digital architecture required to run a personalised training operation for approximately 558,000 civil servants. The core objective here is the setting up and integration of platforms to manage the access, booking, payments, and evaluation of learning materials. This involves transitioning away from heavy manual processes to maximise technological efficiencies. At this stage the project team has identified the central deliverable as a unified online portal allowing learners to access the full National School offering. Key technologies in scope for procurement include, but are not limited to, a new Learning Management System (LMS)/ Learning Experience Platform (LXP), Customer Relationship Management (CRM) systems to centralise stakeholder engagement, and design/delivery tools. Pillar 3: Future Learning Operations (FLO) The Learning Operations project is responsible for building the actual systems, processes, and internal capabilities required to run the day-to-day training operations in-house. Their core objective is establishing an integrated operational function by April 2028 that supports over 558,000 civil servants in completing their learning journeys. It is highly dependent on the digital and commercial pillars to develop the underlying platforms that support operations. Market Involvement As part of the initial phases of the programme, the project teams are keen to connect with the market and gain insight into current trends, operations and barriers. sig_654e236c4fe1c73fa01a.description: The Contracting Authority is tendering a contract regarding a common Operating Platform for the Contracting Authority's IT system portfolio. After Transition In, where the Support Systems are transitioned to the Operating Platform, the Supplier shall be responsible for operation, including Data Centre operation/Hybrid Cloud Custom Services/Hybrid Cloud Standard Services and Infrastructure operation, as well as Support and maintenance of the Operating Platform. Furthermore, after Transition In, the Supplier must ensure Subsequent Transitions to and Transformations of the Operating Platform. The purpose of the common Operating Platform is, among other things, to obtain secure and stable operation with high availability as well as a modern technological platform with a high degree of scalability that supports the needs of the Customer and the municipalities. It is the Contracting Authority's business need that all Services are delivered with high delivery reliability and robustness, and that the Supplier demonstrates proactivity in the collaboration. In addition to the focus on secure and stable operation, the Supplier must ensure a successful Transition In of the Support Systems with the least possible disruption to the Contracting Authority's business, as well as Subsequent Transitions and ongoing Transformation, including a gradual transition to Hybrid Cloud Standard Services and, to the extent that it supports the needs of the Contracting Authority and the municipalities, Managed Public Cloud Services. In connection with Transition In, a high level of information security must be established, which must be continuously maintained and improved throughout the Contract. The contract has the following 4 main services: I. Transition In, where the Contracting Authority initially wishes for the establishment of and secure and stable transfer to an Operating Platform for the Support Systems, based on Hybrid Cloud Services, with the implementation of, for example, project management, transition organisation, building of operational capacity, transfer of Environments and data, and takeover of knowledge from the Outgoing Supplier. Subsequently, the Contracting Authority wishes to carry out successive Subsequent Transitions for a number of the Contracting Authority's other IT systems from the current operating models to the Operating Platform, based on Hybrid Cloud Services. II. Ongoing Services for the Operating Platform, including; a. Support; b. Hybrid Cloud Services, including Hybrid Cloud Standard Services and Hybrid Cloud Custom Services; c. Tools for supporting Application Suppliers; d. Governance, Operational Processes, security services, Documentation, and operational reporting. III. Service catalogue with the use of standardised methods, technologies, and services, through which the Contracting Authority wishes to be able to provision services on a cloud platform that; a) Offers a wide range of services; b) Is accessible via the public internet; c) Has a publicly available price structure with settlement of services according to consumption on subscription terms. IV. Methods and tools for supporting collaboration with the Contracting Authority and the Contracting Authority's application suppliers, where the Contracting Authority wishes for the delivery of the future operating platform to be supported by proactive collaboration across the Contracting Authority's IT system portfolio.
sig_654e236c4fe1c73fa01a.title: Tender for a common Operating Platform

sig_65ea4307482e23fc5a37.description: Invitation to a supplier conference for the Norwegian Defence ́s digital transformation in Fanehallen 5 October 2026 The Norwegian Defence and Defence Material Agency invites tenderers, research and education institutions as well as other relevant actors to a supplier conference 5 October 2015 at 09.00-12.00 in Fanehallen at Akershus fortress. The Norwegian Armed Forces are facing a historic commitment to digitalisation and technological modernisation. The aim is to strengthen the Norwegian Defence ́s operative ability through a modern digital foundation, increased use of data and artificial intelligence, stronger interaction across the branches of the armed forces and better decision support in all domains. In the coming years, significant investments will be made including modernisation of the Norwegian Armed Forces' secure platforms, the development of the future digital work surface, modernisation of performance critical joint systems (ERP), establishment and modernisation of data centre, network and communication capacity, strengthened cyber security, utilisation of artificial intelligence as well as the establishment of modern platform and cloud services. The Norwegian Armed Forces cannot realise and succeed with this ambition alone. A successful digital transformation requires close cooperation between the defence sector, the supplier market, academia and other actors in the total defence. The aim of the conference is therefore to give the market insight into the Norwegian Armed Forces' strategic direction, planned commitments and future needs, at the same time as facilitating an open dialogue on possibilities, technology development and forms of cooperation. Topics that can be expected to be addressed at the supplier conference: The Defence Staff: Strategic Framework and Direction Vision, strategic guidance and relevant priorities for the development of a data-driven defence, including the status of the Norwegian Armed Forces' digital transformation and presentation of new management documents. How data, artificial intelligence and digitalisation shall contribute to increased operative effect. The Norwegian Armed Forces: The sector's need for digital capabilities and the effect Road ahead for digital capabilities: Strategic commitments, priorities, future needs and desired effects for the sector's digital development. Norwegian Defence Materiel Agency: Procurements and market dialogue Strategies for procurement and market involvement in order to realise the future of digital defence. The conference is a part of the Norwegian Defence ́s market dialogue and is being held to increase mutual understanding between the defence sector and the market. The information presented shall contribute to better predictability for suppliers and form the basis for future procurements and collaboration possibilities. Participation in the conference does not provide any competitive advantage in later procurements. Any future procurements will be made in accordance with the procurement regulations and announced in the ordinary way. Register via the link below: The supplier conference 5 October 2026 Registration deadline is 1 October, 15:00. Due to capacity and security reasons, there can be limits on the number of participants. Each company is invited to provide up to two representatives if the company has fewer than 200 employees, three representatives of 200-400 employees and four representatives if the company has more than 400 employees. There will be access and ID control by the entrance. The strategic management documents will be digitally made available right after the conference. The meeting will be held physically and the language will be Norwegian. We hope that you will participate - together we shape the digital defence of the future and make innovation operative defence ability. Well met! The Norwegian Defence Staff | The Norwegian Armed Forces | Norwegian Defence Materiel Agency
sig_65ea4307482e23fc5a37.title: Supplier conference on the Norwegian Defence ́s digital transformation 5 October 2026.

Keighley Central (BD20, BD21, BD22) 2. Bolton Woods (BD2, BD18) 3. Barkerend and Bradford Moor (BD3) 4. Parkside (BD5) This tender only relates to the Parkside area of Bradford The focus of the research The research is about what makes a healthy urban place. We want to design research questions with the community in order to answer the following overarching themes: • What urban and environmental factors have an impact on wellbeing and which of these does the community prioritise? • How do healthy places develop over time? • How do different communities experience and benefit from different features of urban places over time? • How can we measure and track changes in urban places that are important for health and wellbeing? How will it work? By bringing together community members who live in and are impacted by changes in urban areas, and those responsible for decisions about them, we want to produce relevant and impactful research that can reduce unfair and avoidable differences in health (health inequalities) and improve health and wellbeing long-term. In order to do this HUP wants to work with community organisations with expertise in engagement of often marginalised groups and an underlying ethos of working in partnership. Together we will create a ‘Community Collaborative’ – a community-based research partnership – which will involve the HUP team, community organisations, and other stakeholders (such as residents, schools, places of faith, clubs, policy makers, council members and more). The Community Collaborative will work together to produce evidence on what makes a healthy urban place and explore how we can achieve healthier cities. We will share the findings and learning from the research within communities in creative ways, and develop community-led reports for policy makers and government to influence future positive changes in urban areas. What will a Community Collaborative involve? The HUP team are looking for community organisations in each site to join us in partnership over the lifetime of the HUP programme until spring 2027. As a partnership, we’ll all bring something to the table: • HUP will bring research skills, provide training for those in the local community (staff or service users), support local communities to get involved in and/or lead research, and help create opportunities for community members to meet with policy makers and implementors. • Community organisations will bring local knowledge and lived experiences, skills in community & participatory engagement, introductions to community members, and access to physical assets, such as rooms and buildings. Community organisations can apply to be a HUP partner to Bradford Teaching Hospitals Foundation Trust. Funding will be provided for core costs (e.g. staff time, use of building and for carrying out specific research projects. Organisations within one area can apply alone or in partnership, and at more than one site if they have required links to the community. What the research process will look like At each site, the organisations involved in the Community Collaborative will jointly organise some 'inception' workshops with the HUP team. Together, we'll decide how we want our partnership to run (e.g. our ways of working, etc). We’ll start to explore factors that have impacted on wellbeing in the local urban area over time. Jointly we’ll prioritise what we want to explore first and will decide how we want to learn about it. We might, for example, decide together to develop a series of fun, creative and engaging mini-projects in which community members can be trained as community researchers to find out about healthy urban places. The findings and learnings from these projects will be shared with our communities, the wider public and those involved in policy making locally, regionally and nationally. The allocation of funds for this will be jointly decided. The Collaboratives will run for 2 years, with most of the work being conducted in 2025 and 2026, and finalising the process in 2027. Funding will reflect this, with the bulk of funding being provided in 2025 and 2026. However, during the process, we’d hope to be able to identify further opportunities and funding to work together on research in the future. What is expected of a collaborative partner? Community organisations will have a range of responsibilities that are noted in more detail in the procurement specification. Briefly, they will be co-partners in the Community Collaborative, and over the length of the funded period will: • Contribute to the set up and development of the Community Collaborative • Attend and assist in organising, facilitating and hosting meetings & workshops in the local area • Connect the HUP team to community members and service users • Co-design community-based research with the HUP team and wider stakeholders • Co-design creative ways of engaging community members in finding out about healthy urban places • Co-design engaging ways of sharing the learning and findings of research • Distribute payments to community participants in the research – for example, any community researchers who get involved in finding out about healthy urban places • Attend city-wide Collaborative meetings in Bradford and with partners in Liverpool Lot 1: .

sig_66b9ac335d1e3cef31cd.description: With this notice, Istekki announces the organisation of market dialogues for a service voucher and purchased service system. The purpose of the dialogue is to ensure that those preparing the procurement have access to as comprehensive and up-to-date a picture of the market and available solutions as possible. The subject of the procurement is the service voucher and purchased service system entity and its interfaces with other systems, the delivery project (including e.g. migrations, conversions), maintenance and support of off-the-shelf software, support services, separately ordered expert services, as well as customer service. Further development may be carried out on the procured system during the contract period. The service voucher and purchased service system is used for granting service vouchers and payment commitments and for purchasing services from private service providers or other public actors. Through the system, it is necessary to centralise the creation and use of service vouchers and purchased service orders (payment commitment) and the settlement of accounts for rendered services to private service providers or other public actors. The service voucher and purchased service system must take into account needs from the perspectives of the service organiser, the service producer and the customer using the service. Through the system, the service organiser must have the option to manage service provider agreements, plan service provision, grant service vouchers and payment commitments, allocate payments, handle correction requests and monitor various report views. The service provider must have the option to apply to become a service provider through the system. In addition, the service provider must be able to record the service received by the customer in the system and thereby handle settlement based on approved transaction entries. The customer must receive the granted service voucher / payment commitment for use via the system. The service voucher customer must have the option to compare or view service providers, monitor the execution of the service from the system and provide feedback on the service. The contracting authority will organise the market dialogues either as remote meetings or in writing, or utilising both methods. The market dialogues will be held in Finnish. Istekki will notify the companies participating in the dialogue of more detailed schedules and instructions later. Please note that the information, descriptions and estimates of the publication date of the tendering procedure presented in this notice are merely preliminary and indicative. Final schedules will become more precise as preparation progresses. If you are interested in participating in the market dialogue, please notify us of your interest no later than 11.09.2026 at 14.00 to hankinnat@istekki.fi. If you wish, you can also attach Finnish-language brochures or other material regarding your own service. It is worth noting that this notice does not oblige Istekki Oy to carry out the procurement in the manner presented in this document or its appendices. A potential tendering procedure may also be omitted. No separate remuneration is paid for responding to the dialogue or participating in any presentation events. We would like to mention again that this is not a contract notice or call for tenders. The purpose is to familiarise oneself with the market situation and gather information related to the subject of the procurement to support the planning of the upcoming tendering procedure. Responding to the request for information is voluntary and is not a prerequisite for participating in a potential tendering procedure or bind Istekki to publish a tendering procedure. At the same time, however, we greatly appreciate suppliers' participation, as it helps us build the upcoming tendering procedure into as functional and clear an entity as possible.
sig_66b9ac335d1e3cef31cd.title: Service voucher and purchased service system, market dialogue

sig_67da10303e40f5199415.description: ARTE G.E.I.E. in Strasbourg employs 590 people on permanent contracts and 300 people on temporary contracts: fixed-term contracts, freelance workers and intermittent workers. The HRIS ensuring administrative management and payroll is SAP ECC6, with a migration to SAP S/4HANA planned. It is currently supplemented by a UKG solution to cover the functionalities of an electronic safe, electronic signature and electronic personnel file. The purpose of the contract is the supply, implementation, hosting, maintenance and support of an integrated solution for the digitisation of human resources management processes covering the following functions. The interfaces, documentation and support are provided at a minimum in French and German. • Employee digital safe. Personal space held by the employee, intended for the storage and availability of HR documents provided to them for a period of at least fifty years, from the date of their deposit or signature. It allows ARTE to satisfy the obligation to make the payslip available in electronic form as provided for in Article D. 3243-8 of the Labour Code. This space remains accessible to the employee after the end of their employment contract and beyond the term of the contract. • Electronic personnel file. Documentary archive with probative value, accessible to authorised personnel, constituting the employee's individual file for the duration of their employment contract as well as during the recruitment phase that precedes it and the legal retention period that follows it. The solution ensures classification by document type, search, guarantee of integrity and traceability of access and actions, the lifecycle, and retention periods. • Electronic signature. Signature service whose level of proof is adjustable according to the process concerned, for internal as well as external signatures, in individual or bulk mode, including automated signatures for documents issued in series. It guarantees the retention of associated evidence and their retrieval. • Employee portal. Service allowing the employee to consult their documents and initiate human resources management requests by means of standard forms and configurable validation workflows, with progress tracking. • Distribution of individual human resources management documents. Secure, individualised and traceable distribution of documents produced by ARTE to each employee, including employment contracts and amendments, letters, management decisions, certificates and end-of-contract documents, regardless of the upstream production process. This function covers in particular the distribution of payslips, carried out in five campaigns per month. The solution supports the employee's objection to the digitised delivery of their payslip. The contract includes the recovery, in the electronic personnel file, of documents and signature evidence created since 2019. It includes a commitment to service continuity, reversibility at the end of the contract, as well as the regulation of any use of artificial intelligence excluding the collection, reuse or training based on ARTE's data. The hosting, processing, administration and backup of data are carried out exclusively on the territory of the European Union or the European Economic Area, including for each subcontractor. The contract involves the processing of personal data. Selected candidates must demonstrate, during the procedure, their ability to present appropriate guarantees regarding data protection, which must be maintained throughout the execution of the contract. The procedures and documents to be produced will be specified in the consultation.
sig_67da10303e40f5199415.title: Integrated solution for the digitisation of HR processes

sig_68225bdb357591370d7b.description: Technical renewal and digital expansion of the parking system for Smart Parking Lot LOT-0000: Bad Homburg v. d. Höhe municipal area, Smart Parking - parking system for Smart Parking. The subject is the technical renewal and digital expansion of the existing parking systems at 5 locations of Kur- und Kongreß-GmbH Bad Homburg v. d. Höhe, as well as the complete renewal of the parking system in the Karstadt multi-storey car park. The goal is a modern, service-oriented and functionally uniform parking infrastructure. The existing facilities are to be supplemented in such a way that modern digital parking processes based on number plate recognition, QR code functions, cashless web payment, digital discounting and self-service functions for short-term and long-term parkers can be used consistently and across all locations. The intention is not an isolated replacement of individual devices, but the functional expansion of an already existing overall system. Scope of services: delivery, installation, integration, commissioning and acceptance of the components at all locations; provision and setup of the central software and control computer components. Technical requirements and integration: - All components must be centrally manageable via the existing control computer/cell computer topology. - A continuous parking process (entry - identification via ticket, number plate or QR code - payment at machines/web service/discount point - exit - audit-proof accounting) must be guaranteed across the entire system. - Interfaces, firmware/backend versions and data models must be provided by the manufacturer in a coordinated manner. Installation, commissioning and acceptance: - Installation and commissioning during ongoing operation while minimising downtime; coordination with the project manager. - Acceptance criteria and partial acceptances: partial acceptance per location after successful functional/integration test; formal final acceptance after complete system integration. Other services: - Complete technical documentation in German. - Instruction/training of personnel: instruction of operating personnel per location as well as administrator training for the control computer system. A maintenance contract must be concluded for the maintenance of the systems, which covers the following areas: software, control/cell computer, availability of a technical service centre reachable 24/7, on-call service for on-site maintenance & repair.
sig_68225bdb357591370d7b.title: Bad Homburg v. d. Höhe municipal area, Smart Parking - parking system for Smart Parking

sig_6858bb78cc291b25b1ab.description: The project is aimed at potential international travellers and describes the possibility of active travel in Germany (focusing on hiking, cycling, and canoeing where applicable). The experience does not present individual destinations or tourism products, but rather conveys the characteristic qualities of Germany as a diverse active travel destination. The focus is on typical travel experiences and the combination of nature, physical activity, culture, culinary enjoyment, and relaxation that characterise active holidays in Germany. The project serves not only to impart knowledge, but the guest should be addressed, "taken by the hand", complete simple tasks, and be emotionally engaged. This has at least the same priority as the information. Objective: Extension of the length of stay. The project is to be developed for the output channels virtual reality (including inflight entertainment on aircraft with VR headsets), mobile, and web in order to generate the widest possible reach. This pilot project concerns a new type of destination marketing in which combinations of user engagement, user guidance, and content presentation from gaming, VR, artificial (AI-supported) content generation, and real content are combined. The bidder must combine these different skills and create an appealing, interactive product that fascinates customers with Germany as a travel destination. In addition to virtual environments, scenarios, and avatars (or digital entities/objects), the project should also incorporate existing media from the GNTB (photos, films, drone footage, 360-degree panoramas, etc.) and present them in an impressive, interactive form. Depending on the concept, further media may need to be digitally created, purchased, or shot. In addition, the use of (a few) Gaussian splats is planned for the first time, provided it makes sense in terms of content and technology. To our knowledge, the planned mix of (partially photorealistic) digitally created content and real images, panoramas, videos, and avatars is unprecedented in tourism marketing. Further information can be found in the service description in the tender document. Lot LOT-0000: Active travel in Germany. sig_68e9e3c7d8bb768a7d86.description: The employee survey in The Norwegian Defence Estates Agency is carried out annually, usually at the end of January/February. The Norwegian Defence Estates Agency has had a very high response percentage in recent years, between 82 % and 87%. In 2025, the survey was sent out to just over 2,000 respondents. The Norwegian Defence Estates Agency currently uses Rambøll as its supplier and they are responsible for the entire process - from dispatching and administration to analysing the results. The results will be presented in an insight report that will be presented to the management team. sig_68fb7a7789389a47f1f5.description: The Council is considering the future procurement of an independent assessment of the efficiency, effectiveness and long term sustainability of Housing Services and the HRA. While a robust 30 year HRA Business Plan is already in place, the Council wishes to obtain independent assurance on current arrangements and identify opportunities for improvement, innovation and value for money. This Prior Information Notice (PIN) is issued for the purpose of early market engagement only and is intended to inform the scope, approach and procurement strategy for any potential future tender exercise. Publication of this PIN does not constitute a commitment by East Renfrewshire Council to commence a procurement process. Lot 1: . East Renfrewshire Council manages a ring fenced Housing Revenue Account (HRA) which supports the delivery of social housing and associated landlord services. The Council is considering the future procurement of an independent assessment of the efficiency, effectiveness and long term sustainability of Housing Services and the HRA. While a robust 30 year HRA Business Plan is already in place, the Council wishes to obtain independent assurance on current arrangements and identify opportunities for improvement, innovation and value for money. This Prior Information Notice (PIN) is issued for the purpose of early market engagement only and is intended to inform the scope, approach and procurement strategy for any potential future tender exercise. Publication of this PIN does not constitute a commitment by East Renfrewshire Council to commence a procurement process. Indicative Scope of the Requirement: Should the Council proceed to a formal procurement exercise, it is anticipated that the scope of services may include, but would not be limited to, the following areas: - A strategic review of Housing Services, including performance, capacity and value for money. - Independent assessment of the robustness and long term sustainability of the HRA Business Plan. - Benchmarking and comparative analysis against Local Authorities of comparable size and stock profile and Registered Social Landlords with similar stock archetypes. - A detailed review of repairs and voids service delivery, including performance, cost control, productivity and customer experience. - Review of the factoring service, including financial performance, customer experience and options to move towards full cost recovery. - Review of stores and materials management arrangements within the context of a DLO led repairs model. - Review of sheltered housing provision, including revenue and capital costs and the relationship with the HRA. Across all areas, the Council anticipates a strong focus on evidence based analysis, benchmarking, customer feedback and elected member priorities, together with practical and deliverable recommendations. Information Sought from the Market - Economic operators are invited to provide non binding information to assist the Council in shaping any future procurement exercise. Responses may include information on: - Relevant organisational experience in delivering comparable Housing Services, HRA or landlord service reviews. - Experience working with Local Authorities and/or Registered Social Landlords of comparable scale and complexity. - Indicative approaches to delivering a commission of this nature, including benchmarking and stakeholder engagement. - Capacity to deliver the requirement and typical delivery models. - Innovative approaches or added value relevant to Housing Services. - Indicative commercial models and key cost drivers for similar commissions. This is not a tender or pre qualification exercise and no evaluation or scoring will take place at this stage. Submission of Expressions of Interest - This Prior Information Notice is issued for the purpose of market engagement only. Economic operators who wish to express an interest in this opportunity, or to provide information to assist the Council in shaping any future procurement exercise, are invited to submit a brief, non binding written response. Responses should be clearly marked “PIN Response – Housing Revenue Account Efficiency Review” and submitted to mary.harvey-welsh@eastrenfrewshire.gov.uk Responses should be limited to 4 x A4 and provided by 12 noon, 30th April 2026.. The Council reserves the right not to proceed to a formal procurement process and shall not be bound by any information received in response to this PIN.
sig_68fb7a7789389a47f1f5.title: Assessment of the Efficiency, Effectiveness and Long Term Sustainability of Housing Services and the Housing Revenue Account (HRA)

sig_69babc41467b57400b44.description: The ministerie van Buitenlandse Zaken, the Directorate-General for Consular Affairs and Visa Policy, NetherlandsWorldwide (NWW) wishes to conclude a Framework Agreement with one contractor for the provision of a Facility Contact Centre to support NWW. The Facility Contact Centre supports NWW in handling first-line customer contact in Dutch and English. The service provision consists of a structural base staffing (pilot flame) that provides support during the regular service provision throughout the year, supplemented by the possibility to flexibly scale capacity up and down when the situation requires it. Partly based on experience figures from recent years, the expected future need and indexations, the scope of the Assignment has been estimated. The estimated value of the Assignment amounts to approximately € 750.000,-- excluding VAT per year, therefore € 3.000.000,-- excluding VAT over a term of 4 years. The maximum value is set at € 6.000.000,--. sig_6a02644bff19ddbe229a.description: The purpose of the tendering procedure is to conclude a framework agreement pursuant to Section 131 of the Act with a single contractor. The subject of performance of public contracts awarded under the framework agreement shall be the provision of consultancy and advisory services for the needs of the contracting authority. The subject of performance of public contracts awarded under the framework agreement is outlined in the draft framework agreement (annex to the tender documentation). The subject of performance of public contracts awarded under the framework agreement is the provision of qualified services in the preparation of the PPP project Reconstruction, Modernisation and Operation of Public Lighting in Pilsen. This involves the provision of consultancy and advisory services in the field of project management, the provision of quality management consultations, economic advisory services and other advisory services. The services provided will include, in particular, the availability of staff capacities in the field of PPP project preparation to be made available to the contracting authority, specifically consisting in: (a) the preparation of background materials for the implementation of the PPP project including proposals, amendments and/or peer reviews of the PPP project; (b) project and programme management and the provision of organisational, management and administrative services relating thereto, including support in coordinating contractors; (c) quality and risk management and the provision of independent supervision and auditing of the contracting authority's projects and the provision of project management and service management support; (d) the provision of services related to PPP project management and quality control of PPP services; (e) the provision of consultations, analyses, preparation of background materials and documents in the field of certification and quality management; (f) the provision of other specialist and consultancy services in the field of PPP. The provision of Services will be implemented on the basis of a primary order issued without undue delay after the framework agreement enters into force. Particularly important activities may then be ordered by separate orders based on specific requirements of the contracting authority with a specific specification of performance deadlines, through sub-contracts concluded on the basis of written calls from the contracting authority. The method of awarding public contracts under the framework agreement is described in detail in the framework agreement.
sig_6a02644bff19ddbe229a.title: Framework agreement for the provision of consultancy and advisory services – preparation of a PPP project

sig_6a0771203f9257f3029c.description: This is an information request, which is not a procurement notice or call for tenders. The purpose of the information request is to gather information concerning the subject of the procurement for a future tender process. Responding to the information request is not a precondition for participating in any possible subsequent tender process. To ensure the success of the future tender process, however, it would be important that tenderers provide the contracting authority with the requested information as comprehensively as possible. The information request does not oblige Istekki Oy to carry out the procurement as described in the information request or its appendices, and the tendering procedure may also be left unperformed. This information request examines the market situation, functional and technical features, supplier pricing principles and price level of the remote dialysis system. Respondents to the information request will not be paid compensation for preparing the information request or participating in any presentation meetings related to the information request. The subject of the information request is a remote dialysis comprehensive platform solution (home dialysis). The subject and objectives of the procurement are described in more detail in the attached document. Based on the responses to the information request, market dialogue sessions may be organised where suppliers can present their own services, products and alternatives for the implementation of the procurement subject. If market dialogue sessions are organised, they will be conducted in the Finnish language. Istekki will notify the companies participating in the sessions of the exact schedules later. Istekki will select and invite the participants to the dialogues. If necessary, multiple dialogue sessions may be organised, and the participants may also include the contracting authority's end customers. The contracting authority reserves the right to also organise written dialogue rounds and rounds for commenting on draft tender documents. Responses to the information request must be submitted by 3.2.2026 at the latest by 14.00. The questions to be answered and instructions for responding to the information request are in the appendix.
