sig_6a0ea0101631906fdc67.description: The subject of the contract is the lot-by-lot supply, installation, integration and commissioning of software solutions for radiation therapy at St. Elisabethen-Klinikum Ravensburg, a site of Oberschwabenklinik gGmbH. Lot 1 comprises an SGRT system (Surface Guided Radiation Therapy) including all necessary software components for patient positioning and monitoring as well as integration into the existing IT and LINAC infrastructure. Lot 2 comprises the treatment planning software (Treatment Planning System, TPS) for irradiation planning for photons and electrons, including installation, data migration from the legacy system, training of operating personnel and maintenance/support. Both lots will be awarded under a negotiated procedure with a call for competition. Tenderers may apply for one or both lots. Contract execution will take place during ongoing clinical operations. The subject of this lot is the supply, installation, integration and commissioning of a system for surface-guided radiation therapy (Surface Guided Radiation Therapy, SGRT) including all necessary software and hardware components for patient positioning and monitoring. The service includes complete connection to the hospital's existing linear accelerator and IT infrastructure, training of operating personnel as well as maintenance and support over the envisaged period.; A treatment planning system (TPS) for the radiation therapy of Oberschwabenklinik gGmbH is being procured. The system is intended to enable the planning of photon-guided irradiations with the existing linear accelerators while supporting all relevant clinical workflows (3D-CRT, IMRT, VMAT). Complete integration into the existing IT and PACS environment is expected, including interfaces to the R&V system, DICOM-RT and archiving system. The service includes supply, installation, commissioning, validation, training of specialist personnel and maintenance.
sig_6a0ea0101631906fdc67.title: Lot-by-lot supply, installation and commissioning of an SGRT system and/or a radiotherapy planning system

sig_6a1c3dbeafff2d320ec8.description: Dundee City Council intends to procure a construction consultant resource and project management system to improve the planning, allocation and monitoring of architectural, engineering and specialist consultancy resources across its capital and housing programmes. The system will complement existing corporate and client-side systems, including Civica, by providing enhanced resource planning, capacity forecasting, workload visibility, timesheet reporting and management information. The objective is to improve service efficiency, strengthen forward planning, support evidence-based resource decisions and provide greater assurance over programme delivery, capacity utilisation and value for money. Lot 1: . Dundee City Council is undertaking this Prior Information Notice (PIN) and market engagement exercise to better understand the solutions currently available within the market for construction consultant resource and project management software. The information gathered will assist the Council in developing its procurement strategy, refining its requirements and determining the most appropriate route to market. As part of this exercise, the Council intends to invite selected suppliers to participate in product demonstrations, currently anticipated to take place during early October 2026 (please note, these dates are indicative only). These demonstrations will provide an opportunity for the Council to gain a greater understanding of available solutions, functionality, implementation approaches and delivery models. Suppliers wishing to be considered for participation in the demonstration stage are requested to complete and return the attached questionnaire. The information provided will be used solely for market engagement purposes and to assist the Council in identifying suppliers whose solutions appear capable of meeting the Council's requirements. Completed questionnaires should be submitted by 12 Noon on 25 September 2026 to trina.forbes@dundeecity.gov.uk. Suppliers who do not submit a completed questionnaire will not be considered for participation in the demonstration stage. The Council reserves the right to limit the number of demonstrations undertaken and participation in this market engagement exercise will not confer any advantage or disadvantage in any subsequent procurement process. Additional information: This PIN is issued for market engagement purposes only and will not be used to evaluate, select or exclude suppliers in any future procurement process. Information received will help Dundee City Council understand the market, develop its requirements and determine the most appropriate procurement approach. Participation is voluntary and does not commit the Council to proceed.
sig_6a1c3dbeafff2d320ec8.title: Procurement of Construction Consultant Management Software

sig_6a25f60d592dc1362e77.description: This is an invitation/request for information for a market dialogue (not a prior information notice, contract notice or call for tenders). No tenders are submitted in response to the request for information; instead, by registering for the market dialogue, entities indicate their willingness to participate in the preparation of the procurement. SUBJECT: Kela is planning a competitive tendering process for a centralised printing and inserting line concerning A4 sheet printers and related software, peripherals, maintenance services, supplies and printing paper. The market dialogue will survey market solutions as well as technical and functional implementation alternatives, particularly regarding printing and software solutions. The procurement will replace the printing line reaching the end of its lifecycle with new A4 sheet printers suitable for continuous and heavy-duty use. The scope also includes print management software, a delivery and commissioning project, training as well as other services and supplies that ensure the uninterrupted continuation of letter production in Kela's production environment. Currently, the printing line processes over 20 million A4 sheets and several million letters annually. In addition, the procurement includes an inserting machine modification project and its maintenance services. In the inserting machine modification project, the inserting machine will be modified to receive finished A4 sheet stacks, or it can be replaced entirely with another device. Subdomains of the market dialogue: 1) A4 printers, software and maintenance services – Printing devices and related software – Maintenance and support services – Necessary peripherals and supplies 2) Inserting machine modification project and maintenance service – Inserting machine modification work – Device maintenance and support 3) Paper suppliers – Printing paper supply package Suppliers may register for one or more subdomains according to their offering. General material common to the dialogue will be provided to all participants. In addition, separate subdomain-specific questions and materials will be targeted to each subdomain. This ensures that operators can provide relevant and expert feedback regarding their specific subdomain. During the dialogue, subdomains may also be merged if necessary for the procurement. MARKET DIALOGUE: The aim of the market dialogue is to form as comprehensive a picture as possible of the solutions offered by the market and to ensure that the requirements of the tendering process are appropriate, feasible and treat the market equally. During the dialogue, participants are asked to, among other things: - present the offering available on the market - answer questions concerning the procurement - comment on preliminary minimum requirements, for example regarding conflicts of interest - present potential development proposals to improve the solution and the tendering process. The dialogue will be carried out in a versatile manner: partly through in-person meetings in Jyväskylä, partly by email and, if necessary, via remote connection using Kela's Microsoft Teams. The material related to the market dialogue is in Finnish. The market dialogue will be conducted principally in the Finnish language; if necessary, the dialogue can also be conducted partially in English. The contracting authority has no obligation to translate documents or other material related to the market dialogue unless the contracting authority specifically decides otherwise. A party participating in the market dialogue is responsible for obtaining any translations it needs and for their accuracy at its own expense. Preliminary schedule of the dialogue: - Familiarisation with the offering, defining the subject, familiarising with the subject: Until June 2026 - Finalisation of the call for tenders: July-September 2026 The schedule and the alignment of phases will be reviewed in more detail with tenderers during the dialogue. Participation: Interested participants are requested to declare their willingness to participate in the market survey by email to it.tarjouskilpailut@kela.fi by 25.3.2026. Example of message content: Message subject: Company xx participation in xxx market dialogue Message: It is advisable for the message to indicate the supplier's name, business ID and contact person through whom the dialogue will be conducted, as well as the subdomain being participated in. Confidential material may be handled during the dialogue and, consequently, all persons handling confidential material, location data and other confidential information must sign a non-disclosure agreement. Persons participating in the handling can be added during the dialogue if necessary. Kela will send the non-disclosure agreements electronically to the designated handlers for signature before handling begins. Other: The request for information does not oblige the contracting authority to carry out the actual procurement or to implement the procurement in the manner described in the request for information. The contracting authority is not obliged to take into account the responses received to the request for information when drawing up the call for tenders and the contract template. No compensation is paid to those who responded to the request for information for responding to it. Answering the request for information does not bind the supplier to participate in the tender contest, nor is it a prerequisite for participating in the actual tender contest later. Answering or failing to answer the request for information does not affect the tenderer's position in the actual tender contest. Information obtained through the request for information will be treated confidentially.
sig_6a25f60d592dc1362e77.title: Market dialogue - Cut-sheet printers for centralised printing

sig_6a57c8318f2348677f8f.description: Forest management services will be awarded in the year 2026 or 2027 by concluding a contract for each lot. The cumulative area of the lots is 14257,68 ha. The area of each lot is specified in the description of the lots. The services involve the development of a forest management plan, a product of the management activity with technical-organisational content, ecologically grounded, through which, for a period of time, the works necessary to be executed in a production unit are established, in order to bring and, subsequently, to maintain the structural characteristics of the stands and the forest as a whole at the values corresponding to the optimal structural model defined in accordance with the ecological, social and economic objectives pursued through sustainable management. According to the provisions of Art. 63 para. (11) of Law no. 331/2024 on the Forestry Code, as subsequently amended and supplemented, it is necessary that the development of forest management plans be carried out through public procurement procedures. The management of the state-owned forest fund constitutes a priority obligation of the forest fund administrators. The method of managing the state-owned forest fund is regulated by forest management plans. Forest management plans and their amendments are approved by order of the head of the Authority. In the case of state-owned land, the management plans provide data and information necessary for their registration/updating in the centralised inventory of state public domain assets and for registration in the integrated cadastre and land registry system. Requests for clarification formulated by tenderers during the advertising period of the participation notice can be made with a deadline of at least 15 days before the deadline for submission of tenders (the 16 day). The contracting authority will respond to all requests for clarification formulated in compliance with the above deadline, only once, in a consolidated manner, 10 days before the deadline for submission of tenders (the 11 day). sig_6b692a82e072d7a22034.description: The National Violent Death Reporting System (NVDRS) is CDC's state-based surveillance system for violent deaths and suicides. NVDRS combines information from death certificates, coroner or medical examiner reports, including toxicology reports, and law enforcement reports to provide comprehensive, incident-level data on the circumstances surrounding violent deaths. Through this Notice of Funding Opportunity, CDC will support eligible state, territorial, and local government entities, or their bona fide agents, in operating and modernizing NVDRS. Recipients will conduct statewide or territory-wide surveillance by collecting, linking, managing, analyzing, and submitting high-quality data on violent deaths and suicides. A central focus of this NOFO is timely and complete data reporting through two coordinated reporting processes: quarterly provisional data pulls and annual data closeout. Beginning in Year 1, recipients will prepare data for CDC's quarterly provisional data pulls to support earlier access to preliminary, actionable information. Recipients will progressively update case records as additional source documents and information become available. Annual data closeout is the primary process for producing the complete, finalized, and validated NVDRS dataset for each data year. Recipients must ensure that all eligible cases are fully abstracted, updated, validated, and completed using all required and available data sources by the annual closeout deadline. The finalized annual dataset supports national reporting, analysis, dissemination, and public health action. This NOFO also emphasizes modernization of data systems and workflows to increase efficiency, reduce reporting burden, improve data quality and timeliness, and enhance data usability. All recipients will complete a modernization readiness assessment within six months of award and implement at least one modernization pilot during the period of performance. Pilot activities may include automated data import and extraction, electronic data exchange and interoperability, workflow automation, data-quality tools, and enhanced data analysis and visualization. With CDC approval, recipients may also participate in optional activities that link NVDRS data with other relevant data systems to improve surveillance and expand public health insights. The intended outcome is a sustainable, modernized national surveillance system that produces timely provisional data and complete, reliable, high-quality annual data to inform violence and suicide prevention and support public health action.
sig_6b692a82e072d7a22034.title: Modernizing Violent Death and Suicide Surveillance Using the National Violent Death Reporting System (NVDRS)

sig_6b717637e2d7dc2a6ac8.description: MARKET DIALOGUE The subject of the market dialogue is the planned procurement of translation, language editing, subtitling and transcription services for the needs of Väylävirasto. Väylävirasto produces a wide range of official communications, expert content and stakeholder-targeted materials in multiple languages as part of its statutory duties. Translation and language editing services are a key part of the accessibility, quality, comprehensibility and consistency of official communications. BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVES The subject of the procurement is a comprehensive service package for translation, language editing, subtitling and transcription services, through which subscribers can procure translation services for various language pairs, language editing for texts written in the target language, and subtitling and transcription services for video and audio materials. Service needs are focused in particular on the Swedish and English languages. The materials to be handled are principally factual texts, presentations, documents (e.g. call for tenders, contracts), speeches, brochures, articles and web content. Subtitling and transcription services relate, inter alia, to videos, online events and audio recordings, taking accessibility requirements into account. The aim of the procurement is to ensure a high-quality, cost-effective and reliable service package that supports subscribers' communications, information accessibility and the fulfilment of official obligations. The objective is a procurement model that enables smooth ordering, consistent end results and an administratively light operating method even in situations where the volume of assignments is large and the value of individual assignments is small. By means of the market dialogue, the contracting entity seeks to obtain information on service models existing in the market, pricing structures, quality assurance practices, and the utilisation of artificial intelligence and other automation as part of the production of translation and language editing services. The dialogue will also examine various contractual and supplier models, including the suitability of single-supplier and multi-supplier models. The procurement includes a cooperation model in which the subscriber and the supplier systematically develop the service throughout the contract period. The aim of the cooperation is the continuous improvement of the service, taking into account the subscriber's guidelines and terminology, and developing the service to meet changing needs and operating environments. The subject matter, scope and technical solutions of the procurement may be refined and/or changed as the procurement preparation and market dialogue progress. PRELIMINARY TIMETABLE The subscriber's target timetable for carrying out the market dialogue and procurement is: - Market dialogue (technical dialogue), February-March 2026 - Publication of the call for tenders and calculation period, March-April 2026 - Comparison of tenders and procurement decision, April-May 2026 - Contract entry into force and commencement of cooperation, May 2026 onwards ----- ADDITIONAL NOTICE DETAILS This notice is a prior information notice. This notice does not request tenders. The prior information notice is accompanied by an invitation to a market dialogue, whereby all suppliers interested in the procurement have the opportunity to engage in a technical dialogue concerning the procurement with Väylävirasto. The purpose of the technical dialogue is to discuss the subject of the procurement and its definition at a general level. The technical dialogue does not bind Väylävirasto to carry out the procurement. Nor does the technical dialogue bind the supplier to participate in a possible tendering procedure. The technical dialogue will be organised through commenting on draft versions of the call for tenders material and answering the subscriber's questions relating to the subject of the procurement. Instructions for registration: The supplier must notify its interest in participating in the market dialogue by 25.2.2026 at 12.00 by sending a message to tommi.aarnio@vayla.fi with the subject heading: "Käännöspalvelut - markkinavuoropuhelu" [Translation services - market dialogue]. The supplier is requested to provide the following information in the message: - the email address of the supplier's contact person The subscriber reserves the right to also invite suppliers to bilateral negotiations or to continue the technical dialogue in another manner to be announced separately, which will be notified later if necessary. The descriptions presented in this prior information notice and the estimated publication date of the procurement notice, as well as the draft dialogue materials to be provided later, are preliminary and indicative prior information regarding the procurement. Participating companies will not be paid compensation for responding or participating.

sig_6bdf90904780068f720d.description: The delivery of an integration platform that connects applications and data. This also includes the transition and implementation from the current integration platform to the new one. As a frame of reference, the province uses an API-led architecture approach (system APIs, process APIs and experience APIs). Integrations are made accessible in layers: from source systems via business logic to consuming applications. The province subsequently develops and defines integrations independently. The contract is not divided into lots, because the integration platform and the associated services and additional assignments form a strongly cohesive entity. Development, management and further development are closely intertwined and have mutual dependencies. sig_6c48e904f3c8b7763564.description: Public Health Wales (PHW) have an ongoing requirement for an Infection Prevention and Control Case Management and Surveillance system supplying cross-hospital electronic infection case management, immediate alerting of information relevant to infection control to ward staff and others including health protection specialists, and in depth and real-time reporting for clinical and public health action. The current system interfaces with existing hospital information systems including surgery databases, patient administration and laboratories. It builds upon the information supplied to find, link, and at once inform the IPC and wider teams to critical infection control scenarios. Immediate alerting of these scenarios ensures prompt management of the infection event, resulting in better outcomes for the patient, reduced risk of onward transmission in the hospital or community setting and early identification of critical situations such as an outbreak. The system also helps maximise clinical time by reducing the workload required to link all this information through an enabling prospective and real time information on events, as opposed to retrospective manual case review. The connection into Public Health Wales NHS Wales Trust (PHW) Enterprise Monitor function ensures that PHW, Welsh Government and local Health Boards, all benefit from sharing correct and transparent data with a national picture available of the infection position across the acute sector within Wales. The current contract for NHS Wales is with Baxter Healthcare and has been in place since August 2023. This agreement is led contractually by PHW on behalf of itself and all NHS Wales organisations. This agreement is due to expire in August 2027. Lot 1: .

sig_6c8a0c2a7cec95c30dbf.description: Die BREPARK GmbH intends to introduce a central service portal for the digitalisation and optimisation of customer management and the associated business processes. Lot LOT-0000: Service Portal/Digital Customer Management, V0470/2026. The BREPARK GmbH intends to introduce a central service portal for the digitalisation and optimisation of customer management and the associated business processes. The future system is intended to serve as a central platform for managing customers, contracts, access media, billing and communication with customers. The planned scope of services comprises in particular the provision, setup, customisation and operation of an integrated service portal with the following components: End Customer Portal (EKP): A digital portal through which customers can independently use services provided by BREPARK GmbH. This includes in particular registration, management of customer data, conclusion and management of contracts, viewing of parking operations and invoices, as well as communication with BREPARK GmbH. Employee Portal (MA Portal): A central work surface for employees of BREPARK GmbH for managing and processing customer transactions. This comprises in particular the maintenance of customer data, processing of contract enquiries, management of contracts and access media, execution of checking and approval processes, and support for internal administrative processes. Business Customer Portal (GKP): The solution must provide a business customer portal through which authorised business customers can independently manage their contract-related data and access permissions. BREPARK manages various parking facilities on behalf of third parties and manages long-term parking permissions for business customers, amongst other things. Around 7.000 access media for business customers are currently managed. The aim is to provide business customers with a digital option for independently managing their permissions and access media, thereby simplifying administrative processes. The service portal is to be integrated into the existing system landscape of BREPARK GmbH. This includes in particular connection to SAP Business ByDesign as the leading ERP system and the required interfaces to existing parking management and access systems. The contractor must provide an operational overall system which fulfils the requirements of this specification of services and enables the further development of the digital customer processes of BREPARK GmbH. In addition to the provision of the software, the scope of services also includes the required configuration, customising, integration into the existing system landscape, data migration, execution of tests, commissioning, and the required training, maintenance and support services for ongoing operations. Implementation takes place as an overall system. The contractor bears responsibility for the total technical and functional integration of all required components and interfaces.
sig_6c8a0c2a7cec95c30dbf.title: Service portal/Digital Customer Management, V0470/2026

sig_6d0f19cfde402dbd9dc3.description: The purpose of this contract is the performance of actuarial study services, consulting, financial management assistance and the redesign/maintenance of projection tools for all schemes managed by the CNBF. This contract is an ordinary public contract with mixed prices, concluded pursuant to Articles R. 2112-6 et seq. of the Public Procurement Code. The total estimated amount of the contract amounts to 600 000 excluding VAT over its entire duration. It combines two distinct remuneration and execution methods: 1. An annual fixed-price portion: • It covers recurrent mandatory annual actuarial study services and corrective maintenance. • These services apply automatically upon notification of the contract without prior issuance of an order form. • They are remunerated on the basis of a firm fixed price appearing in the unit price schedule (BPU). 2. 2. A unit-price portion based on order forms: • It covers specific and ad-hoc prospective studies (reform projects, equity analyses, etc.), additional simulations, training actions as well as upgradeable maintenance of the tool and major upgrading or redesign of the Excel projection tool. • These services are executed as needs arise by the issuance of order forms, on the basis of the unit prices appearing in the Unit Price Schedule (BPU). • The order form portion is concluded with a maximum amount of 300 000 excluding VAT over the total duration of the contract. sig_6d2b297d9c88d9c9864f.description: The National Institute of Mental Health (NIMH) intends to issue a single-source cooperative agreement award to the University of California, Santa Cruz. The award will renew the Data Resource and Administrative Coordination Center (DRACC), a component of the Scalable and Systematic Neurobiology of Psychiatric and Neurodevelopmental Disorder Risk Genes (SSPsyGene) Consortium. The long-term goal of SSPsyGene is to systematically study how risk genes for neurodevelopmental and psychiatric disorders (NPDs) affect molecular, cellular, circuit, systems/organismal biology. The renewed DRACC will refine its focus on developing a sustainable knowledge base, with shared terms, definitions, and data standards that are interoperable with other knowledge platforms and will enable the use of artificial intelligence to accelerate research on brain function and NPDs. This resource will be made available for broad use by the biomedical community. Projects that propose to build on the DRACC's current role in refining methods and standards to harmonize data from the SSPsyGene Assay and Data Generation Centers and facilitate submission to data archives are encouraged. This is a forecast for a single source NOFO that will invite application(s) from eligible organization(s) to apply. Please see Section III. Eligibility for additional information. In accordance with NIH standard peer-review processes, the application(s) will be peer-reviewed, and only meritorious application(s) will be considered for funding.

sig_6d2d1f9ad2aefc6fc710.description: Since 1 April 2026, the new public law organisation Sanadura has been ensuring healthcare provision in the Upper Engadine. As an independent public law institution of the sponsoring municipalities of the Upper Engadine, Sanadura guarantees needs-based and economical care for the population in the region. It is responsible for regional healthcare provision and in particular for the operation and safeguarding of the retirement centres as well as the Spitex services. As part of the organisational realignment, an independent, modern and future-proof ICT infrastructure is to be established for Sanadura. The aim is to create a stable, secure and efficient technical basis for the operation of all organisational units. Further details on the initial situation can be found in the document "Part B Performance Specification - Specifications" section 2.1 Initial situation. The procurement of the new ICT infrastructure is carried out via the present public tender. It comprises an operation and support contract duration of 4 years. The exact content and scope of the procurement object can be found in section 2 of this document as well as in the document "Part B Performance Specification - Specifications" and "Part C Appendix 3: Tender Forms".

sig_6dabd753c32e71f5ef91.description: Description of the procurement: The Danish Agency for Digital Government (Digitaliseringsstyrelsen) operates on behalf of the Danish State a national qualified trust service for the management of qualified electronic signature creation devices under Regulation (EU) No 910/2014 as amended by Regulation (EU) 2024/1183 (eIDAS2). As part of modernising the signing service to meet the requirements of eIDAS2, the Agency is procuring a Qualified Signature Creation Devices (QSCD) to be installed and operated within the Agency's data centers (currently two). The Contract includes an Option to upgrade the throughput capacity of the QSCD and an Option to extend the deployment to a third data centre. The Contract covers the Initial Delivery of the certified QSCD in accordance with eIDAS2. The Initial Delivery includes all Licences, Documentation, and support necessary for the Agency to install and operate the QSCD as part of its qualified trust service. The QSCD must integrate with the Agency's existing infrastructure, including the Agency's certificate authority, authorisation server, and signing components. The Supplier's principal obligations comprise: (a) the Initial Delivery of certified QSCD Hardware sized and configured for operation across two data centres with redundant active/active configurations with a defined minimum production throughput per second, measured in RSA 4K operations equivalent; (b) Ongoing Services, including support and maintenance of the Hardware, security patching, and up to two replacements of Hardware during the contract term to maintain valid certifications; (c) Ordered Services, comprising Time-Based Services (services for installation, configuration, key ceremonies, and similar tasks) and Options; and (d) Cross-cutting Services, comprising Documentation and security, provided as an integral part of the Ongoing Services and Ordered Services throughout the term of the Contract.
sig_6dabd753c32e71f5ef91.title: Qualified Signature Creation Device (QSCD)

sig_6ded036e88f2a8424bb6.description: Invitation to market dialogue. Sykehusinnkjøp HF hereby invites tenderers to a market dialogue for the procurement of a laboratory information system for the health companies in Helse Nord. The market dialogue is a part of the preliminary work for the procurement and is being carried out because the Contracting Authority would like input for the procurement from potential suppliers, possibly also from other interested parties. As a part of this process, suppliers are invited to provide input to the procurement prior to the announcement. The feedback makes it possible to make a decision about the type of procurement and procurement procedure. Based on input from the market dialogue, the Contracting Authority will, as needed, open to a closer dialogue with some of the suppliers for further details and discussions. The contracting authority would like input on the following points: Short presentation of the supplier/tendererWhich the specialist areas the system is meant to cover (see further information on all disciplines within the laboratory service in annex "Invitation to market dialogue") About the solution, including brief information on functionality, possibilities and limitations, and: Describe how the system is built up in the tender documentation. modules, and which advantages this provides. How the system is deployed to clients; web based and/or sw deployed on clients. By the latter; whether there are specific requirements for clients. How the system will be deployed back-end. Describe how the system supports portable devices (tablets etc.). References to customers where the system is in use (and possibly which parts of the system they use). The tenderer ́s thoughts on how the system will support future development within the disciplines, e.g. within AI, integrations (i.a. FHIR), personalised medicine, etc. Input for the procurement as regards the expected functionality described in chapter 5 (see annex "Invitation to Market Dialogue"):How does the system ensure user friendliness, intuitive user interface and training? How does the system cover the overall description and for each of the disciplines covered by the solution? If there is functionality that cannot be offered we would like to know this. Which disciplines the solution covers and whether it covers all disciplines within the laboratory service (note possible exceptions for transfusion medicine/blood bank). How the system supports decision support functionality. How the solution supports artificial intelligence. How the system supports personalised medicine. How does the system support different integration mechanisms with other systems (FHIR, message exchange in accordance with Norwegian requirements, etc.?) Delivery. Which factors affect delivery time and how do you handle risk? All the functionalities are ready developed and can be delivered. If there is functionality that needs to be developed, it is desirable to know. Delivery model: cloud and/or local installation. If the system is cloud compatible; about Norwegian requirements are complied with. Whether there are specific requirements for HW and underlying SW-platform for customers. Short proposals as to how the system will be implemented at Customer Provisions that the Customer is expected to fulfil. Frequency of release bicycles and response to new functionality and error recovery. Integrations: does this require assistance from customers? Describe the pricing model and what factors affect the total cost of ownership (TCO) Licenses Maintenance/support price driven factors. And input that the tenderer deems important. Deadline for written feedback on the above mentioned points from interested parties: 28.11.2025. This is only a prior information notice in order to get information on the market and to have a dialogue with relevant suppliers. The actual competition may be announced at a later date. Feedback on or questions to the market survey is done in the Mercell communication module. After this market survey, the contracting authority will assess the need to hold meetings(s) with relevant interested parties.

sig_6e410eacad34c2b05f1c.description: This is not a prior information notice, contract notice or call for tenders, but a notice on the initiation of a market dialogue as part of procurement planning and an invitation to participate in the market dialogue. Vantaan kaupunki and other municipalities are jointly planning a tender contest for a low-carbon assessment tool for detailed local planning, so the procurement will likely be carried out as a joint procurement group of several contracting authorities. The contracting authorities are surveying suppliers' interest in participating in the market dialogue for the low-carbon assessment tool for detailed local planning. The subject matter of the procurement is a browser-based software service delivered via the data network for assessing the climate impacts of land use plans, with which the contracting authority can assess and compare the climate impacts of detailed local plan level land use plans based on the carbon footprint and carbon handprint calculated by the tool. The subject matter of the procurement includes implementation projects for the low-carbon tool, rights of use, support and maintenance services, supplementary expert services ordered separately, and additional procurement opportunities. The aim is to obtain a solution that is suitable for the Finnish land use and construction context and for the evaluation of detailed local plan level land use plans. The solution is also intended to be further developed to improve the assessment of the climate impacts of urban land use planning. Commercial use of the low-carbon assessment tool for detailed local planning will start according to municipality-specific schedules estimated during Q2/2026-Q1/2027. The solution to be procured must preliminarily include the following key functionalities and features: - The solution is map- and GIS-based. - The evaluation method of the solution must take into account the entire life cycle of the land use plans being evaluated, including the climate impacts of the project before use, during use and after use, as well as impacts outside the life cycle and potential climate benefits. - The solution must be able to utilise national and city-specific parameters and data. - The evaluation method must comprehensively take into account the climate impacts of detailed local plan level land use projects, also considering climate impacts other than those produced by buildings, such as the climate impacts of transport or energy consumption. - The solution takes into account the Finnish Green Building Council's definition of a carbon-neutral built area. Operators participating in the market dialogue are requested to register for the market dialogue and provide answers to the preliminary questions presented in the market consultation notice by Friday 13.3.2026 by 12 to the following address: jonna.hirvonen@vantaa.fi. Registrations must be headed as follows: "Registration for market dialogue: Procurement of a low-carbon assessment tool for detailed local planning". Registrations must contain the following information: - Name of the participating company - Name, telephone number and email address of the contact person - Name of the solution offered by the company - Answers to preliminary questions
sig_6e410eacad34c2b05f1c.title: Information request and invitation to market dialogue: Procurement of a low-carbon assessment tool for detailed local planning

sig_6e8d7451ceffcad884f2.description: David Ross Education Trust is inviting tenders for the implementation and ongoing provision of a secure, modern and user-friendly Human Resources Information System and payroll solution. The solution will support approximately 2,200 employees across the Trust's 36 academies and central functions. It must support the full employee lifecycle and the accurate, timely and compliant operation of payroll. The requirement includes: core HR and employee record management; payroll calculation, processing and statutory reporting, including Teachers' Pension Scheme and multiple Local Government Pension Scheme arrangements; employee and manager self-service; recruitment, onboarding and employee lifecycle processes; absence, leave and contractual change management; workflows, approvals, reporting and management information; integration and secure data exchange; data migration, configuration, testing, training and implementation; security, data protection, business continuity and disaster recovery; and ongoing support, maintenance, system updates and service management. The Trust will continue to operate payroll through its in-house payroll team. The contract will be for a maximum period of ten years, with break options available to the Trust at the end of years five and eight. Tenders will be evaluated on the basis of 60% quality and 40% price. The Trust may invite shortlisted bidders to participate in a supplier demonstration as part of the evaluation process. All tender documents, communications, clarification questions and submissions must be managed through the InTend portal. The deadline for tender submissions is 09:00 BST on 19 October 2026. Lot 1: .

sig_6eb9572aae3b7818c770.description: The National Institute on Aging (NIA) intends to publish a Notice of Funding Opportunity (NOFO) to solicit applications to develop, operate, and sustain a cloud-based data storage and computing platform that democratizes access to large-scale Alzheimer’s disease (AD) and AD-related dementias (ADRD) genetic and genomic data. The platform must be secure, scalable, and interoperable. The platform will support the NIA Genetics of Alzheimer's Disease Data Storage Site (NIAGADS), the primary NIA-supported repository for the archiving and distribution of human genetic data related to AD/ADRD. The purpose of the platform will be to: Enable efficient ingestion, curation, harmonization, and analysis of multi-ancestry, large population-scale datasets; Provide robust analysis, visualization, and artificial intelligence -ready resources within secure cloud workspaces; Ensure compliance with federal security and data-sharing policies; Promote interoperability with other NIH- and NIA-supported repositories; and Provide user support, training, and community engagement. The NOFO aims to foster collaboration, accelerate discovery, and maximize the scientific value and impact of AD/ADRD genetics research for the broader research community. By improving data accessibility, interoperability, reporting, reproducibility, and scalable computational systems that enable rigorous, reproducible, and transparent research, the NOFO seeks to align with the NIH’s plan for Gold Standard Science and the AD/ADRD Research Implementation Milestones . Additionally, the NOFO seeks to address the Academies of Sciences, Engineering, and Medicine's recommendation of ensuring broad, secure access to high-value datasets and enhancing data usability to maximize the return on research investments and support future discoveries in AD/ADRD. Moreover, the NOFO intends to directly advance NIA’s Strategic Directions , particularly Goal G to support the infrastructure and resources necessary for high-quality research, by strengthening data sharing, computational infrastructure, and research rigor across the AD/ADRD community. The NOFO intends to utilize the U24 activity code. Applications are not being solicited at this time. This notice is being provided to allow potential applicants sufficient time to develop meaningful collaborations and responsive projects.
sig_6eb9572aae3b7818c770.title: The NIA Genetics of Alzheimer's Disease Data Storage Site (NIAGADS)

sig_6ed7cd14dea6dc521d15.description: The overarching goal of this notice of funding opportunity (NOFO) and its companion opportunities is to establish the Precision Medicine with AI: Integrating Imaging with Multimodal Data (PRIMED-AI) Program to support development of innovative, reliable, cost-effective, and sustainable multimodal AI-based clinical decision support (CDS) tools. PRIMED-AI CDS tools are based on the integration of clinical imaging with other types of multimodal health data to enhance care for patients with a wide range of health conditions. The PRIMED-AI Program seeks to catalyze the adoption of AI-based CDS tools into clinical workflows to enable novel personalized medicine strategies that address significant health challenges.The purpose of this NOFO is to create a Logistics Center for the PRIMED-AI Program to facilitate and coordinate PRIMED-AI activities to maximize impact for the PRIMED-AI community. Within the Logistics Center, three integrated Cores will serve the functions of Administration, Evaluation, and Outreach for the PRIMED-AI Consortium. It is expected that the Logistics Center will work closely with other PRIMED-AI consortium members to collect, curate and disseminate information regarding tools developed by the PRIMED-AI award recipients, and will facilitate widespread access and awareness across the relevant scientific, patient, and clinical communities.
sig_6ed7cd14dea6dc521d15.title: Logistics Center for Precision Medicine with AI: Integrating Imaging with Multimodal Data (PRIMED-AI) (U24 Clinical Trials Not Allowed)

Part 1) - Procurement of technologies for server rooms The subject matter of this part of the public contract is the comprehensive supply, expert implementation and subsequent commissioning of a complete technological solution for the expansion and supplementation of the existing data centre infrastructure, both physically and technologically. Specifically, this involves the installation and integration of physical infrastructure elements, a modern air conditioning system, an uninterruptible power supply, a CCTV system for monitoring and security purposes, fire safety systems and the establishment of an optical connection with a dedicated backup server room, which will ensure high availability and operational continuity. Part 2) – Procurement of network technologies The subject matter of this part of the public contract is the supply, implementation and commissioning of a comprehensive solution to increase LAN access security and modernise the backbone and access network infrastructure. This includes the replacement of active components in both the access and backbone layers, the deployment of a network access control (NAC) system with support for IEEE 802.1X and the supply of central switch management in the form of on-premises or cloud management. New switches (2 backbone switches and 7 access switches) will be deployed within the access layer to ensure secure connection of end devices using authentication and authorisation based on IEEE 802.1X. This part forms the basic communication and authentication layer of the infrastructure and is designed in direct succession to the security, monitoring and logging systems specified in the technical specification - part 3, with which it must be fully interoperable at the level of access control, security events, logging and automated response. Part 3) – Supply and implementation of security and monitoring software The subject matter of this part of the public contract is the supply, implementation and commissioning of high-performance servers to increase system availability, strengthen operational computing power by supplying two high-performance rack servers and an enterprise All Flash disk array. The aim is to expand the computing and storage capacity of the hospital infrastructure with an emphasis on high performance, redundancy, scalability, advanced management and security features, including support for virtualisation, high availability and data services. Furthermore, the supply, implementation and commissioning of a comprehensive solution for the security of the organisation's perimeter, security policy management and cyber threat detection. This includes the deployment of a high-availability firewall cluster, a central security event management system and training of responsible personnel. Finally, the supply and installation of a system for central log collection and the supply and installation of hardware and software equipment that form a comprehensive solution for long-term and detailed monitoring and evaluation of network traffic using data flows (NetFlow, IPFIX, sFlow, etc.). The solution specified in this part is designed as a superior security, analytical and management layer that builds on the network and authentication infrastructure defined in the technical specification - part 2 and uses it as a primary source of network data, identities, events and telemetry. sig_6fcb6f1f758a9219b3e3.description: This invitation to tender ('ITT') relates to Lake District National Park Authority's (the 'Authority') procurement for a Countryside Land Management and Estate Maintenance Framework Agreement, for our Ranger Services Team and others. Successful Tenderers will be appointed onto a multi-supplier Framework Agreement divided into Lots. The Framework Agreement will be available for use by the Authority and by other bodies in the Authority's network by prior agreement. The Authority is seeking a mix of contractors to bid for a place on the Framework Agreement, including companies, consultants, sole traders, and Small and Medium Sized Enterprises. This procurement is divided into Lots (and sub-lots in the case of Lot 4). Suppliers may bid for one or more Lots/sub-lots provided that you can supply at least one of the services mentioned in the Lot Specification at Table A. Please note that you do not need to be able to provide all of the services listed in the Lot specification, provided you can supply at least one of the services mentioned in that Lot you may submit a tender. All Prices should be submitted as a maximum for provision of your goods/services and will be a commitment for the duration of the Framework Agreement, subject to the allowed increase in price annually. This Framework Agreement will allow for Direct Award and Further Competition of Call-off Contracts. Tenderers should read the instructions contained in this ITT carefully before submitting a response. Failure to comply with the requirements set out in this ITT may result in the rejection of the Tender. Tenderers are advised to acquaint themselves fully with the extent and nature of the goods and/or services in the Statement of Requirement and with the Terms and Conditions. Participation in this procurement automatically signals that the Tenderer accepts the Terms and Conditions contained in this ITT. If a Tenderer is awarded a place on any Lot of the Framework, a draft Framework Agreement will be provided after all awards have taken place (est. February - March 2027). Any award is not legally binding and subject-to-contract until the final Framework Agreement between the Authority and the Tenderer is signed. The Lake District National Park Authority looks after the Lake District National Park, encouraging people to enjoy and understand its beauty and supporting those who live and work here. Further information about the LDNPA, including our statutory functions, is available on our website. We are working towards making the Lake District an inspirational example of sustainable development in action. We want its prosperous economy, world class visitor experiences and vibrant communities to come together in sustaining the spectacular landscape, wildlife and cultural heritage here. Details of how we are doing this are outlined in our Vision: Our purpose and vision - Lake District National Park Our Ranger Services Team at LDNPA has a focus on maintaining and improving the Rights of Way and other access in the Lake District National Park, while encouraging and educating users in responsible outdoor recreation on accessible land and navigable lakes. They support visitor management and nature recovery initiatives, and the enhancement and maintenance of our rural properties, in line with our strategic priorities. They work closely with communities to help them meet their needs in ways that contribute to our Vision. The Ranger Team's workload includes project work, such as the Coast-to-Coast and Fix the Fells. The Historic Environment Team commissions specialist consultancy support to inform the conservation, management and enhancement of the National Park's historic environment. This may include heritage impact assessments, conservation area appraisals, historic building recording, conditions surveys, archaeological investigations, landscape and townscape character assessments, design advice, and other specialist heritage and built environment studies to support planning, conservation and place-shaping objectives. Our needs are specific and will vary. We are looking for Suppliers who understand the work we do and not only can provide exceptional services, but who can contribute to our wider Vision for the Lake District. Please note that the Lot Descriptions in section 2 are included to provide some background information on the work of the Authority. The following are examples of types of services which may be required by our Ranger Service. This is not exhaustive but is intended to demonstrate the breadth of the services which will be required: Providing services on a recurring and annual basis, such as our bridge maintenance responsibilities and sourcing of materials for daily use; Providing advice and practical work on specific public sector funded projects, such as the Coast-to-Coast project. Providing specific advice to our internal team of individuals and organisations with whom we operate, for internal projects involving our own land and property, and also to our partner organisations such as Fix the Fells. Lot 1: Bridges Supply, Repair and Maintenance. The Authority supplies, installs and maintains bridges on public rights of way throughout the National Park including bridleways and footpaths for use by horse riders, cyclists, mobility scooters and pedestrians. We are seeking suppliers who can assist with the following: • Supply bridge materials as component parts and/or complete structures in a variety of materials including recycled plastic, metal, timber, concrete, stone. These bridges will need to be to our specification or bespoke design in some cases. • Using the materials listed above, build and install those bridges in a wide variety of locations, including some remote and difficult to get to. This can include machine work, working with helicopter delivery companies, working with hand tools, demolition and construction of abutments. • To repair existing bridge structures in situ, including replacement of handrails, decking boards, beams, abutments e.g. stonework. • To provide designs to structural engineers' standards to meet the supplied specifications for a wide range of bridge types, including footbridges, bridleway bridges and those suitable for road traffic in some instances. This might include reviewing and revising our existing designs and specifications, to producing bespoke designs for individual unique locations and bridge types. • For structural engineers to inspect the current condition of bridges and abutments to check they meet the standards for the required user groups and to sign off newly installed bridges to verify that they meet the required specification and standards. • To provide, erect and use scaffolding, including in remote locations, to complex designs, to enable the team to carry out maintenance and construction work on the bridges and other rights of way work in a safe and secure manner, following current industry and health and safety standards. Services required: • Supply of prefabricated bridge kits • Provision of materials e.g. timber/ plastic/ metal • Bespoke design of bridges • Installation of bridges • Repair of bridges • Engineer surveys on bridges • Scaffolding on bridges to support safe installation or repair Lot 2: Supply of Materials. The Authority requires qualified suppliers for the supply, delivery and installation of materials and services to support our countryside construction and maintenance projects. It aims to ensure high-quality, timely, and cost-effective delivery of materials and services while complying with health, safety, and environmental standards. It also aims to facilitate the provision of locally sourced materials to reduce transport mileage, to support the economic wellbeing of the National Park, and to showcase local products. Suppliers under this framework must demonstrate relevant experience, proven quality standards and the capacity to meet delivery schedules. Services and materials will be provided according to defined specifications, with monitoring of performance through key indicators such as timeliness, quality, and responsiveness. Suppliers must ensure that all materials supplied meet relevant British Standards or industry-recognised equivalents. Goods required: • Pipes/drains • Grass seed • Treated and some graded timber for fencing and the construction of timber boardwalks • Gates • Waymark roundels for Public Footpaths, Bridleways, Byways and permitted routes • Local stone (from the Lake District) for construction of unbound surface paths, stone for drainage works and dry-stone walling and bridge revetments • Plastic boardwalks from 1m to 3m width with non-slip finish • Metalwork (gate springs, gate hinges, catches screws, nuts, etc.) • Screened (inert) topsoil • Fingerposts and Waymarkers • Benches • Fencing wire • Metal fencing (i.e. Clipex) • Native tree species grown from seeds sourced in seed zone 301, or if unavailable, 302. Lot 3: Minor Practical works under £50,000. The Authority requires a range of qualified suppliers for delivery of practical works and services supporting our countryside access and nature conservation projects across the National Park. This often requires working in remote locations with challenging access. All work standards and specifications will be set out in relevant documents. All work will need to be carried out to all relevant legislative requirements by appropriately trained and qualified staff. Examples of the types of work the Authority requires are: construction, repair and maintenance of structures, furniture and surfaces forming part of Public Rights of Way work (PROW) such as footpaths, bridleways and byways. Surfacing -The supply, construction, repair and maintenance of; • Un-bound, bound, crushed stone or tarmac paths. • Machine construction of profile inversion (subsoil) paths • Supply and delivery and laying of stone flags • Construction and repair of pitched stone paths using local stone. Drainage works - The supply, construction, repair and maintenance of; • Plastic drainage of all sizes. • Stone culverts • Drainage ditches. Fencing, Walling and hedgerows- The supply, construction, repair and maintenance of; • All forms of fencing including Post and rail, post and wire, metal estate style • Drystone and bound (mortared) walling in local vernacular style. • Hedgerows planted and maintained in the local vernacular style. Vegetation management • Mechanical and chemical control of vegetation on public rights of way, open land and formal sites including control of Invasive Non-Native Species (INNS). Countryside Furniture - The supply, construction, repair, and maintenance of; • Wooden and metal fingerposts, signs, benches, gates stiles, boardwalks and other countryside furniture. Tree Works • Surveying, planting, felling, maintaining and high access rope work relating to tree management. • Supply of native tree and plant species. Transportation • Transportation of plant, machinery, materials to accessible parts of the National Park. Habitat Restoration Works • Restore peatland areas by hand and or machine. • Planting of native species Traffic Management Supply and management of traffic control systems on public highways up to 'A' road standards. Please see our Rights of Way Specification Resource Pack at Appendix 1. Services required: • Surfacing • Drainage installation and maintenance • Sub soiling • Installation of stone flags • Pitching to create paths • Fencing • Walling • Vegetation control and clearance • Installation of countryside furniture (e.g. fingerposts/benches) • Tree works • Planting (trees and hedgerows) • Spraying (herbicides) • Hedge trimming • Salting and gritting paths • Trail sweeping • Mooring works (Ullswater/servicing) • Graffiti removal • Woodland management through thinning, coppicing, halo thinning, girdling, and processing of timber • Bracken management through mowing, rolling, or chemical application • Scrub management • Hedge laying • Grassland restoration and management activities; mowing, baling, weed wiping, harrowing, seeding, plug planting • Chemical control of invasive, non-native species Please also see Appendix 1 of the ITT. Lot 4: Consultancy and Specialist Services. The Authority requires a range of consultancy services to assist it in carrying out its statutory duties and project work. Our work is incredibly varied, and consultancy is required in relation to all stages of a project from feasibility, design, planning, and surveying. We require specialist advice in relation to Rights of Way, and lake/water works. Other areas of the Authority's work include historic buildings and environment, planning and architectural surveying so we welcome consultants from a range of specialist practice areas. Advice sought could be, for example, in the form of written reports, design drawings to agreed standards, survey datasets (in agreed formats) or overseeing the delivery of defined projects around nature recovery or access and recreation related works. This Lot is divided into three individual sub-lots based on the type of consultancy required. Lot 4a: Access and Recreation services required: • Traffic management e.g. traffic lights • Planning consultancy • Structural engineering design • Construction Design and Management works • Electronic counting surveys - people, horses, vehicles, bikes etc • Rights of Way consultants • Project managers • Visitor monitoring and data • Property management and consulting Lot 4b: Natural Environment: • Ecological surveys (e.g. habitat surveys using NVC, UKHAB frameworks/Habitat condition monitoring using BNG or CSM methods/specialist surveys for taxonomical groups i.e Bryophytes, Lichens, protected species groups, insects) • Baseline surveys • Biodiversity Net Gain Habitat Management and Monitoring Plans • Biodiversity Net Gain Habitat bank monitoring survey and reporting • Habitat and property management and monitoring planning • Drone Surveys • Geospatial surveys Lot 4c: Historic Environment: • Historic Structure Surveys (e.g. condition surveys, archaeological and structural assessments and repair schedules) • Archaeological surverys (e.g condition surveys, fieldwork, heritage assessments) • Contract administration services for Historic Structure Construction Projects Lot 5: Training and Development. he Authority requires qualified companies to provide essential training to ensure that individuals working in various roles are equipped with the knowledge and skills needed to work safely and in compliance with regulatory requirements and legislation. The training requirements cover a range of topics, including first aid, manual handling, chainsaw, plant and equipment operation (to name a few - please see Appendix 2 for a full concise list), which are required to minimise risks and ensure a safe working environment. Courses will need to be accredited by recognised bodies, providing learners with the necessary qualifications to meet industry standards. • First aid • Manual handling • Practical countryside management training e.g.: walling, fencing • Plant and machinery operations e.g.: 4WD training, chainsaws, quad bikes, strimmers; • Species management training (e.g tree conditions surveys) • Please see Appendix 2 of the ITT for a list of all training requirements. Lot 6: Supply and repairs of Equipment, Plant and Machinery. The Authority has an internal fleet of various machinery, equipment and plant. We require services for maintenance and servicing of all types of equipment, plant, and machinery. We also require suppliers who can source and provide new equipment, plant and machinery as required. For example, current categories include: • Plant: diggers, dumpers, tracked power barrows, remote flails, chippers. • Vehicles: land rovers, pick-ups, 4x4s, electric vans and cars. • Power tools: compressors, jet washes, cement mixers, drills, stone saws, angle grinders chop saws etc. • Hand tools: spades, panel saws, shovelers, tampers, steel bars etc. • PPE: chainsaw trousers, hard hats, eye protection, hearing protection etc. • Fuel (Aspen, diesel, petrol, LPG etc.) • Servicing and safety inspections (e.g. LOLA checks on lifting strops and chains, and general servicing of tools like compressors) • Bi-annual service of outboard motors for patrol boats • Servicing of patrol boat trailers • Annual servicing of life jackets, patrol boat radar systems and CCTV systems. We require maintenance and servicing of all machinery and vehicles. Services required: • Servicing • Repairs • Maintenance (boats, outboard engines, trailers, lifejackets, diggers, dumpers, radar, CAT scanners, generator calibration) • Inspection of kit/ equipment • LOLER items checks • Supply of new machinery as required Lot 7: Helicopter Operations. Provide helicopter operations for the transportation of stone and other materials to remote locations throughout the Lake District: movement of prebagged fell stone in one-ton bags to high altitude worksites on popular mountain paths. Stropping, bunding and prepping materials such as flagstones, fence posts or bridge materials prior to flying. Providing specialist safety advice to officers involved in helicopter operations - before during and after any operations. Provide experienced ground crew for hooking on and assessing loads, receiving loads where necessary and ensuring specialist kit or equipment such as signage strops and radio headsets are available. To provide an indication of volume, in 2025 LDNPA flew over 400 tonnes of stone to high altitude sites. Suppliers must hold all relevant Civil Aviation Authority (CAA) approvals, USL Licensing and operate in accordance with UK aviation regulations. Services required: • Transport of materials and equipment within the Lake District National Park using helicopters • Airlift operations • Load preparation (stropping, bunding) • Ground crew provision • Flight planning and risk assessment Lot 8: Higher Value Practical Works - £50,000 and over. The Authority secures frequent bids for grant money provided by national, regional and local government as well as charitable organisations and private funding organisations. This funding enables the Authority to undertake larger scale and usually multi-facetted projects or programmes of work varying in value from the high tens of thousands of pounds to the low millions of pounds. Such projects may involve delivery of one type of product or service across a range of sites throughout the park or a multi-facetted project including access, nature conservation, interpretation, and conservation of the heritage-built environment. We are looking for suppliers who can provide work at scale and across a range of areas, either directly or by acting as Primary Contractors and providing project management and delivering work through co-ordinating multiple suppliers and contractors. Examples of such work packages include the establishment of the Coast-to-Coast National Trail, barn restoration through the Farming in Protected Landscapes programme and Access for All projects. The type of work is similar to that contained in Lots 1, 2, and 3 but at large scale. Services required: • General construction project work (see description) • Sub soiling • Stone flags • Pitching • Construction Design and Management work • Supply and construction of bridges • Public path works • Securing relevant consents, assents and planning permissions • Woodland Management • Grassland restoration • Riverbank Stabilization
