sig_701abf3815f1a1223dcc.description:
The contribution service of ARD, ZDF, Deutschlandradio (hereinafter referred to as "Contribution Service" or "Client" or "AG") intends to replace the existing Db2-z/OS platform with a modern, open target platform based on PostgreSQL in on-premises operation. The subject matter is the technical migration of the existing database and application components without functional changes. The objective is the complete, high-performing and secure executability of all affected applications on PostgreSQL. The eight work packages to be performed by the contractor (AN) within the scope of the overall project are described below. The tasks are to be performed in close cooperation and coordination with the project team of the Contribution Service. 1. Migration of the Db2 database to PostgreSQL - Analysis of the database and development of a migration plan with the aim of transferring the Db2 database to PostgreSQL. - Migration of the database structure including all relevant database objects incl. tables, indexes, views, triggers. The management of schema changes under PostgreSQL is to be supported by a Liquibase model. Stored procedures are not part of the migration, as their replacement has already taken place. - Migration of data from the Db2 database to PostgreSQL. - Verification of the correctness of the migration by suitable test procedures. 2. Conversion of the Db2 SQL statements used in the applications into functionally equivalent PostgreSQL statements - Conversion of the Db2 SQL statements used in the applications into functionally equivalent PostgreSQL statements. - Support of the Client in proving the correct functionality of the applications. - If application errors occur, solution concepts must be developed, coordinated with the Client and implemented to ensure the correct functionality of the applications. In doing so, an adaptation of the application code (e.g., Java in RUBIN) should be avoided if possible. 3. Optimisation of the performance of the PostgreSQL database and sizing of the hardware required for on-premises operation - Optimisation of the performance of the PostgreSQL database through suitable tuning measures, so that the performance requirements of the Client are met. - Elaboration of a hardware sizing on the basis of which the Contribution Service can procure the hardware required for on-premises operation for the operation of the applications without further conceptual preliminary work. - Proof of compliance with the performance requirements of the Contribution Service by means of suitable test procedures on the hardware procured by the Contribution Service (this is carried out according to the sizing specifications of the AN). 4. Setup of the required system environments and infrastructure as well as design of the required operational processes - Setup of the server infrastructure and the associated system software (operating system, database) using the Ansible Automation Platform. - Setup (installation, integration, establishment of operational readiness) and operation of the required system environments (development, reference, training, test, production) for the individual applications in cooperation with the team of the Contribution Service. - Management of test environments and test data - Documentation of the corresponding procedure and operational processes. - Design and testing of the required operational processes (backup and recovery, system monitoring, etc.). - Transfer of responsibility for these tasks to the Contribution Service team by the milestone "Trial Operation". 5. Development of a tool for pseudonymisation / anonymisation and test data generation - Development or integration of a commercial tool for pseudonymisation/anonymisation of data in accordance with the functional requirements of the Contribution Service. - Development or integration of a commercial tool for the generation of consistent test data (subsets of production data) for development and test environments as well as for performance measurements 6. Qualification of users - Transfer of the necessary integration and operational know-how to the Contribution Service team. - Support and assistance of Contribution Service experts in taking over operational tasks. - Conducting training courses and other qualification measures in the areas of PostgreSQL, operational tools and others. 7. Go-live and support during the start-up phase - Preparation of the go-live of the applications. - Go-live fine planning - Conducting dress rehearsals for the go-live of the applications. - Support of the go-live, standby - hypercare for a period of nine months. 8. Project and release management - The project is organised with project and sub-project management as well as a steering committee. The AN ensures professional project planning, project control and project reporting and establishes risk management appropriate to the risk. - At the project and sub-project level, dual staffing with representatives of the Contribution Service and the AN is planned. - All necessary deadline meetings, workshops, etc. are to be prepared, moderated and documented by the AN. - All results and in particular decisions made are to be documented properly, in detail and comprehensively by the AN. - Templates and models are to be agreed between the Contribution Service and the AN. - The Confluence system or another system provided by the Client is to be used as the project repository. - The AN shall provide for the establishment of a project office (PMO) (however, an on-site establishment at the Contribution Service is not required). The description of the tendered services is continued under section 5.1 of this notice. Continuation of the description of the tendered services from section 2.1 of this notice.

- The project office supports project management on both the Contribution Service and contractor sides for administrative tasks (recording and administrative tasks, information preparation and distribution, planning tasks, report preparation, etc.). - The AN provides release management to coordinate the further development of the applications by the Contribution Service and the migration activities over the course of the approx. three-year project duration. The following services are not the subject of this tender: - Provision of the PostgreSQL database software, operating system software - Procurement of the hardware and system technology required for operation. - Procurements of tools and software tools required by the Client for the operation of the systems beyond the end of the project or permanently. It is intended, provided that a sufficient number of applications to participate by suitable tenderers is received, to limit the number of tenderers who will be invited to submit tenders in the subsequent negotiation procedure to three suitable tenderers. Unsuccessful tenderers will be informed in writing of their elimination. The restriction of the circle of tenderers is based on objective, non-discriminatory criteria (cf. this notice and Part A. Conditions of Participation of the Participation Brochure) The Contribution Service will suspend the negotiation procedure for a period of 2 months after the conclusion of the competition for participation over the turn of the year. The selected bidders will receive information before the suspension of the procedure that they belong to the limited circle of bidders. In addition, the Contribution Service will inform them via the communication function of the dtvp procurement marketplace about the resumption of the negotiation procedure and the provision of the tender documents as well as the invitation to submit initial tenders on the dtvp procurement marketplace. The procurement procedure will be continued with at least one negotiation round for 2 months after the conclusion of the competition for participation and the previously described suspension of the procedure. The awarding authority will only invite the three selected suitable bidders to submit an initial tender based on the detailed tender documents including a detailed description of services. In addition, for quality assurance purposes, the implementation of a 2-month pitch is planned. Bidders will receive technical documents, test data without production reference as well as selected SQLs and code snippets, carry out an exemplary trial migration, analyse risks and outline (partial) solution concepts including procedures for hardware sizing. The pitch fee is 20.000 euros net. The pitch results feed into the quality evaluation. Further details on the pitch as well as the concrete schedule for the implementation of the pitch and the parallel preparation of the initial tenders can be found in the tender documents, which will be made available to the bidders belonging to the limited circle of bidders after the conclusion of the competition for participation and the 2-month procedure suspension via the invitation to submit the initial tender on the dtvp procurement marketplace. SELECTION OF THE LIMITED CIRCLE OF BIDDERS The Contribution Service will select a maximum of 3 bidders for the negotiation procedure. If more than 3 applicants are suitable after checking the applications to participate, the selection will be made on the basis of the following objective criteria: The Contribution Service will award a maximum of 200 points for the reference list submitted by the applicant. Within the framework of awarding the maximum 100 points per specified migration reference, the Contribution Service will exclusively base its decision on the two reference contracts of the applicant that were confirmed by the reference client during the reference check, meet the specified minimum requirements and achieved the highest score during the evaluation. In the event that more than three applicants belong to the restricted circle of applicants due to an equal number of points, all these applicants with the same score will also be invited to submit a tender. In detail, the awarding of points is based on the following criteria: a) Comparability of the source system in the reference project (15 points) - Replacement of a DB2 database from a mainframe system: 15 points b) Data volume of the reference project related to structured data (max. 30 points) - > 2 TB (minimum requirement) to 5 TB: 10 points - > 5 TB to 10 TB: 20 points - > 10 TB: 30 points c) Technical complexity of the data model and application logic (max. 40 points) - High data integrity: The migration included a data model with high referential integrity with foreign keys: 5 points - High object variety: The migration included the migration/re-creation using triggers: 5 points - High object variety: The migration included the migration/re-creation using views: 5 points - High application binding: The migration included the adaptation of embedded SQL: 5 points - Combined technical complexity: In addition, it is evaluated whether the migration required a combination of the above-mentioned techniques. Full points will be awarded if the migration included the cumulative application of foreign keys and triggers and views: 20 points d) Scope of operational responsibility in the reference project (max. 10 points) - Operational responsibility for 3 (minimum requirement) to 6 months: 5 points - Operational responsibility for > 6 months to 12 months: 10 points e) Type of client in the reference project (max. 5 points) - Client from the private sector: 0 points - Public sector client: 5 points Further details on the competition for participation can be found in the participation brochure provided on the dtvp procurement marketplace.

sig_702054ac59d9cdae4923.description: Kent Fire and Rescue Service (KFRS) is exploring options for a Project Portfolio Management (PPM) solution to support the planning, management, oversight and reporting of projects and programmes across the organisation. KFRS is open to different solution and delivery models, including established Software as a Service (SaaS) products and Microsoft/Power Platform-based solutions. Please note: For the purposes of this market engagement, KFRS is only seeking responses in respect of solutions which are currently available for procurement through an existing Government Commercial Agency (GCA) framework (formerly CCS). Suppliers should identify the relevant framework, Lot (where applicable) and service/solution listing within their response. The purpose of this exercise is to undertake a short and proportionate test of the market before KFRS determines its procurement strategy and route to market. In particular, KFRS wishes to understand: •what potentially suitable solutions are available within or around the stated affordability envelope; •the broad alignment of available products with KFRS's functional and technical requirements; •the different solution and service models available and the respective responsibilities of KFRS and the supplier; •indicative licensing/subscription, implementation, support and ongoing configuration/development costs; •the extent to which solutions allow KFRS to retain appropriate control and portability of its organisational data; •any observations from the market which may help KFRS refine its requirements; and •the specific GCA/CCS framework, Lot and/or service listing through which the proposed solution can be procured. Nature of this Exercise This is a preliminary market engagement exercise and not a competitive procurement or invitation to tender. The functional and technical requirements provided with this brief represent KFRS's current understanding of its needs. They are being provided to give suppliers sufficient information to determine whether they have a product or solution that could potentially meet the requirement. Suppliers are not required to provide a detailed response against each individual requirement or complete the requirements schedules on a line-by-line basis. Responses will not be evaluated or scored as tender submissions. Instead, KFRS is seeking a brief, high-level response that will enable us to understand whether a proposed solution appears sufficiently aligned with our needs to warrant further exploration. KFRS would also welcome constructive feedback on the requirements themselves. This may include identifying areas which would benefit from clarification, or alternative approaches or current market capabilities which KFRS should consider. Please respond via the Kent Business Portal. Additional information: The contracting authority considers that this contract may be suitable for economic operators that are small or medium enterprises (SMEs). However, any selection of tenderers will be based solely on the criteria set out for the procurement.
sig_702054ac59d9cdae4923.title: GB-Maidstone: Preliminary Market Engagement via GCA Framework - Brief Project Portfolio Management Solution

sig_7045af439be9eef5607e.description: The subject of the procurement is a purchasing and purchase invoice processing system. The purchasing and purchase invoice processing system must support the City of Tampere's order-to-pay process and act as a core tool in process management, contract utilisation, financial monitoring, and the generation of procurement data. The role of the system is to enable transparent, traceable, and data-driven procurement processes, as well as to streamline manual work across the various stages of purchasing and purchase invoice processing. The system must ensure that purchases are directed to the correct contracts and suppliers, and that order approval, account coding, and monitoring take place consistently. Purchase invoice processing covers the electronic receipt, matching, verification, approval, account coding, and monitoring of purchase invoices throughout the processing lifecycle. The system must support the processing of both purchase-order-based and non-order-based purchase invoices, enable the use of automation and rule-based guidance, and ensure the accuracy, timeliness, and consistency of invoice processing. Purchase invoice processing must integrate seamlessly with purchasing, contracts, and financial monitoring so that data relating to invoices can be utilised in reporting and data-driven management. The core objectives of the purchasing system are: 1. Purchasing that reinforces data-driven management, transparency, and open data: The system produces structured and comparable procurement data and enables a transparent and traceable order-to-pay process that can be utilised in city-level and national-level reporting and analytics. 2. Process streamlining and reduction of manual work: A modern purchasing system automates repetitive work steps, streamlines the processing of orders and purchase invoices, and ensures consistent operating methods, thereby reducing manual work and improving overall process efficiency. 3. Increasing the purchase order rate and contract-compliant purchasing: The system directs purchases to tendered contracts and ensures that purchase orders are used systematically in all procurements, supporting the target of raising the City's purchase order rate to 90 %. 4. Process accuracy and compliance with instructions: The system ensures compliance with procurement legislation and the City's procurement and ordering instructions, handles preliminary control of the budget and appropriations, and reinforces the consistency and accuracy of the entire process. TECHNICAL DIALOGUE The contracting authority wishes to carry out a technical dialogue regarding the procurement in two parts: 1. 22-4-8.5 functional and non-functional requirements of the system 2. 27.5.-18.6 system requirements and contract terms The contracting authority wishes to verify market solutions and its own requirements through the technical dialogue. If you are able to offer a purchasing and purchase invoice processing system solution, register for the technical dialogue by 30.4 at the email address hankinnat@tampere.fi. You may use "Registration for technical dialogue/procurement of purchasing and purchase invoice processing" as the subject line of the message. We will deliver the materials and related detailed information in a reply message.
sig_7045af439be9eef5607e.title: System solution for purchasing and purchase invoice processing

sig_709b4a814385a0bdc3b7.description: The project "Strengthening the socio-economic participation of women in Burkina Faso" (ProFemmes) aims to improve the socio-economic participation of women in selected regions of Burkina Faso. The project targets individual businesswomen and those whose livelihoods are directly or indirectly linked to micro, small and medium-sized enterprises (MSMEs) and cooperatives that are important for women's employment and income. The project also targets women in vulnerable situations, including those who are internally displaced. This objective is pursued through three closely connected areas of action. First, ProFemmes strengthens the entrepreneurial capacities of women-led MSMEs, cooperatives and individual businesswomen, especially in agricultural and forest value chains, by improving their business, management and digital skills and supporting their market presence and competitiveness. Second, the project enhances women's technical and financial capacities to engage in new or more viable income-generating activities, for example in water and sanitation in the region Djôrô or in crafts, services and trade in Fada N'Gourma, often in close coordination with existing programmes such as PEA and ProSPS. Third, ProFemmes improves the socio-economic conditions for women's financial co-decision at household level by building basic financial skills among couples and promoting shared decision-making on household income, savings and investments, using gender-transformative tools such as Ecole de Maris and GALS. Geographically, the project focuses on the region of Djôrô (formerly Sud-Ouest) and the commune of Fada N'Gourma in the Goulmou region (formerly Est). ProFemmes follows a "Next Level" approach, working mainly with women who already run economic activities or are embedded in relevant economic structures, and helping them move from informal, short-term activities to more sustainable, market-oriented livelihoods. Implementation is carried out by GIZ on behalf of the German Federal Ministry for Economic Cooperation and Development (BMZ), in close coordination with national and local partners and with other German development projects, in order to generate structural, gender-transformative effects beyond short-term income gains. This call for tenders aims to select a contractor to support the implementation of the project "Strengthening the socio-economic participation of women in Burkina Faso" (ProFemmes). The project is commissioned by the German Federal Ministry for Economic Cooperation and Development (BMZ) and implemented by the Deutsche Gesellschaft für Internationale Zusammenarbeit (GIZ) GmbH in a politically fragile context marked by internal displacement and the structural marginalization of women. This call for tenders aims to select a specialised service provider to implement key service packages for the project. Potential bidders are organisations experienced in private sector development, value chain promotion, gender-transformative approaches, financial inclusion and multi-actor coordination in fragile contexts, with strong operational capacity in Burkina Faso. The contractor will act as an operational implementation unit for ProFemmes in the region of Djôrô and, indirectly, in Fada N'Gourma. The tendered services focus mainly on Output 1 (entrepreneurial empowerment) and Output 3 (financial co-decision making at household level). Under Output 1, bidders are expected to: - Analyse relevant agricultural and forest value chains and identify market opportunities for women-led cooperatives and individual entrepreneurs. - Conduct diagnostics of target enterprises and segment beneficiaries into appropriate support pathways (e.g. intensive SME/GTA-Loop coaching with MEBF versus lighter, adapted support). - Design and implement integrated support packages (training, coaching, mentoring, technical assistance) that strengthen operational performance, market presence, competitiveness and digital skills, in close coordination with MEBF Under Output 3, bidders are expected to: - Develop and implement measures that build basic financial literacy among couples (budgeting, saving, responsible borrowing) and introduce simple household financial tools, potentially in digital form. - Facilitate gender-transformative dialogue and reflection formats (using approaches such as GALS, GTA-Loop, Ecole de Maris) to promote joint financial decision-making and reduce conflict risks linked to changing gender roles. - Achieve quantitative targets for men open to shared budgeting and households reporting improved financial competences, working primarily with households where women are already economically supported under Outputs 1 and 2 ("Next Level" approach). Across all service packages, the contractor must maintain continuous technical coordination with GIZ and with related projects (PEA, ProSPS and others); strictly align all measures with the project's indicator framework and targets; strengthen ownership and participation of local partner institutions and actors. This includes annual operational planning, regular reporting, contribution to results monitoring, risk management and adaptive management of activities based on evolving context and findings. In sum, the tender seeks a competent, gender- and market-oriented implementation partner able to translate ProFemmes' strategic objectives into concrete, high-quality services for women, enterprises and households, within a complex, multi-project landscape in Burkina Faso.
sig_709b4a814385a0bdc3b7.title: 10027986-Support for the socio-economic empowerment of women in Burkina Faso

The objective of uni-assist e.V. is to develop a new service IT system to support admission preparation at German higher education institutions. Starting from a proprietary software (aBIS) that has reached the end of its lifecycle and in view of the accelerating digitalisation of admission preparation, the continuing growth in interest among international degree seekers in studying in Germany, as well as the currently frequently described demand for (international) skilled workers in Germany 1 it is essential for the association to quickly establish a new system in order to (i) provide international prospective students with an intuitive and easy-to-use platform for submitting their study applications, (ii) enable the German higher education institutions organised within the association to conduct a transparent and fair selection procedure, (iii) map internal evaluation processes efficiently and with high quality, and (iv) develop recommendations for action and procedural optimisations for internal and external stakeholders based on the generated data. Central objectives of the new development are (i) the gradual technological replacement of the legacy system, (ii) the increase in the degree of automation in the procedural processes, and (iii) the most complete possible digitalisation of the processes with (iv) a simultaneous increase in usability for users as well as (v) the preservation and assurance of all (data protection) legal standards. For this purpose, the contracting authority requires the following IT services (category): 1. Support in software development (e.g. programming, managing Scrum teams, testing) 2. Support for requirements management 3. Support in system administration 4. Support in maintaining and further developing IT and data protection security 5. Support in the coordination of the software development project and consulting for the IT department (e.g. PMO, project management, agile coaching, data management) After its foundation, uni-assist developed a complex, cross-institutional software: aBIS (assist Applicant Information System). sig_7134fbf7fa12cfaf3ae8.description: The subject of this tender is the procurement of a highly available virtualization platform including the required hardware, software licences, manufacturer support and services to replace or modernise the existing virtualization infrastructure of the Gemeinschaftsklinikum Mittelrhein. The new solution must ensure the operation of currently around 300 virtual machines in an active-active data centre architecture and provide the essential functions of the existing VMware vSphere Enterprise Plus / VMware Cloud Foundation environment with functional equivalence. These include in particular high availability, automated load balancing, live migration of virtual machines, cross-location operation and central administration. The tender is designed to be open to all manufacturers and technologies. Solutions based on alternative virtualization platforms as well as concepts in which VMware continues to be used can be offered. The solution offered must meet the functional, technical and economic requirements defined in the tender documents. Bidders must submit an architecture and migration concept that provides either for the continued use of the existing Dell VxRail hardware or its complete replacement. The use of hyperconverged as well as classical 3-tier architectures is permitted. The use of VMware vSAN is not a prerequisite. The scope of services also includes the provision of all required hardware and software components, the integration of the existing Veeam Backup & Replication environment using agentless backup procedures, the implementation including knowledge transfer as well as support for the migration of all virtual machines. The existing VMware subscription ends on 30.03.2027. The solution offered must therefore be fully operational, migrated and accepted, including all productive workloads, by 15.03.2027 at the latest. The period between 15.03.2027 and the expiry of the existing VMware licensing serves as a risk buffer and stabilization phase. Lot LOT-0001: Renewal of virtualization environment. The detailed description of the procurement is described in the specification of services.

sig_7139b581997293fd95ed.description: This is a combined Sources Sought/Request for Information (RFI) notice. Any information submitted by respondents to this request is strictly voluntary. All information received from this Sources Sought/RFI notice will be used for planning and market research purposes only. The United States (U.S.) Government will treat your response to this Sources Sought/RFI notice as information. The information provided may be used by the Air Force to develop an acquisition strategy, statement of work (SOW), statement of objectives (SOO), and performance work statement (PWS) and associated specifications. Respondents are advised that the U.S. Government will not pay for any information or administrative costs incurred in response to this Sources Sought/RFI notice; all costs associated with responding to this Sources Sought/RFI notice will be solely at the interested parties’ expense. All submissions become Government property and will not be returned. Respondents are advised that the Government is under no obligation to provide feedback with respect to any information submitted. To the maximum extent possible, please submit non-proprietary information. Any proprietary information submitted should be identified as such and will be handled accordingly and protected from disclosure. Proprietary information will be safeguarded in accordance with the applicable Government regulations. The Government shall not be liable for damages related to proprietary information that is not properly identified. Any submissions in response to this Sources Sought/RFI constitutes consent for that submission to be reviewed by Government personnel and Advisory & Assistance Services (A&AS) Contractor employees supporting AFLCMC/ES. The responses may be forwarded to other Government entities in consideration for applicability to other programs. All Government and Department of War (DoW) contractor personnel reviewing Sources Sought/RFI responses will have signed non-disclosure agreements and understand their responsibility for proper use and protection from unauthorized disclosure of proprietary information. All members of the Government and contractor team will be reminded of their obligation to protect such information to the maximum extent permitted or required by the Economic Espionage Act, 18 United States Code (U.S.C.) 1831 et seq., and other applicable statutes or regulations. In addition, Government members will be reminded of their obligation to afford protection under the Trade Secrets Act, 18 U.S.C. 1905. 1.0 Introduction The Aerospace Management Foreign Military Sales (FMS) Branch (AFLCMC/ESAN) is seeking market information to identify highly mobile, production-ready, commercial solutions to support the modernization of Ground Control Approach (GCA) and Precision Approach Radar (PAR) systems capabilities in support of the Brazilian Air Force and potentially other FMS partner nations. 2.0 Objective The primary objective of this Sources Sought/RFI notice is to identify new systems to replace existing L3Harris GCA-2000 and PAR-2000 systems to improve the Brazilian Air Force’s ability to support radar surveillance and precision landing operations. Based on the review of responses to this Sources Sought/RFI notice, the Government may elect to release a formal Request for Proposal (RFP) at a future date. The Period of Performance (PoP) for any subsequent contract effort will remain variable and dependent upon the maturity and deployment timelines of the offered solutions. Under any future resultant contract, the prime contractor will be required to execute a comprehensive modernization effort, to include the delivery of all required radar equipment, provision of initial spares, and the execution of all necessary site modifications and system integration. 3.0 Desired Capabilities The below capabilities integrate specific parameters required by the Brazilian Air Force. 3.1 General System must demonstrate the capability to achieve full flight inspection certification (FAA/ICAO standards) for both Airport Surveillance Radar (ASR) and Precision Approach Radar (PAR) functions. 3.2 Transportation a. Threshold (T): Setup within 8 hours by 4 personnel. Transportable by KC-390 aircraft. b. Objective (O): Setup within 4 hours by 2 personnel. Roll-on/Roll-off capable on KC-390 with zero major disassembly. 3.3 Equipment Specifics 3.3.1 Surveillance a. Primary Surveillance Radar (PSR) Range & Altitude Threshold (T): Minimum range of 30 NM. Altitude coverage up to 10,000 ft AGL. Objective (O): Minimum range of 60 NM. Altitude coverage up to 18,000 ft AGL. b. PSR Probability of Detection (T): 80% or higher. (O): 90% or higher for a 2m2 target. c. Secondary Surveillance Radar (SSR) Range & Altitude (T): Minimum range of 60 NM and altitude coverage up to 18,000 ft AGL. (O): Range of 100 NM and altitude coverage up to 35,000 ft AGL. d. SSR Modes & Capability (T): Must support ATCRBS, Modes 3/A, C, S, and ADS-B. (O): Full support for all Threshold modes plus native cryptographic integration for secure military Mode 5 e. SSR Probability of Detection (Pd) (T): 90% or higher. (O): 95% or higher. 3.3.2 Precision Landing a. PAR Coverage & Switch Time (T): Service up to 6 runways, switchable within 60 seconds. (O): Service > 6 runways, switchable in under 30 seconds. b. PAR Instrumented Range (T): Reliable azimuth/elevation tracking and detection out to a minimum range of 10 NM. (O): Reliable azimuth/elevation tracking and detection out to 20 NM or greater. c. PAR Target Capacity (T): Track up to 50 aircraft in azimuth and 22 aircraft in elevation. (O): Track over 100 combined aircraft simultaneously. d. PAR Detection Probability (2m2 target) (T): 90% probability at 10 NM. (O): 95% probability at 15 NM in rain and 20 NM in clear weather. e. PAR Resolution (T): Range: 400 ft, Azimuth: 1.2 degrees, Elevation: 0.6 degrees (all with greater than or equal to 80% probability). (O): Margins improved by 20% over threshold values. f. PAR Accuracy (T): Range: less than or equal to ±100 ft (or 2%). Azimuth: less than or equal to ±30 ft. Elevation: less than or equal ±20 ft. (O): Margins improved by 20% over threshold values. 3.3.3 Communications Data Interoperability (T=O): Output standard ASTERIX Eurocontrol data format for all surveillance outputs. ATC Positions, Display, & Automation (T): Two (2) ATC positions. Explain and provide detailed documentation of the proposed a. ATC automation/display system. (O): Fully modular system expandable up to six (6) ATC positions. ATC Radio Communications (T): Each ATC position must have UHF/VHF transmit/receive capability and the ability to simultaneously monitor UHF/VHF Guard frequencies. (O): Fully integrated voice switch system with secure, encrypted transmit/receive capability. 3.3.4 System Reliability & Redundancy (T=O): Backup PSR transmitter or redundancy in the system is required. Backup power (UPS) is required. Mean Time Between Critical Failure (MTBCF) > 2,000 hours. 3.3.5 Maintainability (MTTR) (T): Mean Time to Repair (MTTR) < 30 minutes. (O): Mean Time to Repair (MTTR) < 15 minutes. 3.3.6 System Operational Certifications Identify whether or not the system has any/all of six (6) certifications for operations in both CONUS and OCONUS: Air Traffic Control Radar Beacon System (ATCRBS) Identification Friend or Foe (IFF) Mark XII System (AIMS); Cybersecurity; Interoperability and Supportability (I&S); National Airspace System (NAS); Spectrum; and Transportability (air, ground and sea). 3.3.7 Ancillary & Support Equipment Requirements (T): Identify all generators, environmental control unit (ECU), hardware/software, and ancillary equipment requirements necessary to support standalone system operations. (O): Offer integrated, self-contained auxiliary systems that minimize external logistics footprint and setup time. 3.4 Maintenance Capabilities a. Operator and maintenance technical manuals/data provided. b. No more than four quantity maintenance personnel to set up and maintain desired. c. Mean Time Between Critical Failure (MTBCF) 2000 hours desired. d. Mean Time Between Failures (MBTF) 250 hours desired. e. Mean Time to Repair (MTTR) less than 30 minutes desired. f. Long term sustainment and supportability. g. Maintenance training course. 3.5 Delivery and Support a. Worldwide contract logistics support is highly desired. b. Identify size, weight and power constraints including any unique requirements to support a rapid deployment in potentially austere climate conditions. c. Identify depot and sustainment mechanisms currently in place. 4.0 Questions Please answer the questions below. For any yes/no answers, please describe, to the extent possible, how you perform the activity and/or service in question. 4.1 Company Information & Status Interested potential sources shall respond by identifying: a. Interest in this effort. b. Small business status; including small, small-disadvantaged, women-owned, Historically Underutilized Business Zone (HUBZone) and/or service-disabled veteran and covering all socio-economic programs. 4.2 Capabilities Interested potential sources should identify their capabilities and recent experience (within the last 5 years) in providing navigational aids (NAVAIDS) systems and services similar to the capabilities listed in this Sources Sought/RFI notice. Responses should address existing solutions that provide the capabilities described. If your existing solution does not currently meet all of the desired capabilities outlined in Section 3.0, describe your capability to modify or adapt the system to fully satisfy the Governments’ requirements. 4.3 Training Experience Describe your experience in training personnel of varying skill levels in the use, mastery, and maintenance of the provided solutions. 4.4 Sustainment Experience Describe your experience with solutions that successfully support the sustainment of Government Furnished Equipment (GFE) or similar equipment operations. 4.5 Past Performance Details In delineating previous experience, identify the complexity, scope, dollar value, start and end dates of the effort, customer point of contact. Relate scope of these past efforts to the requirements identified above and describe breadth of experience in delivering similar systems. Identify if the past effort has been part of an FMS project. 4.6 Cost & Schedule Estimates In addition to detailing how the proposed solution meets all performance requirements, please provide a response to the following questions: a. What is the estimated total cost of the proposed solution, broken down by estimated unit production cost and any required Non-Recurring Engineering (NRE)? b. What is your production capacity and estimated timeline/delivery schedule from contract award date to full delivery and satisfaction of all performance requirements? c. Are systems meeting the capabilities delineated above currently fielded (Y/N?). If not, what is your estimated schedule to complete development and/or any modifications to deliver fully operational system—to include any required government testing--within 12 months of contract date? d. Identify long lead items. e. Identify any contractual vehicles available for potential use by this Agency to procure systems; include contract number, period of performance and point of contact. 5.0 Submission Instructions Please submit responses to this Sources Sought/RFI notice via e-mail to the Contracting Officer, Contract Specialist and Program Manager below, no later than 08 October 2026. Responses shall not exceed 20 single spaced, 8.5.x11 inch, single sided pages in length, and shall be an UNCLASSIFIED PDF. Sources Sought/RFI responses should address the systems’ ability to meet the requirements outlined in Section 3 and answer all capability assessment questions in Attachment A. The font shall be 12pt Times New Roman. Ms. Kelsey Ribeiro, Contracting Officer, Email: Kelsey.Ribeiro@us.af.mil Ms. Marilyn Hockersmith, Contract Specialist, Email: marilyn.hockersmith.1@us.af.mil Ms. Cynthia Canavan, Program Manager, Email: Cynthia.Canavan.1@us.af.mil The information should also include the following business contact information in a cover letter: Company Name and Address Commercial and Government Entity (CAGE) Code Point of Contact (POC) name for further clarification or questions POC Telephone Number POC Email Address Please refer any questions regarding this Sources Sought/RFI notice to the Contract Specialist and Contracting Officer. This Sources Sought/RFI notice is issued solely for informational purposes. It does not constitute an RFP or a promise to issue an RFP in the future. This Sources Sought/RFI does not commit the Government to contract for any supply or service in any manner. Respondents are advised that the Government will not pay for any information or administrative costs incurred in response to this Sources Sought/RFI; all costs associated with responding to this RFI will be solely at the interested parties’ expense. Not responding to this Sources Sought/RFI does not preclude participation in any future RFP, if any is issued.

sig_7181f96b85e030152f2b.description: MARKET DIALOGUE The subject of the market dialogue is the procurement of a system for the remote monitoring and management service of maritime safety equipment currently under preparation for the needs of Väylävirasto. Väylävirasto is responsible for the maintenance, development and usability of maritime safety equipment in Finland as part of the authority's tasks in fairway management. The remote monitoring service is a key part of the operational reliability, situational awareness and remote management entity of safety equipment. BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVES The subject of the procurement is the implementation, maintenance and ongoing development of a remote monitoring and remote management service for maritime safety equipment. The service receives status, fault and location data from safety equipment, processes and stores the data, and forwards it to the key systems of Väylävirasto, particularly Reimari and analytics solutions. There are approximately 1 800 pieces of remotely monitored safety equipment, some of which are fixed and some floating, and some of the equipment can also be managed remotely. The equipment communicates via a mobile network, and in the target state, message transmission is based on the LTE-M network and the MQTT protocol in accordance with IALA specifications, with secure encryption. In the target state, the remote monitoring and management service is located in Väylävirasto's cloud environment (AWS). The service is responsible for the processing of all received remote monitoring data, including raw data storage, data processing, the provision of interfaces and necessary calculation operations, such as post-calculation of position measurements. The remote monitoring service does not provide a separate user interface, but the data is viewed via Reimari. The procurement includes system maintenance to ensure that the service remains operationally reliable, secure and responsive to users' needs throughout the contract period. Maintenance covers, among other things, technical support, updates, bug fixes, and compatibility with safety equipment and integrations. Ongoing system development is also implemented as part of the procurement. The aim of ongoing development is to gradually enable new functionalities, interfaces and integrations, and to support changes in the operating environment, technology and legislation. The procurement also examines various architectural options for communication between safety equipment and the remote monitoring service. The procurement includes a cooperation model in which the contracting authority and the supplier develop the service in a planned and long-term manner. The objective is a comprehensive solution that supports the lifecycle management of safety equipment, the utilisation of data and the continuous improvement of the service. One (1) supplier will be selected as the service provider. The subject, scope and technical solutions of the procurement may be refined and/or modified as the preparation of the procurement and the market dialogue progress. PRELIMINARY SCHEDULE The contracting authority's target schedule for the implementation of the market dialogue and procurement is: - Market dialogue (technical dialogue), January-February 2026 - Publication of the call for tenders and calculation period, March-April 2026 - Evaluation of tenders and award decision, April-May 2026 - Contract entering into force and commencement of the development project, during the year 2026 ----- ADDITIONAL INFORMATION ON THE NOTICE This notice is a prior information notice. This notice does not constitute a request for tenders. The prior information notice includes an invitation to a market dialogue, whereby all suppliers interested in the procurement have the opportunity to engage in a technical dialogue concerning the procurement with Väylävirasto. The purpose of the technical dialogue is to discuss the subject of the procurement and its definition at a general level. The technical dialogue does not bind Väylävirasto to carry out the procurement. Nor does the technical dialogue bind the supplier to participate in a potential tendering procedure. The technical dialogue is organised through commenting on draft versions of the call for tenders documentation and answering the contracting authority's questions related to the subject of the procurement. Instructions for registration: Suppliers must express their interest in participating in the market dialogue by 11.2.2026 by 12.00 by sending a message to the address tommi.aarnio@vayla.fi with the subject: "Kaukovalvonta - markkinavuoropuhelu". Suppliers are requested to state the following information in the message: - the supplier's contact person's email address The contracting authority reserves the right to invite suppliers also to bilateral negotiations or to continue the technical dialogue in another manner to be announced separately, which will be notified later if necessary. The descriptions presented in this prior information notice and the estimated publication date of the contract notice, as well as the dialogue draft materials to be provided later, are preliminary and indicative prior information on the procurement. Participating companies will not be paid any compensation for responding or participating.

sig_7184071bd66d805d60a4.description: Background Registers of Scotland (RoS) is undertaking a strategic review of its current data licensing position as part of its ambition to maximise the value of the data it holds. RoS currently delivers a range of statutory and commercial data products to a diverse customer base, including citizens, public sector bodies, and commercial organisations. This breadth of demand has led to an increasing need to develop scalable and sustainable data products. The development of these products is shaped by existing licensing arrangements, including the Public Sector Geospatial Agreement (PSGA) and Postal Address File (PAF) frameworks. These define the terms under which data can be used, reused, and shared, particularly where third-party data is integrated with RoS datasets. RoS is seeking specialist support to work with existing RoS departments to define a data strategy that reflects the organisation’s current and future priorities. Purpose of this Notice This notice is issued to engage with the market and identify organisations with expertise in public sector data licensing, data commercialisation, and governance. The feedback received will inform the scope, structure, and requirements of a potential future procurement exercise. Scope of Potential Requirement RoS is seeking a partner to provide expertise and support in the following areas covering both current and future activity. 1. Review of Current Licensing Landscape Assess RoS’s current licensing arrangements, including PSGA, PAF, and other third party agreements Identify constraints, risks, and opportunities in the current model Advise on how existing frameworks can be leveraged to support data products and services while ensure statutory obligations remain paramount 2. Definition of Data Principles Support RoS in developing clear data principles covering: Data sharing and reuse Commercialisation and monetisation Transparency, fairness, and public value Ensure alignment with public sector obligations, corporate objectives and customer expectations 3. Recommendations and Implementation Roadmap Provide actionable, practical recommendations for: Optimising the use of RoS data Enabling new data products and services Managing licensing risks and compliance Clear options, trade-offs, and decision frameworks to support senior decision-making Develop an implementation roadmap that RoS can deliver internally 4. Capability and Skills Development Identify the organisational skills, roles, and capabilities required to: Sustain data commercialisation Govern data and licensing frameworks effectively Recommend approaches to embed these capabilities within RoS operations Key Context for Suppliers RoS operates within a complex licensing environment, particularly where third party data is embedded in its products There is a tension between legacy licensing models and ambitions for more open, scalable data products, which has been identified as a systemic issue RoS is exploring different strategic options, including changes to licensing arrangements and potential use of external partners to support commercialisation Market Engagement RoS invites expressions of interest from organisations with experience in: Public sector data licensing and governance Data commercialisation and product development Navigating complex multi party licensing frameworks Supporting organisations to unlock the value of their data assets Responses to this notice will help shape the design of any future procurement. sig_718ef16b94c184173290.description: The purpose of the framework agreement is, firstly, to ensure maintenance in operational condition, maintenance in security condition and third-party application maintenance (preventive, corrective, evolutionary and adaptive) by taking over the source code of the VALERIE (Val-de-Marne Exploitation et Régulation Informatisées des Effluents) information system and its related applications. It also includes the development of new business applications. Secondly, its purpose is to ensure maintenance in operational condition, through third-party application and hardware maintenance, and maintenance in security condition, of the Artificial Intelligence Information System of the Deputy Directorate for Operations (SI IA-DAE), dedicated to collecting and providing input data to AI engines, and collecting and presenting their results for the purpose of operating the Val-de-Marne sanitation network. The services consist of ensuring: Preventive, corrective, evolutionary and adaptive maintenance of the applications and hardware infrastructure of the VALERIE information system; The development of new business applications; Database administration; IT security; The supply, integration and implementation of hardware; Technical assistance in IT and telecommunication networks; Training actions.; The services consist of ensuring: The physical hosting of the virtualisation server containing the entire application solution; The administration and maintenance of this server, the hypervisor and its virtual machines; The administration and maintenance of the buffer physical machine hosted at the buyer's premises; Third-party application maintenance (preventive, corrective, evolutionary and adaptive) of specific developments; Taking charge of the proper operation, parameterisation and updates of the commercial or open-source third parties applications used; Administration of the databases used; Management of various data import and export interfaces; Acquisition of data coming from these interfaces; Scheduling and archiving of all data with a view to their retransmission to an external AI engine; Collection and archiving of results from the calculations of this AI; The development of views for operating these results on the Panorama E2 supervision software.

sig_719c57caeed697069b5c.description: NHSScotland is exploring options for the potential procurement of a multi-channel remote health monitoring and communication solution capable of supporting the delivery of enhanced care pathways, including home and mobile health monitoring. Remote health monitoring (RHM) is a digitally enabled model of care that allows people to record, submit and share clinically relevant health information from their home or community setting. This enables health and care teams to monitor health status, support self management and intervene proactively, reducing the need for routine face-to-face contact. RHM can support management of long term conditions to reduce escalation and prevent admissions and can also support earlier discharge and hospital at home models where appropriate. Connect Me is NHSScotland’s national remote health monitoring service, currently delivered using the Inhealthcare platform. The service supports the collection of measurements and patient reported information through a range of channels including automated telephone calls, SMS messages and digital access via web browser or mobile application. Lot 1: . This PIN serves as a soft market test to assess available options, continuity of key services, migration approaches and indicative costs. A Market Research Questionnaire can be downloaded from the Additional Documents area and returned as instructed within the document by noon on Monday, 25 May 2026. Suppliers are also invited to attend an online briefing session on 7 May 2026 at 2:30PM. Teams login details will be confirmed via this Public Contracts Scotland portal.

sig_71a636995c5e6bc24f51.description:
Supply of a forest fire location system divided into two parts. Part No. 1 - Supply, installation and commissioning of a forest fire monitoring system based on long-range fire-fighting cameras together with software for automatic smoke detection. Part No. 2 - Supply, installation and commissioning of a complete unmanned aerial vehicle system with an automatic docking station for fire monitoring of forest areas. A detailed description can be found in the relevant parts of the contract. The subject of the contract consists of sets of equipment together with installation and commissioning, the task of which will be to enable automatic detection and location of forest fires, including long-range fire-fighting cameras mounted on observation towers together with necessary accessories and the equipment of the Inspectorate's Alarm and Dispatch Point (ADP). The purpose of the system will be to carry out continuous fire monitoring of forest areas. Fire-fighting cameras mounted on observation towers are to work with the supplied software for automatic fire detection, which is intended to increase the effectiveness of monitoring in the given area. The image from the cameras must be sent to the ADP via a radio link in the unlicensed band, supplied and installed under this contract. The transmission system must be designed in a way that enables the future change of the transmission medium from radio to fibre-optic without the need to replace cameras, software and active network devices, with the exception of terminal devices used for connecting the fibre optic.. The Baczków and Hysne towers should be retrofitted with an Off-Grid power supply installation, and the ADP with a UPS emergency power supply system. The power supply must meet the requirements of PN-EN 62040-5-3:2017-05 (UPS systems) or equivalent. The installation must meet the requirements of PN-EN 62446-1:2016-08 (Photovoltaic installations) or equivalent, PN-EN 62446-1:2016-08/A1:2019-01 (Testing of PV installations) or equivalent, PN-EN 62109-2:2011 (Inverter safety) or equivalent and PN-EN IEC 62619:2023-02 (Lithium battery safety) or equivalent. The contract includes: - dismantling of the existing fire monitoring system, - supply and installation of 3 cameras for observing forest areas on the Baczków, Hysne and Dąbrowa fire-fighting towers, - supply and installation of sprinklers together with a fluid tank for the mounted cameras, - supply and installation of an off-grid power supply on the Baczków and Hysne towers. The installation must meet the requirements of PN-EN 62548 (Photovoltaic installations) or equivalent, PN-EN 62446 (Testing of PV installations) or equivalent, PN-EN 62109 (Inverter safety) or equivalent and PN-EN IEC 62619 (Lithium battery safety) or equivalent. - supply and installation of an alarm system and anti-burglary cameras on the fire-fighting towers, - supply and installation of radio links establishing connections: ● Baczków tower – Hysne tower in the 5 GHz band, ● Hysne tower – Dąbrowa tower in the 5 GHz band, ● Dąbrowa tower – Church in the 60 GHZ band with a backup 5 GHz, ● Church – Inspectorate building in the 60 GHZ band with a backup 5 GHz, ● Baczków tower – Dąbrowa tower in the 5 GHz band (redundant connection), - supply and installation of devices to provide backup communication 5G/LTE, - supply and installation of ADP equipment: ● supply and installation of 3 televisions for observing images from fire-fighting cameras, ● supply and installation of a computer with two monitors, ● supply and installation of a control console, ● supply and installation of a UPS emergency power supply. The power supply must meet the requirements of PN-EN 62040 (UPS systems) or equivalent. - supply, installation and commissioning of an automatic smoke detection system, - training on system operation. The Contractor is obliged to execute a complete work from the point of view of the purpose it is to serve. The Contracting Authority permits the installation of additional devices not included in the specification if they are necessary to achieve the required functionalities. Other information can be found in the procurement documents - Appendix No. 2 to the ToR; Supply, installation and commissioning of a complete unmanned aerial vehicle system with an automatic docking station for fire monitoring of forest areas - equipment under the FEnIKS project entitled: Comprehensive project for the adaptation of forests and forestry to climate change - prevention, counteracting and limiting the effects of threats related to forest fires (FIRE 2). 1. Subject of the contract 1.1. The subject of the contract is the supply of one complete, factory-new and unused UAS system comprising an unmanned aerial vehicle, an automatic docking station, a multi-sensor observation head, a control device, software, accessories, installation, configuration, commissioning, training and warranty service. 1.2. The system will be intended primarily for: automatic and ad-hoc patrols of forest areas during the fire hazard period; remote verification of smoke or fire alarms, including alarms transmitted by the alarm and dispatch point, camera system or rescue services; locating heat sources and determining their coordinates; live transmission in the visible and thermal imaging band; monitoring fire development, access roads, endangered objects and control after extinguishing a fire. 1.3. The subject of the contract has been described through functional requirements and minimum performance parameters. The Contracting Authority does not require a product of a specific brand or a single manufacturer's solution. However, all elements must form one compatible system, for the correct operation of which the Contractor is responsible. 2. Basis and rules for describing the subject of the contract. The description was drawn up taking into account in particular Article 16, Article 99, Article 101 and Article 105–107 of the Act of 11 September 2019 on Public Procurement Law (unified text: Journal of Laws of 2026, item 793 as amended). References to standards are to be understood as references to the indicated standard or an equivalent standard.

• Each indicated parameter is a minimum parameter, unless expressly stated otherwise. • Structurally different technical solutions are permitted if they ensure at least the same functionality, level of security and performance parameters. • If meeting a requirement requires an additional module, licence, modem, antenna, service or accessory, this element must be included in the tender and price. • All costs necessary to use the full functionality of the system for the period indicated in the OPZ must be itemised in the price form. Other information can be found in the procurement documents - Appendix No. 2 to the ToR

sig_71b044f6ea8a0fde2b93.description: The U.S. Embassy Athens Public Diplomacy Section (PDS Athens) of the U.S. Department of State is pleased to announce funding is available through its Public Diplomacy Grants Program in fiscal year 2025. This is an Annual Program Statement, outlining our funding priorities, the strategic themes we focus on, and the procedures for submitting requests for funding. Please carefully follow all instructions below. The deadline for grant applications is July 11, 2025. Funding decisions will be made on these applications on a rolling basis after this deadline, with a goal of informing all applicants of the final funding decision by September 30, 2025. Applicants may apply for funding between $25,000 and $100,000 . Please use the grant application documents and budget template found on the Embassy website https://gr.usembassy.gov/education/ . Purpose of Grants program: PDS Athens invites proposals for projects that strengthen ties between the United States and Greece through concrete demonstrations of cooperation between our two peoples, aiming at making America safer, stronger and more prosperous . All grant proposals must convey an element of American history, culture, or shared values. Competitive proposals should support a priority program area (see below). They should also include a connection with American expert/s, organization/s, or institution/s that will promote increased cooperation between the people of the United States and Greece even after the program has finished. Priority Program Areas: The Public Diplomacy Section is focused on the following priorities in the form of programs, exchanges, and media opportunities that: Promote American Excellence in Emerging Technologies Celebrate 250 Years of American Excellence: Spotlight on America’s Achievements, Innovation, and Leadership Promoting American Excellence in Emerging Technologies Greek students and professionals in emerging technologies have demonstrated a strong technical foundation that can be strategically leveraged to benefit U.S. technology firms and bolster American leadership in critical industries. By channeling this talent to serve the needs of American companies, we can reinforce U.S. technological dominance, strengthen innovation pipelines, and ensure that international engagement directly supports American economic and strategic priorities. We invite proposals aimed at enhancing U.S.-Greece technological cooperation in ways that clearly advance U.S. national interests. Proposals must focus on initiatives (not conferences) that help U.S. firms address critical workforce and skill shortages, expand the reach of American products and innovation standards, and create structured pathways for Greek talent to contribute to U.S.-driven innovation. Prioritized activities include, but are not limited to: Public-private partnerships that connect U.S. technology firms with high-potential Greek talent through American-led career readiness programs, skills development, and reskilling/upskilling initiatives tailored to U.S. industry standards and needs. Training modules designed for integration into Greek higher education or vocational curricula that: Align directly with the needs of U.S. employers; and Target high-demand fields such as artificial intelligence (AI), biotechnology, cybersecurity, data analytics, and cloud computing—strengthening the global competitiveness of U.S. firms. Innovation bootcamps that feature U.S. technologies, platforms, and products, familiarizing international talent with high-quality American tools and practices. Collaborative projects between U.S. technology companies and Greek educational institutions to promote the adoption and use of American-developed AI and other emerging technologies, reinforcing the global footprint of U.S. innovation. All proposals should demonstrate a clear benefit to the United States and prioritize American commercial and strategic interests, consistent with the principles of the America First policy. Celebrating 250 Years of American Excellence: Spotlight on America’s Achievements, Innovation, and Leadership On July 4, 2026, the United States will commemorate the 250th anniversary of the signing of the Declaration of Independence. This historic milestone presents a powerful opportunity to celebrate American excellence, leverage people-to-people ties, and highlight our achievements, legacies, and contributions as part of America’s story of excellence. We invite proposals that underscore American excellence and contribute to the celebration of America250 , highlighting this momentous occasion through impactful and engaging programs. We welcome submissions that promote U.S.-Greece bilateral engagement and spotlight American achievements, innovation, leadership, and the role of faith and religion in democratic societies. Proposals should feature initiatives (not conferences), and include activities such as (but not limited to): Podcasts and/or public lectures on U.S. history, its ties to Greece, democracy, and its global impact Roadshows showcasing 250 years of American innovation and U.S.-Greek cooperation Sports activities or themed games/events Secondary educational modules that will reach Greek classrooms and help to enhance Greek students’ and educators’ positive understanding of America All proposals should demonstrate a clear benefit to the United States and prioritize American strategic interests, consistent with the principles of the America First policy.

In accordance with Articles L. 2124-1 and R. 2124-1 of the Public Procurement Code, this consultation is subject to a formalised procedure for the following reason: - The estimated value of the requirement exceeds the European thresholds. The formalised procedure applied to this consultation is the open invitation to tender procedure defined in Articles L. 2124-2 and R. 2124-2-1° of the Public Procurement Code. The planned public contract is a service contract within the meaning of Article L1111-4 of the Public Procurement Code. This consultation concerns a contract for intellectual services subject to the provisions of the General Administrative Terms and Conditions applicable to intellectual service contracts approved by the order of 30 March 2021. EPFIF has been commissioned by the State to assist the public partners of the ORCOD of Les Lochères in Sarcelles (95) in order to: => Reinforce the expertise available to the State services, and ensure that the identified urgent actions can effectively be advised to the local authority acting as project owner for the ORCOD and deployed; => Define intervention strategies adapted by sector and by co-ownership, as part of a strategic study carried out and financed by EPFIF, on an exceptional basis, on behalf of the State. This consultation therefore aims to carry out technical, legal, land and financial diagnoses for all co-ownerships, as well as a comprehensive housing programming study. The diagnoses will be conducted on almost all the co-ownerships in the Les Lochères district, divided into 3 sectors: - Entrée de Ville, - Les Flanades, - Watteau. All of these studies will enable EPFIF to: => Strengthen expertise and systematise knowledge on the condition and operation of the co-ownerships in Les Lochères, => Propose a prioritised roadmap based on the identified urgencies, => Ultimately define a comprehensive operational strategy. sig_720dc99be366cd8692dc.description: The Administrative Directorate of the WDR intends to conclude a framework agreement for advisory, conceptual and technical support services for the "Business Warehouse" project. The project is designed as a multi-year transformation and implementation project. The aim of the project is the functional design and gradual introduction of an integrated management model that links strategic planning, resource allocation, portfolio and performance assessment, and transparency regarding resources, costs and impact. The project thus serves to further develop the enterprise-wide management capability of the WDR. The contractor shall support the project from detailed design through the implementation phase to going live and the transition to regular operations. The subject of this tender is exclusively advisory services, the functional design and the technical support of the project across all project phases. Also expected is the functional design and support of the technical implementation as well as the translation of functional requirements into actionable process, data and system requirements. The technical implementation and software development itself are not the subject of this tender. The contract is tendered as a framework agreement without any obligation to purchase. The contract term is 27 months from the start of services; the WDR receives the option to extend the contract once by a further year. The estimated call-off volume is approx. 350 person-days; the maximum volume is 400 person-days. Upon reaching the maximum volume, the possibility of further call-offs from the framework agreement ends. The estimated call-off volume does not entail any obligation for the WDR to call off services to this extent. sig_721e0d11269ecb523bcf.description: The procurement to be carried out is classified as an administrative services contract, given that its object consists of performance obligations involving the development of an activity or directed at obtaining a result other than a works contract or supply contract, as established in articles 17 and 25 of Law 9/2017 of 8 November, on Public Sector Contracts (hereinafter, LCSP). In the Canary Islands, GUIRRE is the Canary Islands Waste Information System, an in-house tool of the Department of Ecological Transition and Energy developed to respond to data management in the field of waste and for the communication thereof to the Ministry with competence in the matter. Through the aid proposed in the Sectoral Conference, it is proposed to procure a service to, via GUIRRE:  Improve the exchange of information with eSIR.  Automation and digitalisation of administrative procedures, management and electronic processing of files and databases relating to waste regulations.  Information analysis and data processing. Likewise, the digitalisation of administrative procedures within the competence of the Autonomous Community is sought in order to adapt them to the requirements established in Royal Decree 203/2021 of 30 March, approving the Regulations on the performance and operation of the public sector by electronic means, to guarantee easily usable and accessible digital services, aligned with European interoperability frameworks, and which allow intelligent automation (via Business Process Management and/or Robotic Process Automation) in all or part of them. All of this would lead to:  An improvement in the quality of the public service. Unified management of administrative procedures. Automation and digitalisation of administrative procedures.  Greater ease in the work of professionals.  A monitoring and legality control system.  An electronic administrative management system Said object corresponds to the following codes of the European Commission's Common Procurement Vocabulary (CPV) nomenclature 72200000 Software programming and consulting services 72600000 Computer support and consulting services

sig_7261d10a5ba6062b8177.description: The BWI GmbH is considering awarding a framework agreement for the purchase of unmanned aerial vehicles (referred to as UAVs/drones) onto which magnetometers are loaded for the reconnaissance of mines and ordnance, and the temporally indefinite transfer of associated drone control/planning software, evaluation/ordnance detection software plus the necessary maintenance and support services. In addition, services in the form of further development services (this also includes on-site supervision of troop trials) and training services are required. The framework agreement will be awarded in the amount of 5.068.266,44 EUR (upper limit: 7.602.399,66 EUR) (net) by means of a negotiated procedure with a call for competition pursuant to Section 11 Paragraph 1 Sentence 1 Alt. 2 VSVgV. sig_729b45308c6d2eb6e263.description: Background Arendal municipality has an ongoing need for graphical services connected to information material and visual communication aimed at inhabitants and internal target groups. The municipality produces some material itself, but needs external assistance for assignments that are more complex, time consuming or require special professional competence. The procurement shall ensure access to capacity and relevant competence within graphical design, at the same time as the municipality takes care of the need for uniform visual communication and clear identity. The municipality shall be one sender. It is also important to ensure that material and visual deliveries fulfil the requirements for universal design and ensure accessible and understandable communication for different user groups. The municipality therefore needs to establish a new framework agreement that provides predictable access to graphical assistance as needed, both for smaller ongoing assignments and for major or more strategic deliveries. Description of the assignment The procurement is for graphic services for Arendal municipality. The delivery shall cover the development and production of various types of graphical material and visual elements, including information material, reports, presentations, templates, graphics for digital surfaces, infographics, illustrations and professional design consultancy services. The assignments will vary in extent and complexity. The municipality needs a tenderer who can assist with both smaller, limited assignments and large deliveries that require more planning and close cooperation with the contracting authority. Minor assignments means limited deliveries such as, for example, an ad, poster, presentation or simple illustration. Larger deliveries means assignments that include planning, coordination and multiple sub-services, such as a report or campaign material. The deliveries shall be able to be used further in the municipality ́s own channels and tools, and it is important that the deliveries can be further developed and adapted internally. The framework agreement shall also include the design of profile material and profile articles, as well as graphic materials connected to the use of, among other things, vehicles, buildings and work clothes. Web design for arendal.kommune.no is not included in the procurement. It is important to have clear contact points, effective clarifications and a good understanding of the municipality ́s graphical profile, communication needs and targets for clear, available and recognisable communication.
sig_729b45308c6d2eb6e263.title: Graphic services

sig_72fc7eb88055e268874c.description: Government and the nation face a talent shortfall in artificial intelligence (AI) and cybersecurity. The CyberAICorps Scholarship for Service ( CyberAI SFS ) program welcomes proposals that address AI and cybersecurity education and workforce development. CyberAI refers to using AI in cybersecurity as well as providing security and resilience for AI systems. The Scholarship Track provides funding to establish, or to continue, scholarship for service programs with integrated AI and cybersecurity components (CyberAI). Scholarship recipients must be U.S. citizens or lawful permanent residents and work after graduation in the AI or cybersecurity mission of a government organization for a period of at least the length of the scholarship. The Innovation Track supports projects that enhance preparation of AI and/or cybersecurity professionals. Projects may expand existing educational opportunities, curricula, degree programs, educational pathways, methods and interventions, and partnerships among institutions of higher education, government, and employers. Two statutes authorize this program: 15 USC §7442 (cybersecurity) and 42 USC §18993 (AI). CyberAI SFS aligns with the Executive Order 14277 to prioritize AI within scholarship for service programs. CyberAI is managed by NSF’s Directorate for STEM Education in collaboration with the U.S. Office of Personnel Management (OPM) and U.S. Department of Homeland Security (DHS).
sig_72fc7eb88055e268874c.title: Artificial Intelligence and Cybersecurity Education Innovation and Scholarship for Service (CyberAI SFS)

sig_7301433f6d2a0ac4a43d.description: This Notice of Funding Opportunity (NOFO) invites exploratory grant applications, hereafter referred to as the Novel Experiential Technologies Assisting Individual learning Hubs or NExT AI Hubs (formerly Learning Disabilities Innovation Hubs), to address the impact of Artificial Intelligence (AI) technologies on developmental outcomes in children diagnosed with or at risk for developing a specific learning disability (SLD) impacting reading, writing, and mathematics. NExT AI Hubs include a single Research Project and a Leadership Core that support the goals and aims of the Hub. This NOFO seeks to serve as a catalyst to 1) speed the maturation of nascent/novel, high-impact, high-risk research that advances understanding of the role AI technology plays in supporting, improving, or limiting the learning, cognitive, and socio-emotional needs of children at risk for or diagnosed with SLDs, 2) build an evidence base for the SLD community to inform policy or practice, and 3) provide project-embedded, career-enhancing research and professional development opportunities to support the next generation of transdisciplinary SLD scientists. This initiative provides opportunities to support planning and building a body of research and corresponding intellectual infrastructure to enable NExT AI investigators to compete for large research and program project opportunities in the future.This NOFO aims to integrate research topics that are of relevance to various research programs at the Eunice Kennedy Shriver National Institute of Child Health and Human Development (NICHD) and align with the NICHD Strategic Plan. The NOFO intends to build cross-programmatic, transdisciplinary and cross-cutting scientific research, and critically nurture the development of early career investigators capable of conducting this research.
sig_7301433f6d2a0ac4a43d.title: Novel Experiential Technologies Assisting Individual Learning (NExT AI) Hubs (P20 Clinical Trial Optional)
