sig_73d5b9dfde12629efcc1.description: COMBINED SYNOPSIS/SOLICITATION Solicitation Number: 7571MN26R00052 (Previous Solicitation was 7571MN26R00026) This is a combined synopsis/solicitation for commercial products prepared in accordance with the format in subpart 12.6, as supplemented with additional information included in this notice. This announcement constitutes the only solicitation; proposals are being requested and a written solicitation will not be issued. The solicitation number is 7571MN26R00052. This solicitation is issued as a Request for Proposals (RFP). The solicitation document and incorporated provisions and clauses are those in effect through Federal Acquisition Circular (FAC) 2026-01. QUESTIONS Questions regarding this solicitation shall be submitted in writing to the Contracting Officer at Chaunda.Stewart@hhs.gov no later than September 16, 2026 at 5:00pm Eastern Time (ET). No faxes or phone calls please. Questions received after this deadline will not receive a response. PROPOSALS The proposals must be submitted no later than September 25, 2026 at 12:00 pm Eastern Time (ET). The offeror shall submit four (4) separate volumes in electronic versions in portable document format (PDF) format of the technical proposal (Volume I), the business/cost proposals (Volume II), past performance (Volume III) and technical proposal demo of web portal (Volume IV) to the Government. Late proposals will not be accepted. AMENDMENTS The Government may issue amendments to this solicitation. Offerors shall acknowledge receipt of all amendments in accordance with the instructions provided in each amendment. Any amendment to this solicitation will be posted to SAM.gov. Offerors are responsible for monitoring SAM.gov for amendments, updates, and other information concerning this solicitation. NAICS The North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) code for this acquisition: NAICS Code (Primary): 423450 – Medical, Dental, and Hospital Equipment and Supplies Merchant Wholesalers NAICS Code (Secondary): 424210 – Drugs and Druggists’ Sundries Merchant Wholesalers PURPOSE The purpose of this contract is to acquire medications, vaccines and medical supplies (MVMS) for Federal Occupational Health (FOH) locations through a nationwide, contractor managed web-based ordering portal to support the Program Support Center under the Department of Health and Human Services. This contract aims to consolidate operations, offering a more convenient, reliable and cost-effective approach to MVMS procurement. Additionally, the contract will enhance FOH’s ability to maintain comprehensive oversight of MVMS procurement activities. This requirement is a commercial service and will utilize FAR Part 12/15, as supplemented. The Government intends to issue a single award for a period not to exceed five (5) years. BACKGROUND Federal Occupational Health (FOH) improves the health, safety, and productivity of the federal workforce. As the largest provider of occupational health services in the federal government, FOH supports more than 300 federal entities and over one million federal employees nationwide, including the District of Columbia and U.S. Territories. FOH delivers comprehensive occupational health services and consultation through Interagency Agreements (IAAs) with federal departments and agencies at the national, regional, and local levels. Services range from core occupational health and safety programs to structured clinical, wellness, behavioral health, and environmental health solutions. FOH retains sole responsibility for consulting with customer agencies, while the contractor facilitates delivery of services outlined in the Performance Work Statement (PWS) as well as the solicitation found in the attachments section. FOH sets the standard for promoting a culture of health and safety across the federal workforce. Program effectiveness depends on the expertise and performance of contractor-managed operations, including procurement of Medications, Vaccines and Medical Supplies (MVMS). Historically, FOH has sourced MVMS from multiple vendors, including the Program Support Center’s fulfillment center. This contract will consolidate MVMS procurement into a more efficient, reliable, and cost-effective model; reduce reliance on government purchase cards and unstable supply chains; and strengthen FOH oversight of procurement activities. Please ensure all documents attached to this solicitation are read throughly.
sig_73d5b9dfde12629efcc1.title: Federal Occupational Health - Medications, Vaccines, and Medical Supplies (MVMS)

Part 1) - Procurement of technologies for server rooms The subject matter of this part of the public contract is the comprehensive supply, expert implementation and subsequent commissioning of a complete technological solution for the expansion and supplementation of the existing data centre infrastructure, both physically and technologically. sig_74c799560328d6793623.description: Nest is seeking to appoint one supplier to provide, implement and support one hosted software-as-a-service solution for Nest Invest, comprising two mandatory capabilities: Asset Allocation and Total Portfolio View. The Asset Allocation capability must support Nest Invest’s multi-level fund-of-funds structure and its controlled, model-driven asset allocation process. This includes strategic and tactical asset allocation, portfolio modelling and optimisation, configurable targets, limits and tolerances, portfolio rebalancing, asset restrictions, workflow and approval controls, auditability, scenario analysis and the generation of implementation instructions or outputs for downstream parties. The Total Portfolio View capability must provide a consolidated view of Nest Invest’s portfolio across public and private assets, including positions, exposures, performance and look-through information where available. It must support aggregation and analysis across Nest Invest’s fund structure. The supplier will be required to provide software licensing or subscription services; implementation and configuration; integration with retained data sources and Nest Invest’s planned cloud data platform through appropriate data interfaces and APIs; transition and migration from the incumbent IRP solution; testing and user acceptance support; training and documentation; go-live and transition support; and ongoing hosting, maintenance, technical support and product-roadmap services. The solution must be configured for Nest Invest and supplied electronically as a hosted service. Investment and portfolio data will be received from retained sources, including the fund administrator and custodian, and the solution must generate the required information, reporting and implementation outputs for Nest Invest and its downstream processes. The contract will be awarded to one supplier for an initial term of five years. Nest may extend the contract for an additional two years and subsequently for a further one year, giving a maximum potential term of eight years. The contract does not guarantee any minimum volume of services or minimum expenditure. Lot 1: . None

sig_74e3de4dc80f2cd9b72c.description: The Defense Counterintelligence and Security Agency (DCSA) Innovation Gateway is a competitive solicitation that will result in the award of prototype projects under Other Transaction Agreements (OTA). It is our commercially-focused front door for innovators. Our goal is simple: to partner with creative companies to solve our most critical mission challenges. Innovation Gateway Process The Innovation Gateway is a general announcement of DCSA’s general areas of interest (Digital Transformation Enablement, Data Integration and Advanced Analytics, Cyber and Industrial Security, Digital Workforce and Governance). The general soliciation includes criteria for selecting Solution Concept Papers and soliciting the participation of all proposers capable of satisfying the Government’s needs. Proposal requests will be issued via ‘Innovation Calls’ that are published separately under the DCSA Innovation Gateway at various times during the open period of this solicitation. Innovation Calls will be published via Sam.gov through separate solicitation postings referencing the DCSA Innovation Gateway. Proposers are required to use the Solution Concept Paper Template (DCSA Innovation Gateway Attachment 1) to submit their solutions. The Government will only accept proposals in response to Innovation Calls. Unsolicited proposals that are not in response to an Innovation Call will not be reviewed by the Government. sig_75a3dfeacef639c5452e.description: ***SUMMARY ONLY - SEE ATTACHED COMBINED SYNOPSIS/SOLICITATION DOCUMENT FOR FULL DETAIL*** APS _ Combined Synopsis/Solicitation Brief: Combined Synopsis/Solicitation for Commercial Items Agile Professional Services ("APS”) Department of the Army Project Name: Agile Professional Services ("APS") Solicitation Number: W900KK-26-R-A023 NAICS Code: 541990 (All Other Professional, Scientific, and Technical Services) Set-Aside: Total Small Business Set-Aside Contract Type: Labor Hours/T&M 1. General Information This combined synopsis/solicitation is issued by Army Contracting Command - APG - Orlando Division to procure Agile Professional Services ("APS"). The acquisition is structured to support critical technical and professional operations under a flexible framework, to be proposed and developed by the successful offeror. Key acquisition parameters include: • Set-Aside Status: 100% Total Small Business Set-Aside. • Small Business Size Standard: $19.5M as defined by SBA regulations. • Primary NAICS Classification: 541990 — All Other Professional, Scientific, and Technical Services. • Contract Vehicle Type: Labor Hours/T&M 2. Solicitation Details This announcement constitutes the only solicitation; proposals are being requested and a written solicitation will not be issued. This combined synopsis/solicitation is prepared in accordance with the format in FAR Subpart 12.6, as supplemented with additional information included in this notice. The solicitation document and incorporated provisions and clauses are those in effect through Federal Acquisition Circular FAC 2025-06, effective August 27, 2025.and DFARS Publication Notice (DPN) July 2, 2026. As described in the attached FAR 52.212-2, The Army will adopt aspects of FAR Part 15 evaluation procedures. Considering the novel, and commercial, nature of these services this is deemed necessary to balance fairness, transparency, and competition with the interests of expediency and flexibility 3. Description of Requirement CPE ST3 has a need for Agile Professional Services (APS) support services to provide the organization with the ability to augment its Military and Government Civilian workforce in order to execute its mission. The services will be limited to providing professional support services, under a Performance Based Services model, to CPE ST3 and CPE ST3 customers for limited requirements which are related to CPE ST3’s mission. Since its inception, CPE ST3 has relied on contractor support to conduct its mission in all phases of life cycle management due to insufficient personnel within the organization to successfully perform the required services. This model of a Government footprint with a scalable contractor workforce has enabled CPE ST3 to be very flexible and agile in its mission to support the changing needs of the Army. The services to be performed will include related activities in support of all aspects of providing responsive integrated and interoperable infrastructure for simulation, training, testing, and threat solutions. APS support services are required for effective, efficient, and responsive full lifecycle management of efforts to include, but not limited to: vision statements and doctrine, development of architectures, program support (e.g., acquisition and budget planning, business and financial programming and execution, modeling, simulation, simulator, training device, and instrumentation development, documentation, fielding and execution, system analysis and integration, integrated logistics support, strategic planning, contingency and mission support, security cooperation/international relations, program oversight, independent verification validation and test evaluation, prototype development, sustainment and operations, and analysis of emerging technologies support), and subject matter experts on military tactics, techniques, and procedures. Potential areas of growth are envisioned but not limited to be in the areas of Cyber and Information Warfare, Robotics, Unmanned Vehicles, Home Station Training, Multi-Sensory Simulation, Artificial Intelligence, Hypersonics, Directed Energy, Electronic Warfare, Autonomous Systems, Multi-Domain Integration, Target and Threat Systems, Environment Modeling, Human Performance Training, Security Cooperation, Nuclear Engineering, and Medical Training. The critical performance requirement is the successful development and transition of CPE ST3 from a traditional, staffing-based support model to a task-based, outcome-driven Agile delivery framework that is to be developed by the Performer. Success will be measured by the contractor's ability to develop and iterate, through performance under the resultant contract, a framework that both provides the following, and is able to be replicated across future requirements. 4. Period of Performance / Performance Locations: Total Performance Period shall not exceed 66-months: • Base Period – (15-Feb-27 to 14-Aug-27) Agile Development and Transition In • Option Period 1 – (15-Aug-27 to 14-Aug-28) – Enterprise Performance • Option Period 2 – (15-Aug-28 to 14-Aug-29) – Enterprise Performance • Option Period 3 – (15-Aug-29 to 14-Aug-30) – Enterprise Performance • Option Period 4 – (15-Aug-30 to 14-Aug-31) – Enterprise Performance • Option Period 5 – (15-Aug-31 to 14-Feb-32) – Enterprise Performance and Transition Out • Option Period 6 – (15-Feb-32 to 14-Aug-32) – Option to Extend the Term of Service under FAR 52.217-8 * Work will be performed at Government facilities, Contractor facilities, and Remote locations. Primary Government sites include Orlando, FL, and Redstone Arsenal, AL (including 24/7 operations). Additional Government sites include: Fort Campbell, KY; Fort Hood, TX; Fort Drum, NY; Fort Irwin, CA; Fort Polk, LA; Fort Rucker, AL; Fort Bragg, NC; Hohenfels, Germany; and Camp Humphreys, South Korea. 5. Applicable FAR Provisions/Provisions: See Attachment 7. The provisions and clauses apply to this acquisition and are incorporated by reference or full text as applicable. The full text of the FAR and DFARS clauses may be accessed electronically at https://www.acquisition.gov/. 6. sig_75c0fa08c21be15707ca.description: The present single-supplier framework agreement with call-off orders has as its object the supply, installation, parameterisation, commissioning and maintenance of an Automatic Incident Detection (AID) software solution for the tunnels of ASF, COFIROUTE and ESCOTA. The contract, which involves the establishment of a single-supplier framework agreement with call-off orders, with a maximum value, concerns the supply, integration, parameterisation, commissioning and maintenance of an Automatic Incident Detection (AID) solution for motorway tunnels, including software, associated IT infrastructures, and support and maintenance services. The supply of the AID solution includes the software, as well as the servers necessary for its operation. The integration services include the installation of the solution within the contracting authority's information systems in accordance with the expressed security requirements. The parameterisation services include the adaptation of the software to the technical characteristics of each tunnel in order to achieve the required performance, as well as the execution of tests, possibly at night. The commissioning services include putting into production and transferring the operation of the AID to the contracting authority's teams. The maintenance services include software maintenance to be carried out during the term of the framework agreement, as well as support services. The supply of cameras is not included in this framework agreement. By way of indication, for all motorway companies, the average requirement is estimated at 15 tunnels representing 300 cameras to be connected to the AID solution.
sig_75c0fa08c21be15707ca.title: Call-off framework agreement for the supply, implementation and maintenance of an Automatic Incident Detection (AID) software solution for tunnels

sig_75cb8027dd0a372677f1.description: The Universiteit van Amsterdam (UvA) and the Amsterdam University of Applied Sciences (HvA) intend to jointly procure a new Document Management System (DMS) to replace the current DMS. The aim of the procurement is to contract a future-proof, secure and user-friendly DMS solution that supports the UvA and HvA in the sustainable management, making accessible and archiving of digital documents and files. The contract includes, among other things, the supply of the DMS solution, implementation and configuration, migration of existing documents, metadata and files, integrations with the existing IT environment, training and knowledge transfer, management, maintenance, support and further development. The offered solution must connect to the existing information provision of the UvA and HvA and, among other things, provide support for document and file management, metadata, workflows, authorization, retention periods, archiving, destruction, searching, audit trail and integrations with the existing Microsoft 365 environment. In addition to the quality of the offered solution and services, the evaluation will look at the implementation and migration approach, future-proofing, security and compliance, and user experience, adoption and self-reliance. The price also forms part of the evaluation. As part of the award procedure, mandatory demonstrations will be organised in which tenderers demonstrate the offered solution on the basis of various practical situations. The contract will be awarded to the tenderer with the economically most advantageous tender based on the best price-quality ratio (BPKV).
sig_75cb8027dd0a372677f1.title: Vervanging Document Management Systeem (DMS)

sig_762ba23d57fff125fa3e.description: PRE-SOLICITATION NOTICE TO NEGOTIATE ON A SOLE SOURCE BASIS The Office of Acquisition and Agreements Management (OAAM), Acquisition Management Division (AMD), of the National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST), on behalf of the NIST Material Measurement Laboratory (MML), intends to negotiate on a sole source basis with Grenova, Inc. (formerly Peak Analysis and Automation, Inc.), 1900 Ellen Road, Richmond, VA 23230-4213 (UEI: XSCGMEZKBZB9), for the acquisition of a new Living Measurement Systems Foundry (LMSF) automation system and equipment necessary to modernize the existing Government-owned LMSF automation system. NIST requires a complete, integrated laboratory automation solution to expand the capabilities of the existing LMSF. The Contractor shall furnish one new LMSF automation system capable of supporting automated microbial culture, sample preparation, and analytical workflows. The system shall include all required laboratory instrumentation, robotic liquid handling equipment, robotics, automated plate handling and storage equipment, biological containment equipment, computers, software, firmware, licenses, accessories, and other components necessary to provide a complete and fully operational automation system. The Contractor shall also furnish a new Hamilton Company MicroLab STAR liquid handling platform and all associated hardware, software, firmware, licenses, and integration components necessary to modernize the existing Government-owned LMSF. The replacement platform shall be integrated with the remaining Government-owned equipment while preserving the existing system's automation functionality, software operation, laboratory workflows, operating parameters, and measurement methodologies. As part of furnishing the new and modernized LMSF automation systems, the Contractor shall provide all necessary system design, configuration, integration, programming, Factory Acceptance Testing (FAT), delivery, installation, Site Acceptance Testing (SAT), commissioning, documentation, operator training, and warranty support necessary to provide NIST with complete and operational systems. The anticipated acquisition will be Firm-Fixed-Price and will consist of an eighteen (18)-month base period for delivery, integration, installation, testing, training, and acceptance of the new and modernized LMSF automation systems. The acquisition is also anticipated to include three (3) one-year option periods for maintenance and support following expiration of the applicable warranty periods. Sole source determination is based on the following: NIST's minimum requirement is not simply for commercially available laboratory instrumentation. The Government requires a second LMSF automation system that functions as a measurement-equivalent and interoperable automation platform with the existing LMSF. The new and modernized systems must preserve compatibility with existing laboratory workflows, automation routines, software functionality, operating parameters, and measurement methodologies. Grenova, Inc. (formerly Peak Analysis and Automation, Inc.) designed, integrated, delivered, installed, and commissioned the Government's existing LMSF automation system and has subsequently provided maintenance, technical support, and system upgrades. As the original system integrator, Grenova possesses unique knowledge of the existing LMSF system architecture, hardware and software integration, automation programming, equipment interfaces, control strategies, and operational characteristics. NIST has operated and characterized the existing LMSF for approximately eight years. During this period, NIST has quantified contributions to measurement uncertainty associated with robotic manipulation, liquid transfers, incubation, spectrophotometric measurements, and other automated operations. The Government therefore requires the second system to reproduce the operational characteristics of the existing LMSF sufficiently to permit the two systems to function as interchangeable measurement systems without introducing unacceptable differences in measurement performance. The modernization of the existing LMSF requires replacement of the currently integrated Hamilton MicroLab STAR liquid handling platform while maintaining the functionality of the remaining Government-owned automation system. Successful modernization requires integration of the replacement equipment with existing robotics and instrumentation and migration or preservation of applicable automation software, configuration files, control logic, drivers, communication settings, automation routines, and operational parameters. The original LMSF was acquired under Contract No. SB134118SU0017. The original contract did not include FAR clause 52.227-14 or otherwise establish Government rights to use technical data, including designs developed under the award. Consequently, it is unclear to what extent the Government may use the original system's hardware and software designs, integration information, automation routines, and related technical information to enable another source to reproduce the existing LMSF design. Market research indicates that Grenova is the only known source capable of furnishing the complete requirement, including a functionally equivalent LMSF automation system, the equipment and integration necessary to modernize the existing Government-owned LMSF, and follow-on support for both systems. Acquisition from another source is expected to result in substantial duplication of cost and unacceptable delays associated with redevelopment, integration, testing, requalification, and validation of an alternative system. The North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) code for this acquisition is 334516 – Analytical Laboratory Instrument Manufacturing, with a small business size standard of 1,000 employees. No solicitation package will be issued. This Notice of Intent is not a request for competitive quotations; however, responsible sources that believe they can satisfy the Government's requirements may submit a written capability statement demonstrating their ability to furnish the complete requirement. Capability statements shall specifically address the respondent's ability to: Furnish a complete laboratory automation system incorporating robotic liquid handling equipment, laboratory instrumentation, robotics, automated plate handling, automation software, and biological containment equipment; Furnish and integrate equipment manufactured by multiple Original Equipment Manufacturers (OEMs) into a unified laboratory automation system; Furnish a system capable of operating interoperably with the Government's existing LMSF while preserving or reproducing existing automation routines, software functionality, operating parameters, laboratory workflows, and measurement methodologies; Furnish and integrate a replacement Hamilton Company MicroLab STAR liquid handling platform into the existing Government-owned LMSF while preserving the functionality and performance of the remaining system; and Provide the warranty, maintenance, replacement parts, software support, and technical support necessary to sustain both LMSF automation systems. Respondents shall identify any Government-furnished technical data, system design information, software, interface documentation, proprietary information, licenses, or other information that would be required for the respondent to furnish a system satisfying the Government's requirements. Responses must be received by September 24, 2026. A determination by the Government not to compete the proposed acquisition based upon responses to this notice is solely within the discretion of the Government. Information received will normally be considered solely for the purpose of determining whether to conduct a competitive procurement.

sig_76b65243e3cf6f2cefb5.description: Huoltovarmuuskeskus invites market operators interested in the procurement to respond to a request for information and to register for the market dialogue. The subject of the procurement is an on-premises project portfolio tool that enables the management of programme and project activities. The objective of the procurement is to tender for software that: • supports current and developing project portfolio and programme management, and • reduces the amount of manual work related to processes and reporting. • The system solution to be procured and the supplier's operations must meet the security requirements for security-classified information. • In addition, the system also supports the work of an external project manager during the project planning, implementation, monitoring and closing phases. The aim is, in principle, to procure off-the-shelf software that can be configured according to the requirements and needs of HVK. REQUEST FOR INFORMATION AND BILATERAL MARKET DIALOGUE SESSIONS With this request for information, Huoltovarmuuskeskus (hereinafter HVK) is launching a market survey for the procurement. The purpose of the request for information is to identify potential market operators, collect information on solution alternatives available on the market, and compile insights regarding the subject of the procurement and its implementation. Furthermore, the goal of the request for information is to collect information from market operators and ensure that the procurement planning is based on the current market situation. In the request for information, service providers are asked to present preliminary alternatives for project implementation models. In addition to the request for information, the contracting authority may, if necessary, organise market dialogue sessions. Bilateral discussions on other matters related to the implementation of the project can also be held during the market dialogue. More detailed descriptions of the subject of the procurement, the request for information questions, and instructions can be found as an attachment to this notice. INSTRUCTIONS FOR RESPONDING TO THE REQUEST FOR INFORMATION We ask market operators to: a) Respond to the questions in the attached questionnaire in a free-form manner no later than 21.1.2026 at 16. - Message subject/heading: "Huoltovarmuuskeskus/ project portfolio - Request for information" - Responses are to be sent by email to anni.partanen@kpmg.fi b) In connection with responding, the market operator may register for a more detailed market dialogue session to be held via Teams. MARKET DIALOGUE The contracting authority reserves the right to organise an oral market dialogue session and the possibility to limit the number of candidates invited to the oral market dialogue section. The session requires the signing of a non-disclosure agreement. Potential market dialogue sessions will be held via Teams on 28.1.2026. The estimated duration of the session is 60-90 minutes. The contracting authority reserves the right to change and refine the schedule. Supplier-specific market dialogue invitations will be delivered to the registered market operators after the deadline for the request for information. The discussions will be held in Finnish. Participation in the market dialogue is not a condition for participating in the procurement process to be carried out later.
sig_76b65243e3cf6f2cefb5.title: REQUEST FOR INFORMATION: Procurement of a project portfolio as an On-Premises solution

sig_76e8b1f0b3f7be62f9f4.description: The subject of the contract is the design, development and operation of an event- and user-based RMV-KombiTicket system as Software as a Service (SaaS). The system is used for the issuance and management of public transport travel authorisations in conjunction with event and service tickets. It includes, in particular, web access for RMV administrators, a web app and the appropriate interfaces for connecting event organisers and ticketing service providers. The RMV-KombiTicket is to be provided as HandyTicket-Mobil, HandyTicket-Wallet and Print@Home-Ticket. Users must be able to retrieve a successfully issued RMV-KombiTicket in all three ticket forms and use it as a valid travel authorisation. Issuance must be enabled both through direct retrieval by the event organiser and through personalisation and activation by the user. In addition, a procedure for the provision and distribution of event codes without a direct interface connection must be provided. The system must support the user roles of user, event organiser, ticketing service provider and RMV, each with appropriate functions and authorisations. In addition to the technical implementation, the contractor shall assume responsibility for the secure, reliable and permanently available operation of the RMV-KombiTicket system, including the associated services.
sig_76e8b1f0b3f7be62f9f4.title: RMV-KombiTicketsystem (Wallet, Mobil und Print@Home)

sig_76efaff15002776a3b58.description: Banedanmark expects to publish the tender for acquiring a solution to monitor and diagnosing railway telecommunications and signalling systems in Spring 2026. To be sure that the process for tender and the contract is aligned with the capabilities of the market, Banedanmark wishes to invite potential vendors for a written market dialogue and verbal hearing regarding the upcoming tender for acquiring a solution to monitor and diagnose railway telecommunications and signalling systems. The purpose of the market dialogue is to get the markets feedback on the scope and if it is aligned with the market regarding the composition of the products/services, the commercial conditions, the price structure, market conditions, risks, and the partnership after having entered the contract etc. In that way Banedanmark will be able to optimize the tender material accordingly to how the market is today before making the tender public. The market dialogue process is the following: Banedanmark has attached an appendix to this document, which Banedanmark request the potential vendors to answer and return via EU-Supply. - Appendix 1 Questionnaire and answers (Potential vendors must fill out this document). The potential vendors must return their answers through EU-Supply not later than 05.12.2025 Depending on the answer’s Banedanmark will have the option to invite potential vendors to a digital meeting via Microsoft Teams. The selection of potential vendors to the meeting will be done through the criteria, to secure a representative of the market, to discuss the answers and possible implications. The topics in Appendix 1 will provide the initial questions for the market dialogue. If the potential vendors are invited for a meeting and find it relevant, they are welcome to send any suggestions for other topics that should be discussed during the market dialogue. The digital meeting will be held, if relevant, 11.12.2025 and 12.12.2025. Banedanmark will, with the invite to the digital meeting, send a Teams link. The duration of the meeting is approx. 1,5 hours (CET+1) in the span of 8-16 Thursday (11.12.2025) and 8-12 Friday (12.12.2025). If the potential vendor suggests meeting times/dates, Banedanmark will try to accommodate those requests.

sig_76f807f0b1843e44a55d.description: The subject of the public contract is the supply, installation and commissioning of a complex interactive projection system for shooting training intended for the training of security forces and other authorised users. The system must form a single functional unit enabling the implementation of shooting training using both live weapons and weapons with laser shooting simulation. The system includes, in particular, projection technology, hit detection equipment, control and evaluation software, audiovisual and communication equipment, as well as all related technical and safety elements necessary for operation in a shooting range environment. The system must allow for the projection of static and dynamic shooting scenarios, real-time hit evaluation, archiving and subsequent analysis of shooting progress, and support for the creation and editing of custom training scenarios by the user. The delivery also includes complete integration into the shooting range area, including the installation, calibration and commissioning of all components, the supply of necessary hardware and software equipment, the provision of safety measures and protection of technologies against the effects of shooting, as well as the supply of related accessories for the implementation of training. Work of Education Welfare Team, penalty notices, Exclusions, AP, EOTAS, Elective home education, Entertainment Licences and chaperones • Children's Centres (Hubs) – capturing activity data across Family Hubs within the Borough and reporting. • EIS – Case Management – providing flexible case management functionality to support workflows, referrals, tasks, alerts, contacts, chronology, document management, correspondence, assessments, outcomes, audit trails and reporting. sig_772ae379ef76d578b1d6.description: The subject of the public contract is the replacement (dismantling) of existing radio water meters for hot and cold water (hereinafter referred to as "hot water" and "cold water") with the supply and installation of new water meters with remote data reading, including the provision of monthly consumption information. The water meters will be fitted to water distribution systems in installation shafts of residential and non-residential units. Consumption values will be activated via a portal service (data bus) and access to the customer portal will be provided, which will supply monthly consumption information for individual service recipients in accordance with applicable legislation. Furthermore, the replacement of heat cost allocators (hereinafter referred to as "heat cost allocators") with the supply and installation of new meters with remote data reading, including the provision of monthly consumption information and apportionment services in residential buildings in the Contracting Authority's territory. The meters will be fitted to heating elements in individual flats and non-residential premises, or in the case of heat meters on central heating pipes. This public contract also includes the provision of services defined by the terms of the agreement on reading and apportionment services in accordance with Act No. 67/2013 Coll., an Act regulating certain issues related to the provision of supplies associated with the use of flats and non-residential premises in a building with flats, as amended, and in accordance with Decree No. 269/2015 Coll., on cost apportionment as amended. The agreement on reading and apportionment services will be concluded for a period of 10 years (cycle of radio modules and buses), a binding draft of which forms Annex No. 5 of the tender documentation. Before commencing implementation, it is necessary to contact the technician of the housing and other management department, who will specify which of the residential units will be vacant during implementation (will hand over keys), and which residential units and premises will be used by tenants during implementation. The selected supplier (contractor) shall notify tenants one week before the commencement of work that the existing radio meters will be replaced with meters featuring remote data reading. The notification shall be made in the form of written information placed in a visible location (lift, main door, notice board). The subject of performance is described in detail in the specification of the subject of performance, which forms Annex No. 3 of the tender documentation.

sig_7742494ace2653389dea.description: U.S. Customs and Border Protection (CBP), Laboratories and Scientific Services (LSS), intends to issue a purchase order to Orange Photonics, 176 Newport Road, New London, NH 03257, on a sole source basis for the purchase of two (2) portable cannabis analyzers for use in laboratory and field settings. The analyzers will support rapid screening and triage of drug seizures, commodities, and potentially violative items by assisting with the detection and identification of cannabinoids and determining the relative dry weight amounts of detected cannabinoids. The required analyzers shall be human-portable, self-contained, capable of analyzing samples in under 20 minutes, able to store analysis data onboard, and able to transfer data files and results to a USB flash drive. The requirement includes inside delivery, setup, initial software configuration, in-person training, hard-sided carrying cases, and accessories and consumables needed to conduct 200 scans/analyses, 100 per unit. All deliverables, including setup and training, shall be completed within 30-60 calendar days after the date of contract award. This notice is neither a request for proposals nor an invitation for bids. The Sole Source Justification will be posted in accordance with Revolutionary FAR Overhaul (RFO) 12.102(a). All interested parties must express their interest and capabilities in writing via email to wymeatric.l.lyons@cbp.dhs.gov prior to the closing date of this notice. Verification of receipt of responses is the sole responsibility of the interested party. If no responses are received by September 23, 2026, at 3:00 PM ET, a written quotation will be requested from Orange Photonics, and award will be made accordingly. sig_7795d029695c27bc2a5f.description: The subject of the public contract is the renewal of the network packet broker technology. Packet broker technology ensures the centralisation and optimisation of network traffic management for cyber security tools, thereby enabling effective security analysis. It fundamentally improves network visibility (visualisation maps) and protection against cyber threats. The packet broker thus essentially functions as an intelligent "router" of network data, which ensures that security tools receive precisely the data they need, in the correct format and in the required volume. The use of this technology effectively reduces licensing costs for security technologies (XDR, SIEM) by allowing only relevant traffic into these tools and eliminating duplicate data. The subject of this public contract therefore includes: a) Ensuring HW and packet broker technology licences according to the requirements of the technical specification. b) Ensuring support for the supplied packet broker technology for a period of 36 months. c) Ensuring consultations during migration up to a maximum extent of 10 man-days (MD)
sig_7795d029695c27bc2a5f.title: Technological renewal of the MHMP network packet broker

Procedure aimed at concluding a framework agreement 3 in parts for Visit Hungary Nemzeti Turisztikai Szervezet Közhasznú Nonprofit Zrt. for the performance of strategic media agency, digital media agency and market research tasks. In order to achieve the Contracting Authority's communication objectives, the Contracting Authority plans to implement complex communication and media campaigns on domestic and foreign target markets. The aim of the Contracting Authority's communication activity is to promote Hungary for tourism purposes, strengthen inbound tourism from abroad, stimulate domestic tourism, and present the Hungarian tourism offering domestically and internationally. The task of the Winning Tenderer is to perform the tasks specified in the Technical Specification for the Client on the basis of the framework agreement, individual orders, and briefs handed over by the Client. The Contracting Authority wishes to conclude a framework agreement for the performance of strategic media agency tasks up to a net framework amount of 3.200.000.000 HUF. The Contracting Authority undertakes an obligation to call off 70% of the framework amount. In order to achieve the Contracting Authority's communication objectives, the Contracting Authority plans to implement complex communication and media campaigns on domestic and foreign target markets. International tourism advertising campaigns may be implemented in multiple countries, with a different media mix and target group approach per country. The task of the Winning Tenderer is to perform strategic media agency, media planning, media buying, campaign management, reporting, and other auxiliary tasks directly related to media appearances for the Client on the basis of the framework agreement, individual orders, and briefs handed over by the Client. The exact professional content, performance deadline, quantity, technical parameters and individual expectations of the tasks are contained in the individual orders. The Contracting Authority's domestic campaigns are typically implemented with a net campaign spend of the magnitude of 250 million HUF, over an average campaign period of 6–8 weeks. Campaigns of the Contracting Authority affecting target markets outside Hungary are typically implemented with a net campaign spend of the magnitude of 80 million HUF, over an average campaign period of 8–10 weeks. Tasks to be performed in particular: - preparation of a media strategy, integrated media mix and media plan in harmony with the Contracting Authority's communication objectives, - preparation of market, media market, competitor and target group analyses adapted to the campaign's objective, target markets, target groups and channels, - strategic media agency tasks on specified channels - preparation, execution and monitoring of campaigns, campaign management, preparation and execution of media buying tasks, and continuous optimisation of campaigns, - proposal for a KPI system adapted to the nature, objective, channels and target markets of the given campaign, as well as tracking, interpretation and evaluation of campaign performance, with special regard to tourism KPIs - preparation of regular, inter-campaign and campaign-closing reports according to an agreed reporting structure. The Winning Tenderer is obliged to designate one permanent contact person. Detailed requirements set against performance are contained in the technical specification and draft contract.; The Contracting Authority wishes to conclude a framework agreement for the performance of digital media agency tasks up to a net framework amount of 820.000.000 HUF. The Contracting Authority undertakes an obligation to call off 70% of the framework amount. In order to achieve the Contracting Authority's communication objectives, the Contracting Authority plans to implement complex communication and digital media campaigns on domestic and foreign target markets. International tourism digital advertising campaigns may be implemented in multiple countries, with a different digital media mix, targeting logic, platform usage and target group approach per country. The task of the Winning Tenderer is to perform digital media agency, digital media planning, digital media buying, campaign management, optimisation, measurement, analytics, reporting, and other auxiliary tasks directly related to digital media appearances for the CA on the basis of the framework agreement, individual orders, and briefs handed over by the CA. The Contracting Authority's domestic digital campaigns are typically implemented with a net budget of the magnitude of 50–60 million HUF, over an average campaign period of 8–9 weeks. Digital campaigns of the Contracting Authority affecting target markets outside Hungary are typically implemented with a net budget of the magnitude of 50–60 million HUF, over an average campaign period of 8–9 weeks. Tasks to be performed in particular: - formulation of a digital campaign strategy and digital media plan, development of digital targeting, platform and channel proposals, - performance of digital media buying and campaign management tasks, continuous tracking and optimisation of campaign performance, support for measurement and analytical settings, - evaluation and reporting of digital KPIs, (with special regard to tourism relevance) - support for the compilation of performance certification documentation, - preparation of a digital campaign strategy, digital media mix and digital media plan in harmony with the Contracting Authority's communication objectives, - preparation of market, digital media market, competitor and target group analyses adapted to the campaign's objective, target markets, target groups, digital channels and advertising platforms, - performance of media agency tasks on specified channels and platforms, - preparation of digital campaigns, - launching of digital campaigns, campaign management, preparation and execution of digital media buying tasks, and continuous optimisation of campaigns, - establishment, management and operation of an agreed advertising account structure, - support for the establishment, operation and, where necessary, development of the measurement environment related to digital campaigns, - preparation of inter-campaign reports and campaign-closing evaluation. The Winning Tenderer is obliged to designate one permanent contact person. Detailed requirements set against performance are contained in the technical specification and draft contract.;

The Contracting Authority wishes to conclude a framework agreement for the performance of market research tasks up to a net framework amount of 320.000.000 HUF. The CA undertakes an obligation to call off 70% of the framework amount. In order to achieve the Contracting Authority's communication objectives, the CA plans to implement complex communication and media campaigns on domestic and foreign target markets. Research and analysis tasks may also cover domestic and international target markets, different target groups, campaigns, brands, destinations, communication objectives, consumer motivations, media usage characteristics, tourism decisions or campaign effectiveness issues. The CA's research projects are of a mixed nature: they include quantitative research with larger sample sizes directed at Hungary and affecting target markets outside Hungary, primary research affecting multiple target markets, as well as smaller-element qualitative, motivational, service quality, mystery shopping or other decision-supporting research tasks. The Contracting Authority generally performs the implementation of a residential quantitative research of 1000 persons once a year in 10-15 countries, and in addition initiates a minimum of 2 qualitative, small-group focus group researches in Hungary (focus groups are generally implemented with 4–8 groups, with an average participation of 6 persons per group) and manages a nationwide mystery shopping annually with a minimum of 80 trial purchases. The task of the Winning Tenderer is to perform market research, data acquisition, analysis and decision-supporting tasks for the CA on the basis of the framework agreement, individual orders, and briefs handed over by the CA. Tasks to be performed in particular: - preparation, organisation, execution, analysis and documentation of research, data acquisitions, analyses and decision-supporting materials founding, supporting or evaluating marketing and communication activity. - preparation of a research plan or methodological proposal adapted to the given research, data acquisition, analysis or decision-supporting task, - organisation, execution, coordination and control of research data recording, fieldwork or data collection. - processing, checking, cleaning, systematisation, analysis, interpretation of data available as a result of research or data acquisition, and formulation of decision-supporting conclusions, - with the prior approval of the CA, may carry out data purchases, procure syndicated research, or utilise an external data source or study on behalf of the CA, - performing administration related to possible research modifications, data recording changes, cancellations, data purchase or syndicated research limitations, - the Winning Tenderer is obliged to present the results of the given research, data acquisition, analysis or decision-supporting task according to a structure agreed with the Client. The Winning Tenderer is obliged to designate one permanent contact person. Detailed requirements set against performance are contained in the technical specification and draft contract.

sig_77cef8d490f54bd5e1a6.description:
The project comprises the planning and execution of internal audits and security revisions in the area of information security to maintain the information network of the EU Paying Agency Brandenburg-Berlin, which is certified based on BSI IT-Grundschutz in accordance with ISO 27001. The ISO 27001 certification is proof of the Union law eligibility criterion of "security of information systems" of the EU paying agency (Article 1 in conjunction with Annex I point 3 letter B of Delegated Regulation (EU) No 2022/127) and requires the regular execution of internal audits and security revisions in accordance with BSI IT-Grundschutz. Internal personnel resources and competencies for carrying out internal audits are not available, which is why, in accordance with chapter 8.3, BSI standard 200-1, it has been decided to award the execution of the audits to external experts. The previously awarded project with the same project content expires in the year 2026, which is why a multi-year follow-up project is being awarded to ensure continuous and long-term internal auditing until 2030. The subject matter of the project shall be flexibly retrievable auditing services for the information network of the EU paying agency, which consists of the organisational units of the Ministry for Agriculture and Nutrition, Environment and Consumer Protection Brandenburg (MLEUV) and the directly subordinate State Office for Rural Development, Agriculture and Land Consolidation (LELF), as well as the other bodies involved in the paying agency procedure (districts, state forestry enterprise, investment bank and technical service providers), which as outsourcing partners or the components outsourced to them, shall represent the essential audit subjects of the audits. Based on an jointly prepared audit schedule, four audits per year are planned. The project is to be awarded to demonstrably experienced experts in the field of information security revision or ISMS auditing in accordance with BSI IT-Grundschutz. Lot LOT-0001: Internal audits and security revisions to maintain the information security of the EU paying agency in the MLEUV. The contract subject matter comprises the planning and execution of internal audits and security revisions for an information network certified on the basis of BSI IT-Grundschutz in accordance with ISO 27001 and its participating outsourcing partners. The information network to be audited "Operational running of the EU Paying Agency Brandenburg-Berlin" consists of the organisational units of the Ministry for Agriculture and Nutrition, Environment and Consumer Protection of the State of Brandenburg (MLEUV) and the directly subordinate State Office for Rural Development, Agriculture and Land Consolidation (LELF), which perform the professional tasks of approval, control, disbursement, accounting and administration of arrears of subsidy funds of the European Agricultural Guarantee Fund (EAGF), the European Agricultural Fund for Rural Development (EAFRD) and the European Maritime, Fisheries and Aquaculture Fund (EMFAF), as well as the other bodies involved in the paying agency procedure (districts, state forestry enterprise, investment bank and technical service providers), which are treated as outsourcing partners. The essential audit activities are to be carried out for the outsourced components of the information network at the outsourcing partners. With these institutions, a transfer of paying agency tasks has been agreed on the basis of responsibilities ordinances, transfer ordinances or other regulations. Based on a federal-state interface model for EU paying agencies coordinated with the Federal Office for Information Security (BSI for short), the outsourcing relationships are essentially differentiated into: 1. Organisational interfaces (S-O): Institutions that perform transferred tasks of approval and control within the business processes of the paying agency and use central paying agency specialist applications within the information network to fulfil tasks, as they do not provide central paying agency specialist applications themselves and do not operate any specific application environments. In Brandenburg, this currently affects: - 14 approval offices (offices for agriculture) in the districts, - the State Forestry Enterprise (LFB), - the Investment Bank of the State of Brandenburg (ILB). 2. Technical interfaces (S-T): Institutions of the technical operation of the central paying agency specialist applications and systems as well as data storage. In Brandenburg, this currently affects: - the central Brandenburg IT service provider (ZIT-BB), - Land Surveying and Basic Geographic Information Brandenburg (LGB) - init AG for the operation of an application procedure. A medium three-digit number of persons work in the information network. Every year, several million euros in a three-digit amount of EU, federal and state funds are administered. The paying agency specialist applications essentially comprise client/server and web applications, for which an IT system landscape consisting of terminal, web, application and database servers is deployed. Use is made by administrative units using virtual clients via the state administration network of the State of Brandenburg. Applicants access the online application systems operated in a demilitarised zone (DMZ) via the internet. In coordination with the client and based on the documentation of the ISMS, the contractor shall draw up and carry out a multi-year audit schedule. The planning and execution of the audits takes place with the participation of the information security officer of the EU paying agency. Based on empirical values, four audits per year are to be carried out with different procedure participants respectively, which should be flexibly retrievable.

Per audit, the workload in person-days (PD) is estimated at approx. 10 PD. The contract subject matter comprises the audits for the years 2027 up to and including 2030. The client reserves the right, with the award of optional services, if contractor capacities are available, to commission further audits in accordance with the schedule of services for the year 2026. Accordingly, the following scope of work is expected - 2026: 2 audits - 20 PD (optional, upon availability) - 2027: 4 audits - 40 PD - 2028: 4 audits - 40 PD - 2029: 4 audits - 40 PD - 2030: 4 audits - 40 PD - Total: 18 audits - 180 PD The execution of the audits should take place along the relevant standards for audits and security revisions according to the BSI IT-Grundschutz methodology (BSI auditing scheme or the guideline for IS revisions based on IT-Grundschutz). The client reserves the right to optionally commission the contractor in the year 2026 with up to two (2) further audits for two (2) audit subjects in accordance with the schedule of services.
sig_77cef8d490f54bd5e1a6.title: Internal audits and security revisions to maintain the information security of the EU paying agency in the MLEUV

sig_77cfc2e56b98f9c2e2c5.description: With this call for tenders, the Berufsgenossenschaft Verkehrswirtschaft Post-Logistik Telekommunikation intends to conclude a framework agreement for the procurement of services related to M365. Selected professional associations provide IT services jointly or purchase services specifically through one body and subsequently recharge the service internally. This model is also applied to this call for tenders. BG Verkehr, as the contracting party, assumes contract management for a total of three participants. The following are to be audited under the contract to be concluded with BG Verkehr: - BG Verkehr - BG ETEM - BGHW The aforementioned professional associations are entitled to call off from the framework agreement tendered here. The aim is, firstly, the continuous, structured assessment of relevant changes in Microsoft 365 as well as the comprehensible classification of their effects on configuration, security, compliance/data protection, operation and user acceptance in the context of the special role of accident insurance institutions. It should be noted that further SaaS services from Microsoft 365 may be introduced in the future and therefore an evergreen approach with forward-looking assessment, prioritisation and concrete recommendations for action per contract is required. It should also be noted that new functions or changes to already introduced functions may be subject to co-determination by the staff council. Corresponding assessments and recommendations for action must also be provided for this. Secondly, a conformity check of the tenants regarding data protection and compliance is to be carried out at longer intervals (annually). An approximation or alignment of the tenants to a common standard over the term of the contracts is desirable, but cannot be guaranteed to the contractor for the simplification of their activities. For the professional associations as carriers of statutory accident insurance, other regulatory requirements apply in addition to the GDPR, which arise, for example, from the Tenth Book of the Social Code (SGB X). The permanent guarantee of an appropriate level of protection is an essential goal; in addition to internal data, sensitive personal data of insured persons are processed. Further details can be found in the tender documents. The contracting authority and the authorised call-off entities require consulting and support services for the ongoing review of the change notifications issued by Microsoft, combined with usage recommendations and other services (M365 Evergreen Management). Even if the ongoing review of individual changes is carried out with great care, it may be necessary in total to check the resulting operating environments from time to time for compliance with regulatory requirements, as these are also subject to change and can continue to develop. Finally, the contracting authority and the authorised call-off entities require support and advice for this annual review and documentation (M365 Compliance Audit). Against this background, the contracting authority plans to commission a provider of M365 consulting services in the area of evergreen management and compliance audit for a limited period. The framework agreement comes into effect with the award. The contract term is 24 months. The term begins on the first of the month following the award of the contract. The contract is automatically extended after the expiry of 24 months by 12 months each time (extension option), unless the contracting authority terminates the contract in writing at the latest 3 months before the expiry of 24 months or 36 months. The contract ends at the latest after 48 months, without the need for termination. Further details can be found in the tender documents.

sig_7878a26982273c6ddef9.description: The objective of this procurement is to secure a modern, cloud-hosted, configurable off-the-shelf Grant Management System capable of supporting the full grant lifecycle for applicants, assessors, panellists, and Arts Council staff. The solution will provide a secure and accessible digital platform for application management, assessment workflows, award administration, post-award monitoring, reporting, and integration with the Arts Council’s existing Finance Management System. The organisation's strategic preference is for a solution that requires minimal custom development and can be configured using standard platform functionality. The replacement programme will be delivered through a phased implementation approach centred on the successful completion of a Proof of Concept (PoC) using a live Arts Council funding programme. This approach is intended to validate vendor capability, system performance, user experience, and organisational readiness before progressing to full production deployment. The Arts Council is seeking a long-term technology partner capable of delivering a proven solution while supporting a structured, low-risk transition from the existing environment. The new system must support bilingual service delivery (Irish and English), modern digital user experiences, robust security controls, workflow automation, management reporting, and interoperability with current and future finance platforms. The solution should also align with public sector best practice, including cloud-first principles, accessibility requirements, data protection obligations, cybersecurity standards, and emerging NIS2 requirements.

sig_7893b4cf744ecf10e15f.description: GENERAL Fimea has started preparing for the procurement of the Fimea.fi website renewal. Fimea is a central agency under the Ministry of Social Affairs and Health that acts as the licensing and supervisory authority for medicines, medical devices, blood and tissue products, biobanks, and operators in the pharmaceutical sector intended for humans or animals. As part of the preparation of the procurement, the contracting authority is conducting a market dialogue. The actual procurement will be implemented as an open procurement procedure. Please note that this is a market survey notice and not a call for tenders. This market survey notice does not yet request tenders. Participation in the market dialogue is completely voluntary. Participation or non-participation in the market dialogue does not affect a tenderer's opportunities to participate in the procurement procedure to be implemented later. The market dialogue does not oblige anyone to participate in the actual tendering, nor does it exclude anyone from it. PRELIMINARY DESCRIPTION OF THE PROCUREMENT The aim of the procurement is to renew the Fimea.fi website and content management system so that the public site is user-friendly, accessible and supports the management of up-to-date content. The procurement will preliminarily be implemented using a hybrid model consisting of three separate parts: 1. Service design service, expert work • Design of user journeys and concepts • Definition of user interface and information architecture • Visual plan • Architecture description and solution description • Accessibility plan 2. New content management system and website implementation • Ready-to-use content management system (using SaaS model) • Renewed site structure and user interface • Language versions (Finnish, Swedish and English) • Content management features (preview, scheduling, version history) • Integrations and technical interfaces • Accessibility and data protection • Commissioning, training and documentation 3. Maintenance and further development Fixed-price maintenance: • Includes continuous usability of the service, security updates, backups, monitoring and SLA services. • Fixed monthly price for the contract period Hourly-rate minor development: • Includes small changes and additional features according to the agile model. • Invoicing according to actual work at an hourly rate. Both parts will be implemented as a SaaS service, where the supplier is responsible for technical management and continuity. The service design and definition phase as well as the implementation project are preliminarily scheduled for the years Q2/2026 – Q2/2027 and the maintenance and further development phase from Q3/2027 onwards. The website will be renewed at the same time in terms of appearance and structure in a way that better serves users. The basic content of the website will publish text, images and attachments. Contents will also include embedded videos or audio files. Embedded audio/video files are hosted on other services. The contents (articles and podcasts) of the Sic web magazine are intended to be integrated as part of the Fimea.fi entity as part of the website implementation. However, the web magazine will not be brought to the Fimea.fi site as a separate entity. MARKET DIALOGUE The market dialogue is intended for companies interested in tendering, and it includes commenting on preliminary tender documents before the publication of the call for tenders. Written commenting on the tender documents is preliminarily planned to be organised around the turn of January and February 2026. The publication of the actual call for tenders is preliminarily planned for February 2026. The information provided in this notice and in the market dialogue itself is preliminary and may change as the preparation progresses. The announced schedule of the procurement is also preliminary and may change as the preparation of the procurement progresses. Please note that the market survey does not include a question & answer phase. Companies interested in the procurement are requested to register in accordance with the instructions described below. REGISTRATION FOR THE MARKET DIALOGUE Companies interested in the procurement are requested to report their contact details by email to the address kilpailutus@hansel.fi. The registration shall be headed as follows: "Fimea.fi verkkosivu-uudistus – Ilmoittautuminen markkinavuoropuheluun". State in the message the name of your organisation and the email address of the contact person to whom the draft tender documents will be delivered. We request registrations for the market dialogue no later than by 23.1.2026 at 12:00. Hansel Oy acts in a consulting role in the procurement.
sig_7893b4cf744ecf10e15f.title: Invitation to market dialogue: Fimea.fi website renewal

sig_78bbeba7443412408449.description: The subject of the contract is the implementation and maintenance of an Information Security Management System (ISMS) and a SOC, along with training, at the Prof. W. Orłowski Independent Public Clinical Hospital of the Centre of Postgraduate Medical Education in Warsaw, which has been divided into two packages. Package no. 1 - Implementation and maintenance of an Information Security Management System (ISMS) The subject of the contract is the implementation and maintenance for the Contracting Authority of an Information Security Management System (ISMS) compliant with the PN-EN ISO/IEC 27001:2023-08 standard, covering: a) the drawing up of comprehensive ISMS documentation and procedures, including an Information Security Policy, operational procedures and incident response procedures, b) the implementation of the ISMS within the Contracting Authority's structures, together with appropriate technical and organisational configuration guidelines, c) the planning of processes for monitoring the effectiveness of the implemented ISMS and its continuous improvement, d) the provision of training to the Contracting Authority's personnel: e-learning training on the implemented ISMS documentation and raising awareness in the field of cybersecurity (cyber hygiene) — for current and future employees — as well as on-site training for the Contracting Authority's manager. e) the maintenance and improvement of the ISMS for a period from the implementation and formal handover of the ISMS up to 36 months from the date of signing the contract, covering periodic ISMS reviews, the updating of documentation and the risk register, compliance reviews, support during inspections and audits, and recommendations for corrective and improvement actions. A detailed description of the subject of the contract concerning package no. 1 can be found in attachment no. 2 to the SWZ. Package no. 2 - Provision of a Security Operations Centre service (SOC Service) The subject of the contract is the provision of a Security Operations Centre service (hereinafter: SOC Service), covering: a) The SOC Service shall be provided for a period of 36 months from the date of conclusion of the contract (including pre-implementation analysis and commissioning). b) The SOC Service must be performed by an entity providing cybersecurity services that meets the organisational and technical conditions resulting from the Act of 5 July 2018 on the national cybersecurity system, in the wording in force from 3 April 2026 (amended by the Act of 23 January 2026, Journal of Laws of 2026, item 252), and the implementing acts to this Act. c) The SOC Service shall be provided in real time, on a continuous basis, 24 hours a day, 7 days a week, for 365 days a year (24/7/365). d) For the purposes of providing the SOC Service, the Contractor shall provide a SIEM system and an Incident Management System in a service model, on the Contractor's platform or within the Contracting Authority's infrastructure, together with documentation and technical support for the entire duration of the provision of the SOC Service. e) The operational procedures of the SOC Service (incident classification, response scenarios, playbooks) must be consistent with the ISMS documentation being prepared under this procedure, in particular with the major incident management procedure and the logging and monitoring policy. A detailed description of the subject of the contract concerning package no. 2 can be found in attachment no. 3 to the SWZ. The Contracting Authority does not require the submission of evidentiary means regarding the subject matter together with the tender. Information on evidentiary means regarding the parties can be found in Chapter 8 of the Specification of Contract Conditions. A detailed description of the subject of the contract constitutes attachment no. 2 to the SWZ.; A detailed description of the subject of the contract constitutes attachment no. 3 to the SWZ.

sig_78c5b72c81dbabda0bf0.description: Industrial biotechnology offers enormous potential for sustainable growth by replacing fossil raw materials with renewable biological resources, achieving climate targets and strengthening competitiveness. Germany is well positioned in the research and development of bioeconomic products and processes. Previous funding measures by other departments and the federal states show that bioeconomic products and processes can be implemented on a laboratory scale. However, there is a lack of broad implementation of bioeconomic products and processes on an industrial scale. Therefore, to support the transformation of the economy into a sustainable, climate-neutral economic model, the funding programme "Industrial Bioeconomy" was initiated, which started with the entry into force of the "Directive for funding the use and construction of demonstration plants for industrial biotechnology" of 16 December 2020 on 29 December 2020 (BAnz AT 28.12.2020 B2). This funding guideline was superseded by the "Funding guideline for the establishment of an industrial bioeconomy through the further development and scaling of bio-based processes and the establishment of regional innovation clusters" (BAnz AT 27.09.2024 B1), published in the Federal Law Gazette on 27 September 2024. The aim of the programme is to unlock the potential of new bio-based processes for industry and to transfer sustainable products into broad application. In order to reduce the economic and technical risks of development and market launch, the funding is intended to demonstrate the potential of bio-based products and processes at an early stage. Projects are funded that have a high potential for industrial application, the creation of new value creation and new jobs, strengthen the market position of the participating companies and make a relevant contribution to sustainability. sig_78e20f1ffea36bd743b3.description: The National Institute of Allergy and Infectious Diseases (NIAID) seeks to advance its mission by supporting multidisciplinary, consortium-based research using precision systems biology approaches to uncover links among chronic illnesses, infectious diseases and microbiomes. There is an urgent scientific and clinical need to understand the pathways by which infections lead to chronic lifelong health issues or alternatively, how long-term illnesses might predispose or exacerbate acute infections. The objective is to harness cutting-edge technologies along with longitudinal patient cohorts and biobank data for comprehensive analysis of genetic, environmental, and lifestyle factors leading to advances in prevention and treatment strategies for both chronic and infectious diseases. The cutting-edge technologies may include multi-omics, computational modeling, artificial intelligence, organoid-based validation systems, and integration of real-world data, alongside improved access to digital health records and advanced clinical informatics tools. The goal is to generate meaningful insights into disease progression and host-pathogen interactions. Grant authorities that allow NIAID to forecast this opportunity are as follows: Sections 301 and 405 of the Public Health Service Act as amended (42 USC 241 and 284) and under Federal Regulations 42 CFR Part 52 and 2 CFR Part 200.
sig_78e20f1ffea36bd743b3.title: Precision and Systems Biology to Uncover the Link Between Chronic and Infectious Diseases
