sig_7922b435cef825e3fe8f.description: This is a request for information, which is not a prior information notice, a contract notice or a call for tenders. The purpose of the request for information is to survey the market and collect information regarding the subject of the procurement for a future tendering process. Responding to the request for information is not a prerequisite for participating in the tendering process. To ensure the success of the future tendering process, it is important that tenderers provide the contracting authority with the requested information as extensively as possible. This request for information is used to clarify the supply available on the market regarding substitute management systems and suppliers. A substitute management system enables a single centralised service channel for the sudden substitute needs of professionals. With the help of a substitute management system, we want to streamline substitute management processes. The need is to find a modern and user-friendly, off-the-shelf SaaS system intended for the management and coordination of substitutes, as well as for the notification and booking of temporary work shifts. In addition, we want to improve and modernise the user experience of our substitute management systems so that the applicant experience and communication are improved. The systems must be integrable via standard interfaces with, among other things, the client organisation's user information and access rights management service. The objectives of the services are equal accessibility, timeliness and continuity. The goal of the procurement is to move from heavy services to proactive and preventive services, whereby the effectiveness of the services can be improved. We offer system solutions to our clients in the social and health care sector as well as the municipal sector. The scope of the future procurement, the procurement method and the parties will be specified as the preparation of the call for tenders progresses. DESCRIPTION OF THE PROCUREMENT The goal of the procurement is to find a system: - that is an easy-to-use, off-the-shelf SaaS solution - that can be integrated into the client organisation's AD and reporting environment via open interfaces - that is information secure and takes data protection into account - whose supplier has a clear implementation model that includes extensive documentation and guidance for the client and contracting organisation - that can be used on mobile devices and via a browser. In addition to the system procurement, the procurement includes connection interfaces to other systems, licences, a delivery project, maintenance and support for off-the-shelf software, as well as other separately ordered expert services, for example, the planning and implementation of system change and development needs and development projects. The solution must scale to the organisational structures of social and health service organisations and the municipal sector. The implementation of the solution must be based on generally used standards and system-independent interfaces. The solution to be procured must function as part of the existing technical and functional environment. The solution includes at least two separate environments in terms of its functions; production and test/training environments, which are identical in their basic structure. OPERATING ENVIRONMENT The following are descriptions of the operating environments of the organisations related to the request for information, which are requested to be used in describing the functionality and pricing model. Users of the data transmission system are, for example, users from wellbeing services counties and municipal organisations. Users of the information systems are also stakeholders and external users. RESPONDING TO THE REQUEST FOR INFORMATION The request for information must be answered by 25.9.2025 at 12:00. Responding takes place by email to the address hankinnat@istekki.fi. Please head your message as follows: "Markkinavuoropuhelu: Sijaisvälitysjärjestelmä" (Market dialogue: Substitute management system). Responses to the Questions attachment of the request for information must also be submitted with the response. You may also attach, for example, brochures to the response. Based on the responses received, Istekki Oy will select 3–5 suppliers to present their solutions in one-hour Teams meetings. The meeting between the selected respondent, Istekki and the representatives of the clients will be recorded. The information provided at the request for information stage will be treated as confidential. Please indicate in your request for information response which of the times below suit you best: Mon 29.9. at 10 – 11 Mon 29.9. at 13 – 14 Mon 29.9. at 14 – 15 Tue 30.9. at 11 – 12 Tue 30.9. at 12 – 13 Tue 30.9. at 13 – 14 The times will be confirmed supplier-specifically after the response time for the request for information. The tendering service automatically creates deadlines for submitting questions and responding to the request for information. Instead of these deadlines, the deadlines in the request for information document shall be followed.

sig_7930cd76349c9ff07931.description: Shropshire Council is undertaking Preliminary Market Engagement (PME) to understand the current market for digital solutions that support unpaid carers. This engagement will help inform the Council’s future commissioning approach before any decision is made about whether to tender, use an existing compliant route, develop an alternative model, or take no further procurement action. Shropshire Council has an established Unpaid Carer Support offer. Recently this has become an all-age offer supporting Young Carers and Parent Carers. The Unpaid Carers portal will be an online offer which will be available to Unpaid Carers 24/7 throughout the journey of their caring role. We are aware there are a large proportion of people who do not identify as an Unpaid Carer, we envisage the portal will support with that identification and will provide relevant up to date information to support families in a preventative manner. Any proposed solution should offer the following support: Increase the identification recognition and early interventions for unpaid Carers Delay and reduce the need to access high-cost statutory provision Improve accessibility to information, advice and guidance, improve links and signposting to services that are already available nationally, regionally and locally. Support Unpaid Carers to access self-help and self-management support to reduce the need for Unpaid Carers crisis interventions. Include access to Unpaid Carers 'self-assessment' focused on individualised outcomes The solution should have the capacity to collect and produce relative data regarding demographics, ethnicity, age range as well as information such as when and where the portal is accessed. sig_79859348fc30fb367b2e.description: The aim of Hansel Oy is to establish a dynamic purchasing system (DPS), the preliminary subject matter of which is software and ICT expert services. Joint procurement enables the procurement of the following services as needed, among others: 1. Software: The customer's procurement subject matter may be various software. In addition to software, expert work related to software can be procured, such as tailoring software to the customer's needs, configuration, further development, as well as support and maintenance. Both open source and closed source software are included in the subject matter of the DPS. The customer's procurement subject matter may also be a licence brokerage service (for example, resale). Software can be delivered on a licence basis, installed in the customer's own environment, or on a service basis as a SaaS implementation. 2. The following ICT expert services are included in the procurement subject matter: ICT management and service management services, ICT solution design, software development and quality assurance services, support and maintenance services, as well as IT asset management. The aim is for the establishment phase of the dynamic purchasing system to start in March-April 2026. *Read more about the dynamic purchasing system: https://www.hansel.fi/hankintatietoa/dynaaminen-hankintajarjestelma-dps/ GENERAL Please note that this is a market survey notice (hereinafter notice), and this notice does not yet request applications to participate. All information presented in this notice is preliminary and indicative prior information. The information provided in this notice is preliminary and may change as preparation progresses. REGISTRATION Companies interested in the dynamic purchasing system in question are requested to register for market dialogue no later than 6.2.2026 via this notice in the Hilma web service. The contracting authority will not respond at this stage to questions sent via the "Questions and Answers" section. MARKET DIALOGUE Draft material related to the dynamic purchasing system under preparation will be sent to registered companies for comments during approximately February-March 2026. Registered companies will be given the opportunity to comment on the draft material in writing. The market dialogue and materials will be in Finnish. Participating or not participating in the market dialogue does not prevent participation in a possible procurement procedure. No compensation will be paid to those who participated in the market dialogue for participation.

The software service is intended to support the entire procure-to-pay process in the target state, including purchase requests (free text, catalog, punchout catalog), purchase orders, order confirmations, receipt of goods, invoice receipt and processing. As part of the invoice processing functionality, the system must also include e-invoicing operator capabilities, enabling the sending and receiving of electronic invoices in accordance with applicable standards and integration requirements. Additionally, the system must include functionalities for supplier management, contract management, and mini competitions. The procured SaaS service must include user licenses for all Fingrid employees. The procurement also includes an implementation project, which is preliminarily planned to start during the first half of 2026. The implementation is intended to proceed in phases and be completed by Q4/2026. The support and advisory service included in the procurement serves as a second-level support channel (2nd line support) for Fingrid’s key users/application owners in case of incidents. In addition, during the contract period, the Client may procure development work, project work, and extensions to expand and improve the subject of the procurement. A more detailed description of the procurement is provided in Annex 1 of the procurement notice, Project Description.
sig_79e0e0f37e6fa41befc5.title: Procurement of a Purchase to Pay -system

sig_79e38c24604df002ebc6.description: BACKGROUND AND PURPOSE OF THE REQUEST FOR INFORMATION Helsingin kaupunki, kaupunkiympäristön toimiala (hereinafter "KYMP") is preparing a tendering procedure "Procurement of a central traffic light control system". Before initiating the actual procurement procedure, KYMP is surveying the market supply, willingness and interest to tender for the procurement in question, and is seeking answers to questions related to the planned procurement. The request for information is not a procurement notice or a call for tenders, but rather a market dialogue. The publication of the request for information does not initiate a tendering procedure. The procurement notice and call for tenders will be published later. The request for information does not oblige the contracting authority to carry out the actual procurement. Answering the request for information is not a prerequisite for participating in any later tendering procedure that may be organised. Market operators will not be paid any compensation for answering the request for information or participating in the market dialogue. Information obtained through the request for information may be used in the preparation of procurement documents. BACKGROUND AND SUBJECT OF THE PROCUREMENT The Urban Environment Division (KYMP) is procuring a new central traffic light control system. The purpose of the new central traffic light control system is to replace at least one of the Client's existing central traffic light control systems. The new central traffic light control system will enable the Client to replace systems that are at the end of their lifecycle. The new System will also offer more advanced features than before, as well as a more advanced user experience. In addition, the key objectives of the procurement are: - Support the organisation's strategic and operational goals - Improve operational efficiency, quality and transparency - Enable the development and expansion of digital services - Reduce manual work and overlapping systems - Ensure information security, data protection and operational reliability The background and subject of the procurement are described in more detail in the annex to the request for information, Description of the subject of the procurement. REQUEST FOR INFORMATION KYMP requests informal answers to the questions in the document "Muutosehdotustaulukko_tekniseen markkinavuoropuheluun_TARJOAJA_TÄYTTÄÄ" attached to the request for information, and to mark any proposed changes. Please submit your answers by email to kymp.icthankinnat@hel.fi at the latest by 2.4.2026 at 16.15. KYMP will treat the answers confidentially. PROCUREMENT PROCEDURE AND SCHEDULE Preliminary schedule for the procurement: March 2026 Request for information April 2026 Publication of call for tenders May-June 2026 Procurement decision and conclusion of procurement contract

sig_7a0605e2d53099ee79b1.description: Initial situation Workforce scheduling is increasingly caught today between operational requirements, the individual needs of employees (work-life balance) and a changing working culture. Developments such as new work, interprofessional collaboration and greater employee participation in shift planning are gaining in importance and placing new demands on planning. Transparent, balanced and automated workforce scheduling not only promotes employee satisfaction, but also has positive effects on the quality of care. At the same time, all of this helps to strengthen employer attractiveness and retention, particularly among nursing staff in core operations. These trends require a planning environment that combines efficiency and participation, optimally controls resources and supports a consistent, employee-oriented planning culture. The current method of workforce scheduling (PEP) as well as the current implementation of the PEP solution "Polypoint" do not support the organisational and technical change necessary for this. Polypoint is also used in the field of time management. Against this background, the project PEP4US is intended to create a new, user-oriented and future-proof solution that integrates technical, organisational and cultural dimensions, both for workforce scheduling and for time management. The aim is to strengthen workforce scheduling as a strategic element of corporate development and to make a significant contribution to the implementation of the strategic measures "New Work in core operations" and "Strategic resource management". In addition, the project is closely linked to HOCH's strategic digitalisation priorities in order to leverage synergies, contribute to process efficiency in core operations and drive the transformation holistically. A detailed description of the actual situation is provided in the specifications document LH01 Chapter 2. The tender aims to find the product most suitable for the current and future needs of HOCH Health Ostschweiz, as well as the other customers of the DIT IT Department, and a reliable and experienced partner for the introduction and support of the future solution. Description Target vision The procurement object comprises the introduction and operation of a central, integrated, high-performance and both organisationally and technologically future-proof solution for workforce scheduling and time management at HOCH Health Ostschweiz and its subsidiaries (approx. 9'700 employees, several wage types and working time models as well as numerous roster sheets and shifts). The solution should enable cross-organisational, standardised and automated workforce scheduling with participation. Existing standalone solutions with overlapping functions will be replaced; the existing interface and integration landscape will be retained. Workforce scheduling, participation, qualifications/skills In future, planning is to be system-supported and largely automated. The solution must generate shift roster proposals, take availabilities, qualifications and statutory requirements into account, and in particular efficiently support pool staff planning. A uniform database and consistent planning logic across all organisational units must be ensured. Employees must be able to record and view their availabilities, shift requests and absences via intuitive, role-based interfaces. Automated shift roster proposals must take demand data, qualifications and operational requirements into account. This reduces manual effort, standardises planning processes and strengthens transparency, fairness and employer attractiveness. The solution must enable transparent and fair planning processes. Employees must be able to understand how assignments come about and how requests and framework conditions are taken into account. In addition, the solution must support harmonised planning processes with a standardised recording of qualifications, experience and deployment preferences. This creates the basis for a needs-based, fair and transparent workforce scheduling. Pool/pool management The solution must support hospital-wide pool and roster management and control assignments, qualifications and resources across locations and departments. The functions of the previous planning tools are to be integrated and planning, communication and control combined in one solution. Connection to IKM Integral Capacity Management The connection to the IKM creates the basis for data-based coordination between demand and workforce scheduling. The solution must enable the connection and active use of demand planning for personnel demand planning and thus support the personnel module in the IKM. Time management, time recording The tasks of time management, including statutory requirements and other sets of rules, must be fully supported. Time recording must be possible via various channels, in particular via a mobile app and existing T&A (time and attendance) terminals, including defined correction options by employees. Multiple employments The solution must fully support multiple employments and enable a transparent, consolidated presentation. This is particularly necessary in a hospital environment with several functions or areas of deployment per employee. Reporting, evaluation The solution should provide role-based access to relevant system and transactional data. In addition to standardised reports, for example on time accounts or statutory requirements, individual evaluations by HR, IT administrators and specialist departments should be possible. This includes analyses of operations

sig_7a0e15ccd6aad2646098.description: The London Borough of Newham is undertaking a comprehensive market intelligence and engagement exercise to inform the future design and delivery of its Housing Repairs, Maintenance, Compliance and Capital Investment Programme. The Authority is currently considering a long-term programme of works and services with an indicative value of between £288 million and £416 million over a potential ten-year period, covering a broad range of specialist housing services including compliance, building safety, planned investment, major repairs, adaptations, voids and asset improvement programmes. The proposals outlined within the accompanying draft specification are intended solely to support this engagement process and should be viewed as initial concepts that will be refined through consultation with the market. The purpose of this survey is to gather intelligence from organisations operating across the housing, construction, compliance, asset management and wider property sectors. The Authority is seeking views on market capacity, capability, commercial models, lot structures, delivery approaches, innovation, digital solutions, social value, sustainability and emerging legislative requirements. Feedback received will help shape future procurement, commercial and service delivery strategies, ensuring that any subsequent procurement exercise is informed by current market expertise and is structured to maximise value, resilience, competition, innovation and positive resident outcomes. The Authority welcomes responses from organisations of all sizes, including SMEs, specialist providers, consortiums, manufacturers, consultants and principal contractors. This exercise represents a unique opportunity for the market to help influence the future direction of one of London's largest housing investment and asset management programmes, and the Authority strongly encourages all interested organisations to participate For more information about this opportunity, please visit the eSourcing portal at: https://www.delta-esourcing.com/tenders/UK-UK-London:-Solar-installation./KAD82PW44U To respond to this opportunity, please click here: https://www.delta-esourcing.com/respond/KAD82PW44U Lot 1: . None

sig_7a27d06c692430595354.description: The Council is initiating a pre-market engagement exercise to inform the forthcoming procurement of a Partnering Adviser. This dialogue is not part of the formal tender process but is designed to gather insights from experienced market participants on the proposed scope, delivery model, and commercial expectations. The Partnering Adviser will play a key role in supporting the mobilisation and operational delivery of the Council’s Repairs, Maintenance, and Capital Delivery contract along with a number of compliance contracts, helping to drive value and foster collaborative working practices. Feedback from this engagement will directly influence the final tender documentation, ensuring it reflects current market capabilities, best practice, and aligns with the Council’s strategic objectives. Interested parties are encouraged to participate in this dialogue to help shape a robust, transparent, and commercially sound procurement process that delivers mutual benefit for both the Council and its delivery partners. The link to the pre-market dialogue questionnaire can be found - https://www.in-tendhost.co.uk/supplyhertfordshire/aspx/ProjectManage/9660. Lot 1: .

sig_7a45a2d78564f2f09a47.description: Region Midtjylland is planning to conduct a tender for a dose monitoring system for performing patient dosimetry within the specialties of conventional X-ray, mammography, interventional procedures, CT, fluoroscopy, DEXA and hybrid scanners in nuclear medicine, so that the region can comply with Executive Order No. 1387 of 18 November 2025 on patient dosimetry and diagnostic reference levels, which enters into force on 1 January 2026. In this context, the region wishes to conduct a market dialogue to gain insight into the market, so that a forthcoming tender best reflects the capabilities of the market in relation to the region's needs, while at the same time uncovering potential risks so they can be mitigated. The result of the market dialogue is to be used, amongst other things, to assess what is standard in the market, so that the region has the best possible basis on which to structure the tender and draw up the tender documents. Initially, the region wishes to invite potential tenderers to a dialogue meeting with the region. The region expects that the dialogue meetings will be used, partly for participants to demonstrate how their solutions support a number of cases, and partly to hear participants' views on a number of requirements, including security requirements, which the region intends to impose on the supplier. The region reserves the right to continue the market dialogue with participants after the dialogue meetings, including asking follow-up questions to participants and potentially sending parts of the tender documents out for consultation with participants. The dialogue meetings are expected to take place in week 5 in 2026 at the region's Department of Procurement and Medical Technology (Aarhus). The meetings will be held individually with each company and are expected to have a duration of a maximum of 2 hours. The meetings will be held in Danish or English at the company's request. In the event of high interest, the region reserves the right to invite only a limited number of companies. In that case, emphasis will be placed on achieving diversity in the types of products/services that the selected companies can offer. Emphasis will also be placed on the market penetration of the product/service among companies. Companies wishing to participate in the market dialogue are asked to send an email to thomas.krogh.larsen@stab.rm.dk and Laura.Brinch.Norregaard@stab.rm.dk no later than 12 January 2026, at 12 with information about their product and/or service. Once a participant has registered, the region will send the participant the material needed for the dialogue meetings as soon as possible, including the cases and requirements. However, if registration takes place after 19 December at 12, the region reserves the right to send the material to the participant only in week 2 2026. Region Midtjylland encourages potential tenderers to participate in the market dialogue.
sig_7a45a2d78564f2f09a47.title: Market dialogue regarding the tender for a dose monitoring system for Region Midtjylland

sig_7a64ef18d7dd087476c3.description: The subject of the contract is the temporary provision of the IdentityManager standard software with the specified modules. This includes: - Right to use the functions of the applications, including the specified modules for individual users in accordance with the total quantity defined further below - Costs incurred by the operation of the software at the manufacturer's site, under the requirement that the software, together with the specified modules and including all data storage, must run on systems that are protected within the EU by the requirements of the GDPR - Costs incurred by the operation of the software at the manufacturer's site, under the requirement that a dedicated, separate virtual/logical infrastructure is used by the manufacturer for the execution of the software, which ensures a strict separation of the software instance used by the ILB, including data storage, from other customers who use the same functions at the manufacturer's site. - Standard support from the product manufacturer - Right to use various connectors within the timeframe acquired by the right to use the software. - Separate instances for productive systems ("production instance") as well as development and test systems ("test instance") Further information on the nature and functionality of the software in question can be found in Part B, Service Description. One Identity Manager from OneIdentity Base Engine: One Identity Manager is a market-leading standard software for Identity Governance and Administration (IGA), which centrally controls user accounts, access rights and the associated risks in complex IT landscapes. The software enables seamless, transparent and audit-proof management of identities across on-premises, hybrid and cloud environments. One Identity Safeguard PASM: The core module secures the entire lifecycle of privileged access credentials; passwords and SSH keys are stored in a hardened vault (appliance or SaaS) and rotated automatically. Access credentials are released exclusively via a policy-based workflow with optional approval levels (e.g. four-eyes principle, time-limited access). In addition, this module acts as a proxy and records all administrative sessions (e.g. via RDP and SSH) without gaps. The recordings include video, keystrokes and metadata. The entire data traffic is monitored in real time, with predefined rules enabling the immediate blocking of suspicious or unwanted actions. This ensures complete, audit-proof traceability. Connectors: Licences must be offered for the items in Chapter 1.1 - Application list for interface integration. Note: a different, varying duration is required for each connector here.
sig_7a64ef18d7dd087476c3.title: Provision of IdentityManager standard software with the One Identity Safeguard PASM module and connectors

The assignment comprises the provision of system support for the management of wellness allowances for monthly-paid employees and an option for hourly-paid employees (hereinafter referred to as the Service). The Service shall support the entire process for managing wellness allowances and function as a digital tool for both employees and administrators at the Municipality. The assignment includes a comprehensive commitment for the Service, which encompasses the system support that forms part of the Service as well as associated services required for the Service to be introduced, used and function over time. The Service also comprises the following options: Option 1 Management of wellness allowances for hourly-paid employees. Price for Option 1 is included in the evaluation of bids. The tenderer shall state the price for Option 1 in the Price Schedule Appendix. If such price is not stated, the bid may be rejected. The Municipality has the right, but not the obligation, to exercise this option during the contract period. Option 2 Administering the management of expense receipts and supporting the disbursement of reimbursement from the Municipality to the employee for purchases of wellness services from wellness suppliers affiliated with the Service. (voluntary) Price for Option 2 is not included in the evaluation of bids. The Municipality has the right, but not the obligation, to exercise this option during the contract period. If the Supplier can provide this functionality, the price for Option 2 shall be submitted in the Price Schedule Appendix. Option 3 Benefit bicycles (voluntary) The option concerns the Supplier being able to offer support through the Service for the administration and management of benefit bicycles for the Municipality's employees for private use. The solution may be provided through a third-party supplier affiliated with the Service. The Municipality has not currently made a decision on the introduction of benefit bicycles and no requirements regarding such functionality are therefore set within the framework of this procurement. The option is not covered by the evaluation and the Tenderer shall therefore not submit any price for the option. The Municipality decides unilaterally if, when and to what extent the option is to be utilised during the contract period. The Municipality reserves the right to refrain from utilising the option and to, in whole or in part, procure a corresponding service or functionality through a separate procurement. sig_7adc538f5fd2c51095a1.description: The contracting authority is striving for the digital modernisation of its individual agendas. One of these agendas is the parking policy of the city of Olomouc (hereinafter also referred to as the "PPMO"). Currently, the territorial scope of the parking policy applies to only two parking zones (A and B). In the planned expansion to zones C and D (including their sub-areas), it is also necessary to adjust and strengthen the existing part of the PPMO, which handles the registry of parking permits. Therefore, the contracting authority has decided to procure the acquisition of services for a new, modern system for the registry of parking permits, whereby these services will be used to optimise faster processing for citizens, ensure connection to state administration registries, and connection to other PPMO systems for more efficient processing of transferred data, and a modern graphical interface meeting current trends will also be achieved. The provision of the services of the system for the registry of parking permits must also fulfil all current legislative and security requirements. The subject matter of performance of this public contract is: a) performance of a requirements analysis, processing and implementation of the target concept, establishment and commissioning of the Portal Solution for the registry of parking permits (hereinafter referred to as the "PPMO Portal Solution"), data migration, testing, provision of training, provision of licences and provision of all other related performance necessary for the proper commissioning of the PPMO Portal Solution; b) provision of the PPMO Portal Solution as a service (in service mode), ensuring its maintenance and support, provision of the IT infrastructure necessary for the operation of the PPMO Portal Solution; c) provision of development services, analytical and methodical services, implementation of change requests and provision of other related performance based on the requirements of the contracting authority. A more detailed specification of the subject matter of performance is contained in the relevant parts of the tender documentation (hereinafter also referred to as the "TD"), in particular Appendix No. 2 and Appendix No. 3 of the TD. The types of parking permits are outlined in Appendix No. 12 of the TD. The types of parking permits may change over time.

sig_7b9f8253f870f2b59f85.description: The subject of procurement is the analysis, design, development, implementation, testing, commissioning, user training, and warranty maintenance of the integrated information system for agroecological zoning of the Republic of Croatia (hereinafter: AEZ system). The system must represent the central national platform for the collection, management, analysis, modelling, visualisation, and distribution of agroecological data and the results of agroecological analyses. The aim of the system is to establish a unified digital environment that enables the identification and monitoring of agroecological zones, the assessment of suitability for individual agricultural crops, the preparation of scenario analyses, and support for expert and strategic decision-making in the field of agricultural policy, natural resource management, and adaptation to climate change. The system must enable the processing of large amounts of spatial and temporal data, the execution of complex analytical processes, and the distribution of results via web GIS interfaces and standardised service interfaces. In the document Annex I – Project of Agroecological Zoning of the Republic of Croatia 2025–2028, the services as well as the functional and non-functional requirements that the delivered application solution must include are described in detail. All of the above are necessary elements of the delivered solution. Phase 1 – Establishment of the geospatial platform and basic functionalities Phase 2 – Development of the agroecological zoning analytical system Phase 3 – Production application of agroecological zoning Upon completion of the project, a fully functional solution must be delivered to the Contracting Authority which enables: 1. calculation of the national agroecological zones of the Republic of Croatia 2. assessment of suitability for agricultural crops 3. comparison of different climate scenarios and development scenarios of individual agricultural crops based on input data and predictive models 4. centralised management of spatial and analytical data 5. web GIS review of agroecological zones 6. data exchange via standard OGC and REST services 7. long-term upgradability and sustainability of the system
sig_7b9f8253f870f2b59f85.title: Agroekološko zoniranje

This is not a call for tenders, procurement notice or prior information notice, but a notice of the initiation of market dialogue as part of procurement planning. Espoon kaupunki has initiated the preparation of a local detailed planning software procurement and invites suppliers to a market dialogue. The subject of the procurement is a CAD software solution compliant with the Act on the Built Environment Information System (431/2023) and the requirements of the Ryhti system for the production of data model-based local detailed plans. The local detailed planning software solution is used for the design and drawing of local detailed plans at various stages of the planning process together with other systems in use within the Urban Environment sector of the City of Espoo. In addition to this, the software solution is used for traffic planning and making 3D models. In traffic planning, precise street geometries are drawn up and it is ensured that sufficient space is reserved for traffic arrangements and intra-block functions, such as parking and service traffic. Traffic planning carries out general planning, street maps and cross-sections, among other things, as well as the design of street grading, in connection with which longitudinal and cross-section profiles are produced. The drawing up of a local detailed plan is a long-standing process lasting an estimated 2-5 years. Fewer than 100 local detailed plans are completed in Espoo per year, and approximately 90% of them also include traffic plans. In a single local detailed planning project, there are on average approx. 100 documents related to local detailed planning and traffic planning, which are stored mainly in the document management system. The local detailed planning and traffic planning software solution has a total of approximately 65 users. Currently, local detailed planning and traffic planning at the City of Espoo is carried out mainly using Bentley design software. In addition to this, local detailed planning data is managed in the Trimble Locus municipal information system and the document management system. In the future, the permanent plan identifier will be obtained from the Ryhti system into Trimble Locus's plan register, from where it is copied into the local detailed plan drawing software. Local detailed plans are transferred as a JSON file transfer to Trimble Locus Cloud for export to the Ryhti system. Plans are transferred to the Ryhti system from Trimble Locus, where the management of plan objects and plan amendments as well as the transfer of plan attachments to the Ryhti system also take place. The management of reference data utilised in the drawing up of traffic plans will continue to take place in the document management system. The resulting street maps and other material supporting planning will be attached as part of the local detailed plan description annex material and transferred to the Ryhti system. Swept path analyses are carried out using AutoTURN software. The subject of the procurement is a system to be procured as a service, provisionally in accordance with the following: - Ready-to-use CAD software with user licenses - Local detailed plan Ryhti objects database - Service deployment and customisation for Espoo - Application maintenance services - Additional procurement opportunities related to the subject of the procurement - System further development and expert services according to Espoo's needs. The functionalities of the local detailed planning and traffic planning software solution are aimed to cover, among other things, the following: - Tasks related to local detailed planning design - Production of data model-based local detailed plans - Traffic planning - Making 3D models illustrating plans - Making 3D models of traffic planning streets - Ryhti objects database - File-based transfer of plan data to the Ryhti system via the Trimble Locus municipal information system - Reporting - Management of user roles and user rights. The purpose of the market dialogue is to survey the market situation concerning the local detailed planning software procurement. Espoon kaupunki wants to hear potential suppliers' thoughts on the implementation of the procurement procedure and the preparation of the invitation to tender. MARKET DIALOGUE SCHEDULE The market dialogue will provisionally take place in two phases: 1. Via Teams provisionally during weeks 43-44. The contracting authority reserves the right to invite a maximum of 4 suppliers to the first phase of the dialogue based on the request for information responses. The aim of this first phase is to familiarise oneself with companies and products on the market, for example, through suppliers' company and product presentations and demos. 2. Tender documents will be sent to those who registered for the market dialogue for commenting during an estimated period between November 2026 and January 2027. The second phase of the market dialogue will take place electronically. Written material will be sent to all those registered for the market dialogue for review. The dialogue of the second phase will cover the content of the preliminary invitation to tender, requirement specifications and contractual terms. The contracting authority reserves the right to hold additional dialogues as the market survey progresses. The contracting authority's aim is to launch the actual procurement procedure in the spring of 2027 and the implementation project provisionally in the autumn of 2027, such that the new system can be put into use in the spring of 2028.

sig_7c81fa0efc36e2e2f76b.description: The ekom21 - Kommunales Gebietsrechenzentrum Hessen (hereinafter: ekom21) is a body governed by public law pursuant to the Hessian Data Processing Association Act (DV-VerbundG). It is the central IT service provider for Hessian municipalities and their institutions. From locations in Giessen, Darmstadt, Kassel and Fulda, it comprehensively supplies its end customers with modern information and communication services (ICT) of all kinds. The approximately 500 members in Hesse and other customers nationwide include approx. 29.000 end users from local authorities and other public institutions, such as districts, cities, municipalities, municipal eigenbetriebs, special-purpose associations, institutions, hospitals and residential homes. In the governmental sector, ekom21 serves numerous state associations, ministries and regional administrative offices. In total, ekom21 thus provides services for six million citizens. The range of tasks of ekom21 is growing and changing continuously, which goes hand in hand with a steady expansion of the customer base. In order to accommodate the requests of our customers for a data protection management system (DPMS), a corresponding partner must be commissioned. For this reason, ekom21 is tendering a DPMS for its customers. Primarily, a cloud-based data protection management system (SaaS) is to be procured that supports, documents and controls all processing activities pursuant to Art. 5 30 General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR), the Federal Data Protection Act (BDSG) as well as the Hessian Data Protection and Freedom of Information Act (HDSIG). The aim is to reduce the effort for risk and impact assessments, the register of processing activities (RoPA), data subject requests, contract and sales management as well as audit evidence, while simultaneously increasing compliance quality. Lot LOT-0000: Data protection management system. The procurement procedure aims at the conclusion of a framework agreement with an economic operator. The framework agreement is intended - without establishing an obligation to purchase - to enable the demand-driven provision, introduction and long-term support of a "data protection management system" as well as associated services for customers of ekom21. The maximum value of the framework agreement amounts to 1.000.000,00 million € (net). Further details can be found in the procurement documents.
sig_7c81fa0efc36e2e2f76b.title: Data protection management system

sig_7cfb0d0cf53077dbe97a.description: DCMS are seeking to commission "what works" research into the impact and effectiveness of AI adoption interventions within DCMS sectors. We are interested in two broad sets of questions. The first is analysis of how businesses within DCMS sectors that are in the process of adopting AI achieve this, the challenges they face and the opportunities and benefits realised. We anticipate this will be explored through an ethnographic study that observes how individuals and teams actually use AI tools in their jobs. The second set of questions is what policy interventions work best to support businesses that wish to adopt AI, which we anticipate will be answered by testing hypothetical interventions through randomised control trials (RCTs). Bidders will be able to propose alternative methodologies if they think they suit these questions better; the core need for this project is to produce direct, robust evidence of what works, as opposed to what is self-reported (e.g. through interviews, focus groups, surveys, and similar) to work. This project will be commissioned either through a Competitive Flexible Procedure under the Procurement Act 2023, or through the RM6126 Research and Insights framework. This is part of the DCMS Science and Analysis R&D Programme, which supports R&D capability within the department. This project will run concurrently aside three other large projects across 2027-2030, these include; mapping the specific "user pathways" audiences take to find, consume, and value information; a continuation of previous research to develop data-intensive approaches for capturing engagement at unticketed cultural, heritage, and sporting events/activities/locations, e.g. using mobile app data to model how people participate in our events; and a continuation of previous research to design and improve methods for holistically tracking the long-term impact of major events, tested on a major event. Lot 1: .

sig_7db0c7239c986ab729fc.description: The NSF State and Regional AI Infrastructure Hubs program aims to expand access to the compute required for AI-enabled scientific discovery and to transform the research, education, and training opportunities offered by institutions of higher education. AI Infrastructure Hubs will connect researchers to new compute infrastructure that leverages contributions from state governments, research institutions, industry, and philanthropy, accelerating AI-enabled discovery across science and engineering and developing a skilled technical workforce for AI use in the scientific enterprise. The program responds to a core tenet of Science: A New Golden Age to renew America’s research and development (R&D) for changes in today’s scientific enterprise, including the role of AI in laying the foundation for a new era of scientific discovery and the growing role of industry and philanthropy in funding R&D. In response, the Administration’s FY28 R&D Priorities Memorandum called for investing in AI for science as a national mission and expanding the scale of, and flexible access to, advanced compute and data infrastructure that researchers now require for frontier scientific discovery. Each AI Infrastructure Hub will be organized as a flexible state or regional consortium of state and local governments, research institutions, philanthropies, and the private sector. Consortia will be responsible for all funding for new or expanded computing, data, and AI resources, whether on-premises or cloud-based. NSF will fund each Hub’s consortium coordination, AI infrastructure workforce development, and faculty training and coursework development in leveraging AI for science.
sig_7db0c7239c986ab729fc.title: U.S. National Science Foundation State and Regional Artificial Intelligence Infrastructure Hubs:

It includes, among others, the following capabilities: • Monitoring of infrastructures and associated technical components, including servers, operating systems, containers, databases, middleware, network components linked to applications, message queues, APIs and integration platforms. • Monitoring of applications and end-to-end transactions, with capabilities for anomaly detection, accelerated diagnostics, dependency analysis and root cause identification. • Monitoring of user experience, both real and synthetic, for critical applications and user journeys. • Collection, centralisation, normalisation, correlation and exploitation of telemetry data, including metrics, events, logs and traces. • Provision of dashboards adapted to different roles and levels of responsibility, including management, IT operations, application teams, the NOC/support and application and service managers. • Definition, measurement and monitoring of service level indicators, including SLIs/SLOs, golden signals and error budgets, as well as associated alerting mechanisms. • Integration with existing ITSM tools and processes, including for incident, problem, change, escalation, reporting and service review management. • Implementation of intelligent alerting mechanisms, allowing for noise reduction, correlation of alerts, their prioritisation based on business impact and their routing to the responsible teams. • Analysis of the impact on IT services and critical business services, based on dependencies between users, applications, technical components and the services concerned. The goal of the contract is to conclude a cascading Framework Agreement with all Tenderers who have submitted a compliant offer. The Tenderer ranked best according to the award criteria will be considered the active Contractor. The other Tenderers whose offer is compliant will be considered reserve Contractors. Their contract will be activated in the event of failure of the active operator (cascade). Furthermore, Sibelga reserves the right to contract licences directly with the supplier of the selected framework. sig_7f53d5b12ba539041af9.description:
Delivery/provision of a cloud-based software system for time recording (time management - ZWS) & personnel deployment planning (PEP) for medical services, nursing services & other service types. The subject of the procurement procedure is the provision of a cloud-based software solution (Software as a Service) for time recording (time management – ZWS) and personnel deployment planning (PEP) for the medical service (approx. 720 employees), the nursing service (approx. 2.180 employees) and other service types (approx. 1.372 employees – medical-technical service, functional service, administrative service, personnel of the training centres). In addition, approx. 500 internal and approx. 300 external students must also be managed in the system. A market-available standard solution is expressly being tendered, which can be adapted to the client's requirements through parameterisation. Individual solutions or in-house developments are excluded. This applies in particular to the bidirectional interface to the existing SAP ERP R/3 HCM infrastructure as well as to the new SAP S/4HANA environment. Further requirements for implementation, parameterisation, training and process standardisation are part of the tender documents or the specifications. The software must cover the following task areas in particular and must be provided as an integrated overall solution: -Personnel deployment planning incl. holiday and absence management (PEP) -Time management (ZWS) -Preparatory payroll accounting through the creation of collective agreement-relevant wage types in hourly or € values -Employee Self Service (ESS) -Manager Self Service (MSS) -Reporting and statistics. The interaction of these task areas is indispensable for efficient and modern personnel deployment planning, control and accounting. For this reason, these tasks must be closely linked and should appear as a single unit from a technological and user perspective. The solution must be able to be integrated without problems into the IT infrastructure available at the KC (SAP ERP R/3 HCM & SAP S/4HANA HCM & SAP IS-H/i.s.h.med) and must necessarily communicate with the software solutions already in use via standardised interfaces (state of the art). Both master data as well as attendance, absence and wage data must flow uni- and bidirectionally (depending on the data type) via the interfaces. The interface must necessarily work with change data records (data records to be changed in SAP are deleted and newly created or overwritten with new data records) in order to ensure the highest degree of automation and to minimise the need for manual intervention as far as possible. To map smooth processes, the PEP solution must ensure a consistent, secure and media-break-free data exchange. This is essential, especially for employee payroll accounting, and if it were to fail, it would have a lasting negative impact on the operation of the KC. The most automated transfer possible of required data from the legacy systems must be ensured. The new PEP solution must be able to import data from the IS-H/i.s.h.med, convert it into personnel requirements and integrate it into the deployment planning. With the help of the PEP solution, the wage types currently required at the Klinikum Chemnitz for the correct payroll accounting of all service types must be generated in accordance with the collective agreement regulations and transferred to the SAP HCM payroll and salary system in a time-controlled manner. In the medical collective agreement, 39 different wage types must currently be mapped, and in the non-medical collective agreement, 32 wage types. In some cases, wage types are created on an individual employee basis and depend on different conditions such as department, employee qualification, individual agreement. Especially with on-call duties, it happens that within a department, on-call duties are remunerated according to a fixed flat rate or according to the collective agreement regulations. The software solution must be able to map these constellations even within a month (see also the specifications). The connection of employees to the new PEP software solution is to take place in pre-defined waves. Accordingly, it must be ensured that some of the employees continue to be managed on the SAP PEP and other employees on the new PEP solution. The contractor must ensure that both systems function productively in parallel for the duration of the implementation and rollout and do not influence each other. The S/4HANA migration of the SAP ERP R/3 HCM planned in 2026 (Unicode conversion, database migration and S/4 application) must be taken into account. This concerns both project management and the function (bidirectional integration with the legacy systems HCM and ERP and the migration target, no PEP function maintenance after S/4HANA migration in the HCM). In addition, integration with the parallel project S/4HANA migration is required. The PEP solution is to be introduced on the current SAP HCM version ECC 8. Starting 2026, the transition of the SAP ERP R/3 HCM to SAP S/4HANA HCM is to take place, and with it the migration of the PEP software to the new system. Accordingly, it is assumed that the contractor has already successfully migrated the interfaces of their software solution from SAP ECC to S/4HANA and that all required functions are also fully available in the integration with an S/4HANA system (HCM and ERP). A project-specific EVB-IT cloud contract & service contract will be concluded for the procurement. The draft contract is part of this publication as well as the tender documents for the initial offer and can be further specified by the client within the framework of the procurement negotiations. The procurement is for a minimum contract term of 36 months after operational readiness has been established.

Thereafter, the contract shall be extended by one year at a time, unless it is terminated by one of the parties six months before the end of the contract. Details on this can also be found in the tender documents of the subsequent offer phase or offer phases.
sig_7f53d5b12ba539041af9.title: Delivery/provision of a cloud-based software system for time recording (time management - ZWS) & personnel deployment planning (PEP) for medical services, nursing services & other service types

sig_7f9ff0375af0d5a9ad72.description: This Tender Notice is issued by Tai Tarian as a Competitive Flexible Procedure in accordance with the requirements of the Procurement Act 2023. Tai Tarian is seeking to award a Contract to a single Supplier for the Provision and Implementation of an Integrated Business Solution. As part of its programme of change, Tai Tarian is seeking a comprehensive end-to-end solution that supports intuitive data collection, removes duplication of data, improves operational efficiency and effectiveness, retains a golden thread, enhances customer service and supports informed decision-making through full end-to-end case management, integrated workflows, automation, real-time reporting and management information. The solution must have fully documented, openly published version-controlled APIs supporting real-time, bi-directional integration with third-party systems and the Tai Tarian data platform. The solution must operate on a common data model so that a single record of the customer, property and interaction is maintained without duplication or synchronisation between modules. The solution must be cloud-based, scalable, secure and compliant with all relevant Welsh and UK legislation and regulatory requirements, including (but not limited) to GDPR, Renting Homes Wales Act 2016, Welsh Housing Quality Standards 2023 and Building Safety Act (Wales) 2026. It must support efficient data management, robust tailored reporting and analytics capabilities, and facilitate effective engagement with tenants, contractors and other stakeholders through modern digital channels. The successful Supplier will be required to provide an integrated business solution and all associated licences, implementation, configuration, integration, support and maintenance services necessary to deliver a cloud-based, scalable and secure solution supporting a range of business functions including (but not limited to), customer services, housing operations, asset management, compliance management, property services, financial management, document and records management, portals, mobile working, case management, workflow, scheduling, reporting and analytics and AI and agents. Tai Tarian recognises that Tenderers may utilise third-party software components as part of their proposed solution. Such arrangements will be permitted provided the Tenderer assumes full responsibility for the delivery and performance of the overall solution and demonstrates that the proposed solution operates as a fully integrated and cohesive solution. Further details of the procurement, including the scope of the Contract, solution and process requirements, procurement process, evaluation methodology and contractual arrangements, are set out in the Procurement Documents. sig_8081a37c02bc740e0e53.description: Birmingham City Council (the Council) is seeking to commission a specialist behavioural science consultancy to design and deliver a comprehensive behavioural systems model to understand the drivers of car and vehicle dependency across Birmingham and determine targets for behavioural interventions. This work will directly support the development and implementation of the city’s Healthy Streets programme, which aims to shape neighbourhoods that are safer, easier to navigate, and more pleasant to live in by supporting greater use of walking, cycling and public transport, and decreasing dependence on private vehicles. Vehicle dependency is a multifaceted behavioural challenge influenced by numerous interacting factors, such as habits, feelings of safety and ease, access to transport options, and broader environmental and societal influences. To address this complexity, BCC requires a robust, evidence‐informed modelling approach capable of identifying the most influential behavioural drivers and the highest‐impact opportunities for change. The Council will be using its free to use e-tendering system (in-tend) for the administration of this procurement process and potential suppliers must register with the system to be able to express an interest. If you wish to express an interest in this opportunity please click on the following link to access https://in-tendhost.co.uk/birminghamcc/ and submit your details to register which will enable you to download all relevant ITT documentation via My Tenders. If you are unable to register with In-tend or have any questions or problems on how to use this web site please either email us at: etendering@birmingham.gov.uk Your completed request for quotation submission should be returned by noon 8th October 2026 via the ‘in-tend’ system https://in-tendhost.co.uk/birminghamcc The contract for the services will commence 9th November 2026 and will be in place for a period of 10 months. sig_80cecc72fbd80a65e5c5.description: The purpose of this request for information is to ask suppliers for their views regarding the tendering of the IT expert services framework agreement planned by the Bank of Finland ("contracting authority"). The objective of the framework agreement is to ensure sufficient, versatile and long-term expert resourcing to support the Bank of Finland's IT operations. This is not a contract notice or a call for tenders, but a request for information for a market survey, the objective of which is to obtain comprehensive additional information regarding the planned procurement so that any future tendering process can be carried out as appropriately as possible and to ensure that the planned procurement is technically and operationally feasible. The request for information collects views and feedback from market operators on the planned procurement entity, including: • the scope and structure of the procurement, • requirements and contract terms, • service descriptions and sub-areas, • obligations set for the supplier. The contracting authority does not commit to carrying out the procurement that is the subject of the request for information. Decisions on launching a possible procurement process will be made after the market survey. RESPONDING TO THE REQUEST FOR INFORMATION Responses are requested in writing by the deadline. No compensation will be paid for participating in the market survey. The views and amendment proposals presented by the supplier in the market survey will be processed in the contracting authority's internal preparation. The contracting authority is not obliged to take the presented proposals into account, and the market survey does not create privileges or a priority position for suppliers in a possible later procurement procedure. The background material for the request for information is a draft of the key documents of the procurement (e.g. description of the subject of the procurement, service descriptions, requirements, pricing model and contract drafts). Suomen Pankki requests suppliers to examine the material as a whole and to answer the questions presented, particularly from the perspective of whether the supplier would realistically be able to submit a tender and fulfil all requirements and terms as they are.

sig_80dbdc1ce16db1d3fca0.description: Forest management services will be awarded in the year 2026 (field phase 2027) by concluding a public procurement contract for the Stejaru Forestry Office. The total area of the Stejaru Forestry Office is 8798,32 ha. The services involve the development of the forest management plan, a product of the management activity with a technical-organisational content, ecologically grounded, through which, for a period of time, the works necessary to be executed in a production unit are established, for the purpose of bringing and, subsequently, maintaining the structural characteristics of the stands and the forest as a whole to the values corresponding to the optimal structural model defined in accordance with the ecological, social and economic objectives pursued through sustainable management. According to the provisions of Art. 63 para. (11) of Law no. 331/2024 regarding the Forestry Code, with subsequent amendments and additions, it is necessary that the development of forest management plans be carried out through public procurement procedures. The management of the state-owned public forest fund constitutes a priority obligation of the forest fund administrators. The method of managing the state-owned public forest fund is regulated by forest management plans. Forest management plans and their amendments are approved by order of the head of the Authority. In the case of state-owned public lands, the management plans provide data and information necessary for their registration/updating in the centralised inventory of state public domain assets and for registration in the integrated cadastre and land registry system. Requests for clarifications formulated by tenderers during the advertising period of the participation notice can be made with a deadline of at most 15 days before the deadline for the submission of tenders. The contracting authority will respond to all requests for clarifications formulated in compliance with the above deadline, once, in a consolidated manner, 10 days before the deadline for the submission of tenders. Services for the development of the forest management plan for the state-owned public forest fund managed by the Tulcea Forestry Directorate – Stejaru Forestry Office, field phase 2027, for the area of 8798,32 ha. The services include preparatory works, field data collection, data processing and drafting of the forest management plan, development and expansion of the GIS database and management maps, preparation of the necessary environmental documentation, obtaining the regulatory act issued by the competent authority for environmental protection, supporting the documentation within the Technical Commission for Forestry Approval (CTAS) and obtaining the order for the approval of the forest management plan.
sig_80dbdc1ce16db1d3fca0.title: Forest management services - Stejaru Forestry Office 2026 - Tulcea Forestry Directorate

Therefore, the software must be updated regularly. The supplier NES software is in use at IWB. The Software Investment Protection (SIP) Platinum Service covers all further developments and system improvements. NES maintenance (SIP Service Platinum) includes software and firmware updates within the same releases as well as upgrades to further releases for meters, DC/DCN and NES system software (head end system), NES provisioning tool and NES diagnostics tool as well as telephone and web-based technical support. Based on the software used at IWB, "SIP Platinum" or equivalent is required. sig_814884a0b6cde5bdad83.description: ***THIS OPPORTUNITY IS SET-ASIDE FOR WOMEN-OWNED SMALL BUSINESS (WOSB) CONCERNS*** **A LIVE NIMS DEMONSTRATION WILL OCCUR 09 SEP 2026, SEE L.8 FOR DETAILS** The AJW-2 Directorate, AJW-2131 Implementation Services Group, provides technical, engineering, financial, budget, and management support to Technical Operations programs using the NAS Integration Support Contract (NISC IV Contract) and Technical Support Services Contract (TSSC).These are task order contracts that present contract managers with the task of managing the entire Task Order Management lifecycle, the Financial Management lifecycle encompassing the obligation and de-obligation of funds by integrating with FAA’s financial systems, PRISM and Delphi and the Invoice/Payments lifecycle. The NISC IV contract will also be transitioned to NISC V contract during the award period, which will require a new system to support the NISC V contract, while maintaining the NIMS system to close out the NISC IV contract. This work requires a support contractor that will provide Operations and Maintenance services for the NIMS systems that is used to manage the current NISC IV contract using the existing technology stack and will provide quality assurance and quality control to ensure uninterrupted system availability. In addition, the vendor should maintain and run reports if required from CMIS system that was used to support the NISC III contract and is currently not active. The work also requires the vendor to serve as a Subject Matter Expert (SME) capable of providing design, development, testing, deployment and documentation of the new software that will be required to support the NISC V contract when required. This includes, but is not limited to, making recommendations regarding the selection of software architecture and software development tools that will be required to develop the new system. The Contractor must provide operations and maintenance support for the NIMS/CMIS system, provide quality assurance and quality control, provide security compliance and ensure uninterrupted system availability. This effort also requires the vendor to serve as a SME and provide support with system architecture, software recommendations, system design, development, testing, deployment, and documentation for a new system to support NISC V contract requirements when required. Contractor will maintain NIMS/CMIS security certifications required to operate the software and its associated server hardware. The Contractor must also provide transition support to any potential new vendor at the contract’s end. ***THIS OPPORTUNITY IS SET-ASIDE FOR WOMEN-OWNED SMALL BUSINESS (WOSB) CONCERNS*** **A LIVE NIMS DEMONSTRATION WILL OCCUR 09 SEP 2026, SEE L.8 FOR DETAILS**

sig_8159667ab70b2daa7ef0.description: Aberdeen City Council is seeking market engagement to inform the potential procurement of a city-focused Aberdeen Destination Marketing and Development Service, funded through the Aberdeen Visitor Levy, which is due to apply from 1 April 2027. The proposed service would support Aberdeen’s position as a leading visitor destination by delivering destination marketing, city promotion, market intelligence, business engagement, product development and visitor economy development activity. It would seek to increase awareness of Aberdeen, grow visitor numbers and length of stay, support accommodation demand, amplify the city’s cultural, events, heritage, hospitality, leisure and business tourism offer, and contribute to the city’s wider economic transition. The service is expected to focus on Aberdeen city while recognising that the wider regional offer — including landscapes, coastline, castles, golf, food and drink, outdoor activity and touring itineraries — forms an important part of the destination proposition. The Council is also interested in how the service should interface with convention bureau and business events activity where this supports additional visitors, bed nights and economic value for the city. This Prior Information Notice is for market engagement only. It is not a call for competition and does not commit the Council to a procurement, contract award or any particular delivery model. Lot 1: . Aberdeen City Council is considering the procurement of an Aberdeen Destination Marketing and Development Service to support the objectives of the Aberdeen Visitor Levy and the sustainable growth of the city’s visitor economy. The service is expected to be delivered as a city-focused programme for Aberdeen. Its purpose will be to promote Aberdeen as a distinctive destination for leisure and business visitors, encourage people to visit, stay longer and spend more, and support the development of a strong visitor offer across the city’s venues, events, festivals, culture, attractions, hospitality and tourism businesses. The anticipated scope may include destination marketing and communications, city promotion, business engagement, visitor economy development, product and itinerary development, travel trade support, market intelligence, performance evaluation and reporting. Where included within the final scope, the service may also interface with convention bureau and business events activity where this supports additional visitors, accommodation bed nights and economic value for Aberdeen. The service will be expected to complement, rather than duplicate, wider regional destination activity, while maintaining a clear focus on improving Aberdeen’s position as a visitor destination. It will also be expected to support transparent public reporting on the use and impact of Visitor Levy proceeds, including evidence of outputs, outcomes and performance against agreed indicators. This notice is intended to inform market engagement and procurement planning. Any future procurement will be subject to Council approvals, final service specification, available budget and the applicable procurement process.
sig_8159667ab70b2daa7ef0.title: Aberdeen Destination Marketing and Development Service

sig_81a86606d6aed4cc0b6c.description: The Ogden Air Logistics Complex (OO-ALC) at Hill Air Force Base, Utah, intends to issue a solicitation to provide comprehensive management and supply of aircraft coatings and sealants. This effort aims to ensure uninterrupted aircraft maintenance operations through robust inventory management, timely delivery, and technical support. This effort will include frequent ordering and quick delivery on specified items. The selected contractor will be responsible for continuous deliveries and support of Coatings and Sealants, including: 1. Order Fulfillment and Material Handling: Sourcing, storing, and delivering all required coatings and sealants (see attached list). This includes meeting a strict four (4) hour delivery timeline for urgent requirements and handling specialized materials, such as Premixed Frozen Material (PFM) requiring transit at -80F. The contractor must maintain a minimum of 85% shelf life for all products upon delivery. The contractor will also be responsible for managing shelf-life and ensuring proper storage and handling of the products prior to delivery. 2. FMS-3600 Coating Management: For this specialized product, implementing a lock and key ITAR-compliant storage system and maintaining rigorous chain of custody for the material. 3. Technical Assistance: Providing technical assistance that includes rapid response (within one business day) to material failures, on-site technical support during monthly visits, product change support, and quality audit reporting. 4. Online Ordering System: Furnishing a secure, web-based ordering and tracking system with real-time visibility of lead times and minimum stock levels (MSLS). 5. Ramp-Up Plan: Executing a ramp-up plan to achieve full performance readiness within eight (8) months of contract award. The anticipated contract will be a Firm Fixed Priced (FFP) IDIQ to include an 8-month ramp up period, a 5-year ordering period, and a 6-month allowance for remaining deliveries on the back end. Total period of performance is anticipated to be 6 years and 2 months. This is a total small business set-aside. The Government anticipates awarding a single contract. All interested small businesses are encouraged to respond. The official solicitation will be posted on SAM .gov. The Government intends to award a single contract resulting from the upcoming solicitation to the responsible offeror whose proposal represents the best value to the Government. This effort requires Contractors to be CMMC level 2 self-certified, therefore if you are not currently level 2 certified and are interested in this requirement you will need to begin the process to become level 2 certified immediately. The solicitation draft documents are attached. These documents are subject to change before the official solicitation posting. Dates on the solicitation are subject to change based on the actual award date. Please review and submit any questions or suggestions to the point of contacts on this 15-day synopsis. The anticipated solicitation number is FA8224-26-R-0010 (subject to change). The anticipated solicitation release date is October 2, 2026 (subject to change).
