sig_822641108af6f5162179.description: Tipperary County Council Procurement of Single-Party Framework Agreement for Architect-Led Integrated Design Team Consultancy Services for Clonmel, Co. Tipperary. Tipperary County Council is undertaking a competitive tendering process for the establishment of a Single-Party Framework Agreement for Architect-Led Integrated Multi-Disciplinary Consultancy Services for Public Realm, Landscape and Building Upgrade Projects in Clonmel, Co. Tipperary. The Framework Agreement will require the successful Consultant to provide, either directly or through its proposed multi-disciplinary team, all of the following services: 1. Architectural Services – Public Realm 2. Conservation Architectural Services 3. Landscape Architectural Services 4. Civil and Structural Engineering Services 5. Quantity Surveying Services 6. Project Management Services 7. Project Supervisor Design Process (PSDP) Services 8. Employer’s Representative Services 9. Public Liaison / Stakeholder Engagement Services 10. Mechanical and Electrical Engineering Services 11. Planning Services 12. Archaeological Services 13. Fire Engineering Services Only Applicants capable of providing all of the above disciplines and associated specialist expertise, whether in-house, through subcontractors or as part of a grouping/consortium, will be considered. This competition will be conducted using a restricted procedure. At Stage 1, Applicants will be assessed against the suitability and selection criteria set out in the Suitability Assessment Questionnaire. It is intended that the five highest-scoring Applicants, subject to a sufficient number meeting all minimum requirements and rules for selection, will be invited to participate in Stage 2. At Stage 2, shortlisted Applicants will be issued with the Invitation to Tender and associated tender documentation. Tenders will be evaluated in accordance with the award criteria and weightings set out in the Invitation to Tender. The highest-ranked compliant Tenderer will be appointed to the Single-Party Framework Agreement and will also be awarded the Initial Contract. The Initial Contract will relate to the further development and delivery of public realm and associated projects in Clonmel. Clonmel Town Centre requires a significant streetscape and public realm upgrade. A design previously received Part VIII approval; however, the design now requires further development, amendment and coordination to reflect the current project scope and available funding and to bring the project through detailed design, tender, construction and handover stages. Tipperary County Council has also acquired a protected structure for which design development and a Part VIII planning process will be required. The Architect-Led Design Team may therefore be required to deliver a combination of public realm, landscape, civil engineering and building upgrade works, including works to protected and heritage structures. The Architect will act as Lead Consultant and will be responsible for coordinating and managing the full multi-disciplinary design team, programme, cost and delivery of the projects. During the construction stage, the Design Team will be required to provide ongoing technical support, respond to queries arising on site and advise on proposed variations and other matters affecting the delivery of the works. Projects arising under the Framework Agreement are anticipated to be funded, in whole or in part, through the Towns and Cities Regeneration Investment Fund (TCRIF) and/or other available funding programmes. Please note that an ITT is not required for this stage of the tender process.
sig_822641108af6f5162179.title: Tipperary County Council Procurement of Single-Party Framework Agreement for Architect-Led Integrated Design Team Consultancy Services for Clonmel, Co. Tipperary

sig_8227979e95ca042cc209.description: This Notice of Funding Opportunity (NOFO) invites a single cooperative agreement application for the Resource Center for the Cardiovascular Repository for Type 1 Diabetes (CaRe-T1D). The purpose of CaRe-T1D is to support innovative, discovery and mechanistic research through the study of human cardiovascular (CV) tissue. This research seeks to better understand cardiovascular disease (CVD) in type 1 diabetes, highlight differences compared to type 2 diabetes, and ultimately guide the development of therapies to treat this major cause of morbidity and mortality for individuals with type 1 diabetes. To achieve these goals, the Resource Center will expand the CaRe-T1D biorepository of human CV tissue, further develop the data commons for data sharing and for artificial intelligence (AI) tools, coordinate the research activities of the investigative teams in the CaRe-T1D consortium, and make CaRe-T1D resources accessible to the broader research community. This NOFO is associated with the Special Diabetes Program (https://www.niddk.nih.gov/about-niddk/research-areas/diabetes/type-1-diabetes-special-statutory-funding-program/about-special-diabetes-program) which funds research on the prevention, treatment, and cure of type 1 diabetes and its complications, including unique, innovative, and collaborative research consortia and clinical trials networks.This is a Notice of Funding Opportunity (NOFO) for a Single Source that will invite application(s) from eligible organization(s) to apply. Please see Section III. Eligibility for additional information. In accordance with NIH standard peer-review processes, the application(s) will be peer-reviewed, and only meritorious application(s) will be considered for funding.
sig_8227979e95ca042cc209.title: Single Source Competition: Continuation of the Cardiovascular Repository for Type 1 Diabetes (CaRe-T1D) - Resource Center (U24 Clinical Trial Not Allowed)

sig_82391277c8002fad1f98.description: This notice is to advise bidders this opportunity is live on e-Tender Wales until 10:00 on 12/10/2026. The Senedd requires software solutions to support media monitoring, press office management, social media management and social media listening activities. These services play an important role in helping the Senedd understand the reach, impact and effectiveness of its communications activity, monitor public and media discussion, and support engagement with people across Wales. The procurement has been structured into four separate lots to enable suppliers to bid for individual, multiple, or all lots with one or multiple systems. Lot 1: Media Monitoring. The software is required to monitor keywords on local, national and UK-wide media. This will include print, digital and broadcast media. The system must be able to monitor Welsh language media, and be able to collate coverage. Lot 2: Press Office Management. The Senedd's News Team requires a press office management system to support media relations, enquiry handling, contact management and media distribution activities. The system should help improve efficiency, strengthen relationships with journalists and ensure organisational knowledge is retained and shared across the team. Lot 3: Social Media Management. The software should enable the Senedd to efficiently plan, publish, manage, monitor and evaluate content across its official social media channels. It should support day-to-day communications activity, audience engagement, campaign delivery and performance reporting. Lot 4: Social Media Listening. The software should provide comprehensive monitoring, analysis and reporting of online conversations relevant to the Senedd, supporting proactive reputation management, audience insight, campaign evaluation and early identification of emerging issues. The Commission may purchase more user licences, credits or other consumables based on unforeseen demand and needs.
sig_82391277c8002fad1f98.title: Media Monitoring Software

sig_8276de9a42260431b0f2.description: By the present procurement procedure, the EIT KIC Urban Mobility S.L. hereby being referred to as “EIT UM” or the “Company” is aiming to identify a provider (hereinafter, referred to as “Provider”) to support the Digital Platform for EIT Urban Mobility community, presently known as “Mobility Innovators”. This document, along with its annexes, constitute a Request for Proposal (RFP) issued by EIT Urban Mobility for a potential procurement of services in the field of online communities. EIT Urban Mobility community is made of over 270 partners and larger ecosystem of more than 1,200 stakeholders as we work together to make the transition to more sustainable urban mobility and liveable urban spaces. This community includes industry, including large enterprises, SMEs, and startups, universities and education institutions; students and alumni; research and technology organisations; governments at local, regional, national and EU-level; and non-governmental organisations (NGOs). Two years ago, EIT Urban Mobility launched its private digital community platform, Mobility Innovators, which brings together our vibrant community of innovators described above. The platform already has more than 1,500 active users and serves as the central platform for collaboration and engagement within our community. Mobility Innovators enables partners and stakeholders to access information, documents and opportunities shared by EIT Urban Mobility, register for events, and engage in discussions with peers across sectors. It connects organisations from industry, research, academia, and the public sector, fostering collaboration to advance the transition towards more sustainable and liveable urban mobility. Our goal in this next phase is to further grow and activate the community, expand platform functionalities, and enhance user experience to ensure Mobility Innovators continues to support EIT Urban Mobility’s role as Europe’s leading innovation community for urban mobility.
sig_8276de9a42260431b0f2.title: Rfp Digital & Private Platform for EIT Urban Mobility Community - “Mobility Innovators”, 26-28

sig_82fc41a02c6ce982dcca.description: This tender opportunity is being issued by Homerton Healthcare NHS Foundation Trust who is acting as the contracting Authority for the procurement of a Finance & Accounting Procure-to-Pay (P2P) System. Suppliers are invited to submit proposals that meet the requirements of both organisations, in alignment with the scope and specifications. sig_834b50668c90225a3c0c.description: At the NAO, we have a business need to access reliable market and financial information to inform our financial audit and value for money audit work. Around 50 financial audit teams across the office accessed these services in the 2025-26 cycle. This is a business-critical need, used in providing independent evidence to support key assumptions in asset and liability valuations and historical pricing. Our value for money audit work also requires access to high-quality market, corporate, financial, geopolitical and sector intelligence that is not readily available through standard internet searches or publicly available government sources. We require the provision of a product that provides quick and efficient access to asset and liability prices as well as economic and market data. The minimum requirements for this service are as follows: • A software product capable of meeting International Standard on Auditing (ISA) 500 requirements that provides quick and efficient access to asset and liability prices, such as bonds, equities and fund investments in both a real-time and historic basis, and the ability to price derivative instruments such as interest rate swaps. • The software must also provide economic and market data such as current and past FX rates, access to financial indexes, basic company financial and performance metrics, sovereign and corporate credit ratings, macroeconomic data and forecasts (such as GDP). • We require flexibility to retrieve data for a variety of dates and timepoints and in different formats for larger vs smaller volume requirements. The volume of data we require varies from day to day and the software should be able to accommodate changes in the volume of requests without compromising service or performance, as well as high-volume requests. • Unlimited access to a dedicated helpdesk to help resolve routine queries over functionality and performance, as well as more complex aspects of the software. In addition, access to an account manager is required, who can efficiently resolve any issues with the software. • Regular training, as well as the opportunity to occasionally engage in 'deep dives' i.e. more detailed questions surrounding methodology (such as valuations for particular financial instruments or datasets). Both of these benefits are required at no extra cost above the core subscription. • The software itself must be available for use year-round and for 24hrs a day. Any supplier IT/service outages must be resolved promptly and as a priority. • Ability to retain retrieved data on our audit files in accordance with statutory requirements is essential. The provider must permit the unrestricted retention and storage of market data and supporting evidence on NAO audit files, ensuring compliance with audit methodology and quality requirements. sig_8453eb2b8e3eacbbb0c9.description: NOTE: Updated submission in below text now reflects a 9 Oct 26 date in line with the General Information submission date. This Request for Information (RFI) is issued for informational and market research purposes only in accordance with RFO (Revolutionary FAR Overhaul) Part 10. It does not constitute a solicitation, a Request for Proposal (RFP), or a promise to issue RFP in the future. The Government will not reimburse any company or individual for expenses associated with preparing or submitting information in response to this RFI. The information provided may be used by the U.S. Air Force in developing its acquisition strategy, Statement of Work (SOW), and performance specifications. Interested parties are responsible for adequately marking proprietary or competition-sensitive information. BACKGROUND / DESCRIPTION The United States Air Force (USAF) operates a fleet of MH-139A aircraft for security and support missions. The aircraft is primarily used for security and transportation patrols across extensive intercontinental ballistic missile (ICBM) fields, while supporting search and rescue missions, and personnel/cargo transport. The aircraft platform is a commercial Leonardo AW139 helicopter modified by Boeing for military use. The existing fleet is twenty-six (26) aircraft with approximately thirty (30) additional aircraft planned in production. The fleet is disseminated at six (6) CONUS AFB locations. SCOPE OF REQUIRED CAPABILITIES The Air Force Materiel Command (AFMC) is seeking information from industry sources on the potential capability to provide Contractor Logistics Support (CLS) Services for the MH-139A (Grey Wolf) helicopter platform. The information provided by industry responders will be used to assess logistical support capability from contractors in the marketplace to assist the United States Government (USG) in refining its acquisition strategy as the MH-139A fleet transitions from its current Interim Contractor Support (ICS) and Interim Supply Support (ISS) postures to continued sustainment. The functional areas include, but are not limited to the list below:? Material Acquisitions Purchasing Management Support for Helicopter Rotable/Repairable Assets, Parts, and major Line Replaceable Units (LRUs) (e.g., engines, main gearboxes): Manage high-value components that can be physically repaired and reused rather than thrown away as well as disposable items that may or may not have a life limit. Purchasing Management Support for Consumable/Expendable Support: Manage a consumables program of parts as well as sourcing “one-time use” items required for daily maintenance. Purchasing Management Support for Test and Support Equipment: Procuring the specialized tools, stands, and calibration equipment necessary to test aircraft systems and to perform depot-level maintenance. Procurement Planning:?Execute timely, "just-in-time" procurement of scheduled maintenance materials to ensure parts are on hand prior to the commencement of heavy inspection events, minimizing aircraft downtime.? Inventory Management Inventory Stores Management: Operating the physical warehouse on base, tracking stock levels, and ensuring parts are ready for immediate issue to the flightline. Tool Crib Support Management: Manage and track check-in/check-out tooling usage for daily maintenance activity. Spares Management and APSR Integration: Maintain 100% floor-to-ceiling accountability of all Government Furnished Property (GFP) and spares using an approved DoD Accountable Property System of Record (APSR) (e.g., ELMS) that provides Total Asset Visibility (TAV) to the Government. Support Equipment (SE) Transition: Execute a 100% joint inventory, resolve discrepancies, and manage the physical relocation of all SE and tooling from incumbent facilities to operational bases, while maintaining strict calibration (AFMETCAL) and diagnostic software version control. FIAR and Accountability: Ensure strict adherence to Financial Improvement and Audit Readiness (FIAR) guidance by sustaining verifiable audit trails for all asset lifecycle transactions, enabling accurate financial valuation, and supporting independent audits to guarantee total operational accountability." Maintenance Management Heavy (Depot Level) Maintenance Management Unscheduled / Time Inspection Events Unscheduled Hourly Inspection Events: Inspections triggered strictly by aircraft flight hours Depot Flow Plan (DFP): Develop, maintain, and execute a comprehensive Depot Flow Plan (DFP) detailing aircraft retrofit and modification schedules to be coordinated with the SPO. Over and Above (O&A) Management: Possess a structured process to identify, document, estimate, and execute O&A repairs for unprogrammed work (e.g., severe corrosion or structural defects) discovered during inspections. Analytical Condition Inspections (ACI): Integrate structured ACI activities into planned depot work to foreclose structural integrity risks. Depot component Level Maintenance Management Scheduled / Time Inspection Events Maintainers must proactively execute TCTOs and engineering directives. Maintainers must also submit, respond to, and resolve technical requests, coordinating directly with Field Service Representatives and OEM engineers as required. Scheduled Hourly Inspection Events: Inspections triggered strictly by aircraft flight hours Modifications, Technical Order/Engineering Order event activity: Physically installing hardware/software upgrades or safety modifications on the aircraft flightline Depot-level repair actions must comply with directed TCTOs and engineering dispositions. Heavy (Depot Level) Maintenance Management Unscheduled / Time Inspection Events Unscheduled Hourly Inspection Events: Inspections triggered strictly by aircraft flight hours Reliability and Engineering Data Analysis: The contractor shall establish a robust data analytics program to provide the Government with full transparency into component lifecycle health. This includes conducting continuous Failure Modes, Effects, and Criticality Analysis (FMECA) and providing detailed maintenance shop data. The contractor must generate and report true Reliability, Availability, and Maintainability (RAM) metrics (e.g., Mean Time Between Failure [MTBF], Mean Time To Repair [MTTR]) for both the airframe and individual components Component Depot Level Maintenance Activity Repair Order Management – Outsourcing Service Orders Component Warranty Management Component Modifications Programs Airworthiness Directives, TCTOs, Service Bulletins, Service Information Letters: Monitoring and implementing FAA, OEM, or military airworthiness alerts to ensure the aircraft remains legally certified to fly. Contract Field Team Provide CFTs for tasks requiring shop facilities, tooling, support equipment, processes beyond organizational level capability technical manuals, and/or personnel of higher technical skills. Field Team Logistics: For all CFT deployments, the contractor shall be solely responsible for coordinating all personnel requirements, scheduling work, obtaining workspace, securing base access/clearances, and provisioning all required tools and Support Equipment. Engineering Support OEM Engineering Reach-Back and Data Currency: The contractor shall establish and maintain a direct line of communication and authorized data exchange with the Type Certificate (TC) holder (Leonardo). Technical Order and Engineering Order Management STC Management Deficiency Report Analysis and Investigation Health and Usage Monitoring Systems (HUMS): The contractor shall utilize aircraft diagnostic data (e.g., from HUMS/HELIWISE systems) to actively review fleet health, predict component degradation, and recommend proactive or unscheduled maintenance prior to catastrophic failure. Reliability and Maintainability Management Program (RAMMP): Manage a formal RAMMP in accordance with the Life Cycle Sustainment Plan (LCSP) to address, track, and correct R&M problems. This includes providing analysis to the SPO to help prioritize product improvements and tracking the implementation of all approved modifications by individual tail number. Technical Publications and Documentation: Demonstrate?authorized access to, and the authority to use, all OEM proprietary technical data, drawings, maintenance manuals, and engineering dispositions necessary to perform the?1200-hour?and four-year?inspections?on the AW139/MH-139A platform.? OEM Portal and Technical Data Reach-Back: The contractor must secure and maintain direct, authorized access into Leonardo's customer portal (Wingman Portal) to download and manage the distribution of all technical publications, including Service Bulletins, Service Information Letters, manual maintenance revisions, and Flight Manuals. This includes access to Interactive Electronic Technical Publications (IETP) and a regular summary of IETP changes. The contractor must also possess a clear process to receive and propose updates to Flight Manuals based on changing military operational profiles. ?? Sustainment/Obsolescence Program: PMA Management DER/ODA Management DMSMS monitoring, surveillance, and mitigation Parts Development and Redesign Program for Obsolescence Items Obsolescence Working Group (OWG): Provide active representation to the program's OWG to assess supply chain risks, react to obsolescence challenges, and evaluate alternate part sourcing. Spares Requirements Review Board (SRRB) for the replenishment of the sustainment of spares. This excludes all initial spares. Personnel and Certifications:?Personnel should hold appropriate FAA certifications (e.g., A&P licenses) and possess at least five years of experience with this specific airframe or comparable complex, commercial-derivative rotary-wing platforms." Implement robust workforce management plan addressing recruitment, retention, and succession planning to ensure long-term program stability and minimize turnover risk.? Possess the capability to provide familiarization and over-the-shoulder training to?Government personnel, as?required, on specific maintenance procedures or contractor-managed?logistics?systems. ?? Supply Chain and Logistics:?Supply Chain and Logistics: Demonstrate a robust supply chain management system for sourcing, stocking, and managing the repair of all assets, including major Line Replaceable Units (LRUs) and engines. This system must utilize historical fleet data to conduct advanced supply modeling and predictive data analysis, actively forecast failure rates, plan/schedule maintenance events, and ensure parts are prepositioned to support complex troubleshooting and repair actions. Predictive Logistics and Consumption Tracking: Demonstrate a robust supply chain management system for sourcing, stocking, and managing the repair of all assets. The contractor must utilize historical fleet data to conduct advanced supply modeling. sig_8483447c0cd102b900be.description: The project will develop a coherent framework for understanding how territorial cohesion and resilience operate under conditions of persistent low growth, demographic contraction and structural decline. Based on European-wide territorial mapping, it will elaborate typologies of territories facing persistent low growth and demographic contraction, and produce territorial maps of vulnerability, adaptive capacity and resilience. Through comparative qualitative case studies across different territorial contexts, it will document adaptive territorial practices and governance innovations. Finally, the project will offer practical policy guidance suggesting how cohesion policy, territorial governance and resilience planning frameworks may need to evolve in response to persistent low growth and structural territorial contraction.
sig_8483447c0cd102b900be.title: ESPON ARISE - Adaptive Resilience and Inclusive Strategies for Europe’s Structurally Declining Territories

sig_8504c197352dd25adf51.description: The tender concerns the procurement of an AI mammography solution for the Region of Southern Denmark and the Central Denmark Region, respectively. This is an IT system. As far as the Central Denmark Region is concerned, this is an option only. The Central Denmark Region may therefore choose to exercise or refrain from exercising the option to purchase an AI mammography solution. As a result of an increased population and an increasing average age in the population, an increase in the incidence of breast cancer is being seen in Denmark. An increase is expected from approx. 4.800 in 2024 to approx. 5310 cases of breast cancer in 2028. Early detection through breast cancer screening and best-practice treatment are considered crucial elements for reducing breast cancer-related mortality and morbidity in women. The breast cancer screening programme in the Region of Southern Denmark performs approx. 70.000 screenings annually. In addition, approx. 17.000 clinical mammography examinations are carried out annually. It is expected that approx. 10% of the clinical mammography examinations will be performed as tomosynthesis. For the Central Denmark Region, approx. 65.000 screenings and approx. 15.000 clinical mammography examinations are performed annually. Each screening examination consists of 4 X-ray images, 2 standard projections per breast. In cases of previous breast cancer and breast-conserving surgery, this is supplemented with a 3. projection. Today, each individual X-ray image is examined by two independent breast radiologists. If there is disagreement, the images are reviewed by a 3. examination. There is generally an increasing demand for breast diagnostics. Among other things, an increasing number of patients are being referred for investigation in fast-track breast cancer pathways as a result of an increase in the screening population as well as new investigation and treatment options. At the same time as the increasing need for mammography examinations, there is a nationwide challenge with a shortage of breast radiologists. Artificial intelligence (AI) solutions based on deep learning technology have in recent years shown great progress within medical image analysis, particularly with regard to the detection of breast cancer on mammograms. The tendered AI solution must be implemented at the Region of Southern Denmark's four hospital units (Odense University Hospital, Hospital Lillebælt, Hospital Sønderjylland and Esbjerg/Grindsted Hospital), which perform mammography examinations. The purpose of the acquisition of an AI mammography solution is therefore • to ensure that the national requirements for breast cancer screening can be maintained in the future, and • to free up breast radiologist resources for other tasks in connection with the detection of breast cancer. The solution must thus be able to relieve the "1. examiner" in the mammography screening programme as well as provide decision support in clinical mammography. Should the Central Denmark Region exercise the option, the solution for the Central Denmark Region will need to be installed at the following hospital units: Aarhus University Hospital, Regional Hospital Viborg and Regional Hospital Randers. The tender generally includes the following sub-services: • The AI solution itself • Installation, setup, operation and calibration of the system • Training of radiologists, system management and operating personnel • Maintenance and support of the AI solution As part of the tendered Contract, the following options are also offered for the Contracting Authority: • Possibility of using the AI solution in clinical mammography • Support for tomosynthesis (3D) in mammography screening • Purchase of additional screenings cf. Annex 3 Regarding options, reference is further made to the Draft Contract, clause 8, as well as Annex 2 and 3. The contract, including the Requirements Specification cf. Annexes 1, 2 and 8, contains a detailed description of the tendered products. The acceptance test in the Region of Southern Denmark is expected to be approved in early June 2026.
sig_8504c197352dd25adf51.title: Procurement of AI Mammography solution for the Region of Southern Denmark and the Central Denmark Region - Re-tendering

sig_854a54ad4f998e6cee70.description: Notice of Intent for Sole Source The Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) in Research Triangle Park (RTP) in Durham, North Carolina intends to award, on a sole source basis, and in accordance with RFO 6.103-1(b), a contract to AB SCIEX LLC for a Protective Equipment Maintenance Agreement (EMA) for the X500R Mass Spectrometer. This procurement is recommended to be processed without full and open competition. EPA’s Office of Chemical Safety and Pollution Prevention (OCSPP) Office of Mission Critical Operations, Risk Assessment Support Division’s Laboratory is needing a Protective EMA for the X500R Mass Spectrometer, which is needed to ensure proper equipment performance and reliability. This instrument is vital to generate data for many aspects of OCSPP’s mission to gain knowledge about chemicals and their associated effects on human health and the environment. The AB SCIEX LLC Protective EMA for the X500R Mass Spectrometer shall include: Service and maintenance that enables the equipment to operate and perform according to manufacturer’s specifications, without deviation. Documented verification that, after maintenance, instrument operation is fully consistent with manufacturer’s specifications, without deviation. Service by highly trained engineers who are factory trained and currently certified on the relevant systems by the instrument manufacturer to have the expertise necessary to maintain the systems. Replacement of components that cannot be repaired. Parts, labor, and travel for remedial repairs at no additional charge. Two preventative maintenance visits per year for the X500R QTOF mass spectrometer. One preventative maintenance visit per year for the LC system and gas generator. Use of certified AB Sciex replacement parts for optimal instrument performance. Use of replacement parts manufactured by AB Sciex or by AB Sciex’s partner vendors. Use of new or factory remanufactured replacement parts only. Response time of 48 hours or less for initiation of service (excluding weekends). Telephone and e-mail access for instrument technical support: Telephone and e-mail access for application support. System software (Analyst or OS software) maintenance and technical support (on-site, or by telephone or e-mail) for the X500R QTOF Mass Spectrometer, including version upgrades, online training, support for software use for installation, configuration, accessing and installing patches, instrument operations, data processing, accessing or developing scrips or macros, and templates. This Notice of Intent is not a request for proposals. This notice of intent is for information purposes only; therefore, no solicitation will result from this announcement. The intended contract will be awarded as a one year contract with two (2) - 12 month option periods. All capability statements received within 15 days after publication of this notice will be considered by the Government. Responses must be supported with clear and convincing evidence to clearly be able to provide theservices outlined and itemized pricing that is sufficient to make a determination that competition is feasible. A request for documentation will not be considered as an affirmative response. A determination by the Government not to compete based on responses to this notice is solely within the discretion of the Contracting Officer. Information received will be considered solely for the purpose of determining whether to conduct a competitive procurement. Submit questions or concerns via email (using PDF, MS Word, Excel attachments) to Contract Specialist, Jeremy Melby, at melby.jeremy@epa.gov. No telephone calls will be accepted. The NAICS code for this procurement is: 811412 – Appliance Repair and Maintenance

sig_855ece8a72cd97f0f3c4.description: The Klein Schietveld is part of the habitat directive area “Klein en Groot Schietveld”, BE2100016, Restoring the natural hydrology of the Klein Schietveld, quality improvement of groundwater-dependent vegetation, restoration and quality improvement of the fens and bank zones and creating connections between existing populations are some priority efforts for the habitat directive area. This is being investigated in an ecohydrological study of the Klein Schietveld. The ecohydrological study consists of two lots, with a focus on: - Lot 1: system research into the Klein Schietveld and restoration of the groundwater management, without compromising critical (military) infrastructure - Lot 2: on improving the hydrology and layout of the fens, taking into account the threatened species present Lot 2 is part of the implementation of layout measures for the LIFE project Life Heroes programme Marshes are among the most threatened ecosystems and the most important carbon stocks in the world. In addition to their unique biodiversity, they provide various ecosystem services, such as water supply, water purification, flood protection, carbon sequestration, climate regulation, production of raw materials and food, tourism and recreation. They also have significant aesthetic and cultural value. In the context of the European Biodiversity Strategy 2030 and the new EU Nature Restoration Law, LIFE HEROES focuses on restoring and expanding nutrient-poor marshlands in Flanders. Eutrophication, acidification, dehydration, overgrowth and invasive alien species are the greatest threats to the decline of unique fauna and flora (dragonflies, butterflies, amphibians and plants) and the degradation of the most important underground carbon reservoirs in Flanders. LIFE HEROES focuses on ecosystem restoration to address the current biodiversity and climate crisis and to restore ecosystem services of nutrient-poor wetlands. The project offers a first implementation of the EU Nature Restoration Law by prioritising restoration efforts related to wetlands and carbon-rich systems. The Life Heroes project focuses on Natura 2000 areas and targets EU habitats (3110, 3130, 3160, 7110, 7140, 7230,91E0) and addresses the main threats to wetlands (eutrophication, drought and invasive species). Within this framework, the specific objectives are as follows: A. Restoration of oligotrophic systems at landscape level B. Restoration of habitats and restoration of species C. Stakeholder engagement. On the specific assignment documents (work sheets, invoice,...) relating to this programme, the following reference must be used: Project 101215863 — LIFE24-NAT-BE-LIFE HEROES Lot 1: research into system operation and hydrological restoration of the Klein Schietveld.; LOT2: research into system operation and restoration of the fens in the northern part of the shooting range (LIFE HEROES)

sig_85675749643cdece19fd.description: Smart Applications Management Limited (SAM) is the trading name of South West Smart Applications Limited, a Membership based central purchasing body, which owns and runs the National Mobilities Procurement Hub for its Members. The Goods and Services will be supplied via Award Without Competition and by Competitive Selection Process. Lot 1 of this Framework is seeking the provision of On Vehicle Digital Technology (AVL, CCTV, APC, TLP, Comms, On Bus Destination, AVA, Bridge Strike Systems & Vehicle Compute Capability). Lot 1 - has 9 parts: Lot 1 - Part 1 - Automated Vehicle Location (AVL) Solution Provision of an integrated Automated Vehicle Location solution capable of accurately determining and communicating vehicle location in real time. The solution shall support route, journey and stop association, estimated arrival/departure information and integration with other onboard and back-office systems. Requirements include resilient positioning, industry-standard data interfaces, remote configuration, monitoring, diagnostics, reporting, security and ongoing support throughout the solution lifecycle. Lot 1 - Part 2 - Closed Circuit Television (CCTV) Solution Provision of a comprehensive onboard CCTV solution providing appropriate internal and external vehicle coverage for passenger safety, operational management and incident investigation. The solution shall support continuous high-quality recording, secure storage and retrieval, authorised access and evidential integrity. Requirements include integration with other onboard systems, equipment health monitoring, remote diagnostics, secure communications, configurable camera arrangements and enhanced analytics where required. Lot 1 - Part 3 - Automatic Passenger Counting (APC) Solution Provision of an Automatic Passenger Counting solution capable of accurately recording passenger boarding and alighting and determining vehicle occupancy without driver intervention. The solution shall provide reliable passenger-count data for operational, planning and passenger-information purposes and integrate with onboard and central systems. Requirements include appropriate counting accuracy, standardised interfaces, secure data transfer, reporting, monitoring, diagnostics, remote management and resilient operation. Lot 1 - Part 4 - Traffic Light Priority (TLP) Solution Provision of a Traffic Light Priority solution enabling suitably equipped vehicles to request priority at traffic signals based on vehicle location, route and operational circumstances. The solution shall support configurable and conditional priority strategies and integration with vehicle, roadside and central systems. Requirements include secure, low-latency communications, monitoring and reporting, remote configuration, interoperability, performance analysis, testing, cybersecurity and ongoing technical support. Lot 1 - Part 5 - Comms Tool (Radio) Solution Provision of an onboard communications solution enabling reliable and secure voice and data communication between drivers, vehicles and operational control functions. The solution shall support operational messaging, service information, alerts and emergency communications through an appropriate driver interface. Requirements include integration with other onboard systems, secure communications, operational logging, remote configuration, equipment monitoring, diagnostics and resilient operation across the vehicle fleet. Lot 1 - Part 6 - On-Bus Destination Solution Provision of integrated on-bus destination equipment capable of clearly displaying route and destination information to passengers and intending passengers. Solutions shall support appropriate front, side and rear displays, accessibility and visibility requirements and integration with onboard systems to automate displayed information. Requirements include remote configuration, operational overrides, equipment monitoring, diagnostics, secure communications, robust vehicle-grade equipment and ongoing maintenance and support. Lot 1 - Part 7 - Audio Visual Passenger Information (AVA) Solution Provision of an accessible onboard Audio Visual Passenger Information solution delivering automated visual and audible information concerning routes, destinations, next stops, disruptions and other relevant passenger messages. The solution shall integrate with vehicle location and onboard systems to trigger information accurately. Requirements include accessible presentation, remote and priority messaging, configurable content, secure communications, monitoring, diagnostics, resilient operation and ongoing system support. Lot 1 - Part 8 - Bridge Strike Prevention Solution Provision of an onboard Bridge Strike Prevention solution designed to reduce the risk of vehicles approaching or striking structures with insufficient clearance. The solution shall use vehicle dimensions together with accurate location, mapping and detection information to provide timely audible and visual driver warnings. Requirements include reliable hazard identification, minimisation of false alerts, offline resilience, secure updates, event logging, diagnostics and onboard-system integration. Lot 1 - Part 9 - Vehicle Compute Capability (VCC) Solution Provision of a robust onboard Vehicle Compute Capability providing a shared computing platform for hosting, integrating and managing multiple vehicle applications and data services. The solution shall provide sufficient processing capacity, storage and future scalability while supporting secure application separation and interoperability. Requirements include edge processing, secure communications, remote software management, monitoring and diagnostics, onboard-system integration and future expansion throughout its operational lifecycle. Lot 2 is for Franchising and Wider Transport Ticketing & Payment Consultancy Services. It has 6 Parts: Lot 2 - Part 1 - Franchised Bus Scheme Development and Implementation Support The provision of specialist consultancy services to support the development, assessment and implementation of bus franchising schemes. Services may include business cases, network and commercial design, financial modelling, consultation, procurement, mobilisation, integrated fares and ticketing, assets and technology, contract management, service permits, independent assurance and stakeholder engagement. Lot 2 - Part 2 - Transport Ticketing Management Policy Advice The provision of strategic, policy and management consultancy relating to transport ticketing and payment systems. Services may encompass ITSO, Stored Value, contactless EMV, barcode and QR ticketing, Account Based and Multi-Token Ticketing, Mobility as a Service, and wider ticketing initiatives across public-sector authorities, transport operators and national organisations. Lot 2 - Part 3 - Transport Ticketing Technical & Revenue Scheme Delivery The provision of technical consultancy and delivery support for transport ticketing schemes, including development of technical specifications, implementation and integration of ITSO and other ticketing technologies, Electronic Ticket Machines and ticketing readers. Services may also include management of multi-platform implementations and development of technical solutions through engagement with relevant stakeholders. Lot 2 - Part 4 - Transport Ticketing Governance, Research and Competitive Bidding Services The provision of specialist support relating to transport ticketing governance, research, procurement and competitive funding or bidding activities. Services may include governance advice for public and commercial organisations, preparation of grant, tender and franchise submissions, support for public procurement exercises, and research activities contributing to sustainable transport policy and delivery. Lot 2 - Part 5 - Entitlement (Concessionary) Travel Management Services The provision of management, policy and project support for entitlement and concessionary travel schemes, with particular emphasis on revenue reimbursement and apportionment. Services may include multi-operator and multimodal schemes, multiple ITSO HOPS and Customer Management Systems, and schemes operating across multiple ticketing channels, technologies and participating organisations. Lot 2 - Part 6 - Technical Entitlement (Concessionary) Support Services The provision of specialist technical support for entitlement and concessionary travel schemes, including reimbursement implementation, revenue modelling and apportionment, ETM data analysis, national reimbursement guidance and alternative allocation methodologies. sig_85b94feae9775980fa7f.description: The subject of the public contract is the development of digitalisation, standardisation and interoperability in all hospitals of the Nemocnice Plzeňského kraje (NPK) Group. The subject of the supplies for individual entities according to their specialisations is a hospital information system (HIS), the supply and implementation of an integration platform (ESB) for eHealth, which will ensure the sharing of medical documentation between NPK hospitals, the connection of hospital information systems to exchange networks, and central digital eHealth services (IDRR). The aim of the modernisation and consolidation of NPK hospital systems is the uniform standardisation of electronic medical documentation, the uniform implementation of eHealth identifiers and the use of reference data from master registers, and uniform connection to central eHealth services and exchange network services for the exchange and sharing of electronic health records of medical documentation with authorised recipients via information systems and technologies. The subject of performance also includes the modernisation of the existing HIS at Stodská nemocnice, a.s. A variant solution is the replacement of the existing system. The choice of the final solution will be decided during the competitive dialogue. The supplies of the integration platform (ESB) include interfaces and services for connection to the infrastructure of systems and services of the Accredited Affinity Domain (AAfD), the National Contact Point for eHealth (NCPeH) and the Integrated Data Interface for eHealth (IDRR), or other central services. The subject of the public contract further includes service provision for a period of 48 months for the modernised information systems, application software, related technologies and equipment.
sig_85b94feae9775980fa7f.title: EHEALTH IN HOSPITALS OF THE NEMOCNICE PLZEŇSKÉHO KRAJE GROUP – SUPPLY OF HIS, ESB AND INTEGRATIONS (2. announcement)

sig_85bec1a283e55de29bb2.description: Vantaan kaupunki is planning the procurement of a new cultural heritage system to replace the current collection management system (Kirsti), which was implemented in 2014. The current system is technically obsolete, slow, and difficult to develop. The goal is a modern, easy-to-use, and efficient solution that supports museum operations, cultural heritage management, and digital transition. The system must support, among other things, object, image, AV, paper, and cultural environment archives, a reference library, actor information, and press clippings. Integrations are required for Finna, Finto, MapInfo, Matti, the Finnish Heritage Agency's spatial data, and the PAS service. Key features: efficient search, clarity, ease of use, and compliance with GDPR requirements. Users: Museum staff, consultants, authorities, collection service customers, and the public via Finna. Targeted benefits: Better availability of information, increased work efficiency, reduction of unnecessary work, and improvement of processes. Strategic importance: supports the digital transition, has a broad impact, and generates value for over 10 000 residents.
sig_85bec1a283e55de29bb2.title: Procurement of a cultural heritage system

sig_85ff439fa2b3ba675ab9.description: The objective of the procurement is to enter into an agreement for the procurement of digital teaching aids and teaching resources for the Oslo School. The Oslo School has participated in a R&D project together with KS since 2017. the R&D project ends in its current form in summer 2024. In order to achieve autonomy and freedom of methodology in the choice of teaching aids, a use-based payment model is required where schools have access to all products and pay in arrears in arrears in accordance with actual use. Digital teaching aids and teaching resources consist of a market that is constantly developing. To a small degree, traditional approaches cover the schools ́need for flexible access to a wide range of teaching aids. The aim is also that an overall ecosystem shall make the procurement process of digital teaching aids and learning resources easier for school owners and more in line with the needs of the schools and pupils. The dynamic procurement scheme is for continuous delivery of digital teaching aids (freestanding or as part of teaching aids/learning universe), teaching resources, resource banks (news, pictures, movies, audio, music, etc.), teacher guides, teacher resources, assignment/trial collections and mapping tool with accompanying teacher overview, glosses, etc. that are delivered over the internet ("Software-as-a-service") for teaching purposes. The agreement also includes digital books and installed apps with Feide sign-in for teaching purposes. The diagnostic tool, which requires special competence to use, is not included. Digital services, which only have a functionality for delivering teaching aids that shall be physically implemented, are also not included. The agreement does not include the purchase of services that do not have Feide sign-in, including apps for iPads that are purchased via the App Store/Apple School Manager.

sig_8608455ddad914e0e75c.description: This notice (PIN) announces a public market consultation and provides information on a planned pre-commercial procurement (PCP) on the subject of the "Low-Voltage Toolkit". The project responds to the need for a cost-effective, scalable, platform-independent and user-friendly toolkit for active distribution network management in low-voltage networks – particularly for small and medium-sized distribution network operators and municipal utilities. The toolkit is intended to include the following core functions: (1) Visualisation of the low-voltage network through automated data integration, processing and modelling, which brings together measurement data, network documentation and external information (e.g. weather and market data). (2) Reliable low-voltage state estimation (LV DSSE), which delivers robust statements on voltages, currents and loads even with low measurement density and in near real time. (3) Automated topology detection, which detects and corrects erroneous or incomplete network diagrams and also correctly maps complex urban structures. (4) Forecasting models that identify bottlenecks and voltage violations at an early stage and incorporate external information (e.g. weather and market data). (5) Comprehensible decision support for network operators, including via user-friendly visualisations, recommendations for action and warnings that can be integrated into existing workflows. (6) Semi-automated congestion management with transparent workflows ("Suggest – Evaluate – Confirm – Execute") instead of fully automated network operation. (7) Plug-and-play approach for integration into a large proportion of existing infrastructures at distribution network operators; the tools are intended to be modularly introduceable (e.g. initially only a topology detection module or state estimator), in contrast to current solutions which often require extensive hardware conversions and high investments. Those addressed are in particular small and medium-sized distribution network operators, municipal utilities, manufacturers of network control and planning software, data platform providers as well as research institutions with relevant expertise. Further information on the upcoming public market consultation and the planned PCP can be found here http://go.fzj.de/2eVf9 in the German language.
sig_8608455ddad914e0e75c.title: Pre-commercial procurement (PCP) of research and development services for a toolkit for active low-voltage distribution network management.

sig_8634aabaa94ddd059a39.description: This Request for Information (RFI) is issued for informational and market research purposes only in accordance with RFO (Revolutionary FAR Overhaul) Part 10. It does not constitute a solicitation, a Request for Proposal (RFP), or a promise to issue RFP in the future. The Government will not reimburse any company or individual for expenses associated with preparing or submitting information in response to this RFI. The information provided may be used by the U.S. Air Force in developing its acquisition strategy, Statement of Work (SOW), and performance specifications. Interested parties are responsible for adequately marking proprietary or competition-sensitive information. BACKGROUND / DESCRIPTION The United States Air Force (USAF) operates a fleet of MH-139A aircraft for security and support missions. The aircraft is primarily used for security and transportation patrols across extensive intercontinental ballistic missile (ICBM) fields, while supporting search and rescue missions, and personnel/cargo transport. The aircraft platform is a commercial Leonardo AW139 helicopter modified by Boeing for military use. The existing fleet is twenty-six (26) aircraft with approximately thirty (30) additional aircraft planned in production. The fleet is disseminated at six (6) CONUS AFB locations. SCOPE OF REQUIRED CAPABILITIES The Air Force Materiel Command (AFMC) is seeking information from industry sources on the potential capability to provide Contractor Logistics Support (CLS) Services for the MH-139A (Grey Wolf) helicopter platform. The information provided by industry responders will be used to assess logistical support capability from contractors in the marketplace to assist the United States Government (USG) in refining its acquisition strategy as the MH-139A fleet transitions from its current Interim Contractor Support (ICS) and Interim Supply Support (ISS) postures to continued sustainment. The functional areas include, but are not limited to the list below:? Material Acquisitions Purchasing Management Support for Helicopter Rotable/Repairable Assets, Parts, and major Line Replaceable Units (LRUs) (e.g., engines, main gearboxes): Manage high-value components that can be physically repaired and reused rather than thrown away as well as disposable items that may or may not have a life limit. Purchasing Management Support for Consumable/Expendable Support: Manage a consumables program of parts as well as sourcing “one-time use” items required for daily maintenance. Purchasing Management Support for Test and Support Equipment: Procuring the specialized tools, stands, and calibration equipment necessary to test aircraft systems and to perform depot-level maintenance. Procurement Planning:?Execute timely, "just-in-time" procurement of scheduled maintenance materials to ensure parts are on hand prior to the commencement of heavy inspection events, minimizing aircraft downtime.? Inventory Management Inventory Stores Management: Operating the physical warehouse on base, tracking stock levels, and ensuring parts are ready for immediate issue to the flightline. Tool Crib Support Management: Manage and track check-in/check-out tooling usage for daily maintenance activity. Spares Management and APSR Integration: Maintain 100% floor-to-ceiling accountability of all Government Furnished Property (GFP) and spares using an approved DoD Accountable Property System of Record (APSR) (e.g., ELMS) that provides Total Asset Visibility (TAV) to the Government. Support Equipment (SE) Transition: Execute a 100% joint inventory, resolve discrepancies, and manage the physical relocation of all SE and tooling from incumbent facilities to operational bases, while maintaining strict calibration (AFMETCAL) and diagnostic software version control. FIAR and Accountability: Ensure strict adherence to Financial Improvement and Audit Readiness (FIAR) guidance by sustaining verifiable audit trails for all asset lifecycle transactions, enabling accurate financial valuation, and supporting independent audits to guarantee total operational accountability." Maintenance Management Heavy (Depot Level) Maintenance Management Unscheduled / Time Inspection Events Unscheduled Hourly Inspection Events: Inspections triggered strictly by aircraft flight hours Depot Flow Plan (DFP): Develop, maintain, and execute a comprehensive Depot Flow Plan (DFP) detailing aircraft retrofit and modification schedules to be coordinated with the SPO. Over and Above (O&A) Management: Possess a structured process to identify, document, estimate, and execute O&A repairs for unprogrammed work (e.g., severe corrosion or structural defects) discovered during inspections. Analytical Condition Inspections (ACI): Integrate structured ACI activities into planned depot work to foreclose structural integrity risks. Depot component Level Maintenance Management Scheduled / Time Inspection Events Maintainers must proactively execute TCTOs and engineering directives. Maintainers must also submit, respond to, and resolve technical requests, coordinating directly with Field Service Representatives and OEM engineers as required. Scheduled Hourly Inspection Events: Inspections triggered strictly by aircraft flight hours Modifications, Technical Order/Engineering Order event activity: Physically installing hardware/software upgrades or safety modifications on the aircraft flightline Depot-level repair actions must comply with directed TCTOs and engineering dispositions. Heavy (Depot Level) Maintenance Management Unscheduled / Time Inspection Events Unscheduled Hourly Inspection Events: Inspections triggered strictly by aircraft flight hours Reliability and Engineering Data Analysis: The contractor shall establish a robust data analytics program to provide the Government with full transparency into component lifecycle health. This includes conducting continuous Failure Modes, Effects, and Criticality Analysis (FMECA) and providing detailed maintenance shop data. The contractor must generate and report true Reliability, Availability, and Maintainability (RAM) metrics (e.g., Mean Time Between Failure [MTBF], Mean Time To Repair [MTTR]) for both the airframe and individual components Component Depot Level Maintenance Activity Repair Order Management – Outsourcing Service Orders Component Warranty Management Component Modifications Programs Airworthiness Directives, TCTOs, Service Bulletins, Service Information Letters: Monitoring and implementing FAA, OEM, or military airworthiness alerts to ensure the aircraft remains legally certified to fly. Contract Field Team Provide CFTs for tasks requiring shop facilities, tooling, support equipment, processes beyond organizational level capability technical manuals, and/or personnel of higher technical skills. Field Team Logistics: For all CFT deployments, the contractor shall be solely responsible for coordinating all personnel requirements, scheduling work, obtaining workspace, securing base access/clearances, and provisioning all required tools and Support Equipment. Engineering Support OEM Engineering Reach-Back and Data Currency: The contractor shall establish and maintain a direct line of communication and authorized data exchange with the Type Certificate (TC) holder (Leonardo). Technical Order and Engineering Order Management STC Management Deficiency Report Analysis and Investigation Health and Usage Monitoring Systems (HUMS): The contractor shall utilize aircraft diagnostic data (e.g., from HUMS/HELIWISE systems) to actively review fleet health, predict component degradation, and recommend proactive or unscheduled maintenance prior to catastrophic failure. Reliability and Maintainability Management Program (RAMMP): Manage a formal RAMMP in accordance with the Life Cycle Sustainment Plan (LCSP) to address, track, and correct R&M problems. This includes providing analysis to the SPO to help prioritize product improvements and tracking the implementation of all approved modifications by individual tail number. Technical Publications and Documentation: Demonstrate?authorized access to, and the authority to use, all OEM proprietary technical data, drawings, maintenance manuals, and engineering dispositions necessary to perform the?1200-hour?and four-year?inspections?on the AW139/MH-139A platform.? OEM Portal and Technical Data Reach-Back: The contractor must secure and maintain direct, authorized access into Leonardo's customer portal (Wingman Portal) to download and manage the distribution of all technical publications, including Service Bulletins, Service Information Letters, manual maintenance revisions, and Flight Manuals. This includes access to Interactive Electronic Technical Publications (IETP) and a regular summary of IETP changes. The contractor must also possess a clear process to receive and propose updates to Flight Manuals based on changing military operational profiles. ?? Sustainment/Obsolescence Program: PMA Management DER/ODA Management DMSMS monitoring, surveillance, and mitigation Parts Development and Redesign Program for Obsolescence Items Obsolescence Working Group (OWG): Provide active representation to the program's OWG to assess supply chain risks, react to obsolescence challenges, and evaluate alternate part sourcing. Spares Requirements Review Board (SRRB) for the replenishment of the sustainment of spares. This excludes all initial spares. Personnel and Certifications:?Personnel should hold appropriate FAA certifications (e.g., A&P licenses) and possess at least five years of experience with this specific airframe or comparable complex, commercial-derivative rotary-wing platforms." Implement robust workforce management plan addressing recruitment, retention, and succession planning to ensure long-term program stability and minimize turnover risk.? Possess the capability to provide familiarization and over-the-shoulder training to?Government personnel, as?required, on specific maintenance procedures or contractor-managed?logistics?systems. ?? Supply Chain and Logistics:?Supply Chain and Logistics: Demonstrate a robust supply chain management system for sourcing, stocking, and managing the repair of all assets, including major Line Replaceable Units (LRUs) and engines. This system must utilize historical fleet data to conduct advanced supply modeling and predictive data analysis, actively forecast failure rates, plan/schedule maintenance events, and ensure parts are prepositioned to support complex troubleshooting and repair actions. Predictive Logistics and Consumption Tracking: Demonstrate a robust supply chain management system for sourcing, stocking, and managing the repair of all assets. The contractor must utilize historical fleet data to conduct advanced supply modeling. Crucially, the contractor must track and report both component failure rates AND true consumption rates to prevent obscured sustainment costs. This data must be actively used to plan/schedule maintenance events and ensure parts are prepositioned to support complex troubleshooting and repair actions. Cybersecurity Risk Management Framework: manage all aspects of cybersecurity in accordance with DoDI 8510.01. This includes obtaining and maintaining a platform level Authority to Operate. Facility and Quality Certifications: Part 145 Repair Station: The contractor's facilities performing heavy maintenance, depot-level component repair, and major inspections shall be certified in accordance with 14 CFR Part 145. Part 142 Training Center: Contractor personnel operating and supporting simulator training devices shall follow quality and instructional standards commensurate with 14 CFR Part 142. INFORMATION REQUESTED FROM INTERESTED PARTIES? Interested parties are requested to provide a capability statement addressing the following items. Please limit your response to no more than ten fifteen (15) pages.? Company Information:? Company Name, Address, and Website Point of Contact (Name, Title, Email, Phone) CAGE Code and Unique Entity ID (UEI) Financial System Capability: Confirm your organization's capability to invoice and process payments electronically via the Government's mandated Wide Area Workflow (WAWF) / Procurement Integrated Enterprise Environment (PIEE) system. Business Size Status under NAICS 488190 (e.g., Small Business, 8(a), Woman-Owned, etc.) Business Size Status under NAICS Code 336413 (Aircraft Manufacturing), with a size standard of 1,500 employees. Please self-certify for all applicable categories: Small Business (Yes/No) Woman-Owned Small Business (WOSB) (Yes/No) HUBZone Certified (Yes/No) Service-Disabled Veteran-Owned Small Business (SDVOSB) (Yes/No) Company Ownership (Domestic or Foreign-owned). Capability Narrative Technical Capability, Logistics, and Sustainment:? Provide a detailed narrative describing your company's ability to meet the requirements outlined in Section 3.0. Describe your facility, its size, location, and the specific strategic business unit of your organization that possesses the logistics support activity; please detail if any experience is on Leonardo helicopters. Explain the basis of your authority to access and use OEM proprietary engineering data, diagnostic software, and technical documentation. Describe the training, certifications, and experience level of your technical workforce as it relates to this airframe. Facility Certifications: Describe your organization's FAA certifications. Specifically, detail your status as a 14 CFR Part 145 Certified Repair Station and your experience operating in compliance with 14 CFR Part 142 Training Center standards. Describe your company's process for managing the supply chain for a major inspection event. RAM Metrics and Consumption Analytics: Describe your capability to perform FMECA and generate accurate RAM metrics (MTBF, MTTR). Specifically, how will your organization track and report true component consumption rates to the Government, distinct from standard failure rates, to ensure full transparency of sustainment costs? Past Performance and Relevant Experience: Provide a brief summary of up to three (3) relevant contracts from the past five (5) years where your company provided?depot-level maintenance or?comparable heavy inspections on complex rotary-wing?aircraft. Experience on the Leonardo AW139 is highly preferred. Include contract?numbers, customer, period of performance, and a brief description of the work performed. SUBMISSION INSTRUCTIONS Responses shall not exceed 15 pages (single-sided, 12-point font). Submit responses electronically by?3:00 PM Eastern Time on [10/01/2026]. Mark all proprietary information clearly. Unmarked information will be considered publicly releasable. Be advised that government-contracted support personnel may handle submissions under non-disclosure agreements. Prospective contractors must be registered in the System for Award Management (SAM) at?https://www.sam.gov.

sig_86a204079f2c82c65933.description:
WISTA stands for Wissenschafts- und Wirtschaftsstandort Adlershof and is a state-of-the-art technology park in the Adlershof district of Berlin (Treptow-Köpenick borough). It is considered one of the most advanced high-tech parks in Europe and is a central hub for science, business, and start-ups. WISTA Adlershof is a location with an area of approx. 4,2 km2, approx. 1.300 companies, research institutions, and university institutes with 28.000 employees. The WISTA Management GmbH acts as a site developer, service provider, and economic promoter. It supports companies, research institutions, and start-ups at the site and fosters innovation and growth in the region. In addition to its real estate portfolio, WISTA possesses its own campus network, which consists of a high-performance cable network as well as a 5G infrastructure. The network has been continuously expanded and technologically developed since 1998 – from classic telephony and data services to Gigabit and 10G connections, cloud and UCC integration, campus-wide Wi-Fi and IoT applications, through to local 5G and current network 4.0 topics. It thus forms an essential digital infrastructure of the campus and is the subject of the expression of interest procedure. The attractiveness of the campus network stems from its established telecommunications infrastructure at a dynamically growing high-tech location. The network has an existing customer base, established line routes and network nodes, as well as redundant carrier connections. Additional development prospects arise from the continuous expansion of the campus through new buildings, the expansion potential for cloud, security, and UCC services, as well as the addition of a local 5G campus network. The campus network thus offers a resilient infrastructural foundation with further economic and technological growth potential. The reasons for the sale by WISTA are a strategic further development of the campus network by a specialised provider with qualified personnel and the necessary expertise. Subject of sale: Passive infrastructure (fibre optic, copper, conduits, manholes, cable distribution cabinets, building connections) Active infrastructure (switches, routers, servers, telecommunications system) Customer contracts (insofar as transferable, consent/transfers still to be checked) Frequency allocation 5G (not alienable, subsequent use/transfer still to be checked from a regulatory perspective, application for own allocation required) Land/line rights (insofar as transferable, easements/permissions still to be checked) Software/licences (insofar as transferable, licence terms still to be checked) Cable network: The WISTA campus network at the science and business location Adlershof forms the central communication infrastructure for voice and data services in the core area of the technology park. It currently serves around 400 customers as well as approx. 4.400 participants in the voice sector and is therefore an essential location factor for Germany's largest science and technology park. The existing infrastructure includes a high-performance cable duct system, a line network based on copper and fibre optics with a total length of almost 20 kilometres, as well as a Gigabit Ethernet backbone. Technically, fibre optic backbone connections, single-mode and multi-mode fibre optic cables, copper cables, copper cross-cables, and FM cables with 100 double cores are used in particular. At the active network and services level, the campus network includes transmission and switching equipment for voice and data communication, routing/switching components, data core and access areas, network gateways to wide area networks, as well as a communication network consisting of communication systems from the manufacturer Unify. The users' existing voice and data infrastructure is connected to the network; some users are connected via LAN ports under 100 Mbit/s or VDSL, while other users have connections from 100 Mbit/s. The WAN connection is designed to be redundant with at least two external carriers and has two redundant gateways with 100 Gbit/s. The campus network is particularly interesting as an established, operator-capable infrastructure with an existing customer base, available line routes, documented network gateways, and development potential. The future operator is to operate, maintain, further develop, and actively market the network to users on their own responsibility. In addition to the existing copper, fibre optic, and fibre infrastructure, the existing customers, the available telecommunications and data network components, the expansion potential at the growing Adlershof location, and the possibility of introducing new cloud, security, VoIP, and UCC services are of value. 5G network: The WISTA 5G campus network is designed as a local private 5G campus network at the science and business location Adlershof. It serves as a supplement to the existing cable infrastructure and is to be gradually expanded at outdoor and indoor locations. Initial expansion has been carried out in the area of Albert-Einstein-Straße 16 (central outdoor location) as well as in the showroom/a:head context (indoor location). The regulatory basis for the 5G infrastructure is a local frequency allocation by the Federal Network Agency for the frequency range 3.700–3.800 MHz. The allocation holder is WISTA Management GmbH. The allocated bandwidth is 100 MHz; the frequency allocation is limited until 20.02.2030. The allocation area covers an area of approx. 0,873273 km2. Technologically, the 5G infrastructure is based on a Nokia DAC/NDAC Medium+ environment with 5G standalone architecture, Edge Core, NDAC manager, Nokia AirScale components, HPE Edge servers, router and switching components, and SIM kit. WISTA Management GmbH intends to sell its cable network and 5G campus network at the science and business location Adlershof.

Only 99 years were stated as the duration because the announcement platform mandates the specification of a limited period. The sale is permanent and is not intended to be reversed after 99 years.
sig_86a204079f2c82c65933.title: Sale of campus network

sig_86b7cd8a6590a4b2e207.description: Supply, implementation, maintenance and support of an integrated LMS and VLE platform for digital training in Highway Code and Professional Competence. VDAB wishes to purchase a digital learning platform that supports VDAB clients and affiliated partners in preparing for the theoretical examinations for the various driving licence categories (including B, C, CE, D and DE) and the professional competence of professional drivers. The platform must prepare students for passing their theoretical driving test in an accessible, interactive and high-quality manner. The learning environment must be suitable for a broad target group, including job seekers, non-native speakers and students with diverse learning needs. The learning content offered must therefore be developed according to contemporary didactic principles and must focus as much as possible on: simple and clear language, adapted to students with limited language proficiency or a non-native background; a visual and interactive learning method in which complex traffic situations are made understandable; the use of animations, illustrations, videos and realistic traffic situations to present the subject matter in an attractive and contemporary way; sufficient exercises, simulations and feedback moments so that students can learn independently and evaluate their knowledge; a clear structure and user-friendly navigation, so that students can work at their own pace and level. The learning content must always be aligned with current regulations and official examination requirements regarding the highway code, driving licences and professional competence. The contractor is responsible for updating the content throughout the entire duration of the agreement in the event of changes to regulations, including changes to the Highway Code, the driving licence and professional competence. The platform must provide functionalities for monitoring learning paths, progress and student results. In addition, it must be compatible with the VDAB digital learning environment and offer efficient support to students, supervisors, teachers and administrators. The solution must contribute to the VDAB objective of guiding job seekers towards sustainable employment in an efficient and inclusive manner, particularly within shortage occupations such as transport and logistics.
sig_86b7cd8a6590a4b2e207.title: Supply, implementation and maintenance of an integrated LMS and VLE platform for highway code and professional competence
