Any interested economic operator has the right to request clarifications/additional information regarding the contract documents 22 days before the deadline set for the submission of tenders. The contracting authority shall respond clearly and completely to all requests for clarifications/additional information regarding the contract documents on the 12-th day before the tender submission deadline. The contracting authority will not respond to requests for clarifications submitted after the set deadline. Description of the products to be purchased and their destination: Processing and storage architecture Complex monitoring and storage solution Train traffic monitoring solution Processing and storage architecture A central component and a local component are provided. The initial architecture of the applications within the IRIS system was conceived in the context of activities distributed across railway locations throughout Romania to a radial topology network implemented with SDH technology and low transfer speed (32 kb/s for small work points and up to 1 Mb/s for large work points). For this reason, the applications were designed with a distributed architecture (client components on users' workstations, local servers) or with the elimination of the process/services layer. With technological evolution, data transmission speeds on the RENTRAD network have increased to a min. of 10 Mbps for locations with 1-2 workstations. In this way, conditions were created for the consolidation of operations in the central datacenter while maintaining local architectures in the regional agencies of Societatea Informatică Feroviară SA. The local architectures will implement virtualisation solutions and will be used for process/service servers and for the administration of regional IT infrastructure. In defining the requirements for the technical specifications, several objectives were pursued: - The architecture will be implemented in the form of several medium virtualisation clusters; - The virtualisation solutions were chosen according to the nature of the hosted applications (Oracle Virtualization for the Oracle environment, Hyper-V for the Windows application environment, and RedHat OpenShift for the containerised staging environment); - Separation of production and development/testing/training environments into distinct clusters in order to ensure safe testing conditions in the event of firmware updates; Use of virtualisation platforms that allow the implementation of multi-tenant solutions with isolation. In this way, zones with different security levels can be implemented on each cluster (critical production environments, development environments, testing workflows); - Separation of the storage platform into two components: - high-performance storage (all-flash, at least 4 controllers, NVMe transfer, high transfer rate, block only) for the production environment, - storage with a classical architecture (low transfer rate, low disk speed, large capacity, block and file) for historical data, cluster for DMZ and repository; - All servers will be of the enterprise class but with a general architecture so that they can be easily replaced in the event of a failure; - Network equipment must integrate into the architecture in operation in the central datacenter. The local component consists of two servers each, installed in the data rooms of the regional IT agencies, a NAS-type storage device and equipment. A NAS-type storage device identical to those in the regional agencies will be installed in the Informatică Feroviară datacenter and is intended for saving operational information, service documentation, and intermediate data. The solutions must have capacities for capacity expansion. Complex monitoring and cybersecurity solution The components of the solution must ensure the following functionalities: - Communications infrastructure monitoring: - Ensuring network visibility in the core zone and the datacenter router zone, - Monitoring traffic information in the core zone and the datacenter router zone; - Protecting the internal network through detection and response solutions against cyber attacks with a local sandbox environment; - Increasing the security level of essential services by ensuring: - Access management for privileged users (system and database administrators, content administrators, users with access to confidential and critical information); - Database access monitoring; - Vulnerability management; - Access control towards the TSM-ERTMS network; - Security information and event management (SIEM). Train traffic tracking solution This solution is addressed to the technical personnel within CNCFR involved in train traffic programming and tracking activities as well as to those in the railway traffic safety compartments. The following components are included: - Workstations for CNCFR personnel involved in the process of programming and tracking train traffic and in railway traffic safety; - Integrated system for the retrieval, display, and management of video sources which will retrieve information from the traffic tracking subsystem; - Videoconferencing solution. The products requested for the IT infrastructure targeted within this project create a computing platform with a complex central architecture and local (regional) architecture that allows the implementation of a high security level. Contract duration: 84 months (60 months representing the warranty period) from the date of signing the contract by both parties. sig_877e7905fb2f342203d2.description: BARMER is planning to transition its electronic patient record (ePA) to a future-proof, modular digital platform ("eCare App") and to make existing services as well as gematik-certified components flexibly integrable. The planned app architecture provides for decoupling central functionalities - app framework, gematik modules, insured persons' frontend as well as value-added services and TI components - from one another and providing them in a modular manner via standardised interfaces. The focus is on the development of an app framework with plug-in technology and the step-by-step integration of existing modules and services (e.g. laboratory values, medication lists, e-prescription, record management). sig_87e924f6c5a3b9ecd871.description: The University is seeking the provision, implementation, transition and ongoing support of a SaaS Enterprise Backup and Recovery solution. The SaaS solution shall integrate with the University's existing infrastructure and support the protection of workloads hosted across VMware, Microsoft Hyper-V, Proxmox and physical server environments. Lot 1: . The option is a cloud-based design platform, accessible via a secure web interface, offering enhanced scalability and reduced infrastructure overhead. The solution will integrate with a University of Dundee-hosted virtual machine to enable secure data exchange and computational workflows. Installation of server-side components will be managed by the DDU Data Management and Computational Chemistry teams, with network provisioning supported by DTS. Ongoing maintenance and updates will be provided by the vendor.

sig_8810568850dc2662a41a.description: The London Borough of Barnet (the "Council") is seeking to engage with the market in preparation for the procurement of Level 3 Oracle Cloud Fusion Support Services for its Oracle Cloud Fusion environment. This engagement is part of the Council’s strategic transition to a new support partner following the conclusion of its current post-implementation support contract. The Council is issuing this notice in accordance with Sections 16 and 17 of the Procurement Act 2023 to invite potential providers to participate in early market engagement activities. Please note: this is not a call for competition. Scope of the Requirement The Council is seeking a highly capable support partner with demonstrable experience supporting UK Local Authorities to provide Level 3 support across the following Oracle Cloud components: •Oracle SaaS (Fusion Applications): Finance, Procurement, Human Capital Management (HCM), Payroll, Time & Labour (OTL), iExpenses, and Enterprise Performance Management (EPM) •Oracle Integration Cloud (OIC) and Platform as a Service (PaaS) •Oracle Cloud Infrastructure (OCI) and Oracle Database •Custom integrations and reporting (OTBI, BI Publisher, SmartView, ADFDI) The successful partner will be expected to: •Resolve complex technical and functional issues escalated from the Council’s internal support team •Manage quarterly patching and environment refreshes •Provide strategic input into change governance and roadmap development •Deliver continuous improvement and value-added services, including automation and innovation •Support knowledge transfer and internal capability building A Market Engagement Event will be held on: Thursday 23 October 2025 Time: 11:30-12:30 Virtual (MS Teams) This session will provide an overview of the Council’s Oracle Cloud environment, support model, and procurement timeline. It will also offer an opportunity for suppliers to ask questions and provide feedback that may shape the final procurement approach. Next Steps Interested providers are encouraged to register their interest and attend the Market Engagement Event. Further details, including how to register, will be published alongside this notice. To view this notice, please click here: https://londonbarnet.delta-esourcing.com/delta/viewNotice.html?noticeId=982971474 Lot 1: .

sig_8827d073b9a26c3a1c19.description: The 22 july centre invites tenderers to participate in a market dialogue before the planned procurement of a digital partner. The aim of the market dialogue is to obtain input from the market on how the centre ́s total need for digital services can best be covered, including whether the market can deliver a comprehensive solution through one supplier, possibly with the use of sub-suppliers, or whether the need should be divided up. The 22 july centre is a national memorial and learning centre under the Ministry of Education and Research. The centre is facing several development processes connected to digital communication, teaching, communication and security. The need includes i.a. management and further development of the existing website, digital teaching systems, technical operations and security, monitoring and stand-by, communication services as well as the implementation of a new visual profile. The market dialogue will be carried out through a written input note, and individual tenderers may be invited to one-to-one meetings. Participation in the market dialogue is voluntary, does not obligate the parties and is not a prerequisite for participation in any later competition. The deadline for submitting the input note is Monday 04.05.2026, 12:00. The input note will be delivered by email: post@22julisenteret.no.

sig_885f62654a70046ee804.description: Heka is extensively renewing its information systems in the coming years. The most central objectives for all system development are improving the customer experience, digitising operating methods, and improving the quality of information supporting decision-making. The subject of this procurement is accounting and internal accounting, as well as accounts payable solutions, the related implementation project, and ongoing maintenance service. In addition, a budgeting system may be added to the procurement later based on a framework agreement. The solution package will be implemented at Heka and Heka's subsidiary, Kiinteistö Oy Laivalahdentori. The goal is a so-called off-the-shelf software solution that covers Heka's needs. The primary objective is to procure the solution as a cloud or SaaS service. The solution must enable flexible integrations with systems outside the procured solution. Systems already in use and the renewing solutions must function side-by-side as a whole, relying on the existing technical environment where necessary. It must be possible to transfer the data required in the solution from source systems and to source systems via a data warehouse. Some data may be transferred directly between the source system and the procured solution. The procured solution must enable the transfer of master data with a master data system outside the procurement in both directions. With this request for information, suppliers are invited to a market dialogue regarding questions related to the procurement. The goal of the request for information is to obtain comprehensive information regarding the procurement so that a potential call for tenders can be carried out as appropriately as possible. This request for information is not a call for tenders, and it does not bind Heka to publish a call for tenders later. The contracting authority does not commit to carrying out the call for tenders in the described manner. All information and requirements presented in the request for information and its attached materials regarding the planned procurement are still preliminary at this stage and may change. Responding to the request for information does not bind the supplier, and responding to the request for information is not a prerequisite for participating in a potential call for tenders to be published later. The contracting authority may use the information received through the request for information in the planning of the procurement. The information collected through the request for information will remain confidential. The goal is to launch the procurement procedure during the spring of 2026. A contract notice will be published regarding the procurement. We ask you to familiarise yourself with the attached appendices (01-02) and to respond to the questions presented in the "Questions" document (appendix 03). Please also indicate in the document whether you would be willing to present the solution you are offering via Teams. We ask you to send the completed "Questions" appendix 03 as well as the "Requirements" appendix 02 by 7.1.2026 at 15.00 by email to hankinnat@hekaoy.fi.

sig_88b55dc6e9c42a2b3d1f.description: The Contracting Authority is looking for 1 Contractor to conclude an Agreement that provides for the Contract “Koningswei in Tilburg, participation in Construction Team and optionally subsequent realization including 2-year maintenance” for the Space and Spatial Execution departments of gemeente Tilburg. The Koningswei project concerns the redesign of the Koningsplein in the centre of Tilburg. The existing predominantly stony square is being transformed into a green recreational park — an intensive green roof / roof garden on the deck of the existing Koningsplein multi-storey car park. The Contract comprises two phases that are tendered in conjunction: Phase 1 - Construction Team phase (Services) and Phase 2 - Realization and Maintenance phase (Works). The core of the assignment lies in the intensive green roof / roof garden: construction of a park on the deck of the existing multi-storey car park, provided with trees (in tree bunkers) which require a preparation process, shrubs, perennials, a water retention and infiltration system, a buffer tank for irrigation, final and temporary paving, play area, rainwater drainage, adaptation and retention of the existing pergola. The structural possibilities and water-tightness of the existing parking deck form a hard design precondition. The Contractor is expressly expected to provide implementation-technical added value in the construction team phase in the areas of constructability, phasing, cost control and environmental management in a highly urban context. The Contractor also acts as V&G (Safety & Health) coordinator for the design phase and has a coordination obligation with regard to the total Construction Team, the tree supplier(s) and sub-contractors for public lighting. Reference is further made to the Tender Document. Koningswei in Tilburg, participation in Construction Team and optionally subsequent realization including 2-year maintenance. See project description.
sig_88b55dc6e9c42a2b3d1f.title: Koningswei in Tilburg, participation in Construction Team and optionally subsequent realization including 2-year maintenance

sig_88e0872ef590871ada55.description: This Special Notice provides interested parties with information regarding the availability of the draft Request for Proposal (dRFP), review requirements, the tentative acquisition schedule, and the upcoming Industry Day and Site Visit. This notice is for planning purposes only and does not constitute an invitation for bids, request for proposals, or quotes, nor does it indicate that the Government will contract for the items described herein. The Government will not reimburse respondents for any costs associated with submitting feedback or attending the events outlined in this notice. The 30th Contracting Squadron (30 CONS/PKD) at Vandenberg Space Force Base (VSFB), CA, is requesting industry feedback on the dRFP for the Facility Readiness and Maintenance Execution (FRAME) contract. FRAME is the follow-on acquisition to the current Launch Operations Support Contract (LOSC) (Contract #FA4610-23-D-0001, currently performed by Call Henry, Inc.). FRAME follow-on acquisition is 100% Small Business Set-Aside. The North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) code for this effort is 561210 Facilities Support Services (small business size standard is $47M). Description of Services, Background, and Objective: FRAME is a non-personal services contract that provides maintenance, repair, modification, and modernization for?over 130?facilities, property, and equipment (P&E)?supporting?the nation’s space mission, defense, and test activities at VSFB and its associated geographically-separated locations. The scope of work involves facility infrastructure and systems (including water and gas mains, roads, generators, power distribution, HVAC, waste systems, and roofing) alongside the execution of distinct sustainment projects and?standby support for urgent repairs during select?launch operations to ensure maximum operational readiness. Additionally, the contract encompasses the inspection,?testing,?and certification of all Space Launch Delta 30 cranes and elevators. A key change under this follow-on acquisition is that the South Vandenberg Power Plant (SVPP) is no longer a requirement and will not be carried over from the legacy LOSC to the new FRAME contract. The primary objective of the FRAME contract is to ensure Real Property Installed Equipment (RPIE) and facilities are maintained and operationally ready for a variety of ballistic missile, space, guided weapon, and aircraft test and evaluation missions in support of Space Launch Delta 30 (SLD 30), 30th Civil Engineer Squadron (30 CES), 4th Launch Squadron (4 LS), 2nd Range Operations Squadron (2 ROPS), Missile Defense Agency (MDA), U. S. Space Forces - Space (S4S), 18th Space Defense Squadron (18 SDS), Sentinel, 30th Operations Support Squadron (30 OSS), 2nd Space Launch Squadron (2 SLS), the National Reconnaissance Office (NRO), and various other Range Users. Mission Essential Services: The FRAME contract contains some mission-essential requirements which require continued support during peacetime, national emergency, and/or wartime scenarios. Tentative Acquisition Schedule: dRFP Release: 8 Sep 26 Final RFP Issuance: 12 Nov 26 Proposals Due: 16 Jan 27 Anticipated Award: 18 Dec 27 Performance Start:?1 Apr 28 4. Industry Day and Site Visit Event Details Interested businesses are invited to register for the upcoming two-day event. Representatives will have the opportunity to attend a briefing detailing the contract structure, tour key range facilities, and participate in one-on-one sessions with the Government program team. Dates: September 22, 2026 (General Briefing & Tour) – September 23, 2026 (One-on-One Sessions) Location: Vandenberg Space Force Base (VSFB), CA Maximum Attendees: Limited to two (2) representatives per prospective company due to base logistical constraints. Registration and RSVP Deadlines: Attendee RSVP & Security Vetting Submission: No later than Friday, September 11, 2026, at 16:30 Pacific Time. Provide your full name and company. Late requests may not be processed. One-on-One Meeting Request: Companies interested in booking a one-on-one session with the program office must explicitly request it via email by Tuesday, September 15, 2026, at 16:30 Pacific Time. Slots are limited and will be scheduled on a first-come, first-served basis. Maps and a tentative agenda are attached to this announcement to assist registered attendees with navigation and scheduling. Base Access & Entry Requirements: All site visit attendees must report to the Vandenberg Visitor Control Center (VCC), located at 6 California Blvd (Santa Maria Gate) prior to entry (VCC hours: 0600-1800). Arrive Early: Attendees are strongly encouraged to arrive early to the Visitor Control Center to allow sufficient time for base entry processing and to avoid delays getting to the briefing. Identification for Non-CAC Holders: Attendees who do not possess a Common Access Card (CAC) must present a REAL ID-compliant credential or a valid U.S. Passport. If an attendee does not have a REAL ID or a Passport, they must bring and present a standard state-issued Driver's License or ID card, a Birth Certificate, and a physical Social Security Card to obtain a base visitor pass. Foreign Nationals will not be able to participate due to the time necessary to vet access. 5. Important Site Visit Disclaimers & Rules of Conduct: Change of Solicitation Terms: Please understand that nothing said during the Industry Day briefings, site tours, or one-on-one sessions by any Government representative changes the terms, conditions, specifications, or requirements of the solicitation. If a change to the solicitation is determined to be necessary based on what is discussed or observed, it will be formally issued as a written amendment via email. Photography and Video Restrictions: No photography or video recording is permitted on this installation at any time, unless specific, designated areas are explicitly pointed out and authorized by the hosting Facility Manager. 6. Submission of Questions & Comments (CRM) The Government is actively seeking industry feedback on the Draft PWS and planned acquisition strategy to ensure clear, high-performing requirements. To submit questions or comments concerning the acquisition and dRFP, prospective offerors must use the official Comment Resolution Matrix (CRM) Excel spreadsheet (which will be posted with the Draft RFP documents). Completed CRM spreadsheets must be returned to the Points of Contact listed below. The deadline for submitting dRFP and Industry Day comments is September 29, 2026, by 16:30 Pacific Time. 7. Primary Points of Contact For all RSVP submissions, one-on-one requests, CRM question submittals or administrative questions, please send correspondence via email to BOTH of the following representatives: Primary POC (Contracting Officer): Katherine Williams, 30 CONS/PKD Email: katherine.williams.9@spaceforce.mil Secondary POC (Contract Specialist): Sabrina Swain, 30 CONS/PKD Email: sabrina.swain.1@spaceforce.mil

sig_88fe649111a131b35915.description: The subject of this tender is the procurement of a central, high-performance, scalable and highly available backup infrastructure for Magdeburg University Hospital. The aim of the tender is to provide a future-proof and demand-oriented expandable central backup solution that enables reliable backup as well as fast and reliable recovery of the business-critical and medically relevant data and IT systems arising at Magdeburg University Hospital. The solution to be procured must take into account the requirements for secure, highly available and permanently available operation in a KRITIS-relevant environment and thus make a significant contribution to the operational safety, fail-safe operation and resilience of the IT infrastructure of Magdeburg University Hospital. The overall solution to be procured is to consist of four coordinated system components: • a high-performance all-flash backup appliance for processing large amounts of data and a high number of parallel backup and restore processes, • a highly available backup storage system as the primary backup target with integrated deduplication function, • a high-performance enterprise rack server as a Veeam backup server as well as • two appropriately dimensioned enterprise rack servers as Veeam backup proxies. The backup infrastructure is to be designed in such a way that it takes into account the existing and foreseeable future requirements of Magdeburg University Hospital. In addition to the delivery of the required hardware and software, including all components and licences required for intended operation, the scope of services also includes the professional installation, configuration and integration of the overall solution into the existing IT infrastructure of Magdeburg University Hospital. Furthermore, the scope of services includes the commissioning of the overall solution as well as the execution of the required functional, performance and acceptance tests. The contractor must provide a fully functional and ready-for-operation overall solution that complies with the requirements laid down in the specification of services and the schedule of services. All services are to be provided in compliance with the legal, regulatory and technical requirements applicable at the time of service provision as well as the relevant norms and standards. Lot LOT-0000: Central backup system. Procurement of a central, high-performance, scalable and highly available backup infrastructure for Magdeburg University Hospital. The specific functional requirements result from the schedule of services.
sig_88fe649111a131b35915.title: Procurement of a central backup system

sig_88febc65a127ab508f9e.description: University of Limerick is seeking to procure an enterprise-level, cloud-based Systematic Review Management Platform to support researchers, academics, students, librarians and research support staff in conducting high-quality evidence synthesis activities across the institution. The proposed solution must provide an integrated end-to-end workflow for systematic reviews and related evidence synthesis methodologies, including citation management, screening, full-text review, data extraction, risk of bias assessment, collaboration, reporting and publication-ready outputs. The platform should facilitate efficient collaboration between internal and external researchers, provide enterprise-grade administration and reporting capabilities, and support recognised methodologies such as systematic reviews, scoping reviews, rapid reviews, mixed-methods reviews and meta-analyses. The successful Tenderer will be required to deliver a fully managed Software-as-a-Service (SaaS) solution, including implementation, training, ongoing support, systematic review methodological expertise, security and compliance assurances, and enterprise-level service management. The solution must align with the University's information governance, security, accessibility and architectural requirements, while providing value for money and supporting the University's strategic ambition to strengthen research excellence and evidence-informed decision-making across the institution.
sig_88febc65a127ab508f9e.title: UL1084 Enterprise-level Systematic Review Management Platform to the University of Limerick

sig_89acec772031c0972bea.description: The subject of the framework agreement for the procurement is the provision, implementation, and configuration of a web-based, audit-proof, and configurable specialist application for the funding management of Netzwerk Universitätsmedizin NUM GmbH (NUM). The scope of services comprises in particular software provision, hosting, and technical operation by the contractor, setup and customising, data migration, interfaces, and exports including system-neutral transfer to the financial software selected at a later date, a documented API, support, maintenance, training, and documentation. The subject of the framework agreement for the procurement is the provision, implementation, and configuration of a web-based, audit-proof, and configurable software solution for the funding management of Netzwerk Universitätsmedizin GmbH (NUM). The solution must digitally map the funding processes from application through review, approval, contract creation, payment request, and interim and final reports. NUM is in an organisational transition phase. Previous processes are partially connected to existing structures of Charité, external project management agency processes, SharePoint or file shares, Excel tables, PDF documents, and easyOnline/XML data. In future, the office is to establish its own structures for processing, reviewing, and documenting funding processes. The software must support both administrative processing and review (currently the Administration, Finance, and Controlling team) and specialist processing and review (currently the Science Management team). The respective reviews take place in parallel, sequentially, or consecutively depending on the process. Input masks, checklists, review notes, task lists, and status logic must therefore be able to traceably depict both review perspectives. The software does not execute the actual payment order, bank execution, or direct retrieval from the Federal Treasury. However, it must provide the data required for forwarding the funds in a structured and system-independent manner. Since the client's financial software will only be selected after this procurement, the technical transfer must be possible via at least a documented, configurable exchange format. The concrete target format and field assignment will be agreed upon in the implementation project after the financial software is selected. The actual retrieval of financial funds from the Federal Treasury and the bank execution take place outside the software. The provision of the retrieval data package and the technical implementation of the agreed data exchange are part of the scope of services. The subject of the tender is an integrated specialist application for funding management with which administrative and specialist review, processing, and decision-making processes can be fully digitally mapped. Document management is a central component of this specialist application and must ensure the process-related linking, structured storage, versioning, management, and retrievability of documents. What is being sought is therefore neither a pure document repository nor an isolated form system, but an end-to-end funding management solution. Insofar as products, procedures, or manufacturers are named in this specification of services, this is done exclusively to describe the required scope of services; equivalent solutions are permitted. Existing target systems of the client determined before publication, or those determined prior to publication, are clearly named in the procurement documents, including the required integration scope.

sig_8a2ff45572d92c9c256c.description: MARKET DIALOGUE The subject matter of the market dialogue is the expert services in information security and data protection under preparation as well as the assessment services of conformity assessment bodies for information security for the needs of Väylävirasto. BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVES Väylävirasto is putting out to tender the following two expert service procurements: Expert services in information security and data protection This tender procures experts to support the safeguarding and development of information and cyber security, data protection and information management of Väylävirasto. Väylävirasto has several different administrative or technical projects and undertakings underway in which operations are developed and existing information systems are renewed or new ones are ordered. What all these projects and undertakings have in common is that they must implement information security and the fulfilment of central government information security requirements in a manner suitable for the organisation. The subject matter of the procurement is information and cybersecurity consulting and auditing services. The work takes place largely in a multi-supplier environment, but also as internal consulting for individual projects or undertakings. Information security audits are also carried out regularly in the supplier environment. In addition, an assessment is made of, among other things, the impact of information security instructions directed at central government on the projects and operations of Väylävirasto. In addition to the office environment, the subject matter of the procurement is the infrastructures managed by Väylävirasto (Finnish Transport Infrastructure Agency), i.e. state-owned road, rail and waterways. Each transport mode has its own cyber security development needs, which in certain respects may differ significantly from each other. The aim of the procurement is to obtain a partner for Väylävirasto with which the organisation's and the various transport modes' information and cybersecurity development can be carried out. Assessment services of conformity assessment bodies for information security This tender procures conformity assessment body services to support the safeguarding of the information and cybersecurity, data protection and information management of Väylävirasto. Within the scope of this contract, conformity assessment bodies will produce assessment services in the role of an information security conformity assessment body approved by the Finnish Transport and Communications Agency (Traficom). When offering and producing assessment services, the information security conformity assessment bodies must comply with the current legislation, official regulations, recommendations, guidelines and other obligations directed at conformity assessment bodies by the authorities concerning conformity assessment body activities. Particular attention must be paid to the instruction issued to conformity assessment bodies by the Finnish Transport and Communications Agency for information security conformity assessment bodies 210/2016 O. During the course of the dialogue, the contracting entity will separately assess the need for a market dialogue regarding the assessment services of conformity assessment bodies for information security. The following dynamic purchasing systems (DPS) of Hansel Oy will be used as the procurement procedure for both tenders: Expert services in cyber security and data protection 2025 Assessment services of conformity assessment bodies for information security 2021–2028 Hansel Oy's dynamic purchasing systems are open to all, and all companies meeting the suitability requirements may join them. Those interested in participating in the tenders are therefore requested to join the dynamic purchasing systems. PRELIMINARY SCHEDULE The contracting entity's target schedule for carrying out the market dialogue and the procurement is: - Market dialogue 12/2025-1/2026 - Publication of the invitation to tender 1/2026 - Calculation period 1-2/2026 - Comparison of tenders 2/2026 - Procurement decision and continuation 2-3/2026 ----- ADDITIONAL INFORMATION ON THE NOTICE This notice is a prior information notice. This notice does not request tenders. The prior information notice is accompanied by an invitation to a market dialogue, whereby all suppliers interested in the procurement have the opportunity to conduct a technical dialogue concerning the procurement with Väylävirasto. The purpose of the technical dialogue is to conduct a general-level dialogue on the subject matter of the procurement and its definition. The technical dialogue does not bind Väylävirasto to carry out the procurement. Nor does the technical dialogue bind the supplier to participate in any potential competitive tendering. The technical dialogue is organised through commenting on draft versions of the invitation to tender material and answering the contracting entity's questions related to the subject matter of the procurement. The preliminary date for submitting the draft versions of the invitation to tender material and questions is 12.12.2025. The contracting entity reserves suppliers approximately two weeks for commenting. Instructions for registration: The supplier must declare its interest in participating in the market dialogue by 10.12.2025 at 12.00 at the latest by sending a message to the addresses paul.kinnunen@vayla.fi, pirita.tuikka@vayla.fi and aino.mannikko@vayla.fi with the subject heading: "Tietoturvan hankinnat- markkinavuoropuhelu" (Information security procurements - market dialogue). The supplier is requested to state in the message to which email addresses the market dialogue material will be delivered. The supplier is requested to state the following information in the message: - email address of the supplier's contact person. The contracting entity reserves the right to also invite suppliers to bilateral negotiations or to continue the technical dialogue in another separately notified manner, which will be notified of later if necessary. The descriptions presented in this prior information notice and the estimated publication date of the procurement notice, as well as the draft materials of the dialogue to be delivered later, are preliminary and indicative prior procurement information. Participating companies will not be paid compensation for answering or participating.

sig_8a8294f19b8f37f5b23d.description: The project will develop a coherent framework for understanding how territorial cohesion and resilience operate under conditions of persistent low growth, demographic contraction and structural decline. Based on European-wide territorial mapping, it will elaborate typologies of territories facing persistent low growth and demographic contraction, and produce territorial maps of vulnerability, adaptive capacity and resilience. Through comparative qualitative case studies across different territorial contexts, it will document adaptive territorial practices and governance innovations. Finally, the project will offer practical policy guidance suggesting how cohesion policy, territorial governance and resilience planning frameworks may need to evolve in response to persistent low growth and structural territorial contraction.

sig_8c312876c641ea21f026.description: THIS IS NOT A PRIOR INFORMATION NOTICE, CONTRACT NOTICE OR CALL FOR TENDERS, BUT A NOTICE OF THE LAUNCH OF A MARKET DIALOGUE AS PART OF PROCUREMENT PLANNING. Länsi-Uudenmaan hyvinvointialue is mapping suppliers' interest in the tendering for the coordination of resources, patient visits and space utilisation planning. The subject of the procurement is the better coordination than previously of customer and patient visits and space utilisation planning and monitoring. In the target state, space and resource planning is carried out using a scalable system entity. In the future, it can be linked to, among other things, the Numeron work shift planning system, property information system and patient and customer information system to be introduced in the wellbeing services county. Currently, health and social welfare professionals in the wellbeing services county use a single patient and customer information system from the same product family (SosiaaliLifeCare, TerveysLifeCare or both). In the target state, it would be essential that the professional would not need numerous systems to manage patient and customer work entries, appointments, arrivals and room bookings. The wellbeing services county currently does not have a master system for spatial data. The data is fragmented across different systems. Consequently, data-driven management views related to spatial efficiency are also not comprehensively available. In the future, for patients and customers, the wellbeing services county's own application Lunna will be the main transaction portal through which the customer or patient can handle their health and social welfare matters, and e.g. make appointments, register for appointments and receive (physical) customer guidance at the location. Länsi-Uudenmaan hyvinvointialue invites suppliers to market dialogues to discuss their solution models and present their products. The market dialogue discussions will take place in May during weeks 20 and 21 in Otaniemi, Espoo. The duration of the presentation session is preliminarily planned to be approximately two hours per supplier. Länsi-Uudenmaan hyvinvointialue reserves the right to invite the number of suppliers it deems necessary to the presentation session. Expressing interest in the information request does not bind suppliers to participate in the tendering procedure, nor is it a prerequisite for participating in the tendering procedure. Suppliers interested in the procurement are requested to declare their interest in the procurement via the tarjouspalvelu.fi portal. Expressing interest in the information request does not bind the service provider/supplier to participate in the tendering procedure, nor is it a prerequisite for participating in the actual tendering procedure later. Interest in the procurement is requested to be submitted by 06.04.2026 at 12.00 via the tarjouspalvelu.fi portal. We will contact everyone who has expressed their interest.

sig_8cab755f3e31b4ef5778.description: The overarching goal of this notice of funding opportunity (NOFO) and its companion opportunities is to establish the Precision Medicine with AI: Integrating Imaging with Multimodal Data (PRIMED-AI) Program to support development of innovative, reliable, cost-effective, and sustainable multimodal AI-based clinical decision support (CDS) tools. PRIMED-AI CDS tools are based on the integration of clinical imaging with other types of multimodal health data to enhance care for patients with a wide range of health conditions. The PRIMED-AI Program seeks to catalyze the adoption of AI-based CDS tools into clinical workflows to enable novel personalized medicine strategies that address significant health challenges.The purpose of this NOFO is to catalyze the translation of Artificial Intelligence (AI)-enabled, image-centered, multimodal CDS tools, developed as Software as a Medical Device, from training and testing of prototypes towards clinical applications that address unmet health challenges in precision medicine. These projects are expected to have high potential for demonstrable, positive impact on patient outcomes and/or healthcare processes.

sig_8cd7b85ff300eecc505c.description: Carmarthenshire County Council is undertaking an Early Market Engagement exercise to better understand the care rostering, scheduling and workforce management solutions currently available within the market. The Council currently utilises a rostering and scheduling solution across its Residential and Domiciliary Care Services and wishes to engage with suppliers to understand available products, functionality, market developments and delivery models that may support future service requirements. This exercise is intended to inform future planning and does not represent a commitment to undertake a procurement process. The Council is particularly interested in solutions that support: • Domiciliary Care scheduling and visit management. • Residential Care rostering and workforce management. • Workforce resource teams and shared staffing models. • Mobile working for frontline care staff. • Leave, absence and availability management. • Skills, compliance and workforce competency management. • Payroll, travel and workforce payment processes. • Reporting, operational oversight and management information. • Continuity of care and workforce utilisation. • Integration with care management, HR, payroll, finance and identity management systems. The Council intends to provide a high-level requirements document to interested suppliers and may invite suppliers to demonstrate how their solution supports the functional areas identified. Participation in this engagement is for information and planning purposes only and does not commit the Council to any procurement or award. All interested parties are encouraged to register their interest by 22/09/26 to participate in the demonstration sessions which we are planning to hold in October. Details of any formal tender will be provided in due course. Lot 1: . None

sig_8ceb6a750d48331c8bf4.description: The German Academic Exchange Service (DAAD) is the world's largest organisation for the international exchange of students and researchers as well as the internationalisation of German universities. Since its foundation in the year 1925, the DAAD has supported over 2,9 million academics at home and abroad. As an association, it is supported by German universities and student bodies. In addition to awarding scholarships, the DAAD promotes the internationalisation of German universities, strengthens German studies and the German language abroad, supports developing countries in building efficient universities and advises decision-makers in cultural, educational and development policy. To this end, it maintains an external network with regional offices, information centres and information points in more than 60 countries. Worldwide, more than 1.200 committed employees in Bonn, Berlin and regional offices work towards the goals of the DAAD. The DAAD is financed predominantly from federal funds from the Federal Foreign Office, the Federal Ministry of Education and Research, the Federal Ministry for Economic Cooperation and Development and the European Union. Other sponsors include foreign governments, companies, foundations and the Stifterverband für die Deutsche Wissenschaft. The DAAD is inviting tenders for services in the areas of usability, user experience and continuous success measurement. A contractor (AN) is sought with specific competence and experience in the areas of usability, user experience, conducting user acceptance tests, continuous success measurement, optimisation and requirements analysis. The AN designs and conducts user-centred studies (e.g. usability tests, acceptance tests, user surveys, target group interviews), continuously measures the success of existing and new features, analyses information architecture, navigation and interaction design and derives concrete optimisation proposals from this. In addition, it supports the DAAD in requirements analysis and prioritisation of further development needs and documents the results in compact, decision-oriented reports for the product managers. The services mentioned below can be commissioned in combinations adapted to the respective project, both in individual studies and in long-term projects. Corresponding tasks may also have to be carried out for mobile apps under Android and/or iOS, possibly also accompanying development. So far, however, no development is specifically planned. The DAAD expects the following services from the contractor: a) Usability and user acceptance tests (in-person or remote) b) User surveys and target group interviews (in-person or remote) c) Laboratory use or rental for in-person tests d) Conception of customised UX monitoring systems for continuous success measurement e) Creation of personas and user structure analyses f) Workshops and design thinking (in-person or remote) g) Consulting, continuous optimisation support, content review and expert analysis h) Result documentation and presentation i) Web analysis and user tracking For further information, please refer to the service description in Annex 02.
sig_8ceb6a750d48331c8bf4.title: Framework agreement for services in the areas of usability, user experience and continuous success measurement

sig_8cf1e207a9a48d031589.description: This notice of intent is NOT a request for competitive proposals. The Government intends to negotiate with only one source, LinQuest Corporation, for the continuation of Systems Engineering, Integration, and Test (SEIT) support pursuant to RFO 6.103-1, Only One Responsible Source and No Other Supplies or Services Will Satisfy Agency Requirements. The contemplated action will extend the period of performance of the current CPIF contract for an anticipated 12-months and four 3-month option periods, for a potential total extension of 24 months if all options are exercised. The requirement anticipates a level of effort equivalent to approximately 380 FTEs providing continued SEIT support across the MSEIT mission areas described below. Exercise of any option is subject to the Government's requirements, availability of funds, and applicable contractual and statutory authority. The Government intends to extend the period of performance of the existing CPIF MSEIT contract with LinQuest Corporation to maintain continuity of critical SEIT support while the Government completes its follow-on acquisition activities. The Government has determined that transitioning this interim requirement to another source would result in substantial duplication of cost and/or unacceptable delays in fulfilling the agency's requirements. This determination is subject to consideration of any timely responses received as a result of this notice. The purpose of this acquisition for the Space Systems Command (SSC) Military Communications & Position, Navigation, and Timing (MilComm & PNT) Directorate (SSC/CG) is to provide Systems Engineering, Integration and Test (SEIT) support under the Military Communications SEIT (MSEIT) program. The requirement supports the effectiveness and efficiency of all Military Communications (MilComm or MILSATCOM) systems engineering capabilities, to support the creation and control of system definitions and technical baselines, to support development of end products, and to standardize and streamline engineering processes and products across SSC/CG. The required effort includes relevant expertise and experience with system- of-systems integration of space, mission control, communications planning, cryptographic key management and service user terminal programs, and associated interfaces. Support includes Directorate and program level configuration and data management, architecture management, risk, opportunity, and issue management, requirements management, verification, validation and test, schedule management, cybersecurity, logistics, and sustainment. The contractor will also support communication, collaboration, and integration among Military Communications programs, functional areas, external stakeholders, and interfacing programs. All responsible sources may submit a capability statement which will be considered by the Government. Interested parties must submit sufficient information demonstrating their capability to satisfy the Government's requirements and must identify their business size and socio economic status, as applicable, including (i.e. 8(a), Historically Underutilized Business Zone (HubZone), Woman-Owned Small Business (WOSB), or Service Disabled Veteran-Owned Small Business (SDVOSB), or Large Business). Responses should, at a minimum, address the respondent's relevant technical experience, ability to perform the required scope and a comparable level of effort, knowledge and experience with comparable system-of-systems integration efforts, ability to meet the required performance schedule and any other information demonstrating the respondent's capability to satisfy the Government's requirements without unacceptable disruption to mission support. Responses shall be submitted to the Contracting Officer and Contract Specialist no later than 10AM PDT on 23 September 2026. Responses submitted in response to this notice are for the Government's consideration in determining whether a competitive acquisition is appropriate. A determination by the Government not to compete this proposed contract action based upon responses to this notice is solely within the discretion of the Government. Submission of information in response to this notice is voluntary. The Government will not reimburse respondents for costs incurred in preparing or submitting a response. This notice does not constitute a solicitation, and the Government is not obligated to award a contract as a result of this notice.
sig_8cf1e207a9a48d031589.title: Notice of Intent: MILITARY SATELLITE COMMUNICATIONS (MILSATCOM) SYSTEMS ENGINEERING, INTEGRATION AND TEST(MSEIT)

The services are tendered as a framework agreement. The client is looking for a service provider to support it in the procurement of vehicles and equipment for civil protection. The contractor must in particular provide the following predominantly technical services, while the legal assessment and decision remain with the client: - Carrying out market surveys on the vehicles and equipment to be procured for civil protection, in particular with regard to the current state of the art and technical possibilities - Drawing up specifications taking into account technical specifications and the special needs of civil protection - Developing proposals for suitability and award criteria, including technical evaluation criteria - Processing technical applicant/tenderer questions - Processing complaints, in particular preparing complaint response letters - Evaluating requests to participate or tenders as well as developing award proposals for the contract award - Preparing prior information notices - Preparing procurement records - Advising in review procedures In addition, the contractor must optionally support and accompany the client upon respective call-off after the respective award in the procurement process, for example at construction meetings, prototype inspections, quality inspections and acceptances and, where applicable, also regarding the warranty phase after acceptance. Legal advice services are not covered by the contract. The services are tendered in the form of a framework agreement. The client determines the specific services to be provided and their deadlines individually in each individual contract. The contractor has no entitlement to the call-off of services from the framework agreement. There is no entitlement to further commissioning. The type and scope of the individual commissioning can vary per individual project. The client is entitled to an ordinary right of termination at any time for each individual contract issued on the basis of the framework agreement. The client reserves the right to commission any further special services. The framework agreement has a maximum duration of four years from the start of the services with regard to the non-optional services pursuant to Section 21 Paragraph 6 of the Ordinance on the Award of Public Contracts (VgV). Insofar as the client calls off the optional services, the conditions of the framework agreement for the individual contracts issued until the maximum duration is reached shall continue to apply until their final processing by the contractor even after termination of this framework agreement. The maximum quantity of services expected under the framework agreement amounts to up to a total of 500 vehicles and equipment, which the client can call off bundled in individual contracts for each individual contract.

sig_8d37de87e460fcc3ef51.description: The MSHIP Program is an initiative by TransnetBW aimed at supporting Germany's energy transition by developing a sustainable, scalable, and efficient grid management system. It focuses on modularity, automation, and simplicity to enhance operational security and reduce costs. The architecture is based on a self-hosted, cloud-native platform specifically designed for secure and data-driven operations. The MSHIP - LFC ensures continuous monitoring of the power balance and thus a stable energy supply. The controller detects deviations in the power balance or frequency and activates the appropriate secondary control power providers on a price-based basis to stabilize the balance and thus also the frequency. In addition, a controller is to be developed for special emergency situations in which no conventional control power market environment is available. The purpose of this RFI is to identify potential providers and solutions that can meet the requirements of the MSHIP - LFC. The RFI is intended to provide an initial market overview and to evaluate possible technological approaches and their ability to integrate into the existing MSHIP architecture. The aim is not to commit to a specific system, an architecture or provider in advance. Openness to different approaches remains the main guiding principle. The information gathered will serve as a basis for future decisions and possible tenders. Participation in this market exploration will not result in any advantages or disadvantages for the participants as potential bidders in a future - not yet binding - tender procedure. Please note that also responses are invited and will be considered that do not cover all listed functionalities.
sig_8d37de87e460fcc3ef51.title: MSHIP Market Survey for LFC

sig_8da9325aa41095cb85f2.description: The SIDEC du JURA wishes to acquire, for its own needs and those of the local authorities of Jura, computer hardware, management software and their maintenance. In order to successfully carry out this mission, SIDEC is setting up a Dynamic Purchasing System to acquire them, authorised by deliberation No. 2328 of 5 October 2024 and a purchasing body, authorised by deliberation No. 2347 of 25 January 2025. A Dynamic Purchasing System (hereinafter referred to as the "DPS" or "System"), without being a contract as such, is a fully electronic purchasing technique which allows economic operators admitted to participate in the DPS to be put into periodic competition for the award of several public contracts called specific contracts (SCs), comparable to call-off framework agreements. In other words, throughout the validity period of the DPS, any operator may apply to be admitted. Once admitted, the operator is informed directly of upcoming specific contracts and may submit bids without having to resubmit a whole series of supporting documents. The DPS is divided into several categories according to the type of product. It is possible to be admitted to one or more categories. Consequently, any operator admitted to a given category is invited, if they so wish, to tender for each corresponding specific contract. The specific contracts are themselves divided into lots, one per product. Each operator is free to submit a tender for one or more lots. Each resulting contract will be of the call-off contract type, with a maximum for each contract Notification 1th consultation; Lot 2 covers the acquisition of office computer hardware according to the needs of SIDEC and the contracted Jura local authorities; lot 3 covers the supply of office and utility software; lot 4 corresponds to the maintenance of hardware and supply of small equipment
sig_8da9325aa41095cb85f2.title: SIDEC - DPS - IT CONSULTATION FOR HARDWARE, SOFTWARE AND MAINTENANCE - 4 lots

sig_8dfed59770476e947318.description: For the electric commercial vehicles, Disposal + Recycling requires power distribution cabinets in the two motor vehicle halls at the Forsthaus energy centre, each with at least 6 charging points, distribution boxes for the individual vehicles and a load management system (software). The power distribution cabinets must meet the following requirements: · Suitable for use in depots (municipal works yards) with fixed, schedulable charging times. · Suitable for 24/7 use in a frost-protected environment (hall, marquee). · Suitable for normal charging and rapid charging of individual vehicles. · Equipped with LAN, WLAN and mobile communications (at least 4G). The distribution boxes for the individual vehicles must be compatible for CCS charging cables with 5 m, 7 m and optionally 10 m. The boxes must have at least IP54 protection. Wall mounting is intended in principle. Optionally, ceiling mounting with a cable reel featuring a 7 m long cable is to be tendered. The installation (excluding electrical installation) of the power distribution cabinets and distribution boxes must be carried out by the tenderer. Commissioning is to be carried out by the supplier and must be recorded in a report. The electrical installations are tendered separately and are not part of the scope of services. However, the software for load management must be offered as well. Since Energie Wasser Bern is constructing a new building on the site of the Forsthaus energy centre from July 2027, the distribution cabinets and boxes of the North motor vehicle hall must be accommodated in a provisional structure (temperature-controlled marquee) and will only be installed in the motor vehicle hall after a construction period of approx. 3 years. The distribution cabinets and boxes for the East motor vehicle hall can be installed at the final location upon delivery. The installation of the infrastructure must take place by early June 2027 at the latest. With regard to the software, it is important that not all vehicles are charged simultaneously, but rather that the entire available time (approx. 16 hours to 06.30 hours) is utilised. In addition, the system must restart automatically in the event of a power or network failure and issue a notification. Furthermore, the following requirements are placed on the software: · Locally installed hardware/software solution, also possible web-based, which controls the charging processes locally. · Autonomous functionality of the system even in the event of an internet failure or malfunction. · Arbitrary scalability when retrofitting additional charging points. · Immediate clearance of the charging process following successful authentication. · Online access (web UI) via desktop computer and mobile end devices. · German language selection. · Display of energy consumption per vehicle live and retroactively. · Evaluations and statistics on energy consumption, charging processes and efficiency per vehicle as well as comparison options between the vehicles. · Export of consumption and charging data (e.g. CSV or Excel). · Guarantee that the software will be actively supported for at least five years after acceptance of the installation (delivery of security patches, adaptation to new versions of peripheral systems, elimination of functional errors, etc.). The detailed technical requirements can be found in the bill of quantities in the appendix. The bill of quantities must be completed in full without references to additional documents. Product, brand, design or type designations are dispensed with. If such designations are listed in exceptional cases, equivalent alternatives are permitted. Equivalence must be proven by the tenderer.
sig_8dfed59770476e947318.title: Charging infrastructure and load management for electric lorries

sig_8e17c1ee514b9c2b594c.description: The purpose of this contract is to conclude a framework agreement with a single contractor for the supply, renewal, extension and support of IBM webMethods licences, subscriptions, maintenance and support rights, as well as for the provision of expertise services directly related to these for the contracting authority's existing IBM webMethods environment. The basic requirement consists of the extension of maintenance and support for the existing perpetual IBM webMethods licences. During the term of the framework agreement, the contracting authority may also, depending on its actual needs, order, among other things, the following products, rights and services: • additional IBM webMethods licences and subscriptions; • additional or fixed-term maintenance and support rights; • extended support; • IBM Expert Labs or other expertise services for which support by IBM is proven; • assistance with lifecycle management, capacity expansion, containerisation and controlled modernisation; • a predefined 'hypercare' service and temporary support 24 h/24, 7 d/7. LCM wishes to maintain the existing core-based licensing model and guarantee the continuity, support, lifecycle monitoring and controlled evolution of the existing IBM webMethods integration environment. During the term of the framework agreement, LCM may, within the limits of the existing IBM webMethods technology stack, evolve towards container technology. The framework agreement is therefore not aimed at the choice of a new B2B integration platform, but at the preservation, support and controlled modernisation of the existing B2B IBM webMethods integration environment. The framework agreement relates exclusively to the products, usage rights, maintenance and support rights as well as the services necessary and directly related to the preservation, management, support and controlled evolution of the contracting authority's existing B2B IBM webMethods integration environment. The contract does not have as its object the acquisition of a new integration platform or the replacement of the existing IBM webMethods platform. It aims to guarantee the continuity, compatibility, support, security and lifecycle monitoring of the existing environment. sig_8e6aa294f87c09cd46f5.description: Danmarks Nationalbank (the Customer) seeks to establish a framework agreement with one Supplier for the provision of specialized cybersecurity advisory and assessment services. As the operator and overseer of critical financial infrastructure in Denmark, Danmarks Nationalbank supports essential processes and systems that require a high level of security, resilience, and trust. The Customer continuously introduces new technologies, vendors, services and architectural changes that may impact its security posture. To ensure informed decision-making and maintain an appropriate level of cyber resilience, the Customer seeks access to independent technical experts capable of evaluating cybersecurity risks from an adversarial perspective. The purpose of the agreement is to provide the Customer with on-demand access to highly skilled technical cybersecurity experts with offensive security backgrounds, capable of delivering rapid, pragmatic and risk-based assessments of new technologies, systems, solutions, architectures and security-related questions. The service shall complement the Customer's internal cybersecurity capabilities by providing independent expert judgement, specialized technical expertise and threat-informed analysis to support secure decision-making, risk management and operational resilience. The Supplier shall provide access to cybersecurity specialists with relevant expertise across infrastructure, cloud, applications, identity and access management, emerging technologies, adversarial techniques and offensive security methodologies.

sig_8eb81562f40e543c4ca0.description: The Advanced Research Projects Agency for Health (ARPA-H) is soliciting proposals from small business concerns (SBCs) that possess the research and development (R&D) expertise to conduct innovative research that will contribute toward ARPA-H mission needs, Small Business Innovation Research (SBIR), and Small Business Technology Transfer (STTR) program objectives. Please see the cover page of the attachment "SBIR_STTR_BAA_FY26" for applicable Stage 1 and Stage 2 deadlines for each open topic. Please see the Attachment H "ARPA-H_SBP_Government_Answered_Questions" for responses to the Q&A period. The purposes of the SBIR and STTR programs are to: (a) stimulate technological innovation; (b) strengthen the role of small business in meeting Federal research/research & development (R/R&D) needs; (c) foster and encourage participation by socially and economically disadvantaged small business concerns and women-owned business concerns; and (d) increase private sector commercialization of innovations derived from Federal R/R&D, thereby increasing competition, productivity and economic growth. For purposes of the SBIR and STTR programs, a small business concern is any business concern that, on the date of award, (1) is organized for profit, with a place of business located in the United States, which operates primarily within the United States or which makes a significant contribution to the United States economy through payment of taxes or use of American products, materials or labor; (2) is in the legal form of an individual proprietorship, partnership, limited liability company, corporation, joint venture, association, trust or cooperative, except that where the form is a joint venture, there must be less than 50 percent participation by foreign business entities in the joint venture; (3) more than 50% directly owned and controlled by one or more individuals (who are citizens or permanent resident aliens of the United States), other business concerns (each of which is more than 50% directly owned and controlled by individuals who are citizens or permanent resident aliens of the United States), or any combination of these; OR more than 50% owned by multiple venture capital operating companies, hedge funds, private equity firms, or any combination of these. No single venture capital operating company, hedge fund, or private equity firm may own more than 50% of the concern; AND, (4) has, including its affiliates, no more than 500 employees. Note: This size standard is established by law for the SBIR program, regardless of the NAICS Code assigned. See 13 C.F.R. § 121.702. PLEASE SEE SECTION 8 OF THE BAA FOR FURTHER INFORMATION ARPA-H 01 -?Development of an annual test to inform women about their future fertility?-?The purpose of this topic is to discover new biomarkers that provide women with actionable data for fertility planning.? Results from this work will help inform the program manager regarding the feasibility of future programs focused on enhancing natural fertility before the need of IVF and guiding the development of women’s health monitoring and improvement tools. This work will develop a diagnostic test that can assess fertility status and generate an estimated timeline for the onset of infertility. This topic seeks to develop a test that is affordable, suitable for at least annual use, and provides user-friendly results for patients and care teams to support childbearing decisions.??? ARPA-H 02 -?Versatile Bioadhesives?- The purpose of this topic is to develop next-generation bioadhesive platforms that can safely and reliably seal, bond, and repair a wide range of tissues in challenging clinical conditions, including wet, bloody, and mechanically dynamic environments. These platforms may also be designed to deliver biologics or small molecules as part of treatment. The goal is to create bioadhesives with key performance attributes such as strong tissue adhesion, controlled degradation, reversibility, biocompatibility, and broad compatibility across multiple tissues and organs. If successful, this topic could enable widely deployable solutions for hemostasis, leak prevention, tissue repair, and device fixation, ultimately helping reduce complications and improve patient outcomes across many care settings ARPA-H 03 -?Universal Platform for Living Adaptive Toxin-removal (UNI-PLAT)?-?The purpose of this topic area is to catalyze the development of a universal, “plug-and-play” synthetic biology platform that enables next-generation microbial chassis capable of performing a broad array of programmable functions. While this solicitation primarily uses toxin removal as a proof-of-concept in relation to chronic disease management, the platform is intended to be adaptable to a range of challenges across industries such as environmental remediation, biomanufacturing, agriculture, holistic medicine, and therapeutic discovery. The broader goal is to create a stable, reliable, and easily reprogrammable microbial platform that demonstrates potential for cross-sector impact beyond the initial use case.? ARPA-H 04 -?Breaking Ground: The First Curative, Durable, Non-Surgical Therapy for Endometriosis?–?The purpose of this topic aims to develop treatments for endometriosis that are non-surgical. Proposers are expected to develop novel, non-surgical therapies to decrease the size or deactivate endometrial implants, to decrease inflammation cause by implants, and / or prevent growth or regrowth of the lesions. Broadly, this should be a novel, non-surgical, curative treatment for endometriosis. ARPA-H 05 -?ARPA-H Lineage Topic?-?The purpose of this topic supports the advancement, commercialization, and translation of technologies that originated from ARPA-H funded efforts. It is intended to help small businesses and startups develop viable products based on these technologies. ARPA-H’s goal is to give small businesses an off-ramp to finish developing their technology/product, explore secondary or interim applications of the technology, and time to achieve self-sufficiency. ARPA-H 06 -?Rapid Comprehensive Diagnostic Test for Multi-System Autoimmune Disease?-The purpose of this topic is to spur the development of novel, rapid diagnostic assays for multi-system autoimmune disease, which?represents?an unmet healthcare need. Moreover, in its ideal embodiment this diagnostic test might allow typical primary care physicians to diagnose and predict tissue-specific autoimmune disease manifestations, thereby streamlining referral of the patient to a specialist. This goal is made more?feasible?by recent technological developments including the ability to detect tissue-specific signatures of immune-mediated stress by assessing circulating cells and/or?tissue-specific molecular products.?? ARPA-H 07 -?Virtual Human Brain for the Development of Neurosurgical Robotics -?The purpose of this topic aims to take a first step toward AI-assisted intracranial microsurgery by creating a high-resolution, physically and anatomically accurate virtual human brain.

sig_8f2b0eb238d2e4596b74.description: The purpose of this prior information notice is to inform about and prepare the market for a coming competition. This prior information notice is not intended to shorten the tender deadline in accordance with the Public Procurement Regulations §20-2 (2). NHN wants to start a procurement process for broadband access for small and medium sized locations. The accesses are used by members in the health network, service providers and entities in the central health management. The accesses represent an important part of a robust and secure infrastructure for transporting digital services for the entire health and welfare sector. Limitations: Accesses to large locations such as hospitals, computer centres etc. are not a part of this procurement. The aim is to enter into an agreement with one or several tenderers. Furthermore, we see great opportunities in further developing digital interaction systems that make NHNs and the supplier's work processes more efficient for the establishment, operation and termination of accesses. The Contracting Authority intends to sign a contract by the end of 2026, starting the agreement from January 2027. About NHN: NHN is a government company owned by the Ministry of Health and Care Services. Our task is to develop, administer and operate national e-health systems and infrastructure. We are responsible for national e-health services such as e-prescription, helsenorge.no, core journal and basic data. We also provide services within ICT, procurements and archives for the health administration agencies. NHN operates 80 national ICT systems and has 1,000 capable employees distributed across offices in Trondheim, Oslo, Tromsø, Moss and Svalbard. Read more at the https://www.nhn.no. At the time of the prior information notice, NHN plans to conduct the procurement in accordance with the Norwegian Public Procurement Act and Regulations, based on the procedure competitive procedure with negotiation after prior publication above the EU/EEA threshold (1.49 MNOK) pursuant to FOA Parts I and III. To further strengthen the market’s ability to participate in the competition, and to facilitate a well‐executed procurement process, NHN is considering market research and supplier dialogue in accordance with FOA §§12‐1 and 12‐2. Any supplier dialogue will be announced via Mercell and Doffin/TED as a follow-up to this prior information notice. We intend to engage in dialogue with the market to obtain additional information and insights related to our needs.
