sig_8f663c8212a320d25699.description: 1. INTRODUCTION & SYNOPSIS This announcement is a formal Request for Prototype Proposal (RPP) issued by the Mission & Installation Contracting Command (MICC) – Fort Campbell on behalf of the Directorate of Public Works (DPW) at Fort Campbell, Kentucky. The Government is seeking competitive prototype proposals to design, integrate, and execute a modernized facility management solution across 58 unaccompanied housing (barracks) facilities. The prototype will integrate an advanced, secure Enterprise Asset Management (EAM) software platform with cross-trained physical maintenance execution to streamline work order triage, optimize Between Occupancy Maintenance (BOM), and execute proactive Preventative Maintenance Orders (PMO). Authority: 10 U.S.C. § 4022, Other Transaction Authority (OTA) for Prototype Projects. Agreement Type: The Government intends to award a single Other Transaction (OT) agreement. Follow-on Production / Sustainment: Offerors are advised that in accordance with 10 U.S.C. § 4022(f), successful completion of this prototype project may result in the award of a non-competitive, follow-on production/sustainment agreement or contract without further competition. 2. BACKGROUND Fort Campbell DPW is responsible for maintaining unaccompanied housing infrastructure that directly impacts Soldier readiness and Quality of Life (QoL). The current operating model relies heavily on manual administrative workflows, disparate tracking mechanisms, and reactive maintenance practices, leading to extended vacancy timelines during unit rotations, misdiagnosed service dispatches, and increased facility wear. This prototype project seeks to validate a modernized operational model that combines commercial best practices with enterprise Army platforms (including integration with ArMA, GFEBS, and the forthcoming enterprise IBM Maximo migration). Key modernization elements include QR-code-enabled request intake, automated work order routing, decentralized parts staging solutions (e.g., smart lockers), and dual-track maintenance (physical inspections for legacy systems and sensor-based monitoring for modern equipment). 3. ELIGIBILITY This RPP is open to all responsible business entities. In accordance with 10 U.S.C. § 4022(d)(1), an award may only be made if at least one of the following conditions is met: At least one nontraditional defense contractor or small business participates to a significant extent in the prototype project; OR All significant participants in the transaction other than the Federal Government are small businesses or nontraditional defense contractors; OR At least one-third (1/3) of the total cost of the prototype project is to be paid out of funds provided by sources other than the Federal Government (cost share); OR The Senior Procurement Executive provides written approval for exceptional circumstances. 4. PROPOSAL SUBMISSION & KEY DATES Proposal Instructions: Interested Offerors shall submit a comprehensive proposal package consisting of: Technical Approach (addressing EAM integration, physical maintenance, and predictive monitoring) Integrated Logistics & Sustainability Plan (addressing supply chain, SOPs, and knowledge transfer) Management, Programmatic, & Lifecycle Approach (Integrated Master Schedule, risk management, and scaling) Cost / Price Proposal Performance Work Statement (PWS) (directly derived from Attachment 001, Statement of Objectives) Key Dates: Questions Due Date: Sep 16, 2026, at 11:00 AM Central Time (CT) Site Visit Date: Sep 17, 2026, at 10:00 AM CT Proposal Due Date: Sep 25, 2026, at 11:00 AM Central Time (CT) Submission Instructions: Method: All questions and proposals must be submitted electronically via email. Email Address: evan.m.rea.civ@army.mil 5. GOVERNMENT POINTS OF CONTACT (POCs) Agreements Officer (AO): Eric C. Boston (eric.c.boston.civ@army.mil) Agreements Specialist / Contract Specialist: Evan M. sig_8f6b49f9ed8ec5cf26f3.description: Public information and project visibility services include: 1) Preparatory activities aimed at information and raising visibility • Public survey • Communication strategy 2) Project promotion • Design, production and delivery of promotional and informational materials 3) Informing target audiences with the aim of boosting visibility • Implementation of the communication strategy and communication plan • Internet promotion of the project • Organisation and preparation of events 4) Strengthening the Contracting Authority's capacity for project implementation purposes with the aim of project sustainability • Employee training on public speaking • Information and visibility guidelines for post-project activities • Crisis manual for preventive purposes of the Contracting Authority • Public relations aimed at boosting visibility • Relations with all types of publics determined by the communication strategy • Arranging interviews and guest appearances • Responses to enquiries from all types of publics • Press releases 5) Evaluation of implemented activities and preparation of reports in accordance with specified EU procedures • Monitoring and collection of media coverage (press clipping) • Analysis of project media activities. Public information and project visibility activities are mandatory elements of any project financed by EU funds. The purpose of these activities is: • to present the project, project idea, objectives and results; • raising awareness among the public, media and stakeholders regarding the role of the European Union and publishing the fact that the EU is co-financing the project; • to share acquired knowledge and experience, both professional and relating to project management. The subject of procurement is not divided into lots as it represents a functional and technical whole, as determined by the Feasibility Study and the Application to EU funds, and the Tenderer is obliged to offer the subject of procurement in its entirety, meaning the tender must cover all items of the Bill of Quantities. Therefore, the subject of procurement is not divided into lots because the management service relates to a single project financed by European Union funds, which represents a single functional, technical, implementation, financial and administrative entity. Although the project encompasses multiple activities, all activities are mutually linked in terms of deadlines, financing, reporting, risk management and communication with other stakeholders. Splitting the information and visibility service into lots would lead to a division of responsibilities, difficult coordination, potential uncoordinated action by multiple contractors, an increased risk of delays and irregularities, and difficulties in achieving project objectives. Following the above, the tenderer must offer the subject of procurement in its entirety. The subject functions and tasks are interconnected and interdependent, and division into lots would render the provision of the subject services less efficient and complicate the implementation of the contract.

sig_8fefea72088ce0135a52.description: THIS IS NOT A CONTRACT NOTICE OR A CALL FOR COMPETITION BUT A REQUEST FOR INFORMATION FOR MARKET RESEARCH AND TECHNICAL DIALOGUE. This request for information is used to survey the market and obtain information regarding the procurement. The contracting authority is not initiating a tendering procedure by publishing the request for information; instead, any procurement notice and call for competition will be published later. The request for information does not oblige the contracting authority to carry out the actual procurement. Responding to the request for information is not a prerequisite for participation in a possible later tendering procedure. Suppliers will not be paid compensation for responding to the request for information or participating in market dialogue. Responses given to this request for information will be used in planning the procurement of expert services to support the management of software assets (licence management). Expert assistance is needed flexibly across several different areas. The main user of HUS's centralised licence management system and product responsible persons for different areas maintain information on the most important software rights in a centralised system (Matrix42, SAM tool). In addition, supplier-specific portals are in use. In the planned procurement, the licence experts of the supplier to be procured would analyse and report quarterly on the current situation regarding agreed software rights (e.g. Microsoft, Oracle, Adobe and IBM manufacturers). They would compare information from different supplier portals with information in the centralised SAM tool, observe deficiencies and provide HUS with recommendations related to optimisation and compliance. The supplier should provide SAM Manager expertise, helping to manage valid software contracts. The supplier should advise on products, contract models, software lifecycles and usage rights. In addition, the supplier is hoped to provide support in building the management model for licence management. It is planned to include as an option in the procurement the entry of licence, cost and contract information into the SAM tool by the supplier instead of HUS personnel. HUS-yhtymä is renewing its ITSM system. In connection with this, the integration of licence management as part of this entity will also be evaluated. External expertise will also be needed for this. The purpose of the request for information is to survey suppliers available on the market and their service range. The purpose is to clarify service solutions, pricing principles and the cost level for the budget. HUS-yhtymä requests suppliers interested in the procurement described above to notify the contracting authority of their interest and attach to the response a general description/brochure of the service solution you offer for the need described above. Please note that all material is intended solely for conducting this market dialogue. The contracting authority will treat your response confidentially. Based on the responses to the request for information, clarifying questions may be presented to the supplier and/or an opportunity offered to present their solutions in a manner to be notified later. Suppliers that have responded to the request for information may possibly receive preliminary call for competition documents for comment. Responding or failing to respond to the request for information does not affect the supplier's position in a potential tendering procedure. We ask that responses to the request for information and notifications of interest be submitted no later than 20.3.2026 at 12:00 to the address kilpailutus.ict@hus.fi. sig_90116dd5159cffb33fea.description: The Student Loans company (SLC) have an agreement for Enhanced Security Operations Managed Service expiring April 2028. Requirement A Enhanced Security Operations Managed Service - MXDR Service The Supplier will provide a Managed Extended Detection and Response (MXDR) capability operating on a hybrid customer/supplier model. MXDR Service The Supplier will provide: • 24x7x365 monitoring of SLC security telemetry. • L1 and L2 Security Operations Centre capability (SLC retain L3). • Incident identification, triage and investigation. • Security use-case monitoring and tuning. • Management of Microsoft Sentinel detections. • SOAR playbook execution and optimisation. • Escalation management. • Alert enrichment. • Threat hunting capability. • Malicious activity investigation. • Service governance and performance management. • Security reporting at operational, tactical and strategic levels. Security Engineering (Operational) The Supplier shall provide: • L3 Engineering support for Sentinel. • Analytics rule development and tuning. • SOAR playbook management. • Connector maintenance and health monitoring. • Logging optimisation. • Onboarding and validation of agreed log sources. • Detection engineering support. • Detection gap analysis and monitoring coverage reviews. • Security use case development and continuous improvement. • Monitoring health checks. • Monitoring and remediation of ingestion issues. • Security platform optimisation. • Proactive automation support and development. • Threat intelligence-led detection improvements. Data Loss Prevention (DLP) & Phishing The Supplier shall: • Monitoring, triage and investigation of DLP, phishing, business email compromise (BEC), malicious email, malicious attachment and malicious URL alerts. • Investigation of suspected data loss, data exfiltration and policy breach events. • Support for user reported phishing submissions. • Escalation and coordination of confirmed incidents in accordance with agreed response procedures. • Identification and analysis of phishing campaigns, attacker infrastructure, indicators of compromise and emerging attack trends. • Recommendations for improvements to DLP policies, email security controls, detections and response processes. • Monthly reporting, trend analysis and security improvement recommendations. Reporting The Supplier shall provide: • Weekly operational reports. • Monthly service reports. • Quarterly service reviews. • KPI and SLA reporting. • Security metrics and trend analysis. Requirement B Enhanced Security Operations Managed Service - Vulnerability Management Service The Supplier shall provide Vulnerability Management services Monday to Friday, UK Core Hours (09:00-17:00). Vulnerability Management The Supplier shall: • Monitor vulnerability management queues. • Investigate vulnerability notifications. • Manage vulnerability triage. • Validate vulnerability findings. • Perform exploitability assessments. • Provide remediation recommendations. • Support exposure management activities. • Support CTEM activities. Stakeholder Engagement The Supplier shall: • Conduct monthly technical review meetings. • Support resolver teams. • Assist remediation planning. • Review remediation performance. • Provide vulnerability prioritisation guidance. Dashboarding & Reporting The Supplier shall: • Maintain executive dashboards. • Enhance Power BI reporting. • Produce technical reports. • Produce executive reports. • Produce PCI compliance reports. • Produce risk trending reports. Tooling The Supplier shall support: • Microsoft Defender for Endpoint. • Rapid7. • SLC PCI ASV Scanning tooling. • Jira. • Power BI. Requirement C Enhanced Security Operations Managed Service - Breach Attack Simulation Service The Supplier shall provide a Breach Attack Simulation (BAS) capability, currently using AttackIQ or similar. BAS Service The Supplier shall: • Operate and maintain the BAS platform. • Deploy and maintain BAS agents. • Configure integrations. • Execute scheduled simulations. • Execute customer-specific simulations. • Execute retests following remediation activities. Adversary Simulation Testing scenarios shall include: • Initial Access. • Execution. • Persistence. • Privilege Escalation. • Credential Access. • Lateral Movement. • Command and Control. • Exfiltration. • Malware. • Ransomware. • Advanced Persistent Threat activity. Security Validation The Supplier shall assess: • Security control effectiveness. • Security monitoring effectiveness. • Detection coverage. • Response capability. • Incident handling. • Use-case effectiveness. Reporting The Supplier shall produce: • Monthly BAS reports. • Executive summaries. • Technical findings. • Remediation recommendations. • Retest outcomes. Requirement D Enhanced Security Operations Managed Service - Cyber Threat Intelligence Service The Supplier shall provide strategic, operational and tactical Cyber Threat Intelligence services. Threat Intelligence Managed Service The Supplier shall provide: • Threat Intelligence reporting. • Integration into Microsoft Sentinel. • Indicator of Compromise feeds. • Threat actor intelligence. Operational Intelligence The Supplier shall provide: • Threat alerts. • Vulnerability intelligence. • Emerging threat notifications. • Campaign tracking. • Industry specific intelligence. Strategic Intelligence The Supplier shall provide: • Threat landscape assessments. • Quarterly threat reports. • Executive intelligence briefings. • Board level threat summaries. • Sector specific threat reporting. Security Operations Support The Supplier shall provide: • Intelligence support during incidents. • Threat hunting support. • Intelligence driven use-case creation. • Intelligence enrichment services. Requirement E Enhanced Security Operations Managed Service - Digital Forensics & Incident Response Retainer Service The Supplier shall provide a DFIR Retainer available 24x7x365. Cyber Incident Response The Supplier shall provide: • Incident investigation. • Malware analysis. • Threat containment. • Threat eradication. • Recovery support. • Crisis management support. • Regulator support. • On-site support Digital Forensics The Supplier shall provide: • Evidence acquisition. • Chain of custody management. • Endpoint forensics. • Server forensics. • Network forensics. • Cloud forensics. • Forensic reporting. Readiness Services The Supplier shall provide access to: • Tabletop exercises. • Incident simulations. • Executive workshops. • CSIRT training. • Lessons learned reviews. Retained Consultancy The Supplier shall provide specialist support including: • Security strategy input. • Audit support. • Major incident reviews. • Regulatory engagement support. • Ransomware negotiation services. Requirement F Enhanced Security Operations Managed Service - Security Architecture & Engineering Support Services The Supplier shall provide specialist Security Architecture and Engineering services on a call-off basis. Security Architecture The Supplier shall provide: • Security architecture reviews. • Security design authority support. • Secure by Design reviews. • Solution security reviews. • Threat modelling. • Architecture governance. • Security requirements definition. • Architectural risk assessments. Security Engineering The Supplier shall provide: • Technical security engineering. • Security tool implementation. • Security configuration reviews. • Security hardening activities. • Technical control implementation. Strategy & Transformation The Supplier shall provide: • Security roadmap development. • Target operating model development. • Control framework assessments. • Security maturity reviews. • Improvement planning. Governance & Assurance The Supplier shall provide: • Security assessments. • Risk management support. • Audit support. • KPI development. • Board reporting support. • Security governance support. • Independent design and control assurance. • Security exception and risk acceptance reviews. • Third party and supplier security assessments. sig_90272ec0d70d8c4bc2a3.description: SKI hereby invites tenders for a dynamic purchasing system (hereinafter the System) regarding the procurement of management consultancy services. The System includes the procurement of management consultancy services within the 6 service areas below. The content of the service areas is defined in more detail in Annex C. Subject of the System: Service area 1: Strategy and organisational development. Under this service area, services falling within one or more of the following five sub-areas may be purchased: 1. Sub-area 1: Strategy analysis 2. Sub-area 2: Strategy development 3. Sub-area 3: Strategy implementation 4. Sub-area 4: Organisational analysis and design as well as 5. Sub-area 5: Structural implementation. Service area 2: Business processes and efficiency. Under this service area, services falling within one or more of the following three sub-areas may be purchased: 1. Sub-area 1: Process analysis and process optimisation 2. Sub-area 2: Outsourcing 3. Sub-area 3: Public-private partnership (PPP). Service area 3: Analyses and evaluations. Under this service area, services falling within the following sub-area may be purchased: 1. Sub-area 1: Analyses and evaluations. Service area 4: Systems and management. Under this service area, services falling within one or more of the following three sub-areas may be purchased: 1. Sub-area 1: Finance and economic management 2. Sub-area 2: Quality and risk management 3. Sub-area 3: Control and optimisation of administrative processes. Service area 5: Human resources. Under this service area, services falling within one or more of the following three sub-areas may be purchased: 1. Sub-area 1: Leadership and employee development 2. Sub-area 2: Culture and behavioural development 3. Sub-area 3: Personnel policy. Service area 6: Green services. Under this service area, services falling within the following sub-area may be purchased: 1. Sub-area 1: Green services. The system is divided into 2 categories: • Category 1 Competence purchase • Category 2 Task purchase. Both categories concern the procurement of services, where those in category 1 are procured as hours, while those in category 2 are procured as a finished result (report, analysis, etc.). The procurement of services in both categories assumes that these are commonly used and generally available on the market at the time of procurement. The system can therefore not be used to procure services that are not generally available on the market. It is voluntary for all SKI customers, as listed in Annex B, Customer List, to make use of the system when they need to procure management consultancy services. Procurement of Competence purchase. In category 1, customers can procure management consultancy services within the 6 service areas described in Annex C, to meet the customer's competence needs. The consultancy services can be procured in the following way: Purchase of consultancy hours (number of hours x hourly rate).; Procurement of management consultancy services for task resolution. In category 2, customers can procure management consultancy services within the 6 service areas described in Annex C, to fulfil a specific task. The consultancy services can be procured in the following way: Purchase of task resolution at a fixed price.

sig_90a14e14039ee7844efb.description: Bournemouth University ("BU" or the "University") is exploring options for the provision of a co-managed Security Operations Centre (SOC) service to enhance and future-proof its cyber security operations capability. The University is seeking market feedback from experienced Managed Security Service Providers to better understand available service models, implementation approaches, commercial arrangements and indicative costs. BU has invested significantly in its internal cyber security capability and Microsoft security technologies, including Microsoft Sentinel, Microsoft Defender XDR, Entra ID Protection, Security Copilot and related services. The University is now considering how external specialist support could complement its in-house team through a co-managed SOC operating model. The key objectives of a future service are expected to include: - Enhancing monitoring, detection and response capabilities through either 24/7 or out-of-hours SOC coverage. - Improving threat detection, triage, false-positive reduction and incident response effectiveness. - Providing additional specialist expertise, operational resilience and surge capacity during major incidents or periods of heightened risk. - Maintaining and continuously improving detection rules, playbooks, automation and security monitoring capabilities. - Leveraging threat intelligence, sector insight, automation and AI-enabled capabilities to strengthen cyber resilience and operational effectiveness. - Establishing a robust governance, reporting and service management framework with clear responsibilities between BU and the supplier. - Maximising the value of the University's existing Microsoft security investments while minimising the need for additional tooling wherever appropriate. The University wishes to understand how the market can support these objectives, together with the costs, benefits, risks and implementation considerations associated with different service models. Supplier feedback received through this Preliminary Market Engagement exercise will help inform the University's future requirements, budget planning and procurement strategy. Lot 1: .

sig_90f42497d49596b7b5fd.description: AWE Plc ("AWE") is embarking on a critical transformation of its infrastructure as part of the national endeavour to support the United Kingdom's nuclear deterrent. AWE has been refining and formalising a new approach to infrastructure delivery designed to drive greater consistency, pace, and long-term value. This model is now being actively implemented. AWE is publishing this Preliminary Market Engagement Notice to inform and update the market regarding the establishment of the 16-year Client Partnership Framework (CPF). The pre-market engagement activities covered by this notice are for consultation on specific areas as prior market engagement took place under a Prior Information Notice (PIN) 3186 issued on 22nd April 2024. The new approach is structured around an integrated model for AWE's Infrastructure Projects Delivery (IPD) portfolio. Over the next 18 months, AWE will competitively procure or directly appoint suppliers across its three major infrastructure programmes, which will be supported by the new Client Partnership Framework (this procurement). The three major programmes are: 1) Future Materials Campus (FMC) a programme to renew existing facilities for the manufacture of nuclear components, storage of nuclear materials, provide improved science and analysis capabilities, and invest in new capabilities for nuclear material recovery. For FMC, we are seeking professional services suppliers to support client-side delivery, and ideally those that have experience in supporting the delivery of nuclear infrastructure build and associated commissioning. 2) Future Infrastructure Programme (FIP), focusing on delivering AWE's wider infrastructure needs in relation to new office accommodation; laboratories; testing facilities, site services, and advanced manufacturing facilities. For FIP we are looking for professional services suppliers to support client-side delivery, and ideally those that have experience of supporting whole life infrastructure, including design, build, maintenance. 3) Estates and Liabilities (E&L) management. Our sites have been operating for several decades, and as a result many facilities are reaching the end of their operational life. Liabilities management runs programmes to safely decommission and demolish these legacy facilities and manage the waste generated and are seeking suppliers with experience of the same. CPF will support FIP, FMC and E&L by providing client management services covering engineering, programme and project management and productivity to enable AWE as the Client to plan, control and scrutinise project investments for sensitive services and works - helping AWE retain its position as an informed, intelligent client at all stages of programme delivery. Services provided under the CPF (a range of design, technical, programme management and specialist services) will support AWE to effectively oversee and scrutinise the FIP, FMC and E&L Delivery Partners and ensure that these infrastructure programmes are delivered to time, cost and quality. Services will be required to support various programme stages including feasibility, design, development, construction and commissioning of infrastructure. As the programmes grow over the coming years, AWE is taking steps to ensure its supply chain is appropriately structured to support future delivery requirements. The arrangement will create a client partnership to act effectively as a trusted government partner. CPF will plan and design the investment portfolio, while providing the effective oversight to delivery partners (appointed via a separate procurement exercise) for time, cost and quality. The primary location is the Aldermaston site. The sites at Aldermaston and Burghfield are owned by the Ministry of Defence, with the management and operations carried out under contract by AWE and the nuclear site licence, environmental permits and other regulatory permissions held by AWE plc. AWE is independently regulated by several organisations including the Office for Nuclear Regulation (ONR), the Defence Nuclear Safety Regulator (DNSR), the Environment Agency (EA) and the Defence Nuclear Security Regulator (DefNucSyR) Each Supplier shall comply and carry out professional services in accordance with the Client's security requirements. AWE reserves the right to instruct Suppliers to deliver services at other AWE-owned or prospective site locations. sig_90f473a48a12a0b28cd3.description: SURF is at an advanced stage in preparing the procurement of service management software (ticketing system) on behalf of the participating organisations. The tender documents and procedures themselves will take place in the short term. Please note! These will be published with TenderNed references other than this prior information notice. After publication, a reference to the actual procurement procedures will be placed in this prior information notice. In broad terms, the intended Contract consists of the delivery of a service management software solution (the System), the implementation of the System at the participating organisations and related services. A service management software solution concerns a software solution with which service-providing processes are streamlined and supported, as a rule also referred to as a “ticketing system”. The System supports the registration and handling of Tickets and reporting on them. Although the contract is broadly similar, there is a distinction in needs among the participating organisations. Some of the participating organisations need a System that can (now or in the future) be expanded to support more processes than just IT service management, for example processes in the context of facility management and HR, while other institutions do not have this need and require a System that primarily supports IT service management. With the intended procurement procedure, SURF wishes to meet the needs of both “groups” of participating organisations. The contract is therefore divided into two procurement procedures that are mutually related. A distinction is made between a System that can support multiple processes, with at least support for ITSM processes and FMIS processes (an “Enterprise Service Management solution (ESM)”) and a solution that only supports ITSM processes (an ITSM solution). Tenderers may choose whether they participate in only one procurement process or both. With regard to the ESM solution, it applies that minimum support must be offered for IT service management processes (ITSM) and facility management processes (FMIS). The support of ITSM processes concerns the minimum purchase by a participating organisation. However, the Tenderer is obliged to also offer the support of FMIS processes in accordance with the requirements and wishes in this context, but the actual support thereof is optional for a participating institution to purchase. The support of other processes, such as, for example, processes in the context of building management, HR, finance, risk management, legal affairs and student affairs, can also optionally be part of this Contract, on the understanding that it must remain service management software. This means, for example, that a participating organisation can purchase service management software to support, for example, HR processes, but that this is not the same as setting up a full HR suite. The ESM procurement procedure will lead to a number of Framework Agreements with the winning Tenderers, after which participating organisations will organise a mini-competition for their individual contract, in which the exact processes that the relevant participating organisation wishes to purchase will be further specified. Award of the Framework Agreements will take place on the basis of the best price-quality ratio. With regard to the ITSM solution, it applies that this will only support IT service management processes (ITSM) and that these contracts do not include support for FMIS processes or other processes. For this procurement need, a Dynamic Purchasing System will be set up by SURF, in which participating organisations will place a further request for their individual contract.

sig_913b82db81f618e71dcf.description: The Federal Republic of Germany is obliged under the Regulation on the European Health Data Space (EHDS Regulation) to set up a National Contact Point for eHealth (NCPeH) in order to ensure connection to the MyHealth@EU infrastructure. The NCPeH serves for the secure exchange of structured health data in the event of treatment. The intended use cases include: • E-prescription (ePrescription and eDispensation, short: ePeD) • European electronic health record for patient summaries (Patient Summary, short: PS) • Results of medical examinations, including laboratory and other diagnostic results and related reports (Medical Test Results) • Discharge reports (Discharge Reports) • Medical imaging and image findings (Medical Imaging Studies and Reports) A distinction is made here between Land A and Land B scenarios. For the so-called Land B scenarios, in which data from EU citizens is transmitted to Germany, an NCPeH proxy and a client-side WebApp running in the browser (name: EU-Webportal WebApp) are provided in addition to the NCPeH specialist service. gematik is examining the contract to award the development, provision and operation of the NCPeH proxy and the EU web portal (incl. EU-Webportal WebApp) to an external service provider. The following presentation of the system landscape serves as an overview of the procurement subject. The components in the yellow box, including their subcomponents and interfaces, are to be developed, provided and operated.

sig_92caf0427995304453c5.description: The Universität Hamburg (hereinafter 'UHH'), as a university of excellence with more than 43.000 students and approx. 6.000 employees, is one of the most research-intensive universities in Germany and at the same time one of the largest training institutions in Northern Germany. With its 'Flagship University' concept in the Hamburg metropolitan region, it maintains innovative and cooperative links with scientific and non-scientific partners. It produces future-oriented social goods for the location – but also nationally and internationally – namely education, knowledge and the exchange of knowledge, under the guiding principle of sustainability. The executive boards of the 6 Hamburg universities signed a Letter of Intent in April 2024 regarding the joint IT operation of the Hamburg universities. The aim here is to establish a joint organisation that is controlled by the universities and understands, bundles, and implements their needs, and provides high-quality IT services specifically for scientific institutions across the entire service spectrum. A service centre is to be built and established with the goal of creating synergies and thus providing digital services more efficiently, in a more targeted and user-centred manner, more comprehensively, and at the same time with better quality and protection against cyberattacks. In the course of this joint IT operation, it is necessary to create a joint, federated Identity and Access Management (IAM) structure for the Hamburg universities. The overarching goal is the provision of services for all Hamburg universities based on established federation technologies. Each university is to be equipped with a local IAM system, and the then technology-compatible systems are to be integrated into a joint, federated state identity and access infrastructure. The authoritative management of identities remains decentralised at the individual institutions. A central master directory is to be set up to hold the personal attributes necessary for joint operation. Such a federated infrastructure enables the universities to participate in jointly or centrally provided services (e.g. cloud, collaboration and e-learning services) and at the same time significantly increases the security of access, as modern, open standards such as SAML, OpenID Connect (OIDC), SCIM and FIDO2 are to be implemented throughout. For an organisation-independent, uniform and permanent identification of users, e.g. also when changing between universities, the nationwide federation service of the German National Research and Education Network (DFN-AAI), including the eduID service, is to be used as a basis. The joint state federation is intended as a sub-federation within the DFN-AAI in order to enable cross-university coordination beyond a uniform attribute set. The project aims to design, build and transfer this joint federated state IAM infrastructure into regular operation. A later inclusion of further scientific institutions in Hamburg is not excluded.
sig_92caf0427995304453c5.title: Establishment of a joint federated identity and access management infrastructure for Hamburg universities

sig_93b42c4d078a0b1e073b.description: The Pathways to Enable Secure Open-Source Ecosystems (PESOSE) program supports the translation of open-source science and engineering-focused research products into safe and sustainable ecosystems that address national and societal challenges. Open-source tools such as software, hardware, machine learning models, languages, and data platforms are designed to be shared as they are publicly-accessible and modifiable. These tools spark innovation in critical fields as varied as artificial intelligence (AI) and cloud computing, banking, healthcare, research, education, next-gen manufacturing, mobility, and National security (including cybersecurity). PESOSE supports the creation of managing organizations for these ecosystems, ensuring strong governance, distributed development, and broad user communities across academia, industry, and government. PESOSE also supports enhancements to the safety, security, and privacy of Open-Source Ecosystems (OSE) by addressing significant vulnerabilities, both technical and socio-technical, to improve the resistance of the ecosystem against threats. This solicitation seeks three types of proposals, allowing teams to propose specific activities to: 1) scope and plan the establishment of an OSE, 2) establish and expand a sustainable OSE based on a robust, promising open-source product that meets an emergent societal or national need, and 3) improve the safety, security, and privacy of an existing OSE and its products.
sig_93b42c4d078a0b1e073b.title: Pathways to Enable Secure Open-Source Ecosystems (PESOSE)

sig_94078d3150647e3ceb5f.description: Creation of a dynamic purchasing system aimed at the contractualisation of intellectual service missions to support the implementation of pooled resource organisations between projects implemented by Expertise France and located within the same geography. To apply for the DPS, it is mandatory to register on the PLACE platform, via which the consultation documents can be downloaded and responses must be submitted. Applications may be submitted by natural persons, private companies, public establishments and/or associations. As a public agency for international technical cooperation, Expertise France works alongside partner countries to advise and support them in strengthening their public policies. To this end, the agency coordinates and implements national or regional scale projects in the main areas of public action: - democratic, economic and financial governance; - peace, stability and security; - climate, biodiversity and sustainable development; - health and human development. The cooperation activity conducted by Expertise France results in the concentration of activities in certain geographies, which require, based on findings and concerted discussions, the pooling of resources within shared offices or project support units (PSUs). As part of its organisational transformation, Expertise France has set up a Task Force dedicated to decentralisation. This initiative aims to strengthen and accelerate the decentralisation process by consolidating the means of implementation, support and management of field activities. The main objective of the Decentralisation Task Force (DTF) is to coordinate and ensure the effective deployment of decentralised structures, including Country Offices, Project Support Units (PSUs), as well as shared offices and decentralised project teams. In this context, the " Decentralisation Task Force Expertise Network " enables the rapid mobilisation of appropriate technical expertise, specialised in change management and the establishment of decentralised structures, in the intervention countries of Expertise France, in accordance with the defined target organisations. The intellectual service missions will support the implementation of pooled resource organisations between projects implemented by Expertise France within the same geographical area. The expertise missions awarded under this DPS will thus contribute to optimising and strengthening the capacities deployed in the field, in a decentralised approach and with an improvement in project management by the Agency. The expertise missions, once validated by the DTF team, will be the subject of specific contracts awarded under this DPS. Each specific contract will be awarded to the operator that has submitted the most economically advantageous tender, on the basis of the award criteria set out in the contract notice or, where the call for competition is published by means of a prior information notice or a periodic indicative notice, in the invitation to confirm interest. These criteria may, where applicable, be further specified in the invitation to tender. The selected tenderer will then execute the mission under the direct supervision of the field team and under the coordination of the DTF team, for the entire duration of the mission. Deliverables will be validated by the DTF team, in liaison with the relevant departments. The duration of the expertise missions will be specified in each specific contract and may not exceed the validity period of the DPS.
sig_94078d3150647e3ceb5f.title: Decentralisation Task Force Expertise Network Dynamic Purchasing System (DPS) aimed at the contractualisation of intellectual service missions to support the implementation of pooled resource organisations between projects implemented by Expertise France and located within the same geography.

sig_941f6f866f93ffc2709d.description: The Advanced Research Projects Agency for Health (ARPA-H) is soliciting proposals from small business concerns (SBCs) that possess the research and development (R&D) expertise to conduct innovative research that will contribute toward ARPA-H mission needs, Small Business Innovation Research (SBIR), and Small Business Technology Transfer (STTR) program objectives. Please see the cover page of the attachment "SBIR_STTR_BAA_FY26" for applicable Stage 1 and Stage 2 deadlines for each open topic. Please see the Attachment H "ARPA-H_SBP_Government_Answered_Questions" for responses to the Q&A period. The purposes of the SBIR and STTR programs are to: (a) stimulate technological innovation; (b) strengthen the role of small business in meeting Federal research/research & development (R/R&D) needs; (c) foster and encourage participation by socially and economically disadvantaged small business concerns and women-owned business concerns; and (d) increase private sector commercialization of innovations derived from Federal R/R&D, thereby increasing competition, productivity and economic growth. For purposes of the SBIR and STTR programs, a small business concern is any business concern that, on the date of award, (1) is organized for profit, with a place of business located in the United States, which operates primarily within the United States or which makes a significant contribution to the United States economy through payment of taxes or use of American products, materials or labor; (2) is in the legal form of an individual proprietorship, partnership, limited liability company, corporation, joint venture, association, trust or cooperative, except that where the form is a joint venture, there must be less than 50 percent participation by foreign business entities in the joint venture; (3) more than 50% directly owned and controlled by one or more individuals (who are citizens or permanent resident aliens of the United States), other business concerns (each of which is more than 50% directly owned and controlled by individuals who are citizens or permanent resident aliens of the United States), or any combination of these; OR more than 50% owned by multiple venture capital operating companies, hedge funds, private equity firms, or any combination of these. No single venture capital operating company, hedge fund, or private equity firm may own more than 50% of the concern; AND, (4) has, including its affiliates, no more than 500 employees. Note: This size standard is established by law for the SBIR program, regardless of the NAICS Code assigned. See 13 C.F.R. § 121.702. THE FOLLOWING ARE THE CURRENTLY OPEN RESEARCH TOPICS. PLEASE SEE SECTION 8 OF THE BAA FOR FURTHER INFORMATION ARPA-H 01 -?Development of an annual test to inform women about their future fertility?-?The purpose of this topic is to discover new biomarkers that provide women with actionable data for fertility planning.? Results from this work will help inform the program manager regarding the feasibility of future programs focused on enhancing natural fertility before the need of IVF and guiding the development of women’s health monitoring and improvement tools. This work will develop a diagnostic test that can assess fertility status and generate an estimated timeline for the onset of infertility. This topic seeks to develop a test that is affordable, suitable for at least annual use, and provides user-friendly results for patients and care teams to support childbearing decisions.??? ARPA-H 02 -?Versatile Bioadhesives?- The purpose of this topic is to develop next-generation bioadhesive platforms that can safely and reliably seal, bond, and repair a wide range of tissues in challenging clinical conditions, including wet, bloody, and mechanically dynamic environments. These platforms may also be designed to deliver biologics or small molecules as part of treatment. The goal is to create bioadhesives with key performance attributes such as strong tissue adhesion, controlled degradation, reversibility, biocompatibility, and broad compatibility across multiple tissues and organs. If successful, this topic could enable widely deployable solutions for hemostasis, leak prevention, tissue repair, and device fixation, ultimately helping reduce complications and improve patient outcomes across many care settings ARPA-H 03 -?Universal Platform for Living Adaptive Toxin-removal (UNI-PLAT)?-?The purpose of this topic area is to catalyze the development of a universal, “plug-and-play” synthetic biology platform that enables next-generation microbial chassis capable of performing a broad array of programmable functions. While this solicitation primarily uses toxin removal as a proof-of-concept in relation to chronic disease management, the platform is intended to be adaptable to a range of challenges across industries such as environmental remediation, biomanufacturing, agriculture, holistic medicine, and therapeutic discovery. The broader goal is to create a stable, reliable, and easily reprogrammable microbial platform that demonstrates potential for cross-sector impact beyond the initial use case.? ARPA-H 04 -?Breaking Ground: The First Curative, Durable, Non-Surgical Therapy for Endometriosis?–?The purpose of this topic aims to develop treatments for endometriosis that are non-surgical. Proposers are expected to develop novel, non-surgical therapies to decrease the size or deactivate endometrial implants, to decrease inflammation cause by implants, and / or prevent growth or regrowth of the lesions. Broadly, this should be a novel, non-surgical, curative treatment for endometriosis. ARPA-H 05 -?ARPA-H Lineage Topic?-?The purpose of this topic supports the advancement, commercialization, and translation of technologies that originated from ARPA-H funded efforts. It is intended to help small businesses and startups develop viable products based on these technologies. ARPA-H’s goal is to give small businesses an off-ramp to finish developing their technology/product, explore secondary or interim applications of the technology, and time to achieve self-sufficiency. ARPA-H 06 -?Rapid Comprehensive Diagnostic Test for Multi-System Autoimmune Disease?-The purpose of this topic is to spur the development of novel, rapid diagnostic assays for multi-system autoimmune disease, which?represents?an unmet healthcare need. Moreover, in its ideal embodiment this diagnostic test might allow typical primary care physicians to diagnose and predict tissue-specific autoimmune disease manifestations, thereby streamlining referral of the patient to a specialist. This goal is made more?feasible?by recent technological developments including the ability to detect tissue-specific signatures of immune-mediated stress by assessing circulating cells and/or?tissue-specific molecular products.?? ARPA-H 07 -?Virtual Human Brain for the Development of Neurosurgical Robotics -?The purpose of this topic aims to take a first step toward AI-assisted intracranial microsurgery by creating a high-resolution, physically and anatomically accurate virtual human brain.

sig_94329553e52c261ebc1a.description: The client's IT encompasses a very wide range of services from merchandise management and billing systems such as SAP through control centre systems to apps, such as MVGO. IT demand sometimes grows faster than internal staff can be built up and should it decrease, reducing internal staff is sluggish. This scaling requirement is addressed by awarding services to external parties. One form of this is the external takeover of testing of software applications in a scope appropriate for each application (test concept, test management, test case definition, execution of functional and non-functional tests (e.g. L&P tests, regression tests, exploratory tests, ...), test automation). This support takes place in both traditional and agile environments. The client currently has 3 candidate groups of applications for which they wish to outsource testing. The known support effort is approx. 3 to 5 FTE. During the contract term, applications may be added, removed, or the annual effort for them may fluctuate. A framework agreement is being tendered. The individual applications are commissioned via call-off (possibly also with multiple call-offs). The client's experience shows that domain knowledge is essential for service delivery, especially when testing. The tender covers the following domains: • Public transport sales: Sales processes (app- and web-based sales channels, mass customer billing) • Purchasing and logistics (SAP MM/SD/CS) • Finance (SAP FI/CO) • Maintenance including mobile maintenance (SAP PM, app applications) There is no obligation for the client to exhaust the contract under this framework agreement. Services are fundamentally to be provided remotely. Exceptions that require on-site service delivery are workshops and, where applicable, tests in connection with hardware that is only available on-site at the client (e.g. a ticket vending machine). Other special conditions for contract performance: Contract execution in German, written and oral; within EU GDPR
sig_94329553e52c261ebc1a.title: SV-JMÄ-251014-004, Managed Testing - Application Tests

sig_948f997e226b2727a5ab.description: The National Institute on Aging (NIA) intends to publish a Notice of Funding Opportunity (NOFO) to solicit applications that develop or incorporate novel, cutting-edge study designs/methods/analytic approaches through the use of machine learning, artificial intelligence, and adaptive designs to allow the discovery of health/function profiles at the level of the individual and that could lead to the implementation of personalized prevention plans/interventions for cognitive/brain health in older adults. The initiative would allow for both basic research in animal models, as well as the development of profiles for humans, which would span levels of analysis from cellular to societal. Applications are not being solicited at this time. Notice is being provided to allow potential applicants sufficient time to develop meaningful collaborations and responsive projects. This NOFO will utilize the R01 activity code. Investigators with expertise and insights into this area of aging research are encouraged to begin to consider applying for this new NOFO.
sig_948f997e226b2727a5ab.title: Novel Approaches to Advance Precision Aging and Cognitive Health

sig_94b098030ca701df42ae.description: The dynamic purchasing system covers the Contracting Authority's ongoing procurement of technical consultants. The dynamic purchasing system is divided into 10 independent categories, for which Applicants who meet the suitability requirements are pre-qualified, and in which the Contracting Authority's mini-tenders are conducted. A category must be viewed as an independent framework agreement. An economic operator can thus apply for admission to the system for one, several or all categories. An economic operator must be admitted as a Participant in a category in order to have the opportunity to bid on the mini-tenders that may be published for the category in question. The categories covered by the system are described in more detail in Annex 1 – Category Overview. The category includes, among other things, advice on (non-exhaustive): - Total building programme for larger projects, incl. new construction - Room programme - Visions for construction; The category includes, among other things, advice on (non-exhaustive): - Light - Sound - Ventilation (per 01.08.2026) - CTS systems - EMS - energy management; The category includes, among other things, advice on room layout of (non-exhaustive): - Theory classrooms - Laboratories - Specialist rooms for e.g. sports, sports halls, offices, canteen and common areas; The category includes, among other things, advice on (non-exhaustive): - Roofing felt - Tiled roofs - Skylights; The category includes, among other things, advice on (non-exhaustive): - Fire regulations - Static calculations; The category includes, among other things, advice on (non-exhaustive): - LCA calculation - Energy optimisation (e.g. solar cells) - Recycling of materials - Certification; The category includes, among other things, advice on (non-exhaustive): - Toxic substances in both buildings and subsoil - The load-bearing capacity of the subsoil; The category includes, among other things, advice on (non-exhaustive): - User involvement in conversions, extensions and new buildings; The category includes, among other things, advice on (non-exhaustive): - Surveys - Changes to cadastral boundaries; The category includes, among other things, advice on (non-exhaustive): - Landscape architecture - Parking - Outdoor sports areas - Multi-purpose courts - Outdoor recreational areas

sig_94b4877e1ed2fd22c641.description: Subject matter of the tender for a framework agreement for strategy consulting for public contracting authorities with integrated implementation competence: The contracting authorities are to be supported both in the development of strategic target images and in their translation into concrete, implementable measures. The subject of the framework agreement is strategy consulting for public contracting authorities with integrated implementation competence: The contracting authorities are to be supported both in the development of strategic target images and in their translation into concrete, implementable measures. The framework agreement deliberately does not provide for separate lots for this. Since implementation competence is an integral part of every consulting service here and is not to be provided downstream by a second provider, the entire service is procured from a single source. This avoids the interface problem between "strategy" and "implementation" and keeps the procedure lean. The framework agreement is concluded with a single contractor (individual contract model, no multi-partner model). Commissioning in individual cases takes place via direct individual call-offs by the contracting authorities on the basis of the conditions defined in the framework agreement.
sig_94b4877e1ed2fd22c641.title: Strategy consulting

sig_94d0836410ef6a9595ae.description: The procurement concerns the XR, metaverse and web3 sub-implementations of the supra-municipal XR Museum project. The procurement will be carried out dynamically and the individual sub-projects will be tendered at a later stage among the suppliers selected in this procurement. The XR Museum is a joint project between the museums of Järvenpää, Kerava and Tuusula to build a fully virtual museum centre. In addition to the municipal museums, the private museums Ainola and Lottamuseo are also involved. The project has received funding from the European Union's Next Generation EU structural funding. The project started in spring 2023 and the new museum will open in spring 2025. The project is led by a steering group of representatives from the participating museums and municipalities. The project will be implemented by a separate project team. The XR Museum consists of different XR, metaverse and web3 implementations. Most of these are browser-based, but we also work on VR productions, for example. The aim is to create experiential and interactive ways to experience the art and culture of the region. All applications produced by the project will be designed and tested in collaboration with audiences and stakeholders, and participatory processes will be integrated into all sub-projects. So far, the project has produced 360-photo constructed remote tours and a model of the artist's home Villa Kokkonen. Work is underway to build a metaverse environment and create an event space for the museum. Future work will include the production of more modelling and browser and VR experiences using these. sig_953d35e7ecb0dc9c7a32.description: The aim of the award procedure is to commission a high-performing managed service provider (MSP) that will take over the complete planning, management, implementation and operational transfer of the brownfield transformation of the existing SAP ECC system landscape to SAP S/4HANA Cloud, Private Edition, as part of "RISE with SAP". The subject of the contract is a holistic transformation and operational service. This includes in particular the technical and functional analysis of the existing system landscape, the SAP S/4HANA conversion, the transfer to the private cloud environment, test migrations and data conversion, the adaptation of custom developments, add-ons and interfaces, as well as the implementation and optimisation of the relevant commercial processes. In addition, SAP Fiori, reporting and embedded analytics, as well as the necessary integration services, in particular using the SAP Business Technology Platform and the SAP Integration Suite, must be taken into account. The contractor shall accompany the transformation including tests, cutover, go-live, hypercare, training and handover to regular operations and shall subsequently take over the agreed managed services as well as operational, support and further development services. In this context, particular account must be taken of the clean core approach, the maintenance of ongoing clinical operations, the existing dependencies on SAP IS-H, i.s.h.med, SAP HCM and other peripheral systems, as well as requirements regarding data protection, information security, compliance, availability, scalability and an orderly exit scenario. The contractual basis is intended to be the conclusion of an EVB-IT cloud contract, which covers both the transformation and implementation services up to acceptance and the managed services, operational, support and further development services to be provided thereafter.
sig_953d35e7ecb0dc9c7a32.title: TNWB: S/4HANA procurement

sig_95cf5ff5ad4732ed2382.description: Pursuant to Article L. 2113-2 of the Public Procurement Code, SMO Nord Pas-de-Calais Numérique acts as a central purchasing body in the sense that this buyer acquires supplies or services for other contracting authorities, public undertakings or contracting entities. The purpose of this contract is the supply of: • personal RGS** and eIDAS authentication and signature certificates, on a USB key type medium, for the agents and elected officials of the member local authorities and public establishments; • NFC cards on a physical medium, intended for the agents and elected officials of the member local authorities and public establishments, supplied according to the same ordering, delivery and handover procedures as personal certificates on a physical medium (cf. point 3.5). The Syndicat mixte Nord-Pas-de-Calais Numérique, in partnership with the Territorial Civil Service management centres of the Nord (Cdg59) and the Pas-de-Calais (Cdg62), operates a central purchasing body for the local authorities and public establishments of the Nord and Pas-de-Calais departments. This central purchasing body facilitates access to the authentication and electronic signature certificates necessary for the dematerialisation of administrative procedures and documents. It offers member entities a shared system, allowing them to benefit from negotiated rates and a simplified ordering process. At the date of launch of this consultation, 560 local authorities and public establishments belonging to the central purchasing body have access to a dematerialised platform allowing them to order their certificates directly. This contract is a continuation of the previous contract. It aims to guarantee the continuity of the service provided to the members of the central purchasing body, within an updated regulatory framework marked in particular by the evolution of the eIDAS regulation 2.0 and the strengthening of security requirements. This consultation pursues the following objectives: - To guarantee, for all members of the central purchasing body, the continuity and quality of the service for the supply of RGS** and eIDAS certificates; - To promote the consistency of digital public services open to users and facilitate their adoption, thanks to interfaces and operating modes that are similar from one local administration to another; - To promote the dematerialisation of exchanges in order to save time, eliminate time or location constraints, reduce costs related to paper and postage, and optimise the tracking and searching of documents; - To allow fully digital management of data and documents produced internally or transmitted by partners, whether they are administrations, citizens or suppliers.
sig_95cf5ff5ad4732ed2382.title: CONTRACT FOR THE SUPPLY OF RGS** AND EIDAS 2.0 AUTHENTICATION AND SIGNATURE CERTIFICATES (NATURAL PERSONS) AND SERVER CERTIFICATES (WEB)

sig_95d910cedef83f709841.description: DESCRIPTION OF THE SUBJECT The subject of the procurement currently being prepared is a company, credit and control information retrieval service for the use of Valtiokonttori. Valtiokonttori is an agency under the Ministry of Finance (VM), which is responsible for state debt management, investment and financial services, as well as the administration and supervision of state loans, guarantees, warranties and interest subsidies. In addition, it handles the state's central accounting and the preparation of financial statements, as well as compensation and benefit matters. Valtiokonttori maintains a financial information repository for municipalities and wellbeing services counties, produces analysis and reporting services for the state administration, manages the EU's Recovery and Resilience Facility, and maintains an electronic procurement notification system. Valtiokonttori manages loans, interest subsidies and state guarantees and warranties granted by the state. Up-to-date company, credit and control information is needed daily, e.g. in making payment and grant decisions and in risk management. The goal of Valtiokonttori is to renew the currently used - company and credit information retrieval service - control service - integration into the Microsoft Dynamics CRM system The service has approximately 40 users, of which 2 users act as main users. The subject of the procurement possibly also includes a sanctions list retrieval service. In addition to written comments on the draft tender documentation, the Contracting Authority reserves the possibility to meet interested companies in Teams meetings. REGISTRATION FOR THE MARKET DIALOGUE We ask companies interested in tendering in the competitive tendering to register for the market dialogue by providing the following information by email to the address kilpailutus@hansel.fi with the subject "VK/4262/2025 Valtiokonttorin company, credit and control information retrieval service": • company name and business ID • name of the contact person • email address of the contact person. sig_95f9baedbbe9315de7ed.description: The aim of this procedure is to procure modern and autonomous mobile systems intended for monitoring fruit and vegetable crops. The Contracting Authority expects the delivery of three systems in identical hardware and functional configuration, enabling their parallel use in different locations or by different user teams. The subject of the contract is a complete, integrated system combining the functions of a mobile robotic platform, measurement, data acquisition and processing systems, and analytical software supporting plant condition assessment. The aim of the contract is to create a tool enabling repeatable, automated and spatially located measurements in actual agricultural and horticultural production conditions, in a more accurate and efficient manner than classical manual observations. The system is to support ongoing crop monitoring and provide data for the further development of analytical algorithms, including solutions based on artificial intelligence methods. The ordered robots are to act as mobile measurement platforms, capable of working in various agrotechnical conditions. The robots must be adapted to work in actual agricultural conditions, including variable ground, terrain unevenness, moisture, dust, mud, vegetation and farm infrastructure elements. Each system should also be adapted for transport between locations and include appropriate transport equipment enabling safe loading and unloading without the use of specialist lifting devices.
sig_95f9baedbbe9315de7ed.title: Construction and delivery of a robot meeting the requirements of precision horticulture in the form of an autonomous electric platform equipped with remote sensing sensors

sig_9615901c52843cc4f9ad.description: Danmarks Nationalbank ("Nationalbanken") is Denmark's central bank. Nationalbanken's operations are based on the Act on Danmarks Nationalbank from 1936, according to which Nationalbanken's task is to maintain a secure monetary system in Denmark and to facilitate and regulate the circulation of money and lending. This task description remains applicable to Nationalbanken's role and responsibility as a central bank. Nationalbanken performs a number of socially critical tasks, including the operation and monitoring of critical payment infrastructure as well as the exercise of central monetary policy functions. The processes, systems and data supporting these tasks are of crucial importance for financial stability and confidence in the Danish financial system. Nationalbanken's business needs must ensure that the contract supports a high level of delivery security, robustness and continuity in the provision of the Services. The Supplier is therefore expected to exhibit a proactive approach to both daily delivery and the handling of risks, opportunities for improvement and technological development. Nationalbanken has a high focus on information security, and the Supplier must ensure a security level corresponding to that found in comparable organisations with a corresponding threat profile. Nationalbanken's security requirements apply to all deliveries and activities carried out for or on behalf of Nationalbanken as part of the provision of the Contract's Services. This places high demands on security, robustness and operational resilience. On this basis, requirements are set that the Supplier must, throughout the contract period, be certified according to ISO/IEC 27001:2022 or an equivalent international standard. In addition, the Contract requires that the Supplier complies with SWIFT CSP requirements and can document this compliance to both Nationalbanken and SWIFT. Nationalbanken primarily uses Microsoft-based technologies and tools in its IT architecture and system support. Furthermore, Service Delivery Management is based on ITIL v3 principles and processes. The purpose of the contract is to establish supplier cooperation for the delivery of services related to IT workplaces, device management, on-site support and service desk. The IT workplace includes, among other things, the supply and support of desktop computers, laptops and peripheral equipment, as well as service desk functions and related operational and support services. In addition, support for tablets and smartphones. In connection with the implementation of Windows 11, Nationalbanken has carried out a major replacement of older devices, which has led to a significant modernisation of Nationalbanken's PC portfolio. This is a high-end PC model issued to all employees and external consultants. The Supplier must in this connection acquire ownership of certain assets (hardware). The Supplier must act as a central contact interface (Single Point of Contact) for the covered services and engage in close cooperation with Nationalbanken's internal functions, Nationalbanken's Service Integrator and other suppliers. Nationalbanken uses a multi-supplier setup, and the Supplier must therefore support effective integration and cooperation with other suppliers, including relevant service management processes and tools. The Customer makes the Customer's ITSM solution available to the Supplier for use in the subsequent provision of the services. The Supplier must use Nationalbanken's ITSM solution for the processes, case registrations, knowledge articles, updates and activities designated by Nationalbanken. Likewise, Nationalbanken makes a collaboration platform available to the Supplier for use in the collaboration between Nationalbanken and the Supplier. The Supplier may be met with requirements to observe the Act on Transfer of Undertakings.

sig_966964fa4ce72f0599dd.description: This procurement description outlines the context and requirements for Sunderland City Council ("the Council") for the appointment of a Managing Agent to provide a range of key services at the Council's Business Centres ("the Centres") namely, Evolve Business Centre, Sunderland Software Centre, and Washington Business Centre. The Council previously procured the construction and delivery of the Centres over the period from 2006 to 2014 (drawing on resources secured through the European Regional Development Fund ("ERDF") alongside the Council's own resources) to support the economic development of the city, creating facilities for businesses to start up and grow within the city. All of the Centres have been managed throughout their lifetime directly by the Council and together, as at end July 2025, are home to 75 businesses, collectively employing a total of 363 people. It is now considered that external expertise is required from a Managing Agent to provide a combination of strategic and operational leadership and management services to work alongside the Council in order to drive optimum performance from the Centres, both in terms of securing operational efficiencies and maximising economic impact (considered to be the dual objectives). It is proposed that the Managing Agent would be required to deliver the following core services on behalf of the Council as the owner of the Centres: • Strategic management of the Centres including targeted improvement of operational practices - with responsibility for procuring and appointing all contractors and with day-to-day supervision of the Council's retained staff operations. • Marketing and letting of vacant spaces. • Integrated culture of business development / support to stimulate business growth and expansion. • ICT Managed Service Provision available to businesses on an opt in / opt out basis and • Delivery of repairs and maintenance. Lot 1: .
sig_966964fa4ce72f0599dd.title: The Appointment of a Managing Agent for Sunderland City Council Business Centres

sig_96b721fbe0907b462a8b.description: Modernisation of the central firewall system in the Forschungsverbund Berlin e.V. Lot LOT-0000: Modernisation of the central firewall system in the Forschungsverbund Berlin e.V.. The aim of the project is the modernisation of the overall firewall and security architecture incl. next-generation endpoint protection of the research association. The future solution must meet the current and future requirements for information security, availability, scalability, multi-tenancy, traceability of administrative activities and economical operation. General requirements for the new firewall structure: - Multi-stage firewall structure with centrally operated perimeter firewall cluster and segmentation firewall clusters per institute, whereby different manufacturers must be provided (dual-vendor strategy) B-criterion in BM - VLAN- and IP-based institute-related segmentation - Virtual domains for segmentation of the perimeter firewall of corporate IT - At least two appliances per geographical location in active-passive operation - Expansion of backbone throughput to 10 gigabits per second with the option to expand to 40 gigabits per second without replacing the hardware as well as loop-free design of the network - Number of simultaneous sessions: 20.000 to 65.000; number of VPN uses per institute: at least 40 to 70 users; maximum all employees in the FVB (1.600 employees) - Consideration of QoS mechanisms for VoIP and latency-sensitive applications - Granular, association-wide uniform role and authorisation concept for administrative access - Multi-factor authentication for users (native or via identity provider) and administrators (native) - NGFW functionalities: o IPS and IDS o Application IP o Geo IP filter - Separation of networks (e.g. laboratory networks) via VLAN - Central DNS security service, DoS defence, content filtering and advanced threat protection as well as the integration of external blacklists at perimeter level - Powerful and practicable DoS defence - Common, multi-tenant WAF service for web applications - Platform support for VPN access for Windows, Linux and MacOS - Compliance check for all operating systems - Central management for perimeter (mandatory) and segmentation firewalls (optional) - Tenant separation with granular graduation of administration rights - Open interfaces to support REST- or XML-based APIs, Syslog, Net-Flow/IPFIX, SAML, LDAP, RADIUS and other common market integration interfaces - Remote access: the support of established procedures with split tunnelling and carrier-grade NAT must be provided - Identification of institute affiliation, for example via certificates or naming conventions - SSL interception (inbound for published services as well as outbound for critical servers/clients - E-mail security, multi-tenant, optionally acquirable per institute - Sandbox functions - Out-of-band management - Min. interface for the automatic integration of certificates - IPv6 future-proofing (a conversion to IPv6 is not planned within the scope of the project) - Central, multi-tenant log management with at least three months retention period, local buffering or short-term fallback retention and interfaces to a possible SIEM - Tenant-related and institute-specific logging Suitable support and service services must be offered for the procured hardware, software, subscriptions and management components. These include fault clearance, maintenance, software support, manufacturer and system house support, hardware replacement, patch and release management, operational support and a comprehensible escalation process. The availability of the future solution is to be set at at least 99,9 % per year. The specific SLA design, in particular reaction times, recovery times, service times, planned change windows and emergency changes, will be discussed jointly in dialogue taking into account redundancy, economic efficiency and operational risk. In addition, NOC services with security analysis must be provided by the future service provider. Pure SOC services are to be treated as a supplementary option or add-on. For SOC-related services, in particular monitoring, triage, analysis, alerting, initial processing, incident response, notification chains, on-call duty, multi-tenancy, SIEM/SOAR connection, log sources, sensor technology, reporting and communication channels must be considered.
sig_96b721fbe0907b462a8b.title: Modernisation of the central firewall system in Forschungsverbund Berlin e.V.

sig_96d47f00ae49803bb358.description: The National Agency for Digital Judicial Investigation Techniques (ANTENJ) manages the sovereign tools implemented in the field of electronic communication interceptions and other digital investigation techniques. In this capacity, it provides magistrates and investigators with several IT tools that make up the Information System for Digital Judicial Investigation Techniques (SITENJ). In this context, the purpose of this procedure is the provision, by a publisher of a standard market solution, of a solution enabling active monitoring of potential illicit use in the digital space of data originating from the SITENJ which, in the vast majority of cases, are strictly subject to the secrecy of the investigation or instruction. The detail of the services and functionalities appears in the consultation file but the solution must at a minimum offer a service of: 1) permanent monitoring and reporting of information to administration users (automated detection and alert); 2) active search at the request of said users (detection based on the elements transmitted). See market description
sig_96d47f00ae49803bb358.title: Provision in SAAS mode of a digital solution for monitoring and detecting potential misuse of data from the ANTENJ information system and associated services ("DADRIM")
