sig_971ad5f0459d229fae7b.description: The contracting authority is PD - Berater der Öffentlichen Hand GmbH. A client of the contracting authority has established 2021 with the Quality Sign for Sustainable Buildings (QNG), an umbrella brand for sustainable construction in Germany. The Quality Sign for Sustainable Buildings (QNG) is intended to promote sustainable construction on a broad scale in Germany and to ensure a minimum quality for "sustainable buildings". In addition, it is intended to create a legally secure basis for the award of funding that enables grants in the construction sector to be in compliance with social objectives (sustainability objectives). Since 2022 the contracting authority has been supporting the client with the establishment and setting up of a QNG office with all associated activities, such as a hotline, operation of a website and further development of the QNG requirements with the associated publications. In order to provide up-to-date information on the seal and the processes to be observed, the QNG website https://www.qng.info/ was developed and set up in the year 2022 with an external service provider. The QNG website represents a knowledge platform that processes ongoing developments and changes, and provides users with basic procedures, interfaces and assistance. The contract is awarded in two lots: - Lot 1: Hosting, further development and support of the existing website - Lot 2: Technical support (pool of experts) for the Quality Sign for Sustainable Buildings (QNG). The lot-specific tasks are described in more detail below. Bids may be submitted for one or for both lots. The contractor assumes continuous support, operation, hosting, and provision of the server infrastructure for the operation of the already existing website. Services include: 1. Website support, provision of licences 2. Website hosting and optimisation 3. Hosting and further development of an AI-based, self-learning chatbot The contractor shall ensure a seamless transition from 01. January 2027. The contract has a term of 4 years. The basis for the award in Lot 1 is an EVB-IT cloud contract.; The pool of experts is intended to provide support for consultations on enquiries resulting from the application of the QNG in practice, as well as for the further development of the QNG requirements and the introduction and implementation phase of the revised requirements. Services include: • Support for the content-related further development of the quality seal • Support for the revision and quality assurance of the associated documents with regard to comprehensibility and technical correctness • Support for the creation or revision of accompanying materials such as FAQs and quick answers • Creation of training materials for certification bodies and auditors as part of the introduction of the revised requirements • Support for the processing of complex or technically demanding enquiries, where applicable support for the ongoing quality assurance of new FAQs and quick answers The commencement of services is 01.01.2027. The contract has a term of 4 years. The basis for the award in Lot 2 is a service contract. There is no fixed purchase quantity. The estimated volume results from the estimated quantity specified in the price sheet. The contract is limited to 280.000 euro.
sig_971ad5f0459d229fae7b.title: Web hosting and professional support (expertise pool) for the "Quality Seal for Sustainable Buildings" (QNG)

sig_976f102fa5ac2e929074.description: Bærum municipality would like to invite the market to a dialogue in connection with a coming procurement in order to cover the municipality ́s need for digital joint user equipment/AV equipment (DFB) with the accompanying services. This market dialogue is a replacement/update of previously completed market dialogues. See previously completed market dialogue: https://doffin.no/notices/2023-653193 Invitation to market dialogue - Framework agreement for the procurement of digital joint user equipment/AV equipment and the accompanying services Bærum municipality invites tenderers to a market dialogue with suppliers for a framework agreement for the procurement of digital joint user equipment/AV equipment and accompanying services. The aim of the procurement is to replace the current framework agreement for the procurement of "Digital joint user equipment - meeting room equipment and infotainment". The new agreement will cover an equivalent area and the need for digital joint user equipment (DFB) for all entities and buildings where Bærum municipality is responsible for such joint equipment. The municipality has separate agreements for client control and user-related equipment. Bærum municipality would like to invite the market to a dialogue in connection with a coming procurement in order to cover the municipality ́s need for digital joint user equipment/AV with the accompanying services. The intention is that the agreement shall cover Bærum municipality ́s total need for digital joint user equipment/AV equipment, entertainment, meeting room equipment, accessories and accompanying services in the contract period. The contract shall ensure that digital joint user equipment/AV equipment for Bærum municipality ́s entities and buildings always has access to updated equipment/products and services with modern and good quality. The aim is not to replace the existing equipment that covers the current user need. In addition to the delivery and operation of new equipment, we would like a new supplier to provide support and service for the current equipment. The consultancy services will be strengthened in the contract and the tenderer must reckon on assisting the Contracting Authority as needed, both as regards assessment/supplementation of equipment, support and maintenance. Expanded support and assistance can be required at major events and video conferences. The aim of the market dialogue is to gain insight into the market now and forward, establish increased knowledge on the supplier market, inform about the coming planned procurement and get any feedback on the planned procurement before the announcement. Bærum municipality is one of Norway's largest municipalities. Both inhabitants and employees have high expectations for the municipality ́s IT systems, both in regard to response, availability, information security, cost efficiency as well as the ability to implement new functions quickly and efficiently. According to Bærum municipality ́s digitalisation strategy, the municipality ́s employees and inhabitants shall experience "One Bærum - digital first choice" via, among other things, access to best and correct practices in service deliveries, access to process support and technology to simplify our own everyday lives and get a better tool for interaction, case processing and service production. The procurement is planned to be carried out as a tender contest with notice before summer 2026. Tenderers are invited to a joint card information meeting in Kommunegården in Sandvika for orientation of the upcoming planned procurement friday 13.03.2026, 09:00 – 10.00. Tenderers who are interested in a short 1:1 meeting with Bærum municipality if the procurement can register their interest.1:1 meetings will be held on the same day (13.03.2026) (up to 30 minutes for each tenderer) – if there are more registered participants than we have set aside, an extra day will be set aside for 1:1 meetings. Tenderers can inform and/or ask questions to the Customer at the 1:1 meeting. Tenderers who register for the market dialogue will be sent parts of the tender documentation draft for a planned competition, so that they can provide input on the tender documentation before the competition is announced. The aim of the written input is to get a general description of the tenderer ́s system and feedback sent out documentation and a planned procurement. The meetings will be confidential and only for internal use by the work group in the municipality. Input from the dialogue can be used in the subsequent competition. Written input shall only be relevant for the competition. A template will be sent out to provide feedback to suppliers who register for the dialogue conference. The deadline for registering for the Dialogue conference and 1:1 meetings is 09.03.2026, 16:00. Enrolments are to be sent as a notification on the case in Mercell. The Contracting Authority would like feedback from tenderers for the planned procurement and draft of competition documents by: Thursday 09.04.2026, 16:00. Emphasis is put on the fact that participation in the dialogue meetings is neither necessary nor required to participate in the subsequent competition. Communication will take place through Mercell.For further information about Bærum municipality, see www.baerum.kommune.no The meetings will be held in Kommunegården in SandvikaAdresse: Arnold Haukelands plass 10, 1338 Sandvika

sig_97ade33b90377832169a.description: Procurement of an integrated chromatographic instrument and data management platform for an analytical research laboratory Lot LOT-0001: Chromatography Data System (CDS). Procurement, delivery, installation, configuration, integration, commissioning, training, documentation, warranty and support of a Chromatography Data System (CDS) as a central platform for instrument control, data acquisition, data processing, reporting, auditability and controlled management of chromatographic data. The CDS must support the integration of the analytical systems procured under lots 2 to 5 and provide functions for data integrity, user and role management as well as for connection to institutional data management structures. Lot LOT-0002: GC-MS/FID system. Procurement, delivery, installation, commissioning, integration, training, documentation, warranty and support of a gas chromatography-mass spectrometry system with a dual detector configuration consisting of a flame ionisation detector (FID) and a single quadrupole mass spectrometer (MSD). The system is used for the qualitative and quantitative analysis of small molecules and metabolites in complex sample matrices and must support integration into the central Chromatography Data System (CDS). Lot LOT-0003: UHPLC with dual detection. Procurement, delivery, installation, commissioning, integration, training, documentation, warranty and support of an ultra-high-performance liquid chromatography system (UHPLC) with dual detection consisting of a PDA/DAD detector and a universal gradient-compatible detector for non-UV-absorbing compounds. The system is used for the separation, detection and quantification of organic compounds in complex matrices and must support integration into the central Chromatography Data System (CDS). Lot LOT-0004: LC-MS single quadrupole. Procurement, delivery, installation, commissioning, integration, training, documentation, warranty and support of an LC-MS single quadrupole system with an integrated liquid chromatography front end. The system is used for the qualitative and quantitative analysis of small molecules, metabolites and impurities as well as for carrying out high-throughput screening workflows including flow injection analysis (FIA). Integration into the central Chromatography Data System (CDS) must be ensured. Lot LOT-0005: Semi-preparative HPLC. Procurement, delivery, installation, commissioning, integration, training, documentation, warranty and support of a semi-preparative HPLC system for the isolation, purification and recovery of organic compounds in the milligram to gram range. The system must support automated and traceable fraction collection, purification workflows and integration into the central Chromatography Data System (CDS).
sig_97ade33b90377832169a.title: Procurement of an integrated chromatographic instrument and data management platform for an analytical research laboratory

This ITT is expected to result in the setting up of a Framework Agreement with multiple suppliers, with the ultimate purpose of securing the best value for money in the provision of equipment/software and its associated maintenance and support services, and other services to build a Network Security Layer that will be purchased and installed by ECMWF at its Data Centre located in Bologna and its three offices sites located in Reading, Bologna and Bonn. The ITT will also include: (i) professional services for the design validation and onsite engineer presence during the deployment phase if and when required; (ii) training of ECMWF staff. ECMWF may reopen the Framework on a competitive basis at a later date to add additional suppliers to the Framework on the same conditions. In addition, this ITT intends to place an order for an Initial Purchase (Lot 1) comprising equipment from the supplier providing the best solution and value for money for this Initial Purchase, which has also been selected for the Framework. The contract for the Initial Purchase is anticipated to be awarded in December 2026. Suppliers must submit Tenders to supply the Initial Purchase for inclusion onto the Framework.

sig_981f60924d2f84773b74.description: GENERAL This is not a procurement notice or request for tenders, and the notice does not launch a procurement procedure. The aim of this information request and market sounding is to obtain additional information on options available on the market and to hear suppliers' views on the subject of the procurement so that any subsequent procurement procedure can be carried out appropriately. Answering the information request or participating in the market sounding has no effect on the position of market operators in any actual procurement procedure that may be initiated later. BACKGROUND AND SUBJECT OF THE PROCUREMENT Digi- ja väestötietovirasto (DVV) is planning and preparing a procurement through which, on the basis of the resulting contract or contracts, DVV may procure, as needed, the printing and processing services for the right-to-vote notifications (so-called notification card) and their annexes defined in the Election Act, as well as other related printing, enveloping and folding services. The whole to be put out to tender includes - the production of paper and electronic notification cards and their delivery for sending, as well as - the distribution service for paper notification cards in accordance with the Postal Act, and the return of undelivered consignments to the sender address - in the case of electronic consignments, their transfer for sending to the Suomi.fi Messages service, and the production of the metadata required for this - expert services for preparing the graphic layout of these consignments In addition, the procurement may include other information letters for European Parliament elections as well as regional and municipal elections. The regular elections during the new contract period in the years 2027-2030 will be the following: 1. Parliamentary elections 2027 2. Regional and municipal elections 2029 3. European Parliament elections 2029 4. Presidential election 2030 In addition to regular elections, the contract covers any other elections that will be held during the contract period. Occurrence in the contract period is determined according to the date of election day (in the case of the presidential election, 1. election). Such non-regular elections may be, for example, a presidential election held mid-term due to the death or permanent incapacitation of the president, or early parliamentary elections ordered by the President of the Republic, or elections to be rerun following a court decision as a result of an appeal. In addition to elections, the contract also covers corresponding procurements in state consultative referendums. The notification card is regulated by section 21 of the Election Act. Other election-related information drawn up by the Ministry of Justice may be attached to the notification card consignment. As a rule, in all election types, in addition to the notification card sheet itself, a list of advance polling stations in the recipient's local area and an information insert about the body to be elected in the election are attached to the consignment. In addition, in the presidential election, two notification cards are sent to each person entitled to vote, one for each (possible) round of the two-round election. Other attachments are also possible; for example, during the pandemic caused by the Covid19 virus, municipal elections held featured an additional insert page about health safety in voting. The smallest composition for a notification card consignment is 3 sheets (notification card, one sheet for the list of advance polling stations, information leaflet about the body to be elected), and at most the size of the consignment could be (estimated) 7 sheets. The purpose of the notification card is to provide information on the approach of elections and the recipient's right to vote in them, and to give them the opportunity to request further information and, if necessary, rectification from the authority in good time if they consider that any information relating to their right to vote shown on the notification card is incorrect. In some rarer situations, the notification card can also be used to streamline the voting procedure, but it is never a prerequisite for voting or sufficient proof of identity and right to vote at the polling station. Notification cards are drawn up on forms according to the formula confirmed by the Ministry of Justice (VaaliL 193 §). For paper consignments of notification cards, their manufacturer produces windowed envelopes with election-specific prints and takes care of enveloping the consignments. Regarding the regular elections of the contract period put out to tender, estimates of the quantities of electronic and paper letter post are presented in the annex to this notice. The stated estimates of the distributions of the format and delivery method of notification cards have been estimated on the basis that the legislation on the priority of digital official communication will be completed and its application will begin in the spring of 2026. INFORMATION REQUEST AND MARKET SOUNDING The information request section of this notice presents questions to potential tenderer candidates interested in the procurement. The information request aims to survey market operators' views on, among other things, whether it is appropriate to put the service package out to tender in one or two parts (production and distribution separately). On the basis of the responses received to the information request, DVV may, at its discretion, also hold more detailed bilateral discussions on the specifications of the procurement and/or request comments on the preliminary tender documents from those who responded to the information request prior to the actual procurement.
sig_981f60924d2f84773b74.title: Information request and market sounding: Production and distribution services for election notification cards 2027-2030

sig_985973cf72f36e8bcb7b.description: All Zurich notaries are simultaneously bankruptcy offices and land registry offices. Zurich bankruptcy offices are obliged not only to keep their own files from a bankruptcy proceeding, but also the business files of the respective bankrupt company. The statutory retention obligation is generally 10 years (for individual files 30 years). In particular for the ten-year retention of business files, the notaries currently operate nine so-called central archives. The nine central archives are located at seven sites and are each affiliated with a local bankruptcy office/notary. The management of an archive (storage inventory, additions and removals) is carried out by a notary employee from the local notary. An IT application provides an overall overview of the capacity utilisation of the individual archives. The increasing number of bankruptcies in the Canton of Zurich means that the volume of bankruptcy and business files is also increasing and the existing central archives of the notaries are reaching the limit of their capacity, and in some cases have already reached it. For this reason and the need not to additionally burden the bankruptcy offices of the canton with storage services, the management of the Notary Inspectorate has decided to outsource the storage of bankruptcy files as a future-proof, scalable solution.
sig_985973cf72f36e8bcb7b.title: Centralised archiving for bankruptcy files

sig_988058399897c0071507.description: Complex generic drug products represent an increasing share of the generic marketplace and may have distinct user interface differences compared to reference listed drug (RLD) products. A modernized post-market surveillance approach is needed to compare clinical outcomes between complex generic products and their corresponding RLD products to monitor for potential issues with therapeutic equivalence and to inform regulatory decision making. Real-world data (RWD) combined with machine learning (ML) and/or artificial intelligence (AI) could help to identify post-market signals efficiently in an automated and repeatable fashion, facilitating timely regulatory action. The purpose of this funding opportunity is to develop and test an AI- or ML-based algorithmic RWD model for post-market surveillance of complex generic drug products.
sig_988058399897c0071507.title: Utilizing Real-World Data and Algorithmic Analyses to Assess Post-Market Clinical Outcomes in Patients Switching Amongst Therapeutically Equivalent Complex Generic Drug Products and Reference Listed Drugs (U01) Clinical Trial Not Allowed

sig_991b334a8fd52a465ea5.description: The Norwegian Police Directorate announces a competition for a research assignment in connection with the introduction of a new model for service development (MTU) in the police force. The model for service development involves new ways of working for the entire organisation. The implementation will involve changes in work forms, interaction, management and decision making. To ensure learning, quality and adjustment during the process, before new practices are allowed to join the organisation, the National Police Agency wants a research environment to carry out action research, or other type of follow-up research where researchers collaborate closely with the business, parallel to the implementation. The assignment shall support a structured and systematic learning process. The overall objective of the assignment is to support the implementation of the model through continual learning and to create an understanding of any change needs. The research shall contribute to concretising the goal achievement of the MTU and giving an independent assessment of whether this strengthens the police ́s ability to solve the social mission. The research theme is in the tender documentation.
sig_991b334a8fd52a465ea5.title: Research on introduction of a new model for service development (MTU) in the police.

sig_991d901148fa3cfbeae6.description:
The service is divided into the following main areas, in relation to which the successful tenderer will be called upon to perform the activities described in the Technical Specifications to meet the various requirements: a) consulting services for the development of industrial plans, including the related strategic and economic-financial analyses; b) strategic consulting services for individual corporate projects, including industrial development initiatives, organisational rationalisation, technological development, evaluation of industrial synergies, and corporate or Group restructuring operations; c) programme/project management services to support the implementation of industrial plans and strategic projects, including monitoring activities, organisational change management, performance measurement, management reporting, and support for the achievement of project objectives. The activities may involve the preparation of studies, analyses, business plans, economic-financial projections, programmatic documents, work plans, management reports, monitoring dashboards, and any other documentation functional to the pursuit of the objectives defined by RAI. The successful tenderer must support RAI in relation to the requirements expressed from time to time within the scope of the services covered by the Framework Agreement, ensuring for the entire duration of the contract the availability of professional skills suitable for covering the entire range of activities provided for by the tender documentation, as well as the organisational capacity necessary to ensure, where requested, the simultaneous execution of multiple project interventions. The project and economic regulation of the services is based on the weeks/Full Time Equivalent (FTE) model. The consideration for each intervention will be determined on the basis of the estimated project effort and the composition of the required team, defined through the mix of professional figures provided for by the Technical Specifications and calibrated according to the complexity, duration, objectives, and outputs of the assignment. The activities will be activated through specific implementing contracts, within which the sizing of the intervention, the reference team, and the related methods of execution will be identified. The resources employed in the execution of the services will remain at all times under the exclusive employment of the successful tenderer and will operate under its direction, coordination, and organisational responsibility. The successful tenderer will retain exclusive power over all employment, hierarchical, organisational, disciplinary, and management matters regarding the resources employed. RAI will exclusively define the requirement, the objectives of the intervention, the expected outputs, the related timelines, the methods of interaction with its own structures, any locations for the performance of the activities, and the criteria for verifying the services rendered. The operational organisation of the activities, the identification of the resources to be employed, and the management of the project team will remain the exclusive competence of the successful tenderer, without prejudice to compliance with the professional requirements provided for by the tender documentation and anything possibly offered during the tender. For a detailed description of the technical and functional characteristics of the service as well as the methods of its execution, please refer to the technical tender documentation. Pursuant to art. 120 paragraph 1 letter a) of the Code, Rai S.p.A. reserves: - the right, should the contract amount not be exhausted upon the expiry of the contract duration, to extend the duration of the relative contract for the time necessary for the use of the entire contract amount; - the right to request from the contractor, during the duration of the contract, in the event of unforeseen needs that determine an increase or decrease in the requirement for services, an increase or decrease in the services, under the same conditions, for an amount up to euro 360.000,00, also pursuant to art. 120 paragraph 9 of the Code; in such an event, the contractor cannot assert the right to terminate the contract. In exceptional cases, upon the occurrence of the conditions indicated in art. 120 paragraph 11 of the Code, the duration of the contract (if applicable as extended pursuant to art. 120, paragraph 1, letter a) of the Code as provided above), still in the course of execution, may be extended for the time strictly necessary for the conclusion of the procedure for identifying the new contractor. In such a case, the contractor will be required to execute the services covered by the contract at the same prices, terms, and conditions provided for therein. The total value of the contract is equal to Euro 2.160.000 net of VAT and/or other taxes and legal contributions for the period of 36 months, divided as follows: i) Euro 1.800.000,00 net of VAT and/or other taxes and legal contributions, as the amount for the base duration of 36 months of the contract not subject to discount; ii) Euro 360.000,00 net of VAT and/or other taxes and legal contributions, as the maximum amount for any variations in increase pursuant to art. 120, paragraph 1 letter a) and paragraph 9 of Legislative Decree 36/2023. The amount of safety costs for risks from interference is equal to euro 0,00 (zero/00) as, pursuant to Legislative Decree no. 81/2008 and subsequent amendments and additions and the Resolution of 05/03/2008 of the A.N.A.C. (formerly A.V.C.P.), for the services covered by this procedure there are no interfering risks and the preparation of the D.U.V.R.I. is excluded.

The value of the Framework Agreement has been estimated based on an analysis of RAI's prospective requirements referring to the entire contractual duration and taking into account the different types of services provided for by the Technical Specifications, as well as the methods of executing the interventions by professional teams composed of figures characterised by different levels of seniority. The economic valuation was carried out through a model based on weeks/FTE (Full Time Equivalent), which represent the conventional unit of measurement of the project effort required for the execution of the individual interventions. The reference average rate equal to EUR 10.014,00 per 1 FTE/week, determined on the basis of the rates of the individual professional profiles and the relative percentages of employment provided for the different standard team configurations governed by the Technical Specifications, will therefore be subject to a discount. This rate constitutes the unit economic parameter used for the valuation of the interventions requested by RAI within the scope of the Framework Agreement and was determined taking into account the different compositions of the teams and the different levels of seniority of the professional figures that compose them. The aforementioned total amount represents a maximum expenditure ceiling that is not binding for Rai, up to the limit of which the various types of services covered by the contract may be commissioned, through the issuance of specific implementing contracts. Therefore, also in order to fully exploit the advantages of this type of contract and mitigate the risks of any unforeseen needs that were not previously planned or plannable, the total amount of the contract is not subject to a discount. Instead, the reference average rate equal to EUR 10.014,00 per 1 FTE/week will be subject to a discount, it being understood that the consideration for each implementing contract will be determined by applying the single percentage discount offered by the successful tenderer to this rate and taking into account the project effort required, expressed in weeks/FTE, as well as the composition of the team necessary for the execution of the intervention, defined according to the complexity, duration, objectives and the mix of professional skills required.

sig_99261c1bd47690033773.description: The subject matter of the dynamic purchasing system (DPS) consists of knowledge management and artificial intelligence platforms, licences, and expert services. Actual procurements are made on the basis of separate requests for tenders through internal competitions within the DPS, in which the contracting authority specifies and describes its detailed procurement need. The subject matter of the procurement of platforms and licences may be, for example, a solution based on commercial off-the-shelf software for knowledge management, software usage rights, licences, and/or a software solution based on open source code. The subject matter may additionally include tools intended for, among other things, knowledge management administration, data warehouse automation, integration, analytics and reporting, as well as visualisation. The subject matter of the expert services can be specified in areas such as the following: • Knowledge management and AI consulting • Planning and management of data governance and management projects • Conceptual, data, and interface modelling as well as architecture definition • Development, testing, training, and planning of maintenance, administration, and monitoring for extract, transform, load (ETL) chains and integrations • Planning, development, testing, training, and planning of maintenance, administration, and monitoring for data warehouses, data cubes, and data lakes • Planning, development, testing, training, and planning of maintenance, administration, and monitoring for visualisations and reporting • Development of analytics, advanced analytics, machine learning, and robotics • User interface and application development (Chatbot, etc.) • Definition and development of cost accounting • Definition of services, processes, and governance models • Selection, consulting, and training of tools used in development The contracting authority does not commit to procuring any minimum quantity within the DPS. A procurement contract concluded within the DPS does not grant the supplier an exclusive right to provide the service. In internal competitions of the dynamic purchasing system, the contracting authority requests an assurance from the tenderer that the tenderer company, or those companies or persons in whose ownership, possession, or control the tenderer company is, or its subcontractor, is not burdened by sanctions imposed by the European Union or the United Nations (UN) or by sanctions or asset freezing decisions imposed by Finnish authorities. The contracting authority shall exclude from the internal tendering procedure of the purchasing system tenderers who do not meet the aforementioned requirement. The contracting authority also has the right to terminate the procurement contract with immediate effect if the supplier is burdened by any of the above-mentioned sanctions or asset freezing decisions.

sig_9936af3fe823c1bfa3a7.description: In the autumn of 2023, the HL Center decided to work towards a new permanent exhibition on the Holocaust. The new permanent exhibition will build upon and enhance the unique national responsibility that the HL Center holds for the dissemination of the history of the Holocaust and related themes. The HL Center has prepared an exhibition brief for the new exhibition. This document defines the overarching goals, principles for the development of the concept and thematic content, as well as the framework for the organisation and implementation of the project. It is intended to serve as the cornerstone for the realisation of the main project. A prequalification process will now be carried out, followed by a tender competition in the form of a competitive dialogue to select the exhibition provider who will collaborate with the centre in realising the new permanent exhibition. The main project is planned to begin in 2026, and the new exhibition is scheduled to open to the public in the autumn of 2028.

sig_9988be44fc524f729b36.description: At the BWB sewage treatment plants and sewage pumping stations, the PI System from the company AVEVA (formerly OSIsoft) is used for the long-term archiving of process data. The Berliner Wasserbetriebe currently operate 9 PI Data Archive Servers. These are supplied with data via approx. 50 OPC Interfaces. In total, the measured values, up to 40.000 - 50.000 data points, are collected and archived in the smallest possible resolution (> 1 second). They serve as a data source for the Asset Framework, PI Vision, a simulation server, as well as for external customers who need to access live and historical data. For this purpose, the API interface of the PI System is also required. The retention of historical data goes back to the year 1999. It includes all existing measured values and data points. These are permanently mapped in the PI Data Archive and are therefore available for retrieval within milliseconds at any time. The following questionnaire is intended to evaluate whether a migration to an alternative system is possible and economically viable.
sig_9988be44fc524f729b36.title: Market exploration for PI System

Furthermore, an indefinite maintenance contract (24/7/365) is to be procured for the new system, which ensures both prompt fault clearance and further development in accordance with regulatory requirements. Both the contractor and the contracting authority may terminate the contract at the earliest forty-eight (48) months (= waiver of termination) after expiry of the warranty/guarantee period. The place of performance is Vienna and the commencement of performance is immediately following the award. The contract begins after acceptance of the system. Payment for the maintenance contract is made for the first time after expiry of the warranty period of 2 years after acceptance. The following service components are to be offered optionally: • a contingency of 500 hours for activities within the meaning of the basic contract (cf. SR item 1.2) • Extensible Interface Capability (cf. 14.1 TecSpec) • Operating Mode "MONITOR LOCAL" (cf. 14.2 TecSpec) • SMA Interface (cf. 14.3 TecSpec) • Electric Storm Warning (cf. 14.4 TecSpec) • Alternate Airport for Military Aviation Display (cf. 14.5 TecSpec) • SWIM Interface (cf. 14.6 TecSpec). sig_99c1a0bc280ab73c1b83.description: An Post requires a suitably qualified Security Partner to deliver a managed Security Operations Centre (SOC) and Security Information and Event Management (SIEM) service across its technology estate. The successful Supplier will be responsible for providing a resilient, secure, and professionally managed cybersecurity capability that supports continuous security monitoring, threat detection, incident analysis, alert triage, incident response, escalation management, compliance assurance, service reporting, and ongoing service improvement. The Supplier will work collaboratively with An Post personnel and relevant third-party providers to ensure comprehensive monitoring coverage, effective management of security incidents, and alignment with An Post's security, resilience, governance, and regulatory requirements. The service will include the provision, operation, management, and continuous enhancement of security monitoring and incident management capabilities, including support for Microsoft Sentinel as An Post's current SIEM platform. The Supplier must also be capable of supporting alternative SIEM technologies should An Post's security architecture evolve during the contract term. In addition, the Supplier must be able to monitor and manage security event sources across both Microsoft and non-Microsoft technologies, including platforms that do not natively integrate with Microsoft Sentinel. The scope of the service is expected to include, but is not limited to, managed cybersecurity operations, threat detection and analysis, incident management and response, security platform support, threat intelligence, governance and reporting, and the provision of suitably qualified cybersecurity personnel to support service delivery.

sig_99f9bef848b651fa1187.description: This Expression of Interest (EOI) outlines Macmillan Cancer Support's request for agencies to collaborate on designing, testing and delivering a new cancer information and support offer(s). The project is part of Macmillan's 2025 strategy commitment to reach more people living with cancer and to improve the support we offer for people who experience inequitable access to cancer care and treatment. The design challenge for this project is "How Might We develop a scalable solution that helps people understand their rights, choices and influence in decisions about their care, irrespective of their confidence, self-advocacy skills or system knowledge?" This is an end-to-end Innovation project that we require to be delivered in its entirety by the supplier(s), with input and guidance from Macmillan. This includes insight development and analysis, solution development, prototyping and testing of a Minimum Viable Product (MVP). The solution should be scalable and likely be digital or include digital elements. The supplier must have extensive experience designing with communities and individuals that are marginalised. The supplier should be an expert in approaches including designing from the margins and embed meaningful and equitable participatory approaches into every phase of the project. Given the nature of the requirements, we are open to working with 2 suppliers who can deliver different elements or phases of the project. The agency must be able to recruit participants who reflect Macmillan's priority cancer support audiences to take part in user research, co-design and testing of solutions; people who have been diagnosed with cancer in the past 5 years. This includes people who are currently undergoing anti-cancer treatment (more details in attachment). Timelines • Expression of interest response deadline by 10/03/2026. • Selected agencies will receive the full RFP pack in March / April. • The anticipated project duration is 4-6 months from kick-off. The final timeline will be agreed with Macmillan during the tender process. Supplier Response Instructions Via email, interested suppliers should provide: (1) A brief outline of their research, design and innovation approach, including how they will use design from the margin approaches (see examples here); (2) evidence of prior engagement and participatory work with marginalised communities (3) evidence of developing and delivering scalable products and/or services (especially digital) (4) identification of gaps in their ability to meet the full requirements and if there are gaps (5) willingness to partner with another agency. Responses at this stage do not need to be extensive. Responses should be sent to procurement@macmillan.org.uk with the subject line EOI - Innovation Advocacy/Empowerment.
sig_99f9bef848b651fa1187.title: Expression of Interest for a Macmillan Cancer Support Innovation project

On 26.09.2025, the contracting authority signed with the North-West Regional Development Agency in its capacity as Managing Authority, the financing contract no. 375/26.09.2025, SMIS code 338511, entitled 'Integrated traffic monitoring and smart mobility system in municipiul Satu Mare' which aims to achieve the investment objective 'Public transport and road traffic management - components: bus stops and intersections' through the North-West Regional Programme 2021-2027 - Increased use of public transport and other forms of ecological urban mobility (Urban mobility)'. Municipiul Satu Mare intends to carry out the expansion of the traffic management system for public transport and the establishment and modernisation of SMART bus stops which aim to increase the attractiveness of public transport and the migration of as many journeys as possible to this means of transport, to the detriment of travel by personal vehicle by increasing the degree of accessibility, attractiveness and safety, and the efficiency of public transport, with positive effects on reducing pollution and energy consumption. The modernisation of public transport infrastructure, the real-time information system, and the promotion of smart solutions for increasing the attractiveness and accessibility of public transport will lead directly to an increase in the quality of life of the municipality's citizens. Increasing the safety of citizens in public spaces will also be ensured by the introduction of a video surveillance system at public transport stops. At the same time, Municipiul Satu Mare is considering the expansion and modernisation of intelligent transport systems, with the aim of increasing traffic safety and optimising urban traffic. The municipality's road network has a radial structure, with four major access directions, and the crossing of the Someș river and the railway is limited, these constituting natural barriers that frequently generate congestion zones. At the same time, the predominance of collector-category streets leads to intense traffic at main intersections, which requires the adoption of modern solutions for traffic regulation and control. In this context, the proposed investment aims at the implementation of an integrated traffic light and road traffic monitoring system, complementary to the public transport management system, contributing to the creation of a unified smart urban mobility system. The project involves the installation of traffic lights at 37 intersections / pedestrian crossings located on the main arteries of the municipality, 15 LPR camera locations and 5 speed signalling panel locations, as well as their integration into a centralised command and control system; the contracting authority will respond to clarifications on the 11-th day before the deadline for the submission of tenders. Furthermore, the number of days by which clarifications may be requested before the deadline for the submission of tenders/applications is 20 days. The modernisation of public transport infrastructure, the real-time information system, and the promotion of smart solutions for increasing the attractiveness and accessibility of public transport will lead directly to an increase in the quality of life of the municipality's citizens. Increasing the safety of citizens in public spaces will also be ensured by the introduction of a video surveillance system at public transport stops. The local public transport service is part of the sphere of community public utility services and includes the totality of actions and activities of public utility and general economic and social interest, carried out at the level of administrative-territorial units for the purpose of ensuring local public transport. The modernisation/expansion of specific public transport infrastructure, the interventions will have the effect of increasing the quality and efficiency of the public transport service and will implicitly lead to the attraction of an additional number of passengers, beneficiaries of the service. Within the investment objective, the following is desired: 1. The creation of a command and control centre for the smart stop system, and an IT system that allows citizens access to real-time information on public transport, including journey planning facilities and specific functionalities for persons with disabilities. 2. The establishment and modernisation of 100 smart public transport stops of various sizes, with a view to increasing the degree of passenger satisfaction and increasing the degree of use of public transport means.

By carrying out the investment, the aim is to achieve the following objectives: Safety and security: • Increasing safety and security through the introduction of the video monitoring system at public transport stops; Economic efficiency: • Making public transport more efficient by increasing the number of users, due to the increased attractiveness and accessibility of this mode of travel; respectively by reducing travel times and fuel consumption; • Increasing the efficiency of public transport through better correlation of transport supply with actual travel demand; respectively increasing the attractiveness of public transport and the percentage of use of this mode of transport; Environment: • Reducing pollution, including noise pollution, caused by urban traffic. Quality of the urban environment: • Increasing the degree of accessibility of citizens to points of interest in the project's area of influence through the use of alternative modes of travel; • Increasing the quality of life of the citizens of Satu Mare Municipality by providing public transport stops, respectively by providing real-time information on urban traffic; the contracting authority will respond to clarifications on the 11-th day before the deadline for the submission of tenders. This report substantiates the necessity and opportunity of implementing a traffic light and road traffic monitoring system in Municipiul Satu Mare, in correlation with the objectives assumed through the financing contract no. 375/26.09.2025, SMIS code 338511, entitled 'Integrated traffic monitoring and smart mobility system in municipiul Satu Mare', financed through the North-West Regional Programme 2021–2027. Municipiul Satu Mare is considering the expansion and modernisation of intelligent transport systems, with the aim of increasing traffic safety and optimising urban traffic. The municipality's road network has a radial structure, with four major access directions, and the crossing of the Someș river and the railway is limited, these constituting natural barriers that frequently generate congestion zones. At the same time, the predominance of collector-category streets leads to intense traffic at main intersections, which requires the adoption of modern solutions for traffic regulation and control. In this context, the proposed investment aims at the implementation of an integrated traffic light and road traffic monitoring system, complementary to the public transport management system, contributing to the creation of a unified smart urban mobility system. The project involves the installation of traffic lights at 37 intersections / pedestrian crossings located on the main arteries of the municipality, 15 LPR camera locations and 5 speed signalling panel locations, as well as their integration into a centralised command and control system. The proposed system will include: • traffic lights for vehicles and pedestrians; • traffic detection systems; • video monitoring systems; • LPR systems (where applicable); • speed information panels; • integrated command and control centre, correlated with the public transport and smart stop management system. The implementation of this investment is in accordance with the objectives of the financed project and contributes directly to: Safety and security: • increasing road and pedestrian traffic safety through intelligent traffic regulation and video monitoring of intersections; • reducing the risk of road accidents; Economic efficiency: • streamlining traffic and reducing travel times; • reducing fuel consumption and optimising transport costs; • correlating traffic flows with public transport, with a view to increasing its attractiveness; • Environment: • reducing pollutant emissions and noise pollution generated by road traffic; Quality of life: • improving urban mobility and accessibility to main points of interest; • increasing the comfort and safety of citizens in public spaces. By carrying out this investment, complementarity with public transport modernisation measures (smart stops, real-time information, traffic management systems) is ensured, contributing to the achievement of the objectives established through the project call PRNV/2023/481.A/1 – Priority 4: A region with sustainable multimodal urban mobility, respectively the promotion of sustainable urban mobility and the reduction of carbon emissions. The contracting authority will respond to clarifications on the 11-th day before the deadline for the submission of tenders. Furthermore, the number of days by which clarifications may be requested before the deadline for the submission of tenders/applications is 20 days.

sig_9a717a6eb198dcbccd00.description: Terveyden ja hyvinvoinnin laitos (THL) is planning a tender for a condition monitoring system for its Kuopio office. THL is an independent state expert and research institute that promotes the well-being, health and safety of people. The institute's laboratories store millions of samples as well as reagents required for analytics in various storage conditions. The condition monitoring system must centrally collect temperature and alarm data from all measurement points. The primary objective of the system is to provide alarms when temperature limits are exceeded and to manage these alarms. The system must also be able to monitor and record condition data in both normal and alarm conditions. Monitoring and operational update tasks are intended to be performed by THL users. The intention is that the system will include all components required from measurement to alarm and data recording, with the exception of THL's existing sensors used in deep-freeze freezers (Pt100), which are intended to be used as part of the system. THL's Kuopio office deep-freeze freezers currently use approximately 20 Pt100 sensors. The deep-freeze freezers have a separate 4-conductor Pt-100 sensor, which is attached to the transmitter with a spring loaded connector. REGISTRATION INSTRUCTIONS FOR MARKET SURVEY (HEREINAFTER MARKET DIALOGUE): Companies interested in the procurement are requested to register by 1.10.2025 at 12:00 by email to kilpailutus@hansel.fi with the following information: - Message subject: "Olosuhdevalvontajärjestelmä Kuopion toimipisteeseen - markkinavuoropuhelu" - Message content: 1) Company name and business ID 2) Contact person's name and email address 3) Experience in supplying a condition monitoring system (in what kind of environment does the company's monitoring system operate) 4) Do you have any obstacles to using the above-described THL-owned sensors as part of your system? 5) How would the existing sensors (Pt-100) be connected to transmitters/SaaS service in your system? 6) If the information provided above is not sufficient, what information do you still need about the sensors owned by THL? 7) What is the response time for maintenance, troubleshooting, and delivery of replacement and spare equipment to Kuopio? IMPLEMENTATION OF MARKET DIALOGUE: The contracting authority will send draft materials of the tender for a written comment round as the preparation process progresses. No compensation will be paid to those who participated in the market dialogue. Hansel Oy acts in a consulting role in the market dialogue and the potential tender.

sig_9b0dcb019dbedcf267c5.description: Procurement of research-based services in the project "Digital Smart Regulations" for occupational health and safety - Development and testing of approaches for the use of digitised regulations and rules in occupational health and safety Lot LOT-0001: Procurement of research-based services in the project "Digital Smart Regulations" for occupational health and safety. Starting point of the project: Digital solutions are useful for the drafting, provision and application of technical rules in the field of occupational health and safety. This applies both to rule-making in the occupational health and safety committees at the Federal Ministry of Labour and Social Affairs (see https://www.bmas.de/DE/Arbeit/Arbeitsschutz/Arbeitsschutzausschuesse/arbeitsschutzausschuesse.html ), as well as to the publication of the rules by the BMAS and their application in companies as well as for advice and enforcement. In the field of standardisation, the concept "Digital Smart Standards" is available from the Digital Standards Initiative by DIN and DKE (IDiS) (see https://www.dke.de/idis ). This was applied as an example in a previous research project F 2542 of the BAuA (see https://www.baua.de/DE/Forschung/Forschungsprojekte/f2542 and project website https://digiasr.blogs.ruhr-uni-bochum.de/ ). A methodology for the step-by-step development of machine-readable and machine-executable testing rules was derived from this (A. Aziz, D. Napps, M. König, S. Gabriel, A. Richter, S. Voß (2025): Approaches for the transformation of technical rules for workplaces into digital rules. https://www.baua.de/DE/Angebote/Publikationen/Fokus/F2542-2). Subject matter of the contract and objectives: Based on the existing approaches and findings, a study is to be conducted to investigate the extent to which approaches for "Digital Smart Standards" can be transferred to further areas of the body of regulations and rules on occupational health and safety, and whether the occupational health and safety rules drawn up in the occupational health and safety committees can be converted into "Digital Smart Regulations", i.e. into level 2 "Machine-readable document", and further developed in future for level 3 "Machine-readable and executable content" and level 4 "Machine-readable and interpretable content". This study is the subject of the services to be provided by the contractor. The aim is to draw up recommendations for action for the further digitalisation of occupational health and safety regulations and rules in Germany. In key technical application contexts and use cases, which are to be selected in cooperation with the occupational health and safety committees at the BMAS, the processes from creation through management and provision to the operational application of rules as well as implementation options must be considered. Requirements from occupational health and safety regulations and rules must be taken into account in practice, particularly during risk assessments by employers. The contractor must therefore investigate in the project how the contents of the occupational health and safety rules can be applied in exemplary digital implementations of the risk assessment processes and in any existing data models and coordinated with further requirements. The contractor systematically compiles and evaluates the results and derives concrete recommendations for action based on them. The project contributes to making the respective body of rules clearer and easier to apply digitally for users in future, as well as to making the processes for creating, further developing, administering and providing the rules more efficient.
sig_9b0dcb019dbedcf267c5.title: Procurement of research-based services in the project "Digital Smart Regulations" for occupational health and safety

sig_9b6a3d2bbbf334a862d7.description: suHCO (Systemic Sustainability Transition Solution for Health Care Organisations) is a European project funded under the Horizon Europe programme (Grant Agreement No. 101226802) and implemented through a Pre-Commercial Procurement (PCP) scheme. The project aims to support health and care organisations in their transition towards more sustainable and environmentally responsible models by fostering the development of innovative digital solutions. Through the PCP process, suHCO will procure research and development services for the creation of an AI-enabled digital platform capable of helping healthcare organisations assess their sustainability performance, identify improvement opportunities, plan and implement actions, monitor progress, and support evidence-based decision-making. The future solution is expected to integrate sustainability knowledge, regulatory requirements, standards, best practices and relevant data sources, providing users with practical guidance tailored to their organisational context. It should also support sustainable procurement processes, impact assessment, reporting activities and organisational change management. The project is driven by a Buyers Group composed of healthcare organisations from Spain, Italy and Wales. The solutions developed during the PCP will be progressively designed, prototyped and validated in real healthcare environments to ensure their relevance, usability and scalability. By bringing together healthcare providers, technology developers and sustainability experts, suHCO seeks to stimulate innovation and contribute to the sustainability objectives of European health systems. Procurement will take the form of pre-commercial procurement (PCP), where R&D service contracts will be awarded in parallel to different R&D providers in a phased approach. This will allow alternative, competing solutions to be compared. Each selected operator will receive a framework contract covering three R&D phases. The three phases are: Solution design, prototype development, original development and validation and testing of a limited volume of the first products or services. After each phase, interim evaluations are conducted to select the best of the competing solutions. The contractors with the best value for money will be offered a specific contract for the next phase. The selected operators will retain ownership of the intellectual property rights (IPRs) they generate during the PCP and will be able to use them to exploit the full market potential of the solutions developed. Testing is expected to take place in Catalonia (Spain), West Wales (UK), Treviso (Italy). This testing may also serve as a first customer test reference for the contractors. The selected suppliers will retain ownership of the intellectual property rights (IPRs) they generate during the PCP and will be able to use them to exploit the full market potential of the solutions developed, i.e. beyond the procurement. This procurement is funded by the European Union's Horizon Europe Research and Innovation Programme under Grant Agreement No. 101226802- suHCO (https://suhco.eu/). The EU has awarded a grant for this procurement but is not participating as a contracting authority in the procurement.
sig_9b6a3d2bbbf334a862d7.title: Pre-commercial Procurement of an innovative Systemic Sustainability Transition Solution for Health Care Organisations (suHCO)

sig_9b81b9f135780581cc55.description: NOTE: Updated submission in below text now reflects a 9 Oct 26 date in line with the Genreal Information submission date. This Request for Information (RFI) is issued for informational and market research purposes only in accordance with RFO (Revolutionary FAR Overhaul) Part 10. It does not constitute a solicitation, a Request for Proposal (RFP), or a promise to issue RFP in the future. The Government will not reimburse any company or individual for expenses associated with preparing or submitting information in response to this RFI. The information provided may be used by the U.S. Air Force in developing its acquisition strategy, Statement of Work (SOW), and performance specifications. Interested parties are responsible for adequately marking proprietary or competition-sensitive information. BACKGROUND / DESCRIPTION The United States Air Force (USAF) operates a fleet of MH-139A aircraft for security and support missions. The aircraft is primarily used for security and transportation patrols across extensive intercontinental ballistic missile (ICBM) fields, while supporting search and rescue missions, and personnel/cargo transport. The aircraft platform is a commercial Leonardo AW139 helicopter modified by Boeing for military use. The existing fleet is twenty-six (26) aircraft with approximately thirty (30) additional aircraft planned in production. The fleet is disseminated at six (6) CONUS AFB locations. SCOPE OF REQUIRED CAPABILITIES The Air Force Materiel Command (AFMC) is seeking information from industry sources on the potential capability to provide Contractor Logistics Support (CLS) Services for the MH-139A (Grey Wolf) helicopter platform. The information provided by industry responders will be used to assess logistical support capability from contractors in the marketplace to assist the United States Government (USG) in refining its acquisition strategy as the MH-139A fleet transitions from its current Interim Contractor Support (ICS) and Interim Supply Support (ISS) postures to continued sustainment. The functional areas include, but are not limited to the list below:? Material Acquisitions Purchasing Management Support for Helicopter Rotable/Repairable Assets, Parts, and major Line Replaceable Units (LRUs) (e.g., engines, main gearboxes): Manage high-value components that can be physically repaired and reused rather than thrown away as well as disposable items that may or may not have a life limit. Purchasing Management Support for Consumable/Expendable Support: Manage a consumables program of parts as well as sourcing “one-time use” items required for daily maintenance. Purchasing Management Support for Test and Support Equipment: Procuring the specialized tools, stands, and calibration equipment necessary to test aircraft systems and to perform depot-level maintenance. Procurement Planning:?Execute timely, "just-in-time" procurement of scheduled maintenance materials to ensure parts are on hand prior to the commencement of heavy inspection events, minimizing aircraft downtime.? Inventory Management Inventory Stores Management: Operating the physical warehouse on base, tracking stock levels, and ensuring parts are ready for immediate issue to the flightline. Tool Crib Support Management: Manage and track check-in/check-out tooling usage for daily maintenance activity. Spares Management and APSR Integration: Maintain 100% floor-to-ceiling accountability of all Government Furnished Property (GFP) and spares using an approved DoD Accountable Property System of Record (APSR) (e.g., ELMS) that provides Total Asset Visibility (TAV) to the Government. Support Equipment (SE) Transition: Execute a 100% joint inventory, resolve discrepancies, and manage the physical relocation of all SE and tooling from incumbent facilities to operational bases, while maintaining strict calibration (AFMETCAL) and diagnostic software version control. FIAR and Accountability: Ensure strict adherence to Financial Improvement and Audit Readiness (FIAR) guidance by sustaining verifiable audit trails for all asset lifecycle transactions, enabling accurate financial valuation, and supporting independent audits to guarantee total operational accountability." Maintenance Management Heavy (Depot Level) Maintenance Management Unscheduled / Time Inspection Events Unscheduled Hourly Inspection Events: Inspections triggered strictly by aircraft flight hours Depot Flow Plan (DFP): Develop, maintain, and execute a comprehensive Depot Flow Plan (DFP) detailing aircraft retrofit and modification schedules to be coordinated with the SPO. Over and Above (O&A) Management: Possess a structured process to identify, document, estimate, and execute O&A repairs for unprogrammed work (e.g., severe corrosion or structural defects) discovered during inspections. Analytical Condition Inspections (ACI): Integrate structured ACI activities into planned depot work to foreclose structural integrity risks. Depot component Level Maintenance Management Scheduled / Time Inspection Events Maintainers must proactively execute TCTOs and engineering directives. Maintainers must also submit, respond to, and resolve technical requests, coordinating directly with Field Service Representatives and OEM engineers as required. Scheduled Hourly Inspection Events: Inspections triggered strictly by aircraft flight hours Modifications, Technical Order/Engineering Order event activity: Physically installing hardware/software upgrades or safety modifications on the aircraft flightline Depot-level repair actions must comply with directed TCTOs and engineering dispositions. Heavy (Depot Level) Maintenance Management Unscheduled / Time Inspection Events Unscheduled Hourly Inspection Events: Inspections triggered strictly by aircraft flight hours Reliability and Engineering Data Analysis: The contractor shall establish a robust data analytics program to provide the Government with full transparency into component lifecycle health. sig_9bbc52f64dff547fec2a.description: The Göttinger Verkehrsbetriebe GmbH (GöVB) is a municipal transport company 100% owned by the City of Göttingen. It operates local public transport in the city of Göttingen and adjacent regions and ensures the daily mobility of residents and guests with its bus fleet. As a sectoral contracting authority within the meaning of § 100 of the Act against Restraints of Competition (GWB), GöVB is responsible for the procurement of services and systems that secure the operation and further development of local public transport. GöVB pursues the goal of gradually converting its bus fleet to alternative, in particular electric, drive systems. In doing so, it makes a significant contribution to sustainable mobility, the reduction of emissions, and the achievement of the climate targets of the City of Göttingen. The expansion of the e-bus fleet is accompanied by a considerable need for modern charging infrastructure that enables efficient, reliable, and economical operational management. To support this transformation, GöVB is planning the introduction of a charging and load management system (LLEMS). This system is intended to enable intelligent control and monitoring of all charging processes at the depot and, in the future, also in scheduled service. The focus is on ensuring vehicle availability, grid and load optimisation, and the safe and economical operation of electromobility in local public transport in Göttingen.
sig_9bbc52f64dff547fec2a.title: Göttinger Verkehrsbetriebe GmbH - Charging, Load and Energy Management System (LLEMS) (Market exploration)

sig_9c80d0bb7dbdefcd3c06.description: Revenue Scotland is seeking information from the market in relation to the next version of / replacement for its existing tax administration platform, SETS. The current platform supports the collection and operational management of devolved Scottish taxes. It enables taxpayers and their agents to submit tax returns and make payments to Revenue Scotland, and enables staff to process returns, manage taxpayer records through a number of statutory processes, reconcile inbound & outbound payments with tax declared, and undertake tax compliance activity and operational casework. Lot 1: . Revenue Scotland is seeking a strategic partner to help it deliver and support a cloud-hosted tax administration and case management platform for the collection and operational management of devolved taxes in Scotland. The system will manage tax data, support staff in administering tax returns and taxpayer records, and enable efficient case management of statutory tax management processes, workflow automation, and integration with external systems. Additionally, the solution needs to provide reporting capabilities in terms of management information and data export to our own analytics platform. We anticipate additional taxes and legislative change being introduced over the lifetime of the contract, and so the solution should be flexible enough to easily accommodate new functionality. Through this Prior Information Notice, Revenue Scotland wishes to consider the fullest range of modern, UK-based cloud-based solutions which support: - A portal for taxpayers and agents to view, edit and submit tax information - case management - workflow automation - operational processing - integration with other corporate systems such as our finance (general ledger) systems, contact management (telephony), and third-party print and post solutions. The next version of SETS will support at least five taxes and must provide a highly configurable and scalable platform capable of supporting evolving tax policy and operational requirements. Currently up to 80 back-office staff users across a range of different functional teams use the platform. Revenue Scotland welcomes engagement from suppliers with experience of delivering platforms capable of supporting complex administration and case management.. This contract may be split into lots, where market intelligence has suggested this to be viable and beneficial
sig_9c80d0bb7dbdefcd3c06.title: Scottish Electronic Tax System (SETS)

sig_9d5282bd403bcdb3d090.description: **This notice supercedes UK3 Planned Procurement Notice reference 2026/S 000-078126, which was issued on 3rd August and modified on 17th of August.** **This contract is an Exempt Contract within the meaning of the Procurement Act 2023, in accordance with Schedule 2, paragraph 25 of the Act (national security). Accordingly, this procurement does not constitute a covered procurement and the provisions of the Procurement Act 2023 relating to covered procurements do not apply. Where any provisions of the Procurement Act 2023 are expressed to apply more generally to a “procurement”, the Authority has determined that those provisions are inapplicable in the circumstances of this procurement, having regard to the fact that the application of any such provision would be inconsistent with, or would undermine the operation of, the national security exemption. Any reference by the Authority to concepts, procedures or terminology derived from the Procurement Act 2023 is for convenience only and does not consititute an acknowledgment that the Act, or any particular provision of it, applies to this procurement or any resulting contract. ** The UK Space Agency (UKSA), as part of the National Space Operations Centre (NSpOC) programme, intends to commence a competitive procurement for the deployment of a sovereign, high‐power space surveillance radar in the Southern Hemisphere (final location is still to be determined but bidders should note the requirement to deploy into the Southern Hemisphere) to enhance the UK's Space Surveillance & Tracking (SST) and Space Domain Awareness (SDA) capability. It is expected that the radar system will operate as a key national asset, providing enhanced detection, tracking and custody of resident space objects, particularly small-size debris and operational satellites in Low Earth Orbit. It will deliver significant improvements to UK resilience, space safety, collision avoidance, re-entry monitoring, fragmentation detection, and wider civil-military situational awareness objectives. The budget for this hardware requirement is capped at £25,000,000 exclusive of VAT and will cover the following elements: * Radar hardware (including, but not limited to, antenna systems, signal generation/timing/processing hardware, power systems, cooling and thermal management) * Radar software (noting the Authority is likely to specify software covers both edge and cloud elements, with a 10 year licence including free security and basic maintenance updates) * Software development to integrate software with wider Government systems (including capture and implementation of user stories/change requests to better exploit the equipment provided) * Two separate training courses - one focused on tasking/sensor capabilities and one focused on hardware support and maintenance * Obtaining spectrum rights and permissions: whilst the Authority will support the appointed contractor with this, responsibility will rest with the appointed contractor * Software and hardware support and maintenance for the initial 3 year contract term * Cyber assurance * Project and contract management (including interface with the infrastructure contractor) * Collaboration around installation and commissioning at final deployment location The following is currently expected to be in scope of the infrastructure and enabling works contract, which is expected to be valued at £5,000,000 exclusive of VAT. Prospective bidders should note that at least some staff are likely to require SC or DV clearance for this requirement. To assist prospective bidders with planning, an indicative requirements list is provided below. Depending on final deployment location, some of these elements may not be required: * Planning investigation and, if required, planning consents * Site surveys and ground works (including environmental and site safety surveys) * Enabling works to prepare the site for radar deployment (e.g. construction of concrete base) * Site civils and foundations (design and build) * Power and data connectivity * Potential utilities connections as required (e.g. drainage) * Collaboration around installation and commissioning at final deployment location * Temporary or permanent access to site, as required * Site security (e.g. perimeter fencing, CCTV, gates) * Site support * Project and contract management (including interface with the radar hardware contractor) The following is expected to be in scope of neither contract: * Ongoing utilities costs * Spare components (the radar contractor will be expected to include in the pricing schedule the cost of spare components) A suitable location for deployment has been identified but discussions cannot progress further until the actual equipment specification and characteristics are known. The appointed contractor will therefore be required to work closely with the Contracting Authority and the appointed infrastructure contractor to ensure successful deployment. Bidders will be provided with details of the broad location and constraining assumptions at PSQ stage to assist with technical responses, but should note the final location is unlikely to be disclosed until tender stage. The Contracting Authority will only enter into discussions relating to deployment locations with bidders under NDA, noting that detailed discussions will not be possible at SQ stage. Please note the Contracting Authority will not respond to any further queries raised on the technical specification or conditions of participation at this point: these will need to be raised as formal clarifications via the e-tendering portal in accordance with the timetable specified in the procurement documents. Lot 1: . None
