sig_9d9ffc50e7cd2401e0ac.description: The contracting authority is tendering a contract regarding Transition In, development of the Modernised Support Systems, application operation, application maintenance, support, ordering services, including further development of the Support Systems, as well as Transition Out. The contract consists of the following 3 main services: I. Transition In, including, among other things, a secure and stable takeover of the application responsibility for the Support Systems, implementation of, for example, project management, transition organisation, transfer of source code and documentation, implementation of technical transition and necessary transformation, takeover of knowledge from the outgoing supplier as well as establishment of the operations organisation, including establishment of the collaboration with the operations supplier. II. Ongoing services for the Support Systems, including; a. Support, including, among other things, responsibility for Service Desk, user administration, handling of incidents, problems, service requests, early life support, cf. the operational processes, with the aim of ensuring high availability for the users; b. Application operation, including, among other things, database operation, operation of middleware, backup, restore, monitoring and logging, 2. and 3. line support, configuration, patch, and release and deployment management, cf. the operational processes, and operational reporting with high requirements for uptime and response times; c. Application maintenance, including, among other things, ongoing and preventive maintenance of the IT systems, minor changes, new versions, bug fixes, release management, cf. the operational processes, with the aim of supporting high requirements for uptime and response times; d. Governance, including close collaboration with the operations supplier, operational processes, security services, documentation and operational reporting. III. Agile development, e.g. via a design and planning phase, including proof of concept, as well as a development phase based on the supplier's product vision and advice. Development of the Modernised Support Systems takes place agilely in close collaboration between the parties regarding support for the contracting authority's business goals and needs, so that the Modernised Support Systems can be implemented after a time-limited period. Development includes any new functionality as well as any re-implementation and reuse of parts of the current Support Systems. Further development of the Support Systems also takes place agilely in close collaboration between the parties. It is the contracting authority's business need that all services are delivered with high delivery reliability and robustness, and that the supplier demonstrates proactivity in the collaboration. In Transition In, the supplier must take over the application responsibility for the Support Systems and, from the transition day, deliver ongoing services, including, among other things, application operation, application maintenance and further development, to the Support Systems. The further development will take place in a close, agile collaboration with the contracting authority. The supplier must also, in a close, agile collaboration with the contracting authority, carry out a modernisation of the Support Systems based on the contracting authority's modernisation wishes. The Support Systems are part of the overall joint municipal infrastructure, and the supplier must therefore collaborate partly with the other suppliers, including the operations supplier as well as suppliers who deliver other parts of the joint municipal infrastructure, and partly with users of the infrastructure. It is the contracting authority's business goal and need, among other things, to give parts of the current Support Systems a quality boost in the form of a modernisation that supports the Modernised Support Systems appearing attractive, reliable, future-proof and secure, so that the municipalities also in the future have a strong foundation to deliver the best digital services to the citizens in an increasingly more coherent, efficient and modern public sector.

BITMARCK Holding GmbH and BITMARCK GmbH intend to conclude framework agreements for the provision of various IT services for the BITMARCK corporate group. The procurement is divided into 20 specialist lots. The services include, in particular, project coordination, security analyses, SQL support, specification services, workplace application management, SAP HCM application management, testing services, telematics services, Java backend development, SPPM management, SAP application development, test environment management, test automation, specialist consulting, migration, performance tests, IT consulting, UX and UI design, process modelling and vulnerability management. Companies may submit tenders for one lot, several lots or all lots. The examination and evaluation will be carried out separately for each lot. Framework agreements are to be concluded with a maximum of five companies per lot. The subject of this lot is IT services for the structuring, planning, coordination and quality assurance of IT projects in the environment of the products, solutions and services of the BITMARCK corporate group. IT project management involves the implementation of projects according to the project management method of BITMARCK. This method was adapted in close alignment with PRINCE2 to the requirements of BITMARCK and the BITMARCK customers in the statutory health insurance (GKV) environment. The aim is to obtain external specialist expertise for the methodical planning, documentation and tracking of project-related requirements and results. sig_9eeb0e95df78e643035a.description: This is not a procurement notice or a request for tenders, but a market survey and request for information. The National ID forum (informal forum) has decided to organize a joint RFI event. The idea is to organize a single RFI involving several national agencies and ministries, which would maximize synergy benefits and be a cost-effective model. The ID Forum is a national informal cooperation forum that focuses on comprehensive identity management, its development, and creating a situational picture. The aim is to produce national services that develop capacity in identity management, coordinate training and information events, and improve the common situational awareness and ability to combat abuse. Identity is therefore at the heart of the forum and is dealt with within the remit of each member organization. The ID Forum consists of several Finnish agencies and ministries; Immigration Service (FIS), Border Guard Force (BGF), National Bureau of Investigations (NBI), National Police Board (NPB), Police departments, Customs, and Ministry of Foreign Affairs (MoFA). The subject of the RFI and information about the procedure are described in more detail in Appendix 1.

sig_9f256e95ecb472f792e8.description: The Norwegian Public Roads Administration would like to carry out a market survey to map which tenderers offer systems for financial management in road projects. There is a need for IT system support for areas such as cost estimation, financial project management and follow-up, uncertainty management and price bank (experience prices used for estimating future projects). The objective of the survey is to gain better insight into what systems are available in the market, how these are technically and functionally designed and which delivery models are offered. It is particularly interesting to examine if there are systems that support several or all of the above mentioned areas in one and the same system. Furthermore, we would like information on whether systems that only cover one or some of the areas can be further developed or configured so that several of the areas can be delivered in one system that safeguards all or most of the value chain. The market survey shall form the basis for any new procurement, and contribute to the Norwegian Public Roads Administration designing a competition that is well adapted to the market and at the same time cover the identified needs in an efficient and future-oriented manner.
sig_9f256e95ecb472f792e8.title: System for cost estimation, financial management and uncertainty management in road projects.

sig_9f771e609eb8b71cf361.description: Broad Horizons Education Trust is currently exploring options for the future provision of its payroll services commencing in September 2027. The Trust currently has an estimated headcount of 1408 employees across 18 sites/academies, processed on a monthly pay cycle. The purpose of this Request for Information is to engage with potential suppliers prior to any formal procurement to: Inform our procurement strategy, scope, and specification. Gauge market interest, capacity, and capabilities. Understand standard market pricing models, implementation timelines, and risk mitigation strategies. The primary objectives of this engagement are to: Gauge current market interest, capacity, and capabilities across service delivery models Seek supplier feedback to refine and finalize the procurement strategy, technical specification, and performance KPIs. Understand commercial and pricing models. Inform system integration requirements to ensure a successful go-live for September 2027. Key operational requirements include: Full and seamless transition Full management processing of monthly payrolls. Comprehensive public sector pension scheme administration, returns, and compliance-specifically Teachers' Pensions Scheme (TPS) and Local Government Pension Scheme (LGPS) Pay scales - To be able to cope with Teaching pay scales, support staff pay scale, apprenticeships plus off-scale pay grades where needed Pay awards and increments To be able to apply pay awards to current staff automatically For back pay to be automatically calculated To be able to chose to backdated pay awards to some leavers To be able to apply increments at different dates for some staff To be able to apply 'No Increment' for specific contracts Integration capability with existing HR and Finance systems and simple data input Integration with MIS - currently Arbor - to provide a 'single source of truth' from which reports and data flows Access for Employees - To efficiently be able to download payslips, P60s etc. To efficiently be able to update personal details, including bank account details Knowledge and experience working with MATs in the education sector. Please email procurement@bhetrust.co.uk for further details and a questionnaire. Lot 1: .

sig_9f8973bfd621c9f402e2.description: The subject of the contract aims to provide cloud resources in Microsoft Azure on a subscription basis, with a reservation period for the main computing resource of - 3 years, for the installation and operation of the Moodle e-learning and distance learning platform. Scope of the service: Provision of a single virtual machine for Moodle, running under Linux; Provision of managed disks for the operating system and data; Provision of public network connectivity and a static public IP address/resource in accordance with the calculation; Provision of a backup service for Azure VMs with LRS redundancy; Provision of a capability for centralised management, monitoring, administration and optimisation of resources; Provision of support through an electronic ticketing platform/portal; Minimum technical requirements for the virtual machine: Resource type - Virtual machine in Microsoft Azure; VM size - Standard_E20as_v5 or equivalent/better; vCPU - minimum 20 vCPU; RAM - minimum 160 GB RAM; Operating system - Linux; Reservation - 3 years reserved capacity for the VM resource; Local temp disk - not required; Premium Storage support - Yes; Purpose - Moodle platform, database and applicable components in a single VM. Storage and backup requirements: OS Managed Disk - 1 managed disk P4, 64 GB-LRS; Data Managed Disk - 1 managed disk Premium SSD P40-LRS; Backup - Azure Backup for 1 VM instance up to 2 TB-LRS; Backup tier - Standard tier, without Archive tier-LRS. Network connectivity requirements: Public IP - Static public IP address; Public IP Prefix - Public IP Prefix resource, if applicable according to the calculation; Internet egress - Minimum 500 GB monthly outgoing internet traffic; Management, security and support requirements: The solution must have an interface for centralised management and policy definition in Microsoft Azure; It must be possible to monitor, manage and optimise the resources used; It must be possible to use multi-factor authentication for administrative access; The contractor must provide access to an electronic platform/portal for registering and tracking support requests; The tenderer must have the right to provide Microsoft Azure services as a CSP partner or equivalent provisioning model compatible with the Microsoft Customer Agreement. Requirement for an implemented and functioning helpdesk system - The tenderer must have an established and functioning helpdesk system, ensuring 24-hour support for the communication system with access via a single number of the type 0700 xxxxx or 0800 xxxxx with national coverage and a web-based interface. The tenderer must describe in detail the service procedure provided by the helpdesk system and indicate a link to the system where its functionalities can be checked. The tenderer must certify that they have successfully implemented projects using a help desk system with a 7x24 hour monitoring centre. Contract term - The contract enters into force as from 15.10.2026 and has a duration of 3 (three) years from the activation of the commissioned services. Service activation period - up to two days from the entry into force of the contract. The contracting authority shall pay the contractor the contract price after the activation of the service, the presentation of a mutually signed protocol and an original invoice, within a period of 30 /thirty/ days.
sig_9f8973bfd621c9f402e2.title: Reserving a virtual server in a Microsoft cloud for a period of 3 years for the installation of the MOODLE system

1. The subject of the contract is the delivery, installation and maintenance of a Passenger Counting System for 284 vehicles of ZTM Operators. The contract has been divided into two tasks. The first task – delivery, installation and maintenance of a Passenger Counting System for 181 buses of ZTM Operators. The task involves retrofitting 23 BN-type buses and 23 CN-type buses of PKM Gliwice Sp. z o.o., 90 BN-type buses and 45 CN-type buses of PKM Katowice Sp. z o.o., manufactured no earlier than in 2014, providing transport services commissioned by ZTM Katowice, with 611 sensors and 181 central units, switches, GSM communication modules/at least 4G in LTE standard or newer, GPS locators and an appropriate number of batteries. The task has been divided into three parts. The first part includes implementation: a) Delivery, installation and commissioning of equipment in buses together with the necessary accessories and cabling, as well as software for this equipment, b) Obtaining a certificate from the GZM PCS contractor (specified in the integration agreement together with appendices) for the solution supplied to the buses (if the Contractor does not possess such for the supplied solution), c) Integration of the supplied equipment with the central software of the GZM Passenger Counting System (GZM PCS) regarding the transmitted data in accordance with the requirements of the Description of the Subject of the Contract, d) Preparation and delivery of as-built documentation, e) Ensuring correct operation during the implementation period on the terms specified in the second part. The second part includes maintenance of the “Vehicle PCS”: a) Warranty and service of the System, b) In the case of an indirect server-to-server connection, maintenance and service of the intermediary server and APN connectivity and VPN tunnel supplied by the Contractor, including the possibility for the Contracting Authority and persons indicated by it from ZTM and Operators to report faults for the aforementioned elements 24 hours a day / for 7 days a week / 365 days a year, c) In the case of an indirect server-to-server connection, carrying out the activities included in the Exit Procedure, intended to ensure the Contracting Authority the continued operation of the solution after the end of the contract with the Contractor, in particular the assignment to the Contracting Authority of the contract for a dedicated APN network held by the Contractor, as well as the commissioning of the intermediary server solution at the location indicated by the Contracting Authority, together with the transfer of licenses enabling the use of the software installed by the Contractor. The Contractor guarantees the correct operation of the solution for the duration of the warranty contract; d) Termination of the Contract, sending all data regarding the intermediary server to GZM cloud resources, so that the functionality of the applied solution is maintained. The third part includes the right of option: an order under the right of option, which includes the possibility of extending the maintenance period in full or limited scope for a period not exceeding 5 years. The third part will be implemented according to the contractual provisions as for the second part. Details regarding the option are described in the draft contract provisions constituting Appendix no. 9.1 to the Procurement Documents. sig_9fdf6e3ef1329529ed82.description: The Advanced Research Projects Agency for Health (ARPA-H) is soliciting proposals from small business concerns (SBCs) that possess the research and development (R&D) expertise to conduct innovative research that will contribute toward ARPA-H mission needs, Small Business Innovation Research (SBIR), and Small Business Technology Transfer (STTR) program objectives. Please see the cover page of the attachment "SBIR_STTR_BAA_FY26" for applicable Stage 1 and Stage 2 deadlines for each open topic. Please see the Attachment H "ARPA-H_SBP_Government_Answered_Questions" for responses to the Q&A period. The purposes of the SBIR and STTR programs are to: (a) stimulate technological innovation; (b) strengthen the role of small business in meeting Federal research/research & development (R/R&D) needs; (c) foster and encourage participation by socially and economically disadvantaged small business concerns and women-owned business concerns; and (d) increase private sector commercialization of innovations derived from Federal R/R&D, thereby increasing competition, productivity and economic growth. For purposes of the SBIR and STTR programs, a small business concern is any business concern that, on the date of award, (1) is organized for profit, with a place of business located in the United States, which operates primarily within the United States or which makes a significant contribution to the United States economy through payment of taxes or use of American products, materials or labor; (2) is in the legal form of an individual proprietorship, partnership, limited liability company, corporation, joint venture, association, trust or cooperative, except that where the form is a joint venture, there must be less than 50 percent participation by foreign business entities in the joint venture; (3) more than 50% directly owned and controlled by one or more individuals (who are citizens or permanent resident aliens of the United States), other business concerns (each of which is more than 50% directly owned and controlled by individuals who are citizens or permanent resident aliens of the United States), or any combination of these; OR more than 50% owned by multiple venture capital operating companies, hedge funds, private equity firms, or any combination of these. No single venture capital operating company, hedge fund, or private equity firm may own more than 50% of the concern; AND, (4) has, including its affiliates, no more than 500 employees. Note: This size standard is established by law for the SBIR program, regardless of the NAICS Code assigned. See 13 C.F.R. § 121.702. AMENDMENT 01 - July 8, 2026: Amendment 01 of this solicitation extends the deadline for Stage 1 Solution Summaries from July 10, 2026 to July 17, 2026. This amendment revises language in the following sections: cover page, 2.2, 2.3, 2.4, 2.6, 2.8, and 8. Amendment 02 corresponds with Stage 1 encourage/discourage letter distribution for topics 01, 02, 03, 04, 06, and 07. Please check your email inbox for your Stage 1 encourage/discourage letters on or around August 17, 2026. Topic 05 Stage 1 letters and Stage 2 submission deadline will be distributed at a later date. This amendment revises language in the following sections: cover page and 8. Amendment 03 corresponds with Stage 1 encourage/discourage letter distribution for topic 05. THE FOLLOWING ARE THE CURRENTLY OPEN RESEARCH TOPICS. PLEASE SEE SECTION 8 OF THE BAA FOR FURTHER INFORMATION ARPA-H 01 -?Development of an annual test to inform women about their future fertility?-?The purpose of this topic is to discover new biomarkers that provide women with actionable data for fertility planning.? Results from this work will help inform the program manager regarding the feasibility of future programs focused on enhancing natural fertility before the need of IVF and guiding the development of women’s health monitoring and improvement tools. This work will develop a diagnostic test that can assess fertility status and generate an estimated timeline for the onset of infertility. This topic seeks to develop a test that is affordable, suitable for at least annual use, and provides user-friendly results for patients and care teams to support childbearing decisions.??? ARPA-H 02 -?Versatile Bioadhesives?- The purpose of this topic is to develop next-generation bioadhesive platforms that can safely and reliably seal, bond, and repair a wide range of tissues in challenging clinical conditions, including wet, bloody, and mechanically dynamic environments. These platforms may also be designed to deliver biologics or small molecules as part of treatment. The goal is to create bioadhesives with key performance attributes such as strong tissue adhesion, controlled degradation, reversibility, biocompatibility, and broad compatibility across multiple tissues and organs. If successful, this topic could enable widely deployable solutions for hemostasis, leak prevention, tissue repair, and device fixation, ultimately helping reduce complications and improve patient outcomes across many care settings ARPA-H 03 -?Universal Platform for Living Adaptive Toxin-removal (UNI-PLAT)?-?The purpose of this topic area is to catalyze the development of a universal, “plug-and-play” synthetic biology platform that enables next-generation microbial chassis capable of performing a broad array of programmable functions. While this solicitation primarily uses toxin removal as a proof-of-concept in relation to chronic disease management, the platform is intended to be adaptable to a range of challenges across industries such as environmental remediation, biomanufacturing, agriculture, holistic medicine, and therapeutic discovery. The broader goal is to create a stable, reliable, and easily reprogrammable microbial platform that demonstrates potential for cross-sector impact beyond the initial use case.? ARPA-H 04 -?Breaking Ground: The First Curative, Durable, Non-Surgical Therapy for Endometriosis?–?The purpose of this topic aims to develop treatments for endometriosis that are non-surgical. Proposers are expected to develop novel, non-surgical therapies to decrease the size or deactivate endometrial implants, to decrease inflammation cause by implants, and / or prevent growth or regrowth of the lesions. Broadly, this should be a novel, non-surgical, curative treatment for endometriosis. ARPA-H 05 -?ARPA-H Lineage Topic?-?The purpose of this topic supports the advancement, commercialization, and translation of technologies that originated from ARPA-H funded efforts. It is intended to help small businesses and startups develop viable products based on these technologies. ARPA-H’s goal is to give small businesses an off-ramp to finish developing their technology/product, explore secondary or interim applications of the technology, and time to achieve self-sufficiency. ARPA-H 06 -?Rapid Comprehensive Diagnostic Test for Multi-System Autoimmune Disease?-The purpose of this topic is to spur the development of novel, rapid diagnostic assays for multi-system autoimmune disease, which?represents?an unmet healthcare need. Moreover, in its ideal embodiment this diagnostic test might allow typical primary care physicians to diagnose and predict tissue-specific autoimmune disease manifestations, thereby streamlining referral of the patient to a specialist. This goal is made more?feasible?by recent technological developments including the ability to detect tissue-specific signatures of immune-mediated stress by assessing circulating cells and/or?tissue-specific molecular products.?? ARPA-H 07 -?Virtual Human Brain for the Development of Neurosurgical Robotics -?The purpose of this topic aims to take a first step toward AI-assisted intracranial microsurgery by creating a high-resolution, physically and anatomically accurate virtual human brain.

With jurisdiction in the matter, the City of Aix-en-Provence controls the hierarchy of all-mode travel within its territory. To this end, the City relies, on the one hand, on the collection of data on pedestrian, cyclist (and other EPAM) and motor vehicle flows (public transport, private vehicles, heavy goods vehicles, motorised two-wheelers) to establish an inventory of the situation (diagnosis) or to evaluate the impact of a development, for example; and, on the other hand, on traffic plan studies, junction design, etc., making it possible to respond to the various challenges of sharing public space in terms of mobility. Thus, the purpose of this contract is to carry out urban travel surveys and specific studies, at all scales, from the junction to the city. This contract comprises 2 lots, - The 1st lot relating to surveys/counts, has the purpose of carrying out flow data collections, inventories, diagnoses and evaluations of developments carried out, - And the 2nd lot relating to studies, has the purpose of considering the design of developments with a view to making travel modes safer. The framework agreement will be executed by issuing order forms. Each lot will be subject to separate award. The services are settled by unit prices. The contract provides for an integration clause : - Lot 1 - Collection / counting of all-mode flow data : 100 hours/year - Lot 2 - Traffic and junction design studies of all types; implementation of traffic light junction programming : 50 hours/year or 3 weeks of work experience per year Collection of all-mode travel flow data
; Traffic and junction design studies of all types, implementation of traffic light junction programming
sig_9fea6ba0a414292f8cfe.title: FRAMEWORK AGREEMENT FOR COUNTING SERVICES AND MULTI-MODE TRAVEL STUDIES FOR THE CITY OF AIX-EN-PROVENCE (2 LOTS)

sig_9feb5763347fe22f0e13.description: This prior information notice serves exclusively to conduct a market survey in accordance with § 28 para. 1 of the German Public Procurement Ordinance (VgV) in preparation for a possible future procurement. However, a procurement procedure is not initiated by conducting this market survey. As part of such a market survey, the GIZ would like to obtain an overview of suitable potential solution providers to identify marketable systems for an integrated system portfolio for the digital support of its global procurement and contract processes, as the GIZ currently does not have sufficient market knowledge of the companies available on the market and potentially interested in the contract to be awarded. The goal is to identify a future-proof solution environment that meets high requirements for legally compliant procurement, supplier management, contract transparency, and international applicability. Companies interested in participating in this market survey are therefore requested to declare their interest to the specified email address. The GIZ will then send a questionnaire to the company, which will then be considered in the course of the market survey. Participation in the market survey is voluntary and does not oblige the GIZ to carry out a procurement, nor does it oblige the participants to conclude a service or supply contract.

Name of procedure: Support and consulting for medical and related systems. Ensuring operational support for the medical and related systems operating at Semmelweis Egyetem and consulting through the conclusion of a framework agreement. The framework agreement shall remain in force for 24 months from its entry into force or until the framework amount is exhausted. Framework amount: net 85 000 000 HUF. The Contracting Authority operates a mixed system consisting of the character-based MedSolution and the web-based e-MedSolution IT system, with the necessary subsystems, interfaces, database management and middleware components. The number of users of the MedSolution / e-MedSolution system exceeds 4.000 named users. The maximum number of concurrent users is 1.200. Pursuant to Section 2/A ( 1 ) of Government Decree 29/2022 (I. 31 ) on central health informatics services, the MedSolution / e-MedSolution system is a hospital information system provided as a public service by ESZFK (Health Informatics Service and Development Centre), which the Contracting Authority is obliged to use under the legislation. (2) Users pursuant to paragraph (1) are obliged to use the hospital information system provided by the Service Centre. Main modules and function groups: • outpatient administration module • inpatient administration module • surgical module • pharmacy module • medication module • nursing module • care module • dental module • EFI module • ward stock requisition module • waiting list module • patient appointment booking module The systems operating at the Contracting Authority are operated by the Contracting Authority's application operations team, which provides L1 and L2 support in relation to the systems. The subject of this procurement procedure is the engagement of resources necessary to perform the L1 and L2 support activity, which covers the following main tasks: End-user support ( L1 ), - its aim is to provide a quick and simple solution and relieve the higher-level resolving groups in handling basic issues. • Receipt and logging of tickets. Receipt, logging and administration of reports received from end-users via telephone, email and ticketing system • Basic troubleshooting. Resolution of simple technical problems, such as password reset, modification of software settings, checking network connection. • Information gathering. Detailed and accurate documentation of reports, which assists resolution at further levels if there is no resolution at the L1 level • Forwarding of problems. If a problem exceeds the remit of L1 support, it is forwarded to the L2 or higher support group. • Administration and setting of permissions in respect of MedSolution / eMedSolution and related subsystems Expert support ( L2 ) – its aim is to handle more complex problems requiring deeper expertise, which require a specialist with specialised, more detailed knowledge. • Handling of events escalated by L1 support, proposing solutions or handing over to the licence manufacturer • Receipt, coordination and documentation of development needs • Testing of developments and introduction of functions • Performance of module owner tasks, such as consulting, system parameterisation, introduction, testing. • Tasks related to the preparation and processing of monthly reports; • Provision of regular and ad-hoc data supplies • Expertise and project management related to medical systems • Performance of parameterisation and operational tasks related to the interfacing of subsystems • Organisation and holding of end-user training • Keeping user documentation continuously up to date Planned service hours for 24 months: Service Manager: 500 hours Medical Consultant: 1800 hours Medical System Operator: 3800 hours Main service period: Monday to Friday from 8:00 hours to 17:00 hours Central European Time (CET), excluding Saturdays, Sundays and all public holidays in Hungary. In detail, as set out in the Technical Specification forming part of the procurement documents.

sig_a116bdb035226ad5a861.description: The subject matter of the procurement is the procurement and implementation of an Extended Detection & Response (XDR) solution, with the aim of significantly increasing IT security through modern detection and response mechanisms and, in particular, identifying advanced threats early and addressing them effectively. Lot LOT-0001: Extended Detection & Response (XDR) solution. Klinikum Esslingen operates an extensive IT infrastructure with numerous IT endpoints, including PCs, thin clients and servers. In addition, there are networked medical devices (IoMT) and building management systems (BMS), which are not, however, the subject of this tender. The endpoint security currently in use is based on a signature-based basic solution (Sophos) that does not provide advanced functions such as behavioural analysis or Endpoint Detection & Response (EDR). The project pursues the following strategic and operative goals: • Replacement of the existing signature-based endpoint security with an XDR solution featuring behavioural analysis, machine learning and forensic analysis capability in accordance with the state of the art • Establishment of complete endpoint visibility and control for all IT endpoints (clients and servers) of Klinikum Esslingen • Activation of Sophos Synchronized Security: real-time communication between endpoint agents and the existing Sophos XGS Firewall for automated network isolation of compromised endpoints • Creation of forensic analysis capabilities: continuous endpoint telemetry recording, root-cause analysis and threat hunting across all endpoints • Activation of cross-domain correlation (XDR): linking endpoint events with firewall, email, cloud and identity data sources as well as preparing the MDR service connection • Fulfilment of regulatory requirements from NIS-2 and GDPR regarding endpoint security as well as orientation towards the state of the art (B3S Gesundheit) • Support for vulnerability management through endpoint-based vulnerability visibility
sig_a116bdb035226ad5a861.title: Extended Detection & Response (XDR) – Lösung

sig_a13549229a37d324346d.description: The purpose of the framework agreement is the execution of renovation and rehabilitation services for the property and real estate assets of user purchasers of the Purchasing Central Body. This framework agreement is multi-supplier (up to 3 suppliers per lot). It combines the 2 forms distinguished by Article R. 2162-2 of the Public Procurement Code. For all lots, the purchaser executes the framework agreement through purchase orders and/or subsequent contracts for services that would not be satisfied by the orders. The framework agreement is divided into 28 technical lots (14 intellectual service lots, 13 works lots, 1 Supply and Services lot). Each of the 14 technical "intellectual services" lots and the "Supply and Services" lot is divided into 18 regional geographical lots. Each of the 13 technical "works" lots is divided into 100 departmental geographical lots. That is, a grand total of 1570 lots: Project Management Assistance (AMO); Building Project Management (MOE); Urban Planner - Landscape Architect; Roads and Diverse Networks Engineering Consultancy; Control Body (BC); Health and Safety Coordinator (CSPS); Scheduling, Management and Coordination (OPC); Surveyor; Geotechnical Engineering Consultancy; Environmental Engineering Consultancy; Pollution Engineering Consultancy; Technical, Energy, Asbestos and Lead Assessor; Heritage Digitisation (BIM); Structural Engineering Consultancy; Demolition - Asbestos Removal; Structural Work, Masonry and Facade; Framework - Waterproofing - Roofing - Cladding; Partitioning - Suspended Ceilings - Plastering - Insulation; Joinery and Metalwork; High Current - Low Current - Home Automation; Heating - Ventilation - Plumbing; Painting and Coverings; Green Spaces; Roads and Diverse Networks; Cleaning; Multiservices and Energy Performance; Prefabricated and Modular Buildings; Structural Damage Insurance (DO) and All Risks Construction (TRC)

Collectively, our Members manage more than 90% of UK' social housing stock, with PfH helping them to achieve efficiency savings using a wide range of services including framework agreements, dynamic purchasing systems, spend analyses, strategy reviews, consolidated billing and comprehensive reporting. PfH is a contracting authority under section 2 of the Procurement Act 2023 and a centralised procurement authority under section 1(4) of that Act. Please refer to www.pfh.co.uk for additional information. sig_a1d31a611e6e4549cb68.description: The objective of the procurement is to acquire IT project manager and expert resources to support, among other things, the definition, programming, testing and management of the Finnish Tax Administration's new and existing systems. The expert resources will operate in projects, development tasks and ongoing service production. The purpose of the procurement is to secure specialist expertise and sufficient resources. The procurement is divided into six (6) lots, for each of which three (3) suppliers and three (3) reserve suppliers will be selected. The lots and their contents are described in more detail below. More detailed descriptions of the contents of the assignments for the procurement lots are described in the appendix Description of the subject matter of the procurement in section 3. The objective is for the contract to enter into force on 16.11.2026. The contract shall be valid for 72 months. Verohallinto develops and maintains digital services primarily as cloud-based and cloud-native solutions. The development work utilises application, integration, data and platform services provided by the Microsoft Azure cloud platform, as well as modern software development, information security and operational practices. Solutions vary in scope and criticality from mission-critical core applications to more limited services targeting specific business needs. The subject matter of the procurement for this lot is expert services for cloud-based software development implemented in the Microsoft Azure environment. The lot includes in particular architecture design for cloud solutions and cloud applications, application and integration development, DevOps, the development and maintenance of cloud platforms, and the technical information security of cloud environments and applications. Key expert roles include cloud solution architect, cloud application architect, cloud software developer, integration developer, cloud DevOps specialist, cloud platform specialist and technical information security specialist.; The subject matter of the procurement for this lot is expert services for applications and information system solutions utilising artificial intelligence, generative artificial intelligence and machine learning. The solutions are implemented primarily in the Microsoft Azure cloud environment, utilising the artificial intelligence capabilities offered by Microsoft Foundry and other Azure services. The solutions can be standalone AI applications or parts of broader information systems, digital services and software solutions. Expert work concerning new technologies may relate to the assessment of the possibilities, suitability, information security and risks of technologies, experiments and prototyping, software and hardware integration, the development of embedded systems, preparation for deployment, or the practical utilisation of technologies. Key expert roles for AI applications include AI application specialists, AI developers, AI solution architects, machine learning specialists and software developers participating in the implementation of AI applications.; The subject matter of the procurement for this lot is expert services aimed at improving the efficiency, quality and transparency of the organisation's operational and data-driven processes through automation, hyper-automation, analytics and systematic development methods. The subject matter of the procurement for this lot is primarily process automation expert services as well as process analytics and process development expert services in a cloud-based operating environment.; The Finnish Tax Administration's technological operating environment strongly includes the development of infrastructure, analytics, information security and cloud services. The Finnish Tax Administration uses the Gentax core taxation system and several smaller systems (e.g. supporting administration). The National Incomes Register and the Positive Credit Register are also the responsibility of the Finnish Tax Administration. The subject matter of the procurement for this lot includes: - project manager services for the development, creation and deployment of operating models and processes, as well as the development of related applications. The scope of impact of operational development can be internal to the organisation and/or customer-related. - technical project manager services, particularly for the areas of infrastructure and information security - Scrum master/team lead services for operational and technical development teams.; The subject matter of the procurement for this lot is IT service management expert services for the ServiceNow environment, as well as expert services specialised in ServiceNow development for architecture, consulting and development tasks. The tasks include ICT architecture and expert tasks in the ServiceNow modules used by the Finnish Tax Administration, including (* supplemented 4.9.2026): • ITSM (IT Service Management) • ITOM (IT Operations Management) • ITBM / SPM (Strategic Portfolio and Demand Management) • SecOps / SIR* (Security Operations) • IRM (Risk Management)* • CMDB (Configuration Management)* • IAM / AM (Access Management, Identity Management)* Expert tasks may include system development, configuration, maintenance, testing and training tasks for the modules in question, as well as related functional and technical architecture design.; The subject matter of the procurement for this lot is user-driven development expert services. By expert service, we mean working under the direction of the Finnish Tax Administration as part of the Finnish Tax Administration's development teams or in close cooperation with them, consulting, business sparring and/s or the implementation of various assignments. Verohallinto can also order fixed-price assignments for e.g. system accessibility audits.

sig_a29b2f741e4c35e93408.description: The contracting authority has two data centres whose physical infrastructure has been completely renovated. As part of this renovation, the structured network cabling, including patch cables, patch panels, cassettes and associated accessories, was replaced. The existing data centre environment comprises approximately 78 racks. The existing structured cabling infrastructure consists mainly of components from the brand Reichle & De Massari AG and includes in particular: • U/FTP CAT 6A copper cabling; • multimode fibre optic cabling; • single-mode fibre optic cabling; • MPO cabling; • patch panels, cassettes, connectors and associated accessories; • cable routing and management systems; • components that integrate into an automated infrastructure management system for the physical network layer. The data centres are also equipped with rack PDUs from the Schneider Electric APC range and associated lockable power cables. Changes to the infrastructure, replacements, extensions and new network projects regularly create a need for additional cabling, patch cables, PDUs, power cables and accessories. The existing infrastructure must remain operational and newly delivered components must be certified as interoperable with the existing infrastructure. The contracting authority's infrastructure standards also provide for the use of UTP CAT 6A cabling, single-mode OS1/OS2 cabling and multimode fibre within the network and data centre environment. 2.2. To-Be description The contracting authority wishes to conclude a framework agreement with a suitable market player for the delivery on demand and, where applicable, the installation, connection, testing and certification of the physical data centre cabling, PDUs, power cables and associated accessories. The future framework agreement must enable the contracting authority to respond quickly and in a technically controlled manner to: • modifications and extensions to the existing data centre infrastructure, while maintaining compatibility and interoperability with the existing infrastructure, in particular: o existing trunks; o existing patch panels; o existing accessories. The future mission will include: 1. Horizontal cabling The supply and installation of copper, fibre optic and MPO cabling between racks, both via prefabricated systems and via systems where cable and cassette are supplied separately and connected on site. 2. Vertical cabling The supply of patch cables and other cabling components to connect IT equipment within the racks, including standard, slimline or fine versions. 3. Cabling components and accessories The supply of patch panels, cassettes, connectors, adapters, cable management systems, labels and other associated parts. 4. PDUs and power cables The supply of rack PDUs, including single-phase and three-phase versions, and associated lockable power cables. 5. Installation, testing and certification Carrying out installation, measurement and testing work, providing test and calibration reports, certifying the installed cabling and providing as-built documentation. 6. Technical assistance Providing technical support and expertise for changes, incidents, problems and future projects in the data centre environment. The future solution must connect technically and functionally to the existing infrastructure. This must take into account, among other things: • interoperability with existing patch panels, cassettes, connectors and accessories; • compatibility with existing infrastructure management systems; • maintenance of warranties for existing certified systems; • compatibility with existing PDU infrastructure management interfaces and software; • minimal disruption to the operational data centre environment; • avoiding unnecessary replacement of existing and usable components. The concrete technical specifications, minimum requirements, implementation conditions, price inventory and award criteria are not part of this selection phase. They will be included in the special specifications that will be provided to the selected candidates during the second phase. The sole purpose of this selection guide is to identify candidates with the required financial and economic capacity as well as the technical and professional capacity to implement the future framework agreement. Candidates only submit a request to participate in this phase. They do not yet have to submit a tender, price inventory or detailed technical solution. Only selected candidates will be invited to submit a tender during the second phase.
sig_a29b2f741e4c35e93408.title: Framework agreement for the supply, installation, connection and testing of data centre cabling, PDUs and associated accessories

sig_a3030bd160378da8ba20.description: Lillehammer, Øyer and Gausdal municipalities plan in autumn 2026 to implement a joint procurement of a new education administrative system that shall support the core processes within nursery, primary and secondary schools and educational-psychological service (PPT). An option is also to be considered to include functionality for the adult education. The procurement will be carried out in cooperation between the municipalities, with the support of their joint ICT services from IKOMM AS. Gausdal municipality has approx. 6,150 inhabitants and an education offer that includes three municipal and two private nurseries, as well as three primary and single secondary schools. The municipality has approx. 580 pupils in primary and secondary schools and more than 250 children in nurseries. The school sector has approx. 130 employees and the PPT service consists of approx. 5 employees. Lillehammer municipality has approx. 29,700 inhabitants and a more comprehensive education offer with 11 municipal and 16 private nurseries, as well as six primary schools, two secondary schools and one combined 1-10 schools. The municipality has approx. 2,860 pupils and approx. 1,300 nursery children. Skole og SFO employs approx. 450 employees and the PPT service has approx. 26 employees. Øyer municipality has approx. 5,150 inhabitants and an education offer consisting of two municipal and three private nurseries, as well as two primary schools and one secondary school. There are approx. 560 pupils in primary and secondary schools and approx. 245 children in kindergarten. The school sector has approx. 110 employees and the PPT service consists of approx. 7 employees. All the figures are approximate and will be further clarified in the further work. The PPT services cover all three municipalities and handle a broad spectrum of case types connected to follow-up of children and youths. The education area is one of the municipalities ́ largest and most socially critical areas of service. The systems used must therefore support efficient administrative processes, good services for children, pupils and guardians, as well as ensure compliance with strict requirements for privacy and information security. The current system portfolio is compound, and the municipalities see a clear need for modernisation and a better connection between the systems. The aim of the procurement is to establish a future orientated and flexible system architecture that provides support to work processes across the disciplines, and that at the same time facilitates gradual further development in the coming years. The municipalities would particularly like to explore a modular approach to the procurement. This means that tenderers can offer systems for all or parts of the need. The intention is to facilitate a "best-of-breed" approach, where functionality, quality and performance in the individual modules are assessed together, at the same time as whole and integration is taken care of. The municipalities would like, among other things, in the market survey to highlight how suppliers are working on the further development of their systems, plans for the use of KI, including plans and obligations from now onwards in a 3-5 year perspective. Furthermore, it is important to gain insight into the risk picture related to implementation, including experiences with migration, training and change management in equivalent municipal projects. It will also be central to highlight how the systems can be integrated with other system portfolios, including case and archive systems, as well as relevant national joint components. Information security and privacy will be a consistent theme, given that the solutions should handle sensitive information about children, pupils and users of PPT and adult education. Furthermore, the municipalities would like information on the tenderers ́ capacity and implementation ability, as well as references from equivalent deliveries in the municipal sector. At first the market survey will be carried out as a written RFI (Request for Information), where interested suppliers are invited to respond to a set of questions included in the notice. Based on the received answers, a selection of tenderers can be invited to dialogue meetings for further details on relevant topics. Physical dialogue meetings are planned for the first week of June. The implementation of the market survey is in accordance with public procurement regulations, cf. The Law on Public Procurements and the Public Procurement Regulations. The market dialogue will be carried out in accordance with the basic principles of competition, equal treatment and predictability and will not give individual tenderers the competitive advantage in a later procurement. Participation in the market survey and any dialogue meetings is voluntary and is not a part of a formal competition. The information collected can be used as a basis for further work on the tender documentation, including an assessment of the contract strategy, any division into lots and the choice of an execution model. The deadline for submitting replies to the RFI is 15.5.26. The dialogue meetings are planned to be held in the period 2.6 and 3.6 as physical meetings carried out in IKOMM ́s premises in Lillehammer. Further information is in the attached RFI document.
sig_a3030bd160378da8ba20.title: OAS - Education administrative solutions for Lillehammer, Øyer and Gausdal municipalities - Market survey

sig_a313894175b835fb0039.description: Iraq faces a persistent gap between its people and the financial system. Banks have long leaned on large state-owned institutions, credit has flowed mainly to established borrowers, and micro and small businesses along with women entrepreneurs and displaced communities have been largely left out. ProDIGI project, full name Promoting Employment in the Digital and Green Economy in Iraq, is trying to change that in a practical, grounded way. ProDIGI is a multi-donor initiative commissioned by the German Federal Ministry for Economic Cooperation and Development (BMZ), co-financed by the European Union, and implemented by the Deutsche Gesellschaft für Internationale Zusammenarbeit (GIZ) GmbH. The project covers central and southern Iraq as well as the Kurdistan Region, with a focus on areas where joblessness, displacement, and limited access to services overlap. Within the project, Output 3 targets the financial inclusion side of the challenge. The starting point is a clear-eyed look at what the sector lacks: financial service providers that are capable, willing, and equipped to design products that fit the people they are supposed to serve. Banks and microfinance institutions in Iraq today mostly offer standardised products with high collateral requirements and limited digital capabilities. Reaching women led small businesses, rural communities, or young entrepreneurs running green or tech ventures requires a different kind of product, and often a different kind of institution. To bridge that gap, the project works directly with Iraqi financial service providers: banks, microfinance institutions, digital payment companies, fintechs, and government lending programmes. The approach combines needs assessments, hands-on advisory services, staff training, product design support, and pilot testing. The goal is not to deliver a finished product from outside, but to build the knowledge and process capacity within each institution so that change remains after the project ends. By the close of the assignment, at least three new or significantly adapted financial products must be in place, and these products must be actively reaching real users at a minimum of 950 individuals and 50 companies. The work also emphasises gender equality: women-led businesses are a priority target group, and all capacity-building activities must include a meaningful share of women participants. The broader context matters too. Iraq's Central Bank launched the national financial inclusion strategy that encourages digital payments, SME lending, and consumer protection improvements. ProDIGI project aligns directly with those priorities, making it both a practical intervention at the level of individual institutions and a contribution to the country's wider financial sector development. The selected firm will work directly with three to five financial service providers (FSPs) operating in Iraq. These may include commercial banks, microfinance institutions, digital payment providers, fintechs, and government lending schemes. GIZ will have pre-selected up to two FSPs before the contract starts, so work can begin without delay. The remaining FSPs will be selected by the contractor and GIZ jointly, based on agreed criteria. Lot LOT-0001: 10009293-Development of inclusive financial services and products. The assignment is structured around three work packages. The first covers the selection and appraisal of partner FSPs. The contractor will conduct an institutional diagnostic for each FSP, reviewing their current product offering, business model, lending processes, digital infrastructure, client outreach capacity, and staff skills. Based on that analysis, a cooperation agreement will be signed with each FSP, along with a detailed work plan laying out what the collaboration will achieve and by when. This phase should be completed within the first three months. The second work package is where the core technical work happens. The contractor will support FSPs in designing or adapting financial products that genuinely respond to the needs of target groups, particularly women-led businesses, rural borrowers, and MSME clients who currently lack access to suitable financing. The process follows a structured product development methodology: from prototype design, through pilot testing, to assessment and refinement, and finally roll-out. Alongside the product work, the contractor will help FSPs develop marketing materials and outreach strategies, adjust internal procedures and manuals, and train front-line staff such as loan officers and branch managers. At least three financial product prototypes must be developed by the fifth to seventh month, piloted by month eight, and formally adopted with updated manuals by month ten. The third work package covers cross-cutting contributions: occasional training inputs for financial sector stakeholders such as the Central Bank of Iraq and sector associations; support for GIZ's monitoring and evaluation activities; and at least three public communication outputs, case studies, blog posts, fact sheets, or similar, documenting the work done with each FSP.
sig_a313894175b835fb0039.title: 10009293-Development of inclusive financial services and products

sig_a3465975540f6b50a997.description: The purpose of the contract is the implementation of an integral platform that allows the complete data lifecycle to be managed efficiently and securely, as well as an inter-administrative data space that facilitates sharing and exchanging information reliably. Furthermore, the contract comprises the provision of services necessary for its customisation, commissioning, operational support and evolution. This includes the implementation, configuration, integration, commissioning and support of an Integral Data Governance Platform and an Inter-administrative Data Space for the Junta de Communities of Castilla-La Mancha in an on-premise modality, intended to provide the functional and technological capabilities necessary for the deployment of the Data Governance System (as established in article 15 of Decree 12/2026, of 31 March, regulating Data Governance in the Junta de Communities of Castilla-La Mancha) and to enable the sharing, management, cataloguing, governance and interoperability of data between the various units of the regional Administration, other public administrations and, where applicable, the remaining agents of the data ecosystem, under principles of security, sovereignty, trust, traceability and regulatory compliance. The platform must provide, amongst others, capabilities for cataloguing and metadata management, data governance and quality, lineage, semantic management, inventory of data sets and products, policy management, discovery and consumption of data, interoperability, secure information sharing and support for the creation of a data market (Data Marketplace), allowing progressive evolution towards an inter-administrative data space aligned with the Data Union Strategy and the Data Strategic Plan of Castilla-La Mancha 2026-2030. In addition, support services aimed at increasing and promoting a data culture within the Administration are considered, as well as all those that provide support and serve to drive the corporate strategy regarding data, including those for support and assistance in the drafting of data-related policies, instructions and procedures.
sig_a3465975540f6b50a997.title: Services relating to data governance and data lifecycle management

sig_a376c611990807e7c34a.description:
The National Forest Administration - ROMSILVA is implementing the project "Information System for the Management of the Forest Fund Administered by Romsilva", SMIS Code 348488, financed by the Intelligent Growth, Digitalisation and Financial Instruments Programme (PoCIDIF), Priority 2 - Digitalisation in central public administration and the business environment, Policy Objective 1 - A more competitive and smarter Europe, by promoting innovative and smart economic transformation and regional ICT connectivity, Specific Objective (ii) - Harnessing the benefits of digitalisation, for the benefit of citizens, companies, research organisations and public authorities, Action 2.2 E-government and digitalisation for the benefit of citizens - 2.2.1 E-gov in public administration/institutions. The object of this procurement consists of the provision of development services for the Integrated Information System. This software platform is of national necessity and aims to efficiently implement national and community obligations regarding the administration of the national forest fund. Following the achievement of the procurement objectives, the Contracting Authority aims to: - decrease incidents regarding illegal logging at a national level; - improve the information and IT systems available to public authorities for the protection, conservation and development of the national forest fund; - support the objective of continuity in forest management through modern digital means; - streamline the public services provided by Romsilva and the operational processes that support them; - inform citizens regarding access to the national forest fund, the need for its protection and ensuring its integrity to limit the effects of climate change; - support landowners in the national forest fund in fulfilling their obligations according to the regulatory framework in force. Through the conduct of this procedure, the contracting authority aims to digitise and significantly improve the public services provided by the institution to the direct beneficiaries of ROMSILVA by implementing (development, implementation, support, technical assistance) at the institution level an integrated information system, but also training a number of people regarding the administration and use of the platform developed within the project. The general objective is the digitalisation and significant improvement of the public services provided by the institution to the direct beneficiaries of ROMSILVA by implementing at the institution level an integrated information system that supports the main activities of carrying out the process of concluding contracts for the protection and administration of the forest fund (forestry services), requests for timber inventory, issuing approvals for access to national and natural parks administered by ROMSILVA, issuing permits for recreational fishing, providing information related to the administered forest fund, providing information regarding access to land in the national forest fund, as well as resolving petitions, by integrating, streamlining and automating internal work processes and flows and the institution's business functions. The implementation of the advanced integrated information system will extensively digitise interactions with natural and legal persons, thus optimising both the internal processes that support the provision of public services, ensuring their superior quality, as well as increased accuracy and efficiency. The specific objectives of the project are: S.O. 1 – Improving the institution's interaction through digital tools with public service beneficiaries, natural and legal persons, regarding the administration and protection of the forest fund - Implementation of an online portal of the virtual private space type for the provision of fully online public services to citizens and legal persons; - Increasing the transparency, efficiency and accessibility of public services made available to citizens and the business environment; - Standardisation of formats, streamlining of collection and superior capitalisation of data collected in interaction with beneficiaries; - Diversification of digital interaction methods, online communication, transmission and validation of documents and reports in relation to beneficiaries. S.O. 2 – Facilitating the activities of issuing authorisations/permits for natural person beneficiaries - Significant improvement of timber inventory processes on the agricultural land of natural and legal person beneficiaries; - Facilitation of processes for issuing authorisations for carrying out recreational/utility activities carried out in the forest fund. S.O. 3 – Supporting the activity of informing society regarding the protection and importance of the national forest fund and the impact on the environment - Consolidation of information related to the protection and importance of the national forest fund at the level of the general population to ensure the improvement of the quality of life of all citizens; - Facilitation, through digital means, of access to complete, correct information from official sources related to the rules applicable during recreational (tourist), sports or utility activities that take place in the forest fund, to reduce the negative impact on the environment and to contribute to forest conservation. S.O. 4 - Streamlining the internal activity of Romsilva - Automation of work processes and operational access to data necessary for carrying out the activity, both from internal systems and from external data sources; - Supporting operational interoperability objectives with other public institutions with a role in the management of the national forest fund;

- Increasing the quality of internal reports that support decision-making processes at Romsilva level. S.O. 5 - Training and instruction of the personnel who will administer and use the new information system created.
sig_a376c611990807e7c34a.title: Development services for the Integrated Information System within the project "Information System for the Management of the Forest Fund Administered by Romsilva" SMIS Code 348488

sig_a386abddb53e69aa736a.description: Dyfed-Powys Police (DPP) currently have a Motorola provided Guardian Integrated Communications Control System (ICCS) at their Force Communications Centre (FCC) based at Carmarthen, Wales. The ICCS is resilient across two sites, the secondary site being located at Ammanford which is approximately 15 miles east of Carmarthen and is equipped with a secondary FCC for DR functionality. DPP require the recording of all incoming and outgoing radio transmissions via the Airwaves network and when this is replaced by Emergency Services Network (ESN). DPP require a product to provide an additional bulk radio recording system that records up to 48 Airwave talk groups when operating within business as usual or in fall back modes and when using handheld radios. Dyfed Powys Police FCC operate on a 24/7, 365 days per year on a shift rotation basis. At any one time there could be up to 20 radio operators listening to and making radio transmissions within the DPP Force area via the Airwave network. Many of the transmissions relate to high-risk, life or death type incidents and are essential evidence used in investigations. It is therefore critical that the product is resilient and able to record all transmissions at all times. It is essential that all incoming and outgoing transmissions on all Airwave channels monitored within the FCC (at Carmarthen and/or Ammanford) are recorded and downloadable and able to be submitted as evidence in investigations and court proceedings or replayed for training purposes. It is also essential that transmissions are recorded from multiple users on up to 48 separate Airwave channels at the same time without cross-over or interference with each other. DPP also require the functionality to be able to merge multiple transmissions relating to a single incident into one recording for evidential purposes. Lot 1: .
sig_a386abddb53e69aa736a.title: CMS - Bulk Recording System

sig_a40a8adf098b749304a2.description: By & Havn is facing the task of transforming Levantkaj in Nordhavn from an existing container terminal into a modern city district. With the current local plan proposal, it is expected that approx. 350.000 square metres of floor space for housing, service businesses and public functions as well as approx. 50.000 square metres of parking distributed across two parking structures on Levantkaj can be established. The local plan will also enable the construction of an elevated metro line, a new metro station as well as pedestrian and cycle connections linked to the main connections in Nordhavn. The local plan proposal will designate the area as a mixed residential and commercial area with the character of a residential area with an expected distribution of housing and commerce of 75/25 with associated facilities such as a school and football pitch, day nurseries, church, sports hall complex, care centre, etc. The local plan proposal is expected to be politically approved in Q4 2026, and the final local plan is expected to be adopted in Q3 2027. By & Havn will be responsible for construction works, establishment of parking structures as well as the sale of building rights, and By & Havn has an ambition that all urban areas are DGNB-certified to a minimum of Platinum. In connection with By & Havn's upcoming sale of building rights, By & Havn wishes with this tender to conclude an agreement with an adviser on economic and commercial consultancy related to By & Havn's development of primarily ground floors containing retail and public-oriented service businesses at Levantkaj, which By & Havn will carry out in a joint venture with a collaboration partner/investor. The adviser's service relates to consultancy on, as a starting point, approx. 6.000 – 7.000 m2 retail and public-oriented functions on the ground floors - which is the area that the joint venture is to own and let out - and does not comprise assistance with the sale or development of other residential building rights or other properties on Levantkaj. However, By & Havn is considering the possibility of expanding the joint venture company's task to include parts of the commercial plots. The tendered agreement consists of two main parts (main tasks), which may overlap in time: • Business plan: Preparation of a detailed business plan for use in the process regarding finding a collaboration partner/investor. The business plan must describe how a company between the collaboration partner/investor and By & Havn is to be structured and describe at a detailed level, among other things, liquidity, ownership distribution, rent level, phasing in of rent and return requirements, etc. • Organisation and implementation of a process to find a collaboration partner/investor: With inspiration from the process during By & Havn's development of the Århusgadekvarteret in Nordhavn, By & Havn wishes to find a collaboration partner/investor who can enter into a joint venture with By & Havn to own ground floors containing retail and public-oriented service businesses at Levantkaj with a view to joint letting. The collaboration partner/investor must be the active party in locating the right tenants for these ground floors. The adviser must assist in organising and implementing a process to find the right collaboration partner/investor, including identifying potential candidates as well as conducting negotiations. In connection with the preparation of the business plan and through dialogue with potential collaboration partners/investors, the adviser must assess together with By & Havn whether some of the commercial plots are to be included in the joint venture collaboration, in order thereby to create a more attractive business case. The execution of the agreement is expected to be initiated immediately following the conclusion of the contract, which is planned to take place immediately before the Christmas holiday 2026. As a clear starting point, the agreement runs until the joint venture agreement with the collaboration partner/investor has been concluded. Based on the expectations for the adoption of the local plan for Levantkaj, it will be optimal for By & Havn if the contract with the collaboration partner/investor (the joint venture agreement) is in place before 1 August 2027 and preferably already before the industrial summer holiday starts. However, By & Havn acknowledges that a number of circumstances may lead to it not being possible to have the joint venture agreement in place within the desired timeframe. In any event, the adviser must anticipate that the work on both main tasks will be intense and require a competent and flexible project organisation. By & Havn has chosen to tender one single contract instead of dividing the contract into lots, as it is By & Havn's assessment that it is firstly necessary to have a joint business plan for the whole of Levantkaj, and secondly that it is clearly most appropriate in relation to interfaces and in relation to rapid execution that the same adviser performs both main tasks.
sig_a40a8adf098b749304a2.title: Udviklingsselskabet By & Havn I/S tender for an agreement on financial advisory services and assistance regarding the development of retail and public-oriented service businesses at Levantkaj
