sig_a4d9ea61c5c212fc525c.description: Background: Although many of the world"s fastest-growing economies are in Africa, trade among African countries remains limited. The continent mostly exports raw materials and agricultural products, while it imports machinery, equipment, and food mainly from outside Africa. The African Continental Free Trade Area (AfCFTA), which is one of the African Union"s (AU) flagship projects for the implementation of its Agenda 2063, aims to change this. It is expected that, with the introduction of the free trade zone, intra- African trade will be 15% to 25% higher by 2040 (UNECA). The AfCFTA agreement has been signed by 54 of the 55 African Union Member States (MS) and became effective under international law in May 2019. The full implementation of the AfCFTA will lead to a continental single market of more than 1.4 billion people with an aggregate GDP exceeding USD 2 trillion. Our Approach: The GIZ implemented project "Support to the African Continental Free Trade Area (AfCFTA) II" cofinanced by the BMZ and the EU, seeks to improve framework conditions for the realisation of the AfCFTA and supports the outstanding negotiations and the implementation of the AfCFTA. For this, the programme supports the African Union, specifically the Department for Economic Development, Trade, Tourism, Industry, Minerals (ETTIM) and the AfCFTA Secretariat at the continental level in the coordination of AfCFTA implementation. On the regional level the programme cooperates with Regional Economic Communities (RECs), specifically EAC (East African Community), ECOWAS (Economic Community for West African States) and SADC (South African Development Community, plus additional RECs based on request). The programme also supports Member States (Ethiopia, Ghana, Ivory Coast, Kenya, Malawi, Rwanda, Tunisia, Zambia, plus additional Member States based on request) by working with national institutions, like trade ministries and customs, to implement the agreement. Lastly, the programme works closely with private sector and civil society actors to increase trade under the AfCFTA. Together with the named partners, the programme covers interventions across all technical areas of the AfCFTA. The EU co-financed part of the programme, the EU Technical Assistance Facility, operates as a multi-partner contribution agreement between the European Commission, GIZ (lead implementing agency), Expertise France, and FIAP. A Project Management Unit, which is housed in the AfCFTA Secretariat, oversees the implementation of the programme and the execution of activities. Lot LOT-0001: 10022598-Short-Term Expert Pools to support negotiations and implementation of the African Continental Free Trade Area (AfCFTA). The project seeks the services of a consulting firm to provide technical experts under different short-term expert (STE) pools, which can be deployed flexibly according to the specific demands of the project. The Contractor will contribute to the implementation of all BMZ and EU outputs of the project. The overall goal of this assignment is to support the implementation of the AfCFTA at the continental, regional, and national level by providing advisory services and capacity building for governmental as well as private sector and civil society stakeholders. When the need for support to the project"s partners within a particular thematic area is identified, experts shall be mobilised to provide demand-driven technical advisory services and/or capacity building to national, regional, and continental government partners and/or the project itself. The contract is for the provision of pools of qualified STE to cover a broad range of issues relating to AfCFTA negotiations and implementation in general and the programme objectives in particular. The services to be provided under the contract include measures for human capacity development and organisational and technical advice in the following thematic areas: - Removing barriers to Trade in Goods, Trade in Services and Digital Trade - Support for further AfCFTA negotiations (among others on Rules of Origin, Trade in Services) - Support for the ratification of the Phase II Protocols (Competition Policy, Intellectual Property Rights, Investment, Digital Trade, Women & Youth in Trade) - Implementation of AfCFTA regulations at the national and regional levels - Monitor and review the implementation of AfCFTA Protocols in African Union Member States (AU MS) - Improve access to trade information to relevant line ministries and to the private sector - Support the African private sector to trade under AfCFTA rules on the national and regional level - Support relevant authorities to setup inclusive policies for women & youth traders to participate in trade under AfCFTA The contractor will identify and manage pools of STE that will assist the initiatives in the programme"s areas of intervention. While the project operates Africa-wide, it focuses interventions at national level in 8 countries: Ethiopia, Ghana, Ivory Coast, Kenya, Malawi, Rwanda, Tunisia, and Zambia. At REC level it focuses at EAC, ECOWAS, and SADC. Interventions to additional AU MS and RECs will be implemented based on partner demand. Across the work packages named below, the contractor is responsible for the following tasks: - Supporting the GIZ in defining the required expertise to reach the project objectives under the described outputs - Identifying and proposing suitable experts from the STE pool - Selecting experts together with the GIZ team - Managing the deployment of experts Expected services that may be included in the work packages are: - Technical, operational, and strategic policy advisory services in the thematic areas listed above - Support in developing, drafting and reviewing reports, studies, analyses, position papers, guidelines, action plans, strategies, implementation plans, legislation, regulations in the thematic areas listed above. - Research and analysis, including diagnostic missions to assess implementation efforts of the AfCFTA protocols, identify obstacles and propose measures to advance implementation. - Facilitation of private sector participation in policy-making processes, facilitation of dialogue and coordination between public and private sector actors relevant to AfCFTA negotiations and implementation - Facilitation of national, regional, and continental workshops and conferences, including interpretation and translation services and providing expert inputs - Provision of support services to the project, including on optimising M&E systems, the design of communication materials, workshop moderation, translation and interpretation services. Deliverables will mainly be in English or French, but may also be in the other official AU languages (Arabic, Portuguese, Spanish, Swahili) depending on the context of the activity The required services are focused, but not limited, on five work packages which are oriented to different stakeholders: Work package 1: Strengthen the AfCFTA Secretariat"s capacity to guide and monitor AfCFTA implementation. Work package 2: Strengthen AUC ETTIM"s capacity to support and monitor the enabling environment for production of goods and services for African markets. Work package 3: Support the coordination of the AfCFTA implementation approach among selected RECs (EAC, ECOWAS, and SADC). Work package 4: Support the domestication and ratification of the AfCFTA Protocols and their Annexes in selected AU MS. Work package 5: Enable private sector actors to trade under AfCFTA rules on the country and regional level. Additionally, the contractor is required to support the provision of support services to the project as well as to partner institutions at the continental, regional and national level under all the work packages above. This includes communication services, moderation services, Monitoring & Evaluation support, translation services, and interpretation services.
sig_a4d9ea61c5c212fc525c.title: 10022598-Short-Term Expert Pools to support negotiations and implementation of the African Continental Free Trade Area (AfCFTA)

Berliner Energie und Wärme GmbH (BEW) operates an independent IT system landscape. This serves to support central business processes in the areas of power generation, heat supply, grid operation, trading, billing, human resources and corporate management. The contractors (CR) provide application management services for defined applications and systems of BEW. The objective is the stable, secure and economical operation of all applications, including business-critical ones, taking into account regulatory requirements, information security and service quality. The CR provides all services on the basis of BEW's ITIL-oriented ITSM processes. The objective of this procurement is to commission a qualified service provider to ensure stable, secure and economical operation of the IT applications. The CR undertakes application management services in second- and third-level support (L2/L3) and thus contributes to the sustained availability, maintainability and security of the applications. The commissioned services are intended in particular to: • ensure the operational stability of applications, • efficiently analyse and resolve faults and errors, • minimise security risks and • sustainably support the technical lifecycle of applications. The services comprise ongoing operations, technical support as well as reactive and preventive application services within the framework of a regulated service and support model. The scope of services includes: • Application Management (L2/L3 support) • Release, update and patch management • Security, stability and compliance requirements The lots are divided as follows: Lot 1: SAP ERP Lot 2: SAP HR Lot 3: SAP IS-U Lot 4: ServiceNow Lot 5: Microsoft Dynamics 365 CE and Power Platform. Lot 6: BI / Data & Analytics. Lot 7: Integration platform (Azure Integration Suite & BizTalk) The SAP ERP lot comprises error analysis, troubleshooting and implementation of minor further developments of SAP ERP ECC 6.0 (SAP on-premises) modules of Berliner Energie und Wärme GmbH (BEW) for the technical safeguarding of core commercial processes. The CR provides the services in second- and third-level support and ensures stable, secure and traceable module operation. SAP basis operation is tendered separately. In the multi-provider model, the CR actively participates in the analysis and resolution of cross-lot incidents and changes; the overarching end-to-end responsibility remains with the contracting authority. The services are provided on a time and materials model. To manage complexity, a distinction is made between two service levels: • Level 2 support (L2): Focus on incident handling, service requests and minor functional adjustments with an effort typically of up to one working day. • Level 3 support (L3): Execution of complex changes (in accordance with the 10 PT rule), root cause analyses as well as architecture consulting and further developments.; The lot 2 comprises error analysis, troubleshooting and the implementation of minor further developments of the human resources management systems of Berliner Energie und Wärme GmbH (BEW). This includes the technical implementation of the contracting authority's functional requirements in SAP HCM as well as technical support for the transformation towards cloud services (in particular SuccessFactors). The contractor is responsible for the application operation of the HR systems as well as the implementation of functionally prioritised requirements into technically suitable solutions. The services are provided on the basis of time and materials.. The CR provides the services in second- and third-level support and ensures stable, secure and traceable module operation. SAP basis operation is tendered separately. In the multi-provider model, the CR actively participates in the analysis and resolution of cross-lot incidents and changes; the overarching end-to-end responsibility remains with the contracting authority. To manage complexity, a distinction is made between two service levels: • Level 2 support (L2): Focus on incident handling, service requests and minor functional adjustments with an effort typically of up to one working day. • Level 3 support (L3): Execution of complex changes (in accordance with the 10 PT rule), root cause analyses as well as architecture consulting and further developments.; The lot 3 comprises error analysis, troubleshooting and implementation of minor further developments of the SAP IS-U modules of Berliner Energie und Wärme GmbH (BEW) for the technical safeguarding of billing processes. The CR provides the services in second- and third-level support and ensures stable, secure and traceable module operation. SAP basis operation is tendered separately. In the multi-provider model, the CR actively participates in the analysis and resolution of cross-lot incidents and changes; the overarching end-to-end responsibility remains with the contracting authority. The services are provided on a time and materials model. To manage complexity, a distinction is made between two service levels: • Level 2 support (L2): Focus on incident handling, service requests and minor functional adjustments with an effort typically of up to one working day. • Level 3 support (L3): Execution of complex changes, root cause analyses as well as architecture consulting and further developments.; The lot 4 comprises operational service delivery, administration and strategic further development of the contracting authority's ServiceNow platform. As a leading enterprise service management system, ServiceNow bundles processes from the IT, asset management, HR and HSE areas into a central platform, thereby enabling optimal use of cross-departmental synergies. Hosting is provided as SaaS in ServiceNow's data centre on production, test and development instances for currently approx. 3.500 users.

The CR must have certified partner status with ServiceNow (e.g. Premier or Elite Partner) in order to ensure access to extended support, roadmap information and partner resources for BEW. The objective is to provide a high-performance, user-friendly and deeply integrated platform that acts as a "single source of truth" for IT operations. The CR provides the services under its own responsibility within the agreed service hours. The CR is obliged to proactively view and process the tasks. The necessary accesses (accounts) are provided by BEW.; The lot 5 comprises operational service delivery as well as technological further development of the contracting authority's central Microsoft ecosystems. This includes the Microsoft 365 collaboration suite, the Power Platform as well as Dynamics 365 CRM CE and Microsoft Power Pages. The objective is to provide a secure, highly available and scalable platform for digital collaboration, business process automation and the hosting of critical cloud workloads within a hybrid zero-trust environment. The services are provided on the basis of time and materials. The contracting authority assumes strategic control and prioritisation of the backlogs. Assigned applications and modules: The scope of services comprises the following components: * Microsoft 365 collaboration suite (Sharepoint and Power BI), * Microsoft Power Platform (model-driven apps, canvas apps, Power Automate Cloud & Desktop), * Microsoft Dynamics 365 CRM CE (modules: Sales, Customer Insights, Service Enterprise) as well as * Power Pages (portals incl. external Entra ID integration).; The lot 6 forms the technological foundation for data-driven decision-making and artificial intelligence at BEW. The focus is on the operation and further development of a scalable lakehouse platform based on Microsoft Azure and Databricks. sig_a5382d147b5149e5af49.description: Automation Marketplace DPS Intelligent automation services and solutions, including automation technologies, services, consultancy and licences. Updates 26/09/24: We have extended this agreement until November 2026. You will be able to buy and run tenders for services until the new expiry date. Description A Dynamic Purchasing System (DPS) that offers automation services and licences for use by the public sector, including their associated bodies and agencies. Automation services are needed to streamline processes and systems for public sector customers. The agreement offers the following services: strategy and business transformation problem solving with tech solutions resources and training software licences What is out of scope? Products and services out of scope include but are not limited to: any hardware and infrastructure hosting networks or connectivity services Benefits accessible route for suppliers – accessible for all suppliers (including SMEs) and suppliers can apply to join at any time government specific terms and conditions (Ts&Cs) – these have been created based on an agile approach using the public sector contract a dynamic filtering system – giving buyers flexibility based on their requirements. Suppliers receive notifications of competitions that are relevant to their service offering and buyers can easily identify potential eligible suppliers supports innovation – suppliers can add new services (within scope) during the lifetime of the DPS, meaning buyers can keep up with fast-moving market developments open to all public sector buyers – including central government departments and the wider public sector access to Cabinet Office (CO) automation task force – receive advice and support from the task force who specialise in the implementation of automation technologies, services and licences Products and suppliers Please read the 'How to buy' tab below for detailed instructions on how to find out which suppliers are on this agreement. Lot 1: Automation Marketplace DPS Understanding the opportunity, setting a strategic direction and target operating models. This filter allows buyers to build an evidence base and the sub-filters are areas to focus on. Expires: 15/11/2026 How to buy You must run a mini competition to select a supplier. There is no option for direct award. Before running your mini competition, find out which suppliers could meet your requirements using the Dynamic Purchasing System (DPS) Marketplace. The steps below outline how to search for suppliers, create a shortlist and carry out a mini competition. Register as a buyer on the Dynamic Purchasing System Marketplace. Note: although pages are headed ‘Supplier registration’ this is also where you can register as a buyer. Navigate to the Automation Marketplace DPS under Technology, choose the ‘Access as a buyer’ option and confirm your acceptance of the customer access agreement. On your ‘Manage your DPS Category Exports’ page you now have 2 options: view appointed suppliers click on the link to create a new category export. This is how you filter the suppliers that can meet your requirements. When creating a new category use the filtering tool (select all that apply) to specify your requirements and create your supplier shortlist. Save your filtered list of capable suppliers by clicking the ‘Save Category’ option and give the shortlist a unique name specific to your competition. From your ‘Manage your Category Exports’ page you can then export the list of suppliers and contact details (export is to an Excel spreadsheet) Quit the DPS. Use the list to run a Further Competition. Invite the suppliers identified by the DPS to bid against your detailed specification, evaluation criteria and contract format. The list is valid for only 2 working days , from the date of its creation, because new suppliers may apply to join at any point. If your Call for Competition excludes eligible suppliers it potentially breaches procurement regulations. You will need to get a fresh supplier list (steps 3.2 to 5) if you don’t use your list within 2 working days by clicking the ‘Search Again’ option for your export. You can use our eSourcing tool to run a Call for Competition. The tool is free to use for public sector buyers, or you can use your organisation’s own procurement tool. Your tender process should be proportionate to the value and complexity of your requirement. suppliers will need a reasonable period of time to review and prepare a response. This includes allowing sufficient time for suppliers to ask clarification questions and consider your answers before the deadline for written responses. Evaluate the responses. Request from the winning supplier(s) any required evidence that they can meet your requirements. Set a 2-day deadline for submitting evidence. If you’re satisfied with the evidence, award the contract Where appropriate, notify of the award on Contracts Finder. Contact Our customer services team is available Monday to Friday, 9am to 5pm. Email the team if you need help completing your procurement or call 0345 410 2222 Documents Updates Crown Commercial Service (CCS) became Government Commercial Agency (GCA) on 1 April 2026. Documents published before this date may still refer to CCS. All contract documents remain valid for existing and new contracts, and there are no changes to how you work with us. sig_a5656958da206bcbea74.description: Invitation to participation in the market dialogue. Asker, Bærum and Drammen municipalities plan to hold a competition for a new contract for the operation and development of websites on Optimizely DXP. Before the competition is announced, we would like a dialogue with the market in the form of one-to-one meetings with relevant tenderers, who can offer systems that cover the municipalities ́needs. The dialogue meetings will be held digitally during week 9. We would like to carry out a combined procurement process to enter into three separate contracts with the same tenderer. The municipalities have in common that we use the same CMS (Optimizely DXP) on version CMS12. The aim is that cooperation, development and sharing across the municipalities take place seamlessly between the three municipalities. Through new contracts a collaborating partner shall be able to support the operation and development of the websites in Asker, Bærum and Drammen municipalities. A collaborating partner must be able to contribute to and deliver the following (the list is not exhaustive): - Stable and safe operation - High competence in Optimizely DXP and resource robustness. - Continual improvement - Development and future orientated focus. - User-oriented focus - Consultancy and competence sharing. - Project management in development. System integration - Design and concept development Close dialogue in both daily operation and development. We would like tenderers to give a presentation of their service offer, which states something about how they can contribute to fulfil the municipalities ́needs. We would also like tenderers to have prepared answers to questions defined in annex 2. Tenderers wishing to participate can register their interest by sending an email to elfrid.nygaard.stabellini@asker.kommune.no, and at the same time state the preferred time for the meeting: - Monday 23.02: 10.00-11.30 - Monday 23.02, 12.30-14.00 - Monday 23.02, 14.30-16.00 - Tuesday 24.02, 08:30 - 10:00. - Tuesday 24.02, 10.30-12.00 - Tuesday 24.02, 13.00-14.30 The registration deadline is 19.02.2026. Annex 1 - Agenda Dialogue Meeting 1. Presentation of meeting participants and cards on the municipalities ́needs. 2. Presentation from the tenderer and review of questions and answers in Annex 2. Annex 2 - Questions and Answers The questions shall be reviewed in the dialogue meeting, and answered and returned in written form to the customer by 27.02.2026: 1.Technical operation and stability A. How do you ensure stable and secure operation of Optimizely DXP for customers with complex needs? B. How do you work with proactive operation and continual technical improvements? c. How will you describe your form of cooperation and dialogue with customers (response time, CRM, regular status meetings)? 2. Development and future oriented focus A. Can you describe how you internally ensure competence development and further development of your employees? B. Beside the main delivery covered by this agreement, assistance can be required for major development projects throughout the contract period. There may be a need for more capacity and special competence from the tenderer. Do you have the opportunity to carry out projects of a larger nature and set aside large amounts of resources in limited periods? Key competence in major projects may, for example, be linked to artificial intelligence in order to proactive information work on the websites and to make content available to target groups that can have challenges with using digital channels. c. How do you envisage that a municipal web will look like in 5 years? 3. Work across three municipalities A. What competence do you have in the municipal sector (or similar entities/organisations) Please give examples. B. How will you organise the cooperation so that development, operation and further development occur seamlessly across Asker, Bærum and Drammen municipalities? How can you facilitate re-use of systems across the municipalities? c. What experiences do you have with working with several customers in joint projects? d. How do you ensure good priorities when three municipalities shall share the same supplier? How do you ensure that there are enough resources with the right competence available? 4. User focus and availability A. How do you work with user testing and insight and how do you use this for continual improvement? 5. Design and concept development A. How do you work with design and concept development at Optimizely DXP, and what methods do you use to make systems uniform and user friendly? Describe how you involve ordering, handling design principles, and ensuring consistency in both visual and content design. 6. How do you share experiences, insight, and best practice with the customers you work with? Do you, for example, have forums or seminars that your customers can participate in for inspiration and competence development? 7. Can you discuss how your company currently works with environment and sustainability and what actions do you take to reduce damaging environmental impact? 8. Can you describe the price model you use? Annex 3 - Documentation that shall be submitted after the dialogue meeting. Deadline: 27.02.2026 1. Presentation from the dialogue meeting, including replies to the questions in annex 2. 3. Three reference customers with a comparable solution (with contact information). 4. Generic price list for their consultants based on seniority and competence.
sig_a5656958da206bcbea74.title: Market dialogue on operation and development of the municipalities ́ websites.

sig_a56a9baaa1057472584e.description: The subject of the procurement is a quality and monitoring information system for the use of Helsingin kaupungin sosiaali-, terveys- ja pelastustoimiala, which is provided as a comprehensive service by the supplier selected for the procurement. The objective of the procurement is to create a unified, user-oriented information system that supports the quality and monitoring of service production, serving employees, supervisors and management, as well as the support and maintenance services that serve the operations. The background to the need and objective is the need to develop a unified system that gathers scattered monitoring data together and supports its systematic utilisation in management and decision-making. Changed legislation, especially the Act on the Supervision of Social and Health Services (741/2023), requires the improvement of the quality, consistency and reporting of monitoring data. The system entity that is the subject of the procurement includes the following architectural, functional and supportable modules: -Quality and monitoring entity (Monitoring tool) -Reporting sections, including irregularities, adverse events and hazards, and the entity of serious adverse events -Entity related to the activities of social and patient ombudsmen -Management of medication administration permits. The subject and requirements of the procurement are described in more detail in the annexes to the call for tenders.
sig_a56a9baaa1057472584e.title: Quality and monitoring information system

sig_a5adb091bedccd2650d4.description: Intro and purpose: The European Free Trade Association (EFTA) is issuing this Request for Information (RFI) to identify potential technology vendors and solutions for replacing the current Case, Records, and Document Management system. This RFI is intended to gather information about available solutions and suppliers to inform the development of a Request for Proposal (RFP) expected to launch in March 2026. We invite technology vendors with relevant expertise to provide information about their solutions, implementation approaches, and experience with similar organizations. Responses to this RFI will help EFTA better understand the current market landscape and refine our requirements for the formal procurement process. This RFI is for informational purposes only and does not constitute a commitment by EFTA to issue an RFP or award a contract. About EFTA: The European Free Trade Association is an intergovernmental organization established in 1960 to promote free trade and economic integration between its member states: Iceland, Liechtenstein, Norway, and Switzerland. EFTA manages various trade agreements, including the European Economic Area (EEA) Agreement, which allows three of its members to participate in the EU's single market. The EFTA Secretariat operates across three locations: Geneva (headquarters), Brussels, and Luxembourg. With approximately [staff number] personnel, the Secretariat supports Member States in promoting free trade and economic integration through six operational divisions. Our work requires comprehensive document, records, and case management capabilities to support trade facilitation, legal, and administrative functions across multiple duty stations and in collaboration with external stakeholders in Member State ministries.
sig_a5adb091bedccd2650d4.title: EFTA - New Case, Records and Document system

sig_a5b36780e05dbdacbda9.description: This is an invitation to a market survey, not a contract notice or a call for tenders. Keski-Uudenmaan hyvinvointialue is preparing the procurement of development expert services. The procurement will be carried out in the dynamic purchasing system TKIO expert services Keski-Uudenmaan hyvinvointialue (hereinafter TKIO procurement system). The procurement system can be found here: https://tarjouspalvelu.fi/UX/TP/SiirryTarjouspyyntoon?p=1254&tpId=580376 The intention is to carry out the procurement of development expert services as an internal competition in the TKIO procurement system category 2 Development of service systems or in the category 4 Strategic development or in both of the aforementioned categories. The intention is to send the call for tenders in early December 2025. The subject of the procurement is expert services for the strategic development of social and health care. The contracting authority uses the expert service, for example, to support the strategic development of financial sustainability, effective and accessible services, and personnel competence and well-being. The expert services to be procured are mainly used by the wellbeing services county as an organiser in strategic development. The purpose of the expert service is to: • produce information, competence and support for identifying changes in the operating environment and implementing strategic changes • produce national and international comparative data and insights to support the contracting authority's strategic development • produce competence and support for change management • produce competence and support for the implementation of projects. The contracting authority invites 1) suppliers interested in providing development expert services to submit an application to participate in the TKIO procurement system and especially in its category 2 Development of service systems and category 4 Strategic development 2) suppliers interested in commenting on the draft procurement documents. The contracting authority requests suppliers interested in commenting on the documents to register by 5.12.2025 at 12. Registration link (You can access the registration by copying the link below and pasting it into the browser's search field): https://forms.office.com/e/qr9g1TnYbg The contracting authority reserves the possibility to send draft documents for comments to all suppliers who have familiarised themselves with the TKIO procurement system. The contracting authority may also carry out the market survey at its discretion in other non-discriminatory ways, such as supplier meetings. Expressing interest and participating in the survey does not bind the supplier to submit an application to participate or to participate in the tendering process. It is also not a prerequisite for participating in the actual tendering process later.

sig_a62c0e60302a4669edc5.description: 2M-IT Oy acts as an in-house company for its owner-customers as a service provider and service integrator for the comprehensive services it offers relating to financial, HR and general administration systems. The services consist of a number of different service components, which 2M-IT produces itself or procures from its subcontractors as part of these comprehensive services. Subcomponents of the service include, for example, IT supplier licences and expert services; IT services, which cover, for example, data communications connections and related services, as well as data centre and capacity services. In addition, the components include various development projects and testing, as well as post-implementation support services, which may consist, for example, of first-line support provided by the 2M-IT service desk, and possible second-line application support. System suppliers provide the portion of application support required for this comprehensive post-implementation support service. It is also possible to purchase the entire package as the supplier's SaaS service. The services offered by 2M-IT Oy to its customers consist of coordinating existing solutions and new solutions and shaping them into unified system packages, producing the aforementioned service components, and expert services essentially related to the packages or entirely new services related to financial, HR and general administration systems. The task of 2M-IT as an in-house company is to develop the services it offers to its owner-customers. During the validity period of the dynamic purchasing system („DPS”), the aim is to create regionally more uniform comprehensive services that enable uniform and modern, automated services in the financial, HR and general administration sectors across the entire wellbeing services county level. Implementations can streamline, make more efficient and develop processes and operations. Based on the procurements made within this DPS, 2M-IT may procure licences for financial, HR and general administration systems and other related services (e.g. implementation projects and services produced during development) as well as expert services, excluding basic IT and data communications packages. The procurements made within this DPS can be used to carry out the subcontractor procurements necessary to assemble the various regional service packages. Geographical areas, 2M-IT customers and other necessary matters will be specified in more detail in the procurements made within the DPS. The subject of procurement made within the DPS may be licences and/or services and/or expert services relating to financial, HR and general administration systems, or packages consisting of licence usage rights, services and expert services.

sig_a62c53dd120a0e386c4f.description: NAICS CODE: 541715 FEDERAL AGENCY NAME: Department of the Air Force, Air Force Materiel Command, AFRL - Rome Research Site, AFRL/Information Directorate, 26 Electronic Parkway, Rome, NY, 13441-4514 BAA ANNOUNCEMENT TYPE: Initial announcement BROAD AGENCY ANNOUNCEMENT (BAA) TITLE: Artificial Intelligence and Next Generation Distributed Command and Control BAA NUMBER: FA8750-23-S-7006 PART I – OVERVIEW INFORMATION This announcement is for an Open, 2 Step BAA which is open and effective until 30 AUG 2028. Only white papers will be accepted as initial submissions; formal proposals will be accepted by invitation only. While white papers will be considered if received prior to 1600 hours Eastern Standard Time (EST) on 30 AUG 2028, the following submission dates are suggested to best align with projected funding: FY24 by 13 SEP 2023 FY25 by 15 Mar 2024 FY26 by 15 Mar 2025 FY27 by 15 Mar 2026 FY28 by 15 Mar 2027 Offerors should monitor the Contract Opportunities on the SAM website at https://SAM.gov in the event this announcement is amended. CONCISE SUMMARY OF TECHNOLOGY REQUIREMENT: Artificial Intelligence (AI) holds great potential in transforming the Department of the Air Force (DAF) and Joint Force Command and Control (C2) capabilities across strategic, operational, and tactical levels by enabling decision makers to effectively assess the battlespace, rapidly explore, create, and select the best plan, and direct and monitor forces at pace and scale in a distributed setting. This BAA is interested in exploring new and advancing existing AI and distributed C2 concepts. By accelerating the research & development of novel AI-based and distributed capabilities to support Joint All Domain C2, the DAF can achieve a strategic decision advantage, where AI becomes a key and prevalent component to future C2 systems. With the rise of AI-based applications also comes new challenges to include the ability to effectively manage, monitor, and adapt deployed AI capabilities and effective C2 in a distributed and contested environment. Distributed operations is a critical component of Next-Generation C2. Key to the DAF transitioning from a single monolithic C2 node to multiple distributed C2 nodes is the ability orchestrate operational processes, while optimizing for limited resources. Through the development of distributed C2 capabilities the DAF can achieve an agile, fully mobile, distributed, and virtualized C2 operational capability. This BAA is interested in key areas for advancing C2 capability for the DAF to include but not limited to development and application of AI to C2, new concepts and techniques for the battle management and orchestration of AI at pace and scale, how the use of AI by adversaries can be considered in the C2 planning and execution process and distributed and collaborative C2 to enable C2 anywhere and anyplace. BAA ESTIMATED FUNDING: Total funding for this BAA is approximately $99M. Individual awards will not normally exceed 48 months with dollar amounts normally ranging from $200K to $20M. There is also the potential to make awards up to any dollar value as long as the value does not exceed the available BAA ceiling amount. ANTICIPATED INDIVIDUAL AWARDS: Multiple Awards are anticipated. However, the Air Force reserves the right to award zero, one, or more Procurement Contracts, Other Transactions, or Assistance Instruments, for all, some, or none of the solicited effort based on the offeror’s ability to perform desired work and funding fluctuations. There is no limit on the number of OTs that may be awarded to an individual offeror. TYPE OF INSTRUMENTS THAT MAY BE AWARDED: FAR based Procurement contracts, DODGARS based grants and cooperative agreements or other transactions (OT) under 10 USC 4021, 10 USC 4022 and 10 USC 4023 (previously 10 USC 4002, 2371, 10 USC 4003, 2371b and 4004, 2373) depending upon the nature of the work proposed. In the event that an Other Transaction for Prototype agreement is awarded as a result of this competitive BAA, and the prototype project is successfully completed, there is the potential for a prototype project to transition to award of a follow-on production contract or transaction. The Other Transaction for Prototype Agreement itself will also contain a similar notice of a potential follow-on production contract or agreement. AGENCY CONTACT INFORMATION: All white paper submissions and any questions of a technical nature shall be directed to the cognizant Technical Point of Contact (TPOC) as specified below (unless otherwise specified in the technical area): BAA PROGRAM MANAGER: Gennady Staskevich AFRL/RISC 525 Brooks Rd Rome, NY 13441-4505 Telephone: (315) 330-4889 Email: gennady.staskevich@us.af.mil Questions of a contractual/business nature shall be directed to the cognizant contracting officer, as specified below (email requests are preferred): Amber Buckley Telephone (315) 330-3605 Email: Amber.Buckley@us.af.mil Emails must reference the solicitation (BAA) number and title of the acquisition. Pre-Proposal Communication between Prospective Offerors and Government Representatives: Dialogue between prospective offerors and Government representatives is encouraged. Technical and contracting questions can be resolved in writing or through open discussions. Discussions with any of the points of contact shall not constitute a commitment by the Government to subsequently fund or award any proposed effort. Only Contracting Officers are legally authorized to commit the Government. Offerors are cautioned that evaluation ratings may be lowered and/or proposal rejected if proposal preparation (Proposal format, content, etc.) and/or submittal instructions are not followed. sig_a62ce7ae50674cb84864.description: Machine Learning and Artificial Intelligence (AI) are enabling extraordinary scientific breakthroughs in fields ranging from protein folding, natural language processing, drug synthesis, and recommender systems to the discovery of novel engineering materials and products. These achievements lie at the confluence of mathematics, statistics, engineering and computer science, yet a clear explanation of the remarkable power and also the limitations of such AI systems has eluded scientists from all disciplines. Critical foundational gaps remain that, if not properly addressed, will soon limit advances in machine learning, curbing progress in artificial intelligence. It appears increasingly unlikely that these critical gaps can be surmounted with increased computational power and experimentation alone. Deeper mathematical understanding is essential to ensuring that AI can be harnessed to meet the future needs of society and enable broad scientific discovery, while forestalling the unintended consequences of a disruptive technology. The National Science Foundation Directorates for Mathematical and Physical Sciences (MPS), Computer and Information Science and Engineering (CISE), Engineering (ENG), and Social, Behavioral and Economic Sciences (SBE) will jointly sponsor research collaborations consisting of mathematicians, statisticians, computer scientists, engineers, and social and behavioral scientists focused on the mathematical and theoretical foundations of AI. Research activities should focus on the most challenging mathematical and theoretical questions aimed at understanding the capabilities, limitations, and emerging properties of AI methods as well as the development of novel, and mathematically grounded, design and analysis principles for the current and next generation of AI approaches. Specific research goals include: establishing a fundamental mathematical understanding of the factors determining the capabilities and limitations of current and emerging generation s of AI systems, including, but not limited to, foundation models, generative models, deep learning, statistical learning, federated learning, and other evolving paradigms; the development of mathematically grounded design and analysis principles for the current and next generations of AI systems; rigorous approaches for characterizing and validating machine learning algorithms and their predictions; research enabling provably reliable, translational, general-purpose AI systems and algorithms; e ncouragement of new collaborations in this interdisciplinary research community and between institution s. The overall goal is to establish innovative and principled design and analysis approaches for AI technology using creative yet theoretically grounded mathematical and statistical frameworks, yielding explainable and interpretable models that can enable sustainable, socially responsible, and trustworthy AI.
sig_a62ce7ae50674cb84864.title: Mathematical Foundations of Artificial Intelligence

sig_a6a4fbe2e1f8f46b3c6b.description: Iarnród Éireann – Irish Rail (IÉ) is seeking to establish a contract for the design, supply, configuration, integration, commissioning, support and maintenance of a Station Services Mediation System (SSMS). The SSMS will provide the central processing, integration and management platform for real-time passenger information services across the Iarnród Éireann railway network. The system will interface with existing and future IÉ operational systems, including timetable systems, signalling systems, Passenger Information Display Systems (PIDS), Long Line Public Address (LLPA) systems and external passenger information platforms. The solution will support the phased migration from IÉ's existing Customer Information Systems to the future Centralised Traffic Control and Communications Based Interlocking (CBI) environment while maintaining continuity of passenger information services throughout the transition. The scope includes all necessary software, licences, configuration and integration services, testing, commissioning, migration, documentation, training, maintenance, technical support, cybersecurity updates, lifecycle and obsolescence management required to provide a fully operational and supported SSMS solution. The proposed contract will be for an initial period of eight (8) years, with an option for IÉ to extend the contract for a further three (3) years at its discretion.
sig_a6a4fbe2e1f8f46b3c6b.title: 9947 Station Services Mediation System (SSMS)

sig_a6ef63b560c76eb08cdf.description: The subject of the contract is the implementation of the task entitled "Effective infrastructure for collective water supply in the Lipno Municipality", divided into three parts. Part I covers the supply and replacement of 2 547 water meters together with telemetry modules and the implementation of a remote reading system. Part II covers the implementation of a GIS system, conducting a measurement campaign, and the creation and calibration of a hydraulic model of the water supply network. Part III covers work on the active water supply network related to the replacement of hydrants and gate valves together with associated works. Supply and replacement of 2 547 water meters together with 2 547 IoT telemetry modules and a service buffer of 50 modules, together with the configuration and commissioning of a unified remote reading system, data transmission, documentation, and training. The contract also includes the provision of SIM cards and data transmission for a period of 10 years. A mandatory site visit is required to verify the coverage and availability of the network in the area of contract implementation, on the terms specified in the SWZ.; The subject of Part 2 of the contract is the implementation of a GIS system, conducting a measurement campaign, and the creation and calibration of a hydraulic model of the Lipno Municipality water supply network, together with the commissioning of the system, documentation, training, and support.; Part III covers work on the active water supply network in 141 locations, including 70 complete hydrant nodes DN80 together with the replacement of the gate valve DN80, 10 complete hydrant nodes DN80 without replacing the existing gate valve DN80 and 61 complete replacements of gate valves DN100. The total material scope includes 80 hydrants DN80, 70 gate valves DN80 and 61 gate valves DN100. The contract also includes all earthworks, assembly and restoration works, and other activities required by the OPZ

sig_a6f7707a951d73d1de15.description: This is a request for information, which is not a procurement notice or call for tenders. The purpose of the request for information is to gather information concerning the subject of the procurement for a future competition. Responding to the request for information is not a prerequisite for participating in the competition. To ensure the success of the future competition, however, it would be important for tenderers to provide the contracting authority with the requested information as broadly as possible. The request for information does not oblige Servica Oy to carry out the procurement as described in the request for information or its annexes, and the tendering procedure may also not be carried out. No compensation will be paid to those who responded to the request for information for responding to it or participating in presentation events related to it. Tenderers are requested to familiarise themselves with the contracting authority's preliminary call for tenders and draft contract, as well as other relevant annexes. The contracting authority aims to comply with the principles of public procurement in the procurement, which are equality, non-discrimination, transparency and proportionality. The contracting authority asks tenderers to pay attention to the following matters: 1) Is sufficient information related to the procurement available in the call for tenders to make submitting a tender possible? 2) Are the requirements of the call for tenders in proper proportion to the quality of the procurement and the characteristics of the services? 3) Are there requirements or conditions in the call for tenders that could prevent the emergence of equal and non-discriminatory competition? 4) Is there incorrect or contradictory information in the call for tenders? 5) Is the presented pricing model such that submitting a tender is possible? The contracting authority is not obliged to answer questions or change the content of the procurement based on the tenderers' responses. sig_a70d48788e7c199ea108.description: The contracting authority is striving for the digital modernisation of its individual agendas. One of these agendas is the parking policy of the city of Olomouc (hereinafter also referred to as the "PPMO"). Currently, the territorial scope of the parking policy applies to only two parking zones (A and B). In the planned expansion to zones C and D (including their sub-areas), it is also necessary to adjust and strengthen the existing part of the PPMO, which handles the registry of parking permits. Therefore, the contracting authority has decided to procure the acquisition of services for a new, modern system for the registry of parking permits, whereby these services will be used to optimise faster processing for citizens, ensure connection to state administration registries, and connection to other PPMO systems for more efficient processing of transferred data, and a modern graphical interface meeting current trends will also be achieved. The provision of the services of the system for the registry of parking permits must also fulfil all current legislative and security requirements. The subject matter of performance of this public contract is: a) performance of a requirements analysis, processing and implementation of the target concept, establishment and commissioning of the Portal Solution for the registry of parking permits (hereinafter referred to as the "PPMO Portal Solution"), data migration, testing, provision of training, provision of licences and provision of all other related performance necessary for the proper commissioning of the PPMO Portal Solution; b) provision of the PPMO Portal Solution as a service (in service mode), ensuring its maintenance and support, provision of the IT infrastructure necessary for the operation of the PPMO Portal Solution; c) provision of development services, analytical and methodical services, implementation of change requests and provision of other related performance based on the requirements of the contracting authority. A more detailed specification of the subject matter of performance is contained in the relevant parts of the tender documentation (hereinafter also referred to as the "TD"), in particular Appendix No. 2 and Appendix No. 3 of the TD. The types of parking permits are outlined in Appendix No. 12 of the TD. The types of parking permits may change over time.
sig_a70d48788e7c199ea108.title: Portal solution for parking permit recording (PPMO)

sig_a70d6fe2ae0f41162ace.description: The Council has identified a need for supported living for c800 with disabilities in Hertfordshire over the next five years (2025-2030) This includes provision for people: • Transitioning from children’s services • Currently residing with family who now need a home of their own. • Currently residing in residential care whose support needs have reduced. • Currently residing in supported living which is shared and are now needing self-contained housing. • Currently residing in supported living outside of Hertfordshire who wish to return to return. The Council is exploring the best approach to work with developing Registered Providers (both Housing Associations and Local Authorities) (‘RPs’) to deliver, own and manage accommodation on Council owned land via a long lease (virtual freehold). The Council is currently undertaking preparatory work on six Council owned land-led sites with a view to progressing design and enabling works during 2025-26, construction in 2026/27 – 2027/28 and completion and handover in 2027–30. The Council will obtain planning approval on all six sites via Regulation 3 and where demolition/enabling works are required on the site the Council will undertake this work prior to long lease disposal to an RP to develop and build the new accommodation. The Council is carrying out PME in relation to this project. The Council will consider the feedback received to help inform the Council’s options, requirements and further decision making. For the avoidance of doubt, this stage of the project is not part of a formal procurement process and the Council is not committing, at this stage, to carrying out such a process. Participation or non-participation in the PME shall not prevent any supplier participating in a potential future procurement, nor is it intended that any information supplied as part of the PME shall place any supplier at an advantage in a potential procurement process. Participation in the PME will be at each organisation’s own cost. No expense in responding to this PME will be reimbursed by the Council. To access the PME documentation please visit the Council’s e-tendering system Supply Hertfordshire, run by Intend at https://in-tendhost.co.uk/supplyhertfordshire and follow the on-screen guidance. To participate in this PME, organisations must return their completed Supplier Questionnaire (Appendix A of the PME Document), together with any supporting documents, through the Correspondence area of this project by the return deadline of 12.00 Noon on 28th October 2025, as per the PME documentation and e-tendering system. Supplier Questionnaires received after the deadline may not be reviewed at the Council’s sole discretion. Please make sure that you have submitted your Supplier Questionnaire following the instructions within the PME documentation and e-tendering system. The Council will not be held accountable for any errors made by an organisation in submitting their Supplier Questionnaire. If you are experiencing problems with the Supply Hertfordshire website, In-Tend offer a help section which includes a dedicated UK support desk which can be contacted via email: support@in-tend.co.uk or Telephone: +44 1144070065 for any website/technical questions, Monday to Friday, 8:30-17:00. sig_a737d568f912d506e0a5.description: The subject of the dynamic purchasing system (DPS) is IT specialist services for Energiavirasto. The subject of the dynamic purchasing system thus includes the following services, which are divided into two categories (sub-areas): 1) Development and maintenance work for Energiavirasto systems 2) Development and maintenance services for the Energiavirasto data processing environment Energiavirasto has case management systems for external customer service and internal work. In system development, Energiavirasto uses its own software development model and architecture (Energiavirasto Framework for Application Development, 'EFAD'). The systems are built in Microsoft Azure and M365 environments, for which we require experience from suppliers. The tasks include, for example, system definition, development, system modification work, continuous service maintenance tasks, security development, data migrations and interface service development. System developers, administrators and architects monitor and utilise public cloud services in the provision of services, with the main emphasis on the Microsoft Azure environment, but not necessarily limited to it. The goal of Energiavirasto is to acquire efficient, productive and high-quality competence and expertise for system development and maintenance work as well as other project-related tasks related to the subject of the procurement. The development work takes place in accordance with the delivery model of Energiavirasto, which Energiavirasto will specify in connection with each internal competition. As a general rule, the delivery model means that Energiavirasto is responsible for project management and the experts work under the management of Energiavirasto. Suppliers are required to have versatile evidence of competence in application development on the Microsoft Azure platform and maintenance of the environment in question. The systems of Energiavirasto are developed entirely in a serverless (PaaS) environment. A more detailed description of the required competence is provided in connection with each internal competition, and the areas of competence and their weightings may vary in internal competitions on a project-by-project basis. During the duration of the DPS, all interested candidates can submit an application to participate in it. There is no limit to the number of candidates that can be accepted into the DPS. This DPS is valid until the date stated in the contract notice. Energiavirasto has the right to suspend the dynamic purchasing system during its validity, close it temporarily or change its validity. Energiavirasto carries out procurements through internal competitions of the DPS. It is possible to conduct internal competitions throughout the duration of the DPS, starting, however, after the establishment phase. Internal procurements are put out to tender among the suppliers accepted into the DPS. Internal competitions may include one or more items. The items are defined in more detail in the calls for tenders. For one project or procurement of a service, expert services can be acquired from one or more suppliers according to the needs of Energiavirasto. Procurement contracts made on the basis of the DPS can in principle be valid for the duration of the DPS or for a shorter period. However, it is possible to agree on an option of up to 2 years in the contracts. Energiavirasto has estimated that the total estimated value of the procurement during the duration of the DPS is approximately 5 200 000 euros. Energiavirasto carries out procurements according to its needs. Energiavirasto is not committed to specific procurement volumes. The value of the procurement may also change. The development and maintenance work of the systems of Energiavirasto includes the maintenance and development of the individual systems, system development model and architecture of Energiavirasto.; The development and maintenance work of the data processing environment of Energiavirasto includes development and maintenance work on the IT platform used by Energiavirasto, which may relate, for example, to data security, technical solutions and the utilisation of services offered by the platform.
sig_a737d568f912d506e0a5.title: Maintenance and development work for the systems and data processing environment of Energiavirasto

sig_a7d1f416274e89243a7d.description: Henneberg Clinics - Mobile Laboratory Automation and Robotics The subject matter is the planning, delivery, integration, conformity assessment, commissioning, acceptance and service of a fully mobile robotics/automation solution for barcode-supported sample flow between intake, pre-analytics, analysis systems, special dispensing, cooling and archiving. The solution must function as an overall system with laboratory equipment, LIS/middleware, building infrastructure and operator processes. Not the subject matter of this lot are medical laboratory services, the permanent provision of laboratory personnel, or the immediate procurement of transport or cleaning robots. Laboratory equipment and laboratory IT are procured separately. However, the robotics contractor remains responsible for the complete mechanical, electrical, software, control and safety engineering integration of the overall system they offer. Target image and functional equivalence: • Permanent robotics-supported in-house laboratory operations at the Hildburghausen site from 01.01.2027; no transitional supply. The first expansion stage is the mobile laboratory robotics system. • Documented peak intake: maximum approx. 30 samples per hour. The solution must not be unnecessarily oversized for this, but must demonstrate a comprehensible operational reserve. • Fully mobile, autonomously navigating robotics systems (AMR) or functionally equivalent mobile automation solutions are permitted. Stationary robot cells, linearly guided systems and permanently installed tracks do not meet the target image. • The solution offered is not an isolated robotics island: it is seamlessly integrated into order, sample, equipment, result, priority and error management and networked via a centrally provided orchestration and fleet management software. The software and platform architecture must be provably scalable for subsequent transport and cleaning robotics at two sites of the clinic association. A common or interoperable traffic logic, building and elevator interfaces, identity and certificate management, as well as a uniform operating and service concept must be provided. The initial procurement must not create unnecessary binding to proprietary laboratory equipment or closed building interfaces. Open, documented interface specifications that can be handed over to the contracting authority are a minimum requirement; a device-side extension to SiLA 2 or a functionally equivalent open standard must be presented. The contractor must describe the entry with a robust core workflow and the subsequent expansion with additional tasks, grippers, equipment, rooms and robotics domains in a technically and commercially comprehensible manner.

sig_a845c8ec58fb938f4a6a.description: The Finnish Medicines Agency Fimea (later Fimea) is preparing the procurement of a system for receiving, validation and reviewing marketing authorisation applications for medicinal products and other regulatory submissions. Fimea is primarily looking for a software as a service (SaaS) off-the shelf solution that is provided from a public cloud. The system shall enable the necessary integrations with Fimea's other systems, which will be defined later. The procurement will also include the deployment, support and maintenance services for the system to be procured. Life cycles of the medicinal product dossiers (sequences and attributes) must be migrated to the system. Migration will be part of the procurement. The purpose of this request for information is to identify potential tenderers and to gather information on the solutions available on the market. Following the market dialogue, a call for tenders for the procurement will be prepared. DESCRIPTION The system to be procured shall support the receipt and validation of regulatory submissions, as well as the view and review of application materials. The system shall ensure a smooth and consistent user experience for the marketing authorisation specialists and to minimise manual steps through automated workflow functionalities. Preliminary requirements for the procurement are: - Data import functionalities: The solution shall support automated and manual import of regulatory submissions related to medicinal products. • Different types of submissions: o eCTD (electronic Common Technical Document, all formats), (v)NeeS (Non-eCTD electronic Submission), non-standard based submissions, ASMF (active substance master file), PSUR (Periodic Safety Update Report) • The sources of data: o Common European Submission Portal (CESP) o Other possible sources, e.g. EMA Common Repository (CR), Union Product Database (UPD), PSUR repository o Manual import of material (e.g. from email) to the system also enabled - The system sends a notification about a new submission and forms a job queue - Technical validation of regulatory submissions, including all versions of eCTD - Flexible dossier and sequence management for agency administrators - API capabilities: The system shall include flexible API capabilities to enable integrations with other relevant systems and repositories, such as case management systems and archiving solutions - User management: The system shall include advanced user management features, enabling the administration of access rights and roles for different user groups - View and review of the dossier in the system • Different view modes (single sequence vs. cumulative view of the application) • Advanced search functionalities • Possibility to use AI-assisted review: The system shall include or support the integration of AI#assisted tools - The location of the data needs to be in the EU region, and the cloud service provided by the service supplier

sig_a8e32368747fa9182e47.description: XC Trains Limited (XC) operates passenger rail services over those routes listed within Appendix 2 of the ITP document. XC is a unique operation in that it runs from the Southwest in England to the North of Scotland and is the most extensive rail franchise in Britain, calling at more than 100 stations. XC serves 7 of the 10 largest UK cities with 7 routes radiating from a central hub in Birmingham. The Service Quality Regime (SQR) was set up by the Department for Transport (DfT) to incentivise Train Operating Companies (TOCs) to ensure customer experience standards across the railway network are maintained and improved. The regime is defined in the National Rail Contracts (NRCs) that exist between TOCs and the DfT, including XC's NRC. The NRC sets out the obligations that TOCs have to deliver to ensure compliance with the Contract, and the repercussions if they are not. XC's SQR has been in place since late 2021 and has seen a few changes since it first started. XC is also proud to have helped the DfT trial changes to SQR during this time to pave the way for other TOCs following in the future. THE PROJECT This Procurement is undertaken by XC on behalf of itself, and a successor operator of the XC. The key elements and strategic objectives of the Project are: - Train Service Regime (TSR) inspections by inspectors; - Customer Service Regime (CSR) inspections by mystery shoppers; - Accessible Customer Service Regime (ACSR) inspections by mystery shoppers with additional accessible needs; - Provision of mobile devices to the supplier inspectors and mystery shoppers for running inspection forms; and - Inspection data quality assurance. Further details of the requirements can be found within the associated documents. Lot 1: .

sig_a8f679baea262f7d8cbc.description: Background Many developing countries and emerging economies are negatively impacted by trade constraints resulting from red tape in the form of complicated customs documents, import surveillance and border procedures that lack transparency. High transaction costs make it difficult for them to tap into global value chains and make their businesses less competitive. Many enterprises are thereby denied opportunities to grow through trade. In 2017, the World Trade Organization"s (WTO) Trade Facilitation Agreement (TFA) entered into force with the objective to simplify, modernize and harmonize export and import processes in order to facilitate the cross-border movements of goods. It also establishes measures for effective cooperation between customs and other relevant authorities on trade facilitation and customs compliance. Additionally, it contains provisions for technical assistance and capacity building. Measures to facilitate trade play an important role across a variety of policy areas and sectors. They have a positive effect on food security, rural development, consumer protection, investment promotion and good governance among others. Project rationale The GIZ global program "Partnerships for Sustainable Trade" (PST) has been commissioned by the German Federal Ministry of Economic Cooperation and Development (BMZ) to establish measures that facilitate trade and support environment and climate protection. Its duration is from 07/2024 to 12/2027. The program focuses on implementing the Trade Facilitation Agreement of the World Trade Organization (WTO) and promotes cooperation between companies, business and trade associations as well as state institutions. As an implementation partner of the Global Alliance for Trade Facilitation (the Alliance), it aligns development objectives with economic interests. The Alliance supports low and middle-income countries in streamlining trade-related processes to move goods across their borders as quickly, safely, and cost-effectively as possible. The Alliance is an initiative that puts public private partnership at the heart of its approach to trade reform, believing that governments and businesses of all sizes working together represents the best way of delivering transformative, positive change. The Alliance is jointly hosted by the World Economic Forum, the International Chamber of Commerce and the Center for International Private Enterprise and works in cooperation with the Deutsche Gesellschaft für Internationale Zusammenarbeit (GIZ) GmbH. It is currently funded by the governments of Canada, Germany, Sweden, and the European Union (EU). Program measures include: - Planning and implementing trade facilitation measures in various countries in Africa, the Balkans, and Asia; - Increasing efficiency and reducing customs clearance costs by digitising processes and commercial documents; - Simplifying import and export procedures in developing and least developed countries (LDCs) through digital solutions and public-private partnerships; - Supporting developing countries in representing their interests in the multilateral trading system and in the WTO. The program is co-funded by different donors. At the beginning of 2025, the EU joined the Alliance as a new donor through co-funding the GIZ program. The EU contribution to the Alliance focusses on strengthening trade facilitation in least developed countries. Further co-financing comes from the World Trade Organisation (WTO) for the implementation of projects of the WTO Trade Facilitation Assistance Facility and by the EU Delegation to Madagascar for the implementation of an Alliance project in the country. Structure of the PST program The overall objective of the project is: In countries of the Global South, government, private actors or non-governmental organizations are equipped with improved instruments and competencies for the further development of the multilateral trading system for a Just Transition. The program is structured in 4 different Outputs: Output 1: Selected countries of the Global South are equipped with options for action for an inclusive, economic, and ecologically sustainable development of the multilateral trading system. Output 2: Proven trade facilitation instruments are embedded in selected countries of the Global South. Output 3: Innovative, climate and environmentally friendly approaches to trade facilitation have been further developed. Output 4: Trade facilitation instruments are embedded in selected LDCs. The project countries are specified in the Terms of Reference. The PST program seeks the services of a consulting firm to provide technical experts under different short-term expert (STE) pools, which can be deployed according to the project proposals and operational plans of each project country. The services will be delivered mainly by short-term experts in form of technical and administrative services for the development and implementation of specific trade facilitation measures in partner countries. The services also cover cross-cutting areas such as stakeholder engagement, workshop and training facilitation, and process management. Specifically, in the context of the respective in-country project workplans, the experts are foreseen to provide expertise in technical fields aimed at change management and capacity building of the respective identified border agencies. The services to be delivered in the project countries include: - Conducting analyses and gap assessments on specific IT solutions or processes for Customs and other border agencies - Business process engineering of customs and logistics procedures - Technically oversee the implementation of IT solutions by IT solution providers - Support Customs and other partner agencies in developing and implementing change management plans - Developing and facilitating public-private dialogue formats - Developing training materials and conducting trainings (specifically train the trainer approaches) - Potentially, support for the scoping of Global Alliance for Trade Facilitation projects through fact finding missions and concept/proposal development[LL2.1]. Several new projects will be designed in the coming months. Potential countries for these new projects include Brazil, Cote d"Ivoire, Kenya, India, Indonesia, South Africa. Specifically, the following technical areas within respective work packages are covered through services provided by the STE pools: Work package 1. Customs modernisation and digitisation, including change management and process optimisation - Stabilizing and upgrading (ASYCUDA) and other customs management systems, - Reviewing customs management processes and drafting standard operating procedures (SOPs), - Supporting customs in piloting and rolling-out newly developed IT solutions or re-engineered processes; including specifically for airfreight and express clearance procedures. Work package 2. Support for specific Customs procedures - Improving customs workflows for tariff valuation and classification, fall-back and continuity procedures, - Development and roll-out of advance ruling systems. Work package 3. Risk management, including Authorised Economic Operator Schemes - Review existing risk management approaches, - Revision of selectivity rules, - Gap analysis of the policy and regulatory framework and on-the-ground implementation, - Development and proposal of improved risk management systems, approaches, or specific rules, adaptation or extension of existing approaches and systems to cover additional specialised cases, such as perishable goods, express shipments, or low value shipments, - Development and implementation of preferential schemes for trusted economic operators (Authorised economic operator schemes), - Pre-arrival processing of manifest information to trigger risk analysis, - Post Clearance Audits. Work package 4. Import and export permits/ certificates - Implementation of the IPPC ePhyto certification solution, - Development and implementation of processes / digital solutions for issuing (electronic) certificates for fish exports (eFish) as well as for animal products (eVet), - Digitisation of line Ministry agencies" import/export permit or certification processes (e.g. by Ministry of Agriculture, Bureau of Standards, Animal health board, etc.), - Process re-engineering, improvement of phytosanitary risk management systems, - Integration of the approvals/permits into the respective customs management systems and any other relevant platform (e.g. trade single windows), - Revision of workflows and processes. Since the focus of this tender lies on the provision of technical expertise through the mobilisation of short-term experts, the contractor is expected to implement rigorous processes for the selecting, preparing, training and steering the experts assigned to carry out the advisory services.
