sig_a9621991a0ec5f1287b9.description:
Maintaining and swiftly empowering a digitally competent working society that contributes to a productive and competitive economy despite demographic change and skills shortages is in the strategic interest of the Federal Government. Securing the skills base is crucial, in particular, for the competitiveness of companies. In view of an ageing society, there is an urgent need for action to keep employees in businesses under good and healthy working conditions for as long as possible, to tap into unused domestic potential and to make the working world more inclusive and diverse. Digital technologies and, above all, Artificial Intelligence (AI) offer the opportunity to keep people with age-related, cognitive or mental impairments in the labour market or to integrate them for longer and in better health, and to create an environment suited to older people and those with disabilities. The research contract to be awarded (performance period: 2027–2028) aims to identify the opportunities and needs of Small and Medium-sized Enterprises (SMEs) and workers with impairments regarding the use of technological support in the workplace and thus to unlock labour potential with the aid of digitalisation and AI. Since there is as yet no systematic and comprehensive presentation of this, there is a need for practice-oriented and practicable scientific research on how SMEs can support employees with impairments in the workplace through the use of new technologies (e.g. AI). A contribution is also to be made to safeguarding the experiential knowledge of employees and strengthening existing (advisory) structures by supporting higher-level institutions (e.g. inclusion offices, chambers of industry and commerce, top-level business associations) in advising SMEs on issues relating to digital transformation. The research contract is being tendered Europe-wide as a competitive dialogue with a preceding call for competition. The services may be provided by a consortium. In order to achieve the set objectives, the contractors implementing the research project must perform at least the following work packages. The precise design is to be explained by the tenderers within the framework of the competitive dialogue: 1. Basic research and needs analysis: o Conducting an empirical-exploratory study to identify and systematically present the needs of SMEs and their employees with impairments. o Preparation of an overview of suitable technological and AI-based solutions. o Suitability testing of AI technologies for specific fields of work; if they are not suitable, the need for alternative solutions is to be demonstrated. 2. Implementation strategies and implementation: o Development of implementation proposals and assistance for the implementation and long-term use of the identified technologies. o Identification and creation of target-group-appropriate information resources and channels. o Integration of feedback and evaluation through a co-creative approach. 3. Review and adaptation: o Review and testing of the developed information resources and channels, as well as their refinement and adaptation. o Examination of the effectiveness of the (AI) support instruments. 4. Dissemination including a broad-impact support service across the board: o Continuous dissemination to enhance the public profile of the project objectives and results. Addressees of the research contract: scientific institutions, universities and research institutions. Subject matter and addressees of the research measure: SMEs and higher-level institutions, which are to be involved accordingly in the implementation of the project. The perspectives of affected workers, self-representation, advisory and self-help organisations and associations of and for people with disabilities must also be taken into account. Lot LOT-0000: Making inclusive use of labour potential through digitalisation and AI. sig_a9893005460ff4aa4292.description: The subject matter of the service to be provided is the client's media management, i.e. all activities associated with the procurement, administration, maintenance, logistics, technology and service as well as the application of the media used by the client. The subject matter of the service to be provided is the client's media management, i.e. all activities associated with the procurement, administration, maintenance, logistics, technology and service as well as the application of the media used by the client. This comprises in particular: • personal consultation of the client, • the provision and operation of an online platform for professional information management (administrative portal), • the provision and operation of an online database including the procurement of licences for a legal information system, • the delivery of media and specialist media and • the delivery of specialist literature for trainees. The client is a statutory health insurance fund operating flexibly on the market. Therefore, the services must also be provided for future additional locations on the same terms. The delivery of brochures, flyers and comparable media that are not publishing products is not the subject matter of the service. The contractor shall advise the client independently of publishers and products on the selection and administration of the literature and specialist information inventory used alongside the legal information system in the form of digital and paper-based media. The contractor has comprehensive expertise in the field of social security (focusing on health and long-term care insurance), which guarantees professional advice for media in European, federal and state law. All media are to be made available as online variants, where available. In addition to use under Citrix, use via mobile end devices (e.g. tablet, smartphone) must also be enabled. The contractor shall advise the client on the selection of products in a future-oriented manner. They shall support the client in continuously optimising the individual requirements of the client's staff and corporate divisions under economic efficiency aspects, while equipping as many demand points as possible with uniform media. The client's media structure is primarily geared towards electronic media. The primary focus here is on the homogeneous equipment of all teams with, where possible, a single uniform product. Additional electronic solutions, loose-leaf publications, trade journals and bound literature are only to be procured in exceptional cases, in compliance with fixed book prices. The contractor shall provide an online platform / administrative portal for professional specialist information management. Access to the online works used by the client in particular must be ensured via this platform. The absolute upper limit for call-offs within the scope of this framework agreement is 130.000 €. The estimated net contract value is 1.650.000,00 € (field 5.1.5) or 1.920.000,00 € gross. The absolute upper limit for call-offs within the scope of this framework agreement is gross 1.960.000,00 €.

The continuity of the technical management of the current environment is no longer guaranteed after the expiry of the existing management agreement, making timely go-live of the new Solution necessary for the continuity of the business-critical, primary processes of the NZa. The desired Solution consists of three coherent yet separate lots: a Case System, a Document Management System (DMS) with records management functionality, and an omnichannel solution for consolidating customer contact. With this, the NZa aims to support case-oriented working, file formation, archiving and customer contact via multiple channels in an unambiguous and structured manner, with a sustainably accessible and reliable information management system tailored to the processing of sensitive personal data. The core of this tender is the new case system, with which the NZa works case-orientated. See documents; When handling cases, the NZa processes many documents. This includes both documents sent by e-mail, for example, and physical documents arriving via the scanning facility. A DMS is required for keeping and managing information in a proper, orderly and accessible state.; The NZa has customer contact via multiple channels: e-mail, telephony, online forms and chat. In order to ensure that we can serve our customers optimally, it is important to consolidate information from these various channels. An omnichannel solution should provide a solution here.

sig_a9ca8221a2856ecefe15.description: The subject of the procurement is the development of a new electronic system for the Croatian Science Foundation for the submission of project proposals, evaluation and monitoring of funded projects. Hrvatska zaklada za znanost (HRZZ) as the Contracting Authority, is the central national organisation for the funding of scientific, higher education and technological programmes and projects in Croatia. Every year, HRZZ announces a series of calls for proposals to support scientific research, thereby ensuring stable funding for research groups engaged in internationally and/or nationally significant scientific issues that create new knowledge and improve existing knowledge through basic, applied or development research. In order to ensure the selection and funding of the best projects, HRZZ has developed a project proposal evaluation procedure based on the internationally accepted practice of peer review, in which scientists from Croatia and abroad participate. The procedure for applying to HRZZ calls for proposals, the evaluation and selection of project proposals, and the monitoring of the implementation of contracted projects takes place via the Electronic System for Project Submission and Monitoring (hereinafter: EPP system). In this regard, the existing EPP system was developed in 2011. and has been upgraded several times over the years. The total server space it currently occupies is ~720 GB. The total number of active registered users in the system is 21.875, while on an annual basis about 7.000 users in various roles and 30 HRZZ employees work with the system. However, following the above, it is necessary to build a new modular system that the Contracting Authority can independently adapt to the type of call for proposals, the type of evaluation procedure and the involved users. The system must allow the Contracting Authority to select from predefined elements those that will be used in a specific call period (e.g. criteria for checking applicant eligibility, cards or forms that the user fills out, mandatory fields, documentation for uploading, etc.). Following the above, a detailed description of the subject of procurement is contained in the Technical Specifications document, which forms Appendix I to this Procurement Documentation.
sig_a9ca8221a2856ecefe15.title: Development of a new electronic system for the Croatian Science Foundation for the submission of project proposals, management and monitoring of funded projects

sig_aa7ec166aa9f05539ff0.description: The Arts Data Bank is a gross financed department under the Ministry of Climate and Environment. Artsdatabanken is considering announcing a tender for an external review of the IT portfolio. We would like to discuss with the market whether the descriptions of the assignment seem recognisable in the market and how costly such an assignment is. The market dialogue will be held through a digital meeting Wednesday 14 May 0900-1000. The draft for the notice will be sent as registered at the latest on Monday 11 May. After the meeting, five 30 minute meetings have been set aside with individual tenderers. Registration for an individual meeting can take place at the same time as register for the market dialogue. Individual meetings will be awarded on a first come, first served principle. Registration shall be sent by sending an email to the postmottak@artsdatabanken.no. The Arts Data Bank has, via the Digitalisation Council, received a recommendation to carry out an external review of the IT portfolio. • What does it cost to manage and further develop the different systems? • Where can you have internal operational advantages by thinking about consolidation and reuse? We would like an as-ice mapping of the technical solutions, with a focus on cost picture in money and personal resources, and technology/architectural choices. Are there changes we can make to be better rigged for the future? The majority of the systems in the portfolio are developed by the Arts Data Bank. We envisage that the following deliveries from an external supplier can be useful: • Mapping the services in the cloud infrastructure. I.a. visual overview of our services, with connections and dependencies between them. • An assessment of technical choices for infrastructure and cloud systems. • An assessment of infrastructure costs and what we can possibly do to reduce costs • A calculation of the development costs? • An assessment of resource use for managing the portfolio we have • Plan for liquidation of services that have been decided to discontinue or have been assessed for liquidation. • Assess vulnerability connected to the choice of cloud suppliers connected to security problems. The Arts Data Bank invites potential suppliers to a dialogue on how the procurement can best be arranged. Central themes we would like dialogue around include — o If the notice is sufficiently detailed in order to submit a tender. o Whether the frame of the notice is realistic. o If the evaluation criteria facilitate fair competition.
sig_aa7ec166aa9f05539ff0.title: Market dialogue - Review IT portfolio

sig_aa9bf871720f9c6c88a4.description: The Assignment comprises the supply, implementation and support of a new Energy Management System (EnMS) for the Universiteit Leiden. A well-functioning Energy Registration and Monitoring System (EBS) forms an integral part of the EnMS solution. An EBS is legally required for the majority of buildings. The EnMS solution must therefore comply with the applicable guidelines as established by the Netherlands Enterprise Agency (RVO). With this tender, the Contracting Authority aims to have a scalable, future-proof and securely configured SaaS solution that unlocks reliable energy information and provides support for legal obligations, financial processes and sustainability objectives. The EnMS acts as the primary system for long-term storage, management and analysis of the Contracting Authority's energy data. The EnMS must integrate in a robust and traceable manner with existing systems and data sources of the Universiteit Leiden and be suitable for data exchange within the existing information provision. The Assignment consists of the following components: the supply, implementation and support of an EnMS as a SaaS solution, the supply of monitoring services focused on data quality and continuity, the supply of additional functionality modules and dashboards (optional). There is no purchase obligation for component 3. The Contracting Authority wishes to be able to purchase modules and dashboards optionally and separately from each other according to use during the term of the Agreement. Whether or not the full offering of component 3 is provided does not constitute grounds for exclusion. The extent to which the functionality of the requested modules and/or dashboards is offered will, however, be taken into account in the quality assessment of the tender.
sig_aa9bf871720f9c6c88a4.title: Energy Management System

sig_aac4251745c9d32957be.buyer_name: City of Helsinki, Urban Environment Division
sig_aac4251745c9d32957be.description: Please note: this is not a call for tenders, a contract notice or a prior information notice, but a notice of the initiation of a market dialogue as part of procurement planning. The City of Helsinki Urban Environment Division (hereinafter KYMP) has initiated the preparation of the 4/26 procurement and invites service providers to participate in a market dialogue. KYMP is surveying solutions available on the market based on Automatic License Plate Recognition (ALPR) for mobile parking enforcement. The subject of the procurement is an ALPR camera system, which consists of: • ALPR cameras to be installed in a vehicle and related peripheral equipment • a back-end system for the cameras (e.g. analytics, management and reporting user interfaces, interfaces) • possible cloud services and/or local system components The system must be capable of: • automatically reading vehicle registration numbers in urban traffic • identifying vehicles that are in violation of parking regulations (e.g. unpaid parking, incorrect parking, exceeding time limits) • producing information in real time or near real time to support parking enforcement The primary intended use of the system is to improve the efficiency of: • paid parking enforcement • incorrect parking enforcement Possible other uses may include: • supporting the enforcement of vehicle removal operations • producing situational and monitoring information related to parking and traffic flows • collecting guidance and analytics data concerning parking behaviour The purpose of the market dialogue is to survey the market situation regarding the procurement, the solution alternatives available on the market, and various implementation, licence and service models. Through the market dialogue, KYMP wishes to obtain insights from service providers to support the preparation of the future competitive tendering, including the definition of the subject of the procurement, potential procurement models and the key content of the contract. Written material will be sent to those registering for the market dialogue for comment. The written material will be sent to those who have registered for preliminary review during the spring of 2026. In addition, KYMP reserves the possibility to discuss the details of the tender competition to be organised with the service providers registering for the market dialogue. We request service providers interested in participating in the market dialogue to register by 31.5.2026 to the address kymp.icthankinnat@hel.fi. Please head your registration message as follows: "Markkinavuoropuhelu -ALPR-kamerajärjestelmä". At the same time, please provide the name and contact details of your contact person whom we can contact. The market dialogue and the information provided therein do not bind any participating party, nor is it a prerequisite for participating in the actual tender competition later. If the procurement is proceeded with, the official call for tenders will be published no earlier than during the year 2027. No compensation will be paid to the participating companies for responding or participating. Responses will be treated confidentially.
sig_aac4251745c9d32957be.title: Invitation to market dialogue: ALPR camera system

sig_aae16276a97f67affed1.description: Forest management services will be awarded in the year 2027 by concluding a contract for each lot. The cumulative area of the lots is 20.310,27 ha. The area of each lot is specified in the description of the lots. The services involve the development of the forest management plan, a product of the management activity with technical-organisational content, ecologically grounded, through which the works necessary to be executed in a production unit are established for a period of time, with the aim of bringing and, subsequently, maintaining the structural characteristics of the stands and the forest as a whole at the values corresponding to the optimal structural model defined in accordance with the ecological, social and economic objectives pursued through sustainable management. According to the provisions of Art. 63 para. (11) of Law no. 331/2024 on the Forestry Code, as subsequently amended and supplemented, it is necessary for the development of forest management plans to be carried out through public procurement procedures. The management of the state-owned public forest fund constitutes a priority obligation of the forest fund administrators. The method of managing the state-owned public forest fund is regulated by forest management plans. Forest management plans and their amendments are approved by order of the head of the Authority. In the case of state-owned public land, the management plans provide data and information necessary for their registration/updating in the centralised inventory of state public domain assets and for registration in the integrated cadastre and land register system. Number of days before which clarifications can be requested before the deadline for submission of tenders/applications 18 days. The contracting authority will clearly respond to requests for clarification on the 11-th day before the deadline set for the submission of tenders. NOTE: The contracting authority is not obliged to respond to requests for clarification/additional information that have not been addressed within the established deadline. Forest management services for the Lunca Timisului Forestry Office - DS Timis, with an area of 9.388,78 ha; Forest management services for the Timisoara Forestry Office - DS Timis, with an area of 10.921,49 ha

sig_aafec3bc82d1f24961f9.description: The subject of the procurement is an electronic resident appointment booking software service (hereinafter Software Service). The Software Service enables service users to book, cancel, reschedule and confirm appointments in accordance with national development, as well as to view booked appointments (including proxy services). The comprehensive services of the appointment booking system will be expanded Itä-Uudenmaan hyvinvointialue to primary health care, oral health care and social services. Itä-Uudenmaan hyvinvointialue electronic appointment booking has been in use in limited services, but now that the region has moved to using only one supplier's customer and patient information system entity (Tieto / Lifecare), the service is intended to be expanded. Appointment booking functionalities are intended to be introduced in primary health care, oral health care and social services. Electronic appointment booking is intended to free up professionals' time from the telephone, as well as to streamline the customer's service experience, as appointments can be booked regardless of time and place. The estimated value of the procurement, excluding VAT, calculated in accordance with the Public Procurement Act for the contract period, including the software service, implementation, expert services and options, is 600 000,00 euros (€). The contract period is fixed for two (2) years, after which it will continue until further notice.
sig_aafec3bc82d1f24961f9.title: Procurement of an electronic appointment booking system for social and health services

sig_ab526670871463f8a727.description: The DBT Digital, Data and Technology team leads on development of AI tools and services within the Department for Business and Trade. It does so through an ‘AI3’ model, which aims to identify, test, develop and evaluate use cases for applying artificial intelligence within the Department. This model consists of three parts: • AI Lab: Rapid, time limited exploration and assessment of AI use cases and experiments • AI Factory: Development and operationalisation of experiments into production ready tools and components • AI Operations: Maintenance, scaling, and operationalisation of AI solutions The Authority is seeking to procure specialist expertise to support delivery of this model. We require this to take the form of suitably-skilled teams and individuals provided by the Supplier joining relevant AI3 teams and project teams within the AI Lab, AI Factory or AI Operations. Supplier resources will work alongside and under the direction of Civil Servants within the DBT Digital, Data and Technology team within the Department. This may be for both short and long-term projects as agreed via statements of work, and requiring a variety of digital and data skills. For a more detailed description of this requirement, please refer to Appendix B of the ITP. Lot 1: AI Lab. AI Lab: Rapid, time limited exploration and assessment of AI use cases and experiments. The Department for Business and Trade (DBT) Digital, Data and Technology (DDaT) team is implementing the ‘AI3’ model to identify, test, develop, and evaluate use cases for artificial intelligence across departmental functions. This model comprises three development phases: • AI Lab: Rapid, time limited exploration and assessment of AI use cases and experiments. • AI Factory: Development and operationalisation of experiments into production ready tools and components • AI Operations: Maintenance, scaling, and operationalisation of AI solutions This lot is focused on the AI Lab phase, which is key to the success of the wider AI3 model. Objectives: The Supplier must provide specialist resources to: • Identify high value AI use cases through structured engagement with HMG stakeholders • Assess the feasibility and potential impact of these use cases • Rapidly prototype and test working experiments, with clear identification of success measures and experiment scope • Ensure ethical, secure, and compliant use of data throughout the process • Support decision making for onward investment and scaling Scope: The Supplier, through provision of its specialists to the Buyer, will be expected to deliver the following through agreed SOWs that will refine the specific deliverables: Use Case Identification: o Facilitate ideation workshops and horizon scanning activities o Engage with the Buyer’s (and potentially wider HMG’s) internal teams to uncover operational challenges and innovation opportunities o Reuse and adapt existing AI solutions from across government and industry Technical Feasibility Assessment o Apply data science and machine learning engineering expertise to evaluate proposed use cases o Recommend appropriate technical approaches and architectures o Collaborate with the Buyer’s teams to ensure alignment with existing infrastructure and standards Data Ethics and Governance o Ensure all AI use cases comply with ethical standards and data governance policies o Advise on responsible AI practices, including bias mitigation and transparency o Support GDPR compliance and data protection assessments Prototyping and Experimentation o Rapidly develop prototypes using standard design patterns for government services o Design and execute experiments to validate concepts o Document outcomes and provide recommendations for further development or discontinuation Collaboration and Integration o Work alongside civil servants and embedded teams o Contribute to lessons learned and continuous improvement exercises Please refer to the ITP (Appendix B) for more information on the required skills and roles needed for this lot. Lot 2: AI Factory. AI Factory: Development and operationalisation of experiments into production ready tools and components. The Department for Business and Trade (DBT) Digital, Data and Technology (DDaT) team is implementing the ‘AI3’ model to identify, test, develop, and evaluate use cases for artificial intelligence across departmental functions. This model comprises three development phases: • AI Lab: Rapid, time limited exploration and assessment of AI use cases and experiments • AI Factory: Development and operationalisation of proofs of concept into production ready tools and components • AI Operations: Maintenance, scaling, and operationalisation of AI solutions This lot is focused on the AI Factory phase, building on the AI Lab. Objectives/Scope: The Supplier must provide specialist resources to develop and operationalise AI into services, tools and components, building on successful experiments from the AI Lab: This will include: • Service and technical architecture design informed by data expertise to translate proofs of concept into robust, user-facing tools and services • Innovation in delivery and application of AI technology, going beyond standard tools and technologies to deliver measurable applications of AI. • Assessing, designing and optimising data science and ML engineering approaches to ensure that technical AI proofs of concept perform in a real-world environment • Partnering with other digital teams within the Buyer’s DDaT team to co-deliver new AI features and components within existing digital and data services • Product and delivery expertise informed by data to ensure rapid, tightly scoped delivery of services within a few months • User-centred design expertise to ensure that products and tools are able to meet user needs, and to identify opportunities for re-use or wider roll-out of products developed • Helping to build skills around operationalisation of AI among civil servants, including core technical and infrastructure skills • Evaluation and performance analysis expertise to identify meaningful metrics for assessing the performance of AI products being delivered and enabling continuous improvement This is not an exhaustive list, and specific deliverables will be defined, refined and agreed with the commission of each SOW. Please refer to the ITP (Appendix B) for more information on the required skills and roles needed for this lot. Lot 3: AI Operations. AI Operations: Maintenance, scaling, and operationalisation of AI Solutions. The Department for Business and Trade (DBT) Digital, Data and Technology (DDaT) team is implementing the ‘AI3’ model to identify, test, develop, and evaluate use cases for artificial intelligence across departmental functions. This model comprises three development phases: • AI Lab: Rapid, time limited exploration and assessment of AI use cases and experiments • AI Factory: Development and operationalisation of experiments into production ready tools and components • AI Operations: Maintenance, scaling, and operationalisation of AI solutions This lot is focused on the AI Operations phase, building on the AI Factory . Objectives The Supplier must provide specialist resources to maintain, scale and support the robust operation of AI tools and components, as well as the underlying data, AI and technical infrastructure used across AI teams. The Supplier will provide specialist resources to: • Scale AI solutions for department-wide use with reliability, security, and maintainability. • Ensure AI components and services are reliable, performant, and secure through strong data, infrastructure, and ML engineering practices. • Enable reuse of technical solutions across multiple use cases to simplify the overall technical landscape. • Recommend infrastructure approaches aligned with the Buyer’s technical guidance. • Ensure compliance with the Buyer’s engineering standards, governance frameworks, and internal assurance processes. • Monitor and manage performance, cost, and environmental impact of AI services, including LLM usage and infrastructure consumption. • Provide product and delivery management for live and mature services, including identifying user-driven improvements and managing enhancements. • Upskill DBT civil servants in operationalising AI, including core technical and infrastructure skills. • Provide guidance and set standards on how the Buyer’s DDaT teams can best deploy AI in their own services, • Continuously improve AI services and tools based on evidence-driven user insights. • Showcase AI Ops work to the wider DBT through demos and show-and-tells. Scope The supplier will be expected to deliver the following (which will be refined on a case-by-case basis as SOWs are agreed): Operationalisation and Scaling • Take AI Factory tools and components and operationalise them into robust, reusable, and scalable services on the Buyer’s infrastructure. • Maintain and enhance live AI services and tools, ensuring alignment with the Buyer’s standards as defined in agreed SOWs. Component Development and Management • Develop and iterate reusable AI components; maintain a shared component library on the Buyer’s infrastructure . • Partner with the Buyer’s digital teams to create components that integrate across multiple digital and data services, promoting efficiency and consistency. sig_ab668499e223ace79d4b.description: As a producer of the highest-quality food and drink, the vast majority of which is exported around the world, Ireland has developed robust and integrated systems governing its agriculture (including aquaculture) and food. In areas like food safety, traceability, animal health and welfare, productivity and breeding, sustainability and innovation, Ireland’s government-sponsored services are world-class. Sustainable Food Systems Ireland (SFSI) is a consortium of public bodies that are responsible for the agriculture (including aquaculture) and food sectors in Ireland. Covering diverse technical and skills domains, SFSI is charged with developing long-term relationships internationally based on the transfer of Irish knowledge, expertise and technologies, in support of the development of safe, secure and sustainable value chains in agri-food. The SFSI consortium members are: Department of Agriculture, Food and the Marine Teagasc - The Agriculture and Food Development Authority Food Safety Authority of Ireland Bord Bia - The Irish Food Board Enterprise Ireland SFSI consortium members can co-operate internationally using a variety of inputs: • expertise in project and programme design • government-to-government advice • delivery of technical assistance • organisation of training and study tours • project and programme monitoring, reviews and evaluation • impact evaluation • creation of financing models for industry support. SFSI consortium membership provides expertise to support partner governments and organizations globally in the following areas: • formulating agricultural (including aquaculture), food and marine sectoral policy, strategies and programmes • building regulatory systems and institutional capability • strengthening food safety at all stages of the supply chain • protecting standards of animal health and welfare and expertise in veterinary services • systems for animal identification, registration and movement control • traceability in the food chain • establishing and improving research and innovation in agriculture (including aquaculture) and food • knowledge transfer, agricultural education and extension services and systems • establishment of producer groups and co-operatives • developing and embedding sustainability programmes at primary and processor levels • SME development and company funding support systems • export promotion in food or commodity sectors • creation and marketing of national or regional brands The Executive Team of SFSI undertakes business development, project preparation and delivery, project management and administration and coordination activities on behalf of the Consortium Members and is the point of contact for overseas clients - governments, agencies and other organisations. The Team can negotiate participation in international food, agriculture (including aquaculture) and rural development projects through direct business development activities and through engaging in open and restricted tenders on behalf of the Consortium members. The SFSI Executive team is a Unit of the Department of Agriculture, Food and the Marine and oversees the administration of this DPS including External Expert appointments on behalf of the Consortium Members. The consortium members will use existing/internal staff resources to provide services. However, they require external experts to supplement the existing resources where necessary. sig_ab7ff793e66f36db5343.description: The objective of the Cybersecurity Innovation for Cyberinfrastructure (CICI) program is to advance scientific discovery and innovation by enhancing the security and privacy of cyberinfrastructure. CICI supports efforts to develop, deploy and integrate cybersecurity that will benefit the broader scientific community by securing science data, computation, collaborations workflows, and infrastructure. CICI recognizes the unique nature of modern, complex, data-driven, distributed, rapid, and collaborative science and the breadth of infrastructure and requirements across scientific disciplines, practitioners, researchers, and projects. CICI seeks proposals in four program areas: 1. Usable and Collaborative Security for Science (UCSS): Projects in this program area should support novel and/or applied security and usability research that facilitates scientific collaboration, encourages the adoption of security into the scientific workflow, and helps create a holistic, integrated security environment that spans the entire scientific cyberinfrastructure ecosystem. 2. Reference Scientific Security Datasets (RSSD): Projects in this program area should leverage instrumented cyberinfrastructure to capture metadata from scientific workflows and workloads as reference data artifacts that can help support reproducible security research, testing and evaluation. 3. Transition to Cyberinfrastructure Resilience (TCR): Projects in this program area should improve the robustness, trustworthiness, integrity, and/or resilience of scientific cyberinfrastructure through testing, evaluation, hardening, validation, and technology transition of novel cybersecurity research. The TCR area further encourages transition activities that advance the deployment and use of reproducibility in CI, workflows, and data. 4. Integrity, Provenance, and Authenticity for Artificial Intelligence Ready Data (IPAAI): Projects in this program area should enhance confidence and reproducibility in AI produced scientific results by improving the integrity, provenance, and authenticity of scientific datasets used by Artificial Intelligence systems.
sig_ab7ff793e66f36db5343.title: Cybersecurity Innovation for Cyberinfrastructure

sig_ac0e10b74e0ba72d034f.description: This notice is a request for information and an invitation to market dialogue, not a procurement notice or a call for tenders. Suppliers are not expected to submit tenders in response to this notice. Provincia Oy is a service centre owned by municipalities and wellbeing services counties, which produces high-quality and cost-effective HR and financial management services for its owner-customers. Together with our system partners, we offer our customers the most modern and efficient financial and HR management system solutions on the market. We are preparing the procurement of a modern comprehensive financial planning system produced as a SaaS service, with which our customers can handle, in addition to versatile budgeting and forecasting operations, also e.g. the planning of their projects and investment ventures. We are not looking for a mere data entry form, but a system that integrates into our operating environment, streamlines our customers' entire financial planning process and minimises manual work as much as possible. In addition, our hope is to be able to utilise artificial intelligence to support financial planning. With this notice, we invite suppliers to participate in market dialogue, the purpose of which is to clarify the details related to the subject of procurement and the requirements. In this way, we are able to carry out the procurement in the most appropriate manner possible. DESCRIPTION OF THE PROCUREMENT The financial planning system to be procured must support the entire budget and financial planning process all the way from basic data definition to budget drawing up, changes, forecasting and monitoring. The planning process proceeds in stages and continues throughout the budget period. The system must enable the management of the budget and operating plan, supplementary budgets and budget changes, as well as the drawing up of forecasts and alternative scenarios in such a way that the integrity of the official budget is maintained. Planning must enable monthly budgeting that can be updated flexibly and regularly during the budget year based on outturn and forecasting. In addition, budgeting must be possible on a rolling basis. Budget data must be comparable with outturn and the system must also support data transfer and validation in accordance with existing accounting structures. As a whole, the objective of the system is to enable continuous, controlled and comparable financial planning throughout the budget period, while taking into account the individual roles and needs of our customer organisations of various sizes. In addition to the system itself, the procurement will include implementation projects, system maintenance services, integration development and testing work, and support services intended for the service centre's technical superusers, such as incident and change management services and necessary training. A more detailed description of the requirements related to the system can be found in the request for information's appendix 1 "Preliminary requirements". These requirements are intended as an opening for discussion and they will evolve during the dialogue. The contracting authority reserves the right to use or not to use the requirements, pricing models, procedures, contract terms, schedules or other similar details related to the procurement raised during the request for information and market dialogue. SCHEDULE AND PROGRESS OF THE PROCUREMENT The plan for progress and scheduling is presented in appendix 2 "Estimated procurement schedule". The market dialogue will be held during May-June in such a way that written material will be circulated for comment to all suppliers who have registered to participate, and in addition the contracting authority may, at its own discretion, invite suppliers to hold separate general-level demo sessions via Teams. The publication of the actual procurement notice and call for tenders will settle for August according to the estimated schedule. According to current information, the procedure to be used will be an open procedure. REGISTRATION FOR THE MARKET DIALOGUE Please declare your interest in participating in the dialogue by 18.05.2026 at 15:00 at the latest with a free-form email to the address hankinnat@provincia.fi and attach to your email the document "Questions to suppliers" which is appendix 3 of this request for information, filled in. You may also, if you wish, attach a general presentation of your company and your product to the email. Title your message "Market dialogue: financial planning system". APPENDICES Appendix 1 – Preliminary requirements Appendix 2 – Estimated procurement schedule Appendix 3 – Questions to suppliers
sig_ac0e10b74e0ba72d034f.title: REQUEST FOR INFORMATION: Financial planning system as a SaaS service

A detailed specification of the subject of performance for this part of the public contract is provided in the Tender Documentation and its annexes.; The subject of performance is the creation of a basic AI platform representing a common technological layer for the provision of artificial intelligence services within an integrated digital ecosystem intended to ensure the fundamental digital transformation of the company BRIDGE PUBLISHING HOUSE INTERNATIONAL a.s. A detailed specification of the subject of performance for this part of the public contract is provided in the Tender Documentation and its annexes.; The subject of performance is the supply and implementation of basic components of an integrated digital ecosystem intended to ensure the digital transformation of the company BRIDGE PUBLISHING HOUSE INTERNATIONAL a.s. The main supplied components are the Digital Content Management Platform and the New Advanced Web, which form a central connected system for the creation, management, distribution and personalisation of digital educational content and the automation of business and administrative processes. sig_ac713fa09508499cc094.description: NHS Supply Chain is preparing a national framework agreement that will support the procurement of dental consumables, clinical solutions, equipment, digital technologies, diagnostics, and practice infrastructure, structured across the following indicative lots: The following lot structure is indicative and subject to final confirmation: Lot 1: Dental Consumables & Appliances Lot 2: Specialist Clinical & Bespoke Solutions Lot 3: Operatory Equipment Lot 4: Dental Laboratory & Digital Solutions Lot 5: Dental Imaging & Diagnostics Lot 6: Dental Environment, Decontamination & Practice Building Lot 7: Mobile Dental Clinics & Equipment Note: For future tenders the following requirements will apply: • ISO Certification: Tenderers must have ISO 9001: 2015 or BS EN ISO 13485:2016 certification or Medical Device Single Audit Program (MDSAP) certification accredited by the United Kingdom Accreditation Service (UKAS) (or international equivalent) to cover all segments of the Tenderer’s and the product’s supply chain. This should include, but not be limited to, sales, manufacturing, storage and distribution ('ISO Certification'). Link for acceptable alternatives https://iaf.nu/en/accreditation-bodies/ (‘Notified Bodies’). • CE Certification and Declaration of Conformity certificates are required where applicable to be presented at submission stage of the tender. • Modern Slavery for Tenderers that have an annual turnover of at least £36 million must have a link to their modern slavery statement on their website • Modern Slavery Assessment Tool (MSAT) Tenderers must have a score of 41% or above within 12 months of the Tender Publication Date via https://supplierregistration.cabinetoffice.gov.uk/ • Evergreen Sustainable Supplier Assessment – Tenderers will need to have completed the assessment and achieved Level 1 within the 12 months prior to the Tender Close Date. Link for instructions and access for this assessment: https://www.england.nhs.uk/nhs-commercial/central-commercial-function-ccf/evergreen/ • Carbon Reduction Plan (CRP): Tenderers must have a valid CRP link on their website that meets the requirements of PPN 006 as outlined in the PPN, OR Where Supplier has no website, the CRP is provided in PDF format that meets the requirements of PPN 006 as outlined in the PPN, OR Excused in exceptional circumstances. • Cyber Security: If you handle patient or personal data, or provide any IT systems, services, or devices you will need to have a Cyber Security Essentials Plus Certificate. Lot 1: Dental Consumables & Appliances. This Lot provides dental consumables and appliance-based solutions designed to support the delivery of routine and specialist dental care across primary, community, and secondary care settings. These products include single use and repeat use materials, small appliances, and consumable items required for preventive dentistry, restorative procedures, orthodontics, minor oral surgery, anaesthesia, and infection control. The scope includes consumables and all associated accessories, where applicable, required to support safe, effective, and compliant dental treatment. Lot 2: Specialist Clinical & Bespoke Solutions. This Lot covers specialist clinical systems, implantology and orthodontic products, as well as bespoke dental laboratory appliances and restorations manufactured to individual patient requirements. It covers powered systems, procedure kits and software enabled treatment solutions that support diagnosis, planning and delivery of specialist dental care. The scope includes devices and all associated equipment, accessories, consumables (where part of a system), maintenance, software, technical support and training. Additionally, it covers the provision of patient specific and bespoke restorations. Lot 3: Operatory Equipment. This Lot provides dental operatory equipment used for routine chairside patient care within dental treatment environments. It includes dental treatment units, delivery systems, operating lights, handpieces, micromotors, ultrasonic scaling systems, mobile treatment carts and associated operatory infrastructure, including suction systems and compressors. This Lot excludes specialist clinical systems used within defined endodontic, implantology, orthodontic and oral surgery workflows, which fall within the scope of Lot 2 – Specialist Clinical & Bespoke Solutions. Lot 4: Dental Laboratory & Digital Solutions. This Lot provides digital dentistry and laboratory solutions spanning the design, manufacture and finishing of dental restorations and appliances, and supports associated digital workflows. It includes CAD/CAM systems, scanners, milling units, 3D printers, sintering furnaces, laboratory equipment and materials. The scope includes equipment and all associated accessories, installation, maintenance, software, technical support, training and, where applicable, validated workflows. Lot 5: Dental Imaging & Diagnostics. This Lot includes both ionising imaging systems (e.g. X-ray, CBCT) and non-ionising diagnostic imaging devices (e.g. intraoral cameras and scanners). It includes intraoral x-ray units, OPG/cephalometric systems, CBCT, digital sensors/PSP systems, intraoral cameras and diagnostic imaging software. The scope includes devices and all associated equipment, accessories, installation, acceptance testing, maintenance, software, technical support, integration and training. Lot 6: Dental Environment, Decontamination & Practice Building. This Lot provides environmental, furniture and fit-out solutions for dental surgeries and decontamination areas. It includes clinical cabinetry and furniture, ergonomic surgery design/refurbishment, decontamination room furniture and workflow systems, and supporting clinical infrastructure components associated with dental environments. The scope includes supply, installation, and, where applicable, design support, project services, maintenance and training. Lot 7: Mobile Dental Clinics & Equipment. This Lot provides mobile dental treatment environments and portable operatory solutions designed to deliver care outside fixed clinical premises. It includes mobile dental vans, trailers and self-contained pods, as well as portable dental chairs/units and field dentistry kits. The scope includes units and associated equipment, installation/commissioning (where applicable), accessories, maintenance, technical support, training and documentation.

sig_ad76b7cd02957cd82289.description: This Sources Sought announcement is being amended to include the RFI document (2 pages) that was inadvertently left out of the previous posting. I. DISCLAIMER a. The Government is conducting market research to identify qualified firms capable of performing an independent code review and software development pipeline modernization for the ShakeAlert Earthquake Early Warning (EEW) Production System. This Request for Information (RFI) announcement seeks capability statements from interested vendors. b. The Government will not pay any costs incurred in the preparation of information for responding to this market survey or the Government¿s use of the information. Any information submitted by respondents to this RFI is strictly voluntary. All submissions become Government property and will not be returned. This request for information does not commit the Government to contract for any supply or service whatsoever. The Government will not provide feedback. c. The US Geological Survey Acquisition Team (GSAT) is not, at the time, seeking proposals or quotes and will not accept unsolicited proposals or quotes. Not responding to this RFI does not preclude participation in any future procurements. II. PURPOSE The DOI, USGS, Earthquake Science Center (ESC) is seeking a qualified firm to conduct a focused, independent code review of the ShakeAlert® Earthquake Early Warning (EEW) Production System. The purpose of this RFI is to identify potential vendors capable of providing services required in the attached Statement of Work. The objective of this contract is to improve the reliability, maintainability, and long-term sustainability of the ShakeAlert production code base through two complementary activities: - A rigorous, module-by-module review of source code quality, correctness, and maintainability. - An assessment of current software development and deployment practices, with concrete recommendations for modernizing the CI/CD pipeline and GitLab workflow. In support of this effort, GSAT is conducting market research to further refine requirements and establish the best acquisition approach. Please note that requirements defined to date may change before issuance of a final RFP/RFQ. III. REQUIREMENTS See Statement of Work, 9 pages, attached. Task 1 - Production Code Review Task 2 - Software Development Practices and CI/CD Pipeline Interested parties shall include the following in their submission: 1. Applicable socioeconomic designation. 2. Business size standard. 3. SAM UEI number. 4. GSA contract number, if applicable. 5. Ability to execute all tasks listed. IV. RESPONSES Responses are requested by October 16, 2026 at 12:00pm PST. Any response received after these dates will also be considered but may not be included in initial reporting or assessments. All responses should be submitted electronically in PDF format and emailed to the points of contact: Charlan Fejarang at charlan_fejarang@ios.doi.gov. The subject line of the email should read as follows, ¿RFI: 140G0326Q0223 - ShakeAlert Production System Code Review.¿ Respondents must submit capability statements and information describing the general approach/solution to addressing the listed requirements. General marketing information or reference to vendor web sites will not be considered responsive to this notice. No telephone, mail, or fax responses will be accepted.
sig_ad76b7cd02957cd82289.title: B--SHAKEALERT PRODUCTION CODE REVIEW

sig_ad84125647c30adc8294.description: Sources Sought Notice Information Introduction This is a Small Business Sources Sought notice. This is NOT a solicitation for proposals, proposal abstracts, or quotations. The purpose of this notice is to obtain information regarding: the availability and capability of qualified small business sources; whether they are small businesses; HUBZone small businesses; service-disabled, veteran-owned small businesses; 8(a) small businesses; veteran-owned small businesses; woman-owned small businesses; or small disadvantaged businesses; and their size classification relative to the North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) code for the proposed acquisition. Your responses to the information requested will assist the Government in determining the appropriate acquisition method, including whether a set-aside is possible. An organization that is not considered a small business under the applicable NAICS code should not submit a response to this notice. Background Research supported and conducted by the National Institute of Allergy and Infectious Diseases (NIAID), National Institutes of Health (NIH), Department of Health and Human Services (HHS), strives to understand, treat and ultimately prevent the myriad infectious, immunologic, and allergic diseases that threaten millions of human lives. This mission is driven by two strategic aims: addressing major infectious diseases, including emerging and chronic infections, and tackling immunologic and allergic disorders. The NIAID Division of Microbiology and Infectious Diseases (DMID) supports extramural research to control and prevent diseases caused by virtually all infectious agents. This includes basic and applied research to develop and evaluate therapeutics, vaccines, medical devices, and diagnostics, which are funded through a variety of research grants and contracts. Through multiple grant- and contract-funded research programs, NIAID supports a broad range of clinical research, including single-center and multi-center Phase 0-4 clinical trials of therapeutics, including both novel agents and repurposed therapies; vaccines, new vaccine formulations, schedules, and modes of delivery; natural history and cohort studies for pathogens of interest; and evaluation of novel diagnostics for selected infectious diseases. These clinical research activities are focused on the improved diagnosis, treatment, and prevention of emerging, infectious, and chronic diseases for public health priorities that address the needs of the United States (U.S.) population. Purpose and Objectives The U.S. Government has a requirement for the establishment and management of a Statistical and Data Coordinating Center (SDCC) to support DMID’s extramural clinical research programs. Project Requirements The project requirements of the SDCC include: 21 CFR Part 11-compliant clinical data management systems for the collection, storage, management, reporting and quality control of study data; preparation of study-related materials; clinical study websites; statistical design and analysis expertise; data management user training; support of study operations, clinical site capability assessment for data management; electronic specimen tracking system; data storage facility; and project/site management. Anticipated Period of Performance The Government anticipates making one (1) contract award. It is anticipated that the duration of the contract will be a maximum of seven (7) years. Other important considerations: Where permissible and appropriate, incorporation of Artificial Intelligence (AI) across the functions of the SDCC are anticipated to be permitted, while enforcing safeguards for participant privacy and regulatory compliances, in alignment with NIH policies and guidances, including Office of Science Policy’s (OSP) Artificial Intelligence in Research: Policy Considerations and Guidance. Final decisions affecting clinical data shall remain subject to documented human review and quality control. Respondents lacking the expertise to address all the technical requirements are encouraged to identify collaborations and partnerships that, through combined expertise, can address all these technical requirements. Capability Statement/Information Sought Interested Sources are expected to have the expertise, personnel, and facilities to meet the requirements of the project. Tailored Capability Statements submitted as a result of this notice shall demonstrate and document the offerors’ qualifications and experience, specifically providing evidence as to its capability to perform this requirement, with particular attention to the following technical areas: Ability to operate and maintain a state-of-the-art 21 CFR Part 11-compliant clinical data system for the collection, management, storage, and reporting of clinical and non-clinical data. Ability to ensure the accuracy, completeness, and timeliness of all data entered into the clinical data management system. Ability to provide clinical trial statistical design and analysis functions for Phase 0-4 clinical trials evaluating therapeutics, vaccines and devices for a wide variety of chronic and infectious diseases. Ability to conduct the preparation, writing, and distribution of the protocol and other study-related materials. Ability to communicate and collaborate with NIAID, grant recipients and contractors, and other study collaborators to facilitate clinical research activities. Ability to facilitate study operations and regulatory requirements through reporting and analytics, and facilitate NIAID’s requirements for oversight and performance monitoring of clinical sites and clinical research activities. Ability to provide training of clinical site personnel and other collaborators on all aspects of clinical data management. Ability to operate and maintain a specimen tracking system. Ability to operate and maintain a secure data storage system. Ability to distribute study data and metadata to NIH- and NIAID-designated repositories and other collaborators. Technical Plan/Approach: appropriateness and adequacy of the plans for conducting all the activities described above. Personnel/Management: adequacy, appropriateness and relevance of expertise, experience, qualifications, and availability of the key professional and technical staff with a project of similar size, scope, and complexity. It is estimated that 60 Full-Time Equivalents (FTEs) will be required for each year of the proposed contract. For the purposes of this notice, a Full-Time Equivalent is one (1) person- whether contractor employee, subcontractor employee, or consultant-who works 2,080 hours per year. It is anticipated that the Government may exercise Options for increased level of effort that may result from unanticipated increases in demand, with the services required under the Options to be of the same scope provided during the Base year. Should the Government elect to exercise any of the Options, the Options may be exercised within the Base period (and within each year of the proposed contract), up to a maximum of additional 90 FTEs. Facilities/Resources/IT Security: adequacy and appropriateness of the facilities and resources dedicated to the project. AI oversight: appropriateness and adequacy of the plans to ensure AI-enabled tools and systems are subject to documented human review and quality control. Past Performance: Past performance is considered essential. In addition to demonstrating that an offeror has met the above qualifications, interested parties must identify at least three (3) other projects of similar size and complexity. Page Limitations: Interested qualified small business organizations should submit a tailored Capability Statement not to exceed 5 pages, excluding resumes. Capability Statements must not include links to internet web site addresses (URLs) or otherwise direct readers to alternate sources of information. Font size must be 10 to 12 points. Spacing must be no more than 15 characters per inch. Within a vertical inch, there must be no more than six lines of text. Print margins must be at least one inch on each edge of the paper. Print setup should be single sided on standard letter size paper (8.5” x 11” in the U.S., A4 in outside the U.S.). All proprietary information should be marked as such. Required Business Information: UEI. Company Name. Company Address. Company Point of Contact, Phone and Email address Current GSA Schedules and/or Government-wide Acquisition Contracts (GWACs) appropriate to this Sources Sought. Do you have a government-approved accounting system? If so, please identify the agency that approved the system. Type of Company (i.e., small business, 8(a), woman owned, veteran owned, etc.) as validated via the System for Award Management (SAM) located at https://www.sam.gov/index.html. This indication should be clearly marked on the first page of your Capability Statement (preferably placed under the eligible small business concern’s name and address). Number of Copies: Please submit one (1) electric copy of your response as follows: All Capability Statements sent in response to this Small Business Sources Sought notice must be submitted electronically (via e-mail) to Cindy Hargett, Contracting Officer, at cindy.hargett@nih.gov in Microsoft Word or Adobe Portable Document Format (PDF). The e-mail subject line must specify reference number 75N98026R00169. Common Cut-off Date Electronically submitted tailored capability statements are due no later than 3:00 PM (Eastern Time) on September 30, 2026. CAPABILITY STATEMENTS RECEIVED AFTER THIS DATE AND TIME WILL NOT BE CONSIDERED. Disclaimer and Important Notes This notice does not obligate the Government to award a contract or otherwise pay for the information provided in response. The Government reserves the right to use information provided by respondents for any purpose deemed necessary and legally appropriate. Any organization responding to this notice should ensure that its response is complete and sufficiently detailed to allow the Government to determine the organization’s qualifications to perform the work. Respondents are advised that the Government is under no obligation to acknowledge receipt of the information received or provide feedback to respondents with respect to any information submitted. After a review of the responses received, a pre-solicitation synopsis and solicitation may be published in Federal Business Opportunities. However, responses to this notice will not be considered adequate responses for a solicitation. Confidentiality No proprietary, classified, confidential, or sensitive information should be included in your response. The Government reserves the right to use any non-proprietary technical information in any resultant solicitation(s).

sig_add465c5a2eb03875c78.description: OneCRM NL is TenneT’s consolidated Microsoft Dynamics 365 platform for relationship and stake holder management in the Netherlands. The solution serves as a shared platform for storing, maintaining and managing customer and stake holder information. It supports business unit- specific processes through configuration and role based access enabling both standardization and flexibility. OneCRM NL enables a centralized and con sistent view of stakeholders, interactions and related data, while allowing tailored usage aligned with the needs of individual departments. The platform is operated as part of the Microsoft Power Platform and follows standardized govern ance, data models and Application Lifecycle Management (ALM) practices. This ensures data qual ity, scalability and controlled extensibility across all participating business units.

sig_adf3ec62fa9c411ec75b.description: The Contractor shall provide Think Trends Software as an Agentic AI and Document Intelligence solution capable of processing structured, semi-structured, and unstructured adverse event documents, including scanned PDFs, handwritten or machine-generated forms, narratives, attachments, medical records, product complaints, lab reports, follow-up submissions, and case correspondence. The solution shall support end-to-end adverse event document processing through the following capabilities: A. Agentic Document Intake and Classification Think Trends Software AI agents shall automatically receive, classify, and route adverse event documents by submission type, FDA Center, product category, source, urgency, and case-processing requirements. The intake agent shall identify whether a document relates to drugs, biologics, devices, veterinary products, tobacco products, combination products, or other FDA-regulated products. Key capabilities include: • Automated ingestion of scanned PDFs, forms, emails, images, attachments, and electronic documents. • Classification of documents by Center-specific workflow, product type, and reporting pathway. • Detection of new cases, follow-up cases, duplicate submissions, incomplete submissions, and supporting attachments. • Intelligent routing to appropriate review queues, case-processing teams, or downstream systems. B. Agentic OCR and Intelligent Data Extraction Think Trends Software Agentic OCR shall combine optical character recognition, computer vision, natural language processing, large language models, and rule-based validation agents to extract key adverse event data elements from complex documents. The platform shall extract and structure critical case information, including: • Reporter, patient, animal, subject, or consumer information. • Product information, including drug, biologic, device, tobacco, or veterinary product details. • Adverse event terms, symptoms, outcomes, seriousness, and event narratives. • Dates, timelines, exposure details, dose, route, duration, lot numbers, manufacturer information, and product identifiers. • Medical history, concomitant products, lab results, device problem codes, clinical narratives, and follow-up information. • Center-specific data elements required for CVM-Drugs and CVM-Food, CDRH, CTP, CDER, CBER and HFP. C. Center-Specific Adverse Event Processing Agents The Contractor shall configure specialized AI agents within Think Trends Software to support unique regulatory and operational needs across FDA Centers. Each agent shall apply Center-specific data models, validation logic, terminology, business rules, and review workflows. Examples include: • CVM Agent: Processes veterinary adverse event reports, animal species, breed, weight, product exposure, dosage, outcome, and veterinarian/reporter information. • CDRH Agent: Processes device-related adverse events, device identifiers, manufacturer information, malfunction details, patient impact, and device problem descriptions. • CTP Agent: Processes tobacco product adverse experiences, product use patterns, health effects, consumer narratives, and product category information. • HFP Agent: Processes HFP-specific adverse event reporting requirements and associated workflows. • CDER Agent: Process drug product adverse experiences, product use patterns, health effects, consumer narratives, and product category information. • CBER Agent: Processes biologics product adverse experiences, product use patterns, health effects, consumer narratives, and product category information. D. Case Validation, Quality Control, and Human-in-the-Loop Review Think Trends Software shall incorporate validation agents to compare extracted data against business rules, required fields, confidence thresholds, terminology standards, and case-processing logic. Records that meet defined thresholds may proceed automatically, while exceptions shall be routed for human review. Key quality-control features include: • Confidence scoring at field, document, and case levels. • Source traceability to page, section, table, and line references. • Automated flagging of missing, inconsistent, conflicting, or low-confidence data. • Human-in-the-loop review screens for case processors and safety reviewers. • Reviewer acceptance, correction, override, and approval workflows. • Full audit trail of AI extraction, human edits, and final approved values. E. Data Standardization and Regulatory Output Generation Think Trends Software shall transform extracted adverse event information into structured formats required for case management, analytics, and downstream regulatory processing. The platform shall support configurable mappings to FDA data standards, Center-specific systems, XML structures, APIs, and reporting formats. Capabilities include: • Normalization of adverse event terms, product names, dates, identifiers, and narrative fields. • Mapping to Center-specific safety data models and controlled terminology. • Generation of structured case records for downstream review and processing. • API-based integration with FDA systems, case-processing platforms, data lakes, document repositories, and workflow tools. • Export to XML, JSON, CSV, database tables, or other required formats. F. Agentic Workflow Automation and Triage Think Trends Software shall automate repetitive case-processing steps while maintaining reviewer control for regulatory decisions. The system shall support configurable AI agents capable of executing multi-step workflows, requesting missing information, summarizing case narratives, identifying seriousness indicators, detecting duplicates, and prioritizing work queues. Workflow automation shall include: • Case prioritization based on seriousness, product risk, event severity, due dates, and Center-defined rules. • Automated summarization of long adverse event narratives and supporting attachments. • Duplicate and follow-up detection across submissions. • Exception handling and escalation workflows. • Generation of reviewer-ready case summaries. • Dashboard visibility into case volumes, processing status, aging, backlog, error rates, and productivity metrics. G. AI-Enabled Redaction for FOIA Compliance ThinkTrends will provide AI-powered redaction capabilities to support FDA's obligations under the Freedom of Information Act (FOIA). The platform will automatically identify and redact personally identifiable information (PII), protected health information (PHI), commercially confidential data, law-enforcement-sensitive content, and other exemption-covered materials from adverse event documents prior to public release or response to FOIA requests. Key capabilities include: • Automated detection and redaction of PII and PHI, including patient names, addresses, dates of birth, medical record numbers, Social Security numbers, and other personal identifiers. • Identification and suppression of trade secrets, proprietary formulations, manufacturing processes, and commercially confidential submitter information protected under FOIA Exemption. • Detection of law-enforcement-sensitive and inter-agency deliberative content subject to FOIA Exemptions. • Configurable exemption profiles aligned to FDA FOIA policy, Center-specific guidance, and applicable federal regulations. • Confidence-scored redaction recommendations with source traceability, enabling FOIA reviewers to accept, modify, or override AI-proposed redactions. • Human-in-the-loop review workflow allowing FOIA analysts to validate, annotate, and finalize redacted documents before release. • Generation of redacted PDF and document versions with visible redaction markers, exemption codes, and reviewer audit annotations. • Full audit trail recording every AI-proposed redaction, reviewer decision, exemption code applied, and final release determination. • Support for bulk redaction processing across large FOIA request batches, including multi-document packages and rolling requests. • Integration with FDA FOIA tracking systems, document repositories, and case management workflows. 1.3 SALIENT FEATURES OF THINK TRENDS SOFTWARE Think Trends Software provides the following differentiating capabilities relevant to FDA adverse event reporting modernization: 1. Agentic OCR Beyond Traditional OCR: Think Trends Software does not merely convert images to text. It applies AI agents that read, interpret, validate, cross-check, and structure regulatory information from complex adverse event documents. 2. Center-Agnostic Core with Center-Specific Configuration: The platform provides a common document intelligence foundation while allowing FDA Centers such as CVM, CDRH, CTP, and HFP to configure unique workflows, data models, rules, and outputs. 3. End-to-End Adverse Event Case Automation: Think Trends Software supports intake, classification, extraction, validation, triage, routing, human review, data transformation, and downstream submission/output generation. 4. Human-in-the-Loop Regulatory Control: The system keeps FDA reviewers in control by allowing them to review, correct, approve, or override AI-generated outputs before final case acceptance. 5. Explainability and Source Traceability: Each extracted field can be traced back to the original source document, page, section, and text reference, supporting transparency, auditability, and reviewer confidence. 6. Confidence-Based Processing: Think Trends Software assigns confidence scores to extracted data and automatically routes low-confidence or inconsistent records for human review. 7. Multi-Document and Multi-Format Processing: Think Trends Software shall process scanned PDFs, structured forms, unstructured narratives, tables, handwritten content where feasible, images, attachments, correspondence, and supporting records. 8. Duplicate and Follow-Up Detection: AI agents shall compare incoming submissions against existing records to identify potential duplicates, follow-ups, related cases, and case-history updates. 9. Reviewer-Ready Case Summaries: Think Trends Software shall generate concise adverse event summaries, chronology, product-event relationships, missing-field lists, and review-ready case packages. 10. Secure FDA-Aligned Deployment: Think Trends Software shall be deployable in secure government cloud, FDA-managed, or approved hosting environments with role-based access, audit logs, encryption, and integration with enterprise identity management. 1.4 TECHNICAL REQUIREMENTS Implementation of Think Trends Software for adverse event document processing is expected to deliver the following outcomes: • Reduction in manual data entry and repetitive case-processing tasks. • Faster adverse event intake, triage, and reviewer preparation. • Improved data quality through AI-assisted validation and standardization. • Greater consistency across FDA Centers while preserving Center-specific workflows. • Enhanced traceability, auditability, and regulatory transparency. • Improved ability to manage high-volume document backlogs and surge workloads. • Increased reviewer productivity through AI-generated summaries and exception-based review. • Scalable platform foundation for future FDA adverse event modernization initiatives. Please view the attached Request for Quote (RFQ) RFQ FDA-SOL-75F40126Q00384 document for additional information.
