sig_ae09df885b46a839920c.description: BACKGROUND AND PURPOSE OF THE INFORMATION REQUEST Helsingin kaupunki, kaupunkiympäristön toimiala (hereinafter referred to as "KYMP") is preparing a procurement procedure regarding the "Procurement of an application for infrastructure construction supervision and situational awareness". Before initiating the actual procurement procedure, KYMP is surveying the market supply, willingness and interest to tender for the procurement in question, and is seeking answers to questions related to the planned procurement. The information request is not a contract notice or a call for tenders, but a market dialogue. The publication of the information request does not initiate a procurement procedure. The contract notice and call for tenders will be published later. The information request does not oblige the contracting authority to carry out the actual procurement. Answering the information request is not a prerequisite for participating in any later procurement procedure that may be organised. Market operators will not be paid compensation for answering the information request or participating in the market dialogue. Information obtained through the information request may be used in the preparation of procurement documents. BACKGROUND AND OBJECT OF THE PROCUREMENT The Urban Environment Division (KYMP) is implementing the procurement of an application for infrastructure construction supervision and situational awareness. The City of Helsinki has not previously used a system intended for infrastructure construction contract management. In the current situation, information related to an individual contract is scattered across the systems of the Client and contractors, a large part of communication takes place solely via email, operating models in different contracts and among contractors vary, and up-to-date information is not easily accessible to all parties to the contract or in cover situations. In the current situation, contract management processes such as reporting, site diaries and defect repairs lack modern tools that can be smoothly utilised in fieldwork; instead, a large part of the entries are first made on paper and recorded digitally afterwards. Tools intended for the management of infrastructure site contracts have been piloted and test-used in the sector, and it has been observed that the use of a contract management system can speed up and streamline, among other things, the preparation of inspection reports and the sharing of reports between the parties. The key objective of the procurement is the procurement and implementation of a system suitable for monitoring infrastructure construction projects from project preparation to the end of the warranty period, and particularly for management, tasks, communication and field conditions during the contract implementation phase. The background and object of the procurement are described in more detail in the appendix to the information request, Description of the object of the procurement. INFORMATION REQUEST KYMP requests informal answers to the questions in the document "Change proposal table_for technical market dialogue_TENDERER_FILLS IN" attached to the information request, and to mark any proposed changes. Please submit your answers by email to kymp.icthankinnat@hel.fi no later than 17.4.2026 at 16.15. KYMP will treat the answers confidentially. PROCUREMENT PROCEDURE AND SCHEDULE Preliminary schedule of the procurement: March 2026 Information request May 2026 Publication of the call for tenders June 2026 Procurement decision and conclusion of the procurement contract

sig_ae40c4d24780928b67c8.description:
Supply of a forest fire location system divided into two parts. Part No. 1 - Supply, installation and commissioning of a forest fire monitoring system based on long-range fire-fighting cameras together with software for automatic smoke detection. Part No. 2 - Supply, installation and commissioning of a complete unmanned aerial vehicle system with an automatic docking station for fire monitoring of forest areas. A detailed description can be found in the relevant parts of the contract. The subject of the contract consists of sets of equipment together with installation and commissioning, the task of which will be to enable automatic detection and location of forest fires, including long-range fire-fighting cameras mounted on observation towers together with necessary accessories and the equipment of the Inspectorate's Alarm and Dispatch Point (ADP). The purpose of the system will be to carry out continuous fire monitoring of forest areas. Fire-fighting cameras mounted on observation towers are to work with the supplied software for automatic fire detection, which is intended to increase the effectiveness of monitoring in the given area. The image from the cameras must be sent to the ADP via a radio link in the unlicensed band, supplied and installed under this contract. The transmission system must be designed in a way that enables the future change of the transmission medium from radio to fibre-optic without the need to replace cameras, software and active network devices, with the exception of terminal devices used for connecting the fibre optic.. The Baczków and Hysne towers should be retrofitted with an Off-Grid power supply installation, and the ADP with a UPS emergency power supply system. The power supply must meet the requirements of PN-EN 62040-5-3:2017-05 (UPS systems) or equivalent. The installation must meet the requirements of PN-EN 62446-1:2016-08 (Photovoltaic installations) or equivalent, PN-EN 62446-1:2016-08/A1:2019-01 (Testing of PV installations) or equivalent, PN-EN 62109-2:2011 (Inverter safety) or equivalent and PN-EN IEC 62619:2023-02 (Lithium battery safety) or equivalent. The contract includes: - dismantling of the existing fire monitoring system, - supply and installation of 3 cameras for observing forest areas on the Baczków, Hysne and Dąbrowa fire-fighting towers, - supply and installation of sprinklers together with a fluid tank for the mounted cameras, - supply and installation of an off-grid power supply on the Baczków and Hysne towers. The installation must meet the requirements of PN-EN 62548 (Photovoltaic installations) or equivalent, PN-EN 62446 (Testing of PV installations) or equivalent, PN-EN 62109 (Inverter safety) or equivalent and PN-EN IEC 62619 (Lithium battery safety) or equivalent. - supply and installation of an alarm system and anti-burglary cameras on the fire-fighting towers, - supply and installation of radio links establishing connections: ● Baczków tower – Hysne tower in the 5 GHz band, ● Hysne tower – Dąbrowa tower in the 5 GHz band, ● Dąbrowa tower – Church in the 60 GHZ band with a backup 5 GHz, ● Church – Inspectorate building in the 60 GHZ band with a backup 5 GHz, ● Baczków tower – Dąbrowa tower in the 5 GHz band (redundant connection), - supply and installation of devices to provide backup communication 5G/LTE, - supply and installation of ADP equipment: ● supply and installation of 3 televisions for observing images from fire-fighting cameras, ● supply and installation of a computer with two monitors, ● supply and installation of a control console, ● supply and installation of a UPS emergency power supply. The power supply must meet the requirements of PN-EN 62040 (UPS systems) or equivalent. - supply, installation and commissioning of an automatic smoke detection system, - training on system operation. The Contractor is obliged to execute a complete work from the point of view of the purpose it is to serve. The Contracting Authority permits the installation of additional devices not included in the specification if they are necessary to achieve the required functionalities. Other information can be found in the procurement documents - Appendix No. 2 to the ToR; Supply, installation and commissioning of a complete unmanned aerial vehicle system with an automatic docking station for fire monitoring of forest areas - equipment under the FEnIKS project entitled: Comprehensive project for the adaptation of forests and forestry to climate change - prevention, counteracting and limiting the effects of threats related to forest fires (FIRE 2). 1. Subject of the contract 1.1. The subject of the contract is the supply of one complete, factory-new and unused UAS system comprising an unmanned aerial vehicle, an automatic docking station, a multi-sensor observation head, a control device, software, accessories, installation, configuration, commissioning, training and warranty service. 1.2. The system will be intended primarily for: automatic and ad-hoc patrols of forest areas during the fire hazard period; remote verification of smoke or fire alarms, including alarms transmitted by the alarm and dispatch point, camera system or rescue services; locating heat sources and determining their coordinates; live transmission in the visible and thermal imaging band; monitoring fire development, access roads, endangered objects and control after extinguishing a fire. 1.3. The subject of the contract has been described through functional requirements and minimum performance parameters. The Contracting Authority does not require a product of a specific brand or a single manufacturer's solution. However, all elements must form one compatible system, for the correct operation of which the Contractor is responsible. 2. Basis and rules for describing the subject of the contract. The description was drawn up taking into account in particular Article 16, Article 99, Article 101 and Article 105–107 of the Act of 11 September 2019 on Public Procurement Law (unified text: Journal of Laws of 2026, item 793 as amended). References to standards are to be understood as references to the indicated standard or an equivalent standard.

• Each indicated parameter is a minimum parameter, unless expressly stated otherwise. • Structurally different technical solutions are permitted if they ensure at least the same functionality, level of security and performance parameters. • If meeting a requirement requires an additional module, licence, modem, antenna, service or accessory, this element must be included in the tender and price. • All costs necessary to use the full functionality of the system for the period indicated in the OPZ must be itemised in the price form. Other information can be found in the procurement documents - Appendix No. 2 to the ToR

sig_ae99381798bcbb6aa0b8.description: The municipality has the objective of carrying out cleaning activities in the outdoor space for clean, green and grey areas more effectively and efficiently, so that the visual quality in the city improves further. To realise this objective, we want to deploy smart, mobile camera technology. This technology acts as a preview by monitoring the city on a regular or variable basis and recognising work that has been carried out or is required. This concerns, for example, various forms of (litter) waste and other types of waste in the public space (for example, fly-tipping). The recognised activities are translated into data, which then serves as input for drawing up the work distribution and execution planning in the various areas and vehicles. These images must be converted into data on the spot and immediately (i.e. in the vehicle/on the bicycle). With this data, the execution can be targeted towards locations where pollution has actually been found. Expected scope of the framework agreement The municipality expects to purchase an expected total value of € 1.200.000,- over the entire duration (maximum 4 years) of the framework agreement. This amounts to an annual expected value of € 300.000,-. Maximum scope (or: limit) of the framework agreement The maximum total value over the entire duration (maximum 4 years) of the framework agreement is € 1.800.000,-. This amounts to an annual maximum value of € 450.000,-. As soon as the maximum amount is reached, the framework agreement ends automatically. You cannot derive any rights from these values.

sig_aeb74ace210c4b154643.buyer_name: German Federal Bank, Procurement Central Division
sig_aeb74ace210c4b154643.description: The progressive digitalisation of core business processes, geopolitical developments and rising European requirements for data sovereignty and compliance require a future-proof and resilient IT infrastructure. As the independent central bank of the Federal Republic of Germany and part of the European System of Central Banks (ESCB), the Deutsche Bundesbank establishes the highest requirements for the autonomy, sovereignty and performance of its IT portfolio. To achieve the combination of these ambitious goals, the Deutsche Bundesbank requires reliable partners also for sovereign cloud services. With the strategic decision to use sovereign cloud services in addition to other public cloud services, the Deutsche Bundesbank pursues the goal of strengthening the digital sovereignty and security of its IT infrastructure without having to dispense with the innovative strength and scalability of modern public cloud offerings. In the course of this strategic orientation, the Deutsche Bundesbank is therefore initiating a structured market exploration. The aim of this measure is to systematically determine the performance and suitability of the sovereign cloud services available on the market. In doing so, it is to be examined in particular to what extent the existing service portfolios of the providers meet the technical, legal, organisational and security-related requirements of the Deutsche Bundesbank. This market exploration therefore focuses on cloud computing offerings that fulfil the European Commission's understanding of full digital sovereignty ("Technology and operations under complete EU control, subject only to EU law, with no critical non-EU dependencies", cf. EU Cloud Sovereignty Framework). The Deutsche Bundesbank reserves the right to define the concept of digital sovereignty more broadly and deviating from the aforementioned scope. Further details on the Deutsche Bundesbank's requirements for sovereign cloud services can be obtained exclusively upon request from the email address provided in the contact details. This market exploration also serves to involve the market at an early stage in a potentially pending EU-wide procurement procedure by the Deutsche Bundesbank for the procurement of cloud services and forms, among other things, a basis for decision-making for its technical design. This market exploration is not a procurement procedure directed at the award of a public contract and does not constitute either an offer or an invitation to conclude a contract. The implementation of a procurement procedure, including with a different service scope, remains reserved. Participation in this market exploration has no consequences (neither preferential treatment nor disadvantage) for the participating company within the framework of a potential future procurement process. Participants in this market exploration have no entitlement to the acquisition of knowledge from the results of the market exploration.
sig_aeb74ace210c4b154643.title: Market exploration: Sovereign cloud services for the Deutsche Bundesbank

sig_b0c1708c04f418b41358.description: In the field of traditional software, Software Bills of Materials (SBOMs) – that is, parts lists containing information about software components and their dependencies – have long been in use and are even required by the Cyber Resilience Act (CRA). This requirement also applies to AI systems, yet the idea of an SBOM specific to AI systems is relatively new. Initial approaches therefore carry the risk that they do not cover all necessary aspects with regard to the transparency of the AI supply chain. In this project, the concept "SBOM for AI - Minimum Elements" published within the G7 framework is to be put into practice and a technical implementation of the defined criteria developed for this purpose. The SBOM for AI is to be generated automatically and output in a suitable format. The developed implementation is subsequently to be made available to all stakeholders in order to make an important contribution to the cybersecurity of AI systems.
sig_b0c1708c04f418b41358.title: Project 1034: Technical implementation of an SBOM for AI (SBOM4AI)

sig_b154032bf832453654ce.description: THIS IS NOT A PRIOR INFORMATION NOTICE, CONTRACT NOTICE OR CALL FOR TENDERS, BUT A NOTICE OF THE LAUNCH OF MARKET DIALOGUE AS PART OF PROCUREMENT PLANNING. Länsi-Uudenmaan hyvinvointialue is surveying suppliers' interest in the tendering process concerning a financial planning system. Länsi-Uudenmaan hyvinvointialue (LUVN) is responsible for organising social welfare and healthcare services as well as rescue services in its region. The wellbeing services county employs approximately 10 000 persons, and its annual net expenditure is approximately 2 billion euros. Operations are managed as an entity of five service areas and forty service lines. Approximately 400 persons participate in financial planning annually, and the entity to be planned covers approximately 1 000 cost centres. This information request is part of a market dialogue, the aim of which is to survey the solutions available on the market to support financial planning. The information request is not a contract notice, nor does it bind the wellbeing services county or suppliers to subsequent procedures. 1. SUBJECT OF THE PROCUREMENT AND OBJECTIVE LUVN is planning the procurement of a financial planning system, which can be used to prepare a budget, financial plans, forecasts and other financial planning at various levels of the organisation. The objective is to survey possibilities to improve the quality, rolling nature, consistency, transparency and operational reliability of financial planning in the wellbeing services county's extensive operational entity. The objective is also to automate processes by, among other things, utilising artificial intelligence. The following features, among others, are desired from the system: - Preparation of budget and forecasts - Personnel planning: Planning is carried out on a FTE basis so that the output contains both a personnel plan and a monetary budget - Internal invoicing: cost allocation and support for invoicing processes. The organisation operates 3 responsibility areas (Digital Services, Service Centre, Property Services), whose costs are invoiced to the rest of the organisation on the basis of causation. The entity is significant both in terms of financial impact and required workload - Purchase service planning: customisable driver-based calculation models and planning structures - Extensive support for calculation dimensions: mandatory and optional entry dimensions - High-quality data transfer and reporting features - The system must provide an interface through which data can be transferred at a frequent update interval to the customer's database 2. PARTICIPATION IN THE MARKET DIALOGUE Suppliers are invited to participate in the market dialogue by responding to this information request. The requested information is provided in section "Other information" of the form. The questionnaire responses collect basic company information, contact details, and in-depth system information, which serve as the basis for selecting the suppliers with which LUVN will hold further discussions in the form of remote meetings. Any additional information and attachments are requested to be attached to the response in section "Other information, Brochure / other possible attachments". 3. IMPLEMENTATION OF THE MARKET DIALOGUE The wellbeing services county will process the information provided by all suppliers and, if necessary, organise separate remote meetings where understanding of the functionalities of the systems and their suitability for the organisation's needs can be deepened. Participation in the market dialogue is voluntary and does not bind suppliers to future procurement procedures.
sig_b154032bf832453654ce.title: INFORMATION REQUEST: Procurement of a financial planning system

sig_b1beabd691d4eaf994e6.description: The Contractor shall provide Think Trends Software as an Agentic AI and Document Intelligence solution capable of processing structured, semi-structured, and unstructured adverse event documents, including scanned PDFs, handwritten or machine-generated forms, narratives, attachments, medical records, product complaints, lab reports, follow-up submissions, and case correspondence. The solution shall support end-to-end adverse event document processing through the following capabilities: A. Agentic Document Intake and Classification Think Trends Software AI agents shall automatically receive, classify, and route adverse event documents by submission type, FDA Center, product category, source, urgency, and case-processing requirements. The intake agent shall identify whether a document relates to drugs, biologics, devices, veterinary products, tobacco products, combination products, or other FDA-regulated products. Key capabilities include: • Automated ingestion of scanned PDFs, forms, emails, images, attachments, and electronic documents. • Classification of documents by Center-specific workflow, product type, and reporting pathway. • Detection of new cases, follow-up cases, duplicate submissions, incomplete submissions, and supporting attachments. • Intelligent routing to appropriate review queues, case-processing teams, or downstream systems. B. Agentic OCR and Intelligent Data Extraction Think Trends Software Agentic OCR shall combine optical character recognition, computer vision, natural language processing, large language models, and rule-based validation agents to extract key adverse event data elements from complex documents. The platform shall extract and structure critical case information, including: • Reporter, patient, animal, subject, or consumer information. • Product information, including drug, biologic, device, tobacco, or veterinary product details. • Adverse event terms, symptoms, outcomes, seriousness, and event narratives. • Dates, timelines, exposure details, dose, route, duration, lot numbers, manufacturer information, and product identifiers. • Medical history, concomitant products, lab results, device problem codes, clinical narratives, and follow-up information. • Center-specific data elements required for CVM-Drugs and CVM-Food, CDRH, CTP, CDER, CBER and HFP. C. Center-Specific Adverse Event Processing Agents The Contractor shall configure specialized AI agents within Think Trends Software to support unique regulatory and operational needs across FDA Centers. Each agent shall apply Center-specific data models, validation logic, terminology, business rules, and review workflows. Examples include: • CVM Agent: Processes veterinary adverse event reports, animal species, breed, weight, product exposure, dosage, outcome, and veterinarian/reporter information. • CDRH Agent: Processes device-related adverse events, device identifiers, manufacturer information, malfunction details, patient impact, and device problem descriptions. • CTP Agent: Processes tobacco product adverse experiences, product use patterns, health effects, consumer narratives, and product category information. • HFP Agent: Processes HFP-specific adverse event reporting requirements and associated workflows. • CDER Agent: Process drug product adverse experiences, product use patterns, health effects, consumer narratives, and product category information. • CBER Agent: Processes biologics product adverse experiences, product use patterns, health effects, consumer narratives, and product category information. D. Case Validation, Quality Control, and Human-in-the-Loop Review Think Trends Software shall incorporate validation agents to compare extracted data against business rules, required fields, confidence thresholds, terminology standards, and case-processing logic. Records that meet defined thresholds may proceed automatically, while exceptions shall be routed for human review. Key quality-control features include: • Confidence scoring at field, document, and case levels. • Source traceability to page, section, table, and line references. • Automated flagging of missing, inconsistent, conflicting, or low-confidence data. • Human-in-the-loop review screens for case processors and safety reviewers. • Reviewer acceptance, correction, override, and approval workflows. • Full audit trail of AI extraction, human edits, and final approved values. E. Data Standardization and Regulatory Output Generation Think Trends Software shall transform extracted adverse event information into structured formats required for case management, analytics, and downstream regulatory processing. The platform shall support configurable mappings to FDA data standards, Center-specific systems, XML structures, APIs, and reporting formats. Capabilities include: • Normalization of adverse event terms, product names, dates, identifiers, and narrative fields. • Mapping to Center-specific safety data models and controlled terminology. • Generation of structured case records for downstream review and processing. • API-based integration with FDA systems, case-processing platforms, data lakes, document repositories, and workflow tools. • Export to XML, JSON, CSV, database tables, or other required formats. F. Agentic Workflow Automation and Triage Think Trends Software shall automate repetitive case-processing steps while maintaining reviewer control for regulatory decisions. The system shall support configurable AI agents capable of executing multi-step workflows, requesting missing information, summarizing case narratives, identifying seriousness indicators, detecting duplicates, and prioritizing work queues. Workflow automation shall include: • Case prioritization based on seriousness, product risk, event severity, due dates, and Center-defined rules. • Automated summarization of long adverse event narratives and supporting attachments. • Duplicate and follow-up detection across submissions. • Exception handling and escalation workflows. • Generation of reviewer-ready case summaries. • Dashboard visibility into case volumes, processing status, aging, backlog, error rates, and productivity metrics. G. AI-Enabled Redaction for FOIA Compliance ThinkTrends will provide AI-powered redaction capabilities to support FDA's obligations under the Freedom of Information Act (FOIA). The platform will automatically identify and redact personally identifiable information (PII), protected health information (PHI), commercially confidential data, law-enforcement-sensitive content, and other exemption-covered materials from adverse event documents prior to public release or response to FOIA requests. Key capabilities include: • Automated detection and redaction of PII and PHI, including patient names, addresses, dates of birth, medical record numbers, Social Security numbers, and other personal identifiers. • Identification and suppression of trade secrets, proprietary formulations, manufacturing processes, and commercially confidential submitter information protected under FOIA Exemption. • Detection of law-enforcement-sensitive and inter-agency deliberative content subject to FOIA Exemptions. • Configurable exemption profiles aligned to FDA FOIA policy, Center-specific guidance, and applicable federal regulations. • Confidence-scored redaction recommendations with source traceability, enabling FOIA reviewers to accept, modify, or override AI-proposed redactions. • Human-in-the-loop review workflow allowing FOIA analysts to validate, annotate, and finalize redacted documents before release. • Generation of redacted PDF and document versions with visible redaction markers, exemption codes, and reviewer audit annotations. • Full audit trail recording every AI-proposed redaction, reviewer decision, exemption code applied, and final release determination. • Support for bulk redaction processing across large FOIA request batches, including multi-document packages and rolling requests. • Integration with FDA FOIA tracking systems, document repositories, and case management workflows. 1.3 SALIENT FEATURES OF THINK TRENDS SOFTWARE Think Trends Software provides the following differentiating capabilities relevant to FDA adverse event reporting modernization: 1. Agentic OCR Beyond Traditional OCR: Think Trends Software does not merely convert images to text. It applies AI agents that read, interpret, validate, cross-check, and structure regulatory information from complex adverse event documents. 2. Center-Agnostic Core with Center-Specific Configuration: The platform provides a common document intelligence foundation while allowing FDA Centers such as CVM, CDRH, CTP, and HFP to configure unique workflows, data models, rules, and outputs. 3. End-to-End Adverse Event Case Automation: Think Trends Software supports intake, classification, extraction, validation, triage, routing, human review, data transformation, and downstream submission/output generation. 4. Human-in-the-Loop Regulatory Control: The system keeps FDA reviewers in control by allowing them to review, correct, approve, or override AI-generated outputs before final case acceptance. 5. Explainability and Source Traceability: Each extracted field can be traced back to the original source document, page, section, and text reference, supporting transparency, auditability, and reviewer confidence. 6. Confidence-Based Processing: Think Trends Software assigns confidence scores to extracted data and automatically routes low-confidence or inconsistent records for human review. 7. Multi-Document and Multi-Format Processing: Think Trends Software shall process scanned PDFs, structured forms, unstructured narratives, tables, handwritten content where feasible, images, attachments, correspondence, and supporting records. 8. Duplicate and Follow-Up Detection: AI agents shall compare incoming submissions against existing records to identify potential duplicates, follow-ups, related cases, and case-history updates. 9. Reviewer-Ready Case Summaries: Think Trends Software shall generate concise adverse event summaries, chronology, product-event relationships, missing-field lists, and review-ready case packages. 10. Secure FDA-Aligned Deployment: Think Trends Software shall be deployable in secure government cloud, FDA-managed, or approved hosting environments with role-based access, audit logs, encryption, and integration with enterprise identity management. 1.4 TECHNICAL REQUIREMENTS Implementation of Think Trends Software for adverse event document processing is expected to deliver the following outcomes: • Reduction in manual data entry and repetitive case-processing tasks. • Faster adverse event intake, triage, and reviewer preparation. • Improved data quality through AI-assisted validation and standardization. • Greater consistency across FDA Centers while preserving Center-specific workflows. • Enhanced traceability, auditability, and regulatory transparency. • Improved ability to manage high-volume document backlogs and surge workloads. • Increased reviewer productivity through AI-generated summaries and exception-based review. • Scalable platform foundation for future FDA adverse event modernization initiatives. Please view the attached Request for Quote (RFQ) RFQ FDA-SOL-75F40126Q00384 document for additional information.

sig_b1e5dadbbba123ada14c.description: Istekki Oy is putting out to tender telecommunications connections and related services for itself and its customers and is organising a market dialogue as part of the preparation for the tender. The procurement may be divided into parts. Istekki Oy will decide on the number of possible parts and more detailed information after the market dialogue. The final terms of the procurement will be published in the contract notice and the invitation to tender with its annexes. According to the contracting authority's current preliminary view, the procurement procedure is an open procedure and, according to the contracting authority's current preliminary view, a multi-supplier framework agreement or a dynamic purchasing system (DPS) will be established for the procurement. The purpose of the market dialogue is to give potential tenderers the opportunity to discuss the implementation of the procurement and to provide views and feedback to support the preparation of the procurement. We greatly appreciate the participation of potential tenderers in the market dialogue, and the views presented by each participant will be taken into account in the preparation of any potential tender. The contracting authority requests interested participants to register for the market dialogue by 12.5.2026 at 11 by email to hankinnat@istekki.fi. Based on the responses received, Istekki Oy will select at least 5 participants for a bilateral discussion. The discussion sessions will be held according to the preliminary schedule estimate in May-June 2026. All bilateral discussion sessions are of the same length and the same matters will be discussed with each participant. The market dialogue also includes an opportunity for participants to comment on the draft procurement documents, according to the preliminary schedule estimate in August 2026. Participation in a bilateral discussion, registration for the market dialogue, commenting on procurement documents or other participation in the market dialogue does not oblige tenderers to participate in the tender competition and is not a prerequisite for later participation in the actual tender competition, nor does it affect the tenderer's position in the tender competition itself. Likewise, participation in a bilateral discussion is not a prerequisite for any potential commenting on draft procurement documents. This is not a contract notice or an invitation to tender, but a notice of the initiation of a market dialogue as part of the preparation of the procurement. The actual procurement procedure will be started by the publication of a contract notice. All information in this notice is preliminary estimates that are not binding on the contracting authority. The final terms and information relating to the subject of the procurement and the procurement process will be published in the actual contract notice. It is good to note that this notice or the market dialogue itself does not oblige Istekki Oy to carry out the procurement in the manner presented in this document or its annexes. A potential tender competition may also be left unorganised. No separate compensation will be paid for participating in the market dialogue.

sig_b1f961554688efa86265.description: KS Digital has, on behalf of the Committee Council, established a work group that shall review how the municipal sector can cooperate on the future childhood and school administration systems (OAS/SAS), digital ecosystems and possibilities for future joint procurements. The work includes both education and school administrative systems (OAS/SAS), the digital eco-system included in them, and how the municipal sector can strengthen coordination, standardisation and any future joint procurements. As a part of this work, we invite the supplier market to a dialogue. We want insight into how the market assesses developments in the area, what technological and organisational possibilities exist, and how the municipal sector and the supplier market together can contribute to a more open, coherent and future orientated digital ecosystem for the education sector. The work is anchored in a reported need from the municipalities for stronger coordination in relation to requirements, standardisation, architecture, data sharing, procurements and further development of digital systems in the area of adolescence. The aim is not to define a new system, but to assess how the municipal sector together can contribute to a more coherent, open and future orientated digital ecosystem for children, youths, guardians, employees, managers, owners and associated services. An important goal is also to contribute to a supplier market that supports this development, through clear common needs, standards and framework conditions that stimulate innovation and sustainable development of the systems. Information on the market dialogue including registration will be in the tender https://ksdigital.no/markedsdialoger-og-anskaffelser/

sig_b1faf1e54c42ab25bd16.description: 1. The subject of the contract is the supply, including placement, installation and commissioning, of water supply infrastructure equipment for the Dziadkowice Municipality, as well as the supply and implementation of a remote water meter reading system. 2. The subject of the contract has been divided into 2 parts and includes: 2.1. Part 1 – the supply and installation of 65 above-ground hydrants DN80, 33 gate valves (DN200 – 4 units, DN150 – 24 units, DN100 – 5 units), a water dispenser including commissioning, and the purchase, planting and maintenance of 110 trees. 2.2. Part 2 – the supply and replacement of 751 water meters with remote reading modules (DN15 – 80 units, DN20 – 650 units, DN25 – 8 units, DN32 – 9 units, DN50 – 2 units, DN100 – 2 units), the supply of equipment, software, licences, system implementation, integration with the WODA system, tests, documentation and training. The Contracting Authority allows for the submission of a tender for one or both parts and does not limit the number of parts that may be awarded to one Contractor. 3. The detailed scope, technical parameters, locations, method of installation, acceptance and documentation are defined by the Description of the Subject of the Contract (OPZ), technical designs and the projected contract provisions specific to a given part – Annex 1A to the SWZ. The Beneficiary declares compliance with the DNSH principle; the contractor is obliged to carry out deliveries in a manner that ensures the maintenance of this compliance and to provide the required evidence. Requirements concerning Part 1 The scope of Part 1 includes in particular: 1) the supply of complete equipment and materials; 2) the dismantling of existing elements; 3) the execution of earthworks and assembly works; 4) the performance of required tests; 5) flushing and disinfection; 6) surface restoration; 7) the execution of required signage; 8) the preparation and handover of as-built documentation; 9) the commissioning of the water dispenser; 10) the execution of plantings including their maintenance during the warranty period – in accordance with the OPZ, design documentation and technical designs. Within the scope of Part 1, the Contractor shall obtain the required consents, arrangements and permits related to the occupation of the road lane or the introduction of traffic management, shall provide the required signage and site security, and shall bear the associated costs. Warranty – minimum 24 months for the supplied equipment. The warranty period for gate valves and hydrants is one of the tender evaluation criteria. The detailed scope, technical parameters, locations, method of installation, acceptance and documentation are defined by the OPZ, technical designs and the projected contract provisions specific to a given part – Annex 1A to the SWZ.; Requirements concerning Part 2 The scope of Part 2 includes in particular: 1) the supply of brand-new water meters and radio modules compatible with them; 2) the dismantling of existing water meters; 3) the installation and sealing of new water meters; 4) the performance of test readings; 5) the implementation and commissioning of the remote reading system; 6) the supply of a collection kit and required IT equipment; 7) the provision of required licences; 8) the migration or import of data from the WODA system (INFO-SYSTEM Groszek) used by the Contracting Authority; 9) the performance of required tests; 10) the preparation and handover of documentation; 11) the conduct of instructional training on the operation and maintenance of the supplied equipment and system; 12) The Contractor shall agree with the Contracting Authority on the principles for contacting water consumers and the dates for water meter replacement. Consumer data may be provided to persons performing the replacement only to the minimum extent necessary and using secure communication channels.; 13) With regard to each water meter whose replacement requires agreeing on a date with the owner or tenant of the premises, the Contractor shall make at least three documented contact attempts, including at least one after 15:00 on working days or on a Saturday. After three unsuccessful attempts, the Contractor shall hand over to the Contracting Authority, on the basis of a report, the unused set: the water meter together with the assigned radio module. In such a case, only the price of the supply of this set shall be settled, without remuneration for the dismantling and installation service.; 14) The warranty for water meters and radio modules is at least 60 months, and its extension is one of the tender evaluation criteria. For the remaining equipment, the remote reading system, integration and software, the Contracting Authority requires at least 60 months of warranty, service or support – appropriate to the nature of the service. The Contractor shall provide a subscription and software updates for the remote reading system for a period of 60 months.; 15) For a period of at least 60 months from the acceptance of the system, as part of the tender price, the Contractor shall provide: a) service; b) software updates; c) security patches; d) technical support; e) required licences; f) the ability to use the system and the data stored within it. 16) The expiry of the warranty period must not result in the Contracting Authority losing access to the stored data or being deprived of the ability to download or export it. 17) The supplied measuring instruments must meet the requirements for legal metrological control and possess the required declarations of conformity, markings and documentation enabling their lawful use. 18) The remote reading system must ensure at least: a) full support for 751 water meters; b) the recording and handling of alarms; c) the storage of reading history; d) data export; e) integration with the WODA system used by the Contracting Authority; f) the performance of secure backups; g) the ability to restore data from a backup. 19) The Contractor may process water consumer data only on the documented instruction of the Contracting Authority and to the extent necessary for the execution of the contract. For Part 2, the personal data processing entrustment agreement constituting part of the Projected contract provisions – Annex no. 3B to the SWZ – shall apply. The detailed scope, technical parameters, locations, method of installation, acceptance and documentation are defined by the OPZ, technical designs and the projected contract provisions specific to a given part – Annex 1A to the SWZ.

Federal Agency Name: Air Force Research Laboratory ARA Title: Neutron Strategic Technology Advanced Research (Neutron STAR) Advanced Research Announcement (ARA) ARA Type: This is an Open ARA; initial announcement SUBMISSION DATES ARE INDEFIINITE UNTIL FURTHER NOTICE PROGRAM SUMMARY: This is an Open ARA announcement pursuant to the authority of 10 U.S.C. §4023 Procurement for Experimental Purposes. AFRL is interested in receiving white papers regarding nuclear-related research and development, including, but not limited to modeling and simulation of re-entry environments, materials characterization, nuclear explosion monitoring, and design, fabrication and experimentation of nuclear delivery. Dialogue between prospective Offerors and Government representatives is strongly encouraged. This solicitation intends to use the acquisition authority provided by 10 U.S.C. §4023. This authority applies to the acquisition of items related to “...ordnance, signal, chemical activity, transportation, energy, medical, spaceflight, and aeronautical supplies, including parts and accessories, and designs thereof, that are necessary for experimental or test purposes in the development of the best supplies that are needed for the national defense.” Consequently, white papers and proposals should address how the proposed effort provides benefits to the national defense relative to the parameters of this authority, and a strategy for verifying those intended benefits. *Please see the attached Neutron Star Industry User Guide for guidance on definitions, processes, submission requirements and evaluation criteria.* BACKGROUND: AFRL’s Geo Space Division (RVBN) positions AFRL to steward, develop, and deliver leading technologies to the warfighter and the nuclear enterprise to ensure the National defense. Thus, proposed solutions should be innovative and substantially improve national defense capabilities across the domains of national nuclear deterrence operations. While the Government describes discrete topic areas below, it also anticipates that certain comprehensive technology solutions and prototypes may require multidiscipline approaches that address two or more topic areas. The topic areas covered under this announcement may be used in any combination. The Government reserves the right to add, delete or modify the topic areas as necessary. Industry-Government Communication: Dialogue between prospective Offerors and Government representatives is strongly encouraged throughout the life of this ARA. However, communication shall be limited to the Contracting/Agreement Officer once full proposals are submitted for evaluation/review. Discussions should focus on understanding Government objectives and requirements, feasibility of prospective offeror approach, and prospective offeror prior similar efforts. Discussions shall not constitute a commitment by the Government to subsequently fund or award any proposed effort. No guidance related to technical approach will be given. Offerors are advised that only Contracting or Agreement Officers are legally authorized to contractually bind or otherwise commit the Government. ANNOUNCEMENT DETAILS: This is a HYBRID ANNOUNCEMENT. This announcement includes an open request for white papers as described below. Additionally, individual solicitations for white papers (Two-Step solicitation) and/or proposals (One-Step solicitation) related to discrete requirements may be issued. AFRL reserves the right to collapse a white paper (Two-Step solicitation) into a One-Step if the situation warrants and the white paper contains sufficient technical detail to do full technical proposal evaluation instead of white paper evaluation. Open Announcement Request: AFRL/RVBN is soliciting white papers on the research effort described in the below topic areas pursuant to the authority of 10 U.S.C. §4023, Procurement for Experimental Purposes. White papers submitted pursuant to the open announcement request follow the two-step procedures described below. White papers submitted under the open announcement request may be retained for 12 months. Open Announcement Submission: Unclassified White papers must be submitted to the Neutron Star Org Box at afrl.rvkb.afrlneutronstardms@us.af.mil. DO NOT DELIVER any classified portion of the white paper to this address. If it is determined that a classified white paper is required, please contact the Neutron STAR Org Mailbox for specific delivery instructions. Additional instructions for white paper submissions can be found in the Neutron STAR Industry User Guide attached to this announcement. Individual Solicitation Request: Individual Solicitations, except for Limited Solicitations, for white papers and proposals will be issued under this announcement via the Government Point of Entry (GPE) at https://sam.gov. Notification of Individual Solicitations may be announced on other platforms (i.e. www.grants.gov) and will direct Offerors to the GPE for full solicitation details. Individual Solicitation Submissions: Submission requirements for Individual Solicitations will be specified in the solicitation details of each Individual Solicitation. Individual Solicitation Variations: Variations of the ARA Individual Solicitation process are available for use. The following types are commonly used but are not considered all inclusive. One-Step: The one-step process is used to request full technical and cost proposals from each Offeror. The proposals are reviewed in accordance with the solicitation criteria and typically all, part, or none of a proposal may be selected for award. Two-Step: The two-step process is used to request white papers and Rough Order of Magnitude (ROM) costs. The Individual Solicitation must state whether an unfavorable white paper review will bar the Offeror from further consideration. The Government may retain unselected white papers for a specific period, which will be identified in the individual solicitation. White papers submitted under the open announcement request may be retained for 12 months. Full proposals are requested from those Offerors selected in the white paper review process. After proposals are received, they are processed and reviewed in accordance with the One-Step process. Limited Individual Solicitations: This approach allows for solicitation to a limited group of potential offerors. Request for Proposals (RFP) or Requests for white papers will be issued directly to potential offerors without a requirement to publish to the GPE. The Government may issue solicitations that combine one or more of the above approaches. Announcement Modifications: Due to the dynamically evolving nature of US nuclear deterrent mission and warfighter needs, this announcement is subject to updates, revisions, or additional topic areas. Therefore, Offerors are highly encouraged to continually monitor https://sam.gov to ensure they receive the latest guidance for this announcement. The Government shall provide updates to this announcement no less than annually. Updates may include changes to topic areas, submission requirements, administrative changes, evaluation criteria, solicitation methods, etc. (not an inclusive list). Type of Contract/Instrument: The Government reserves the right to award the instrument best suited to the nature of the research proposed. Accordingly, the Government may award any appropriate contract, agreement or assistance instrument type under the authorities below: Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) 10 U.S.C. §4021 "Other Transaction for Research” 10 U.S.C. §4022 "Other Transaction for Prototype" 10 U.S.C. §4023 "Procurement for Experimental Purposes" 15 U.S.C §3710a – Cooperative Research and Developments Agreements 15 U.S.C §3715 – Partnership Intermediaries 32 C.F.R. §22.215 – Grants and Cooperative Agreements The Government anticipates that a mix of contract/ instrument types will be used throughout the life of this announcement. Generally, awards under this announcement or any Individual Solicitations may be Cost-Plus-Fixed Fee (Completion and Term), Cost Reimbursement, Firm Fixed Price, Cost Sharing, and Incentive. NOTE: If a Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) type contract is recommended as the award type authority, then the FAR clauses will be referenced at the Individual Solicitation level or within the Request for Proposal. The FAR and FAR supplement provisions and clauses will be incorporated by reference. The full text of these provisions and clauses can be found at https://www.acquisition.gov. If an assistance instrument (grants or cooperative agreements) is recommended as the award type, then articles and guidance found under DoDGARS, 200 CFR, OMB/DoD Policy shall be used and followed as appropriate. If an Other Transaction (OT) is recommended as the award type, then the FAR references and clauses will not apply. The terms and conditions of an OT agreement shall be developed and negotiated on a case-by-case basis. Estimated Program Cost: The overarching announcement has an unrestricted ceiling. However, Individual Solicitations may elect to provide an estimated program value or funding profile for planning purposes. Anticipated Number of Awards: The Air Force anticipates awarding multiple awards for this announcement. However, the Air Force reserves the right to award zero, one, or more grants, agreements, other transactions, or contracts for all, some or none of the solicited effort based on the Offeror’s ability to perform desired work and funding availability. There is no limit on the number of awards that may be made to an individual Offeror. Award Schedule: The anticipated period of performance will be determined through dialogue between prospective Offerors and Government representatives for each topic area and specified in each individual award. Individual Solicitations may elect to provide a desired technical execution schedule for planning purposes. Deliverables: Hardware and software deliverables will be specified within a separately priced contract/award line items and data deliverables will be specified on individual Contract Data Requirements List(s) (CDRLs) in any resultant contract or an OT article. Within Scope Award Modifications: Offerors are advised that due to the inherent uncertainty of research and development efforts, awards resulting from this announcement may be modified during performance to make within scope changes, to include but not limited to, modifications which increase overall contract/award ceiling amount. System for Award Management (SAM) Registration: Before the Government can issue an award, an Offeror must be registered in the System for Award Management (SAM). If an Offeror was previously registered in Central Contractor Registration (CCR), the information has been transferred to SAM. However, it is in the Offeror’s interest to visit SAM and ensure that all their data is up to date from SAM and other databases to avoid delay in award. SAM replaced CCR, Online Representations and Certifications Application (ORCA), and the Excluded Parties List System (EPLS). SAM allows firms interested in conducting business with the federal government to provide basic information on business capabilities and financial information. To register, visit https://www.sam.gov. sig_b284571d28359b987a79.description: The Brandenburg IT Service Provider (ZIT-BB) is the central service provider for the direct state administration of Brandenburg for the provision of IT services. Its extensive task portfolio includes, amongst other things, the planning, provision and operation of technical infrastructure as well as the coordination and support of both authority-specific and cross-authority and joint IT procedures. Its area of responsibility also includes IT security management for the state administration's IT infrastructure and responsibility for the Computer Emergency Response Team (CERT). From its central location in Potsdam, ZIT-BB currently supports approx. 18.000 workstations in the Brandenburg state administration. The number of workstations to be supported will increase further in the coming years. With the centralisation of the state administration's IT, supporting the authorities and institutions of the State of Brandenburg in the planning, design and use of information technology, as well as consulting on IT security issues, has become a core field of activity for the operation. Furthermore, ZIT-BB provides services in accordance with the Brandenburg e-Government Act, in particular for municipalities, administrative offices and municipal associations of the state. The main location of ZIT-BB is located at Steinstraße 104-106 in 14480 Potsdam. Due to its nationwide responsibility, ZIT-BB has branch offices in Cottbus, Frankfurt (Oder), Wünsdorf, Gransee and Eberswalde, among others. It operates its data centre in Berlin. Lot LOT-0001: External Information Security Officer for the Brandenburg IT Service Provider. This procurement is intended to commission an External Information Security Officer (ISO) for the Brandenburg IT Service Provider. The described services are to be provided immediately after contract award and end at the latest upon reaching the upper limits defined under section 4.1 in the EVB-IT service contract. The contracting authority assumes a scope of 700 person-days. Further details on the subject matter of the contract are regulated in the description of services part B.
sig_b284571d28359b987a79.title: External Information Security Officer for the Brandenburg IT Service Provider

Höhe station" (SBHG) from the year 2026. The communication services comprise, as continuously provided services, among other things, the project-accompanying management and coordination of public relations as well as the project-accompanying maintenance and care of PR instruments. Previously, the route of the U2 ends at Gonzenheim stop. The integration of the U2 in Bad Homburg station takes place north of the existing S-Bahn tracks in the area of the former so-called prince's track (Fürstengleis). The planned route alignment necessitates the conversion of the technical equipment of Deutsche Bahn's infrastructure facilities, the planning of which is the subject of this tender. The planning of the new construction measure is already taking place. sig_b2c19703e21270dde32c.description: This is a notice of a future procurement. This is not an actual contract notice or call for tenders, and it does not initiate a procurement procedure. The notice concerns a joint procurement planned by the wellbeing services counties of East Uusimaa, Central Uusimaa, and West Uusimaa, as well as Vantaa-Kerava, regarding a comprehensive service for medical devices. An information session has already been held previously regarding the procurement, where the planned content of the procurement was presented. However, the content has changed significantly from what was previously announced, so the contracting authorities wish to inform everyone of their new plans extensively. The purpose of this notice is to survey potential operators in the market and request their comments on the prepared procurement material drafts. The goal is to procure a comprehensive service for medical devices for all participating regions according to the individual needs of each region. The need is to procure all activities related to the lifecycle management of medical devices, such as: acquisition (survey of current devices), acceptance inspections and registrations, periodic maintenance, fault repairs and disposals, and a device register. The procurement materials will be sent to all interested parties. Interest in commenting on the materials should be notified by email to the address lisa.alho@keusote.fi by 27.11.2025. Comments on the materials are requested to be submitted to the same address by 1.12.2025. The procurement will be carried out as a negotiated procedure, and the first notice is intended to be published soon after receiving the suppliers' comments, during the latter part of the year 2025. With this market dialogue, we aim to ensure a competitive procurement that takes into account the operators' thoughts on the current state of the market and their capability to participate in the procurement procedure. Participating or not participating in this market dialogue does not exclude participation in the potential actual procurement. The market dialogue is an open exchange of information, and no view, opinion, statement, or document from this market dialogue binds or obligates either party to anything. Participating or not participating in this market dialogue does not exclude participation in the potential actual procurement. No fee is paid for participating in the market dialogue.

The objective of the 36-month manufacturer support can be divided into two parts: 1. Provision of support officially provided by the manufacturer's engineers in the event of hardware or software errors occurring alongside the proper operation of the Avaya system, for the purpose of fault clearance. 2. Software tracking throughout the entire support period, which makes available to the MNB the latest versions and security updates for all software of the system. The manufacturer thereby ensures that its systems can be operated securely, faultlessly and with the expected functions throughout their entire lifecycle. sig_b345b4676fb8c00bbe58.description: The draft call for tenders, draft agreement and other annexes delivered as attachments to this technical dialogue are all still preliminary drafts, even though their structure and content may resemble highly finalised procurement documents. The documents must not be interpreted as final procurement documents, nor are the procedural details, deadlines, agreement terms, comparison criteria or other details presented therein to be considered final solutions binding upon the client. Following the dialogue, the client will assess, based on the feedback received, which points will be clarified, relaxed, amended or possibly removed prior to the actual competitive tendering. 1. Purpose of the dialogue The purpose of this technical dialogue is to ensure that the call for tenders, draft agreement and annexes prepared by the client give service providers an accurate and sufficient picture of the service being procured. The dialogue does not request binding tenders, but rather the market's view on how the documents are interpreted, which points require clarification and which terms are possibly too strict or otherwise difficult in practice. In the dialogue, the client particularly wishes to evaluate: - whether the subject of the procurement, division of responsibilities and service descriptions are understandable - whether the service level requirements, reporting and agreement terms are realistic - whether implementation, data management and data protection are described sufficiently clearly - how service providers see the operators' compensation and billing model as most workable in practice. 2. Client's initial description of the service - The procurement concerns the driving arrangement and ride dispatching service for school transport. The procurement does not include transport operations. - The service includes software service, route planning and maintenance, operational driving arrangement, transport dispatching, deviation management, operational communication, reporting and audit material. - Daily-rate vehicles and overflow vehicles will be tendered separately as transport services. - The client makes administrative decisions regarding transport entitlements, service level and the administrative content of customer profiles. The service provider does not make independent administrative decisions. - The client acts as the data controller and the service provider as the data processor. The client's data and the operational data concerning the client generated in the service belong to the client. The client particularly welcomes views on whether the described service package is feasible in practice, which requirements drive costs most significantly, and which terms or metrics are expedient and realistically achievable from the market's perspective.
sig_b345b4676fb8c00bbe58.title: Technical dialogue: Driving arrangement and ride dispatching services (school transport)

sig_b34881107d37152caafe.description: The subject of the procedure is the conclusion of framework agreements with several companies for the provision, introduction, operation, maintenance and further development of a network management system for low voltage (hereinafter NMS). The scope of services is described in full in the service description (Annex 03). General requirements. Overarching requirements for the NMS, in particular regarding architecture, data storage, interfaces, information security, scalability, as well as integration into the existing system and process landscape of the eligible company. Functional scope 1: Calculable low-voltage network model (digital twin) including integration into ERP, GIS and EDM systems as well as mapping of actual and target switching states. Functional scope 2: Integration of measurement data from local network stations and TAF values, network calculation, determination of network status as well as controllability checks. Functional scope 3: Network-oriented control in accordance with § 14a EnWG and § 9 EEG including verification and documentation. Extended functional scope: Network calculation for network planning, automated network connection testing as well as redispatch 2.0 and prospectively redispatch 3.0. The Thüga Aktiengesellschaft is procuring as a central purchasing body in accordance with § 4a SektVO in the name and on behalf of the participating affiliated companies (currently around 100 companies of the Thüga Group). On the basis of the contract terms negotiated in the procedure, the individual participating companies will conclude individual framework agreements based on the EVB-IT contracts.

sig_b39560577bfcb6d535fd.description:
Acquisition of specific equipment intended for equipping a "Smart Grid" educational technical platform at Lycée Pablo Neruda (Saint-Martin-d'Hères, 38), divided into 7 lots: HV/LV delivery/distribution substation, residential area, infrastructure area, industrial area, tertiary sector area, digital tools area, and educational City Grid laboratory. The contract includes the supply, delivery, installation, connection, parameterisation of the equipment as well as teacher training. The detailed technical specifications for each lot appear in the CCTP. Supply, installation, connection and commissioning of an HV educational teaching set reproducing an automated and communicating urban electrical distribution substation. The set comprises: an 24 kV insulated secondary MV switchboard of the SM AIRSET IQI type or equivalent, supplemented by two C5 switchboard panels and two P5 protections for the simulation of an urban network loop; a remote control interface integrating automatic loop reconfiguration (EPAS technology or equivalent) with a self-healing function; a thermal monitoring control system (wireless sensors of the TH110 type); a simulated dry HV/LV transformer equipped with a DGPT2 protection; a main low-voltage switchboard (MLVS) with an interlocking chain and primary/secondary injection case; a simulated HV loop under LV voltage (400V three-phase) integrating anti-arc electric protection and real-time diagnostic sensors. The service includes on-site teacher training on the operational handling of the equipment, as well as technical documentation and an educational file with practical work scenarios. The detailed technical specifications appear in the CCTP, lot no. 001.; Supply, cabling, parameterisation and commissioning of an educational residential area comprising 4 distinct dwellings (chalets or 3D modular construction of approximately 12 m2 each), interconnected to the platform's smart grid network. Each dwelling implements a different home automation technology: dwelling no. 1 under the Zigbee protocol (tableau connected GTL, intrusion detection, residential VDI, air-to-air heat pump, dual-flow mechanical ventilation) ; dwelling no. 2 under the Thread/Matter protocol with FTTH fibre optic connection; dwelling no. 3 under the MyHome system (SCS bus, video door entry system, backed-up alarm, thermodynamic water heater); dwelling no. 4 combining Zigbee, safety equipment (water leak, smoke, temperature/humidity detectors) and fibre optic connection. Each dwelling integrates shutter management, controlled lighting, energy and fluid metering, a residential electric vehicle charging station, and touchscreen tablet supervision. The service includes the installation, connection, parameterisation and complete cabling of the 4 dwellings, as well as on-site teacher training. The detailed technical specifications appear in the CCTP, lot no. 002.; Supply, cabling, connection and commissioning of an educational "connected street" of approximately 18 metres, interconnected to the platform's smart grid network and supplied from an LV public distribution connection point (REMBT). The set comprises: a connected and didactic public lighting system (4 LED masts with remote management, supervision, measurement and presence detection, integrating a Wi-Fi hotspot, IP loudspeaker and IP camera as associated equipment); a fibre optic infrastructure in a street cabinet; two communicating electric vehicle charging stations (mono 4,6 kW and tri 22 kW, with energy management box and vehicle presence simulation); a complete urban video protection system (IP cameras, recording bay, optical drawer); a connected urban dynamic display system; a mobile resistive load of 8 kW making it possible to simulate real consumption on the network. The service includes the installation, connection, parameterisation, cabling of all the equipment, the necessary specific developments as well as on-site teacher training. The detailed technical specifications appear in the CCTP, lot no. 003.; Supply, installation, connection and commissioning of an educational industrial area comprising a communicating MLVS/main general enclosure ensuring the distribution, protection, control-command and measurement of electrical energy (reactive energy compensation, multi-feeder monitoring, Modbus/Ethernet gateway), as well as two didactic communicating industrial systems: an industrial pump study, maintenance and test system (horizontal multistage centrifugal pump, IoT gateway and IO-Link smart sensors) and a qualification system simulating food-processing mixing equipment (control cabinet with lockable feeders, inverter-backed variable speed drive, automation console on a type M340 PLC or equivalent). The set allows for functional analysis, assembly/disassembly, commissioning, preventive and corrective maintenance activities. The service includes the connection of the MLVS and the systems, the laying of cable routes, parameterisation, commissioning, specific developments as well as on-site teacher training. The detailed technical specifications appear in the CCTP, lot no. 004.; Supply, installation, connection and commissioning of an educational tertiary area representing an office building connected to the platform's smart grid network. The set comprises a communicating MLVS/main general enclosure ensuring distribution, service continuity via a source changeover switch, protection, control-command and load shedding of part of the circuits; a lighting management system under the DALI and Zigbee protocol with building management systems (BMS), integrating temperature and CO2 sensors, controlled inertia radiators and supervision software;

a compact, high-efficiency dual-flow educational air handling unit (AHU) with heat recovery, filtration and control via a communicating BMS programmable logic controller (KNX, LonWorks, Modbus TCP/IP, BACnet IP); as well as an integrated VDI infrastructure (patch panel, RJ45 category 6a cabling). The service includes the connection of the main low-voltage switchboard and all systems, the installation of cable routing, parameter setting, commissioning, specific developments and on-site training for teaching staff, including the monitoring of software updates. Detailed technical specifications are set out in the CCTP, lot no. 005.; Supply, parameter setting and commissioning of a virtual reality device (wireless headset such as Oculus Quest 3 or equivalent with controllers, tracking and associated laptop) and 9 immersive training scenarios in a realistic environment, with a minimum of 12 licences valid for at least 3 years per scenario: electrical authorisation B1V (electrician operative), electrical authorisation BS (elementary intervention officer), electrical authorisation BR (general intervention officer), electrical authorisation B2/BC (work and lockout/tagout officer), High Voltage authorisation H0/H1, photovoltaic authorisation BP, maintenance and diagnostics, and smart grid discovery. The service includes the installation, parameter setting and commissioning of the equipment as well as on-site training for teaching staff. Detailed technical specifications are set out in the CCTP, lot no. 006.; Supply, installation and commissioning of a Smart Grid educational laboratory with a power output of 6 kW intended for the comprehensive study of the energy chain (generation, transmission, distribution, consumption), for the vocational baccalaureate in Electrotechnology and BTS Energy Environment Systems. The laboratory comprises: a programmable source making it possible to emulate various generators (nuclear, thermal, wind, photovoltaic) with the generation of phase imbalances, harmonics and variable frequency (0-300V AC per phase, 15 Hz to 1,2 kHz); a transport cabinet reproducing a configurable three-phase line over two lengths (10 km and 50 km minimum), highlighting line losses and voltage drops; a regeneration module acting as a programmable consumer (regenerative electronic load 350V/30A/9kW, resistive, inductive, capacitive, rectified types); a measurement unit and supervision server enabling real-time visualisation of all electrical quantities (voltages, currents, powers, harmonics up to rank 32, power factor), with malfunction detection and optional integration of Linky communicating meters. The solution covers three progressive levels of educational skills, from smart grid discovery to mastery of the Energy Management System (EMS). The service includes delivery, installation, configuration, commissioning and on-site training for teaching staff. Detailed technical specifications are set out in the CCTP, lot no. 007.

sig_b3aff275208f654a526c.description: The UK Home Office (referred to hereafter as the Authority) is inviting prospective bidders to take part in a series of pre-market engagement activities for the Authority's planned QAT procurements. The Authority currently has a number of contracts for QAT capability, aligned to portfolios across the Home Office. The future commercial strategy is to consolidate these services into two core testing capability contracts by Autumn 2027. The exact scope, duration and values of the new contracts is still to be confirmed, however the current expectation is that each contract will have a minimum term of 3-years, with a maximum spend of £150m (including any extensions). The intention is to compete these contracts via the GCA Dynamic Purchasing System, RM6148, however the pre-market engagement is open to all suppliers. Before any tender activity is launched, the Authority wishes to invite feedback from prospective bidders on the proposed strategy and gather information that will help it to refine its procurement and contracting approach further. Key topics that the Authority wishes to explore include, but are not limited to: 1. Route to market 2. Transition approach 3. Key Performance Indicators & contractual incentives (i.e. Service Credits) 4. Cost drivers 5. The use of innovation and AI to drive efficiency 6. Roles and Capability 7. Tooling and hardware 8. Removing barriers for SMEs 9. Support in the transformation from a Programme SDLC to a Product SDLC, including using experience gained from other clients to help shape and drive the change 10. Support in the transformation from Quality Assurance to Quality Engineering, including using experience gained from other clients to help shape and drive the change This engagement shall start with an in-person event from 10:30 until 13:00 on Monday 27th July at the TechUK office in London; 10 Saint Bride St, London, EC4A 4AD. Each supplier may bring a maximum of 2 delegates to the day, and should confirm who these individuals are no later than 17:00 (BST) on Thursday 23rd July. Suppliers can register their interest for this event by registering an account on the Authority's eSourcing Portal (https://homeoffice.app.jaggaer.com) and navigating to the opportunity titled 'pqq_823 - Pre-Market Engagement for Home Office Quality Assurance & Test Engineering (QAT) Contracts'. Technical Proposal - The technical proposal must ensure that the proposed pump, motor, and meter are not just individually compliant, but are fully integrated and rated to work safely together in a Class I, Division 1 hazardous location. Fuel Pump: • Flow Rate (GPM): Must match the system's operational requirements (e.g., refueler truck loading vs. bulk transfer); • Material Compatibility: Housing, seals, and gaskets must be compatible with the specific fuel type (JP-8, F-24, Diesel, Mogas); • Inlet/Outlet Size: Flange dimensions must match existing piping to prevent flow restriction. - IAW • API 610 (Centrifugal Pumps) or API 676 (Rotary Pumps) where applicable & • Manufacturer curves showing NPSH (Net Positive Suction Head). b. Fuel Meter: • Accuracy & Repeatability: Must meet strict tolerances for custody transfer or inventory control; • Register/Pulser: Mechanical register or electronic output must interface with the existing Fuel Facility Control System (FFCS) or Automated Fuel Service Station (AFSS); • Pressure Rating: Maximum Working Pressure (PSI) must exceed the pump's deadhead pressure. - • NTEP (National Type Evaluation Program) or OIML certification for custody transfer & • Weights & Measures approval. d. Integrated System: • Physical Footprint: The new components must fit on the existing concrete pad and align with current piping configurations; • Coupling & Alignment: Method of coupling the motor to the pump (e.g., flexible coupling with non-sparking coupling guard). - IAW • NFPA 30 (Flammable and Combustible Liquids Code) & • Unified Facilities Criteria (UFC) 3-460-01 (Design: Petroleum Fuel Facilities). 2.
