sig_b498b4f3a2517da9153d.description: The subject of the public contract is the delivery, implementation, integration, commissioning and provision of support for software solutions based on artificial intelligence intended for clinical decision support at St. Anne's University Hospital in Brno. The performance of the public contract is designed as the provision of software in the form of a cloud solution (SaaS). The supplier shall provide software operated in a cloud infrastructure, whereby: - installation of a full-fledged on-premise solution is not required, - data processing and storage will take place within the EU/EEA, unless another regime is expressly approved in writing by the contracting authority while simultaneously meeting all legal and security conditions), - integration into the contracting authority's systems (PACS, NIS) will be ensured via standard interfaces. The scope of performance therefore includes: - a time-limited usage right (licence/subscription) for the duration of the contract, - provision of operation, availability, updates and technical support as part of the service. The performance includes in particular: • delivery of medical devices in the form of software meeting the requirements of MDR (EU) 2017/745, • their integration into the contracting authority's information systems (PACS, NIS), • commissioning into live operation, • provision of service, technical support and updates for the duration of the contract. The supplier shall be insured for the entire duration of the contract against liability for damage caused in connection with the performance of the contract, with a minimum limit of indemnity in the amount of 5 000 000 CZK per one insurance event for each part of the public contract. The public contract (PC) is divided into 2 separate parts: Part 1 PC - AI Software for prostate cancer screening using artificial intelligence algorithms Part 2 PC - Software using artificial intelligence algorithms in chest X-ray diagnostics. The subject of this part of the public contract is the delivery, implementation, integration and support of a software solution based on artificial intelligence intended for clinical decision support in the evaluation of prostate magnetic resonance (MR). The offered software must be a medical device within the meaning of Art. 2 para. 1 of Regulation (EU) 2017/745 of the European Parliament and of the Council on medical devices (MDR) and must be duly placed on the market in the European Union. The system must be intended as a clinical decision-support tool for the detection, localisation and assessment of lesions suspicious for clinically significant prostate cancer. The aim of the system implementation is in particular: • increasing the quality and standardisation of prostate MR evaluation, • support for the early detection of clinically significant findings, • reduction of variability between evaluators, • streamlining the workflow of the radiology department, • support for multidisciplinary cooperation (radiology – urology). The system must not serve as a substitute for a doctor's clinical judgement; the final diagnostic decision is always made by an authorised healthcare professional.; The subject of this part of the public contract is the delivery, implementation, integration and operation of a software solution based on artificial intelligence intended for clinical decision support in the evaluation of chest X-ray images. The offered software must be a medical device within the meaning of Art. 2 para. 1 of Regulation (EU) 2017/745 (MDR) and must be duly placed on the market in the European Union. The system is intended as a clinical decision-support tool for the detection and evaluation of pathological findings on chest X-rays. The system will be operated primarily at the Department of Imaging Methods and the Emergency Department of St. Anne's University Hospital in Brno and possibly at other workplaces of the contracting authority. The final clinical decision is always made by a healthcare professional.
sig_b498b4f3a2517da9153d.title: Software using artificial intelligence algorithms for clinical practice

sig_b4cb85529a2d918a2c26.description: The purpose of this combined Broad Agency Announcement (BAA) under Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Part 35 and Funding Opportunity Announcement (FOA) under 2 Code of Federal Regulations (CFR) 200.204 (henceforth referred to as “BAA”) is to solicit research proposals for submission to the U.S. Army Artificial Intelligence Integration Center (AI2C) for funding consideration. This Broad Agency Announcement (BAA), for the Army Artificial Intelligence Integration Center (AI2C), is issued under the provisions of paragraph 6.102(d)(2) and 35.016 of the Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR), which provides for the acquisition of basic, applied, and advanced research and that part of development not related to the development of a specific system or hardware procurement. This will be done through the competitive selection of proposals, and 10 U.S.C. 4001, 10 U.S.C. 4021, and 10 U.S.C. 4022, which provide the authorities for issuing awards under this announcement for basic, applied, and advanced research. The definitions of basic and applied research may be found at 32 CFR 22.105. Proposals submitted in response to this BAA and selected for award are considered to be the result of full and open competition and in full compliance with the provisions of Public Law 98-369, "The Competition in Contracting Act of 1984" and subsequent amendments. The Army Artificial Intelligence Integration Center (AI2C) is seeking artificial intelligence research and development whitepapers and proposals in support of new technologies and translational research-based approaches that support the identification, alignment, and exploitation of basic, applied, and advanced research. AI2C’s foundational research mission spans basic research (budget activity 6.1) and applied research (budget activity 6.2) as defined by 32 CFR 22.105 but may include advanced technology development (budget activity 6.3) and advanced component development and prototypes (budget activity 6.4) when opportunities arise to directly or indirectly help achieve AI2C’s mission. This publication constitutes a BAA for awards as contemplated in FAR 6.102(d)(2) and 35.016 as well as a merit-based, competitive procedure in accordance with the Department of Defense Grant and Agreement Regulations (DoDGARS) at 32 CFR 22.315(a) and the Office of the Under Secretary of Defense for Acquisition and Sustainment Other Transaction Guide version 2.0 dated July 2023.

SOLICITATION ANNOUNCEMENT: AN/BYG-1 APPLICATIONS The Department of the Navy, Naval Sea Systems Command (NAVSEA), on behalf of the Portfolio Acquisition Executive for Undersea (PAE Undersea) and the Director, Submarine Programs (DSP), is releasing the formal solicitation for the AN/BYG-1 Applications requirement from the Submarine Combat and Weapons Control Program Office (PMS 425). This notice follows the previously published Draft Request for Proposal (RFP) and Industry Day event. The Government has reviewed the feedback received during and after the Industry Day and has revised the requirements accordingly for this final solicitation. SCOPE OF THE REQUIREMENT (GENERAL OVERVIEW) AN/BYG-1 is the U.S. Navy’s Submarine Combat Control System. The AN/BYG-1 provides tools for the analysis of surface, sub-surface, and airborne contacts operating in the vicinity of own-ship and within the mission theater. This analysis supports command and decision-making, payload and attack control functions, determination of ballistic data for legacy torpedoes, and initiation of firing sequence for all payload types in support of submarine mission areas. The scope of this solicitation encompasses the development, testing, integration, delivery, logistics, and full-lifecycle sustainment of compiled AN/BYG-1 software baselines. This includes current, future, and legacy AN/BYG-1 applications as part of a modernized capability delivery framework. Key objectives and technical efforts under this contract include: Deliver AN/BYG-1 capabilities and baselines in alignment with Submarine Tactical Requirements Group priorities Decouple AN/BYG-1 applications from hardware and software dependencies Implement microcontainer/microservices AN/BYG-1 architecture Transform AN/BYG-1 development and test environments by increasing virtualization and establishing a common, shared infrastructure Develop and integrate tactical decision aids that leverage artificial intelligence and machine learning technologies Assist with the design, development, and integration of combat control system elements to support international cooperative agreements and joint programs. ACCESS TO SOLICITATION DOCUMENTS AND CLASSIFIED DATA The AN/BYG-1 Applications solicitation, Statement of Work (SOW), and associated unclassified attachments are designated as Controlled Unclassified Information (CUI) and will not be posted directly to SAM.gov. These documents will be made available exclusively via the secure Electronic Technical Information Center (E-TIC) portal hosted by the Advanced Interactive Management Technology Center (AIMTC). Additionally, portions of the Government Furnished Information, specifically, the classified software source code provided to support proposal development are classified at the SECRET level and will be transmitted physically. Documents made available during this procurement may contain classified data and/or technical data whose export is restricted by the Arms Export Control Act. Foreign participation shall be limited by applicable legal authorities, regulations, and other security classification requirements as specified in the DD Form 254. Consolidated Access Request Instructions Prospective Offerors must submit a single, consolidated access request email to the Points of Contact listed below to obtain E-TIC portal access and the classified GFI software package. Email Attachments Required: DD Form 254: A completed copy of the DD Form 254. Block 6 must verify that the requesting company possesses a Defense Counterintelligence and Security Agency (DCSA) issued SECRET facility clearance (FCL) and SECRET safeguarding capability. CRITICAL SECURITY NOTE FOR AWARD ELIGIBILITY: While a SECRET FCL is sufficient for proposal preparation and GFI access, the Offeror must ultimately possess a fully adjudicated TOP SECRET facility clearance and TOP SECRET safeguarding capability, issued by the U.S. Government, no later than contract award. The Government will not sponsor facility clearance upgrades or personnel clearance upgrades for the purpose of proposal submission or contract award eligibility. DD Form 2345: A current, approved copy of the company’s DD Form 2345 (Military Critical Technical Data Agreement). Executed Terms of Use Agreement (TOUA): A signed copy of the TOUA, executed by the Offeror's Facility Security Officer (FSO) or authorized corporate representative. Email Body Requirements: Subject Line: Format as N00024-26-R-6222 Access Request - [Insert Company Name]. Company Info: Provide the Company Name and active CAGE Code. E-TIC Representative: Provide the full name, official company email address, and phone number of the designated individual who will serve as the E-TIC account holder. Classified Media Request (Yes/No): State explicitly whether your company is requesting delivery of the classified software source code. Classified Mailing Info (Required only if requesting Classified Media): Provide the name and contact information of the company's FSO, along with the verified Classified Mailing Address of your facility as registered in the National Industrial Security System (NISS). If your company is NOT requesting the classified source code, please state "Not Applicable" or "N/A" for these fields. E-TIC Portal Registration (Unclassified/CUI Documents) Once the Government approves the consolidated request, the designated E-TIC representative must complete their account setup on the AIMTC portal. Access requires a DoD Common Access Card (CAC) or an approved DoD External Certification Authority (ECA) Certificate, along with an active Joint Certification Program (JCP) registration number. For New AIMTC Account Requests: Visit https://aimtc.nuwc.navy.mil and complete the AIMTC Account Request Form. For Existing AIMTC Account Holders: Log into https://aimtc.nuwc.navy.mil, click “My Profile”, and update your fields exactly as follows: Name: First name, middle initial, last name. Foreign National: Select "Yes" or "No". Email Address: Official company email only (no Gmail, Yahoo, etc.). Branch or Code: PMS425 Phone Number: Requestor's direct phone number. NUWC Sponsor POC: Eun-Ja O. Rau NUWC Sponsor Code: PMS425 Justification: "Prospective Offeror for the PMS425 AN/BYG-1 Applications" Scroll down, expand “E-TIC (Electronic Technical Information Center)”, select "BYG-1 Applications Solicitation", provide your justification, and click “Send.” For AIMTC account issues, contact AIMTC_Webmaster@us.navy.mil. Please note that you will not be able to access the PMS425 AN/BYG-1 Applications until your account request is approved by the Approval Official and processed. Please allow for processing. If E-TIC access has not been granted within five (5) business days of your initial email package submission, please contact the Points of Contact listed below for status. The proposal due date will not be extended due to late or incomplete access requests. Over the course of the procurement, the Government may provide E-TIC updates or additional materials to the same designated company representative. Transmission of Classified Media (Software Code) Upon successful verification of the Offeror's FCL, safeguarding capabilities, and NISS mailing address provided in the consolidated email request, and formal approval of the Offeror's E-TIC access (including receipt of the executed TOUA and approved DD Form 2345), the Government will package and transmit the classified media in strict accordance with 32 CFR Part 117 (NISPOM). Classified material will be dispatched via USPS Registered Mail (or Government-approved commercial express carrier authorized for Secret transport). A double-envelope system will be utilized. The outer envelope will feature no classification markings. A signed Classified Material Receipt will be enclosed in the inner envelope. The Recipient must execute and return this receipt to the Government within five (5) business days of delivery. PROPOSAL SUBMISSION Proposals in response to this solicitation must be submitted electronically via the PIEE Solicitation Module no later than October 19, 2026, at 1600 (4:00 PM) Eastern Daylight Time. Detailed instructions for proposal preparation and submission are specified in Section L of the solicitation document provided on the secure E-TIC portal. SUBMISSION OF QUESTIONS AND COMMENTS All questions and comments regarding this solicitation must be submitted using the Offeror’s Question Submittal Form in its original Excel format. Weekend/Holiday Rule: If the twenty-fifth (25th) calendar day falls on a Saturday, Sunday, or Federal Holiday, the deadline is automatically extended to 1600 (4:00 PM) Eastern Time on the next consecutive business day. Questions received after this designated deadline will not be considered or answered. sig_b510d6e57398d64501e6.description: The Provincial Act (Provinciewet), the Municipalities Act (Gemeentewet), the Water Authorities Act (Waterschapswet) and the Act on Public Bodies BES include the obligation to offset any incidental income of actively serving, full-time political office holders. The manner in which data on incidental income must be provided and the consequences of failing to provide this data are regulated in the legal status decrees. The offsetting is carried out using an application by the administrative body (or administrative bodies) where the political office holder is or has been employed in the previous calendar year. The contract to be put out to tender relates to the provision of a helpdesk where questions from contact persons and political office holders regarding the execution of the calculation of the incidental income of these decentralised political office holders for the purpose of offsetting income from non-office-related secondary positions are answered. The agreement lasts a maximum of 12 years and its scope is €70.000-€80.000 per year. The maximum scope thus amounts to €960.000

sig_b520decbe8b7969a9634.description: Enhanced Information Service for Emergency Calls (EISEC) or caller line identification (CLI) enables fire control room operators to confirm the caller's location swiftly. This is a critical first step in the call handling process, since the line could be 'cut', leaving the location unknown. EISEC technology provided by call handling agencies allows the billing address of the phone from which emergency calls are being made to be displayed to the control room operator. This speeds up the information process. This technology can also be used to locate the whereabouts of mobile phone callers, identifying the cell network from which they are calling. Additional information: Provides Location of caller on emergency lines

Within the investment objective "DigiTEL Green Pilot Project - Retrofitting of the 220/110/20 kV Mostiștea substation as a digital substation concept with low environmental impact" – Procurement 1, the following contract objects have been defined: • Object 1 - Sub-object 1.1: Electrical Substation; - Sub-object 1.2: Related Systems (Digital Twin, Augmented Reality, Robotic Assistance/inspection and drones); • Object 5 – The electronic security system (ESS) of the objective and the fire security system (FSS); • Object 6 – The photovoltaic system. The detailed description can be found in the tender documentation. Number of days by which clarifications can be requested before the deadline for the submission of tenders: 22 The contracting entity shall respond clearly and completely to all requests for clarification / additional information in two stages, as follows: - on the 17th calendar day from the publication of the contract notice and - on the 11th calendar day before the time limit for the submission of tenders. The contracting entity shall respond only to requests for clarifications addressed by economic operators by the established time limit. 1.1 Object 1 – Retrofitting of the Mostiștea substation This object consists in turn of two sub-objects and the corresponding Specifications: 1.1.1 Mostiștea electrical substation The 220 kV substation shall be of outdoor type, with air insulation, implemented with conventional equipment, located on the decommissioned surface of the current 220 kV substation. The 110 kV substation shall be of indoor type, equipped with enclosed switchgear panels, with air/technical gas insulation, in three-phase construction. The 20 kV substation shall be located in the building of the current medium voltage substation. In this project, two new, independent auxiliary services units have been provided, namely a direct current (d.c.) unit and an alternating current (a.c.) unit respectively, as follows: • a d.c. auxiliary services unit supplying the d.c. consumers of the 220 kV, 110 kV, 20 kV substation, autotransformers AT1, AT2 and transformer units T1 and T2 110/20 kV; • an a.c. auxiliary services unit supplying the a.c. consumers of the 220 kV, 110 kV and 20 kV substation Within the work "DigiTEL Green Pilot Project - Retrofitting of the 220/110/20 kV Mostiștea substation as a digital substation concept with low environmental impact", the technical condition module will be implemented in accordance with the Smart Grid reference architecture, for asset management at the level of the Mostiștea substation, called "Condition Monitoring System (CMS)". In the telecommunications field, within this project the following shall be performed: • ensuring the technical equipment for data and/or voice transmissions (HW&SW) necessary for: o carrying out the traffic required by the EMS/SCADA System; o remote control of the substation from the CTSI/DET level; o monitoring and parameterisation of protection systems from the level of the SSCPA of the Bucharest Branch and the DEN headquarters; o data-voice transmissions for operation and maintenance needs; o ensuring telecommunication facilities for the control of the substation; o the interzonal oscillation monitoring system (synchrophasors); o ensuring the transmission channels for metering data, local metering and power quality data. o ensuring hardware redundancy for interfaces that receive/transmit data and/or voice, which require this. o creation of telecommunication facilities to ensure the voice and/or data traffic requirements due to the emergence of a new Integrated IT/Information System, provided, at this stage, to be composed, in principle, of the following Systems:  Components/Sub-systems of the Asset Management System in Procurement 1 of the project:  AR, Digital Twin and PIA  BMS (also receives information from SIS - Integrated (Physical) Security)  Integrated (Physical) Security; • provision of technical equipment for cybersecurity (HW&SW); • provision of transmission equipment for teleprotection (HW&SW) Construction and installation works related to the performance of retrofitting works in the 220/110/20 kV Mostiștea substation as a digital substation concept with low environmental impact: The new control block building will be a ground floor + 1 storey construction, designed according to the nZEB concept and as an intelligent building. Within this project, a dedicated building management system (BMS) architecture will be provided at the level of the Bucharest Branch, capable of integrating both the local BMS from the Mostiștea substation and the future BMS systems belonging to the other electrical substations under the management of the Bucharest Branch. The BMS system to be implemented in the Mostiștea substation will have the following integrated: • The control block; • The 110 kV GIS building; • Old medium voltage building; • Relay containers and photovoltaic installation container; • Perimeter lighting in the substation. 1.1.2 Related systems: I. Digital Twin and Augmented Reality – consisting mainly of: • equipment (hardware and/or software), (re)configurations, services, tests/measurements and works in:  The 220/110 kV Mostiștea Substation;  Bucharest Branch;  CNTEE Transelectrica SA Head Office. • integration/interfacing with the telecommunications infrastructure; • integration/interfacing with the systems in the 220/110/20 kV Mostiștea electrical substation from which it retrieves data/information, mainly:  Condition Monitoring System;  BMS; • integration into the Beneficiary's existing and new installations. II.• Substation robotic inspection assistance (Intervention and Assistance Platform - PIA). In the 220/110/20 kV Mostiștea substation, advanced monitoring solutions will be implemented by developing inspection and analysis platforms that include both physical robots, such as drones and hardware robots, and software robots, capable of improving monitoring, maintenance and intervention processes.

1.5 Object 5 – "Electronic Security System (ESS) of the site and Fire Security System (FSS)" The 220/110/20 kV Mostiștea substation shall be provided with the ESS+FSS Integrated Security System. 1.6 Object 6 – Photovoltaic System Within the investment project "DigiTEL Green Pilot Project - Retrofitting the 220/110/20 kV Mostiștea substation as a digital substation concept and with low environmental impact", considering the nZEB building and energy efficiency requirements as well as the transition to GIS technology of the 110 kV substation, on the surface of the current 110 kV substation cleared following the retrofitting, a ground-mounted photovoltaic system shall be implemented, with photovoltaic panels mounted on a metal structure, and with the related equipment mounted in a dedicated metal container. Estimated contract execution duration - 40 months according to the execution schedule in the specifications.

sig_b62fed6617ef5e4b3bf0.description: Description Essex Record Office (ERO) is seeking to engage with the market to understand available solutions and supplier capabilities that can support the modernisation of its archive management, digital preservation and public access services. ERO is undertaking this Preliminary Market Engagement (PME) exercise to inform future procurement activity and ensure that any proposed solutions align with the organisation's statutory responsibilities, service requirements and long-term digital preservation ambitions. ERO is looking to understand the market's ability to provide solutions that can deliver the following outcomes: • Replacement of the current in-house developed Archive Management System (SEAX), which underpins over 80% of ERO's operations and public-facing services, including income-generating online services. • The archive management system will need to: o facilitate viewing the catalogue on-site at Essex Record Office locations and online o provide free access to digital and digitised collections on-site at Essex Record Office locations o provide online access, outside of ERO locations, to digital and digitised collections via a subscription service o facilitate the creation of user accounts with role dependent security/access levels o provide a paywall to access certain collections o manage the personal data of users of the service, including taking payments from them • Support for statutory archive, records management and civil registration functions. • Secure, scalable and standards-compliant digital preservation capabilities to support the long-term preservation, integrity and accessibility of digital records. We require a solution for preserving digital records with retention periods of 100 years or more, as well as potentially shorter retention periods. The solution must be able to deal with a variety of file formats including proprietary software files and a range of sound and moving image files. • Progression towards National Digital Stewardship Alliance (NDSA) Level 4 digital preservation maturity. Specifically, we require: o For digital records storage: three copies in at least two geographic locations (storage will need to be in the UK or EU) o A means of controlling, auditing, and recording file permissions o A means of recording sufficient metadata about the files using an appropriate metadata standard e.g. METS (Metadata Encoding and Transmission Standard), PREMIS (PREservation Metadata: Implementation Strategies), BagIt (BagIt File Packaging Format) and/or Dublin Core o Periodic integrity checking and disaster simulation, and a means of regularly updating the results of these checks o A means of recording details of people and software that have accessed or taken preservation actions on files. • Improved management and discovery of digital assets through modern digital asset management capabilities. • Enhanced public access, search and discovery through modern online archive and catalogue services. • Improved customer journeys and increased public engagement. • Support for current income generating services and potential for enhanced income generation opportunities. • Integration capabilities with existing and future corporate platforms and digital services. • Modern, intuitive and user-friendly interfaces for both staff and public users. As a minimum, we will need: o The ability to allow members of the public to access suitable digital preservation files o A means of providing redacted access copies of the content where necessary o A means of recording when files have been accessed and by whom o A means of ensuring the content is protected from unauthorised changes and any loss • Scalable architecture capable of supporting current digital holdings of 88.8TB and significant future growth over the coming decades. • Strong governance, audit, compliance and security features to support statutory and regulatory requirements, including the Public Records Act, Freedom of Information legislation and Data Protection requirements. Background Archive Management System It is estimated that over 80% of the work of the ERO is currently managed through an in-house developed tool called SEAX. SEAX was created by Essex County Council as a bespoke system. It was created over 25 years ago in a now archaic programming language. Seax Explorer was written in VB (Visual Basic) and uses forms to create the different screens of its various modules (e.g. Catalogue Manager, Accession Manager, etc.). These forms have been written in a custom language based loosely around XML and are stored within the Seax Explorer database. The online element of the system is known internally as Seax PAM and to the public as Essex Archives Online. This includes our online catalogue and income-generating subscription service and income-generating single-image service. Seax PAM was written using .NET framework and C# and is currently using an old version of .NET framework. We are seeking a modern, sustainable and future-proofed solution for managing our requirements for accessioning, cataloguing, storage locations, document production, reader management and user access (at the ERO and online). The ERO has a staff of around 25 people. Up to 12 users are likely to require login access to the staff side of the AMS, including generic logins for Searchroom staff, document production staff, volunteers, etc. Digital Preservation As of July 2026, the ERO has 88.8TB of digital data. This figure is expected to grow at an estimated rate of 5TB per year. Within the 88.8TB of data, 3.3TB consists of born-digital records; the other 85.5TB being content the ERO has digitised from its manuscript, image, sound and video collections. This data is all currently stored on Microsoft Azure Cloud Storage. Most of the content is listed in basic form on a spreadsheet. Detailed metadata at file level is being added as resources allow. Further documentation about rights is kept in separate filing and on our archive management system (alongside information about our paper and analogue collections). The ERO has a dedicated ingest PC through which we process digital collections as they arrive. We are able to take images of disks using ISO Buster software, transfer files as they are or transfer them to a file format with greater longevity. Transfers can be made using Teracopy software and we can interrogate the files we receive using TNA’s Droid software. The main element of NDSA (National Digital Stewardship Alliance) Digital Preservation Level 1 we are not currently achieving is the requirement to have two complete copies of our digital content in separate locations. Our aim is to progress through the NDSA digital preservation levels to meet NDSA Level 4. Areas of Interest ERO is particularly interested in understanding solutions relating to: • Archive Management Systems (AMS) • Digital Preservation Management Systems (DPMS) • Digital Asset Management Systems (DAMS) • Preservation storage and hosting solutions • Public catalogue and online archive access platforms • Migration services from legacy archive systems • Integration and API capabilities Contract Considerations At this stage, ERO is seeking supplier feedback on: • Appropriate contract lengths and commercial models • Implementation and migration timelines • SaaS, cloud-hosted and hybrid delivery models • Opportunities for phased delivery across AMS, DPMS, DAMS and public access capabilities • Scalability to support long-term digital preservation requirements. The information gathered through this PME will help shape ERO's future procurement strategy, solution design and business case development. Lot 1: .

sig_b6910da06f7879fe555e.description: 1. The subject of the contract is the supply, including placement, installation and commissioning, of water supply infrastructure equipment for the Dziadkowice Municipality, as well as the supply and implementation of a remote water meter reading system. 2. The subject of the contract has been divided into 2 parts and includes: 2.1. Part 1 – the supply and installation of 65 above-ground hydrants DN80, 33 gate valves (DN200 – 4 units, DN150 – 24 units, DN100 – 5 units), a water dispenser including commissioning, and the purchase, planting and maintenance of 110 trees. 2.2. Part 2 – the supply and replacement of 751 water meters with remote reading modules (DN15 – 80 units, DN20 – 650 units, DN25 – 8 units, DN32 – 9 units, DN50 – 2 units, DN100 – 2 units), the supply of equipment, software, licences, system implementation, integration with the WODA system, tests, documentation and training. The Contracting Authority allows for the submission of a tender for one or both parts and does not limit the number of parts that may be awarded to one Contractor. 3. The detailed scope, technical parameters, locations, method of installation, acceptance and documentation are defined by the Description of the Subject of the Contract (OPZ), technical designs and the projected contract provisions specific to a given part – Annex 1A to the SWZ. The Beneficiary declares compliance with the DNSH principle; the contractor is obliged to carry out deliveries in a manner that ensures the maintenance of this compliance and to provide the required evidence. Requirements concerning Part 1 The scope of Part 1 includes in particular: 1) the supply of complete equipment and materials; 2) the dismantling of existing elements; 3) the execution of earthworks and assembly works; 4) the performance of required tests; 5) flushing and disinfection; 6) surface restoration; 7) the execution of required signage; 8) the preparation and handover of as-built documentation; 9) the commissioning of the water dispenser; 10) the execution of plantings including their maintenance during the warranty period – in accordance with the OPZ, design documentation and technical designs. Within the scope of Part 1, the Contractor shall obtain the required consents, arrangements and permits related to the occupation of the road lane or the introduction of traffic management, shall provide the required signage and site security, and shall bear the associated costs. Warranty – minimum 24 months for the supplied equipment. The warranty period for gate valves and hydrants is one of the tender evaluation criteria. The detailed scope, technical parameters, locations, method of installation, acceptance and documentation are defined by the OPZ, technical designs and the projected contract provisions specific to a given part – Annex 1A to the SWZ.; Requirements concerning Part 2 The scope of Part 2 includes in particular: 1) the supply of brand-new water meters and radio modules compatible with them; 2) the dismantling of existing water meters; 3) the installation and sealing of new water meters; 4) the performance of test readings; 5) the implementation and commissioning of the remote reading system; 6) the supply of a collection kit and required IT equipment; 7) the provision of required licences; 8) the migration or import of data from the WODA system (INFO-SYSTEM Groszek) used by the Contracting Authority; 9) the performance of required tests; 10) the preparation and handover of documentation; 11) the conduct of instructional training on the operation and maintenance of the supplied equipment and system; 12) The Contractor shall agree with the Contracting Authority on the principles for contacting water consumers and the dates for water meter replacement. Consumer data may be provided to persons performing the replacement only to the minimum extent necessary and using secure communication channels.; 13) With regard to each water meter whose replacement requires agreeing on a date with the owner or tenant of the premises, the Contractor shall make at least three documented contact attempts, including at least one after 15:00 on working days or on a Saturday. After three unsuccessful attempts, the Contractor shall hand over to the Contracting Authority, on the basis of a report, the unused set: the water meter together with the assigned radio module. In such a case, only the price of the supply of this set shall be settled, without remuneration for the dismantling and installation service.; 14) The warranty for water meters and radio modules is at least 60 months, and its extension is one of the tender evaluation criteria. For the remaining equipment, the remote reading system, integration and software, the Contracting Authority requires at least 60 months of warranty, service or support – appropriate to the nature of the service. sig_b73609a1959d2a08b811.description: Dolwen Residential Care Home is a 32-bedroom facility that was built in the 1960s. It is struggling to meet the complex needs of citizens who require residential care. The purpose of the project is to provide premises that are fit for purpose, modern and accessible, and which have sufficient space for current and future provision. It will use digital technology and Artificial Intelligence. It will be well-located to provide care closer to home and meet the health and care needs of local people, including unmet needs, i.e. provision for the elderly who are mentally frail, and support service delivery within the building itself and in the local community. At present, the following issues need to be addressed at Dolwen home: - Small rooms which limit the service provider's ability to meet the needs of residents; for example, there are rooms that are suitable for hoists, but this is not the case throughout the facility. This restriction limits who can be provided with accommodation, depending on their needs. - None of the rooms are en-suite, and they do not offer sufficient living space or the facilities expected by modern standards. - The service provider is struggling to meet complex needs, which means it is not possible to provide accommodation for patients as they would like. A wide range of factors influences the proposal: - an expected increase in the older population of Denbighshire to 30.9% by 2040; including the fact that current facilities will not be suitable for the needs of residents; improving service provision; bringing services closer to the community; improving current provision for older people and the need to overcome limitations such as access, space and parking, and meeting Denbighshire's challenge and goal to be carbon neutral by 2030. This project, which is led by Denbighshire County Council (DCC) in collaboration with Community Housing, Denbighshire Voluntary Services Council and Betsi Cadwaladr University Health Board, is a project to review the potential development of Dolwen Residential Care Home. The project proposes an extension and modernisation work for Dolwen, including: - Residential capacity for the mentally frail elderly, i.e. developing a dementia wing. - Providing an extra care lite model in the older people's housing facility bordering Dolwen, in partnership with Community Housing. - A hub and spoke model of community support on an outreach and in-reach basis in conjunction with Community Housing and Denbighshire Voluntary Services Council. - Upgrading and modernising the current residential facility from 32 to 50 beds. This will include an extension and will enable the current accommodation to be redeveloped to ensure that it meets future complexity needs, e.g. a hoist in every room and en-suite facilities. - Improving current dementia support provisions in the community of Denbigh and the surrounding area. sig_b73c43bfb419c9e44341.description: EUROMOD is the tax-benefit microsimulation model of the European Union (EU), which covers in a consistent manner the tax-benefit systems of all EU Member States. The model allows to study the effects of taxes and social benefits on household incomes and work incentives for the population of each country and for the EU as a whole. EUROMOD is unique in its area as it features great flexibility in the scope of its simulation and ensures cross-country consistency of the modelling approach and comparability of the results. The model is widely used by the Commission services in the European Semester context and other EU policy initiatives. Additionally, the model represents a valuable research infrastructure for the academic community in the area of fiscal policy analysis, with highly cited research conducted using EUROMOD being published in top journals. The contracts are intended to provide the Commission with services that support the development and update of the microsimulation model EUROMOD for 26 EU country-specific modules. The modules are as follows: Lot 1: Support to EUROMOD for Austria Lot 2: Support to EUROMOD for Belgium Lot 3: Support to EUROMOD for Bulgaria Lot 4: Support to EUROMOD for Croatia Lot 5: Support to EUROMOD for Cyprus Lot 6: Support to EUROMOD for Czechia Lot 7: Support to EUROMOD for Denmark Lot 8: Support to EUROMOD for Estonia Lot 9: Support to EUROMOD for Finland Lot 10: Support to EUROMOD for France Lot 11: Support to EUROMOD for Germany Lot 12: Support to EUROMOD for Greece Lot 13: Support to EUROMOD for Hungary Lot 14: Support to EUROMOD for Ireland Lot 15: Support to EUROMOD for Italy Lot 16: Support to EUROMOD for Latvia Lot 17: Support to EUROMOD for Lithuania Lot 18: Support to EUROMOD for Luxembourg Lot 19: Support to EUROMOD for Malta Lot 20: Support to EUROMOD for Netherlands Lot 21: Support to EUROMOD for Poland Lot 22: Support to EUROMOD for Portugal Lot 23: Support to EUROMOD for Romania Lot 24: Support to EUROMOD for Slovenia Lot 25: Support to EUROMOD for Spain Lot 26: Support to EUROMOD for Sweden

sig_b74505fae1d50624d50e.description: Northern Trains Limited, is a Train Operating Company (TOC) that operates passenger rail services in the North of England. Northern Trains Limited is publishing this notice to establish a contract for the supply of Train Planning (Timetabling & Diagramming) software and implementation services. The nature of the arrangement is that the software and implementation services will be supplied under NTL's IT Services Agreement. NTL will award a contract under either of the following scenarios: (1) A contract will be awarded to the top scoring supplier under Lot 1, or (2) A contract will be awarded to the top scoring suppliers in Lots 2 & 3. Accordingly the overall value of the Notice is reflective of this. Where used throughout this notice, the meaning of Train Operating Companies includes all and any of those train operating companies who, currently or in the future, provide services for the carriage of passengers by railway: a. under a franchise agreement with the Secretary of State within the meaning of section 23(3) of the Railways Act 1993 or b. under, or secured under, the Secretary of State's duty in section 30(1) of the Railways Act 1993; or c. in accordance with legislation which supersedes or amends the powers referred to in a) and b), including where such powers are transferred from the Secretary of State to another body. The list of current providers of services for the carriage of passengers by railway under these provisions can be found at https://www.gov.uk/guidance/public-register-of-rail-passenger-contracts. Novation or Assignment The contract may be novated or assigned by Northern Trains Limited to Train Operating Companies, or to DFT Operator Limited (company number: 07141122) or any successor parent company to a Train Operating Company, following a corporate restructuring or similar circumstance. Other Information Northern Trains Limited expressly reserves the right: i. not to award any suppliers the contract referred to in this notice; and ii. in no circumstances will the customer be liable for any costs incurred by the suppliers. Lot 1: Train Planning Software - Single Platform. NTL is seeking to procure a single solution that will be used by the Service Planning department to deliver the following capabilities: •Planning and development of timetables for submission to Network Rail. This does not include the allocation of specific units. The successful supplier will be required to implement the solution in line with the following: •Full production implementation of a system by March 2027, with a period of parallel running completed prior. •A system and operational cutover before or during March 2027, with no material impact on the BAU activities and capabilities of the NTL Service Planning department. Fidelis Elevate technology is a key security element of MHMP, which ensures the detection of cyber events, their investigation, mitigation and remediation. Currently, MHMP operates Fidelis Elevate to the following extent: o Fidelis Elevate Network 1Gbit - provides in-depth analysis of network traffic at L2 - L7 layers with a retention of 90 days; o Fidelis Elevate Endpoint - analyses endpoint behaviour (5 300). The subject of this public contract for MPP is: a) supply of Fidelis Appliance XA4 (HW) – 2 units; b) supply of Fidelis Network Sensor (HW) – 1 Gbit; c) related licences to the extent of: o Fidelis Elevate Network 1Gbit (retention 60 days) incl. manufacturer support for a period of 36 months; o Fidelis Elevate Endpoint (1 400 endpoints) incl. manufacturer support for a period of 36 months; o Fidelis Elevate Deception – 501 IP addresses incl. manufacturer support for a period of 36 months; d) provision of operational support for the system according to the Catalogue Sheets for Fidelis technology for a period of 36 months; e) development work to the extent of 100 man-days (MD) for the duration of the Contract; f) exit services to the extent of 5 MD. ('VoKB') and the regulations and methodological guidelines of the NÚKIB.

sig_b7d7def91dc097edaa1c.description: Procurement of a UCC solution for the State of Hesse The project comprises a modern and comprehensive communications solution that integrates numerous central components. The following expectations are placed on the tendered service: In the area of telephony and voice (formerly HessenVoice), contemporary voice communication is provided that replaces and expands existing systems. In addition, the softphone functionality enables telephony to be used directly via PC or mobile end devices without the need for additional hardware. Webex is currently used as the web conferencing solution (VKS); however, the solution should also support future developments and hybrid working forms in the best possible way. In addition, chat and messaging functions create a secure and efficient platform for text-based team communication. High requirements apply to security and data protection as well as accessibility in order to offer all employees secure and inclusive access to the solution. The operator model defines clear responsibilities and processes for operation, while accompanying training measures support the introduction and foster acceptance. The solution will be fully compatible with the HessenPC and enable secure, high-performance access via the HessenNetz connection. Another component is the provision as a price-per-port Full Managed Service, which impresses with transparent pricing and comprehensive service management. Manufacturer neutrality is respected in order to avoid dependencies and ensure long-term flexibility and openness to competition. The procurement and implementation of the tendered UCC solution takes place with special consideration of the requirements for information security, data protection and interoperability with existing authorities' infrastructures. For use in public administration, compliance with the compendium for internal organisational telecommunication systems with an increased protection requirement (KomTK ) published by the Federal Office for Information Security (BSI) must be ensured. This guideline defines binding security measures - including technical, organisational and infrastructural requirements - for telecommunication systems with an increased protection requirement and serves as a benchmark for the planning, operation and safeguarding of the offered solution. The protection of personal data is a central criterion in the selection and implementation of communication systems. The legal requirements of the General Data Protection Regulation ("GDPR") and the Hesse Data Protection Act ("HDSIG") provide for safeguarding the rights and freedoms of data subjects and consistently implementing data protection principles - such as lawfulness, purpose limitation, data minimisation, accuracy, storage limitation, integrity and confidentiality. While Unified Communications solutions are primarily designed for applications with a normal protection requirement in accordance with the specifications of the Federal Office for Information Security ("BSI") when using cloud components, there are scenarios in which a higher level of security is required. In cases where a higher level of security is required, an on-premise system is frequently used, which is operated entirely within the own IT infrastructure and can thus better meet the requirements for a high or very high protection requirement. By operating in a controlled environment, a higher degree of control over data flows, access protection, encryption as well as emergency and recovery measures can be ensured. Unified Communications and Collaboration (UCC) solutions represent a central component of modern IT infrastructures and serve the integrated networking of a wide variety of communication and collaboration services. In order to meet the operational requirements for reliability, security, scalability and interoperability, specific technical prerequisites are indispensable. These requirements form the basis for the selection, implementation and operation of a high-performance UCC solution that ensures efficient and uninterrupted cooperation within the organisation. In order to bring about rapid project success, close cooperation between the contractor and the contracting authority is necessary. The contractor MUST closely coordinate with internal and external stakeholders on the part of the contracting authority as part of the implementation in order to take account of necessary and inevitable interactions with other systems of the contracting authority (e.g. firewall, network, etc.) as early as possible in the implementation of the project and to implement necessary adjustments and interventions on these systems as smoothly and time-critically as possible. The service contents presented in this specification MUST be provided by the contractor for the contractually defined period in full and with ultimate responsibility for the outcome, flexibly according to the respective needs of the contracting authority in the form of a "Managed Service". Within the scope of this tender, special emphasis is placed on the accessibility of the Unified Communications and Collaboration (UCC) solution to be supplied. Accessibility means that the solution can be used unrestrictedly and equally by all users, regardless of individual impairments or restrictions. This includes in particular people with visual, hearing, motor or cognitive impairments. The detailed service requirements can be found in the respective chapters of the service specification (Chapters 1 - 7).
sig_b7d7def91dc097edaa1c.title: Procurement of a UCC solution for the State of Hesse

sig_b88b90a90c1e247f6069.description: The Ogden Air Logistics Complex (OO-ALC) at Hill Air Force Base, Utah, intends to issue a solicitation to provide comprehensive management and supply of aircraft coatings and sealants. This effort aims to ensure uninterrupted aircraft maintenance operations through robust inventory management, timely delivery, and technical support. This effort will include frequent ordering and quick delivery on specified items. The selected contractor will be responsible for continuous deliveries and support of Coatings and Sealants, including: 1. Order Fulfillment and Material Handling: Sourcing, storing, and delivering all required coatings and sealants (see attached list). This includes meeting a strict four (4) hour delivery timeline for urgent requirements and handling specialized materials, such as Premixed Frozen Material (PFM) requiring transit at -80F. The contractor must maintain a minimum of 85% shelf life for all products upon delivery. The contractor will also be responsible for managing shelf-life and ensuring proper storage and handling of the products prior to delivery. 2. FMS-3600 Coating Management: For this specialized product, implementing a lock and key ITAR-compliant storage system and maintaining rigorous chain of custody for the material. 3. Technical Assistance: Providing technical assistance that includes rapid response (within one business day) to material failures, on-site technical support during monthly visits, product change support, and quality audit reporting. 4. Online Ordering System: Furnishing a secure, web-based ordering and tracking system with real-time visibility of lead times and minimum stock levels (MSLS). 5. Ramp-Up Plan: Executing a ramp-up plan to achieve full performance readiness within eight (8) months of contract award. The anticipated contract will be a Firm Fixed Priced (FFP) IDIQ to include an 8-month ramp up period, a 5-year ordering period, and a 6-month allowance for remaining deliveries on the back end. Total period of performance is anticipated to be 6 years and 2 months. This is a total small business set-aside. The Government anticipates awarding a single contract. All interested small businesses are encouraged to respond. The official solicitation will be posted on SAM .gov. The Government intends to award a single contract resulting from the upcoming solicitation to the responsible offeror whose proposal represents the best value to the Government. This effort requires Contractors to be CMMC level 2 self-certified, therefore if you are not currently level 2 certified and are interested in this requirement you will need to begin the process to become level 2 certified immediately. The solicitation draft documents are attached. Dates on the solicitation are subject to change based on the actual award date. Please review and submit any questions or suggestions to the point of contacts on this 15-day synopsis. The anticipated solicitation number is FA8224-26-R-0010 (subject to change). sig_b89bf65f484706260e7c.description: The RMO is undertaking a process to incorporate AI into Road Asset Management practises in Ireland, in key areas such as image recognition, autonomous data analysis, technology and applications. The Road Management Office (RMO) intends to run a competitive procurement process for the establishment of a Multi Supplier Framework for the provision of Artificial Intelligence (AI) Road Pavement Condition Rating and associated Road Asset Survey Services in 2026. This will result in the establishment of a Framework Agreement available for use by framework clients . As part of this process the RMO is undertaking an analysis of market capabilities, technologies and systems available, processes currently in use, and general market dynamics. Our aim is to establish a fit for purpose Framework Agreement for the provision of Artificial Intelligence (AI) Road Pavement Condition Rating and associated Road Asset Survey Services for the proposed term 2027 to 2031. Please note that this is not a tender competition and we are not seeking tenders at this stage, it is purely an information gathering exercise seeking the views of market operators on possible approaches that may be taken in any potential tender process.

sig_b8df9178fb2e1adf6314.description: UHS is seeking to engage with interested parties to discuss and refine an opportunity to become a strategic endoscopy partner to the Trust. UHS provides a regional endoscopy service to a population of 3m+, offering a comprehensive range of diagnostic and therapeutic interventions. Following a fire earlier this year, UHS has reviewed its long-term endoscopy requirements and is considering a new purpose-built regional diagnostic endoscopy centre situated close to the main hospital. UHS has existing endoscopy equipment to the value of approximately £8-10m. This will need to be refreshed throughout this contract. UHS has an indicative budget of £20-25m for the design and construction of the new centre. This will be designed to meet current and projected future endoscopy and motility needs, 'a one-stop-shop' and be an important centre to both trial new technology and techniques and provide training for the next generation of the endoscopy workforce. This opportunity is to explore and discuss how a partnership approach may drive better outcomes for patients, for innovation, for UHS clinicians, and for the partner[S(1.1][L(1.2]. This opportunity may include, but not necessarily be limited to: 1: Provision of endoscopy equipment to a new offsite location, both for the use of clinicians undertaking NHS clinical activity, and for use as a test bed for innovation and new technique development, and for use within a training environment. 2: Regional Training Centre: The physical co-location of experienced UHS staff, clinicians, data, patients with an industry partner seeking to promote best practice and create future workforce. 3: Joint Innovation Deal & Test Bed: The provision of a live, data-rich NHS environment to validate new technology, and techniques, for example artificial intelligence (AI) diagnostic tools and ergonomic designs and potentially the exploitation of emerging shared Intellectual Property. This would also include SME and VCSE participation for research and innovation. 4: Commercial Sponsorship Opportunity with Associated Rights and Benefits: In addition to the core procurement opportunities above, there is potential to explore a complementary commercial sponsorship arrangement, which may include the provision of value-in-kind goods and/or services that support contract delivery. This strategic partnership approach would identify and agree a range of associated rights and benefits for suppliers who also become sponsors. These may include appropriate sponsor recognition, opportunities for collaboration and innovation, shared learning, thought leadership engagement, and other mutually agreed activities that support the objectives of all parties. UHS, with support from the Department of Health and Social Care (DHSC), is trialling the integration of commercial sponsorship into this procurement opportunity to explore how strategic partnerships can deliver additional value while supporting the successful delivery of contract outcomes. Whilst this notice is not intended to create a commitment to a contract, it is running alongside a live funded NHS capital project to develop designs and take forward the concept of a regional endoscopy centre. This hybrid procurement and sponsorship model is being piloted by the Department of Health and Social Care (DHSC) and UHS, offering potential suppliers a unique opportunity to play an active role in delivering a best-in-class new facility for patients: supporting improved care, championing innovation and delivering lasting benefits for all parties. To ensure fair and open competition in any future procurement, the developing design and specification will remain supplier-neutral and will not be tailored to any specific manufacturer, supplier or solution.
sig_b8df9178fb2e1adf6314.title: Co-Developing the 'Digestive Disease Centre' at University Hospital Southampton, Hybrid Procurement and Sponsorship Opportunity

sig_b901c8042d6d2634044a.description: This Assignment is financed from official Danish development assistance through the Danish Africa Water facility (Danish Finance Act § 06.32.01.32). Emphasis is therefore on providing safe and affordable access to water for all (Sustainable Development Goal 6.1), increase water-use efficiency and ensure freshwater supplies (Sustainable Development Goal 6.4) and to raise capacity for planning and management of climate change (Sustainable Goal 13.5). The Ministry of Foreign Affairs, Royal Danish Embassy, Nairobi (RDE) is the funding agency and Water Resources Authority (WRA) is the Recipient of the outcome of the Assignment. The Assignment aims at operating with a high level of local content by engaging local partners with the view of increasing the long-term sustainability of digital systems and ease of their future maintenance as well as enhanced dialogue on water use with local communities. The Water Resources Authority (WRA) is a state corporation established under Section 11 of the Water Act, 2016 and mandated to regulate the management and use of Kenya's water resources on behalf of the national government. WRA formulates standards and regulations, issues and enforces water permits, sets water-use fees, and advises the Cabinet Secretary on national water-resource policy. WRA operates through a decentralised structure comprising one head office, six basin offices, 26 sub-basins, eight laboratories and three satellite offices. WRA is currently undertaking the development of an Enterprise Architecture as part of the Government’s Digitization of Government Services Performance Contracting initiative, in alignment with the Government Enterprise Architecture framework and applicable Government ICT standards. Kenya has a comparatively clear formal water-resource governance architecture, but implementation is constrained by incomplete coordination across national, basin, county and sub-catchment levels, limited basin and sub-basin resources, and overlapping institutional interfaces. WRA already operates digital permitting, e-billing, smart-metering, hydrological monitoring, GIS and laboratory systems; however, these features remains fragmented and have not yet been demonstrated to provide an end-to-end authoritative record linking the water user and abstraction point to the permit, meter, reading, invoice, payment, inspection and hydrological context. The core information-management challenge is not the absence of digital systems, but their fragmentation across field monitoring, permitting, metering, billing, enforcement and hydrological decision support. WRA is working to create integrations between its various IT solutions, but the vision for this project is to support components in establishing a single point of entry/IT solution—hereinafter referred to as WRIMS—that will ensure integration among all existing IT solutions, as shown in the diagram below and elaborated in the background document on WRA’s existing IT environment. The Assignment regarding Improved Data Collection, Monitoring and Revenue Base for Water Resource Management in Kenya (hereafter “IMPRODATWRM”) is expected to be designed to close the institutional and information-management gap while strengthening WRA's own-source revenue base and the evidence available for sustainable allocation. The Assignment is to support WRA in transforming its fragmented digital landscape into an integrated, interoperable WRIMS environment that connects the full operating chain - from registration and permitting through meter/device management, reliable measurement, validation, billing, payment reconciliation, inspection and enforcement, and will connect these regulatory transactions to basin-level hydrological information. Shared identifiers, GIS references, data-governance rules and interoperable interfaces are essential across this chain. The Assignment is to support WRA in transforming its fragmented digital landscape into an integrated, interoperable WRIMS environment that connects the full operating chain - from registration and permitting through meter/device management, reliable measurement, validation, billing, payment reconciliation, inspection and enforcement, and will connect these regulatory transactions to basin-level hydrological information. Shared identifiers, GIS references, data-governance rules and interoperable interfaces are essential across this chain. The Assignment will align with and leverage the resulting business, data, application, technology and security architectures to guide the design and implementation of WRIMS, while supporting the operationalisation of the EA, particularly in systems integration, interoperability, data governance, ICT infrastructure and cybersecurity. The Assignment is divided into three phases: Phase I: Detailed verification, system analysis and preparation Phase II: A Kenyan-led option assessment and decision Phase III: Design, build, test, roll-out and stabilised operation

sig_b98b33aafd7fb1d67d5d.description: The procurement includes the replacement of existing mechanical locks, as well as delivery, installation, commissioning of a new and complete electronic locking system, including lock cylinders, digital keys and the accompanying access control administration system. A framework agreement shall be signed with one tenderer for a period of two years, with an option for an extension for 1+1 year, so that the maximum total contract period is four years. Product The estimated need for the entire framework agreement period is 600-800 lock cylinders and 15-20 keys. The key system can either be based on physical keys or digital access via the app, depending on the offered system. The contracting authority plans to make a first call-off immediately after the contract has been signed. This call-off is expected to include replacement at approx. 200 installations, equivalent to approx. 400 locks. The stated volume is an estimate, and the contracting authority reserves the right to increase or reduce the volume within the contract ́s limits if budgetary conditions, capacity or progress require this. Services Installation of cylinders is included in the contract. The service contract is not included in the contract. The operation of hardware (cylinders and keys) is included in the operations contract that the Agency for Urban Environment has on technical traffic installations (26-BYM-2025) and in future equivalent agreements. The software/cloud service of the locking system. The procurement is for the licence, operation and support of the software. The contract also includes the establishment of the lock system, including training of the administrator, the construction of an account and access structures in cooperation with BYM.

sig_b995ddcaa48c6826f568.description: Open-quantity framework agreements are concluded for development services required by DB Systemtechnik. DB Systemtechnik works on extremely demanding digitalisation projects in the field of rail vehicle technology. The project portfolio thus encompasses challenges of the entire railway system, i.e. rail vehicles, their components, the infrastructure and the corresponding interfaces. For the initiation, definition, planning, control and successful completion of these technically demanding projects, DB Systemtechnik is looking for experienced partners with broad methodological expertise and industry know-how for consulting and project management services.; DB Systemtechnik uses various sensors, measurement and data loggers to acquire, process, transmit to the land side and evaluate process, diagnostic and operating data from rail vehicles and railway assets. For the development of customer-specific and standard assemblies based on embedded technology and railway-compatible measurement and sensor modules, DB Systemtechnik is looking for development partners and suppliers. The services cover all steps, from conception to the approval-ready hardware product that can be implemented in the vehicle by the client, including the necessary basic software. The suppliers are experienced in the development of railway-approved embedded hardware and software and have established certified development and production processes. They master documented series-delivery and quality processes and are experienced in supply chain and obsolescence management in the railway sector.; Within the scope of digitalisation projects in the railway sector, DB Systemtechnik develops customer-specific products which, among other things, require the development, modification and operation of specific applications. For this purpose, suppliers and development partners are sought who can efficiently develop reliable, robust and secure software solutions and use structured and proven development methods and certifiable development processes for this purpose. The suppliers have comprehensive knowledge and experience in the field of architecture, software development, CI/CD, software testing and quality assurance for embedded systems in critical environments. All software solutions must comply with the standards for approval in rail vehicles and operation in the railway sector.
sig_b995ddcaa48c6826f568.title: Developer service provider pool for DB Systemtechnik

sig_b996bbc49a913244c444.description: This pre solicitation is conducted under the logistic cost sharing (LCS) program. The Government anticipates issuing a solicitation for the purchase, installation, and integration of DoD Anti-Ram Listed Active Vehicle Barrier (AVB) systems and associated Access Control Point (ACP) control systems at the Morin and Main Gates, Osan Air Base, Republic of Korea (ROK). Under this commercial acquisition, the Contractor shall be responsible for the demolition, removal, and disposal of existing AVBs; executing all necessary foundation, civil, and electrical site work; and performing the complete installation, point-to-point wiring, and power integration of the newly furnished equipment. Additionally, the Contractor must execute complex Programmable Logic Controller (PLC) reprogramming and system integration across multiple gatehouses, overwatch booths, vehicle inspection centers, traffic lights, and communication enclosures to achieve a fully synchronized, fail-safe ACP operation capable of maintaining full security functionality under both normal and power-loss conditions. The Performance Work Statement (PWS) containing all specific technical, execution, and commissioning requirements is attached for upcoming solicitation.
sig_b996bbc49a913244c444.title: ACTIVE VEHICLE BARRIERS AND ASSOCIATED CONTROL SYSTEM AT OSAN AIR BASE

sig_b9e44041454269a4f2c0.description: Digipolis is looking, for the City of Antwerp among others, for a partner responsible for the supply, installation and maintenance of: • Sensors and reading out the current fill level of small-volume waste systems such as paper bins and other (waste) systems; • Software to monitor the current fill level of (waste) systems, predict the fill-level evolution based on historical measurement data and then plan the complete and most optimal route for collection vehicles to carry out emptying. In doing so, the available vehicles must be deployed optimally in the field depending on the required capacity for emptyings. This software is used for both existing, already installed sensors and sensors to be installed in the future. It is not the intention to replace all existing sensors. However, all sensors, existing and new, must be consultable in a single software system. The software must also be able to include unique, self-chosen collection points, e.g. for collecting illegal dumping, in the route calculation. The purpose of this contract is to achieve optimal emptying taking into account personnel, working time, vehicles, weight, volume, consumption, CO2 emissions, costs and traffic situations. The contract is divided into two lots: • Lot 1: framework agreement for the supply, installation and maintenance of sensors for above-ground waste systems and paper bins including real-time API with sensor data. • Lot 2: framework agreement for offering a software solution as described above. • Lot 1: framework agreement for the supply, installation and maintenance of sensors for above-ground waste systems and paper bins including real-time API with sensor data.; • Lot 2: framework agreement for offering a software solution as described above.

sig_b9f714354b6d0c2112d2.description: Room booking software for desk sharing It is intended to introduce software for workstation and room booking in the desk sharing areas of the City Administration of Chemnitz. The system is intended to support flexible configuration of bookable resources (workstations, meeting rooms, possibly also vehicles). This should not only be booking software but also an optimisation of workspace, and therefore an evaluation function should also be available. A total of approx. 1.800 resource-based licences are required, which can be used by a total of approx. 5.000 users. The subject of this contract consists of works supervision services and project management consultancy services during the implementation of the project "Rehabilitation of Pod Roș – Anastasie Panu tram lines". The project "Rehabilitation of Pod Roș – Anastasie Panu tram lines" is composed of 2 items: - Item 1 - "Rehabilitation of Pod Roș – Anastasie Panu tram lines", respectively - Item 2 - "Extension of Pod Roș – Anastasie Panu tram running track". Within item 1 - "Rehabilitation of Pod Roș – Anastasie Panu tram lines", it is proposed to rehabilitate the infrastructure and superstructure of the tram running track, on the section between Pod Roș and Anastasie Panu street up to the intersection with Sfântul Lazăr street. Within item 2 - "Extension of Pod Roș – Anastasie Panu tram running track", it is proposed to extend the tram line from Podu Roș on the section between the intersection of Palat street with Sfântul Lazăr street, respectively Sfântul Lazăr street with Anastasie Panu street. The general objective of the project is the reduction of carbon emissions in county capital municipalities through investments based on urban mobility plans. The main objectives are the rehabilitation of the infrastructure and superstructure of the tram running track on the section between Pod Roș and Anastasie Panu street up to the intersection with Sfântul Lazăr street and the extension of the infrastructure and superstructure of the tram running track on the section between Pod Roș - Sfântul Lazăr street intersection with Anastasie Panu street in the Municipality of Iași. As a result of correlating the two objectives, it is proposed: - the rehabilitation of the infrastructure and superstructure of the tram running track, on the section between Podu Roș and Anastasie Panu street - in the Municipality of Iași by transforming Anastasie Panu street (from the intersection with Sf. Lazăr street) and Palat street into a one-way street descending towards Podu Roș which will include the dedicated descending lane for buses and trams; - moving the wire corresponding to the tram's descending direction, the Anastasie Panu street – Palat street – Podu Roș direction to the curb; - the wire corresponding to the ascending direction will have the route Podu Roș – Sf. Lazăr street – Sf. Vineri pedestrian passage (intersection of Sf. Lazăr St. with Anastasie Panu St.), - the dismantling of the running track from Piața Palat street and its arrangement as a pedestrian area; - establishment of a single running track on Sfântul Lazăr street, positioned on the left side of the street, near the curb. sig_baf88bfdde099b508258.description: The Bundesbank manages four staff canteens under its own management. The management of a further eight Bundesbank canteens is carried out by external caterers under contract management. For the canteens under its own management, the Bundesbank uses an inventory management system and a checkout/payment system on its own infrastructure (cash or direct debit for internal employees; cash for external employees and guests). The checkout/payment system is integrated into the Bundesbank's SAP landscape. Orders to suppliers are placed by PDF/email; a B2B connection is not available. In daily operations, many steps are currently carried out manually or twice due to a lack of integrations. The same checkout/payment system is used in the contract-managed canteens (including integration into SAP), but inventory management is carried out independently by the caterers outside the Bundesbank's IT landscape. The inventory management system and checkout/payment system are outdated, meaning that the Bundesbank has initiated a project to replace these systems with a SaaS solution. With this new SaaS solution, which is then to be introduced in the following one to two years, modern payment methods (cards, mobile end devices, digital euro) are to be introduced alongside cash and direct debit. In addition, the solution is to be B2B-capable in order to enable a B2B connection of suppliers. Further focus is placed on automation and digitalisation in order to significantly reduce manual effort, e.g. during stocktaking, and the associated sources of error. In the course of this strategic alignment, Deutsche Bundesbank is initiating a structured market exploration. The aim of this measure is to systematically determine the performance and suitability of the SaaS-based gastro-system platforms available on the market (inventory management with checkout and payment system). In particular, it is to be examined to what extent the existing service portfolios of the providers meet the technical, legal, organisational and security requirements of Deutsche Bundesbank. A key focus is inter alia on: - Support for modern payment methods (cash, direct debit, cards, mobile end devices, digital euro) - B2B capability including connection of suppliers - Integration capability into the Bundesbank's SAP landscape - Functions for automation and digitalisation (e.g. for stocktaking) - Operation as SaaS in a BSI C5-certified cloud - Use both in canteens under own management and contract management - German-language project management, support and documentation This market exploration also serves to involve the market at an early stage in a potentially upcoming EU-wide procurement procedure by Deutsche Bundesbank for the procurement of the described services and forms, amongst other things, a basis for decision-making for its technical design. This market exploration is not a procurement procedure directed at the award of a public contract and constitutes neither an offer nor an invitation to conclude a contract. The execution of a procurement procedure, including with a different service scope, remains reserved. Participation in this market exploration has no consequences for the participating company (neither preference nor disadvantage) in the context of a potential future procurement process. Participants in this market exploration have no entitlement to the acquisition of knowledge from the results of the market exploration. Further details on Deutsche Bundesbank's requirements for the SaaS solution described above are available exclusively upon request to the stored e-mail address: Projekt-GastroSys@bundesbank.de
sig_baf88bfdde099b508258.title: Market exploration: GastroSys - SaaS solution for gastronomy systems of Deutsche Bundesbank
