sig_bb832c82657f27a49cef.description: This Competition forms one of three (3) proposed programmes (outlined below) under Enterprise Ireland’s new National Accelerator Programme, a flagship initiative under Startup Ireland as part of Enterprise Ireland’s "Delivering for Ireland, Leading Globally (2025-2029)" strategy. Enterprise Ireland will use the Panel as and when requirements within their scope arise. However, there is no obligation upon Enterprise Ireland to use the Panel in every instance. Should the circumstances arise, the Panel as a whole may be terminated in accordance with the Panel terms and conditions. The Panel may also be employed for the award of accelerator related programmes connected with new sectoral / specialist needs in response to industry developments, trends and new technologies. To this end Enterprise Ireland will exercise its sole discretion in determining whether new accelerator programmes come within the sector or specialist area initially indicated by Applicants. Panel Members may be requested to deliver accelerator programmes falling within the scope of the panel either fully, partially, or variations of same including delivery of accelerator programmes which are closely related. Enterprise Ireland currently has a requirement for an AI Specialist Accelerator Programme and therefore intends to award an Initial Call-Off Contract immediately following the establishment of the Panel. Applicants should note that the closing date for the call for initial work is Monday 7th of September 2026 @ 12 Noon Irish Time. Applicants, who are in the AI specialist area, are requested to submit, with their Application for admission on to the Panel, a separate tender response (“Response”) to the Supplementary Invitation to Tender published with this Panel Application. The Response to the Supplementary Invitation to Tender should be submitted via the eTenders post-box facility on www.etenders.gov.ie only, as a separate document. Responses to the Supplementary Invitation to Tender must use the response document issued with the Supplementary Invitation to Tender. For the avoidance of any doubt Applicants (in the AI specialist area) are not required to submit a response to the Supplementary Invitation to Tender. The full scope of requirements under this Panel can be found in the Panel documents.
sig_bb832c82657f27a49cef.title: 2026/006 Establishment of a Panel for the coordination, design, implementation, and training for the National Start-up Accelerator Programmes – Sectoral/Specialist

sig_bbaa67d3434176080901.description:
The subject of the contract is to ensure access to data from electronic information resources (hereinafter also referred to as "EIR"), which serve as a source of information for the needs of conducting scientific research and the development of science within the Slovak Republic. The subject of the contract is to ensure access to data from bibliographic and bibliometric electronic information resources for a period of 48 months, which serve as a source of information for the needs of conducting scientific research and the development of science within the Slovak Republic, as well as for the needs of recording publication activity and evaluating science. Society-wide order As part of ensuring science and research and responding to the needs of securing scientific and technical tasks in all science and research institutions in Slovakia, as well as in connection with the provisions of Decree of the Ministry of Education, Research, Development and Youth of the Slovak Republic No. 397/2020 Coll. of 5. December 2020 on the central register of publication activity records and the central register of artistic activity records, the electronic information resource Web of Science "or equivalent" must meet the requirements demonstrating the suitability of the database as a specific source of information with a defined structure and content for the evaluation of science and research and the registration of publication activity of higher education institutions in the Slovak Republic. The contracting authority also allows for an equivalent solution to the Web of Science databases that meets all the parameters listed below. 3. Specification of the subject of the contract – minimum scope: The bibliometric citation database is to be a multidisciplinary database that provides an exceptionally broad view of published scientific works, and thus of science and research on a global scale. The bibliographic and bibliometric database must offer tools for sorting, refining and rapid identification of results, with a focus on the results of work in the fields of science, technology, medicine, social and human sciences and the arts. These are the following database titles: Web of Science Core Collection or equivalent: A bibliographic database serving as a primary source for searching for renowned scientific information and evaluating scientific publication activity. In terms of content, it must cover journal titles, books and conference proceedings from at least 200 subject categories, from natural, technical, medical sciences to arts and humanities for tens of thousands of peer-reviewed scientific journals (including open access journals and Early Accessed documents, i.e. a version made available before it is published by the publisher). The database must further contain conference proceedings and book data. The database must allow for the establishment of benchmarks for evaluating science worldwide, which serve to evaluate and compare the results of scientific publication activity based on transparent and globally accepted criteria. The database must allow for citation tracking, which shows how often and by whom each publication has been cited (among others, an extensive citation network of scientific publications and cited references in the Web of Science Core Collection). The Web of Science Core Collection must contain at least: • Science Citation Index Expanded (SCIE) or equivalent, • Social Sciences Citation Index (SSCI) or equivalent, • Arts & Humanities Citation Index (AHCI) or equivalent, • Emerging Sources Citation Index (ESCI) or equivalent, • Conference Proceedings Citation Index or equivalent, • Book Citation Index or equivalent....... A detailed description of the subject of the contract is defined in the tender documents; The subject of the contract is to ensure access to data from an electronic information resource – a database, for a period of 48 months, which serves as a source of information for the needs of conducting scientific research and the development of science within the Slovak Republic. 3. Specification of the subject of the contract – minimum scope: The ProQuest Central Premium Package "or equivalent" database must have multidisciplinary content across all major subject areas of academic research and teaching while also including subject-specialised content at least to an extent comparable to a solution that integrates 8 specialised disciplinary collections / solutions in a single search environment. We require that the ProQuest Central Premium Package "or equivalent" database provides access to at least 8 collections composed of databases from all scientific fields including economic sciences, healthcare and medicine, social sciences, arts and humanities, education, natural sciences and technology, agricultural sciences, religion, philosophy, linguistics and literature. The collection must contain full texts from at least 12 000 scientific journals, at least 2 000 economic and professional journals. The electronic information resource must provide access to at least 1 500 newspaper and journal titles. It must also include dissertations and theses, case studies, market and economic reports, pre-print versions of working papers, video recordings, all on a user-friendly platform with simple and intuitive operation and with artificial intelligence support. Required basic quantitative indicators: • at least 35 000 titles, of which at least 20 000 with full texts. • on the Ebook Central platform or "equivalent" at least 240 000 e-books with full text. • at least 75 % of titles in the English language, international content in other national languages including, for example, Spanish, French, German, Portuguese and others. According to individual document types: • scientific and professional periodicals (including peer-reviewed), • newspapers and current news, • economic analyses at the industry and state level and company profiles, • research reports and conference proceedings, • dissertations and theses, • electronic books, • case studies for economic (and applied natural) sciences, • multimedia content (video recordings), • bibliographic and abstract databases............................. A detailed description of the subject of the contract is located in the tender documents;

The subject of the contract is to ensure continuous online access to a scientific electronic information resource of the CAS SciFinder Discovery Platform type or an equivalent solution for authorised users of the contracting authority and institutions designated by it for a period of 48 months. The information resource must provide an integrated web environment for searching and professional work with scientific literature, patents, chemical substances, chemical reactions, analytical methods, formulations, regulatory data and supplier information in the fields of chemistry, pharmacy, biochemistry, biomedicine, materials science and related disciplines. 3. Minimum functional requirements The information resource must enable in particular: a) searching in professional literature, patents, chemical substances, reactions and related scientific data by keywords, author, organisation, patent, chemical name, molecular formula, chemical structure, substructure, structure similarity, CAS RN registration number or equivalent identifier, b) support for natural language searching, relevance ranking of results, combined text and structure searching, filtering, sorting, saving, exporting results and creating alerts, c) searching, comparing and evaluating chemical reactions including experimental procedures, reaction conditions, yields, catalysts, solvents, atom mapping and linking to related substances and publications, d) retrosynthetic planning and design of synthetic pathways including comparing alternative procedures, taking into account the availability of starting materials, yields, costs and available patent information, e) searching and comparing analytical methods, experimental protocols or bioanalytical procedures, f) working with formulations, components, commercially available products, supplier and regulatory information, g) working with citation and reference links between documents, substances, reactions and patents............. A detailed description of the subject of the contract is defined in the tender documents

sig_bbb72442a0ca7d3eb273.description: THIS IS A PTAG SOURCES SOUGHT REQUEST FOR INFORMATION (RFI) ONLY. This PTAG 6.1.1 Sources Sought (request for information) Notice (RFI) is strictly for market research ONLY.? It is for informational and planning purposes and shall NOT be construed as a solicitation or as an obligation or commitment by the Government at this time. PTAG The Government contemplates utilizing the Alternative Competition Method in accordance with the Patent and Trademark Office Acquisition Guidelines (PTAG) and the Patent and Trademark Office Efficiency Act 35 U.S.C. 2(b)(4)(A). This Sources sought notice is intended as preliminary market information gathering which the United States Patent and Trademark Office (USPTO) will use to determine which contractor(s) is/are the most likely to successfully meet the agency’s needs and are thereby eligible to participate in an alternative competition. As a result of this market research, the?solicitation will only be issued to the/ those qualified contractor(s) that is/are deemed most likely to successfully meet the agency’s requirements as stated below. This RFI is being made available under PSC U008 - EDUCATION/TRAINING- TRAINING/CURRICULUM DEVELOPMENT and NAICS: 611430 - Professional and Management Development Training REQUEST FOR INFORMATION – PTA TRAINING CONSULTATION, ELEARNING & DELIVERY BACKGROUND The United States Patent and Trademark Office (USPTO) intends to make a firm-fixed price award to a single firm that can fulfill this requirement which includes three (3) major elements. Training Consultation for Program Revision; Development of eLearning Content; Training Delivery Support Services. USPTO’s Patent Training Academy is the training program responsible for preparing new hires to be patent examiners. It is designed to give new examiners the skills, knowledge, and confidence they need to begin their careers. In FY 2026, USPTO hired 963 new examiners. Currently, the training program is delivered over 10-weeks and is comprised of a 125-course curriculum. The program follows a university-style model that uses a mix of large-lectures and small group lab sessions to give examiners opportunity to apply what they have learned. Through a combination of the use of a practice training application, active learning exercises, lecture and dedicated examination time, the goal of the program is to provide patent examiner new-hires the needed competencies to successfully examine in a Technology Center (TC) with guidance from experienced examiners. OBJECTIVE The objective of this RFI is to seek capable contractors who could provide the USPTO with Training Consultation for Program Revision, Development of eLearning Content, and Training Delivery Support Services. REQUIREMENTS: Training Consultation for Program Revision: The USPTO seeks firms with experience in instructional design consultation services, to include: Expertise in instructional design and adult learning theories and principles. Experience providing solutions to enhance engagement and learning in large training programs with extensive curriculums, specifically more than 40 courses in a single curriculum. Experience with providing innovative solutions including AI to enhance learning and taking complex, detailed curriculum and transforming the curriculum to provide faster acquisition of job skills and application of content. Ability to work with subject matter experts to refine learning objectives and ensure content alignment with learning objectives for highly complex legal and examination procedure topics. Ability to work with subject matter experts to review and revise course activities for highly complex legal and examination procedure topics. Ability to work with subject matter experts to review and revise course pedagogy for highly complex legal and examination procedure topics. Ability to work with subject matter experts to guide the assessment of learning objectives and outcomes. Experience in providing consultation services for legal content. As directed, develop training content and related deliverables. Development of eLearning Content: The USPTO seeks firms with experience in the development and implementation of eLearning content, to include: Expertise in the design of eLearning content, using standard eLearning authoring tools such as Articulate Storyline 360, Adobe Captivate, etc. Expertise in incorporating instructional design and adult learning theories and principles to eLearning content. Experience in building in adaptive gamification into eLearning content. Experience in designing microlearning content. Ability to work with subject matter experts to ensure the design correctly represents legally accurate materials. Experience in incorporating clean visuals, graphics, and ensuring 508-compliance of all materials. Experience in graphic design, visual clarity, and technical writing to ensure clear instructions and flow of all eLearning content. Experience in intuitive, learner-centered design. Experience in clearly defining design processes, to include steps in design processes, timelines, and checkpoints for subject-matter expert review. Ability to convert 25 courses into eLearning modules in 3 months. Courses range from 1 hour to 2.5 hours’ worth of content. Training Delivery Support Services: The USPTO seeks firms with experience in the implementation of Training Delivery Support Services, to include: Experience providing training in person and online, using agency collaboration tools such as MS Teams. Experience in ensuring best practices in engagement and adult learning theory are incorporated into training delivery. Ability to deliver training on all agency examination processes, procedures and tools accessing patent applications, in-house tools for searching US and Foreign Patents that allow examiners to generate correspondence to applicants, case management tools. Ability to deliver professional training that is consistent with USPTO standards to support professional development to USPTO patent examiner employees. The training must be conducted by a variety of means including in person, in a classroom or lecture setting, and/or using agency collaboration tools such as MS Teams. Please state if you have specific experience with intellectual property (IP), patent examination, and patent prosecution processes. Experience in ensuring continuity in training to avoid re-scheduling of training classes. sig_bc36d4f46e434011d441.description: It is the ambition of the Welsh Government to develop a thriving and confident agriculture sector in Wales built around innovation and growth, to rise to the challenges we face and make most of the opportunities available. In July 2025 the Welsh Government published its Sustainable Farming Scheme designed to ensure Welsh Government support for agriculture in Wales delivers against the four Sustainable Land Management objectives of the Agriculture (Wales) Act: - Produce food and other goods in a sustainable manner - Mitigate and adapt to climate change - Maintain and enhance the resilience of ecosystems and the benefits they provide - Conserve and enhance the countryside and cultural resources, promote public access to and engagement with them, and to sustain the Welsh language and promote and facilitate its use. Innovation will play a key role in delivering this scheme. In 2023, the Welsh Government published an Innovation Strategy for Wales. Innovation in food and Agri-Food Tech was seen as a key part of Wales’s future economic development. In late 2023, the Welsh Government published an Agri-tech action plan for Wales. The development and adoption of Agri-Tech and Precision Agri-Tech is a strategic area of growth for the Welsh economy and one the Welsh Government deems requiring of focussed attention and a road map for development. The action plan has four priorities: 1. Accelerate Home Grown Welsh Agri-tech Capabilities. 2. Drive on-farm adoption to achieve productivity and efficiencies (incl. Environmental) gains ‘more for less’. 3. Deliver environmental benefits and help transition to Net Zero. 4. Support educational and skills development to equip future and existing agricultural professionals to exploit Agri-tech to its fullest. SCOPE: Cattle mortality data may provide valuable information on animal health, disease emergence and herd management. However, there are opportunities to make better use of mortality data alongside wider animal health surveillance information to generate timely intelligence that supports veterinary decision-making, farmer engagement and evidence-based policy. Improving the collection, access, interpretation and communication of mortality intelligence could enable earlier identification of disease risks, encourage preventative herd health management and support the delivery of the Animal health and welfare framework | GOV.WALES for Wales, while contributing to the objectives of the Sustainable Farming Scheme. We are therefore seeking innovative technologies, digital tools, data-driven approaches or other novel solutions that improve the collection, integration, analysis and application of cattle mortality intelligence to support proactive animal health management. Lot 1: . None

sig_bc517cb3a5e61dfdbab5.description: The UK Government's Partnering for Accelerated Climate Transitions (UK PACT) programme is inviting proposals from qualified suppliers or consortia to deliver technical assistance to the government of Bangladesh. Bangladesh is establishing the foundations for participation in high-integrity carbon markets, including Article 6, CORSIA and voluntary carbon markets. While progress has been made through the establishment of a carbon market framework and supporting governance arrangements, further support is needed to operationalise these systems across government, strengthen institutional coordination, and enable Bangladesh to use carbon markets to support delivery of its NDC 3.0 unconditional mitigation targets. The assignment will provide targeted technical assistance and capacity building to strengthen Bangladesh's carbon market governance, authorisation processes, MRV, reporting and institutional readiness. Working with relevant government agencies, including MoEFCC, DoE, the Power Division, Ministry of Finance and other line ministries, the project will support practical implementation of carbon market rules, CORSIA readiness, UNFCCC reporting requirements, and inclusive, high-integrity market participation. Key outputs are expected to include governance and coordination tools, an authorisation and safeguards toolkit, CORSIA readiness and reporting support, a structured government capacity-building programme, and sector readiness briefs identifying future carbon market investment opportunities. The project aims to strengthen Bangladesh's ability to participate in high-integrity carbon markets, unlock climate finance, improve institutional capability, and support implementation of national climate targets. Interested suppliers are invited to review the documentation provided in this notice, and submit their applications to: targetedfund@ukpact.co.uk
sig_bc517cb3a5e61dfdbab5.title: Bangladesh Carbon Market Governance & Readiness Sprint

sig_bcc2350d3e85d43e278e.description: Negotiated procedure without prior call for competition. The delivery can only be carried out by a specific economic operator for the following reasons: absence of competition for technical reasons. Explanation: The award of the procurement of passenger counting sensors and the necessary adjustments to the MOBILEguide software can only be carried out by INIT GmbH, as there is no competition for technical reasons in accordance with § 13 paragraph 2 no. 3 b) SektVO. The defined requirements in their extensive abundance and combination cannot be met by any other potential tenderers. In this case, only INIT GmbH is able to fulfil the listed requirements. The on-board computers used on Rheinbahn vehicles originate from the company INIT GmbH. Only the company INIT GmbH possesses the necessary technical knowledge to carry out any system additions to the on-board computer software in order to be able to connect these to the central component of the ITCS of the Rheinbahn AG. In the absence of generally binding standardisation, the software of the central component of an ITCS and the software of the on-board computers used on vehicles in public transport only possess the same processes if they are procured from the same system manufacturer. The processes are manufacturer-specific standards and as such are subject to trade secrets; they are therefore not generally and freely available. In this regard, the company INIT GmbH possesses a unique selling point due to the existing on-board computers at Rheinbahn, which must be included. In the absence of generally binding standardisation, a bidirectional interface between the central ITCS and the on-board computers used on the vehicles as a mobile component of an ITCS is only fully functional if the participating interface partners are procured from the same system manufacturer. The interface is a manufacturer-specific standard and as such is subject to trade secrets; it is therefore not generally and freely available. In this regard, the company INIT GmbH possesses a unique selling point due to the existing on-board computers at Rheinbahn, which must be included. As a result of the examination for the procurement of the central components of the ITCS, it must be determined that the company INIT GmbH possesses a unique selling point regarding mandatory requirements to be fulfilled for the services to be procured. Consequently, a public call for competition would be misleading and the associated effort would be temporally and economically inappropriate for all market participants. The procurement law limits of the public contracting authority's freedom to define the scope of services are adhered to, provided that the definition is objectively justified by the subject matter of the contract, the contracting authority has provided comprehensible objective, contract-related and actually existing reasons for this, and the definition does not discriminate against other economic operators. An artificial and therefore impermissible restriction of competition does not exist. The date of the conclusion of the contract with INIT GmbH cannot be entered, as this day is only possible 10 calendar days after the publication of this notice. The procurement office cannot determine exactly at the time of entry when the period of 10 calendar days begins, as the publication is carried out by the Official Journal and generally takes several days that cannot be precisely determined. The procurement office therefore points out that the conclusion of the contract between the Rheinbahn AG and INIT GmbH will take place 10 days after the publication of this notice. Precise information on the deadlines for lodging appeals: §160 para. 3 GWB reads: The application is inadmissible insofar as 1. the applicant has identified the asserted infringement of procurement regulations before submitting the review application and has not complained about it to the contracting authority within a period of ten calendar days; the expiry of the period according to § 134 paragraph 2 remains unaffected, 2. infringements of procurement regulations that are recognisable from the notice are not complained about to the contracting authority by the expiry of the deadline for application or submission of tenders specified in the notice, 3. infringements of procurement regulations that only become recognisable in the procurement documents are not complained about to the contracting authority by the expiry of the deadline for application or submission of tenders, 4. more than 15 calendar days have passed since receipt of the notification from the contracting authority that it does not intend to remedy a complaint. Sentence 1 does not apply to an application for a declaration of the ineffectiveness of the contract according to § 135 paragraph 1 number 2. § 134 paragraph 1 sentence 2 remains unaffected. Name and address of the contractor: Official name: INIT GmbH Postal address: Käppelestraße 4-10; Town: Karlsruhe NUTS code: Karlsruhe Postal code: 76131 Country: Germany Internet address: https://www.initse.com/

sig_bce26bb82fff0b151fc2.description: Lot 1: Provide civil engineering services to support the maintenance of the existing fibre network infrastructure and assist with the design and construction of new customer connections and network extensions as required. Lot 2: Provide comprehensive network design and surveying services to support the deployment of fibre infrastructure Lot 3: Provide comprehensive GIS Design and Asset Management System services to support the deployment of fibre infrastructure. • Conduct detailed physical surveys of proposed routes and sites. • Assess existing infrastructure for suitability and compliance. • Develop high-level and low-level fibre network designs. • Produce accurate GIS/CAD drawings and associated documentation. • Identify and mitigate risks associated with design and deployment. • Provide structured project management, including progress tracking and reporting. • Deliver any additional services required to complete the design and survey process effectively.; sig_bd89e58073bcdb90ec3a.description: The purpose of the tender is to re-establish the SUF's existing dynamic purchasing system regarding IT consultancy services in the health sector, as the dynamic purchasing system is undergoing a renewed tender with minor adjustments compared to the old dynamic purchasing system due to a platform change. The tender for the dynamic purchasing system for IT consultants in the health sector is divided into the following 11 categories: Category 1 IT architecture in relation to the healthcare system and associated security components. Category 2 BI, management information, data analysis on health data. Category 3 Project management in relation to the procurement and implementation of health systems. Category 4 Advice and assistance for process and implementation in connection with health systems in a cross-sectoral perspective. Category 5 Advice within infrastructure, mobility, MDM and related strategy in the healthcare system. Category 6 Test management. Category 7 Data warehouse development, expansion and maintenance. Category 8 Development, expansion and maintenance of auxiliary programmes. Category 9 Advice and assistance for operation, system administration and maintenance of health systems. Category 10 Project Contract Management for IT contracts within the health and care sector. Category 11 Compliance regarding IT systems, processes and data within the health and care sector. Includes services such as, but not limited to, advice on IT architecture specifically in relation to the healthcare system, including special IT architecture and security issues regarding the handling and exchange of personal sensitive data in care systems. In addition, for example, advice within IT security issues in relation to national security components and cross-sectoral cooperation within the health sector.; Includes services such as, but not limited to, advice and data analysis specifically within the health sector and based on health data. The advice includes, among other things, qualification and delivery of management information based on data analysis as well as more general Business Intelligence on health data.; Includes services such as, but not limited to, project management for the procurement and implementation of health systems, including planning and management of user training for health staff, management of the relationship with, and deliveries from, internal and external technical suppliers.; Includes services such as, but not limited to, advice and assistance for processes in connection with the implementation of new health and care systems. The advice also includes, among other things, advice on the implementation of new health systems in a cross-sectoral perspective, where experience from sectors other than the municipal one (regional, general practitioners, etc.) can be utilised.; Includes services such as, but not limited to, strategic advice on the procurement, use and implementation of mobile devices in a health perspective as well as infrastructure such as WAN, LAN and WiFi. The advice also includes, among other things, advice on contractual and commercial conditions, including operation, SLA and market standards within the public agreement infrastructure (SKI and state agreements) in relation to procurements within the area.; Includes services such as, but not limited to, advice on and handling of test management in connection with the procurement and implementation of welfare technologies and health-related IT systems. In addition, the advice includes, among other things, test management specifically in relation to municipal use and interfaces to other sectors in the healthcare system.; Includes services such as, but not limited to, further development of existing data warehouse solutions in SUF as well as maintenance of the same, primarily based on, but not limited to, Microsoft SQL and SSIS. Development and maintenance also include, among other things, presentation of data analyses from health-related information in various welfare technologies and IT systems via dashboards and similar automated consolidated views of complex data.; Includes services within, for example, but not limited to, new or further development of existing or new auxiliary programmes in SUF as well as maintenance of the same. Development and maintenance include all auxiliary programmes that can help SUF in various contexts. This may cover programmes that take over sub-functions of previous systems or it may include full or partial new development of new programmes to cover special functions for the City of Copenhagen, Health and Care Administration.; Includes services such as, but not limited to, advice and assistance for operation, system administration and maintenance in connection with the implementation of new and old health and care systems. The advice also includes, among other things, advice on operation, system administration and maintenance of new and old health systems, where experience from other similar systems can be utilised.; Includes services such as, but not limited to, Project Contract Management for IT contracts within the health and care sector, including, for example, assistance with the optimisation of contract management of the covered contracts, help with the capitalisation of the contracts' potential, assistance with projects regarding IT procurements by, for example, EU tenders or mini-tenders on existing framework agreements or dynamic purchasing systems.; Includes services such as, but not limited to, advice, project management and executing tasks in connection with MDR, GDPR and NIS2, as well as other legislation in relation to IT compliance, including, for example, implementation of EU regulations and other legislation regarding IT compliance, assessment and interpretation of the legislation in question, executing tasks regarding compliance, project management in relation to the implementation of compliance.

sig_be106f643384cfe81f5f.description: The subject of the upcoming procurement is the design, delivery and implementation support services of an external service provider for TVET teacher training to be carried out in Ethiopia. The procurement supports the digital transformation of the country’s Technical and Vocational Education and Training (TVET) system as part of Specific Objective 2 (SO2) of the DESTA, Digital Ethiopia: Skills and TVET Action programme. The objective of the procurement is to strengthen the digital, pedagogical and institutional capacities of Ethiopian TVET teachers and teacher trainers so that they are able to deliver high-quality, learner-centred, gender-responsive and accessible digitally enabled vocational education. Particular attention will be paid to gender equality and the inclusion. The selected tenderer will be responsible for the design and delivery of the first training programme of a three-tier TVET Trainers’ Digital Competence Pathway: Foundation Programme in Digital TVET and Learner-Centred Pedagogy, while the three-tier programme also includes advanced-level training and a Training of Trainers (ToT) programme. The training programme will be delivered using blended learning modalities (face-to-face, distance and online learning) and will leverage Ethiopia’s national Moodle-based learning management system. The service package includes (based on preliminary information): • design and delivery of the training programme and implementation plans in cooperation with national stakeholders and EDUFI • design and production of an open online course on foundations of digital and learner-centred pedagogy • facilitation of trainings, workshops, mentoring and peer-learning activities • assessment of teachers’ competences and certification • strengthening of institutional capacity for the sustainable implementation of digital TVET education • management of travel costs and daily allowances for training participants. The procurement will be implemented in several regions of Ethiopia and will support broader national objectives related to education, employment and digitalisation, as well as the priorities of EU and Finnish development cooperation. GENERAL INFO Please note that this is a prior information notice (hereinafter referred to as 'the notice') and that this notice is not a call for tenders. The information provided in this notice is preliminary and may change as preparation progresses. The aim is to publish the final call for tenders in June 2026. REGISTRATION AND QUESTION TO POTENTIAL TENDERERS Potential tenders of this procurement are invited to send their contact details by e-mail to kilpailutus@hansel.fi with the subject line:"Digital training programmes for TVET trainers in Ethiopia – Market dialogue” In the registration email, participants are kindly requested to provide the following information: - contact details - responses to the questions outlined below 1. How will you integrate inclusion and gender-responsivity principles into the training content and delivery methods? 2. How will you integrate basic digital skills (LMS, etc.) into learner-centred pedagogy? 3. What team composition and expertise do you consider essential for designing and delivering this training and online course? 4. How would you structure and schedule the blended learning approach, balancing intensive face-to-face weeks in computer labs with remote learning periods? 5. How will you tailor the training content and delivery to address sector-specific digital technology needs (e.g., agriculture, hospitality)? 6. How will you incorporate and adapt the strengths of Finnish pedagogical practices to this context? 7. How would you organise payment transactions (managing travel costs and daily allowances) for training participants? Please send your participation and answer to the above questions at the latest on 12 May 2026. Answers may be submitted in English. The personal data of the registered persons will only be used for contacts related to this upcoming procurement. MARKET DIALOGUE The contracting authority reserves the opportunity to send a draft of the invitation to tender to potential tenderers for comments. In a so-called market dialogue, potential suppliers will be given the opportunity to comment on the draft material in writing.
sig_be106f643384cfe81f5f.title: Digital training programmes for TVET trainers in Ethiopia

sig_be66e1ff3b415b7ed9d0.description: Despite a growing awareness of the consequences of plastic pollution for the marine environment, there remains a persistent threat from ALDFG that is newly introduced into the marine environment or has in some cases already been present there for decades. The aim of UNSEA is therefore to systematically prevent the further input of ALDFG into the North Sea and Baltic Sea, reduce the negative ecological and socio-economic impacts, and identify and recover historical waste, particularly in ecologically sensitive areas. Both commercial, secondary and sports fishing in the North Sea and Baltic Sea are to be addressed. Excluded from the project scope are aquaculture and mariculture and inland fishing. Existing requirements and agreements of relevant national and international legal provisions are currently still fragmented, without financial backing and are partly up for discussion for various reasons. UNSEA is therefore intended to bring together the various sub-aspects in a coherent framework for action, focusing on the implementation of cost-efficient and operational measures. The aim is to rethink and holistically approach the handling of fishing gear waste from fishing, to anchor circular economy principles in the management of fishing gear, and in doing so also to address specific findings such as dolly ropes (scuff protection threads on bottom trawls) and net sections from repair work that are frequently found in the marine environment. Over its duration, the project is to provide the seed funding required for this and in parallel create long-term structures with clear responsibilities for continuation by the Federal Government and the Länder. For the first time, a cross-sectoral mechanism is to be established and implemented which also includes the exchange of knowledge and information. The project can build on existing legal frameworks, recommendations from research and politics, preparatory work within the framework of measure and action plans, and voluntary industry initiatives. In particular, the 2016 established Round Table on Marine Litter (RTM, www.muell-im-meer.de), which is coordinated by the Umweltbundesamt and the State of Lower Saxony, has already carried out comprehensive conceptual preparatory work that can be used as a basis for work for UNSEA. Through this, insights into the scale of the problem have been gained and suitable methods as well as existing and missing elements in the chain from search to environmentally sound recovery of ALDFG where possible have been identified. Furthermore, the results and recommendations of two pilot projects for the implementation of the recovery of lost fishing gear in Mecklenburg-Western Pomerania (MV) and Schleswig-Holstein (SH) are to be taken into account. While the project in MV has already been completed (https://www.wwf.de/fileadmin/fm-wwf/Publikationen-PDF/Deutschland/WWF-Abschlussbericht-Landesprojekt-Verlorene-Fischereigeraete.pdf), the publication of the final report of the SH project is expected for August 2026 with planned follow-up activities for the mapping and recovery of fishing gear waste. The work under UNSEA is to be closely coordinated with these activities in order to avoid duplication of effort.
sig_be66e1ff3b415b7ed9d0.title: UNtangling our SEAs (UNSEA) – A holistic solution approach to avoid the pollution of the marine environment with fishing gear

sig_beb84f55de3cf7b6e7a1.description: The City of Helsinki Employment Services Public Utility provides employment services to, among others, foreign-language clients who have no skills in Finnish or Swedish or whose skills are weak. Therefore, efficient interpretation solutions are required to support communication between the client and the guiding employee, ensuring that foreign-language clients receive the full benefit of the employment services. The City has existing interpretation service agreements in place for on-site and remote interpretation assisted by an interpreter. Consequently, the City of Helsinki Employment Services Public Utility is procuring an AI-assisted interpretation service. The interpretation service must be capable of providing interpretation in multiple languages. The service must utilise artificial intelligence to provide real-time interpretation. The interpretation service must be confidential and privacy-protecting (the City of Helsinki data protection requirements must be met and will be delivered separately later). The service must be easy to use for both clients and service providers, and the user interface can be used on various devices (computer, smartphone, tablet, etc.). The subject of the procurement is described in more detail in appendices 1 Service Description of the Subject of Procurement and 2 Requirement List.

sig_bec77b8d4fce0fcb4ce4.description: This public notice is a combined synopsis/solicitation for commercial items prepared in accordance with FAR Part 12 and utilizing FAR Part 15 procedures. The solicitation is being released as an Indefinite Delivery, Indefinite Quantity (IDIQ) contract competition. This contract shall include two performance areas to encompass all aspects of procuring new Digital Talking Book Machines and maintaining the new and existing stock at the Library. Performance Area 1 (PA1): DTBM DA2 Production, Parts, and Support This PA includes DA2 units, warranties, spare parts, software development, and other requirements described in Section C. NLS requires Digital Talking Book Machine (DTBM) version DA2 units in quantities sufficient to continue distribution to all audio readers enrolled in the program and maintain a reasonable stock to allow timely replacement of devices in the field to facilitate service, repair, or maintenance of removed devices. NLS requires support for those units including spare parts, software development, and warranty repairs. Performance Area 2 (PA2): Existing Device Support, Incumbent This PA includes proprietary spare parts and software development as described in Section C. NLS also requires repair and support services for the existing incumbent-manufactured NLS DTBM DA2 units (approximately 63,000). This includes spare parts and platform sprints to ensure the units remain safe, functional, and accessible so that the Library’s patrons have the fullest access to materials in the NLS collection. Please see all attachments for the full details of this requirement and instructions for submitting a proposal. Questions are due by 5:00pm eastern time, September 14, 2026. Proposals are due by 5:00pm eastern time, October 5, 2026.
sig_bec77b8d4fce0fcb4ce4.title: Digital Talking Book Machines - Library of Congress

sig_becd34ff8606e3c8f432.description: Social Service Time (MDT) is a programme of the Ministry of Education, Culture and Science, in collaboration with young people, social organisations, schools, municipalities and other ministries. During this programme, young people – between the ages of 12 and 30 – choose to develop their talents, meet new people and at the same time do something for someone else and/or society. In this way, the involvement of young people in society is increased. The nature of the assignment concerns all aspects of data handling required for carrying out the ongoing monitoring research. The purpose of the assignment is to collect data on young people and projects participating in Social Service Time (MDT). In addition to data collection, the data must also be managed and made accessible, monitored and managed, via multiple tools/files/dashboards/databases. The collected data is used to gain insight into the effects and impact of MDT. Maximum €3.303.000,- excl. VAT for an assignment with a duration of 2 years and the option to extend 2x by 1 years. sig_bf044cea98ad0eddb9c3.description: The subject of the procurement is the provision of maintenance and support services for telecommunications network devices and related network services (hereinafter the "Service"). The procurement covers comprehensive maintenance, monitoring, support and operational services for VR's telecommunications network environment, including network devices located in datacentres, offices, rolling stock (trains and buses) and other operational locations. The Service also includes the maintenance of certain related network services required for the operation of the telecommunications environment. The Service includes, but is not limited to, the following: - Service transition and implementation; - 24/7 monitoring of the telecommunications network environment; - Incident management and fault resolution; - Replacement of failed network devices in accordance with the agreed service levels; - Device configuration changes and other agreed maintenance activities; - Network monitoring, preventive maintenance and operational support; - Service management and designated service management personnel; - Maintenance of network documentation; - Reporting, including service level, capacity and operational reporting; - Integration with VR's agreed service management and ticketing solutions; - Other maintenance, support and expert services related to the telecommunications network environment, ordered separately where required. The procurement concerns maintenance and support services only. Ownership of the telecommunications network devices, software licences and the overall network architecture shall remain with VR. VR is responsible for the procurement of network devices and strategic network architecture, while the selected Supplier shall provide the Services in accordance with the agreed contractual responsibilities. The Service is intended to support VR Group's operations in Finland, Sweden, Denmark and Latvia. The Service may also be extended to other VR Group companies or countries during the contract period. A more detailed preliminary description of the procurement is set out in Annex 1 – Preliminary Description of the Procurement. The subject of the procurement described herein is preliminary and may be further specified, clarified and supplemented during the negotiated procurement procedure. The final scope of the procurement, the detailed requirements and the contractual terms will be set out in the Final Invitation to Tender and its annexes.

sig_bf18767f6cc839b68645.description: Kirkon keskusrahasto is initiating a market dialogue with this notice regarding the potential procurement of a document management system. PURPOSE OF THE MARKET DIALOGUE The aim of the market survey is to survey alternative solutions on the market and build an overall picture of the technical, functional and economic benefits of the various alternatives, as well as to help evaluate them objectively before launching a potential procurement. This request does not request or submit tenders, but invites interested tenderers to participate in the market survey. The information that emerges during the market survey will remain strictly confidential and will be used solely for the planning of a potential procurement. Neither the invitation nor the market survey itself obliges the contracting authority to carry out the procurement in the manner described in the request for information or in any other way. No compensation will be paid for registering for the market survey, responding to it or participating in the meeting, nor is participation a prerequisite for participation in a potential tender process. DESCRIPTION OF THE CURRENT STATE The current document management system is Tweb by Triplan Oy, and it is currently used by 9 diocesan chapters, nearly sixty parish economies and the Church Office, each of which forms its own registry within the system (multi-registry model). Parishes have been able to adopt the document management system if they wish. There are a total of 207 parish economies. In addition to case and document management, the system includes official decisions, meeting management, a publication portal and trustee portals for the General Synod and parishes. A speech review section for the General Synod has been customised for the General Synod portal, from which representatives' speeches can be imported into the document management system and published online. Documents produced by the General Synod are published in the General Synod portal during the meeting, and it serves as a data bank for General Synod representatives and committee secretaries. The system features a customised registry-specific mass deletion functionality. The system does not contain a separate archiving feature, nor have electronic transfers been made from it to any other system. In addition to producing meeting management, the Church Office and some diocesan chapters have retrospectively imported digitised and born-digital diary material into the system; other organisations use it solely as a document management system. Operations in accordance with the description of the current state, as well as the aforementioned functions customised for the current system, are central to the church's operating environment, which the document management system must support. At present, a particular shortcoming is an electronic long-term archiving solution integrated as part of the document management system package. REGISTRATION FOR THE MARKET DIALOGUE Suppliers can declare their interest in participating in the market dialogue by submitting a declaration of interest and a brief presentation of the document management system they offer, including reference projects, in Finnish by email to hankinnat.kirkkohallitus@evl.fi at the latest by 15.5.2026. CONTACT AND SELECTION OF SUPPLIERS FOR THE DIALOGUE Kirkon keskusrahasto will contact all operators who have expressed their interest after the deadline has passed. As a rule, 6 suppliers will be invited to the dialogue, selected by comparing the submitted system presentations and reference projects against the needs described above. According to the preliminary schedule estimate, the market dialogues are scheduled to take place in August-September in weeks 34-37 via Teams. The market dialogues will be conducted in Finnish.
sig_bf18767f6cc839b68645.title: Invitation to market dialogue: Document management system

sig_bf2e9107a30c194ce5eb.description: The purpose of the Invitation to Tender is to select one (1) economic operator (hereafter “Contractor”) for the component acquisition, delivery, assembly, hardware and software installation and maintenance of an AI-ready EuroHPC machine (“Supercomputer”) to establish an associated “AI Factory” and that will be owned by the EuroHPC JU. The EuroHPC JU will conclude one contract with the successful tenderer in order to acquire, deliver, install and maintain the High-End Supercomputer hosted by the respective Hosting Entity. Therefore, the prospective Contractors should have proven experience of acquiring, delivering, installing and maintaining Supercomputers in similar environments as the ones required in this procurement procedure. The solutions to be procured are expected to outperform existing solutions regarding several of the following aspects: • Performance/TCO; • Programmability and usability; • Versatility; • System stability; • Power and energy efficiency; • Computing density. A high-performance GPU-accelerated computing partition to be delivered as part of the Discoverer ++ GPU & CPU Partition. The solution is designed to support AI workloads, large-scale simulations, and data-intensive research across a wide spectrum of scientific and industrial domains. LOT 1 should contain two different GPU compute infrastructure with fast interconnect and one AI optimized storage with direct GPU access feature.; The cluster must offer at least two AI accelerator chips based on -wafer scale, integrating hundreds of thousands of cores into a single silicon wafer, designed for large-scale deep learning workloads. The Specialized AI Servers must assume the delivery and installation of homogeneous cluster with height density at least 32 AI accelerators or more with very high speed (based on the same hardware and software configuration) compute nodes (servers). This tender specification defines the requirements for procuring FPGA AI-accelerated systems for the BRAIN++ AI Factory at Sofia Tech Park. Each server unit must be configured to host and efficiently operate 4x FPGA accelerator cards, designed for high-performance computing workloads with emphasis on memory-intensive applications.; A high availability N+1 UPS solution with 2N(N+1) for the most critical loads.
sig_bf2e9107a30c194ce5eb.title: Acquisition, Delivery, Installation and Hardware and Software Maintenance of Discoverer++ AI Supercomputer

sig_bf3ae200ba572e488c45.description: Within the GCA Energy Category, we operate a managed service on behalf of the public sector, aggregating their energy demand and purchasing on the wholesale market under a number of risk strategies. In order to support these activities, we require a cloud-based energy portfolio management solution, suitable for managing the GCA Energy portfolio frameworks, which includes; c.1,200 customers, c.108,000 power / gas meters, c. 80,000 sites There is currently no system in place to meet these requirements. This requirement will run on a 3 month trial period. If after the trial period concludes successfully, the supplier will be awarded the subsequent contract term and value. The value included in this notice is for the trial period only. Any subsequent contract term is subject to further budgetary approval which, will be confirmed at the future procurement stage. The proposed system must be able to accurately record the customer portfolio data for both gas and power, including site and meter information and assigned trading strategy. Each of the meters is assigned to a customer and a site. Each meter is attached to current and future Gas / Power buying strategies with varying buying lengths. The system must support the ability for nominated energy suppliers to access the meter data for their assigned customers. We also require the ability for customers to complete a self-serve audit of their portfolio and buying strategy, including the ability to request changes and additions to their portfolio. The system should have the The ability to extract data via API (REST) to integrate with the rest of our data infrastructure The successful supplier will be expected to provide ongoing management maintenance of the solution throughout the duration of the contract to ensure its effective running and optimisation. The dates included in this notice are indicative and subject to change. GCA intend to run this procurement opportunity via commercial agreement Demand Management & Renewables DPS RM6313. Should you intend to bid, you will need to onboard onto the agreement. Please follow the below link and click "access as a supplier": https://supplierregistration.cabinetoffice.gov.uk/dps/RM6313?nav=0

sig_bf5e743f13ae39e7a39c.description: IKOMM AS invites tenderers, on behalf of Enebakk municipality, to a market survey for the procurement of a new map and management system for water and sewage. Enebakk municipality shall procure a new map and management system for water and sewage in autumn 2026 in the municipality. The municipality needs a future orientated, comprehensive and user-friendly system for managing the water and sewage network. The system shall support both administrative and operative activities and facilitate efficient interaction between employees in offices and personnel in the field. The system must be available via modern web technology and function on different devices (PCs, tablets and mobile), so that registration, updating and posting can be carried out where the work actually takes place. The system shall support efficient registration and management of the pipeline network, manholes and the accompanying technical installations, including the use of GNSS/GPS equipment for precise surveying. The system shall meet strict requirements for information security and stand-by, reduce operational and maintenance costs and ensure that the municipality meets the current environmental and reporting requirements. >: We would like to carry out a market survey (RFI) in order to gain insight into relevant systems, technology and suppliers. Furthermore, we would like to invite up to 3 tenderers to public dialogue meetings to take a closer look at the options that can offer to ensure a good future orientated procurement. Other municipalities in the region will also be invited to participate in this market survey in order to possibly participate in a future competition. > > > > The dialogue meetings are planned to be held in early April as physical meetings in IKOMM ́s premises in Vinterbro, but with an option for participation in Teams. Relevant tenderers will be selected based on relevance, experience and references from equivalent and comparable municipal systems. The objective of the market survey is to: * Gain insight into what systems and suppliers are available in the market * Examine how the tenderers handle technical requirements, integration, security and stand-by * Using the knowledge to improve the requirement specifications and choice of procurement strategy. > This market dialogue will be carried out as a voluntary and non-binding request for information (Request for Information – RFI), cf. FOA § 9-3 and § 12-2, which allow contracting authorities to obtain information about the market before any competition. > > This is not part of a competition and does not involve any obligations for Enebakk municipality or for the tenderers who choose to provide answers. > > Tenderers who participate in the market dialogue will not be given any kind of competition, and participation (or lack of participation) will not lead to exclusion from a later competition. Any future procurements will be implemented in accordance with public procurement regulations, and all tenderers will be able to compete on equal terms. > We therefore invite interested suppliers to provide written input and possibly participate in dialogue meetings. Participation is voluntary and the market dialogue is not binding for the municipality or suppliers. Good if suppliers can give feedback on the possibility of participation in the dialogue meetings that are planned. > attached a disposition/questionnaire for the market survey. > All dialogue will take place in the KDV tool Artifik for traceability. Please use Artifik support if this tool is unknown to suppliers.
sig_bf5e743f13ae39e7a39c.title: Market survey for a new management system for water and sewage Enebakk municipality.

sig_bf9b598cf8293cad25d0.description: The Public Affairs Section (PAS) at U.S. Embassy Tunis invites creative and engaging proposals for programs that strengthen ties between the United States and Tunisia, highlight shared values, and promote bilateral cooperation in ways that make America safer, stronger, and more prosperous. Please see Section C. Program Description for more information. This Annual Program Statement (APS) outlines our funding priorities and the strategic themes we will focus on in FY2025, and the procedures for submitting requests for funding. Based on availability of funding, PAS Tunis will award grants, fixed amount awards, or cooperative agreements between a minimum of $10,000 and up to a maximum of $200,000 (U.S. dollars) each for projects that advance the priorities outlined in this APS. Please carefully follow all instructions in the full announcement. Proposals that fail to conform to the requirements outlined in this APS will not be considered. All proposed programs must include an American element or a connection with American expert(s), organization(s), or institutions in ways that promote increased understanding of U.S. policies, perspectives, and society and/or celebrate U.S. culture and values. Proposals that include programming outside Greater Tunis or across multiple governorates and/or promote increased collaboration and networking among alumni of U.S. government programs are encouraged. PAS Tunis invites creative and engaging proposals for programs that strengthen cultural, educational, professional, scientific, and business ties between the United States and Tunisia through programming that highlights shared values, strengthens people-to-people ties and institutional linkages, and promotes bilateral cooperation, and makes America safer, stronger, and more prosperous. Competitive proposals must focus on at least one grant priority area outlined below. Examples of possible PD small grant proposals include, but are not limited to: · Subject-matter expert, academic, and professional lectures, seminars, and speaker programs that include U.S. speakers/experts. · Programs that strengthen relationships and linkages between U.S. and Tunisian higher education and cultural institutions. · Educational, artistic, and cultural programs, including programs that strengthen English language teaching and learning, music, musical theater, dance workshops, master classes, and performances, live theatre performances, art exhibitions, and sports and culinary diplomacy initiatives that increase mutual understanding between the people of the United States and Tunisia. · Programs, including podcasts, that promote economic empowerment, entrepreneurship, or that share U.S. experiences related to addressing community challenges, including the management of water or energy resources, waste management, urban design and planning, and preparing for and mitigating natural or human-caused disasters. · Cultural heritage conservation and preservation programming, including through the use new and immersive technologies, such as VR technology. (Note: This funding cannot be used to support construction-related activities. End note.) Priority Program Areas and Strategic Themes: Proposals must address at least one of the six priority areas outlined below: · Economic Prosperity and Entrepreneurship: Initiatives that prioritize mutual prosperity, expand economic and commercial links between the United States and Tunisia, promote U.S. entrepreneurial values and practices, and that share best practices of successful U.S. business partnerships, startups, and investors with the aim of increasing economic opportunities for U.S. and Tunisian businesses and investors. · INNOVATION and Collaboration in science and technology: Initiatives that promote collaboration and academic partnerships in STEM fields (science, technology, engineering, and mathematics), including cybersecurity, space, energy, water security, food security, smart agriculture, health technology, and artificial intelligence (AI) between U.S. and Tunisian academic and research institutions, non-governmental organizations, and private companies, as well as programs that promote interest in STEM education among young people. · EDUCATIONAL LINKAGES AND ENGLISH LANGUAGE : Initiatives that expand collaboration and partnerships between U.S. and Tunisian higher education and research institutions through programs and professional and academic exchanges; programs to strengthen English language instruction in Tunisian universities and colleges; programs to expand the teaching of English in sign language and braille; and other programs that support and promote English language learning among Tunisian youth. · LEADERSHIP: Initiatives that provide leadership training inspired by U.S. experiences, models, and best practices to Tunisian young people (high school and university students and young professionals) to help them become effective leaders in their communities and professional field of choice. Such training may include English language, public speaking and interpersonal communication, emotional intelligence, critical thinking and problem solving, financial literacy, goal-setting, and mental health management strategies. · MEGA DECADE OF SPORTS: Programs that leverage the “Mega-Decade in Sports” in North America (2023-2034) when the United States will host the 2025 FIFA World Club Cup, the 2026 FIFA Men’s World Cup, the 2028 Summer Olympics and Paralympics in Los Angeles, and the 2034 Winter Olympics and Paralympics in Salt Lake City, in ways that strengthen people-to-people ties between the United States and Tunisia, promote American values and demonstrate American excellence and leadership in sports and tourism. · Celebrating American Excellence AND U.S.-Tunisian Enduring Partnership: Programs that 1) celebrate U.S. scientific or sport prowess, innovation, economic dynamism, agricultural strength, and national parks and tourism during the 250th anniversary year of U.S. Independence; 2) leverage people-to-people ties and promote the establishment of U.S-Tunisian institutional linkages through cultural diplomacy, including artistic and cultural workshops, performances, exhibitions, or other activities that celebrate American excellence in visual and performing arts, music, cultural heritage protection, and film during the 250th anniversary year of U.S. Independence and the 228th anniversary year of the 1797 treaty of friendship between the U.S. and Tunisia; AND/OR 3) leverage people-to-people or institutional ties through sports or cultural diplomacy initiatives to increase awareness and understanding among broad elements of Tunisian society of the history and benefits of the over two centuries of U.S.-Tunisian friendship, trade, and security cooperation.
sig_bf9b598cf8293cad25d0.title: Annual Program Statement (APS) for Fiscal Year 2025

sig_bfefaf518e9101b75e2a.description: Conducting consumer research on purchasing behavior in Belgium (2027–2031) The fresh vegetables sector within VLAM is launching an information campaign aiming at increasing the awareness of the sustainability efforts of the fresh vegetable sector. VLAM and APAQ-W wish to conclude a new framework agreement with an interested and qualified company to conduct research into the purchasing behaviour of Belgians for the next five calendar years, from 2027 to 2031 inclusive. VLAM (Vlaams Centrum voor Agro- en Visserijmarketing) and APAQ-W (Agence wallonne pour la Promotion d'une Agriculture de Qualité) are the promotional organisations for the Flemish and Walloon agricultural, horticultural, fisheries and agri-food sectors respectively. Both organisations support the marketing of primary products through promotion, communication and market-supporting research. More information about both organisations is available at www.vlam.be and www.apaqw.be. In order to develop and implement various types of campaigns for the different product and service groups and to fulfil their role as a knowledge centre/consumer observatory for the various sectors, sufficient consumer insight is required: • Figures on consumer purchasing behaviour (prp; person responsible for household purchases) in Belgium with regard to food and ornamental horticulture products (flowers, plants, trees, etc.) in general and, in particular, the products promoted by VLAM and APAQ-W. • Trends and developments, over a minimum period of 5 years and measured in a uniform and comparable manner, in consumer purchasing behaviour (prp) for these products, together with interpretation of the figures. • Special analyses of purchasing behaviour data, such as identifying potential target groups, rapid monitoring of purchasing behaviour during promotional campaigns and in the event of sudden changes in the societal context, including crises. VLAM and APAQ-W have chosen to jointly procure this consumer purchasing behaviour research as a framework agreement (through a procurement procedure in which VLAM acts as a central purchasing body with the participation of APAQ-W; see earlier in these tender specifications), because efficiency gains can be achieved for both the contracting authorities and the research agency.

sig_c0523eb82f29eae8f146.description: The Universitätsklinikum Heidelberg (UKHD) is one of the largest and most renowned medical centres in Germany. Every year, approximately 80.000 patients receive inpatient and semi-inpatient treatment in its specialist clinics, and more than 1.000.000 patients are cared for on an outpatient basis. The Heidelberg campus unites scientific institutes and clinics of the UKHD, offers rich opportunities for cooperation with the life science and humanities faculties of the University, and simultaneously maintains established co-operations with internationally renowned non-university large-scale research institutions. The increasing complexity of and growing demands on the IT infrastructure in healthcare require reliable and efficient management of the IT landscape. In the context of the UKHD, it is of decisive importance that operational and clinical applications run constantly available and without faults in order to ensure optimal patient care and smooth operation. Lot LOT-0001: Provision of implementation, project and operational services for IT applications in the hospital environment. As part of this procurement procedure, the University Hospital is issuing a framework agreement for the provision of support services in IT application management (anticipated) from 1 February 2027 for the following 4 years (planned) incl. extension options. A transition that is as gradual as possible to transfer the services from operations outsourced from the existing provider to an external service provider is planned for the period Q1/Q2 2027. The complete takeover of the provision of all contractual services into regular operations is to take place by 01.07.2027 at the latest. The Centre for Digitalisation and Information Technology (ZDI) of the Universitätsklinikum Heidelberg is operationally divided into individual areas. Supported by contractors as external service providers, they assume end-to-end responsibility regarding the IT of the respective core processes of the contracting authority in order to be able to ensure secure and stable operation, but also the further development of IT performance. Directly affected by the tender and the procurement subject are the areas for Operational Information Systems (BIS), for Hospital Information Systems (KIS), for Integration, Special Systems and Archiving (ISA) as well as directly the ZDI itself. The scope of the tender covers the service requirements of the client for operational services in application management. This includes, in particular, smooth application operation, the rapid and permanent rectification of incidents and problems, as well as releases, upgrades and updates in coordination with the client. Furthermore, this encompasses other supportive project services that are in a direct or close substantive connection with the aforementioned operational services. The future contractor is expected to provide comprehensive and holistic services within the framework of a managed service in order to implement the client's requirements regarding IT architecture, IT security and IT service integration. The integration of IT services based on the ITIL v4 framework must be provided holistically for all specialist areas. In this context, the client will manage the contractor(s) and provide the IT hardware required at the client's locations as well as some of the required software licences.
sig_c0523eb82f29eae8f146.title: Provision of implementation, project and operational services for IT applications in the hospital environment

sig_c0580f79e230c910a4cf.description: In the past almost 20 years since the founding of the Federal Government's Cultural and Creative Industries (KKW) initiative, the framework conditions, market structures, value chains and challenges for the KKW have changed fundamentally. Hardly any sector has been as strongly affected by the effects of the change brought about by transformation, the platform economy, digitalisation and artificial intelligence as the KKW, with impacts including on creative production, distribution and the exploitation of rights. The coming years will be characterised by further profound technological, economic and social upheavals. Digitalisation (especially artificial intelligence), sustainability and new forms of audience engagement have become the central drivers of change. After almost 20 years, it is therefore time to take stock on the one hand, and to look ahead and create foundations for strategic options for action on the other. In order to be able to conduct the further strategy process on an evidence-based footing, a qualitative and quantitative baseline study on future projections for the KKW is to be commissioned. The last baseline study, 'Macroeconomic Perspectives of the Cultural and Creative Industries', also produced on behalf of the BMWE, dates from the year 2009. The study is intended to develop a projection for the coming decade in order to provide strategic responses to structural changes in the sector. The aim is to critically examine the future viability of the KKW, to identify risks and to develop a forecast of opportunities and trends. The study 'Cultural and Creative Industries 2037' (working title) is intended to provide a foundation for the long-term strategic orientation of political and economic steering instruments with the help of future-oriented and forecasted scenario analyses. For a future projection up to 2037, it is therefore crucial not only to extrapolate existing growth trajectories, but to systematically include structural breaks, new value creation logics and disruptive technological developments in the forecast. The Federal Government's projections on macroeconomic growth are to be appropriately taken into account as a basis here. The study is intended to create a scientific foundation for the strategic further development of the Federal Government's Cultural and Creative Industries initiative and, in doing so, to provide in particular a long-term strategic orientation for political and economic steering instruments. The strategy is aimed prospectively at decision-makers from politics, business and administration, as well as at the actors in the cultural and creative industries themselves, who want to jointly set the course for a sustainable, innovative and economically strong creative ecosystem for the next generation.
