sig_c0f330fe5ebd4fbb8725.description: 1. INTRODUCTION & SYNOPSIS This announcement is a formal Request for Prototype Proposal (RPP) issued by the Mission & Installation Contracting Command (MICC) – Fort Campbell on behalf of the Directorate of Public Works (DPW) at Fort Campbell, Kentucky. The Government is seeking competitive prototype proposals to design, integrate, and execute a modernized facility management solution across 58 unaccompanied housing (barracks) facilities. The prototype will integrate an advanced, secure Enterprise Asset Management (EAM) software platform with cross-trained physical maintenance execution to streamline work order triage, optimize Between Occupancy Maintenance (BOM), and execute proactive Preventative Maintenance Orders (PMO). Authority: 10 U.S.C. § 4022, Other Transaction Authority (OTA) for Prototype Projects. Agreement Type: The Government intends to award a single Other Transaction (OT) agreement. Follow-on Production / Sustainment: Offerors are advised that in accordance with 10 U.S.C. § 4022(f), successful completion of this prototype project may result in the award of a non-competitive, follow-on production/sustainment agreement or contract without further competition. 2. BACKGROUND Fort Campbell DPW is responsible for maintaining unaccompanied housing infrastructure that directly impacts Soldier readiness and Quality of Life (QoL). The current operating model relies heavily on manual administrative workflows, disparate tracking mechanisms, and reactive maintenance practices, leading to extended vacancy timelines during unit rotations, misdiagnosed service dispatches, and increased facility wear. This prototype project seeks to validate a modernized operational model that combines commercial best practices with enterprise Army platforms (including integration with ArMA, GFEBS, and the forthcoming enterprise IBM Maximo migration). Key modernization elements include QR-code-enabled request intake, automated work order routing, decentralized parts staging solutions (e.g., smart lockers), and dual-track maintenance (physical inspections for legacy systems and sensor-based monitoring for modern equipment). 3. ELIGIBILITY This RPP is open to all responsible business entities. In accordance with 10 U.S.C. § 4022(d)(1), an award may only be made if at least one of the following conditions is met: At least one nontraditional defense contractor or small business participates to a significant extent in the prototype project; OR All significant participants in the transaction other than the Federal Government are small businesses or nontraditional defense contractors; OR At least one-third (1/3) of the total cost of the prototype project is to be paid out of funds provided by sources other than the Federal Government (cost share); OR The Senior Procurement Executive provides written approval for exceptional circumstances. 4. PROPOSAL SUBMISSION & KEY DATES Proposal Instructions: Interested Offerors shall submit a comprehensive proposal package consisting of: Technical Approach (addressing EAM integration, physical maintenance, and predictive monitoring) Integrated Logistics & Sustainability Plan (addressing supply chain, SOPs, and knowledge transfer) Management, Programmatic, & Lifecycle Approach (Integrated Master Schedule, risk management, and scaling) Cost / Price Proposal Performance Work Statement (PWS) (directly derived from Attachment 001, Statement of Objectives) Key Dates: Questions Due Date: Sep 16, 2026, at 11:00 AM Central Time (CT) Site Visit Date: Sep 17, 2026, at 10:00 AM CT Proposal Due Date: Sep 25, 2026, at 11:00 AM Central Time (CT) Submission Instructions: Method: All questions and proposals must be submitted electronically via email. Email Address: evan.m.rea.civ@army.mil 5. GOVERNMENT POINTS OF CONTACT (POCs) Agreements Officer (AO): Eric C. Boston (eric.c.boston.civ@army.mil) Agreements Specialist / Contract Specialist: Evan M. sig_c0f7471166943ec601b9.description: The term intends to enter into a contract for licences for the KI based tool Claude from the supplier Anthropic. Justification for the choice: The term needs an advanced, general KI-tool that can be used by employees across disciplines, including developers, designers and other roles. The aim is to support analysis, development and interaction assignments in line with Sikt's strategic targets for the use of artificial intelligence. After completed needs and market assessments, Visibility ́s assessment is that Claude currently appears to be the best suitable solution for the purpose, particularly in light of: *support for secure and final user-controlled access to data and integrations based on open standards, **good interaction between different user groups, including close collaboration between developers and other professional environments, technical prerequisites for integration with Sikt's existing platform services and architecture. Visibility has assessed alternative systems in the market, including, among other things, Copilot, Gemini, ChatGPT and Cursor, but they are not currently assessed to cover the need to a sufficient degree, especially in terms of the combination of access management, integration options and use across roles. The market for KI tools is developing quickly. The choice of Claude is therefore based on an assessment of available systems at the time of the procurement and is not intended to establish any type of long-term standardisation or supplier binding. Procurement form: The term has examined the possibility of acquiring Claude through the existing framework agreement for software licenses, but has been confirmed that the product cannot be delivered through it. Direct procurements from Anthropic are thus the only available procurement route. Extent and value of the procurement: The procurement concerns licences for Claude, with a staged and needs managed employee disclosure. The estimated total contract value is NOK 3,500,000. The actual cost will depend on the number of users and actual use over time. Options: No options.

sig_c1114644e365759a47be.description: The present notice is not intended to initiate a procurement procedure nor to prepare one. It serves solely for market consultation. The Staatsinstitut für Schulqualität und Bildungsforschung (ISB) is conducting a market consultation in preparation for a procurement in the area of BayernCloud Schule (hereinafter: ByCS), which provides digital applications and services for the Bavarian school community. The contracting authority is examining the future provision, further development, integration and operation of a digital board application for the ByCS. The existing application is a browser-based interactive whiteboard software. The subject of the market consultation is the question of whether suitable market participants are in a position to take over, maintain, service and further develop the existing ByCS board or its code base, or to replace the existing ByCS board with another functionally and technically suitable board application. The aim of the market consultation is to obtain reliable information on solutions available on the market and fundamentally suitable for the described requirement. In particular, it is to be investigated whether an already available or adaptable board application can meet the functional, technical, data protection and operational requirements of the contracting authority and can be integrated, operated, maintained and further developed into the ByCS environment. Within the scope of the market consultation, insights are to be gained in particular as to whether and, if applicable, by whom the described services can be provided. Lot PAR-0001: Free State of Bavaria - Staatsinstitut für Schulqualität und Bildungsforschung (ISB) regarding tender for info services. The existing digital ByCS board application is a browser-based interactive whiteboard software for use in in-person and remote phases of teaching. The application was developed on behalf of the Bavarian State Ministry of Education and Cultural Affairs as a component of BayernCloud Schule and is continuously developed further. In doing so, the application is to fulfil the following criteria in particular: - Platform-independent (device types, operating system) - Browser-based - Responsive design - Offline app / PWA - GDPR-compliant design - Accessible according to WCAG - Collaboration - Very good writing feel / high quality of pen input with palm rejection - Suitable for primary schools -> Simplicity - Special school scripts integrable with individual menus - WOPI connection - Files can be saved offline - Sharing mechanism / permissions between teachers and pupils - Import/export of PDF files and images - Integration of websites and videos - Customisations to ByCS possible (design, repositories, CSP, ...) - Set square and compass - Import of GGS files (previous format) possible Within the scope of the market consultation, insights should be provided in particular on - the extent to which market participants are in a position to take over, maintain, service and further develop the existing board application; - whether other board applications suitable for school use are already available on the market; - whether such applications can meet the functional and technical requirements of the contracting authority; - whether and under what conditions an alternative application can be integrated into the ByCS environment; - what technical, operational and economic risks are associated with the different solution variants. Please contact markterkundung@abante.de by 20 September 2026, 23.59 hrs at the latest if you are interested in participating in the local market consultation. Your participation will not be remunerated. There is also no entitlement to participate in any procurement procedure that may subsequently follow. The decision as to whether a procurement procedure must be carried out is precisely what is to be brought about by the local market consultation. In your initial enquiry, please state as detailed as possible what qualifies you and what capacities you have to provide the envisaged services if the contracting authority decides on a procurement on the market. This is necessary in order to be able to assess the seriousness of the enquiry.

sig_c18c574df88e52eea3b9.description: The Home Office (HO) is the government department responsible for safeguarding the nation through border control, immigration, passport issuance, policing, fire services, counter-terrorism and drugs policies. UK Visas and Immigration (UKVI) plays an integral role in delivering this vision, managing millions of applications annually, enabling foreign nationals to visit, study, work or settle in the UK. As part of the evolution of existing services, UKVI pursues the transformation and modernisation of services in a manner that enhances customer experience and ensures accurate and efficient outcomes. One of the core services delivered by UKVI is the Life in the UK test, an essential component of the route to settlement in the UK and to UK citizenship. The Life in the UK Secure Digital Test and Digital Online Learning Materials Service (LITUK) Project is procuring a new service; enabling the continued delivery of front-end services, balancing continuity with improvements and transformation. LITUK aims to move to a 'Digital-by-Default' approach, while upholding the rigorous standards necessary to support UKVI immigration decisions. The successful provider will deliver a service that combines technological innovation with security assurance, enabling customers to demonstrate their knowledge of life in the UK with confidence and convenience throughout their UK immigration journey. The purpose of this third round of Preliminary Market Engagement is to share information relating to the Authority's vision for the LitUK service and the procurement approach. At this stage, no final decisions have been made regarding the preferred solution. Please Note: the content of this Preliminary Market Engagement Notice may be subject to change. Lot 1: . None

sig_c1af6f59bca95c4857f3.description: The Bars of Admission (RAKs) in Germany are corporations under public law and currently represent over 160.000 admitted lawyers. Their legal basis is formed by the Federal Lawyers' Act (BRAO). There are a total of 27 Bars of Admission in Germany. The 11 Bars of Admission issuing the tender here are actively involved in the project and contribute their professional, organisational and technical requirements to the design. The participating chambers exhibit varying organisational structures, member numbers and IT landscapes, which underlines the need for a flexible and scalable solution. However, the various Bars of Admission are essentially subject to the same legal requirements, which are primarily dictated by the Federal Lawyers' Act (BRAO). In total, the eleven participating chambers currently look after around 132.000 members, who are administered and supported by approximately 370 employees. To support their tasks, 22 chambers currently use a software solution from DATEV eG. This solution covers core administrative processes, particularly in the areas of personnel administration, billing and complaint or case management. DATEV eG has terminated the existing software solution effective 31.12.2027. This decision makes timely planning and procurement of a suitable successor solution necessary. Against this background, the eleven local Bars of Admission have joined forces with the objective of replacing the currently used software solution, procuring a suitable successor solution and successfully introducing it. The project group is led and coordinated by five Bars of Admission (Frankfurt am Main, Hamburg, Hamm, Munich and Stuttgart). The aim is to procure a modern, high-performance and future-proof software solution that meets the specific requirements of the chambers and completely or with enhancements maps the previous functionalities of the DATEV software. In advance, a structured survey of the technical and functional requirements was conducted. This forms the basis for the drawn-up requirements catalogue. The DATEV software currently in use and to be replaced is utilised in the chambers for the following task areas: (1) Personnel administration: Administration of master data of natural and legal persons, admissions, status changes, specialist lawyer designations, training systems, resignations and reactivations. (2) Billing: Administration and billing of membership fees, charges, credit notes, etc. (3) Complaint management: Administration of professional law procedures, in particular complaints (4) Archiving and deletion: Archiving and deletion of data records from personnel and complaint management The software is deeply integrated into the work processes of users and forms a central basis for daily administrative work. Currently, the eleven participating Bars of Admission each operate independent instances of the DATEV software. While the basic functionalities are comparable in all chambers, differences exist in the specific configuration, particularly with regard to individually defined data fields, differing data structures and chamber-individual usage concepts. The project pursues the overarching objective of identifying a suitable successor solution for the discontinued DATEV software and procuring it within the framework of a structured, voluntary tender procedure.
sig_c1af6f59bca95c4857f3.title: Procurement procedure for a Chamber of Lawyers administration system

sig_c1bd567ef6b192706741.description: SUBJECT OF THE PROCUREMENT The subject of the procurement is the municipality's outsourced financial and payroll administration services, including both service production and the necessary information systems. The selected service provider is responsible for the municipality's overall financial management, which includes bookkeeping, participation in the preparation of the financial statements and budget, statutory financial reporting including municipal data reporting, VAT reporting and tax returns, financial planning, purchase and sales ledgers, payment transactions, and entering memorandum vouchers into bookkeeping. Personnel and payroll administration services cover payroll calculation for the municipality's various collective agreement sectors (KVTES, OVTES, TS), maintenance of personnel data, service period calculation, reporting of absences and income to the incomes register and Kela, as well as the payment of travel and expense claims and trustee allowances. The municipality has approximately 250 employees whose payroll calculation must be handled monthly. The procurement package covers only the municipality's services, not, for example, the municipality's subsidiaries. The currently used systems are FPM for financial planning, Sarastia365 BI for financial reporting, Dooap for purchase invoices, Sarastia365 TalousApp for sales invoicing, and Sarastia365 MuistioApp for memorandum vouchers, as well as Populus 25.2.0 for personnel administration. The service provider must also have the capability for system integration, including sales invoicing from billing systems commonly used in various sectors, such as early childhood education, the water utility, and construction and permit supervision. In connection with the procurement, the possibility of replacing the current financial planning and HR systems with more appropriate solutions will be surveyed. The procurement may include options, such as the electronic archiving of permanently retained financial and personnel administration documents in the contracting authority's own archive, and HR system interface solutions with third-party systems, such as occupational healthcare or employee benefit services. CONTRACT PERIOD The contract period is five (5) years. The contracting authority has the right to extend the validity of the contract by an option period of two (2) years. SCOPE OF THE PROCUREMENT Based on previous outcomes, the annual value of the procurement has been approximately 280 000–330 000 euros (VAT 0 %). sig_c223abe46d53959419b1.description: Technology Ireland ICT Skillnet intends to establish a Dynamic Purchasing System (DPS) comprising suitably qualified providers capable of delivering Enterprise AI Adoption and Capability Development Services. The purpose of the DPS is to provide Technology Ireland ICT Skillnet with a flexible mechanism through which specialist expertise can be engaged to support organisations in the planning, governance, adoption, deployment and operationalisation of Artificial Intelligence (AI). The DPS is not intended to procure specific AI software products, platforms or technology solutions. Rather, it is intended to provide access to expertise and support services that assist organisations in identifying opportunities, developing organisational capability, implementing appropriate governance arrangements, evaluating potential AI applications, deploying AI solutions and building long-term organisational readiness. Services commissioned under the DPS may vary depending on organisational requirements, sectoral context and levels of AI maturity. Support may be delivered through consultancy assignments, facilitated workshops, assessments, mentoring, capability-building initiatives, implementation guidance, peer-learning activities and other engagement approaches. sig_c25f10c06d95c429dfbc.description: The Department of the Air Force, Air Force Test Center (AFTC), Support Service Branch (PZZF) at Edwards Air Force Base, CA, intends to award a sole-source, standalone Firm-Fixed-Price (FFP) contract for software development and systems integration services to modify the government-owned Mission Termination System (MTS). The core objective is to design, integrate, and test an Autonomy Government Reference Architecture (A-GRA) compatible interface service and message processor natively within the existing MTS flight-test safety watchdog architecture. This project will deliver a certified Technology Readiness Level 9 (TRL 9) product enabling Software-in-the-Loop (SITL), Hardware-in-the-Loop (HITL), and live flight testing of autonomously controlled Unmanned Aerial Systems (UAS) and Collaborative Combat Aircraft (CCA) at the 412 TENG Experimental Test Force (ETF). 2. SOLE SOURCE AUTHORITY The proposed acquisition will be conducted under the simplified acquisition procedures of Revolutionary FAR Overhaul (RFO) Subpart 13.1, as authorized by RFO 13.106-1(b)(1), Soliciting from a Single Source. The Government intends to award this requirement as a sole-source contract to: Proposed Contractor: Weather Gage Technologies, LLC (WGT) CAGE Code: 7U9F7 Socioeconomic Status: Small Veteran-Owned Business Address: 2709 Thyme Dr, Edgewater, MD 21037 3. TECHNICAL JUSTIFICATION & MARKET RESEARCH FINDINGS Comprehensive market research conducted under RFO Part 10 has determined that Weather Gage Technologies is the only commercial source capable of satisfying this requirement without the Government incurring unacceptable technical, safety-of-flight, and schedule risks. Unique Technical Expertise: The MTS is a highly specialized Run Time Assurance (RTA) safety watchdog built upon the Testing Autonomy in Complex Environments (TACE) codebase originally developed by Johns Hopkins Applied Physics Laboratory (JHU APL). WGT possesses proprietary codebases, custom interface design patterns, and certified testing experience on this exact architecture. Prior Proven Navy Performance: WGT successfully designed and integrated similar A-GRA interfaces on an MTS variant for U.S. Navy test partners under contract N68335-26-C-0206. WGT's existing design patterns cannot be replicated by other entities without a complete, bottom-up redesign of the safety software. GSA eBuy RFI Results: A formal Request for Information (RFI1825881) was issued on GSA eBuy to Multiple Award Schedule (MAS) Category 54151S to assess broader market capability. Out of 30 qualified vendors, 28 submitted formal "No Bid" responses, one submitted a non-conforming capability statement at $0.00, and one vendor submitted an unviable, highly inflated estimate of $2,558,560.00 (more than 27 times the estimated program value). WGT did not submit a GSA eBuy bid and has confirmed they maintain no authorized third-party resellers or strategic schedule partners. Interagency Non-Viability: NAWCAD procurement officials have formally confirmed that the Navy's SBIR Phase II contract cannot be leveraged by outside agencies, requiring the Air Force to execute a standalone open-market purchase order directly to the sole source. Any other developer attempting this integration would require a lengthy learning curve to master the TACE codebase, resulting in severe delays to active CCA test programs, estimated at several hundreds of thousands of dollars in redundant engineering and safety certification costs. 4. THIS IS NOT A REQUEST FOR COMPETITIVE QUOTES This publication is for informational purposes only and does not constitute a formal Request for Proposal (RFP) or Request for Quote (RFQ). No solicitation package is available. However, in accordance with RFO Part 5, any interested party that believes it possesses the technical capability to meet this requirement may submit a written capability statement. Capability statements must provide clear, documented evidence of the vendor's prior engineering experience with the TACE/MTS safety watchdog codebase and A-GRA compliance. All submissions received within five (5) calendar days of the publication of this notice will be evaluated solely for the purpose of determining whether a competitive procurement is in the best interest of the Government. A determination by the Government not to compete this proposed contract based upon responses to this notice is solely within the discretion of the Contracting Officer. Points of Contact Contract Specialist: Josiah L. Broadway Email: josiah.broadway@us.af.mil Contracting Officer: Christina M. Day Email: christina.day.6@us.af.mil
sig_c25f10c06d95c429dfbc.title: Notice of Intent to Sole Source: Mission Termination System (MTS) to Autonomy Government Reference Architecture (A-GRA) Software Upgrade

sig_c26b43449065e94e880d.description: As part of a market survey, BGB-Gesellschaft der Rechtsanwaltskammern Berlin, Bremen, Düsseldorf, Frankfurt am Main, Hamburg, Hamm, Köln, München, Nürnberg, Sachsen und Stuttgart (hereinafter the Purchaser) wishes to enquire about current providers on the market and available solutions for a new management system. After completion of the market survey, the results will be evaluated for the next project steps and for a potentially intended procurement procedure. As part of the market survey, interested companies are invited to participate in discussions and present their solution portfolio. The procedure can be found in the following explanations. The subject of the market survey is the evaluation of possible solutions for a new management system. The sought-after management system should cover the following rough functional modules and exemplary use cases: 1. Personnel management o Management of natural and legal persons (different person types) o Manage training occupations o Manage trainees o Manage reference relationships between persons 2. Billing o Record and calculate membership fee data o Carry out membership fee billing o Create new fees/credits o Bill fees/credits o Manage outgoing invoice ledger 3. Complaint management / Case management o Create complaint/case o Manage complaint/case o Manage complaint/case overview 4. Archiving and deletion o Archive and delete data records o Search archived data records 5. Administration o Manage roles and permissions Participation in the market survey: 1. To participate in the market survey, we ask you to send us appointment proposals (approx. 1 hour) by email to florian.blauensteiner@reqpool.com or to markus.mycinski@reqpool.com by 26.09.2025 at 13:00. For appointment proposals received later, we cannot guarantee that participation is still possible. 2. During the appointment, we would like to talk about your solution portfolio. In addition, you can send us a presentation of your existing solution. The following three aspects are particularly important to us: • Price structure / licensing model • Expandability or possibility for software adjustments • Existing references 3. It is expressly emphasised that, beyond the publication of this preliminary information, companies will also be invited independently to participate in the market survey. This enables the implementation of a broad and transparent market survey and does not prevent other interested parties from participating in this market research. 4. The Purchaser reserves the right not to invite all companies to market survey discussions. In this case, there is the possibility to participate in the market survey in text form. Notes on the procedure: 1. The market survey discussions will be conducted in German. 2. There are no costs associated with your participation in this market survey. No costs will be reimbursed for your expenses incurred. 3. It is expressly pointed out that this is a preparatory market survey and not the award of a public contract. 4. The legal recourse to review bodies is not available within the framework of this procedure. 5. Participation in the market survey does not constitute a prerequisite for later participation in a possible procurement procedure. 6. The Purchaser reserves the right to change or adapt the performance requirements discussed in the market survey in a potentially later procurement procedure. 7. Participation in the market survey does not give rise to any claim for the implementation of a procurement procedure or the award of a public contract. 8. It cannot yet be communicated whether and when a tender will be initiated. Furthermore, no statement can yet be made about possible types of procedure.

sig_c286fcbe8807f4ad3370.description: Glasgow City Council (GCC) manages a framework for the delivery of consultancy services in the area of Business Growth. The consultancy services are delivered to SMEs with growth potential across the city, to help deliver sustainable and inclusive growth and improve business start-up and survival rates in the city. With the current framework concluding in March 2027, GCC is now looking to establish a new framework. These services are delivered under a multi-Lot framework, through a mix of 1-2-1, both face to face and online, and group consultancy sessions related to an anticipated 10 specific specialist areas. The council encourage bids from businesses of all sizes, including sole traders, and encourage a diverse and competitive supplier base. The procurement process has been designed to be proportionate, transparent and accessible, with requirements focused on capability and delivery rather than organisational size. Sole traders are encouraged to engage where they can demonstrate their ability to meet the specified requirements. Lot 1: Business Structuring Business Governance, Legal and IP. The Business Governance, Legal and IP Lot will provide support to help determine the assignment and coordination of roles, power and responsibilities within a business. It also defines how information flows between the different levels of management. Introducing a formal organisational structure can help put your business in a better position to achieve its objectives. Services for this Lot should include, but not be limited to, the following: Board Development Company Structuring Franchising Business Succession Company Governance Ethical Management Intellectual Property Lot 2: Business Growth, Sustainable Growth and Productivity. The Sustainable Growth and Productivity lot will provide support to identify areas of improvement processes which help with improving some measure of an enterprise's success. Business growth can be achieved either by boosting the top line or revenue of the business with greater product sales or service income, or by increasing the bottom line or profitability of the operation by minimizing costs. Business growth is a function of the business lifecycle and can be influenced by industry growth trends. Services for this Lot should include, but not be limited to, the following: Strategic Planning Sales & Marketing Change Management Pitching & Procurement Procurement Operations Management Turnaround Mergers & Acquisitions Lot 3: Upskilling, Leadership and Resources. The Upskilling, Leadership and resources lot will provide support to involve reviewing existing Leadership Development processes and preparing a report on their future suitability and/or making recommendations for future actions. It will also provide a range of support across leadership and management as well as capacity building and comprehensive HR support. Services for this Lot should include, but not be limited to, the following: Organisational Development and Succession Planning Leadership and Management Capacity Building and HR Support Lot 4: Financial Readiness and Planning. The Finance Lot will allow support to be provided across a range of areas which will help with the efficient and effective management of money / funds in such a manner as to accomplish the objectives of the organisation. Strategic financial management not only manages a company's finances but allows them to be managed with the intention to succeed. Services for this Lot should include, but not be limited to, the following: Financial Management Financial Readiness Preparing for Investment Alternative Finance Company Valuation Taxation Lot 5: Design and System processing. The Design and System Processing Lot will integrate design thinking principles into a range of organisations across different industry sectors. Promoting the use of design principles and educating SMEs on the benefits directly linked to innovation, sustainability and resilience, this Lot will see an increase in available support that creates design-led companies who can improve effective strategy and product/service development and manage organisational change. Services for this Lot should include, but not be limited to, the following: Problem Solving Development Testing and validation Lot 6: Sales and Digital Marketing. Sales and marketing share two key roles within businesses: attracting more customers and developing and retaining the existing customer base. They also share the collective underlying goal of bringing in more revenue. When sales and marketing work together a substantial improvement is seen on important performance metrics. Variations persist between Business to Consumer (B2C) and Business to Business (B2B) and as a result of differing routes to market (particularly considering the impact of digital) but the above holds fairly true irrespective of the business model. Expert services under this Sales and Digital Marketing Lot assist businesses with the practical approach to marketing, including writing a marketing plan and establishing a marketing communications plan for integrating traditional and digital communications. It will also offer support with developing a marketing and/ or sales strategy, with pricing and market penetration strategies Services for this Lot fall under the following sub-categories; Digital Sales: Marketing Strategies: Branding: SEO Maximisation including Social Media and website Lot 8: Digital Transformation. The Digital Lot will provide support to businesses to use technology to benefit to its internal and external operations. The types of digital support will be varied but will allow businesses to use Technology solutions to help their business to the next level. Services for this Lot should include, but not be limited to, the following: Social Media eCommerce Support Data Analytics Mobile or internet technologies Customisation of software or App development Cloud Computing AI Digital Strategy Cyber Security Lot 9: Sustainable and Net Zero support. Sustainability expert support topics span core pillars like environmental compliance, carbon accounting, circularity, and ESG reporting. They also encompass strategic organisational needs, including Leadership & Culture, Carbon Accounting & Carbon Baseline Assessment, Supply Chain Engagement and Regulatory Compliance & Climate Risk Services for this Lot should include, but not be limited to, the following: Leadership and Culture Carbon Accounting and Carbon Baseline Assessment Regulatory Compliance and Climate Risk Sustainability and Sustainable Marketing Circular Economy Lot 10: Business Acceleration. This Lot will provide support in a different, shorter, more targeted, and innovative way for organisations at various stages of growth. Since the pandemic feedback from businesses has shown that most are now looking for shorter, sharper more focussed interventions. These interventions could focus on emerging themes and could target the key and emerging sectors. It is envisaged that these interventions will be demand driven and will be required on an as needed basis. They could combine traditional teaching methodologies with guidance and mentorship. These programmes could include expert support from Lots 1-9 Business Growth; Business Structuring; Leadership and Skills; Financial Management; Design Thinking and Innovation; Sales and Marketing; Internationalisation; Digital Development and Innovation and Green Business Support. Suppliers will be contacted by the Council when a specific intervention is required, Evidence suggests that organisations who engage with business accelerators benefit from the opportunity presented, leading to greater collaboration with other entrepreneurs and businesses that can yield benefits that allow the business to grow at an accelerated rate. An overview of the objections and intentions of Accelerator programmes is; Acceleration: Learning-by-doing is vital to the process of scaling any venture, and the point of any type of acceleration programme is to accelerate that process. In this way, businesses are able to compress a large amount of learning into a shorter period of time. Our Accelerator programmes will deliver relevant, accessible and practical learning for the leaders of ambitious businesses in the city looking to scale up. It will equip participants with the skills and tools to shape their own learning. It could encourage participants to take ownership of their own development and assume responsibility for coaching their own management teams to embed learning throughout the organisation. It may also help to address organisational, operational, and strategic challenges that the business may face It could also include access to experienced entrepreneurs and mentors, business model refinement, advice on start-up capital, and the opportunity to pitch to potential investors. Any Accelerator programmes required under this Lot will require to be delivered over a specified period. Most programmes will accommodate between 12 – 15 eligible organisations, with a maximum of 15 participating in any programme. Smaller cohorts may be required on occasion. Lot 7: Preparing for Global Growth. The Internationalisation Lot will support businesses access overseas markets, offering an opportunity to increase sales to a much wider customer base. Exporting can be profitable for businesses of all sizes and lead to new job opportunities. Scottish businesses trading internationally have high productivity rates and are often more competitive, with research suggesting that SMEs who export perform better financially and grow more than twice as fast as those that do not. There is already a comprehensive support structure nationally through SDI for exporting support, therefore this Lot aims to fill the gaps in expertise or support businesses unable to leverage other public sector support. Services for this Lot should include, but not be limited to, the following: Support for Exporting , including tariffs and taxes Market Analysis and Development Structuring for Internationalisation

sig_c296d685b63f931fd290.description:
The subject of the tender is the conclusion of a framework agreement on the provision of specialist consulting for an identity and access management project of Municipal Utilities Bielefeld. The aim of the project is the further development of IAM processes, the design of role and permission models as well as the introduction of a central technical IAM solution. Lot LOT-0001: Procurement of a consulting service for specialist consulting within the scope of an identity and access management (IAM) project for Municipal Utilities Bielefeld (SWB). Municipal Utilities Bielefeld operate a heterogeneous IT landscape with a multitude of applications and systems. The management of user identities and access rights is currently carried out partly in a decentralised and system-related manner. To improve the control of identities and permissions, a central structure for managing digital identities is being established as part of an IAM project. The aim of the IAM project is the introduction of a central IAM service for managing digital identities as well as for the structured and role-based allocation of permissions for applications and systems. For this purpose, an IAM governance structure is to be established as well as a technical IAM solution introduced and rolled out. Specifically, this means the further development of IAM processes, the design of a role and permission model, the introduction of a central IAM solution as well as integration of applications (from Q3 2027) and the preparation of organisational structures for the future operation of the IAM service. The project is managed by an external project management in close cooperation with the IP business division of Municipal Utilities Bielefeld. In the course of the project, the achievement of the following milestones is generally envisaged: • Elaboration and coordination of an IAM governance structure • Elaboration of a role-rights structure for SWB • Introduction of a technical IAM solution incl. implementation of a pilot • Successive rollout of the technical IAM solution to the entire SWB The subject of the tender is the provision of external specialist consulting to support the IAM project of Municipal Utilities Bielefeld. The consulting service comprises support for the implementation phase of the IAM project through two roles. 1. IAM management consulting 2. IAM process consulting Exactly one person is provided for each role. IAM management consulting supports the IP business division with organisational and strategic issues in connection with the introduction of the IAM service. Core tasks of IAM management consulting are: • Support with the organisational classification of IAM within the IT organisation • Further development of governance structures in the IAM environment • Support with the definition and staffing of roles and responsibilities • Evaluation of organisational impacts of IAM structures and processes • Support with the integration of IAM into existing security and governance structures • Elaboration of decision-making bases for management and project control • Support with coordination with relevant stakeholders • Support with the further development of the organisational operating model for the IAM service • Consulting on covering relevant regulatory requirements • Developing an implementation strategy on guidelines, processes and the tool solution • Coordinating content-related dependencies with other projects and line initiatives • Support with the manufacturer-independent selection of an IAM tool solution IAM process consulting supports the functional design of the processes for managing digital identities and permissions. Core tasks of IAM process consulting are: • Analysis of existing processes for managing identities and permissions • Elaboration of processes for the lifecycle of digital identities • Support with the design of joiner-mover-leaver processes • Development and structuring of a role and permission model • Structuring of processes for granting and changing access rights • Support with the integration of applications into IAM processes • Design of processes for recertification of permissions • Analysis of existing permission structures in applications • Creation of functional concepts and process documentation in the IAM environment • Support with the introduction of the processes and the tool solution • Technical support with required provided services and contribution obligations for the implementation of the tool solution • Elaboration of test cases based on the process descriptions and requirements for the tool solution For IAM management consulting, there is a maximum quantity of 440 person-days or 3.520 hours. For IAM process consulting, there is a maximum quantity of a total of 385 person-days or 3.080 hours Hybrid service provision is generally permissible. A binding ratio between remote and on-site deployments cannot currently be specified. The contracting authority determines the project-related required presence demand. On-site deployments in Bielefeld may be required in particular for project kick-off, workshops, steering committees, coordination meetings with central stakeholders and other appointments with presence requirements. The contractor must ensure that corresponding on-site appointments can also be attended with a reasonably short lead time. The concrete scope of presence services is determined by the contracting authority in accordance with the requirements of the project progress The framework agreement does not establish any minimum purchase obligation on the part of the contracting authority. The quantities, hourly rates, reference quantities, demand values and maximum quantities specified in the procurement documents serve exclusively to determine the contract value, the comparability of bids and the award evaluation.

There is no entitlement to actual commissioning or utilisation of these quantities or services. Call-offs within the meaning of these procurement documents are understood exclusively as individual commissions of services triggered by the contracting authority within the framework of the framework agreement.

sig_c2bc3c40b300a65a5571.description: SYNOPSIS The Air Force Life Cycle Management Center (AFLCMC), C3BM?Directorate,?Wright Patterson?Force Base (WPAFB),?Ohio?is conducting market research seeking vendor interest for?a?Ground-Based, Medium-Caliber Gun Weapon System. ? This is a Request?For?Information (RFI) only. This RFI is issued solely for market research purposes. It?does not constitute?a Request for Proposal (RFP) or a promise to issue an RFP in the future. This request for information does not commit the Government to contract for any supply or service whatsoever. Further, the Air Force (AF) is not seeking proposals, nor will it accept unsolicited proposals at this time.?? Respondents are advised that the United States Government will not pay for any information or administrative costs incurred in response to this RFI. All costs associated with responding to this RFI will be solely at the interested party’s expense. Not responding to this RFI does not?preclude?participation in any future RFP, if any is issued. It is the responsibility of the potential offerors to?monitor?the Government’s point of entry (www.sam.gov) for?additional?information?pertaining to?this requirement.? Additionally, Non-Government A&AS support may be?utilized?in the review process of RFI submissions. These non-governmental support staff are covered directly by Nondisclosure Agreements (NDAs) with the US Government as a condition of employment. Any respondent to the RFI with concern should notify one of the POCs found in Section 7.?? PURPOSE The Government is conducting market research to identify potential industry sources capable of providing solutions for a Ground-Based, Medium-Caliber Gun Weapon System that fires affordable munitions, enables defense against air and missile threats with an initial focus on subsonic cruise missiles (CM) and Unmanned Aircraft Systems (UAS) to provide persistent defense in support of United States Air Force assets. The objective of this RFI is to gather information regarding industry capability. ACQUISITION STRATEGY? The program's acquisition strategy is currently in development.? SCOPE/REQUIREMENTS The scope of this RFI is centered on solutions that strictly prioritize fifteen baseline attributes essential to operational success that can engage both cruise missiles and UAS (groups 1-5) threats in accordance with the reference documents. To effectively assess and compare air defense weapon system performance, there are fifteen critical baseline operational and technical parameters that must be analyzed in unison. These key metrics begin with the system's Salvo Probability of Kill (Pk) evaluated against both Cruise Missiles (CM) and Unmanned Aircraft Systems (UAS) Groups 1-5 at maximum range and altitude, ensuring robust lethality against diverse modern threats. The physical footprint of the engagement envelope is defined by its Effective Slant Range and Elevation Coverage, while the capacity for sustained operations is dictated by Magazine Depth and the system's ability to execute Raid Handling against saturating attacks. Furthermore, modern multi-domain operations require seamless Integrated Sensor Capability, deep C2 System Integration, and broad System Interoperability across joint networks. From an efficiency and sustainment standpoint, the system must balance its Cost Per Engagement and Manpower requirements, supported by a reliable Built-in-Test (BIT) framework for rapid diagnostics. Finally, tactical utility is rounded out by the platform's overall Transportability, stringent Weapon Safety protocols, and its comprehensive Multi-Domain Engagement Capability to counter threats across various operational environments. Fifteen Baseline Requirements: Salvo Probability of Kill (Pk) vs CM at max range and altitude Salvo Probability of Kill (Pk) vs UAS Groups 1-5 at max range and altitude Effective Slant Range Elevation Coverage Magazine Depth Raid Handling Integrated Sensor Capability C2 System Integration System Interoperability Cost Per Engagement Manpower Built-in-Test (BIT) Transportability Weapon Safety Multi-Domain Engagement Capability When designing and evaluating next-generation defense systems, the development team must navigate critical trade-offs across three primary Trade Space Attributes to balance lethality, situational awareness, and operational flexibility. First, the system must optimize Munition Performance versus Munition Cost and Gun Capability, ensuring that the interceptor's velocity, maneuverability, and terminal effects are maximized without driving the cost-per-engagement to unsustainable levels or exceeding the physical constraints of the host platform. Second, developers must carefully select the Organic Sensor Capability and Phenomenology—integrating the right mix of radar, electro-optical, infrared, or radio-frequency sensors—to ensure reliable target acquisition and tracking across varying weather conditions, environments, and countermeasure scenarios. Finally, the entire architecture must remain Rapidly Deployable, maintaining a lightweight, modular, and transportable footprint that can be swiftly projected into austere theater environments to meet emergent threats. Trade Space Attributes: Munition Performance vs. Munition Cost/Gun Capability Organic Sensor Capability and Phenomenology Rapidly Deployable RESPONSE GUIDELINES THE CONTRACTOR'S RFI RESPONSE SHALL BE: Page Limit: 10 pages or less (cover page is not included in page count) Format: Submissions must be provided in PDF Submissions must be provided in PDF?with naming convention: CompanyName_SystemName_DDMMYYYY Font: One (1)-inch margins; Times New Roman 12 font Classifications: All responses must be UNCLASSIFIED. If proprietary data is included, it must be clearly marked. Provide the following business information for your company/institution and for any teaming or joint venture partners. Company Name Address Point of Contact Unique Entity ID (UEI) CAGE Code Phone Number E-mail Address Web Page Address Specify whether your company is a U.S. or foreign-owned firm Company Size Status Business System Status Facility Clearance Level (RFP release may contain classified components.) Anticipated North American Industry Classification System Code (NAICS Code): 332994 The Government anticipates the North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) code for this effort to be 332994 - Small Arms, Ordnance, and Ordnance Accessories Manufacturing. If your organization believes another NAICS code is more appropriate for this requirement, please provide the suggested NAICS code along with a brief, objective justification supporting why the alternative code is a more accurate representation of the planned scope of work. The final NAICS determination will depend on the final acquisition strategy and selected contract vehicle. ORGANIZATIONAL CONFLICT OF INTEREST: Organizational Conflict of Interest (OCI), as defined and discussed in FAR 9.5, Organizational and Consultant Conflicts of Interest, is a concern in all acquisitions across the Department of Defense. Early involvement with our industry partners is a key element of the OCI process, and it is critical for the Government to be able to identify any potential OCI issues as early as possible for acquisition. SUBMISSION DUE DATE: 09 OCTOBER 2026, 1700, EST. Late responses may not be reviewed. SUBMISSION: Responses should be submitted electronically to the contracting officer (CO). Primary CO: Christine Basham, christine.basham.1@us.af.mil Secondary CO: Veronica Schoultz, veronica.schoultz@us.af.mil PLEASE NOTE: All interested contractors must be registered in SAM to be eligible for award of Government contracts. The Government reserves the right to consider a small business set-aside based upon responses hereto for any subsequent action. If submitting company proprietary information or competition sensitive information, please make sure it is CLEARLY MARKED. To aid the Government, please segregate proprietary information to the maximum extent possible. All segregated proprietary information will be protected by the Government. DISCLAIMER THIS IS AN RFI ONLY. The information provided in this RFI is subject to change and is not binding on the Government. The Air Force has not made a commitment to procure any of the items or services discussed above, and release of this RFI should not be construed as such a commitment or as an authorization to incur cost for which reimbursement would be required or sought. All submissions become Government property and will not be returned. QUESTIONS Any questions should be submitted to the Contracting Officer(s) as identified above. Joint Publication 3-01, “Counter Air and Missile Threats”, dated 23 March 2012. https://defenseinnovationmarketplace.dtic.mil/wp-content/uploads/2018/02/JointDoctrine-CounteringAirandMissileThreats.pdf

INTRODUCTION & SYNOPSIS This announcement is a formal Request for Prototype Proposal (RPP) issued by the Mission & Installation Contracting Command (MICC) – Fort Campbell on behalf of the Directorate of Public Works (DPW) at Fort Campbell, Kentucky. The Government is seeking competitive prototype proposals to design, integrate, and execute a modernized facility management solution across 58 unaccompanied housing (barracks) facilities. The prototype will integrate an advanced, secure Enterprise Asset Management (EAM) software platform with cross-trained physical maintenance execution to streamline work order triage, optimize Between Occupancy Maintenance (BOM), and execute proactive Preventative Maintenance Orders (PMO). Authority: 10 U.S.C. § 4022, Other Transaction Authority (OTA) for Prototype Projects. Agreement Type: The Government intends to award a single Other Transaction (OT) agreement. Follow-on Production / Sustainment: Offerors are advised that in accordance with 10 U.S.C. § 4022(f), successful completion of this prototype project may result in the award of a non-competitive, follow-on production/sustainment agreement or contract without further competition. 2. BACKGROUND Fort Campbell DPW is responsible for maintaining unaccompanied housing infrastructure that directly impacts Soldier readiness and Quality of Life (QoL). The current operating model relies heavily on manual administrative workflows, disparate tracking mechanisms, and reactive maintenance practices, leading to extended vacancy timelines during unit rotations, misdiagnosed service dispatches, and increased facility wear. This prototype project seeks to validate a modernized operational model that combines commercial best practices with enterprise Army platforms (including integration with ArMA, GFEBS, and the forthcoming enterprise IBM Maximo migration). Key modernization elements include QR-code-enabled request intake, automated work order routing, decentralized parts staging solutions (e.g., smart lockers), and dual-track maintenance (physical inspections for legacy systems and sensor-based monitoring for modern equipment). 3. ELIGIBILITY This RPP is open to all responsible business entities. In accordance with 10 U.S.C. § 4022(d)(1), an award may only be made if at least one of the following conditions is met: At least one nontraditional defense contractor or small business participates to a significant extent in the prototype project; OR All significant participants in the transaction other than the Federal Government are small businesses or nontraditional defense contractors; OR At least one-third (1/3) of the total cost of the prototype project is to be paid out of funds provided by sources other than the Federal Government (cost share); OR The Senior Procurement Executive provides written approval for exceptional circumstances. 4. PROPOSAL SUBMISSION & KEY DATES Proposal Instructions: Interested Offerors shall submit a comprehensive proposal package consisting of: Technical Approach (addressing EAM integration, physical maintenance, and predictive monitoring) Integrated Logistics & Sustainability Plan (addressing supply chain, SOPs, and knowledge transfer) Management, Programmatic, & Lifecycle Approach (Integrated Master Schedule, risk management, and scaling) Cost / Price Proposal Performance Work Statement (PWS) (directly derived from Attachment 001, Statement of Objectives) Key Dates: Questions Due Date: Sep 16, 2026, at 11:00 AM Central Time (CT) Site Visit Date: Sep 17, 2026, at 10:00 AM CT Proposal Due Date: Sep 25, 2026, at 11:00 AM Central Time (CT) Submission Instructions: Method: All questions and proposals must be submitted electronically via email. Email Address: evan.m.rea.civ@army.mil 5. GOVERNMENT POINTS OF CONTACT (POCs) Agreements Officer (AO): Eric C. Boston (eric.c.boston.civ@army.mil) Agreements Specialist / Contract Specialist: Evan M. Rea (evan.m.rea.civ@army.mil)

sig_c2daa1092440e7279955.description: 1. The subject of the contract is the supply, including placement, installation and commissioning, of water supply infrastructure equipment for the Dziadkowice Municipality, as well as the supply and implementation of a remote water meter reading system. 2. The subject of the contract has been divided into 2 parts and includes: 2.1. Part 1 – the supply and installation of 65 above-ground hydrants DN80, 33 gate valves (DN200 – 4 units, DN150 – 24 units, DN100 – 5 units), a water dispenser including commissioning, and the purchase, planting and maintenance of 110 trees. 2.2. Part 2 – the supply and replacement of 751 water meters with remote reading modules (DN15 – 80 units, DN20 – 650 units, DN25 – 8 units, DN32 – 9 units, DN50 – 2 units, DN100 – 2 units), the supply of equipment, software, licences, system implementation, integration with the WODA system, tests, documentation and training. The Contracting Authority allows for the submission of a tender for one or both parts and does not limit the number of parts that may be awarded to one Contractor. 3. The detailed scope, technical parameters, locations, method of installation, acceptance and documentation are defined by the Description of the Subject of the Contract (OPZ), technical designs and the projected contract provisions specific to a given part – Annex 1A to the SWZ. The Beneficiary declares compliance with the DNSH principle; the contractor is obliged to carry out deliveries in a manner that ensures the maintenance of this compliance and to provide the required evidence. Requirements concerning Part 1 The scope of Part 1 includes in particular: 1) the supply of complete equipment and materials; 2) the dismantling of existing elements; 3) the execution of earthworks and assembly works; 4) the performance of required tests; 5) flushing and disinfection; 6) surface restoration; 7) the execution of required signage; 8) the preparation and handover of as-built documentation; 9) the commissioning of the water dispenser; 10) the execution of plantings including their maintenance during the warranty period – in accordance with the OPZ, design documentation and technical designs. Within the scope of Part 1, the Contractor shall obtain the required consents, arrangements and permits related to the occupation of the road lane or the introduction of traffic management, shall provide the required signage and site security, and shall bear the associated costs. Warranty – minimum 24 months for the supplied equipment. The warranty period for gate valves and hydrants is one of the tender evaluation criteria. The detailed scope, technical parameters, locations, method of installation, acceptance and documentation are defined by the OPZ, technical designs and the projected contract provisions specific to a given part – Annex 1A to the SWZ.; Requirements concerning Part 2 The scope of Part 2 includes in particular: 1) the supply of brand-new water meters and radio modules compatible with them; 2) the dismantling of existing water meters; 3) the installation and sealing of new water meters; 4) the performance of test readings; 5) the implementation and commissioning of the remote reading system; 6) the supply of a collection kit and required IT equipment; 7) the provision of required licences; 8) the migration or import of data from the WODA system (INFO-SYSTEM Groszek) used by the Contracting Authority; 9) the performance of required tests; 10) the preparation and handover of documentation; 11) the conduct of instructional training on the operation and maintenance of the supplied equipment and system; 12) The Contractor shall agree with the Contracting Authority on the principles for contacting water consumers and the dates for water meter replacement. Consumer data may be provided to persons performing the replacement only to the minimum extent necessary and using secure communication channels.; 13) With regard to each water meter whose replacement requires agreeing on a date with the owner or tenant of the premises, the Contractor shall make at least three documented contact attempts, including at least one after 15:00 on working days or on a Saturday. After three unsuccessful attempts, the Contractor shall hand over to the Contracting Authority, on the basis of a report, the unused set: the water meter together with the assigned radio module. In such a case, only the price of the supply of this set shall be settled, without remuneration for the dismantling and installation service.; 14) The warranty for water meters and radio modules is at least 60 months, and its extension is one of the tender evaluation criteria. For the remaining equipment, the remote reading system, integration and software, the Contracting Authority requires at least 60 months of warranty, service or support – appropriate to the nature of the service. The Contractor shall provide a subscription and software updates for the remote reading system for a period of 60 months.; 15) For a period of at least 60 months from the acceptance of the system, as part of the tender price, the Contractor shall provide: a) service; b) software updates; c) security patches; d) technical support; e) required licences; f) the ability to use the system and the data stored within it. 16) The expiry of the warranty period must not result in the Contracting Authority losing access to the stored data or being deprived of the ability to download or export it. 17) The supplied measuring instruments must meet the requirements for legal metrological control and possess the required declarations of conformity, markings and documentation enabling their lawful use. 18) The remote reading system must ensure at least: a) full support for 751 water meters; b) the recording and handling of alarms; c) the storage of reading history; d) data export; e) integration with the WODA system used by the Contracting Authority; f) the performance of secure backups; g) the ability to restore data from a backup. 19) The Contractor may process water consumer data only on the documented instruction of the Contracting Authority and to the extent necessary for the execution of the contract. For Part 2, the personal data processing entrustment agreement constituting part of the Projected contract provisions – Annex no. 3B to the SWZ – shall apply. The detailed scope, technical parameters, locations, method of installation, acceptance and documentation are defined by the OPZ, technical designs and the projected contract provisions specific to a given part – Annex 1A to the SWZ.
