sig_c2e3600912c302a7bd79.description: The purpose for this amendment is to respond to the following questions: Question-1. Domestic Applicant Definition: Section D.1 of the RFP states the Challenge is "open to all types of domestic applicants other than individuals." Our company is a U.S.-registered entity, though its ultimate parents are in Canada and Europe. Could you confirm whether an entity with this ownership structure qualifies as a "domestic applicant" for purposes of serving as the lead applicant/Recipient of a cooperative agreement under this RFP? Response-1. For the purposes of this project, a U.S. registered entity will be evaluated as a domestic applicant. Question-2. Citizenship-Based Funding Restriction: We understand that MARAD/META cooperative agreements may include a restriction on using award funds for "work to be done or done in a facility owned by someone other than a Citizen of the United States (as defined in 46 C.F.R. § 315.3(b))." Could you confirm whether this restriction, or an equivalent, will apply to cooperative agreements resulting from this RFP, and if so, how it would apply to a design team whose naval architecture/engineering firm is U.S.-registered and performs all work domestically, but has foreign parent ownership? Response-2. For the purposes of this project, a design team located in the U.S. working at a U.S.-registered firm and performing all work domestically would not fall under the restriction. Question-3. Team Lead Eligibility vs. Preference: Section B notes a preference for "team leads represented by U.S. companies, those with U.S. headquarters, and those operating under the U.S. flag." Could you confirm whether this operates solely as an evaluative preference, or whether it functions as a disqualifying eligibility criterion for a team lead whose ultimate parent is a foreign entity? Response-3. The preference for "team leads represented by U.S. companies, those with U.S. headquarters, and those operating under the U.S. flag" is an evaluative preference. A U.S. registered entity with U.S. offices and staff performing work domestically, would fall under consideration as a domestic applicant for this project. ======================================================================= U.S. Maritime Administration (MARAD) A Study on Vessel Design Challenge RFP No. 693JF726R000016 REQUEST FOR PROPOSALS (RFP): The Maritime Administration’s (MARAD) Maritime Environmental and Technical Assistance (META) program is issuing a request for proposals (RFP) for a Vessel Design Challenge (Challenge). This Challenge intends to fund multiple design teams willing to undertake integrated design work to improve fuel efficiency and reduce vessel underwater radiated noise (URN) to create the next generation of U.S. vessels. Individual awards depend on number of designs proposed for the package. Awards are intended to be for not less than $150k and likely not more than $450k. Project completion timeline is 12-18 months. Total funding available is up to $1.25 million. PROGRAM DESCRIPTION: The META program (46 U.S.C. § 50307) is investigating the interconnections between broader fuel efficiency, reducing URN from vessels, and exploring potential co-benefits. It is the policy of the United States to revitalize and rebuild domestic maritime industries and workforce to promote national security and economic prosperity. Accomplishing this requires making United States-flagged and built vessels commercially competitive in international commerce, rebuilding America’s maritime manufacturing capabilities, and expanding and strengthening the recruitment, training, and retention of the relevant workforce. The most promising opportunities for optimizing fuel efficiency gains and achieving URN reductions are in the early ship design stage, using a systems approach. This requires intentional and integrated ship designs that prioritize fuel efficiency while simultaneously reducing URN. Advanced fluid dynamic modeling enables comparison among hull, engine, and propeller design and arrangement, providing valuable information to the industry about the return on investment (ROI) for various technology and design optimizations at the design phase. Individual technologies claim to provide efficiency and noise reduction benefits, but the additive cost-savings have not been quantified for applying technologies in series and demonstrating increased efficiencies across multiple areas. Recently published studies summarized the state of knowledge and availability of technologies that can be applied to vessels to improve energy efficiency while reducing vessel generated URN. Those reports crosswalk not only the interoperability of technologies and design elements, but the potential reductions, costs, and return on investment. The next phase is to demonstrate, through modeling, the benefits that can be realized through a systematic design approach integrating technologies with input from naval architects, shipyards, and technology suppliers on the efficacy of these approaches. By using this approach, Teams will begin at the drawing table to quantify the benefits of innovative technology integration into the design phase for application on new vessels. The Vessel Design Challenge is intended to facilitate the demonstration of novel vessel designs that meet or exceed international benchmarks for fuel efficiency and URN source levels. This Challenge is intended to fund multiple Design Teams willing to undertake this kind of integrated design work to create the next generation of U.S. vessels. PROPOSAL CONTENT Proposed Vessel Design: Design proposals can include: Existing projects that would be redesigned, Forthcoming projects that are just beginning the design specification phase, and Designs that are theoretical or more experimental which aim to create a new approach or design. There are no restrictions on eligible vessels, however, given the mission of the Maritime Administration, vessels should be commercially useful and generally would not include small watercraft, recreational vessels, or fisheries vessels. Eligible designs include vessels operating in coastal or inland waterways as well as the Great Lakes. Ideal proposals will be for new design approaches or design modifications that couple hull-machinery-propulsion approaches to maximize fuel efficiency, URN reduction, and ROI. Technologies should be centered around performance and demonstrating the feasibility and economic achievability of these combined approaches and should be dictated by capacity needs set by industry requirements (tug capacity, crew capacity, operations support, range, TEU, cargo etc.). Designs should note specifically the technology readiness level and the commercial availability of any technologies used. Design Team: The approach to the Challenge will include a design team. Teams should include description of partnerships, collaborations, and/or processes that will ensure success of the proposal. Further, proposals should identify the Team’s capabilities, related experience, techniques, or unique combinations of these that are integral factors for achieving the Challenge objectives to include experience that supports ability to successfully manage and achieve project goals and objectives of similar type and scope. Development of an ideal team should represent the concept of a design-build approach and include: Naval architect(s) Marine Engineer(s) Shipyard(s) Owner/operator/buyer (can be more than one) Technology provider(s) (including fuel supplier, as needed) May include operator/charter party, BCO, logistics partners, port/city/public entity, private financing partner. Teams may submit one or more vessel designs to the Challenge. Funding amounts will be based on: the number of vessel designs proposed their technology innovation, or a combination thereof One or all proposed designs may be funded depending on proposals. There is no limit to number of teams an organization can participate in, however, an organization may only “lead” one team/proposal. No identical teams with rotating “leads” will be permitted. Preference will be given to proposals with team leads represented by U.S. companies, those with U.S. headquarters, and those operating under the U.S. flag Methods: Proposals must include a detailed description of the design and modeling approaches that will be used to meet the Design Challenge Parameters as noted below, including those for fuel burn estimates and URN source level as well as modeling for return on investment and similar economic estimates and valuations. Timeline: The proposed plan should include the expected timeline (not to exceed 18 months) inclusive of kick off meetings with MARAD, design and technology integration and assessment, interim progress report detailing vessel design and technology application progress, data collection and analysis, and final report deliverables. Budget: All proposals must include a compete, detailed, and justifiable budget with general line items for various design components and stages including fuel, URN, and ROI evaluation and calculations. Budgets should demonstrate market conditions or similar that support these budget estimates. Description of key personnel, qualifications, and expected level of effort should also be included. Proposals may also include any additional considerations, outreach, or analysis recommended to achieve the goals of the project. Design Challenge Parameters Design specifications: The objective is for designs to meet or exceed these specifications for fuel efficiency improvement and noise reduction. Recognizing that this is a demonstration of technical feasibility and economic achievability, if these design specifications are not achievable, alternative efficiency and noise improvements should be documented demonstrating the current limits of technologies. These specifications should be considered aspirational to test the limits of the possible within the bounds of the practical. Energy Efficiency: 30% efficiency improvement over a typical vessel design with conventional hull and machinery arrangements and fuels. Underwater Radiated Noise Source Level: Underwater radiated noise source level is defined using the radiated noise level (RNL). RNL is the source level that has been calculated assuming sound pressure decays geometrically with distance from the source, with no influence of the sea-surface or seabed and is often used to quantify source levels of vessels. Below are the equations for URN limits for self-propelled commercial vessels. The limits are stated in decidecade band RNL (dB re 1 ?Pa2·m2). Frequency range / Hz Transit / dB re 1 μPa2·m2 10-100 169.5+1.5log10(f) 100-1000 191-9.5log10(f) 1000-50000 199-12log10(f) Operational Conditions: Vessels designs should be able to meet or exceed the specifications under what would be considered normal operational parameters for that vessel. The intent is not for these vessels to need to employ special operations or change their normal patterns, routes, or timetables to achieve the reductions. Normal operations should be considered: Typical transit/operating conditions Transit non-working; and working for under-tow/station keeping 85% maximum continuous rating Measurement Standard: ANSI/ISO standards or an appropriate and defensible adaptation of these to suit the needs and conditions of the operational state should be described. Fuel efficiency estimation methods should be described based on industry and/or international reporting requirements (e.g. Class society, IMO) Deliverables The main deliverable is a preliminary vessel design that includes some technical details including the hull form for hydrodynamics and fuel efficiency and the selection of propulsion and power systems (engines, propellers, and other machinery) based on the ship’s operational requirements and sufficient to meet the design specifications of the Challenge. Designs should also be validated for general stability and load analyses for the ship’s safety under various conditions. Design analysis should include the technology combinations, design adjustments, machinery and propulsion arrangements that achieve desired efficiency and URN specifications. Designs should note the technology readiness level and the commercial availability of any technologies used. Each design must include a full breakdown of the anticipated costs compared to a conventional design, including an anticipated ROI timeline and total ROI for the anticipated lifetime of the vessel. This should include a description of the additional costs for each technology element and the design and anticipated construction costs. There is no preferred technology or fuel/engine approach, but final reports should describe in reasonable detail those arrangements and technology combinations used to achieve the specifications. Since this is a concept demonstration for feasibility and economic achievability, challenges and barriers to meeting design specifications should be explicitly described. This should include findings regarding cost differences in achieving partial reductions; for example, the difference in cost between reducing fuel consumption increased rapidly after a certain point or the achievability of URN reduction became exponentially more expensive after a specific dB reduction. It should also include barriers to technology sourcing or availability and the realities of potentially building these vessels in the shipyard, i.e. does the experience exist at U.S. yards to integrate the design technologies and arrangements? These design components, technology and cost evaluations, and lessons learned should be included in a final report that can be made publicly available. Any intellectual property or business sensitive information, to include design plans and/or drawings, results of modeling, or technology or cost specifics will remain internal to the project team and Maritime Administration as not to undermine any competitive advantage. The final deliverable is participation in a debrief with MARAD to share results and lessons learned. There may be opportunities to debrief with other Challenge teams, pending willingness and interest to do so. FEDERAL AWARD INFORMATION: MARAD will provide funding through a cooperative agreement for the execution of this Design Challenge. This announcement is an expression of interest only and does not commit MARAD to make any award. To be considered for selection, the contractor participating in the Challenge must be able to complete it within 18 months from time of award. The final report and other summary materials will be publicly available and posted to the META webpage. Proposals in response to this RFP are limited to 20 pages and must be received within 120 days of the publication of this notice. Proposals will be screened for use of Artificial Intelligence (AI) tools. Any use of AI tools in generating content for the proposal must be clearly identified and justified. MARAD reserves the right to fund one or none of the proposals received under this RFP. MARAD is not responsible for reimbursing the costs that applicants incur to prepare and submit their proposals in response to this RFP. Technical and cost proposals (or any other material) submitted in response to this RFP will not be returned. It is MARAD’s policy to treat all proposals submitted under this RFP as sensitive competitive information and to disclose their contents only for the purposes of evaluation. All applicants must be registered and current with SAM.gov at the time of award. ELIGIBILITY INFORMATION. 1. Eligible Applicants: Open to all types of domestic applicants other than individuals. 2. MARAD is seeking to provide full funding through cooperative agreement for the proposals that provides sufficient, verifiable, and detailed data on how to reach the objective of this Design Challenge. MARAD will fund 100% of the total cost of the project. Proposals must include a detailed cost breakdown that shows how Federal funds will be used for the project. Please see Section E.2 for information on proposal format requirements. 3. Systems for Award Management (SAM) Requirements. MARAD will not make an award to an applicant until the applicant has complied with all applicable unique entity identifier and SAM requirements. If an applicant has not fully complied with the requirements by the time MARAD is ready to make an award, MARAD may determine that the applicant is not qualified to receive an award and use that determination as a basis for making an award to another applicant. Please see Section E.3 for information on SAM requirements. MARAD will not make an award to any applicant with an exclusion in SAM. APPLICATION AND SUBMISSION INFORMATION Address to Request Application Package. This RFP contains all the information needed to submit a proposal and be considered for award. No specific application form or other materials need to be obtained from MARAD. Content and Form of Application. Proposals are limited to 20 pages and must be received within 120 days of the publication of this notice. Proposals must provide sufficient, verifiable, and detailed information covering all elements of the “Proposal Content” described in section B.1 above. Unique Entity Identifier and System for Award Management (SAM). Each applicant is required to: (a) be registered and current in SAM before submitting its application; (b) provide a valid unique entity identifier in its applicant; and (c) continue to maintain an active SAM registration with current information at all times during which it has an active Federal award or an application or plan under consideration by a Federal awarding agency. MARAD will not make an award to an applicant until the applicant has complied with all applicable unique entity identifier and SAM requirements. If an applicant has not fully complied with the requirements by the time MARAD is ready to make an award, MARAD may determine that the applicant is not qualified to receive an award and use that determination as a basis for making an award to another applicant. Submission Dates and Times. The deadline for proposal submission is 12:00 PM EST on the closing date listed for this RFP on SAMS.gov Please submit proposals in PDF format attached to an email. Send proposals to Christian Onwudiegwu/Contract Specialist at Christian.onwudiegwu@dot.gov and Kelly Mitchell-Carroll at K.mitchell-carroll@dot.gov, Office of Acquisitions. Do not send paper copies, or other media of the proposal via post office or delivery service. Proposals received by MARAD after the deadline will not be considered for award. An email will be deemed “received” by MARAD on the date and time the email was “sent” to the email address in Section E.7, below, as determined by MARAD’s servers. Intergovernmental Review. This funding opportunity is not subject to Executive Order 12372, “Intergovernmental Review of Federal Programs.” l Funding Restrictions. Applicants are advised to review 2 CFR Part 200, Uniform Administrative Requirements, Cost Principles and Audit Requirements for Federal Awards as supplemented by 2 CFR Part 1201 for cost principles used to determine allowable costs of work performed under Federal awards. Other Submission Requirements. Proposals must be submitted by the deadline set forth in Section E.4 above by electronic mail to Christian Onwudiegwu at Christian.onwudiegwu@dot.gov and Kelly Mitchell-Carroll at K.mitchell-carroll@dot.gov. Please include the Funding Opportunity Number and Title in the Subject Line. APPLICATION REVIEW INFORMATION Review and Selection Process. MARAD will set up an internal review team to evaluate all proposals that are submitted under this announcement. All eligible proposals will be evaluated within four weeks after the closing date. If the review team has any questions on an individual proposal, it will notify the applicant for clarification. The proposals will be evaluated against the following criteria: Well-documented and context-appropriate plan to undertake and successfully demonstrate the design integration of technology to achieve the fuel efficiency goal, URN limit, and economic analysis required by the Challenge. Clear application of methods supporting vessel design, technology integration, data collection, assessment, and analysis to include specifications for fuel efficiency and URN modeling consistent with international and class standards and reference to existing guidelines, standards, and notations. Methodologies must include descriptions of major analytical approaches being proposed for the Challenge components to meet the Design Challenge Parameters. Methodology also includes any specific models and data sources intended to be used for each component of the Challenge. The Team’s capabilities, related experience, technical knowledge, techniques, or unique combinations of these that are integral factors for achieving the Challenge objectives to include experience that supports ability to successfully manage and achieve Challenge goals and objectives of similar type and scope. Detailed project timeline with descriptions of key decision points and areas of uncertainty. Budget and justification demonstrating appropriate and defensible cost per component, personnel, timeline, and final deliverables; including consideration of the experience and capability of key personnel involved, the number of hours budgeted for key people, and the role, value, and level of participation of any noted partners. sig_c2fd482315cec4293609.description: This is a request for information of a system that includes tools for both curriculum and schedule planning work in a university context. With this RFI Aalto University is seeking information on suppliers interested in delivering the services described. Aalto University is a foundation university as provided in the Universities Act (558/2009) and started operations at the beginning of 2010. Aalto has six schools and approximately 20 000 students, 4800 staff of which over 400 are professors. Aalto’s curriculum planning process involves our 3,100 academic staff members including 120 programme directors, supported by 100 curriculum planners in the learning services. The work covers over 80 degree programmes, 700 study modules and 3500 study units. Curriculum data is updated based on the length of the curriculum period, which is currently two academic years. Aalto’s scheduling process involves the aforementioned 3,100 academic staff members, 66 timetable planners, and 3 room booking system admins. The planning encompasses classes for 16 184 students in 250 spaces. With the forthcoming procurement and contract our goal is to establish a long-term partnership with a supplier who can cater to our evolving curriculum and schedule planning needs in alignment with our strategy in an agile manner. REQUIREMENT FOR THE SYSTEM CONTAINING CURRICULUM AND SCHEDULE PLANNING TOOLS Aalto University needs a system primarily for schedule planners, curriculum planners, and teachers to efficiently draft and publish curricula and timetables collaboratively. The desired system should also provide comprehensive analytics and reporting tools to support management with strategic activities on all levels of the university, such as programme directors and department heads for degree programme -level planning, deans for school-level planning, and various members of steering groups for Aalto-level planning. The system should provide advanced contemporary solutions for curriculum mapping and automatic scheduling. The system should be a finished product that has been in active use for several years in the higher education sector. Please see attached Appendix 1 for providing a general description about the procurement and our aims towards the procured service. TERMS OF THIS RFI Contracting authority may use the information it receives during the RFI process for the planning and preparation of the actual invitation to tender. Note! This is NOT a prior information notice, a procurement notice, a contract notice nor an invitation to tender. This notification and/or answering to it do not create any obligations for the contracting authority or for those who choose to answer it. The contracting authority does not pay any compensation for taking answers to this RFI. The information provided by the contracting authority is preliminary at this point and it is subject to change. Taking or not taking part in the RFI does not change the standing or status of a supplier in the procurement process. INSTRUCTIONS ON HOW TO RESPOND TO THIS RFI With this RFI Aalto is requesting system suppliers to announce their interest in participating in a market dialogue. We request you to inform us about your interest to participate in this RFI by 28 April 2026 at 2 pm CET / 3 pm EEST via email to anna-liisa.auramo@aalto.fi, riikka.rissanen@aalto.fi and heli.jarvela@aalto.fi (please use all names as recipients). Mark "Request for information: Curriculum and Schedule planning system" as the subject of the message. Please send the following information in your response: • Appendix 1. General presentation of your company and the system you could provide • Appendix 2. Q&A template filled in with your responses - Supplier information - Answers to the “Questions from Aalto” - Comments on how you could provide solutions to our user stories - References - Investment planning - Questions from the Supplier, if you wish to pose any NOTE! In case your answers contain trade secrets or other classified information, please mark the sensitive information clearly into the materials provided. NEXT STEPS Upon receiving answers, Aalto University may contact the interested participants. Aalto University reserves the right to invite suppliers for further discussions regarding this RFI to obtain information to the necessary extent on market and suppliers providing relevant services, give out information regarding the needs of Aalto University and to clarify any issues related to the object of the procurement. Discussions may also be held with suppliers other than those who responded to the request for information. REQUEST FOR INFORMATION APPENDICES Appendix 1. Object of procurement Appendix 2. Q&A template

sig_c322df730dcee6452275.description: THIS IS A NOTICE OF INTENT TO AWARD SOLE SOURCE AND IS NOT A REQUEST FOR COMPETITIVE PROPOSALS. This synopsis is hereby issued in accordance with Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Part 5.203 to announce the Government's intent to increase the programmatic ordering ceiling of the Mission Training Complex Capability Support (MTCCS) II, Multiple Award Task Order Contract (MATOC), by $129M on a noncompetitive basis. Services under this MATOC encompass non-personal operational, technical, administrative, and program management services supporting individual through collective MC training. The ceiling increase applies across the existing MTCCS II MATOC suite comprising the following base contracts: Base Contract Contractor W900KK-24-D-0003 Booz Allen Hamilton Inc W900KK-24-D-0004 CSA Global LLC W900KK-24-D-0005 General Dynamics Information Technology W900KK-24-D-0006 Northrop Grumman Systems Corporation W900KK-24-D-0007 Phoenix Logistics LLC W900KK-24-D-0008 Valiant Global Defense Services Inc. W900KK-24-D-0009 Applied Training Solutions LLC W900KK-24-D-0010 Core Government Services Corporation W900KK-24-D-0015 Veteran's First LLC W900KK-24-D-0014 Nemean Trideum Joint Venture LLC W900KK24D0012 Evocati Solutions JV W900KK24D0013 Liberty Business Solutions W900KK24D0020 Thalin W900KK24D0022 Gemini Technical Services The Army Contracting Command Aberdeen Proving Ground Orlando Division (ACC-APG-ORL) and the U.S Army Combined Arms Center have identified a critical need to increase the MTCCS II MATOC cumulative ceiling to ensure uninterrupted execution of the Army’s Mission Training Command (MTC) Program. The contemplated $129M ceiling increase is necessitated by environmental landscape changes and operational training demands, guaranteeing the continuation of vital Mission Command (MC) training delivered to units throughout the Army. Due to the ongoing operational tempo and specialized scope of work, no other contractors are currently positioned to assemble and mobilize the required administrative infrastructure, program management, and subject matter experts without creating an unacceptable mission lapse. Awarding the requirement to any sources other than the established MTCCS II contract holders would cause significant disruption of ongoing mission-critical training services. This is not a request for competitive quotes. sig_c33a20807edc4227b7b7.description: The contracting authorities are conducting a competitive dialogue for the development of a chatbot for the Bergisches Servicecenter as well as for the administrations of the three contracting authorities in accordance with the provisions of the German Public Procurement Ordinance (VgV). The tender aims to develop a chatbot for the Bergisches Servicecenter and the three contracting authorities, which is to be used to execute or perform, among other things, both the services of the Bergisches ServiceCenter and the services of the administrations of the cities of Remscheid, Solingen and Wuppertal at the level of information provision to the public and interaction regarding the administrative services of the three cities. In the future, the chatbot is to be further developed in line with the current state of the art, particularly at the interaction and transaction level as well as for internal administrative support. The contracting authorities shall be entitled, both jointly for the Bergisches Servicecenter and individually, to call off services from the contractor regarding the developed chatbot (cf. draft contract, Annex C to the 2. Letter of Procedure). The subject of the contract is the development of a chatbot system to fulfil service tasks or services of the Bergisches Servicecenter at the level of information provision to the population of the cities of Remscheid, Solingen and Wuppertal. Regarding the functional scope of the chatbot, the solution concepts must take into account the future further development of the interaction and transaction level as well as the possibility of internal administrative support. Furthermore, the subject of the contract also includes the maintenance, further development and adaptation of the chatbot system. On the one hand, the chatbot system should be able to implement, within the framework of providing information to citizens, companies and other information seekers, in particular direct information on available services, forwarding to corresponding services and information, and prospectively, at the interaction and transaction level, among other things, advice on services. On the other hand, with regard to internal administration, the chatbot system is prospectively intended to support, among other things, text management, research assistants and an internal service bot. The chatbot is to be implemented in particular as a multilingual, AI-supported large language model, with transparent, consistent and friendly or citizen-oriented language, with constant citation of sources, and in compliance with data protection and IT security law.

sig_c3808ae8c24d6ecf5756.description: South Lanarkshire Council are looking to notify the market of a potential future contract opportunity to deliver Sign In/Sign Out facilities for Operatives within Grounds Services and Waste Services, although it is possible that this may be extended to other Services within the Council in the future. This facility would initially be required for approximately 900 employees across 10 separate locations. Given the nature of the duties which these Operatives carry out, the use of cards, fobs, and lanyards is not practical for Health & Safety reasons. The preference would be to use fingerprint reader technology, although the facility to manually sign in or sign out using alternative methods, such as a username/password or PIN, would be required for both onsite and offsite use. As South Lanarkshire Council has recently implemented Oracle Fusion Cloud and uses the Oracle Time and Labour (OTL) module of that system within some Service Areas, it is a requirement that any Sign In/Sign Out System operates or integrates directly with the OTL module. The link between the two systems would allow for the transfer of sign in/sign out details, working patterns, annual leave, sickness absence, public holidays, season shutdowns, new starts, departures, etc. Grounds Services and Waste Services are looking to go out to tender in April 2026, with an award date of June 2026, and an implementation start date of September 2026. Please complete and return market engagement questionnaire to Georgie.Howley@southlanarkshire.gov.uk to register your interest. Lot 1: . sig_c3f73ce8284f2e4ade1a.description: The Contracting Authority is tendering a contract regarding a common Operating Platform for the Contracting Authority's IT system portfolio. After Transition In, where the Support Systems are transitioned to the Operating Platform, the Supplier shall be responsible for operation, including Data Centre operation/Hybrid Cloud Custom Services/Hybrid Cloud Standard Services and Infrastructure operation, as well as Support and maintenance of the Operating Platform. Furthermore, after Transition In, the Supplier must ensure Subsequent Transitions to and Transformations of the Operating Platform. The purpose of the common Operating Platform is, among other things, to obtain secure and stable operation with high availability as well as a modern technological platform with a high degree of scalability that supports the needs of the Customer and the municipalities. It is the Contracting Authority's business need that all Services are delivered with high delivery reliability and robustness, and that the Supplier demonstrates proactivity in the collaboration. In addition to the focus on secure and stable operation, the Supplier must ensure a successful Transition In of the Support Systems with the least possible disruption to the Contracting Authority's business, as well as Subsequent Transitions and ongoing Transformation, including a gradual transition to Hybrid Cloud Standard Services and, to the extent that it supports the needs of the Contracting Authority and the municipalities, Managed Public Cloud Services. In connection with Transition In, a high level of information security must be established, which must be continuously maintained and improved throughout the Contract. The contract has the following 4 main services: I. Transition In, where the Contracting Authority initially wishes for the establishment of and secure and stable transfer to an Operating Platform for the Support Systems, based on Hybrid Cloud Services, with the implementation of, for example, project management, transition organisation, building of operational capacity, transfer of Environments and data, and takeover of knowledge from the Outgoing Supplier. Subsequently, the Contracting Authority wishes to carry out successive Subsequent Transitions for a number of the Contracting Authority's other IT systems from the current operating models to the Operating Platform, based on Hybrid Cloud Services. II. Ongoing Services for the Operating Platform, including; a. Support; b. Hybrid Cloud Services, including Hybrid Cloud Standard Services and Hybrid Cloud Custom Services; c. Tools for supporting Application Suppliers; d. Governance, Operational Processes, security services, Documentation, and operational reporting. III. Service catalogue with the use of standardised methods, technologies, and services, through which the Contracting Authority wishes to be able to provision services on a cloud platform that; a) Offers a wide range of services; b) Is accessible via the public internet; c) Has a publicly available price structure with settlement of services according to consumption on subscription terms. sig_c447dffcae6a7a3e1937.description: INTRODUCTION The Centre for Emergency Communication (CFB) of the Danish Emergency Management Agency is preparing a procurement procedure for a contract concerning the 112 solution. The contract will cover the operation, maintenance, support and further development of the existing 112 application. The existing 112 solution is described in the attached background note Annex A. Against this background, CFB is conducting a market dialogue with potential tenderers in two phases. In the first phase, CFB is asking tenderers to answer the questions set out in Annex B. In the second phase, CFB will invite up to five tenderers to a follow-up meeting in order to elaborate on the information. First of all, we therefore ask tenderers to answer the questions in the questionnaire and upload it in the ETHICS procurement system. TIMETABLE FOR THE MARKET DIALOGUE The market dialogue has been published in the Official Journal of the European Union in a prior information notice dispatched on 15 December 2025. We will receive answers to the questions no later than 12 January 2026 at 12:00, after which we will select tenderers for follow-up meetings, which we expect to hold on 27 and 28 January 2026. We expect the meetings to have a duration of 11⁄2-2 hours. If a tenderer is invited to market dialogue, the tenderer will be notified no later than 21 January 2026. The agenda for the meetings will be sent out with the invitation, and the agenda will be based on an elaboration of the questions that the tenderer has answered. We will select tenderers based on the submitted answers. The selection will be made based on, inter alia, an assessment of tenderers' relevant experience with similar tasks, tenderers' relevant considerations regarding the task's deliverables, including transition-in, as well as tenderer's answers regarding matters that the tenderer considers to be essential for tendering for the task. THE TENDER We expect to publish the tender in the second quarter of 2026. The procurement procedure will be a negotiated procedure in accordance with the provisions of the Defence and Security Directive. The tender documents will be drawn up in Danish, and answers in Danish will be required with the exception of system documentation and similar. ANSWERING THE QUESTIONS The questions appear in Annex B, and the answer must appear exclusively in the form and not in separate annexes. The questions can be answered in Danish or English. The completed form must be uploaded via the ETHICS procurement system no later than 12 January 2026 at 12:00. CONDITIONS FOR PARTICIPATION It is voluntary for tenderers to participate in the market dialogue, and it is without significance for the subsequent tender whether a tenderer has participated. We will treat the information received as confidential, subject to the limitations arising from the right of public access to documents, cf. the Public Administration Act. QUESTIONS Questions concerning the market dialogue can be asked in the ETHICS procurement system.
sig_c447dffcae6a7a3e1937.title: Tender for support, operation, maintenance and further development of 112

sig_c458251ec268696db888.description: The regions wish to conduct a market dialogue regarding the procurement of a new system to ensure improved IT support for the processes of handling and dispensing free-of-charge medicine (VFM). The lack of IT support complicates the dispensing of free-of-charge medicine generally and particularly in relation to the transparency that clinicians, patients and other healthcare actors are accustomed to from pharmacies in the primary sector. At the same time, the risk of errors increases, partly because data is transferred manually between multiple systems. Effective IT support will facilitate the procedure and ensure an automated and patient-safe solution that enables standardised data collection and settlement between the regions as well as close management and monitoring of medicine consumption. In addition, there is a desire to support dispensing in the patient's region of residence regardless of the place of treatment/region of treatment. The core functionality is based on existing, new and adapted functionality in FMK as well as the procurement of a new VFM Client, whose main purpose is to be the hospital pharmacy staff's portal for order receipt, processing, accounting and documentation for the dispensing of free-of-charge medicine. This VFM client is the subject of a potential upcoming procurement, which this market dialogue concerns. On this basis, the regions desire a dialogue with a number of suppliers regarding how a VFM client could be designed and developed. The regions primarily desire discussions with suppliers who have experience with health IT solutions and domain knowledge within medicine management and FMK. For the use of the market dialogue, the regions have drawn up the document "Proposal for market dialogue - IT support for the dispensing of free-of-charge medicine" as well as Annex 1 and Annex 2, which are respectively the preliminary functional requirements for the VFM client and an architecture annex. Interested suppliers must send their expression of interest to Christoffer Hejle Madsen, christoffer.madsen@rn.dk, no later than Friday 15 May 2026 at 23:59. The regions expect to hold individual dialogue meetings with up to six companies. The meetings are expected to be held as physical meetings in Aalborg on 9 and 10 June respectively. If there are more than six interested companies, the regions reserve the right to select six that are assessed to have, inter alia, domain knowledge within medicine management and FMK, company size and experience with similar development projects. Interested suppliers therefore also have the opportunity, together with their expression of interest, to submit a brief description of the company and experience in relation to the tasks described in the material. The description may occupy a maximum of 1 page.
sig_c458251ec268696db888.title: Procurement of an IT system to support the dispensing of medicinal products free of charge (VFM)

The required services include, but are not limited to: • Provision of Microsoft Teams Voice capability; • Telephony connectivity (e.g. SIP trunking and public telephony network access); • Migration from the Authority’s existing telephony solution; and • Ongoing support, maintenance, and service management. The solution must enable the Authority users to make and receive calls via Microsoft Teams using assigned Direct Dial-In (DDI) numbers and support a modern, flexible working model across office and remote users. The successful Tenderer shall be responsible for end-to-end delivery of the service, including design, implementation, transition, and ongoing operation. See tender documents for further details

sig_c5413b14a87460db9909.description: The Municipality intends to procure a modern, future-proof and comprehensive operational system that strengthens the quality, legal certainty and efficiency of social services. The system must enable digital, cohesive and automated work processes that provide case handlers and service providers with: • increased overview and transparency, • improved decision support, • reduced administrative burden. The procured system is to constitute a central digital platform for the work of social services and be fully integrable through open APIs and standardised information flows, enabling the Municipality to create a cohesive end-to-end solution across system boundaries. The system must be configurable, scalable and adaptable to changing operational needs, new legislation and technical developments. The Municipality's information must be retainable, transferable and reusable without technical or financial obstacles, while maintaining information quality and supporting long-term sustainable information management. Digitalisation and automation are to replace manual tasks, duplicate documentation and parallel support systems to the greatest extent possible. The system shall thus contribute to: • legally secure and uniform case handling, • a good working environment, • high and traceable information quality. Full traceability must exist throughout the information chain – from decisions, interventions and execution to follow-up, changes in system configurations and integrations. The Municipality must at all times be able to track how information has been handled, by whom and on what grounds.
sig_c5413b14a87460db9909.title: Social Services operational system

sig_c57817db33a5b42f1ddb.buyer_original: Freistaat Thüringen, vertreten durch das Thüringer Ministerium für Soziales, Gesundheit, Arbeit und Familie (TMSGAF) vertreten durch das Thüringer Landesamt für Verbraucherschutz
sig_c57817db33a5b42f1ddb.description:
An IT application is to be procured as a SaaS cloud solution for the digitisation of processes relating to trichinella testing, the management of monitoring samples in the animal health sector, and management in the event of an outbreak of African Swine Fever (ASF). The IT application must be compatible with the hunting statistics application from Condition – Integrierte Softwarelösungen GmbH. This is used in the Free State of Thuringia to record bag data (data on wild animals killed by hunters). The IT application should be available both as a web application (usable in common browsers) and as a mobile app (iOS and Android operating systems). Within the scope of the tender, an app is defined as an application that must be installed on a mobile device before use by the user and can only be used there. As a rule, this takes place on a smartphone or tablet using a so-called app store. There will be two main user groups: a) administrative or laboratory staff b) non-administrative users (e.g. authorised hunters). The non-administrative users record data on killed or slaughtered animals. If necessary, they also submit applications for the testing of these animals for trichinella and/or certain wildlife diseases to the competent authorities or the competent testing facility of the Free State of Thuringia. The test results should be retrievable via the IT application. The competent authorities (veterinary and food monitoring offices of the districts and independent cities - veterinary authorities) operate the trichinella testing laboratories. These should be able to access the application data recorded by external users in the IT application via their own user interface and transmit the test results back to the applicants. In addition, laboratory software should be made available to the competent authorities, with the help of which testing activities can be documented on the basis of the application data. In the case of monitoring samples in the animal health sector, the client's laboratory at the Thuringian State Office for Consumer Protection is the competent testing facility. The laboratory software (LIMS) in use there should be able to access the information on the samples entered by the users via the HIT database. The IT application must therefore have an interface to the HIT database. A direct connection to the LIMS is not intended. The IT application is to be made available to administrative staff for mapping internal administrative processes, as well as to affected users outside the administration for data entry and application submission, and for receiving notifications from the competent authorities. While the use cases of trichinella testing, management of monitoring samples in the animal health sector, and the interface to the hunting statistics application are to be available permanently, the use case of management in the event of an outbreak of African Swine Fever (ASF) is only to be usable and available on an ad-hoc basis. Furthermore, introductory support and training for the staff of the competent authorities should be included in the offer as an initial service. The contract is concluded via an EVB-IT cloud contract. The procurement is carried out by the client for use by all districts and independent cities in Thuringia. The use of the IT application for the aforementioned purposes is mandatory for the districts and independent cities. For hunters, however, use is optional. This means they can refrain from using the IT application. The previous analogue system for sampling will continue to be used in parallel for the time being. The 21 veterinary and food monitoring offices of the 22 districts and independent cities in the Free State of Thuringia are, among other things, responsible for receiving and testing samples of slaughtered or killed animals intended for human consumption for Trichinella spp. Furthermore, there are responsibilities with regard to granting permission for the taking of samples intended for trichinella testing by non-administrative persons. Citizens who wish to make use of the aforementioned administrative services should be enabled to record the required application data digitally in accordance with the principles of the Online Access Act (OZG), to submit the application paperlessly to the respective competent veterinary and food monitoring office, and to receive the notifications from the competent authorities. In addition, the possibility should be created to comply with further reporting obligations (e.g. the recording of hunting bags by hunters) in digital form. The testing of wild boar for Trichinella spp. only takes place if the animal is to become food. Based on experience to date, this leads to the testing of up to 30.000 head of wild boar per year in Thuringia. These figures fluctuate. In addition, the veterinary surveillance authorities are responsible for implementing regular monitoring of killed wild animals for certain animal disease pathogens. Depending on the current animal health status, the number of samples is expected to vary between approx. 5.000 and 30.000 samples per year. Data entry and application submission as well as the receipt of notifications should also be made possible here for the respective affected citizens. The recorded data should be transmitted via the application to the State Office for Consumer Protection responsible for testing the samples. The application part for the management of ASF outbreaks should be based on the aforementioned application parts in terms of operation (esp.

the monitoring of killed wild animals for certain animal disease pathogens) and interact with them in terms of content in accordance with the technical requirements. This application part should be activatable on an ad-hoc basis for each affected authority (veterinary authorities of the districts and independent cities and, if applicable, the client). In addition to an ASF outbreak in Thuringia, it should also be used in the context of exercises to prepare for an outbreak. A final application part includes the recording and reporting of hunting bags by hunters. This report includes all huntable animal species. For this documentation obligation, the kill data from the aforementioned application parts should be reusable, but it should also be possible to record new kill data. A corresponding interface is to be provided for the necessary data exchange with the hunting statistics application of Condition – Integrierte Softwarelösungen GmbH. The hunters already have direct access to the hunting statistics application. The interface should enable them to gain access from within the IT application and thus facilitate reporting through data transfer. The application is to be provided for use by administrative personnel in the Free State of Thuringia as well as the respective affected citizens in the Free State of Thuringia. As a result, the licence and terms of use must enable use by employees of the state, the municipalities, and by non-administrative persons. The number of future users cannot be precisely quantified at present, as the use of the IT application is optional for hunters. However, the number of hunters in Thuringia can be a reference point; it amounts to approx. 13.000. In addition, there are approx. 100 administrative staff.
sig_c57817db33a5b42f1ddb.title: Provision, operation (incl. hosting), and support of an IT application for the digitisation of processes relating to trichinella testing, the management of monitoring samples in the animal health sector, management in the event of an outbreak of African Swine Fever (ASF), and a software interface to the hunting statistics application

sig_c5990e4963af4f52e345.description: Hanover Housing Association has been providing housing and support services across Scotland for over forty years. Managing approximately 150 homes with an aspect of care, predominantly for older people, Hanover is committed to enabling tenants to live independently within their communities. Hanover provides housing with care and very sheltered housing services which can range from light touch interventions such as reminding tenants to take medication to helping tenants with daily tasks such as personal care. Lot 1: . Hanover has initiated a Care and Support Systems Review at senior management level to address challenges caused by varied case management practices, inefficient data handling, and outdated digital tools. Two critical areas of improvement have been identified: - Care Scheduling/Planning – modernising currently paper-based processes, ensuring person-centred care and real-time updates. Although a full eMAR system is not required, medication management is a large area requiring support. - Rota Management – replacing fragmented manual scheduling with a centralised, digital platform. Through this forthcoming procurement, Hanover aims to secure a solution that will: - Improve service quality and tenant engagement through modern, digital care planning. - Increase operational efficiency and staff satisfaction via streamlined rota management. - Enhance safety, compliance, and oversight of medication management. - Provide integrated reporting, dashboards, and mobile accessibility. - Support compliance with relevant regulatory frameworks. The service will operate within a framework of continuous improvement with which the service provider will be required to engage; bringing innovation, sharing ideas, and implementing improvement measures to increase operational effectiveness/efficiency and drive out waste.
sig_c5990e4963af4f52e345.title: Provision of a Digital Care and Support System – Care Scheduling/Planning and Rota Management

sig_c5a615a74cdb9a73d4b7.description: Istekki is currently developing the procure-to-pay process. The key objectives of the development project are: • to ensure the functionality and consistency of the entire procure-to-pay process and operating methods • to define the system architecture and tender or select the necessary systems so that their use becomes more efficient and they support the operating models and set objectives • to ensure that Istekki's contracted suppliers perform in accordance with their contracts, that cooperation develops, and that operating models generate added value for both parties • to continuously improve and develop supplier cooperation, particularly with strategic and important suppliers • to provide visibility and manageability through data and reporting • to enable system controls throughout the entire process. In developing the procure-to-pay process, we are focusing in particular on developing ordering practices and supplier management, while at the same time examining the operating methods of the entire process broadly and the following tools: • the tendering system, • the contract management system, • the SRM (Supplier Relationship Management) system, • the purchase order system, • the warehouse management system, and • the purchase invoice processing system . We want to understand what kinds of packages each company has to offer so that the data flow of the entire procure-to-pay process is seamless and efficient. It is equally important for us to figure out in what parts it is advisable to make the tenders so that, on the one hand, the system package supports our operations efficiently, and, on the other hand, many companies are able to submit a tender. The purpose of the request for information is to collect information regarding the subject of the procurement for the upcoming tender process. Answering the request for information is not a prerequisite for participating in any subsequent tender process. However, to ensure the success of the upcoming tender process, it would be important for tenderers to provide the contracting authority with the requested information as extensively as possible. The request for information does not oblige Istekki Oy to carry out the procurement as described in the request for information or its appendices, and the tender competition may also not be carried out. Those who have answered the request for information will not be paid compensation for making the request for information or for participating in any presentation events related to the request for information. The request for information must be answered no later than 17.12.2025 by 12.00. A response form with advance questions is attached to the request for information in Tarjouspalvelu. Responses must be sent at the same time as registering as willing to participate in the market dialogue. Answering takes place by email to the address hankinnat@istekki.fi. The information provided will be treated confidentially. Information session We are organising a Teams session where we will present our needs and objectives to interested tenderers on Monday 15.12.2025 at 9-10. At the same time, there will be an opportunity to ask questions. Register for the information session using the accompanying link (by copying the link below into your browser): https://forms.office.com/Pages/ResponsePage.aspx?id=ewb-5OsjeUaP1ZOOp9lZERdEXEuHF6JJgdbtjascEOxUMjhGWVVFRzZBUlo5OFZBSThBQldBRVhJOS4u The registration link for the information session can also be found in Tarjouspalvelu in attachment 2 of the request for information. Any additional information questions should in principle be asked as part of the request for information responses. The contracting authority will not publish additional information questions submitted during the request for information phase.

sig_c5dd603289a67dbf574a.description: Welcome to the Dynamic Purchasing System (DPS) for Expertise for the Control Room of the Future program and adjacent subjects. Note: This Dynamic Purchasing System is a continuation on the Mercell platform of the DPS that was previously operational on the Negometrix platform with Negometrix reference 159478 for which formal notice 2021/S 087-226573 was published on 5-May-2021 on the TED website. If your company was already qualified for participation on the Negometrix platform, a simplified procedure applies for re-establishing your qualification, see question 2.1 on the Mercell platform. TenneT will renew and innovate the (IT) systems that it uses for controlling and balancing its grids in the period 2021-2031. In connection with this, TenneT expects to be needing extensive external expertise, related to existing and new technologies and ways of working, in particular related to the challenges that TenneT faces in the energy transition. Compared to current ways of working, innovations will be needed to handle e.g. the increasing infeed of solar and wind energy that is far more difficult to predict and control than traditional generation. The subject of this tender procedure is a Dynamic Purchasing System (DPS) for expertise (including the development of algorithms and IT Tools) that TenneT needs in connection with the renewal of its (IT) systems related to the control and balancing of the electricity transmission grid. Initially, the DPS contains the following categories of expertise: 1. power system control and monitoring; 2. energy platforms and interconnected IT systems; 3. data analysis, artificial intelligence and machine learning; 4. system and process implementation. This Tender Dossier contains the rules for the Application by Economic operators for qualification under this DPS. In order to become qualified for one or more of the categories, the Economic operator has to fulfil all the requirements of this DPS. In addition, the Economic operator needs to the answer all Mercell questions, and submit the requested documents and-or evidence at the respective Mercell question with the submission of its Application. During the course of time, the specific assignments (contracts) under the DPS will be tendered for which all suppliers that have qualified for the particular category will be invited to submit an offer. Any interested supplier may at any moment during the lifetime of the DPS submit a request to be qualified for participating in the tender procedures for specific assignments within one or more of the categories of this DPS. Your request will be accepted if it satisfies the applicable requirements and if you accept the stated conditions. Once you have qualified, you will automatically receive a notification when TenneT publishes a request for proposal for a specific subject within a category for which you have qualified. TenneT emphasises that it would also like to attract small and medium sized companies to this DPS. Qualification requests will be processed by TenneT in the sequence of receipt. TenneT will inform you as soon as possible and endeavors to do so within 10 working days from the date of receipt about the acceptance or rejection of your qualification request. During the lifetime of the DPS, TenneT will be entitled to add new categories, to close existing categories, and to split-up existing categories in to one or more categories.

sig_c5f4ed68ce0e43596109.description: Dumfries and Galloway Council intend to commission an organisation to develop and implement the creation of a local Poverty dashboard, designed to provide a clear, accessible view of child poverty across Dumfries and Galloway. The dashboard should be accessible to partner organisations and any other interested party. Dumfries and Galloway Council serve a region of around 148,000 people across the South West of Scotland, stretching from Stranraer in the West, to Moffat and Annan in the East. We are the 3rd largest local authority by area in Scotland. The latest published statistics show that the rate of child poverty in Dumfries and Galloway is 22.7%. This equates to 5,672 children and young people living in poverty in the region. For example, there are some real challenges around improving health outcomes for those experiencing poverty in the early years and to ensure that all families eligible for free school meals are reached. Lot 1: . Dumfries and Galloway have received funding through the Scottish Governments Fairer Futures initiative. The project is early in its inception but has the long-term goal to deliver systematic change in the way public services support parents and families out of poverty. Our approach is to use existing principles and approaches to put families first, focusing on prevention rather than cure. To help achieve this, accurately measuring poverty and low income is crucial, and the availability of real-time data is vital for effective policy-making. The dashboard would have geographic layers, allowing users to explore poverty data at varying levels of granularity, offering insights into where support is most needed, with a particular focus on priority groups identified by the Scottish Government. These include lone-parent households, families with a disabled member, large families, and households with a mother under the age of 25. It is hoped that data can be gathered that will make meaningful impact to household income, targeting those who are not currently accessing all the additional help and support they can. In addition it’s important that we understand the landscape of our household in poverty, not in our dense areas of deprivation. It would be sage if this could also include pertinent health related data around missed appointments, or additional useful information which might allow for a targeted approach to reduce health inequality. The dashboard should; -Filter data by employment status, housing tenure, and age group, enabling a nuanced understanding of the different dimensions of poverty. -Be a dynamic platform with regularly updated data, that can be continually used to inform decision making. -Be publicly accessible, this openness is essential for building trust and ensuring that anti-poverty efforts are responsive to the lived experiences of families across the region. The purpose of the Poverty Dashboard is to make it easier for the Council and its partners, working with our families in poverty, to easily identify the areas of greatest need to support an evidence based and targeted approach when tackling poverty and inequality in the region.. It is anticipated that this procurement requirement will be conducted through Quick Quote portal as a non-regulated procedure, interested organisations are encouraged to express an interest to be added to the quick quote where this goes as planned.

sig_c615b8d7d5b0ed6423e9.description: The Municipality of Arâches-la-Frasse is the organising authority for the public service of the ski lifts of the Les Carroz and Flaine ski areas, both of which are integrated into the connected Grand Massif ski area. The Les Carroz area is operated by SEM SOREMAC under a public service delegation expiring on 30 September 2029. The Flaine area is the subject of a separate contract, operated by GMDS, which expires in April 2029. The proximity of these expiry dates leads the Municipality to initiate a global reflection on the future management method, the contractual scope, the economic balance, the governance and the conditions for the takeover or transfer of assets, contracts, rights, obligations and personnel necessary for operation. The Municipality is considering various orientations: management by a local public company or the conclusion, after competitive tendering, of a public service delegation (unified or otherwise). This lot has as its object a mission of legal and financial project management assistance for the preparation, choice and implementation of the future management method for the public services of the Les Carroz and Flaine ski lifts; This lot has as its object to provide the Municipality with a complete technical diagnosis, an evolution strategy and a multi-annual investment programme sufficiently precise to allow the elected officials to arbitrate, to the holder of lot no. 1 to model the legal and financial scenarios, and then to integrate the technical requirements into the selected system

sig_c61aead6a7e5fda93e12.description: NOTICE OF ADMINISTRATIVE CLARIFICATION *** ADMINISTRATIVE NOTICE: NOT AN AMENDMENT *** Solicitation #: 75R60226R00026-A1 Title: Evidence Reviews of Newborn Screening Genetic Conditions The Health Resources and Services Administration (HRSA) Maternal and Child Health Bureau (MCHB) is issuing this administrative clarification to all prospective offerors regarding Volume II: Past Performance Proposal Instructions. The Government wishes to remind all potential bidders of the flexible mechanisms built into Volume II: Alternative Reference Types: Per Page 5 of Attachment 2, offerors (specifically small businesses) who have not held relevant Federal prime contracts are explicitly permitted to submit past performance references from state/local governments, private sector clients, or Federal projects utilizing subcontractors. The Neutral Rating Safety Net: Per Pages 8 and 9 of Attachment 2, offerors without a record of relevant past performance, or for whom information is not available, shall receive an "Unknown Confidence (Neutral)" rating. The Government will neither penalize nor reward the offeror for this rating, and the proposal will be evaluated strictly on Technical Merit and Price. A lack of traditional federal prime contractor references does not render a proposal non-responsive, incomplete, or ineligible for award. The final proposal submission deadline remains unchanged: Tuesday, September 22, 2026, at 5:00 PM EDT. This notice is for informational purposes only and does not constitute an amendment to the solicitation. ************************************************************************************************************************************** AMENDMENT 0001: The purpose of this amendment is to formally publish industry Q&A, update technical layout page exemptions, re-baseline the Attachment 2a pricing template, and delete the GSA MAS prerequisite. Notice Type: Combined Synopsis / Solicitation (Amendment 0001) Solicitation Number: 75R60226R00026 Title: HRSA/MCHB Newborn Screening Systematic Evidence Review IDIQ (with Concurrent Award of Task Order 1) Classification Code: R499 – Support—Professional: Other NAICS Code: 541690 – Other Scientific and Technical Consulting Services Response Deadline: Tuesday, September 22, 2026, at 5:00 PM EDT The Health Resources and Services Administration, Maternal and Child Health Bureau (HRSA/MCHB) has officially released Amendment 0001 for Solicitation #75R60226R00026. This amendment addresses industry pre-proposal inquiries, issues the official Government Q&A log, updates Technical Volume layout exemptions, and distributes an updated pricing template vehicle. Offerors are strictly cautioned that initial proposals must adhere to the revised Core Task framework and utilize the re-baselined spreadsheet template to be eligible for the Best Value Trade-off evaluation pool. Proposals utilizing the original version 1 spreadsheet template will be rendered non-responsive and excluded from evaluation. 1. Core Revisions and Material Document Changes Eradication of Standalone Task 8: The master procurement vehicle contains seven (7) evaluated Core Tasks. The post-award "Artificial Intelligence Compliance and Risk Management Plan" requirement—previously designated as an isolated Task 8—has been completely removed as an independent task area. The AI Compliance requirements are officially absorbed as an administrative sub-component under Task 2 (Program Management) across all attachments. Standalone "Task 8" terminology has been entirely removed from the modified statements of work and deliverable schedules. Expanded Volume I Technical Page Count Exemptions: To ensure the Government receives the level of resource granularity necessary to execute a rigorous price realism evaluation under Subfactor (c), the administrative Compliance Matrix and the comprehensive Staff Loading Chart are now classified as page-exempt Appendices. These components may be appended to Volume I and will not count against the strict 25-page narrative ceiling. Electronic Document Layout Flexibility: Offerors are explicitly authorized and encouraged to configure digital page sizes for the Staff Loading Chart or complex timeline graphics to an 11 x 17-inch landscape "Tabloid" format within their PDF submissions to maximize legibility. Primary Principal Investigator (PI) Mandate: Bidders may name multiple co-PIs or workstream leads across the varied newborn screening scientific tasks to ensure adequate specialized coverage. However, the proposal must clearly designate one single Primary Principal Investigator whose resume will serve as the baseline for compliance scoring under Subfactor (b). GSA MAS Prerequisite Deletion: Section 6.1 of the solicitation package has been amended to delete the text indicating that an active GSA Multiple Award Schedule (MAS) contract is an ordering prerequisite. This is a standalone, full and open competitive procurement vehicle. 2. Volume III Price Template Re-Baseline (Attachment 2a) Offerors are strictly required to download and utilize the updated Attachment 2a spreadsheet template uploaded with this notice. Key corrections implemented include: Travel NTE Plug Correction: Hardcoded formulas on the Summary Tab have been adjusted to lock Option Periods 2 through 4 to "NA," lowering the evaluated travel footprint from $175,000.00 down to $70,000.00 to match the exact 2-year active duration of Task Order 1. LCAT Rate Cell Activation: Structural data-entry fields have been enabled for the Senior Medical Officer / Clinician LCAT role, and Tab 4 mapping cells have been unlinked from the Epidemiologist tracking structures. Task 6 Unit Uniformity: The Unit Type designation for the Simultaneous Systematic Review capacity line item has been re-baselined from "Each" to "LOT" to reinforce that this deliverable operates on a firm-fixed capacity lot model. 3. Critical Administrative Milestones Past Performance Questionnaires (PPQs): Offerors must instruct their client references that completed PPQs must be sent directly to the Government via email no later than Friday, September 18, 2026, by 5:00 PM EDT. Final Electronic Submission: The electronic proposal closing date remains unchanged and is strictly due no later than Tuesday, September 22, 2026, by 5:00 PM EDT. All submissions must be split across sequential emails if they exceed the 25 MB HRSA server constraints. 4. Acknowledgment Requirements Offerors must acknowledge receipt of Amendment 0001 by signing and returning the completed SF-30 form within Volume III (Price and Administrative Proposal) of their final electronic submission packet. All other terms, clauses, and conditions of the initial Request for Proposal announcement remain entirely unchanged and in full legal force. Primary Points of Contact: Elizabeth Van Absher, Contracting Officer: EVanAbsher@hrsa.gov Ms. Shawn Horton, Contract Specialist: SHorton@hrsa.gov List of Uploaded Attachments: SF-30 Amendment 0001 (Signed PDF) Attachment 1c - TO 1 SOW-A1 (PDF) Attachment 1d - TO Deliverables-A1 (PDF) Attachment 1e – TO 1 QASP-A1 (PDF) Attachment 2 - Instructions to Offerors-A1 (PDF) Attachment 2a - Pricing_Template-A1 (Excel) Attachment 2b - PPQ-A1 (PDF) HRSA-75R60226R00026 - Consolidated Questions (PDF) The Health Resources and Services Administration, Maternal and Child Health Bureau (HRSA/MCHB) is releasing this full and open competitive solicitation to establish a Multiple-Award pool of approximately three (3) to five (5) Indefinite-Delivery, Indefinite-Quantity (IDIQ) contracts. The primary objective is to secure highly specialized scientific methodologies, systematic clinical evidence reviews, and core programmatic support for the Newborn Screening Recommended Uniform Screening Panel (RUSP). The master IDIQ ordering period is five (5) years (a 12-month Base Period plus four sequential 12-month Option Periods) with an aggregate collective ceiling value of $15,111,361.00. 2. Acquisition Framework & RFO Protocols This commercial services procurement is being conducted under the dual frameworks of FAR Part 12 (Commercial Products and Services) and the streamlined negotiated procedures of FAR Part 15 under the Revolutionary FAR Overhaul (RFO) framework. 3. Concurrent Track 1 Award Stream Concurrently with the establishment of the Master IDIQ pool, the Government will award Task Order 1 (“Support for Evidence Reviews and Newborn Screening Processes and Reports”) as a strict Firm-Fixed-Price (FFP) order. Award Without Negotiations: In accordance with RFO protocols, the Government intends to evaluate proposals and award the Master IDIQ contracts and the concurrent Task Order 1 based strictly on initial proposals received, without formal negotiations. Offerors are strongly cautioned to submit their most competitive technical approaches and binding ceiling pricing in their initial volumes. Future Agility: The restriction against negotiations applies solely to the initial master pool setup and Task Order 1. For all subsequent task order competitions, the Contracting Officer fully reserves discretionary authority to conduct streamlined negotiations, request spot-discounts, or issue clarifications. 4. Proposal Structure and Submission Instructions All qualified commercial, academic, non-profit, or public entities may submit a proposal. Submissions must consist of three separate volumes: Volume I – Technical Proposal: Strictly limited to 25 pages (resumes and letters of commitment may be appended dynamically and are excluded from the limit). Volume II – Past Performance: Submission of three (3) prime or major subcontractor references. Volume III – Price Proposal: Utilizing the mandatory Government-provided Excel template to establish binding ceiling rates. 5. Important Milestones Pre-Proposal Questions: All technical, administrative, or pricing questions must be submitted via email no later than Wednesday, September 9, 2026, at 3:00 PM EDT. Inquiries must utilize Attachment 4 – Q&A Submission Template (Excel format). Final Proposal Submission: Proposals must be submitted electronically via email no later than Tuesday, September 22, 2026, at 5:00 PM EDT. LIST OF ATTACHMENTS. The following documents form a part of this RFP and any resulting Indefinite Delivery Indefinite Quantity vehicle: 1449 (PDF) Attachment 1: IDIQ Statement of Work (SOW) – HRSA-RUSP Priorities (PDF Format, 8 pages) Attachment 1a: IDIQ Schedule of Deliverables for SOW (Word Format, 3 pages) Attachment 1b: IDIQ QASP (PDF Format, 2 pages) Attachment 1c: Task Order 1 Statement of Work (SOW) Attachment 1d: Task Order 1 Schedule of Deliverables Attachment 1e: Task Order 1 QASP Attachment 2: Instructions to Offerors and Evaluation Factors for Award (PDF Format, 11 pages) Attachment 2a: Pricing Spreadsheet (Volume III, Excel Format) Attachment 2b: Past Performance Questionnaire (Word Format, 12 Pages) Attachment 3: Section K Contractor Representations and Certifications (PDF Format, 2 pages) Attachment 4: QA Submission Template (Excel)

sig_c64e3891e886e006794e.description: Norwegian Defence Materiel Agency wishes to map which climate and environment considerations related to energy use, energy efficiency and circular practices in data centres, that can be relevant to demand for future procurements of computer centre services. The purpose is to gain insight into how suppliers currently work with renewable energy, waste heat, energy efficiency and emission reporting, uncover regional and technical variations that can affect the delivery, and assess verifiability, available documentation and possible challenges in the making of requirement specification. The market survey is not binding, does not constitute a competition and the answers will not be used for qualification or evaluation in later procurement procedures. The information will only be used as decision support when designing requirements and criteria, and when following-up contracts. Tenderers are encouraged to respond as specifically as possible, but it is acceptable to state intervals, describe variations or account for limitations related to security, third party agreements or business sensitive information. Input on challenges and consequences with different requirements is particularly valuable. See the attached document for further questions and further information on this market survey. If there are questions for Norwegian Defence Material Agency when preparing answers to this market survey, we request that these are sent through the message function in Mercell. The deadline for submitting answers to the market survey, is set to 11th May 2026, 12:00. Replies are to be sent through the message function in Mercell.
