sig_c6f470efe37cb0aae868.description: Development of a connector for linking operational management information systems, which will ensure data exchange of information between operational and information centres of the Fire Rescue Service of the Czech Republic, specifically between regional operational centres and the national operational centre with the operational and information centres of neighbouring states. The connector will be used for the automated transmission of information about the type and location of an incident, requests for cooperation of Integrated Rescue System components, the status of equipment and its GPS position, and about the intervening units of the Fire Rescue Service of the Czech Republic and neighbouring states. The connector's information will also include a map section of border areas up to a distance of approximately 50 km from the state border on the territory of the Czech Republic and the neighbouring state. The implementation of this public contract consists of three interconnected parts. The first part is the development of the Connector, which includes the development and delivery of software, implementation and commissioning of the system within the Fire Rescue Service of the Czech Republic. The second part is ensuring the connection of the Connector with neighbouring states. The third part is the delivery of map materials. A separate part is the provision of SLA, operation, support and development of the Connector.
sig_c6f470efe37cb0aae868.title: Development of a connector for linking the operational management information system of the Fire Rescue Service of the Czech Republic with neighbouring states

sig_c766e67fd02e97d3b9a6.description: The subject of this tender is the design, development and prototypical implementation of a system for the automated detection of dead branches within the infrastructure of Autobahn GmbH des Bundes. Functional specification: AI-based detection of dead branches 1. Introduction and objectives The subject of this tender is the design, development and prototypical implementation of a system for the automated detection of dead branches within the infrastructure of Autobahn GmbH des Bundes. The objective is to provide a digital tool that supports visual inspection through AI-based image analysis, thereby significantly increasing the efficiency and safety of maintenance measures. The specific technical implementation is at the discretion of the bidders. All relevant legal and regulatory requirements must be complied with during the design, development and implementation of the AI system. In particular, the contractor must ensure that the AI system to be developed is in accordance with the requirements of Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 on Artificial Intelligence (AI Act), insofar as it is applicable.2. Functional requirements for the system (service programme) The service to be provided must fulfil the following core functions, which must be demonstrated in a proof-of-concept (PoC) and in a subsequent prototypical application. 2.1. Data acquisition The system must be capable of capturing visual data (images or video sequences) from a mobile unit (e.g. a vehicle) in a quality suitable for AI analysis. Function: Automated and continuous capture of image material of the surrounding tree landscape. 2.2. AI algorithm for image evaluation The core of the application is an AI algorithm that performs an automated analysis of the captured image data. Function: Automatic detection, classification and spatial localisation (positioning) of dead branches. Requirement: The algorithm must achieve a defined minimum hit rate and reliability under various environmental conditions (daylight, shadows, weather). The results must be clearly assignable and traceable. 2.3. Frontend application (user interface) The system must provide a user-friendly interface for displaying and managing the analysis results. Function: Graphical processing of the AI results for practical use. Requirement: The frontend must enable a clear display of the detected dead branches on a map. In addition, the frontend must contain functions for validation, commenting and approval of the results by the user. 2.4. Data management and interfaces Requirement: A self-sufficient system must be offered which enables data entry and data integration and whose results can be viewed. Integration into existing IT systems of Autobahn GmbH is not intended and is not required. The AI system will be operated entirely by the contractor. The contractor must provide the data and analysis results generated during the provision of the service in electronic form. Formats must be used that are both readable by the contracting authority and machine-processable. Further technical interfaces or system connections are not part of the service to be provided. 3. Non-functional requirements Beyond the functions mentioned, the following qualities of the system are important: Scalability: The system must be designed in such a way that it can be expanded to larger data volumes and further areas of application if required. IT security: The entire architecture and data processing must comply with current IT security standards, particularly with regard to the protection of data and systems in critical infrastructure. Maintainability: The system should be designed so that it can be easily maintained and further developed. The usage rights for the developed software (AI) remain exclusively with Autobahn GmbH des Bundes. 4. Project result Proof of functionality (PoC): After the first phase, a functional proof (PoC) must be provided that demonstrates the feasibility of the AI-based detection. Prototypical application: The final result is a fully functional, prototypical application that meets all the functional and non-functional requirements mentioned above and can be tested in practice. Note: The decision regarding the specific technical implementation (e.g. programming languages used, specific AI frameworks, etc.) is left to the bidders. The decisive factor is the fulfilment of the described functions and objectives. The contract duration is 24 months from the start of the contract. Within this period, the AI system must be fully developed and provided. The data deliveries in accordance with section 2.4 must also be provided regularly within this period.
sig_c766e67fd02e97d3b9a6.title: AI-based detection of dead branches

sig_c771b6d9c7a0b9958f38.description: This contract constitutes a single-award framework agreement within the meaning of the regulations relating to public procurement. It sets the conditions applicable to recurring services as well as to additional services and developments that may be ordered as the contracting authority's needs arise during its term. The purpose of the framework agreement is the supply, implementation, maintenance, support and development of an integrated human resources management system, covering in particular: • complete payroll management for contract, statutory, authorised, volunteer and pensioner staff (including management of bonuses, absences, career breaks, attendance fees, tax and social security declarations, etc.); • time and attendance management, including clocking in/out, leave validation, encoding and validation of teleworking, mission management, planning, as well as agent access via web portal and mobile application. The contract aims to guarantee complete functional and technical consistency between these two areas, in a single and integrated approach. It does not include the supply of physical clocking terminals. The contracting authority already has these. Tenderers must ensure the compatibility of their solution with the use of current time clocks (see Annex E). The contract will be concluded for a maximum duration of 10 years. The duration of this contract is explained by the investments and developments necessary for the provision of a solution meeting the needs and constraints of HYGEA.

Fermanagh and Omagh District Council (FODC) is currently considering whether to initiate a procurement process to establish a contract with a Supplier to digitise and dispose of records. This would establish a contract with a supplier to collect, prepare, digitise and index hard copy planning records and safely dispose of the physical copies. This Pre Market Engagement exercise will also inform the Council of the availability of Frameworks when determining the final Procurement process. The Council is also wishing to explore a potential option for online access to the final digitised records for the public, which will generate revenue and overall enhance operational efficiencies, including cost reductions and ensuring the long-term integrity of historical records. The broad scope of the project is outlined in more detail in the Attached Questionnaire. Before commencing the procurement process, FODC is undertaking pre-market research and seeks to assess; • the level of market interest in participating, • the potential options available in the market, and • in particular the potential to make use of emerging technologies, including AI. No part of this process should be read as generating an expectation in relation to any future procurement process for this project. This market engagement exercise does not guarantee the commencement of a commercial competition resulting in monetary income or future outlay. **PLEASE NOTE: ALL COMPLETED QUESTIONNAIRES MUST BE SUBMITTED VIA THE eTendersNI PortaI.*** Respondees are not required to wait until the closing date to submit a response. sig_c7ae57afa624c3022150.description: As part of the "C-Roads" project (CRG-3), a replacement for the analogue-radio-based public transport priority system for motor omnibuses is to be tested. Unlike the predecessor project "LOGIN" (Optimal traffic signal control in local public transport), in which a proof of concept for C-ITS-based public transport priority could be provided with the participation of various research partners, C-Roads relies on production-ready hardware available on the market. sig_c7f0b7c8993ae6e8b586.description: This is not a procurement notice or a call for tenders, but an information request/market survey with which Kaarinan kaupunki and the Municipality of Lieto (hereinafter the contracting authorities) are surveying the market for the procurement of capacity services. The purpose is to survey the operators in the market and to gather comments from suppliers. The objective is to obtain comprehensive information to support the implementation of the future procurement. Both the Municipality of Kaarina and the Municipality of Lieto aim to tender server capacity services as an open procedure due to an expiring agreement. The estimated commencement date of the agreements is September-October 2026. Description of the information request and invitation to market dialogue. Kaarinan kaupunki and the Municipality of Lieto are organising a joint market survey for the procurement of scalable and modern capacity services that meet certified security requirements (physical and information security): Katakri, ISO27001 or equivalent. Suppliers are requested to respond in writing to the questions concerning the procurement and to state their interest in participating in the market dialogue. Kaarinan kaupunki and the Municipality of Lieto produce their own basic IT services and also maintain their own servers. REGISTRATION Suppliers must respond to the questions in the information request and state their interest in participating in the market dialogue by Fri 6.2.2026 at 12.00 in the supplier service at https://kaarina.toimittajapalvelu.fi/. The contracting authorities will treat the responses confidentially. Based on the responses to the information request, the contracting authorities will continue the market survey with separate market dialogues. The market dialogues will be implemented as Teams discussion sessions between the Municipality of Kaarina, the Municipality of Lieto, and the supplier. The discussion sessions will be held with a maximum of six (6) suppliers. If there are more than six (6) companies registered for the market dialogue, the contracting authorities will select the most suitable suppliers for the dialogue based on their own criteria. The dialogues are intended to be implemented during February 2026. Any additional information concerning the discussions will be provided to the operators heard after registration. ADDITIONAL INFORMATION ABOUT THE NOTICE This notice is an information request for a market survey and dialogues. This notice does not request tenders. The descriptions presented in this notice are preliminary and indicative advance information on the procurement. The information request does not oblige the implementation of the procurement in the manner described in the information request. The contracting authority is not obliged to take into account the responses received to the information request when drawing up the call for tenders. Please note that all material is intended solely for the information request and the conduct of market dialogues. The market dialogues do not bind the contracting authorities to implement the procurement, nor do they bind the supplier to participate in a potential tendering procedure. Participating companies will not be paid compensation for responding or participating. Responding or failing to respond to the information request does not affect the tenderer's position in the actual tendering procedure. SCHEDULE The preliminary schedule plan aiming for the commissioning of the solution is as follows: - Invitation to participate in the market survey, January 2026 - Submission of market survey responses, February 2026 - Selection of suppliers for the market survey discussion, February 2026 - Market survey discussions, February 2026 - Publication of the call for tenders, March 2026 - Submission of tenders, March-April 2026 - Selection of solution, April 2026 - Contract negotiations, April-May 2026 - Service transfer and start-up project May-September 2026 - Production readiness September-October 2026
sig_c7f0b7c8993ae6e8b586.title: Information request / invitation to market dialogue: Capacity services

sig_c8711bccf2d90af0e921.description: Translink seek to engage with suppliers that can provide a suitable solution for a comprehensive Real-Time Bus tracking, prediction generation, operational and historical monitoring, display content and management solution across its Metro and Ulsterbus Fleet (c. 1660 buses). The solution will be used by Bus Service Operators to effectively monitor and manage Bus fleet related operations in real time as well as Passenger Information and Communication throughout Northern Ireland. Translink require the system to be capable of interfacing with on-street and on-board non-proprietary hardware through RTIG-T047 protocol, ensuring the provision of RTPI on existing Metro, Glider, and Ulsterbus services continues without interruption. Additionally, suppliers will be required to provide all necessary maintenance services. Before embarking on a tender process, we wish to engage with the marketplace to gather information which will be used to inform the sourcing strategy for this contract and thus, the procurement process. We are therefore seeking to engage with experienced Real Time Passenger Information and associated providers, which are capable of fulfilling the requirements listed above. It is anticipated that this contract will commence Q2 2027. Our requirements include, but are not limited to the following: · An open data approach to enable integration to ensure interoperability with other client systems to enhance data flow and automate manual processes. · Integrate with future systems and journey planners. · Provide comprehensive maintenance services for on-street and on-board hardware. · Ensure minimal quantity and frequency of faults and maintain the serviceability of the system. · Fleet Management & Live Vehicle Tracking. · Provide a predictive analysis solution that can support decision-making for control room staff · Driver Interface & Public Address system for Glider. · Performance and Management Reporting. · Provide drivers with intelligence on service performance and communication options. · Provide accurate and timely information about bus arrivals and departures at stops. · Provide on street display content management services. · Facilitate automated audio-visual next stop announcements on vehicles, configurable to multiple languages and tailored branded graphics. · Improve disruption management including passenger messaging. · Support future methods for providing information to passengers. · Implement a solution compatible with RTIG national standards for Traffic Signal Priority. sig_c8830f81cf1575e5bc83.description:
UWV purchases aids (communication facilities, suitable furniture and innovative aids) under this procurement framework for persons who are entitled to aids for the work and/or education situation. The estimated value of the contract is approximately €6,5 million per year. Custom furniture is a lot under the category: Suitable furniture. In this category, we request furniture to provide support at school or in the workplace that deviates from standard furniture. This category is characterised by the fact that the furniture must be able to be assembled to compensate for the user's individual limitations. Some aids will have to be completely adapted for the user. The aids in this lot must be able to be custom-adapted for every user. The aids within this lot: - School furniture: The purpose of school furniture is to physically support the pupil with a disability in such a way that the limitations are compensated. The pupil can follow the lesson with a suitable seating solution and/or at a functional work surface. - Office furniture: The purpose of office furniture is to physically support the User with a disability in such a way that the limitations are compensated. The User is able to carry out their work with a suitable seating solution and/or at a functional desk. Read more about this lot in Appendix 3 - Overview of Aids.; Driver's seats is a lot under the category: Suitable furniture. In this category, we request furniture to provide support at school or in the workplace that deviates from standard furniture. This category is characterised by the fact that the furniture must be able to be assembled to compensate for the user's individual limitations. Some aids will have to be completely adapted for the user. The purpose of the driver's seat is to physically support the user with a disability in such a way that the limitations are compensated. The user is able to operate their vehicle from a good seating position. The driver's seat can be installed in a variety of vehicles, such as a passenger car, lorry, forklift or crane. Read more about this lot in Appendix 3 - Overview of Aids.; Care furniture is a lot under the category: Suitable furniture. In this category, we request furniture to provide support at school or in the workplace that deviates from standard furniture. This category is characterised by the fact that the furniture must be able to be assembled to compensate for the user's individual limitations. Some aids will have to be completely adapted for the user. Care furniture is used to support the daily care of the user with a disability at a work or education location. The user is facilitated in making a transfer, is able to go to the toilet or can be changed by a carer. By care furniture we mean at least: - Electrically operated and mechanically mobile patient hoists, active or passive. Optionally available with slings and lifting bags in various sizes; - Changing tables, mechanically or electrically adjustable, including mattress and braked wheels. Available in various sizes and can be extended with accessories; - Toilet chairs in adult or child sizing, in the variants over the toilet, height-adjustable, mobile, tiltable. Can be extended with various accessories. Read more about this lot in Appendix 3 - Overview of Aids.; Communication aids is a lot under the category: Communication facilities. In this category, we request aids that ensure that information or communication is made accessible to people with a disability. Some aids must be able to be adapted to the individual needs of the User, for example by specific software or by linking various aids to the employer's or school's system. The following aids are included in this lot: - Braille displays - Electronic aids for enlarging or reading out text - Other communication aids (filter glasses and subtitling for group conversations) Read more about this lot in Appendix 3 - Overview of Aids.; Communication software and supporting IT resources is a lot under the category: Communication facilities. - Specialist software: Software that enables the user to take in information from a computer, making operation of the computer possible. The software is specifically intended to support users with a visual or motor disability because information is, for example, enlarged, read out, output in Braille, or operation of the computer via voice input is made possible. - Other specialist software: Software such as voice technology that converts whispered speech or affected speech into a clear, understandable voice or eye-tracking that makes operation of a computer possible through eye movement. - Supporting IT resources: Specialised software can be supplied in combination with hardware. By hardware, we mean supporting IT resources such as a laptop or tablet on which an operating system is installed. To operate these properly, an adapted keyboard or mouse may be necessary. Accessories such as a bag for the laptop may also be required. All these items fall under the heading of supporting IT resources. - Scripting: You are able to write scripts to be able to operate specific programmes using the supplied screen-reading or magnification software. The scripting ensures that the supplied software functions optimally with the specific programmes the user works with. Read more about this lot in Appendix 3 - Overview of Aids.;

Aids within the Innovation category are innovative solutions that do not fall under existing categories or other UWV procurement processes, such as new technologies, applications or products for specific target groups that are no longer experimental. Read more about this in Appendix 3 - Overview of Aids.

sig_c89edd1a0c56ec3ed85e.description: Limerick City Centre is undergoing a holistic change in the way that it manages its commuter traffic. The way in which commuters can use the road network within the city centre is being changed with the introduction of viable alternatives to the traditional car centric philosophies of the past. Enhancements through the introduction of Active travel infrastructure and future plans with respect to LSMATs and Bus connects projects will provide commuters with real viable alternatives when travelling to and from the City centre. The Mayoral program, supported by the Draft Limerick City Centre Transport Plan has the potential to enact further change in the way the city is viewed from a commuter perspective. Limerick City and County Council are aware that the proposed changes will create a number of opportunities and challenges for commuters, with one such challenge being the change to existing on street parking. It is the intention of this appointment to develop a parking strategy that will provide Limerick City and County Council a clear philosophy in the management of the existing and projected on street parking in the short, medium and long term as the projects outlined above come to fruition.

sig_c8d8a5a5f2c5bab2ebbc.description: Spark DPS Buy emerging technology products and services, including Internet of Things (IoT), AI and automation, simulated environments, wearables and new improvements in security. Description Spark: the Technology Innovation Marketplace can help government and public sector to access new and emerging technology products. This dynamic purchasing system (DPS) uses a filter system that helps customers find suppliers. The filter system includes defined technology areas developed with customer input. It focuses on emerging technologies predicted to have the largest impact over the next 2 to 5 years. There are 8 technology areas you can filter by: Internet of Things (IoT) Artificial Intelligence (AI) and automation Simulated and enhanced environments Engineering/materials science Data Wearables Transport Security Each of these areas contains between 3 and 17 sub-categories. The DPS filters help customers to identify and shortlist suppliers. The 2 main filters are: problem area technology type You can also filter by: location security classification Suppliers can apply to join the marketplace at any time, and identify their areas of expertise as part of the application process. Successful suppliers need to demonstrate their ability to offer suitably innovative products that meet either of the following 2 definitions: radical innovation: offering a new product, service, process or strategy introduced into a market designed to make a significant impact by completely replacing existing technologies and methods for example, streaming services replacing video rental stores disruptive innovation: creates a new market and value network and eventually disrupts an existing market and value network displacing established market-leading firms, products and alliances for example, light emitting diodes (LEDs) replacing traditional light bulbs As well as their ability to provide innovative products, the supplier’s contract example needs to explain the benefits for the end user and must be approved and confirmed by the customer. Once an application is complete, it can take can take up to a maximum of 15 working days to assess and appoint a supplier to the marketplace. A downloadable copy of the bid pack is available on the supplier registration service . Benefits access to proven technology innovation to solve public sector problems agility and flexibility to meet the public sector’s changing technology needs this agreement has no lots, use the filter system to produce a list of potential suppliers based on your needs quality and price assessment filtered to an individual customer’s requirements an efficient tender process and approach to finding potential solutions, including the option of using a 2 stage competition process and supplier presentations can be used for any size project, there is no minimum or maximum value Products and suppliers Please read the 'How to buy' tab below for detailed instructions on how to find out which suppliers are on this agreement. Lot 1: Spark DPS Expires: 15/02/2029 How to buy Make sure you have received budget approval and have read the RM6094 Spark customer guidance before using this agreement. The following instructions are for conducting a simple call for competition without use of: pre-tender market engagement (PTME) capability assessment presentation These are all also possible under the RM6094 Spark DPS. These terms are explained in the customer guide. Register as a buyer on the Dynamic Purchasing System Marketplace. note: although pages are headed ‘Supplier registration’ this is also where you can register as a buyer Go to the RM6094 Spark DPS under Technology and choose the “access as a buyer” option and confirm your acceptance of the customer access agreement. On your “manage your DPS category exports” page you now have 2 options: view appointed suppliers. click on the link to create a new category export. This is how you filter the suppliers that can meet your requirements When creating a new category use the filtering tool (select all that apply) to specify your requirements and create your supplier shortlist. Save your filtered list of capable suppliers by clicking the “save category” option and give the shortlist a unique name specific to your competition. From your “manage your category exports” page, export the list of suppliers and contact details. Export is to an Excel spreadsheet. Quit the DPS. Use the list to run a further competition. Invite the suppliers identified by the DPS to bid against your detailed specification, evaluation criteria and contract format. the list is valid for only 2 working days, from the date of its creation, because new suppliers may apply to join at any point if your call for competition excludes eligible suppliers it potentially breaches procurement regulations. You will need to get a fresh supplier list (steps 3.2 to 5) if you do not use your list within 2 working days by clicking the “search again” option for your export use our eSourcing tool to run a call for competition the tool is free to use for public sector buyers, or you can use your organisation’s own procurement tool Your tender process should align with the value and complexity of your requirement. Suppliers will need a reasonable period of time to review and prepare a response. This includes allowing enough time for suppliers to ask clarification questions and consider your answers before the deadline for written responses. Evaluate the responses. Request from winning supplier(s) any required evidence that they can meet your requirements. Set a deadline for submitting evidence for 2 days. If you are satisfied with the evidence, award the contract. Where appropriate, notify of the award on Contracts Finder . Explanation of terms: Pre- tender market engagement (PTME) This is optional but recommended and allows you to communicate with suppliers ahead of issuing your final specification to ensure that the market has a clear understanding of your requirements. It also allows you to: shape your specification gather ideas on new innovations understand if there are any changes within the market that may influence your requirements This exercise is not about refining your shortlist. You must provide an outline of your specification and you can ask suppliers specific questions regarding your requirements and specification and for feedback. Capability assessment This is optional but recommended and helps you to identify which suppliers from your shortlist are going to be most suitable. It can be used to refine your shortlist or to assess if any suppliers are capable of meeting your requirement. You can use a series of yes and no questions that suppliers must pass to get to the written stage. Face to face presentation This is also optional. It happens after the evaluation of the written proposals. It is an opportunity for face to face dialogue with the suppliers who were successful in reaching this stage. Suppliers can present more detailed proposals and answer any specific questions you may have regarding their written response. sig_c90d560f6a5febac5f2d.description: The Environmental Health team of the Care Department is responsible for the preparation, implementation and substantiation of preventive health policy regarding environmental health in Flanders. Environmental health is the component of preventive health policy that focuses on the prevention, early detection and intervention of environmental health damage through a multidisciplinary approach involving at least the scientific disciplines of medicine, toxicology, epidemiology, healthcare, environmental technology and environmental science. Within the Flemish Medical Environmental Health Network (VMMN), the team collaborates with various authorities, knowledge institutions and partner organisations for this purpose. The core activities of the team include climate and health, risk analysis, the promotion of a healthy public space, environmental health focus areas, recreational and drinking water quality, indoor environment, nature and health, and soil and health. Analyses are carried out to assess the environment-related health impact, and advice is formulated on environmental health aspects. However, the knowledge landscape within medical environmental science is growing extremely rapidly. New scientific insights, technological developments, changing regulations and international societal developments ensure a continuous stream of information. The systematic monitoring, assessment and application of this knowledge is currently largely manual and requires considerable staffing efforts. This increases the risk of knowledge gaps, while the Care Department is expected to base advice, policy decisions and health impact analyses on the most up-to-date and reliable insights. To address this challenge, the Care Department wishes to develop an AI-mediated knowledge surveillance system. This system must automatically detect, process, structure and make relevant information from internal and external sources accessible to policy officers and experts. The solution supports the monitoring of scientific literature, policy documents, reports, regulations and other knowledge sources, translating them into usable document fact sheets and syntheses. The system focuses on the four central storylines within Environmental Health: Substances of Very High Concern, Climate and Health, Healthy Public Space, and One Health. Knowledge is organised according to the source-exposure-burden-effect chain (SEBE), allowing users to find and apply relevant insights more quickly in dossiers, risk analyses, policy preparation and advice. These initiatives have their legal basis in the Prevention Decree, the Decree on General Provisions of Environmental Policy regarding environmental hygiene aspects, and the EIA Decree, and are deployed in accordance with the prioritisation of the Environmental Health health objective and the climate health plan. The intended solution supports human expertise but does not replace it. Interpretation, validation and policy-related explanation always remain the responsibility of substantive experts. Therefore, a human-in-the-loop approach is chosen, whereby AI-generated output is supplemented with quality controls and human validation. Furthermore, the solution must comply with applicable requirements regarding privacy, information security, AI governance and regulations, including the GDPR and the EU AI Act. It must connect to the Microsoft and Windows environment of the Care Department and be aligned with the Policy Information and Data (BID) and Communication and IT (CIT) departments, creating a secure, scalable and sustainably manageable solution that can also be applied in other teams within the Care Department.
sig_c90d560f6a5febac5f2d.title: Development of an AI-mediated knowledge surveillance system for environmental health

The aim is also to strengthen proactiveness and continuous development and ensure that the services take into account the special characteristics of the administrative network and educational network. sig_c9c9983895f4468f1aef.description: The purpose of this assignment is to conduct an intervention study into the effectiveness of existing preventive measures for reducing exposure to PFAS and heavy metals (at minimum lead and cadmium) via indoor dust in approximately 100 Flemish families with young children (0-6 years). The focus is on the "wet cleaning" measure, but any additional measures or combinations of measures may also be investigated. The study must provide insight into: • the effectiveness of preventive measures for reducing concentrations of PFAS and heavy metals in indoor dust; • the conditions under which these measures are most effective; • the influence of the frequency, quality and consistency of the application of the measures; • the possibilities for refining existing health advice for citizens. In addition, the assignment aims to strengthen the knowledge base regarding indoor dust by: • the development of reference values for concentrations of PFAS and heavy metals in indoor dust; • the further substantiation of a uniform and reproducible sampling methodology (settled dust) for indoor dust in comparison with outdoor dust. The contractor is responsible for the preparation, execution, analysis, interpretation and reporting of the study. The assignment includes, among other things: • project coordination; • development of a research protocol and study design; • preparation of questionnaires and procedures for participants; • development of an intervention strategy; • recruitment of participants; • execution of the sampling campaign; • laboratory analyses; • statistical analysis and scientific interpretation; • development of reference values for the measurement results; • the further substantiation of a uniform and reproducible sampling methodology for indoor dust; • feedback of the results and support with communication; • final reporting and transfer of the research data. The results of the study must support the Department of Care in the further scientific substantiation of health advice, communication and policy decisions regarding exposure to chemical substances via indoor dust.
sig_c9c9983895f4468f1aef.title: Intervention study into the effectiveness of preventive measures for reducing exposure via indoor dust

sig_c9e697a6cb69b664217d.description: **UPDATE 5 APRIL 2024: The proposal submission date has been updated to 24 April 2024. The FOA has been amended to reflect this submission date and include a Question and Answer document based on questions received from interested applicants. Other than the updated proposal submission date in the FOA, the actual FOA Amendment has not been changed. However, the answers provided in the Q&A document are considered part of the FOA Amendment.** **CYCLE 2 UPDATE 20 MARCH 2024 - THE OPPORTUNITY WEBINAR FOR CYCLE 2 WILL BE HELD ONLINE VIA MS TEAMS AT 1500 EDT ON 22 MARCH 2024 AT THE FOLLOWING LINK: https://dod.teams.microsoft.us/l/meetup-join/19%3adod%3ameeting_5fa41fe6fa874484b473d8a6ba7921c6%40thread.v2/0?context=%7b%22Tid%22%3a%22fae6d70f-954b-4811-92b6-0530d6f84c43%22%2c%22Oid%22%3a%22e9f6fc39-8f22-44e5-8bd0-64f0cde32305%22%2c%22IsBroadcastMeeting%22%3atrue%7d **UPDATE 14 MARCH 2024 - CYCLE 2 HAS BEEN POSTED TO THE ANNOUNCEMENT. PLEASE REVIEW THE UPDATED ANNOUNCEMENT IN FULL FOR SUBMISSION TIME, UPDATED TOPIC, AND FUNDING AMOUNT AND SCHEDULE CHANGES FROM CYCLE 1** TACTICAL BEHAVIORS FOR AUTONOMOUS MANEUVER COLLABORATIVE RESEARCH PROGRAM (TBAM-CRP) Future Army forces will be called upon to operate and maneuver in multi-domain operations (MDO), against a modern and capable peer adversary. The battlefield of the future may impose additional constraints on maneuver forces such as disruption in communication as well as positioning services. To field a highly capable fighting force in this future battlefield, novel tactics and doctrines leveraging nascent technologies in robotics and autonomous systems (RAS) will need to be developed. Teams of RAS will serve an increasingly critical role in the future force to deliver situational awareness, defend key locations or positions, or take point in dynamic and hazardous situations. Resilience to disruptions, failures, or unexpected scenarios, is a key quality for teams of RAS to operate alongside other future Army forces. The US Army Combat Capabilities Development Command (DEVCOM) Army Research Laboratory (ARL) is focused on developing fundamental understanding and informing the art-of-the-possible for warfighter concepts through research to greatly improve the scope of mission capabilities of teams of RAS, develop robust and resilient approaches to plan under extreme conditions of uncertainty, to learn coordinated strategies for groups of agents to achieve a common objective, all within a complex maneuver environment including adversaries. The Tactical Behaviors for Autonomous Maneuver Collaborative Research Program (TBAM-CRP) is focused on developing and experimentally evaluating coordinated and individual behaviors for small groups of autonomous agents to learn doctrinal as well as novel tactics for maneuvering in military relevant environments. The TBAM-CRP will leverage developments in other internal and extramural programs as well as identify new research directions to find novel solutions to these maneuver problems in analogical simulations representing complex realistic terrain. The Tactical Behaviors for Autonomous Maneuver Collaborative Research Program (TBAM-CRP) will consist of a series of sprint efforts executed with annual program reviews. Each topic will be focused on addressing a different set of scientific areas which will support the research aims of an associated ARL researcher from a related internal essential research program (ERP) or mission-funded program. The TBAM-CRP has been developed in coordination with other related ARL-funded collaborative efforts (see descriptions of ARL collaborative alliances at https://www.arl.army.mil/business/collaborativealliances/) and shares a common vision of highly collaborative academia-industry-government partnerships; however, it will be executed with a program model adapted from the Scalable, Adaptive, and Resilient Autonomy (SARA), which established a new paradigm for collaborative research. Some key properties of this new approach are described below: • TBAM-CRP sprint topics will be offered on a two-year cycle. Proposals will be solicited for a possible two-year period structured as a first-year pilot followed by a second-year option where the option may be awarded based upon progress assessed at an annual review. The FOA will be amended annually to identify a specific problem statement and scope for that specific cycle. The topics for each cycle will be chosen to address the long-term program goal. • Five new topics (Cycles 1-5) are expected in FY22, 24, 26, 28, 30. Each topic will be carefully chosen based on the previous accomplishments in the prior cycle(s), the development of new technologies and capabilities in the broader research and development communities, and the Army’s evolving needs for future capabilities. • For each topic, funding will be provided to those Recipients selected under a cooperative agreement (CA). • Enhanced Research Program funding from ARL or Other Government Agencies (OGAs) may become available during a cycle which provides a mechanism for growth and enhancement within the TBAM-CRP. A proposal should not include any discussion of the Enhanced Research Program. Recipients receiving a CA will be notified and provided details if the opportunity for Enhanced Research Program funding becomes available during their award period of performance. • There is no limitation on the place of performance, although on-site collaboration at ARL facilities and with ARL researchers as well as with other Recipients are encouraged. Research outcomes in this program must, at the very least, be demonstrated in sophisticated simulations of relevant environments. Together with ARL collaborators, these results may be adapted for higher TRL experimentation on surrogate platforms at ARL test facilities such as the Robotics Research Collaboration Campus (R2C2) at Graces Quarters, Aberdeen Proving Ground, Maryland. • Recipients will be furnished with access to the ARL Autonomy Stack software suite as well as all relevant simulation tools and multi-agent learning support. • Recipients will be provided with information about the current state of the Autonomous Systems Enterprise (ASE) with an overview of developments in the associated collaborative research alliances including Distributed and Collaborative Intelligent Systems and Technology (DCIST), Scalable, Adaptive, and Resilient Autonomy (SARA), as well as internal ARL essential research programs including the AI for Maneuver and Mobility (AIMM), Emerging Overmatch Technologies (EOT), and Versatile Tactical Power and Propulsion (VICTOR). Capabilities demonstrated in simulation should reflect significant appropriate developments. This midpoint review is expected to take place as a mini symposium where Recipients can share results with one another along with the ARL community to foster further collaboration. • At the end of the second year, a capstone demonstration will be executed by those Recipients receiving an option to their award in a set of simulated relevant environments, either those environment scenarios provided by the Government and other program performers, or optionally of a specific environment developed by the Recipient to exhibit their developed capability. Any system level capability demonstration that can be made with the internal ARL collaborator or description of capability development and program contribution can also be made at this time. These system demonstrations are expected to coincide to foster further integration and adoption with related internal research programs as well as partner organizations from within the DEVCOM, other Army and DoD service branches and agencies, in addition to other government agencies. Proposals that follow the requirements of the FOA will be evaluated in accordance with merit-based, competitive procedures. These procedures will include evaluation factors and an adjectival and color rating system. A review team, consisting of a qualified group of Government scientists and managers will evaluate the compliant proposals and provide the results of that evaluation to the decision-maker for the Government. Relevant internal research program materials approved for public release and contact information will be provided to potential proposers during introductory presentations to help facilitate identification of collaboration between proposers and individual ARL researchers or internal research programs. Additional connections to ARL programs can be identified during the proposal review process. Eligible applicants under this FOA include institutions of higher education, nonprofit organizations, and for-profit organizations (i.e., large and small businesses) for scientific research in the knowledge domains outlined throughout this Funding Opportunity. Federally Funded Research and Development Centers (FFRDC) may propose as well, with effort as allowed by their sponsoring agency and in accordance with their sponsoring agency policy.

sig_ca77100797b91d4e799c.description: Public employment services (PES) are the main agencies carrying out employment policies directly accountable to governments. They are set up to facilitate the labour market integration of jobseekers and the payment of unemployment and/or welfare benefits. PES are also the main actors implementing activation policies in the Member States, and they play an important role in facilitating successful labour market transitions and integration. The quality of their services has direct consequences for the impact of employment policies on the ground which makes PES key actors in fighting unemployment and tackling labour shortages in Europe. The aim of the contract is the provision of PES-specific expertise, methodological, operational and logistical support to the PES Network’s activities. This with the objective to support the implementation of Union-wide, evidence-based benchlearning among PES to compare, with appropriate methodology, the performance of their activities in relation to an Excellence Model in the areas of PES responsibility. This activity will be complemented by technical support to provision of mutual learning activities. sig_ca777df15499f5642027.description: THIS IS NOT A CONTRACT NOTICE OR CALL FOR TENDERS BUT AN INFORMATION REQUEST FOR MARKET CONSULTATION AND TECHNICAL DIALOGUE: This information request is used to survey the market and obtain information regarding the procurement. The contracting authority will not initiate a tendering procedure by publishing the information request, but a potential contract notice and call for tenders will be published later. The information request does not oblige the contracting authority to carry out the actual procurement. Answering the information request is not a prerequisite for participation in a possible subsequent tendering procedure. Suppliers will not be paid compensation for responding to the information request or participating in the market dialogue. The responses given to this information request will be used in planning the procurement of overall services related to the maintenance and operation of HUS's internal network, the "HUSnet network". HUS-yhtymä's IT Management is planning to renew the comprehensive service agreement for the HUSnet network. The computer network is a critical part of HUS-yhtymä's operations and includes a wide infrastructure of approx. 250 sites in the Uusimaa region as well as connections to cloud services. The equipment base consists of, among other things: - approx. 3 000 L2/L3 switches - approx. 10 000 WLAN access points - firewall environments - peripheral systems. The purpose of the information request and market dialogue is to survey various solution alternatives with which HUS-yhtymä's network environment can be maintained and developed, taking into account potential future requirements. Market dialogues will be held during February-March as in-person or Teams meetings. Service providers are requested to register by 11.2.2026 at kilpailutus.ict@hus.fi. Subject of the message: "HUS 580-2025/HUSnet services". In their responses, service providers are hoped to present their key service descriptions related to, among other things, network management, maintenance and development. In addition, presentations of reference implementations are desired. Advance material speeds up the dialogue held in the meeting. When proceeding to the procurement phase, suppliers who have responded to the information request may receive preliminary tender documents for comment.

sig_cb1bb32e7f6145733053.description: This is a SOURCES SOUGHT NOTICE. This is NOT a solicitation for proposals, proposal of abstracts or quotations. The purpose of this notice is to obtain information regarding: (1) the availability and capability of qualified sources; and (2) whether commercials sources and services are available in the marketplace. Your response to the information requested will assist the Government in determining the appropriate acquisition method, including whether a set-aside is possible. This notice is issued to help determine the appropriate acquisition method including small business socioeconomic set aside possibilities and to determine the availability of commercial or non-commercial companies technically capable of meeting the Government's potential requirement. It is not construed as a commitment by the Government to issue a solicitation or ultimately award a contract. Responses will not be considered as proposals or quotes. No award will be made as a result of this notice. The Government will NOT be responsible for any costs incurred by the respondents to this notice. This notice is strictly for research and information purposes only. Furthermore, it should be noted that any future solicitations that may be issued as a result of this notice, or in response to this requirement, may be issued using a different solicitation number from the one identified above. Background The National Institute on Drug Abuse (NIDA) was established in 1974, and in 1992 it became part of the National Institutes of Health, Department of Health and Human Services. NIDA’s mission is to advance science on drug use and addiction and to apply that knowledge to improve individual and public health through: 1) strategically supporting and conducting basic, clinical, and epidemiological research on drug use, its consequences, and the underlying neurobiological, behavioral, and social mechanisms involved; and 2) advancing the translation, effective implementation, and dissemination of scientific research findings to improve the prevention and treatment of SUDs, reduce adverse health consequences associated with drug use, and enhance public awareness of addiction as a chronic but treatable medical illness. NIDA’s Clinical Trials Network (CTN) was established in 1999 to bridge the gap between research and practice to improve treatment of substance use disorders (SUD) nationwide. The CTN seeks to address critical research questions with direct relevance to clinical practice and the needs of patients. Over the last two decades, the CTN’s research infrastructure and agenda have evolved to reflect the changing landscape of the SUD treatment community, transformation of health care systems, and emerging scientific advancements. The CTN has been engaging providers in general medical settings and healthcare systems, and in 2015 the Network built upon and expanded its research portfolio encouraging adoption of innovative bioinformatics approaches, new technology, and "learning healthcare system" principles to enhance the efficiency of SUD clinical research and clinical care. The CTN conducts clinical trials in sites located across the nation and in other countries. These are usually studies of behavioral, pharmacological, and integrated behavioral and pharmacological treatment interventions in rigorous, clinical trials to determine efficacy, effectiveness, practicality, and feasibility across a broad range of treatment settings and diversified patient populations, and to transfer research results to physicians, clinicians, providers, and patients. These studies are typically Phase III clinical trials, but can also include Phase I, Phase II, Phase IV, and/or registry trials or surveys. More information on the CTN and the CTN’s research portfolio is available at https://nida.nih.gov/organization/center-clinical-trials-network-cctn/clinical-trials-network-ctn. Requirement NIDA is seeking capability statements from businesses having the capability to act as a data, statistics, and clinical trial service center; providing data and clinical research services and resources in managing and carrying out approximately 20 independent trials in drug use and addiction research at any given time. NIDA requires vendors capable of providing systems for data management, statistical analysis, document management and clinical trial services. The data systems will be used to manage and implement clinical data capture, data analysis, information exchange, scientific discovery efforts and clinical evaluation of promising new substance use disorder treatment medications and interventions in order to further NIDA’s mission. NIDA conducts single and multi-site clinical trials through grants, contracts and cooperative agreements in sites located across the nation and in other countries. These are usually studies of behavioral, pharmacological, and integrated behavioral and pharmacological treatment interventions in rigorous, clinical trials to determine efficacy, effectiveness, practicality, and feasibility across a broad range of treatment settings and diversified patient populations and to transfer research results to physicians, clinicians, providers, and patients. These studies could be Phase I, Phase II, Phase III, and/or Phase IV type trials. They may also include registry type trials or surveys. Although no actual clinical trials will be conducted under this requirement, the project activities will be integrated and central to NIDA trials in the following areas: Establish and administer state-of-the-art, secured web-based systems for the collection, storage, management, quality assurance, and reporting of study data as well as systems to facilitate the collection and management of participant and site level electronic health records data. Assist in the design and analysis of clinical trials, including the development of the statistical sections of protocols, study design, randomization and stratification methods, power and sample size calculations, interim monitoring and analysis plans, and data analytic plans. Review and monitor the quality of study data including the development and management of a computerized data monitoring system that executes quality assurance and quality control procedures to evaluate accuracy, timeliness and completeness of data submitted by the clinical sites, including verification of the clinical and laboratory data used to determine that study participants have reached protocol-defined endpoints. Monitor trial performance and progress and maintain a secure web-based clinical trial performance monitoring system to track key trial performance metrics (e.g. key dates, recruitment, availability of primary outcomes, missing data, etc.). Coordinate meetings of study Data and Safety Monitoring Boards (DSMB) to include the preparation and presentation of reports on safety, data integrity, and site performance as well as coordination of meeting sites, materials, travel support, etc. Participate in relevant committee and subcommittee meetings including representation by the contract Principal Investigator on the CTN Steering Committee and representation by other senior data and statistical experts on other relevant CTN committees, subcommittees and workgroups. Provide consultation, data analytical services, and expertise in certain fields relating to study design and analysis, compiling and editing of clinical data, and other services related to clinical trials operations that might be required. Instructions: The established NAICS code is 541715 Research and Development in the Physical, Engineering, and Life Sciences (except Nanotechnology and Biotechnology). The U.S. Small Business Administration establishes a size standard for 541715 of 1,000 employees or fewer. Interested large or small business organizations shall demonstrate and document in the submitted capability statement extensive experience in the technical areas listed above. Furthermore, information sent should be relevant and specific in the technical area under consideration, on each of the following qualifications: Work Experience: Capable Vendors must demonstrate the capability and experience to act as a data, statistics, and clinical trial service center; providing data and clinical research services and resources in managing and carrying out approximately 20 independent trials in drug use and addiction research at any given time. NIDA requires vendors capable of providing systems for data management, statistical analysis, document management and clinical trial services. The data systems will be used to manage and implement clinical data capture, data analysis, information exchange, scientific discovery efforts and clinical evaluation of promising new substance use disorder treatment medications and interventions in order to further NIDA’s mission. Organizational Experience: Capable Vendors should describe previous similar projects in the area(s) specified above and where the work was of a similar size and scope. In the response be sure to indicate if you were the prime contractor or a subcontractor. If a subcontractor, be sure to identify your roles and responsibilities as the subcontractor; what percentage of work your subcontract was responsible for; and identify the prime contractor. Personnel: Capable Vendors should identify personnel with the appropriate education, credentials, training, qualifications, experience, and competence to carry out the projects and the tasks identified above. Knowledge and experience in this field of work is critical, and the overall work efforts should be led by professionals who have earned a doctorate degree in a related field of study. Individual efforts and tasks should be led by professionals who have earned a master’s degrees in a related field of study. Basic credentials for proposed personnel will require experience in clinical trials management, biostatistics, drug use and addiction research, data management, statistics. Capable Offerors shall demonstrate how they have staffed similar key personnel on other contracts. Facilities: Capable Vendors should describe the physical space (e.g. offices, meeting rooms, server room, etc.) necessary to accommodate the required staff and equipment as well as the necessary mechanical systems (e.g. HVAC, fire suppression, redundant power, etc.); IT systems and hardware necessary to support the work including sufficient internet access, electronic data collection systems for study data, in-house or cloud based servers for storage of study data, and business software such as the MS Office suite; and security measures including physical and IT access controls, system monitoring, data backup processes, and firewalls. Interested Offerors should describe their facilities or demonstrate its ability to obtain the facilities necessary to support the requirements discussed above. The Government will assess the appropriateness of the responses based on the described work experience, organizational experience, personnel, and facilities described in the capability statement. If the Vendor proposes to team with another organization, please be sure to include the capabilities of any potential proposed partners. The Government will consider any other specific and relevant information about this procurement that would improve our consideration and assessment of the information presented. Documentation may include, but not be limited to, contracts both Government and commercial the organization performed, references, i.e., names, titles, telephone numbers and any other information serving to document the organizations capability, e.g., awards, commendations, etc. THIS IS NOT A REQUEST FOR PROPOSALS: This notice is for information and planning purposes only and does not commit the Government to any contractual agreement. The Government does not intend to award a contract based on responses under this announcement nor otherwise pay for preparing any information sent for the Government's use. Any proprietary information should be so marked. The Government reserves the right to use information provided by respondents for any purpose deemed necessary and legally appropriate. Any organization responding to this notice should ensure that its response is complete and sufficiently detailed to allow the Government to determine the organization’s qualifications to perform the work. Respondents are advised that the Government is under no obligation to acknowledge receipt of the information received to provide feedback to respondents with respect to any information submitted. All capability statements must provide the following: 1) company name, address; and DUNS number; 2) point of contact; 3) phone/fax/email; 4) NAICS Code(s); 5) business size and status; 6) the capability information in response to the requirement and qualification identified in this notice; and; 7) type of small business your organization classifies itself as, if applicable (i.e.: women-owned, HUBZONE, etc.). Based on preliminary market research, the Government has determined that the requirements described herein do not meet the definition of a commercial product or commercial service as defined in RFO 2.101, and therefore, RFO Part 12 procedures are not applicable to this requirement. However, if a capable vendor believes that these services or products qualify as commercial under FAR 2.101, the vendor may submit a written justification for the Contracting Officer's consideration. Such submissions must be provided to the Contracting Officer no later than September 30, 2026 at 1:00 PM EST. Capability statements must be SUBMITTED ELECTRONICALLY NO LATER THAN 1:00 P.M. (EST) WEDNESDAY, SEPTEMBER 30, 2026 to the primary point of contact. The Subject line for the submission should include the Title and this Sources Sought Number (75N98026R00157OT).

sig_cb22e8fe1c7ac296ad80.description: Abertay University is a specialist university based in Dundee with approximately 5,000 students. The University is seeking to modernise and enhance its digital experience platforms to better support student recruitment, engagement, communication and service delivery. As part of this market engagement exercise, suppliers are asked to consider the University's scale, resources and strategic ambitions when outlining potential solutions, delivery approaches and indicative costs. This will help ensure responses are proportionate to Abertay's requirements while providing a sustainable foundation for future digital transformation initiatives. Abertay University is seeking to engage with the market to understand the availability of solutions capable of delivering a modern, integrated digital experience platform, or integrated set of platforms and services, to support the University's website, intranet and web/mobile portal requirements. Lot 1: . The University is seeking to improve student recruitment and conversion, enhance staff and student engagement, strengthen digital communications, simplify content management and provide a more joined-up and personalised digital experience across its key digital channels The scope includes: - A public-facing website serving as the University's primary digital channel for student recruitment and conversion, marketing and communications, promotion of courses and research, and engagement with prospective students, partners and external stakeholders. - A staff and student intranet platform providing audience-specific content and communications. - A web and mobile portal experience (currently delivered through the myday platform) providing staff and students with personalised access to university services, learning resources, communications, academic information and other digital services. The University is interested in understanding whether these requirements are best met through a single platform, a suite of integrated products, or an alternative architectural approach, together with the associated benefits, risks, implementation considerations and indicative costs. The University wishes to gather information from suppliers on potential solutions, delivery approaches, operating models, implementation considerations and indicative costs to inform a future procurement strategy and business case.
sig_cb22e8fe1c7ac296ad80.title: Web Content Management System (website, intranet and web/mobile portal)

sig_cb7978fbabd6d82fcf38.description: Update - 14 Sep 26 The purpose of this update is to clarify procurement history of this requirement. While this is not a follow-on acquisition, portions of this requirement are currently being satisfied under FA251824D0001 awarded to Gemini Technical Services JV, LLC. I. General Information: The Government does not intend to award a contract on the basis of this Sources Sought or reimburse any costs associated with the preparation of responses. This Sources Sought is issued solely for informational and planning purposes and does not constitute a solicitation. All information received in response to this notice marked "Proprietary" will be handled accordingly. In accordance with RFO 15.101(c), responses to this notice are not offers and cannot be accepted by the Government to form a binding contract. Responses to this Sources Sought will assist the Government in determining the potential level of interest, competition adequacy, and technical capabilities of industry respondents (specifically small businesses) to provide the required products and services. The Government may also use this information to assist in determining whether a small business set-aside (or other socioeconomic set-aside) will be appropriate or developing any subsequent small business subcontract participation and small business goal percentages. The Government does not intend to respond to questions posed in Industry responses. The Government does not guarantee any action beyond this notice. Please be advised that all submissions become Government property and will not be returned. Responses that are incomplete and/or not submitted per the Response Submission Instructions may not be reviewed. Interested parties or potential contractors must be registered with the System for Award Management (SAM) before the issuance of a potential Request for Proposals/Quotes to be eligible for contract award or payment if the Government chooses to make an award. Information on registration and annual confirmation requirements may be obtained via SAM.gov. Conflict of interest rules apply, and offerors will be required to submit mitigation plans following the release of the RFP. II. Requirement Information: This Sources Sought notice seeks to identify qualified firms capable of providing comprehensive, non-personal mission support services for the 392d Combat Training Squadron (392 CTS). Under this framework, contractor personnel will deliver core capabilities to plan, integrate, execute, and assess Modeling and Simulation (M&S)-enabled exercises (including SPACE FLAG, FLASH POINT, POLARIS HAMMER, and SPACE SKIES) in support of U.S., joint, and allied warfighters. To ensure the continuous readiness of United States Space Force (USSF), joint and coalition forces, this expertise spans a critical array of warfare domains, including Satellite Communications (SATCOM), Global Positioning Systems (GPS), Electronic Attack (EA), Orbital Warfare (OW), Space Electronic Warfare (SEW), Space Domain Awareness (SDA), Missile Warning (MW), and Offensive Cyber Operations (OCO). Furthermore, contractor personnel will drive operational execution by providing Command and Control (C2) support, intelligence product generation, operations assessments, and lessons learned (L2). This operational framework is firmly underpinned by robust technical requirements, encompassing full-scope IT and cybersecurity support, systems engineering, configuration management, orbital analysis, and sophisticated M&S for the Distributed Mission Operations Center-Space (DMOC-S) and BattleLab enclaves. Ultimately, these integrated capabilities will be leveraged to design, plan, execute, and assess USSF service-level exercises and advanced mission-focused training. Support includes programs identified as Sensitive Compartmented Information (SCI) and Special Access Required (SAR) administered under the enhanced security guidelines/procedures authorized by Department of Defense DODI 5200.01 (DoD Information Security Program and Protection of Sensitive Compartmented Information) and AFI 16-1404 (Air Force Information Security Program). Responses to this announcement are needed to help inform acquisition planning and to identify capable sources. To efficiently and effectively deliver the required supplies/services, it is anticipated that vendors will have specialized experience in large-scale space exercises, complex IT and M&S environments, and managing highly cleared personnel. III. Purpose: The Government is currently considering NAICS Code 541330 (Engineering Services) and Product Service Code (PSC) R425 (Support – Professional: Engineering/Technical) for this requirement. If your firm believes this requirement should be solicited under a different NAICS code or PSC, please include your detailed rationale and supporting market data within your response. This synopsis is encouraging responses from qualified and capable Small Businesses. Firms responding to this Sources Sought must be U.S. owned and must (1) state whether they are a small or large business based on the size standard above; (2) state if they have socioeconomic classification(s) as follows: Small Disadvantaged Business (SDB); section 8(a) small business; Woman-Owned Small Business (WOSB); Economically-Disadvantaged Woman-Owned Small Business (EDWOSB); a Historically Underutilized Business (HUB) Zone small business; Service-Disabled Veteran-Owned Small Business (SDVOSB);. Small Businesses that are in or are considering Joint Ventures or Mentor Protégé Agreements are encouraged to respond to the source sought. Responses from other than small businesses will be reviewed. Note: If the requirement is set aside for small business, the clause RFO 52.219-14, Limitations on Subcontracting, will be included in the contract. The data obtained from this notice will assist the Government in understanding the capabilities available in providing advanced space training, exercise execution, and mission rehearsal capabilities. IV. Scope of Anticipated Effort: The 392 CTS provides space combat training through Live, Virtual, & Constructive (LVC) environments to prepare warfighters to achieve and maintain operational dominance in the space domain. The contractor shall provide Mission Support Services, Information Technology, Communications, and Management Support (ITC&MS), and Advisory and Assistance Services (A&AS). The Government anticipates this requirement will consist of an IDIQ ordering period of five years. Work will primarily take place at Schriever SFB, Suffolk, Buckley SFB, Hurlburt Field, Vandenberg SFB, and other designated facilities. V. General Submission Instructions: The responses submitted shall be in sufficient detail and clarity to provide the Government with the information it needs. Responses to this Source Sought notice shall meet the following standards: Page Limitations: Section 1 Cover Letter: 2 Pages Section 2 Capability Statement: 10 Pages Section 3 PWS Review: 3 Pages Text Size: No smaller than 10 point Text included in graphics, tables, and figures can be no smaller than 9 point No embedded documents Fully address Sections 1-3 as outlined above Responses that are incomplete and or do not follow these Response Submission Instructions may not be reviewed Electronic version of your response only in Microsoft Word or PDF compatible files VI. Section 1 - Cover Letter: The cover letter shall include the following: Company information: Company name 2 points of contact and with contact information (name, address, phone number, website URL, if available, and email address) Cage Code, UEI, and DUNS Number Short description of the company (history, experience in similar service activities/supplies, etc.). Company business size with socioeconomic classification based on the designated NAICS code Information on any potential teaming arrangements, joint ventures, or significant subcontracting arrangements. VII. Section 2 – Capability Statement: Please provide detailed responses to the following questions based on the draft PWS. For each area, identify your firm's current or recent (completed within the last five years) contracts or subcontracts that match the scope, complexity, and magnitude of this PWS. Highlight prime contract experience supporting Space Force Delta-level organizations, Distributed Mission Operations Nodes, or equivalent joint distributed simulation hubs of similar financial magnitude: Plan and Execute Large-Scale Joint LVC Exercises (USSF Service Exercises). Plan, coordinate, execute, and assess large-scale (700+ participants) military exercises. Detail your proven experience managing the full Joint Exercise Life Cycle (JELC) across geographically distributed nodes. Provide a specific historical example of where you translated joint space doctrine into dynamic Master Scenario Events List (MSEL) injects (e.g., simulated orbital debris, electronic attack) within a LVC environment. Finally, describe your capability to conduct post-exercise analysis and deliver formal After-Action Reports (AAR). Recruit and Retain Specialized TS/SCI/SAP Personnel. Explain your relevant experience in recruiting, clearing, and retaining qualified personnel with Top Secret (TS)/Sensitive Compartmented Information (SCI) clearances and Special Access Program (SAP) eligibility. Include historical metrics (such as average time-to-fill rates for tactical space domains and historical retention rates exceeding 90%). DMOC-S Operations. Operate, sustain, and manage the DMOC-S and its complex M&S environment certified to Joint National Training Capability (JNTC) standards. Provide a specific example of how your team successfully operated systems involving missile warning, Signals Intelligence (SIGINT), and operational RF communications. Demonstrate your experience managing distributed simulation networks (e.g. JTEN, DMON) and utilizing standard architecture protocols (e.g., DIS, HLA) to link space simulators with joint air, land, and maritime simulators. Multi-Domain Information Technology (IT) and Cybersecurity Support. Deliver comprehensive IT, cybersecurity, and network engineering support across multiple security enclaves (e.g., AFSCI, SIPRNet, Stone Ghost/FVEY coalition networks) at both primary and distributed locations. Detail your experience maintaining system configurations, securing Assessment and Authorization (A&A) packages via eMASS under the Risk Management Framework (RMF), and performing concurrent cybersecurity auditing (such as STIG compliance). Decribe your experience rapidly-restoring network outages during high-tempo, simulated LVC exercise operations without degrading the training audience’s experience. Professional Planning and Control Force (PPCF) Support. Manage and oversee a distributed workforce of full-time, embedded M&S and exercise planners deployed to geographically separated USSF Component Commands (e.g., SPACEFOR-INDOPAC, SPACEFOREUR-AF). Describe your firm’s experience interfacing directly with senior combatant command staff. Provide examples of previous contracts your company has had that had embedded planners responding to local theater commanders’ Operational Plans. Surge Capacity and Contingency Operations. Manage, schedule, and execute approximately 15,000 hours of surge support annually, frequently requiring 24/7 operations to support exercises with little to no notice. Detail contractual experience executing large-scale, short-notice surge requirements. Specifically, how you maintained and deployed a pool of cleared, pre-screened, or cross-trained personnel to sustain 24/7 operations during massive events without causing mission failure or degrading steady-state services. VIII. Section 3 - SOW/PWS Review: Please identify areas within the draft PWS that are unclear, restrictive, or present execution obstacles, referenced by PWS paragraph number. Additionally, outline any best commercial practices, industry innovations, and recommendations for the most effective contract type and pricing structure to efficiently support the 15,000-hour annual exercise surge requirement.

The subject of the contract is the implementation of pilot studies serving to gather empirical data for the purposes of testing methodological and organisational solutions supporting the accessibility of education and monitoring the effectiveness of support provided to children and pupils in the education system.
