sig_cbb9280876598968a99b.description: This notice serves exclusively to conduct a non-binding market consultation in accordance with section 28 paragraph 1 of the Ordinance on Public Procurement (VgV). The aim of the market consultation is to inform the market at an early stage about a potential future procurement requirement and to gather insights on technical, economic and organisational solution approaches, current market conditions, the competitive situation and the fundamental feasibility of the planned project. In particular, the market consultation serves to identify advantages and disadvantages of potential performance components, to record existing market experience and to examine whether and to what extent multiple companies can offer comparable services. In this way, a well-founded overview of market interest and the current competitive situation is to be obtained. The present notice is expressly neither a contract notice nor an invitation to submit tenders or requests to participate. No procurement procedure is initiated by conducting the market consultation. The contracting authority is not obliged to conduct a procurement procedure on the basis of the market consultation and is not bound by its results. Participation does not establish any legal claims whatsoever, in particular no claim to the conduct of a procurement procedure or to consideration in any potential subsequent procurement procedure. Participation in the market consultation is voluntary and free of charge. Participating companies will not be reimbursed for any costs incurred by them in connection with participation, the preparation of statements, concepts or the submission of documents. Participation in the market consultation is not a prerequisite for later participation in a procurement procedure and has no influence on a company's chances of being awarded the contract. The contracting authority requests interested market participants to provide meaningful, comprehensible and advanced feedback. In particular, comments on possible implementation variants, economic framework conditions, opportunities and risks, potential problems or obstacles in implementing the intended concept, as well as own ideas and suggestions for improvement are requested. Where possible, feedback should be provided in a structured format. Interested companies are requested to express their interest immediately and informally by email to ta-vergabestellevol@hu-berlin.de and to submit their statements, ideas, proposals for implementation and economic assessments. Following the evaluation of the submitted documents, selected interested parties may be invited to explain their concepts in more detail as part of a structured dialogue. This deepening can take place in the form of an on-site appointment or alternatively via video or telephone conference and serves to clarify open questions and to evaluate the impact of the proposed solution approaches on the requirements of the contracting authority. All documents submitted as part of the market consultation shall become the property of the contracting authority. By participating, interested parties agree that their submitted concepts, evaluations, proposals and other findings may be used to prepare a potential procurement and to develop implementation proposals and, to the extent necessary, may be passed on to the contracting authority, unless this is expressly objected to. Ideas and suggestions from market participants may, where applicable in anonymised form, become part of a later specification of requirements. The contracting authority guarantees the protection of business and trade secrets. Information obtained as part of the market consultation will not be passed on to third parties, with the exception of the contracting authority itself and, where applicable, consulting firms commissioned by it. The market consultation is to be carried out promptly and is expected to be concluded by February 2026. All submitted feedback will be evaluated and made available to the contracting authority in a consolidated form. Should the contracting authority initiate a procurement procedure based on the results of the market consultation, it will take appropriate measures to exclude any distortion of competition. These include in particular the equal treatment of all interested companies, the provision of relevant information to all applicants and tenderers, and the setting of appropriate deadlines. Anticipated schedule • Expression of interest to participate: immediately • Submission of initial concept: 30.01.2026 at 12.00 hours • Presentations and interviews: February 2026

sig_cc13392d2c6618625b23.description: Medway Council (‘the Authority’) is a unitary authority based in Kent, consisting of the main towns of Strood, Rochester, Chatham, Gillingham, and Rainham. The highway network in the Medway towns covers approximately 840km, with 110km of A roads, 37km of B roads, 97km of C road, and 596km of unclassified roads. A safe and effective transport network is therefore key to Medway’s sustainability, both economically and environmentally. To help achieve this the Council are inviting applications to join Medway Council’s Road Safety Audit Framework (MCRSAF). The MCRSAF will allow the Authority, as the Overseeing Organisation, to quickly and efficiently commission an outside contractor to undertake road safety audits on behalf of the Authority for highway schemes and interventions. The aim is to have a pool of high-quality auditors that the Authority can call upon to undertake Road Safety Audits quickly, cost effectively, to a high standard, and in accordance with the requirements and methodology of GG119 of the Design Manual for Roads and Bridges, with the Authority acting as the Overseeing Organisation. The Framework Contract is anticipated to commence on 1st November 2026 and will continue for a period of two years, with the option of extending the Framework Contract for an additional two years thereafter, via two separate one year extensions. For more information about this opportunity, please visit the eSourcing portal at: https://www.delta-esourcing.com/tenders/UK-UK-Chatham:-Road-inspection-services./7664JF53XM To respond to this opportunity, please click here: https://www.delta-esourcing.com/respond/7664JF53XM Lot 1: .

sig_cc2a89a7cc9fd496b5e0.description: The Department for Digital, Culture, Media and Sport (DCMS) intends to procure commercial satellite-derived Earth Observation (EO) data and associated Earth Observation services for use across the UK public sector. The procurement will support improved access to commercial EO capabilities, reduce duplicated procurement activity, enable greater sharing and reuse of data across government, and support evidence-based decision making across a range of public sector activities. The procurement has been designed following extensive engagement with public sector users and suppliers and reflects the Authority’s objective of establishing a more coordinated approach to the acquisition and use of commercial EO data and services. The procurement will comprise two Lots: Lot 1 – Core Commercial Earth Observation Data A contract for the supply and licensing of core commercial optical satellite-derived Earth Observation data for use across the UK public sector. The successful supplier will provide data, associated rights, metadata, quality assurance information and supporting services required to support delivery through an access model. Lot 2 – Specialist Earth Observation Services A single-supplier call-off contract for specialist Earth Observation data products, monitoring services and analytical capabilities. Anticipated demand does not constitute guaranteed expenditure or supplier revenue. The procurement will be conducted using a Competitive Flexible Procedure through the Government Commercial Agency Space Technology Solutions Dynamic Market (RM6370). The Authority intends to award one contract under each Lot. Contracts are expected to be awarded for an initial period of three years with an option to extend for up to one additional year. The procurement is expected to support public sector use cases including environmental monitoring, infrastructure management, climate resilience, emergency response, agricultural monitoring, rural payments, land management and wider policy development. It has been structured to support both established suppliers and specialist providers, including SMEs, consortia and supply chain arrangements where appropriate. The information in this notice remains subject to final decision-making and suppliers should refer to the Tender documentation once published for final details. Dynamic Market Participation Participation in the procurement will be limited to suppliers admitted to the CCS Space Technology Solutions Dynamic Market (RM6370). Suppliers who are not currently members of the Dynamic Market are encouraged to apply for admission as soon as possible. As the Dynamic Market remains open throughout its lifetime, suppliers may seek admission at any stage prior to the procurement closing date. The Authority wishes to maximise competition and encourages all capable suppliers to register. Supplier registration: CCS Space Technology Solutions Dynamic Market (RM6370) The Authority recommends that suppliers allow sufficient time to complete the Dynamic Market admission process before the tender submission deadline. Lot 1: Core Commercial Data. Lot 1 covers the supply and licensing of core commercial optical EO data for use across the UK public sector. The scope of Lot 1 may include: • Current commercial optical EO data products. • Historic imagery to support temporal analysis, seasonal comparison and change detection. • Associated metadata and quality assurance information. • Licensing rights and permissions required to support public sector access and use. Data delivery, integration support and associated technical services required to support the Authority's intended delivery model. Lot 2: Specialist EO data products, monitoring services and analytical capabilities. Lot 2 - eligible UK public sector organisations may procure specialist EO data products, monitoring services and analytical capabilities from the awarded supplier via call-off. The scope of Lot 2 may include: • Routine monitoring data services • Higher resolution and tasked data services • Historic and archive data services • Analytics and monitoring services • Validation and decision-support services • Field evidence collection services • Data access, hosting and delivery services associated with specialist EO products and services • Implementation, training and user support services required to support operational use The Lot 2 contract will not create a commitment by the Authority or any User to place a Call-Off Order.
sig_cc2a89a7cc9fd496b5e0.title: Earth Observation: Data Products and Services for the UK Public Sector 'Public Sector EO'

sig_cc2ed55955b67679d6ab.description: DRS is undertaking a strategic transformation of its rail fleet and asset management system in anticipation of the Maximo contract ending in November 2026. The current system, Maximo 7.6, is underutilised, with less than 20% of its functionality actively used and it presents ongoing challenges. As part of this process, we are hosting a Supplier Engagement Day on Monday, 27th October. On this day we intend to go through more details around our requirements. To be invited, suppliers are invited to contact the email [daniel.scott@ntsglobal.uk] and you will be sent an engagement form to complete. I would ask all supplier that wish to attend the engagement day to return the form by 12:00 noon on 24th October. The project aims to select and implement a modern, fit-for-purpose, off-the-shelf solution by October 2026. This system will enhance user experience, improve integration with the wider digital ecosystem, reduce operational and support costs, and unlock greater value from asset data. The vision is to operate with an intuitive, scalable solution that serves as a single source of truth for all maintenance records and activities, enabling better decision-making, improved compliance, and enhanced operational performance. This transformation will support operational excellence, flexibility, scalability, and long-term sustainability across DRS’s rail operations Lot 1: .

The EnBW Energie Baden-Württemberg AG intends, within the framework of this negotiated procedure with a call for competition, to award framework agreements for IT Consulting: Cybersecurity - Security Operations. This tender aims to conclude framework agreements for the provision of consulting, analysis and optimisation services in the field of cybersecurity, starting from approx. 01.04.2026 until presumably 31.03.2029 with two extension options of 12 months each. As EnBW, we operate not only nationally but also in an international environment and therefore require services not only onshore, but also in nearshore; to establish a common understanding, these classifications are defined below: - Onshore: Germany, Austria - Nearshore: All European states incl. Switzerland, UK and Turkey, but excl. Germany, Austria. Subject of the tender: Security Operations The subject of the tender comprises the further development and optimisation of operational IT security processes with a focus on the analysis and improvement of SOC/CDC structures. This includes the conception and implementation of SIEM use cases, the automation of detection and response measures, and the integration of modern security technologies for the comprehensive monitoring and protection of the IT infrastructure. A detailed service description for this tender can be found in Annex 05_Service Description and 05.1_Annex_Software Development Process. sig_cc439205178d725a8b77.description: Design (DTAC+PT+CS+DE) + technical assistance during the execution of works and execution of works, related to the investment objective ” Sărata Photovoltaic Panel Park”. The number of days up to which clarifications can be requested by economic operators, before the deadline for the submission of tenders : 20 days. The contracting authority shall respond to all requests for clarification and/or additional information received from economic operators, in relation to the tender documentation, 10 days before the deadline for the submission of tenders. The estimated value of the procurement is 20.550.373,85 lei without VAT, of which: Stage I design + technical assistance: 130.000,00 lei without VAT Stage II execution of works: 20.420.373,85 lei without VAT. The Municipality of Bistrița has concluded financing contract no. 1063/28.05.2025 with the Ministry of Energy for the realisation of the project ” Sărata Photovoltaic Panel Park ” , financed through the modernisation programme (MEFM) managed by the Ministry of Energy. Specific Objective I – ESTABLISHMENT OF A PRODUCTION UNIT FOR ENERGY FROM RENEWABLE SOURCES, RESPECTIVELY SOLAR SOURCES The objective targets the acquisition of technological equipment with and without assembly, respectively works, with the aim of establishing a production unit for energy from solar sources. The specific objective envisages the execution of specific works for the operationalisation of a renewable energy production unit to be characterised by the following functional parameters: - Newly installed capacity for producing energy from renewable sources: 3.961,44 kWp / 3.900 kW AC; - Net production of primary energy of 391,16 toe/year from renewable sources; - Total net electricity production of 86.623,20 MWh over a period of 20 years; The specific objective is correlated with the indicators assumed through the Financing Application, contributing to ensuring a significant share of the electricity requirement of the Municipality of Bistrița from renewable sources, namely solar sources. Specific Objective II – REDUCTION OF CARBON FOOTPRINT AND PROMOTION OF THE USE OF ENERGY FROM RENEWABLE SOURCES The specific objective envisages reducing the carbon footprint of the Municipality of Bistrița by reducing greenhouse gas emissions resulting from the production of energy necessary for carrying out its own activity. To this end, the implementation of the investment project contributes to reducing greenhouse gases by 53.004,74 tonnes of CO2 equivalent over a period of 20 years (considering a conversion factor of 0,6119 tonnes of CO2 equivalent/MWh). Also, the specific objective envisages promoting the use of energy from renewable sources, the implementation of the investment project contributing to ensuring self-consumption from renewable sources to the detriment of using energy originating from greenhouse gas emission-generating sources. The specific objective targets the use in a percentage of 100% of the electricity produced at the level of the photovoltaic power plant for the self-consumption of the Municipality of Bistrița. The project “Sărata Photovoltaic Panel Park ” will be carried out on a plot of land located in the extra-muros area of the municipality of Bistrița on an area of 47.593 sqm identified with cadastral number 93614, in the pasture category.

sig_cc50a73d61158c1f39ae.description: The purpose of this Notice of Funding Opportunity (NOFO) is to seek applications for a Community Engagement Evaluation and Data coordination hub (CEED) for the Community-Based Participatory Research (CBPR) consortium: Advancing Data and Practice Transformation (ADAPT) for Optimizing Oral Health for All. In addition to CEED, the ADAPT consortium will include separately funded CBPR projects, which will receive consultative services from the NIH Community Engagement Alliance Consultative Resource (CEACR) and join in the Science Collaborative for Health and Artificial Intelligence Reduction of Errors (SCHARE) platform for the overarching goal of promoting data use and transformational community engagement to optimize oral health for all people. The CEED hub will coordinate communications and various activities in support of CBPR projects and consortium functions in three domains:1) Data Planning, Consultation, and Technical Assistance for Research Methodology and Analytics; 2) Community Engagement Evaluation; and 3) ADAPT Infrastructure and Operational Support.

sig_cdc7add00e747ca0f61a.description: Forest management services will be awarded in the year 2026 (field phase 2027) by concluding a public procurement contract for the Dumbraveni Forestry Office. The area subject to management for the Dumbraveni Forestry Office is 8236.88 ha. The services involve the development of the forest management plan, a product of the management activity with technical-organisational content, ecologically grounded, through which the works necessary to be executed in a production unit are established for a period of time, in order to bring and, subsequently, maintain the structural characteristics of the stands and the forest as a whole at the values corresponding to the optimal structural model defined in accordance with the ecological, social and economic objectives pursued through sustainable management. According to the provisions of Art. 63 paragraph (11) of Law no. 331/2024 regarding the Forestry Code, with subsequent amendments and additions, it is necessary that the development of forest management plans be carried out through public procurement procedures. The management of the state-owned forest fund constitutes a priority obligation of the forest fund administrators. The method of managing the state-owned forest fund is regulated by forest management plans. Forest management plans and their amendments are approved by order of the head of the Authority. In the case of state-owned land, the management plans provide data and information necessary for their registration/updating in the centralised inventory of state public domain assets and for registration in the integrated cadastre and land registry system. Requests for clarification formulated by tenderers during the advertising period of the participation notice can be made with a deadline of at most 15 days before the deadline for submission of tenders. The contracting authority will respond to all requests for clarification formulated in compliance with the above deadline, once, in a consolidated manner, 10 days before the deadline for submission of tenders. Services for the development of the forest management plan for the state-owned forest fund managed by the Sibiu Forestry Directorate – Dumbraveni Forestry Office, field phase 2027, for the area of 8236.88 ha. The services include preparatory work, collection of field data, data processing and drafting of the forest management plan, development of the GIS database and management maps, preparation of the necessary environmental documentation, obtaining the regulatory act issued by the competent authority for environmental protection, supporting the documentation within the Technical Commission for Forestry Approval (CTAS) and obtaining the order for approval of the forest management plan.
sig_cdc7add00e747ca0f61a.title: Forest management services-Dumbraveni Forestry Office 2026 Sibiu Forestry Directorate

sig_cde81e0fd0ae0a773c8a.description: Micro, small and medium-sized enterprises (MSMEs) constitute the overwhelming majority of economic activity in Jordan. MSMEs account for over 99% of all enterprises, employ around 60% of the formal private-sector workforce, and contribute 40% of Jordan Gross Domestic Product (GDP), making them crucial for economic growth, resilience, and job creation. Despite this importance, MSMEs still face obstacles in accessing appropriate and diversified financial products. Access to formal credit remains limited for many MSMEs. According to the Central Bank of Jordan (CBJ) National Financial Inclusion Strategy (NFIS) 2023-2028, only 28.3% of formal MSMEs had a loan or line of credit from a financial institution, highlighting a significant financing gap for smaller firms in Jordan. Financial exclusion is especially pronounced for underserved segments such as informal and women-led enterprises, which often face higher collateral requirements, limited credit histories, and lower formal borrowing rates. Financial inclusion, defined as access to and use of appropriate, affordable, and sustainable financial products and services, remains a priority in Jordan. The CBJ is pursuing ambitious targets to increase overall financial inclusion, reduce gender gaps, and enhance MSME access to finance, including through digital channels and tailored products. The NFIS aims, for example, to increase MSMEs access to formal lending at an average annual rate of 4% for four years. In a similar vein, Jordan"s Green Finance Strategy 2023-2028 aims to mobilize green investments and position the financial sector as a regional leader in sustainable finance. The strategy highlights that a 92.5% of the Jordan National Determined Contribution (NDC) target cost is to be financed by international support and mobilized private capital. As Jordan advances its Green Finance Strategy, a central priority was establishing clear and credible standards for what qualifies as "green" across the financial system. The Jordan National Green Taxonomy, published in February 2026, provides this clarity by offering a common language for the financial system to classify sustainable economic activities in a transparent and consistent way. By anchoring investment decisions to science-based criteria, the taxonomy helps ensure that future capital flows genuinely support Jordan"s low-carbon, climate-resilient transition. Against this backdrop, the Deutsche Gesellschaft für Internationale Zusammenarbeit GIZ-implemented project, Innovative Approaches for the Financial Inclusion of MSMEs in Jordan (I-FIN), takes a holistic, market-driven approach to strengthening inclusive green finance in the country. The project operates across the policy, institutional, and market levels, helping to improve the broader enabling environment, upgrade the technical and operational capacities of financial service providers, and ensure that enterprises can confidently access and benefit from green finance solutions. The overall objective of the project is to ensure that MSMEs in Jordan benefit from a more inclusive financial system that enables inclusive access to green finance and supports environmentally sustainable and resilient business growth, also with a focus on women-led enterprises. The assignment is structured around four interrelated work packages, 5 key experts, complemented by two pools of experts. Work Package 1: Planning and Inception: aims to review, research, and analyse all relevant information to ensure a comprehensive understanding of the assignment and to refine the implementation approach. Work Package 2: Capacity Development and Technical Assistance for Inclusive Green Credit Guarantees and Risk-Sharing Mechanisms: strengthens the staff and institutional capacities of the Jordan Loan Guarantee Corporation (JLGC) in the area of MSMEs inclusive green finance, through tailored staff capacity development and institutional advisory services across seven operational areas: product development and/or adaptation, risk documentation and/or management, strategy development, monitoring, reporting, setting up of an operational unit, and cooperation with Fintechs. Work Package 3: Capacity Development and Technical Assistance for Financial Services Providers: strengthens the institutional capacities of 5 financial services providers across the same seven operational areas and builds the capacities of at least 120 employees (50 of which are women) in the financial service sector. This work package may target public and private financial services providers, while Activity 3.7 targets financial sector associations, training providers, and academic institutions. The Contractor is expected to ensure strong coordination and alignment with a parallel complementary intervention delivering sector-level standardized training, including regular information exchange, harmonization of approaches, and avoidance of duplication. Work Package 4: Advancing Financial Service Providers' Capacity to Access and Mobilize International Climate Finance: supports financial services providers in submitting at least 3 project outlines (1 of which related to the water sector) for mobilising international climate finance in relation to MSMEs to relevant national actors, in close coordination with the CBJ, Ministry of Environment, and industry associations. All support under this assignment shall be aligned with international best practices and relevant national frameworks, including, but not limited to, the Jordan National Green Taxonomy, ensuring consistency with evolving regulatory and policy developments in the green finance landscape.
sig_cde81e0fd0ae0a773c8a.title: 10021232 - Supporting the Financial Institutions Green Transition

sig_ce1ebfc144dfc23a0d0c.description: 1. Objective and subject of the procurement The subject of the procurement is the co-creation and implementation of a gamified simulation or XR-based learning solution intended for upper secondary vocational education and training in the tourism sector. The solution must also be suitable, where appropriate, for university of applied sciences teaching. The procurement is implemented as part of the European Union co-funded Immersive Learning Ecosystem IMMO project in cooperation with Haaga-Helia University of Applied Sciences, the City of Helsinki and Laurea University of Applied Sciences. The objective is to produce an experiential and working-life-oriented learning experience suitable for the immersive room of the IMMO project, by means of which students can practise knowledge, skills and situations related to tourism degree modules and working life competence needs. The solution may relate to one or more tourism competence areas. The tenderer is not required to have ready-made learning content or a ready-made XR solution at the tender stage; instead, the final contents, learning objectives and use cases of the solution will be specified in co-creation. 2. Content of the delivery The procurement comprises the entire development process from design and conceptualisation to final implementation. The delivery includes at least: - requirement and content workshops as well as conceptualisation and scripting; - three co-creation workshops; - construction of learning and demonstration materials; - implementation of development versions and iterative development; - user testing in the IMMO space and utilisation of feedback; - finalisation of the solution and measures related to commissioning; - handover of source code, editable source files, documentation and other agreed materials; and - final reporting and preparation for open publishing. Tourism students, teachers, company representatives and project experts will participate in the co-creation. The supplier is responsible for the development and test environment it requires. Contract obligations shall be performed within the EU/EEA area. The supplier has the right to carry out the design, content production, development, programming, documentation and other implementation work of the solution independently of location in a suitable location of its choice suitable for information-secure work. Working on the customer's premises is required only to the extent that separately agreed meetings, tests, approval procedures or the use of the immersive room of the IMMO project so require. The customer has no obligation to arrange workspaces for the supplier. 3. Key requirements of the solution The solution must: - be gamified in such a way that gamification is a key design principle of the solution; - enable the user's active action, decision-making or problem-solving as well as feedback on the user's choices; - enable the completion of the learning experience multiple times in alternative ways; - support joint learning, teamwork, teacher-led guidance and the simultaneous participation of multiple users; - include a pedagogically justified progression model; - enable the maintenance, development and expansion of learning contents; - meet the technical requirements of the IMMO space described in the Q/A appendix; and - operate in normal use without continuous or in-use internet connectivity. The objective is an approximately 20–30 minute learning experience. The tenderer may utilise existing technologies, game engines, XR platforms and 360-degree contents if the entity meets the requirements set in the procurement documents. 4. Implementation and schedule The supplier must implement the solution in accordance with the principles of agile and iterative development. The supplier will participate in the kick-off meeting held in November 2026 and the first co-creation workshops held in November and December. Different versions of the solution will be tested with users in the IMMO space starting in January 2027. The supplier will participate in the interim review carried out in February 2027 and finalise the solution based on user feedback. The final solution with its contents must be delivered and approved no later than 28.2.2027. 5. Price and key contract terms The fixed total price of the procurement is 35 000 euros excluding value added tax. The price includes all costs arising from the fulfilment of the obligations according to the procurement contract and its appendices. The supplier may invoice the price only when the Customer has approved the final delivery in writing. A six-month warranty is granted for the delivery. A penalty for delay defined in the contract may be charged for a delay for which the supplier is responsible. The EUPL 1.2 licence or another pre-approved compatible open source licence shall in principle apply to the customer application included in the solution and its documentation. The rights, use, modification, sharing and possible open publishing of learning materials shall be resolved on a material-specific basis. The tenderer must attach to its tender a preliminary learning material rights and publishing list and supplement it during the project. The project output must not be published without the Customer's written approval. The draft contract, JIT 2025 Customer applications open source special terms and conditions and JIT 2025 General terms and conditions shall apply to the procurement contract in the order of precedence specified in the contract. More detailed minimum requirements, technical requirements, approval conditions, responsibilities and other contract terms are determined on the basis of the invitation to tender and its appendices.
sig_ce1ebfc144dfc23a0d0c.title: Co-creation and implementation of an XR-based learning solution for vocational education and training in the tourism sector

sig_ce1f32d325492ba5501b.description: Police Scotland wishes to engage potential Suppliers to obtain appropriate information in advance of an Invitation to Tender being issued. Whilst the primary purpose of the procurement exercise is presently focused on a CAD application, Police Scotland are open to discussions around procuring additional integrated functionality. Further information is contained within a Request for Information document which will be made available to Suppliers on request. The planned timescales for the RFI stage are: - Prior Information Notice published on 01/12/2025 - Suppliers to request RFI document and submit any clarifications by 19/12/2025. - Suppliers to submit RFI responses by 30/01/2026. Suppliers wishing to participate at this stage should request the RFI document via the Public Contracts Scotland website. Lot 1: . The forthcoming procurement exercise will include all required software, hardware, project management, installation, testing, test reporting, migration of live and archived data, licensing, support & maintenance, training and any other associated goods or services required to deliver the solution. The current estimated timescale for an ITT being issued is November 2026. This will be confirmed following the supplier engagement stage and assessment of Request for Information responses received from participating suppliers.

The Scottish Sentencing Council seeks to commission a review of relevant academic and jurisprudential literature on the topic of: - Sexual offences involving sexual assault The aim of the literature review on sexual offences involving sexual assault will be to summarise new academic, legal and statistical work relevant to the sentencing of sexual assault as well as any relevant research on the changing nature of sexual assault offending particularly in light of the COVID-19 pandemic and cyber-enabled offending. sig_cef5f71f644c84e946c9.description: YOU CAN STILL INFLUENCE DURING THE MARKET SURVEY PHASE! At the City of Turku, we want to make high-quality procurements and cooperate with companies. We are therefore conducting a market survey before the publication of the actual contract notice. The goal is to inform about the upcoming tendering process, survey the markets for the subject of the procurement, and obtain comprehensive information on the availability of the service, implementation possibilities, and potential suppliers. We will also ask suppliers participating in the market dialogue for comments on the minimum requirements and quality criteria in the procurement documents. The goal of the market dialogue is also to go through the scheduling and implementation of the upcoming tendering process. This is an invitation to a market dialogue concerning the energy consumption monitoring service planned by the City of Turku. Turun kaupunki monitors energy consumption in approx. 600 buildings, of which over 200 have district heating. A measurement hub, which provides more accurate consumption data, can be found in approx. 70 buildings. The goal is to create a digital service that produces energy consumption monitoring, which performs the expert's manual work steps, producing as highly refined information as possible on consumption changes with easy views, explanations, and follow-up measures. The goal is to make consumption monitoring as automatic as possible by reducing manual work steps, such as determining the start time, occurrence, and overall effects of increased consumption. The user should automatically receive the most important prioritised key observations and easily see the analysis of the observation. The market dialogue will be held as a webinar on Teams on 2.10. at 9 -11. Event programme: 9:00-10:00 Presentation of the tendering process 10:00-11:00 Questions, answers, and discussion A warm welcome! REGISTRATION: Registration via the Tarjouspalvelu portal by 25.9.2026 at 16:00 or by email to sari.holmberg@turku.fi. State the persons from your company participating and their email addresses. This notice is not a contract notice or a call for tenders, but an invitation to a market dialogue, which aims to survey the market and develop the procurement's tendering documents. The invitation does not bind those who have responded to it. Not participating in the market dialogue event does not prevent participation in a possible tender competition, and participation in the event does not in any way affect the tenderer's position in the actual tender competition. The contracting entity does not commit to carrying out the procurement based on the market survey, and the presented descriptions/specifications do not bind the client. We announce our upcoming procurements in the Hilma planning tool, where it is possible to set search alerts. Hilma planning tool You can find more information about us at www.turku.fi/hankinnat and we publish current matters on our LinkedIn page “Turun kaupungin hankintapalvelut”.

An updated FAQ will soon be available under "Other Documents" on the right side of this NSPIRES page. ﻿NOTICE: August 4, 2026. Going forward, a $0.09/SBU charge now applies to all proposing to Earth Science (ROSES Appendix A) to use any NASA high-end computing resource. Proposers must account for this in their budget, per the instructions provided in Section 7.3 of ROSES-25 A.1 Earth Science Research Overview . NOTICE: July 30, 2026. An erroneous reference in Section 4.1 to was corrected to refer to Section 4.2 regarding Sub-element of relevance. Section 4.3.3 "Use of Generative AI" was added. On the NSPIRES cover page, the NOI Program Specific Data Cover Page Element was updated to include the Rough Budget estimate per year which is required. New text is in bold and deleted text is struck through. NOTICE: Amended July 20, 2026. This amendment adds this new program element to ROSES-2025. Mandatory Notices of Intent are due by August 20, 2026, and proposals are due October 20, 2026. Any proposal not preceded by an on-time NOI will be declined without review. Proposals submitted to this program will be evaluated using dual anonymous peer review, see Section 4.4. Proposers to this program element are strongly encouraged to use the optional Earth Science Division template for the required summary table of work effort of the proposal; templates are available at https://science.nasa.gov/researchers/templates-for-earth-science-division-appendix-a-roses-proposals. NOTICE: Research security training required starting August 5, 2026. All PIs and any Co-Is that would spend ≥ 10% time on a proposed grants or cooperative agreements must certify they have taken research security training. NASA will be satisfied with the four online research security training modules on the National Science Foundation's (NSF) Research Security Training website at https://www.nsf.gov/research-security/training or the SECURE Center condensed version of the four modules at https://www.secure-center.org/ctm This synopsis is a generic summary that is posted for each of the many individual "program elements" in NASA’s Research Opportunities in Space and Earth Sciences (ROSES) – 2025 solicitation. For specific information on this particular program element download and read the PDF of the text of this program element by going to Tables 2 or 3 of ROSES at https://solicitation.nasaprs.com/ROSES2025table2 and https://solicitation.nasaprs.com/ROSES2025table3 , respectively, click the title of the program element of interest, a hypertext link will take you to a page for that particular program element. On that page, on the right side under "Announcement Documents" the link on the bottom will be to the PDF of the text of the call for proposals. For example, if one were interested in the Solar System Science program (NNH25ZDA001N-SCUBED) one would follow the link to the NSPIRES page for that program element and then to read the text of the call one would click on “C.2 Solar System Science (.pdf)” to download the text of the call. If one wanted to set it into the context of the goals, objectives and know the default rules for all elements within Appendix C, the planetary science division, one might download and read “ C.1 Planetary Science Research Program Overview (.pdf) ” from that same page. While the letters and numbers are different for each element within ROSES (A.10, B.3, etc.) the basic configuration is always the same, e.g., the letter indicates the Science Division (A is Earth Science, B is Heliophysics etc.) and whatever the letter, #1 is always the division overview. In 2025, most program elements will be set up for application via Grants.gov only if requested at least 30 days in advance of the due date. For more on Grants.gov submissions see Section IV(b)v of the ROSES Summary of Solicitation, that may be found at https://solicitation.nasaprs.com/ROSES2025 . The National Aeronautics and Space Administration (NASA) Science Mission Directorate (SMD) released its annual omnibus Research Announcement (NRA), Research Opportunities in Space and Earth Sciences (ROSES) – 2025 (OMB Approval Number 2700-0092, CFDA Number 43.001) on February 21, 2025. In this case "omnibus" means that this NRA has many individual program elements, each with its own due dates and topics. All together these cover the wide range of basic and applied supporting research and technology supported by SMD. Awards will be made as grants, cooperative agreements, or contracts depending on the nature of the work proposed. However, most extramural research awards deriving from ROSES will be grants, and many program elements of ROSES specifically exclude contracts, because contracts would not be appropriate for the nature of the work solicited. Funded Co-Is at government labs will receive inter- or intra-agency transfers . The typical period of performance for an award is three years, but some programs may allow up to five years and others specify shorter periods. In most cases, organizations of every type, Government and private, for profit and not-for-profit, domestic and foreign (with some caveats), may submit proposals without restriction on teaming arrangements. Tables listing the program elements and due dates (Tables 2 and 3 ), a table that provides a very top level summary of proposal contents ( Table 1 ), and the full text of the ROSES-2025 "Summary of Solicitation", may all be found NSPIRES at https://solicitation.nasaprs.com/ROSES2025 . Frequently asked questions for ROSES are posted at http://science.nasa.gov/researchers/sara/faqs . Questions concerning specific program elements should be directed to the point(s) of contact for that particular element, who may be found either at the end of the individual program element in the summary table of key information or on the web list of topics and points of contact at: http://science.nasa.gov/researchers/sara/program-officers-list . General questions concerning ROSES-2025 may be directed to the office of the SMD Deputy Associate Administrator for Research at sara@nasa.gov . Not all program elements are known at the time of the release of ROSES. To be informed of new program elements or amendments to this NRA, proposers may subscribe to: (1) The SMD mailing lists (by logging in at http://nspires.nasaprs.com and checking the appropriate boxes under "Account Management" and "Email Subscriptions"), (2) The ROSES-2025 blog feed for amendments, clarifications, and corrections to at https://science.nasa.gov/researchers/solicitations/roses-2025/ , and (3) The ROSES-2025 due date Google calendars (one for each science division). Instructions are at https://science.nasa.gov/researchers/sara/library-and-useful-links (link from the words due date calendar).

sig_cf9535f03041162a3dab.description: The ITZBund requires services in the area of software lifecycle management (SLM) for deployed software development and project management solutions. The aim of this tender is the conclusion of a framework agreement to ensure the operation as well as the maintenance and (further) development of the existing software development and project management platform Cloud as well as specialist applications of the ITZBund based thereon. In addition, sovereignty is to be strengthened through the expansion of open source tools to be procured. By open source, the ITZBund understands software whose source code is freely available. In principle, everyone is permitted to use, analyse, modify and pass on this free of charge and without restriction in terms of content regarding object and source code. Specifications of the respective relevant open source licence, in particular regarding licence texts, copyright notices or copyleft effects, remain unaffected. The tendered services comprise services along the entire software lifecycle, in particular operational services, maintenance and support services, support services in connection with releases and rollouts, as well as demand-oriented new and further developments of existing software and software-related tools. The client, who can call off services commissioned by its customers, is authorised to call off. The operation of the procured software products generally takes place within the ITZBund; exceptions in special individual cases allow operation at the client's customers with their own licensing. The services mentioned at the outset are tendered in five lots: - Lot 1: Ensuring the maintenance and (further) development of the deployed software development and project management platform Cloud - Lot 2: Ensuring the operation and automated rollout of releases of the deployed software development and project management platform Cloud - Lot 3: Provision of Sonatype software products - Lot 4: Provision of an open source issue tracker including in particular training, support, further development and migration services - Lot 5: Provision of an open source wiki including in particular training, support, further development and migration services This specification of services considers the subject matter of Lot 4: The subject matter of this lot is the provision of an open source issue tracker including associated training, support, further development and migration services. Lot LOT-0000: Provision of an open source issue tracker including in particular training, support, further development and migration services. For the total contract term of 4 years, an upper limit of 1.450 instances and 150.776 staff hours (SH) or 18.847 person days (PD) results for the estimated calculatory costs.

sig_cf9e2be504d6c07be868.description:
Keski-Uudenmaan hyvinvointialueen TKIO procurement system (hereinafter procurement system) forms a central part of the contracting authority's research, development, innovation and competence development activities and procurement platform. It forms the structure of a cooperation model regulated by an agreement between the subscriber and the research, development and innovation partners. The purpose of the services to be competed in the procurement system is to produce research data, development services and innovations as a basis for the subscriber's development activities and management. The procurement system is divided into categories as follows: Category 1 Innovation services Category 2 Development of service systems Category 3 Project services Category 4 Strategic development Category 5 Scientific communities In addition, the subject matter of the procurement includes piloting and experimentation services as well as continuous development and management services for the subscriber's use. The subject matter of the procurement and the operation of the procurement system are described in more detail in the appendix "Principles of the TKIO dynamic purchasing system". The minimum requirements for each category and the competence requirements for applicants at the establishment stage are described in more detail in this call for participation. The subscriber shall define the subject matter and requirements of the assignments to be competed in the procurement system in more detail in each internal call for tenders of the procurement system. The procurement system shall be valid until 31.10.2029, during which time the internal call for tenders of the procurement system shall be carried out. The subscriber may extend the validity of the procurement system with a new contract notice. Suppliers may apply to join the procurement system at the establishment stage and later during its validity by submitting a request to participate in accordance with the call for participation. The procurement procedure is two-stage. To be able to submit tenders, a supplier must first submit a request to participate and be admitted to the procurement system. After this, the supplier may submit tenders by responding to the call for tenders sent by the contracting authority. The contracting authority shall carry out internal competitions within the procurement system in the future as needed. Requests to participate may be submitted to the dynamic purchasing system throughout its duration. All applicants meeting the suitability requirements shall be admitted to the dynamic purchasing system. Actual procurements shall be made through internal competitions of the dynamic purchasing system, in which the subject matter of the procurement is described and specified. Participation in the internal competitions of the DPS is not possible unless the supplier has been admitted to the procurement system. The submission of a request to participate and admission to the procurement system does not oblige the supplier to submit a tender, but suppliers may submit tenders at their discretion. The contracting authority estimates that the value excluding value added tax of the planned procurements covered by the dynamic purchasing system at the time of publication of the call for participation is 5,6 million euros, taking into account all procurements potentially made within the system. The estimate is preliminary and based on the procurement need known at this time. The contracting authority does not commit to any procurement quantities or minimum purchase obligations with this notice. Category 1 Innovation services includes the generation of innovations and futures research. The purpose of innovation services is to produce innovative solutions and new methods for the organisation and production of services in an impactful way. Innovation can also aim, for example, at anticipating the demand for services and substantive change needs. Innovations include, for example, digital operating models, solutions related to the innovative utilisation of technology, or the utilisation of robotics and artificial intelligence in social welfare and healthcare services. Central to innovations is the consideration of customer experience, quality, impact and cost perspectives. Innovations may also relate to operational monitoring models, measurement of results or strategic work. The result of an innovation may also be a commercialised product or service. Category 1 Innovation services additionally includes Piloting and experimentation services, the purpose of which is to test new innovations and services resulting from assignments or other cooperation in practice. Continuous development and management, the purpose of which is the implementation of new or redesigned services, systems or operations resulting from the results of assignments such that the implementation includes their continuous development as part of service production or other activities of the subscriber. See appendix "Principles of the TKIO dynamic purchasing system" for more details.; Category 2 Development of service systems is expert service, the purpose of which is the development of services, service processes, service networks and service systems. The development of service systems includes the collection and analysis of data on the current state, needs and impact of services. The data is utilised in development activities. The development of service systems may include the production of various methods and tools for the subscriber's needs to support the implementation of changes. The service may include the implementation of stakeholder involvement, for example through service design or equivalent means. The development of service systems may also include coaching service, the purpose of which is to support the subscriber in development activities and the consolidation of results. Category 2 Development of service systems additionally includes - Piloting and experimentation services, the purpose of which is to test new innovations and services resulting from assignments or other cooperation in practice. - Continuous development and management, the purpose of which is the implementation of new or redesigned services, systems or operations resulting from the results of assignments such that the implementation includes their continuous development as part of service production or other activities of the subscriber. See appendix "Principles of the TKIO dynamic purchasing system" for more details.;

Category 3 Project Services includes the entire project process management for the subscriber's research, development and innovation activities. Project services include project planning services, project management services and project services. Category 3 Project Services also includes: - Piloting and experimentation services, the purpose of which is to test new innovations and services resulting from assignments or other cooperation in practice. - Continuous development and management, the purpose of which is the implementation of new or redesigned services, systems or operations resulting from assignments, such that the implementation includes their continuous development as part of service production or other subscriber operations. See the appendix 'TKIO dynamic purchasing system principles' for more details.; Category 4 Strategic development consulting is an expert service intended to provide the subscriber with comprehensive support for development activities and change management, from the perspectives of organiser management and service production. Strategic development consulting produces versatile and comprehensive information, expertise and insights into the development of social and health services and specialised medical care, as well as large-scale integration projects. The consulting offers expert knowledge for promoting the effectiveness, customer-orientation and quality of innovation and development activities in social welfare, health services and specialised medical care, as well as for the design, analysis and implementation of new operating models and process complexes. The strategic development consulting expert service includes versatile expertise in improving the effectiveness and productivity of social and health services, financing systems, improving service accessibility, designing service systems and networks, developing data-driven management capabilities and future forecasting. Strategic development can also include service production management services, which can be used to achieve significant cost savings when service production and the producer field in accordance with procurement contracts can be managed more systematically and purposefully. The service production management service can also help the contracting authority to find consistent and replicable operating processes for managing service providers, with which better service effectiveness, customer satisfaction, quality and cost-efficiency can be achieved. Category 4 Strategic development also includes: - Piloting and experimentation services, the purpose of which is to test new innovations and services resulting from assignments or other cooperation in practice. - Continuous development and management, the purpose of which is the implementation of new or redesigned services, systems or operations resulting from assignments, such that the implementation includes their continuous development as part of service production or other subscriber operations. See the appendix 'TKIO dynamic purchasing system principles' for more details.; Category 5 For the scientific community, the procurement system acts as a cooperation platform and procurement channel towards the scientific community, such as universities, higher education institutions, educational institutions, centres of expertise and research institutes. Services procured from the scientific community in the procurement system may include services considered to be scientific activities, which in their content complement projects implemented within the framework of TKIO cooperation. Scientific activity may include any research activity and services in accordance with the subject of the procurement system, but a scientific and research perspective is always emphasised in these services. Services and research activities may be such that the benefit obtained accrues for use in operations other than those of the contracting authority. Services procured from the scientific community may also be research and development services where the benefit obtained accrues exclusively for use in the contracting authority's operations and the contracting authority compensates for the service performed in full. The nature of the service is specified in each call for tenders within the procurement system. Services can also be ordered from the scientific community directly without a call for tenders within the procurement system, if the conditions for the procurement act's scope exemption concerning research and development services (9 section 1 subsection 13 point) are met. Category 5 Scientific community also includes: - Piloting and experimentation services, the purpose of which is to test new innovations and services resulting from assignments or other cooperation in practice. See the appendix 'TKIO dynamic purchasing system principles' for more details.
sig_cf9e2be504d6c07be868.title: TKIO expert services Keski-Uudenmaan hyvinvointialueelle DPS

The Contracting Authority requests written input on as many of the following points as possible: Short presentation of interested party: Description of experience with the Fact Board. Points we would like feedback on: Give a description of the tenderer ́s system and how this covers the needs/purposes described. What are the main features and advantages? What type of delivery model/operational model can be delivered (SaaS, other)? Does the tenderer have input on how any environmental requirements can be set for the system? Price models: Which price models do the tenderer operate with and what price models do the supplier recommend? Can the supplier comply with other models if the contracting authority sees it appropriate? What factors affect the price of the tenderer's system? Quality and security: What requirements do the tenderer have in relation to quality of the system? What measures does the tenderer have that ensure that information security and privacy are safeguarded, with particular focus on sensitive areas such as patient safety? Where is the solution installed? Where are the personnel operating and maintaining the system? What kind of support and training do the service provider offer to ensure users get the most out of their solution? Which support and maintenance services does the tenderer offer? Other: How does the supplier work on innovation and further development of the product? Furthermore, it may be of interest, if relevant for interested party, to hear about the tenderer's experience from similar public tenders, possibly in comparable countries (preferably countries within the EU). sig_d066c19ac10d4e5b715d.description: School Attendance Monitoring of Children and Young People in Care and Children and Young People with an Education, Health & Care Plan (OOC). Wolverhampton City Council (the Council) has a statutory duty to monitor the school attendance of children and young people in care placed in out-of-city independent placements, and for children and young people with Education, Health and Care Plans (EHCPs) attending out-of-city education settings. This duty is primarily governed by the Education Act 1996 and relevant Department for Education (DfE) statutory guidance. To fulfil this responsibility, the Council requires a remote and secure system for collecting and monitoring attendance data for these two cohorts. The overarching aim is to improve school attendance among Wolverhampton pupils placed outside the city by delivering an effective, responsive, and informative service. This will enable the Council to identify and address poor attendance early, ensuring timely intervention in cases of unauthorised absence. The Provider will be expected to: • Contact selected schools attended by Wolverhampton pupils placed out of city. •Liaise with Council officers, parents, and carers when unauthorised absences occur. • Submit regular attendance reports within agreed timescales, using standardised DfE codes. • Provide business support and access to a secure online portal for Council officers and education settings. Lot 1: .
sig_d066c19ac10d4e5b715d.title: School Attendance Monitoring

sig_d06ddb546c44a243d33c.description: Hanover Housing Association is seeking to engage the market prior to a formal procurement for an HR and People Systems platform. The procurement may encompass Core HR, Payroll, Learning Management, Applicant Tracking and associated modules, either as a single integrated solution or a combination of products. This notice invites supplier engagement to inform the scope and structure of the forthcoming procurement. Lot 1: . Hanover Housing Association is undertaking a programme of HR and People Systems transformation and is conducting this market engagement to understand the range of solutions available. Hanover currently operates a number of separate systems and manual processes to support its HR, payroll, recruitment and learning functions. The purpose of this Prior Information Notice is to understand what the market is able to offer — individually and in combination — across the following functional areas, and to explore the trade-offs between integrated single-platform solutions and best-of-breed combinations. Core HR (Required — Implementation by 31 October 2026) Hanover's current HR system is due to be decommissioned and a replacement Core HR solution must be in place by 31 October 2026. This is a firm deadline. Hanover is seeking to understand market capability across the full range of Core HR functionality, including but not limited to: Employee Records and Data Management Centralised, auditable employee records covering personal details, employment history, contractual information, pay and grading, and document storage. The ability to maintain accurate organisational structures including multiple reporting lines, departments and cost centre allocations. Leave and Absence Management Management of all leave types including annual leave, sickness absence, maternity, paternity and other statutory leave. Integration with timesheets, overtime recording and flexi-time arrangements. Automated accruals, carry-over rules and manager approval workflows. HR Case Management End-to-end management of employee relations cases including disciplinaries, grievances, capability processes and investigations. Structured workflows, letter and document generation, case tracking and audit trails. Hanover is also interested in whether performance management — as a process driven by forms and workflows — could be accommodated within this module rather than as a standalone function. Employee Self-Service and Manager Self-Service A modern, intuitive self-service portal accessible via mobile devices, enabling employees to view and update personal information, submit and track leave requests, access payslips and documents, and engage with HR processes without manual intervention. Manager self-service should support approval workflows, team visibility and basic reporting. Reporting and Analytics Standard and configurable reporting across all HR data, including headcount, turnover, absence and equality monitoring. Dashboard views for HR teams and managers, with the ability to export data for use in wider organisational reporting. Compliance and Policy Management Support for statutory compliance requirements including GDPR-compliant data handling, equal opportunities monitoring, and audit logging. Configurable policy acknowledgement and document sign-off workflows. Organisational Design Visibility of organisational structure, headcount planning at a basic level, and the ability to model or represent changes to structure. This links to the Advanced HR requirement for post and establishment management. Onboarding and Offboarding Structured workflows to support the full employee lifecycle from pre-employment through to leaver processing, including right to work checks, document collection, task assignment and system access coordination.. The service will operate within a framework of continuous improvement with which the service provider will be required to engage; bringing innovation, sharing ideas, and implementing improvement measures to increase operational effectiveness/efficiency and drive out waste.
sig_d06ddb546c44a243d33c.title: Provision of an HR and People Systems Platform

sig_d08c4b0dcdd6f24d4f77.description: Tuomi Logistiikka Oy requests tenders on behalf of Pirkanmaan hyvinvointialue (the contracting authority) for a development portfolio solution. The subject of the procurement is a development portfolio solution that serves as the contracting authority's central tool for the management, monitoring and steering of projects, project portfolios and the strategy portfolio. The system must support the entire lifecycle of projects from ideation, prioritisation, resourcing and decision-making to implementation, monitoring and reporting. The solution must include at least the following management entities: - a project portfolio and - a strategy portfolio, which allows for the management of strategy implementation and related projects as a unified whole. The procurement is implemented as a SaaS-based software service (the System). The System is used to manage, among other things, project basic data, schedules, resourcing, financial and funding data, approval processes, and the status of projects, project portfolios and the strategy portfolio for use by management and other stakeholders. The System must support both operational project management and portfolio and management-level decision-making, including reporting, analytics and visual dashboards. The procurement includes the System and its user licences, the necessary implementation and configuration services, and maintenance and support services during the contract period as described in more detail in the procurement documents. Any additional and expert services, integrations and further development will be implemented in accordance with the terms of the call for tenders and the contract. The solution must be user-oriented, and its functionalities must be easily and intuitively adoptable. The solution must be configurable to the contracting authority's needs, and the contracting authority's main users must have the possibility to maintain and develop the system as extensively as possible using the management tools it provides. The solution must include versatile reporting and printing functionalities and support the presentation of information in various dashboards. A more detailed description of the content and requirements of the procurement is presented in the appendices to the call for tenders. The contract will be concluded as valid until further notice. The estimated total value of the procurement is approximately 222 000 euros calculated over a period of four (4) years. The value is an estimate and does not bind the contracting authority. The procurement has not been divided into lots because the entity that is the subject of the procurement forms a functionally and technically unified service entity, which it is not appropriate to divide into smaller parts.

sig_d0d035a1e770e77ef1bb.description: Assumption of the technical programme management of programme P20 The subject of the contract is the assumption of the technical programme management of programme P20 (formerly Police 20/20 programme). Programme P20 was created to implement the Saarbrücken Agenda and is a multiproject spanning several implementation levels and years (target picture 2030+). Its core mandate is to replace the heterogeneous police IT landscape and to unify and harmonise all information systems of the German police forces taking into account applicable legal frameworks. For this purpose, uniform, modern procedures are to be provided that can be used by all police forces of the Federation and the Länder according to equal standards. In order to achieve the target picture 2030+ of police casework through programme P20, a step-by-step approach is pursued. In total, more than 45 projects currently fit together as individual building blocks to form the overall programme P20. Important intermediate pictures have already been achieved. A further important intermediate step is to be achieved in the year 2028.

Investitionsbank Schleswig-Holstein (IB.SH), the central promotional institute of the federal state with currently just under 900 employees, is looking for three framework agreement partners as IT service providers for the provision of IT support services in the field of IT security. --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- It is intended to conclude the framework agreement attached to the documents as Appendix 1, the agreement on data processing on behalf with the three bidders who meet the minimum criteria and occupy places 1-3. --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- The support services specifically required by IB.SH will be called off taking into account the work and project situation, qualification and availability in the context of mini-competitions. The arrangement of these individual call-offs is regulated in Appendix 3 framework agreement (see section 2 of the framework agreement). --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- A framework agreement is to be concluded between IB.SH and three service companies. The framework agreement regulates commissions placed on the one hand by IB.SH and comprising the following services: ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- Description of activities: • Support for the client in technical and technical-organisational matters of IT security / cyber security based on the strategies, policies, roles and responsibilities specified by the client; the list of services is not exhaustive. • Elaboration, concretisation, updating and monitoring of technical IT security standards, technical specifications, operating processes, runbooks and implementation guidelines within the framework of existing internal specifications. • Risk-based assessment, classification and implementation support of technical IT security requirements from operations, change management, projects, architecture, service provider management, regulatory requirements and internal guidelines. • Support for technical IT security, digital operational resilience, recovery and restoration capability and continuity of critical IT services, including technical preparatory work for scenario analyses, emergency exercises, alternative procedures, fallback/exit scenarios and measure tracking. • Initiation, evaluation, implementation and tracking of operational security measures for IT infrastructures, applications, platforms, end devices and operating environments, including on-premises, private cloud, public cloud, hybrid cloud, multi-cloud as well as SaaS/PaaS/IaaS environments. • Coordination, evaluation and further development of technical security architectures, inter alia network and zone concepts, segmentation, firewalling, encryption, PKI, DNSSEC, proxy/gateway services, IAM/PAM, endpoint security, server/client hardening, cloud, container/Kubernetes and API security as well as secure administration models. • Initiation, support, evaluation and tracking of vulnerability analyses, penetration tests, technical security reviews, configuration and hardening checks, readiness checks as well as red/purple team or comparable technical security exercises. • Monitoring and evaluation of external reports on vulnerabilities, threats, attack patterns and security-relevant industry developments as well as derivation, support and documentation of technical measures. • Support with security monitoring, logging, detection and response, in particular for SIEM/SOC requirements, log source onboarding, use case design, alert tuning, detection engineering, SOC provider management, triage processes, playbooks, escalation paths and security-related reporting. • Technical support for handling, containment, analysis, documentation and follow-up of IT security incidents including interfaces to incident, problem, change, emergency and service provider management. • Technical-professional control, evaluation and tracking of service provider reports, security proofs, action plans, audit findings and audit points. • Maintenance, updating and quality assurance of technical IT security documentation, runbooks, control descriptions, verification documentation and technical security concepts. • Technical-professional preparatory work for inspections, audits, revisions and regulatory proofs; the performance of original inspection, audit or control functions is not covered by this. • Support for the data protection officer in technical questions as well as coordination and cooperation with the information security officer / information security management • Carrying out awareness-raising measures for employees on the subject of IT security • Proactive identification, evaluation and target-group-oriented preparation of technical IT security topics within the client's area of responsibility. --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- The support services specifically required by IB.SH will be called off taking into account the work and project situation, qualification and availability in the context of mini-competitions. The arrangement of these individual call-offs is regulated in the framework agreement (see section 2 of the framework agreement).

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- The IB.SH expects an annual workload of approx. 1.250 person-days. There is no entitlement to the purchase of a minimum quantity. --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- The following maximum quantity for the services to be provided applies to this framework agreement in relation to the advertised period: 6.000 person-days. Upon reaching the maximum value, this framework agreement ends automatically without the need for termination. ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
