sig_d1aa86289da9fcd67343.description: Subject and objective of the procurement The subject of the procurement is mobile robotics technology solutions suitable for the urban environment, which perform tasks in the air, on the ground, or in water. This open call for tenders seeks 6–9 pilots to be implemented. The goal is to obtain information on new and innovative solutions that are suitable for challenging urban environments and support the city's services, maintenance, and decision-making. A particular goal is to help small and medium-sized enterprises solve challenges for which there is an acute need, and to grow their business. Blue City – Digital and safe water city Helsinki can be the world's first city that continuously monitors, measures, and secures its water areas with the help of mobile robotics. The goal is to develop autonomous water robots and data solutions that monitor water quality, map the bottom, and support water and maritime safety. 1. Safe beaches and harbours The goal is to develop an automatic monitoring and tracking system that improves the safety of beaches, harbours, and sea areas. The system detects risks and anomalies in time, tracks the movements of swimmers, and identifies emergencies in real time. Robotics can also be utilised in rescue and retrieval tasks, identification of foreign objects, and monitoring the condition of channels. 2. Smart water quality monitoring and stormwater management Water quality monitoring is currently slow and point-based. The goal is to create a real-time water situational picture based on robotics and data analytics, which enables rapid reaction to anomalies. The solution can monitor turbidity, oxygen content, temperature, electrical conductivity, and nutrient concentrations, as well as automatically take water samples for further analysis. 3. Own solution Companies can also propose their own new robotics solution related to the water environment, which brings added value to the City of Helsinki and its residents. The solution must utilise ground, water, or air robotics and produce data that can be utilised in the city's various service areas, for example in the development of infrastructure, safety, or environmental management. Urban Sky – Smart and managed urban airspace Urban airspace is a new infrastructure where drones and sensors operate as part of the city's everyday life. The goal is to build a safe and coordinated airspace where mobile robotics supports monitoring, maintenance, and decision-making. 1. Smart construction site monitoring Monitoring and supervising construction sites takes a lot of resources and is often manual. The goal is to improve the safety, transparency, and productivity of construction sites by monitoring progress and anomalies in real time. 2. Predictive maintenance – detection of leaks and thermal anomalies The city loses significant amounts of energy and water every year due to unnoticed leaks and heat losses. The goal is to develop a system based on air robotics and thermal imaging that identifies leaks and anomalies at an early stage and supports predictive maintenance. 3. Own solution Companies can also propose their own robotics solution utilising airspace that supports the safety, monitoring, or energy use of the urban environment. The solution must utilise ground, water, or air robotics and produce data that supports the city's services and decision-making. Smart Ground – Functional and sustainable city all year round A functional and sustainable city utilises mobile robotics, data, and the circular economy so that the city's infrastructure, maintenance, and logistics work seamlessly every day of the year. It is the city's nervous system that maintains vitality and the smooth running of services without interruptions. 1. Infrastructure condition monitoring and modelling The city has thousands of kilometres of streets, cycle paths, and tunnels, the condition of which is laborious and fragmented to inspect. The goal is to develop a solution that provides a continuous, up-to-date, and automatically updating view of the state of the city's infrastructure. 2. Automation and logistics of winter maintenance In the year 2028 dumping snow into the sea will be prohibited, which requires new ways to manage snow collection and processing. The goal is to develop a predictive and data-driven robotics solution that supports snow collection, transport, storage, and melting in an environmentally friendly and cost-effective manner. 3. Own solution Companies can also propose their own robotics solution suitable for the ground environment, which improves the operation of the city's infrastructure, maintenance, or logistics. The solution can utilise ground, water, or air robotics and produce data beneficial to the city, for example about the environment, traffic, or energy use.
sig_d1aa86289da9fcd67343.title: Urban Mobile Robotics – We are looking for companies to implement robotics pilots

sig_d232b34ff73335e6cfd1.description: The reason for initiating the ecohydrological study is the stability problems in the Kikbeek pool, as a result of which water level rises in function of achieving the conservation objectives cannot currently proceed. The subject of the ecohydrological study is to investigate the effects of higher pool levels (than current ones) in the Kikbeek quarry on the surrounding groundwater-dependent vegetation. Additionally, it is investigated which additional measures for re-wetting in the Habitats Directive area of the Mechelse Heide, Ziepbeekvallei, Neerharerheide and Asbeek are necessary to arrive at a climate-robust system. The aim of the study is to investigate the impact on groundwater levels and boundary conditions from ecology through water level rises of the Kikbeek pool and hydrological restoration measures in the Mechelse Heide, Ziepbeek, Neerharerheide and Asbeek. This must lead to maximising the restoration and conservation of the groundwater-dependent vegetation. The objective is to achieve climate-robust system restoration, without compromising critical infrastructure (such as the E314 motorway) and the stability of the Berg quarry and the Kikbeek pool in the long term. The drafting of hydrological and ecological model predictions must serve to investigate scenarios for water level rise in the Kikbeek pool and to elaborate and evaluate the development of wet nature in the Habitats Directive area of the Mechelse Heide.
sig_d232b34ff73335e6cfd1.title: ECOHYDROLOGICAL STUDY KIKBEEK and SAC MECHELSE HEIDE

sig_d2644fc26f19d34df1ea.description: With this tender, the Contracting Authority aims to contract a supplier for the delivery, implementation and management of a single financial system according to the SaaS principle with associated services. This means that the application does not run locally on the Contracting Authority's systems, but externally on the servers of the supplier to be contracted. The most important specifications of the new financial system to be delivered are: • The application is a so-called Software as a Service (SaaS) application; • The application can be provided with (automated) interfaces with other systems used by the Contracting Authority. The agreement consists of the implementation period and the management period. The implementation period starts after the agreement is signed by both parties and ends after acceptance of the implementation, after which the management period commences. The planned start date of the management period is 1 January 2028. The term of the agreement is set at 4 years and therefore ends on 31 December 2031. The Contracting Authority has the right to unilaterally extend the duration of the agreement 4 times by a period of 2 years. The total duration of the agreement shall be a maximum of 12 years. The agreement shall automatically terminate at the end of the term, on 31 December 2039.

The scope of the contract covers interrelated activities related to the ongoing maintenance of the STRADOM System, technical assistance and ensuring the proper and secure functioning of the STRADOM System. Dividing the contract into lots could lead to difficulties in coordinating activities, dispersion of responsibility, and consequently to the risk of lowering the quality of services provided or disrupting the continuity of the system's operation. For economic and organisational reasons, dividing the contract into lots could also result in increased contract execution costs, the need for additional coordination on the part of the Employer and longer response times to reports and failures, which would be contrary to the principle of effective and rational management of public funds. The failure to divide the contract into lots does not violate the principles of fair competition or equal treatment of contractors and does not restrict access to the contract for micro, small and medium-sized enterprises. 3. sig_d35a7d3ffd39ee9f9280.description: PURPOSE NIOSH intends to support the Centers of Excellence in Total Worker Health® (TWH). These Centers will conduct rigorous research and translation activities to prevent harmful exposures, improve working conditions, and advance worker well-being. The Centers will develop practical, scalable solutions for employers and workers. All projects must use the NIOSH Worker Well-Being Questionnaire (WellBQ) and share data with the HERO Worker Well-Being Clearinghouse. Large Research Projects require economic evaluation. PRIORITY AREAS • High-risk occupations: First responders, vehicle mechanics, and technicians, with emphasis on occupational exposures, related health risks, and prevention strategies • Young workers, SMEs • Chronic disease • Mental health, stress • Substance use disorder • Artificial intelligence (AI), digital technologies This is a multi-component NOFO. COMPONENT STRUCTURE Percentages indicate maximum share of total budget. Overall Component (Required) Provides Center leadership and integration. Applicants should show strong coordination, scientific direction, and alignment across projects. Administration, Evaluation, and Emerging Issues Core (Required; up to 15%) Supports management and Center-wide evaluation. Applicants should describe oversight, data governance, and quality assurance.Optional activities include emerging issues and shared research resources. Outreach, Dissemination, and Impact Core (Required; up to 15%) Supports communication, worker/employer engagement, training, translation, implementation, and dissemination strategies. Research Projects (Required; about 60 to 70%) Includes all research activities. Applicants may propose a mix of projects. Research project distinctions are based on scope and complexity rather than cost. Projects should demonstrate scientific rigor and potential for sustained impact. Small Research Projects (Required; at least one project; up to 3 years) Exploratory, feasibility, early-stage intervention, surveillance, or measurement studies. Priority areas: high-risk occupations, young workers, SMEs. Should show innovation and potential to expand. Large Research Projects (Required; at least one project; up to 5 years) Multiyear etiologic, mechanistic, intervention, or translational studies. Priority areas: chronic disease, mental health, substance use disorder. Economic evaluation is required. Projects should include strong design and analytic plans. Pilot/Feasibility Program (Optional; 12–18 months) Short-term studies generating preliminary data or testing AI/digital technology approaches.

sig_d3771785f2bb25cac5ac.description: The National Institutes of Health (NIH) intends to award a Firm-Fixed-Price Purchase Order to Thomas Jefferson University to Obtain Clinical Cohort of Patients with Associated Clinical Outcomes, Radiologic Images, and Associated De-Identified Radiology Reports. In accordance with FAR 6.302-1, Only One Responsible Source and No Other Services Will Satisfy Agency Requirements, The requested clinical cohorts, radiographic imaging datasets, clinical outcomes data, and de-identified radiology reports are required to support artificial intelligence-based research focused on evaluating liver cancer risk in patients with cirrhosis and indeterminate liver lesions. The research requires datasets that combine specific patient populations with associated imaging studies and clinical outcomes information to enable the development, validation, and evaluation of predictive models. Alternative datasets that do not include the required patient populations, imaging data, clinical outcomes information, and associated radiology reports would not provide the information necessary to support the approved research objectives. The absence of any of these data elements would limit the ability to correlate imaging findings with clinical outcomes and would reduce the scientific validity and reliability of the resulting analyses. Therefore, only datasets containing the required clinical cohorts and associated imaging and outcomes data will satisfy the Government's minimum needs and support the approved research objectives. The objectives of the maintenance agreement are as follows: The objective of this requirement is to acquire clinical patient cohorts, associated imaging data, clinical outcomes data, and de-identified radiology reports to support the development and evaluation of A.I. models for liver disease and liver cancer research conducted by the Liver Diseases Branch. A determination by the Government to compete this proposed acquisition based upon responses received to this notice is solely within the discretion of the Government. The proposed contractor maintains an existing cohort of patients with cirrhosis and associated radiographic images collected at six-month intervals, as well as an existing cohort of patients with cirrhosis and indeterminate liver lesions, including associated clinical outcomes data and radiographic images. These clinical cohorts and associated datasets represent a unique research resource available through the proposed contractor. The combination of longitudinal imaging data, clinical outcomes data, and radiographic images associated with these patient populations is available only through the proposed contractor. As a result, only the proposed contractor can provide the requested deliverables necessary to support the research project. It is anticipated that an award will be issued approximately five (5) calendar days after the closing date of this notice, unless the Government determines that another vendor has the capability to meet this requirement. Please submit responses electronically to davisroshonna@mail.nih.gov no later than 9:00 a.m. EDT on September 25, 2026. Please reference Notice No. 75N98026Q01240 in the subject line of the response.
sig_d3771785f2bb25cac5ac.title: Obtain Clinical Cohort of Patients with Associated Clinical Outcomes, Radiologic Images, and Associated De-Identified Radiology Reports

sig_d3ab4e0744d66fe32242.description: The City of Wolverhampton Council is exploring the introduction of an Additional Licensing Scheme for smaller Houses in Multiple Occupation (HMOs) and a Selective Licensing Scheme for privately rented properties in designated areas. These schemes are part of the Council's strategic approach to improving housing standards, tenant safety, and landlord accountability across the city's growing private rented sector (PRS). To ensure transparency, inclusivity, and legal compliance, the Council is committed to undertaking a comprehensive public consultation before any licensing scheme is introduced. This consultation must engage a wide range of stakeholders-including landlords, letting agents, tenants, residents, and community organisations-and gather meaningful feedback on the proposed scheme's scope, impact, and implementation. The Council is therefore seeking to appoint an experienced external provider to design, manage, and deliver the public consultation process. The appointed organisation will be expected to: • Develop a robust consultation strategy aligned with statutory requirements. • Facilitate engagement through a range of accessible channels (e.g. online surveys, public meetings, stakeholder interviews). • Analyse and report on consultation findings to inform decision-making. • Ensure that the process is inclusive, impartial, and representative of Wolverhampton's diverse communities. Lot 1: .

sig_d4103b772907b36c5b73.description: The Kosovo Energy Project (KEP) is a development cooperation initiative implemented by GIZ, co-financed by the German Federal Ministry for Economic Cooperation and Development (BMZ) and the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Denmark, supporting Kosovo"s transition toward a more sustainable, efficient, and inclusive energy system. KEP aims to help Kosovo fulfil its obligations under the EU Energy Community Treaty by improving energy efficiency and expanding the use of renewable energy, particularly renewable energy for self-consumption in buildings. The project addresses Kosovo"s dependence on lignite-based electricity generation, outdated infrastructure, high energy losses, and low energy efficiency, while supporting alignment with EU energy and climate legislation and the Green Agenda for the Western Balkans. It focuses on strengthening the regulatory, institutional, financial, and technical framework for EE and SC-RE investments. It supports national institutions, especially the Ministry of Economy, the Ministry of Environment, Spatial Planning and Infrastructure, and the Kosovo Energy Efficiency Fund (KEEF), through legal and policy advice, development of secondary legislation and technical standards, and practical tools. A key pillar is improving financing mechanisms by supporting KEEF to design, pilot, and scale funding models that mobilize public and private investment, including in private homes, multi-apartment buildings, public buildings, and businesses. At the municipal level, KEP supports the development of Municipal Energy and Climate Action Plans and strengthens local capacities to plan and implement energy measures in line with national targets. KEP addresses these challenges through five interconnected outputs: Output 1 - Enabling regulation: Supporting responsible institutions to draft, amend and operationalise key legal and regulatory instruments, including secondary legislation and technical standards. The objective is to reduce regulatory uncertainty, streamline procedures and create investor confidence for EE and renewable self-consumption investments. Output 2 - Investment-ready financing: Strengthening and expanding the financial mechanisms of the Kosovo Energy Efficiency Fund (KEEF) to reach households, SMEs and municipalities. Particular focus is placed on multi-apartment buildings and affordability barriers affecting energy-poor households. This includes optimisation of grant, loan and blended finance instruments as well as strengthened monitoring and verification systems. Output 3 - Capable institutions and services: Improving national information and advisory services to ensure that EE and RE-SC solutions are accessible, technically credible and responsive to investor needs. Dedicated formats are promoted to support women as investors and professionals in the energy sector. Output 4 - Local implementation capacity: Supporting municipalities in moving from stand-alone energy efficiency planning towards integrated Municipal Energy and Climate Action Plans (MECAPs), combining EE and RE-SC measures aligned with national objectives. The project also strengthens institutionalised inter-municipal learning and exchange. Output 5 - Inclusive transition and women"s participation: Establishing and anchoring a Women in Energy Network supported through structured capacity building, employability pathways and partnerships to increase women"s representation and career progression in the energy sector as a contribution to a just transition. Through this contract, GIZ intends to commission a service provider to continue the implementation of Outputs 1, 2, 4 and 5. The assignment will contribute to strengthening Kosovo"s regulatory framework, improving access to finance, enhancing local implementation capacities and promoting gender-inclusive participation in the energy transition. This assignment contributes to the overall objective of the Kosovo Energy Project (KEP) to improve the framework conditions for increasing energy efficiency (EE) and expanding renewable energy for self-consumption (RE-SC) in Kosovo. The contractor shall provide technical advisory services, institutional capacity development and implementation support to partner institutions in close coordination with GIZ and relevant national stakeholders. The contractor shall build on previous project achievements, avoid duplication and ensure complementarity with ongoing national reforms and donor-supported initiatives. The contractor is responsible for contributing to the achievement of the expected results under Outputs 1, 2, 4 and 5 of KEP. Activities under all work packages shall be implemented in an integrated manner to maximise synergies between regulatory reform, financing mechanisms, institutional capacity development and gender-responsive energy transition. Work Package (WP) 1: Legal and Regulatory Framework Objective: Improve the legal, regulatory, and technical framework to enable investments in energy efficiency (EE) and renewable energy sources (RES) for self-consumption. Description: The contractor shall provide technical advisory services to strengthen the legal and regulatory framework for energy efficiency and renewable energy for self-consumption in Kosovo. The assignment includes drafting and reviewing legislation, developing technical standards and supporting partner institutions in implementing the new regulatory framework. The expected result is an improved enabling environment that facilitates public and private investment while ensuring alignment with the EU Energy Acquis and Energy Community obligations. Key Outputs / Activities: - Provide technical advisory services to ME, MESPI and KEEF for the drafting, revision and implementation of legislation and regulatory frameworks on energy efficiency (EE) and the energy performance of buildings (EPB). - Support ME, ERO, DSO and TSO in drafting and amending secondary legislation implementing the Law on Renewable Energy and transposing Directive (EU) 2019/944, with a focus on renewable energy for self-consumption (RE-SC). - Strengthen ERO's capacities to develop tariff and revenue methodologies reflecting the revised renewable energy support framework. - Develop national technical standards for EE and RE-SC in line with the EPB Law, the EU Energy Acquis and international best practices. - Develop technical standards for the grid integration of renewable energy and support the simplification of permitting and authorisation procedures. Work package (WP) 2: Financial Mechanisms Objective: Improve access to tailored financing mechanisms for EE and RES investments for self-consumption. Description: The contractor shall support KEEF in improving, expanding and operationalising financing mechanisms for EE and RE-SC investments. Particular emphasis shall be placed on developing financially sustainable instruments that increase investment uptake among households, municipalities and SMEs, while addressing affordability barriers for vulnerable groups. Key Outputs / Activities: - Advisory support to KEEF to fine-tune financing schemes for different target groups (households, SMEs, municipalities). - Design and structuring of support mechanisms and blended financial instruments, with a focus on multi-apartment buildings. - Identification of financing gaps and barriers, including affordability constraints, and formulation of targeted recommendations. - Preparation of recommendations to revise existing KEEF schemes based on lessons learned from pilot programs. - Support to operationalize monitoring and verification systems for EE and RES pilot projects. Work package (WP) 3: Human Capacity Development Objective: Strengthen institutional and human capacities to plan, implement, and monitor EE and RES measures at national and local levels. Description: Work Package 3 provides cross-cutting institutional and human capacity development measures supporting the implementation of Outputs 1, 2, 4 and 5. sig_d41871429d29b9119759.description: XC Trains Limited (XC) operates passenger rail services over those routes listed within Appendix 2 of the ITP document. XC is a unique operation in that it runs from the Southwest in England to the North of Scotland and is the most extensive rail franchise in Britain, calling at more than 100 stations. XC serves 7 of the 10 largest UK cities with 7 routes radiating from a central hub in Birmingham. The Service Quality Regime (SQR) was set up by the Department for Transport (DfT) to incentivise Train Operating Companies (TOCs) to ensure customer experience standards across the railway network are maintained and improved. The regime is defined in the National Rail Contracts (NRCs) that exist between TOCs and the DfT, including in XC's NRC. The NRC sets out the obligations that TOCs have to deliver to ensure compliance with the SQR, and the repercussions if they are not. XC's SQR has been in place since late 2021 and has seen a few changes since it first started. XC is also proud to have helped the DfT trial changes to SQR during this time to pave the way for other TOCs following in the future. The key elements and strategic objectives of the Project are: - A cloud-based database for all SQR-related data, including an SQ Register, reference data, inspection data and rectification evidence data and provision of inspection forms to be used by third party inspectors; - An inspection forms system that will be used by third-party inspectors and Mystery Shoppers on their mobile devices to undertake and submit inspection data and provision of inspection-related notifications; - A web-based Back-office System for XC users and inspections supplier quality controllers to view and work with inspection data including the recording of rectification evidence, and creation and maintenance of application programming interfaces (APIs); - System functionality to generate email notifications in response to triggers linked to data being created or modified within the database; - APIs to enable the system to integrate with other systems; and - Reporting both on a regular cycle and as required. - The purpose of the Procurement is to select a supplier to provide a Service Quality Regime System. Lot 1: .

sig_d4b005e2922278f80f5d.description: A Dynamic Purchasing System (DPS) is a fully electronic procurement procedure that enables suppliers to apply for admission on an ongoing basis and to compete for specific contracts (mini-tenders) within a defined scope. Energinet will use the Comdia platform to support the digital management and operation of the DPS. Energinet is currently conducting a market assessment and preparing procurement materials for the establishment of a Dynamic Purchasing System to be used for the execution of mini-tenders concerning the acquisition of standard software and related services supporting control center operations. Energinet expects to publish the DPS with a set of overarching framework conditions. Following publication, suppliers that meet the defined admission requirements will be able to apply for inclusion in the system. The specific requirements for admission will be made available upon publication of the DPS. Submission of input is voluntary and intended to support Energinet in ensuring that the requirement specifications are aligned with market standards. In this context, suppliers are encouraged to: •Challenge specified requirements •Ask clarifying questions •Add propose adjustments, clarifications, or rewordings •Any ambiguities identified in the material are also requested to be highlighted in the feedback. Energinet reserves the right to freely assess the extent to which received input will be incorporated into the final procurement documents. The content of the draft material may be amended in whole or in part prior to publication. If market participants wish to submit input and/or express their interest in participating in the system, this must be submitted via Comdia no later than 18 May 2026 at 10:00. If a supplier does not express interest in participating in the system at this stage, it will still be possible to apply for admission to the system once it is published.
sig_d4b005e2922278f80f5d.title: Hearing - Energinet Market involvement regarding Dynamic Purchasing System of standard software for operations technology and control center solutions - 26/07722

sig_d4c3965183583a4ea392.description: The object of this procurement is the acquisition of specialised retro-digitisation services for documents belonging to the physical archive held by the General Directorate of Local Taxes and Fees Sector 3, for an estimated volume of 10.000 linear metres of archive. The requested services aim to convert documents from physical to digital format, as well as ensuring their archival and technical compliance, with a view to implementing an efficient electronic document management system that ensures rapid, secure and legal access to the stored information. The services that are the subject of the procurement include, but are not limited to, the following activities: - collection, handling and organisation of the physical documents existing in the institution's archive; - scanning of documents at technical parameters that ensure the legibility, integrity and fidelity of the digital reproduction; - indexing and association of metadata related to each document or file, in order to facilitate the rapid identification and retrieval of information; - structured organisation of digital documents, so that they can be integrated into existing electronic document management information systems; - quality verification of images and indexing accuracy, to ensure a high level of precision and compliance; - handover of physical documents, together with the resulting digital archive. The final result of the contract will consist of: - digitised and indexed documents, organised in a logical and coherent structure; - an organised and easily accessible archival fund, which allows for the rapid retrieval of documents and their integration into the institution's electronic workflows. By carrying out this procurement, the aim is to create a structural and digitised archive, which ensures transparency, information security, operational efficiency and compliance with the applicable legal regulations in the field of archives and document management. According to the provisions of Art. 160 para (1) of Law 98/2016 (hereinafter referred to as “Law 98”) and Art. 103 para (1) of the Methodological Norms to Law no. 98/2016, approved by G.D. no. 395/2016 (hereinafter referred to as “Norms”), any interested economic operator has the right to request clarifications or additional information in connection with the award documentation, observing a deadline of 18 days before the deadline for the submission of tenders. In accordance with the provisions of Art. 160 para. (2) and of Art. 161 para. (1) of “Law 98”, as well as of Art. 27 para. (2)-(4) and of Art. 103 para. (2) of the “Norms”, the contracting authority will respond in a consolidated, clear and complete manner to all requests for clarifications/additional information on the 11 day before the deadline set for the submission of tenders. The contracting authority will not respond to a request for clarifications/additional information received in the interval of 17 days before the deadline set for the submission of tenders, the request being considered to have been submitted late. The modification of the public procurement contract, during its period of validity, may be carried out under the conditions provided for in Art. 221 of Law no. 98/2016 and the provisions of ANAP Instruction no. 1/2021. The Contracting Authority wishes, through this procedure, to extend the support, warranty and subscription/licence services for the existing solutions, without modifying the general architecture in operation and without introducing technologies incompatible with the current environment. The acquisition has a character of operational and technological continuity, being necessary to maintain the level of security, reduce the risks of unavailability, ensure specialised technical support in the event of incidents or malfunctions and maintain visibility over the performance and use of IT resources. This acquisition does not aim to replace the existing infrastructure, but to ensure the continuity of support, warranty and usage rights services for the solutions already in operation, so that they can function in optimal, safe and compliant conditions during the established contract period. The renewal/extension of support, warranty and subscription/licence services related to the existing solutions will be carried out, including, as appropriate, for platforms and products used from the Cisco, Palo Alto Networks, F5 and IBM (namely IBM QRadar, IBM Instana and IBM Turbonomic) ranges, according to the technical requirements detailed in the specifications. The Romanian Automotive Register - R.A. (R.A.R. - R.A.) uses within its IT infrastructure specialised solutions for security, communications, monitoring, observability, resource optimisation and application protection, necessary to ensure the continuity of IT services, protect digital resources and maintain an adequate level of availability, performance and security. These solutions are used for the protection of the central infrastructure, data communications, internally and externally exposed applications, for securing traffic and critical IT services, as well as for monitoring, analysis, correlation of security events, application observability and optimisation of IT resource usage. Since the IT systems of R.A.R. - R.A. support very important operational processes, it is necessary to keep the security, monitoring and administration components in operation functional and updated. The requirements in the specifications are minimum and mandatory. In this sense, any offer of services that deviates from the provisions of the specifications or presents services with characteristics inferior to those provided for therein or that does not satisfy the requirements imposed therein, will be rejected as non-compliant. The acquisition will be finalised by concluding a contract with a single economic operator, for a period of maximum 25 months, of which maximum 24 months is the period granted additionally for warranty, subscriptions/licences and technical support services and 30 days is the delivery and implementation term.

sig_d4dd6ae8c237d43343b0.description: The subject of the procurement is a work ability management system as a SaaS service. The procurement includes the delivery of the system, planning and implementation of the deployment, execution of necessary integrations, and ongoing maintenance and support services. In addition, the contracting authority has the option to procure separately agreed minor development during the contract period. The supplier is responsible for ensuring that the system can be deployed in a controlled manner and that it is integrated into the contracting authority's key back-end systems, such as HR and identity management systems. The migration of legacy data can be carried out as expert work as a separately ordered option in accordance with the hourly rate for expert work stated in the price appendix. The contracting authority shall decide on the implementation of the option at its own discretion during the contract period, and the contracting authority is under no obligation to implement the option or order related services. The system must support the contracting authority's work ability management operating models and processes, in particular early support practices, management of sickness absences, identification and prevention of work ability risks, and support for return to work. The objective of the solution is to improve the timeliness of work ability measures, increase operational transparency, and strengthen data-driven management at all levels of the organisation. The system must provide an up-to-date overall picture of the work ability situation at the employee, unit, and organisational level. It must form a clear, user-friendly, and intuitive whole regarding work ability management processes and offer views and access rights according to user roles. User groups include at least line managers, HR work ability specialists, management, and system administrators. Line managers must be able to utilise the system in their daily work ability management work, while for management, the system must offer summary views, reporting, and analytics to support strategic decision-making. The system must enable versatile reporting for different time periods and organisational levels and offer visual views, such as trends, comparisons, and key performance indicators to support decision-making. The supplier must carry out the deployment in cooperation with the contracting authority so that the solution meets the contracting authority's functional needs and the deployment supports a smooth transition to production use. The objective of the procurement is to improve the effectiveness of work ability management, reduce costs caused by sickness absences, strengthen proactive management, and support the staff's work ability, performance at work, and continuation in work. The system must be a modern, secure, scalable, and easy-to-use solution that supports the long-term development of the contracting authority's operations.
sig_d4dd6ae8c237d43343b0.title: Procurement of a work ability management system

This service must contemplate the implementation and commissioning of the examination booths comprising the following work: 1. Analysis, construction, implementation, commissioning and supervision of the service. It will carry out the definition of processes and functional specifications, current situation analysis, functional design, documentation of requirements and modules, detailed technical design, system development, implementation, stabilization, knowledge management and supervision of the examination service. 2. Support and Incident Management Support service after entry into production, without changes in functionality. Resolution times and incident types (blocking, intermediate, low) are defined. Detailed resolution reports are generated.

sig_d51752b39833df6988a4.description: Valtion talous- ja henkilöstöhallinnon palvelukeskus (Palkeet) is publishing a preliminary notice regarding the procurement of maintenance, support and expert services for Precisely Automate (Winshuttle) licences, as well as the procurement of additional Precisely Automate licences. Palkeet invites tenderers interested in the market dialogue to express their interest and register for the market dialogue by replying to this request for information. This notice is not an invitation to tender, and its publication does not initiate a competitive tendering procedure; rather, this is a request for information related to market research. This does not oblige Palkeet to carry out the actual procurement, and any information provided is non-binding. The subject matter of the procurement will be refined as the market dialogue progresses, and the content of the subject matter may change during the course of it. Failing to reply to the request for information does not prevent participation in a potential competitive tendering procedure, nor does replying to the request for information affect the tenderer's position in the actual competitive tendering procedure. SUBJECT OF THE MARKET DIALOGUE With the commencing market dialogue, Palkeet wishes to familiarise itself with suppliers in the market that can provide maintenance, support and expert services, as well as potential additional licences, for existing Precisely Automate (Winshuttle) licences. Palkeet utilises the Winshuttle Evolve solution in its service production, inter alia in accounting and human resources processes. Winshuttle licences are primarily used for mass runs of financial and HR data in Palkeet's Kieku system (SAP HCM, SAP Finance). For these purposes, Palkeet uses perpetual licences: 60 Studio Runner licences and 10 Studio Developer licences. Support and maintenance services mean the maintenance and version management of Precisely Automate (Winshuttle) licences (e.g. activations, modifications and updates), error correction, and advisory and support services. In addition, there must be an option to separately order further development and other expert services. REQUEST FOR INFORMATION QUESTIONS AND REGISTRATION INSTRUCTIONS We kindly ask tenderers to submit their answers to the request for information questions below. The answers provided, or the failure to reply, do not constitute an obstacle to potential participation in commenting on the draft invitation to tender materials at a later stage. All answers supplied by you and the descriptions attached to them will be treated as confidential and are not public documents. Request for information questions 1. The name of the company registering for the market dialogue, the name of the contact person and the email address. 2. What kinds of references does the tenderer have regarding the maintenance, related support and expert services for Precisely Automate (Winshuttle) licences? What are the licence types and pricing models of the different environments (on-premise/cloud) or use cases for new Precisely Automate (Winshuttle) licences? 3. What are the licence types and pricing models of the different environments (on-premise/cloud) or use cases for the maintenance service of current perpetual Precisely Automate (Winshuttle) licences? Is the model the same with regard to any potential new additional licences? 4. In what different languages can you provide maintenance, support and expert services? Would your supply situation change if all support services could be delivered in English? 5. In what different types of environments (Evolve, Studio Manager, Desktop) have you delivered support services for Precisely Automate (Winshuttle) licences? 6. Which licence terms apply to the maintenance of Precisely Automate (Winshuttle) licences and what about for new licences? Please provide your licence terms as an attachment. 7. Are the current names of Precisely Automate (Winshuttle) licences (Studio Developer and Studio Runner) still in use and if not, what are the names of the licences that correspond to them and are compatible with them? Is there a difference in licence names if the licence is used in an on-premise solution vs. a cloud solution? 8. Is it possible to place Precisely Automate (Winshuttle) licences on dormant status such that they are not used in a given year, and the maintenance fee is not paid for them during that time either, but the licence is put back into use later? 9. Is it possible to transfer Precisely Automate (Winshuttle) licences from one user to another and/or from one customer organisation of Palkeet to another in the middle of a maintenance period and/or when the maintenance period changes? 10. Is there anything else special related to Precisely Automate (Winshuttle) licences or their terms that would be good for Palkeet to be aware of? We kindly ask you to register as a supplier interested in the market dialogue and to send your answers to the questions presented in the request for information by 18.9.2025 at the latest at 15.00 by email to the address kilpailutus@hansel.fi; please title the email "Palkeet Precisely Automate (Winshuttle) -lisenssit, markkinavuoropuhelu". The objective is to engage in market dialogue with industry operators who have notified their contact details and are interested in the procurement, which may include answering questions and commenting on draft invitations to tender in September-October 2025. No compensation will be paid to those who have registered for participation in the market dialogue. The dialogues will be conducted in the Finnish language. Valtion talous- ja henkilöstöhallinnon palvelukeskus (Palkeet) is a corporate service provider operating within the administrative sector of the Ministry of Finance. We produce financial and HR services for central government agencies, institutions, funds and state limited company customers for approximately 80 000 individual wage earners with the strength of around 650 professionals.

sig_d5236fe2ac551b3f0357.description: An observation instrument for children's linguistic and mathematical development is to be developed, pilot tested, validated and tested for reliability, derived from the Brandenburg curriculum. The items for assessing children's competences at the end of the Kita period (3 third of the final Kita year) are designed as "Individual learning status analysis at the transition from Kita to school (ILeA 0)" and configured to be compatible with the existing observation instrument for the "Individual learning status analysis in the first 6 weeks after starting school (ILeA plus)". The aim is an integrated, structurally harmonised observation system that records linguistic and mathematical development in a comparable and compatible structure. Lot LOT-0001: Development, pilot testing, validation and reliability testing of an observation instrument for linguistic and mathematical development. The contracting authority expects a standardised, scientifically sound, streamlined and practice-oriented observation instrument. A uniform conceptual approach is of central importance to the contracting authority in order to keep the need for qualification in practice to a low level and to simplify use by educational professionals with the uniform structure of ILeA 0. The service is divided into four work packages: Work package 1 (development of the linguistic aspects of the observation instrument), work package 2 (development of the mathematical aspects of the observation instrument), work package 3 (creation of a guidance document for the observation instrument), work package 4 (pilot testing, validation and reliability testing of the developed observation instrument). Further details can be found in Appendix 12 (specification of services).
sig_d5236fe2ac551b3f0357.title: Development, pilot testing, validation and reliability testing of an observation instrument for linguistic and mathematical development

sig_d5302691e93901444753.description: INTRODUCTION We kindly request you to submit your response to this information request concerning the procurement of the Amazon Web Service (AWS) cloud platform and related expert services. We greatly appreciate all responses received, and each of them will be taken into account in the preparation of a potential tender process. The purpose of the information request is to ensure that the preparers of the tender process have as comprehensive and up-to-date a picture of the market and available solutions as possible. With this information request, we wish to survey suppliers' offerings of solutions and services that support the design, implementation, management and development of the AWS cloud platform and enable the secure, cost-effective and controlled use of cloud services. The objective is that the overall solution provides a smooth and appropriate user experience for end-users as well as clear operating models for the maintenance of the cloud environment (e.g. governance, information security, monitoring and cost management). At the same time, we aim to familiarise ourselves with the market situation of services related to the cloud platform and expert services, the products and tools possibly associated with their use, contractual terms and commercial terms such as pricing. Please note that the information, descriptions and estimates of the publication date of the tender process presented in this information request are currently preliminary and indicative. The final schedules will be specified as the preparation progresses. RESPONDING TO THE INFORMATION REQUEST Please submit your response and comments by email to hankinnat@istekki.fi at the latest by 27.4.2026 at 14:00 Responses shall be submitted using a separate response form "KYSYMYKSET_markkinavuoropuhelu_Julkipilvikilpailutus_AWS" in the Finnish language so that their processing is as smooth as possible. We kindly ask you to title the message with the subject "RESPONSE TO INFORMATION REQUEST / AWS / SUPPLIER NAME 2026. The information request is answered by the tenderer commenting on the preliminary requirements and conditions of the future tender process attached to the information request (Appendices 1- 9) These include, among other things, minimum requirements, the tenderer's suitability requirements and other possible drafts of procurement materials. The tenderer must provide clear comments on the fulfilment of each requirement, possible needs for clarification, proposed changes and justifications for these. We kindly ask you to present possible clarification or change proposals clearly and consistently. All responses and comments received to the information request will be taken into account in the preparation of the invitation to tender and its appendices. Istekki may, if necessary and at its discretion, invite suppliers to a market dialogue meeting to clarify the responses. A separate Teams meeting link will be sent for the market dialogue meetings. Questions related to the preparation of the procurement procedure may also be posed to suppliers. It is good to note that neither this information request nor the preliminary procurement materials delivered as its appendix obligates Istekki Oy to carry out the procurement in the manner presented in this document or its appendices. Istekki may alter, supplement or delimit the content of the appendices as the preparation progresses. A potential procurement procedure may also be left unorganised. No separate compensation is paid for responding to the information request. We would like to mention once more that this is an information request, not a prior information notice, procurement notice or invitation to tender. The purpose of the information request is to familiarise with the market situation and gather information related to the subject of the procurement as well as comments on the requirements and conditions attached to the invitation to tender to support the planning of the future tender process. Responding to the information request is voluntary and is not a prerequisite for participation in a potential tender process or bind Istekki to publish a tender process. At the same time, however, we greatly appreciate the information and concrete comments provided by suppliers, as they help us build the future tender process into as functional, clear and appropriate an entity as possible. Istekki Oy reserves the right to share information obtained on the basis of the information request for use by its customer-owners for purposes supporting the preparation and planning of the procurement.

sig_d5a5d80997059cc028a2.description: The provision of temporary and interim staff services to the Scottish Public Sector Lot 1: . The Scottish Procurement and Property Directorate (SPPD) is the organisation tasked with procuring requirements on behalf of Scottish Public Sector Bodies. The current Scottish Government collaborative Temporary and Interim Staff Services Frameworks are a suite of four individual multi supplier Framework Agreements which commenced on 13 April 2023 and are due to expire on 12 April 2027. sig_d61374e1e3ef8e6cb455.description: The NSF Engineering Directorate (ENG) has launched a multi-year initiative, theProfessional Formation of Engineers, to create and support an innovative and inclusive engineering profession for the 21 st century. Professional Formation of Engineers (PFE) refers to the formal and informal processes and value systems by which people become engineers. It also includes the ethical responsibility of practicing engineers to sustain and grow the profession in order to improve quality of life for all peoples. The engineering profession must be responsive to national priorities, grand challenges, and dynamic workforce needs; it must be equally open and accessible to all. Professional Formation of Engineers includes, but is not limited, to: Introductions to the profession at any age; Development of deep technical and professional skills, knowledge, and abilities in both formal and informal settings/domains; Development of outlooks, perspectives, ways of thinking, knowing, and doing; Development of identity as an engineer and its intersection with other identities; and Acculturation to the profession, its standards, and norms. The goal of the Research in the Formation of Engineers (RFE) program is to advance our understanding of professional formation. It seeks both to deepen our fundamental understanding of the underlying processes and mechanisms that support professional formation and to demonstrate how professional formation is or can be accomplished. Ultimately RFE aims to transform the engineer-formation system, and thus the impact of proposed projects on this system must be described. Principal Investigators (PIs) should provide a roadmap detailing how they envision the proposed research will eventually broadly impact practice within the engineer-formation system, even if these activities are not within the scope of the submitted proposal. In order to accomplish its goals, RFE welcomes proposals in two categories: Research Projects, and Design and Development Projects. Research Projects address fundamental questions of professional formation, while Design and Development Projects provide new approaches to achieving professional formation. Additional details are provided below. Projects in both categories should address the iterative cycle in which research questions that advance understanding are informed by practice and the results of research are, in turn, translated into practice. In other words, proposals should explain how the research results will travel, translate, transfer, or scale. Successful projects identify specific target audiences, effective communication channels, and novel partnerships to ensure effective propagation and scaling. Proposal titles should begin with either “Research:” or “Design and Development:” as appropriate. Research Projects Research proposals are particularly welcome in the following areas: Research that addresses lifelong learning by the engineering workforce. Research on the impact of engineering education research. Proposals addressing this topic could investigate questions such as: How can we measure the impacts of engineering education research? What are effective strategies for scaling reforms? How can we translate knowledge from research to practice? What are the roles of technologies, networks and communities in achieving impact? RFE does not support efficacy, effectiveness, or scale-up studies for specific interventions. Research that addresses culture change in engineering education. Included in this topic are investigations of normative cultures of engineering at any level in the engineering education ecosystem and how these cultures may disadvantage certain groups. Research that addresses engineering formation at the two-year college level in both formal and informal settings. Research that addresses engineering formation at the graduate education level in both formal and informal settings. Research that investigates engineering in P-12 settings. Research in this area could include understanding of approaches to engineering in P-12, how to develop engineering ways of thinking, or the relationship between practices within the sciences and mathematics and engineering thinking. Research on the transitions between education levels, e.g., from high school to two-year college, high school to four-year college/university, two-year college to four-year college/university, undergraduate to graduate school, education settings to the workforce or professoriate, etc. Research that addresses the relationship between engineering and the public. Proposals addressing this topic could consider the social impact of engineering solutions, citizen engineering, education of an informed public, etc. Research that develops or adapts novel methodologies and frameworks appropriate for studying the professional formation of engineers, and especially minoritized, marginalized, or underserved populations. Research that addresses ways in which new technologies (such as artificial intelligence and machine learning) are changing engineering education. Research to transform engineering education so that all students encounter environmental and social sustainability principles as an integrated part of their education and are equipped with the tools needed to incorporate these principles into their future research, careers, and innovations. Proposals submitted to the Research Projects category should have clear research questions informed by an appropriate theoretical framework and a research design that includes sampling, data collection, and data analysis methods. This category will not support proposals that seek funding primarily to develop tools, curriculum, or laboratories, or that seek to implement classroom innovations that have already been shown to be effective in engineering. The program will evaluate the value of proposals by considering the impact and the cost. Research track projects that are small, exploratory, or speculative are especially encouraged. Larger Research track projects should have a correspondingly larger impact. Design and Development Projects RFE supports Design and Development projects (see https://www.nsf.gov/publications/pub_summ.jsp?ods_key=nsf13126 ) that seek to develop and test new approaches in the following areas related to engineering education : Graduate education. Undergraduate education in new engineering technologies and environmental sustainability. Transitions between education levels, for example high school to two-year college, high school to four-year college/university, two-year college to four-year college/university, undergraduate to graduate school, education settings to the workforce or professoriate, etc. P-12, especially approaches to develop engineering thinking, or providing links between engineering, science, and mathematics. Proposals in this category should propose the design and development of new approaches that are informed by existing literature and theory. There should be clear objectives and the evaluation plan should be designed to determine if those objectives have been met. Projects cannot be solely demonstration projects but must add to the engineering education literature to inform future work.
sig_d61374e1e3ef8e6cb455.title: Research in the Formation of Engineers

sig_d650142ebef09c066cbe.description: RFI Pursuant to Revolutionary Federal Acquisition Regulation Overhaul RFO FAR 15.101(c) DISCLAIMER This is a Request for Information (RFI) issued in accordance with RFO FAR 15.101(c). The Government does not intend to award a contract on the basis of this RFI or otherwise pay for the information requested. Responses to this RFI will be treated as information only and shall not be construed as a proposal. This is not a Request for Proposal (RFP), nor does it constitute a solicitation and shall not be construed as a commitment by the Government. Responses in any form are not offers and the Government is under no obligation to award a contract from this announcement. No funds will be made available to pay for the preparation of responses to this announcement. Any information submitted to this notice is strictly voluntary and will not be returned. Not responding to this notice does not preclude participation in future solicitations. If a solicitation is released, it will not be synopsized on the government-wide point of entry due to national security. Only vendors meeting the security requirements will be provided with additional information pertaining to this requirement. INTENT Background: HQDA G-2. CASTLE KEEP is a customer-facing portal that provides automated workflow services and Sensitive Compartmented Army SCI program reporting, metrics, analysis, and information sharing within the Army SCI community in accordance with DoDM 5105.21 requirements. This is non-personal services contract to provide Software Development and Software Sustainment Support of the Department of Army (DA) SSO’s CASTLE KEEP. The Army Contracting Command Aberdeen Proving Ground (ACC-APG) is issuing this RFI to conduct market research. The intent of the RFI is to identify parties having an interest in bidding on and the resources to support solicitations for G2’s CASTLE KEEP’s sustainable solution for the SSO/SSR community to develop and sustain CASTLE KEEP in Army Commercial Cloud Solutions Provider (AC2SP). The Government retains ownership to software and application tools; upon completion this contract all information will be turned over to the U.S. Government and is U.S. Government property. The identified questions are to encourage competition and exchanges of information. Any voluntary response received will be reviewed to assist the Government in arriving at the most suitable approach. The Government is seeking responses to this RFI that describes vendors’ existing capabilities. Small Business Participation: This RFI is issued on an unrestricted basis (Full and Open) to maximize industry responses. The Government highly encourages submissions from all business sizes and socioeconomic categories (e.g., Small Business, SDVOSB, 8(a), WOSB, HUBZone). Infrastructure Assessment: Vendor shall simulate the realistic threat exploitation techniques within the legacy, existing, and emerging software system's cybersecurity in the mission context of the representative operating environment. Vendor shall apply the cybersecurity testing process with blue teams of Government and Vendor equivalent organizations and red teams of the certified Government and Vendor equivalent organizations during Developmental/Operational Test & Evaluation (D/O T&E).The Blue team assesses the operational network vulnerability with findings for the independent technical review of the network security posture and implements the mitigation techniques for integration into the community security solution to increase the cybersecurity readiness posture. The Blue teams evaluate the security threats/risks in the operating environment and study the network environment and its current state of security readiness. The Red teams simulate the potential adversary's exploitation capabilities against an enterprise's security posture to enhance the enterprise IA/Cybersecurity via demonstration of the impacts of the successful attacks and the needed countermeasure by the blue teams in the operational environment. Cyber Integration: Vendor shall coordinate with Government Agencies and industry partners to support interoperability and integration of other capabilities, maintain adequate certified personnel to meet requirements, and provide qualified staff for CASTLE KEEP software development and sustainment. Vendor shall lease workspace with NIPRNet and JWICS access to support three to four personnel. sig_d6cbbe1ee9be752376d6.description: The aim of the project is the implementation of the new Diavgeia taking into account modern institutional, operational and technological developments, the more correct implementation of the institutional framework with emphasis on the General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR) and the optimal utilisation of Diavgeia information with a data-based architecture and secondarily document-based. The project seeks to increase the efficiency and productivity of public services by enriching the applications of the Diavgeia Programme, supplementing functionality for the collaborative drafting and management of documents to be published based on standardised documents and data structures, and also to add value to the Programme by utilising and enriching the information gathered within it through the use of other information sources with the aim of creating a system of complex reports and other complementary application subsystems and solutions. The new system will allow the monitoring of the operation and organisational structure of public administration in combination with information related to the competences of bodies in the context of multi-level governance and also of personnel as recorded in the Human Resources Register of the Hellenic Republic. The aim is to provide objective evidence for the implementation of the National Administrative Procedures Policy and the prioritisation of the actions of the National Programme for Administrative Simplification. To this end, care has been taken to significantly enhance its interoperability with third-party public sector systems for the dissemination of information without necessarily requiring intervention from the end user. Additionally, through the expansion of information kept in a structured manner (metadata set), it will be possible to capture data groups with special characteristics that enhance transparency at the level of monitoring/evaluation by the general public of indicators related to, for example, the operation and structure of public administration and/or financial figures (public spending). For this purpose, data from other sources and publicly available data will also be utilised to support the monitoring of the operation and action of bodies and to support decision-making. The solution will include the creation of a system for the correct (and as complete as possible per sector) structured collection and processing of data from various public data sources and subsequently making them available to the general public. Illustrative examples of sources are data from systems under development for GOV ERP, HRMS, the Civil Society Organisations Register, ESIDIS, KHMDIS. A distinct subsystem will be developed for further utilisation and extraction of specialised reports with the aim of monitoring the structure, operation and action of public administration as well as monitoring expenditure and procurement and supporting the decision-making process. The system will be scalable for the addition of new sources arising from other actions. Also, within the framework of the action, improvements will be made in relation to identified problems associated with the management of the very large volume of documents collected by Diavgeia at a sharply increasing rate, which also led to the necessary migration of the infrastructure to public cloud services. In this context, advanced services provided by public clouds will be better utilised in order to ensure the uninterrupted provision of services and the monitoring of their provision at the lowest possible cost. The action, taking into account the life cycle of the administrative documents that are published, will address challenges such as the cleaning of multiple copies of the same documents, the extraction of all information in data format and the optimisation of the quality of Diavgeia metadata as well as the automatic publication of important data sets in the central open public data repository www.data.gov.gr. The project also aims to adopt a new architecture that will allow a drastic reduction, by at least 65%, of the required storage space and computational resources while ensuring the proper functioning of the system. To achieve the above goal, both emerging artificial intelligence and language model technologies and techniques for the correct entry of metadata into relevant information will be utilised to facilitate their search, categorisation and utilisation. This contract concerns a single subject matter and is not subdivided into lots due to the project's architecture, the strong interdependencies and complementarity of the individual services that compose it, as well as the high interoperability requirements that must be ensured on the one hand between the functional units (subsystems) to be developed within the framework of this project and on the other hand with third-party systems of Hellenic Republic bodies. The non-subdivision of the contract enhances the quality and security of the project, since unified management reduces the chances of security gaps or incompatibilities appearing between the different systems and facilitates the coordination of its implementation. The duration of the contract is set at thirty-two (32) months including the procedure for checking and acceptance of deliverables. The contract will be awarded on the basis of the most economically advantageous tender, based on the best price-quality ratio. [para. 1.3. & ANNEX I of the Call for Tenders]

sig_d6f20e827ba28a83b6df.description: HZD established the Test Center Hessen in 2022 and has operated it since then as a central organisational unit for standardised test services. Lot LOT-0000: Services for the operation of a test centre. As digitalisation progresses in the state administration, the requirements for quality assurance are also increasing. This is because stable IT operations cannot be guaranteed without sufficiently tested - and therefore quality-assured - solutions. Statutory requirements regarding the security and accessibility of the provided procedures further increase the requirements. Against this background, HZD established the Test Center Hessen (TCH) in 2022 and has operated it since then as a central organisational unit for standardised test services. The Test Center Hessen acts as a central organisational unit for standardised test services and is guided in this by established industry standards and best practices, in particular ISO/IEC 29119 and ISTQB. The Test Center Hessen (TCH) of HZD offers internal and external customers tailor-made services relating to testing. In addition, there are comprehensive services in the form of individually combinable modules. The modules are structured in a largely standardised manner. They can be put together as required. The subject of this tender is the support of the already established and operationally active Test Center Hessen by external IT service providers. The aim of the test centre is in particular to increase software quality and reduce risks in the software lifecycle. To support these aims, the following services are required, among others: • Consulting relating to testing • Standardisation and automation of the testing procedure • Provision of test services in various subject areas (test management, test automation, test data management, load and performance tests, functional (manual) tests including technical quality assurance as well as accessibility tests, see section 4 of the specification of services) • Provision of templates and methods According to the current planning status and taking into account additional requirements of other specialist departments and offices, a total requirement of approx. 37.730 person-days (PD) is assumed for the maximum contract duration of up to 48 months (non-binding estimated quantity).

sig_d7aef53156a66c17afe2.description: The Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Denmark (MFA) is in the process of streamlining the management of its development cooperation. Part of this effort concerns the simplification of the procurement process of key consultancy services relating to development cooperation. Consultancy contracts are currently procured individually by the case worker responsible for the programme or project. Case workers are MFA staff from MFA services at home in Copenhagen and abroad. In the procurement of individual contracts, they are responsible for the choice of procurement modality, the planning, preparation and management of the tender and contracting process. This process is often lengthy, and can have implications on programme and project timelines. Moreover, the fragmentation of the process makes it difficult to use the feedback from case workers on the fulfilment of the assignments. This makes it challenging to harvest learning from past performance and ensure a sustained quality of services. It is in this context that the MFA wishes to consolidate the procurement of consultancy services through a framework agreement with multiple contractors. The streamlining of the management of Danish development cooperation entailed a revision of the Danida – Aid Management Guidelines (https://amg.um.dk/). This foresees a delegation of key tasks to external consultants, primarily appraisals, and thereby an expected rise in the number of consultancy services to be requested. It is therefore an opportune time to seek a more streamlined procurement process of consultancy services. AMGs contain the policies, guidelines, and tools for the MFA’s development cooperation assistance. They cover different forms of Danish development cooperation modalities. The AMG’s Bilateral Guidelines (https://amg.um.dk/bilateral-cooperation/guidelines-for-programmes-projects-country-strategic-frameworks-and-hard-earmarked-multilat-support) and Financial Management Guidelines (https://amg.um.dk/bilateral-cooperation/financial-management) constitute the basic set of procedures for all Danish bilateral development cooperation. The guidelines outline the processes and requirements for the preparation, formulation, quality assurance, approval, implementation, completion and closure of Danish bilateral programmes and projects. The framework agreement is expected to solely cover bilateral development cooperation programmes and projects designed and implemented by Denmark. Therefore, the expected scope of work of consultancy services solely pertains to Official Development Aid (ODA) funds. The framework agreement is also expected to be divided into two lots. Under each lot, the MFA expects to conclude a framework agreement with between three to seven contractor to establish the terms governing contracts to be awarded during the term of the framework agreement, specifically the terms for award of contracts with/without reopening of competition amongst the contractors on the framework agreement. The expected lots reflect the thematic areas and priorities of Denmark’s Strategy for Development Cooperation: Lot 1: Climate change, environment, private sector development, enabling environment and financing. Lot 2: Governance, response to conflicts, forced displacement, irregular migration, health and education. Each lot is expected to require the provision of the following services pertaining to the design and implementation phases of bilateral development cooperation programmes, namely: Formulation of bilateral programmes and projects. This may include preparatory work in the formulation process if and as needed. Appraisal of the design of bilateral programmes and projects as a quality assurance milestone prior to approval. This includes external appraisals and early appraisals of larger or high-risk programmes/projects. Review of bilateral programmes and projects under implementation. This can span inception, midterm and technical reviews as part of the MFA unit’s monitoring and reporting cycle. The estimated values of the procurement and the lots are preliminary estimates.
sig_d7aef53156a66c17afe2.title: Consultancy framework agreement for formulation, appraisal and review of Danish development cooperation programmes and projects

sig_d851fdac8434e5612e4d.description: SKI hereby invites tenders for a dynamic purchasing system for Specialist Systems (02.19 Specialist Systems) The system contains one procurement category: Specialist Systems, delivered as Software as a Service (SaaS). Specialist Systems are supplied as "Software as a Service" (SaaS). Users subscribe to the software and gain access to it via the internet or via the supplier's application programming interfaces. Specialist Systems must support case processing/task handling of one or more of the customers' tasks/services, within one or more of the service areas mentioned below. The customer's needs determine which service area or areas are covered by the specific procurement. A specific procurement may well cover several of the service areas listed below. Specialist Systems as SaaS are characterised by being "on-demand services" which are owned, developed, maintained, managed and operated by the supplier or by the service owner's subcontractor. Services must be fully developed. Consequently, no services can be offered in the dynamic purchasing system that are developed or further developed specifically for the customer. The content of the service must be suitable for use in the Danish public sector. In addition, a procurement of services must comprise the implementation of the service (handover upon supplier change of a service and start-up upon the new establishment of a service) as well as the termination of the service (in connection with the expiry of the delivery contract). Implementation and termination form part of the overall service. Services are thus generic, fully developed solutions that meet uniform needs across customers, although such that these can be simply and quickly scaled and configured to the specific customer's IT environment, e.g. in relation to capacity, number of users or user rights etc. Consequently, services cannot be procured in the dynamic purchasing system that are intended to be developed for the individual customer on the basis of the customer's needs. The system covers all services and performance in the procurement of specialist systems within the service areas specified below. The service areas are based on FORM services. Reference is made to Annex C for a review of the covered service areas. It is voluntary for all SKI customers, as listed in Annex B, Customer List, to make use of the dynamic purchasing system when they are to procure specialist systems "as a Service".
