sig_d899525985c0fb046ac7.description: The DVLA require expressions of interest for the Provision of Direct Debit Solution. The proposed route to market is the Government Commercial DPS (GCA) Open Banking (Data, Digital Payments & Confirmation of Payee Services) DPS - Lot 1. The estimated value of the contract is c£37,500,000 and the contract will run for a 5-year term. DVLA anticipate issuing the award letter in May 2027 with a contract start date of February 2028, which allows around 8 months for transition and mobilisation activities. To find out how to become a supplier on this commercial agreement, visit https://supplierregistration.cabinetoffice.gov.uk/dps/RM6301, download the 'Bid pack', and read the READ FIRST RM6301-DPS Needs. To apply, or to update your responses, click 'Access as a supplier' to login/register. Registration is free and there is no limit on the number of suppliers who can join this DPS Marketplace. The purpose of this Prior Information Notice (PIN) is to inform the market of this upcoming requirement and invite interested suppliers to attend a virtual market engagement event. This event will provide an opportunity for DVLA to outline its proposed requirements, gather market feedback and help inform the future procurement requirements. Background The DVLA is an Executive Agency of The Department for Transport (DfT), based in Swansea. The Agency's primary aims are to facilitate road safety and general law enforcement by maintaining accurate registers of drivers and vehicle keepers and to collect Vehicle Excise Duty (VED). A Direct Debit (DD) payment option was introduced from 1st October 2014 which enables End Users to currently pay the full annual VED amount in one annual instalment, pay for a 6-month licensing period in one instalment or opt to spread the costs evenly over the term of a 12-month licensing period. All options result in an automatic VED renewal, subject to all business requirements being met, unless the End User opts out of the DD scheme. - Currently, over 1.4 million mandates are created per month, this is split between circa new (40%) and renewed (60%) mandates. - On average, Direct Debit payments total approximately £230m a month. sig_d8d1e6875ec91fd9f2e7.description: 1. The subject of the contract is the preparation, launch and provision by the Contractor to the Agency for Restructuring and Modernisation of Agriculture of an IT service in a SaaS model, enabling the automatic identification of land cover classes based on geospatial data, using artificial intelligence technology, in accordance with the Service Description constituting Appendix No. 1 to the draft contract provisions (hereinafter: "dcp") constituting Appendix No. 9 to the contract notice specifications (hereinafter: "CNS") and the Tender Form (Appendix No. 1 to the CNS). Land cover classes: 1.1 Basic land cover classes (hereinafter: "basic classes") – i.e. obligatory, required by the Contracting Authority, land cover classes for which the minimum classification quality indicators amounting to at least: Overall Accuracy 0,85; Recall 0,80; Precision 0,80.: a) Transport areas – (Management Fields (hereinafter: "MF") : K) b) Forests – (MF: L, Z, ZS, O, R) c) Industrial and urbanised areas – (MF: U) d) Settlements with buildings – (MF: D). Note: For the basic classes (classes a-d), the levels of the classification quality indicators (Overall Accuracy; Recall; Precision) shall be binding on the Contractor in accordance with the declaration submitted by the Contractor in the Tender Form. 1.2 Rewarded land cover classes (hereinafter: "rewarded classes") – i.e. non-obligatory, offered additionally by the Contractor within the scope of the tender evaluation criteria (ch. IX pt. 2.2 and 2.3 of the CNS), for which the tender will receive additional points, are: e) Waters – (MF: W, OM, OW, R2, R10), f) Other non-agricultural areas – (MF: I). Note: For the rewarded classes (classes e and f), the minimum levels of the classification quality indicators (Overall Accuracy; Recall; Precision) have not been specified, but their levels shall be binding on the Contractor only in the event of them being offered at a level at least equal to that for the basic classes, in accordance with the declaration for individual classes submitted by the Contractor in the Tender Form. Rewarded classes shall be taken into account in the Contract provided they meet the minimum classification quality indicators specified for the basic classes. 2. The scope of the contract includes the processing of geospatial data in raster and vector formats and the generation of results in the form of vector layers presenting land cover classes, along with the assignment of a classification confidence level for each object. The generated data must be characterised by geometric correctness and topological consistency. The identification of land cover classes is carried out in accordance with the classification used in the Land Parcel Identification System (LPIS) and covers the full range of required classes and their representation in the form of spatial objects. The functionality of the service includes the visualisation of spatial data, the presentation of identification results, their analysis and editing, as well as the export of result data in standard formats and integration with other spatial data services and sources. Data processing should enable the handling of large volumes using parallel processing mechanisms, while maintaining the required performance. 3. As part of the contract, the Contractor shall provide the data processing environment, software and components necessary to carry out the identification process, including artificial intelligence models and the mechanisms for their operation. 4. As part of the execution of the contract, the possibility of selecting input data sources, importing them and processing them to the extent specified by the user must be ensured, both for entire datasets and their extracted parts, taking into account the use of data supporting the identification process. The use of artificial intelligence models and the provision of metrics for evaluating their quality, in particular Overall Accuracy, Precision and Recall, along with the possibility of analysing and reporting them, is envisaged. 5. The Contracting Authority requires the provision of an adequate level of availability, security and reliability, in particular regarding user authentication and authorisation, permissions management, data encryption and business continuity. 6. The Contractor is obliged to provide technical support, deliver user and technical documentation and conduct training for users. 7. As part of the Contract, the Contractor shall provide the Contracting Authority with up to 50 man-hours of consultations regarding the provided Service, during the period referred to in & 3 para. 1 of the dcp. 8. The Contractor shall deliver to the Contracting Authority the user and technical documentation described in pt. 6.4 of Appendix No. 1 to the dcp and educational materials/instructions necessary for using the Service, by the service launch deadline referred to in & 3 para. 2 of the dcp. 9. The consultation service referred to in pt. 8 shall be provided by the Contractor in Polish, including the interface (GUI, Graphical User Interface) to the Service, as well as the documentation referred to in pt. 8 - must be prepared by the Contractor in Polish. 10. The Contractor is obliged to present the results of the land cover class identification for the set subject to evaluation, along with the result data and error matrices by saving them in a dedicated workspace, in accordance with the procedure described in ch. I.1.1 of the CNS, to confirm compliance with the minimum classification quality indicators specified for the basic classes. 11. The Contracting Authority requires that the execution of the subject of the contract take place under the terms and conditions specified in the draft contract provisions together with appendices (hereinafter: dcp) constituting Appendix No. 9 to the CNS.
sig_d8d1e6875ec91fd9f2e7.title: Land cover class identification service using artificial intelligence (AI) methods for the purpose of updating the Land Parcel Identification System (LPIS)

sig_d98c4426fa22c18658f1.description: Oulun kaupunki community and environmental services invite tenderers to a market dialogue. The subject of the market dialogue is the preparation of the procurement of real-time stop displays powered by batteries (battery and/or hybrid solution) for Oulu Region Transport (OSL). The planned procurement concerns stops: • that currently do not have a real-time display • to which it is not possible to implement a fixed electricity connection The objective of the request for information is to examine the technical solutions available on the market, the cost level and feasibility. The objective of the market dialogue is to obtain information on: • the suitability of battery-operated or hybrid solutions for public transport use • different display technologies (e.g. e-paper, LED, LCD) • power consumption and battery life • charging solutions (e.g. solar panels) • data transmission solutions (e.g. mobile network / IoT) • remote management and system integrations • installation solutions and foundation methods • vandalism resistance • lifecycle costs Special attention will be paid to the functionality of the solutions in northern winter conditions. Additional information This is not a contract notice or a call for competition, but a notice of the initiation of a market dialogue to industry operators and potential tenderers interested in the procurement. This invitation to market dialogue does not request or provide tenders, but informs the market about the upcoming procurement procedure. Comments are requested from industry operators interested in the procurement regarding the design, implementation and practical arrangements of the stop displays to be procured, so that the tendering procedure can be carried out in the most appropriate manner possible. One joint information meeting between the contracting authority and service providers will be held during the market dialogue. The information gathered in the market dialogue will remain strictly confidential and will be used solely for the development and design of the procurement. The market dialogue does not oblige the contracting entity to carry out the procurement as described in this document, and therefore the final contract notice and call for competition may differ from the information presented in this invitation or market dialogue. sig_d9979f0b8c35ebe15197.description: NOTE! This is not a call for tenders, procurement notice or prior information notice, but a notice on the initiation of a market dialogue as part of procurement planning. Espoon kaupunki has initiated the preparation for the procurement of a shared vehicle monitoring tool and is inviting suppliers to a market dialogue. The objective of the procurement of the shared vehicle management tool is to implement monitoring in accordance with the micro-mobility permit (18 section) referred to in the Act on Transport Services (3030/2025) within the area of the City of Espoo. The management tool is used to collect and monitor shared vehicle movement data and to set operating rules and restrictions for them. The tool aims to improve urban safety and facilitate urban planning based on shared vehicle usage and regulatory data. The subject of the procurement is a shared vehicle monitoring tool procured as a service as follows: - System as a software-as-a-service (SaaS) - Commissioning and customisation of the service for Espoo - Application maintenance services - Further development and expert services of the system according to Espoo's needs. The functionalities of the shared vehicle monitoring tool are aimed to cover the following: - Basic functions of the management tool, i.e. collecting and displaying usage data of approximately 6000 shared vehicles to the user. - Real-time and visual user interface for monitoring shared vehicles, i.e. displaying map-based information regarding shared vehicles and traffic operators based on the location data of the shared vehicles to the user. - Setting area- and shared-vehicle-operator-specific rules and restrictions for shared vehicles, as well as providing the user with notifications based on the rules and restrictions. - Analysis functions of the collected data as well as scenario analyses (proposals) on rules and measures to be set based on the collected data. - Reporting and statistical functionalities. - Management of user roles and access rights. The purpose of the market dialogue is to survey the market situation regarding the procurement of the shared vehicle monitoring tool. Espoon kaupunki wants to hear potential suppliers' thoughts on the implementation of the procurement procedure and the preparation of the call for tenders. SCHEDULE FOR THE MARKET DIALOGUE The market dialogue will tentatively be conducted in two phases: 1. Via Teams tentatively during week 51. The contracting authority reserves the right to invite 3-5 suppliers to the first phase of the dialogue based on the responses to the request for information. The objective of this first phase is to familiarise oneself with the products on the market, for example through supplier demos. 2. Tender documents will be sent to those who have registered for the market dialogue for comments approximately during weeks 51-2. The second phase of the market dialogue will be conducted electronically. Written material will be sent to all those who have registered for the market dialogue for review approximately during weeks 51-2. The dialogue of the second phase will cover the content of the preliminary call for tenders, the requirement specification and the contractual terms. The contracting authority reserves the right to additional dialogues as the market survey progresses. The contracting authority's objective is to launch the actual procurement procedure in the spring of 2026 and the implementation project by May 2026 at the latest, so that the new system can be taken into use in the summer of 2026. RESPONDING TO THE REQUEST FOR INFORMATION AND REGISTERING FOR THE MARKET DIALOGUE We kindly ask suppliers interested in participating in the market dialogue to register in writing by 10.12.2025 at 16.00 to the address hankinta@espoo.fi. Clearly title your registration message, e.g. "Market dialogue: Procurement of shared vehicle monitoring tool - registration [Company name]". Please provide the name of your contact person at the same time. The market dialogue and the information provided therein shall not bind any participating party, nor is it a prerequisite for participating in the subsequent actual tender contest. The official call for tenders will only be published after the market dialogues have ended. Responses will be handled confidentially.

sig_da733f462fe04eea8224.description: This is not a prior information notice, contract notice or call for tenders, but a notice on the initiation of a market dialogue as part of procurement planning and an invitation to participate in the market dialogue. Polkka - Pohjois-Karjalan tukipalvelut oy is a publicly owned service company that produces high-quality catering, cleaning and logistics services for its owners. The company's owners are the Wellbeing Services County of North Karelia, the towns of Joensuu, Kitee and Nurmes, and the municipalities of Heinävesi, Ilomantsi, Tohmajärvi and Liperi. Polkka operates throughout the region of North Karelia, and its administration is located in Joensuu. The company employs a total of approximately 800 staff. Through its operations, Polkka supports the daily lives and well-being of the region's residents by providing reliable and efficient support services. Polkka is planning a procurement procedure where the subject of the procurement is financial and personnel management services and the associated system package. The subject of the procurement includes financial and personnel management services as well as the implementation project for the system package, user rights, support and maintenance services, separately ordered supplementary expert services, and options for additional procurements. Polkka's financial and personnel management services are currently outsourced to Meidän IT ja Talous Oy. The services are managed in the systems administered by the service provider, the key components of which are Raindance, MRDP, Rondo and UDP in financial management and Populus, Titania, Timecon and RegWeb in personnel management. The procurement provisionally includes the following functions and high-level functionalities: Financial management - Superuser service - Basic data - Purchase invoices and purchase ledger - Sales invoicing and sales ledger - Accounting and financial statements - Payment traffic - Reporting and statistics - Financial planning and budgeting - Cash management - Treasury management - Internal accounting - Fixed assets - Electronic archiving Personnel management - Superuser service - Personnel and employment lifecycle management, HRM - Payroll, remuneration and rewarding - Rostering - Working time management - Travel management - Work ability and well-being as well as occupational health - Advanced reporting - Personnel performance and skills development, HRD - Recruitment - Electronic signature - Electronic archiving The procurement will be implemented through an open procedure. The preliminary schedule for the procurement is as follows: - Market dialogue rounds 3-5/2026 - Procurement 5-8/2026 - Implementation project 8-12/2026 Operators who have registered for the market dialogue and are interested in the procurement have the opportunity to answer preliminary questions raised by the contracting authority, participate in upcoming market dialogue sessions and comment on preliminary tender documents in technical dialogue. In the next phase of the market dialogue, five separate market dialogue sessions will be held via Teams. The market dialogue sessions will be held at the following times: - on Monday 13.4. between 8-15 - on Tuesday 14.4. between 12-16 - on Friday 17.4. between 10-16 If more than five operators interested in the procurement register for the market dialogue, the operators will be selected for the market dialogue sessions based on their answers to the preliminary questions. Operators participating in the market dialogue are requested to register, provide answers to the preliminary questions and submit the requested additional information by 7.4.2026 at 12 to the address: tuomas.vepsa@joensuu.fi. Registrations must be given the following subject line: "Ilmoittautuminen markkinavuoropuheluun: Tahe-hankinta". Registrations must include the following information: - Name of the participating company - Name, telephone number and email address of the contact person - Answers to preliminary questions - Names of the offered system or systems - Solution descriptions of the offered system or systems The sessions will be held via Microsoft Teams. We will send a separate invitation to the Teams meeting to everyone selected for the session. The market survey notice does not oblige the contracting authority to carry out an actual tendering procedure. The information presented in the market survey notice is preliminary, non-binding and indicative prior information. Answering or failing to answer the invitation to the market dialogue does not prevent participation in a possible tendering procedure. Information provided in the market dialogue does not bind the parties. No compensation is paid for participation in the market dialogue. Information provided by operators participating in the market dialogue will be treated confidentially, and the names or other information of the operators participating in the market dialogue will not be published.

sig_dab62d47fafb0b0c849e.description: DSB wishes to gain a better understanding of SAP RISE, and therefore an invitation to a market dialogue concerning this is extended. Background: DSB currently uses an SAP S/4HANA solution, which supports a large number of administrative business processes in the company. S/4HANA runs on-premises via an infrastructure and operations agreement with TCS. This agreement expires in the summer of 2028, which is why DSB must carry out an EU tender presumably in 2027. Against this background, DSB is considering whether the tender should comprise either: - Infrastructure and operation services regarding SAP S/4HANA based on on-premises or, - migration of DSB’s SAP S/4HANA solution to a SaaS solution in a private cloud – which is currently marketed under the name SAP RISE. Therefore, DSB wishes via market dialogue to gain insight into what suppliers in the market offer related to SAP RISE. DSB expects the individual supplier to provide a total overview of deliverables and commercial terms. DSB wishes, among other things, answers to: 1) Description of the current market. 2) Description of the supplier's footprint in the market. Generally and regarding SAP RISE. 3) Contract setup including interfaces to SAP SE. 4) Listing of services linked to the service: 4.1) Which services are delivered as standard? 4.2) Which services can be purchased additionally? 4.3) How are these services designed with regard to SLAs? 5) Description of cooperation model. 6) How and according to which structure does settlement of ongoing operations take place? 7) Description of model for transition and settlement of this. Preferably with TCO assessments. 8) Description of hardware, data centres, and geography used. 9) Description of IT security model and IT security management. DSB expects to conduct interviews with a selection of suppliers in December 2025 and January 2026. The purpose of the interviews is to gather information on which solutions and services are offered in the market. DSB plans to conduct market dialogue meetings with a maximum of six suppliers. If more than the six suppliers apply, DSB will make a representative selection among the expressions of interest received.
sig_dab62d47fafb0b0c849e.title: Invitation to market dialogue regarding SAP RISE

sig_db0c678dc105aa361164.description: The Engineer Research and Development Center (ERDC) is issuing a Commercial Solutions Opening (CSO) pursuant to DFARS Subpart 212.70. Under a CSO, the ERDC may competitively award proposals received in response to a general solicitation, similar to a Broad Agency Announcement (BAA), to acquire innovative commercial products, technologies, or services based on a review of solutions by scientific, technological, or other subject matter expert peers within the ERDC. “Innovative,” for CSO purposes, means any new technology, process, or method, including research and development (R&D), or any new application of an existing technology, process, or method. Under this CSO, all products, technologies, and services shall be treated as commercial items; products, technologies, and services do not have to be “commercially available” to be submitted in response to this solicitation. If the solution meets the requirements of the regulation, the solution is treated as commercial whereby the Contracting Officer will utilize commercial procedures to develop and execute the resultant award. The DoW High Performance Computing Modernization Program (HPCMP) is seeking innovative solutions to establish a new high-performance computing (HPC) system acquisition and support services model that leverages industry best practices to transform how the HPCMP procures, operates, and maintains its newest HPC systems for 2027. The HPC systems being considered are a combination of compute-intensive architectures and artificial intelligence (AI)/machine learning (ML) platforms operating in either unclassified or classified (secret and above-secret) environments. The systems would be geographically distributed at up to three of the five HPCMP DoW Supercomputing Resource Centers (DSRCs). Since the systems will reside on-premises in the DSRCs, the services model must also conform to DoW and local Service policies, especially regarding security (physical, personnel, and cyber). To navigate the current market conditions and meet mission objectives, a new strategy is needed to design, manufacture, deliver, install, operate and maintain one or more HPC systems at one to three different HPC centers. The anticipated systems will be a combination of compute-intensive architectures (mostly CPU-based) and artificial intelligence (AI)/machine learning (ML) platforms (mostly GPU-based) operating in either unclassified or classified (secret and above-secret) environments. Go to https://www.erdcwerx.org/innovative-technology-insertion-of-advanced-hpc-systems/ for all of the CSO details and submission requirements. All solutions must be submitted through the ERDCWERX platform. The ERDC may award a FAR-based contract or an Other Transaction under this announcement. All resultant FAR-based contracts will be firm-fixed price. All items, technologies, and services (including research and development) procured via this CSO are treated as commercial. Applicants from universities and/or non-profit organizations should be aware that commercial clauses will be integrated into the award and should coordinate proposals with associated legal counsel prior to submission.
sig_db0c678dc105aa361164.title: HPCMP Innovative Technology Insertion of Advanced HPC Systems Commercial Solutions Openings (CSO)

sig_db1df9ef6a0b2f7619a1.description: THIS IS A PTAG SOURCES SOUGHT REQUEST FOR INFORMATION (RFI) ONLY. This PTAG 6.1.1 Sources Sought (request for information) Notice (RFI) is strictly for market research ONLY.? It is for informational and planning purposes and shall NOT be construed as a solicitation or as an obligation or commitment by the Government at this time. PTAG The Government contemplates utilizing the Alternative Competition Method in accordance with the Patent and Trademark Office Acquisition Guidelines (PTAG) and the Patent and Trademark Office Efficiency Act 35 U.S.C. 2(b)(4)(A). This Sources sought notice is intended as preliminary market information gathering which the United States Patent and Trademark Office (USPTO) will use to determine which contractor(s) is/are the most likely to successfully meet the agency’s needs and are thereby eligible to participate in an alternative competition. As a result of this market research, the?solicitation will only be issued to the/ those qualified contractor(s) that is/are deemed most likely to successfully meet the agency’s requirements as stated below. This RFI is being made available under PSC U008 - EDUCATION/TRAINING- TRAINING/CURRICULUM DEVELOPMENT and NAICS: 611430 - Professional and Management Development Training REQUEST FOR INFORMATION – PTA TRAINING CONSULTATION, ELEARNING & DELIVERY BACKGROUND The United States Patent and Trademark Office (USPTO) intends to make a firm-fixed price award to a single firm that can fulfill this requirement which includes three (3) major elements. Training Consultation for Program Revision; Development of eLearning Content; Training Delivery Support Services. USPTO’s Patent Training Academy is the training program responsible for preparing new hires to be patent examiners. It is designed to give new examiners the skills, knowledge, and confidence they need to begin their careers. In FY 2026, USPTO hired 963 new examiners. Currently, the training program is delivered over 10-weeks and is comprised of a 125-course curriculum. The program follows a university-style model that uses a mix of large-lectures and small group lab sessions to give examiners opportunity to apply what they have learned. Through a combination of the use of a practice training application, active learning exercises, lecture and dedicated examination time, the goal of the program is to provide patent examiner new-hires the needed competencies to successfully examine in a Technology Center (TC) with guidance from experienced examiners. OBJECTIVE The objective of this RFI is to seek capable contractors who could provide the USPTO with Training Consultation for Program Revision, Development of eLearning Content, and Training Delivery Support Services. REQUIREMENTS: Training Consultation for Program Revision: The USPTO seeks firms with experience in instructional design consultation services, to include: Expertise in instructional design and adult learning theories and principles. Experience providing solutions to enhance engagement and learning in large training programs with extensive curriculums, specifically more than 40 courses in a single curriculum. Experience with providing innovative solutions including AI to enhance learning and taking complex, detailed curriculum and transforming the curriculum to provide faster acquisition of job skills and application of content. Ability to work with subject matter experts to refine learning objectives and ensure content alignment with learning objectives for highly complex legal and examination procedure topics. Ability to work with subject matter experts to review and revise course activities for highly complex legal and examination procedure topics. Ability to work with subject matter experts to review and revise course pedagogy for highly complex legal and examination procedure topics. Ability to work with subject matter experts to guide the assessment of learning objectives and outcomes. Experience in providing consultation services for legal content. As directed, develop training content and related deliverables. Development of eLearning Content: The USPTO seeks firms with experience in the development and implementation of eLearning content, to include: Expertise in the design of eLearning content, using standard eLearning authoring tools such as Articulate Storyline 360, Adobe Captivate, etc. Expertise in incorporating instructional design and adult learning theories and principles to eLearning content. Experience in building in adaptive gamification into eLearning content. Experience in designing microlearning content. Ability to work with subject matter experts to ensure the design correctly represents legally accurate materials. Experience in incorporating clean visuals, graphics, and ensuring 508-compliance of all materials. Experience in graphic design, visual clarity, and technical writing to ensure clear instructions and flow of all eLearning content. Experience in intuitive, learner-centered design. Experience in clearly defining design processes, to include steps in design processes, timelines, and checkpoints for subject-matter expert review. Ability to convert 25 courses into eLearning modules in 3 months. Courses range from 1 hour to 2.5 hours’ worth of content. Training Delivery Support Services: The USPTO seeks firms with experience in the implementation of Training Delivery Support Services, to include: Experience providing training in person and online, using agency collaboration tools such as MS Teams. Experience in ensuring best practices in engagement and adult learning theory are incorporated into training delivery. Ability to deliver training on all agency examination processes, procedures and tools accessing patent applications, in-house tools for searching US and Foreign Patents that allow examiners to generate correspondence to applicants, case management tools. Ability to deliver professional training that is consistent with USPTO standards to support professional development to USPTO patent examiner employees. The training must be conducted by a variety of means including in person, in a classroom or lecture setting, and/or using agency collaboration tools such as MS Teams. Please state if you have specific experience with intellectual property (IP), patent examination, and patent prosecution processes. Experience in ensuring continuity in training to avoid re-scheduling of training classes. The ability to ensure training coverage for a schedule such as the one listed below: Phase 1 Week 1 8:30 a.m. – 5:00 p.m. ET (8-hour days) Week 2 8:30 a.m. – 5:00 p.m. ET (8-hour days) Week 3 7:30 a.m. – 5:00 p.m. ET (9-hour days) Friday Off Week 4 7:30 a.m. – 5:00 p.m. ET (9-hour days) FRIDAY 7:30 a.m. – 4:30 p.m. ET (8-hour days) Week 5 7:30 a.m. – 5:00 p.m. ET (9-hour days) Friday Off Week 6 7:30 a.m. – 5:00 p.m. ET (9-hour days) FRIDAY 7:30 a.m. – 4:30 p.m. ET (8-hour days Week 7 7:30 a.m. – 5:00 p.m. ET (9-hour days) Friday Off Week 8 7:30 a.m. – 5:00 p.m. ET (9-hour days) FRIDAY 7:30 a.m. – 4:30 p.m. ET (8-hour days Week 9 7:30 a.m. – 5:00 p.m. ET (9-hour days) Friday Off Week 10 7:30 a.m. – 5:00 p.m. ET (9-hour days) FRIDAY 7:30 a.m. – 4:30 p.m. ET (8-hour days PROGRAM TIMELINE Contractors would be expected to begin delivering consultation services in October 2026, with an expectation of revised training program initiatives to begin implementation in January 2027. REQUESTED INFORMATION As part of the RFI response, vendors are asked to discuss their ability and provide their solutions and business offerings for this requirement, and to specifically address the questions listed below. General responses with generic capability statements that do not address the specific content of this RFI may not be considered. Training Consultation for Program Revision Describe the largest training program for which your company has been a training consultant. Please include the number of employees impacted and the number of courses impacted. If for a government contract, please provide the contract number and the Contracting Officer. Describe the process you follow in identifying and providing revisions on training content. Provide examples of innovative solutions you have suggested for curriculum revisions. Describe your experience with providing instructional design consultation services for technical, legal, regulatory or IP audiences. If you do not have prior experience providing instructional design consultation services for technical, legal, regulatory, or IP audiences, what risks or challenges would you foresee in delivering this scope of work and how would you propose to mitigate them? Given the anticipated scope of this project, revising approximately 125 courses for implementation by January 2027 (approximately 3 months), please describe your firm’s capacity to support this effort, including staffing, project management approach, relevant experience, and any assumptions or constraints that may affect schedule feasibility. Development of eLearning Content Provide at least 2 specific examples of content that you have redesigned from an in-person delivery model to a computer-based training (CBT) for technical, legal, regulatory, or IP audiences. If for a government contract, please provide the contract number and the Contracting Officer. Provide at least 2 specific examples of eLearning modules in which you have incorporated gamification elements. Describe the content of the module, the specific gamification elements incorporated, and your methods of assessing success. If for a government contract, please provide the contract number and the Contracting Officer. How do you ensure gamified content meets accessibility requirements? Our patent examiner training content is highly technical and complex. Please describe your approach to designing and developing accessible learning for this type of subject matter, including how you simplify complex information, engage learners, and ensure accuracy and usability. Given the anticipated scope of this project, converting a minimum of 25 in-person courses into eLearning modules by January 2027 (approximately 3 months), please describe your firm’s capacity to support this effort, including staffing, project management approach, relevant experience, and any assumptions or constraints that may affect schedule feasibility. Training Delivery Support Services Describe your experience delivering intellectual property (IP), patent examination, patent prosecution, or legal training. If you do not have prior experience delivering intellectual property (IP), patent examination, patent prosecution, or legal training, what risks or challenges would you foresee in delivering this scope of work and how would you propose to mitigate them? Describe your experience delivering training on highly technical and complex topics. How did you prepare your trainers to learn and deliver the content? How would you advise your trainers to respond to questions on highly technical and complex topics for which they may not be fully knowledgeable about the topic? Describe how you ensure that your trainers are providing highly engaging training that incorporates practices in adult learning theory. How do you recruit and prepare trainers for this role? HOW TO RESPOND TO THIS SOURCES SOUGHT NOTICE Questions and responses are to be submitted via email to Roy.Pitman@uspto.gov and Christopher.Ward@uspto.gov. In your email, please include in the subject: "ACQ-26-9999 USPTO PE TRAINING RFI" NO PHONE CALLS PLEASE The response to this RFI should provide USPTO management with an understanding of the contractor’s experience and the range of services provided. This will allow USPTO to conduct thorough market research, identify suitable providers, and make informed decisions. DEADLINES: Questions regarding this RFI are to be submitted via email no later than Monday, September 21, 2026, at 1:00 PM ET Responses are due no later than Monday, September 28, 2026, at 1:00 PM ET Late responses may be considered at the government’s discretion. Responses should include: A capability statement Which includes a detailed response to the “REQUESTED INFORMATION” above. The name of your firm Your SAM.gov UEI number (if available) Whether or not your firm includes NAICS: 611430 - Professional and Management Development Training in your SAM.gov registration. If not, please state in your response that it will be added by the time a solicitation is released. The complete address, email and phone number of the primary contact Your firm’s GSA schedule contract number(s) (if applicable) Note: you must be registered in the SAM.gov database prior to any award of a contract or agreement. Disclaimer: This PTAG Sources Sought Request For Information (RFI) notice is issued solely for Market Research information and planning purposes only and does not constitute a solicitation. All information received in response to this RFI that is marked as proprietary will be handled in accordance with procurement?integrity requirements. Responses to this notice are not offers and cannot be accepted by the Government to form a binding contract. Responders are solely responsible for all expenses associated with responding to this RFI.

sig_db4c659e2692f0df4bde.description: The overarching goal of this notice of funding opportunity (NOFO) and its companion opportunities is to establish the Precision Medicine with AI: Integrating Imaging with Multimodal Data (PRIMED-AI) Program to support development of innovative, reliable, cost-effective, and sustainable multimodal AI-based clinical decision support (CDS) tools. PRIMED-AI CDS tools are based on the integration of clinical imaging with other types of multimodal health data to enhance care for patients with a wide range of health conditions. The PRIMED-AI Program seeks to catalyze the adoption of AI-based CDS tools into clinical workflows to enable novel personalized medicine strategies that address significant health challenges. The purpose of this NOFO is to solicit applications for the creation of a Validation Center to serve as a dedicated hub for the comprehensive evaluation and characterization of AI-enabled, image-based, multimodal CDS tools developed by the PRIMED-AI Consortium, to ensure these tools are reliable, reproducible, and generalizable. The Validation Center will focus on verification, validation, interoperability, and uncertainty quantification to comprehensively characterize performance of the CDS tools developed by the program. The core functions of the Validation Center will involve the systematic validation of PRIMED-AI Consortium deliverables, including those emerging from award recipients under the Playbook, Data-to-Model Academic-Industrial Partnerships, and Model-to-Clinic NOFOs.
sig_db4c659e2692f0df4bde.title: Validation Center for Precision Medicine with AI: Integrating Imaging with Multimodal Data (PRIMED-AI) (U54 Clinical Trials Not Allowed)

sig_db5951a98f9d30d176d3.description: Welcome to submit tenders for Migrationsverket. Migrationsverket hereby invites suppliers to submit tenders in this procurement of a contact centre. The procurement relates to a new contact centre platform (hereinafter referred to as the System). The System shall handle the answering of telephone calls and e-mail messages from the general public and manage the routing and follow-up of incoming cases (emails and incoming calls). The System shall provide functionality for Callback and a module for scheduling. Queue and individual statistics shall also be handled in the System. After the implementation of the System is completed, approximately 200 concurrent agents and 20 administrators are estimated to work in the System. Migrationsverket receives approximately 1 400 000 incoming calls and 400 000 emails per year in the current contact centre system. The System needs to be dimensioned to cope with the demand, which may vary over time. The System shall be hosted as a private cloud service. The core functions of the System – that is, the management of calls, e-mails and the scheduling module – shall be hosted in a server hall owned or exclusively rented by the supplier (or its subcontractor) and this shall have its physical location within the EU/EEA. The supplier shall have full technical and administrative control over the hardware, network and operating platform in the server hall. Migrationsverket will provide a separate service for encrypting free text in incoming e-mail messages before they reach the System. This encryption service shall be hosted locally by Migrationsverket. The technical design of the service is not yet fully defined, but will be developed in dialogue with the supplier during the implementation project. The System shall be able to handle e-mail flows where free text content is encrypted upon receipt and decrypted close to the client in the agent's web browser through a component provided by Migrationsverket. The supplier is not responsible for the development or operation of this encryption service, but shall ensure that the System is technically compatible with its mode of operation and supports secure handling of encrypted e-mail messages in accordance with the specification of requirements. Integrations with the Windows environment and Migrationsverket's telephony operator shall be included. In the procurement, the tenderer shall tender: A private cloud service that is complete and fulfils the mandatory requirements set out in the procurement and the evaluation requirements accepted by the supplier.An implementation project that includes planning, integrations, configuration of system settings, fine-tuning and testing of the System to a fully operational condition.The System shall be set up in a test and training environment, as well as a production environment.Integrations with Migrationsverket's system, which appear in the Specification of Requirements.Necessary documentation for the implementation of integration(s).Documentation.Training.Option regarding, inter alia, a screen sharing function (co-browsing) and chat functionConsultancy services in connection with the System.Services for support, fault clearance and further development of the System
sig_db5951a98f9d30d176d3.title: Kontaktcenter

sig_db984e9fe7f8b57441ff.description: To map various ticketing processes, the State Office for Finance (LfF) requires a new ticketing system, which must be operated in the state-owned data centre of LDI (on-premise or in the rlp-Cloud). The new procedure is intended to replace the previously used SAP SOLUTION MANAGER 7.2 with the SP stack 20 - as of 11/2025 - and the previously used ticketing procedure Zammad. The new procedure is also intended to map tickets from other, non-SAP-based areas. The complete implementation of the new ticketing system (including the necessary connection to downstream systems, acceptance testing and multiplier training) is to take place by 31.07.2027. Productive use of the new ticketing system must therefore be ensured for all connected users (including users from other authorities in the federal state of Rhineland-Palatinate) from 01.08.2027 at the latest. Further details can be found in the attached procurement documents, in particular the specification of services, system environment and contract. Lot LOT-0001: Ticketing system. The subject of the procurement is the creation of the overall system described in the procurement documents, including the establishment of operational readiness by the contractor on the basis of a works contract, as well as system service and the further development of the overall system. The overall system consists of a client-specifically adapted, standard ticketing system software (on-premise or in the rlp-Cloud of LDI / rental) that meets the requirements of modern ticket processing by the client, including associated client-specifically created or adapted integrations into the client's IT system in accordance with the further regulations, in particular in accordance with the functional and technical specifications of the client, cf. specification of services. This includes, inter alia, the integration of the ticketing system software into the SAP landscape operated by the client, inter alia connection to transport management, the mapping of various evaluations and reports, the establishment of knowledge bases and migrations from various source systems. To produce the overall system, the software must, inter alia, be set up and configured, in particular user accounts created and data imported in accordance with the specification of services or system environment, the software connected via interfaces to various tools of the client, the required automation established, high interoperability with the named third-party systems established, tested, test instances set up and operated, and the onboarding process successfully completed, including interface integration with the third-party systems and training courses. Productive use after acceptance of the overall system must be contractually possible for all connected users of the client, cf. specification of services, by 01.08.2027. Further details can be found in the attached procurement documents, in particular the specification of services, system environment and contract.

sig_dba07f55a615cb284e3c.description: Broad Agency Announcement (BAA) Closed Two-Step BAA: SAF/FM Cost Estimating Modeling Data Analytics Research (CEMDAR) The Two-Step Process reduces acquisition resources for both the Government and industry. It may be considered when a large number of proposals are anticipated or to determine if further Government interest is warranted. If further interest is not warranted, industry saves unnecessary bid and proposal costs and the Government saves review time. Broad Agency Announcement Number FA7014-26-S-CS02 Announcement Title SAF/FM Cost Estimating Modeling Data Analytics Research (CEMDAR) Federal Agency Name Secretary of the Air Force Financial Management (SAF/FM) Announcement Type & Acquisition Set-Aside Initial Announcement | 100% Small Business Set-Aside NAICS Code & Size Standard 541745 (Small Business Size Standard: 1,000 employees) Estimated Program Ceiling $24,000,000 (Anticipated Awards: 1 single award) White Paper Submission Deadline October 19, 2026, 1300 hrs Eastern Time 1. Overview Information & Two-Step Solicitation Structure SAF/FM is soliciting white papers on the research effort described herein. White papers must be addressed to the Contracting Points of Contact (POCs). This solicitation is a Total Small Business Set-Aside under NAICS Code 541745. White papers and resultant proposals submitted shall strictly comply with this announcement. There will be no separate formal solicitation issued regarding this requirement. This BAA will be republished at yearly intervals for administrative updates and ease of reference. 1.1 Two-Step Acquisition Sequence Step 1 — White Paper Due Date & Submission: White papers may be electronically submitted upon issuance of this BAA until October 19, 2026, 1300 hrs Eastern Time. Only white papers are accepted at this stage. Submissions must be delivered electronically to AFDW/PK at eric.moss.3@us.af.mil and joseph.spear.1@us.af.mil. Step 2 — Formal Proposal Due Date & Time: Formal technical and cost proposals will be requested solely from offerors whose submitted white papers are evaluated as successfully meeting the operational and research needs of the Air Force. Late Receipt Provisions: White paper and proposal receipts after the specified cutoff date and time shall be governed strictly by the provisions of FAR 52.215-1(c)(3). 1.2 Instrument Types and Contracting Guidance The Air Force reserves the right to award the contractual instrument best suited to the nature of the research proposed. Accordingly, the Government may award any appropriate contract type under the Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR), Other Transaction (OT) for Prototype authority, Grant, Cooperative Agreement, OT for Research, or an applicable technology transfer mechanism. Awards under this BAA are generally anticipated to be cost-reimbursement. Offerors are specifically advised that cost-reimbursement contracts require an accounting system determined adequate by the Government for tracking allocable contract costs. 1.3 Communications & Contracting Points of Contact Dialogue between prospective offerors and Government representatives is strongly encouraged prior to proposal submission. Technical discussions shall not constitute a commitment by the Government to fund or award any proposed effort. Only warranted Contracting Officers possess the legal authority to commit the Government. Inquiries regarding this solicitation should be directed to the Contracting POCs: Primary Contracting Officer: Eric Moss — eric.moss.3@us.af.mil Alternate Contracting Officer: Joseph Spear — joseph.spear.1@us.af.mil 2. Section I — Program Description & Strategic Objectives The Department of the Air Force (DAF) has identified critical operational gaps in the enterprise databases, analytical methods, and predictive tools regularly employed for weapon system cost estimating and analysis. DAF is actively committed to modernizing the efficiency, fidelity, and throughput of its cost estimating capabilities. This requirement invests in strengthening, accelerating, and elevating cost data and analytic capabilities using modern data science and cloud engineering technologies to enable faster, higher-quality, and higher-volume analytic decision support across the DAF cost community. The CEMDAR research initiative executes four fundamental architectural shifts across enterprise cost operations: Platform Modernization: Transitioning from legacy desktop-based analytical tools to secure enterprise cloud platforms (e.g., DAF Data Fabric, VAULT, Envision). Relational Data Integration: Moving from isolated, commodity-specific datasets to integrated, relational architectures linking programmatic, technical, cost, and schedule parameters. Pipeline Automation: Replacing static spreadsheets and recurring manual reporting with dynamic, automated data engineering pipelines. Scalable Predictive Modeling: Advancing from low-volume static cost modeling to highly scalable data collection, curation, machine learning, and empirical analytics. 2.1 Strategic Research Objectives Elevating Data Fidelity: Improving the verifiable quality, authenticity, granularity, and volume of empirical data collected and accessible to DAF cost analysts. Relational Enterprise Databases: Engineering centralized, enterprise-level relational cost, schedule, and technical databases adhering to rigorous data science principles and MIL-STD-881 standards. Analytical Workflow Optimization: Constructing capabilities and streamlined workflows that empower analysts to rapidly synthesize large-scale multi-commodity datasets. Predictive Modeling & Decision Support: Establishing authoritative enterprise datasets and generating dynamic Cost Estimating Relationships (CERs), Schedule Estimating Relationships (SERs), Technical Estimating Relationships (TERs), benchmark metrics, interactive dashboards, and cloud-native cost models. The overarching vision is not only to elevate the timeliness and accuracy of program Life-Cycle Cost Estimates (LCCEs) for budgeting, programming, and acquisition milestone decisions, but also to build an agile capability for rapid high-level force design, alternative architecture trades, and component-level engineering trade-off evaluations. 3. Section II — Technical Description & Core Competencies The Department of the Air Force Cost Analysis Agency (AFCAA) is soliciting white papers (and subsequently formal technical and cost proposals from qualified respondents) addressing innovative synchronization of research related to technical, cost and schedule for DoW/DAF programs across the following five Core Competencies. Submitted white papers must move beyond generic capability statements and clearly articulate the offeror's specific technical approach, proposed system architectures and analytical methodologies. Offerors should include concrete examples of relevant past work, demonstrating proven experience in designing data pipelines, executing predictive cost modeling, and conducting targeted cost specific research within defense or similarly regulated enterprise environments. To ensure holistic technical execution, white papers must also address the following staffing and expertise qualifications: Key Personnel Competencies & Experience: Offerors must explicitly summarize the core technical competencies, relevant project experience, and security clearance/access readiness of proposed Key Personnel—specifically the Contractor Program Manager (PM), the Chief Cost Data Scientist (governing Task 2 Level 1 architectural decisions and CADOM pipelines), and any designated Technical / Data Science Task Leads—substantiating the leadership team's qualification to direct contract activities from Day 1. On-Demand Cost & Commodity Subject Matter Experts (SMEs): Offerors must demonstrate an established, agile capability to deploy specialized Cost and Technical Domain SMEs on an as-required basis. These experts must possess deep commodity and engineering expertise to support targeted cost studies, schedule analyses, and novel data pipeline mapping across diverse defense domains—including Aircraft, Space and Launch Systems, Missiles and Munitions, C4ISR, Cyber and Software Systems, and Operations and Support (O&S) Sustainment. 3.1 Core Competency 1: Enterprise Data Governance, Access, and Research Lifecycle Planning (envisioned PWS Tasks 1 & 2) Task 1 — Data Access Permissions, Proprietary Information Protection, and OCI Governance: Establishes the administrative, legal, and multi-tier security foundation required to ingest proprietary defense data. Offerors must structure and manage Non-Disclosure Agreements (NDAs) across AFCAA, OSD CAPE (for the Cost Assessment Data Enterprise [CADE] repository), Original Equipment Manufacturers (OEMs), and prime/subcontractor tiers. Because weapon system cost repositories contain business-sensitive Proprietary Information (PROPIN), tasks require rigorous OEM engagement protocols, proactive OCI screening, and monitoring to eliminate conflicts resulting from corporate reorganizations or contractor commercial affiliations. Task 2 — Integrated Research Planning, POA&M Execution, and Agile Governance: This area establishes a centralized, contractor-maintained Plan of Action and Milestones (POA&M) serving as the operational roadmap governing all contract activities. The integrated POA&M must establish element-level execution schedules, critical path milestones, risk mitigation triggers, and formal go/no-go evaluation gates integrating all technical efforts: foundational data governance and ingestion, automated Medallion pipeline curation (Task 3), empirical studies and predictive model building (Task 4), acquisition database modernization (Task 5), and surge research directives. To ensure seamless technical integration without compromising Government oversight, offerors must establish a disciplined governance framework that strictly delineates contractor operational management from inherently governmental authority: Contractor Operational Governance: Led by the Chief Cost Data Scientist and Contractor PM, the contractor manages internal agile execution, sprint velocity, data quality gates, and Level 1 Architectural Decisions (internal pipeline scripting, routine algorithms, and code refactoring). The contractor must maintain an Integration and Dependency Matrix linking Task 4 analytical use cases directly to underlying Task 3 data pipelines. Government Technical Oversight: The Government retains all approval and baseline acceptance authority. The AFCAA Technical Lead / COR approves Level 2 Decisions (changes to enterprise data schemas, cloud infrastructure, or CADOM standards), while Level 3 Decisions (cross-agency data sharing and multi-service standards) require stakeholder consensus (AFCAA, OSD CAPE, and Service Cost Centers). 3.2 Core Competency 2: Automated Data Pipeline Engineering & Enterprise Architecture (envisioned PWS Task 3) Cost Analysis Data Operating Model (CADOM) & Medallion Pipeline Architecture: Focuses on architecting, testing, and operationalizing scalable ETL/ELT pipelines unifying disparate programmatic, technical, cost, and schedule data streams into an enterprise CADOM schema. Utilizing modern technologies (Apache Spark, Databricks, Python, SQL, cloud data warehouses), pipelines implement a multi-stage medallion architecture: Bronze (raw ingestion), Silver (cleansed, schema-validated, normalized records), and Gold (curated, high-performance analytical views). Work mandates automated quality gates, comprehensive error-handling and telemetry logging, and full audit lineage tracing Gold metrics back to source records. Target feeds include Cost and Software Data Reporting (CSDR/FlexFile), Selected Acquisition Reports (SAR/MSAR), Earned Value Management (EVM/IPMDAR), Air Force Total Ownership Cost (AFTOC), and defense budget exhibits. Enterprise Metadata Schema, Data Lineage, and Catalog Services: Maintains and enriches centralized metadata models, embedding automated tagging routines during ingestion to tag program identifiers, commodity domains, and MIL-STD-881 Work Breakdown Structures (WBS). Develops searchable data catalog services (e.g., Unity Catalog, Foundry), implements Data Fidelity Scorecards measuring authenticity and normalization readiness, and enforces granular role-based access control (RBAC) and attribute-based access control (ABAC) across proprietary and classified boundaries. Enterprise Analytical Applications & AI/ML Data Infrastructure: Builds cross-cutting analytic applications and ML pipelines, such as cross-commodity benchmarking engines, automated NLP-driven WBS mapping from historical CSDR submissions, and Silver-layer anomaly detection routines. Manages version-controlled infrastructure-as-code and reproducible deployment scripts inside government-controlled Git repositories. 3.3 Core Competency 3: Data-Driven Analytics, Predictive Modeling, and Application Deployment (envisioned PWS Task 4) This technical area encompasses research, predictive modeling, and application deployment executed through approved subtasks in the POA&M. Depending on operational objectives, subtasks will combine data analysis, dynamic model development, custom tool engineering, and targeted empirical studies: Dynamic Analysis, Predictive Modeling & Empirical Studies: Applies regression, econometrics, machine learning, and Bayesian methods to develop dynamic models, empirical CERs, SERs, TERs, and cost growth benchmarks. Research covers core weapon system commodities—Aircraft (Fixed/Rotary/Unmanned), Space & Launch, Missiles, Cyber/Software, and Operations & Support (O&S) sustainment. Focus areas include, for example, expenditure time-phasing, flight test benchmarks, commercial space cost adjustments, agile software metrics, and AI-generated code productivity/defects. Custom Analytical Applications & CADOM Deployment: Designs, packages, and deploys user-facing tools, calculation workbooks, and interactive dashboards connected directly to CADOM pipelines. Automates repetitive estimating workflows (e.g., inflation/escalation, price normalization, trade-off analysis). In alignment with the Integration and Dependency Matrix, models and containerized applications must comply with CADOM standards and include reproducible code and technical documentation. 3.4 Core Competency 4: Specialized Acquisition Databases and Statutory Cost Reporting Administration (envisioned PWS Task 5) Task 5 (Option CLIN) — AFCAA Contracts Database (KDB) Modernization and Analysis: Modernizes and hosts the enterprise AFCAA Contracts Database within cloud platforms (e.g., VAULT). Fuses procurement data from SAM.gov, FPDS, EDA, and USA Spending with internal metadata models (CSDR, SAR, EVM). Constructs BI pipelines, refines contract growth classification buckets, conducts Engineering Change Order (ECO) analyses to isolate cost drivers, issues quarterly database releases to CADE users, and delivers hybrid user training. 3.5 Core Competency 5: Mission Augmentation and Surge Analytical Capabilities (envisioned PWS Task 6) Task 6 (Option CLIN) — RDT&E Surge Research and Rapid Prototyping Support: Pre-negotiated surge mechanism to rapidly deploy specialized cost estimators, data scientists, machine learning engineers, and technical SMEs for high-priority emergent research, algorithm development, and novel methodology prototyping requiring RDT&E funding. 4. Section III — Contractual, Security, and Administrative Requirements Within Scope Modifications: Due to the inherent uncertainty of research and development efforts, awards resulting from this announcement may be modified during performance to execute within-scope adjustments, including modifications to increase contract ceiling. 4.1 Period of Performance and Deliverable Schedule The anticipated period of performance spans 12 to 60 months for the technical effort, tailored to individual award determinations. Hardware and specialized software items shall be determined per contract award. Deliverable Category Contractual Requirement Governing Standard / Delivery Frequency Period of Performance 12 to 60 months total duration Tailored to contract award and CLIN structure Data Items (CDRLs) Research reports, POA&Ms, schemas Specified in resultant Contract Work Statement Software / Codebase Data pipelines, containerized tools Delivered to government repositories; Open/Gov Rights Quarterly Releases AFCAA KDB and CADOM deployments Quarterly release cycles into VAULT/CADE environments 4.2 Security, OPSEC, and Export Control Compliance Facility & Personnel Clearance: Program classification requirements span up to and including Top Secret (refer to RFP DD Form 254). Offerors must maintain an active Facility Clearance and ensure current Cognizant Security Office records are registered with DCSA (www.dcsa.mil). All proposed Key Personnel must hold and maintain an active SECRET security clearance at contract award, and offerors must demonstrate that they have immediate access to personnel that possess the access capability to utilize TOP SECRET / SCI clearances and facilities as required for classified studies and task directives. All non-key contractor and subcontractor personnel assigned to this contract must possess, at a minimum, a favorably completed and adjudicated Tier 2 (T2) background investigation (or higher) on Day 1 of contract performance to support Moderate-Risk Public Trust (MRPT) and Common Access Card (CAC) / system access requirements. ). TS/SCI work is anticipated to be a small fraction of the overall work in year 1 but could vary each year as requirements evolve. Operations Security (OPSEC): Contractors and subcontractors must implement Industrial Security, Information Security, Personnel Security, and OPSEC measures to protect critical program data from adversary exploitation and export breaches. Export Control & ITAR: Technical information generated or utilized may be subject to ITAR (22 CFR 120-131) and EAR (15 CFR 710-774). Where applicable, a Certified DD Form 2345 (Militarily Critical Technical Data Agreement) must accompany formal proposals. DFARS 252.225-7048 applies to all resulting awards. Contractor Performance Assessment (CPARS): Interim annual evaluations and a final evaluation will be conducted. Contractors are provided 14 calendar days to review and submit rebuttals before final determinations by the authority one level above the Contracting Officer. 4.3 Logistics, Base Support, and Intellectual Property Rights Government-Furnished Property (GFP) / Equipment (GFE): In accordance with Section VI of the PWS, the Government will furnish standard encrypted laptops, required application software licenses, and cloud platform tenant environments (e.g., DAF VAULT / Data Fabric) for authorized contractor personnel performing work under resulting awards. Provisioning will occur within 10–15 business days following security badge issuance. No additional GFP/GFE is anticipated; any extra equipment requested in an offeror's proposal must be pre-approved by the Contracting Officer. Primary contract performance will occur at contractor facilities. However, the Government will provide on-site base access, workspace, and local network connectivity for contractor personnel designated to work on-site or attend recurring program reviews at government locations in the National Capital Region (NCR), and other AFCAA Operating locations as necessary. 4.4 Data Rights and Commercial Software Licensing The Government desires the following data rights determinations: Noncommercial Technical Data: Unlimited Rights. Noncommercial Computer Software (NCS) & Documentation: Unlimited Rights. Commercial Computer Software: Customary Commercial License consistent with Federal procurement statutes. Final data rights will be determined during contract negotiations in accordance with RFO and R-DFARs. Third-party commercial and noncommercial software not reasonably identifiable at proposal submission must be formally approved by the Contracting Officer or Contracting Officer’s Representative (COR) prior to incorporation. Software licenses transferred to the Government must not disclaim all warranties via ‘as is’ provisions, must permit use across Air Force and support contractor facilities, and must allow code embedding/derivative works. Licensors must agree to incorporate standard federal preemption terms nullifying any provisions inconsistent with Federal law. 5. Section IV — Proposal Preparation and Evaluation Review This solicitation executes a Two-Step selection process. White papers and proposals must adhere strictly to the guidelines outlined below. The Government reserves the right to review white papers and fund some, all, or none of the proposals received. ONLY WHITE PAPERS ARE BEING SOLICIATED AT THIS TIME. 5.1 Eligibility Information Eligible Offeror: This is a 100% Small Business Set-aside. Cost Sharing or Matching: Cost Sharing is not required. Government Agencies: If a Government agency is interested in performing work, contact the Contracting Officer identified in the BAA. If those discussions result in a mutual interest to pursue your agency's participation, the effort will be pursued independent of this announcement. Other: Foreign Participation: SAF/FM is authorized to exclude all foreign participation at the prime contractor level for the subject procurement. Foreign participation will be addressed for each white paper that have the potential to best meet the Air Force’s needs based on the white paper evaluation information in Section V. Notice to Foreign-Owned Firms: Such firms are asked to immediately notify the Contracting Officer before deciding to respond to this announcement. Foreign contractors should be aware that restrictions might apply which could preclude their participation in this acquisition. There are no limits on the number of white papers/proposals an offeror may submit. You may be ineligible for award if all requirements of this solicitation are not met on the white paper (and later proposal) due date as identified above. 5.2 Step 1: White Paper Submission Format White papers must be structured into four distinct, concise sections. Total of all sections combined should be no more than 30 pages: Offerors must format white paper submissions in accordance with the standard guidelines below. Requirements are kept intentionally streamlined to minimize proposal preparation burden while ensuring equitable technical evaluation. Page Format & Margins: All pages must be formatted for standard 8.5" x 11" paper with a minimum of one-inch (1.0") margins on all four borders. Page orientation must be portrait. Typography & Line Spacing: Narrative text must be single-spaced using Times New Roman (minimum 12-point), Arial (minimum 10-point), or Calibri (minimum 11-point). Text within tables, figures, charts, and diagrams may be reduced to a minimum of 8-point font, provided all content remains legible at 100% zoom. Electronic File Formats: White papers must be submitted electronically via email as a single, searchable Adobe Portable Document Format (pdf) file. The Cost Rough Order of Magnitude (ROM) may also include an optional, unlocked Microsoft Excel (.xlsx) workbook showing active formulas and calculations. Do not submit .zip compressed archives or password-protected files. Header/Footer Information: Headers and footers may fall within margin boundaries and must include the BAA number (FA7014-26-S-CS02), company name, CAGE code, and sequential page numbering ("Page X of Y"). Page Limitations: Pages shall be numbered starting with the cover page being Page 1, and the last page being no greater than Page 30. The Government may remove and not evaluate any pages that exceed the established limitations. Section A — Administrative & Corporate Metadata: BAA Number, Title of Research Effort, Company Name, Business Size, CAGE code, DUNS/UEI number, and Company Technical & Contracting POCs (with direct telephone numbers and email addresses). Section B — Technical Approach & Capability Summary: Statement of task objectives; detailed technical methodology demonstrating alignment with Core Competencies 1 through 5; concrete examples of past work demonstrating automated pipeline engineering and predictive cost modeling; and a concise staffing summary detailing: The qualifications, core competencies, relevant experience, and clearance status of proposed Key Personnel; and The offeror's established approach for providing on-demand Cost and Commodity Subject Matter Experts (SMEs) across weapon system domains as task assignments require. Section C — Cost & Rough Order of Magnitude (ROM): Comprehensive ROM cost estimate reflecting labor, data infrastructure, and travel necessary to execute the proposed research. Section D — Associate Contractor Agreements (ACAs): Identification of anticipated ACA frameworks required to exchange proprietary technical data, software code, and research assets among multiple defense contractors. 5.3 Step 1: White Paper Review Criteria MANDATORY EVALUATION GATE: Only white papers submitted by respondents possessing an active and verifiable Facility Security Clearance (FCL) at the TOP SECRET level (issued and recorded in the Defense Counterintelligence and Security Agency [DCSA] National Industrial Security System [NISS] at the time of white paper submission will be reviewed by the Government. Submissions lacking verification of an active Top Secret FCL at the time of submission will be rejected without consideration. Teaming Arrangements and Joint Ventures: In any contractor teaming arrangement or Joint Venture (JV), the Prime Contractor must independently hold an active Secret FCL at submission. Cleared entities within the proposed teaming arrangement possessing the requisite FCL must perform at least fifty percent (50%) of the direct labor/technical effort. A cleared subcontractor may not on its own fulfill this requirement on behalf of an uncleared prime contractor. Day-1 Vetting Readiness Attestation: Offerors must certify in Section A of their white paper that: All proposed Key Personnel hold active SECRET security clearances at contract award; All labor planned for Day-1 contract performance possesses, at a minimum, a favorably completed and adjudicated Tier 2 (T2) background investigation (or higher); and The offeror possesses verified access capability to deploy appropriately cleared TOP SECRET / SCI analysts as required for classified projects and studies (e.g., representative efforts identified in PWS Appendix A or subsequent POA&M task directives). Technical Relevance: Is the proposed technical approach rigorously consistent with the research domains and technologies listed in this BAA? Government Interest: Does the proposed technical methodology address urgent analytical gaps and provide high-value decision support to SAF/FM and AFCAA? Fiscal Viability: Is appropriate research and operational funding available to support the proposed scope and period of performance? 5.4 Step 2: Full Proposal Preparation & Evaluation Offerors receiving favorable white paper evaluations will receive an official Request for Proposal (RFP) detailing Step 2 technical and cost submission instructions, review criteria, and formal deliverable requirements. Offerors will be notified regarding recommendation for full proposal submission on or about 30 calendar days following white paper receipt. 5.5 Statutory and Administrative Disclosures Acquisition of Commercial Items: The Government is not utilizing FAR Part 12 policies for this solicitation. Interested firms may submit commercial capability statements within 15 calendar days of notice issuance. Support Contractor Participation: Government employees will conduct all evaluations. Commercial contractor personnel providing administrative support to AFDW/PK are bound by non-disclosure agreements protecting proprietary data. Debriefing & Feedback Sessions: Offerors may request a debriefing session consistent with governing BAA and FAR acquisition procedures. Responsibility Matters (FAR 52.209-9): Applies to awards exceeding $600,000 where affirmative responsibility matters are checked under FAR 52.209-7. Proposal Adequacy Checklist: Pursuant to DFARS 215.408, proposals requiring certified cost or pricing data must include the completed DFARS 252.215-7009 Proposal Adequacy Checklist.

Suppliers may respond to the RFI for the entire scope or for one or more individual modules. A potential future procurement may be conducted as an EU-threshold public procurement. This RFI does not constitute a contract notice or an invitation to tender. Responses are nonbinding and will not be used for supplier selection. Senate will not compensate suppliers for any costs incurred in responding to this RFI or participating in the market consultation. Senate reserves the right to suspend, modify or discontinue any potential procurement inr whole or in part. This market consultation is conducted in accordance with the Finnish Act on Public Procurement and Concession Contracts and Article 40 of Directive 2014/24/EU. Further details, questions and response instructions are provided in the attached RFI document. Responses must be submitted by 11.03.2026 at 16:00 (EET) to antti@zealsourcing.fi. Senate may publish anonymised questions and answers to all parties that have reviewed the RFI and may organise supplier-specific discussions or system demonstrations based on the responses received. Please see attachments 1 and 2.

sig_dbd7aff3bd39d681b462.description: The Norwegian Health Archives (NHA) faces a strategic shift in the management of health data - from a focus on delivery, reception and preservation to an increasing need for secure, efficient and flexible analysis and delivery of health data. The Norwegian Health Archives (NHA) invites tenderers to a supplier conference 4 and 5 March 2026, where the aim is to get information on, and understanding of the technological possibilities and limitations that can be found in the market. The supplier conference is part of an RFI (Request for information) before any formal procurement process. A digital webinar will be held 11 February 2026, with the Norwegian Health Archives presenting its needs and use-case, as well as information on the implementation of the conference. The registration deadline for the webinar is 10 February 2026, 12:00. The registration deadline for the supplier conference is 25 February 2026. Se further information is in the attached document.
