sig_dc271027451ea6189531.description: U.S. Maritime Administration (MARAD) A Study on Vessel Design Challenge RFP No. 693JF726R000016 REQUEST FOR PROPOSALS (RFP): The Maritime Administration’s (MARAD) Maritime Environmental and Technical Assistance (META) program is issuing a request for proposals (RFP) for a Vessel Design Challenge (Challenge). This Challenge intends to fund multiple design teams willing to undertake integrated design work to improve fuel efficiency and reduce vessel underwater radiated noise (URN) to create the next generation of U.S. vessels. Individual awards depend on number of designs proposed for the package. Awards are intended to be for not less than $150k and likely not more than $450k. Project completion timeline is 12-18 months. Total funding available is up to $1.25 million. PROGRAM DESCRIPTION: The META program (46 U.S.C. § 50307) is investigating the interconnections between broader fuel efficiency, reducing URN from vessels, and exploring potential co-benefits. It is the policy of the United States to revitalize and rebuild domestic maritime industries and workforce to promote national security and economic prosperity. Accomplishing this requires making United States-flagged and built vessels commercially competitive in international commerce, rebuilding America’s maritime manufacturing capabilities, and expanding and strengthening the recruitment, training, and retention of the relevant workforce. The most promising opportunities for optimizing fuel efficiency gains and achieving URN reductions are in the early ship design stage, using a systems approach. This requires intentional and integrated ship designs that prioritize fuel efficiency while simultaneously reducing URN. Advanced fluid dynamic modeling enables comparison among hull, engine, and propeller design and arrangement, providing valuable information to the industry about the return on investment (ROI) for various technology and design optimizations at the design phase. Individual technologies claim to provide efficiency and noise reduction benefits, but the additive cost-savings have not been quantified for applying technologies in series and demonstrating increased efficiencies across multiple areas. Recently published studies summarized the state of knowledge and availability of technologies that can be applied to vessels to improve energy efficiency while reducing vessel generated URN. Those reports crosswalk not only the interoperability of technologies and design elements, but the potential reductions, costs, and return on investment. The next phase is to demonstrate, through modeling, the benefits that can be realized through a systematic design approach integrating technologies with input from naval architects, shipyards, and technology suppliers on the efficacy of these approaches. By using this approach, Teams will begin at the drawing table to quantify the benefits of innovative technology integration into the design phase for application on new vessels. The Vessel Design Challenge is intended to facilitate the demonstration of novel vessel designs that meet or exceed international benchmarks for fuel efficiency and URN source levels. This Challenge is intended to fund multiple Design Teams willing to undertake this kind of integrated design work to create the next generation of U.S. vessels. PROPOSAL CONTENT Proposed Vessel Design: Design proposals can include: Existing projects that would be redesigned, Forthcoming projects that are just beginning the design specification phase, and Designs that are theoretical or more experimental which aim to create a new approach or design. There are no restrictions on eligible vessels, however, given the mission of the Maritime Administration, vessels should be commercially useful and generally would not include small watercraft, recreational vessels, or fisheries vessels. Eligible designs include vessels operating in coastal or inland waterways as well as the Great Lakes. Ideal proposals will be for new design approaches or design modifications that couple hull-machinery-propulsion approaches to maximize fuel efficiency, URN reduction, and ROI. Technologies should be centered around performance and demonstrating the feasibility and economic achievability of these combined approaches and should be dictated by capacity needs set by industry requirements (tug capacity, crew capacity, operations support, range, TEU, cargo etc.). Designs should note specifically the technology readiness level and the commercial availability of any technologies used. Design Team: The approach to the Challenge will include a design team. Teams should include description of partnerships, collaborations, and/or processes that will ensure success of the proposal. Further, proposals should identify the Team’s capabilities, related experience, techniques, or unique combinations of these that are integral factors for achieving the Challenge objectives to include experience that supports ability to successfully manage and achieve project goals and objectives of similar type and scope. Development of an ideal team should represent the concept of a design-build approach and include: Naval architect(s) Marine Engineer(s) Shipyard(s) Owner/operator/buyer (can be more than one) Technology provider(s) (including fuel supplier, as needed) May include operator/charter party, BCO, logistics partners, port/city/public entity, private financing partner. Teams may submit one or more vessel designs to the Challenge. Funding amounts will be based on: the number of vessel designs proposed their technology innovation, or a combination thereof One or all proposed designs may be funded depending on proposals. There is no limit to number of teams an organization can participate in, however, an organization may only “lead” one team/proposal. No identical teams with rotating “leads” will be permitted. Preference will be given to proposals with team leads represented by U.S. companies, those with U.S. headquarters, and those operating under the U.S. flag Methods: Proposals must include a detailed description of the design and modeling approaches that will be used to meet the Design Challenge Parameters as noted below, including those for fuel burn estimates and URN source level as well as modeling for return on investment and similar economic estimates and valuations. Timeline: The proposed plan should include the expected timeline (not to exceed 18 months) inclusive of kick off meetings with MARAD, design and technology integration and assessment, interim progress report detailing vessel design and technology application progress, data collection and analysis, and final report deliverables. Budget: All proposals must include a compete, detailed, and justifiable budget with general line items for various design components and stages including fuel, URN, and ROI evaluation and calculations. Budgets should demonstrate market conditions or similar that support these budget estimates. Description of key personnel, qualifications, and expected level of effort should also be included. Proposals may also include any additional considerations, outreach, or analysis recommended to achieve the goals of the project. Design Challenge Parameters Design specifications: The objective is for designs to meet or exceed these specifications for fuel efficiency improvement and noise reduction. Recognizing that this is a demonstration of technical feasibility and economic achievability, if these design specifications are not achievable, alternative efficiency and noise improvements should be documented demonstrating the current limits of technologies. These specifications should be considered aspirational to test the limits of the possible within the bounds of the practical. Energy Efficiency: 30% efficiency improvement over a typical vessel design with conventional hull and machinery arrangements and fuels. Underwater Radiated Noise Source Level: Underwater radiated noise source level is defined using the radiated noise level (RNL). RNL is the source level that has been calculated assuming sound pressure decays geometrically with distance from the source, with no influence of the sea-surface or seabed and is often used to quantify source levels of vessels. Below are the equations for URN limits for self-propelled commercial vessels. The limits are stated in decidecade band RNL (dB re 1 ?Pa2·m2). Frequency range / Hz Transit / dB re 1 μPa2·m2 10-100 169.5+1.5log10(f) 100-1000 191-9.5log10(f) 1000-50000 199-12log10(f) Operational Conditions: Vessels designs should be able to meet or exceed the specifications under what would be considered normal operational parameters for that vessel. The intent is not for these vessels to need to employ special operations or change their normal patterns, routes, or timetables to achieve the reductions. Normal operations should be considered: Typical transit/operating conditions Transit non-working; and working for under-tow/station keeping 85% maximum continuous rating Measurement Standard: ANSI/ISO standards or an appropriate and defensible adaptation of these to suit the needs and conditions of the operational state should be described. Fuel efficiency estimation methods should be described based on industry and/or international reporting requirements (e.g. Class society, IMO) Deliverables The main deliverable is a preliminary vessel design that includes some technical details including the hull form for hydrodynamics and fuel efficiency and the selection of propulsion and power systems (engines, propellers, and other machinery) based on the ship’s operational requirements and sufficient to meet the design specifications of the Challenge. Designs should also be validated for general stability and load analyses for the ship’s safety under various conditions. Design analysis should include the technology combinations, design adjustments, machinery and propulsion arrangements that achieve desired efficiency and URN specifications. Designs should note the technology readiness level and the commercial availability of any technologies used. Each design must include a full breakdown of the anticipated costs compared to a conventional design, including an anticipated ROI timeline and total ROI for the anticipated lifetime of the vessel. This should include a description of the additional costs for each technology element and the design and anticipated construction costs. There is no preferred technology or fuel/engine approach, but final reports should describe in reasonable detail those arrangements and technology combinations used to achieve the specifications. Since this is a concept demonstration for feasibility and economic achievability, challenges and barriers to meeting design specifications should be explicitly described. This should include findings regarding cost differences in achieving partial reductions; for example, the difference in cost between reducing fuel consumption increased rapidly after a certain point or the achievability of URN reduction became exponentially more expensive after a specific dB reduction. It should also include barriers to technology sourcing or availability and the realities of potentially building these vessels in the shipyard, i.e. does the experience exist at U.S. yards to integrate the design technologies and arrangements? These design components, technology and cost evaluations, and lessons learned should be included in a final report that can be made publicly available. Any intellectual property or business sensitive information, to include design plans and/or drawings, results of modeling, or technology or cost specifics will remain internal to the project team and Maritime Administration as not to undermine any competitive advantage. The final deliverable is participation in a debrief with MARAD to share results and lessons learned. There may be opportunities to debrief with other Challenge teams, pending willingness and interest to do so. FEDERAL AWARD INFORMATION: MARAD will provide funding through a cooperative agreement for the execution of this Design Challenge. This announcement is an expression of interest only and does not commit MARAD to make any award. To be considered for selection, the contractor participating in the Challenge must be able to complete it within 18 months from time of award. The final report and other summary materials will be publicly available and posted to the META webpage. Proposals in response to this RFP are limited to 20 pages and must be received within 120 days of the publication of this notice. Proposals will be screened for use of Artificial Intelligence (AI) tools. Any use of AI tools in generating content for the proposal must be clearly identified and justified. MARAD reserves the right to fund one or none of the proposals received under this RFP. MARAD is not responsible for reimbursing the costs that applicants incur to prepare and submit their proposals in response to this RFP. Technical and cost proposals (or any other material) submitted in response to this RFP will not be returned. It is MARAD’s policy to treat all proposals submitted under this RFP as sensitive competitive information and to disclose their contents only for the purposes of evaluation. All applicants must be registered and current with SAM.gov at the time of award. ELIGIBILITY INFORMATION. 1. Eligible Applicants: Open to all types of domestic applicants other than individuals. 2. MARAD is seeking to provide full funding through cooperative agreement for the proposals that provides sufficient, verifiable, and detailed data on how to reach the objective of this Design Challenge. MARAD will fund 100% of the total cost of the project. Proposals must include a detailed cost breakdown that shows how Federal funds will be used for the project. Please see Section E.2 for information on proposal format requirements. 3. Systems for Award Management (SAM) Requirements. MARAD will not make an award to an applicant until the applicant has complied with all applicable unique entity identifier and SAM requirements. If an applicant has not fully complied with the requirements by the time MARAD is ready to make an award, MARAD may determine that the applicant is not qualified to receive an award and use that determination as a basis for making an award to another applicant. Please see Section E.3 for information on SAM requirements. MARAD will not make an award to any applicant with an exclusion in SAM. APPLICATION AND SUBMISSION INFORMATION Address to Request Application Package. This RFP contains all the information needed to submit a proposal and be considered for award. No specific application form or other materials need to be obtained from MARAD. Content and Form of Application. Proposals are limited to 20 pages and must be received within 120 days of the publication of this notice. Proposals must provide sufficient, verifiable, and detailed information covering all elements of the “Proposal Content” described in section B.1 above. Unique Entity Identifier and System for Award Management (SAM). Each applicant is required to: (a) be registered and current in SAM before submitting its application; (b) provide a valid unique entity identifier in its applicant; and (c) continue to maintain an active SAM registration with current information at all times during which it has an active Federal award or an application or plan under consideration by a Federal awarding agency. MARAD will not make an award to an applicant until the applicant has complied with all applicable unique entity identifier and SAM requirements. If an applicant has not fully complied with the requirements by the time MARAD is ready to make an award, MARAD may determine that the applicant is not qualified to receive an award and use that determination as a basis for making an award to another applicant. Submission Dates and Times. The deadline for proposal submission is 12:00 PM EST on the closing date listed for this RFP on SAMS.gov Please submit proposals in PDF format attached to an email. Send proposals to Christian Onwudiegwu/Contract Specialist at Christian.onwudiegwu@dot.gov and Kelly Mitchell-Carroll at K.mitchell-carroll@dot.gov, Office of Acquisitions. Do not send paper copies, or other media of the proposal via post office or delivery service. Proposals received by MARAD after the deadline will not be considered for award. An email will be deemed “received” by MARAD on the date and time the email was “sent” to the email address in Section E.7, below, as determined by MARAD’s servers. Intergovernmental Review. This funding opportunity is not subject to Executive Order 12372, “Intergovernmental Review of Federal Programs.” l Funding Restrictions. Applicants are advised to review 2 CFR Part 200, Uniform Administrative Requirements, Cost Principles and Audit Requirements for Federal Awards as supplemented by 2 CFR Part 1201 for cost principles used to determine allowable costs of work performed under Federal awards. Other Submission Requirements. Proposals must be submitted by the deadline set forth in Section E.4 above by electronic mail to Christian Onwudiegwu at Christian.onwudiegwu@dot.gov and Kelly Mitchell-Carroll at K.mitchell-carroll@dot.gov. Please include the Funding Opportunity Number and Title in the Subject Line. APPLICATION REVIEW INFORMATION Review and Selection Process. MARAD will set up an internal review team to evaluate all proposals that are submitted under this announcement. All eligible proposals will be evaluated within four weeks after the closing date. If the review team has any questions on an individual proposal, it will notify the applicant for clarification. The proposals will be evaluated against the following criteria: Well-documented and context-appropriate plan to undertake and successfully demonstrate the design integration of technology to achieve the fuel efficiency goal, URN limit, and economic analysis required by the Challenge. Clear application of methods supporting vessel design, technology integration, data collection, assessment, and analysis to include specifications for fuel efficiency and URN modeling consistent with international and class standards and reference to existing guidelines, standards, and notations. Methodologies must include descriptions of major analytical approaches being proposed for the Challenge components to meet the Design Challenge Parameters. Methodology also includes any specific models and data sources intended to be used for each component of the Challenge. The Team’s capabilities, related experience, technical knowledge, techniques, or unique combinations of these that are integral factors for achieving the Challenge objectives to include experience that supports ability to successfully manage and achieve Challenge goals and objectives of similar type and scope. Detailed project timeline with descriptions of key decision points and areas of uncertainty. Budget and justification demonstrating appropriate and defensible cost per component, personnel, timeline, and final deliverables; including consideration of the experience and capability of key personnel involved, the number of hours budgeted for key people, and the role, value, and level of participation of any noted partners. FEDERAL AWARD ADMINISTRATION INFORMATION Federal Award Notices. The successful applicant(s) will be notified by MARAD’s Office of Acquisition via telephone; however, the telephone call is not the actual award or the authorization to begin performance. All awards will be made by a cooperative agreement signed by MARAD’s Agreement/Grants Officer. After an award has been made, a representative from the MARAD’s Office of Innovation will schedule a kick-off meeting for the project. Unsuccessful applicants will be notified via email. Administrative and National Policy Requirements. Applicants are advised to review 2 CFR Part 200, Uniform Administrative Requirements, Costs Principles and Audit Requirements for Federal Awards as supplemented by 2 CFR Part 1201, for applicable administrative and national policy requirements. For a copy of the general terms and conditions of the Federal award made under this RFP, please contact Christian Onwudiegwu at christian.onwudiegwu@dot.gov. Federal awards made under RFP may include additional terms that are specific to the project, including without limitation awardee information, project description, funding details, and appropriate data rights clauses. Reporting. Applicants are advised to review 2 CFR Part 200, Uniform Administrative Requirements, Costs Principles, and Audit Requirements for Federal Awards, as supplemented by 2 CFR Part 1201, for applicable reporting requirements. Federal awards made under this RFP may include additional reporting requirements that are appropriate for the specific project to be funded by MARAD. FEDERAL AWARDING AGENCY CONTACT For any questions relating to the technical or programmatic aspects of this RFP, please contact Alyson Azzara at Alyson.Azzara@dot.gov. For any questions about the administration of this funding opportunity and any awards, please contact Christian Onwudiegwu at Christian.onwudiegwu@dot.gov. cc: Kelly Mitchell-Carroll at K.mitchell-carroll@dot.gov. OTHER INFORMATION Applicants must identify all proprietary information in its submission. MARAD is not obligated to make any Federal award as a result of this RFP.

sig_dc273cee705cd9813c72.description: Kansaneläkelaitos (Kela) is surveying solutions available on the market for property management and maintenance software and a construction project bank. Kela's objective is to ensure that the management, development and maintenance of properties and work environments are implemented efficiently, economically and in a user-oriented manner. Future software must support comprehensive property management, the maintenance and development of system performance, and promote energy efficiency and responsibility. SaaS software must be suitable for versatile real estate portfolio management and offer flexible integration possibilities with other systems. In this way, we ensure that Kela can utilise data and processes seamlessly and meet future requirements. Software: 1. Property management software - Property data and documents - Reporting support - Efficient and responsible property management 2. Construction project bank - Project and construction document management 3. Property maintenance software - Maintenance and equipment management - Energy consumption and ESG monitoring - Comprehensive reporting and BI analytics - Monitoring of operating and maintenance costs The objective of the market dialogue is to: - Survey solutions and new operating models available on the market - Receive feedback on the subject matter and service content of the procurement - Gather insights on contract terms - Obtain information on pricing bases and responsibility criteria We particularly hope for insights on the following themes: - Versatile and customisable reporting capabilities - Project management and maintenance features - Access rights management and information security - Integrations with other systems (e.g. financial management, maintenance) - Usability and mobile usage solutions Procurement model: The software will be procured as a SaaS (Software as a Service) service, whereby the procurement contract includes full system maintenance and usage support in addition to the software licence. Registration for the market dialogue: Kela asks interested suppliers to register and submit a short preliminary presentation of their solution and a description of how the system would meet Kela's objectives. Market dialogue may also be conducted as Teams discussions, and the contracting authority may initiate dialogue before the registration period ends. Registration: Send the official name of the company and the contact person's email address to: it.tarjouskilpailut@kela.fi Subject in message: Work environment software, registration (sections 1–3) Deadline: By 31.12.2025.

sig_dc7d4b0214ccaf561bc6.description: The Landesverband Lippe, a public-law body, intends to modernise the Externsteine information centre and stage the surrounding area in Horn-Bad Meinberg digitally as an integrated "Externsteine Experience World". The Externsteine, which attract around 600.000 visitors per year, are to be further developed into a sustainable, interactive and low-barrier experience venue. The visitor centre, which is currently not accessible and technically obsolete, forms the central starting and experience point. Lot LOT-0001: LVL Externsteine. The subject of the procurement is the modernisation of the Externsteine information centre and the digital staging of the surrounding area into an integrated "Externsteine Experience World". What is being procured is a concept together with its implementation, meaning on the one hand the conceptualisation including all planning services and official approval and authorisation procedures, and on the other hand the complete implementation including any construction services, IT services and further services (such as support and training). The contract is awarded as a staged contract: Upon the award of contract, solely stage 1 (drawing up of the concepts) is commissioned, whereas the implementation services (stage 2) as well as the granting of licences, technical support and training (stage 3) are tendered as options, on the calling-off of which the contracting authority decides within five months after acceptance of stage 1. The concept, the planning of the implementation and the implementation itself are to be designed freely by the contractor, but must meet certain minimum requirements based on the actual situation coupled with the available budget and the statutory provisions. General requirements: - The Externsteine and the entire surrounding area are subject to nature conservation, and all services to be conceptualised must be consistent with the requirements arising therefrom. The contractor must ensure that both the concept already and the complete implementation comply with all nature conservation law requirements. This also includes all necessary measures taken for the implementation of the concept. - The historical documents and data on the Externsteine are provided by the Landesverband Lippe and the Externsteine Conservation Association and are not to be compiled by the contractor, but are to be prepared didactically and scenographically, digitalised and compiled depending on the type of use. - This project is funded in part by a subsidy from the State of NRW and is therefore to be conceptualised and implemented in such a way that all funding law provisions are fully complied with. - A Progressive Web App or a mobile app for iOS and Android is to be conceptualised, programmed and made available for download in the common app stores, which contains natural history, geological and historical information on the Externsteine and depicts the area including paths and sights, and the app must also contain the link to the homepage so that current information can be accessed directly. Further content is to be conceptualised and implemented by the contractor. Further functions that allow visitors to experience the site actively must be present - a WhatsApp scavenger hunt is to be conceptualised as well - Every software must be compatible at least with ChromeOS and Windows 11 or higher, if available at the time of performance - every hardware must be compatible at least with ChromeOS, additional compatibility with Microsoft Windows 11 or higher, if available at the time of performance, is desirable. Information centre requirements: - Insertion of inspection openings everywhere where information technology is installed and/or will be installed - Replacement of obsolete hardware - Utilisation of the existing screen openings in the walls and the central X made of painted wood - No structural changes to the basic structure of the rooms - Preservation of the analogue stations in the display cases - Installation (indoor) including furnishing with software, licences and a moderation dashboard of a social wall; the moderation is taken over by the Landesverband Lippe - At least production and installation of a tactile relief of the Externsteine formation and the Descent from the Cross relief as a 3D print - Revision and modernisation as well as new creation of digital content including didactic aspects - Expansion of the use of the cinema - Digital content must be provided on physical data carriers (USB sticks, locally on a PC) in order to enable simple exchange and to be able to offer an integrated visitor experience even in the event of an internet outage; the file formats must be playable independently of the operating system - Excluded from this are contents whose existence is purely online (SocialWall, App) - Creation of barrier-free access to contents - Reliable and easily analysable visitor counter - Sign stating that the measure is subsidised according to the specification from the approval notice. Further specific requirements can be found in sections V and VI of the specification of services (Appendix B01). The project is financed in part from public subsidy funds. Binding under funding law are a total budget of 620.000 EUR (thereof 372.000 EUR subsidised, distributed across financial years 2026 and 2027) as well as a cost breakdown of 255.000 EUR furnishings/scenography, 25.000 EUR construction costs and 340.000 EUR technology costs. All services are to be rendered by the end of calendar year 2027. The basis of the contract is an EVB-IT cloud contract and an EVB-IT system contract.

sig_dcc46098575b55940870.description: Supply of thermal orthophotos for the area of Region Hannover 1. Background The Region Hannover has set itself the ambitious goal of being climate-neutral by the year 2035. The energy-efficient refurbishment of the building stock is a central component for achieving this goal. In particular, improving the thermal insulation of buildings offers considerable potential for reducing CO2 emissions and increasing energy efficiency. In order to raise awareness among owners of residential and non-residential buildings regarding potential heat losses and refurbishment needs, a comprehensive thermal imaging map is to be created. The aim is to create a low-threshold information basis through a visually prepared presentation of thermal radiation data. The interactive online map should make it possible to classify one's own building stock in a regional context and initiate further steps if necessary. By linking with the advisory services of the climate protection agency Region Hannover (KSA) as well as existing funding programmes, the project is intended to trigger concrete refurbishment measures. 2. Contents and procedure The subject of the contract is the supply of thermographic digital orthophotos (DOP), i.e., distortion-free and georeferenced thermography recordings, for the area of Region Hannover. The contractor's delivery service includes carrying out the flight including preparation as well as the transmission of the processed data.
sig_dcc46098575b55940870.title: Supply of thermal orthophotos for the area of Region Hannover

sig_dddffdfb7fbbaa3d2f49.description: DESCRIPTION OF THE PROCUREMENT AND MARKET DIALOGUE The subject of the planned procurement is the acquisition of expert services for the establishment, development and operation of a centralized AI and Data Factory service (hereinafter the “AI & Data Factory”). The AI and Data Factory will support the Contracting Entity in developing, deploying, maintaining and continuously improving data, artificial intelligence, machine learning and analytics solutions and capabilities throughout their lifecycle. The AI and Data Factory service may include, but is not limited to, the following services: Decision Intelligence and Data Platform services Design, development, testing, deployment and continuous lifecycle management of Decision Intelligence solutions, including business intelligence, data science, machine learning, deep learning, generative AI and agentic AI, as well as related data platform capabilities. The services may include, for example: - design and implementation of data, business intelligence, advanced analytics, machine-learning and AI solutions; - continuous development, maintenance, monitoring and lifecycle management of Decision Intelligence solutions; - continuous validation and quality assurance, including model behaviour, outputs, end-result quality, data quality and data usage; - development, deployment and operation of AI and AI agent governance practices; - development, operation and continuous improvement of data platforms; and - other AI-, data-, analytics- and technology-related expert and consulting services supporting the objectives of the procurement. Data Governance and Management services Data governance and data management services may be provided as part of projects, continuous development activities and ongoing data management operations. The services may include, for example: - external data sourcing, data content development, data validation and data migration; - continuous data quality monitoring and improvement; and - development, implementation and follow-up of master data management processes for agreed data domains. The services are expected to be delivered in close collaboration with the Contracting Entity’s internal experts and other suppliers. The preliminary allocation of responsibilities between the Contracting Entity and the Supplier or Suppliers will be further specified based on the procurement preparation and market dialogue. The Contracting Entity intends to select 3 - 5 or more Suppliers. The final procurement and service delivery model, including the number of Suppliers and the allocation of responsibilities, will be determined during the preparation of the procurement. OBJECTIVES OF THE MARKET DIALOGUE The Contracting Authority seeks market input on the planned scope of the procurement, service model, preliminary service descriptions, procurement structure, competence requirements, commercial models and other elements relevant to the successful establishment and operation of the AI Factory. Suppliers are encouraged not only to comment on the Contracting Authority's preliminary proposals, but also to challenge the proposed approaches and suggest alternative, innovative or more effective solutions and operating models based on their experience, market practices and emerging AI capabilities. The Contracting Authority particularly welcomes ideas that may improve the scope, structure, flexibility, scalability, commercial model or long-term effectiveness of the procurement. The purpose of the market dialogue is to utilize market expertise in developing the procurement and to ensure that the final approach is feasible, proportionate, future-proof and aligned with market capabilities, while enabling innovation and the effective adoption of evolving AI technologies, services and operating models. PRELIMINARY TIMETABLE - Market dialogue: H2/2026 - Publication of the Invitation to Tender: Q1/2026 - Evaluation of tenders: H1/2027 - Procurement decision: H1/2027 - Contract commencement: H1/2027 ADDITIONAL INFORMATION This notice is a Prior Information Notice. It is not a contract notice or a call for tenders. The Prior Information Notice includes an invitation to participate in a market dialogue. All interested suppliers are invited to participate in technical discussions with the Contracting Entity concerning the planned procurement. The purpose of the dialogue is to discuss the procurement at a general level and to obtain market feedback on the proposed scope and definition of the procurement. Suppliers interested in participating in the market dialogue are requested to submit their expression of interest by email to tommi.aarnio@vr.fi no later than 28 September 2026 at 12:00 noon (Finnish time). Participation in the market dialogue does not oblige the Contracting Entity to proceed with the procurement, nor does it oblige suppliers to participate in any subsequent tendering procedure. Interested suppliers will be provided with preliminary procurement materials and/or questions for review and comments. The Contracting Entity may organize written consultation rounds, joint market dialogue sessions and, where considered appropriate, bilateral meetings with selected suppliers. The Contracting Entity reserves the right to amend the scope, content, procurement model, timetable and market dialogue process during the preparation of the procurement. No compensation will be paid to suppliers for participating in the market dialogue or for providing comments.
sig_dddffdfb7fbbaa3d2f49.title: REQUEST FOR INFORMATION: AI & Data Factory - Expert Services for AI and Data Development, Governance and Continuous Operations

sig_dde1696066b8d991bfd1.description: The objective is to manage user identities, roles, and permissions centrally, in an automated and audit-proof manner in the future. The scope of services includes the provision of the IAM software, complete implementation and integration into the existing IT infrastructure, the migration of existing data, comprehensive testing, and ongoing German-language support. The solution must be operated entirely within the ALDB infrastructure. The licences are to be provided for a minimum term of two years, with a maximum of four years. Functionally required are, in particular, joiner, mover, and leaver processes, role and permission management, access requests, approval workflows, identity governance, administration, reporting, audit logging, and interfaces to existing systems such as Active Directory, HR systems, databases, and Kubernetes environments. In addition, a secure backup and recovery concept, a minimum availability of 95 % per month, and regulated training and acceptance processes are provided for. Operational go-live is to take place following a successful test and acceptance phase, at the latest by 01.12.2026. An exit concept must be provided for the end of the contract. The project comprises the following service components: a) Provision of the IAM software solution (on-premise) The contractor must provide the offered Identity & Access Management (IAM) solution as an on-premise solution. This includes all software licences, including all modules and functionalities required to fulfil the functional, technical, and security-related requirements defined in this specification of services. Licencing must enable the management of the intended number of user identities, roles, permissions, target systems, and applications, as well as demand-driven scaling to support future expansions of ALDB's IT landscape. b) Consulting services, implementation, and integration The contractor is responsible for the complete planning, implementation, configuration, parameterisation, integration, commissioning, test support, and professional and technical guidance throughout the entire project duration. The scope of services includes, in particular, the integration of the IAM solution into ALDB's existing IT infrastructure, including the connection of all agreed source and target systems, Active Directory, Microsoft Entra ID, Kubernetes environments, and other business-critical applications. Furthermore, the organisational structure, the role and permission concept, identity lifecycle management, provisioning and de-provisioning processes, approval workflows, access requests, recertification processes, and audit and reporting functions are to be implemented and configured. All implementation and integration work must be carried out in such a way that ALDB's ongoing business operations are not impaired. c) Testing Following the award of the contract and prior to operational go-live, a test environment must be provided that largely corresponds to the subsequent productive environment. Comprehensive functional, technical, integrative, security-related, and professional acceptance tests must be carried out prior to go-live. Operational go-live may only take place after the successful completion of all tests and written approval by ALDB. d) Migration The contractor is responsible for the complete planning, execution, and documentation of the migration in coordination with the contracting authority. As part of the migration, all user identities, roles, permissions, organisational structures, configurations, and all data required for the operation of the IAM solution must be transferred completely, consistently, and without data loss into the new system. The migration must be carried out in such a way that interruptions to productive operations are reduced to a minimum and the integrity of all data is ensured at all times. e) Customer Support The IAM customer service to be provided by the contractor comprises technical support, operation, maintenance, and continuous further development of the implemented Identity & Access Management solution in accordance with ALDB's functional and technical requirements. The service meets KRITIS requirements and is German-language support. The scope of services includes, in particular, incident and problem management, error analysis and troubleshooting, software updates, hotfixes, patches, and security-related updates, as well as support for configuration changes, change requests, extensions, and the integration of additional source and target systems. Furthermore, the contractor supports ALDB in optimising existing identity and access management processes, further developing the role and permission concept, and implementing new functional and regulatory requirements.

sig_dde53e36b1b5ef4db120.description: Gol municipality plans, on behalf of the municipalities in Hallingdal, to carry out a market survey on general documentation management in the region. 1.1.1 Background and purpose of the market survey The six municipalities in Hallingdal have started a preliminary study to look at a more comprehensive and future orientated documentation management, at the same time that we must continually deal with archival documentation in new trade systems. Our ongoing procurement of a new electronic patient journal (EPJ) has clarified the need for a total assessment of how archival documentation is handled across trade systems. The current systems are fragmented, with many archive cores and complex set-ups, and present challenges, among other things, for structure, work flow, quality and resource use. The six municipalities have joint ICT operations and cooperate on digitalisation projects and procurements of new digital systems with the accompanying joint contract management. In order to gain insight that can enable us to make good road choices further, we would like to carry out a market survey with potential suppliers. The main focus is the safeguarding of archival information generated in trade systems in accordance with laws and regulations, and it is especially important for us to see this in the light of changed laws, regulations and standards in the archive area, new technology and possibilities for a more comprehensive approach further.
sig_dde53e36b1b5ef4db120.title: Market Survey/RFI - Archive Core

sig_dde965056278242d7989.description: The KVB intends to replace its existing SAP HCM landscape, which is also used for the group company KSG, by way of a carve-out and to transform it to SAP SuccessFactors as a full cloud solution. The contract covers the preparation, implementation, and operational phases, in particular conception and preparation of the requirements specification, implementation, configuration and customising, data migration, integration and interface adaptation, testing, training, project management, change management support, go-live and hypercare, as well as subsequent support during productive operation. In particular, Employee Central, Employee Central Payroll, Time Tracking, Learning, Onboarding, and WalkMe Premium for SuccessFactors are to be introduced. SAP S/4HANA, SAP Integration Suite, and SAP BW on HANA are to be included in particular. The required SuccessFactors licences are already available and are not the subject of the contract. In addition, an optional quota of up to 1.000 person-days is provided for supplementary services. Full productive operation is scheduled for no later than 01.06.2028. Details regarding the scope of services and binding requirements can be found in the service description and the other tender documents. The following binding minimum requirements or knock-out criteria apply to the tender phase: 1. The personnel deployed for the provision of services must possess sound to long-standing, extensive, and in-depth experience and knowledge regarding SAP HCM and SuccessFactors. The bidder must guarantee this in its tender. 2. The bidder must guarantee that the provision of services complies with the current state of the art and recognised technical rules as well as the principle of sensible, appropriate, and economical use, also with regard to further costs such as, in particular, operating costs. In justified cases of doubt, compliance with these requirements must be proven at the contractor's expense. 3. The project language is German. All documentation, minutes, reports, planning, and training materials must be written entirely in German. Meetings, workshops, and training sessions must be conducted in German. The specialist personnel deployed must have a fluent command of the German language in both speech and writing. If German is not the native language, at least a German language diploma of level C1 according to the Common European Framework of Reference for Languages is required. 4. All of the bidder's employees, including external subcontractors and freelancers, must comply with the provisions of the General Data Protection Regulation. The bidder may only deploy persons for whom a written declaration of consent to comply with the General Data Protection Regulation is available. 5. The offered solution must in particular meet the requirements of the General Data Protection Regulation, the Federal Data Protection Act, the principles for the proper keeping and storage of books, records, and documents in electronic form, and for data access, as well as other statutory retention and documentation obligations. 6. Completed personnel-related processes, data sets, documents, and records may only be deleted or archived after the expiry of the respective applicable statutory or professional retention periods. The corresponding process must be designed in a legally compliant and audit-proof manner and documented by means of procedural documentation. sig_dec3d929cc52ef9a1f14.description: Already in 2008 the Klinikum Altmühlfranken in Weißenburg was extended by a specialist medical centre. Now the hospital is to be comprehensively refurbished and extended in two construction phases – due to the age of the building and deficits in the space available and functionality. Part of this application for construction and equipment planning is the 1. construction phase BA1 and here the two sub-construction phases BA1A and BA1E. BA1 – 1. construction phase. In the first construction phase, the existing functional wing is replaced by a new building (BA1A) and subsequently refurbished or converted for subsequent uses (BA1B). In addition, the existing entrance hall is extended and renewed (BA1E). BA1A - New building: The new building in the south-east of the property is planned as a compact structure with an ideal floor plan organisation and direct connection to the main entrance. All highly installed core functions of the hospital are concentrated and accommodated in the new building: - Basement: CSSD, laboratory, changing rooms, archive, laundry exchange point, services - Ground floor: Central emergency admission / central accident and emergency with new patient transport access and outpatient entrance, radiology, endoscopy, functional diagnostics, obstetrics - 1.upper floor: Operating theatre department with same-day surgery, intensive care medicine, on-call service - 2.upper floor: Services. The floor plan provides for a centrally located public access axis in an east-west orientation, to which the individual functional areas and vertical access with lift core are attached. On the 1.upper floor, an inner courtyard is also formed, which ensures the lighting of the respective departments. Optimum processes of hospital operation are achieved in this custom-built new building, and the primary functional deficits of the existing building are eliminated. Due to the self-sufficient construction of the new functional wing BA1A, ongoing operations in the existing building can be continued without impairment. BA1E - New building / refurbishment of entrance hall: Through the new building and its connection to the existing building, a new entrance situation and thus a new forward-looking urban planning appearance of the hospital is created at the same time. For this purpose, the existing entrance hall at entrance level is extended/straightened, thus creating a clear, unambiguous access. The entrance hall at the central location of the hospital is gutted and general functions are accommodated here: - Ground floor: Service facilities with reception/mailroom, pastoral care and social service area - Upper floors: Access with lounge areas. During this refurbishment, a provisional main entrance can be located from the north at the transition to the new building. BA1B - Refurbishment of existing building, outlook (not part of this BAP): After relocation of the core functions of the hospital into the newly constructed building BA1A, the original functional wing is converted accordingly and the following functions are located here: - Basement: Supply/disposal, storage, house and transport service, maintenance/repair, waste disposal, pharmaceuticals, services - Ground floor: Physical therapy, medical service, on-call service, catering with visitor/staff cafeteria with outdoor area - 1.upper floor: Medical service, administration - 2.upper floor: Prayer room, services. As part of the gutting, as a major structural intervention, an inner courtyard is formed on the 1.upper floor for the purpose of lighting the adjacent functions. The entire refurbishment can be carried out in one go, only 4 / 7 the existing catering in the 1.basement initially remains and is dismantled and converted accordingly after completion of the new catering on the ground floor. BA2 - 2. construction phase, outlook (not part of this BAP): In the second construction phase, nursing care is then to be modernised at Klinikum Altmühlfranken Weißenburg. This results in two possibilities: - Refurbishment and extension of the existing nursing wards - New nursing care buildings next to the newly constructed functional wing BA1A, which allows an ideal connection to new nursing blocks in its positioning and floor plan layout. Data-image-video management system consisting of built-in, display monitors and audio system as well as maintenance services
sig_dec3d929cc52ef9a1f14.title: Extension and refurbishment of Klinikum Altmühlfranken Weißenburg 1. BA (sub-construction section 1a)

sig_ded3cad650ed57c711e0.description: Background Troms County (TFK) manages buildings of 218,000 m2, comprising i.a. schools, sports facilities, dental clinics, workplaces and other county buildings. The cleaning services are carried out by approx. 130 cleaners organised by teams, with a focus on flexible work forms, efficient use of resources and quality in the service delivery. The County municipality needs a more uniform, digital and documentable follow-up of cleaning across buildings, rooms and areas. The current systems do not provide sufficient support for registration and follow-up of work performed, deviations and quality measurements. Therefore there is a need for a system that makes it easy for cleaners to register work and register conditions that affect cleaning, for example rooms that cannot be cleaned, deviations or a lack of periodic cleaning. At the same time, the county needs a better overview and management information. Managers should be able to follow the status per building, area and room, identify areas that have not been cleaned and get a better basis for planning capacity, resource use and absence management. The cleaning quality shall be measured and documented in accordance with NS-INSTA 800. TFK would like systems that provide good support for quality follow-up, reporting and analysis, which contribute to increased user friendliness, better decision making and more efficient operation. The procurement is being made to establish a future orientated digital system that provides a better overview, more uniform practice, better documentation and more efficient management of deviations, quality follow-up and resource planning. Description of the assignment The assignment includes the delivery, establishment, operation and support of a digital cleaning system for Troms County. The system shall provide an overview of cleaning per building, room and area and it can be used by cleaners, substitutes, managers, administrators and operations managers where the work is carried out. The system shall support planning, implementation, documentation and follow-up of the cleaning services. The system shall, among other things: Give easy registration of completed cleaning, status and deviations. Support registration and follow-up of periodic cleaning. Give an overview of rooms and areas that have not been cleaned or where deviations are registered. Support quality measurements and documentation in accordance with NS-INSTA 800. Offer reports and management information that supports follow-up, documentation, analysis and resource planning. Support both short term and long term planning of assignments and resources. Be able to integrate with existing and future MOM systems, as well as facilitate future integrations with other support systems, including possibilities for future use of sensor technology, such as dispensers, waste handling, machines and robots. The delivery shall include the necessary establishment and configuration of the building and room structure, user roles and access management, as well as training, user support and administrative assistance in connection with the introduction and use of the system. TFK would like a user friendly and visually oriented system that facilitates efficient operation, good quality control and future development of the cleaning services. Further requirements for functionality, technical conditions, security, privacy, integrations and service level are stated in the requirement specification.
sig_ded3cad650ed57c711e0.title: Digital system for registering cleaning and deviations.

sig_df18b05b8f00aa4ee828.description: Forest management services will be awarded in the year 2026 (field phase 2027) by concluding a public procurement contract for the Fantanele Forestry Office. The total area of the Fantanele Forestry Office is 8895.85 ha. The services involve the development of the forest management plan, a product of the management activity with technical-organisational content, ecologically grounded, through which the works necessary to be executed in a production unit are established for a period of time, with the aim of bringing and, subsequently, maintaining the structural characteristics of the stands and the forest as a whole to the values corresponding to the optimal structural model defined in accordance with the ecological, social and economic objectives pursued through sustainable management. According to the provisions of Art. 63 para. (11) of Law no. 331/2024 regarding the Forestry Code, with subsequent amendments and additions, it is necessary that the development of forest management plans be done through public procurement procedures. The management of the state-owned public forest fund constitutes a priority obligation of the forest fund administrators. The method of managing the state-owned public forest fund is regulated by forest management plans. Forest management plans and their amendments are approved by order of the head of the Authority. In the case of state-owned public lands, the management plans provide data and information necessary for their registration/updating in the centralised inventory of goods in the state's public domain and registration in the integrated cadastre and land registry system. sig_df4e64e9abf385290883.description: Rijkswaterstaat (RWS) has started replacing current traffic signal controllers (TSCs) with intelligent traffic signal controllers (iTSCs). The reason for this is that the iTSC is the new standard and the iTSC facilitates nationally specific target groups, such as the prioritisation of emergency services (including road inspectors), logistics and cyclists. In recent years, in a first tranche, RWS has replaced or converted 19 TSCs into iTSCs. Experience with these first iTSCs shows that they can be of added value in achieving policy objectives aimed at optimising traffic flow and prioritising specific target groups as described above. The contract concerns the supply, implementation and management of C-ITS (Cooperative Intelligent Transportation Systems) applications for iTSCs (intelligent traffic signal controllers). For further information, see the Descriptive Document. see the Descriptive Document. This is a C-ITS application based on CCOL that is hosted locally, in which policy objectives are translated into the control logic by setting parameters, switches and (time) settings. The C-ITS application from this lot is Ivera-oriented. Rijkswaterstaat can largely manage parameters itself via the TSC management centre (currently MobiMaestro). As a result, fewer traffic engineering services are requested for this type of application. This C-ITS application is most similar to the applications used in conventional TSCs, supplemented by the use cases for the iTSC. A maximum of one supplier will be selected for this lot. For further information, see the Descriptive Document. see the Descriptive Document.; This is a C-ITS application hosted locally or in the cloud, in which policy objectives can be configured in the C-ITS application at intersection or network level. The C-ITS application optimises on the basis of the configured policy objectives. For its operation, (traffic engineering) services are requested in this call for tender. How the configuration and optimisation are carried out is the responsibility of the Contractor. A maximum of one supplier will be selected for this lot. see further the Descriptive Document See descriptive document
sig_df4e64e9abf385290883.title: C-ITS applications Directorate-General for Public Works and Water Management 2026

Core Survey Services Non-Exhaustive The required expertise includes, but is not limited to: • Multi-Beam EchoSounder MBES monitoring surveys of all navigation channels, berth facilities, docks, and anchorage areas; • MBES measurement surveys in association with capital and maintenance dredging works, including pre-, interim, and post-dredge surveys; • Assessment of seabed characteristic information from backscatter returns where MBES equipment is used; • Single-Beam EchoSounder SBES monitoring surveys where required, particularly at Dundalk Port and in shallow areas; • Assistance with archaeological and obstruction identification, including geophysical, magnetometer, side scan sonar SSS, and drop-down video DDV services; • Acquisition of intertidal areas and adjacent structures using LIDAR-based methods; • Establishment of new and existing berth fender lines and quay features; • Calibration and validation of port tide gauges and tide boards; • Establishment and/or validation of temporary benchmarks; • Provision of post-processing, quality control, and data management, including delivery of survey data in agreed formats XYZ, LAS, CARIS, PDF, and other formats as required; • Preparation of survey reports, cross-sections, contour plots, and comparison overlays to DPC’s requirements. • Professional indemnity, marine liability, and other insurances in the amounts required under the Framework Agreement. B. Additional Services In addition to the core survey services set out above, DPC may require Framework Members to provide the following additional services under individual call-off contracts: Additional services may include non-exhaustive: • Sub-bottom profiling surveys; • Wreck investigation and obstruction surveys; • Geotechnical sampling support positioning and data integration; • Assistance with environmental monitoring surveys suspended sediment, turbidity, etc.; • GNSS/RTK control network establishment and verification; BIM and GIS integration and delivery of survey data to DPC’s asset management systems. Candidates should note that this list is non-exhaustive, and the successful tenderer may be required to provide other survey services as requested by DPC during the Framework. Important: DPC seeks only Candidates capable of delivering all core services listed in Section 3.1A, whether in-house or through a consortium/grouping. Applications limited to one or more survey types only may be rejected.
sig_dff43af578804364e431.title: Multi-Party Framework for Port Hydrographic Survey Works

sig_dff94dace6fc887b1772.description: Contract title: "Arrangement and execution of tourist routes in the underground of the Queen Luiza Adit" Basic information: The contract concerns the arrangement and execution of tourist routes in the underground of the Queen Luiza Adit. Within one complex of underground workings, it is planned to open two tourist routes for use. The route themed around the elements will be entirely enhanced and modernised, while the route themed around history will be a new product. As part of the contract, the Contractor is obliged to execute two complete tourist routes, which consist of arrangement elements (scenography, structures, etc.), AV equipment, lighting, multimedia content, and multimedia and Ethernet installations. Descriptions of the subject of the contract are contained in 3 design documents: 1. Concept and design of the new underground exhibition dedicated to the elements, created based on the tourist routes in the Queen Luiza Adit, together with annexes. Note: Annex no. 2 to the concept and design contains an update to the specification of minimum technical parameters – it replaces the content of project pages 33-46. 2. Concept and design of the new underground exhibition themed around history, created based on the tourist routes in the Queen Luiza Adit. Note: Annex no. 2 to the concept and design contains an update to the specification of minimum technical parameters – it replaces the content of project pages 41-46, regarding the specification of minimum parameters. 3. Execution of the installation design within the newly designed tourist routes located in the Queen Luiza Adit in Muzeum Górnictwa Węglowego w Zabrzu The scope of this task does not include: AD.1.1 The following is excluded from the procedure: Station 15 Embankment AD.1.2 The production of content for Stations 17 and 18 is excluded from the procedure. The complete musical work will be handed over for the implementation of the stations after the contract is signed with the Contractor. AD.2.1 From station 5 Belt ride – The audio play is excluded Transport device AD.2.2 The following is excluded from the procedure: Station 23 In the Karlik queue (content) Both Station 15 Embankment and the delivery together with the assembly of the transport device will be covered by separate procedures. Location The subject of the contract will be implemented in the underground workings of the Queen Luiza Adit, i.e. the historical facilities of the Main Key Hereditary Adit and the Queen Luiza Mine in Zabrze. Entrances to the workings from the side of ul. Wolności 410, Mochnackiego 12, K. Miarki 8 (access from the side of the water track). The workings are located at a depth of from 0 to -40 metres. Atmospheric conditions in the workings may vary slightly: 1. Workings of the Queen Luiza Mine at ul. Mochnackiego 12 a. High dustiness b. Temperature fluctuating in the range of 11°C -16°C c. Air humidity in the range up to 77% 2. Workings of the Main Key Hereditary Adit a. Temperature fluctuating in the range of 10°C -18°C b. Air humidity in the range up to 84% Documents attached to the detailed description of the subject of the contract: 1. Concept and design of the new underground exhibition dedicated to the elements, created based on the tourist routes in the Queen Luiza Adit, together with annexes – Annex no. 1 to the Description of the Subject of the Contract 2. Concept and design of the new underground exhibition themed around history, created based on the tourist routes in the Queen Luiza Adit, together with annexes – Annex no. 2 to the Description of the Subject of the Contract 3. Execution of the installation design within the newly designed tourist routes located in the Queen Luiza Adit in Muzeum Górnictwa Węglowego w Zabrzu – Annex no. 3 to the Description of the Subject of the Contract 4. Execution of the installation within the newly designed tourist routes located in the Queen Luiza Adit in Muzeum Górnictwa Węglowego w Zabrzu (electrical industry) – project implemented by a separate procedure - Annex no. 4 to the Description of the Subject of the Contract 5. Teletechnical network existing state - The Ethernet installation existing in the Main Key Hereditary Adit is built on single-mode fibre optic cables and S/FTP computer twisted pair. The main backbone of the cable network was based on fibre optic cables. Connections between the server room and individual IT cabinets (SI) are made with 24J fibre optic cable, while connections between multimedia devices are made with S/FTP OUT DOOR type cable. The current existing state is illustrated by the appropriately attached diagrams: 5.1. Diagram 2-05 - SI cabinets cameras detectors, wi-fi det.1 5.2. Diagram 2-05 - SI cabinets cameras detectors, wi-fi det.2 5.3. Diagram 2-05 - SI cabinets cameras detectors, wi-fi det.3 5.4. Diagram 2-05 - SI cabinets cameras detectors, wi-fi det.4 When implementing the contract, accessibility requirements for persons with disabilities must be taken into account in accordance with the document Accessibility Standards for Cohesion Policy 2021-2027. In terms of construction works, the Contractor is obliged to fulfil the following duties: 1) the duty for non-road mobile machinery (i.e. construction machinery – excavators, loaders, bulldozers, etc.) with a power of over 18 kW212 to meet the requirement of being equipped with a particulate filter. 2) the duty of wet cleaning (by the contractor commissioned for the contract) of streets and the area around the construction site that are polluted as a result of construction, 3) sprinkling of bulk material storage sites during rainless periods, 4) the use of stations for removing soil or mud from the wheels of heavy equipment leaving the construction site, 5) the use of covers when transporting dusty materials. (Resolution no. VI62/8/2023 of the Silesian Voivodeship Assembly of 20 November 2023 regarding the adoption of an update to the "air protection programme for the Silesian Voivodeship" adopted by resolution no. vi/21/12/2020 of the Silesian Voivodeship Assembly of 22 June 2020 Dz.U. 2023, item 8625)

sig_e01826a8e1aa506810aa.description: Background and purpose Arendal is located in the central part of Sørlandet. The municipality has approx. 46,000 inhabitants. Arendal municipality has a decentralised school structure with 16 municipal primary and secondary schools, organised as independent entities with separate rectors and management groups. The schools include both combined 1st - 10th schools and pure primary schools (1st - 7th years), as well as a resource centre with tenders across the stages. The municipality has a total of approx. 5,000 pupils in the primary and lower secondary schools. Arendal municipality is in an ongoing change of the school structure. Two primary schools (1st – 7th years) and the secondary school for one school have been decided to be folded. The changes are planned to be implemented from 01.01.2027. The overall responsibility for the school area is at the school office, which follows up on joint priorities, quality work and regulations, and acts as a link between the political level and the schools. The cooperation between the school office and the schools will take place, among other things, through fixed meeting points and joint development work, at the same time that each school adapts the work to local needs. The adult education is organised as a part of the municipality ́s training and is also a user of relevant digital services. Arendal municipality needs a joint system for the administration, distribution and access management of digital teaching aids in primary and secondary schools. The municipality has used a system for this purpose over time and has developed good experience with procurement, licence management and access management in this area. The procurement will be carried out as a result of the expiry of the existing agreement and shall ensure the continuation and further development of this work. Information on the procurement and process is in the document Konkurransegrunnlag_Digital Platform for schools. Scope The estimated annual scope is challenging to estimate. This is connected with the complexity, changes in the school structure and a market with different actors. We estimate that the annual turnover will be NOK 3.0 million excluding VAT, which over 8 years will be NOK 24 million excluding VAT. The contract will have a valid amount of NOK 30 million excluding VAT during the contract period. The estimated scope is based on experiences with the current supplier, market dialogue and indicative prices in the market. The estimated scope is not binding for the contracting authority. The following is not included in this procurement: - Learning platform (LMS) and educational follow-up. - functionality connected to artificial intelligence (KI) - other school administrative systems. The procurement is for the administration and distribution of digital teaching aids and a learning tool. Handling printed teaching aids is not included. The procurement does not include discipline specific teaching aids or individual applications. Reservations All conditions that the tenderer has for the tender shall be stated in the point conditions in the requirement specification document. Alternative tenders Alternative tenders cannot be submitted. Documents Please see the attached documents. Note that the tenderer shall fill in information in the attached documents.
sig_e01826a8e1aa506810aa.title: Platform for the administration and distribution of digital teaching aids and learning tools.

sig_e022c1f9d9df3a2cba1e.description: Data protection awareness tool: The tenderer shall supply: - Implementation: in any case includes advice, guidance, initial setup and connection with SSO (Single Sign-On). - a platform with a continuous, up-to-date and modular offering (information security, privacy, AI and Wpg), in Dutch, modules of a maximum of 15 minutes; - possibility of differentiation by target groups, appropriate to work and risks; - continuous updating on new threats and legislation and regulations, with recognizable practical cases; - a reporting and monitoring function for managers; - setup, management and support during the term; - an SLA. 1750 accounts (estimated value concerns 8 years)

sig_e0248ccfedbf301fe588.description: Nav manages large amounts in society, and the payment of benefits is decisive for the welfare community functioning. The payment of services is a socially critical task for, among other things, ensuring subsistence and is a crucial part of the value chain for all services that nav provides. A technical modernisation of the systems in payment area has been identified in order to support this part of Nav's social mission. A separate contract shall be signed to cover this need for resources.

sig_e09cb2aa998d64d69f62.description: Ards and North Down Borough Council is currently preparing to initiate a procurement process to appoint an Operating Partner for a Creative Innovation Hub in Holywood, Co.Down. The Holywood Innovation Hub is a project funded through investment from the Belfast Region City Deal (BRCD) and Ards and North Down Borough Council. It will focus on micro and small businesses within the digital, creative and screen industries: providing facilities and a secure environment to meet specific security, connectivity and technical needs. The proposed hub is intended to provide accommodation for the creative technology sector, specifically for start-up and smaller firms seeking to grow within the sector. It would also seek to provide accommodation for larger established 'anchor' tenants and potentially act as a short-term flexible base for FDI projects supported by NI Screen. The proposed hub is also intended to create an ecosystem within the creative technology sector: improving skills and employability across Ards and North Down and the overall Belfast Region City Deal (BRCD) region. A primary reason for market failure in this sector is stated as a lack of suitable accommodation. This project will address this situation, supporting the growth of firms in the digital creative sector beyond the initial 'work from home' phase. The capital funding requirement for the proposal is £8,921,200 from the BRCD, with a further contribution of £1.1m from Ards and North Down Borough Council (ANDBC), further funding is required from the private sector to unlock this funding. ANDBC intends to appoint an operator for the Innovation Hub at an early stage of project development. The operator will assume management responsibilities and associated risks as set out in the final contractual structure. The operator will be appointed prior to the procurement of the Integrated Consultancy Team (ICT) responsible for the design of the Innovation Hub, enabling operational requirements and commercial considerations to be incorporated into the design and helping to maximise the hub's long-term economic performance. Prior to initiating the procurement, the Council is undertaking an Expression of Interest (EoI) and Preliminary Market Engagement (PME) Exercise . This EoI/PME exercise is being conducted pursuant to section 16 of the Procurement Act 2023 for the purposes of: (a) developing the Council's requirements and approach to the procurement; (b) designing conditions of participation and award criteria; (c) preparing the tender notice and associated tender documents; and (d) identifying suppliers capable of performing the proposed contract. The pre-market engagement is intended to facilitate high-level conversations to identify potential interested suppliers and capabilities to inform the Council's procurement approach. A summary of the opportunity is detailed in the brochure and questionnaire documents that can be accessed via the CfT documents area (Resource ID 6717503) on the eTendersNI platform (https://etendersni.gov.uk).
sig_e09cb2aa998d64d69f62.title: ANDBC Preliminary Market Engagement Exercise - Appointment of an Operating Partner for a Creative Innovation Hub in Holywood, Co.Down

sig_e0da32aa2d78b1589f71.description: The Defense Contract Management Agency (DCMA) Procurement Center, located at 3901 Adams Avenue, Fort Lee, Virginia, 23801, intends to award a sole source firm fixed price contract to the ManTech Advanced Systems International, 2251 Corporate Park Dr., Herndon, VA 20171 for Sentris Silver Enhanced Subscription. This requirement is classified under North America Industry Classification System (NAICS), 513210 - Software Publishers, with a size standard of $47 million. The Product Code (PSC) is DA10 – IT and Telecom – Business Application/Application Development Software. This will be a Firm-Fixed Price (FFP) contract with a one-year base period of performance plus four one-year option periods from September 30, 2026 – September 29, 2031. This is a sole source notice published for informational purposes only. The Government intends to solicit and negotiate with only one source under the authority of 10 U.S.C. 3204, as prescribed in FAR 6.103-1, Only One Responsible Source and No Other Supplies or Services will Satisfy Agency Requirements. The purpose of this document is to provide a Justification for an Exception to Fair Opportunity for the Sentris Silver Enhanced Subscription. DCMA requires specialized data security software licenses and its associated maintenance. The required software is a data security solution essential to secure Special Access Program (SAP) data by enforcing mandatory data marking, attribute-based access control (ABAC), and cryptographic protection in compliance with Department of Defense (DoD), Committee on National Security Systems (CNSS), and National Security Agency (NSA) regulations. ManTech, the Original Equipment Manufacturer (OEM) software, is the exclusive provider of the proprietary software required for the SAP product line. No other authorized reseller or dealers offer this product. Please note that this is NOT a request for competitive proposals or quotes. Responsible sources may submit a capability statement, which shall be considered by the agency. Any response to this notice must show clear and convincing evidence that future competition would be advantageous to the Government for the requirement identified above. Information received in response to such notice is normally considered for the purpose of determining whether to conduct a competitive procurement; however, a determination by the Government to not compete this requirement is solely within the discretion of the Government. Any response should be emailed to the contracting officer at carol.a.wilkinson10.civ@mail.mil by September 23, 2026, 1000 ET.
sig_e0da32aa2d78b1589f71.title: Sentris Silver Enhanced Subscription
