sig_e12055583437666b947e.description: As a local authority, we have a duty to protect sensitive citizen and staff data, maintain critical services, and demonstrate compliance with national standards and regulations. Cyber threats continue to increase in scale and sophistication, and our existing controls need to be enhanced to reduce risk, improve detection, and shorten response times. We are therefore seeking to engage with the market to understand current capabilities in delivering Extended Detection and Response (XDR) solutions, focused on endpoint and email protection, supported by 24/7 managed Security Operations Centre (SOC) services. Scope of Requirement Suppliers are invited to share details of their solutions and services that can deliver: • An XDR platform capable of detecting and correlating threats across endpoint devices and email systems (e.g. phishing, malware, ransomware, and advanced persistent threats). • Integration with widely used local government environments (e.g. Microsoft 365, Windows-based estate, iOS, Android). • Real-time monitoring, alerting, and response, with automated containment where feasible. • Access to a 24/7 SOC service, including: o Continuous monitoring and triage of alerts o Threat intelligence integration, ideally aligned to UK government/NCSC guidance o Incident response and clear escalation pathways o Regular reporting, dashboards, and compliance outputs to support audits (e.g. PSN, PCI-DSS, Cyber Essentials Plus, ISO27001) Lot 1: .
sig_e12055583437666b947e.title: 002621 - Preliminary Market Engagement (PME) for Extended Detection and Response (XDR) Solution for Endpoint and Email Protection with 24/7 Security Operations Centre (SOC) Services

sig_e15c8199d259452c3ae9.description: I. The subject of the contract is the supply of next-generation LAN network infrastructure to support artificial intelligence in IMiD scientific research. A detailed description and method of contract execution are contained in the assortment and price table attachment no. 2 to the SWZ and the description of the subject of the contract ("OPZ") attachment no. 3 to the SWZ as well as the draft contract attachment no. 5 to the SWZ. II. The Contracting Authority does not permit the submission of partial tenders. The subject of the contract forms a functionally and technically integrated whole, encompassing server infrastructure, network infrastructure, data storage systems, as well as a backup and data protection system. Individual elements require mutual compatibility, integration and proper cooperation within a single IT environment of the Contracting Authority. Splitting the contract could cause integration problems, a dilution of responsibility for the proper operation of the whole, and the necessity to coordinate the work of several contractors. For this reason, dividing the contract into parts is neither technically nor organisationally justified and could increase risks to the continuity of the Contracting Authority's systems. III. In accordance with Article 13 paragraph 1 and paragraph 2 and Article 14 paragraph 1 and 2 of Regulation (EU) 2016 /679 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 27 April 2016 on the protection of natural persons with regard to the processing of personal data and on the free movement of such data, and repealing Directive 95/46/EC (General Data Protection Regulation) (Official Journal of the EU L of 2016 No. 119, page 1) ("GDPR"), we would like to inform you about the rules for processing personal data in cases where the Contracting Authority processes your personal data in connection with the conduct of a public procurement procedure. 2. The controller of your personal data is the Contracting Authority. 3. The Contracting Authority can be contacted regarding matters related to the protection of personal data: 1) by directing a letter to the address of its registered office or electronically via email correspondence to the address: dyr@imid.med.pl or 2) via the ePUAP platform to the address: /IMiDWarszawa/SkrytkaESP. 4. The Contracting Authority has appointed a Data Protection Officer ("DPO"), whom you can contact in matters concerning the processing of your personal data. Contact with the DPO is possible via electronic mail at the address: iod@imid.med.pl, by telephone at no. (22) 32 77 495 or in writing to the address of the Contracting Authority's registered office. 5. sig_e18d87cd612b7b97f83e.description: IT Resource Qualification System Purpose daa intends to establish a Qualification System for the provision of skilled IT contract resources to support the delivery of projects, programmes and business-as-usual activities across the daa IT function. The Qualification System will be available to suppliers with the capability and capacity to source, recruit and supply suitably qualified IT professionals across a range of technology disciplines. Scope The Qualification System will support the engagement of individual contract resources and specialist teams as required by daa. Requirements may arise across a broad range of IT disciplines, including but not limited to: • Project and Programme Management • Business Analysis • Solution Architecture • Software Development • Data and Analytics • Cyber Security • Cloud Technologies • Infrastructure and Networks • IT Service Management • Quality Assurance and Testing • DevOps and Automation • Digital and Customer Technologies • ERP and Enterprise Applications • Applications Support Analyst • IT Business Analyst/Project Manager • MS SQL DBA • Oracle DBA • Cloud DBA • Redhat OpenShift Developer • Integrations Developer • API Developer • Developer • Testing Support / Analyst • QA Lead/Analyst • Oracle Apex Developer • Oracle E-Business Functional/Technical Analyst • Oracle Fusion - Functional/Technical Analyst (HR, Payroll, Financials) • Oracle Fusion - EPM Functional/Technical Analyst • Oracle Unifier Functional/Technical Analyst • Oracle Primavera/P6 Functional/Technical Analyst • EcoSys Functional/Technical Analyst • Business Central Functional/Technical Analyst • Sharepoint Administrator/Developer • Sharepoint Support Analyst • ServiceNow Functional/Technical Analyst • Maximo Application Suite functional/technical Analyst • PCI Compliance Support • Stripe Payments Support • DevOps Engineer • DevSecOps Engineer • Azure Cloud Engineer • AI Engineer • Enterprise Architect Role requirements will be defined by daa as needs arise during the term of the Qualification System. Mini-Competition Process Suppliers admitted to the Qualification System will be invited to participate in mini-competitions for specific resource requirements. New suppliers may apply for admission throughout the life of the Qualification System, subject to meeting the qualification criteria. sig_e1bcda544514a7ae6fc7.description: Fife Council intends to notify the market of a forthcoming procurement for a software solution to manage public access computers across council libraries and facilities. The solution will deliver end‐to‐end functionality for PC booking/sessions, print/copy/scan management, user authentication, and secure payments, with hosting, support, and maintenance services. Lot 1: . The product that will be procured will need to cover the following. PC Booking The system must support booking of public PCs. PC bookings must be configurable by location to reflect site‐specific arrangements. Self‐Service and Staff‐Assisted Booking Members of the public must be able to make PC bookings independently. Staff must be able to create or manage PC bookings on behalf of members of the public. Ability for patrons to book PCs in advance (online, kiosk, staff-assisted). Walk-up access with immediate log-on if PCs are available. Integration with Printing Services The solution must integrate with the existing printing system. It must provide print release functionality and support payments for printing. Library Management System Integration The solution must link to the Spydus Library Management System using LCF protocol for providing borrower authentication. Authentication must ensure only eligible borrowers can access PCs and services. Browsing History Reporting The system must provide reporting on user browsing session history to meet MAPPA agreement requirements. Borrower Type Management & Internet Restrictions The system must manage borrower types to enforce restrictions on internet browsing sessions. Restrictions must be configurable by borrower type or age ranges. Reporting & Analytics The system must provide a variety of statistical reports, including usage, bookings, printing, and browsing session activity. Reports must support operational monitoring and compliance requirements. Export options (Excel, CSV, BI tools). Security & Compliance GDPR-compliant handling of personal data. Role-based access control for staff and administrators. Audit trails and logging of user activity. Accessibility & Usability Compliance with WCAG 2.1 AA accessibility standards. Simple, intuitive user interface for both patrons and staff. Technical Requirements Ability to manage and update programs, shortcuts (internet etc) and windows updates / patches centrally / remotely. Ability for Users to access USB memory Sticks on Public Access PCs Peripherals - System must work with standard peripherals e.g. scanners / headsets Nice to have - Reimage from local drive partition if local PCs. If cloud managed then this would already be in solution but PCs on site would likely become Cloud Managed and allow remote rebuild.. This PIN is for market information and does not initiate the procurement process. No tender documents are available at this stage.
sig_e1bcda544514a7ae6fc7.title: Public Access PC Booking, Print Management, and Authentication Solution

sig_e2248f4dae842a1f41db.description: Provision, implementation and maintenance of digital grade and report card management software for all public general education (ABS) and vocational (BLS) schools in Mecklenburg-Western Pomerania. The Federal State of Mecklenburg-Western Pomerania intends to provide, implement and maintain digital grade and report card management software for all public general education (ABS) and vocational (BLS) schools in Mecklenburg-Western Pomerania. This covers the following school types: ABS: primary schools, regional schools, gymnasiums, evening gymnasiums, cooperative comprehensive schools, integrated comprehensive schools, special schools; BLS: vocational schools, vocational training schools, higher vocational training schools, technical schools, technical secondary schools, vocational gymnasiums. The use of this software is also offered to all non-state-run (private) schools. Use by the schools is voluntary at the time of publication of the call for competition. The provision is tendered in two alternative optional positions: WP 1 as an on-premises solution and WP 2 as software-as-a-service (SaaS). Both operating models must be tendered by bidders and are included in the tender evaluation. After determining the most economically advantageous tender, the contracting authority shall bindingly specify one of the two operating models upon contract award; exclusively this one shall become part of the contract. The digital grade and report card management software serves for the centralised recording, management, evaluation and documentation of pupil performance as well as the preparation and issuance of report cards. The digital grade and report card management software is operated as a separate module within the Integrated School Management System ISY-MV. The objective of the procurement is the introduction of a standardised, web-based and future-proof solution to support school assessment and report card processes. During the term of the framework agreement, the following maximum take-up quantities arise: - Training courses: 2 person-days or units FG2 training, 50 person-days or units user training, 15 person-days or units support training, 10 person-days face-to-face training - Consulting and support services: 10 person-days annually - Further development requirements and customising: 20 person-days annually - Licences: 622 schools

sig_e24c76052c5125d06fac.description: Society relies on chemical processes to turn raw materials into useful products. The Chemical Process Systems (CPS) program invests in fundamental research on chemical and biochemical processes to make them more efficient, sustainable, and resilient. New CPS technologies for manufacturing, biotechnology, critical minerals, energy, food, and other national priorities will help make the U.S. more competitive and secure. Research supported by the CPS program covers the full breadth of chemical and biochemical process innovation. It spans reaction engineering and molecular thermodynamics; reactor design; catalysis; electrochemical systems; separations; and process design. The program encourages proposals that connect the molecular scale to process and plant scales. The CPS program explores active-site structure and function, reaction mechanisms, in situ and operando characterization, durability, and device-level integration. Microreactors, membrane and catalytic reactors, atmospheric plasmas, and other novel configurations are of interest. The program supports research in catalysis and electrochemical systems to produce, use, and store energy, to reduce waste, to process polymers, and to synthesize fuels and chemicals. This includes process and materials innovation to support the nuclear fuel cycle. The CPS program also targets chemical and biological separations that are efficient and scalable. Research includes the design of membranes, sorbents, and specialized interfaces. Advances can be used in gas separations, the recovery of critical minerals, bioprocessing, and protein and water purification. The program supports research in process design and optimization that uses tools such as artificial intelligence, machine learning, and uncertainty quantification. sig_e2ae3a98021df988e49f.description: DESCRIPTION OF THE PROCUREMENT The subject of the procurement is a digital service for domestic newspapers and magazines, which includes a selection of publications and a user interface for accessing, browsing, searching and reading the publications, as well as related support services. The Subscriber is able to obtain various usage statistics on the use of the service and the publications it contains. Access to the digital service for domestic newspapers and magazines must be available to the entire Government (ministries, the Office of the Chancellor of Justice and the Office of the President of the Republic). Access to the service is enabled via IP authentication or SSO single sign-on, which ensure that only the Subscriber's authorised users can access the service. The Subscriber's personnel have access to the service platform maintained by the Supplier as a SaaS service, which contains the domestic newspapers and magazines selected and procured by the Subscriber. The Subscriber's personnel can browse the collection, perform searches on the titles in the collection and select a publication title to read. The features and functionalities of the service platform are presented in Appendix 1 "Minimum requirements". The link or links to individual publication titles in the service will be published on the Subscriber's intranet as well as on other internal sites where information resources procured for the use of the Government are presented to Government personnel. There must be remote access to the service and the publications subscribed to by the Subscriber. Remote access means that, when working remotely, the Subscriber's personnel use the service on devices provided by the employer within the Government network. The procurement includes the possibility of additional procurement during the contract period for individual new newspaper and magazine titles. One magazine can be read simultaneously by a number of users defined in advance for each publication. The newspaper selection can be read by six users simultaneously. The service is available to the Subscriber's personnel around the clock, every day of the year. The Tenderer must attach to its tender a description of the digital service for domestic newspapers and magazines. Based on the tender competition, the Subscriber will select one supplier with whom it will enter into a contract. IMPLEMENTATION PROJECT The implementation of the service must begin upon the signing of the contract and the implementation must be complete 1 months after the signing of the contract. The content of the implementation project is the establishment and commissioning of the service. During implementation, the compliance of the service with the requirements is verified. During the implementation project, the supplier's task is: - To implement all those features to which the supplier has committed in its tender. - To open access for the Subscriber to the newspaper and magazine selection defined in the Price Form in Appendix 2 of the call for tenders. - To assist the Subscriber if necessary during acceptance testing. Implementation ends when all tasks have been completed and the Subscriber has tested the delivered system and found the system's features to be acceptable. If deficiencies are discovered during testing, the Supplier shall correct the deficiencies and the Subscriber shall test them again. Testing continues until the Subscriber declares the phase acceptable, unless the Subscriber considers the system to be so deficient that implementation cannot continue.

sig_e2f409941452f4e28764.description: The purpose of this above-threshold public supply contract awarded in a negotiated procedure with publication pursuant to Section 60 et seq. of the Public Procurement Act (ZZVZ) is to conclude a contract for the supply and provision of operation, maintenance and development of a comprehensive information system for the itemised test item bank (hereinafter referred to as the „Test Item Bank“). The aim of the solution is to replace the existing fragmented records with a modern, secure and centralized digital platform that will ensure high quality and transparency of testing processes. Main functional units and modules: The supplied software must cover the complete testing lifecycle through the following modules: 1. Test item preparation and review module – the lifecycle begins with the creation of test items, which authors create and send for verification among reviewers and possibly a subject-matter expert. During the preparation of test items, authors will be able to use artificial intelligence. 2. Test item module/bank – after the test item is approved, it is integrated into the pool of approved items, from which items can then be selected for tests, psychometric data can be checked (if the item has already been used in a test), or the option to revise the question can be triggered again. 3. Test compilation module – based on the assignment, the user selects suitable questions for the test from the list, while again being able to use artificial intelligence, which, for example, checks the suitability of the test and possibly warns of redundancy of questions or questions that explain each other. 4. Testing module – the user selects the created test here, which they want to share in the form of examination with selected candidates. After the test is carried out, the evaluation and analysis of the test and individual questions takes place in the module. Information from the analysis of sub-questions is written back to the test item bank for possible re-assessment. Use of artificial intelligence (AI): A key part of the solution is the integration of artificial intelligence elements, which will serve as support for authors in creating questions, predicting difficulty, identifying duplicates or logical inconsistencies in tests, and optimizing the structure of test sets based on historical data. Technical and security requirements: • Interoperability: The system must have an open interface (API) for connection to higher education institutions' systems, medical facilities and e-learning platforms. • Security: The solution must comply with cybersecurity and GDPR standards, include two-factor authentication (MFA), data encryption (at rest and in transit) and detailed audit logging. • Infrastructure: The scope of supply also includes the delivery of corresponding hardware equipment (servers, disk storage) and network elements necessary to ensure high availability and redundancy of the system. The scope of supply also includes the integration of the system into the contracting authority's existing ICT infrastructure, training of individual user roles (administrator, author, reviewer, analyst) and provision of technical support during the project sustainability period.
sig_e2f409941452f4e28764.title: Item bank of test tasks

sig_e441f9e2437814408f88.description: The tender procedure is carried out by the contracting authorities as a joint procurement procedure, cf. section 123, subsection 5. The tender procedure is covered by the Danish Public Procurement Act (Act No. 1564 of 15 December 2015 as amended), which implements the Public Procurement Directive (Directive 2014/24/EU). The tender procedure concerns the procurement of diabetes technology by Region Midtjylland, Region Syddanmark, Region Nordjylland and Region Østdanmark (current Region Sjælland and Region Hovedstaden), divided into two subcontracts concerning respectively (1) AID insulin pump systems and (2) continuous glucose monitoring systems (CGM). The tender also covers the system components, accessories and consumables that are necessary or relevant for putting the offered systems into operation and using them as intended. As an integral part of the delivery, the suppliers must also make the associated digital solutions available, including apps and patient and clinician platforms, and provide training for patients and healthcare professionals as well as technical support for patients. The products covered are set out in Contract Appendix 3, while the requirements for the products and associated services are set out in the Contract and the Requirements Specification, cf. Contract Appendix 2. The contract put out to tender, including subcontracts (1) and (2), are framework agreements in accordance with section 24, no. 30 of the Public Procurement Act. Subcontract 1 and Subcontract 2 are separate framework agreements. In connection with the conclusion of the contract, separate contracts and contract appendices will be drawn up (except for contract appendix 5, which is already included in the tender documents in one copy for each participating region) for each of the other participating regions. This means that each region concludes separate contracts/framework agreements with the winning tenderers. The subcontract concerns the procurement of AID insulin pumps in the form of either insulin pumps for infusion sets or patch pumps. The subcontract also covers the system components, accessories and consumables that are necessary or relevant for putting the offered AID insulin pump system into operation and using it as intended, including, depending on the offered system, for example pods, pump bases, PDM/control units, infusion sets and reservoirs. As an integral part of the delivery, the supplier must make associated digital solutions available, including apps and patient and clinician platforms, and provide training in the use of the offered products as well as technical support for patients. The detailed scope of the subcontract appears from the tender documents, including Contract Appendix 2 and Contract Appendix 3.; The subcontract concerns the procurement of continuous sensor-based glucose monitoring systems (CGM). The subcontract covers sensors, receivers and other system components, accessories and consumables that are necessary or relevant for putting the offered CGM system into operation and using it as intended, including, for example, senders/transmitters. As an integral part of the delivery, the supplier must make associated digital solutions available, including apps and patient and clinician platforms, and provide training in the use of the offered products as well as technical support for patients. The detailed scope of the subcontract appears from the tender documents, including Contract Appendix 2 and Contract Appendix 3. As an integral part of the delivery, the supplier must make associated digital solutions available, including apps and patient and clinician platforms, and provide training in the use of the offered products as well as technical support for patients. The detailed scope of the subcontract appears from the tender documents, including Contract Appendix 2 and Contract Appendix 3.

The aim is to get to know available solutions, technological approaches and operating models to support spontaneous line closures and comparable operational restrictions. The focus is on the introduction of an AI-supported evaluation tool for the analysis of dispatch measures and detours as well as the potential use of a data warehouse or lakehouse for the use of historical and analytical data. In addition, suitable integration approaches, data sources and operating models (cloud, on-premises or hybrid) are to be evaluated. Lot LOT-0001: Market consultation in accordance with § 26 SektVO for the intended procurement of an AI evaluation tool and data warehouse/lakehouse. The aim of the market consultation is to draw up well-founded procurement documents through careful planning and to create a reliable calculation basis. Requirements of the specification sheet are to be refined on the basis of the market consultation results.

sig_e4464159e008dbabdcbb.description: Provision, implementation, operation and maintenance of the complete technical infrastructure for the EUDI Wallet Support Organisation. Covers all systems from the self-service portal and ticket management to telephony, knowledge base and identity management. The subject of this tender is the award of services for the technical infrastructure of the EUDI Wallet Support Organisation (EWSO), known as tooling. The contractor shall implement, configure and commission: the ticket and CRM system, the knowledge base and FAQ portal, the in-app bot (or compatibility with the client's internal app bot solution), the telephony and IVR infrastructure, the connection and compatibility with the B2B portal: EUDI Hub, the IAM system, the central event log system and the redaction system. The contractor shall accompany the closed beta phase (Q4 2026) and the go-live phase (Q1 2027) with hypercare support and, following an orderly knowledge transfer, hand over operational system sovereignty to the client's internal team. The services comprise in particular EU-compliant infrastructure ((ISO 27001), no US CLOUD Act exposure), WCAG 21 compliance of all user front ends, a mandatory external penetration test prior to go-live as well as complete system documentation and training of the internal team.

sig_e4495dc4a5fa0d21753a.description: As part of the re-tendering process for TenneT’s Content Collaboration Platform, Lot 2 encompasses a multi-vendor framework agreement focused on the integration, implementation, configuration, migration, and support of platform functionalities tailored to TenneT’s infrastructure project needs. The present tender focuses primarily on TenneT’s German operations. As beneficiaries under the SaaS Agreement, Dutch TenneT operations may optionally draw from the services that are subject hereof. With the re-tendering of the current Content Collaboration Platform, TenneT is aiming to continue achieving a single source of information for all documents generated in infrastructure projects and managing the supplier collaboration (external collaboration) regarding the exchange and management of documents and additional data. The targeted system is facilitating and capturing the complete project lifecycle in addition to providing auditable documentation and information throughout the organization. The tender procedure is divided into two lots, which will be tendered in sequence in two different tenders: Tender 1 [Lot 1] "CDE - Collaboration-Platform for Document and Data Exchange": includes the platform provisioning, development, deployment (Implementation), initial customization and configuration, platform interfaces as well as maintenance and support of the platform and – as a proof of concept and for purposes of a successful transition – the migration of TenneT metadata as well as existing construction projects from the current to the new platform. This tender has been completed. The awarded solution is provided by ThinkProject. Tender 2 [Lot 2]: "CDE – Multi-Contractor Integration": includes intergration and implementation services associated with the platform and comprises subsequent configuration, customization and consulting services in relation to the Content Collaboration Platform. The Lot 1 Provider must always collaborate pro-actively and in a constructive manner with any Lot 2 Contractor(s), e.g. providing access, support and knowledge transfer regarding the platform and implementing technically necessary changes within Lot 1 where mutually agreed with or commissioned by TenneT. Lot 2 will be tendered subsequent to the award of Lot 1. Performance Scope Lot 2 The Lot 2 providers selected during the selection phase must be qualified for the following service areas within the framework of the mini competitions and be able to obtain contracts in these areas: Business Support for CDE Initiatives and Projects The contractor shall provide advisory and operational support for departments and project teams in the context of CDE utilization, in particular: Advising on methodological and operational use of CDE platforms in project environments Supporting data migration processes (e.g., from legacy systems) Assisting with platform configuration and workflow optimization Developing and maintaining structured knowledge management tools (e.g., CDE user guides, training materials, FAQs) Facilitating workshops to gather and refine user requirements Design, Development, and Implementation of Non-Standard Changes This service domain includes support in extending the functional scope of the CDE platform beyond its standard features: Designing and specifying customized solutions (e.g., plug-ins, tailored workflows) Developing enhancements, interfaces, and automation features Supporting innovation initiatives, e.g., through prototyping of new digital tools Providing comprehensive technical and user documentation Performing quality assurance and testing of developed components Integration support for non-standard changes The contractor will provide technical and conceptual support for integrating enhancements into the existing CDE ecosystem: Designing and executing system integration concepts (e.g., CDE ↔ third-party systems) Developing and maintaining interfaces (e.g., REST, SOAP, file-based) Conducting system, integration, and regression testing Monitoring and issue resolution during and after go-live Preparing technical operations documentation (e.g., monitoring and handover guides) Project execution The contractor shall support the delivery of CDE-related (sub-)projects, including: Providing project management services (e.g., project office, timeline planning, reporting, risk management) Conducting requirement analysis and scope definition with business stakeholders Coordinating internal and external implementation partners Reporting to project leadership or steering committees Supporting change and rollout management measures For more details please see "L2 - C11 - Summary of Requirements" and "L2 – N01 – Annex 01 – Service Description" (will be sent after signing the NDA). Both tenders/lots are evaluated and awarded independently of each other. This publication refers only to Tender 2 [Lot 2]. sig_e4c9e6e9a8c3276ad3b3.description: Dear Sir or Madam, Heidelberg University Hospital (UKHD) currently uses a self-developed ABAP-based add-on called BISI for electronic demand notification. As part of the SAP S/4 migration, this demand notification system is to be replaced by a long-term future-proof and modern solution. From a prospective perspective, the demand notification system is intended to support the entire Heidelberg-Mannheim hospital network with all subsidiaries and holdings. UKHD manages 2589 beds. With 87.441 inpatient patients and 1.275.241 outpatient treatment cases, it is the largest employer in the region. 14544 employees from 133 nations are employed at UKHD. The Faculty of Medicine trains 4.750 students. The Corporate Purchasing and Logistics Management division and the pharmacy supply the entire UKHD corporate group including subsidiaries and holdings and also supply external hospitals in the surrounding area. The newly procured tool for demand requests must be intuitive and easy for end users to operate and be based on the look and feel of modern, future-proof, efficient request platforms. This requires that end customers can record and request any demands during demand requests regardless of the product group, article group, purchasing organisation or financing type in the sense of a mixed shopping basket. The tool takes over the routing of requirements into the correct demand channels and controls the follow-on documents. The tool to be procured must be able to be connected to both SAP ECC and S/4 HANA. In this market exploration, UKHD therefore wishes to examine what options the relevant market currently offers for this contract subject, what empirical values can be contributed and what price range these services fall within.
sig_e4c9e6e9a8c3276ad3b3.title: Market exploration regarding a demand notification tool for Heidelberg University Hospital

sig_e5404ce98ddacbdc0d6c.description: The GB IT of the UKJ commits itself at the current point in time to the manufacturer Hewlett-Packard Enterprise (HPE) as the outfitter for extensions and substitutions of the existing IT infrastructure and therefore intends to conclude a framework agreement for the procurement of HPE system components. This is due to the fact that a comprehensive and almost complete data centre infrastructure of the manufacturer HPE exists, which must be permanently expanded and partially or substantially renewed within the scope of lifecycle management. A change of manufacturer would be associated with very high effort and high switching costs. Lot LOT-0001: FA HPE server, SAN and storage infrastructure. The tendering of the framework agreement pursues the objective of enabling an expansion of the existing IT infrastructure during the contract period, replacing components within the scope of lifecycle management that are technically or economically obsolete, and furthermore the delivery of original HPE products. The services comprise the delivery, consultation and maintenance of HPE products in the fields of IT infrastructure, servers, storage, cloud or the provision of HPE software (incl. rental software) as well as associated services. Installation and configuration services as well as measures to establish operational readiness do not explicitly form part of the content of the tender, unless they are listed in the price sheet or are a component of the items in the price sheet or of the included maintenance service. These measures are commissioned separately by the contracting authority as required.

sig_e5740702950e74e82984.description: RVK is a modern transport company that has been under municipal ownership since 1996. The company was formed in 1976 from a merger of the railway and postal bus services. The transport area extends across the Rheinisch-Bergischer district, the left-bank Rhein-Sieg district, the Euskirchen district and the cities of Cologne, Bonn, Leverkusen, Hürth, Brühl and Wesseling. RVK thus connects urban conurbations with sparsely populated, more rural areas. With capacity, competence and many years of experience, RVK ensures that people in the region are on the move reliably and safely – and in an environmentally friendly, sustainable and innovative way. The RVK bus fleet comprises over 600 vehicles, some of which are operated by the company itself and some of which operate on behalf of RVK. The transport network comprises 132 lines with a total length of 2.595 km. In addition, 58 lines are operated by RVK for other transport companies. In total, RVK provides a mileage of approx. 22,6 million km with approx. 23 million passengers annually. Most of the RVK buses are already equipped with TFT interior displays. However, as not all buses have TFT monitors, RVK is procuring at least 100 additional 29 inch TFT interior displays (and up to a total of 350 TFT interior displays) for use in public transport vehicles via a framework agreement. sig_e5c57127e832fb59b09c.description: The object of the contract is the procurement of Services for the preparation of technical-economic documentation, DALI phase, for the investment objective "Studies, documentation for street works - Reconfiguration, rehabilitation and modernisation of the intersection of Chitiliei Road with Bucureștii Noi Boulevard, reconfiguration, rehabilitation and modernisation of Bucureștii Noi (segment Timișului Street - Constanța Bridge), reconfiguration, rehabilitation and modernisation of Griviței Road (segment Constanța Bridge - Carpați Street), reconstruction of Constanța bridge and the creation of an intermodal node", according to the specifications in the tender specifications. The deadline by which any interested economic operator has the right to request clarifications or additional information regarding the award documentation is a maximum of 20 days before the deadline for submission of tenders. The contracting authority will respond clearly and completely to all requests for clarification/additional information on the 11 day before the deadline for submission of tenders. The contracting authority mentions that it will respond to requests for clarification addressed by economic operators by the deadline established in the Contract Notice. Any request for clarification must be transmitted in SEAP (http://sicap-prod.e-licitatie.ro/pub). The programme for the modernisation and rehabilitation of major urban thoroughfares is part of a broader programme to remedy existing deficiencies in urban traffic. The lack of efficient connections between areas of the Municipality of Bucharest affects car traffic, pedestrian traffic and public transport, creating large losses of time and additional fuel consumption. To streamline heavy traffic in the north of the Capital, it is necessary to modernise the infrastructure in this area, ensuring increased safety and comfort conditions. Due to severe degradation, low travel speeds lead to increased CO2 emissions and hinder access for Police, Ambulance and Fire Brigade crews. Implementing the investment in the area of the intersection of Chitilei Road with Bucureștii Noi Boulevard and Griviței Road, together with the reconstruction of the Constanța Bridge and the creation of an intermodal node, will improve access to public services and reduce travel times, increasing the quality of life for residents and people in transit. The duration of the provision of services is 180 calendar days.

sig_e5d13788d4743ecf509c.description: In the current model, the technical implementation of communal services is integrated into the IT organisation established by the State of Fribourg. In particular, SITel ensures contracting with technical service providers and the management of IT developments, in collaboration with the DIGI-FR team, which carries the business needs and ensures functional responsibility for communal services. With the coming to an end of the DIGI-FR program 2023–2026 and the evolution of the legal framework relating to e-government, this model is bound to evolve. From 2027, the municipalities, through the entity responsible for representing them, will take over responsibility for the development, operation and maintenance of their services on the Fribourg virtual counter. They will thus have the capacity to directly commission the necessary service providers and manage the end-to-end technical implementation of their services. This call for tenders aims to establish the capacities required for the development and maintenance of communal services in this new model. The public procurement aims to establish a contractual framework which will subsequently allow the ACF, according to its needs and on the basis of a predefined service catalogue, to award its contracts to referenced partners via single consultations (mini-tenders) in a simplified and competitive procedure.
sig_e5d13788d4743ecf509c.title: Framework contract for e-government DIGI-FR

sig_e5d463b07d7476d5424b.description: New establishment of a digital alerting system in the POCSAG standard (2m band) for non-police emergency response in the Landkreis Emmendingen to replace the analogue 5-tone alerting. The subject of the procurement is the supply, installation and commissioning of a area-wide digital alerting system complying with the POCSAG standard in the 2m band for emergency services organisations in the Landkreis Emmendingen, including migration from the existing analogue 5-tone alerting, the supply of end-user devices as well as maintenance and service provisions. The procurement procedure in question comprises the establishment of 37 digital alerting repeater sites within the district area including antenna and lightning protection technology as well as the electrotechnical upgrading of the structures for these sites. Furthermore, a total of four digital alerters (two fixed installations and two mobile emergency alerters) as well as network and IT technology for the central system technology will be installed at the site of the Integrated Control Centre Emmendingen. The contract is divided into four lots. Lot 1 comprises the digital alerting system technology, in particular the supply, assembly, commissioning and configuration of the digital alerting repeaters and digital alerters with subsequent services on the basis of an EVB-IT service contract with a fixed term of 24 months. Lot 2 includes antenna technology and mast construction, meaning in particular the supply and assembly of antenna masts and lightning protection as well as earthing components. Lot 3 describes the necessary electrical work. Lot 4 comprises the procurement of end-user devices using a shopping-basket principle with call-offs by the respective authorised municipalities or relief organisations. Supply, installation, and commissioning of the central and decentralised system technology of the digital alerting system (including digital alerters, digital alerting repeaters, switches, software), including system integration, tests, training as well as the conclusion of an EVB-IT service contract limited to the first 24 months.; Supply, assembly and commissioning of antenna systems (2m, GPS, LTE), antenna carriers and mast structures including lightning protection and earthing measures and structural analyses, as well as coordination with property owners.; Execution of all electrical connection and installation work at transmitter and technical sites, including power supply as well as documentation in accordance with DIN VDE 0100-600.; Supply, installation, configuration and commissioning of end-user devices for receiving the alarm messages transmitted via the components of lot 1 and of components for remote programming of these end-user devices (server-client structure) and central components for implementing a call-back functionality from and additional alarm information to the end-user devices via the mobile communications network. The procurement of the end-user devices takes place via a framework agreement according to the shopping-basket principle with call-offs by the authorised municipalities and relief organisations.
sig_e5d463b07d7476d5424b.title: Tender for Digital Alerting (Hardware & Installation)

sig_e65b3b1c01dca77388d9.description: Our ambition is to implement a workwear solution that is accessible, and inclusive for all colleagues, incorporating maternity options, religious considerations, gender-appropriate fits, and consistent sizing standards. Lot 1: . Our vision is to create a fully branded, inclusive, and functional workwear and PPE solution that unites every colleague across our organisation reflecting who we are, what we stand for, and the pride we take in serving our communities. We will deliver a modern, high‐quality uniform range designed from the ground up to support the unique needs of our operational, maritime, port, and shore‐based teams. Rooted in the heritage of Caledonian MacBrayne and our communities, our workwear will combine safety, comfort, durability, and unmistakable brand identity in every garment. Our ambition is to implement a workwear solution that is accessible, and inclusive for all colleagues, incorporating maternity options, religious considerations, gender-appropriate fits, and consistent sizing standards. Through clear uniform standards, easy maintenance guidance, and from warehouse to home/work distribution processes, we will set and uphold a new standard for how our brand is worn and represented. Powered by digital self-service ordering tools, our workwear transformation will enhance operational efficiency, improve stock management, and allow us to scale sustainably. Cross-functional collaboration at the early stages will ensure that every voice is heard and every role is understood, creating a sense of ownership, pride, and confidence in the final solution. By learning from industry-leading transformations and working with expert partners, we will introduce a workwear range that not only serves practical needs but also strengthens culture, improves staff experience, and supports our organisation’s evolution. This is more than new uniform, it's an opportunity to reinforce our brand, celebrate our heritage, empower our people, and deliver a workwear experience that is fit for the future.
sig_e65b3b1c01dca77388d9.title: Design, Supply and Delivery of Uniform and PPE

sig_e76cad13ba556c235e05.description: ITZBund requires services in the area of software lifecycle management (SLM) for software development and project management solutions in use. The aim of this tender is to conclude a framework agreement to ensure the operation as well as the maintenance and (further) development of the existing Cloud software development and project management platform and associated specialist applications of ITZBund. In addition, sovereignty is to be strengthened through the expansion of open source tools to be procured. ITZBund understands open source to be software whose source code is freely available. In principle, everyone is permitted to use, analyse, modify and pass on this software free of charge and without restriction in terms of content regarding the object and source code. Specifications of the respective relevant open source licence, in particular regarding licence texts, copyright notices or copyleft effects, remain unaffected. The services advertised encompass services along the entire software lifecycle, in particular operational services, maintenance and support services, support services in connection with releases and rollouts as well as demand-oriented new developments and further developments of existing software and software-related tools. The contracting authority, who can commission services commissioned by its customers, is authorised to call off services. The operation of the procured software products generally takes place within ITZBund; exceptions in special individual cases permit operation at customers of the contracting authority with their own licensing. The services mentioned at the outset are advertised in five lots: - Lot 1: Ensuring the maintenance and (further) development of the deployed Cloud software development and project management platform - Lot 2: Ensuring the operation and automated rollout of releases of the deployed Cloud software development and project management platform - Lot 3: Provision of Sonatype software products - Lot 4: Provision of an open source issue tracker including in particular training, support, further development and migration services - Lot 5: Provision of an open source wiki including in particular training, support, further development and migration services This specification of services considers the subject matter of Lot 5: The subject matter of this lot is the provision of an open source wiki including associated training, support, further development and migration services. Lot LOT-0000: Provision of an open source wiki including in particular training, support, further development and migration services. For the total contract period of 4 years, an upper limit of 1.450 instances and 162.608 person-hours (ph) or 20.326 person-days (pd) results for the estimated calculatory costs.
sig_e76cad13ba556c235e05.title: Provision of an open source wiki including, in particular, training, support, further development and migration services

sig_e778d4c4281ef3fef99c.description: The National Library of Medicine (NLM) seeks applications for research projects that drive groundbreaking innovation and advanced development in the fields of bioinformatics, translational bioinformatics, and computational biology. The primary goal of this initiative is to support the creation and implementation of cutting-edge methods, tools, and approaches that can transform the landscape of biomedical data science. This NOFO aims to address the growing need to leverage transformative technologies — such as artificial intelligence (AI), machine learning, and large-scale computational platforms — to extract actionable knowledge from vast, diverse, and complex biological datasets. By enabling more effective interpretation and integration of multi-dimensional biological and biomedical data, this research will ultimately contribute to improving individual and population health outcomes.

sig_e7d5d6310a2da1c26cbb.description: GENERAL This document is not a procurement announcement, not an Call for tenders, nor will its publication start a Tender Procurement Process. The purpose of this Pre-market consultation notice is to identify potential suppliers operating in the market and their offerings. Responding or not responding to this Pre-market consultation notice does not prevent participation in a possible future tender. This Pre-market consultation notice does not obligate the contracting authority to carry out an actual procurement procedure. All information presented in this Pre-market consultation notice is preliminary and indicative. Laurea University of Applied Sciences operates in five locations in the Uusimaa region in Finland. Laurea offers both bachelor’s and master’s degree studies but also open university studies, specialisation education and continuing education. The fields of study are Business Management, Information technology, Service business, Social Services, Nursing, Health Care and Hospitality Management. Laurea has approximately 9,900-degree students and approximately 13,000 Open UAS students per year as well as about 670 employees. PRELIMINARY SCOPE OF THE PROCUREMENT The scope of the procurement is a Software as a Service (SaaS) online exam proctoring system for Laurea UAS. The system must integrate with Laurea's learning platform (Canvas) and provide video and audio-based proctoring recorded and stored by the system. The procurement does not include a personal live monitoring service by the supplier or the use of artificial intelligence to monitor/check and identify suspected fraud. The procurement includes the deployment of the software service and support and maintenance services separately for each higher education institution. MARKET DIALOGUE The contracting authority reserves the right to engage in market dialogue with the responding companies regarding the planned procurement and the tender documents. In addition, the contracting authority reserves the right to conduct the potential market dialogue either in the form of written comments on the draft tender documents or through one-on-one meetings (via Teams or in person). The possibility to comment on the draft tender documents is preliminary planned to be arranged once before the publication of the final Call for tenders, regardless of the format. Any potential market dialogue will be conducted in English, and all related materials will be provided only in English. No compensation will be paid for participation in the market dialogue. Hansel Oy will act in a consultative role in the procurement process. REGISTRATION FOR THE MARKET DIALOGUE Potential service providers interested in participating in the dialogue are kindly asked to register via email as soon as possible and at the latest by 6 February 2026. Send the name and contact details of the interested service provider to maritta.riskila@laurea.fi. Use a reference "TD for an Online exam proctoring system" and the company name as the subject of the email. The service providers may register in Finnish or English.

sig_e7e767c9b6181b349fa2.description: The National Institute on Aging (NIA) intends to publish a Notice of Funding Opportunity (NOFO) that builds upon its investment in data-driven approaches for the purpose of defining molecular mechanisms of resilience in the presence of various types of Alzheimer's disease (AD) and AD-related dementias (ADRD) risk. The goal of this NOFO is to build a robust program that integrates epidemiologic, genomic, and mechanistic research through the use of data driven, systems-based approaches (including the use of artificial intelligence and/or machine learning methods) to discover the molecular/cellular determinants of resilience to AD/ADRD risk across representative populations. The initiative will support the generation of high-dimensional molecular data from brain and peripheral tissues, including longitudinal data, to enable dynamic modeling of resilience mechanisms and to discover molecular predictors of resilience. Applications are not being solicited at this time. Notice is being provided to allow potential applicants sufficient time to develop meaningful collaborations and responsive projects. This NOFO intends to utilize the U01 activity code. Investigators with expertise and insights into this area of aging research are encouraged to begin to consider applying for this new NOFO.
sig_e7e767c9b6181b349fa2.title: Interdisciplinary Research to Understand the Complex Biology of Resilience to Alzheimer’s and Related Dementias Disease Risk

sig_e7ece7826066941a8bf4.description: DESCRIPTION OF THE PROCUREMENT VR-Group Plc (“VR” or the “Contracting Entity”) is procuring a modern, SaaS-based HR solution to replace its current HRM systems in Finland and Sweden. The solution must provide a secure, reliable, and scalable platform for more than 10 000 employees globally, support country-specific requirements, and enable expansion into additional countries if needed, without major customization. VR is seeking a robust, scalable, and future-ready HR solution delivered as a single, integrated product. The solution will serve as VR’s central employment management platform and provide a reliable, secure, and consistent source of personnel and employment information throughout the employee lifecycle. The solution must enable VR to standardize and streamline core HR processes, reduce fragmented systems and manual work, improve data quality, and support efficient collaboration between HR, payroll, managers, employees, and other relevant stakeholders. The scope of this procurement is limited to the acquisition of the technology, including the HR SaaS solution and the necessary user licences. The implementation of the solution and the related support and maintenance services will be subject to a separate procurement procedure to be conducted after the technology provider has been selected. Thus, the selected HR technology must have a strong partner ecosystem in Finland and Sweden to enable competitive procurement. The new SaaS-based HR solution must include secure, enterprise-grade AI capabilities with appropriate governance and human oversight. The provider must also demonstrate continuous and substantial annual investment in product development. OBJECTIVES OF THE MARKET DIALOGUE VR is conducting a market dialogue to obtain specific, substantiated, and commercially relevant input on the planned procurement scope, requirements and delivery model. VR also seeks verifiable evidence of the solution’s impact on employee experience and customer satisfaction, supported by clearly defined metrics, comparable customer results, and independent research or third-party assessments. Participants must provide concrete, evidence-based responses and clearly distinguish between: - Standard, generally available product capabilities - Configurable functionality - AI capabilities currently in production - AI capabilities planned on the committed product roadmap - Partner-delivered services - Functionality requiring customization The purpose is to ensure that the procurement reflects proven market capabilities, supports VR’s strategic objectives, and enables genuine and effective competition. VR may use the results to refine the procurement scope, mandatory requirements, evaluation criteria, contractual framework, and subsequent tendering process. PRELIMINARY SCHEDULE - Market dialogue in September-October 2026 - Publication of the invitation to tender in November-December 2026 - Evaluation of the tenders and contract award in December 2026 - February 2027 - Contract period starts in November 2027 ADDITIONAL INFORMATION This notice is a request for information. It is not a contract notice or a call for tenders. The request for information includes an invitation to participate in a market dialogue. All interested suppliers are invited to participate in technical discussions with the Contracting Entity concerning the planned procurement. The purpose of the dialogue is to discuss the procurement at a general level and to obtain market feedback on the proposed scope and definition of the procurement. Discussion are held mainly as a written market dialogue rounds. Interested suppliers will be provided with preliminary procurement materials and/or questions for review and comments. The Contracting Entity may organize also joint market dialogue sessions and individual meetings with interested suppliers. Suppliers interested in participating in the market dialogue are requested to submit their expression of interest via the link:https://forms.cloud.microsoft/e/ZSEbHcb4b6 no later than 30th of September 2026 at 12:00 noon (Finnish time). Participation in the market dialogue does not oblige the Contracting Entity to proceed with the procurement, nor does it oblige suppliers to participate in any subsequent tendering procedure. Non-participation in the market dialogue does not prohibit supplier to submit a tender in the subsequent tendering procedure. The Contracting Entity reserves the right to amend the scope, content, procurement model, schedule and market dialogue process during the preparation of the procurement. No compensation will be paid to suppliers for participating in the market dialogue or for providing comments.
sig_e7ece7826066941a8bf4.title: REQUEST FOR INFORMATION: HR Solution as a global Cloud solution for VR Group

sig_e8c9c3ee2a3adc21b527.description: The subject of the dynamic purchasing system (DPS) consists of cloud services and related expert services for the customers of Hansel Oy. Cloud services mean capacity or software services delivered via a data network and produced by the supplier. Customers receive cloud capacity for their use as a service. Customers using the cloud service are not directly responsible for or managing the cloud infrastructure, but can manage, for example, operating systems, middleware and databases. Customers may also potentially manage network components, such as firewalls, via a management console or similar. The supplier provides the necessary server capacity, computing time and/or disk capacity dynamically according to the customer's needs. The required capacity scales rapidly according to current needs. Such services include, among others: - Infrastructure services (Infrastructure as a Service (IaaS)), where the customer acquires infrastructure services for their organisation's use and is themselves responsible for the management and configuration of the platform. These include, for example, server, storage, computing, memory, backup and data communication service capacity. - Container services (Containers as a Service (CaaS)), where the customer acquires container space from servers and is themselves responsible only for the contents of the container and to some extent for the management of the container. - Platform services (Platform as a Service (PaaS)), where the customer acquires a platform for their applications and is themselves responsible only for the applications. - Serverless services (Serverless, Functions as a Service (FaaS)), where the customer acquires certain functions, for example a scheduled event such as once a day/week/month. Cloud services include, among other things: - Monitoring and management services - Dedicated solutions - Hybrid environment monitoring and management services - Production environment, data communications, data protection and backup - Event, service request and access rights management - Version, configuration and change management - Asset management - Service reporting - Service operation development and management Software as a Service (SaaS) services can also be acquired to a limited extent through the DPS's internal competitions as specified below. SaaS services complementing IaaS and PaaS services can be acquired if their use is closely linked to the utilisation of IaaS and PaaS services which are the main subject of procurement. The aforementioned complementary SaaS services and other services complementing IaaS and PaaS services can be acquired from cloud service providers' services and marketplaces (Marketplace). Other SaaS services cannot be acquired on the basis of this DPS. For example, ready-made end-user software, such as CRM or financial management software, cannot be acquired as SaaS services on the basis of this DPS.
sig_e8c9c3ee2a3adc21b527.title: Cloud services 2026

sig_e8ee7eef535b3fa71066.description: GENERAL THL has commenced the preparation of the procurement process for the maintenance and publication of the Finnish-Language Subset of the SNOMED CT Terminology. As part of the preparation of the tendering process, the contracting authority is conducting a market dialogue. Please note that this is a market consultation notice, not a request for tenders. This market consultation notice does not yet invite the submission of tenders. Participation in the market dialogue is entirely voluntary. Participation or non-participation in the market dialogue will not affect a supplier’s opportunities to take part in the procurement procedure to be conducted at a later stage. The market dialogue does not oblige anyone to participate in the actual tendering process, nor does it exclude anyone from it. Details of the market dialogue are below. The Finnish Institute for Health and Welfare (THL) is an independent state-owned expert and research institute that promotes the welfare, health and safety of the population. PRELIMINARY SUBJECT OF THE PROCUREMENT The subject of the procurement is a SNOMED CT terminology management tool and related services, which will be used for producing, maintaining, and distributing Finland’s national SNOMED CT extension, reference sets (refsets), translations, and national releases. The objective is to procure a comprehensive solution that enables the following functional areas: 1) Terminology maintenance and authoring - Creation of new national concepts when the SNOMED CT International Edition does not cover national requirements. - Management of concept descriptions, synonyms, and relationships between concepts. - Logical and technical validation in accordance with SNOMED CT rules. 2) Design and management of reference sets (refsets, subsets) - Creation and maintenance of both extensional and intentional reference sets. - Version control and metadata definition for reference sets. 3) Production and management of SNOMED CT translations - Production of Finnish and Swedish terms using the translation tool. - Quality assurance and approval workflows for translations, including optional computer-assisted translation. 4) Compilation and validation of national SNOMED CT release - Assembling the national extension and all included components into a single release package. - Validation of the release according to SNOMED CT rules. - Production of publication and distribution packages in RF2 format. 5) Workflows, project management and collaboration - Task assignment, role management, approval processes, and workflow coordination. - Support for customized workflows (e.g., integration with Jira). 6) Search functions and terminology browsing - Efficient search across both the SNOMED CT International Edition and the Finnish national extension. 7) Distribution, licensing, and reporting - Distribution of the national release to various stakeholders. - Management of licensing and access control requirements. - Production of quality, translation, and validation reports. 8) Technical implementation and nonfunctional requirements - The solution shall primarily be delivered as a SaaS service, with the service provider responsible for maintenance, versioning, and technical reliability. - Browser-based user interface, APIs (API/FHIR/REST), high-level information security, usability, and scalability. - Support for multiple languages (at minimum English, Finnish and Swedish). - Integration capabilities with national code server infrastructures. The procurement is for a ready-made software-based solution that can be implemented quickly. The contracting authority has the right to propose customization of the solution as described in the tender Please note, that the details given above are preliminary MARKET DIALOGUE The market dialogue sessions will be held via Microsoft Teams during weeks 18 and 19 (28 April – 8 May 2026). Each participant will be invited to an individual session with the contracting authority to ensure confidentiality. Details of the meeting, including the agenda and duration, will be sent to the participant via email. As part of the market dialogue, the contracting authority will provide an opportunity to submit written comments on the preliminary tender materials. Separate information about this will be sent to those who have registered for the market dialogue. Interested parties are kindly requested to register their interest by 23.4.2026, 3.00 PM by contacting kilpailutus@hansel.fi via email. Use: “MARKET DIALOGUE: maintenance and publication of the Finnish-Language Subset of the SNOMED CT Terminology” in the subject line, and provide the participant's name and contact details in the message. Upon registration, participants will receive a scheduled meeting time and a Teams meeting link. The sessions will be conducted on a one-to-one basis between the contracting authority and each participant.
sig_e8ee7eef535b3fa71066.title: INVITATION TO MARKET DIALOGUE: Maintenance and Publication of the Finnish-Language Subset of the SNOMED CT Terminology

sig_e9813d7da4646856555e.description: The subject of the contract is the delivery of a comprehensive debt management and recovery service system for Municipal Transport Company in Bielsko-Biała Limited Liability Company. I) The basic scope of the contract includes: 1. Drawing up and handing over to the Contracting Authority the pre-implementation analysis studies and performing other accompanying work necessary for the implementation of the undertaking, such as, for example, analytical and design work, documentation. 2. Development and implementation of a system for comprehensive management and debt recovery services for MZK. The delivered system is to provide a complete solution in the field of civil law debt collection, including an amicable, judicial and enforcement (bailiff) debt recovery module. 3. Development and implementation of a system managing Control Devices and Inspectors. 4. Granting an indefinite licence to the Contracting Authority for the Platform. 5. Delivery of 11 Inspector Devices together with an application for ticket inspection and generation of additional charges (with the option of printing with payment method designation (bank transfer) and making payments using payment cards, BLIK and other payment instruments. SIM cards will be provided by the Contracting Authority. At the System Design stage, the parties will agree on target solutions: based on a dedicated APN or a set-up VPN tunnel. 6. Provision by the Contractor, during the implementation period and during the period of providing payment services (on Inspector Devices, in the scope of collecting the additional charge for lack of a ticket/entitlement) and service services (maintenance period), of full cloud computing infrastructure and licences necessary to use cloud services to operate the Platform. 7. Operation of the system during the maintenance period (including warranty reviews, maintenance costs of a dedicated SMS gateway, costs resulting from the agreement with the acquiring bank) in a set number of months. 8. The obligation to transfer (migrate) passenger data from the currently operating debt collection service system to the new system. The migration should be carried out in a manner ensuring the completeness of the transferred data, ensuring the possibility of making (in the migration process and after its completion) corrections, changes to data or deletion of data, e.g. outdated lines, streets, etc., while performing this process. The final migration process should be preceded by test migration(s) in order to verify the correctness and completeness of the execution of this process. Currently, the Contracting Authority uses Municom software from PZI TARAN sp. z o.o. (R&G PLUS Sp. z o.o. Group). The database environment is based on the DB2 engine and is located on the Contracting Authority's local server. All accesses to the environment will be granted to the Contractor after signing the contract. 9. Provision by the Contractor of access to a fully functional System, enabling the Contracting Authority to carry out verification and acceptance in an environment reflecting production conditions (training and test environment). 10. Training of System users indicated by the Contracting Authority. [System maintenance and warranty conditions] 11. Provision by the Contractor for a period from 36 to 60 months (according to the bid evaluation criterion) of services in relation to the software and all components delivered as part of: 11.1. maintenance of the Debt Collection System during the warranty period, 11.2. provision of warranty and technical support for the System, 11.3. provision of service services and removal of defects, faults and errors of the System during the warranty period, 11.4. bearing the costs of maintaining a dedicated SMS gateway for sending messages from Inspector Devices (calls for payment), 11.5. Provision of programming support services during the term of the contract in a set number of man-hours, 12. Bearing by the Contractor of the costs of system operation during the maintenance period (including warranty reviews, communication costs in a set number of months. II. The scope of the OPTION RIGHT includes: delivery of additional Inspector Devices in a number not greater than 10 units, which will be identical in terms of all features and functionalities as the Inspector Devices delivered in the basic scope of the contract. Detailed provisions concerning the activation of the option right are contained in the drafted contract provisions, i.e., Appendix No. 1 to the SWZ.

Part 1) - Procurement of technologies for server rooms The subject matter of this part of the public contract is the comprehensive supply, expert implementation and subsequent commissioning of a complete technological solution for the expansion and supplementation of the existing data centre infrastructure, both physically and technologically. Specifically, this involves the installation and integration of physical infrastructure elements, a modern air conditioning system, an uninterruptible power supply, a CCTV system for monitoring and security purposes, fire safety systems and the establishment of an optical connection with a dedicated backup server room, which will ensure high availability and operational continuity. sig_e9a52ffc87a590013627.description: The NHSBSA is a Special Health Authority and an Arm's Length Body of the Department of Health and Social Care. We provide a range of critical central services to NHS organisations (our 'clients'), NHS contractors, health bodies, patients and the public (our 'customers'). The NHSBSA requires a service for the Secure Bulk Destruction & Disposal of Confidential Waste over the course of a four-year contract period. Waste products for destruction include NHS prescriptions and patient medical records as well as waste cardboard. Due to the value that this wastepaper can attract within the paper pulp and paper recycling market, it is expected that the NHSBSA may be able to generate revenue from this contract. At this stage we are seeking high-level input to enable us to assess the market and to inform any future procurement strategy to ensure compliance with The Procurement Act 2023 and/or the Public Contracts Regulations 2015 as the case maybe. Interested parties must register an interest in this RFI via https://health-family.force.com/s/Welcome (search opportunities using system reference C394990). Suppliers can register from Wednesday 15th October 2025 and the RFI documents will be made available on Wednesday 15th October 2025. The window for clarification questions will close on Monday 27th October 2025 at 12:00 noon BST and written RFI responses are requested by no later than Wednesday 29th October 2025 at 12:00 noon BST. The NHS Business Services Authority (NHSBSA) invites all interested economic operators to participate in an RFI. Your organisation’s involvement with our RFI is an invaluable way of us ensuring that, with your input, we have the best support and guidance to inform any subsequent procurement. Please note that at this stage a route to market has not yet been determined. However, should the outcome of this RFI determine that the best value route to market is via a framework then any subsequent invitation to tender and notices will be restricted to those appointed to the applicable framework and will be governed by the Procurement Regulations 2015 or the Procurement Act 2023 as stipulated by the framework in question. Additional Information: Suppliers should note that this RFI is a market research exercise only and it is not an invitation to tender, an invitation to offer an agreement or a guarantee there will be a future procurement exercise. If you do not wish to take part in this RFI exercise, it will not affect any current or future business with the NHSBSA. Participation in this RFI is limited to suppliers that meet the definition of "economic operator" under the Public Contracts Regulations 2015. "Economic operator" means any person, or public entity, or group of such persons and entities, including any temporary association of undertakings, that offers the execution of works or a work, the supply of products or the provision of services on the market. Where a participant does not meet this criteria they may be removed from the RFI process. Disclaimers: (1) No competitive advantage will be gained by the suppliers engaging with the NHSBSA at this early stage and NHSBSA will ensure equal treatment of all interested parties at all times. We will make the outputs of the day available to those Suppliers who are unable to attend. (2) NHSBSA does not bind itself, by conducting this RFI exercise, to commence any procurement procedure or award any contract, and will not in any event be responsible for any costs incurred by invitees in attending and/or preparing for the presentation and individual supplier meeting referred to above. (3) Confidentiality of information which is clearly marked or identified as being confidential and which is reasonably viewed by NHSBSA as confidential will be observed, but NHSBSA does not accept any blanket claims of confidentiality. sig_e9c92664fd86afcef37d.description: NOTE! THIS IS NOT A CONTRACT NOTICE OR A CALL FOR TENDERS BUT A REQUEST FOR INFORMATION FOR MARKET RESEARCH AND TECHNICAL DIALOGUE: Simulation system Subject and purpose of the request for information: The purpose of the request for information is to survey solutions available on the market and, in particular, companies that have the capability to design and implement a large-scale simulation system for the Contracting Authority's needs. The request for information is used to gather information for procurement planning. The Hippos area being built in Jyväskylä offers an international-level complex for physical activity, hobbies and sport. The area strengthens Jyväskylä's position as a centre for physical activity, elite sports, research and education. The Hippos Centre consists of four entities: Sports Centre, Competence Centre, Ice Sports Centre and the HipposPark car park. The Welfare Unit of Jyväskylä University of Applied Sciences is relocating to the 5 and 6 floors of the Competence Centre. Construction will begin in January 2026 and will be completed in late 2027. The commissioning of the premises is planned for August 2027. The subject of the procurement is a simulation system (AV system), which covers the simulation premises and learning premises on two floors as well as control rooms from which simulation situations and connections to various teaching premises are controlled. The simulation system is used to create simulation exercises resembling genuine interaction and customer situations for teaching purposes. The system enables the recording, saving and real-time control of situations. The objective of the request for information is to obtain information so that the planned procurement can be implemented as purposefully as possible. Responding to the request for information is not a prerequisite for participation in the subsequent procurement procedure and does not affect the tenderer's position in the procurement procedure. The matters presented in the request for information are preliminary and may change as the procurement preparations progress. This notice is a market survey used in the preparation of the procurement by Jyväskylä University of Applied Sciences. The contracting authority requests potential suppliers to respond through this request for information and to participate in one-to-one market dialogues. Participation is voluntary and no remuneration is paid for participating. The responses given and discussions held will be treated with complete confidentiality.
