The subject of the contract is the provision of service support for an economic information system. The support will include the following parts: 1. Microsoft Dynamics NAV (hereinafter “MD NAV”) updates within the Microsoft Enhancement Plan. 2. Service and updates for the economic information system, including all its add-ons. Helpdesk service provided via a web portal and development and support service according to the Contracting Authority's requirements. The Contracting Authority has a valid MS BREP "Business Ready Enhancement Plan" (hereinafter “maintenance”) for MD NAV Acct number: 6100645 valid until 29.10.2026. The Contractor shall conclude a contract with the Contracting Authority for the further continuation of maintenance – Microsoft Enhancement Plan for a fixed term until 29.10.2029 inclusive. The provision of the maintenance service shall include the right to use all higher versions, entitlement to service packs and updates, entitlement to support and a guarantee of compatibility with other Microsoft products released by Microsoft for use in the Czech Republic for Microsoft Dynamics NAV. The Contracting Authority requires that the price of this service be fixed for the entire duration of the contract. The contract will be concluded for a fixed term of 3 years from the date it becomes effective. The Contracting Authority requires the commencement of performance under the contract from 30. 10. 2026. Provided that the contractor commences performance according to the Contracting Authority's requirement by 30. 10. 2026, the contract will be concluded for a fixed term until 29.10.2029 inclusive. In the event that the contract becomes effective after 30. 10. 2026, the contractor shall commence the provision of performance under the contract on the date the contract becomes effective, with performance being provided for a period of 3 years. All software solutions (within part 1) will be supplied and implemented in the On-Premise version.; and: Updates to extension modules The Contracting Authority uses extension modules supplied by Konica Minolta IT Solutions Czech a.s. The service includes: - provision of an unlimited right to use all new released versions and updates of these modules for the duration of the contractual relationship. - ensuring such updates and modifications to the EIS that allow for the processing of financial, asset and other necessary data in the EIS in accordance with the legislative requirements of the Czech Republic that are binding on the Contracting Authority. The contractor shall carry out the necessary updates and modifications to the EIS in sufficient time so that they are implemented without serious acceptance reservations no later than 10 working days before the date on which the relevant legislative requirements enter into force and become binding on the Contracting Authority. In the event that the period between the publication of a legal regulation and the date of its entry into force is less than 30 days, and the contractor is unable to ensure the update and modification in advance, the deadline for delivery of the update shall be 30 days from the publication of this regulation. The contractor guarantees the flawless functionality of the reflected changes and simultaneously guarantees the flawless functionality of other system modules that were not affected by the changes made. In the event of identified defects and errors, the contractor undertakes to remove the discrepancies under the conditions stated in point b: Helpdesk Service. The contractor is obliged, when performing the public contract, to take such measures and act in such a way as to prevent the occurrence of damage. If the contractor causes damage to the Contracting Authority or other entities, the contractor is obliged to remove the damage without undue delay and, if this is not possible, to compensate for it financially. All costs associated with this shall be borne by the contractor. The choice of the method of compensation for damage belongs to the Contracting Authority if it is affected by the damage. The service does not include: - provision of an unlimited right to use all new released versions of the Travel Orders module and updates to the Travel Orders module for the duration of the contractual relationship. b: Helpdesk Service The service consists of resolving service requests, complaints about products and services supplied as part of previous performance reported using the web portal. The web portal for reporting service requests must be available 24 hours a day, 365 days a year. The service response to service requests must be ensured according to the priorities listed below. In the event of technical difficulties, there must be an option to submit a request via email or telephone. The following priorities are set for submitting service requests: 1. Emergency – The EIS is unusable in its basic functions. This state may threaten the operational activity of the Contracting Authority or its obligations arising from the law within a time horizon of five working days. 2. High – Some EIS functions work in a limited manner, but this limitation cannot be considered as one that could threaten the operational activity of the Contracting Authority or its obligations arising from the law within a time horizon of two weeks. 3. Standard – There is no danger of direct threat to the operational activity of the Contracting Authority. The contractor shall contractually undertake to commence the resolution of a service request with a given priority and resolve it as follows: 1. Emergency – within 5 hours of reporting, the contractor shall inform the Contracting Authority of the receipt of the request with an expected resolution date as soon as possible, no later than 24 hours from the notification of the service request. The contractor shall ensure the resolution of the request even during non-working days (i.e. Saturdays, Sundays and public holidays). 2. High – within 24 hours of reporting, the contractor shall inform the Contracting Authority of the receipt of the request, commence resolution no later than the next working day, and resolve within 5 working days from the notification of the operational problem 3. Standard – within 48 hours of reporting, the contractor shall inform the Contracting Authority of the receipt of the request, commence resolution no later than within 1 week, and resolve within 2 weeks from the notification of the operational problem. Resolution of a request means: - resolution of the reported (recorded) request or - provision of another acceptable solution or - proposal of an acceptable alternative solution or - provision of instructions for an alternative solution, which, however, does not have to be accepted by the Contracting Authority as a sufficient solution - forwarding the problem for resolution to a third party (e.g. Microsoft, HW supplier, etc.) in the event of a problem caused by the incorrect behaviour of a component supplied or supported by a third party c: Development and support service according to the Contracting Authority's requirements and ensuring compliance with legislation The service consists of drawing on a guaranteed range of hours at a set hourly rate excluding VAT.

The minimum required guaranteed range is set at 10 hours per month. The basis for invoicing will be the hours actually realised and not the guaranteed capacity. The contractor must guarantee the availability of the above-mentioned service in the range of at least 10 hours per month (with the understanding that this indicative range is also set for the purposes of evaluating tenders). However, the Contracting Authority will draw according to its current needs and does not have to use up all the guaranteed hours. At the same time, it may also exceed the number of hours. The contractor will invoice the service based on the actual number of hours consumed, based on the set hourly rate. Requests are submitted via the web portal, where all communication takes place – proposal of the request solution, schedule, determination of labour intensity, price and ordering, or rejection. At the same time, the web portal will send confirmation emails to selected email addresses of the Contracting Authority regarding the entry and status of the request resolution upon every saved change. In the event of technical difficulties, there is an option to submit a request via email or telephone. The service can also be used for consultation visits by a contractor's employee with the aim of providing expert consultations for resolving requests at the Contracting Authority's workplace. It can also be used for the implementation of new versions of updates, upgrades or builds of Microsoft Dynamics NAV application equipment and extension modules with regard to legislative changes. All software solutions (within part 2 of the public contract) will be supplied and implemented in the on-premises version.

sig_ea971947a93b5580d449.description: MARKET CONSULTATION The subject of the market consultation is the procurement of a maintenance operations management system for the tracks of Väylävirasto. BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVES The most central task of the operations management system is to support day-to-day maintenance management by offering various functionalities for equipment and work management ranging from work planning to work reporting, as well as enabling various tracking functions, for example with regard to accumulated work and costs. Another key factor for the system is to support information-driven management, i.e., to provide, inter alia, up-to-date information on maintenance activities carried out on assets and the resulting costs, as well as potential consequential effects over the entire lifecycle of the equipment. The system's functionalities should offer the target organisation the opportunity to implement maintenance operations characteristic of its operations in a process-driven manner, such that the system supports the execution of the process at different stages of the process, in accordance with the functionalities required of it. The efficient implementation of maintenance processes, ensuring both personnel and information security, requires strong support from the operations management system with which operations are managed and monitored. The operations management system should provide an open interface for the target organisation to monitor and manage maintenance operations between different stakeholders, such as in situations where maintenance is procured either partially or entirely as a service. In addition to the primary functionalities of maintenance management, the operations management system should cover a wide range of various functionalities supporting operations. The functionalities of the system can be roughly classified as follows: - Equipment management - Work management - Reports and analysis - Mobile application - User management - Cost tracking - Contract management - Inventory management - Procurement The task of the operations management system is to act in connection with day-to-day maintenance management as part of the broader system architecture of Väylävirasto. For this reason, various integrations with other operational and administrative systems of Väylävirasto will also be necessary. PRELIMINARY SCHEDULE The contracting authority's target schedule for carrying out the market consultation and procurement is: - Market consultation, technical dialogue (commenting on material) September-October 2025 - Market consultation, bilateral negotiations (approx. 3-6 companies) October-early November 2025 - Year 2026 ----- ADDITIONAL INFORMATION ON THE NOTICE This notice is a prior information notice. This notice does not request tenders. The prior information notice is accompanied by an invitation to a market consultation, whereby all suppliers interested in the procurement have the opportunity to engage in a technical dialogue concerning the procurement with Väylävirasto. The purpose of the technical dialogue is to discuss the subject matter of the procurement and its definition at a general level. The technical dialogue does not bind Väylävirasto to carry out the procurement. Nor does the technical dialogue bind the supplier to participate in a potential tendering procedure, nor does it prevent participation if the supplier has not participated in the dialogue. TECHNICAL DIALOGUE AND BILATERAL DISCUSSIONS The market consultation is organised in two phases: 1. As a technical dialogue, where potential suppliers are asked to familiarise themselves with the service description and requirement specification and to answer the contracting authority's preliminary questions (carried out in September-October by email in accordance with registrations) 2. As bilateral discussions, where the contracting authority invites 3-6 suppliers to discussions. The contracting authority will send invitations to the discussions to the selected suppliers as soon as possible. The discussions will take place during October-November 2025 (the following times are preliminarily reserved, participants are requested to reserve the times in their calendars where possible): - Mon 27.10 at 9.30-11 - Mon 27.10 at 14-15.30 - Wed 29.10 at 14.30-16 - Fri 31.10 at 12-13.30 - Mon 3.11 at 14-15.30 - Wed 5.11 at 12-13.30 The times will be confirmed to the suppliers selected for the bilateral negotiations approximately two weeks before the time. In addition to the above, the contracting authority reserves the right for a later scheduled commenting period on draft versions of the final tender documentation and for answering the contracting authority's new questions related to the subject matter of the procurement. INSTRUCTIONS FOR REGISTRATION The supplier must notify its interest in participating in the market consultation by 20.10.2025 at 12.00 by sending a message to tommi.aarnio@vayla.fi and virpi.kukkonen@vayla.fi with the subject heading: "Ratojen kunnossapidon toiminnanohjausjärjestelmä - markkinavuoropuhelu". The supplier is requested to provide the following information in the message: - name, email address and telephone number of the supplier's contact person - a brief description of the supplier (e.g., the company's line of business and main services) - a brief description of the solution offered by the supplier for the procurement subject to the market consultation - information on whether the solution is an already existing solution or a concept under development - the supplier's previous deliveries and references (corresponding to the subject matter of the procurement) The descriptions presented in this prior information notice and the estimated publication date of the contract notice, as well as the dialogue draft materials to be provided later, are preliminary and indicative procurement information. Participating companies will not be paid compensation for responding or participating.

sig_eaf83c3f102e15c95de4.description: The Integrated Rhine Programme (IRP) is a project of the State of Baden-Württemberg (BW) which comprises a total of 13 flood retention basins (FRBs) in various planning and implementation stages on former floodplains between Basel and Mannheim. The IRP specialist information system (FIS IRP) is to be developed as a central repository of the IRP for the safeguarding of relevant data. The project management and consultancy for the client (CA) for this IT project are being commissioned. The services to be provided in this context include the division of the IT project into realistic, economical implementation stages, cost estimates, the preparation of tender documents, in particular the specification of requirements and the acceptance catalogue, for the programming or development of the FIS IRP, the professional and technical support of the CA in procurement processes, and project management during implementation and programming. An optional contract is to be awarded: as a mandatory service, the contractor (CO) is to support the first implementation stage in the development of the FIS IRP; support for further implementation stages is aimed for (options). Table 1 within the preliminary specification of requirements (Annex 1 of the procurement documents) provides an overview of the services to be provided by the contractor with the timeframe envisaged by the CA. Included services mainly comprise, but are not limited to, the preparation of the tender for the programming of the FIS IRP for the 1 implementation stage (with a focus on the creation of the specification of requirements, in which requirements from later implementation stages or the overall project must also be taken into account), the professional and technical support of the CA in the procurement process, and project management during implementation and programming. In the further course of the project, the commissioning of comparable services for the support of further implementation stages is aimed for (optional contract). More detailed provisions on the provision of services can be found in the preliminary specification of requirements (Annex 1 of the procurement documents). The final specification of requirements will be submitted to the successful applicants with the invitation to submit a tender. The FIS IRP is planned as a modular specialist information system with the modules "Operating Data", "Ecology", "Groundwater and Surface Water Models", "Groundwater and Surface Water Data", and "Structures". The FIS IRP is intended to secure the data long-term, make it available for display (including viewing in a geospatial data viewer) and enable cross-cutting evaluation of the data across the entire IRP. The CA has described the FIS IRP with its modules in technical concepts in which the precise contents, functionalities and general technical requirements for the FIS are formulated without specifying particular software or a development environment. The procurement documents contain a brief description of the technical concept (Annex 2). For individual modules, local database applications or data repositories in the form of medium-term implementation solutions have already been created. The applications must be further developed, also for integration into the specialist information system. In the phased development of the FIS IRP planned for the future, the initial focus is on the integration of dynamic factual data, i.e. operating and monitoring data, as well as the development of the geospatial data viewer.
sig_eaf83c3f102e15c95de4.title: IT consultancy and project management in the development of the Integrated Rhine Programme specialist information system (FIS IRP)

sig_eb1bacfb563f9759d7ed.description: Troms County (hereafter called the Contracting Authority) shall enter into a new framework agreement for books and teaching aids. The procurement is now in a preparatory phase and needs mapping is currently being carried out, as well as examining the possibility that the contracting authority ́s total need for all types of books and teaching aids can be covered through a joint agreement. The contracting authority ́s need primarily includes access to teaching materials, textbooks and concretising materials connected to all disciplines and subjects in sixth form education and the vocational college. Furthermore, the contracting authority would like to be able to use digital books and teaching aids, as a supplement to printed books and teaching aids, as well as books available through NDLA. The contracting authority also sees the need for a contract for other types of printed books than teaching aids, such as entertainment and fiction books. Emphasis is put on the fact that the contracting authority has already entered into a separate framework agreement for e-books and e-audiobooks, and that such products are therefore exempt from this hearing. Question 1: As the first part of the market mapping, the contracting authority would therefore like to know whether there are actors in the market who can offer all types of products as mentioned above, including both printed and digital teaching aids for sixth form college and vocational college, as well as a wide range of fiction and entertainment books. The contracting authority envisages the following alternative options to cover the need: Through a joint framework agreement, by dividing the procurement into two sub-contracts; one for all types of teaching aids (printed and digital) and a separate sub-contract for fiction. By dividing the procurement into three sub-contracts; one for printed teaching aids, one for digital teaching aids and one for fiction. Question 2: We would like further market input on which of these three alternatives are feasible and which is best suited to safeguard the contracting authority ́s needs as described above. How should the hearing be answered? Response deadline Thursday 05 March 2026 (12:00). The hearing will be answered through the communication tab in Mercell. The inputs will be treated confidentially and not visualised for other suppliers. Please note that Troms County does not reimburse any costs for participation in the hearing. Once the hearing deadline has expired, we will carefully review all received inputs and assess what input it might be appropriate to include in the final documents. Emphasis is put on the contracting authority not be obliged to comply with the inputs. Tenderers who respond to this hearing may be contacted afterwards if needed for clarification or further questions. Furthermore, it may be necessary to send a draft of the competition documents for a hearing. We therefore recommend all interested suppliers to provide input for this hearing.
sig_eb1bacfb563f9759d7ed.title: Books and teaching aids for Troms County - RFI

sig_eb638801ba7cf7698ac4.description: Benin's economy is experiencing sustained economic growth, with real GDP growth estimated at around 6.4 % in 2023 and projected to remain above 6 % over the coming years. However, this growth has not translated into sufficient decent employment opportunities for the majority of the population. Micro, small and medium-sized enterprises (MSMEs), which represent more than 95 % of registered enterprises, continue to face structural constraints including low productivity, weak integration into markets and value chains, limited access to finance and skilled labour, insufficient digitalisation, and inadequate business support services. Women-led enterprises and enterprises located in northern regions are particularly affected by these challenges. The Government of Benin has adopted several national strategies to strengthen economic productivity, employment promotion and SME competitiveness, including the National Development Plan 2018-2025, the national SME promotion strategy, the national employment policy and the "Benin Alafia 2060" vision. In parallel, the country aims to strengthen labour market governance through improved labour market information systems and territorial employment promotion approaches. The Federal Republic of Germany supports Benin in the implementation of these reforms through, among others, the project "Employment-oriented promotion of the competitiveness of micro, small and medium-sized enterprises" (ProPME 2). The project aims to improve the competitiveness of MSMEs in selected sectors and regions with a positive impact on employment. It focuses on the food processing industry, renewable energies, crafts and services sectors, as well as employment promotion and labour market intermediation. The module is structured around three main outputs: Output 1 aims to strengthen the competitiveness and growth capacities of MSMEs through tailored support, coaching and training measures. Output 2 aims to improve framework conditions for MSMEs through strengthened cooperation mechanisms, institutional support and public-private dialogue. Output 3 aims to improve the conditions for the placement of qualified workers in MSMEs through strengthened employment governance, labour market intermediation and labour market information systems. Benin's economy is growing rapidly, with real GDP growth estimated at approximately 6.4 % in 2023 and expected to remain above 6 % over the coming years. Despite this positive economic dynamic, the labour market remains unable to provide sufficient decent employment opportunities for the growing population. MSMEs account for more than 95 % of registered enterprises and constitute the backbone of the economy. However, they continue to face major structural constraints including low productivity and innovation, weak market integration, limited access to finance and skilled labour, insufficient support services, low digitalisation and inadequate quality assurance mechanisms. These challenges particularly affect women-led enterprises and northern regions of the country. The TVET system and labour market intermediation mechanisms are not yet sufficiently aligned with enterprise needs. At the same time, coordination between employment promotion actors and the territorial implementation of employment policies remain limited. In response to these challenges, the Government of Benin has adopted several strategic frameworks, including the National Development Plan 2018-2025, the national SME promotion strategy, the national employment policy and the "Benin Alafia 2060" vision. In parallel, Benin plans to establish a Labour Market Information System (LMIS) to strengthen labour market analysis, coordination and employment governance. The Federal Republic of Germany supports Benin in addressing these challenges through the project "Employment-oriented promotion of the competitiveness of micro, small and medium-sized enterprises" (ProPME 2). The project aims to improve the competitiveness of MSMEs in selected sectors and regions in Benin with an impact on employment. It builds on the successful approaches developed under the previous ProPME phase and contributes to strengthening MSMEs operating in the food processing industry, renewable energies, crafts and services sectors, as well as to improving employment promotion and labour market intermediation systems. The module is structured around three main outputs: Output 1 aims to strengthen the capacities and competitiveness of growth-oriented MSMEs through targeted support, coaching and training measures. Through improved business models, business management and productivity, MSMEs are expected to increase their competitiveness, create new jobs and improve working conditions. Output 2 aims to strengthen cooperation mechanisms between public and private sector actors involved in enterprise and employment promotion. Through improved public-private dialogue, institutional strengthening and coordination mechanisms, framework conditions for MSMEs are expected to improve, thereby reducing investment barriers and strengthening enterprise competitiveness. Output 3 aims to improve the conditions for the placement of qualified workers in MSMEs. This includes strengthening employment governance structures, improving labour market information systems, strengthening labour market intermediation mechanisms and improving the matching between labour supply and demand. The target group of the module primarily comprises growth-oriented MSMEs in selected sectors and value chains with high employment potential in the regions of Atlantique, Littoral, Ouémé, Mono, Atacora, Borgou and selected municipalities in Donga. Particular attention is given to women-led enterprises, young labour market entrants and graduates of vocational qualification measures. The contractor will support the implementation of Output 3 of the project. The services covered under this assignment focus on strengthening employment governance and labour market intermediation systems at macro, meso and local level. The contractor contributes to the achievement of the module indicator 2 and 3, as well as to the achievement of output indicator 3.2. The contractor is responsible for achieving the output indicator 3.1. Module objective indicator(s) 2: Number of employed persons in selected regions and sectors that have indicated that they benefited from improved working conditions in one of four categories. Module objective indicator(s) 3: Number of newly hired employees in MSMEs in selected regions and sectors. Output indicator 3.1: Number of employees in local and national institutions and committees for employment promotion who use data from the occupational and labour market information system Output indicator 3.2: Number of priority measures implemented under the new national employment policy to improve the placement of skilled workers in micro, small, and medium-sized enterprises (MSMEs). The activities of the contractor are structured around two main work packages: Work package 1: In this work package, the contractor will support the achievement of Output 3 by producing occupational and labour market profiles and regionally tailored labour market factsheets linked to sectors with strong employment potential in the regions of Atacora and Atlantique. The contractor will conduct desk research and field surveys, analyse labour market supply and demand, identify promising occupations and skills gaps, and produce labour market information resources for employment promotion actors and jobseekers. In addition, the contractor will support the establishment of career guidance spaces within AnpE branch offices and develop methodological tools for labour market profiling. Work package 2: Under this work package, the contractor will strengthen the capacities of institutional actors involved in employment governance and labour market intermediation, including DPE, AnpE, CLIDE, ULPE and other relevant stakeholders. Activities include institutional capacity assessments, development of capacity-building plans, training workshops on employment promotion approaches, dissemination workshops on labour market information tools, and training sessions on employment governance and coordination mechanisms.

sig_ebc44d79b10f71c065de.description: Introduction This is a Sources Sought Notice for market research purposes only. This is NOT a solicitation for proposals, proposal abstracts, or quotations. The notice is open to all nonprofit organizations; however, small businesses are highly encouraged to respond. This is NOT a solicitation for proposals, proposal abstracts, or quotations and does not obligate the Government to award a contract. The purpose of this notice is to obtain information regarding: (1) the availability and capability of qualified nonprofit sources; (2) whether they are small businesses; HUBZone small businesses; service-disabled, veteran-owned small businesses; 8(a) small businesses; veteran-owned small businesses; woman-owned small businesses; or small disadvantaged businesses; and (3) their size classification relative to the North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) code for the proposed acquisition. Your responses to the information requested will assist the Government in determining the appropriate acquisition method, including whether a set-aside is possible. An organization that is not considered a nonprofit entity should not submit a response to this notice. Background In 2000 Congress passed the Chimpanzee Health Improvement, Maintenance, and Protection (CHIMP) Act. In the Act Congress designated that the Secretary of Health and Human Services shall provide for the establishment and operation of a national sanctuary system for federally owned and federally supported chimpanzees no longer needed for research. The Division of Program Coordination, Planning, and Strategic Initiatives (DPCPSI), a component of the National Institutes of Health (NIH), is the office responsible for programmatic oversight of the Federally Supported Chimpanzee Sanctuary System (the Sanctuary). Purpose and Objectives In accordance with the CHIMP Act, the NIH is seeking to identify qualified nonprofit private entities capable of operating the sanctuary and providing lifetime care of Federally owned and Federally supported chimpanzees in accordance with the Statement of Work and in compliance with applicable Federal laws, regulations and policies. The primary purpose of this requirement is to operate and maintain a sanctuary providing lifetime care for up to 300 chimpanzees. Project requirements This requirement is to provide for the lifetime care of up to 300 chimpanzees that have been used, or were bred or purchased for use, in research conducted or supported by the National Institutes of Health, the Food and Drug Administration, or other agencies of the Federal Government. Anticipated period of performance The Government anticipates awarding one cost-reimbursement contract, featuring a one-year base period and four one-year option periods. The options periods may be unilaterally exercised by the Government. If the Government elects to exercise these options, the Contractor shall provide the resources as stated above. Other important considerations Respondents should confirm ability to comply with: Animal Welfare Act (9 CFR Parts 1–3) PHS Policy on Humane Care and Use of Laboratory Animals Guide for the Care and Use of Laboratory Animals (8th ed.) BMBL (6th ed.) 42 CFR Part 9 (Standards of Care for Chimpanzees in the Sanctuary System) NRC guidance on NHP occupational health/safety and psychological well-being AVMA Euthanasia Guidelines (2020) 29 CFR 1910.1030 (Bloodborne Pathogen Standard) AAALAC International accreditation (must achieve/maintain) OLAW Animal Welfare Assurance and USDA registration/assurances Capability statement/information sought (a) Staff expertise — including availability, experience, and formal and/or other training, addressed against the key personnel roles in the SOW: Facility Director, Attending Veterinarian, Clinical Veterinarian(s), Behaviorist, Colony Manager, animal care/enrichment technicians (min. 1 per 15 chimpanzees), and consultant veterinarians Applicable licensure (state veterinary license, AALAS LATG certification) and DEA licensing for controlled substance use in chimpanzees (b) Current in-house capability and capacity to perform the work, including: Existing facilities/capacity to house and care for up to 300 chimpanzees, with outdoor access and indoor shelter Veterinary care capability (physicals, TB testing, HCV/HIV testing, vaccinations, emergency/unexpected care) Biosafety and quarantine capability for animals exposed to zoonotic agents (HBV, HCV, HIV, SIV) 24/7/365 staffing capability, including holidays and severe weather Financial capacity to meet the 25% non-Federal cost-share requirement Existing or readily attainable AAALAC International accreditation, USDA registration, and OLAW Animal Welfare Assurance Ability to stand up/maintain required governance bodies (Governing Board of Directors, Sanctuary Chimpanzee Care Committee, Institutional Biosafety Committee) (c) Prior completed projects of similar nature, such as: Operation of large-scale (100+ animal) nonhuman primate or chimpanzee care programs Prior animal transfer/transport and quarantine intake experience Prior development of behavioral management plans, occupational health and safety plans, and disaster/emergency plans (d) Corporate experience and management capability, including: Fiscal management expertise and long-term financial stability Management plan experience (reporting lines, roles, fiscal coordination, decision-making processes) Regulatory compliance history (Animal Welfare Act, PHS Policy, 42 CFR Part 9) Any teaming or subcontracting arrangements anticipated (e) Examples of prior completed Government contracts, references, and other related information, such as: Contract numbers, agencies, periods of performance, and dollar values for comparable work Point-of-contact references who can speak to performance Any history of USDA inspection findings/deficiencies and corrective actions, if applicable Page Limitations Interested qualified nonprofit organizations should submit a tailored Capability Statement not to exceed 15 pages, excluding resumes. Capability Statements must not include links to internet web site addresses (URLs) or otherwise direct readers to alternate sources of information. Font size must be 10 to 12 points. Spacing must be no more than 15 characters per inch. Within a vertical inch, there must be no more than six lines of text. Print margins must be at least one inch on each edge of the paper. sig_ec27b75e698309d4bfb2.description:
An IT application for the digitalisation of processes relating to trichinella testing, the management of monitoring samples in the animal health sector and management in the event of an outbreak of African Swine Fever (ASF) is to be procured as a SaaS cloud solution. The IT application must be compatible with the hunting statistics application of Condition – Integrierte Softwarelösungen GmbH. This is used in the Free State of Thuringia to record bag data (data on wild animals killed by hunters). The IT application should be available both as a web application (usable in common browsers) and as a mobile app application (iOS and Android operating systems). Within the scope of the tender, an app is defined as an application that must be installed on a mobile device before use by the user and can only be used there. As a rule, this takes place on a smartphone or tablet using a so-called app store. There will be two main user groups: a) administrative or laboratory staff b) non-administrative users (e.g. those authorised to hunt). The non-administrative users record data on killed or slaughtered animals. If necessary, they also submit applications for the examination of these animals for trichinella and/or certain animal diseases to the competent authorities or the competent testing facility of the Free State of Thuringia. The test results should be retrievable via the IT application. The competent authorities (veterinary and food monitoring offices of the districts and independent cities - veterinary authorities) operate the trichinella testing laboratories. These should be able to access the application data recorded by external users in the IT application via their own user interface and transmit the test results back to the applicants. In addition, laboratory software should be made available to the competent authorities, with the help of which testing activities can be documented on the basis of the application data. In the case of monitoring samples in the animal health sector, the client's laboratory at the Thuringian State Office for Consumer Protection is the competent testing facility. The laboratory software (LIMS) in use there should be able to access the information on the samples entered by the users via the HIT database. The IT application must therefore have an interface to the HIT database. A direct connection to the LIMS is not intended. The IT application is to be made available to administrative staff for mapping internal administrative processes as well as to affected users outside the administration for data entry and application submission, and for receiving notices from the competent authorities. While the use cases of trichinella testing, management of monitoring samples in the animal health sector and the interface to the hunting statistics application are to be available permanently, the use case of management in the event of an outbreak of African Swine Fever (ASF) is only to be usable and available on an ad-hoc basis. Furthermore, introductory support and training for the staff of the competent authorities should be included in the offer as an initial service. The contract is concluded via an EVB-IT cloud contract. The procurement is carried out by the client for use by all districts and independent cities in Thuringia. The use of the IT application for the aforementioned purposes is mandatory for the districts and independent cities. For hunters, however, use is optional. This means that they can refrain from using the IT application. The previous analogue system for sampling will initially be continued in parallel. Lot LOT-0000: Provision, operation (incl. hosting) and support of an IT application for the digitalisation of processes relating to trichinella testing, the management of monitoring samples in the animal health sector, management in the event of an outbreak of African Swine Fever (ASF) and an interface to the hunting statistics application. The 21 veterinary and food monitoring offices of the 22 districts and independent cities in the Free State of Thuringia are, among other things, responsible for receiving and testing samples of slaughtered or killed animals intended for human consumption for Trichinella spp. Furthermore, there are responsibilities with regard to granting permission for the taking of samples intended for trichinella testing by non-administrative persons. Citizens who wish to make use of the aforementioned administrative services should be enabled to record the required application data digitally in accordance with the principles of the Online Access Act (OZG), to submit the application paperlessly to the respective competent veterinary and food monitoring office and to receive the notices from the competent authorities. In addition, the possibility should be created to comply with further reporting obligations (e.g. the recording of hunting bags by hunters) in digital form. The testing of wild boar for Trichinella spp. only takes place if the animal is to become food. Based on experience to date, this leads to the testing of up to 30.000 head of wild boar per year in Thuringia. These figures fluctuate. In addition, the veterinary monitoring authorities are responsible for implementing regular monitoring of killed wild animals for certain animal disease pathogens. Depending on the current animal health status, the number of samples is expected to vary between approx. 5.000 and 30.000 samples per year.

Data entry and application submission as well as the receipt of notices should also be enabled here for the respective affected citizens. The recorded data should be transmitted via the application to the State Office for Consumer Protection responsible for testing the samples. The application part for the management of ASF outbreaks should be based on the aforementioned application parts in terms of operation (esp. the monitoring of killed wild animals for certain animal disease pathogens) and interact with them in terms of content in accordance with the technical requirements. This application part should be activatable on an ad-hoc basis for each affected authority (veterinary authorities of the districts and independent cities and, if applicable, the client). Use should take place not only in the event of an ASF outbreak in Thuringia but also in the context of exercises in preparation for an outbreak. A final application part includes the recording and reporting of hunting bags by hunters. This report includes all huntable animal species. For this documentation obligation, the bag data from the aforementioned application parts should be reusable, but it should also be possible to record new bag data. A corresponding interface is to be provided for the necessary data exchange with the hunting statistics application of Condition – Integrierte Softwarelösungen GmbH. The hunters already have direct access to the hunting statistics application. The interface should enable them to gain access from within the IT application and thus facilitate reporting through data transfer. The application is to be provided for use by administrative staff in the Free State of Thuringia as well as the respective affected citizens in the Free State of Thuringia. As a result, the licence and terms of use must enable use by employees of the state, the municipalities and by non-administrative persons. The number of future users cannot be precisely quantified at present, as the use of the IT application is optional for hunters. However, the number of hunters in Thuringia can be a guide; it amounts to approx. 13.000. In addition, there are approx. 100 administrative staff.

sig_ec5d079694010ae15d02.description: The United States Department of Veterans Affairs (VA) is a Cabinet-level executive branch department of the Federal Government whose workforce is comprised of approximately 650,000 clinical and non-clinical personnel (of which approximately 450,000 are employees) charged with providing lifelong healthcare services to eligible military veterans at the 1,380 health care facilities, including 170 VA medical centers and 1,193 outpatient sites located throughout the country. Non-healthcare benefits include disability compensation, vocational rehabilitation, education assistance, home loans, and life insurance. The VA also provides burial and memorial benefits to eligible veterans and family members at the 157 VA managed or 125 VA grant-funded cemeteries. VA employs a highly skilled and multi-faceted workforce aligned with its mission, program, and operational needs. Workforce Development is one of the key factors to recruiting and retaining a high-performing workforce. VA employs individuals at every competency and skill level whether they are new to the workforce or experts in their occupation. That said, VA workforce needs differ at every career stage. VA Federal personnel are encouraged annually to complete My Development Plans (MDP). They work with supervisors to determine short and long- term career goals as well as short-term training needs. Training needs are then documented on the MDP. The VA’s Leadership Development Framework (LDF) is based on the Federal-wide United States Office of Personnel Management Executive Core Qualifications. By using the VA LDF, VA personnel will be better able to assess their leadership capabilities for developmental purposes and to support the Department’s workforce, talent development, and succession planning efforts. Certain VA Mission Areas, Agencies, and Staff Offices require its workforce to complete technical competency assessments and leadership competency assessments for non-supervisory positions. VA personnel will complete leadership and technical competency assessments through the Department’s Talent Management System (TMS) 2.0 or Learning Management system of record (LMS). VA personnel must also meet certain training requirements throughout the year. These requirements may be prescribed as Federal Mandatory Training such as No Fear Act, Information Security Awareness, Occupational Health, and Safety, or Telework. Some personnel must complete training required by their occupation or role such as Cyber security role-based training. VA personnel access most of their training through Talent Management System TMS 2.0. This platform provides a common LMS and learning content services that enable VA to maximize the return on taxpayer investment. TMS 2.0 has a robust and secure environment to accommodate approximately 450,000 end users, ~12,000 administrators and over 500 unique domains. TMS 2.0 is the Department-wide system for managing training records and activities at VA. The purpose of this contract is to acquire eContent, Digital Books, Professional Development Training and Support Services to meet the training requirement of VA.

sig_ec999f775ec71fe9b4b4.description: Request for Information (RFI) & Sources Sought (pursuant to Federal Acquisition Regulations- Part 5) Interactive Liquified Natural Gas (LNG) Training Platform Development Issued By: Department of Transportation | Pipeline and Hazardous Materials Safety Administration (PHMSA) Date of Issue: September 9, 2026 Response Deadline: September 28, 2026 SIC/Product Service Code: 7373 Computer Integrated Systems NAICS Code: 541511 Custom Computer Programming Services 1. Introduction The Pipeline and Hazardous Materials Safety Administration (PHMSA) is seeking information from interested parties and potential vendors regarding the development of an Interactive LNG Training Platform. The interactive, virtual LNG plant training platform should allow users to perform virtual plant walkdowns, review piping and instrumentation diagrams (P&IDs), and visualize process flows through the internal components of critical machinery (e.g., valves, vessels, pumps, compressors). This RFI is intended for market research purposes only and supports ongoing agency acquisition planning aligned with modern federal procurement principles. 2. Project Background and Goals PHMSA is committed to enhancing the safety and oversight of Liquefied Natural Gas (LNG) facilities. The objective of this project is to create a digital, high-fidelity, and interactive training environment that allows inspectors to simulate complex operational scenarios and safety inspections. Key goals include: Improving technical competency in LNG facility oversight. Utilizing 3D immersive technologies and digital twin capabilities to bridge the gap between classroom and field. Creating a scalable, modular curriculum that evolves with regulatory standards. Maximizing the leverage of commercial solutions and modern cloud infrastructure. 3. Key Information Requested PHMSA requests that interested respondents provide detailed information on the following categories: 3.1 Company Profile & Administrative Information Please complete the following table to assist PHMSA in market research and business size determination: Company Name Unique Entity Identifier (UEI) CAGE Code Socioeconomic Business Size (e.g., SDVOSB, 8(a), WOSB, HUBZone, Small, Large) Point of Contact Information (Name, Email, Phone) [Vendor Name] [12-character UEI] [5-charac ter CAGE] t[Socioeconomic Status] [Name, Email, Phone] Small Business Capacity: If identified as a small business, please state whether your firm possesses the internal capacity and capability to perform as the prime contractor for a project of this scope or if teaming/subcontracting arrangements would be necessary. 3.2 Technical Capabilities & Innovation Describe your firm’s experience in developing high-fidelity 3D simulations or "Digital Twins" for industrial facilities. What hardware and software requirements do you typically recommend for a platform of this scale? Explain your approach to ensuring interactivity and user engagement within a training module. Commerciality & COTS Analysis: To what extent can your proposed solution leverage existing Commercial-Off-The-Shelf (COTS) software components, modular training engines, or commercial 3D/VR frameworks versus requiring custom government-unique software development? 3.3 Content and Curriculum Design How do you approach mapping technical regulatory requirements (e.g., 49 CFR Part 193) into interactive learning objectives? Describe your capability to develop branching scenarios where trainee decisions lead to different safety outcomes. 3.4 Cybersecurity, Hosting & Data Rights Deployment & Cloud Posture: Describe your solution's typical deployment model (e.g., SaaS, FedRAMP-authorized Cloud, On-Premise, Hybrid) and compatibility with federal cybersecurity frameworks (FAR Part 40 / CUI handling). Intellectual Property & Licensing: Describe your standard licensing structure and approach to data rights for custom-developed 3D models, code, and scenario content (e.g., proprietary licensing vs. Government Purpose Rights / Unlimited Rights). 3.5 Past Performance Please provide details on up to three (3) recent projects of similar scope and complexity: Project Title Client Type (Gov/Private) Core Technology Used Year Completed [Project 1] [Gov/Private] [Tech Stack / Engines] [Year] [Project 2] [Gov/Private] [Tech Stack / Engines] [Year] [Project 3] [Gov/Private] [Tech Stack / Engines] [Year] 3.6 Rough Order of Magnitude (ROM) and Timeline Provide a non-binding estimate of the typical timeline for developing a comprehensive training platform with 5–10 high-complexity modules. Outline standard pricing models (e.g., fixed-price development, recurring licensing fees, maintenance, and ongoing support). 4. Submission Instructions & Industry Engagement Responses should be submitted in electronic format to the point of contact listed below. Please limit technical responses to 20 pages, excluding company brochures or supplemental past performance data. Industry Engagement / Vendor Demos: PHMSA may, at its discretion, invite select respondents to participate in virtual demonstrations or technical exchange sessions to further inform agency acquisition planning. USDOT Point of Contact: Loni Chinn Email: loni.chinn@dot.gov 5. Disclaimer: This RFI is issued solely for information and planning purposes. It does not constitute a Request for Proposal (RFP) or a promise to issue an RFP in the future. PHMSA will not pay for any information or administrative costs incurred in response to this RFI.

sig_ecc646b16c95f9add2d1.description: Die Landesmesse Stuttgart GmbH & Co. KG (LMS) is advertising services of an external Information Security Officer (ISO). The LMS intends to commission services of an external Information Security Officer (ISO) in order to improve the level of security comprehensively and sustainably. The implementation of an internationally recognised standard for information security management systems is envisaged. The security level of the LMS is intended to be aligned with ISO 27001. Certification is not currently planned, but could become relevant from a perspective standpoint (e.g. due to customer requirements). The external Information Security Officer shall be assigned the following tasks in particular: - Development and implementation of security strategies: Creation of security concepts, policies and guidelines tailored to the specific needs of the LMS. This includes the further development of the Information Security Management System (ISMS). - Risk management: Implementation and continuous updating of risk analyses and business impact analyses (BIA) to identify and assess potential threats. - Reporting: Establishment of reporting processes as well as regular evaluation and presentation of security-related information to the specialist departments and management. - Continuous monitoring: Monitoring the effectiveness of the implemented security measures and, as required, adjustment of the implemented measures. - Compliance with statutory requirements: Ensuring that the LMS complies with all relevant laws, regulations and industry standards in the field of information security. - Security incidents: Investigation, processing and risk assessment of security incidents incl. taking measures for damage limitation - Collaboration: Close cooperation with the internal "Information Security Manager" as well as the other specialist departments (especially IT) as well as the Security Operations Center (SOC), the Data Protection Officer and management - Internal and external audits: Support in preparation for internal and external audits on information security - Technical security measures: Involvement in the conception, evaluation and decision on the introduction or modernisation of technologies (e.g. new EDR solution, network segmentation), which is why corresponding IT and IT security architecture know-how should be available with the contractor. The contractor does not have to be responsible for the decisions, but must be able to advise accordingly in the sense of an advisory function in accordance with their role. The subject matter of the procedure is now the Europe-wide procurement of services of an external Information Security Officer (ISO) by means of a negotiated procedure with a preceding call for competition. Further information on the content of the tender will be made available to the bidders who are invited to submit tenders. The services are to be awarded for a period of 24 months (2 years), provisionally commencing on 1 April 2026.
sig_ecc646b16c95f9add2d1.title: Landesmesse Stuttgart GmbH & Co. KG - Europe-wide procurement of services of an external Information Security Officer (ISO)

Emphasis is put on the fact that this is a provisional document in the preparation and shall not be seen as a completed tender documentation. The content can be changed, supplemented or taken out before any competition is announced. Input that the tenderers provide as a part of the market survey shall not be seen as a tender and will not affect the further process or any future competition. Deadline for feedback The deadline for feedback is 14.09.2026, 12:00. The feedback can be submitted either in the answer box belonging to each requirement, or it is also possible to upload a separate document in the upload field.

Because of the close connection, these three subjects are combined and put on the market as a single contract and the tender is not divided into lots. The natural advisory function has a logical coherence with the audit (findings) and it is organisationally efficient and effective to outsource special audits to an accountant who knows the organisation and administration. The contractor to be engaged contributes to the following The contract relates to the provision of accountancy services for ROC Midden Nederland (hereinafter: ROC MN). The scope of the contract is based on the nature, size and complexity of the organisation. ROC MN is an educational institution in secondary vocational education with approximately 1.800 employees and an annual income/expenditure volume of approximately EUR 200 million. The organisation has 16 educational locations and a central supporting organisation with associated administrative processes. The contract is aimed at the appointment of a chartered accountant who: - performs the audit of the consolidated annual accounts pursuant to article 393 paragraph 1 Book 2 of the Civil Code and reports thereon; - fulfils the natural advisory function arising from the findings of the audit, also expressed in a management letter upon completion of the interim audit; - fulfils the special audits (including the audit of funding data) entailed by the operations of ROC MN. Because of the close connection, these three subjects are combined and put on the market as a single contract and the tender is not divided into lots. The natural advisory function has a logical coherence with the audit (findings) and it is organisationally efficient and effective to outsource special audits to an accountant who knows the organisation and administration. See the tender document for further details. Based on the Procurement Act and the ROC MN procurement policy, a European open tendering procedure will be followed.

sig_edde89768d6a64feffa4.description: AMENDMENT 1 TO COMBINED SYNOPSIS/SOLICITATION This amendment is issued to extend the due date for quotations to Wednesday September 23rd, 2026 at 5:00 PM Pacific Time. End of Amendment 1. This is a notice of intent to award on a sole-source basis and a Request for Quotation (RFQ) for commercial services prepared in accordance with RFO FAR Part 12. This notice and the attachments constitute the solicitation. This is not a request for competitive proposals; however, any responsible source may submit a timely capability statement and quotation for consideration. Solicitation No. 75H71326Q00076 is issued for continuation of the existing automated medical claims billing services used by the Indian Health Service (IHS), Portland Area, Western Oregon Service Unit (WOSU) and Warm Springs Service Unit (WSSU). This single SAM.gov posting covers two separate Service Unit requirements. The Government anticipates issuing two independently funded and administered purchase orders, one for WOSU and one for WSSU. Each purchase order will have separate funding, acceptance, invoicing, and payment records. INTENDED SOURCE AND BASIS FOR SOLE SOURCE The Government intends to issue the contemplated purchase orders to Change Healthcare Operations, LLC, 424 Church Street, Suite 1400, Nashville, Tennessee 37219-2367, UEI C7DYEBLK3PE1, doing business under the Optum/Change Healthcare brand. The intended source currently provides the Assurance Plus medical claims billing service used by the supported facilities. Continued use for the one-year interim period avoids duplicate transition, account setup, payer-connection, testing, and training costs and reduces the risk of interruption to claims processing and reimbursement. See Attachment 3 - Single Source Justification for details. A timely submission from another responsible source will be considered before award. An alternate source must demonstrate that it can provide the required service by October 1, 2026 without material transition delay, unpriced implementation work, or interruption to current claims-processing operations. SOLICITATION INFORMATION Solicitation Number: 75H71326Q00076 Request Type: Notice of Intent to Sole Source and Request for Quotation Contract Type: Firm-fixed-price commercial services; one monthly Assurance Plus subscription line item for each Service Unit Set-Aside: Full and Open Competition NAICS Code: 518210 - Computing Infrastructure Providers, Data Processing, Web Hosting, and Related Services Product Service Code: DA10 - IT and Telecom - Business Application/Application Development Software as a Service Issue Date: September 15, 2026 Questions Due: September 16, 2026 at 12:00 PM Pacific Time Quotation/Capability Statement Due: September 16, 2026 at 5:00 PM Pacific Time Anticipated Award Date: September 17, 2026 Submit To: jacob.blalock@ihs.gov and PORAOAcquisition@ihs.gov Email Subject Line: 75H71326Q00076 - Medical Claims Billing Services PERIOD OF PERFORMANCE The anticipated period of performance for each order is October 1, 2026 through September 30, 2027. LOCATION Western Oregon Service Unit. Chemawa Indian Health Center, 3750 Chemawa Road NE, Salem, Oregon 97305. Warm Springs Service Unit. Physical Address: Warm Springs Health & Wellness Center, 1270 Kot-Num Road, Warm Springs, OR 97761. Mailing Address: Warm Springs Health & Wellness Center, PO Box 1209, Warm Springs, Oregon 97761. ASSURANCE PLUS SUBSCRIPTION BASIS Each Service Unit requires a 12-month continuation of Assurance Plus based on 1,200 monthly subscription volume. The respondent shall quote current pricing for each Service Unit and disclose all rates or charges that could apply. Western Oregon Service Unit Monthly subscription volume: 1,200 Current account reference: Change Healthcare customer no. 1207343; site identifier 691-S15Y Current purchase order: 75H71321P00153 Performance period: 12 months Warm Springs Service Unit Monthly subscription volume: 1,200 Current service reference: Existing Warm Springs Assurance Plus service; prior renewal proposal dated January 23, 2026 Performance period: 12 months Pricing basis: 1,200 monthly subscription volume; maintain current scope For each Service Unit, the Offeror shall enter the proposed monthly Assurance Plus subscription price and 12-month total in Attachment 1. In the quotation, also state the applicable per-transaction overage rate, Paper Claims rate, HC Direct rate, and any other mandatory or usage-based charge; state N/A if not applicable. Existing ERA Transactions, Assurance Plus 837 Files Transfer, Assurance Plus Transactions, and related current functions are expected within the existing Assurance Plus scope unless the Offeror clearly identifies otherwise. ATTACHMENTS - Attachment 1 - Schedule of Items - Attachment 2 - Performance Work Statement - Attachment 3 - Single Source Justification QUOTATION REQUIREMENTS The intended source shall submit: Legal business name, address, UEI, quotation point of contact, and confirmation of current SAM.gov registration. A completed Attachment 1 with the proposed monthly Assurance Plus subscription price and 12-month total for each Service Unit, based on 1,200 monthly subscription volume. Confirm whether the quoted monthly subscription includes ERA Transactions, Assurance Plus 837 Files Transfer, Assurance Plus Transactions, payer-response/status/eligibility functions, and standard support; identify any exception. Confirmation of current Business Associate Agreement status and identification of any agreement or amendment required before performance. Any commercial service terms proposed for incorporation into the purchase orders. The quotation shall remain valid for at least 60 calendar days after the response deadline. An alternate source shall submit the same information and a concise capabilities statement showing that it can meet Attachment 2 and begin uninterrupted production service by the required date. BASIS FOR AWARD The Government intends to issue two (2) purchase orders to Change Healthcare Operations, LLC if the company accepts the requirements, submits complete pricing for both Service Units, and the Contracting Officer determines the price to be fair and reasonable. No separate technical proposal is required from the intended source. The Government may issue one, both, or neither purchase order; request clarification; negotiate price or terms; or cancel the solicitation. ORDER TERMS The 1,200 monthly subscription volume stated in this RFQ and Attachment 1 is the pricing basis for each Service Unit. The Offeror shall state what is included in the monthly subscription and how any overage is calculated. Any overage, Paper Claims, HC Direct, or other usage-based rate will apply only if expressly incorporated into the resulting purchase order. Each facility shall be invoiced separately, monthly in arrears, through IPP unless the applicable purchase order states otherwise. The annual base subscription amount will equal 12 times the awarded monthly subscription price. Invoices shall identify the purchase order, service period, monthly Assurance Plus subscription amount, and any separately authorized usage-based charge for the applicable Service Unit. No charge or rate is payable unless it is expressly incorporated into the applicable purchase order or a written modification signed by the Contracting Officer. No option, automatic renewal, evergreen term, or work outside the awarded scope is authorized without a written modification signed by the Contracting Officer. The Contractor shall comply with the applicable Business Associate Agreement and the privacy, security, and accessibility requirements stated in Attachment 2 and the resulting purchase order. sig_ee085171bead09108232.description: With this notice, HUS-yhtymä is establishing a dynamic purchasing system (hereinafter referred to as the DPS) for the procurement of ICT equipment and accessories. The products to be procured are defined in more detail in each competition held within the dynamic purchasing system. At the time of publishing the invitation to participate, HUS estimates that 15 to 30 competitions will be published within the dynamic purchasing system during the years 2025-2035. This quantity is a preliminary estimate which may change significantly as the procurement need and product grouping become clearer. Applications to participate in the dynamic purchasing system may be submitted throughout its entire duration. It shall remain valid until the date stated in the procurement notice, unless suspended or amended while the dynamic purchasing system is in force. Actual procurements shall be made through competitions held within the dynamic purchasing system, in which the subject matter of the procurement is described and specified. A separate contract shall be concluded for each internal competition. The contract period shall be defined separately on a case-by-case basis in the internal competition. A supplier may apply to join the dynamic purchasing system if they meet the suitability requirements stated in the ESPD form and in the section "Criteria for the subject matter of the procurement". All candidates who meet the suitability requirements shall be admitted.

sig_eeb197b1678b4abba95f.description: 1.0 INTRODUCTION & PURPOSE The 434th Contracting Flight (434 CONF) at Grissom Air Reserve Base, Indiana, is conducting market research to identify qualified, experienced, and interested business sources—specifically targeting small business concerns (e.g., 8(a), HUBZone, Service-Disabled Veteran-Owned, and Women-Owned Small Businesses)—capable of performing a Simplified Acquisition of Base Engineering Requirements (SABER) contract. This is a Sources Sought Synopsis for planning and market research purposes only. This is not a Request for Proposal (RFP), Invitation for Bid (IFB), or Request for Quotation (RFQ). No contract will be awarded from this synopsis, and no reimbursement will be made for any costs associated with preparing a response. 2.0 CONTRACT STRUCTURE & SCOPE OF REQUIREMENT The Government anticipates awarding a single-award Indefinite-Delivery/Indefinite-Quantity (IDIQ) construction contract. Ordering Period: Five (5) years (anticipated as a 1-year base period plus four 1-year option periods). Estimated Total Ceiling Value: $10,000,000 over the 5-year period. Project Range: Individual task orders are anticipated to range from $2,000 to $1,000,000, with an average task order range of $50,000 to $250,000. Place of Performance: All work will be performed on-site at Grissom Air Reserve Base, Indiana, and associated geographically separated units (GSUs) if applicable. 2.1 Scope of Work The SABER contractor will be required to furnish all management, labor, materials, equipment, and design services necessary to execute a broad range of concurrent, non-complex minor construction, maintenance, and repair projects. Work will span multiple construction trades including, but not limited to: carpentry, electrical, mechanical, plumbing, roofing, interior/exterior finishes, excavation, masonry, and demolition. 2.2 Tailored Pricing & Software Model (Critical Requirements) To streamline contract administration and expedite project delivery, Grissom ARB will utilize a highly efficient Job Order Contracting (JOC) procurement model: Unit Price Book (UPB) / Construction Task Catalog (CTC): Task orders will be negotiated and priced strictly using a pre-priced unit task catalog, specifically the current edition of the Gordian/RSMeans Construction Task Catalog (CTC) tailored to the Grissom ARB, IN area. No "Mock Project" Price Evaluation: Offerors will compete by bidding fixed, binding Adjustment Factors (coefficients) against the CTC for various work conditions (e.g., Standard Hours / Non-Secure Areas, Standard Hours / Secure Areas, and After-Hours/Weekend Work). Price evaluation for contract award will be strictly quantitative, applying bidded coefficients to Government-established weighted estimated workloads. No mock project or sample line-item estimate will be utilized during source selection. Contractor-Provided Software: The awarded contractor will be required to procure, maintain, and pay all licensing fees for an approved JOC estimating software platform (such as eGordian, eConverge, or an approved technically equal program) for the duration of the contract. The contractor must provide a minimum of two (2) concurrent user licenses to Government personnel at no additional direct cost to the Government. All software costs must be factored into the contractor’s bidded coefficients. 3.0 CAPABILITY STATEMENT REQUIREMENTS Interested sources must submit a Capability Statement (not exceeding 5 pages) demonstrating their ability to perform this specialized contract model. Responses must include the following information: 3.1 Company Profile Company Name, Address, and Website. Point of Contact (Name, Title, Phone, and Email). UEI Number and CAGE Code. Socioeconomic Status under NAICS 236220 (e.g., 8(a) with graduation date, HUBZone, SDVOSB, WOSB, Small Business, or Large Business). 3.2 Bonding Capacity Proof of bonding capability from a Treasury-listed surety. Single Project bonding capacity (minimum of $1.0 Million required). Aggregate bonding capacity (minimum of $5.0 Million required). 3.3 Technical Capabilities & JOC Experience Pre-Priced Contract Experience: Describe your firm’s experience executing contracts utilizing a Unit Price Book (UPB) / Construction Task Catalog (CTC) such as RSMeans or Gordian. Explain your process for developing line-item proposals from a CTC. JOC Software Proficiency: State your firm's capability to utilize JOC-specific estimating software (eGordian, eConverge, or equal). Confirm your willingness and ability to secure, maintain, and provide Government concurrent user licenses for the duration of the contract as an overhead cost. Coefficient-Only Pricing Feedback: Since Grissom ARB plans to evaluate pricing strictly via weighted coefficients (without a mock project), please comment on your firm's familiarity with this evaluation style and outline any risks or best practices you suggest the Government consider in Section L (Instructions to Offerors) regarding coefficient definition. 3.4 Past Performance / Relevant Experience Provide brief summaries of up to three (3) recent (within the last 3 years) and relevant projects of similar scope, complexity, and value (construction values between $100,000 and $1,000,000). For each project, please provide: Project Title and Location. Contracting Agency/Owner and Point of Contact. Contract Type (e.g., SABER, JOC, MACC, traditional design-bid-build). Award Value and Final Contract Value. Brief description of the work and trades managed. 4.0 SUBMISSION INSTRUCTIONS Please submit responses electronically in PDF format via email to: Contracting Officer: Cedric Roberts, cedric.roberts@us.af.mil Disclaimer: This Sources Sought Notice is for informational purposes only. The Government is under no obligation to issue a solicitation based on this notice. All information received in response to this notice that is marked Proprietary will be handled accordingly.

sig_ef12262962b8538c2af0.description: On behalf of the Danish Tax Administration, the Agency for Development and Simplification (UFST) would like to invite suppliers to a market dialogue on a new system for handling new EU legislation in relation to the FASTER directive, which is intended to ensure better, simpler, and more uniform procedures for the relief of excess withholding tax on cross-border investments. The directive is intended to ensure that EU countries have the necessary tools to effectively tackle tax fraud and abuse. The directive can be found here FASTER. With this market dialogue, UFST seeks to gain important knowledge from potential suppliers on the market who have experience from similar areas or solutions. UFST would also like to investigate whether there is a standard solution on the market already that can meet our needs or whether there are plans to develop a solution to support the FASTER directive. The market dialogue should provide insight into whether a standard solution exists or is planned to be developed that can support our needs in relation to: 1. Reporting of several detailed information on dividends from certified financial intermediaries 2. Digital tax certificate residences (eTRC), so that investors only need to obtain one digital certificate from their home country to document which EU country they are residents in 3. A system for ‘relief-at-source’ of dividend tax that will integrate with our existing system-portfolio Examples of business and technical needs (non-exhaustive): • The solution must exchange data to other relevant IT systems in UFST • The solution must integrate access to external foreign IT systems including, for example, a common EU portal • The solution must provide access and the possibility of approval and deregistration of Danish investors • The solution must enable automatic reporting of control data from the certified financial intermediaries • The solution must support case processing so that administrative users can handle situations where reported control data is deficient • The solution must enable the issuance and revocation of eTRCs • The solution must enable the approval and deregistration of certified financial intermediaries • The solution must issue and enforce powers of attorney • Handling of access control and compliance with logging and security requirements • Automatic control of submission data In addition, UFST is interested in what considerations the suppliers make in relation to which technologies and technology stacks the solution is expected to be built on, and whether the solution is implemented in Cloud or On Premise. In addition, it is particularly interesting to have solutions from suppliers that can document experience with larger common solutions in OECD and/or the EU. For the development of the standard solution and its ongoing maintenance, UFST would also like to clarify how the supplier generally intends to ensure: • Maximum automation of workflows • Full compliance with the FASTER directive and functional support of it • User-friendliness, overview (e.g. status), and reporting options • Compliance with existing legislation in the area.
sig_ef12262962b8538c2af0.title: Market research of system support for the implementation of the EU directive FASTER (Fast Track Assured and Safer Tax Excess Refunds)

sig_ef1b4cdc34ab50c1d6ec.description: The primary objective of this contract is to conduct a comprehensive, large-scale study on the current state and effectiveness of cocoa farmer cooperatives and farmer groups in Ghana and Côte d’Ivoire (incorporating but not limited to cooperative societies in Ghana and COOP CA and COOP simplifié in Côte d’Ivoire). This study will represent the first nationally representative analysis of cocoa cooperatives and farmer groups across the two countries. It will uniquely combine data collection at two levels: (1) the organizational governance and operational management of cooperatives and farmer groups, and (2) the individual farmer members, including their engagement, benefits, and challenges. By integrating insights from behavioural economics, collective action theory, organizational studies, and development economics, the study will adopt an interdisciplinary approach to evaluate how structural, managerial, and behavioural factors influence cooperative performance and farmer outcomes. The reason for purchasing this service is to generate actionable insights that enable stakeholders, including farmers, cooperatives, policymakers, and certification bodies, to enhance the effectiveness and sustainability of cocoa production systems in Ghana and Côte d’Ivoire. Specifically, the study aims to assess the readiness of cocoa cooperatives for ARS1000 certification, evaluate cooperative governance and member engagement, and investigate household-level investment strategies, including investments in sustainable agricultural practices or household assets. The ultimate goal is to identify critical barriers and opportunities to strengthen cooperative capacity, improve resource allocation, and reduce the financial and operational burdens of compliance with sustainability standards, thereby contributing to a more sustainable cocoa production system in the region.
sig_ef1b4cdc34ab50c1d6ec.title: Assessment of the Performance and Effectiveness of Farmer Cooperatives and Farmer Groups in the Cocoa Sectors of Ghana and Ivory Coast
