sig_ef8a23b520edd78e6d5f.description: The purpose of the tender is to contract operational services related to the crop monitoring and yield forecasting activities of the JRC.D.5 unit (MARSOP). Implementing Article 25 of the horizontal regulation of the Common Agricultural Policy REG (EU) 2021/2116 on Monitoring Agricultural Resources (MARS), JRC.D.5 provides DG AGRI with timely, independent, and high-quality information on crop state and development, including quantitative forecasts of agricultural yields and production in the EU and neighbouring countries. This information is used by DG AGRI to ensure food security and for decision-making in agricultural markets. The JRC provides matching staff for agricultural analysts and experts producing monthly JRC MARS Bulletins for Commission-internal and public use, which are well received by private sector stakeholders, academics and the general public. Such services have been outsourced since 2000 (MAROSP1-6), financed through a co-delegation with DG AGRI. The operational services sustain the operation and further development of the MARS Crop Yield Forecasting System (MCYFS) at the heart of the crop monitoring activities at D.5. For the current procurement, we plan to organize the operational services for the MARS System in three different lots: - Lot 1: Meteorological Services, Lot 2: Remote Sensing Services, Lot 3: Crop Modelling and Statistics.

sig_efab74e435deeab89cdd.description: As a university of excellence with around 44.000 students, Universität Hamburg (UHH) is not only one of Germany's strongest research universities and largest universities – as a venue for research, teaching and education, it is above all a modern knowledge organisation. Nowadays, this knowledge is primarily held in the form of digital information and processed and imparted using digital tools. However, digitalisation goes far beyond the digital representation of information and its processing using digital methods: In the sense of a synergetic interaction between analogue and digital, digitality has long been an integral part of the reality of studying, research, teaching, learning, life and work at UHH. The corresponding digitalisation strategy of UHH is understood as a university-wide frame of reference for a reflective approach to the opportunities and challenges of digital transformation as well as the successful implementation of digitalisation projects and undertakings. The project "Support by a Managed Security Service Provider (MSSP)" aims to cover the security requirements of UHH's existing IT through a suitable service provider, provided this is not met by internal capacities. The subject of this procurement is the establishment and operation of a Security Operations Centre based at UHH, funded by the BWFG: ▪ Universität Hamburg (UHH) ▪ Hamburg University of Applied Sciences (HAW) ▪ Hamburg University of Technology Universität Hamburg (TUHH) ▪ HafenCity University Hamburg Universität Hamburg (HCU) ▪ Hamburg University of Fine Arts (HfBK) ▪ Hamburg University of Music and Theatre (HfMT). The tender essentially comprises services in the following areas: ▪ Computer Emergency Response Team (CERT) services ▪ Threat intelligence ▪ Security Operations Centre (SOC) ▪ Automation of responses to security incidents ▪ Incident response (IR) ▪ Operation of a Security Information and Event Management (SIEM) system ▪ Vulnerability scans and vulnerability management Overarching goals: ▪ Ensuring holistic operation, monitoring and continuous improvement of information security and proactively increasing the security level at Hamburg's universities ▪ Early detection, assessment and appropriate handling of security incidents ▪ Sustainable reduction of risks for the IT systems, data and business processes of UHH Lot LOT-0001: Managed security services and establishment of a security operations centre. sig_efe909fe1684943581b9.description: The public contracting authority is preparing a contract for the supply of an e-shop platform for the needs of the development of central public procurement. The intention is to supply a new software system designed as a modular platform for managing purchasing processes, supply chain management and monitoring the draw-down of contract budgets. The system primarily serves to connect organisations (buyers) with winning suppliers from public procurements within defined regions. At this stage (preparation of the competition), we consider it essential to familiarise potential tenderers with: a) what is being procured, i.e., the requirements for the subject of the contract, and b) how it is being procured, i.e., the BVA method as an innovative method of e-shop procurement, which is described in more detail in the second part of the document. The Best Value Approach (BVA) method was developed in the USA and is increasingly being used in EU member states in public procurements where quality is exceptionally important. The legality of the method is confirmed by several court decisions (e.g., in the Czech Republic) and it is also trained by the Slovak Public Procurement Office in an effort to enhance competition in quality in the Slovak Republic. Further details are given in the notice of initiation of preliminary market consultations and its annexes at the internet address: https://josephine.proebiz.com/sk/tender/81813/summary

sig_f00f6b1ea5230cedfeab.description:
Stromnetz Berlin GmbH intends to carry out a structured rollout of a video monitoring system (VMS) across its technical sites, operational and administrative sites as well as defined special sites. The aim of the tender is the expansion and rolling implementation of an existing video management system (BVMS) from Bosch Sicherheitssysteme GmbH with the scope of services comprising planning, execution, commissioning, documentation as well as subsequent service and maintenance work. The rollout serves to strengthen the physical security of critical infrastructure installations and properties. The VMS is not intended merely for passive observation, but rather as an active component of the security architecture to detect events, visualise them, support rapid situational assessment and enable subsequent processes. The existing system landscape comprises a central video management system, decentralised video storage, camera technology in the properties, clients for authorised users as well as the client's monitoring and network components. The subject of the contract is divided into 4 lots. The lot structure separates planning and control, technical execution, civil engineering work and service operations, whilst simultaneously establishing a binding overall context. The services are to be coordinated with one another in such a way that planning, civil engineering, installation, commissioning, documentation and operation intermesh within a uniform rollout model. All contractors must take into account project-related interfaces, the client's specifications, the relevant technical regulations and requirements for information security, occupational health and safety, and documentation. The rollout covers all technical sites (substations, network nodes) and all operational and administrative sites of Stromnetz Berlin. The number of sites to be considered ranges from approx. 110 (estimated value) up to a max. of 130 properties (maximum value). Regardless of whether the contract is awarded for individual lots or a combination lot variant, the services offered must ensure a consistent, secure, interoperable and fully documented overall solution. The decisive factor is the complete fulfilment of all requirements set out in the tender documents. The contracts (Lot 1 to Lot 4) become effective upon award of contract and have an initial term for the provision of services from 01.08.2027 – 31.07.2033 (6 years). The client is entitled to extend the contracts by two years, i.e. up to a maximum of 31.07.2035. Lot LOT-0001: Planning services, control, construction supervision and construction management. Lot 1 forms the central control and integration function of the VMS rollout. The subject of the services for Lot 1 is project management and coordination over the entire project duration, the creation and updating of the project organisation, schedule and milestone planning, interface control as well as reporting on costs, schedules, quality, risks and opportunities. The contractor for Lot 1 draws up the detailed concept and the property-related execution and installation planning as a binding basis for the execution services of the further lots. This includes in particular specifications for camera planning, power supply, data supply, earthing and lightning protection, switchcabinet and connection box design, IT security, communication matrix as well as site-specific planning documents. Lot 1 monitors proper execution, coordinates handovers between civil engineering, installation and commissioning, documents defects, accompanies acceptances and ensures complete final documentation. Interface management with regard to Lot 2 and Lot 3 is of particular importance: execution services may only be carried out on the basis of coordinated planning documents; deviations must be recorded and approved via change management. Brief overview of services: - Project coordination and site management, - (Pre-)planning/design of the overall solution, - Object-specific execution and installation planning, - Route/cable planning, - Video storage planning, - Switchcabinet planning, - Documentation, - Condition assessment/commissioning/acceptance. Lot LOT-0002: Execution services, field technology and switchcabinet manufacturing. Lot 2 comprises technical implementation based on the planning and coordination specifications provided by Lot 1. The subject of the services includes the delivery, manufacture and installation of the cabling, field technology, connection boxes and switchcabinets required for the VMS. These include in particular cable routes, power and data cabling, splicing and termination services, installation of camera technology, manufacture of connection boxes and system technology cabinets as well as establishing accessibility to installation heights (greater than 4m). Lot 2 also carries out the dismantling of old components and the withdrawal of existing legacy cabling. It supports the configuration and parametrisation of the field technology and assists with commissioning and acceptances. Lot 2 has an obligation to cooperate in construction site documentation and change management. Implementation is entirely dependent on the approved planning documents. Brief overview of services: - Delivery and manufacture of cable routes and cabling, - Delivery and installation of field technology, - Dismantling of old components and third-party systems, as well as withdrawal of legacy cabling, - Manufacture of switchcabinets and connection boxes, - Configuration and parametrisation of field technology. Lot LOT-0003: Civil engineering and foundations. The contractor for Lot 3 establishes the civil engineering and infrastructural prerequisites for the subsequent installation and commissioning of the video camera technology at approx. 30 locations with corresponding video mast systems. The contractor for Lot 3 is responsible for civil engineering, foundation, earthing and video mast services.

The services shall be provided exclusively on the basis of the planning documents drawn up by Lot 1. The scope of services comprises in particular the creation and backfilling of cable trenches, the laying of ducting and micro-duct bundles, cable drawing chambers and transfer points, compliance with laying depths and protective distances, consideration of site-specific soil, environmental and water protection requirements as well as the restoration of affected surfaces. In addition, mast foundations, foundation and ring earthers as well as support mast systems must be erected and documented in accordance with structural and planning specifications. Lot 3 must execute and hand over its services in such a way that damage-free, standards-compliant and economical further processing by Lot 2 is possible. Brief overview of services: - Civil engineering, foundations and support mast system. Lot LOT-0004: Service and maintenance. Lot 4 comprises the service and maintenance services for the existing and newly commissioned VMS system components. The subject of the services comprises services for the overall VMS system forming the subject matter of the contract, both at the central head-end level and for decentralised hardware and software components at the field level. These include in particular change management, release management, system support, proactive maintenance of operational readiness, service desk as a central single point of contact, incident management, problem management, remote and on-site support, documentation maintenance, consulting, instruction and training, service level management as well as maintenance services. Lot 4 thus assumes structured operational safeguarding of the system after commissioning and supports the client with the stability, traceability, further development and fault clearance of the VMS. Brief overview of services: - Service and maintenance for the video management system and field technology.

sig_f045a19fc14bb5dea42a.description: Great Places seeks to develop a Customer mobile application to complement and extend the capabilities of the existing Customer Portal. This application will serve as a new digital channel for customers. It will enable customers to manage their housing-related services more conveniently from their mobile devices, including rent payments, repair requests and accessing documents. The eventual contract will cover the delivery of core self-service functionalities including: secure customer authentication; ability to view and update personal details and preferences; access to rent statements and arrears; raising, tracking and managing repair requests with appointment booking; submitting and updating Equality, Diversity and Inclusion (EDI) data; accessing documents from the document management system; secure two-way messaging and reminders; reporting anti-social behaviour and environmental issues; and providing feedback and survey responses. The solution must integrate in real-time with our existing systems, comply with accessibility standards (e.g. WCAG), and meet security and data protection requirements. The partner will be expected to provide implementation, integration, testing, training, and post go-live support services, with a roadmap for future enhancements to extend functionality beyond the MVP. sig_f0c289458d8979cc723a.description: The Benelux Office for Intellectual Property (BOIP) is seeking information from suppliers regarding the future of the Benelux Patent Platform (BPP 3.0). The current BPP platform, BPP 2.0, is used by the National Offices of Intellectual Property of Belgium, The Netherlands and Luxembourg to manage their patent grant process in their respective countries. It has been initially built and implemented across 3 countries in 2014-2017, and has been evolving since this time through regular releases for all 3 countries, implementing functional and technological improvements. The vision for the BPP 3.0 platform is an evolution or a re-build of the platform, making improvements to functionality where necessary (e.g. user centricity), but also taking advantage of new technologies, such as making it cloud-ready; if appropriate, taking advantage of AI and other new approaches to software development (e.g. low code package solutions), where impact to users is limited but could create large improvements to the platform and make its maintenance and support more cost-effective. The scope of the services could include: Part 1 – An evolution of the current Benelux Patent Platform that is likely to consist of: · An industry-leading, long-term solution that will need to be configured in such a way to provide as a minimum functionality of the current platform, including specific processes and functionality of the patent industry for National Patent Offices; · It could be a newly build platform, bespoke or off-the-shelf system configured to the needs of the National Offices, which will enable carefully orchestrated business change from a user perspective, making potential transition and data migration as smooth as possible, whilst keeping the business operations uninterrupted. Alternatively, it could be an upgrade and improvement of the current platform, ensuring that future platform is technologically up to date and cloud ready, replacing or upgrading the software stack to the latest versions; · If appropriate, the solution should include services for data migration from the current Platform, including extraction, transformation and loading of the data from the current platform. Part 2 – A managed service for the current and future Benelux Patent Platform that is likely to consist of: · A service desk for internal users of all three Offices to handle incident and problem management; · Consistent releases for all three Offices for new functionality introduced as part of a change management process and maintenance and support of all software components of the Platform; · If appropriate, this should include transition of the managed services from the incumbent Supplier, ensuring uninterrupted operation of the platform and services to its users. Part 3 – Hosting infrastructure for the Benelux Patent Platform that is likely to consist of · The provision of the shared hosting platform for the users of the three National Patent Offices of the Benelux countries and for external users (e.g. patent applicants) of the system, compliant with the ISO27001 requirements. This could be either based on dedicated hardware and infrastructure, or high-assurance cloud environments (public or private) with strict compliance guarantees, taking into consideration data privacy restrictions and EU data residency, GDPR compliance, high availability and a low cost but highly secure infrastructure; · If appropriate, this should include transition of the hosting services from the incumbent Supplier, ensuring uninterrupted operation of the platform and services to its users.
sig_f0c289458d8979cc723a.title: New generation of the Benelux Patent Platform (BPP 3.0)

sig_f0e24f0a815eeb1b6a10.description: HUS requests your tender for a software service that manages HUS Pharmacy's enterprise resource planning, covering the operational areas described in the appendices. Processes and data concerning HUS Pharmacy's medication management will be configured into the software service to be procured. The software service must integrate with the systems used by HUS in its other enterprise resource planning (e.g. Oracle Fusion Cloud). The appendices to the call for tender (appendix 0 and appendices 1: Description of current operations) describe the scope of current operations through verbal descriptions by operational area. The purpose of the descriptions is to familiarise the tenderer with HUS Pharmacy's current operations. The appendices (appendices 2: Description of target state) describe the requirements set for the subject of the procurement by operational area using various process descriptions and listed requirements. The purpose of this is to express to tenderers the minimum requirements set for enterprise resource planning. In addition, objectives for developing current operations are described. Our intention is to replace the current system with a software service (SaaS) that enables process development and guarantees a qualitatively stable operation. HUS is seeking a SaaS-based software service, which must be based on software that is already in production use and ready-made, and a solution configured from it for the contracting authority. The project schedule is planned such that the software service will be implemented during the year 2028. The project will be initiated with a definition phase, in which the made descriptions are refined against the software service offered by the winning tenderer, thereby ensuring that the software service in question meets the set requirements and offers a clear development path. In this definition phase, the implementation project plan is also refined to such a level that the parties can commit to the execution of the project. The definition phase is invoiced on a time basis, for a maximum of 50 000 euros and for a duration of no more than four months. The appendix Description of the implementation project explains in more detail what must be produced during the definition phase. After the definition phase, both parties have the option, if they so wish, to withdraw from the project. Following the definition phase, the contracting authority and the tenderer will negotiate the target workload and price for the project in the manner presented in the call for tender. Other appendices to the call for tender describe requirements related to the implementation phase, ongoing services, and information security. The software service must be capable of being integrated in a conventional manner into various administrative systems. The interfaces of the software service are presented in the appendix "Integrations". Oracle FINA interfaces are individually described in more detail in appendix 2.9.3. The appendix "Draft Agreement" covers operations during both the implementation phase and ongoing services. The appendix "Price Form" describes the calculation of the comparative price of tenders and the procedures for establishing the target price.
sig_f0e24f0a815eeb1b6a10.title: e-Forms 2023 / EU / HUS 486-2023 Pharmacy enterprise resource planning system as a software service

Supply of a forest fire location system divided into two parts. Part No. 1 - Supply, installation and commissioning of a forest fire monitoring system based on long-range fire-fighting cameras together with software for automatic smoke detection. Part No. 2 - Supply, installation and commissioning of a complete unmanned aerial vehicle system with an automatic docking station for fire monitoring of forest areas. A detailed description can be found in the relevant parts of the contract. The subject of the contract consists of sets of equipment together with installation and commissioning, the task of which will be to enable automatic detection and location of forest fires, including long-range fire-fighting cameras mounted on observation towers together with necessary accessories and the equipment of the Inspectorate's Alarm and Dispatch Point (ADP). The purpose of the system will be to carry out continuous fire monitoring of forest areas. Fire-fighting cameras mounted on observation towers are to work with the supplied software for automatic fire detection, which is intended to increase the effectiveness of monitoring in the given area. The image from the cameras must be sent to the ADP via a radio link in the unlicensed band, supplied and installed under this contract. The transmission system must be designed in a way that enables the future change of the transmission medium from radio to fibre-optic without the need to replace cameras, software and active network devices, with the exception of terminal devices used for connecting the fibre optic.. The Baczków and Hysne towers should be retrofitted with an Off-Grid power supply installation, and the ADP with a UPS emergency power supply system. The power supply must meet the requirements of PN-EN 62040-5-3:2017-05 (UPS systems) or equivalent. The installation must meet the requirements of PN-EN 62446-1:2016-08 (Photovoltaic installations) or equivalent, PN-EN 62446-1:2016-08/A1:2019-01 (Testing of PV installations) or equivalent, PN-EN 62109-2:2011 (Inverter safety) or equivalent and PN-EN IEC 62619:2023-02 (Lithium battery safety) or equivalent. The contract includes: - dismantling of the existing fire monitoring system, - supply and installation of 3 cameras for observing forest areas on the Baczków, Hysne and Dąbrowa fire-fighting towers, - supply and installation of sprinklers together with a fluid tank for the mounted cameras, - supply and installation of an off-grid power supply on the Baczków and Hysne towers. sig_f190c6d0543acc5586a5.description: The European Green Deal is the roadmap for making the EU’s economy sustainable. It is a set of policy initiatives with the overarching aim of making Europe climate neutral by 2050. The "Economics of Climate Change, Energy and Transport" Unit (JRC.C.6) of the Joint Research Centre supports the European Commission’s European Green Deal by performing economics-based research in several areas related to energy and climate change. This work includes the development of a reference toolset of economic models and the completion of associated research activities to improve the models' reliability and robustness. The JRC.C.6 Unit is based in Seville, Spain. JRC.C.6 is seeking to strengthen its socio-economic research and modelling capabilities by expanding its coverage of modelling areas and by updating and improving its existing models and toolsets. The unit JRC.C.6 maintains, develops and applies a number of quantitative tools to analyse the impact of different policies on the energy demand and supply sectors, as well as tools for macro-economic modelling. This toolset comprises the EU and global partial equilibrium models POTEnCIA and POLES including their corresponding databases (notably JRC-IDEES), and the global general equilibrium model JRC-GEM-E3. All these tools are able to provide model output in terms of CO2 emissions. The comprehensive modelling of climate change mitigation scenarios requires additional information as regards non-CO2 greenhouse gas emissions as well as on emissions and sinks related to land use, land use change and forestry offsets (LULUCF). Besides, climate action can have important co[1]benefits in terms of reduced emissions of air pollutants and of improved air quality. This Framework Contract aims at supporting the operation of the abovementioned set of models by providing the JRC with data, methods and results relevant for the analysis of non-CO2 greenhouse gas emissions, emissions of air pollutants (including air quality impacts), and LULUCF offsets.
sig_f190c6d0543acc5586a5.title: Provision of services to support economic modelling of climate change and energy policies: Modelling of non-CO2 greenhouse gases, air pollutants, and LULUCF offsets

sig_f1cdfe45e91beb444607.description: Dundee City Council intends to procure a construction consultant resource and project management system to improve the planning, allocation and monitoring of architectural, engineering and specialist consultancy resources across its capital and housing programmes. The system will complement existing corporate and client-side systems, including Civica, by providing enhanced resource planning, capacity forecasting, workload visibility, timesheet reporting and management information. The objective is to improve service efficiency, strengthen forward planning, support evidence-based resource decisions and provide greater assurance over programme delivery, capacity utilisation and value for money. Lot 1: . Dundee City Council is undertaking this Prior Information Notice (PIN) and market engagement exercise to better understand the solutions currently available within the market for construction consultant resource and project management software. The information gathered will assist the Council in developing its procurement strategy, refining its requirements and determining the most appropriate route to market. As part of this exercise, the Council intends to invite selected suppliers to participate in product demonstrations, currently anticipated to take place during early October 2026 (please note, these dates are indicative only). These demonstrations will provide an opportunity for the Council to gain a greater understanding of available solutions, functionality, implementation approaches and delivery models. Suppliers wishing to be considered for participation in the demonstration stage are requested to complete and return the attached questionnaire. The information provided will be used solely for market engagement purposes and to assist the Council in identifying suppliers whose solutions appear capable of meeting the Council's requirements. Completed questionnaires should be submitted by 12 Noon on 25 September 2026 to trina.forbes@dundeecity.gov.uk. Suppliers who do not submit a completed questionnaire will not be considered for participation in the demonstration stage. The Council reserves the right to limit the number of demonstrations undertaken and participation in this market engagement exercise will not confer any advantage or disadvantage in any subsequent procurement process. Additional information: This PIN is issued for market engagement purposes only and will not be used to evaluate, select or exclude suppliers in any future procurement process. Information received will help Dundee City Council understand the market, develop its requirements and determine the most appropriate procurement approach. Participation is voluntary and does not commit the Council to proceed.

sig_f1ff1a84db1ec5d89195.description: This is not a prior information notice, call for tenders, procurement notice or invitation to negotiate, nor does the publication of the notice initiate a competitive tendering procedure. A possible procurement notice and call for tenders will be published later. The request for information does not oblige the contracting authority to carry out the actual procurement. This request for information surveys the market and obtains information regarding the procurement when planning the procurement of the Helsinki City artificial intelligence management system. The objective of this request for information is to obtain information on solutions, capabilities and alternative implementation methods available on the market before the actual potential tendering process. Helsingin kaupunki is preparing a procurement for an artificial intelligence management system, the purpose of which is to enable the management and documentation of obligations in accordance with the EU Artificial Intelligence Act (AI Act) and to support the lifecycle management of all the city's artificial intelligence systems. The artificial intelligence management system enables the management, demonstration and reporting of the obligations of the provider and deployer of the EU Artificial Intelligence Act with regard to high-risk artificial intelligence systems, and supports the management of all the city's artificial intelligence systems, the identification and management of artificial intelligence risks, and communication about artificial intelligence. The artificial intelligence management system will produce information for the city's management, artificial intelligence developers, and the city's services and websites utilizing artificial intelligence. The system will act as a central tool in identifying and managing risks, documentation, preparing communications and supporting deployment processes. Further information on the subject matter of the procurement is described in the appendix "Description of the subject matter of the procurement". sig_f25f26481aae4b630346.description: Hoogheemraadschap van Rijnland is preparing a European public tender for the design, realisation, commissioning, multi-year operation and multi-year maintenance of a green gas installation at AWZI Haarlem Waarderpolder. The installation is part of the overarching project for the renovation and new construction of the AWZI, including the renovation and expansion of the sludge and gas line, the new construction of the water line and the realisation of a new service building. The sewage sludge produced at the AWZI is centrally digested. The resulting biogas is partially upgraded to green gas, partially used for the AWZI's own energy needs and processed with a view to the production of liquid CO2. The sale of green gas and liquid CO2 and the financing of the Work are the responsibility of the contracting authority and do not form part of the contract. The contract is expected to include at least: receipt and conditioning of biogas; upgrading of biogas to green gas quality; separation, purification, liquefaction and storage of CO2; compression, measurement and control facilities and facilities for feeding in green gas; process automation and control; electrotechnical, mechanical and contractually assigned civil engineering and structural facilities; gas safety and explosion safety facilities; testing, verification, validation and commissioning; demonstration of agreed system performance; training, instruction, documentation, certification and transfer; multi-year operation, preventive and corrective maintenance, fault response and process optimisation.

sig_f34031d767ff90ebeb33.description: The subject of the Public Contract is the development, supply and implementation of the National Repository Catalogue (NRC) information system ("NRC System"). The subject of the Public Contract shall consist of the supply of the NRC System, including the design and implementation of the NRC System into the Contracting Authority's IT environment and the realisation of integration links, commissioning of the NRC System including the provision of trial operation. The subject of the Public Contract also includes subsequent operation support, maintenance and development services for the NRC System for an estimated provision period of 48 months. The NRC is designed as a central register intended for the registration and management of data regarding Czech research data repositories. Its aim is to provide reliable, machine-readable and long-term sustainable information on what repositories exist in the Czech Republic, who operates them, what metadata standards and ontologies they use, and to ensure connection to external services. The entire NRC architecture is designed to respect FAIR principles, thereby supporting interoperability, transparency and the re-use of information. The NRC will register all research data repositories that are or will be created within the National Repository Platform (NRP), or that will be connected to this platform. These are primarily 40 data repositories created within the NRP project (so-called pilot repositories) and the Open Science II call (other thematic repositories). These are entirely new repositories (e.g. CzBio) or innovations of existing repositories (e.g. Lindat/CLARIAH). The obligation to register a repository in the NRC is in these cases stipulated by the Rules for Creating New and Modifying Existing Thematic Repositories in the National Repository Platform and arises from the relevant legal acts of the projects. The NRC System must integrate the following components into a single, well-connected functional solution (deployed and customised in-house at NTK): 1. Cordra (NRC knowledge base) 2. Skosmos + Apache Jena Fuseki (vocabulary module) 3. MSCR (Metadata Schema and Crosswalk Registry) For this purpose, two components that are the subject of this public contract shall be developed by the supplier: 1. Middleware (application layer) 2. User interface (UI) Detailed requirements for the NRC System, its technical parameters and the functionalities of the NRC System are given in the NRC System Specification for Consultation Purposes ("NRC System Specification"), which the Contracting Authority shall provide to registered suppliers upon receipt of a signed non-disclosure agreement (see point 4 of the invitation).
sig_f34031d767ff90ebeb33.title: PTK_Pational Repository Catalogue

sig_f39e1119fdcfe02fd7c1.description: Short Description This Notice signals BIST's intention to go to market for the provision of Data Pipelines, Analytics and Visualisation (DPAV) services in support of the National Digital Twin Programme (NDTP) and is for Market Engagement purposes only. The National Digital Twin Programme is a BIST led programme developing trusted, secure and reusable digital twin capabilities across government and wider public sector partners. The programme develops open source technologies, interoperability mechanisms, data sharing capabilities and application-layer services to support improved decision-making through data and digital technologies. Description of the Scope NDTP is seeking to engage with suppliers capable of providing specialist Data Pipelines, Analytics and Visualisation (DPAV) services. The requirement will support the design, development, testing, deployment and continuous improvement of data-driven applications, analytics products, visualisation tools and supporting data pipelines across the NDTP portfolio. The scope may include the development of new applications and analytical capabilities, enhancement and extension of existing NDTP applications, creation of data ingestion and transformation pipelines, integration with nodes, node nets, APIs and data services, and the delivery of user-facing dashboards, maps, visualisations, analytical tools and decision-support capabilities. Suppliers may also be required to support geospatial analysis, scenario modelling, application deployment, technical documentation and transition to operational environments. The successful supplier will be expected to work within NDTP's open source delivery model, contributing code and associated artefacts through NDTP GitHub environments and supporting collaboration with government departments, public sector organisations, technical partners and other suppliers. To aid BIST in developing the specification, we are interested in furthering our understanding of the market and available capabilities. In particular, we would like to hear from suppliers with experience in application development, data engineering, analytics, visualisation, open source delivery, cloud-native technologies and integration of complex data services. Additional information: Additional Information Please note that should we proceed to market we will use the Government Commercial Agency (GCA) Spark DPS RM6094 to undertake this procurement. Only suppliers who are registered on the Spark DPS will be eligible to participate. If this opportunity is of interest, suppliers are strongly encouraged to register as soon as possible, as applications to join the DPS are assessed independently by GCA and processing times may vary. BIST intends to undertake the initial Spark DPS supplier filtering exercise during the week commencing 24th August. Suppliers wishing to be considered for this opportunity should ensure they are successfully registered on the Spark DPS and that their category selections align with the filters set out in Annex A before this date. Following the filtering exercise, BIST will issue a capability assessment questionnaire to the shortlisted suppliers. Completion of the capability assessment will be a mandatory requirement in order to be considered for invitation to tender. It is anticipated that the ITT will be published in September 2026. The contract is expected to have a value of up to £10.5 million and run until October 2029, with the option to extend for up to one additional year. This advance notice is intended to provide suppliers with sufficient time to complete Spark DPS registration and review their selected categories before the procurement is launched. Details can be found at https://www.gca.gov.uk/agreements/RM6094. Any queries relating to registering on the Spark DPS should be directed to GCA as BIST does not have any control over the process or requirements. Annex A - Spark DPS Filters Delivery Method AI & Automation Natural Language Processing Predicted Analytics Prescriptive Analysis Engineering / Materials Science Spatial Computing Data Data Presentation Location UK Security Above Official
sig_f39e1119fdcfe02fd7c1.title: Provision National Digital Twins Programme - Data Pipelines, Analytics and Visualisation PIN

sig_f3a68edde8703acddc60.description: This Challenge presents an exciting opportunity to make a positive difference in protecting children in Scotland from harm, an area of the highest priority for the Scottish Cabinet and partners. Scotland’s child protection system relies on Inter-Agency Referral Discussions (IRDs) to make timely safeguarding decisions for children (over 17,000 IRDs took place during 2024-25). IRDs are effective and work well as a process, however they are currently supported by fragmented IT systems, manual processes and localised records. This results in duplication, delays, and barriers to information sharing across agencies and local authorities. These inefficiencies increase administrative burden, reducing time available for direct support to children and families. The Scottish Government, Police Scotland and the National Social Work Agency (TBC) are seeking innovative solutions that will enable secure streamlined multi-agency information sharing for the existing IRD process, as well as providing real-time local and national data to improve child protection outcomes across Scotland.
sig_f3a68edde8703acddc60.title: CivTech 12.5 - How can technology support multi agency processes for the protection of children in Scotland?

sig_f3b8c5e60f281ca93dcc.description: The purpose of this above-threshold Public contract for services awarded in an open procedure pursuant to Section 56 et seq. of the Public Procurement Act is the conclusion of (i) a contract for the implementation of an application / applications focused on supporting financial risk management for the needs of Risk Tools, HBK System – Rating Calculator (“HBK System – Rating Calculator”; “Implementation Contract”) and (ii) a subsequent contract for the maintenance, support and development of the HBK System – Rating Calculator (“Service Contract”; the Implementation Contract and the Service Contract collectively the “Contracts” or “Contractual Documentation”). The subject of the Public contract is the supply and implementation of a new application or applications focused on supporting risk management tools, and the provision of related services, specifically: - supply and implementation of the HBK System – Rating Calculator; - development of Rating models according to the Contracting Authority's requirements; - independent validation of the developed Rating models; - services leading to the successful implementation of the HBK System – Rating Calculator in the Contracting Authority's environment; - provision of long-term support and maintenance and minor development for a period of 10 years from the implementation of the HBK System – Rating Calculator. Based on the Contracts, the subject of the Public contract will be realised with one supplier, whose tender will be evaluated as the most economically advantageous based on the evaluation of tenders. Rating calculator A rating calculator is a technological solution, i.e. a system / application or functional component that uses a Rating model to systematically evaluate entities. Rating model A rating model is a systematic tool used to evaluate a client's creditworthiness. The goal of the Public contract implementation is the simplification of processes, the use of modern technologies and approaches, and the flexibility of the HBK System – Rating Calculator fulfilling the Contracting Authority's premises. The Contracting Authority points out that through this Public contract it is seeking a supplier that will provide it with a complete solution, i.e. it will both supply and implement the HBK System – Rating Calculator (and ensure its support and maintenance), and create individual Rating models according to the Contracting Authority's requirements and ensure their independent validation. Rating models will be newly created in the HBK System – Rating Calculator with limited use of the Bank's historical client data. The Contracting Authority does not possess the know-how for the creation and implementation of Rating models and the selected supplier therefore cannot expect above-standard cooperation from the Contracting Authority in this area. The Contracting Authority is able to provide the selected supplier with a limited range of data, but is not able to provide the scope of data on which it would be possible to calibrate a Rating model. The subject of the Public contract is the supply, implementation, maintenance, development and support of the HBK System – Rating Calculator (including the development and validation of Rating models), the detailed specification and components of which are set out in detail in the annexes to the Contracts. The performance will be divided into two Contracts, i.e. into (i) the Implementation Contract and (ii) the Service Contract. Based on the Service Contract, the service, maintenance, support and minor development of the System will take place. A closer specification of the subject of the Public contract is regulated in other parts of the Tender documentation, especially in the binding drafts of the Contractual Documentation – Annex No. 6 and 7 of the Tender documentation, and the Technical specification of the Public contract – Annex No. 8. For more, see the TD.
sig_f3b8c5e60f281ca93dcc.title: HBK System – Rating calculator

sig_f407665173fc522d220b.description: Ballerup Kommune wishes to purchase a system that can handle the municipal salary negotiation process for all stakeholders. In a municipality, salary negotiations take place with the involvement of both employees, managers, and trade unions and employee representatives, which makes the task complex. The salary negotiation process involves data from several systems and many different stakeholders: HR, managers both centrally and locally, employee representatives and trade unions, as well as all employees in Ballerup Kommune. Today, the task is handled through manual updating and circulation of Excel sheets with a high risk of errors and GDPR breaches. The purpose of the purchase is to ensure a quality boost of data in salary negotiations, make it more person-independent and transparent for the stakeholders. There is also a desire to reduce the time spent by HR, employee representatives and managers in connection with the salary negotiation process. Ballerup Kommune has prepared a requirements specification and would like to invite suppliers to a market dialogue based on this requirements specification and, naturally, a demonstration of the supplier's solution. It is important to note that a development project is not desired, but rather a standard solution that supports our requirements. The market dialogue will be held at the following times: d. 6. October 2025 10.00-15.30 d. 7. October 2025 12.00- 15.30 d. 9. October 2025 11.30- 15.30 2 hours are allocated per supplier. Suppliers who may be interested in participating in a market dialogue are requested to show their interest by writing to Ballerup Kommune via Mercell no later than 1. October 2025, stating which date and time among the three possible ones above. Ballerup Kommune reserves the right to reject any interested companies if there are too many interested parties or if the company has a solution that is currently only on the drawing board.
sig_f407665173fc522d220b.title: Invitation to market dialogue regarding intended procurement of salary negotiation system

sig_f42dfbd119f70092f405.description: INTRODUCTION Mid Ulster District Council is preparing a procurement for the renewal, supply, management and optimisation of its Microsoft enterprise licensing, associated CSP services and specialist Microsoft expertise. This pre-market engagement exercise will help the Council understand available market models, risks, pricing approaches, support arrangements and proportionate requirements before any formal procurement is issued. PURPOSE AND OBJECTIVES OF THIS PRE-MARKET ENGAGEMENT EXERCISE The objectives are to confirm market interest, test the most suitable agreement route and service model, identify risks or dependencies, understand pricing and governance options, and inform the Council's procurement strategy. This is not a procurement process and responses will not be evaluated as part of any future tender. BACKGROUND INFORMATION The Council's Microsoft estate includes Microsoft 365, Dynamics 365, Teams, Power Platform, Azure, server licensing and associated Software Assurance requirements. Market input is sought on CSP, Enterprise Agreement or other Microsoft agreement routes, billing options, licence optimisation, tenant support, adoption, security and compliance support, escalation and access to qualified Microsoft expertise. STATEMENT OF REQUIREMENTS MUDC wishes to establish a contract with a suitably experienced Microsoft CSP partner to provide: • licensing renewal, supply and management through CSP, Enterprise Agreement or another suitable route; • licence optimisation, proof of licence, inventory records, renewal tracking and compliance reporting; • Microsoft 365, Azure, Dynamics 365, Teams, Power Platform, security, compliance, identity, endpoint and server licensing expertise; • support for billing, subscription changes, incidents, Microsoft escalation, account governance and roadmap advice; The Council also wishes to understand transparent pricing structures, including margins, discounts, billing models, separate professional services rates and how best to separate user subscriptions, device subscriptions, Azure consumption, server licensing, trial/free SKUs and advisory services. Responses should assist the Council in considering proportionate partner status, accreditations, insurance, service capability, support model and future evaluation balance between price, quality and added value. 5.0 PRE-MARKET ENGAGEMENT APPROACH INDICATIVE PROCUREMENT TIMEFRAME 7.0 Indicative milestones: PME published 10th September 2026 ; responses due via eTendersNI by 3.00 pm on 24th September 2026; procurement launch October , contract award December ; licensing renewal / contract commencement 31st January 2027. Lot 1: .

sig_f47670163e5812efefba.description: The Initiative D21 e.V. ("contracting authority") is a non-partisan, non-profit network of business, politics, science and civil society that campaigns for the promotion of digital transformation in Germany. Through studies, recommendations for action and dialogue formats, it supports the development of a high-performing, inclusive and future-oriented digital society. The subject of the tender is the execution, evaluation and documentation of two population-representative surveys within the scope of the project "The digital society - understanding, shaping, strengthening. Mechanisms, levers and success conditions of digital transformation (DiGeVe)" for the Initiative D21. Based on the collected and evaluated data, two publications are to be produced in the years 2027 and 2029. The project is funded by monies from the Federal Ministry of Education, Family, Senior Citizens, Women and Youth. The Initiative D21 is a leading non-profit civil society actor and the largest non-partisan network for the digital society in Germany. With around 140 member organisations from business, science, politics and civil society, the association, as an independent platform, combines social benefit with technological innovation. The association regularly publishes evidence-based studies, such as the D21 Digital Index and the eGovernment MONITOR. These studies provide a sound data basis for a digital transformation that both promotes equal opportunities and social progress and secures economic and state future viability. The studies are published on the association's website. The contractor (hereinafter referred to as the contractor) must carry out two large-scale quantitative primary surveys. To this end, the development and programming of the survey design, including the programming of questionnaires, are to be provided by the contractor (see chapter 2.1 of the specification of services). The contractor must regularly coordinate with the contracting authority (hereinafter referred to as the CA) regarding the content development and design of the questionnaires. The contractor must operatively carry out these data collections (see chapter 2.2 of the specification of services). Operational execution includes at least sampling as well as field management via the weighting and delivery of the quality-assured raw dataset. The data determined as a result of the data collection are to be prepared and statistically evaluated in two runs (see chapter 2.3 of the specification of services). In doing so, the contractor is to design complex statistical analyses and coordinate them jointly with the CA. Subsequently, the statistical analyses are to be carried out. The CA reserves the right to perform quality assurance on the results of the statistical analyses. The substantive interpretation of the results remains with the CA. The contractor must continuously cooperate with the CA (see chapter 2.4 of the specification of services). For further details, see the procurement documents.
sig_f47670163e5812efefba.title: Main study DiGeVe - Data collection & evaluation

sig_f4c779028a33c8757ac6.description: U.S. Maritime Administration (MARAD) A Study on Vessel Design Challenge RFP No. 693JF726R000016 REQUEST FOR PROPOSALS (RFP): The Maritime Administration’s (MARAD) Maritime Environmental and Technical Assistance (META) program is issuing a request for proposals (RFP) for a Vessel Design Challenge (Challenge). This Challenge intends to fund multiple design teams willing to undertake integrated design work to improve fuel efficiency and reduce vessel underwater radiated noise (URN) to create the next generation of U.S. vessels. Individual awards depend on number of designs proposed for the package. Awards are intended to be for not less than $150k and likely not more than $450k. Project completion timeline is 12-18 months. Total funding available is up to $1.25 million. PROGRAM DESCRIPTION: The META program (46 U.S.C. § 50307) is investigating the interconnections between broader fuel efficiency, reducing URN from vessels, and exploring potential co-benefits. It is the policy of the United States to revitalize and rebuild domestic maritime industries and workforce to promote national security and economic prosperity. Accomplishing this requires making United States-flagged and built vessels commercially competitive in international commerce, rebuilding America’s maritime manufacturing capabilities, and expanding and strengthening the recruitment, training, and retention of the relevant workforce. The most promising opportunities for optimizing fuel efficiency gains and achieving URN reductions are in the early ship design stage, using a systems approach. This requires intentional and integrated ship designs that prioritize fuel efficiency while simultaneously reducing URN. Advanced fluid dynamic modeling enables comparison among hull, engine, and propeller design and arrangement, providing valuable information to the industry about the return on investment (ROI) for various technology and design optimizations at the design phase. Individual technologies claim to provide efficiency and noise reduction benefits, but the additive cost-savings have not been quantified for applying technologies in series and demonstrating increased efficiencies across multiple areas. Recently published studies summarized the state of knowledge and availability of technologies that can be applied to vessels to improve energy efficiency while reducing vessel generated URN. Those reports crosswalk not only the interoperability of technologies and design elements, but the potential reductions, costs, and return on investment. The next phase is to demonstrate, through modeling, the benefits that can be realized through a systematic design approach integrating technologies with input from naval architects, shipyards, and technology suppliers on the efficacy of these approaches. By using this approach, Teams will begin at the drawing table to quantify the benefits of innovative technology integration into the design phase for application on new vessels. The Vessel Design Challenge is intended to facilitate the demonstration of novel vessel designs that meet or exceed international benchmarks for fuel efficiency and URN source levels. This Challenge is intended to fund multiple Design Teams willing to undertake this kind of integrated design work to create the next generation of U.S. vessels. PROPOSAL CONTENT Proposed Vessel Design: Design proposals can include: Existing projects that would be redesigned, Forthcoming projects that are just beginning the design specification phase, and Designs that are theoretical or more experimental which aim to create a new approach or design. There are no restrictions on eligible vessels, however, given the mission of the Maritime Administration, vessels should be commercially useful and generally would not include small watercraft, recreational vessels, or fisheries vessels. Eligible designs include vessels operating in coastal or inland waterways as well as the Great Lakes. Ideal proposals will be for new design approaches or design modifications that couple hull-machinery-propulsion approaches to maximize fuel efficiency, URN reduction, and ROI. Technologies should be centered around performance and demonstrating the feasibility and economic achievability of these combined approaches and should be dictated by capacity needs set by industry requirements (tug capacity, crew capacity, operations support, range, TEU, cargo etc.). Designs should note specifically the technology readiness level and the commercial availability of any technologies used. Design Team: The approach to the Challenge will include a design team. Teams should include description of partnerships, collaborations, and/or processes that will ensure success of the proposal. Further, proposals should identify the Team’s capabilities, related experience, techniques, or unique combinations of these that are integral factors for achieving the Challenge objectives to include experience that supports ability to successfully manage and achieve project goals and objectives of similar type and scope. Development of an ideal team should represent the concept of a design-build approach and include: Naval architect(s) Marine Engineer(s) Shipyard(s) Owner/operator/buyer (can be more than one) Technology provider(s) (including fuel supplier, as needed) May include operator/charter party, BCO, logistics partners, port/city/public entity, private financing partner. Teams may submit one or more vessel designs to the Challenge. Funding amounts will be based on: the number of vessel designs proposed their technology innovation, or a combination thereof One or all proposed designs may be funded depending on proposals. There is no limit to number of teams an organization can participate in, however, an organization may only “lead” one team/proposal. No identical teams with rotating “leads” will be permitted. Preference will be given to proposals with team leads represented by U.S. companies, those with U.S. headquarters, and those operating under the U.S. flag Methods: Proposals must include a detailed description of the design and modeling approaches that will be used to meet the Design Challenge Parameters as noted below, including those for fuel burn estimates and URN source level as well as modeling for return on investment and similar economic estimates and valuations. Timeline: The proposed plan should include the expected timeline (not to exceed 18 months) inclusive of kick off meetings with MARAD, design and technology integration and assessment, interim progress report detailing vessel design and technology application progress, data collection and analysis, and final report deliverables. Budget: All proposals must include a compete, detailed, and justifiable budget with general line items for various design components and stages including fuel, URN, and ROI evaluation and calculations. Budgets should demonstrate market conditions or similar that support these budget estimates. Description of key personnel, qualifications, and expected level of effort should also be included. Proposals may also include any additional considerations, outreach, or analysis recommended to achieve the goals of the project. Design Challenge Parameters Design specifications: The objective is for designs to meet or exceed these specifications for fuel efficiency improvement and noise reduction. Recognizing that this is a demonstration of technical feasibility and economic achievability, if these design specifications are not achievable, alternative efficiency and noise improvements should be documented demonstrating the current limits of technologies. These specifications should be considered aspirational to test the limits of the possible within the bounds of the practical. Energy Efficiency: 30% efficiency improvement over a typical vessel design with conventional hull and machinery arrangements and fuels. Underwater Radiated Noise Source Level: Underwater radiated noise source level is defined using the radiated noise level (RNL). RNL is the source level that has been calculated assuming sound pressure decays geometrically with distance from the source, with no influence of the sea-surface or seabed and is often used to quantify source levels of vessels. Below are the equations for URN limits for self-propelled commercial vessels. The limits are stated in decidecade band RNL (dB re 1 ?Pa2·m2). Frequency range / Hz Transit / dB re 1 μPa2·m2 10-100 169.5+1.5log10(f) 100-1000 191-9.5log10(f) 1000-50000 199-12log10(f) Operational Conditions: Vessels designs should be able to meet or exceed the specifications under what would be considered normal operational parameters for that vessel. The intent is not for these vessels to need to employ special operations or change their normal patterns, routes, or timetables to achieve the reductions. Normal operations should be considered: Typical transit/operating conditions Transit non-working; and working for under-tow/station keeping 85% maximum continuous rating Measurement Standard: ANSI/ISO standards or an appropriate and defensible adaptation of these to suit the needs and conditions of the operational state should be described. Fuel efficiency estimation methods should be described based on industry and/or international reporting requirements (e.g. Class society, IMO) Deliverables The main deliverable is a preliminary vessel design that includes some technical details including the hull form for hydrodynamics and fuel efficiency and the selection of propulsion and power systems (engines, propellers, and other machinery) based on the ship’s operational requirements and sufficient to meet the design specifications of the Challenge. Designs should also be validated for general stability and load analyses for the ship’s safety under various conditions. Design analysis should include the technology combinations, design adjustments, machinery and propulsion arrangements that achieve desired efficiency and URN specifications. Designs should note the technology readiness level and the commercial availability of any technologies used. Each design must include a full breakdown of the anticipated costs compared to a conventional design, including an anticipated ROI timeline and total ROI for the anticipated lifetime of the vessel. This should include a description of the additional costs for each technology element and the design and anticipated construction costs. There is no preferred technology or fuel/engine approach, but final reports should describe in reasonable detail those arrangements and technology combinations used to achieve the specifications. Since this is a concept demonstration for feasibility and economic achievability, challenges and barriers to meeting design specifications should be explicitly described. This should include findings regarding cost differences in achieving partial reductions; for example, the difference in cost between reducing fuel consumption increased rapidly after a certain point or the achievability of URN reduction became exponentially more expensive after a specific dB reduction. It should also include barriers to technology sourcing or availability and the realities of potentially building these vessels in the shipyard, i.e. does the experience exist at U.S. yards to integrate the design technologies and arrangements? These design components, technology and cost evaluations, and lessons learned should be included in a final report that can be made publicly available. Any intellectual property or business sensitive information, to include design plans and/or drawings, results of modeling, or technology or cost specifics will remain internal to the project team and Maritime Administration as not to undermine any competitive advantage. The final deliverable is participation in a debrief with MARAD to share results and lessons learned. There may be opportunities to debrief with other Challenge teams, pending willingness and interest to do so. sig_f4f86ef61d6d5a55b90f.description: The subject of the public contract relates to the Contracting Authority's project 'ECOCYCLE COMPACT: ADVANCED GREEN TECH SOLUTIONS FOR EFFICIENT RECYCLING', which is focused on industrial research, experimental development and prototyping of an innovative compact compactor for small and medium-sized operations. The Contracting Authority's project, within the framework of which supplies and services are being procured, is co-financed from the funds of the Operational Programme Technology and Applications for Competitiveness, from the Applications programme – Call III – DEEP TECH (reg. number: CZ.01.01.01/01/24_063/0006887). The Contracting Authority has divided the subject of the public contract into 8 separate lots. The subject of this part of the public contract is an expert analysis of the cyber security of digital, operational and diagnostic data of the ECOCYCLE COMPACT compactor prototype being developed, the design of appropriate security measures, expert cooperation on their implementation and limited verification of selected measures on the prototype.; The subject of the performance of this part of the public contract is the preparation of a strength analysis and structural verification of the pressing frame of the newly developed compactor, including the design and verification of key structural nodes and the creation of methodologies for their further development.; The subject is the supply of 1 pcs of a press brake. The CNC press brake is an electro-hydraulic pressing machine intended for the precise bending of metal components with high accuracy. It is equipped with CNC control for programming bending operations, which will allow for easy modification of production and adaptation of the design of parts as required. The minimum technical specification of the equipment is stated in the procurement documentation.; The subject of this service is the industrial design of the equipment and methodological support for ergonomic verification using virtual reality (VR). The goal is to create a modern industrial device corresponding to current trends in the field of industrial design, ergonomics, serviceability, safety and manufacturing feasibility.; The goal of this service is the development of a comprehensive study focused on the implementation of augmented reality (AR) and remote assistance into the maintenance and service processes of the compactor. The study will address the possibilities of using AR for effective support of workers during assembly, diagnostics, maintenance and service with an emphasis on the elimination of technical risks and the reduction of costs for service visits.; The subject of the service is the preparation of an expert study and a consulting proposal for the implementation of a digital work guide and documentation system for the production and assembly of the ECOCYCLE COMPACT compactor. The service will be based on the available design solution of the prototype, production and assembly documentation, the Contracting Authority's existing work procedures, the information systems used and the requirements of workers involved in production, assembly, inspection and document management.; The subject is the supply of material for the construction of a new generation frame, based on the frame design of 1301-566c (see Annex No. 1 of the procurement documentation). The new frame, which is now in the process of development, will be approximately 1,5× larger compared to the existing version. The supplier shall ensure the complete supply, i.e.: supply of material, supply of flame-cut parts, welding, machining, quality control, marking, packaging, transport to the Contracting Authority, documentation.; The subject is the supply of 1 pcs of a laser welding workstation enabling safe manual laser welding of steel, stainless steel and aluminium parts in the Contracting Authority's production facility. The minimum technical specification of the equipment is stated in the procurement documentation.
sig_f4f86ef61d6d5a55b90f.title: Supply of equipment, materials and expert services for a prototype of an innovative pressing technology

sig_f559dbdaeb69de5ac52b.description: This Invitation to Tender (ITT) is issued by NHS Wales Shared Services Partnership Procurement Services (hosted by Velindre University NHS Trust) ("NWSSP") on behalf of Hywel Dda University Health Board ("HDUHB"), which will act as the lead contracting authority and enter into the resulting agreement. Hywel Dda University Health Board, acting on behalf of Betsi Cadwaladr University Health Board, Cwm Taf Morgannwg University Health Board and Swansea Bay University Health Board, is seeking to procure a modern Community Information System to replace the existing Wales Community Care Information System (WCCIS), which is approaching end of life. The procurement presents a significant opportunity to deliver a strategic digital care record solution supporting integrated health, community, mental health and social care services across Wales. The Authority is seeking a cloud-ready, secure, resilient and highly interoperable platform capable of supporting a shared digital care record, mobile working, multidisciplinary care planning, advanced reporting, and seamless integration with national and local health and care systems. Suppliers will be expected to demonstrate strong implementation and data migration capability, alignment with NHS Wales Digital Architecture principles, robust cyber security and information governance arrangements, and a commitment to innovation, service transformation and long-term scalability. The solution will support a broad range of community services, including Health Visiting, School Nursing, Children's Community Nursing, Safeguarding and Community Nursing services, with the potential for future expansion. The resulting contract will play a key role in enabling person-centred, digitally enabled integrated care, improving information sharing, reducing administrative burden and supporting better outcomes for citizens across Wales. sig_f6005f8a139b8432723e.description: The City of Malmö wishes with this prior information notice to inform potential tenderers that the invitation to tender for the consolidation system is expected to be advertised at the turn of the month April/May this spring in 2026. The prior information notice is published to give tenderers better conditions to prepare their organisation to be able to submit an application in the procurement. The procurement covers a consolidation system. Consolidation means financial consolidation. It must provide a correct overall picture of the group's financial economy (administrative departments, wholly owned companies, partly owned companies and municipal associations). The overall picture is obtained by merging all financial information and eliminating all intra-group balance sheet and profit and loss items. Great weight will be placed on the supplier and the system being able to ensure that laws, rules and recommendations within the economic field can be complied with. The consolidation system must also be user-friendly and well-integrated to enable efficient handling, management and follow-up. The procurement will be carried out as a negotiated procedure where tenderers are given the opportunity to submit an application and feedback on the intended requirements specification to begin with.
sig_f6005f8a139b8432723e.title: System for consolidation of the City of Malmö group

sig_f639d5eed46725a782b6.description: Every year approx. 30,000 persons go up to the vocational test in Norway. The trade and craft test is decisive for trust in the certificate of apprenticeship as documentation of competence achieved. In order to maintain this trust, the test must be of high quality and considered relevant, and candidates must be assessed according to agreed professional standards that are used as consistently across disciplines, test committees and geographical areas as possible. The aim of the framework agreement is to ensure the necessary flexibility, professional breadth and capacity to follow-up the development of the test over time. The agreement also covers the competence test, which is a final assessment for training candidates. The work included in the framework agreement shall contribute to obtaining knowledge, further development of the test, increased quality and a more uniform assessment practice, so that trust in the certificate of apprenticeship and craft certificates as proof of competence is maintained. The work shall be carried out in close cooperation with the contracting authority and relevant actors in vocational and vocational training when necessary to understand problems and ensure professional anchoring, as well as develop implementing and evaluating measures. This can include dialogue with counties, the social work parties, professional advice, test committees and other relevant environments. Further clarifications will be in each call-off. We expect that there will be a continual need for development work, testing, evaluation and professional support during the contract period.
sig_f639d5eed46725a782b6.title: Parallel framework agreement for research and further development of quality and execution of the professional and craft test.
