sig_f64fbd7b1b6867fc525b.description: The City of Helsinki's Culture and Leisure Division is developing data-driven management and, in connection with this, visitor counting for its locations and related solutions. Visitor data is one of the most important key performance indicators for operations: visitor data is used, among other things, for resource allocation, operational planning and development, and for assessing the impact of operations. The goal of the visitor counting service is to collect comparable and accurate visitor data from the division's locations as automatically as possible for analysis and reporting needs. The SaaS (Software as a Service) provided by the supplier includes at least: • production of visitor data from the counting target according to the needs defined by the division • transmission of visitor data by providing an interface (interface service) for transferring data to the division's data warehouse • transmission of visitor data by providing a user interface (user interface service) for viewing the data • collection of visitor data from devices, as well as monitoring and reporting of data accuracy and coverage (incl. verification counts for measurement at defined intervals) • devices used for visitor data collection as a lifecycle service (HaaS service, Hardware as a Service): - installation, commissioning, maintenance, servicing, functionality testing and calibration of devices - monitoring of device operation - removal and recycling of device installations. The contracting authority is currently surveying the procurement of a new data platform and will put it out to tender in approximately late 2026. By submitting a tender, the tenderer undertakes to assist with integrations and to provide an interface from the visitor counting service to the data platform. The estimated total value of the procurement excluding VAT is 1 680 000,00 euros. The estimated value includes the actual contract period of two (2) years and, in addition, one (1) two-year (2) option period. The procurement is divided into three (3) different lots: - lot 1: indoor locations - lot 2: outdoor locations - lot 3: multi-purpose outdoor locations. The tenderer may submit a tender for as many lots as they wish. Tenderers will be selected for the framework agreement based on the most economically advantageous tender. Qualitative requirements (quality criteria) have been set as minimum requirements for the devices and services to be procured, which the offered devices and services must meet. In addition, the price comparison will compare the maximum prices per lot (hereinafter ceiling price) from cheapest to most expensive. The supplier provides a ceiling price according to the most demanding example location of the lot defined by the contracting authority. Based on the tender competition, a framework agreement will be concluded for the subject of the procurement, to which five (5) contract suppliers who have submitted the lowest ceiling price per lot will be selected, unless there are fewer tenderers meeting the requirements. The suppliers selected for the framework agreement do not have exclusive rights to the procurements covered by the framework agreement, but the contracting authority has the right to procure the same subject of procurement also from outside this framework agreement. The contracting authority also does not commit to specific procurement volumes during the framework agreement. A more detailed description of the subject of the procurement is described in this invitation to tender and its appendices. The locations in the lot have one or more entrances to the site. There is a need for location-specific breakdown of visitor data for different indoor locations. Such locations include, for example, libraries, youth centres, cultural centres and sports halls. A more detailed description of the service and the minimum requirements are presented in the Description of the subject of the procurement, Requirement Specification, Service Levels appendix and other appendices of the invitation to tender attached to the invitation to tender. The contracting authority estimates that 80 such locations will be put out to tender during the framework agreement period. The amount is an estimate and does not bind the contracting authority.; The locations in the lot have one or more restricted or unrestricted entrances. There is a need for location-specific breakdown of visitor data for different outdoor locations. Such locations include, for example, fenced tennis courts, skate parks, events in urban space, beaches, outdoor islands and trails. A more detailed description of the service and the minimum requirements are presented in the Description of the subject of the procurement, Requirement Specification, Service Levels appendix and other appendices of the invitation to tender attached to the invitation to tender. The contracting authority estimates that 82 such locations will be put out to tender during the framework agreement period. The amount is an estimate and does not bind the contracting authority.; The locations in the lot have several restricted or unrestricted entrances to the space and it includes several service points or spaces. Breakdown of visitor data is essential. Such locations include, for example, sports parks. A more detailed description of the service and the minimum requirements are presented in the Description of the subject of the procurement, Requirement Specification, Service Levels appendix and other appendices of the invitation to tender attached to the invitation to tender. The contracting authority estimates that 38 such locations will be put out to tender during the framework agreement period. The amount is an estimate and does not bind the contracting authority.
sig_f64fbd7b1b6867fc525b.title: Procurement of visitor counting as a comprehensive service, framework agreement 2026-2028 (2028-2030)

sig_f65cb197fb4b014a93db.description: 1 INTRODUCTION We kindly ask you to submit your response to this Request for Information concerning the planning of the procurement for a questionnaire and event management system. We greatly appreciate all responses received, and each of them will be taken into account in the preparation of any potential tendering process. With this Request for Information, we aim to map supplier offerings regarding systems that support and provide a smooth and appropriate user experience for the end user. More detailed information on the subject of the procurement can be found in appendix 1 "Request for Information Questions" of this Request for Information. The end user of the procurement is Istekki and its owner-customers. At the same time, we aim to familiarise ourselves with the market situation, products potentially related to the use of the system, and contractual and commercial terms, such as pricing. 2 ORGANISING MARKET DIALOGUE Based on the responses to the Request for Information, market dialogue sessions will be organised where suppliers can present their own services, products and options for implementing the subject of the procurement. Based on the responses to this Request for Information, Istekki will select an estimated approximately 3–5 tenderers for the market dialogue. Any market dialogue sessions will be organised at a time specified by 24.3.2025 the contracting authority. If market dialogue sessions are organised, they will be conducted in the Finnish language. Istekki will provide the companies selected for the sessions with more detailed schedules and a Teams meeting link at a later date. Additional information questions may also be posed to suppliers. Please note that the information, descriptions and estimates of the publication date of the actual tendering process presented in this Request for Information are preliminary and indicative. Final schedules will be refined as the preparation progresses. 3 RESPONDING TO THE REQUEST FOR INFORMATION We kindly ask you to submit your response by email to hankinnat@istekki.fi no later than 18.3.2026 at 12.00. The Request for Information is to be answered using the form "Request for Information Questions" attached to this Request for Information (appendix 1). Send the completed form to the specified email address by the deadline. All responses received to the Request for Information will be taken into account in the preparation of the invitation to tender, and they form an important part of understanding the overall picture. It is worth noting that this Request for Information does not oblige Istekki Oy to carry out the procurement in the manner presented in this document or its appendices. A potential tendering process may also be left unorganised. No separate compensation will be paid for responding to the Request for Information or participating in any presentation sessions. We would like to emphasise once again that this is a Request for Information, not a prior information notice, contract notice or invitation to tender. The purpose of the Request for Information is to familiarise with the market situation and gather information related to the subject of the procurement to support the planning of the future tendering process. Responding to the Request for Information is voluntary and is not a prerequisite for participating in a potential tendering process, nor does it bind Istekki to publish a tendering process. At the same time, we greatly appreciate the information provided by suppliers, as it helps us build the future tendering process into as functional and clear a whole as possible.

sig_f69f67ab6ecf615e9e4d.description: The Contractor shall provide Think Trends Software as an Agentic AI and Document Intelligence solution capable of processing structured, semi-structured, and unstructured adverse event documents, including scanned PDFs, handwritten or machine-generated forms, narratives, attachments, medical records, product complaints, lab reports, follow-up submissions, and case correspondence. The solution shall support end-to-end adverse event document processing through the following capabilities: A. Agentic Document Intake and Classification Think Trends Software AI agents shall automatically receive, classify, and route adverse event documents by submission type, FDA Center, product category, source, urgency, and case-processing requirements. The intake agent shall identify whether a document relates to drugs, biologics, devices, veterinary products, tobacco products, combination products, or other FDA-regulated products. Key capabilities include: • Automated ingestion of scanned PDFs, forms, emails, images, attachments, and electronic documents. • Classification of documents by Center-specific workflow, product type, and reporting pathway. • Detection of new cases, follow-up cases, duplicate submissions, incomplete submissions, and supporting attachments. • Intelligent routing to appropriate review queues, case-processing teams, or downstream systems. B. Agentic OCR and Intelligent Data Extraction Think Trends Software Agentic OCR shall combine optical character recognition, computer vision, natural language processing, large language models, and rule-based validation agents to extract key adverse event data elements from complex documents. The platform shall extract and structure critical case information, including: • Reporter, patient, animal, subject, or consumer information. • Product information, including drug, biologic, device, tobacco, or veterinary product details. • Adverse event terms, symptoms, outcomes, seriousness, and event narratives. • Dates, timelines, exposure details, dose, route, duration, lot numbers, manufacturer information, and product identifiers. • Medical history, concomitant products, lab results, device problem codes, clinical narratives, and follow-up information. • Center-specific data elements required for CVM-Drugs and CVM-Food, CDRH, CTP, CDER, CBER and HFP. C. Center-Specific Adverse Event Processing Agents The Contractor shall configure specialized AI agents within Think Trends Software to support unique regulatory and operational needs across FDA Centers. Each agent shall apply Center-specific data models, validation logic, terminology, business rules, and review workflows. Examples include: • CVM Agent: Processes veterinary adverse event reports, animal species, breed, weight, product exposure, dosage, outcome, and veterinarian/reporter information. • CDRH Agent: Processes device-related adverse events, device identifiers, manufacturer information, malfunction details, patient impact, and device problem descriptions. • CTP Agent: Processes tobacco product adverse experiences, product use patterns, health effects, consumer narratives, and product category information. • HFP Agent: Processes HFP-specific adverse event reporting requirements and associated workflows. • CDER Agent: Process drug product adverse experiences, product use patterns, health effects, consumer narratives, and product category information. • CBER Agent: Processes biologics product adverse experiences, product use patterns, health effects, consumer narratives, and product category information. D. Case Validation, Quality Control, and Human-in-the-Loop Review Think Trends Software shall incorporate validation agents to compare extracted data against business rules, required fields, confidence thresholds, terminology standards, and case-processing logic. Records that meet defined thresholds may proceed automatically, while exceptions shall be routed for human review. Key quality-control features include: • Confidence scoring at field, document, and case levels. • Source traceability to page, section, table, and line references. • Automated flagging of missing, inconsistent, conflicting, or low-confidence data. • Human-in-the-loop review screens for case processors and safety reviewers. • Reviewer acceptance, correction, override, and approval workflows. • Full audit trail of AI extraction, human edits, and final approved values. E. Data Standardization and Regulatory Output Generation Think Trends Software shall transform extracted adverse event information into structured formats required for case management, analytics, and downstream regulatory processing. The platform shall support configurable mappings to FDA data standards, Center-specific systems, XML structures, APIs, and reporting formats. Capabilities include: • Normalization of adverse event terms, product names, dates, identifiers, and narrative fields. • Mapping to Center-specific safety data models and controlled terminology. • Generation of structured case records for downstream review and processing. • API-based integration with FDA systems, case-processing platforms, data lakes, document repositories, and workflow tools. • Export to XML, JSON, CSV, database tables, or other required formats. F. Agentic Workflow Automation and Triage Think Trends Software shall automate repetitive case-processing steps while maintaining reviewer control for regulatory decisions. The system shall support configurable AI agents capable of executing multi-step workflows, requesting missing information, summarizing case narratives, identifying seriousness indicators, detecting duplicates, and prioritizing work queues. Workflow automation shall include: • Case prioritization based on seriousness, product risk, event severity, due dates, and Center-defined rules. • Automated summarization of long adverse event narratives and supporting attachments. • Duplicate and follow-up detection across submissions. • Exception handling and escalation workflows. • Generation of reviewer-ready case summaries. • Dashboard visibility into case volumes, processing status, aging, backlog, error rates, and productivity metrics. G. AI-Enabled Redaction for FOIA Compliance ThinkTrends will provide AI-powered redaction capabilities to support FDA's obligations under the Freedom of Information Act (FOIA). The platform will automatically identify and redact personally identifiable information (PII), protected health information (PHI), commercially confidential data, law-enforcement-sensitive content, and other exemption-covered materials from adverse event documents prior to public release or response to FOIA requests. Key capabilities include: • Automated detection and redaction of PII and PHI, including patient names, addresses, dates of birth, medical record numbers, Social Security numbers, and other personal identifiers. • Identification and suppression of trade secrets, proprietary formulations, manufacturing processes, and commercially confidential submitter information protected under FOIA Exemption. • Detection of law-enforcement-sensitive and inter-agency deliberative content subject to FOIA Exemptions. • Configurable exemption profiles aligned to FDA FOIA policy, Center-specific guidance, and applicable federal regulations. • Confidence-scored redaction recommendations with source traceability, enabling FOIA reviewers to accept, modify, or override AI-proposed redactions. • Human-in-the-loop review workflow allowing FOIA analysts to validate, annotate, and finalize redacted documents before release. • Generation of redacted PDF and document versions with visible redaction markers, exemption codes, and reviewer audit annotations. • Full audit trail recording every AI-proposed redaction, reviewer decision, exemption code applied, and final release determination. • Support for bulk redaction processing across large FOIA request batches, including multi-document packages and rolling requests. • Integration with FDA FOIA tracking systems, document repositories, and case management workflows. 1.3 SALIENT FEATURES OF THINK TRENDS SOFTWARE Think Trends Software provides the following differentiating capabilities relevant to FDA adverse event reporting modernization: 1. Agentic OCR Beyond Traditional OCR: Think Trends Software does not merely convert images to text. It applies AI agents that read, interpret, validate, cross-check, and structure regulatory information from complex adverse event documents. 2. Center-Agnostic Core with Center-Specific Configuration: The platform provides a common document intelligence foundation while allowing FDA Centers such as CVM, CDRH, CTP, and HFP to configure unique workflows, data models, rules, and outputs. 3. End-to-End Adverse Event Case Automation: Think Trends Software supports intake, classification, extraction, validation, triage, routing, human review, data transformation, and downstream submission/output generation. 4. Human-in-the-Loop Regulatory Control: The system keeps FDA reviewers in control by allowing them to review, correct, approve, or override AI-generated outputs before final case acceptance. 5. Explainability and Source Traceability: Each extracted field can be traced back to the original source document, page, section, and text reference, supporting transparency, auditability, and reviewer confidence. 6. Confidence-Based Processing: Think Trends Software assigns confidence scores to extracted data and automatically routes low-confidence or inconsistent records for human review. 7. Multi-Document and Multi-Format Processing: Think Trends Software shall process scanned PDFs, structured forms, unstructured narratives, tables, handwritten content where feasible, images, attachments, correspondence, and supporting records. 8. Duplicate and Follow-Up Detection: AI agents shall compare incoming submissions against existing records to identify potential duplicates, follow-ups, related cases, and case-history updates. 9. Reviewer-Ready Case Summaries: Think Trends Software shall generate concise adverse event summaries, chronology, product-event relationships, missing-field lists, and review-ready case packages. 10. Secure FDA-Aligned Deployment: Think Trends Software shall be deployable in secure government cloud, FDA-managed, or approved hosting environments with role-based access, audit logs, encryption, and integration with enterprise identity management. 1.4 TECHNICAL REQUIREMENTS Implementation of Think Trends Software for adverse event document processing is expected to deliver the following outcomes: • Reduction in manual data entry and repetitive case-processing tasks. • Faster adverse event intake, triage, and reviewer preparation. • Improved data quality through AI-assisted validation and standardization. • Greater consistency across FDA Centers while preserving Center-specific workflows. • Enhanced traceability, auditability, and regulatory transparency. • Improved ability to manage high-volume document backlogs and surge workloads. • Increased reviewer productivity through AI-generated summaries and exception-based review. • Scalable platform foundation for future FDA adverse event modernization initiatives. Please view the attached Request for Quote (RFQ) RFQ FDA-SOL-75F40126Q00384 document for additional information.

sig_f6e8231515164450f6a5.description: Artificial Intelligence (AI) Discovery and consultancy services for artificial intelligence (AI), implementation, support of AI systems, end-to-end partnerships, and access to a range of AI technologies. Updates 21 November 2025: We have extended this agreement until 23 February 2029. You will be able to buy and run tenders for services until the new expiry date. Description A Dynamic Purchasing System (DPS) that provides public sector organisations with access to a wide range of Artificial Intelligence (AI) services. What you can buy RM6200 Artificial Intelligence (AI) supports organisations at every stage of their AI journey. It supports: Users new to AI: you can purchase discovery services to help understand AI and its benefits. Established AI users: obtain licensing, customization, and support from suppliers. End-to-end support: choose comprehensive partnerships if you need both discovery and ongoing support. Available AI product types General AI applications, augmented decision making, data and analytics, and virtual assistants or chatbots. Medical AI Technology Health and social care bodies can specifically access applications such as: medical imaging software non-imaging diagnostic software symptom-based software. These applications support functions like screening, diagnosis, and improving system efficiency, in line with the AI in Health and Care Award. Contracts awarded under this agreement can last up to 4 years, based on how complex your project is. The DPS allows you to shortlist suppliers based on your needs using a range of filters. Once you have established your shortlist you can use this to run a further competition. Benefits complies with government standards, including the Data Ethics Framework and AI Procurement Guidelines reduces buying times through an easier route to market ensures ethical buying and supports strong ethics processes offers commercial flexibility to meet the public sector’s AI needs allows supplier shortlisting based on quality, price, and cultural fit (including social value ) provides a dynamic pool of suppliers that can evolve with the market includes bespoke Intellectual Property Rights (IPR) terms for the AI market promotes standards for AI and data-driven technology in healthcare Products and suppliers Please read the 'How to buy' tab below for detailed instructions on how to find out which suppliers are on this agreement. Lot 1: Artificial Intelligence (AI) Expires: 23/02/2029 How to buy Register as a buyer. Note: although pages are headed ‘Supplier registration’ this is also where you can register as a buyer Go to the Artificial Intelligence DPS and log in with your username and password. Click on ‘confirm’ at the bottom of the text, and agree to the terms of use. On your ‘Manage your DPS Category Exports’ page you now have 2 options (in the bottom right-hand corner of the page): view appointed suppliers Buyers are encouraged to conduct pre-market engagement before using the filters click on the link to create a new category export, this is how you filter the suppliers that can meet your needs Use the filtering tool to specify your needs, this will create a list of capable suppliers. Attach filters descriptions document in this section. save your filtered list of capable suppliers by clicking the ‘Save Category’ option shortlisted suppliers are a 100% match to the buyers selected filters from your ‘Manage your Category Exports’ page you can then export the list of suppliers and contact details (export is to an Excel spreadsheet) Log out of the DPS. Use the list to run a further competition. Invite the suppliers identified by the DPS to bid against your detailed specification and evaluation criteria. The list is valid for 2 working days only, from the date of its creation, because new suppliers may be applying to join at any point. if your further competition excludes eligible suppliers it could breach procurement regulations get a fresh supplier list (steps 3.2 to 5) if you do not use your list within 2 working days by clicking the ‘Search Again’ option for your export you can use your own eSourcing tool or the our eSourcing too l to run a further competition. Our eSourcing tool is free to use for public sector Evaluate responses and award the contract. Detailed buyer guidance is available in the documents section. You can watch the How to use the Artificial Intelligence Dynamic Purchasing System video. Documents Updates Crown Commercial Service (CCS) became Government Commercial Agency (GCA) on 1 April 2026. Documents published before this date may still refer to CCS. All contract documents remain valid for existing and new contracts, and there are no changes to how you work with us. sig_f6fe09a24878199d77b7.description: Numera Palvelut Oy (hereinafter Numera or Contracting Authority) requests your tender for a joint procurement concerning Printing and information services (Multifunction devices and related services) in accordance with the call for tender documents. The procurement is not divided into lots; instead, a single supplier will be selected, with whom Numera will draw up mutual procurement contracts.: The competitive tendering is conducted via an open procedure. The selection criterion used for the competitive tendering is the most economically advantageous tender, and the comparison criterion is [the best price-quality ratio]. Detailed information on scoring and comparison criteria is presented in the section Criteria for the subject of the procurement of the call for tender. If several tenderers achieve the exact same score with their tender, the Contracting Authority will draw lots to determine the winner. Drawing lots is an accepted method in procurement law case law. Parallel tenders and alternative tenders are not accepted. The procurement contract shall be valid for a fixed term of two (2) years. Thereafter, the contract shall continue until further notice. Numera's customer communities using the joint procurement and potentially joining it during the contract period are stated in appendix one (1) of the draft agreement. The procurement contract shall enter into force once the procurement decision has become legally binding or the Market Court has granted an enforcement permit for the procurement decision, and both contracting parties have signed a written procurement contract. The notice period for terminating the contract is six (6) months for both contracting parties. A customer participating in the contract may terminate the contract in respect of itself with a notice period of 6 months. By submitting a tender, the tenderer undertakes to comply with all conditions in the call for tender documents and any additional information provided during the procurement procedure. The Contracting Authority has the right to verify the information provided by the tenderer in its tender documents before making the procurement decision. If the information provided is incorrect, the tenderer may be excluded from the procurement procedure. The main subject of the procurement is multifunction devices for uniform use (emphasising A4-sized devices) for printing and scanning, document workflow management, and support and additional services related to the aforementioned devices and their services (e.g. secure printing, management solutions, toner and supply solutions, ordering system, etc.). The focus of the procurement is on cost-effective devices supporting A4 printing, X-archive scanning (healthcare XDS solutions) individual devices agreed on a case-by-case basis, taking GDPR into account in operations, support and maintenance services, and other additional printing services in accordance with the documents. This procurement does not include the procurement of printing paper, printing work, or printing services (e.g. digital and offset printing). It is possible to expand the procurement during the negotiation procedure as an option regarding printers connected to workstations via USB. Numera decides on the implementation of the option. In questions and problem situations related to the use of the tendering service, the tenderer must contact the service provider's (Cloudia Oy / Tarjouspalvelu.fi) Helpdesk: tel. 020 766 1075, tuki@cloudia.fi.

sig_f75214932dc650000c29.description: The tender process comprises a contract for the contracting authority's procurement of the supply, implementation, operation, maintenance and support of an enterprise resource planning (ERP) system. The procurement of an enterprise resource planning system is part of the contracting authority's new strategy to create a greater degree of uniformity in the IT area across the contracting authority's organisation with a view to realising both financial and quality benefits. "Uniformity" does not mean that all units in the organisation must use identical solutions, but that IT decisions are made on the basis of common principles, procedures and guidelines. In this way, coherence, standardisation where possible, and flexibility where necessary are ensured. The purpose of procuring a new ERP system is thus to achieve a higher degree of standardisation and harmonisation of processes across the organisation. This is intended to ensure simpler workflows, reduced complexity and more cost-effective operation. The contracting authority wishes the new ERP system to offer modern technological capabilities, including support for machine learning (ML), artificial intelligence (AI) and other tools that can contribute to increased automation and decision support. Likewise, easy access to new functionality via ongoing upgrades is a central requirement, so that the organisation can quickly exploit new opportunities without extensive customisation. The ERP system must function as the central core of the organisation's transaction layer, where all significant data and processes are collected and handled. This is intended to ensure data consistency, transparency and support an integrated ecosystem of surrounding applications. The annual value of the contract is estimated at three (3) million DKK excl. VAT. In addition, there is a one-off implementation with an expected cost of three (3) million DKK excl. VAT. The duration of the contract is set at 10 years, which gives a total estimated contract value of 33 million DKK excl. VAT. The total volume is indicative only and based on historical data and can therefore not be considered a guarantee of future turnover.
sig_f75214932dc650000c29.title: Competitive procedure with negotiation regarding a contract for the supply, implementation, operation, maintenance and support of an enterprise resource planning (ERP) system for Kredsløb A/S

Market exploration - voluntary prior information - No contract notice The Deutsche Bundesbank intends to obtain information on services for an IT maintenance contract for the research information system "Research Hub" as part of a market exploration in accordance with Section 28 of the Public Procurement Ordinance (VgV). The subject of this market exploration is to gain knowledge about IT services available on the market for the maintenance and further development of the web-based research information system "Research Hub" regarding the takeover of the existing codebase, for ongoing maintenance, security and dependency updates, and technical support (excluding hosting). Interested providers can contact the email address "research-hub@bundesbank.de" by 14.10.2026 with a brief description of their services and their suitability for fulfilling the stated requirements, stating the subject "Markterkundung - IT-Dienstleistungen Research-Hub", in order to participate in this market exploration. The Deutsche Bundesbank reserves the right to use the results of the market exploration for the preparation of a procurement procedure. Market Exploration - Voluntary pre-notice - No Contract Notice The Deutsche Bundesbank intends to gather information, as part of a market exploration pursuant to Section 28 of the Regulation on the Award of Public Contracts (VgV), regarding services for an IT maintenance contract for the research information system "Research Hub." The purpose of this market exploration is to gather information on IT services available on the market for the maintenance and further development of the web-based research information system "Research Hub," specifically regarding the adoption of the existing codebase, ongoing maintenance, security and dependency updates, and technical support (excluding hosting). Interested providers may participate in this market exploration by sending a brief description of their services and their suitability for meeting the stated requirements-with the subject line "Market Exploration - IT Services Research Hub" - to the email address "research-hub@bundesbank.de" by October 14, 2026. The Deutsche Bundesbank reserves the right to use the results of the market exploration to prepare a procurement process. Lot PAR-0001: Market exploration in accordance with Section 28 VgV for an IT maintenance contract for the research information system "Research Hub" - Market Exploration Section 28 VgV for an IT Maintenance Contract for the "Research Hub". This market exploration serves exclusively for information gathering and the preparation of a potential procurement procedure. It does not constitute a call for tenders or prior information within the meaning of procurement law. A procurement procedure will be initiated at a later date if necessary. The web-based research information system "Research Hub" supports, among other things, the management and processing of research projects, publications and associated workflows. The aim of the market exploration is to gain a general overview of the market as well as potentially suitable service providers and their service profiles. The focus is in particular on experience with the takeover, support and further development of existing software systems as well as with comparable applications in the scientific or public environment. At the present time, neither concrete service requirements nor a specific contract model have been defined. The subject of a possible later commission could - depending on further findings and the concrete demand situation - in particular be support services in connection with the ongoing operation, technical support, maintenance and further development of the system. A possible later tender may include content that deviates from or goes beyond this. In this early phase, the Bundesbank would particularly like to know: - whether there is a fundamental interest in potential support in this environment; - what general experience the company has with comparable web-based software systems; - in which areas of software development, system support or technical consulting there are special competencies; - whether there is experience with science-related applications, publication processes, repositories or comparable technical systems; - how the takeover and further support of an existing software solution could be structured in principle; - whether there is a fundamental interest in a non-binding information meeting. Interested companies are requested to submit a brief, general response regarding their service profile and their relevant experience. The response serves exclusively for market exploration and does not constitute an offer or an application to participate in a procurement procedure. Participation in the market exploration does not create any entitlement to later participation in a procurement procedure or any entitlement to a commission. Details of a possible later procedure and its requirements will be determined at a later date if necessary. It does not constitute a request for proposals or preliminary information within the meaning of procurement law. A procurement process may be initiated at a later date, if necessary. The contracting authorities are looking for a tool that offers efficient work flow and automated processes. The use ought to contribute to reduced the organisation's use of resources in procurement processes and contract follow-up and that the company can more easily comply with the regulations. The contracting authorities want a robust, modern and cloud based system that uses new technology to enable efficient data processing, automation of work processes and seamless integration with the existing infrastructure in the counties. The solution is expected to be maintained, upgraded and developed to support legislative changes, adopt new technology, improve the user experience, and provide continual value during the contract period. It is important that the procured system is developed in line with the market and contributes to strengthening the digitalisation work for the procurement discipline. The system shall assist with the transition to data driven everyday life for procurement consultants. In the future, it may be necessary to integrate artificial intelligence into your infrastructure, such as with Microsoft 365 and Microsoft Azure, to improve employee efficiency and provide access to verified information from trusted data sources, while maintaining security and data quality. The contracting authority wants a tool that, in the long term, can connect artificial intelligence to data in KGV/KAV and other parts of the system, so that employees can reliable information through interaction with artificial intelligence, independent of client. The main goals are: Streamlining of the procurement work, repaired complexity in the processes. Automation and improved work flow. Better compliance with the rules. Support for digitalisation and transition to data driven processes. Future integration of artificial intelligence, especially with Microsoft 365 and Azure.Need for integration with archive system FINT (Joint County InTegraions)What is GOOD? FINT Arkiv – Novari IKSFINT is a common digital platform that is used by Norwegian counties to standardise and make information available through open APIs. This contributes to increased efficiency, better data quality and reduced costs by enabling real time reuse of data. FINT Arkiv-integration shall be used by county entities included in this competition. Other affiliated entities may require integration in other ways, adapted to their system landscape. As the Contracting Authority consists of several entities, different archive systems are currently used. With FINT Arkiv, however, the underlying archive system does not function as the interface for the integration - FINT provides a common interface regardless of which archive system is used. Fint Arkiv is used by all of the counties in the country, byantikvaren and Bymiljøetaten in Oslo kommune as well as Sametinget.With FINT Arkiv the counties get an API with a joint information model for standardised exchange of archive information. The tenderer shall develop integrations that are easy to implement, maintain and reuse - and that can be shared with other public entities when relevant. The system shall be based on open standards and it shall provide sufficient documentation for both technical and functional understanding. The API shall support standardised protocols and formats and be available for integration without a need for comprehensive adaptations. The integrations shall be designed with modular architecture that enables reuse and sharing with other public entities. All the necessary documentation connected to the API, data flow and process design shall be provided and suitable for both technical and functional understanding. sig_f79e77664b464d5e454a.description: The far-reaching impact and rate of innovation in the computer and information science and engineering fields has been remarkable, generating economic prosperity and enhancing the quality of life for people throughout the world. More than a decade ago, the National Science Foundation’s (NSF) Directorate for Computer and Information Science and Engineering (CISE) established the Expeditions in Computing (Expeditions) program to build on past successes and provide the CISE research and education community with the opportunity to pursue ambitious, fundamental research agendas that promise to define the future of computing and information. In planning Expeditions projects, investigators are strongly encouraged to come together within or across departments or institutions to combine their creative talents in the identification of compelling, transformative research agendas that look ahead by at least a decade and promise disruptive innovations in computer and information science and engineering for many years to come. Now funded at levels up to $15,000,000 for seven years, Expeditions projects represent some of the largest single investments currently made by the CISE directorate. Together with the Science and Technology Centers and the National Artificial Intelligence Research Institutes that CISE supports, Expeditions projects form the centerpiece of the directorate's center-scale award portfolio. With awards funded at levels that promote the formation of large research teams, CISE recognizes that concurrent research advances in multiple fields or sub-fields are often necessary to stimulate deep and enduring outcomes. The awards made in this program will complement research areas supported by other CISE programs, which target particular computer and information science and engineering fields. Additionally, CISE offers Innovation Transition (InTrans) awards for teams nearing the end of their Expeditions as well as Secure and Trustworthy Cyberspace (SaTC) and Cyber-Physical Systems (CPS) Frontier projects. The goal of InTransis to continue the long-term vision and objectives of CISE’s center-scale projects. Through InTrans awards, CISE will provide limited funds to match industry support.
sig_f79e77664b464d5e454a.title: Expeditions in Computing

sig_f7b493df20383bf0b66e.description: The procedure is organised with a view to concluding a forest management services contract for the area of 22.550,91 ha, the management plan of the Viseu Forestry Office within the Maramureș Forestry Directorate expiring on 31.12.2027, it being necessary to initiate the procurement procedure in good time to comply with legal deadlines. The services involve the development of the forest management plan and, where appropriate, the additional study for modifying the provisions of the forest management plan, a product of the management activity with technical-organisational content, ecologically grounded, through which the works necessary to be executed in a production unit are established for a period of time, with the aim of bringing and, subsequently, maintaining the structural characteristics of the stands and the forest as a whole at the values corresponding to the optimal structural model, defined in accordance with the ecological, social and economic objectives pursued through sustainable management. According to the provisions of Art. 63 para. (11) of Law no. 331/2024 on the Forestry Code, as subsequently amended and supplemented, it is necessary for the development of forest management plans to be carried out through public procurement procedures. The management of the state-owned public forest fund constitutes a priority obligation of the forest fund administrators. The method of managing the state-owned public forest fund is regulated by forest management plans. Forest management plans and their amendments are approved by order of the head of the Authority. In the case of state-owned public land, the management plans provide data and information necessary for their registration/updating in the centralised inventory of goods in the state's public domain and for registration in the integrated cadastre and land register system. Requests for clarification formulated by tenderers during the advertising period of the contract notice may be made with a deadline of at most 18 days before the deadline for the submission of tenders. The contracting authority will respond to all requests for clarification formulated in compliance with the above deadline, once, in a consolidated manner, 11 days before the deadline for the submission of tenders. Forest management plan development services for the state-owned public forest fund managed by the Maramureș Forestry Directorate – Viseu Forestry Office, field phase 2027, for the area of 22.550,91 ha. The services include preparatory work, field data collection, data processing and drafting of the forest management plan, development of the GIS database and management maps, preparation of the necessary environmental documentation, obtaining the regulatory act issued by the competent authority for environmental protection, supporting the documentation within the Technical Commission for Forestry Approval (CTAS) and obtaining the order for the approval of the forest management plan.

sig_f80455249704c571f3c1.description: Keravan kaupunki requests tenders for a maintenance log and facility management system. Keravan kaupunki owns and manages an extensive property portfolio, which includes, among others: - schools - day-care centres - sports facilities - office buildings - other buildings used by the city. Managing the properties requires the coordination of several different data points and processes, such as: - maintenance and servicing tasks - energy consumption - water consumption - environmental conditions - alarms and deviations - reporting and analytics. In the current operating environment, this information is managed in several different systems as well as through partially manual processes. The fragmentation of information makes it difficult to form an overall picture of the state of the properties and slows down decision-making. In addition, the maintenance of properties increasingly emphasises the need to: - improve energy efficiency - identify deviations quickly - move towards predictive maintenance - utilise data to support decision-making. For this reason, Keravan kaupunki is procuring a centralised system that combines operational and analytical data related to properties into a single service.
sig_f80455249704c571f3c1.title: Procurement of a maintenance log and facility management system for the City of Kerava

sig_f84f33b219fc3a9f720d.description: The BMWE intends to tender a contract for the "FRAUEN unternehmen" (WOMEN in business) office. The office is to develop the content of the new priorities specified by the BMWE and develop new measures to sensitise girls and women to professional self-employment together with the "role model entrepreneurs" (VUs). In order to prevent or counteract social conditioning and to promote a cliché-free choice of career, the intention is to increasingly address general education schools in addition to vocational schools and universities. It is in the interest of the contracting authority (CA) to cooperate with other programmes/projects funded by the BMWE, such as the SCHULEWIRTSCHAFT-PREIS or the BMWE initiative group "Gründung in school" (Founding in school), and, where sensible and possible, to develop proposals for cooperation in order to exploit potential synergies. Furthermore, the "FRAUEN unternehmen" initiative is also a measure from the joint action plan "More female entrepreneurs for the SME sector". As part of the action plan, the office also participates actively as a member of the network. Through suitable measures, the topic of "female entrepreneurship" is to be placed more strongly in the public eye. To this end, a greater reach in social media is also to be achieved. Furthermore, a targeted expansion of the circle of active VUs is expected, in particular to include female entrepreneurs from the fields of skilled crafts, STEM, AI and digitalisation, from the East German federal states and rural areas, as well as those female entrepreneurs who have themselves taken over a business. The core tasks of the contract include, in particular, the provision of personnel, basic equipment for carrying out network coordination and project management, travel activities, and internal and external communication, including the annual preparation of a media concept (details in the respective work package). The following services are to be taken into account: - AP 1: Central contact point for VUs and all those interested in the initiative - AP 2: Matching of VUs with the target group - AP 3: Development and expansion of the external network/addressing multipliers and network partners - AP 4: External communication – strengthening the general visibility of the "FRAUEN unternehmen" initiative as well as the commitment of the VUs within the framework of the initiative - AP 5: Internal communication – strengthening the internal network of VUs and supporting the exchange of experience among VUs - AP 6: Monitoring, evaluation of the initiative and preparation of results - AP 7: Targeted expansion of the circle of VUs Lot LOT-0000: Office of the BMWE initiative "FRAUEN unternehmen". sig_f8984983de44f937d6ff.description: Provision of an Integration Platform for Social Security Scotland. Lot 1: . The technology estate on which Social Security Scotland’s business operations run is critical to delivering the services offered to the people of Scotland. Day-to-day business operations both within Social Security Scotland, and those conducted with the support of its partners, are supported by an extensive enterprise architecture of business applications and underlying technologies. These applications and technologies operate in concert by means of an integration platform, which is responsible for exchanging data between internal solutions, and between Social Security Scotland and its external partners. The core business application currently used by Social Security Scotland to facilitate such integration is contracted until the end of 2026 (with the possibility to extend until the end of 2027). It is currently the strategic core platform providing API (application programming interface) lifecycle management and enabling integration with external services. Note that for the purposes of this exercise, the term “integration platform” should be interpreted to mean the systems by which integration and API management are fulfilled. We are developing a strategy of how this service will look moving forward and would like input from suppliers on this by means of a Request for Information.

sig_f8a1fe8a7d4f75e336ab.description:
The subject of the contract concerns the provision of maintenance and technical support services for the IPTO GIS System (hereinafter the "Company") for the years 2027 & 2028, and includes the following: 1.1 Maintenance and support of Smallworld software from the manufacturer General Electric, with which the system was developed, and specifically of: • 26 run-time licences for the Smallworld Core Spatial Technology product, • 4 licences for the Smallworld WebMapServer SOM product, of the Smallworld GeoSpatial Server (GSS) product, • 16 licences for the Smallworld AddOn for Google Maps product • 4 Professional licences for the Smallworld GeoSpatial Analysis product • 80 Lite licences for the Smallworld GeoSpatial Analysis product. This maintenance and support includes: • The provision to the Company of new versions of Smallworld products made available by their developer, GE Energy. New versions may arise due to improvements or the elimination of errors and malfunctions in the software, as well as due to the integration of new features that allow the software to operate in a new environment (operating system, network, etc.). Also, new versions may arise due to the integration of new capabilities or due to monitoring technological developments in both computer hardware and peripherals, and in software (operating systems or other products with which the Smallworld software interacts). New versions also include supplements made available to correct errors in the current version at any given time. New versions are provided in the form of an installation programme, stored in electronic format within one month of the announcement of their release by the developer. • The provision to the Company of detailed manuals for the presentation, analysis and instructions for use of the new features incorporated into the new versions. These manuals accompany the new versions and are provided in electronic format. • The restoration of any anomaly that may occur in the Smallworld software or other software on the computers on which it is used, provided that the anomaly is due to weaknesses in the Smallworld products that appeared during their proper use and not due to misuse of the software, the operating system or the computer. To restore the aforementioned anomalies, the contractor may, at its discretion, either provide the necessary instructions by telephone, email or fax to Company personnel, or make an on-site visit, without additional compensation or remuneration. The contractor undertakes to address every aforementioned anomaly with the aim of resolving it within two working days. • The provision of advice by telephone or via email or fax, firstly for the installation of new versions and any intervention necessary for this purpose, and secondly for addressing critical points and/or malfunctions related to the Smallworld software, whenever they arise. Support is provided during working hours. 1.2 Maintenance and support of specialised applications for IPTO that have been developed, as well as their supporting sub-applications which concern: 1.2.1 Basic Modules  Transmission Lines Application  Substations Application which includes the digitisation of Single-Line Diagrams  Operational Diagram Application which depicts the electrical topology of the equipment,  Fibre Optic Network Application  Real Estate buildings and land plots Application 1.2.2 Supporting sub-applications of the basic Modules • Isolation limits calculation application (dynamic determination-calculation) • Environmental Licensing application for Substation and Transmission Line projects • Application for issuing Isolation Requests (Emergency and Scheduled) for parts of the System to the National Energy Control Centre • Installed equipment report application • Circuit outage and performance indicator calculation application • Geospatial visualisation of the entire IPTO fibre optic network, in combination with the Transmission System as well as the ability to record the relevant technical characteristics • Analysis of fibre optics into optical circuits, including the geographic visualisation function per circuit • Recording and geospatial visualisation of associated equipment (optical connectors, ODF, ODS) • Function for detecting available and unavailable optical circuits as well as the carrier using them. 1.3 Application for the interoperability of the GIS with the SAP EAM The maintenance and support includes in detail: • The upgrading of these applications whenever a new version of Smallworld products is made available. The upgrade includes the modification of the applications so that they are compatible with the new version of Smallworld products at any given time, while simultaneously incorporating all the capabilities of the applications and all the additional capabilities of the new version of the Smallworld products. • The possibility of parallel installation and use of the applications based on both the previous version of the Smallworld products at any given time and the new version of it at any given time, until IPTO S.A. decides to transition from the previous to the new version. • The restoration of any anomaly that occurred in the applications or other software of the computers on which they are used, provided that the anomaly is due to weaknesses in the applications that appeared during their proper use and not due to misuse of the applications, the operating system or the computer. • The obligation of the contractor to respond within one week to any request from the company for the provision of the works. 1.4 Provision of software development services The provision of 40 man-days (MD) of software development work is required, such as improvements, modifications and extensions of the system's applications.

The total estimated value of the contract - including the value of the options - amounts to the sum of six hundred thousand euros (€600.000,00), plus VAT and is broken down as follows: Budget for the subject for a period of twenty-four (24) months: €450.000,00 plus VAT, which constitutes the maximum offer limit for the contractual subject. Options: Value of options with a total estimated value of one hundred and fifty thousand euros (€150.000,00), plus VAT, i.e. 33,3% of the budget for: • increase of the contract subject, by assigning similar services, i.e. increase of the physical – financial subject of the contract, under the same terms and the corresponding unit prices or percentages, in accordance with what is defined, as the case may be, in the Price Tables, and/or • extension of the duration of the contract for up to six (6) months, under the same terms and the corresponding unit prices or percentages, in accordance with what is defined, as the case may be, in the Price Tables.

sig_f8ae74998e3e5212bd22.description: The subject of the contract is the upgrade and expansion of the multi-channel citizen information and service system 1555, which has been operated by 1/10/2022 as a single service hub for citizens and businesses regarding matters falling within the remit of the Ministry of Labour and Social Security and its supervised bodies. As part of the upgrade, the digital architecture and software subsystems, such as the web portal, knowledge base, artificial intelligence solutions and ticketing, are being enhanced so that 1555 can gradually transition from a predominantly voice-centric model to a balanced service model, where more complex and sensitive cases remain with human service through the reinforcement of specialised representatives, while simpler cases are closed via self-service services and automation. Specifically, the use of AI solutions is provided for both citizens and representatives, such as IVRs and AI agents for intent recognition and routing to digital solutions or appropriate specialised representatives, agent assist tools that retrieve content from the knowledge base to reduce errors and handling time, as well as analytics to understand requests and better plan staffing. At the same time, interoperability at the infrastructure or service level with the Citizen Request Management System (CC ticketing) and the utilisation of data from ticketing and the knowledge base are being enhanced, with provision for continuous improvement through feedback and conversation analysis. The operation of specialised consultants will be expanded and enhanced so that citizens have even greater access to personalised information. Digital systems will be further upgraded and new ones introduced with the aim of enhancing service delivery. A team of experts will be able to carry out targeted studies on specific subject matters of the serviced bodies, and surveys may also be conducted to further strengthen the bodies through the project. The development and management of the project are organised into work packages as follows: I. Public communication and service structure II. Technical Infrastructures III. Satisfaction surveys and Quality Assurance IV. Strengthening of bodies on specific subject matters – special surveys V. Project management VI. Service training Upgrade and expansion of a multi-channel citizen service system 1555
sig_f8ae74998e3e5212bd22.title: Upgrade and expansion of a multi-channel citizen service system 1555

sig_f8d9baeecda6b2718052.description: Description: Enterprise Data Pipeline Modernization and Data Consumption Services Purpose and Disclaimer. The Internal Revenue Service (IRS) is issuing this Sources Sought Synopsis for market research purposes to identify capable sources and obtain industry information that will assist the Government in refining its acquisition strategy for Enterprise Data Pipeline Modernization and Data Consumption Services. The Government seeks information regarding commercial availability, capable sources, small business and socioeconomic capabilities, existing contract vehicles, customary commercial practices, and recommendations that may improve competition, performance outcomes, and acquisition efficiency. A Draft Performance Work Statement (PWS) is attached to this Sources Sought Notice and provides additional information regarding the Government's contemplated requirements. The Draft PWS is provided solely for market research and planning purposes and remains subject to change based on market research results and the Government's evolving requirements. There is no solicitation at this time. This notice is not a Request for Proposal (RFP), Request for Quotation (RFQ), Invitation for Bid, or commitment by the Government to issue a solicitation or make an award. Responses are voluntary and will not be considered proposals. The Government will not reimburse respondents for costs incurred in preparing or submitting a response. Respondents should clearly mark proprietary information and should avoid submitting unnecessary proprietary or sensitive information. NAICS Code: 541512 - Computer Systems Design Services. PSC: DA01 - Business Application/application Development Support Services (labor) Background. The IRS is continuing modernization of its Individual Master File (IMF) Program and related taxpayer account processing and data management capabilities. Key initiatives include Individual Tax Processing Engine (ITPE)/Customer Account Data Engine (CADE) 2, Enterprise Data Platform (EDP), Taxpayer Account Management Services (TAMS), IMF Retirement Acceleration (IMFRA), implementation of legislative requirements, and Filing Season readiness. The contemplated requirement will provide enterprise data pipeline modernization, systems integration, technical engineering, data consumption, cybersecurity, DevSecOps, production support, and knowledge-transfer services to sustain and advance these modernization efforts. General Description of Work. The contemplated requirement includes enterprise data pipeline modernization; data engineering and integration; data product development and business intelligence consumption; metadata, governance, security, and data quality; self-service analytics and natural-language query enablement; AI-assisted legacy modernization support; DevSecOps and automation; testing and production readiness; operations and maintenance; and transition and knowledge-transfer services. See Attachment 1 - Draft Performance Work Statement (PWS) for the complete contemplated scope of work. Market Research Objectives. The Government will use information received to assess market capacity, commercial availability, potential acquisition vehicles, small business participation, teaming and subcontracting approaches, and other acquisition considerations. No decision regarding contract vehicle, competition approach, contract type, or set-aside status has been made. Capability Statement and Market Research Questions. Interested parties shall review the attached Draft PWS and provide a concise, tailored response addressing the following: Organization name, address, website, point of contact, telephone number, email address, Unique Entity Identifier (UEI), business size under NAICS 541512, and applicable socioeconomic status. Whether your organization can perform the full scope of the Draft PWS as a prime contractor. If not, identify the specific functional areas your organization can perform. Describe recent and relevant experience performing enterprise data pipeline modernization, data engineering, systems integration, data consumption, DevSecOps, cybersecurity, production support, and related services of comparable scope, scale, and complexity. Identify the customer, approximate value, period of performance, and relevance to this requirement. Describe the organizational, staffing, technical, and management capabilities necessary to perform the requirement, including the ability to recruit, retain, and manage personnel and mitigate performance and schedule risk. If significant subcontracting or teaming is anticipated, describe the contemplated administrative and management structure and the capabilities expected from team members. Are the services described in the Draft PWS available in the commercial marketplace? Identify relevant customary commercial practices, terms, service models, or other market practices the Government should consider. Identify any Draft PWS requirements that may unnecessarily restrict competition or create significant cost, schedule, technical, or performance risk, and recommend alternatives where appropriate. Identify any existing Government contract vehicles available to your organization that could support this requirement, including GSA contract numbers, NASA SEWP contract numbers, or other applicable Governmentwide Acquisition Contract (GWAC) vehicles. Identify your recommended contract type, acquisition approach, or other acquisition strategy considerations and briefly explain why the recommendation would improve competition, innovation, performance outcomes, or acquisition efficiency. Contemplated Dollar Value and Period of Performance. The anticipated total value is between $15 million and $20 million for a one-year base period plus two (2) 12-month option periods. This estimate is provided solely for market research purposes and is subject to change. Contemplated Place of Performance. The primary place of performance is anticipated to be the Contractor's facility. Performance may also be required, as directed by the Government, at IRS locations including Lanham, Maryland; Memphis, Tennessee; Austin, Texas; Dallas, Texas; and Ogden, Utah. Other IRS locations may be added based on future requirements. Submission Instructions. Interested parties that consider themselves qualified to perform the contemplated services are invited to submit a response to this Sources Sought Notice no later than Friday, September 25, 2026, at 2:00 PM Eastern Time. Responses shall be emailed to Jared Alexis at jared.j.alexis@irs.gov and Ebenezer Owusu at ebenezer.k.owusu@irs.gov. Telephone inquiries will not be accepted or acknowledged, and the Government does not intend to provide individual evaluations or feedback regarding capability submissions. Questions. Questions concerning this Sources Sought Notice should be submitted in writing to Contract Specialist Jared Alexis at jared.j.alexis@irs.gov. Attachment: Attachment 1 - Draft Performance Work Statement (PWS), Enterprise Data Pipeline Modernization and Data Consumption Services

sig_f9106a74aac8054cbda7.description: The Council requires a hub where users can access the system and have the ability to find any needed legislation or regulation to help ensure that whatever project they are working on is compliant with government law and standards. Lot 1: . The Council requires a hub where users can access the system and have the ability to find any needed legislation or regulation to help ensure that whatever project they are working on is compliant with government law and standards. A portal is currently used for this requirement that has 2 parts. The first part is the Construction Information Service legislation and technical information management solution. This service ensures that Fife Council will have access to the correct, current and complaint business critical information year-round. This service provides the Council access to 27,000 full-text PDFs with the ability to save, view, print, download, copy and paste any of these documents. There are over 350 publishers that add documents to this service. Fife Council require something equal in quality and quantity to this. The second part of the portal is Occupational Health & Safety Information Service. This single source library holds more than 90,000 documents from more than 400 publishers. The focus of this service is Health, Safety, Environmental and Fire. This service relates to risk management, hazardous substances and operations, control principles, movement of people and vehicles. Fife Council also require something that is equal in quality and quantity to this part of the portal. Overall, the current solution allows access to over 2.3 million industry standards, over 10 thousand engineering manuals, handbooks, reference books, over 76 million technical articles, journals and books, over 107 million patents, patent applications, unity models and abstracts and over 39 million industry-to-industry reference links across all hosted content

sig_f956a0a97d268a0369e2.description: The Technische Universität Darmstadt is among the leading technical universities in Germany and is characterised by innovative research and an international orientation. The university is structured into 13 departments and over 120 institutes. This structure is supplemented by eight directorates, which handle central administrative tasks such as student services, financial and personnel affairs, construction management and international affairs, thereby ensuring the smooth operation of the university. In total, the TU Darmstadt comprises around 24.300 students and about 5.200 employees. A special role is played here by Directorates IV (Real Estate Management) and V (Construction Management and Technical Operations), which are responsible for the administration and management of a total of 210 buildings on the campus. In the course of these demanding tasks, the directorates have relied on SAP ERP software with various modules since 2000. Since 2004, the SAP RE-FX (Real Estate Management) and SAP PM (Plant Maintenance) modules have been used in the aforementioned areas. For construction management, 2019 SAP PS (Project System) including the construction add-on from PROMOS was implemented. Currently, however, many internal processes in the field of building management and maintenance are mapped outside of SAP, as only a small part of the technical requirements can be implemented in SAP. Digital plan data (CAD) and digital spatial data (SAP RE-FX spatial database) are not linked. Data is reconciled manually. Documents are only partially available in digitised form, without reference to other systems. The diverse tasks and processes of the directorates are to be supported in future step-by-step by a uniform solution in the form of a CAFM system. The professional support requirement primarily consists of creating a uniform database in order to better link and evaluate information. Further requirements arise from the specialist tasks with regard to property and facility management and facility operations.
sig_f956a0a97d268a0369e2.title: IMMO4TU

sig_f997918e53159440ef8c.description: The subject of the procurement is the nurse call, fall detection, and movement monitoring systems to be introduced in Helsingin kaupungin sosiaali-, terveys- ja pelastustoimiala. Nurse call systems are used in the social, health, and rescue sectors in hospitals, senior centres, care homes, enhanced assisted living units, health centre inpatient wards, rehabilitation units, and other operating environments requiring round-the-clock care and supervision. In addition, the systems are utilised in home care support services and special units where clients may have a sudden need for assistance that requires a response. Nurse call systems are a core part of daily care and nursing work, as well as client and patient safety. They ensure that requests for assistance are forwarded without delay to the right personnel and that nursing staff are able to prioritise their tasks according to the urgency of the situation. At the same time, they support the occupational safety of staff, for example in threatening and hazardous situations, and enable the monitoring, reporting, and development of operations. The importance of nurse call systems is particularly emphasized in situations where clients' functional capacity is impaired, memory disorders are common, or the need for care is continuous. In such cases, the system's operational reliability, ease of use, and integration with other systems are not merely technical features, but factors that directly affect the quality and safety of care. The objective of the procurement is to ensure that the solutions in use meet current and future needs. This requires the systems to be scalable, compatible with other technologies, and capable of adapting to various care environments without complicating the use of the systems. At the same time, it is ensured that the solutions to be procured fulfil obligations regarding data protection, information security, and official requirements. Overall, nurse call systems are a critical part of the functionality of the service system, and their procurement must be carried out in a way that long-term supports the quality, safety, and cost-efficiency of services. The aim of the tendering procedure for the framework arrangement is to find up to five suppliers capable of delivering a nurse call system to the sector's sites that can handle traditional nurse calls (a client/patient can call a nurse to the room) and additionally utilise new technology that allows the system to proactively alert a nurse to the client's/patient's location in connection with risk situations (e.g., getting out of a bed, falling). The new technology aims to improve client/patient safety within the limits defined by law. A nurse call system is required in all new and renovated hospitals, senior centres, etc. In addition, the social, health, and rescue sector has several sites where a nurse call system was procured in the past but has become obsolete, and for which the supplier no longer provides maintenance and support. These obsolete systems must be replaced with new ones. The solutions that are the subject of the procurement will primarily be acquired as a comprehensive service provided by the suppliers selected for the framework arrangement. The subject of the procurement is described in more detail in the appendices of this call for tenders.
sig_f997918e53159440ef8c.title: Nurse call systems

The customer's objective purchasing need thus dictates which category is to be used. • In category 1 the customer specifies their need for competencies within IT consultancy services and need for number of hours, after which the Tenderer offers competencies and prices. • In category 2 the customer defines the task, after which the tenderer offers a task solution in accordance with the customer's statement of requirements. sig_f9d83fcf12b2cb686566.description: This document is not a contract notice or a call for tenders, but a market consultation in accordance with Section 65 of the Finnish Procurement Act, carried out by the contracting authority (also "HUS Group" and "Client") as described in this request for information. The purpose of this request for information is to clarify issues related to the procurement referred to in the title. The objective of the request is to obtain comprehensive information on the subject matter of the procurement in order to support the preparation of the procurement, so that any potential competitive tendering procedure can be conducted in the most appropriate manner possible. The contracting authority does not commit to carrying out the procurement. Decisions on whether to initiate a possible procurement process will be made after the market consultation. Summary of the description of the procurement: The HUS Group requests tenders for a large cancer panel test (also "product") for HUS Diagnostic Center. Laboratory of Genetics at HUS (Helsinki University Hospital) Diagnostic Center is an SFS-EN ISO 15189:2022 accredited laboratory providing diagnostic genetic testing services to all patients at Helsinki and Uusimaa Hospital District. The services include analysis of both constitutional samples and malignancies. The laboratory provides sequencing services mainly using local sequencing capacity (Illumina NovaSeq 6000, NovaSeq X Plus, Ion GeneStudio S5 Prime equipment). The large cancer panel test is intended for detection of small nucleotide variants (SNVs), indels, gene fusions, copy number variations (CNVs), microsatellite instability (MSI), homologous recombination deficiency (HRD), and tumor mutation burden (TMB) relevant for the genetic profiling of solid tumor samples and/or hematological malignancies as well as plasma samples for cfDNA analysis. The procurement is divided into LOT A and LOT B: LOT A - This lot contains panels for solid tumors and hematological malignancies and analysis software. - This lot includes an option for special panel for salivary gland tumors and an option custom panel. - The HUS Group will decide separately on the use of the option. LOT B - This lot contains panel for cell-free DNA and analysis software. - This test is based on analysis of total nucleic acids (RNA and/or DNA) extracted from paraffin embedded specimens and/or fresh-frozen specimens and from plasma samples. For more information please read the Appendixes.
sig_f9d83fcf12b2cb686566.title: Market Consultation, Large Cancer Panel Test HUS 324-2025
